profile.reviewText: MY BIGGEST FEAR IS always that an album is either warped or pressed off center. I can handle the warp within reason, but off center pressings really get to me deep. This occurs when the stamper after pressing so many copies, moves slightly off center. When the biscuit is then pressed, the result is an off center record that when played, the wow and flutter is very noticeable, especially in the inner tracks, towards the end of the side. I once returned a sealed Aimee Mann "Los In Space" $140- record for this very reason. The off center here is not as bad as in The Beatles White Album, but it is still an annoyance. Rather than go through the hassle of returning it, I just bore a slightly larger spindle hole and must adjust it before playing.
profile.summary: WISH THE US MANUFACTURERS WOULD INVEST MORE TIME ON QUALITY CONTROL

profile.description: Out-of-print on the US. 2 cd set. Sony/BMG.
profile.reviewText: I read a review on Amazon from a reviewer discussing Duran Duran mentioning that the band was excellent as a SINGLES band, but not as an ALBUM band. And if you own a DD album, you will see the truth of that statement as the best tracks are the ones that had been released as singles and often appear in different "hits" compilations, with the rest of the album tracks being forgettable, directionless and dull. I say the same for The Clash. If you were to buy this album, you'd have 95% of all their good songs. There are a few fillers here that I would toss out in exchange for the remaining 5%, but overall these are the tracks you will see in other "best of" compilations that were released years after this one. The only advantage I would see in purchasing more recent compilations are the remastered sound - which is a noticeable improvement over the sound on these discs, and maybe a couple of remixes, but no more than a handful. For the record (no pun intended) I owned/have owned the following titles: "London Calling", "Sandinista", "Combat Rock", and "Give 'em enough Rope" as well as this and other compilations in order to pass judgement on this band. Granted, some of these albums have more good songs than others and no single album can be full of hits, but overall, the average % of hits vs filler material found in Clash albums are 30% (of 10 tracks in an LP, 3 will be good or "hits", the rest will be forgettable).
profile.summary: This is as best as it gets. All other compilations are but rehashes of this one.

profile.description: Audio CD
profile.reviewText:
This was originally released as a cassette around 1981 which you could order from the Devo fan club using a form that was included in their LP "New Traditionalists". No Visa, No MasterCard, just either cash or check. The album contains a lot of their better known songs but in an instrumental format and removing all guitars or drums, also changing the tempo - leaving only muffled keyboards and the bass for an "EZ Listening" experience.
Some songs are still recognizable, while others will take a while to catch. One example ("It's a Beautiful World") can be found in the remastered version CD of the "New Traditionalists" album as the last "bonus" track of the CD. Don't expect high quality sound, as the entire album sounds like it was recorded or mastered with the treble knob all the way down to 0.
I remember paying like $12 for the CD which I later sold for $20 many years ago.
Only because it is no longer in print does this CD command such ridiculously high prices as I see today, but if you were to hear it in you tube, you'd most likely not be moved to pay more than $5- for it, as a novelty item, for completists only, but not as a crucial piece in your collection.
profile.summary: Nice Novelty Item, but not at these prices.

profile.description: Audio CD
profile.reviewText: Matador released this album in 1994, which is really a compilation of tracks from other P5 albums previously released in Japan, to introduce the group to American audiences. With the exception of a couple of filler tracks, the album stands the test of time - I recently bought the vinyl version for a ridiculously low price, and even with the clicks and pops, the music sound fresh and new. What was popular at around 1994? Grunge-which had overstayed its welcome by about 4 years, was finally being buried under 10 feet of concrete; electronic dance music, and the ever diminishing in taste top 40. So when a group appears on the American speakin' shores singing in Japanese and some accented English, the music, the voice and the girl better be good, or risk colossal failure career-wise. Fortunately the band and the album delivers. It is a pity this band did not become more popular than it did: Playing 1 night in some smutty club in NYC was the only stop they made there (they toured other US cities as well, but at better venues), and they were most popular at home and in Europe. Again, we Americans get the shaft from both commercial radio and college radio. Maybe again, FM radio deserves to go the way of grunge... and extinguish itself forever. Radio should have died the day the last LIVE DJ left his/her post. Long Live Pizzicato Five!
profile.summary: Excellent album - but doesn't get the respect it deserves!

profile.description: McCartney's top three 1980 album, out of print in the U.S. & digitally remastered with three bonus tracks added, 'Check My Machine', 'Secret Friend' & the hit 'Goodnight Tonight'. 14 tracks total, also featuring 'Coming Up'. 1993 release.
profile.reviewText:
I own a copy of the 1993 British remasters of this and other McCartney albums. I also have an original vinyl copy of this album. I bought the McCartney I and II package and did not have a chance to listen to the CDs until today.
regarding the 1980 McCartney II album: The remastering job adds barely a little more volume and bass, but no clarity to the sound. I did not have any real high expectations from this particular album as it was recorded under worse conditions than pre-Sgt Pepper albums. If you consider that "Yesterday" sounds like it was recorded in a garbage can, then you have an idea what the album sounds like as it was recorded cheaply at home, and sounds more like a demo than an official release. Having said that, I still love this album for the memories it brings and for the songs themselves. I just wish Paul would have - with all his millions - secured better recording equipment and/or a competent sound engineer. If you already own the 1993 British release, this remastering will not really open your ears to any "new" or "hitherto unheard" sounds. The additional 8 tracks from the 2nd CD: 4 you have already heard on B sides or have seen them in previous "bonus tracks" releases. Buy this release if the price drops significantly and/or if your old copy can't cut it anymore. There is a booklet attached to the digipak case containing some Photos of Paul in the studio, again if you don't have this album, they are not the reason to buy it for. The remastering does not significantly improve the sound even in the bonus tracks you probably already have "Coming up (live)", "Check my machine", "Secret Friend", "Wonderful Christmastime" (you would have thought Sir Paul would have been kind enough to provide the record company with a stereo mix of the song.
profile.summary: Love the album, but the remastering has nothing to write home about

profile.description: RODDY FRAME - SEVEN DIALS - CD
profile.reviewText: This guy is pure filler, low pop, even less rock content, with durability completely empty. Whether he releases an album as Aztec Camera or under his own name, it makes no difference: the album may contain at most 1 passable song, and maybe 1 or two good songs if it was a triple album, but not more than that. I've owned a few and heard his complete works over the course of many years and the bottom line is that while he may write a good song such as "Oblivious", his overall track record is worse than Howard Jones'. Out of 10 albums he's made you are lucky if you can scrape 7 good songs to go into a "best of" compilation. And that is not good value for the money. I played this album over a very famous and popular video website, and i was not impressed at all. Maybe it's that "artist from Scotland" novelty that appeals to anyone after too many drinks in a pub, but like a bad decision, it grows thin and it is regretted the next morning.
profile.summary: 95% Filler, 5% salvageable Scot-pop

profile.description: KISS - UNMASKED (RM) - CD
profile.reviewText:
A common belief among KISS fans, except for the ones who eat, live and breathe all things KISS, is that the opening track is not a KISS composition, but rather from an outsider. Regardless, it is a great opening tune for an album which quickly peaks and then starts the slow descent into mediocrity.
Sharp eared consumers who may have heard previous KISS albums may have noted the complete overhaul of the heavy KISS sound. Although KISS is a heavy band, it is not a "metal" band or even as heavy as Led Zeppelin. They found their niche - heavy, rocking, melodic - but no real message in their lyrics overall aside from "have a good time".
I bought this album when it first came out, and 37 years later, the same impression remains: It is a confused album, devoid of all the fun that were the trademark of the band. I hear Ace contributing 3 songs on this album, which, incredibly, are way better than the 3 that Gene wrote or co-wrote. The rest of the album are essentially Paul's or Paul co-writing. Vini Poncia, producer, is also a co-writer on some of these. However, going from the peak of the album "Shandi", through some interesting tracks "Is That You?", Ace's "Talk To Me" & Two Sides Of The Coin", the poppy "Tomorrow", the good guitar solo in "What Makes The World Go Round", and the incredibly depressive "Naked City", the rest of the album goes limp... The last 3 tracks of the album "She's so European" - along with "YOu're All That I want" - are Gene songs, and the lack of enthusiasm in them as well as the mediocrity, show. Probably the worst tracks on the album, and possibly Gene's worst until that time. Ace's final track "Torpedo Girl" sounds like it would have fit nicely on his 1978 solo album. "Easy as It Seems" features - for the first and possibly the last time on a KISS song - latin congas. Actually, I'm wrong, as the congas reappear on their follow up album "(Music from )The Elder" on Ace's "Dark Light", but at least there, Ace's finger blistering guitar redeems it.
Paul Stanley calls the album "wimpy", primarily due to the glossy poppy production, but I'd rather call it undesirable because of the majority of the songs, as they are of subpar quality. Whereas on "Dynasty" fans hated the popular opening track and biggest single "I Was Made For Lovin' You", the rest of the album still managed to rock, though not as hard as their previous works.
Had KISS taken a much needed break after "Alive II" and their 1978 solo albums, they could have skipped the year 1979 altogether, grabbed the best tracks of what would have been "Dynasty" and "Unmasked", hired Eddie Kramer or maybe Ray Thomas Baker, who had produced Bowie, The Cars, Queen, Foreigner, Journey and Yes, among others - to give them the desired pop appeal while still retaining their kick butt KISS sound, and not losing so many fans. Heck! They could have possibly retained Peter & Ace, brought new life into the band, and even if "The Elder " were released, it would have garnered more respect and even the forgiveness of the early day fans. Who knows? Many of the songs from these 3 albums would have complemented the aging material from the 70s in their concerts, thus creating a larger catalog of staples, as... and forgive me for stating this... I'm tired of hearing "Strutter", "Deuce", or "Love Gun" for the 50 millionth time, as I am sure they are even more sick of playing them.
Bottom line: "Unmasked" is a confused album. A testament to the separation of the band, a weak effort, and the album that, had the band searched for a ROCK producer, could have been much better and one to compete with the likes of Van Halen, Led Zeppelin, Queen, or Motley Crue at that time.
profile.summary: A Sad and Confused Album, Product of a Turbulent Era In The Band's History.

profile.description: Julieta Venegas is one of the most important international Latin Pop-Rock artists at present. She is well known and respected as a performer and accomplished composer, whose talents have pleased fans of all ages and types. This new material allows us to progress further in her musical evolution in surprising new directions. She's composed over 10 new songs on this new CD
profile.reviewText: In this age of untalented "musical" performers who pollute the FM dial by stealing (they call it "sampling") other people's music, or recycling the same sounds over and over to the delight of teens and adults, it is nothing short of a miracle and a satisfying discovery to have someone like Julieta Venegas - a real composer, singer and performer, still with us and releasing album after album full of real good tunes with lyrics that actually say something that is not the standard "me love you long time". If you are a Spanish speaker you'll appreciate the words and music. If you are not - you will want to understand what she is singing about, guaranteed. All instruments are real, barely any synthesizers, no sampling, 100% meat no filler.... Kinda makes you wish your woman could unambiguously express herself the way she does in her lyrics instead of the crap most of them sing these days on both sides of the border.
profile.summary: Beautifully Written, Performed and Crafted.

profile.description: Pro-Ject Debut Carbon: Raising the Bar for Tables Under $500 Now Ships with the Award-Winning Ortofon 2M Red "In the ways that analog trumps digital, I'm confident the Carbon will sonically outperform any cheap CD player, particularly in terms of musical flow and general warmth. Pair it with a Bellari tubed phono preamp and play the combo for a kid weaned on MP3s and he or she is likely to start bawling. Literally. The sense of depth and spaciousness plus the image stability is impressive. Most highly recommended. I don't know what else comes close for $399."  Michael Fremer, Stereophile Pro-Ject's innovative Debut line redefined what an affordable turntable could deliver. Pro-Ject has now once again challenged convention with the Debut Carbon, offering even better performance at an accessible price. The upgrades over the Debut III are numerous, including the addition of an 8.6" completely carbon fiber tonearm that increases stiffness while decreasing unwanted resonances. This results in a higher fidelity presentation of your treasured recordings. Fitted to the carbon fiber arm is a true high-end cartridge, the 2M Red by Ortofon. This arm/cartridge combination is quite capable of exceptional tracking and recovery of the musical nuance found within the records grooves. This excellent upgrade takes this analog package to a higher performance level. "The Debut Carbon nails the basics: dynamic shading and speed constancy. The essentials of what we call 'rhythm and pace' are impressive. Whether for first-time turntable buyers or anyone wishing to enjoy high-quality LP playback without spending a lot of money, Pro-Ject's Debut Carbon is a great way to go."  Wayne Garcia, The Absolute Sound The attractive, piano-gloss finished, resonance-reducing MDF plinth supports a heavier and wider diameter low-resonance platter for smoother rotation and lower wow and flutter. Additionally, a felt record mat is employed for superior r
profile.reviewText: I was seriously considering this turntable based on the stark raving mad positive reviews I've been reading all over. But one day I saw the actual turntable in a record store, selling for close to $100 more, and for the price, it looks like it is cheaply made. Even the box reminds me of inferior products Made In China. I had read about how "clever' and "superior" and "more realistic" the stupid little fishline with the counterweights are compared to the traditional knob anti-skating control. A turntable is basically a spinning platter with a tonearm designed to flow the grooves of the record, and the electronics in the amplifier or pre-amp raise the volume of the signal so that it can be processed to be heard. But when I read about motor hum, the cheap look, that the best thing about this unit is the coat of pain... one has to wonder if these positive reviews are nothing but shills? I have no problem paying $400-$500+ for a quality product. And I understand the photos in a brochure will often look better than the real thing. However, when the unit is presented a cheap package, and the components which you must assemble look like they've been made from the cheapest, most inferior supplier - I'm no expert, but the look and feel is everything - you can't help but wonder if you've been ripped off. You'll do better buying an Audio Technica direct Drive or a used unit that is better built. This is overpriced plastic and cardboard junk.
profile.summary: This is overpriced, overhyped plastic and cardboard junk.

profile.description: Vinyl LP pressing. 2012 release, the 20th album from the Hard Rock legends. The album features contributions from all four members, including co-founders Paul Stanley and Gene Simmons and longtime members guitarist Tommy Thayer and drummer Eric Singer. Monster represents Kiss' nod to the music that first inspired the band to pick up their guitars and flame-throwers, and don makeup to entertain millions. The group goes back to its own beginnings with the Who-like 'Freak,' while Gene lives up to the title track's declaration on the raucous rock of 'Back To The Stone Age' and the bludgeoning 'The Devil is Me.' ''There are no symphony orchestras, boy choirs, keyboards, outside producers or songwriters on this album,'' promises Gene Simmons. ''The best thing we did was to turn inwards to ourselves. Tommy and Eric have revitalized this band, with a work ethic and the talent to back it up. This is a real band effort. Kiss has become a behemoth. We're going where no bands have gone before.''
profile.reviewText: KISS died when they released "Unmasked" in 1980, and with due to the cowardice on the part of Gene and Paul with "The Elder" (1981) the band was done and buried as soon as Ace was thrown out. The removal of the makeup, the constant revolving door of band members as fast and as disposable as the groupies they met on the road, were only desperate gasps for air for a corporate machine that was on its last legs - and should have been given it a dignified death. The mid 90's reunion tours with Ace and Peter were only feeble and pitiful parodies of a band that once was Great. For when the same songs from the 1970s are repeated over and over in every concert, in every tour, it can only mean that the material from any post classic-KISS lineup absolutely stinks and is not accepted by the fans. What is even more obscene is the amount of money earned by the 4 original members but was unfairly distributed against the 2 goys. This album, whose content is subpar to even 1980s releases, is the work of a parody band whose bag of good ideas has been empty for quite some time now. No amount of studio trickery and over-amplified guitar sounds can mask the emptiness that lies beneath this pathetic album. I borrowed it from my local library as I did not want to risk enriching the SS duo any further. And after 2 listens - one in the car, the second in my home stereo - from end to end, I can definitely conclude the clown makeup should come off as well as the 2 hired hands pretending to be part of a band whose dues they never paid. I entered this album already biased against the band, but did listen to it twice to search for a hook, some thing that would neutralize the bias, but found only additional fuel with which to condemn this piece of garbage. If you must have this album, download it for free or copy it from your local library. Let's not fuel Gene Simmons' ego anymore, shall we?
profile.summary: Gene & Paul - with all your millions in the bank, why bother anymore? Let the beast die with dignity.

profile.reviewText: For those who own The Wall in their original vinyl pressing, or on the various CD releases since the 1980s, let me tell you that this 180 gram vinyl remastering is by far the BEST audio version I've heard of this album. The 180 gram LPs I bought came from the UK, a country that in my humble opinion, along with the Japanese and the Germans, manufacture the best quality vinyl in the world. The vinyl is extremely quiet and the sound is full - meaning it's neither bassy nor  "tinny" - it is well balanced and I hear instruments previously buried in the early LP pressings and in the CDs. Though you can adjust your tone controls to your liking - set mine on flat - you can still hear the 15kHz tone from the TV in the track "One Of My Turns". Highly recommended if you can afford it. And if you can't, put it on the credit card before they're all gone and then end up on auction sites for a 3 digit sum.
profile.summary: Not only for the content, but for the 180 gram remastering as well

profile.description: Ska-riffic 2008 two CD compilation from Buster Blood vessel and his mates featuring original recordings from their early '80s hit-making years (and not the re-recordings or live versions commonly featured on BM comps). with 1980 only a few months old the sight of Bad Manners hilarious front man Blood vessel on TV screens across the land singing 'Ne-Ne Na-Na Na-Na Nu-Nu' couldn't help but raise a few smiles. But beneath the humor as epitomized by a slew of singles including 'Lip Up Fatty', 'Lorraine' and 'Can Can' (all included here) was a solid, professional working group. profile.reviewText: EMI/Capitol Records, the same label that shortchanged the Beatles, making millions around the world on the backs of the Fab Four, and paying them (taxable) pennies on the Pound. Such was the depth of the penny pinching stinginess that the band put their trust on the charlatan "Magic Alex", who in the end, cost The Beatles 300,000 Pounds (about $3Million Pounds today) - to build them a brand new state of the art 72 track recording studio. It is little wonder then, that albums such as "Let It Be' brim with anger, insecurity and defeat - leading a short time to "Abbey Road", a more polished effort and in a way (and forgive me fans): sterile. This is not to take away from the music itself, but by then they were no longer a band - McCartney attempting to take over the group via a coup d'Etat,and  shortchanging his band members by secretly buying a larger share of the music publisher that owned their songs, and brutally repressing any input by George (though in the case of Ringo, it is perfectly understandable). Capitol Records has milked the Fab Four legacy with their inept and overall stupid compilation releases, which only made people such as Allen Klein exponentially rich, while starving the band of their dues. If you must have this album, go for the 2009 remaster, not for the rehash/retread of the 1995 release.

profile.description: MAKE OFFER ON THIS OR ANY OF MY OTHER STUFF IN ANY COMBINATION of anything I carry
profile.reviewText: I bought the LP when it originally came out (they advertised it on TV - something that rock bands never do) and (predictably) found the album totally different from their previous works. In retrospect, and considering the previous 2 albums to this one: Dynasty (1979) and Unmasked (1980), it was obvious to even the most casual listener, that the band had abandoned their previous modus operandi of creating music. KISS was still KISS, but looking for a new direction. They already had all the money, women and fame they could ever want, but by then, between the comic books, toys, and thousand other licensed products that had nothing to do with a rock band and more to do with cartoons, they were in danger (or had already become in the rock and roll business) something of a joke, especially after the ill-advised "Kiss Meets The Phantom Of The Park" movie, produced by no other than Hannah-Barbera. However since they were still selling out stadiums, apparently no one thought of telling Simmons and Stanley (but especially Simmons) that no amount of money could buy them back the street credibility they were losing or had already lost. (Music from)The Elder was not the album that alienated many older Kiss fans. It was the last nail on the coffin, but not the cause of their demise. They had already been turned off by the cheesiness of the junk that bore the band's name, added to the "disco" hit "I was Made For Loving You" (1979) and the follow up album recorded in Canada and produced behind mountains of cocaine in the mixing console. If only they had mixed "Unmasked" as a rock album and not a glossy synthesizer production resembling The Human League, tempers would have abated. However with this record which is half a rock album ("The Oath" "Dark Light" Only You" "A World Without Heroes" Escape from the Island" "I"  ) and the other half a bad mix of Star Wars, Barry Manilow, a bad imitation of Iron Maiden, Abba and "You Light Up My Life" - it was considered to be the final insult by those fans who still had some hope something good would come of this. If the bad half of this album had been rejected, and the band written better, more rock oriented songs or instrumentals (think Queen doing the soundtrack of "Flash Gordon" - 1980) they would have had a winner here. A more mature rock album that would bring back the old fans and attract new listeners who worship Steely Dan. Instead the equally addled; one by drugs, and the other by greed: Bob Ezrin and Gene Simmons - couldn't wait to get the product out the door. Damn the cheesiness, the non-existent story, unlearned lessons from past failures, the often wrong but sometimes right howls of disgust from music critics and hardcore fans alike, Ace's loud and clear opposition to the stupidity of the project...GET THEM TRUCKLOADS OF RECORDS OUT TO THE WAITING MASSES PRONTO!! It was Ace who put it best: These are not bad songs. These are just not songs for Kiss. And it was cowardly and cheap of Simmons to disavow the album completely. Whatever Simmons says, Stanley implicitly supports. Peter was out of the band by then. - I've always had a soft spot for Ace as I equate him with George Harrison - who was always suppressed by the hit making duo of Lennon & McCartney - until he had a chance to record an album of his own, which proved to be at least as good, if not vastly superior than the product his former suppressors put out at that time (Harrison's "All Things Must Pass" and Frehley's 1978 solo album). Think of "The Elder" as the equivalent of "Their Satanic Majesties Request". Accept the album for what it is, and embrace the good parts, while rejecting the bad. If anything, it served as a wake up call to Simmons and Stanley to quit appeasing the drug addicts in the production room and get back to making rock records. Though port "Elder" albums never brought them the fortune they once made with their earlier albums, they still remained a strong attraction as long as they played the old favorites and they still put out one hell of a show.
profile.summary: I wish KISS fans wouldn't rag on this album as much as they have

profile.description: 90 digitally remastered tracks - virtually every studio cut made by the group Paul Weller formed with pianist Mick Talbot after The Jam dissolved. Features all 12 tunes from the previously unavailable 1989 album 'A Decade Of Modernism', plus six other cuts making their CD debut & the previously unavailable 'Money-Go-Round (Pt.1 & 2)' (Bert Bevans Alternate Remix). As with The Jam box, it contains no live recordings & comes in a 6 inch x 12 inch longbox with a detailed 112 page color book with liner notes, lyrics, etc. 1998 Polydor release.
profile.reviewText: I give the entire package 5 stars although if I were to rate the albums separately, the ratings would be all over the place. The box consists of 5 remastered albums containing all their singles from the beginning of the band's existence when they took the world by storm to the bitter, tired and confused end. Never ones to remain stuck in one type of music, Paul Weller and Mick Talbot released albums which, though made up of excellent to good songs, the styles and concepts began to be more of a miss than a hit. As you listen to the discs in their proper order, this becomes very evident by the third disc. At that point in their career, they had started off being a soul, jazz, and blues pop band with catchy hooks and interesting lyrics, and then on to engaging in political themes by disc 2, but by disc 3, while the hooks are still there, it is no longer a "happy" band. Disc 4 takes us in to what I'd call the equivalent of "(music from) The Elder" by KISS: a concept album of noble intentions, disparaged and disowned by its creators (but they still collected those checks), but more appreciated as time went by and the original hardcore fans began to mellow out and open their ears to possibilities that should have been, could have been, but were a failure in their time - yet hailed as "masterpieces" nowadays. Disc 4 contains the entire "Confessions Of A Pop Group" album, which has a few moments of brilliance, surrounded by extremely long classical, melancholy pieces, some of them surpassing the 10 minute mark. Very reminiscent of "Chicago at Carnegie Hall" where you have those long tracks such as "It Better End Soon" ( in 5 movements), or "Ballet for a Girl In Buchannon" (in 7 pieces). Clearly this was a half baked and unwise decision on someone's part to go from 3-4 minute songs to weed driven epics that satisfy only diehard fans, completists, and the types of people who dress in black and hang around cemeteries longing for a romantic death instead of the cheesy one that awaits us all at the end of the rainbow. Disc 5 contains the rejected, "lost", legendary suppressed last album "Modernism: a new Decade". Here once again the band attempts to break new ground or actually just jump into the electronic beats bandwagon so that the cursed album sells enough copies to pay the rent. Even then, if it had been released, it probably would have sounded not only dated, but uninspired and embarrassingly bad: sort of Neil Young requesting Milli Vanilli's producers to record his next album "for the kids". In short, if you were to play the 5 discs from beginning to end in one sitting you'd see the brilliance of a band that somewhere in the middle of their career, lost their mojo and their way. You can blame the ever changing landscape of pop music: what was popular in 1984 was old and embarrassing by 1988 -  a band has to keep moving, but not so far away from their core or founding statement that it ends up pleasing or impressing only a very few. Micro brewed beer may be tasty to a large part of the audience, but micro brewed albums are an iron clad guarantee of obscurity and failure.  How Paul Weller Threw It All Away!
profile.summary: THE STORY OF HOW A GREAT BAND LOST THEIR MOJO

profile.description: Best known to the entire world as "The Catman", a foudning member and original drummer of the legendary KISS, Peter Criss has returned with his latest musical project, ONE FOR ALL, a collection showcasing his far-ranging talent as a skillful singer/songwriter and his vast range as a gifted vocalist.
profile.reviewText: Seriously.... Not only is he a has-been hack drummer with delusions of being Frank Sinatra or Barry Manilow.... He should have been able to live comfortably on the millions he made with Kiss. He has had more wasted second chances than Lindsay Lohan and Britney Spears combined. This guy is tied with Yoko Ono and Cibo Matto for the world record of unlistenable albums released. But the saddest thing is that faithful Kiss fans and obdurate believers still buy these CDs, feeding both Peter's ego and bank account, and then getting a major disappointment when Saint Peter keeps on delivering embarrassingly bad songs instead of anything resembling rock music let alone Kiss. It's time to kill the cat and put the animal to rest. No one with an ounce of musical taste could possibly enjoy this alcoholic ramblings of a failed bum musician. It's time for Peter Criss to accept he wasted his many second chances of being a good drummer in a highly successful band, and to put an end to this agony of defeat. Ringo Starr has made similar crappy albums, but he at least could cash in when he brought the other three to play from time to time, no egos. Charlie Watts made some successful jazz albums, but he never abandoned the Rolling Stones, whose albums pay his bills (not the jazz albums). Even I came to a self-admission, I'll never screw Britney Spears and Lindsay Lohan in a threesome or be the next Eric Clapton, and I made peace with myself. Why can't Peter learn?
profile.summary: We should PAY this guy NOT to MAKE ANY MORE ALBUMS... EVER!!!

profile.description: 2010 release from the veteran British vocalist and Roxy Music frontman. The album features musical contributions from Nile Rodgers, Pink Floyd's David Gilmour, Groove Armada, Scissor Sisters, Marcus Miller, Flea, Mani (Primal Scream, ex Stone Roses) and Jonny Greenwood of Radiohead. Olympia sees Bryan Ferry reunite on record with members of Roxy Music, including Brian Eno, Phil Manzanera, and Andy Mackay. This is the first album to reunite them since Roxy Music's seminal album For Your Pleasure in 1973! Olympia is a masterpiece of prolific artistry, blending sultry, elegant lyrics with genius compositions by Ferry, Rhett Davies and innovative, contemporary musicians.
profile.reviewText: I was expecting some memorable music here. After what he'd done in albums such as "Frantic" or "Mamouna", not to mention his previous albums and his stint in Roxy Music, you'd expect great tunes out of this man. Unfortunately it was not to be. I'm not going to comment on the quality of the recording or the mastering, just the music. And it is forgettable. A mortal sin from the likes of Bryan Ferry. Any other schmuck I could accept it, but not from BF. The production is slick and on the side of poppy. BF's voice has aged, but that does not excuse him from this really bad album. Play it if you can from a popular video website, and you'll see what I mean. Not a single memorable or good song here. It appears be an album full of fillers. I am very disappointed. No wonder this album is so cheap for sale on CD here on Amazon. Maybe if he would have taken a bit more time to work on the songs and improve them. I don't know.
profile.summary: I really did not like it.

profile.description: Pink Floyd ~ A Momentary Lapse Of Reason
profile.reviewText: Many hardcore card carrying devout Pink Floyd fans don't consider "A Momentary Lapse Of Reason" a proper Pink Floyd album for reasons ranging from "Roger ain't here" to "the lyrics are dumb". Looking at the album credits, one sees a very large crew and outside songwriters contributing to the album. The results are mixed. There are some good tracks, and some are mere filler. It sounds like a Pink Floyd record. Some will consider this a David Gilmour solo album. But if you consider their last couple of albums, "The Wall" was primarily Roger Waters with a backing band, and by the time "The Final Cut" appeared, the band was alraedy broken up for all practical purposes. Roger Waters may sound like a very calm and mild mannered man, but he is none of that. By all accounts, he was a bully and oppressor, an exploiter and a tyrant. He sued and lost - BIG - over ownership of the Pink Floyd name, At the time of this release (AMLOR), Water's 2nd solo album "Radio K.A.O.S." came out - And, except for the first track on the album, the whole thing just sucks. Deservedly so, while Roger was playing to 75% empty arenas, Pink Floyd (David, NIck and Rick) were playing to overflowing stadiums. Roger Waters is an evil man,
profile.summary: Bully Roger Waters' lesson in humility

'The album's opener is classic rock and an instant attention grabber. A heavy guitar riff with loud drums and souring vocals, it's like nothing The Fireman have ever done before.' The Fireman are back after a ten-year break. Electric Arguments is their third and brand new studio album and it's not the album people might expect from the mysterious duo.'
profile.reviewText: McCartney's biggest problem is his intensive competitiveness that keeps him from thinking clearly, which has only gotten worse starting with "Give My Regards To Broadstreet". At least in the 1970's he was trying to beat John, George, and in a way Ringo. Today he has no more competition and instead of enjoying his billion plus dollars in the bank or worth, he keeps making forgettable and disposable albums. While George made some good and some awful albums in the 1970's, by early 1983 he was done making records, later devoting his energies to being in the company of other great musicians in the "Traveling Wilburys", Ringo with his "All Starr Band". With John gone, Denny Laine alienated, and a lot of talented studio and touring musicians disappointed and cheated - his albums consisted of an ever changing backing group. Even George Martin gave up after couple of albums in the 1980's. The result was a long string of crappy albums, each worse than the predecessor, and in his personal life, still chasing after women younger than his daughters, one of whom had an even bigger ego and rightly so, got some of his millions - barely a drop in his personal fortune. Sir Paul's stinginess and cheapskate personality has been the stuff of legend, the fodder of many biographies, and vouched by many musicians who had the misfortune of being sucked dry and financially cheated by this petulant and plastic souled man. The 2001 track "Freedom" was a total embarrassment from a man who made his billions by being ambiguous and cold in his career of creating poppy, saccharine songs. Frankly, he should take his millions and keep smoking his dope for the rest of his years, but he should be banned from releasing anything anymore. This may be the reason why he's about to beat Ringo in the number of labels he's been recording for, as his material is as irrelevant as his ego for this past couple of decades. The old man should hang it up now. He's become a parody of a parody of his past self now. Sad, disappointing, un-filling, and pathetic.

profile.reviewText: For reasons still evaded by both Messrs. Difford and Tilbrook, but assured of it in a roundabout way by both, by the time of this album was made, relations between the two core members of the band were at an all time low. Being English yobs, it may even have involved brutal physical violence at the studio for all we know. Forget all you think you know about rock bands: to be successful you must be useless as a worker and the more uneducated you are, the better, as it will drive your hunger for success even more than someone who can fall back on his Bachelors Degree in accounting if the band fails. Drink, drugs and violence are the currency of the rock backstage life (and you though RAPPERS were the only violent people around, you innocent fool!). This album was made to "escape" the clutches of the success of their band, Squeeze. What it sounds like is respectable top 40 pop, but at a bad time. If you remember the film "Eddie & The Cruisers", when Eddie reveals his experimental album to the band and gets rejected by the label, the guitarist says 'They want 'On The Dark Side! Why do you want to give them this opera for?' - Exactly the same problem found here and found in their other albums "Cosi Fan Tutti Frutti" and "Sweets From A Stranger" - The Fans Wanted another "Mussels From A Shell". not deep thought personal and/or experimental and politic hinting lyrics.  Consequently, almost as soon as the album failed to chart even in Bolivia, both Messrs. Difford and Tilbrook pointed their accusing finger at the other, and swearing that "This album wasn't us!", thereby casting this LP to the street like some unwanted and unloved child, a situation worthy of a song that would nicely fit in "Cosi Fan Tutti Frutti". And indeed it is a pity as it would have been a well received Squeeze album, had a couple of really horrible tracks been removed (The Apple Tree, Tears For Affection). I went to see them at the Ritz in 1984. true to their ego (or the club's management to sell more overprices NY booze), the opening band went on at 12 midnight, and D&T with their non-squeeze band consisting of 2 drummers which offered no improvement or advantage at all, just a ridiculous novelty - at least The Grateful Dead have a reason: Mickey Hart left and returned, what's THEIR excuse? - finally and generously appeared onstage at 2am (WTF!!). In short, this is another "(music from) The Elder" that is to this day denied and denounced by its creators, consisting of mostly good songs that may have fit better if a few would have been left off, released as b-sides, given to other bands to cover, or reworked further. If you think of this album as just another Squeeze album, then it may be more digestible, and you'd be righting a wrong in the history of the band. if you compare this solo album to Squeeze albums, you'd be disappointed. Or you can just buy the album, enjoy it for what it is, and move on with your life. Hopefully, D&T will one day turn around like Steve Jobs, stop claiming impotence, and embrace this record as part of the family. On that day, the world will be a better place.
profile.summary: THIS IS THE LOST 'SQUEEZE' ALBUM THAT WAS CAST ASIDE AS AN ILLEGITIMATE B4ST4RD SON

profile.description: 2009 studio album from the veteran British outfit, currently celebrating their 30th Anniversary as a recording unit (and all seven original members present and accounted for). The Liberty Of Norton Folgate is their first album of new material since their excellent 1999 album Wonderful. The album contains 14 tracks of quintessential Madness; subversive, expansive British Pop music at its finest. As with all previous Madness albums, The Liberty Of Norton Folgate features songwriting contributions from all band members and is a timely reminder of the ability of this unique act to turn their hand to multiple musical styles. Few bands have come close to soundtracking London in the way of Madness and The Liberty Of Norton Folgate is an audio guide to the greatest city on earth. Features the first single 'NW5'. Lucky 7.
profile.reviewText: Play the samples from "One Step Beyond" then of this album. Hard to believe it is the same band. No complaints about sound quality or musicianship, however the songs in this "concept" album are AWFULLY BAD. Not even Suggs' cheery disposition or the "ska" rhythms and arrangements of the songs can save it. This is not an album from a band that has "matured" but a collection of bad songs that should have never seen the light of day. This was the first Madness album in a decade. Granted, the music styles may have changed:what was cool in 1982 sounds dated today, but it still does not excuse them for creating music better fit for a failed London play (although it would be a huge success on Broadway due to the inability of the American people to move on their regrets for the War of Independence, instead of mentally flogging themselves in perpetuity and secretly envying Canada) and advertising it as a "rock or pop" record. In a nutshell: the album is boring, boorish, forgettable and a complete waste of time. The few good moments are too little too late. Leave the concept albums to the rock gods: Floyd, the Who, Bowie......Styx, KISS (haha!!)
profile.summary: Definitely NOT a "masterpiece" but a boring and forgettable "concept musical" album of rubbish.

profile.description: Venezuela's Funkiest Dance Outfit, Putting Out Crazy, Boogaloo-inspired Rhythms that Make You Wanna Move. profile.reviewText:
If you liked Arepa 3000, then this is the clone album, but without the tasty songs. The band's sound IS here, but the tunes now sound repetitive, and if you've heard this band's previous 3 albums, then you'll realize that this is the same as the 3rd album, and the band is not going anywhere. Their music is not evolving in this album as has in the other 3.
Gone are the clever word play, one track not even bothering, replacing it with an obscene title to attract radio play, and gone are the catchy tunes. Maybe you can salvage a track or two, but by now, the band just sounds like they put out a contractual obligation album, or maybe they got fat and they did not care to explore new music, improve their weak songs, or want to bother any more.
And it's a pity - I saw this band when they just started - I bought their first album based on the COVER without hearing the music first - a gamble that paid off. This band can make even a Bruce Springsteen fan get up and dance.
But here, it's just a great disappointment that - unfortunately - only got worse with their NEXT album.
My recommendation: listen to it online, but before you go out and buy it, listen also to any of their first 3 albums.
But if you must have it, buy it used. Not really worth full price for this one.
profile.summary: The Band Got Fat: Imagine Boston's 2nd and 3rd albums - they both sound like bad copies of the first one. Same here.

profile.reviewText: I thought I could do without eating lunch today so that I could buy Ringo's new album man! I have gone without, gone hungry, even paid the rent late so that I could buy the avalanche of new and remastered Beatles and solo albums. And when I buy them both - the mono, the stereo, the CD and the vinyl editions - band and solo efforts, and especially if they come in a deluxe package such as McCartney's re-releases that cost upwards of $100-, then at last I feel fulfilled..... until I play Ringo's albums. I just can't understand why, with the 150 million POUNDS (NOT DOLLARS) has has in the bank, this man can't afford singing and music composing lessons. It is thanks to fools like me that buy every utterance and guest appearance material ever put out; official AND bootleg. I figure by this stage of the game, all 4 Beatles and/or their estates, owe me some type of job as a curator of all releases Beatle. Should a fire ever consume my home, I'd lose over $200K worth of Beatles albums and memorabilia. Of all the official discographies, who remembers "Scouse The Mouse"?  George Harrison's son Dhani, thought his father was a gardener, as when he was growing up, he hardly ever saw him pick up a guitar - then again, to be fair, if your albums were produced and castrated by Jeff Lynne, you too would  bury your rock'n'roll dreams in the backyard. Jeff Lynne may have written some brilliant music for a brief time while on ELO, but lyrics and mixing albums have never been his expertise. Ringo Starr and Peter Criss were the luckiest drummers in the world: Forever rich, and earning their money on the fumes of fan fantasies and memories of something that for a time was, but never as great as their selective recalls would make them out to be.

profile.description: The third and final album from Deelite features the songs "When You Told Me You Loved Me", "Party Happening People" and "Sampladelic". . [Note: This product is an authorized, licensed CD and is manufactured on demand]
profile.reviewText: Information regarding this group is very hard to come by, even in the age of the internet. But from what little I gather, there were a couple of things that finally killed this group. Elektra records singed a deal with the band, the first album sold billions, but by the time of the second album, the band started mixing political and environmental messages in their music.  Predictably, the Evil Suits from the record label refused to promote the album, and "Infinity Within", while it contains several good songs, musically speaking, falls short of their debut album. The fun is gone. DJ Towa Tei - and you can read a few interviews online - by this time did not get along well with Mr. and Mrs Brill, and left. He barely contributed anything to the second album, and even less, if at all, on the third and final: "Dewdrops In The Garden". DJ Ani Quinn (stage name DJ Ani, DJ On-E" was persuaded to join the group to bring a few beats, in order to show Tei that he is not indispensable. All fo Dee-Lite's releases were the result of collaboration from different artists and DJs. Unfortunately by the second album internal problems, practically killed the group from within. The third and final release is essentially a contractual obligation, and it shows. Yes, there are a couple of good songs there, but the energy in the rest of the album is just gone. WHo knows, maybe less political messages, maybe the suits at Elektra records could have invested a little more in the band for the long run - I mean, if they invested millions on Madonna, who is nothing but a female GG Allin but with a better sound system, why couldn't they stretch out for a few more bucks in promos for THIS band? - and maybe if Kirby & Brill would have kept their relationship professional  - few husband-wife groups ever make it. There is just something repulsive about watching a girl sing and dance provocatively while her gorilla husband is a few yards away with the rage of a jealous bull. Ike Turner was jealous of Tina, and that's why he beat her so much. Maybe they all thought the first record was going to be a flop, and it wasn't. Now they had to tour and fulfill contracts. And since it's 2 boys and the girl: it's the girl that gets recognized. The men get jealous because nobody gives a rat's caboose about them, even if they get recognized. The same thing happened to Blondie, No Doubt, and countless other bands with an attractive female lead singer. Even the Bangles and The Go Go's had that problem: 3 ugly butch gorillas and one honey babe as the lead singer and face. That's show business! The band dissolved. DJ Brill still spins other people's who had a better career than he did music, Lady MIss Kier lost a million dollar lawsuit against some video game company who used her likeness ( you can't beat those suits! ) and currently either sings backup on other people's records, dances in gay pride raves, but the poor girl STILL can't get a record contract, let alone release an album's worth of material. And DJ Towa Tei, has released dozens of albums, remixes, DJ selection mixes, and re-remixes. His best album is "Future Listening". Contains his best songs ( he does not sing). It's like "All Things Must Pass", but well recorded and without the preaching. Of the three, he is the one that left the band first and cashed in on his own work, not on nostalgia tours spinning dance remixes of Nirvana or Hole songs. Latecomer DJ Ani is still in the business of DJing. This is what he was at age 19 when he was asked to join the group This is not the best Deee-Lite album, but it is not a flop either. It is rather, a fitting contractual obligation release. Their swan song as the band is no more. Towa Tei would rather be sentenced to live in a North Korean slave prison than to re-form the band and release an album and/or tour.
profile.summary: Deee-Lite's Contractual Obligation Album But Without the British Humour.

profile.reviewText:
The opening track "Lover Never Felt So Good" is the peak of the album. Once the track is done, it's all downhill from there. The album was cobbled together using Michael's vocals and basic tracks, which were reworked, remixed, and released as full songs. Unfortunately the reason they were shelved in the first place was because the songs needed work, mainly on the melodies.  At the time of his death Michael Jackson was preparing for a highly profitable comeback tour of the UK, and most likely would have had these songs overhauled to make them more palatable. If you compare the contents of this album with anything he released while he was alive, you'll see how, save for the first track, the rest of the album falls short of the MJ songwriting benchmark.
The album was remixed and released with the songs as were, to satisfy the world's demand for any MJ material that had still not seen the light of day. Jermaine and Tito, not wanting to let the carcass of the goose that laid the golden eggs, hired the top producers to take a whack at the tracks, with Papa Joe Jackson ready to crack the whip, as in "Roots" (Google: "Toby") and mercilessly beat the music into the producers and engineers, just as he did when younger, until they yield a sellable product.
Michael Jackson was a highly talented individual, but also deeply disturbed and suffering.
Too bad we can't send his father Joe Jackson to the electric chair.
He was a rapist, a child abuser, and a wife beater.
Rest In Peace Michael. You're better off now. Thank you for the music.

profile.description: Meticulous 1985 album of psychedelic pop 'n' sunny funk jams! Includes "Raspberry Beret" and "Paisley Park".
profile.reviewText: In The Beatles' Anthology DVD, when discussing the Sgt. Pepper's album, one of them says that the whole album concept died right after 3 tracks, as the rest of the songs could easily fit in any of their previous albums. Still this fact did not stop the album from being ranked as the #1 best rock album of all time by Rolling Stone magazine, and probably many other similar rock music publications. Ever since that album appeared, there have been countless other albums by other artists trying to capture that imaginary inexistent essence of what amounts to unicorns and rainbows, the result of some unrestrained acid trip. And even then, these pale imitations yielded a few songs that could serve as a yearning vehicle for the rest of the album to be as good or better than the exceptional single. For the canny artist, this could be a showcase of their alter-ego, and a harmless gamble, as they could always say "it wasn't us" should the album prove to be an embarrassment (The 1978 soundtrack to the film "Sgt. Peppers'), or claim it as "the next step in the artist's development" should it be a COMMERCIAL success. Note I said "commercial" for this is what this album was: a success. Musically speaking it is an album of various musical styles wrapped in a "psychedelic motif" but the psychedelic part of the music is only present on a couple of tracks at most. The album has 3 good singles (America, Pop Life, Raspberry Beret), of which only one (Pop Life) is anything resembling "psychedelic". The other one is the opening track, which is passable, but not good enough to be a good song or a single. The rest of the album is full of pretentious funk and boring fillers. If you ever heard a similar themed album XTC - "Oranges And Lemons" after you were sold on the cover, you'd find pretty much the same pattern there: Psychedelic opening track, hit single, minor single, followed by 13 tracks of bad filler crap over the course of 2 LPs. Psychedelic albums are but a fad, a fake fashion statement not unlike the $100 Tiffany "Punk" Safety Pin, and yet another marketing ploy which still to this day evokes an illusory world but fails to deliver on its promise.
profile.summary: YES, IT'S ANOTHER SGT. PEPPER PSYCHEDELIC WANNABE FAILURE OF THE LOT.

profile.description: Infinity Within by DEEE LITE
profile.reviewText: I bought this CD the day it came out, and let me tell you, the 1990s had their share of hits and misses, more misses than hits, and this open especially bothered me a lot. Granted, nearly every artist and group loathes to release a second album that is a Xerox of the first one, but when bands define what they want to be: metal, pop, dance, etc.. they truly do a disservice to themselves and their fans when they release an album that lacks all the things that made the first one such an catch in the first place. Yes, they have the "Deee-Lite" eclectic team of producers and collaborators to make the "sound" come out, however, the songs here are AWFUL! They appear to be either the rejected tracks from the first one, stuff that was in somebody's forgotten trunk that should have never seen the light of day (see XTC Apple Venus Vol1, and Oranges & Lemons), or songs that were rushed and half-baked on the subway ride to the recording studio. Since the label or the band already paid for the production team, the studio time, and the rest of the team, this sloppy homework done at the last minute is what they had to work with. No time for rewriting or to properly compose good songs as they did with the first one. The label wants another 5 top 10s by the end of the week!! Sadly maybe 2 songs were good enough for me to keep this album in my collection for so many years, but now I will trade it in among with my other undesirables for enough $ to buy something else. The last time a famous artist went from his trade (rock) to a political album, it flopped miserably. Anyone remember John Lennon & Yoko Ono "Some Time In New York City"(1972)? Yes, that one sucked as well. Right after this flop DJ Towa Tei called it quits. He saw the writing on the wall. A sad and bitter decline for a band that had so much promise. I still mourn them.
profile.summary: An unworthy followup to their smash debut album, and a colossal disappointment

profile.description: One of several soundtracks to Werner Herzog films that the group created, this 1975 LP is a transcendent triumph of ambience featuring gorgeous Mellotron work. Good-sized bonus track, too!
profile.reviewText: If you saw the Herzog film "Aguirre Der Zorn Gottes", then you probably remember the haunting music played throughout. This album contains some but not all of the music found in the film. Notably the 2 "Aguirre" tracks, and little else. The 16 minute track Vergegenwrtigung belongs to and is a rehash of the "Nosferatu" soundtrack. Morgengru II and AGnus Dei are not anywhere in the film. And Aguirre III is Aguirre I + Aguirre II. Nothing new here. Missing is the slide guitar or keyboard (can't tell which) solo found in the very beginning of the film, and in the end when Aguirre (Kinski) goes mad and recites a speech declaring himself emperor. While the music contained herein is good, this is not a real soundtrack of the film, but rather an incomplete set of tracks. The same can be said of the Nosferatu album, passing itself as a soundtrack, but is also missing some tracks and giving us only incomplete pieces of longer songs available on previous albums. Maybe somewhere out there there is a bootleg album that will fill in the holes.
profile.summary: Why 3 stars? Incomplete soundtrack album, with junk added

profile.description: Conceptual 1993 album from the Zaragoza, Spain Latin rock masters finds them in peak form. Features the hit tracks 'Nuestros Nombres, 'Tesoro', 'Sirena Varada' plus thirteeen more.
profile.reviewText: Los Heroes Del Silencio is a Spanish band whose heavy melodic sound is similar to a lot of "heavy" American bands such as KISS, but without the theatrics. make up, and largely, without hits or even good songs. HDS is very much image and hype, beyond their sound. in this album, a 2 record set if you wish to pursue that particular avenue of audio, the album begins with the standard creaky noises, "random" guitar tuning and chords, then to kick start the album to a decent rocker song "Nuestros Nombres" - reminiscent of KISS' "The Oath", but then the album going downhill from there musically speaking. The album is well recorded and the CD booklet a tantalizing thing to behold, promising through its images and typeface, an album speaking or sounding of decadence, of mystery, and of something really cool, deep, dark and creepy.... but it disappoints right after the first track. At least "(Music) From The Elder" had some good songs in it despite the silliness of the pseudo storyline. This album has no point, no clear sense of identity beyond the image they sold you, and the songs are quite forgettable and disposable. There are metal and other sorts of guitar driven albums that on the first or second listen, hook you for life. Not this record, not by a mile. This one is only good for 1 track, maybe 2 at best, but then runs out of steam. Being the pride of Spain, this band from Zaragoza reached millions in their native Spain, Germany, and maybe a few other non-English speaking nations who actually took them seriously. You cannot help but laugh and guffaw through some of their lyrics, as they try really hard to be Iron Maiden, and fail to be even Winger. But you don't have to take my word for it: Take the fact that their next album (Avalancha) in which they were by that time, grasping at straws before they broke up; Enrique Bunbury, the lead singer, and face of the band - and the only one that could more or less fake an English name - went solo to an equally unremarkable career. In Avalancha this band turned Nazi (Iberia Submergida), this time trying to be Skrewdriver, but without their worldwide success. It is indeed fortunate that they disbanded as their next project was to be GG Allin and the Murder Junkies, complete with GG's sharing of his most intimate produce. if you still doubt my words, then how to explain the boatloads of used CDs of this title selling for under $2 on Amazon while a new copy sells for almost 10 times that amount? Market forces, the Invisible Hand allocates surplus items to where they are most needed. Apparently there are boatloads of people who bought this album at retail prices and found it to be beyond silly and ridiculous, but bordering on fraud. Buy only for under $2- and remember that $4 are added for shipping. Still overpriced for what it is.
profile.summary: What A Silly and Forgettable Album!

profile.description: CERATI GUSTAVO SIEMPRE ES HOY
profile.reviewText: Fresh from the praise for, and plump from the income from, his 1983 record-breaking album "Thriller", Michael Jackson's Magnum Opus, his next big worry that would haunt him for years during the making, and $30 million in recording budget, that the followup album "Bad" (1987) would not sell as many copies (30 million at that time) as his previous release. Whereas it took MJ 4 years to write and record "Bad" - and it was not "Thriller part II" - it took Gustavo Cerati 6 years to write and record "Siempre Es Hoy", and with mixed results. Of the 17 tracks offered in this CD, you can count on roughly 4 or 5 decent songs, with the rest of them being propped up electronica mixes of not really good tunes, and even worse lyrics - and that is saying a lot, considering Gustavo Cerati's lyrics are all about nothing at all. The remaining 12 or 13 tracks are essentially "Soda Stereo" chord changes and rejected songs, with an electronica makeover. Thanks to the miracle of Studio Electronics Audio Processing 101, even the lamest compositions are made to shine just enough to convince a first time listener to buy the deed. This is the last electronic album GC had released. The next two albums show a return to overamplified guitars, reminiscent of "Dynamo"; but with less developed or interesting tracks. profile.description: BOWIE DAVID BLACKSTAR
profile.reviewText:
If you are hoping to hear the next "Let's Dance", "'Heroes'", "Space Oddity", or "Ashes to Ashes" types of hits, you'd be better off looking elsewhere.
David Bowie knew he was dying, and he completed this album which came out on his birthday this year (2016). A week later he died of cancer.
Many fans will rate this swan song album 5 stars and fill the internet with praises, but the truth is that this is really a depressing album, with no potential singles (no matter what "The Fans" say), and essentially, if you like this type of hard to reach music and poetry because it makes you feel superior to the apes that still listen to Billy Joel and Bruce Springsteen, then this is the snobbish album for you.
It is listenable, but you won't be singling along, or taking it to the car to play while you drive. You will probably play it a second time to try to "get it" like all those cappuccino hipsters that claim they "do" but you won't like it and you will feel like a failure for not loving it. You will not play this album a 3rd time and will either put it in a pile appropriately named "Yogi's Pile of Myerda" to take it to your local CD and vinyl shop to exchange it for store credit before people stop liking it and begin to dump it on Amazon.
I can't even call it a "concept" album, as at least one track came off some play that he wrote or was involved in.
But as a whole, it is a collection of tracks recorded in secret and in a hurry as the clock was ticking, and his body was writhing is convulsive pain as the cancer riddled his innards mercilessly. The album goes nowhere, despite what stories are stringed up in desperation.
Your best bet if you are still curious but won't commit the money, is to borrow it from a sucker friend or from the library.
This is only "interesting" because he died soon after its release, otherwise, Rolling Stone and even the rest of the brainless snobs would give  this no more than 2 stars, but I'm not a liar like anyone rating this myerda 4 or 5. This is David Bowie's "Bronx Salute" to the world - his "Metal Machine Music" as a final farewell .
profile.summary: Worse than anything he ever did, even with Tin Machine

profile.description: CERATI GUSTAVO FUERZA NATURAL
profile.reviewText: Having been familiar with Gustavo Cerati's works as a member of Soda Stereo and as a solo artist, I avoided comparing his band vs his solo career as there are many fans that prefer his Soda Stereo output over his solo works. In most aspects, I disagree, but on this album, which I find lacking in hooks and substance, I will have to agree wholeheartedly. The album contains 14 forgettable tracks that lack the guitar charm of "Amor Amarillo" (1993) or the electronic wizardry of "Bocanada" (1999). Though the album is well produced and the songs contain both electronic and guitar sounds, the music of the songs as well as the lyrics (Cerati was never a good lyricist anyways) here leave you empty, wanting, and a creeping feeling of being cheated. I expect a lot of negative feedback for this review considering that it is his last album before he went into a coma due to brain damage and after about 4 years in that vegetative state, finally died. This album is a very bad ending for a man that had a very successful and brilliant career and life.
profile.summary: Forgettable tracks and (as usual) inane lyrics

top_5.description: This CD is an out of print collectible! It is the original CBS release. Catalog CK 33453. There is a drill hole through the UPC.
top_5.reviewText: MY BIGGEST FEAR IS always that an album is either warped or pressed off center. I can handle the warp within reason, but off center pressings really get to me deep. This occurs when the stamper after pressing so many copies, moves slightly off center. When the biscuit is then pressed, the result is an off center record that when played, the wow and flutter is very noticeable, especially in the inner tracks, towards the end of the side. I once returned a sealed Aimee Mann "Los In Space" $140- record for this very reason. The off center here is not as bad as in The Beatles White Album, but it is still an annoyance. Rather than go through the hassle of returning it, I just bore a slightly larger spindle hole and must adjust it before playing.
top_5.summary: WISH THE US MANUFACTURERS WOULD INVEST MORE TIME ON QUALITY CONTROL

top_5.description: Out-of-print on the US. 2 cd set. Sony/BMG.
top_5.reviewText: I read a review on Amazon from a reviewer discussing Duran Duran mentioning that the band was excellent as a SINGLES band, but not as an ALBUM band. And if you own a DD album, you will see the truth of that statement as the best tracks are the ones that had been released as singles and often appear in different "hits" compilations, with the rest of the album tracks being forgettable, directionless and dull. I say the same for The Clash. If you were to buy this album, you'd have 95% of all their good songs. There are a few fillers here that I would toss out in exchange for the remaining 5%, but overall these are the tracks you will see in other "best of" compilations that were released years after this one. The only advantage I would see in purchasing more recent compilations are the remastered sound - which is a noticeable improvement over the sound on these discs, and maybe a couple of remixes, but no more than a handful. For the record (no pun intended) I owned/have owned the following titles: "London Calling", "Sandinista", "Combat Rock", and "Give 'em enough Rope" as well as this and other compilations in order to pass judgement on this band. Granted, some of these albums have more good songs than others and no single album can be full of hits, but overall, the average % of hits vs filler material found in Clash albums are 30% (of 10 tracks in an LP, 3 will be good or "hits", the rest will be forgettable).
top_5.summary: This is as best as it gets. All other compilations are but rehashes of this one.

top_5.description: Audio CD
top_5.reviewText:
This was originally released as a cassette around 1981 which you could order from the Devo fan club using a form that was included in their LP "New Traditionalists". No Visa, No MasterCard, just either cash or check. The album contains a lot of their better known songs but in an instrumental format and removing all guitars or drums, also changing the tempo - leaving only muffled keyboards and the bass for an "EZ Listening" experience.
Some songs are still recognizable, while others will take a while to catch. One example ("It's a Beautiful World") can be found in the remastered version CD of the "New Traditionalists" album as the last "bonus" track of the CD. Don't expect high quality sound, as the entire album sounds like it was recorded or mastered with the treble knob all the way down to 0.
I remember paying like $12 for the CD which I later sold for $20 many years ago.
Only because it is no longer in print does this CD command such ridiculously high prices as I see today, but if you were to hear it in you tube, you'd most likely not be moved to pay more than $5- for it, as a novelty item, for completists only, but not as a crucial piece in your collection.
top_5.summary: Nice Novelty Item, but not at these prices.

top_5.description: Audio CD
top_5.reviewText: Matador released this album in 1994, which is really a compilation of tracks from other P5 albums previously released in Japan, to introduce the group to American audiences. With the exception of a couple of filler tracks, the album stands the test of time - I recently bought the vinyl version for a ridiculously low price, and even with the clicks and pops, the music sound fresh and new. What was popular at around 1994? Grunge-which had overstayed its welcome by about 4 years, was finally being buried under 10 feet of concrete; electronic dance music, and the ever diminishing in taste top 40. So when a group appears on the American speakin' shores singing in Japanese and some accented English, the music, the voice and the girl better be good, or risk colossal failure career-wise. Fortunately the band and the album delivers. It is a pity this band did not become more popular than it did: Playing 1 night in some smutty club in NYC was the only stop they made there (they toured other US cities as well, but at better venues), and they were most popular at home and in Europe. Again, we Americans get the shaft from both commercial radio and college radio. Maybe again, FM radio deserves to go the way of grunge... and extinguish itself forever. Radio should have died the day the last LIVE DJ left his/her post. Long Live Pizzicato Five!
top_5.summary: Excellent album - but doesn't get the respect it deserves!

top_5.description: McCartney's top three 1980 album, out of print in the U.S. & digitally remastered with three bonus tracks added, 'Check My Machine', 'Secret Friend' & the hit 'Goodnight Tonight'. 14 tracks total, also featuring 'Coming Up'. 1993 release.
top_5.reviewText:
I own a copy of the 1993 British remasters of this and other McCartney albums. I also have an original vinyl copy of this album. I bought the McCartney I and II package and did not have a chance to listen to the CDs until today.
regarding the 1980 McCartney II album: The remastering job adds barely a little more volume and bass, but no clarity to the sound. I did not have any real high expectations from this particular album as it was recorded under worse conditions than pre-Sgt Pepper albums. If you consider that "Yesterday" sounds like it was recorded in a garbage can, then you have an idea what the album sounds like as it was recorded cheaply at home, and sounds more like a demo than an official release. Having said that, I still love this album for the memories it brings and for the songs themselves. I just wish Paul would have - with all his millions - secured better recording equipment and/or a competent sound engineer. If you already own the 1993 British release, this remastering will not really open your ears to any "new" or "hitherto unheard" sounds. The additional 8 tracks from the 2nd CD: 4 you have already heard on B sides or have seen them in previous "bonus tracks" releases. Buy this release if the price drops significantly and/or if your old copy can't cut it anymore. There is a booklet attached to the digipak case containing some Photos of Paul in the studio, again if you don't have this album, they are not the reason to buy it for. The remastering does not significantly improve the sound even in the bonus tracks you probably already have "Coming up (live)", "Check my machine", "Secret Friend", "Wonderful Christmastime" (you would have thought Sir Paul would have been kind enough to provide the record company with a stereo mix of the song.
top_5.summary: Love the album, but the remastering has nothing to write home about

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "J. A. DENNAM, an award winning author and member of Romance Writers of America, resides in a small Kansas town with her husband and four children. She shares many passions for the arts including fine arts, culinary arts and music. Storytelling has been a part of her life since childhood, when insomnia forced a young girl of six into counting popcorn on the ceiling in the dead of night. Confessing her problem to her older sister, they decided to tell each other stories to entice sleep; however, the inevitable snore always tore through her sisters nose before she could utter the words Once Upon A Time. So, the stories began to flow in silence, her imagination taking her to quiet, private places so enthralling, the trick was suddenly to stay awake. Each night, she went to bed anticipating the continuation of the adventure that had been interrupted by sleep the previous night. Soon, insomnia was no longer a problem and the stories would sometimes take months to complete. Those habits carried on to adulthood until the need to purge her stories demanded she put them in print. Her fascination with romance, fast cars and adventure films is what structures her stories today, making Romantic Suspense the genre she was simply born to write.". The summary of the review text is "My Review: Between Faith and Fear".
output:
***WARNING***  While this book can be read as a standalone, there are major spoilers from Truth and Humility at the beginning of this book and in this review.

If you are still reading this remember, I warned you.  In Truth and Humility we met Austin and Danny in Between Faith and Fear, the story revolves around Melanie and Derek.  Two years ago, Mel and Derek shared a moment on the hood of his car, that was days before he was shot and killed by Rena.  Left with his family to grieve their lost, little does she know that their romp on the hood of the car resulted in a child.

DJ (Derek Junior) has become her entire world.  After losing the only man she's ever loved, the only memories she has of him are his photos and his son.  She keeps his memory alive everyday by showing her son the picture of his dad and telling him how much he would have loved him.  Little does she know her entire world is about to be rocked to it's core.

Lurking in the shadows is someone from her past, someone that is going to take her away.  When she leaves Mac behind for the day to go home and pack, she stops in the middle of the road when she sees a black dog emerge from the shadows holding the pink blanket of one of the children from the daycare they run.  Distracted by the dog, she doesn't see the person that opens the passenger door and enters her car drugging her and preparing to take her away.  This person doesn't notice until the dog is in the car and distracted that there is a blue eyed identical version of Melanie strapped into the back seat.

Melanie awakens later in a moldy damp room that was a former classroom face to face with the one woman she never wanted to see again.  None other than Rena who escaped from prison.  There is a man with her, but the man stays in the shadows of the dark room wearing a hood and disguising his voice.  The man finally decides it's time to tell her who he is.  The man is none other than Derek who has returned from the dead.  Turns out he wasn't dead at all.  But there are others among them that want to take not only Derek and Rena back with them, but Melanie and DJ as well.  Someone that will do anything to get to them and harm them.

Derek is not the same man he was when he left.  He appears larger, more on edge, and stay mostly in the shadows wearing a dark hoodie.  He has obtained a series of skills, things he doesn't want to have and a dependency on a drug that his captors addicted him to.  One he cannot live without.

Their reunion is short lived and more lives put in danger when Ty, Danny, and Austin enter the picture.  Those around him are in danger, and there's little he can do to stop the ghosts that are coming for them.  Friends are reunited, enemies are discovered, demons are dealt with.  But in the end who will be friend and who will turn out to be foe?  Can Melanie help to save Rena and Derek before it's too late?

This series is like watching a movie.  I seriously could see the film playing out in my mind, this series would make a wonderful film.  It's heartfelt and action packed.  It has all the makings of some day becoming a great film.  Just like J.A. Dennam says, this book has it all.  Sex, action, love, pain, hurt, oh and did I mention sex with a hot alpha male???  I cannot wait for the next book in this series, this book didn't leave you with a heavy withdrawal waiting for the next book like some cliffhangers do, it does however leave you dying to read the next book.  This series is quickly becoming one of my all time favorites and does not disappoint.  I highly recommend reading this book as well as Truth and Humility.  Like I said, while it can be read alone, it does help to read book one or you will be lost at the beginning.  I give this book an easy 5 stars because it really was one of the best action packed romance novels I have read so far this year.
