profile.reviewText: I wore these on a 360 mile bike ride under jeans and included the tail bone pad and the thigh pads.  They were extremely comfortable and I forgot I was wearing them shortly after I started the ride.  I thought the tail bone pad might cause some seating discomfort but it did not.  THey fit easily under my normal jeans and you would not notice I had them on.  There is a small zipper at the ankle that makes it easier to put them on and off.  The lycra body sock is smooth and snug and the pads are made of soft dense foam.  My guess is that the pads would do well on first impact to protect your corners but my slide off the corners since they are only held in place by the strechable lycra,
profile.summary: Road Tested and comfortable

profile.description: Keystone's kstff100abn 10 in. Flower fan has blue and green interchangeable heads. This cute little flower fan with soft plastic safety blades is perfect for desk or tabletop use. Featuring 2 speed settings, vertical tilt adjustment and safety-touch shut off, you'll keep cool in style.
profile.reviewText:
The base and fan are balanced well.  The base is heavy enough not to tip over and the fan blades are light enough as to not be too bulky.
Instructions to use the fan are thorough and include detailed information to change the fuse if the fan overheats.
Two fan hubs are included, pink and purple.  They are easily removed and replaced to suit your mood.
The blades are not enclosed by a screen, and you accidentally bumped into  them they stop and don't hurt. I think your fingers would be save.
I thought that the fan speeds were odd.  Zero was off,  2 was lowest
setting and 1 was highest setting.  It seems like 1 and 2 should be reversed.
It moves a fair amount of air and would be great sitting on your desk and aimed at you.
profile.summary: Exposed fan blades pose no hazard

profile.description: Handy, practical and requiring minimal user-effort; the X5-25ps less effort stapler from Rapesco offers 25 sheet (20lb paper) stapling with up to 60% less effort required from the user. Available in a range of attractive colors and manufactured from high quality materials to an exacting standard, this stapler is backed by a 15 year guarantee.
profile.reviewText:
The Good:
- Works as advertised!.
- In a side by side comparison to a standard stapler the Rapesco was most definitely easier to staple through a large stack of papers.
- While I cant quantify exactly the 60% less effort they state, I would say yes its about that much less effort after doing several tests.
- We took 25 sheets of standard weight printing paper and the Rapesco had no problems penetrating and performing a perfect staple over about 100 trys!
- It worked equally well with the staples tucked in or out when changing using the plate setting under the head.
-  It works equally well if squeezing in the hand or sitting on a flat surface and fits well in the palm of the hand
- Loading was easy and a little opening near the front gives you a clue if your about out of staples.
- The Rapesco is very light and did not jam once over the 100 staples we performed very rapidly
- Also very competitively priced.

The Bad:
- Not a thing
profile.summary: Definately less effort and easily staples 25 sheets of paper.

profile.description: The MA145 is a Compact AC/DC Clamp Meter with NCV Detector. This Clamp meter takes True RMS measurements for accurate readings of noisy, distorted or non-sinusoidal waveforms. The MA145 can measure up to 300A AC and DC. Complete with carrying case and two LR44 batteries. UL listed with a CAT III 600V safety rating.
profile.reviewText:
The Good:
*  The unit has a nice feature that provides a AC proximity sense or when near an AC current the unit will beep and the display will flash.
*  Current accuracy seemed about correct when measuring current to a single 100W 115VAC light bulb.

The Bad:
  * In order to work the jaws must be clamped around a single wire.
  * Therefore for a AC cord one will have to strip a portion of the out cover to gain enough access to the individual wires to get the clamp around.
  *  The instructions or markings do not mention anything about the insulator on the batteries that must be removed before use.  It appears not to work after power on the first time.
  *  The tiny screw holding the battery cover in place is not captured so it will be easily lost if you are not cautious during its removal.
  * I felt the unit was on the slippery side and could use a textured skin to provide a more confident grip.
  * They don't mention a minimum accuracy in the specs but it is likely a +/- a few least significant digits.
  * It fairly pricey at $100 as of this review and  a quick survey suggests there are alternatives for less than 1/2 the price.

Conclusion:
Adequate performance and function but expensive with equally capable products for 1/2 the price.
profile.summary: Adequate capability but expensive.

profile.description: For anyone who changes positions during the night, this pillow is curved for comfort and shaped for support. The softly curved shape ensures gentle, therapeutic support for the shoulders of side sleepers and the neck of back sleepers, while having a low, comfortable profile for stomach sleepers. Experience less tossing, less turning and more deep sleeping.
profile.reviewText:
Even more so than clothing a pillow depends so much on the individuals preferences.  The Versacurve Sleep Innovations memory foam pillow has a good shape but its firmness make sit hard to get used to.  Here are my observations:.
The good:
  - It is hypoallergenic.
  - My favorite part of the pillow was the curve in the center bottom of the pillow.  Your shoulder fits right in it and is very comfortable for a side sleeper.
  - The cover was easily removable
  - The cover has a soft quilted feeling
  - The cover is washable in cold water.

The Bad or just observations
 - The pillow is dense or even hard especially as the foam settles.  Maybe too firm for some as it was for me.
 -  It is a bit awkward to reposition because of it being so hard and smallish.
 -  For side sleepers the shorter width along with the firmness does not really allow you to wrap the pillow around your head
 - When I removed the cover there were some foam anomalies or perhaps voids in the foam.  It didn't affect the shape or feel, just looked odd.

Conclusion:
The pillow is hard and small.  I would not normally use it unless for some therapeutic reason such as to adapt to a stiff neck.
profile.summary: Nice functional shape but very hard.

profile.description: Ditch the traditional hydration reservoir for the Geigerrig pressurized hydration engine. Simply add pressure to your reservoir using the power bulb and have on-demand water that sprays. Reversible, dishwasher safe design makes cleaning it extremely simple. All Geigerrig engines are covered by a lifetime warranty against leaks for years and years of use. Remove the slide top and easily refill from any river, stream, lake, or pond. Protect your thirst by plugging an Aquamira Frontier Filter inline via the built in quick connects and have a complete hydration and filtration system anywhere you go. The 3 Liter (100 oz.) engine fits the RIG and all larger hydration packs, including your existing pack.
profile.reviewText:
It works fine for me even without the pump.  I carry the bladder zipped up inside my motorcycle tank bag.  I fill with ice and water to the brim and it fits well in the zipped up tank bag and the length of the tube makes the bite valve easily accessible even while riding.  As it turns out I didn't need to pump it up.  I can easily pull water through the bite valve without the pump pressure even when the bite valve is 2 ft above the bladder. The drink tube attaches easily and securely.  I have washed the bag in the dishwasher a few times with no visible effect of fading or discoloring.
After about a year, the bite valve started to leak and I have submitted a warranty request to replace it.  The Geigerrig offers a lifetime warranty.  I submitted a warranty claim, however, it has been 6 weeks and I even spoke with someone who said they would take care of replacing the valve but I have not received or heard anything after 3 trys to get it replaced.  I have reduced my original rating to 3 stars due to their poor customer support.
profile.summary: Works fantastic w/lifetime warranty, but poor customer service

profile.description: The Sentinel 18-Sheet Cross-Cut Shredder is a heavy duty shredder. A 4mm x 43mm Cross-Cut shred for Level 4 security of your personal data. Auto start/stop means you simply leave the shredder on and simply feed the paper, CD/DVD or credit card into the intake. No need to remove staples-just send them through the shredder to save time. A manual reverse function allows you to reverse the cutting blades in the event of a jam. Want to shred CD/DVD media or credit cards? No problem, the Sentinel 18-Sheet Cross-Cut Shredder can do that too. Simple to empty with a slide out 7 gallon wastebasket. No plastic bags required; simply slide out the wastebasket, and dump the shredded material in the dumpster. Casters make moving the Sentinel 18-Sheet Cross-Cut Shredder easy. Equipped with a lighted over-heat indicator to protect the shredder motor. Reliable, easy to use and easy to empty makes the Sentinel 18-Sheet Cross-Cut Shredder a must have for home or office.
profile.reviewText:
For the home user this machine is more than enough.  Cross cut shredding up to 18 sheets simultaneously along with credit cards and CDs..
I ran some tests with the following good and marginal results :

The good;
- Cross cut sizes:  1 or 2 sheets cut just fine into about 1/8 by 1.5 inch lengths.  See picture attached.
- Credit cards and CDs no problem.  The shredder cut those up just fine.
- Staples no problem:  I loaded up 2 8.5x11 sheets with about 30 standard staples along all 4 edges and the shredder chewed up the sheets without jamming or slowing
- Input Overload prevention:  The opening is just larger then the thickness of 18 sheet 20lb paper which is about 1/16" so a nice feature to help keep from over loading.
- Now the bin is great.  Its viewable through the clear front fairly large at 7 gallons and simply slides out to empty it.  Really nice not to have to remove the heavy shredder head to empty.
- Auto start/stop worked every time.  Once you shove the paper in far enough, as long as its near the center where the switch sensor is, it will start and stops a moment after the paper has passed through.

The marginal:
- Its slow:  It takes about 5 seconds to shred a 8.5 x 11 sheet.  In an office this is probably too slow except for personal use.
- 18 sheets do not cross cut:.  I put 18ea 20lb 8.5x11 sheets of paper into the feed.  With the thick mass the shredder did not quite make the cross cut.  It made long cuts and you can see from the picture attached that where it tried but failed to cross cut .  For personal use I would think just fine but it doesn't perform as advertised.
- I thought maybe a little pricey for a home use machine.
- failed after 1.5yrs of home use

Conclusion:  The  machine cut up everything it claimed from credit cards to paper loaded with staples and the ease of viewing the basket and emptying it is a great convenience.  On the negative side it is a bit slow and it did not cross-cut large paper inputs of 18 sheets but was still able to cut lengthwise.  For home use I think the machine would be just fine but on the pricier side.
profile.summary: Fine for home use.  Powerful but a little slow and trouble cross cutting thicker inputs.

profile.description: Preserve the beauty of your floors with Scotch Felt Pads. Equipped with powerful adhesive and durable felt, these floor protectors adhere effortlessly to the legs of your furniture and provide long-lasting protection from gouges and scratches. They come in multiple sizes and colors, so there's a set that blends perfectly with all of your dcor. So help protect your investment, and enjoy your beautiful floors for years to come with Scotch Felt Pads.
profile.reviewText: These won't stay attached to chair legs as the ad picture implies.  I applied these to wooden chair legs that were 1.25 dia at the floor and the chair was on a wood floor made up of sections connected with small "V" seams .  After a few slides of the chair across the wood floor the pads slid off to one side.  These pads are only useful in my opinion for for objects other then chairs and that are stationary.  So as a floor protector from sliding chairs as the product primary purpose implies they fail totally and I can only score 1 star.  To protect surfaces from smaller and lighter items that are moved infrequently these pads can provide protection, but not with the day to day use of chairs.
profile.summary: Fails to protect flooring, won't stay attached to chair legs,  adhesive is weak, slides off during first few chair slide

profile.description: The Phantom Aquatics Impulse 1500 LED Dive Light, Is a portable magnetic controlled flashlight for professional diving use. It is equipped with a totally sealed magnetic controlled side switch that provides flexible operation underwater. Using the latest USA CREE XM-L2(U2) LED, max 1500 lumens output and over 18 hours runtime, this portable diving light offers three brightness levels and one strobe mode for diff- erect diving environment use. Plus simple style appearance, robust water pressure resistant construction, we believe it will be your best lighting tool for diving.
profile.reviewText:
I have not been able to dive with it but I have some observations that I can share.

The lamp is well built.  Milled from a solid aluminum block, the lamp is seamless and rugged but very heavy.  Its rated to survive a drop from 1m per the case labels.  The depth rating of 150m is extreme and the  build suggests it would be good enough at least for recreational diving depths.  The battery compartment, accessed by unscrewing the front assembly,  is sealed with 3 "O" rings for redundancy and heavily coated with silicon grease to provide a tight seal.  The assembly is hard to unscrew attesting to its seal.  The switch is isolated from the electrics as it uses a magnet through the body of the lamp to actuate the switches thus eliminating a potential source of leakage. The lamp end is a sealed unit with 3 high power LEDs hence they would not be user replaceable.

 As an experiment I did leave the lamp sit for many days submersed in 1 ft of water as well as run it through several highest temp dish washer cycles.  The lamp worked as new after that ordeal.

The lamp provides a very respectable 1500 lumens (the high setting) for 7 hours.  Comparing equivalently priced lamps shows this to be very competitive performance.  There is was no documentation provided with the unit so the specification I'm citing is from the case labels.

The lamp is provided with a carrying case, charger, wrist strap, a holder to attach to your dive belt and most impressively a spare set of "O" rings.

There is no beam focus and it does provide a wide presentation.  Holding the switch down will actuate a strobe mode which server as a locator in case separated from your partner.

A bit concerning is the lack of documentation provided with the unit, no suggestion of a warranty nor manufacturer contact info .  A web search was not able to locate the manufacturer but Amazon does show it is made in China.

In conclusion this is a very well built unit and if it lives up to its advertised specification will make a very reliable lamp.  Inspection of the lamps design and some testing suggest it will.  Without proper certification of its specifications, I would recommend to have a backup until the lamp proves itself under real world use.  For that I have held back 1 star.
profile.summary: Extremely Well Built with Bright Long Lasting Light

profile.description: The Oreck Venture bagged canister delivers incredible, quiet hard floor cleaning. Simply choose the perfect suction speed for your mess, then clean while the quiet design muffles the noise. Our innovative slim swivel steering allows you to maneuver around furniture and other obstacles in your home with ease. Above floor cleaning is especially convenient with a 6 ft. Hose and on-board tools. And you'll never need to bend down to wrap up the 22 ft. Cord-just retract it with the push of a button.
profile.reviewText:
Weve used the Oreck Venture now for several days and found it to have powerful suction while being the quietest vacuum we have every owned.  It does however have some functional and quality issues.  Hopefully our observations in this review can help you decide if its a good choice for you.

You should be aware that if you are considering the Venture, it is a hard floor vacuum only.  For carpet you will need the Venture Pro model comes with a carpet nozzle.

Performance:
The suction is powerful and surprisingly quiet.  With this one, you will not have to raise your voice to have a conversation vacuuming.  The vacuum has adjustable suction easily changed with a foot tap and with the setting readily observed by light indicators.  I don't know when I would ever want less then the maximum suction but none-the-less its a feature some may find useful.

Tools:
This model is specifically for hard floors only and comes with 2 large nozzles for that purpose along with 2 other tools for upholstery/dusting and a crevice tool.  The largest of the floor nozzles is without bristles, runs on 2 small wheels and meant to maximize suction.  The largest tool has a slim swivel steering head that would allow one to reach into spaces no taller then the head itself.  The 2nd smaller floor nozzle has  long bristles surrounding the head and is without wheels.  There is a dual use nozzle for use as a dusting brush and upholstery nozzle.  Its small at only about 8 wide and the brush slides without locking into the upholstery nozzle.  Each time I used this tool, the brush would easily slide out.  And a small crevice tool with a small opening to increase air flow.

There is a tool hanger on the end of the vacuum but it will only work with the smaller brushed head.  While both large heads had the adapter to mount to this tool holder, the larger head is too large to fit and drags on the floor.  A picture is attached that illustrate the problem.  The smaller tools store in a compartment on top and easily accessed (also see attached picture)

The metal telescoping extension wand extends and collapses easily and locks at different lengths.  We found the upholstery and crevice tool did not attach securely to the end of the metal wand and easily came off during use.  However, the same tools attached very firmly to the plastic hose handle.

The tools are made of mostly plastic and seem to be of lower durability.  A picture attached shows the wheels on the largest tool which I would expect not pass the test of time.

Features and Functionality:
HEPA Filtering:  Surprisingly, Oreck makes no mention of HEPA filtering on the vacuum or in the manual.  However, the Oreck bag part number 1C used by this machine is actually a HEPA rated bag.  They cost about $3 apiece for a bag.  There are also two additional filters that are easy to remove and can be washed.  I confirmed the HEPA filtering from the manufactures website.

Retractable Power Cord:  The power cord rewind works great and fully retracts the cord to the very end.  However, at 23 it was a bit short and required frequently moving the power plug to another outlet.  A better length would have been 30.

Standup or Roll:  A nice feature is that it will stand up on end which give you that little bit more reach without lifting the vacuum.  The Venture is an attractive looking appliance, sleek and black and rolls easily with 2 large rear wheels and 2 front wheels which rotate 360 degrees so it follows you around easily.

Light:  Pretty light at 16 lbs.

Issues:

Short Wand:  The combine length of the metal wand and the hose handle was 48, a bit too short to be comfortable for someone my height at 5 8.  A similar vacuum I own has a length of 56 as is a much more practical length in my opinion.  A picture comparing the 2 wants is attached.

Short Power Cord:  I felt the cord at 23 was too short and made it a bit inconvient to move the power cord frequently.  A better length would have been 30.

Durability:  The tools as mentioned earlier appear not to be made without long term durability in mind.

Tool Attachment:  The smaller tools do not hold securely enough to the mental wand however they attach snuggly to the plastic hose.

Tool Hanger:  The largest tool does not fit on the vacuums tool hanger.

Conclusion:
The strong suction and quiet operation for me outweigh the drawbacks of the Oreck Venture.  If your looking to vacuum hard floors only, you should put the Venture in your list to consider.
profile.summary: Strong Suction and Extremely Quiet

profile.description: The Canon PIXMA MG5520 all-in-one wireless inkjet photo printer is an advanced printer with a smart design delivering a combination of high performance and real convenience. Print beautiful, borderless photos up to 8.5" x 11" and crisp documents with remarkable quality. The MG5520 offers 4800 x 1200 maximum color dpi with 2pl technology, five individual ink tanks and the ChromaLife100+ system. If a color runs out, you only replace the ink tank you need. Plus, the Snap Edge feature allows for quick access to the ink tanks for easy replacement. With a 2.5" LCD screen, the MG5520 lets you preview your images before you print, and correct your photos with Auto Photo Fix II.
profile.reviewText:
out of the box works awesome.

Started by taking all the tape off and installing ink cartridges.  These are especially cool because a light turns on when they are installed correctly, so you know when they are working or not.  After all of the ink I installed the software (which is available on the CD as well as on Cannons website) and connected it to the wireless router.  Surprisingly easy to connect with the software on the PC as well as the printer.

I noticed there is an app for this type of cannon printers, downloaded it, and printed photos and documents from my phone.  Awesome.  This is especially helpful because I'm often working from Googles cloud to write papers and print them.

After the software it asked for a test print, which worked fine, and then you scan the test print so it can align the print head.

I printed some photos I took on my phone and they turned out OK.  A bit dark because it was a night photo, but still turned out really good considering.  The printer takes all sorts of paper for photo prints.

Scanner function works just as well.  Sends scanned images to your computer the software is installed on or USB drive in the printer.

overall, really awesome.

way better than a brother printer.

.

profile.description: Passive Infrared(PIR) sensors detect occupancy by sensing the difference between heat emitted from the human body in motion and the background space. In order to provide adequate coverage with-in a space, the sensors utilize a unique Fresnel lens which divides the coverage area into zones, thus enhancing the detection of small movement. Once an individual enters a space being monitored, the sensor responds to a change in the infrared background by turning the lights ON automatically. Once the individual leaves and the space is unoccupied for a selected period of time, the lights are turned Off automatically. profile.reviewText:
Rather than punch holes in dry to add a light switch I used this device to turn on kitchen under counter lights automatically.  Installation was straight forward and installed in a standard 2 gang box.  It comes with long wires attached and well labeled to make it easy to hook up.  THere are adustments for time on, motion and ambient light sensitivity (e.g. so as not to turn on during daylight if thats what you choose).  After installation,  it worked 1st time and the test mode which is only a 15second on time was handy to verify operation and adjust the settings.  It comes with a faceplate and a cover for the dial adjustments for a nice clean wall installation.  It senses a wide view angle which is great for my narrow galley kitchen.  It comes on immediately as I enter the  room.
Update:  Of 2 purchased after 16 months of sparse operation the unit failed.
profile.summary: Straightforward to install, Works great, failed after 16 months

profile.description: MasterFlow MF-1050 keeps your tires properly inflated, saving you money and time. This sturdy, rugged air compressor is multi-functional. It is designed for use on trucks, SUVs, 4X4s, and RV tires, but also works well on passenger car tires and inflatable household items. Masterflow air compressors have correctly sized direct drive motors, and a properly sized motor allows more efficient air flow and results in faster inflation time. Includes air compressor, carrying bag, air filter and needle adapters, with a 16 ft hose, and a 10 ft cord for convenient maneuverability. Features a maximum PSI of 150, and a run time of 20 minutes.
profile.reviewText:
I used this to refill Jeep Wrangler tires after deflating them for a trail run.
I used it attached to the battery without the engine running with no problem.  The manual says nothing about requiring the engine to run when using the air compressor.  Other compressors like Harbor Freight require that for the extra voltage.

The Good:
  * Nicely painted, looks quality.
  * Plenty of hose and power cable length.  The power cord is long enough to allow it to sit on the ground and the air hose easily reached the rear tires when attached to the battery in the front engine compartment.
  * The carrying case is nice.  Strong carry straps and easily fits everything without a struggle to put it in.
  *  It has a convenient power switch on the unit.
  *  It was reasonably quiet when pushing air into the tire.
  *  Works well without having to run the engine.
  *  Good air volume output at about 2.5 cfm.  almost 2x as much as I could find for equivalently priced units.
  *  It took 2 minutes to fill a single 31x10" tire from 20pst to 35 psi.
  *  Not too Hot.  After filling all 4 tires immediately one after the other the unit was not to hot to hold or put back in the bag.
  *  It comes with accessories for filling sport balls and air mattresses.  It filled an air mattress in about 45 seconds.
The Bad:
  *  The air pressure meter was very inaccurate.  It read a good 9lbs too high!  I used a separate and accurate meter to measure the air pressure which was also confirmed by the cars internal air pressure measurements.
  *  The air pressure meter has no calibration adjustment but I did use a permanent marker to mark the plastic face of the meter for 35lbs.
  *  The air filter is super cheaply made and must be removed before putting back into its carrying case.
  *  The stem attachment is screw on vs a quick disconnect.
Update Note:  I replaced the air pressure meter and the reading now is very accurate when the compressor is not running.  When the compressor runs it obviously has to pump air at a pressure higher then the tire so you will see the meter bounce around at a higher pressure then the static pressure but when you turn off the compressor the meter should read the final tire pressure.  The original meter was 5-10lbs off.  The replacement meter is very accurate confirmed with 2 other pressure meters.

Conclusion:
  Even with its issues this is a good value especially for the volume of air it provides.  Long term reliability it yet to be determined but after 8 uses no problems found.  The air pressure meter needs to be replaced for accurate readings.
profile.summary: A good value for the volume of air it provides and its relatively quiet but the provided air pressure meter accuracy is way off.

profile.description: Compact 5w Communications External Speaker.
profile.reviewText:
This was installed in a Jeep Wrangler from a radios auxiliary audio output jack supplying 2W.
The speaker is unpowered and only driven by the audio input.
The audio fidelity was better than the internal speaker of the radio.
Max volume setting of 2W was uncomfortably loud which means the speaker has adequate efficiency.
The speaker was plenty loud at about 3/4 volume to heard easily over the wind and engine when traveling on the freeway (you may not know but Jeep Wrangler have a lot of wind noise!).
The cord is 6ft long and terminated with a mono 3.5mm plug.
It was supplied with 2 sheet metal screws to attached the speaker via sloted holes on its swiveling mounting bracket.
The screws held the speaker firmly in place.
The speaker and be oriented and locked in place using the thumb screws on each side.  When tightened the speaker will not move.
 There are no instructions provided, not that you should need them for this simple installation.
The black color was perfect to blend in with the interior of the Jeep.
profile.summary: Efficient enough speaker that is very loud with only 2W of audio.

profile.description: The FL14 is a small yet effective headlamp. The solid and flashing red light features helps users preserve night vision in the dark. The headlamp is also equipped with a high and low feature that allows users to change between the two with the ease of pressing a button located on the top of the headlamp.
profile.reviewText:
This Coast lamp while functional offers less then the many others of this style and price range.  This lamp outputs 37 lumens at a price of $0.44/lumen.  Other equivalent price range lamps offer much more output in the same price range of $0.12/lumen.  When comparing battery life again the Coast lamp lags provided only 9 Hrs vs the 45 hrs for the example lamp already mentioned.  This lamps brightness would be fine for broad area illumination for emergency use and  camping but really not adequate as a work lamp such as for  up close detail work.  The head band is comfortable and adjustable.  A single button conveniently allows a bright and low level white light and a red lamp.
Conclusion:
Coast is a great brand that makes great high power lamps.  But there are many other lamps in price category that offer better performance.
profile.summary: Performance Does Not Seperate it From the Crowd.

profile.description: Magic tub & floor peel & stick caulk is pre-shaped, flexible trim with pre-applied adhesive. It's the perfect finishing touch to refresh or update your tub or floor trim.
profile.reviewText:
There are 2 problems with this coving, the adhesive and the ease of application.
1) The adhesive is applied as a narrower band along the back but does not cover the entire surface (see picture).  Further, the adhesive itself is thick, caulk like, and separates allowing a gap to form between tub and coving.  As a result the outer edges never adhere intimately with the surface.  There is a small gap.  Even after heavy pressure with rollers etc, it will initially appear intimate, but then will pull away and the glue when viewed from the top can be seen to have spread out with thread like connections to both surfaces  Yes the surface was prepared and the glue is sticking to the tub, however the thick adhesive itself separates, allow the edges to pull away form the tub and floor preventing a seamless intimate application.
2)  Secondly, it is difficult to apply and get a nice straight line.  The material is malleable enough to bend vertically and the result is a wavy edge along a 5ft tub bottom.  I suppose with a lot of prep work, laying a straight like with tape to follow would help this issue.

Conclusion:  It fine for a quick fix and probably better then nothing, but for a quality permanent aesthetically pleasing result a more traditional heavier vinyl  coving should be used where a thin adhesive can be applied across the entire surface and its stiff enough to not bend vertically.
profile.summary: Poor adhesion and Wavy Installation

profile.description: Sonic vibration rechargeable toothbrush. Clinically proven to reduce stains.
profile.reviewText:
The Panasonic is very small body tooth brush.  It has 3 settings accessed by sequentially pushing the Mode button for white, soft and sensitive.  The white is the most vigorous.the software reduces the vibrations and the sensitive modulates the vibration at a 1/2 second rate.  I don't see the advantage of ever using any mode that isn't full on.  It came with a small carrying case so the Panasonic would easily fit into a small purse.  The brush is easily detached.  It came with a 2 of brush attachments for gum massage and a small stand to hold them. I compared it to my existing Sonicare and the Panasonic is much less vigorous in it movement and seems to stall easier when pressed against suggesting the motor is not as strong.

I much prefer the more vigorous movement of the Sonicare as I think it would do a much better job of brushing.  Its ok if you need a small sonic brush if you travel occasionally but not as a full time brusher.
profile.summary: Not as vigorous as the Philips Sonicare

profile.description: The first Winmau Blade dartboard was released in 1997 and revolutionized the game of darts by removing all staples and offering the thinnest wiring available, making it the most technologically advanced dartboard of its time. Four generations later, the Blade 4 dartboard continues to pioneer new technologies and bring dart throwers the thinnest wiring available. The Blade 4 features new Dynamic Sector Wiring that is 50% thinner than the Blade 3 for higher scoring potential and better averages. The boards spider wiring is made of high-tensile, galvanized steel that is ultra-durable and deflects darts into the bed and increases the longevity of the board. The Blade 4s staple-free design increases scoring potential by decreasing the amount of wiring on the surface of the board. The Blade 4 is made of super-dense, high-visibility Kenyan Sisal that offers more vivid colors and repairs itself after each dart is removed, extending the life of the board. The Winmau Blade 4 has been used in professional tournaments around the world and is approved by the British Darts Organization (BDO).
profile.reviewText: This is one excellent board.  Heavy at 12 lbs attest to the high quality.  Darts never bounce out because it has a 2nd layer of material the darts can dig into before hitting a hard layer.  I tried, and every hard thrown dart stuck solidly (at least the ones that hit the board:)  Also nice is the very thin metal wire marking the segments that with several throws I never had a dart bounce back because of hitting a wire dead on.  A big plus is the mounting.  It comes with wall plate and adjustable screw pads with threaded inserts in the board that not only allow you to adjust for a straight up and down and side to side board but lock into place so it doesn't move when you strike it or pull darts.  Hey its not going to make me a more accurate dart thrower but it sure is going to make the game more fun!
profile.summary: Best I have ever owned

top_5.description: We don't know when or if this item will be back in stock.
top_5.reviewText:
This is a Suzuki factory  OEM part.
Easy to install:
Comes with all the hardware you need, except for some grease.  Easy to bolt on into existing threaded holes of the bike.  The hard part is the installation of the two springs used to hold it up the stand.  After several failed attempts to pry the springs on, I searched the web and found videos describing the use of small dia rope or strong string to pull the springs into place.  It worked the first try (but Im without a couple shoe strings:))
Rides well:  When I ride (and I ride on some rough roads) I do not hear the stand bouncing as its held firmly in place by the springs and a rubber foot that was provided as part of the install prevents any metal on metal contact.
Easy to use:  Forward and down pressure with your left foot on the stand while simultaneously pulling up and back on the bike will easily get the rear wheel off the ground.
top_5.summary: Easy to install (when you know the trick for installing springs) and works great.

top_5.description: Full Grain Leather and Mesh Upper. Padded collar . Full length cushion sock lining. Shaft height 7 "; Heel height 1.25". Oil-resistant rubber outsole. Cement Construction.
top_5.reviewText:
I took these on a 350 mile ride before evaluating them here.  Im not sure why these are called a motorcycle boots other then for marketing purposes.  It has no toe pad or reinforcement for the gear shift lever nor has protected padding along the outside or front.  In fact the vulnerable outside sides are a mesh like material and not leather, while the inside is leather......seems that's backwards for protection.  No zipper which I knew going in, but after lacing these on and off I can see that a good feature to reduce the time and hassle.  During the ride it was cool in the morning with the wind chill (air temp maybe low 70's) and my toes got very cold to the point I was looking for a place to stop and buy plastic bags to cover my feet.  The toe box materials in no leather nor does it appear to be air permeable but none-the-less one would not be able to use these in cold or even cool weather without additional foot insulation.  As the day heated up into the 80s, the boots became comfortable so for hot riding they would be fine.
On the plus side, they are very comfortable and lite out of the box and required no break in.  The sole pattern is very aggressive so should grab well on dirt/gravel roads.  I bought a size 12 EE and they fit great.
top_5.summary: Not Specifically for Motorcycle

top_5.description: Features Titanium Bonded blades that are 3x harder than untreated steel and will stay sharper longer. Handle material is 70% recycled content and rubber is 100% recycled content. Packaging is post consumer content. Wavy blades for pristine cuts. Blade Tension Control. Corrosion and adhesive resistant. Lifetime Warranty. Green/Black handles. Powered by Clauss.
top_5.reviewText: I used it extensively this weekend filling several garbage cans with the trimmings.  I trimmed bougainvillea branches up to 3/4" thick.  So given that this trimmer style is meant more as a hedge trimmer for smaller diameter stems, I would say it was very impressive that I could cut through such large branches.  It held up and I didn't feel it dull as the day progressed.  It has a wavy cutting edge  which may make it harder to sharpen but that is only an observation as it never dulled to the point I thought I needed to freshen the cutting edge.  I don't understand the value of the tension adjust (green knurled knob at pivot) as  I would think one would always want the pivot to be as friction free as possible. None-the-less it was an excellent trimmer and I thought a great value.
top_5.summary: Cut through larger branches than its intended for

top_5.description: The sleek design features a sliding USB connector, which smoothly extends from the drive at the push of a thumb. The capless mechanical design eliminates the hassle of lost drive caps. The USB connector can be made ready for use with just one hand, for greater convenience when speed is a must.
top_5.reviewText:
It works fine transferring large movie files from my laptop to the ADATA as USB2 but will not work as USB3.  Other mfr flash work find as usb3 on my laptop.  The storage size allows about 6+ full length HD movies to be stored.  the flash drive was recognized by all the devices I used and transferred data from the laptop and to the Sony Bluray player where I played the movies directly from the flash drive.
The connector retractor is nice as it protects the USB connector from damage when carrying in your pocket in computer case and eliminates the eventual loss of a unattached  protective cap.
The device would have been more perfect if it had  loop to attached to a key chain but the photo is clearly shows there is not one and I made the purchase knowing that.
My laptop supposedly has USB 3 and I would get messages when attached it that I should move it to another USB to get the full speed.  So Im not sure if it was operating at the max speed and if this was a computer, driver or other problem.  I can say it played HD 1080P 60Hz movies perfectly..
top_5.summary: Wont do USB3, otherwise Works Great, Connector is Protected and Played HD 1080P Movies Perfectly

I'm only giving it 2 stars at this point instead of 1 since it will work ok enough for text documents, plain, nothing else added text documents. profile.description: ZYMOX Otic is used in dogs and cats for the treatment of acute and chronic inflammation of the external ear caused by bacterial, viral and yeast infections. Treat once a day for 7 days for acute infection and once a day for 14 days for chronic infection. Do not use in conjunction with other topical ear medications or cleaners.
profile.reviewText:
Well my little black cat has terrible issues with allergies.  He is constantly shaking his head and scratching and the allergy medicine we give him just isn't enough.  We thought we'd try this and see how it goes.  He of course did not like having it done but what cat or person for that matter does like stuff getting squirted in their ears right?

We wrapped him in a towel and while my husband held him I administered the drops.  I used cotton pads to hold in his ears and mush around and then at the end we swiped his ears out a little with it.  Cotton balls would work better but we were out of them at the time.

Now even though it says to do it for 7 days in a row, we just didn't have the heart to do that to him and thought we'd see how he did with just one round.

However, doing just ONE treatment of this worked wonders!!  It's been well over a week or so and he's just now needing another treatment.  And he had serious wax buildup so this is already turning out to be a fantastic product!  Glad to have something like this as it will last us a long time, help our lil guy feel better in the end and save us money to boot!
profile.summary: Actually works incredibly well and quickly!

So if you want it to print JUST DOCUMENTS then fine, it's dealable.  BUT anything that is an image/photo that you want to print nearly to the edge then forget it, it won't.  I had images that weren't even the full 8.5 x 11 and it kept shrinking them and if I tried to print true to the size that my image was and not do the "scale to fit" it will cut the image off EVEN if it should all fit on the paper!

My husband and I have looked up everything we can, tried all the different settings and to no avail.  I'm so mad since I know now I'll have to at some point buy a whole new printer and this money was wasted on something that I could have put towards a better printer.

But I'll be honest, yes I know this is a "cheaper" printer when you're on a budget but I had cheap ink jet printers in the past that would print true to size or even all the way up to the edge of the page with no problems!  I'm only giving it 2 stars at this point instead of 1 since it will work ok enough for text documents, plain, nothing else added text documents.  The price of the replacement ink is ridiculous for this too but that's the way of many printers and I wouldn't mind if it actually worked as it should.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "2.0" for a product with description "Follow the story of Max Caulfield, a photography senior who discovers she can rewind time while saving her best friend Chloe Price. The pair soon find themselves investigating the mysterious disappearance of fellow student Rachel Amber, uncovering a dark side to life in Arcadia Bay. Meanwhile, Max must quickly learn that changing the past can sometimes lead to a devastating future.". The summary of the review text is "A cliche filled time traveling sci-fi thriller that's barely any of those things.".
output:
Life is Strange is a Square attempt to get in on TT's sweet delicious adventure moola. And they do a pretty good job, as the main gripe that most people have is picking an option in an adventure game and having it sound way different than a description. Here, when that happens, you rewind to just before the decision point and try again.

The setup and graphics are nifty, and effort and thought went into the journal and the overall look and feel of the game. While nothing really gets you to feel and empathize with the gawky teenager college student, the characters are connectable and the game looks good, and the dystopia feel comes through well with a few well put together characters, including the wanna be boyfriend who refuses to accept he's on planet Friend Zone.

The voice acting is great, but the only nit I have is that the character is so vocal about self doubt, constantly asking "What if?" Granted at critical story points that's important, but you shouldn't be second guessing yourself after every decision, as it sounds like the game is asking you directly "Are you sure you want to do that?"

The main gripe is the same gripe that I have ever since Walking Dead Season 1. No matter how much you try to "tailor" the story, the start and end points are always the same. While I understand that these projects are not bottomless money holes, two or three genreally different endings, with portions of narrative that're determined by past or current actions, its still not present. You know that no matter what you attempt, you're on a hiking path, and while you can walk off path to smell the roses, you can not blaze your own trail. And a rail shooter setup is almost the antonym of "adventure"

Episode 2/3 Update: I will admit that the central points the story pivots around have more of a feel of a choose your own adventure, but while there is a good amount of story that feels unique depending on your decisions, it still rings a little hollow, as the pieces are all always in the same places, they just sound different, and it does feel forced when they make a comment that a particular character is "gone," regardless of whether they have left or are stone dead. And some of the main plot points are aggravating, as you know whats coming over the horizon the minute the situation is set up, as we've all seen or read the story that this seems to be following: who'da thunk that manipulating the past has the possibility of making the present worse? shuky darns!

Episode 4: This episode's plot cost it two whole stars. At the major discovery, the characters reaction is so cartoonish and ridiculous, especially given the monologue a few minutes later that they have to "act like adults." What otherwise could've been a great cat and mouse thriller setup crashes into such a cliched and hackneyed horror movie trope that Voorhees or Myers would've just thrown up their hands and stormed off at how even they can't go for prey this stupid. While I wouldn't be this hard, a mere 40-50 seconds of dialogue would've saved it.

Episode 5 update: The overall plot of this can be summed up thus: "You want to know whats been going on? Well that's too bad!" Thats not to say that the ending is Bad. In other circumstances, it would've been wonderful. It was well acted, put together, and had choices that were really forceful and difficult. But again, they attempted to layer together A Sound of Thunder and Gone, Baby, Gone, and barely failed at both. This was rich and filled with psychological minutia that brought together a lot of disparate threads. Had it been basically entirely inside the main characters head and only in the "real world" for a few minutes, it would've been wonderful. But they simply gloss over a major overarching question, and it cripples the story because you're constantly talking about the plot point you're refusing to talk about.

What started as a Scooby Doo mystery with a Sci-Fi twist struggled to carry both plots simultaneously. The time travel gimmick is tolerable handled but becomes bafflingly clunky very quickly. Despite being under a phantom time limit in certain points, you're dinged later for making a "decision" regarding a character you didn't interact with and barely saw. The quasi-prophetic vision you had in the beginning? Forgotten by day two. The omens? Ignored, outside of a "huh, thats weird." One part tween drama, one part Gone Girl mystery, one part coming of age love story, and one part omen sprinkled A Sound of Thunder time travel thriller? That was a tall order, and while I applaud their valiant attempt, it fell flat on its face due to maybe 3 minutes of content, else wise it would've been 3 stars ecking towards 4.

profile.description: Explore the birthplace of the tech revolution as Marcus Holloway, a brilliant young hacker who has fallen victim to ctOS 2.0's predictive algorithms and accused of a crime he did not commit. In Marcus' quest to shut down ctOS 2.0 for good, hacking is the ultimate weapon.Players can not only hack into the San Francisco Bay Area's infrastructure but also every person and any connected device they possess to trigger unpredictable chains of events in this vast open world.
profile.reviewText:
Watch Dogs 2 continues the quintessential nerd dream: that hacking can open every door in life and make you nigh unto a God, where in reality you're typically hunched over a keyboard for 4 hours to find a single exploit to squeak inside an email account. What comes out is a 2016 remake of Hackers the movie, with you effectively becoming Zero Cool. If they had a Rasta style guy who looked like Mathew Lillard this would be drifting into plagiarism territory. That's not a bad thing, but while I appreciate the change in tone from Watch Dogs almost Sin City like grit and vinegar, this almost brushes up against being a near Austin Powers like hacker parody.

Graphics: Beautiful, Ubi is really stepping into the 4K world, although the step from HD to UHD graphics causes problems with the faces and a few images at distance. People look like they have half a mouthful of caramel while they're talking.

Writing: Effort was put in to make missions feel alive. Yes its go collect this, shoot that guy, drive fast here. The fact that they make a good joke or story about why you're doing that ratchets up the enjoyability by a factor of 8.

Gameplay: Everything is the same. See below bullets.

Pros:
Enjoyable, light story
Entertaining characters
At least make a token effort to sound tech smart (no coding in the hackspace)
Organic, living world
Gorgeous, nearly true to life SF
Believable AI
Decently written side stories
Summon Car doesn't have any lag.

Cons:
Face movements during speech stink
Unrealistic combat and
Pop up central
Some clunky puzzles that rely more on finding that one spot to stand than logic
Pointless collection fests
No garages for car collection

Better than WD1:
Characters and story aren't watered down Batman with extra gravel voice.
Side missions give you a chance to vent frustration on barely papered over stand ins for real life villains, rather than cartoon caricatures.

Worse than WD1:
No crime stopper side missions
No drinking mini game
Basically all the same side gimmicks with hacking

WD2 tries not to take itself to seriously, but it feels like they pushed the pendulum to far. You're not some embittered vigilante out for revenge for a dead niece, but this is so happy go lucky. The setup is too drop in and go, and the whole point almost becomes do what you're told so dedsec will like you, which feels almost sketchy at times.
profile.summary: Ehhhhhh..... Its alright. They needed to dial in tone and feel better.

profile.description: Assassin's Creed is the next-gen game developed by Ubisoft Montreal that will redefine the action genre. While other games claim to be next-gen with impressive graphics and physics, Assassin's Creed merges technology, game design, theme, and emotions into a world where you instigate chaos and become a vulnerable, yet powerful, agent of change. The setting is 1191 AD. The Third Crusade is tearing the Holy Land apart. You, Altair, intend to stop the hostilities by suppressing both sides of the conflict. You are an Assassin, a warrior shrouded in secrecy and feared for your ruthlessness. Your actions can throw your immediate environment into chaos, and your existence will shape events during this pivotal moment in history. Key Features Be an Assassin Master the skills, tactics, and weapons of history's deadliest and most secretive clan of warriors. Plan your attacks, strike without mercy, and fight your way to escape. Realistic and responsive environments Crowds react to your moves and will either help or hinder you on your quests. Action with a new dimension total freedom Eliminate your targets wherever, whenever, and however. Stalk your prey through richly detailed, historically accurate, open-ended environments. Scale buildings, mount horses, blend in with crowds. Do whatever it takes to achieve your objectives. Relive the epic times of the Crusades Assassin's Creed immerses you in the realistic and historical Holy Land of the 12th century, featuring life-like graphics, ambience, and the subtle, yet detailed nuances of a living world. Intense action rooted in reality Experience heavy action blended with fluid and precise animations. Use a wide range of medieval weapons, and face your enemies in realistic swordfight duels. Next-gen gameplay The proprietary engine developed from the ground up for the next-gen console allows organic game design featuring open gameplay, intuitive control scheme, realistic interaction with environment, and a fluid, yet sharp, combat mechanic.
profile.reviewText:
Assassins Creed 3 manages to live up to the hype of its runup, provided you are willing to overlook a bit too much cutscening, way too labyrinthian tutorials, and a large portion of graphical glitches. While I applaud the attempt of Ubi to push the envelope, their flagship title probably isn't where they want to do the first breakout of the "new and improved" Anvil engine.

Graphics (5-10/10): Graphics of the environments are simply stunning. Water flows like water on the sea, clouds and landscapes are pristine and crsip, and fog flows naturally and blocks just the right amount of vision. Trees and buildings feel natural and organic, and nothing is left feeling out of place.

People graphics are... very unsettling. The eyes especially always look like polished stones because of a persistent reflective effect. Clothes and weapons go through objects and people rag doll way too much when killed. Stutters from officers are the worst, with partolling officials getting trapped on railings, shimmying like they are doing the ants in the pants dance, or sinking into the floor but somehow spinning like tops to stare directly at you.

The cutscenes are fantastic, but its almost that they're too detailed. The new engine is great, but leaving it at 60% of capability would've removed a large portion of the problems but still allowed for improvements.

Characters (2-10/10): The characters can make or break a story. Alitair was distant but just involved enough that you felt something for the character. Ezio was entertaining, funny, well developed, and flowed organically from one game to the next, plot hole leaps forward in time be damned.

Desmond is like a pair of dress pants you don't like. You wear them when you have to, and they're annoying, but they do serve a purpose and you can have a quite enjoyable experience in them provided its brief. In other words, perfect. Desmond's story draws to a well deserved and entertaining close, but thankfully he's not the central character.

Haytham Kenway therefore is like slipping into a pair of your favorite jeans: broken in, comfortable, and wearable anywhere. He's erudite, cultured, polite, and willing to rip your heart out through your back after finishing his High Tea.

Connor Kenway... Connor Kenway... ... one must pause long and hard before putting words to this creation. Connor is not something that can be easily shoved into a pants based metaphor. He's frustrating, incredibly naive, stupid and brilliantly intelligent, and willing to put his money with his mouth is. All of his positive and negative aspects sum up to almost zero. He's never truly likable, but never annoyed you enough to make him a legitimate detraction. The fact that they've already leapt to a new ancestor is proof that Ubi at least picked up on that.

Audio (7/10): Audio continues to be top notch. However, while it was great that they got a dozen Mohawk to voice characters, after ten minutes, it was unnecessary in the extreme.

Gameplay (8/10): Improvements abound here, but for one place: the 6 hour "tutorial." Did you know you can choke out a guard instead of kill them if you are empty handed? I didn't, and the game never told you, or that you had a horse summoning whistle, and left you plodding throuh 4-foot deep snow.

AC1's tutorial was seven minutes, all in the Animus. Having one mission explain one new command at a time was a ghastly experience, and it still didn't cover everything that was critical.

The naval portion has to be seen to be believed. I could play a whole game like that and be content. Between bording actions and cannon warfare, its like watching a naval war movie.

New side missions are well placed and a nice addition rather than being a crucial waste of time, ala Codex pages. They help and they're useful, but the game won't screech to a halt so you can go collect them all.

Story (10/10): If you see some of the twists coming, you are probably psychic. Not much more can be said without spoilers.

Overall (8/10): Packaging and unbelievable glitches are the only spots where this game stutters. Suspension of disbelief is great, but when you ride on a horse with a musket sticking through it, it's kind of like being on a plane during takeoff that sucks in a flock of ducks. They're all small things, but you can't ignore how much bumpier the ride suddenly becomes. A few patches and this'll quickly crawl up to 9-10 range. By the time they make the War of 1812 installment for Connor, they'll have the system nailed down.

Update: The Tyranny of King Washington DLC (5/10): The alternate history DLC was very poorly thought out. The first episode is on an entirely new map, an almost nuclear winter New York, and follows a surprisingly bland and boring plot, where Washington is corrupted by the Apple of Eden. New abilities are shoe horned in pretty hard and are absolutely necessary to proceed through the plot, which is a pretty bad thing, as you're supposed to be able to get through on your wit and guile rather than your "spirit power."

The future episodes appear to hold more promise, but so far, I'm unimpressed. I've already purchased the season pass, so hopefully this will improve.

In addition, MP content continues to be added. Not just player purchased items, if you have money that you absolutely have to flush-I mean spend, but cutscenes and "glitched" cutscenes, which can be pretty entertaining. A seroius Gold star for actually adding content rather than just another ten billion prestige levels.
profile.summary: Great addition, but needed more polish

profile.reviewText:
Assassins Creed delivers on its promises right from the beginning. The twist at the opening is a touch hard to swallow, but at least they cover all the glaring plot holes, and it helps that you don't have to deal with the main character speaking with a hard to understand accent or using esoteric terminology. Which is extra good considering there are no subtitles. The storyline is straightforwad in the Assassins role. You fail to eliminate Sir Robert, a Kinghts Templar, while simulataneously failing to complete a vital mission.

Your mission is saved by a fellow assassin, and you are demoted to Novice. To regain your standing, you must elimiate 9 men who're exacerbating the Crusades. Every one seems to be a monster... at first. While many have excuses and reasons that're glazes on something foul and inexcusable, some will manage to slither under your skin as to whether they were truly evil. The butcher doctor, who manages to save some while killing others, in the cause of advancing medical science so he can help all. The slaver, who captures some slaves solely in order that they may have food and shelter.

Visuals/Audio: This is where they make their bank. The landscape is photorealistic in many places, and breathtakingly gorgeous. The houses are well done to the period and locations, as are the people. Motions and movements and realistic, which is much, much harder to do well than it sounds. The audio has some tiny drawbacks, mainly making it hard to hear voices over the background jumble.

Gameplay: Combat is great, and well thought out. While it is somewhat repetitive, the basic enemies can put you down very quickly if your not careful. Some aspects are well done, if annoying. Walking through crowds can draw attention if you jostle too many people, and beggars will block your path constantly in poorer areas. One just annoying fact that they should've caught is some NPC's have an almost magnetic connection to you. The town crazies will constantly shove you, ignoring everyone else, unless you give them a wide berth, and the moment you're shoved you're exposed. But thats one drawback among an otherwise brilliantly put together setup.

Sidequests are somewhat more annoying. The ones in the city are rinse and repeat. Save the citizen by killing 4 guards, pickpocket, eavesdrop, and interrogate sum them up in their entirety. A bit more variety breaking it up would've masked it perfectly. The assassinations themselves are challenging and very engaging. The extra sidequests are as bad if not worse. Find the flags and find the templars. While those sound plausible, and they are for the templars, considering they're much harder fights, the flags are infuriating. You'd think flags would be on buildings and with army encampments, and for the most part they are, but many are also hidden in high grass, down blind alleys, and in the middle of forests. I can not see how those quests can be completed without guides.

Overall: The quests are the only reason this isn't 5 stars. It wouldn't have taken much thought, and little addiitional effort to come up with additional ideas. Aside from that one stain, this game is gorgeous and engaging. Despite how it might make you grind your teeth sometimes, it is one of those ones where you'll find yourself going "Just one more flag.... Is it really 4 am?" Even in retrospect, its worth the $[...] price tag.
profile.summary: Brilliant delivery with only a handful of drawbacks

Keeping the traditional gameplay of Point & Click adventure             games 'The Awakened' has been deeply rethought to offer a totally             new third person view while keeping its original first person view.             The player will be able to switch freely between the two modes to             lead its investigation the way he wants.                                                                               Based on an exciting scenario 'The Awakened' plunges the playerinto the heart of a mysterious and oppressive adventure. Sherlock Holmesassisted by the loyal Doctor Watson investigates strange disappearances whichseem related to the activity of a secret sect which worships the god Cthulhu.Discover the adventures of Sherlock Holmes with a gripping atmosphere for thefirst time ever delivered in a thoroughly intensive and wholly immersivereal-time 3D world.
