profile.reviewText:
Moen makes wonderful pieces. They look wonderful, they are typically easy to install and actually come consistently with everything in the box that you would think should come with a plumbing fixture.

This was a long afternoon to install, with a great, easy sweeping arc faucet handle. The finish looks wonderful and the faucet works great.

The only drawback for this is some of the bracketry wasn't well setup for my lower-middle class bathroom, and the cover to replace my hot and cold knobs didn't fit as nicely as I'd like. It is pretty pricery, given the last piece I got from moen for my kitchen had several additional features, where as this is just a good looking one handle faucet.
profile.summary: Another great piece, but pretty steep for a faucet

top_5.description: Explore the birthplace of the tech revolution as Marcus Holloway, a brilliant young hacker who has fallen victim to ctOS 2.0's predictive algorithms and accused of a crime he did not commit. In Marcus' quest to shut down ctOS 2.0 for good, hacking is the ultimate weapon.Players can not only hack into the San Francisco Bay Area's infrastructure but also every person and any connected device they possess to trigger unpredictable chains of events in this vast open world.
top_5.reviewText:
Watch Dogs 2 continues the quintessential nerd dream: that hacking can open every door in life and make you nigh unto a God, where in reality you're typically hunched over a keyboard for 4 hours to find a single exploit to squeak inside an email account. What comes out is a 2016 remake of Hackers the movie, with you effectively becoming Zero Cool. If they had a Rasta style guy who looked like Mathew Lillard this would be drifting into plagiarism territory. That's not a bad thing, but while I appreciate the change in tone from Watch Dogs almost Sin City like grit and vinegar, this almost brushes up against being a near Austin Powers like hacker parody.

Graphics: Beautiful, Ubi is really stepping into the 4K world, although the step from HD to UHD graphics causes problems with the faces and a few images at distance. People look like they have half a mouthful of caramel while they're talking.

Writing: Effort was put in to make missions feel alive. Yes its go collect this, shoot that guy, drive fast here. The fact that they make a good joke or story about why you're doing that ratchets up the enjoyability by a factor of 8.

Gameplay: Everything is the same. See below bullets.

Pros:
Enjoyable, light story
Entertaining characters
At least make a token effort to sound tech smart (no coding in the hackspace)
Organic, living world
Gorgeous, nearly true to life SF
Believable AI
Decently written side stories
Summon Car doesn't have any lag.

Cons:
Face movements during speech stink
Unrealistic combat and
Pop up central
Some clunky puzzles that rely more on finding that one spot to stand than logic
Pointless collection fests
No garages for car collection

Better than WD1:
Characters and story aren't watered down Batman with extra gravel voice.
Side missions give you a chance to vent frustration on barely papered over stand ins for real life villains, rather than cartoon caricatures.

Worse than WD1:
No crime stopper side missions
No drinking mini game
Basically all the same side gimmicks with hacking

WD2 tries not to take itself to seriously, but it feels like they pushed the pendulum to far. You're not some embittered vigilante out for revenge for a dead niece, but this is so happy go lucky. The setup is too drop in and go, and the whole point almost becomes do what you're told so dedsec will like you, which feels almost sketchy at times.
top_5.summary: Ehhhhhh..... Its alright. They needed to dial in tone and feel better.

top_5.description: Assassin's Creed is the next-gen game developed by Ubisoft Montreal that will redefine the action genre. While other games claim to be next-gen with impressive graphics and physics, Assassin's Creed merges technology, game design, theme, and emotions into a world where you instigate chaos and become a vulnerable, yet powerful, agent of change. The setting is 1191 AD. The Third Crusade is tearing the Holy Land apart. You, Altair, intend to stop the hostilities by suppressing both sides of the conflict. You are an Assassin, a warrior shrouded in secrecy and feared for your ruthlessness. Your actions can throw your immediate environment into chaos, and your existence will shape events during this pivotal moment in history. Key Features Be an Assassin Master the skills, tactics, and weapons of history's deadliest and most secretive clan of warriors. Plan your attacks, strike without mercy, and fight your way to escape. Realistic and responsive environments Crowds react to your moves and will either help or hinder you on your quests. Action with a new dimension total freedom Eliminate your targets wherever, whenever, and however. Stalk your prey through richly detailed, historically accurate, open-ended environments. Scale buildings, mount horses, blend in with crowds. Do whatever it takes to achieve your objectives. Relive the epic times of the Crusades Assassin's Creed immerses you in the realistic and historical Holy Land of the 12th century, featuring life-like graphics, ambience, and the subtle, yet detailed nuances of a living world. Intense action rooted in reality Experience heavy action blended with fluid and precise animations. Use a wide range of medieval weapons, and face your enemies in realistic swordfight duels. Next-gen gameplay The proprietary engine developed from the ground up for the next-gen console allows organic game design featuring open gameplay, intuitive control scheme, realistic interaction with environment, and a fluid, yet sharp, combat mechanic.
top_5.reviewText:
Assassins Creed 3 manages to live up to the hype of its runup, provided you are willing to overlook a bit too much cutscening, way too labyrinthian tutorials, and a large portion of graphical glitches. While I applaud the attempt of Ubi to push the envelope, their flagship title probably isn't where they want to do the first breakout of the "new and improved" Anvil engine.

Graphics (5-10/10): Graphics of the environments are simply stunning. Water flows like water on the sea, clouds and landscapes are pristine and crsip, and fog flows naturally and blocks just the right amount of vision. Trees and buildings feel natural and organic, and nothing is left feeling out of place.

People graphics are... very unsettling. The eyes especially always look like polished stones because of a persistent reflective effect. Clothes and weapons go through objects and people rag doll way too much when killed. Stutters from officers are the worst, with partolling officials getting trapped on railings, shimmying like they are doing the ants in the pants dance, or sinking into the floor but somehow spinning like tops to stare directly at you.

The cutscenes are fantastic, but its almost that they're too detailed. The new engine is great, but leaving it at 60% of capability would've removed a large portion of the problems but still allowed for improvements.

Characters (2-10/10): The characters can make or break a story. Alitair was distant but just involved enough that you felt something for the character. Ezio was entertaining, funny, well developed, and flowed organically from one game to the next, plot hole leaps forward in time be damned.

Desmond is like a pair of dress pants you don't like. You wear them when you have to, and they're annoying, but they do serve a purpose and you can have a quite enjoyable experience in them provided its brief. In other words, perfect. Desmond's story draws to a well deserved and entertaining close, but thankfully he's not the central character.

Haytham Kenway therefore is like slipping into a pair of your favorite jeans: broken in, comfortable, and wearable anywhere. He's erudite, cultured, polite, and willing to rip your heart out through your back after finishing his High Tea.

Connor Kenway... Connor Kenway... ... one must pause long and hard before putting words to this creation. Connor is not something that can be easily shoved into a pants based metaphor. He's frustrating, incredibly naive, stupid and brilliantly intelligent, and willing to put his money with his mouth is. All of his positive and negative aspects sum up to almost zero. He's never truly likable, but never annoyed you enough to make him a legitimate detraction. The fact that they've already leapt to a new ancestor is proof that Ubi at least picked up on that.

Audio (7/10): Audio continues to be top notch. However, while it was great that they got a dozen Mohawk to voice characters, after ten minutes, it was unnecessary in the extreme.

Gameplay (8/10): Improvements abound here, but for one place: the 6 hour "tutorial." Did you know you can choke out a guard instead of kill them if you are empty handed? I didn't, and the game never told you, or that you had a horse summoning whistle, and left you plodding throuh 4-foot deep snow.

AC1's tutorial was seven minutes, all in the Animus. Having one mission explain one new command at a time was a ghastly experience, and it still didn't cover everything that was critical.

The naval portion has to be seen to be believed. I could play a whole game like that and be content. Between bording actions and cannon warfare, its like watching a naval war movie.

New side missions are well placed and a nice addition rather than being a crucial waste of time, ala Codex pages. They help and they're useful, but the game won't screech to a halt so you can go collect them all.

Story (10/10): If you see some of the twists coming, you are probably psychic. Not much more can be said without spoilers.

Overall (8/10): Packaging and unbelievable glitches are the only spots where this game stutters. Suspension of disbelief is great, but when you ride on a horse with a musket sticking through it, it's kind of like being on a plane during takeoff that sucks in a flock of ducks. They're all small things, but you can't ignore how much bumpier the ride suddenly becomes. A few patches and this'll quickly crawl up to 9-10 range. By the time they make the War of 1812 installment for Connor, they'll have the system nailed down.

Update: The Tyranny of King Washington DLC (5/10): The alternate history DLC was very poorly thought out. The first episode is on an entirely new map, an almost nuclear winter New York, and follows a surprisingly bland and boring plot, where Washington is corrupted by the Apple of Eden. New abilities are shoe horned in pretty hard and are absolutely necessary to proceed through the plot, which is a pretty bad thing, as you're supposed to be able to get through on your wit and guile rather than your "spirit power."

The future episodes appear to hold more promise, but so far, I'm unimpressed. I've already purchased the season pass, so hopefully this will improve.

In addition, MP content continues to be added. Not just player purchased items, if you have money that you absolutely have to flush-I mean spend, but cutscenes and "glitched" cutscenes, which can be pretty entertaining. A seroius Gold star for actually adding content rather than just another ten billion prestige levels.
top_5.summary: Great addition, but needed more polish

top_5.reviewText:
Assassins Creed delivers on its promises right from the beginning. The twist at the opening is a touch hard to swallow, but at least they cover all the glaring plot holes, and it helps that you don't have to deal with the main character speaking with a hard to understand accent or using esoteric terminology. Which is extra good considering there are no subtitles. The storyline is straightforwad in the Assassins role. You fail to eliminate Sir Robert, a Kinghts Templar, while simulataneously failing to complete a vital mission.

Your mission is saved by a fellow assassin, and you are demoted to Novice. To regain your standing, you must elimiate 9 men who're exacerbating the Crusades. Every one seems to be a monster... at first. While many have excuses and reasons that're glazes on something foul and inexcusable, some will manage to slither under your skin as to whether they were truly evil. The butcher doctor, who manages to save some while killing others, in the cause of advancing medical science so he can help all. The slaver, who captures some slaves solely in order that they may have food and shelter.

Visuals/Audio: This is where they make their bank. The landscape is photorealistic in many places, and breathtakingly gorgeous. The houses are well done to the period and locations, as are the people. Motions and movements and realistic, which is much, much harder to do well than it sounds. The audio has some tiny drawbacks, mainly making it hard to hear voices over the background jumble.

Gameplay: Combat is great, and well thought out. While it is somewhat repetitive, the basic enemies can put you down very quickly if your not careful. Some aspects are well done, if annoying. Walking through crowds can draw attention if you jostle too many people, and beggars will block your path constantly in poorer areas. One just annoying fact that they should've caught is some NPC's have an almost magnetic connection to you. The town crazies will constantly shove you, ignoring everyone else, unless you give them a wide berth, and the moment you're shoved you're exposed. But thats one drawback among an otherwise brilliantly put together setup.

Sidequests are somewhat more annoying. The ones in the city are rinse and repeat. Save the citizen by killing 4 guards, pickpocket, eavesdrop, and interrogate sum them up in their entirety. A bit more variety breaking it up would've masked it perfectly. The assassinations themselves are challenging and very engaging. The extra sidequests are as bad if not worse. Find the flags and find the templars. While those sound plausible, and they are for the templars, considering they're much harder fights, the flags are infuriating. You'd think flags would be on buildings and with army encampments, and for the most part they are, but many are also hidden in high grass, down blind alleys, and in the middle of forests. I can not see how those quests can be completed without guides.

Overall: The quests are the only reason this isn't 5 stars. It wouldn't have taken much thought, and little addiitional effort to come up with additional ideas. Aside from that one stain, this game is gorgeous and engaging. Despite how it might make you grind your teeth sometimes, it is one of those ones where you'll find yourself going "Just one more flag.... Is it really 4 am?" Even in retrospect, its worth the $[...] price tag.
top_5.summary: Brilliant delivery with only a handful of drawbacks

And yet amidst the daily grind and bustling lives of societythere also exists terrifying places and it is in these confines where you willhave to control your fears retain your focus and ascertain the truth.Sherlock Holmes - 'The Awakened' offers rewarding gameplay a true symbiosis oftwo technologies specific to adventure gam
top_5.reviewText:
If you like Doyle and Lovecraft, than this nice mix will definitely suit you, assuming you don't put an ax through your computer first. The story starts out simply enough, with the servant of a nearby neighbor disappearing. This sets Holmes off on a quest that takes him from London to Switzerland to the US, on the trail of a sect of Cthulu worshippers.

The gameplay is where this nice startoff falls flat on its face. While the mystery parts of it are tolerable, the mini puzzles and mix-n-match inventory is where it truly enrages a player. You can pick locks, but only some, the guards can see through walls and doors, and finding the right piece of inventory to advance the story is a familiar hated enemy for any adventure game fan.

Simply put, you'll need a walkthrough, no if ands or buts, to spot the one piece of data or overlooked interactive piece of environment. either that, or you'll need microscopic eyes and an ability to see the spirites you can actaully interface with.

Enough soapboxing for one review. The voices are great, though some of the extras were awful. When you hear groaning thats more pornographic than painful, you'll know what I mean. The atmoshpere is just right, a median between too creepy and too cartoonish. The graphics are barely passable, but the group, being fairly new, can be forgiven for some start off stumbles. Assuming they learn from their mistakes, their next release could be a 4-5 star.
top_5.summary: Good Story with abysmal delivery

top_5.description: The third installment in the theatrical franchise...A young man with the power to time travel attempts to solve the mystery of his girlfriends death...but in doing so, is he causing the death of many more?
top_5.reviewText:
When you pick up any of the 8 films to die for, you realize you're not going to be in for an exactly oscar winning performance. Nowhere is this more implied than with The Butterfly Effect 3. Sam, a psuedo detective worknig for the police, has a strict "observe and report" outlook on murder, using his TARDIS like abilities to be able to travel back to any point in his life, and presumably to any point where he could easily reached, as he did not find out who any number of assassins or lotto numbers were. Several people, including a physics professor and his little sister are aware of his abilities, trying to reinforce the simple rule than he can't fix things. He responds several times by screaming repeatedly "I can fix this!" leading to the movies downward spiral. Starting from his attempt to save his ex-girlfriend, he sets off the actions of a serial killer, invariably drawing the police closer and closer to himself.

The acting in this is hand and fist above most direct to DVD. There are quite a few scenes that give it the flavor of a soft core porn or a much worse direct to video, but if you can gloss over these homicidal drop-ins, the movie is tolerable, though you can guess with near certainty the outcome. The ending breaks aware from cookie-cutter somewhat, but feels bland and boring. Some good gore and blood without being a nightmare on elm street or friday the 13th make this a solid rent, though there are portions you have to skip. Overall, nothing worth writing home about, but leagues and bound above a Pulse 3 or a Jeffersons.
top_5.summary: You can do worse, but not by much

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "THOR, ONE OF THE GREAT AVENGERS,". The summary of the review text is "One of Marvel's better titles in recent years".
output:
I have followed the Thor series off and on since encountering it as a kid back in the late 60's, but I was quite stunned to see this shockingly offbeat, but utterly engrossing, take on the Thor universe from Marvel's "mature" imprint, Max. This series is as graphic in its depiction of violence as I've ever seen from a mainstream publisher and even underground grue legend S. Clay Wilson will feel like he's been outdone in some areas ! But no matter how over-the-top the violence is, it's integral to the storyline, in which a boatload of Undead vikings arrives in NYC to loot, rape, and murder to their heart's content. Thor's initial encounter with Jaeckelson, the viking leader, is memorable in its brutality and leaves the reader feeling like they've been punched in the stomach. The ensuing chapters detail Thor's collaboration with other Marvel universe heroes, and their efforts to defeat the onslaught. They also introduce some memorable new characters that I, for one, would like to see appearing in a sequel (?) at one time or another.

Glenn Fabry's artwork, while sometimes a bit awkward in rendering human forms in action, succeeds quite well in capturing the apocalyptic tone of the story. Whether focusing on up-close action involving hand-to-hand combat, or aerial battles that offer a relatively drastic change in perspective, the immediacy of the struggle between Thor and his adversaries is effectively communicated without being so cluttered or self-consciously "artistic" that the reader is left peering at the page and trying to puzzle out exactly what's happening. In light of how pervasive the cartoony, expressionistic style of comic art is nowadays,  Fabry's straightforward, realistic draftsmanship is exactly what's required to give Ennis's plot the graphic intensity it needs.

Forget the overwrought, encrusted, heavy-handed melodrama so typical of much of Marvel's output over the past two decades. Thor: Vikings is an unadorned battle between good and evil and never shies from revealing how violent and cruel such a primeval conflict can be. The intensity of the conflict is relieved every now and then by some black humor, but upon finishing the book there was no avoiding the feeling that I'd just been treated to the Battle Royale of the Marvel universe.

profile.description: Garth Ennis, a critically acclaimed writer from Northern Ireland, has been working in the comic book industry for over 20 years, and is most easily recognized as the creator of Preacher, and long-time contributor to Marvel's Punisher. Perhaps his greatest success in recent years has been CROSSED, a horror survival series published by Avatar Press, in which the world has been overrun by sadistic homicidal maniacs. The CROSSED property has been optioned for film by Kevin Spacey’ s Trigger Street Productions. Other Avatar publications by Ennis include STREETS OF GLORY, CHRONICLES OF WORMWOOD, and 303.
profile.reviewText:
In 2008, after watching the rise in popularity of Robert Kirkmans comic book series The Walking Dead, Garth Ennis decided to expand his already enormous output of comics by creating his own zombie apocalypse series titled Crossed. After the first set of issues, Ennis turned scripting duties over to other writers but retained ownership of the title.

Published by Avatar, Crossed took an unabashed splatterpunk approach to the genre, depicting all manner of depraved ultraviolence. Whether or not you think this is wholesome, the fact that Crossed is a thriving series today, nearly a  decade later, means that there is a sizeable readership for splatterpunk comics. And Avatar, an indie publisher who determinedly aims at an adult readership, always seems to find printers willing to risk lawsuits by printing explicit material.

The issues of Crossed that I have read have all more or less stuck to the same paradigm: somewhat bland, pedestrian stories whose main function is to serve as a scaffold upon which the series artists load carnographic imagery designed to keep the Gorehounds satisfied. Theres nothing intrinsically wrong with this, but it does lead me to have modest expectations for material originating from Ennis.

Which brings me to this compilation of Streets of Glory, which ran as an Avatar comic for 6 issues (September 2007  March 2008). For all practical purposes, this was Enniss first attempt at a Western series. And for all practical purposes, its Crossed meets the Clint Eastwood film Pale Rider.

The story is set in 1899 in Gladback, Montana, a small town that represents the old west; however, the reader is alerted that Change is Coming, via a segment featuring an automobile careening down Main Street.

The lead character is the standard-issue Civil War veteran (this time of the Union side) who doesnt say much; has the kind of history that people whisper about; and a knack for sparking   and ending  mayhem: Joe Dunn.

Dunns arrival in Gladstone coincides with the arrival in town of a wealthy magnate named Charles Morrison, who is vague about his reasons for spending time in a frontier outpost so far from his Guilded Age mansion. Then troubling news comes to light: an Apache renegade named Red Crow has traveled far from his usual haunts and taken to committing atrocities in the wilderness outside town.

Dunn, who has tangled with Red Crow in the past, organizes a posse to track down and eliminate Red Crow.

I won't disclose any spoilers, save to say that Red Crow is no minor adversary, and the posses success is by no means assuredand when Joe Dunn discovers the why and wherefore behind Red Crows depredations, he will find himself confronting men who will stop at nothing to gather wealth and power..

The plot of Streets of Glory is competent, if not particularly imaginative. The artwork, by Mike Wolfer, is pretty much the same story: competent, if not imaginative.

There is plenty of grue and gore revealed in the pages of Streets, enough to make it vie with Crossed in terms of gross-out quotient. If you're into splatterpunk then youll find Streets satisfies. However, someone looking for a more nuanced examination of Frontier Violence may wind up ill at ease.

The verdict ? Streets of Glory is a reasonably effective attempt by Ennis to do a Western comic. It doesnt break any new ground, save for its Gore Index, but its story and art are markedly superior to the other major contemporary Western title, DCs Loveless. Given the rarity of contemporary Western titles, Streets can be said to help keep the genre in some semblance of vitality.
profile.summary: 'Crossed' meets 'Pale Rider'

profile.description: 1990, mass market paperback reprint edition (of a work originally published in 1964), Collier, NY, 189 pages. Science fiction novel.
profile.reviewText:
`The Whole Man' was first published in 1964 as a fix-up of three stories Brunner published in the late 50s in sf magazines. The novel went through a number of reprintings, with various publishers, throughout the 60s and 70s.

The story opens in the near-future, in a city unnamed but probably London. The social order has collapsed; anarchists are detonating bombs, and food is scarce. UN forces are converging on the city to restore order. Amidst this unrest, a sickly, impoverished woman named Sarah Howson gives birth to  a male baby.

Gerald Howson is underweight, suffers from a clubbed foot, and a spinal malformation; as he matures he becomes a recluse in his rundown neighborhood. When his mother dies at an early age Gerald is left to fend for himself as best he can. But Gerald has a gift to offset his deformity; he can `hear' extraordinarily well. In fact, Gerald Howson is a telepath, perhaps the most gifted such being on the planet.

In due course Howson finds himself recruited into an elite unit of UN telepaths, stationed in Ulan Bator. The UN telepath unit is charged with using their abilities to control violence and conflict throughout the world. Gerald's talent enables him to do more than simply tap into the thoughts of others; he is able to enter into the intense dream state, or `catapathic trance', that can ensnare the too self-indulgent telepath.

When one of the UN's most important telepaths becomes caught in a catapathic trance, it's up to Gerald Howson to intrude upon the man's fantasy and restore sanity. But such a therapy is not without risk, for once inside his patient's daydream, Howson is vulnerable to the whims and decisions of his host; a false move, and Howson will find his own psyche fatally trapped within the selfsame trance.....

`Whole' is typical of Brunner's fix-ups from the late 60s - early 70s; a workmanlike effort, but devoid of the conscious effort he applied to newer works such as `The Shockwave Rider' and "The Sheep Look Up'. `Whole' suffers in part from its rather fragmented origins; the narrative thread linking the three main segments of the book is a bit thin.

There is not much in the way of real action in the novel; rather, it is a deliberately-paced character study of Gerald Howson's emotional journey from being a crippled outcast to the `whole man' of the book's title.

I suspect `The Whole Man' will really only appeal to Brunner completists and to those looking for the type of `inner space' - directed novel that came of age during the New Wave movement.
profile.summary: underwhelming mix of sf and humanism

profile.description: Drawing strongly on history, this intriguing story makes us fear for the future.
profile.reviewText:
This 1977 novel is a fast-paced and entertaining example of a 70's thriller, and worth picking up if you can find it in a used bookstore or rummage sale. The subject matter remains relevant to comtemporary audiences, particularly in the wake of the anthrax bioterror outbreak in the eastern US in the Fall 2001. "The Black Death" will appeal to the Robin Cook / Michael Crichton audience as well as anyone with an interest in medical thrillers.

The plot is straightforward: while vacationing in California, a teenage girl takes an up-close photograph of a wild rodent, and in so doing inhales the bacterium Yersinia pestis. She returns to New York City with a bad cough. But what she thinks is the flu is actually highly virulent pnemonic plague, and soon a hooker and an apartment building doorman are infected and coughing up bloody sputum.

City public health department director David Hart and his able nurse assistant Dolores Rodriguez must battle the indifference of the political and medical establishments in a desperate endeavor to contain the chain of transmission. If they fail, then New York City will become engulfed in an epidemic of plague (the medieval "Black Death" of the title) and thousands will die as civilization collapses around them.

The unique squalor of mid-70s New York, in late summer, is communicated very well and will no doubt evoke some nostalgic (if that's the right word) feelings in readers familiar with that era. The city swelters in suffocating heat, a strike by the sanitation union means the streets are filled with mounds of putrefying garbage, city finances are so decrepit that public services- such as rodent control- are barely functioning, and crime is rampant.

All of these problems combine to enhance the opportunities for plague transmission, and while not wishing to spoil the storyline, it's clear that things will get worse before they get better.

The authors show some skill in putting together a very readable and engrossing narrative while dropping medical and microbiological factoids to fill the reader in on the hows and whys of epidemiology and infectious disease control. Pneumonic plague is a fearsome condition and the arrival of what is usually an exotic and little-encountered disease in a modern metropolis is rendered with intensity and gruesome flavor.

The book does suffer from the inclusion of a sub-plot involving that 70's staple, the power-mad national security director. In this case it's a General Cosgrove, whose past history of covert actions and Cold-War paranoia leads him to regard the epidemic as an opportunity to seize control of the apparatus of government. The passages outlining this conspiracy are interspersed with the main storyline and tend to slow it down and distract the reader. While the narrative does drag a bit mid-way through the book, the last 20 or so pages pick up the pace and the story becomes more suspenseful. However, the novel's ending is abrupt and underdeveloped and shows signs of an editor's too-heavy hand, perhaps in regard to trimming the book's length.

Nonetheless, "The Black Death" satisfies as a well-written and well-plotted thriller best read on a warm summer afternoon.......to the accompaniment of traffic, jet planes flying overhead, sirens, and other city-associated noise...... and maybe the Rolling Stones' "Some Girls" album playing in the background............
profile.summary: An effective 70s-style medical thriller

profile.description: NY 1961 1st (stated) Dutton. 218pp. Near Fine in Good DJ, small bit of price tag stuck to rear.
profile.reviewText:
This 1976 Signet paperback is a Beach Read aimed at the same audience who religiously purchased Peter Benchley's `Jaws' a few years earlier. It combines the aquatic theme of `Jaws' with another staple of 70s Pop Culture, the eco-horror story (think `Frogs', `Squirm', `Phase IV', `Prophecy').

Things start off near the Florida Keys with a lethal attack on a cabin cruiser by a blue whale. Next, a Maine lobsterman gets pincered to death (?!) when the crustaceans he hauls up in his lobster pots are less than resigned to being cooked for dinner. Then, at the Delaware Shore, we learn that schools of  sea bass are coming into the shallows to deliberately bite some chunks from unsuspecting swimmers.

What is going on ?

Square-jawed science journalist Aran Holder decides to investigate. As the attacks grow in frequency and body count, it becomes disturbingly clear that an unprecedented phenomenon is taking place among the various creatures of the sea: united in a hatred of the depredations visited on the oceans by Man, they are launching a war against him...and their biggest weapon has yet to be revealed....

`Deadly Deep' is an adroit mix of pulp thrills, some `Day of the Dolphin' - style philosophizing,  just the right amount of grue, and - of course- swingin' 70s chicks in bikinis, short shorts, and halter tops. Author Messman knows he's not been commissioned to craft a great work of literature, but a readable novel designed for a sunny day at the shore.

Anyone looking for a dose of 70s eco-horror will be at home with `Deadly Deep'.

(note: an expanded version of this Review originally appeared at 'The PorPor Books Blog' in March 2010)
profile.summary: Enjoyable 70s eco-horror novel

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "Much more than your average dog treat, our artisanal jerky is crafted with slow smoked usa- raised country chicken and only 100% natural ingredients. Real jerky treat for dogs. Contains no fillers, wheat, corn, soy, by products, artificial colors or flavors, added fat, or added sugar. Proudly raised, grown and produced in America. Bring the ranch home.". The summary of the review text is "My very picky dog gobbles these up without hesitation".
output:
My tiny Chihuahua is a very picky eater.  She will refuse bacon or steak or cheese when she is not in the mood to eat.  But she doesn't refuse these Prairie Dog chicken jerky.  As soon as I open the bag her nose starts to twitch and she comes running.  She gobbles up the treats in seconds and starts dancing for more.  I have been making homemade jerky to give to my dog, but she actually likes this stuff better.  She is now refusing my homemade treats in the hopes of getting the Prairie Dog strips.  Ungrateful mutt.

And if you think the Prairie Dog is expensive, check out the Blue Buffalo Wilderness brand.  Their chicken jerky runs about $3+ and ounce or about $50 a pound.  Wow.

profile.description: Etta Says! Duck Jerky, From All Natural American Farms! These yummy Duck Jerkey treats will melt in yer mouth, so make sure your hoomans git plenty of em'. Tell your hooman that this Duck Jerky is made with whole Duck and preserved naturally, has no artificial fillers, coloring, preservatives, or by-products. I'm pure bred American dog, and 12 or so out of the 10 dogs I surveyed prefer home-grown treats. Paws down...imports stink! My treats are 100% natural. These treats are the perfect size for any pooch. Taste is in the tongue of the beholder. And I be holdin' the best treats this side of the Pacific!
profile.reviewText:
I have a VERY picky Chihuahua, and she gobbles these things up.

I used to buy her Waggin Train's Duck Jerky, but I threw the whole bag away after reading the negative reviews on consumer affairs.  I was hunting for a new duck jerky treat, when I found this brand.

They arrived quickly from Amazon, but when I opened the package I was a little startled.  I was expecting flat pieces of meat, but these are shaped like round, thin tubes.  They remind me of Pup-Peroni(which my dog won't eat).

But Peanut could care less about the shape, all she cares about is the great taste.  And all I care about is that they are made in the US, contain no grain, and are made from healthy stuff.

profile.reviewText:
I really enjoyed Season 1 of this TV show.  It was quirky, unique, and a lot of fun.  Parts of it were over-the-top, but it was funny in its outlandishness.  I finished watching the 10th episode, and was amazed that every story arc ended in a cliff-hanger.  What was going to happen to the people inside the bunker, and more important how were the people outside the bunker going to survive?  Is Jamie the Son of God, or is he a prophet like Moses (well Jamie did part the Thames).

After the last episode I went to find out when Season 2 would start, and much to my disappointment I discovered that the show had had been CANCELED.  There would be no Season 2.  The cliff-hangers would never be resolved.  If I had known that, I never would have watched the first season.

So now I am left with all these unanswered questions.  Maybe SyFi will pick it up and produce a Season 2.
profile.summary: Canceled  there will be no Season 2, and Season 1 ended with monumental cliff-hangers

profile.description: Pet the Hair Away! Great for all Dogs & Cats. Your pet will love the True Touch Five Finger Deshedding Glove! It mimics the loving touch of your hand for a relaxing massage and includes 180 soft silicone grooming tips to groom your pet with ease. The hair sticks to the glove, making it easy to peel and throw away. Minimize shedding and keep your house clean with the True Touch Deshedding Glove.
profile.reviewText:
I have to say that this glove works really well at gathering the loose hair from my long-haired Chihuahua.  I never considered her a shedder until I saw what accumulated on this glove after just a few minutes.  Her hair is white and apricot so it is very noticeable against the dark blue and black of the glove.  Most of the hair accumulated on the finger sections of the glove, and it was easy to clean the hair from the glove by just pulling on section loose and watching the rest of the hair mat follow.

But as much as I like the glove, my Chihuahua doesnt seem care for it.  When I gently stroke her body with the nubby, rubber tips of the glove she turns and gives me a hurt look.  Eventually she will squirm to get away.  So if you have a larger dog with a thick coat, the stroke of this glove might be soothing; but for a 4 lbs dog with long fine hair and sensitive skin, this glove is a little too rough.

profile.description: AmazonBasics brings you everyday items at a great value. An Amazon Brand.
profile.reviewText:
I have a long commuter van ride to work, and this pillow makes sleeping/relaxing in the van a little easier.  This pillow is large enough to support and cushion my back when I lean against the window, and it puffy enough to support my head when I snag a bench seat to myself and can lay down flat.

The pillow is made of an airtight vinyl fabric shell that is filled with quarter-sized pieces of foam.  The foam moves freely inside the fabric shell, so the shape of the pillow can be twisted and flatted to suite your needs. When you want to store the pillow you roll it into a tight tube which forces the air out of the bag and creates a vacuum inside, rolling up the pillow also compresses the foam pieces to a fraction of their normal size.  To inflate the pillow you open the air valve which allows air to flow into the pillow and also allows the foam pieces to expand from their compressed shape.  It takes a little strength to roll up the bag and force all the air out, but the inflation process is effortless.

The fabric used to make it pillow is nice.  It has a soft, slick feel that reminds me of microfiber.  The fabric is also semi-waterproof.  If water splashes on the fabric the water will bead and roll off, but if the water sits for more than a few seconds the fabric will absorb the water (but the fabric does dry quickly).

The only thing I don't like about the pillow is that the fabric makes these crinkling, plastic sounding noises when you touch it.  A noisy pillow is not an issue when it is being used in a creaky van barreling 80 mph down the highway, but if you are covertly trying to catch a few Zzzs in your cubicle at work, a noisy pillow is a dead giveaway.
profile.summary: Comfortable, but a little noisy  makes crinkling sounds when you touch it

profile.description: The Perfect Solution for Households with Pets.
profile.reviewText:
I was pleasantly surprised with the power and suction of this Dirt Devil Pet vacuum.  I have a small Chihuahua who likes to hide her dry kibbles/treats on the carpet and this vacuum had no trouble sucking up her hidden treasures.  The vacuum also did an excellent job picking up the hair.  I never knew she shed so much until I saw all the hair whirling around in the clear canister.  (With my previous bag vacuum the amount of hair was hidden from view.)

Things I like about the vacuum:

  Suction is great.  It had no trouble picking up dirt, hair, and cheerios.

  The Dirt Cup is easy to empty.

But there are a few things that I don't like about the vacuum.

  The vacuum requires a lot of assembly, and the instructions are missing some important steps.  Step 2 has you attaching the dirt cup, but my dirt cup just wouldn't stay attached.  Every time I attached it, it would fall off.  Finally I realized that I needed to install the filter and filter cover first and then attach the dirt cup.  The instructions never mentioned that part!  Step 4 is another "winner".  It has you securing the handle to the back panel of the vacuum using a long screw, but after attaching the handle to the body the "screw" has nothing to screw into!  The instructions forget to mention that there is another plastic doodad that straddles the handle and the front of the vacuum.  The screw gets inserted through the handle and back panel and INTO the plastic doodad.  I think Dirt Devil needs to spend a little more time and effort on the assembly instructions.

  The headlight is dim.  Half the time I can't even tell if it is on.

  The Pet Power Brush tool has a special clamp that allows you to store the attachment when not in use, but it keeps falling off.  The clamp is not strong enough to hold it in place when the vacuum is being pushed around.

  There is a little clamp on the handle that is supposed to hold the cord and keep it out of the way.  But like the Power Brush clamp is not strong enough and the cord keeps pulling free.

  The power cord and the hose are a little short.

  The On/Off pedal and the Handle Release Pedal feel a little flimsy.  I haven't had any problems with them yet, but I hold my breath every time I press them.

So this Dirt Devil has a few little flaws, but it excels in the most important feature: SUCTION.  This vacuum will pick up anything!
profile.summary: Good vacuum for the price, but takes a lot of assembly and assembly instructions are horrible

profile.description: DRP-SMSONWDSWSTORM
profile.reviewText:
The first thing I noticed with the headphones was of course the cool Star Wars insignia.  The emblems are made of thick, molded plastic, and the red color of the Galactic Empire contrasts nicely with the black of the ear cups and headband.  Very stylish and eye-catching.  Things like the stitching, lettering, screws and hinges show superior construction and a great attention to detail.

The second thing I noticed about the headphones was the heavy, pulsating waves of sound.  It really does feels like you are sitting right next to the subwoofer.  If you crank up the volume you can literally feel the vibrations from your eyeballs to your toes.  Try it with Shinedowns Boom-Lay, Boom-Lay, Boom to see what I mean.  Overall it has a good clean sound, but be aware that it is heavy on the low frequencies, and lighter on the mid and higher frequencies.  Great for Rock with lots of bass, not so great for opera.

Comfort-wise the headphones are better than most.  On my head the fit is not too snug or too loose.  The memory foam that covers the ear cups and headband is soft and pillowy, and the faux leather that covers the foam is soft and supple.  With my glasses on I can wear the headphones for about 30 minutes without discomfort, but without my glasses I can wear them comfortably for hours.  The only comfort issue I had with the headphones was the placement of the Mic: I found it a bit too high on the cord.  And because the headphone don't have a Bluetooth option, a little longer cord would also be nice.

If you travel a lot these headphones are an ideal companion.  They fold up into a compact shape that won't take up too much room, and the semi-rigid casing case will protect them from bumps and bruises.  They do an okay job of canceling out normal background noise, but don't expect too much.  In a busy airport or crowded plane you will still hear everything going on around you.

So all-in-all the SMS Audio STREET is one of the best headphones Ive tried, and if you are a Star Wars fan they are a must have item to add to your collection.
profile.summary: Heavy on the bass, can feel the beat down to your toes

profile.reviewText:
In this world of vacuums that are laser guided, app controlled, and Wi-Fi enabled, it is nice to find a low-tech version that works just as well.  And this Fuller Sweeper works amazingly well.  I used it on tile, hardwood, an area rug, and high pile carpet and it picked up every speck of dirt I saw.  It also picked up a lot of stuff I didn't see.  When I emptied the dirt bin (which opens and dumps with just a push of your finger), clumps of dog hair fell out.  Now I had just used my Neato the day before so either this thing does a better job than my $400 robot vacuum or my 4 lb. Chihuahua is losing all her hair.

Other things I like about the sweeper are its lightness and its maneuverability.  It can slip under furniture, maneuver around table legs, and get into corners with its little edges brushes.  It is also unobtrusive.  I can stand it in the living room behind a plant and no one ever sees it.  I like having it handy so I can pick up the dust bunnies when I see them and not allow them time to escape and multiple.

And of course it quite.  The rollers do make a swooshing noise as you push it across the floor, but nothing obnoxious like the whine of a powered vacuum.  The Fuller will be great during parties when you want to sweep up a (dry) mess but don't want to disturb your guest.

So I love my little Fuller Carpet Sweeper.  It won't replace my regular vacuum for deep carpet cleaning, but it is an amazing tool for picking up small messes.

The set includes every single item you will ever need to bake anything.
profile.reviewText:
I love baking in silicone bundt and loaf pans, so I decided to give this Sorbus set as a house warming gift.  The set is a fantastic bargain at 29.99 for 8 individual molds. ( I actually got 9 mold in my set.  There was also a waffle mold.)  But the one thing that disappointed me was that the set had absolutely no labels, directions, or instructions anywhere on the molds, packaging or in the box.  I thought about printing the Amazon product page and including that with the gift, but decided that would look too tacky. The pans themselves were sealed in plastic bags; sometimes with multiple molds folded and stuffed into a single bag.  The set just didn't look attractive enough to give as a gift.

I was so concerned about not having any instructions on the pans that I bought another cupcake mold from a different manufacture to add to the gift.  This pan came in a cardboard box that was covered with instructions/information on maximum cooking temperature, cleaning instructions, storage instructions, different ways you could use the pans, and info on safety of the silicone for cooking.

I also liked the second cupcake mold better than the Sorbus mold.  It was a little thicker and felt sturdy.  The Sorbus mold felt floppier.  Because I kept the Sorbus pan I had to try it out, and sure enough once I filled the floppy Sorbus cupcake mold with batter I wasn't able to lift the mold without is bending in the middle and dumping the batter out.  I had to place the cupcake mold on a cookie tray to get in into the oven.  Ive never used a silicone cupcake mold before, just bundt molds; is this normal?  (Note: the other molds in the set were much sturdier than the cupcake and mini muffin mold.)

Anyway after I baked the cupcake they easily popped out of the silicon pan, but I found that the bottoms had burned. The sides were fine, so I guess the contact with the cookie sheet made the bottoms of the cupcakes burn.  I guess I need to use a cooking/cooling rack instead of a cookie sheet.

So this Sorbus set is a good bargain and a great purchase if you want to keep them for yourself, but I don't think it is packaged well enough to give as a gift.  Also, think about buying a baking rack to help transport the molds to and from the oven.

3) The biggest issue that I have with the knife is the placement of the power button. During the time it took me to slice a 10 lb roast I had to switch from my left to my right hand several times to give my thumb a rest.  I do have "texter's thumbs" so maybe the placement of the button wouldnt be a problem for someone with healthy fingers.  In hindsight I guess I should have looked for a knife with a trigger style power button instead of a button on the top.  My bad.

So this is an okay electric knife as long as you don't have arthritis in your thumbs.
profile.summary: Works okay, but a little heavy, and placement of power button causes thumb fatigue

profile.description: Say 'Cheers' with something sweet. Make cookie shot glasses using this non-stick pan. Just fill the 6 cavities with cookie dough, press the inserts in and bake. After the cookie cups have cooled, coat the inside with your favorite flavor or color of Candy Melts Candy, then fill with mousse, ice cream or milk. Includes one 6 cavity pan with 6 inserts.
profile.reviewText:
Well I cant say that I had a whole lot of success with this Sweet Shooters cookie pan, but knowing what I know now I think my second attempt will look better.

Tip #1: you really need to follow the recipe provided and use mini chocolate chips.  I just used regular sized chips and I think the chips kept the plunger/insert part of the pan from centering correctly.  Because the plunger was not centered, the sides did not bake to an even thickness.  And because sections of the cookie shooters were very thin, some of the cookies broke apart when I tried to twist them out of the pan.

Tip #2:  Two tablespoons wasn't enough dough to fill up the cavity.  When I pushed the plunger/insert down, the cookie dough did come out the top like it is shown in the picture.  I will try 3 tablespoons next time.

Tip #3:  When you force the plunger/insert into the cookie dough that is filling the cavity make sure the plunger goes STRAIGHT down.  If it is a little off center the walls of the finished cookie shooter will not be uniform which will cause problems when you try to remove the finished cookies.

Tip #4:  Dont force the plunger all the way to the bottom.  I think I forced it down too much which caused the hole to form at the bottom of all my finished cookie.

Tip #5:  Put something heavy on top the pan to keep the plunger/insert from floating up during baking???  While I was baking the cookies, the plunger floated half way out of the cavity.  About 12 minutes into the baking time I had to reach into the hot oven and pushed the plunger back into the cavity.  Next time I might put a little baking pan on top of the plungers to keep them in place.

Tip #6:  The tops of my cookies came out very messy and ragged looking.  Dont know what would help this problem other than more cookie dough.

Tip #7: Make sure you grease the pan very, very well.  I sprayed the pan with cooking oil, but I still had trouble getting the cookies out. One cookie completely crumbled, and a second cookie shooter lost its bottom when I pulled it out.  I will use solid shortening next time.

Another issue with the pan is the way the directions/instructions were presented.  There are some instructions printed on the back on the box, but the most important instructions about how to prep and use the pan are buried in the chocolate chip cookie recipe that is printed on a small slip of paper.  It would be nice to have all the instructions on the back of the box.

So these Sweet Shooters are a cute idea, but it is going to take me a few tries to get the technique perfected.
profile.summary: First attempt was a flop, but I learned a lot so next attempt should look better

I like these poop bags.  They are bigger, thicker, stronger and actually less expensive than the bags I have been using.  The scent is nice too; very subtle with just a hint of citrus.  The bags open easily without having to do that annoying two minutes of rubbing to get the two side apart, and I haven't found any bags where the bottom edge wasn't sealed. profile.description: A true trend-setter! Cut this cake to find a surprise of hidden treasures inside. The special insert allows you to bake a hollow center cake. Cool and fill the center cavity with assorted candies, cookies or other treats and "glue" the halves together with frosting. Let your imagination run wild to create animals, sports balls, celestial bodies, faces and more! Make birthday cakes or baby shower "reveal" cakes with blue or pink inside. A Nordic Ware exclusive and the only pan of its kind. Proudly made in the USA.
profile.reviewText:
I bake a lot (and have experienced a lot of baking mishaps over the years) but this cake pan/cake had me crying in frustration.  But in the end the cake turned out so cute I decided not to stomp on the pan and throw it in the trash.

Lessons learned:

1) DON'T OVERFILL - The instructions say you can use a box mix with the pan, filling the pan 3/4 full.  I used a 16oz Ducan Hines mix and thought the pan looked 3/4 full, but apparently not because as the cake baked the semi-liquid batter rose up and spilled into the inverted dome of the pan.  I actually had to take the half-baked cake out of the oven and scoop the raw batter out of the dome.  What a mess.

2) DON'T OVERFILL Part 2 - For the second cake I removed one cup of the batter before pouring into the cake pan.  The batter was barely touching the bottom of the inverted dome, but I still had a little batter spill into the dome while baking. Guess with this particular brand of cake mix I need to remove 1-1/2 cups of batter.

3) DON'T  UNDER FILL - If you under fill the cake pan with batter the cakes will not be the same size.  Ideally you want the cake to puff up enough to cover the slats that hold the dome to the main pan.  You will need to cut the extra cake off the slats before you can turn the slats and remove the dome, but this ensures that both cake halves are the same size.

4) CANDY YOU PUT INSIDE DOES MATTER - I filled my cake with gummy worms.  In hind-sight this was not the best choice.  It was impossible to cut through the gummy worms.  So select candy that a knife can push aside while cutting.

5) USE A DENSE CAKE MIX - LIKE POUND CAKE - The biggest problem I had with the cake was structural.  After frosting the cake I noticed that the shape was changing.  It was flattening and looking less and less like a rounded ball.  I thought it was my imagination so I keep going with my decorating.  But soon I noticed a split in the base cake.  I tried to fill the gap with icing and hold it together with wooden skewers, but the cake kept splitting.  Finally I took a long piece of plastic wrap, cut it into a ribbon shape, tightly tied the ribbon around the base of the cake, and stuck it in the refrigerator.  This chilled the cake and stopped it from splitting more, and I was able to finish decorating the cake.  So the moral is: don't use a light and fluffy boxed cake mix.  You need something dense and heavy enough to hold the weight of the cake, the candy, and the decorations.  A dense pound cake would be the best.

6) BAKE AND EAT ON THE SAME DAY - The instructions included with the pan advise to bake and eat the cake on the same day.  At first I didn't understand this recommendation, but after watching my cake slowly deflate I understood the warning.  The inside of the cake is hollow.  Sure you fill the cavity with a little bit of candy, but the candy does not provide any support for the cake.  So every hour that the assembled cake sits, the sides will spread and the top will flatten.  My cake looked like a soccer ball slowly losing air.  And when you cut the cake the sinking problem accelerates.  So bake, decorate, and eat the puppy fast.

So this cake pan is a cute concept, but it is not a simple pan to use.  It takes a bit of thought, planning, and trial-and-error.
profile.summary: Had a lot of "Problems" the first time, but cake turned out well in the end

profile.description: 31334HB Features: -Includes bake pan and broil rack with 2 rack positions. -Easy Reach collection. -Removable roll-top door for easy cleanup. -Capacity: 4 Slice. Product Type: -Toaster oven. Finish: -Gray. Number of Slices: -4. Dimensions: Overall Height - Top to Bottom: -8.97 Inches. Overall Width - Side to Side: -16.12 Inches. Overall Depth - Front to Back: -11.93 Inches.
profile.reviewText:
I have been using this HB Toaster Oven for a few weeks, and like most things it has it pros and cons.  It works well for toasting and heating up small items, but it can't "bake" things like cupcakes.  The exterior of the unit gets very, very hot, and the mechanical timer is ridiculously noisy.

Pros:

&#10004 The unit heats up quickly, and does a nice job of toasting and warming food.  Can also bake those refrigerated slice & bake cookies.

&#10004  The roll top cover is surprisingly functional.  Having the top roll back and disappear into the oven make it easy to access your food, and the unique design is also a lot safer because (unlike other toaster ovens) you don't have to reach over the hot, open door to access your food.

&#10004 The unit is easy to clean.

Cons:

&#10008 The mechanical controls on this HB Toaster Oven are imprecise, noisy, and a pain to use.  To toast a piece of bread you must turn the knob past the 10 minute mark and then back to the desired toast darkness.  Unlike a regular toaster there is no "preset" darkness available, so your toast comes out different each time.

&#10008 The mechanical timer dial is very, very noisy.  Drive you crazy loud.  The instruction manual advises you to unplug the toaster oven after each use, but even if you unplug the unit, the timer keeps ticking until it winds down (or until you turn the knob to shut the timer off manually).

&#10008 Doesn't bake cakes/cupcakes/muffins very well.  I tried baking some mini cakes and muffins in the toaster oven and they did not come out very well.  The tops were burnt and the inside was gooey.

&#10008 The exterior of the unit gets very, very hot.  Hot enough to burn skin.

&#10008 After closing the roll top cover a tight seal is not formed between the closed roll top cover and the main body of the unit.  When closed there are several visible gaps between top and the rest of the unit.  A lot of heat escapes from these gaps which contribute to the elevated temperature around the toaster oven.

&#10008 The inside dimensions of the unit are very tight so there is not much room between the oven rack and the crumb try. This tight fit makes it almost impossible to use an oven mitt to pull the rack out of the oven.  I ended up using a fork to grab the rack and pull it out.

&#10008 The tight fit also makes it dangerous to reach into the unit to turn your warming food.  The narrow opening between the rack and the upper heating element is an accident waiting to happen.

So despite a few flaws, if your kitchen is short on space (and you don't mind the sound of ticking timers) this toaster oven would be a good fit.
profile.summary: Ticking of the mechanical timer is very loud

profile.description: Apple iPhone 6S 64GB Verizon - Factory Unlocked - Rose Gold. Grade A condition with little to no wear on housing and screen. Comes with device, box, head set, charger and wall adapter. No other accessories are included. IMEI has been cleared with Verizon and is factory unlocked.
profile.reviewText:
I upgraded from a 4S, so the 6S is a major improvement.  The screen quality is amazing, the camera is super, and the battery life is so much better.  The 6Ss case is smooth, sleek, and light weight.  It makes my 4S look like a hockey puck.  I haven't seen much use for the Force Touch yet, but Im sure the apps will start incorporating the feature.

But my problem with the phone is the Home Button.  It sporadically gets hot and I mean burning hot.  When the button heats up the screen goes black and the phone shuts itself off.  The only way to get the phone to respond is a hard boot (press the Home and Power buttons at the same time for 10 seconds).  I contacted Apple and they said to stop using the phone and they would contact me about a replacement or a repair.  But what really worries me that they asked if anything else was damaged due to heat/sparks/flames coming from the phone.  They also asked if I had to seek medical attention for burns.  Yikes.  At the very least this problem stops my morning alarm from going off, and at the worst is could catch something on fire.

Update:  Apple sent me a new phone.  There are all kinds of theories floating around the web as to what is cause this problem, but my lowly opinion is a faulty ID sensor.
profile.summary: Beware of a burning hot Home Button and the black screen of death (as opposed to MicroSofts blue screen of death)

profile.reviewText:
This Cuisinart Ceramic Glazed pizza stone works fine for fresh pizza.  The crust bakes evenly and the top, bottom and side get a nice, even brown crust.  Cutting the pizza directly on the stone doesnt damage the glazed surface, and cleanup is very easy.  I have several Pampered Chef stones and the cleaning the Cuisinart stone is definitely easier.  The Cuisinart also doesnt stain and discolor like the regular clay stones.

But (and this is a big but) I don't like baking cookies and scones on the Cuisinart stone.  The smooth, slick surface of the glaze causes the baked items to spread much more than on the rougher surface of the PC stone.  I made a batch of scones and baked half on the Cuisinart and half on my old stone, and the Cuisinart baked scones were noticeably flatter and more spread out. So Cuisinart stone works great for pizza, but I don't like how it causes my scones and cookies to spread and flatten.

profile.description: Neato Botvac
profile.reviewText:
I loved my first robotic vacuum, a Neato XV, but unfortunately the refurbished unit I purchased only lasted 18 months.  But now Im glad it conked out because this new Neato Botvac Connected is so much better.  The suction is better, the dust bin is larger, and it doesnt get stuck under the furniture.  I also like the little brush on the side of the unit which helps to clean the shoe molding and corners of hard surface floors.  If you are interested, this CNet report gives some interesting stats on the various robotic vacuums: http://www.cnet.com/products/neato-botvac-connected-robot-vacuum/2/

Im a little embarrassed to say the setup of the Botvacs WiFi took me a few tries.  I couldn't get the Neato to connect to the WiFi and the App until I gave the Neato a name.  I didn't really care about personalizing it, the default name of Neato was fine with me, but the connection process wouldnt work until I changed the machines name.  So I called it Gizmo, and once the thing had a name the WiFi setup continued without a hitch.

After setup I set Gizmo loose to clean, and it ran, and ran, and ran.  It took it about 1-1/2 hours but it did clean about 1800 sq ft of hard surface/rug covered floor.  I had it set to Turbo and while it was a little noisy, we still managed to watch TV while it cleaned under our feet.  I was also impressed that it didn't get trapped anywhere.  My old Neato always got stuck under the sofa and I would have to constantly fish him out.  The new Neato Botvac doesnt get stuck under the furniture but it has accidentally closed doors and gotten trapped in bathrooms and bedroom closets.

So cleaning the tile and hardwood floors I put Gizmo in the carpeted bedrooms.  The carpet is a mid-pile shaggy style and the Neato had no problem traversing the room.  Every inch of the carpet showed track marks proving that Gizmo had passed that way.  And I really, really like the notifications sent to my phone when Gizmo is finished cleaning.  This is very handy, because I usually don't let the Neato run on its own.  I always pick it up and place it in the room I want cleaned.  With the App I can be sitting/working in another room and get a notice on my phone when Gizmo is finished.

Like the old Neato, cleaning out the dust bin on the Neato Botvac is simple.  Just pull the filter off the over-sized bin and all the gunk just falls out.  And to remove the stuff from the filter itself I simply tap it on the cement driveway outside.

The App that comes with the Neato Connected is also nice.  The ability to start and stop the unit is handy, and the option to control its movements and direction is wonderful.  With the old Neato trying to get it to clean a spot to my liking was almost impossible.  With the Connected unit and the remote control I can get it to vacuum the same spot a hundred times if I think it is needed.

So I really do love this vacuum.  Each year the robotic vacuums seem to get better and better.  Better suction, better handling, better battery life.  But I still have one pie-in-the-sky feature that I want added -- I would like the App to show me a map of my house and let me mark on the App the areas of the house that I want it to clean and the areas I want it to avoid.  Maybe that will be in the next version of the Neato.

Update 12/26/2015  I went to use my Neato and it was dead!  Oh no!  And I couldn't get the thing to charge.  I pulled and pushed it onto the base a hundred times and it would not charge.  Wi-Fi was off, time was set back to 12:00, and it kept telling me the battery was low.  But then I remember I had switched off the LED option.  I had turned the LED option off because I didn't like the constant glow of the two square lights (they looked like eyes glowing in the dark).  But apparently Neato doesnt like its eyes turned off, because as soon as I turned the LED option back on, the unit started to charge again.  I will have to experiment some more and see if it was just a fluke.
profile.summary: Neato Botvac works even better than my old Neato XV

profile.description: Each piece of Lagostina cookware represents quintessential Italian culture. Celebration of food, life, family and friends. Of memorable gatherings around the table. Of spirited conversation. Since 1901, Lagostina' s core values of impeccable Italian craftsmanship, high-quality materials, technological innovation and elegant design have endured. Today, as Italy's premium cookware brand, we continue to stand behind these core values with a lifetime guarantee. The set includes 8-Inch Skillet, 10-Inch Skillet, 12-Inch Skillet, 1-Quart Covered Saucepan, 2-Quart Covered Saucepan, 3-Quart Covered Saucepan, 3-Quart Covered Deep Saut Pan, 6-Quart Covered Stockpot.
profile.reviewText:
This Lagostina set is my first experience with stainless steel cookware, and I have to say I've been extremely happy so far.  I've been using the set for about two weeks and I can't think of one negative thing to say about them (which is unusual for me).  I have lots of positive things to wax on about, but by far the best thing about the cookware is that is doesn't have a long list of "dont" associated with it.  With all the different kinds of pot, pans, skillets and stones I have in my house it is difficult remembering what I can and can't do with each one.  But this Lagostina cookware can handle just about anything: dishwasher, metal utensils, induction cooktops, oven, refrigerator, etc.  Using the Lagostina is stress and worry free.

So onto the Pros:

First off the set is beautiful.  It is shiny and polished, and the "Lagostina" logo engraved in the handle looks very classy.  The pots/pans/covers have a brushed steel look and the handles are polished almost to a mirror finish.  Very nice.

The first meal I cooked in a Lagostina pot was Shrimp Creole.  On my electric cooktop the pot heated quickly and evenly.  No hot spots developed and there was no sticking of the roux to the bottom of the pot.  And one of my favorite things about the pot was that even though the sauce inside was boiling, THE LONG HANDLE DID NOT GET HOT.  Yes, I know I'm shouting but I was so happy to find that I could hold the pot by the handle without having to use a towel or oven mitt.  Even the small handle on the lid stayed cool enough to touch.  The lid handle does get a little hotter than the long handle on the pot, but not hot enough to need protection.

Stainless steel is not good at radiating heat so stainless pots must have a copper or aluminum core to ensure even cooking.  The Lagostina have an aluminum core, and the aluminum covers the bottom of the pan.  I haven't been able to find out if the aluminum core goes up the side of the pan too, but I haven't had and problem with food sticking to the sides so I guess it is not a big issue.

Cleanup was easy and stress-free with these pots and pans.  I did notice that the red sauce from the Shrimp Creole caused discoloration of the pot.  Hand washing did not remove the spots, but a cycle in the dishwasher had the pot looking bright and shiny again.  The fact that the pots and pans are dishwasher safe is a major plus.  I cant do that with my Magnalite, my Teflon, my enamel clad, or my cast iron.  The fact that I can safely put the Lagostina in the dishwasher is a major selling feature in my mind.  Not so much to get the pot clean (I always pre-wash anyway), but just to get rid of the spots and stains.

In my next test I boiled some water.  Again those spots showed up on the stainless steel, but the dishwasher made them vanish.

Next I scrambled some eggs.  I read that there are issues with food sticking to stainless steel pans, but I didn't have any major problems.  Yes the eggs did stick a bit, but nothing that a plastic scouring sponge didn't whisk away.  Although I did follow an internet tip and heated the pan before I oiled it.  Supposedly heating the pan first causes it to expand and close the microscopic pores in the steel.  If you add oil/food to a cold pan the food can get trapped in the pores as the metal starts to expands which in-turn cause the sticking.  Dont know if this is true.  Will have to do more testing.

Lagostina states on the box that high grade stainless maintains the purity of flavors, but after cooking a few of my standard dishes I haven't noticed that cooking with stainless steel pots makes my food taste any better/different than food cooked in my Magnalite pots.

Cons:

As I mentioned earlier, so far I haven't found and cons or problems with these Lagostina pots.  Although I do wish that they would have put the dual handles on the 3 Qt sauce pan.  When it is full, the3 Qt  pot is too heavy to lift with just the long handle.

So I'm loving my Lagostina pots, and they have quickly become my cookware of choice.  I automatically reach for them now, and my poor Magnalite pots have started to collect dust.
profile.summary: I've fallen in love with these Lagostina Stainless Steel pots and pans

profile.description: Tailored light blue stripes subtly decorate the Simply Fine Chirp Blue Stripe Platter. Accenting the stripes of this generously sized platter are the bright watercolor brushstrokes of two floral branches. Crafted of gleaming white fine china, this beautiful dinnerware serving piece is also dishwasher, microwave, freezer, and oven safe, and guaranteed chip resistant. Wonderful for any table setting, both formal and casual.
profile.reviewText:
I really like this updated Lenox Chirp design.  It is colorful without being too bold, detailed without being too ornate.  It has both birds and flower, yet it is not frilly or fussy looking.  The design works great in either a formal or casual setting, and while the design has a definite Spring/Summer feel, they would still look great at a Christmas or Thanksgiving dinner if paired with solid plates.

The Chirp design has been around for years, but this updated setting has pale blue lines that edge the large dinner plate, bowl and cup.  I really like the blue stripes a lot better than the solid aqua or solid red on the previous versions.  The stripes make the design look crisp and clean, and somehow airy; like the birds could actually lift up the plate and carrying it off.

Size-wise the dinner plate is nice a large, and can hold lots of food.  But be aware that the plate is mostly flat with only a slight depression in the center.  This plate would not be ideal for serving foods with a loose sauce or gravy; one wrong move and the sauce would go sloshing off the side.  The bowl in the set is nice and deep and the perfect size for cereal or the soup course of a meal. (Bowl is not big enough if soup is the meal!)  The cup/mug is a little small for my use.  It is more like a petite tea cup than a coffee mug. The salad plate on the other hand is a little large (although it would be a nice dinner plate for a child).  I would prefer the set come with a smaller plate that could be used for bread or dessert.

The quality of the pieces is great.  The painted design has a slightly raised feel, but nothing too noticeable.  The finish on the plate is silky smooth without any bumps in the glaze or china.  The plates are light too.  My old plates are heavy ceramic, so the Lenox plate feels like a feather in comparison.  The cups seem very durable too.  I accidentally dropped the cup on the living room rug while unpacking and the cup didn't chip or break!

So this blue stripped Chirp is a lovely, lovely pattern. Bright, cheerful, and perfect for any occasion.
profile.summary: The blue stripped Chirp is a lovely, lovely pattern. Bright, cheerful, and perfect for any occasion

profile.description: Frigidaire Gallery Series: FGMV154CLF 1.5 cu. ft. Over-the-Range Convection Microwave Oven with 900 Cooking Watts, 2-Speed 300 CFM Exhaust Fan, Sensor Cooking, Glass Turntable and Convection Cooking Rack: Stainless Steel
profile.reviewText:
This microwave came preinstalled in the new home I just purchased. It looks stylish and very high-end, but if I microwave something with a lot of moisture (like a baked potato) steam constantly spews from the microwaves top vent. I don't mind the steam, but the placement of the vents at the top of the microwave forces all the hot air and moisture straight up and onto the overhead cabinet. The stem is causing the veneer on the cabinet to discolor and peel. I contacted the contractor who installed the microwave and he said everything was installed correctly. Not sure what to do to fix this problem. In the mean time Ive resorted to opening the doors of the overhead cabinet before I start the microwave.

So beware of venting this microwave from the top. It just might end up destroying your cabinets.

Also, be aware that the microwave door fogs up when microwaving high moisture food. It can take an hour for the fog in the door to dissipate, and looks very unsightly.

Update:  After three visits from the service company, it was decided that something was wrong with the microwave.  The repairman actually cautioned me not to use the microwave because it was a fire hazard.  After waiting a few weeks (thankfully I had another microwave) the new microwave was delivered and installed.  And amazingly this one works.  The door doesnt fog up,  and the steam coming out of the top vent was reduced by about 75%.  There is still a little steam, but nothing that would seriously damage the overhead cabinet.

So if the door of your Frigidaire Gallery is fogging up or excessive steam is coming out of the vents Get it replaced, pronto.
profile.summary: Door fogs up. Heat and steam from the microwaves top vent is warping my cabinet

profile.description: These professional polycarbonate candy/chocolate molds are made from extremely durable and rigid material designed to leave a professional gloss to all candy and chocolate. Made from BPA free polycarbonate
profile.reviewText:
I just started making chocolate from bean-to-bar, and I have tried a variety of molds. This polycarbonate mold was the best of the bunch.  The mold is very rigid plastic so it doesnt bend when you fill with chocolate or tap the mold on a hard surface.  The chocolate pops out with a nice sheen and doesnt have any of those contraction rings on the surface of the chocolate.

Also be aware that the molds are small.  Each cavity holds about 3/4 - 1 oz of chocolate (depending on how close to the top you fill the cavity), and its length and width is a little larger than my finger.  But the molds make the perfect sized chocolate bar for tasting events.  The segments of the bar easily break apart, so one bar is enough for six people to sample.
profile.summary: Finished bar is about 1oz and a little longer and wider than a finger - great size for tasting

profile.description: Walk with pride in the womens Allrounder by Mephisto Nimbo Rivets mary jane. Featuring water-resistant leather upper, this elegant mary jane features Velcro closure that gives a customized fit. Its superior synthetic lining offers excellent comfort. There is a removable synthetic insole that massages your foot gently. Finally, this mary jane has a rubber/TPU outsole that offers exceptional grip. Grab the womens Allrounder by Mephisto Nimbo Rivets mary jane for its excellent craftsmanship and unique design.
profile.reviewText:
Due to problems with bunions I have been searching for some new shoes that give me better arch support and more room in the toe box.  I was scouring the clearance rack at a local shoe store when I found these Allrounders.  I had never heard of Mephisto before and I was shocked at the original price, but at 85% off they were a steal.  Best of all the fit was perfect.  The toe box was roomy, there was plenty of arch support, and the cushion insoles felt great.  The shape of the rubber soles also forces my weight forward and keeps me from putting too much weigh on my heels.

My only complaint with the shoe is I find the Velcro strap across the top of my foot is a little high which causes it to rub slightly against my ankle.  Im going to wear them at work and since I sit most of the day the rubbing won't be a problem, but if I had to walk long distances in these shoes I think the strap would eventually give me a blister.
