profile.description: Don't let the size of this CorningWare Dutch oven fool you; it's lightweight so you can effortlessly carry it from the kitchen to the table. Plus, it has ergonomic handles that are easy to grasp. With its French White styling, the Dutch oven will be a beautiful addition to any table setting. The clear glass lid allows you to keep an eye on your favorite recipe.
profile.reviewText:
I have to say that this CorningWare Cast Aluminum Dutch Oven looks gorgeous.  The fluted lines are elegant, and the cover, with its mix of glass and shiny chrome, is very classy.  It is also very easy to clean (nothing sticks), and the Braised Herb Chicken that I cooked in the pot came out wonderfully moist and delicious.

BUT if you scrutinize the bottom of the box your will find a LONG, LONG list of Dos and Donts that you must follow (and remember) if you want to keep yourself and the pot safe.  I read the warnings (honestly I did), but I still managed to harm the cover of my pretty new Dutch Oven.  The meal I was cooking said to bring the contents of the pot to a boil and then cover and lower heat to a simmer.  But as soon as I put the glass cover on the pot of still boiling liquid, the glass cover started to pop.  The pops were not very loud, but they were noticeable and somewhat alarming.  After the temperature of the glass cover equalized with the contents in the pot, the popping noise stopped.

After about 30 minutes of simmering I removed the hot cover and placed it on heat-resistance glass trivet.  As soon as the two touched, the glass cover started to pop and then made a cracking noise that I was sure would shatter the glass.  I backed away and let the cover cool.  Later when I inspected it I didn't find any cracks in the glass, but I did find some hairline fractures in the aluminum edge that rings the cover.  The fractures were all clustered near the production seam/join in the aluminum ring.  I can only guess that the thermal shock of placing the hot glass cover on the glass trivet caused the seam to somehow expand and fracture.

I re-read the instructions and this statement jumped out and slapped me in the face, "Do not handle hot glass covers with damp or wet cloth/potholder or put on a cool or wet surface."  Wow, that is really strict.  When I'm cooking every cloth and potholder ends up damp, and every surface when compared to the hot cover is "cool".  And once you place the hot cover on any surface, the moisture will transfer from the hot cover to the surface thereby making the formerly dry surface wet!  Help!!  What am I supposed to do with the hot cover when I take it off the pot?  Hold it in my hand until it cools?  I have other aluminum and glass pot covers and never had a problem with thermal shock before.

But this CorningWare Dutch Oven is just too pretty to give up on, so I will have to experiment and find a way to keep the cover safe.  I will also need to print out a copy of the Safety and Usage Instructions.  A few years down the road I know I'm not going to remember all those rules.  Especially the weird one about salt (see below), and the fact that you can't put it in the dishwasher.

Below is a partial list of the Safety and Usage Instructions from the bottom of the box:

 Never let cookware boil dry or use on high heat.
 Handles and knobs may get hot.  Always use potholders.
 DO NOT use cookware under a broiler, in a microwave oven, on inductions stoves, gas grills, or over a campfire.
 Do not place glass covers directly on range top burner, under a broiler or microwave browning element, or near any direct heat sources.
 Do not handle hot glass covers with damp or wet cloth/potholder or put on a cool or wet surface.
 Match cookware to burner size and adjust burner so heat does not extend up side of plan.
 To prevent scratching use heat resistant plastic, nylon or wooden cooking utensils or non-stick ceramic finish.
 Avoid using sharp-edged or metal utensils.
 Care: Hand wash only.
 To prevent warping let cookware cool before coming into contact with water.
 To remove burned on food, soak before cleaning and scrub with a plastic scouring pad.
 Do Not use abrasive scouring powders, pads or steel wool.
 Thoroughly wash pan after each use.  Use hot soapy water to avoid staining caused by food or grease residue buildup.
 Avoid long-term storage with foods.
 Some foods and salt can "pit" the surfaces and make it difficult to clean.
 Add salt to liquid only after it reaches the boiling point, and stir to dissolve completely.
 Use of high heat may cause food to stick.

** Update 5/6/2015 **
I've come to the realization that it doesn't matter one iota that I can't put this Dutch Oven in the dishwasher.  Last night I burned a pork roast in this pot... It was my own fault I didn't have enough liquid in the pot and I wasn't paying attention. Anyway I pulled the pork roast out before it was ruined, but the bottom of the pot was covered in black, charred on crud. It looked really, really bad, but after the pot cooled I soaked in in water and all the crud simply floated away. I didn't even have to scrub the pot. Just rinsed it off and it was absolutely clean. Really amazing.

The popping noise that the cover makes as it heats and cools still scares me, but I can live with the noise if the cleanup is that easy.

** Update: 5/31/15 **
Made some French Bread in the dutch oven.  It came out great, but the lid is still popping like crazy.
profile.summary: Long list of  Do's and Don'ts associated with this Cookware  also, when heated, the glass cover pops alarmingly

profile.description: Scrunch soft storage organizes and stows toys to blankets and more! Concealing or corraling has never been so easy. Some times you need storage, some times you don't. Pop for use, scrunch to store.
profile.reviewText:
At first glance I loved the way the Utility bin looked.  The color and texture looked classy and stylish.  I filled it with lots of stuff (remotes, magazines, kindle, pad & ink pen, etc), and put it in the living room.  But the room is very sunny and I noticed that I could actually see through the fabric of the bin and see the shapes of everything inside (see picture).  I figured something that thin would be easy to puncture, and sure enough when I looked closely at the bin I found several holes where things inside the bin had punctured the fabric.

So this utility bin would be great to hold soft, non-pointy items, things like magazines, linens, clothing.  But don't put anything sharp or angular inside or you will risk ripping the fabric.
profile.summary: Looks good from a distance, but very thin and translucent up close.  Easy to puncture.

profile.description: Trail running and photography. Mountain biking and photography. Snowboarding and photography. Adventure sport athletes who like to go fast and light - but equally like to capture the moment - will enjoy the freedom and comfort of this pack.
profile.reviewText:
This is a wonderful backpack for day hikes, or sightseeing.  It is sturdy and very well-made.  The straps are wide and comfortable and don't dig into your flesh even when you have a tired kid hanging onto the bottom loops yelling, "I don't like nature, I want to go home!"  The pack holds a small DSRL and extra lens securely in a well-padded compartment, and the camera compartment is situated on the side of the bag so it is easy to unzip and remove the camera for unexpected shots.

The only gripe I have about the bag is all the snaps, belts, cords, buckles, pockets and compartments.  Even the waist straps have little zippered pouches!  If feel like I need a map to tell me where I put everything, and I need a manual to explain what each strap and snap is for.  Think Swiss Army Knife with 500 tools.

So if you are an organized person this bags is probably Nirvana, but if you are messy at heart this backpack, with all its secret compartments and safety straps, will give you the willies.
profile.summary: Great bag, but too many snaps, belts, buckles, cords, zippers, pockets, and compartments

profile.description: Opus Antique Bottle Hummingbird Feeder Green 10oz Hummingbirds and hummingbird admirers will be attracted to this classic glass feeder with an antique design. Holds 10 ounces of nectar and features a sea-green glass bottle with brushed silver accents. In addition, the feeder features four decorative flower feeding ports surrounding its base. Remember to clean your feeder once every two weeks with mild soap and water solution. The new antique bottle feeders are sure to attract hummingbird enthusiasts, highlighting a classic style with a twist on tradition. Metal hanger attached for ease of hanging.
profile.reviewText:
This hummingbird feeder looks like a beautiful piece of Yard Art.  In the morning light the heavy glass bottle glows and the brushed copper base shimmers.  The little copper flowers are also awesome, so intricate and detailed.

The only thing that worries me is the absence of hummingbirds.  I do have a few hummingbirds in my yard, but I haven't seen one visit the feeder.  I'm worried that the little copper flowers are not bright enough, and there is not enough contrast between the color of the flower and the color of the base.

profile.summary: No Hummingbirds yet, but the feeder is a beautiful piece of Yard Art

profile.description: Clear Complete Scalp Care Anti Dandruff Shampoo and Conditioner relieve your scalp. Our CUCUMBER and MINT infused formulas silken hair, and contain Zinc Pyrithione to help eliminate flakes. With a fresh and invigorating scent, our Complete Scalp Care system helps sooth itchy, flaky scalp. Infused with CUCUMBER, known to alleviate dryness, and MINT, our formulas are designed to leave your hair and scalp feeling nourished and refreshed. Used daily with the conditioner, the shampoo alleviates itchy, flaky scalp and your hair feels moisturized and is free of visible flakes.
profile.reviewText:
This Clear Anti-Dandruff, Scalp Reliever shampoo is working well so far.  I have oily hair but also flakes and horrible scalp itch.  This shampoo helps to calm the scalp itch and reduces the flaking.  It also isn't adding any additional oil to my already oily hair.  The shampoo is lightweight, suds like crazy, washes away cleanly (although I did notice some white residue my tubs drain).  The scent is very mild.  I can smell a faint whiff of mint, but honestly if I hadnt read Mint & Cucumber on the label I probably wouldnt have recognized it.

I have been using Head & Shoulders and Scalpicin for years with good results.  Honestly I don't think the Clear shampoo works as well as the H&S Eucalyptus formula, but it still works reasonably well.  I think I will alternate between the two just to give my hair some variety, and not allow my scalp to become resistant to any one formula.

profile.description: Adorable mason jars set is perfect for keeping your flatware neatly organized, Holds utensils, candles, napkins, flowers, condiments, etc. Mason jars measures 4" diameter x 6-inch each, Tray 4.5 x 15-inch.
profile.reviewText:
I really like the look of these jars.  They are an unusual and interesting way to arrange flatware for a party.  And the design is very neutral so you can dress up the jars and tray to match any holiday or event.

But I did have one problem with the jars  they are a little too tall for the plastic flatware that I used.  When I first put the forks and spoons in the jar only the top inch of the utensils were sticking up over the jars rim.  It was very hard to grab one without touching all the other spoons and forks around it.  In the end I had to stuff the bottom of each jar with tissue wrapping paper so the spoons and forks would extend over the top and spread out in a nice fan pattern.  I also wish they would give you a piece of chalk with the set.  I didn't have any chalk in the house so I had to borrow some from the kid next door.

So very unique way to set out forks, spoons and knives, but just measure the length of your flatware and be prepared to buy something to put in the bottom of each jar.
profile.summary: Jars are a little too tall for my plastic flatware

profile.description: Constructed of durable polycarbonate abs, dual spinner wheels allow free movement in all directions, highly polished retractable push button reinforced handle, interior hanging zipper pocket & buckle tie belt.
profile.reviewText:
I really, really like the look of this suitcase.  The color and design are eye popping.  It is easily the most recognizable case on a luggage carousel filled with boring black, gray, and blue.

But after just one trip the semi-hard surface was covered in scuffs, gouges, and streaks of greasy residue.  This is my first hard case, and for some reason I thought it would be more durable.  I was completely surprised at how easily it was damaged.

But in spite of its newly "distressed" surface I still love this case.  It can hold a ton of stuff, the spinning wheels work like a dream, and it is hilarious watching my macho, teenaged boys drag the "flower monstrosity" (their words not mine) around airport terminals.
profile.summary: Eye popping good looks, but semi-hard surface scuffs and gouges easily

profile.description: Lovely gift idea for the tea drinker in your life. Consider this for a birthday gift.
profile.reviewText:
The teacup is very dainty and elegant looking.  It holds about 7 ozs of liquid so it is not too small or too large.  The floral design (cant tell if it is a camellia or magnolia) on the cup and saucer is very stylish with lots of detailed elements.  Overall the color combinations used are very pretty, but for some reason the colors on my cups and saucer look very pale and muted.  The blues look a little washed out and the white and purple of the flowers seem to fade into the blue of the background.  On the product description photos the colors on the set are vibrant and seem to pop with life, but under the normal light of my dining room the colors are just a little bland.

So very, very nice cup and beautiful design, just wish the colors had a little more pizzazz.
profile.summary: Colors are paler and more muted than I expected

profile.description: Features and Benefits Double wall vacuum insulated keeps liquids hot or cold more than 12 hours Constructed with double wall stainless steel, this 18 ounce bottle is virtually unbreakable and built to withstand the demands of everyday use. Thermos vacuum insulation technology locks in temperature to preserve flavor and freshness. Leak-Proof and Worry-Free The vacuum insulated cup comes equipped lid which operates simply with the push of a button. And because of the double wall insulation, the stainless steel body stays cool to the touch with hot beverages and condensation-free with cold beverages. Extra handle on the bottle cover. With extra handle on the bottle cover, convenient to hold and drink.
profile.reviewText:
This thermos really does keep my tea/coffee piping hot for hours.  It saves me from constantly running to the microwave to re-heat my beverage.  I just brew a pot of tea, dump it into the thermos ( hold a little more than 2 cups), and throughout the morning I pour out a few ounces to drink.  Whats inside the thermos stays as hot (~200 degrees) as when I first poured it in; yet the outer shell stays cool to the touch.

The thermos is also easy to open and close, and unlike other flask I've tried there is no "trick" or "special threading" need to get the top to fit correctly.  It has a long-necked, screw on top, and a snap button that opens and closes to allow the liquid to pour out.  When you put the open/close button in the closed position a rubber stopper is forced into the neck of the flask which prevents leaks.  If you are storing a cold beverage you can drink directly from the flask, but if storing a hot beverage use a cup.  I learned this lesson the hard way.  The thermos is so well insulated you cant tell that the liquid inside is scalding hot until you drink from it.  Ouch.

I also did some testing to see if the thermos was as leak proof as the manufacturer claimed.  I filled it up and turned upside down.  I shook it several times and kept it in that position for over an hour.  And Im happy to report  no leaks.  Then I did another test.  This time I filled it up, poured some liquid from the flask, and then closed it again.  Under this scenario I did see a tiny bit of seepage, but I think the seepage was just liquid that was clinging to the open/close button after I poured some liquid through the opening and it wasn't seepage from the main body of the thermos.  Plus the little screw on cup gives another level of protection, because if something does seep out of the flask it will but caught and trapped by the cup.

So this Life Sky thermos is a great way to keep your coffee/tea at the perfect temperature without constantly nuking it in the microwave.  And the metallic purple color of the flask is pretty too.

** product provided for review **
profile.summary: Keeps my tea/coffee piping hot for hours  no more trips to the microwave to re-heat

profile.description: Protect your Microsoft Surface Pro 3 with the Belkin Sleeve. This stylish zip-up case provides a secure fit for the Microsoft Surface Pro 3. The neoprene material and soft inner lining protect the screen and backing from scratches and damage while on the go. With its lightweight portfolio-style design, the sleeve provides a professional aesthetic for business or pleasure.
profile.reviewText:
This Belkin sleeve is soft and sleek, and it is the perfect size for the Surface Pro 3 and its attached keyboard and stylus.  The sturdy zippers open 2-1/4 sides of the sleeve so it is very easy getting the device in and out.  Width-wise, there is more than enough room for the SP3, keyboard and the stylus, but this brings me to my only gripe about the sleeve: the stylus holder.  Inside the sleeve there is a 1 inch elastic tube to hold the stylus, but the tube is much, much too narrow.  If I push really hard and wiggle the stylus around I can force about an inch of the stylus into the elastic tube, but that is about as far as it will go.  But you can just lay the stylus next to the SP3 and zip them up together.

Other observations:

1) The front and back padding is a little thin.  The edges of the sleeve have thick bumper cushions to protect the corners and sides of the SP3, but I found the cushioning on the front and back of the sleeve a little thin.  I carry my SP3 into my backpack and it tends to get bumped and knocked around a lot so I would have been happier if the padding were a little thicker.  (But I'm probably just being paranoid and over-protective).
2)  The color of the sleeve is not a match for the purple Microsoft SP3 keyboard.  The Belkin purple is darker and more maroon-ish.  More like Wine or Plum or Burgundy in color.  And the inside fabric is pink.

So this Belkin sleeve is a perfect size for the SP3 and its accessories.  And the soft, cushion-y fabric of the sleeve will protect the SP3 from those unavoidable bumps and knocks.
profile.summary: Perfect fit for SP, keyboard, and stylus.  But stylus holder is too tight to actually use

profile.description: First cup. Fourth cup - with Keurig, it's always a fresh cup. The OfficePRO K145 Brewing System brews a perfect cup of coffee, tea, hot cocoa or iced beverage in under one minute at the touch of a button. Now everyone in your office can brew what they love. This brewer has an Auto Off feature so when set it turns off after two hours of non-use. With the choice of three cup sizes, the OfficePRO brewer offers a removable drip tray to accommodate travel mugs. Includes a Bonus 12 Count K-Cup variety box.
profile.reviewText:
I have used many different Keurig models over the years, and I have never encountered one that was this noisy.  I literally jump every time the pump engages.  The pump on my old Keurig made a loud humming noise, but the pump on the K145 sounds like a fog horn.  The vibration from the pump also causes the water reservoir to rattle, and makes the whole machine knock against the counter top.

I know the pump is supposed to be industrial strengthen, but honestly the pump on my 20 year old washing machine makes less noise.

On a positive note I really the controls on this model.  Love the red light that tells you when the water is heating, and the flashing blue light that tells you when the machine is ready to brew.  The water heats up very fast, and the brew cycle is quick.
,
This K145 model has a lot of great features, but Im probably going to return it because of all the noise it makes.

Also, watch the pricing.  The system is sold by various companies and fulfilled by Amazon.  I purchased at $123 and the very next day it was offered at $90.  A few hours later it was going for $104.  All Prime shipping.  So just watch it over a few days to get the best pricing.

Update 8-2016 - This OfficePRO died a few days ago.  I turned it on to warm up and the crazy thing just started spewing water.  It drained half the water in the reservoir before it dawned on me what was happening.  None of the light on the panel were lit up, and the heating element wouldn't turn off.  After all the water was gone, steam starting pouring out of the machine and the side of the machine was boiling hot.  I turned it off before it caught on fire.  I never liked this machine.  Going back to the Classic Keurig.
profile.summary: Very, very noisy.  I jump every time the pump starts

profile.description: Lightweight warmth with a channeled grid backing for faster wicking and quick-drying comfort. Shaped Hem Product. medium-regular Fit
profile.reviewText:
This crew is soft and comfortable, and feels great against the skin.  The fabric is lightweight and breathable.  Sadly I haven't been able to test the moisture-wicking abilities of the crew because it has been just too dang hot to wear while bicycling.  It is Mid-October and it is still running in the high 80s during the day!  But I have worn it while walking the dog on chilly mornings and the crew kept me toasty warm.

The only thing I don't like about the crew is the pocket in the front.  Having a zippable pocket is great, but I don't like the way it looks.  There is just too much contrast between the ultra-black colored pocket and the soft gray color of the shirt.  And the pocket is noisy.  It makes loud crinkling sounds every time I move.  Im hoping that after a lot of washings the pocket fabric will soften and it will stop making so much noise.

profile.description: A stainless steel interior and 24 preprogrammed settings put the Cuisinart Microwave Oven in a class all its own. The ideal cooking environment, nonporous stainless will not absorb orders, moisture or food particles. Preprogrammed one-touch controls quarantine that everything from reheating coffee, to defrosting cutlets, to cooking fish or making 2, 4, or 6 strips of crispy bacon will be done right. This 1000-watt, 1.0-cubic-foot oven lets you cook from scratch, and do it a little healthier without any oil or butter. With its stainless steel interior, stainless steel door and sleek control panel, this is a new generation of microwave - from Cuisinart, of course!
profile.reviewText:
I'm an avid baker so what really got me excited about this appliance was the convection oven.  Who would have thought you could bake (really bake) in a microwave.  But I was skeptical at first so I setup a comparison test.  I mixed up some cake batter and divided it between two identical mini tube pans.  One pan went into the Cuisinart and one went into by big convection oven.  I removed the cake from the Cuisinart after 14 minutes and my big oven after 16 minutes.  Both were golden brown and rose exactly the same amount.  I literally could not tell them apart, and they tasted exactly the same too.  I was amazed at how well the Cuisinart worked.

But don't let my baking enthusiasm give you the impression that the Cuisinart is perfect, it does have some flaw.  Below are some pros and cons...

Pros:
 You can bake in it.  Really bake in it.
 It only takes 10 minutes to preheat the convection oven to 350 degrees.
 Actually bakes faster than my big convection oven.  Note: I place my cake pans on the grill rack so the hot air can flow completely around the pan.
The microwave works fine, but it is a little slower to boil water than my old unit of the same wattage.
The grill works fine.  I was able to grill some bone-in chicken thighs (I like them well done)  in about 40 minutes.

Cons:
 The convection oven struggles to heat the appliance above 350 degrees.  It only took 10 minutes to get from room temp to 350 but it took 25 minutes to get from room temp to 425 degrees.
 When the oven completes it preheating and you open the door the temperature drops  100 degrees in only a few second.  You need to be quick when putting pans in or checking for "doneness".  The temperature doesn't seem to drop as rapidly at the higher (400+) temperatures.
 The light in the oven is very weak.  It is too weak to accurately judge the "doneness" of your baked items.  To get a good look you must open the door which is a problem because that allows the hot air to escape.
 The mesh on the observation window is too dense.  The openings in the mesh are so small it is hard to see through it and get a good look at what is going on inside.  All microwaves have this mesh on the glass, but this one is so much harder to see through.
 The top and sides of the unit get very, very, very hot.  Hot enough to give a bad burn.
 The oven is complicated to operate.  Everything involves a sequence of steps.  In the end I made a laminated "cheat sheet" of the most common functions.
 Because the oven does so much the front panel is crammed with lots of button.  Lots of very small buttons.  You almost need a magnifying glass to read the text written on each button.
 The stainless steel shows a lot of fingerprints.  I wish the front panel and door release were made out of a different kind of material.
 The door release mechanics feels a little flimsy.  I'm afraid it will break if I push too hard.  But it hasn't broken yet so it must be sturdier than it feels.

So quite a few minor "cons" with this unit, but nothing I would consider critical.  And because it is multipurpose (and can bake, microwave, and grill) it is ideal for a small kitchen or great as a backup or overflow appliance in a larger kitchen.
profile.summary: Bakes as well as my big convection oven

profile.description: 7.4qt (7L) Domina Vitamin Pressure Cooker combines safety, functionality, and modern design for cooking that is up to 2x faster. Remove lid for flawless stove-to-table serving. - Exclusive, patented one-handed drop lid opening system - Durable 18/10 stainless steel construction with signature mirror polish finish.
profile.reviewText:
I have been using the old fashion twist-cover pressure cookers all my life, so this Lagostina looks like a work of art in comparison.  The Lagostina  is sleek, modern, and very high tech looking.  So far Ive used it to cook some pickled pork, red beans, and cabbage.  The Lagostina works as expected, and all the food came out great, but I encountered a few gotchas.

The first head scratcher was getting the cover on and off.  The design of the cover is very curious, and unlike the easy twist-off cover of my old cheap-o pressure cooker, removing the cover of the Lagostina takes some practice.  The cover sits inside the pot and when the handle is engaged it pulls the cover up and forms a tight seal between the cover and the wide lip of the pot.  When you release the tension on the handle, the round/flat cover actually bends into an elongated bowl shape.  To remove the cover from inside the pot you need to turn the cover sideways and down so you can maneuver the elongated/pointed end out first.  If you don't position the cover correctly, it won't fit through the opening of the pot.  Very interesting.

Once the pot is filled with food, the bowl shaped cover is inserted back inside the pot, and using the power of the lever the metal cover is flattened and pulled up tight against the rim of the pot.  The cover is locked in place until it is released again by unlocking the handle.  With other pressure cookers I always had a fear that the cover would get blown off, but with the Lagostina I have no such fear.  That lid isn't going anywhere.

The actual cooking process is very easy and the pressure release valve is simple to use and understand.  I don't think the Lagostina cooks as fast as my old twist-top pressure cooker, but my old pot is much bigger so I guess the pressure can get much higher.

The pressure release valve on the Lagostina was another gotcha.  I was cooking pickled pork (to use as seasoning) and after the appropriate cooking time I followed the directions and turned the pressure valve to Steam to release the pressure.  Well it released the pressure, but along with the steam it also spewed out oily pork grease all over the stove, counter top, and cabinets.  The instruction booklet warns about steam spray but I didn't realize how bad it would be.  So I won't be using the pressure release valve again.  I will just let it cool down slowly.  The instructions also say not to put the hot pot under running water to cool it off  this is something I always did with my old pressure cooker.  The Lagostina is also not dishwasher safe, and you need to change the gasket every five years.

So this Lagostina works great and is a very nice looking pot  a show piece even, but it also has a wonky cover and an over-efficient pressure release valve.
profile.summary: Like it, but the cover is like jigsaw puzzle and it spits out a lot of juice when you release the pressure

profile.description: Ace Collins defines himself as a storyteller. He has authored more than sixty books that have sold more than 2.5 million copies. He has also been the featured speaker at the National Archives Distinguished Lecture Series, hosted a network television special and does college basketball play-by-play. Ace lives in Arkansas. Learn more about him by visiting AceCollins.com.&nbsp;
profile.reviewText:
Get a hankie handy before you start reading this book  I was blubbering by page 18.

Service Tails is a compilation of stories about people and the service dogs that saved them.  But unlike Ace Collins book: Mans Best Hero, the dogs in this book provide just as much emotional saving as physical saving.  Yes the dogs are trained to guide the blind, be the ears for the deaf, or assist the weak, but they also give hope to the hopeless and build bridges to the isolated.  When the people in these stories are at their lowest, when they are ready to give up the fight, the service dogs allows them to knock down the mental and physical barricades and realize that life is still full of endless possibilities and opportunities.

Im a big dog lover but also a history buff, so my favorite chapter in the book was the first.  The first chapter briefly explains how the service dog movement started in the US.  The topic was so interesting I would love to read a whole book on just that topic.  My least favorite chapter was the last  Service Forgotten.  That one made me want to scream in anger and beat someone to a bloody pulp, but it also has me looking into adopting a retired service dog.

So if you love dogs and want more proof that they are the most selfless creatures on earth  read this book.  It is touching, inspiring, and very educational.
profile.summary: I was crying by page 18  touching and heartwarming (except for the last chapter  that one made me MAD)

These socks are pretty neat.  They fit by size 8 foot really well.  They are not too tight or too loose.  The elastic band around the ankles fits especially well.  It is tight enough to stay in place, but not tight enough to dig into my skin and leave a mark.  Ive use them during workouts and I find that they don't get as smelly as my regular socks.  They handle repeated washing without any fading or unraveling of seams.  I don't put them in the dryer, but they dry within a few hours just sitting in the warm laundry room.

But the best feature of these socks is how soft and cushiony they are.  They almost feel like slippers.  Nice.
profile.summary: Almost feel like slippers, wash well and don't get smelly like my regular socks

profile.description: The old-school lunch box is getting PackIt's cool twist! The Classic Freezable Lunch Box is the only horizontal lunch box with built-in cooling that chills food and drinks for hours. The secret is PackIt's groundbreaking technology: a freezable gel liner is integrated into the walls of the lunch box. The design eliminates the need for separate ice packs or gel packs. To use, simply flatten the lunch box and place it in the freezer overnight (12 hours for optimal results). In the morning, the walls of the lunch box will be completely frozen and ready to chill items for hours. PackIt lunch bags and lunch boxes keep food cooler longer, which allows you to pack healthy foods that would spoil in other lunch boxes such as dairy, deli meats, salads, fruits and veggies. The Classic Freezable Lunch Box by PackIt easily fits an entire meal and a 12 ounce (340ml) drink. A top-load design makes this lunch box simple to pack, and its kid-friendly zipper closure locks in cold, dry air. This innovative lunch box also features a mesh side pocket for a small water bottle or snacks, and a slim exterior zip pocket for ID cards or wipes. A buckle handle lets you clip the lunchbox onto totes, backpacks or sports bags. PackIts Classic Lunchbox is made from nontoxic poly canvas and has a food-safe, water-resistant lining. Like all PackIt products, the Classic Lunchbox is made from PVC-, BPA-, phthalate-, formaldehyde- and lead-free materials. Care: wipe thoroughly or hand wash the interior and spot clean exterior; allow bag to dry completely before freezing. Not machine or dishwasher safe. PackIts Classic Freezable Lunch Box measures 8.25 inches tall, 10 inches wide and 4.25 inches deep while open. When collapsed, it measures 10 inches wide, 8.5 inches deep and 2.25 inches tall for easy storage in the freezer.
profile.reviewText:
This freezable lunch bag really does keep your perishable foods cold for hours.  I packed my lunch at 5am and even after opening and closing it several times during the day my pickle was still cold at 3pm.  But this bag is heavy: 3 or 4 times as heavy as the neoprene bag I usually use.  The bag also takes up a lot of room in my backpack (and the freezer), and the inside of the bag sweats a lot during the day.  The inside beads up with moisture and makes everything a little damp.

So I guess this bag is a little overkill for just bringing lunch to work everyday, but if you were bringing it on a day trip the extra cooling time would justify the weight.
profile.summary: Keeps things cold, but heavy and inside sweats

profile.description: 325S Features: -Mixed seed tube type feeder.-Even seed technology that allows separate chambers to empty equally.-Sure lock cap system keeps squirrels out.-Two independent seed compartments that can be filled with two different types of seed to attract a larger variety of birds.-Made in the USA.-Capacity: 4.5 lbs. Color/Finish: -Finish: Rustic Brown. Dimensions: -Dimensions: 15" H x 8.25" W x 8.25" D.-Weight: 2.45 lbs.
profile.reviewText:
This is a beautiful and stylish feeder.  I've only used it for a few weeks but it seems well-made and sturdy, and the feed doesn't get wet during a heavy downpour of rain.  But the best part of this feeder is the dual compartments that let use two different feeds in the same container.  There is also a hollow tube down the center that allows you easily fill the bottom compartment without disassembling the entire thing.  This is a very nice feature, but I wish the tube extended all the way to the top of the upper compartment.  The tube stops about a 2 inches from the top so you need to be careful when pouring the seed into the tube (they tend to go flying).  In the end I found a funnel that made the job of fill the bottom compartment a lot easier.

The only hesitation I have about the feeder is that it attracts doves that monopolize the feeder and scare off the smaller song birds.  The perch encircling the feeder is wide enough for the doves to balance on, so they will sit on the perch and eat and eat and eat until everything is gone.

I have a second feeder with a smaller perch and this seems to work much better in my yard.  The smaller birds eat from the feeder and the doves sit on the ground and gobble up whatever falls their way.

So if you have a lot of dove or black birds in your area, this might not be the best choice.
profile.summary: Large perch allows Doves to monopolize feeder

profile.description: The Rabbit Wing Corkscrew is an essential tool for any home bar or kitchen. This classic corkscrew's twin arms provide extra leverage to remove wine corks with ease. Constructed of durable plastic and stainless steel for long service life. Designed to fit any size bottle. Dishwasher-safe for easy cleaning. This corkscrew is backed with a 5-year warranty.
profile.reviewText:
Im only an occasional drinker of wine, and up to this point I had only used an old-fashion corkscrew, but this Wing Style may make a frequent wine drinker out of me yet.  It is so much easier to use than my curly icepick style corkscrew.  The screw easily penetrated the cork and with just a light touch the wings pop the cork out of the bottle.

The only negative I have with the 4043 Rabbit is all its thin plastic parts.  It just feels fragile in my hands.  I don't think it is attractive enough to display on the counter, so it will be stuffed into over-packed kitchen utensil drawer.  I just hope the thin plastic won't crack after banging around the drawer for a few months/years.
profile.summary: Works well, but most of the parts are made out of plastic

profile.description: An Amazon Brand.
profile.reviewText:
These Amazon Basic puppy pads look so much better than the regular pads I buy.  The Amazon pads lay flat and have none of that unsightly cotton bunching around the folds.  The carbon pads absorb a lot of liquid, they don't leak, and they don't have an unpleasant smell.

BUT my baby girl is afraid of them!  She eyes them with suspicion and walks a wide path around them just to avoid putting a paw on the gray colored cotton.  I have tried putting her food on the pad and even her peanut butter crisps, but she still won't go anywhere near the pad.  Im sad about this because I really like the look of the Amazon pads.  Oh well, guess it is hard/impossible to teach an old dog to use a new pad.
profile.summary: Great looking pads, but my old Chihuahua is afraid of them

profile.description: The French Perle White Everything Bowl features intricate detailing inspired by hand-embroidered fabrics. A carved beaded motif of scrolls and jewel-like elements punctuates the sophisticated, elegant look.
profile.reviewText:
This is a nice mug that has a classy, elegant look.  I find that it is a little too heavy to use in the car, but it works great at home or in the office.  It does just an average job of keeping the liquid hot, but you can pop it into the microware to reheat when needed.

The only thing I really don't like about the mug is the finish along the rim.  The mug I received is white, but the entire rim is covered in splotchy brown glaze.  At first glance I thought the mug was dirty, but when the color wouldnt wash off I realized the brown was part of the finish.  Im not sure if it is supposed to be there or if it is a flaw.  If the splotches were deliberate wouldnt the brown antiquing be on the entire mug?  If the brown splotches had covered the whole mug, it would have been interesting look.  Something like a country or distressed feel.  But having the brown color just on the rim it makes the mug look dirty.
profile.summary: Nice mug, but weird splotchy brown color on the rim

profile.description: Our Happy Birthday Minis are made from high quality, durable felt and are the perfect addition to your Birthday Celebrations!! Use them year after year. They will soon be a favorite tradition. Our banners are sturdy and durable unlike paper or cardboard banners! These will last! Each banner piece measures 3.25 inches wide by 5.25 inches tall. Each piece is laser cut with letters layered and applied. Polka Dots and stripes make this banner whimsical and fun. Our buntings are made from a think felt that is both stiff and sturdy. It measures 3mm thick; not your average craft store felt. This gives it a neat textural and dimensional look. Comes with 14 banner pieces and a simple, white grosgrain ribbon for stringing. All strung together (as pictured), the bunting measures 60 inches wide. You can space yours out along the ribbon to suit your needs in length. You can add your favorite ribbon, tulle, string or rope to make a more custom look! This banner is durable enough to toss in your Holiday box for storage without getting ruined.
profile.reviewText:
The colors of this birthday banner are bright and festive, and the quality of the piece is very good.  The felt is thick and durable, and will probably last for many years and many birthdays.  But I do wish the block were a little larger.  The banner seemed to get lost among all the other decorations.

Another thing to be aware of is that this thing doesnt come assembled.  Give yourself 10-15 minutes to string each block onto the provided ribbon.  And don't rush or the ribbon will get all twisted as you thread it.  Also make sure you sort the letters correctly or you may accidentally get HAPY instead of HAPPY and have to take it apart and start all over.
profile.summary: Cute but letters a little small.  Comes unassembled so allow 15 minutes to string together

profile.description: Eliminate messy countertops with the convenient Rachael Ray Cucina Tools 2-Piece Lazy Solid Spoon Set that features two professional-quality silicone kitchen spoons boasting innovative, modern design and earthy, rustic color. Cleverly designed notches on the spoons clip directly on the sides of cookware, containing drips inside pots and pans, not on countertops or stovetops. The inviting set includes 10-1/2 inch and 12-inch spoon sizes to choose from when preparing a rich lemon caper sauce and spooning it over pan-seared halibut. Clip one of the spoons to the side of a skillet when creating Rachael's savory Deviled Crab Risotto Milanese to conveniently keep the kitchen tool easily within reach. An ideal partner for all cookware interiors, including nonstick, the silicone spoon set is heat safe to 500 Degree F and dishwasher safe for convenience. This colorful kitchen spoon set is a great complement to many other attractive items in the Rachael Ray Cucina collection.
profile.reviewText:
There are a lot of things I like about these Rachael Ray Lazy Spoons.  The notched handle which lets you suspend the spoon on the edge of the pot is ingenious.  No more dips, no more laying multiple spoons on a plate and watching them float in a puddle of congealing sauce/gravy/etc.  And no more mixing up spoons.  Hang the spoon to its pot so your kids won't use the chili spoon to scoop up the Alfredo sauce.  Another thing I like is the soft rubber edge of the spoon.  It is stiff enough to scrape the food off the bottom of the pot, but not so stiff that it would scrape the non-stick pans.

But on the negative side I found the size of the spoon's bowl is a little small (2  x 3") and the depth is a little shallow (about 6/16").  The spoon is good for stirring, but not as good for ladling out food.  I also found it peculiar the way the textured rubber surface seems to attract lint.  Before using the spoons I washed and dried them.  The kitchen towel was white, and after drying the spoons I found lots of tiny white fibers all over the rough, rubber surface of the spoon.  I tried flicking, blowing, and wiping the lint off, but it wouldn't budge.  I actually had to individually pick each piece of lint off the spoon.  I have lots of rubber spatulas, and I have never encountered this lint-sticking problem before.  The only thing I can figure is that the RR spoons have a rough textured surface that the lint seems clings to.  I also use a lot of hand cream, and I notice that after holding the spoons the handle shows white smudges.  Between the smudges and the lint, the spoons just look a little dingy.  If the spoons came in white instead of  brick red, I don't think the clinging lint and hand cream residue would bother me as much.

So 5 stars for ingenuity, 3 stars for practicality
profile.summary: Ingenious design, but textured rubber surface attracts lint

profile.description: MAXCUT Does It All. The MAXCUT Multi-Cutter takes on the hardest cutting jobs and comes back for more. Serrated blades grip and cut while compound action powers through hundreds of materials, from leather to shingles to 20 gauge steel. Blade design includes a twine cutter, wire cutter, bottle opener and wire bending holes for added versatility.
profile.reviewText:
With this cutter I don't have to worry about buying things with "frustration free" packaging because this baby will snip through a plastic clamshell package like its tissue paper.  No more sliced fingers or ruined scissors; no more careful and fearful use of a box cutter.  Just snip, snip and my item is freed from its plastic cage.

I also tried the cutter on a variety of other materials.  It worked great on stiff cardboard, and the neat wire cutting gizmo is interesting to play with.  I was chopping apart wire just for the fun of it.  It was able to effortlessly cut through a thin metal door shoe, weather stripping, foam pipe insulation, aluminum siding, as well as some shingles I had floating around.  But I didn't have much luck getting the twine cutting gizmo to work, it just shredded the twine.  I also had trouble cutting through suede and some old towels I use to wash the car.  But strangely the cutter worked fine on some thick landscape fabric and a floppy mouse pad.  It looks like it can cut fabric that has a plastic or rubber component to it ??? Just guess here.

Also be aware that the cutter is on the heavy side and it is also large.  I had a trouble gripping and squeezing the handles of the cutter when they were fully released.  I imagine if I tried to use the cutters for an extended period of time my fingers and hand would start to cramp.

So this Wiss cutter is a handy tool to have in your collection.  With this cutter I will no longer be defeated by plastic clamshell packaging.
profile.summary: Cuts through plastic clamshell packaging like butter

profile.description: Cuisinart presents a countertop oven that's the ultimate combination of size, style and smarts. The big, 1.2 cubic foot Microwave Convection Oven and Grill looks like it belongs in a high-end commercial kitchen. Brushed stainless steel and black frame a sleek control panel that offers single and combinations settings for an unlimited number of cooking options. A multi-stage cooking feature that automatically shifts form one function to another makes perfect results easier than ever. This is a new generation of microwave - and It's from Cuisinart, of course!
profile.reviewText:
I'm an avid baker so what really got me excited about this appliance was the convection oven.  Who would have thought you could bake (really bake) in a microwave.  But I was skeptical at first so I setup a comparison test.  I mixed up some cake batter and divided it between two identical mini tube pans.  One pan went into the Cuisinart and one went into by big convection oven.  I removed the cake from the Cuisinart after 14 minutes and my big oven after 16 minutes.  Both were golden brown and rose exactly the same amount.  I literally could not tell them apart, and they tasted exactly the same too.  I was amazed at how well the Cuisinart worked.

But don't let my baking enthusiasm give you the impression that the Cuisinart is perfect, it does have some flaw.  Below are some pros and cons...

Pros:
 You can bake in it.  Really bake in it.
 It only takes 10 minutes to preheat the convection oven to 350 degrees.
 Actually bakes faster than my big convection oven.  Note: I place my cake pans on the grill rack so the hot air can flow completely around the pan.
The microwave works fine, but it is a little slower to boil water than my old unit of the same wattage.
The grill works fine.  I was able to grill some bone-in chicken thighs (I like them well done)  in about 40 minutes.

Cons:
 The convection oven struggles to heat the appliance above 350 degrees.  It only took 10 minutes to get from room temp to 350 but it took 25 minutes to get from room temp to 425 degrees.
 When the oven completes it preheating and you open the door the temperature drops  100 degrees in only a few second.  You need to be quick when putting pans in or checking for "doneness".  The temperature doesn't seem to drop as rapidly at the higher (400+) temperatures.
 The light in the oven is very weak.  It is too weak to accurately judge the "doneness" of your baked items.  To get a good look you must open the door which is a problem because that allows the hot air to escape.
 The mesh on the observation window is too dense.  The openings in the mesh are so small it is hard to see through it and get a good look at what is going on inside.  All microwaves have this mesh on the glass, but this one is so much harder to see through.
 The top and sides of the unit get very, very, very hot.  Hot enough to give a bad burn.
 The oven is complicated to operate.  Everything involves a sequence of steps.  In the end I made a laminated "cheat sheet" of the most common functions.
 Because the oven does so much the front panel is crammed with lots of button.  Lots of very small buttons.  You almost need a magnifying glass to read the text written on each button.
 The stainless steel shows a lot of fingerprints.  I wish the front panel and door release were made out of a different kind of material.
 The door release mechanics feels a little flimsy.  I'm afraid it will break if I push too hard.  But it hasn't broken yet so it must be sturdier than it feels.

So quite a few minor "cons" with this unit, but nothing I would consider critical.  And because it is multipurpose (and can bake, microwave, and grill) it is ideal for a small kitchen or great as a backup or overflow appliance in a larger kitchen.
profile.summary: Bakes as well as my big convection oven

profile.description: The Sunbeam Quilted Heated Mattress Pad delivers comfort and soothing warmth throughout the night. Choose from ten heat settings to help alleviate neck, shoulder, and back aches. ThermoFine technology automatically adjusts to your setting based on room and body temperature.
profile.reviewText:
The bottom line is this heated mattress pad works and works exceptionally well.  It heat quickly and evenly, and keeps you toasty warm throughout the night.

But there are a few things about the heated pad that makes go "Hummm..."

1.  The plug to attach the pad to the power cord is on the foot of the mattress, and instead of being on the side of the mattress it is located on the TOP. See picture in gallery.  When I stretch I can feel the bulky plug with my toes.  The other mattress warmer used in the house has the plug on the side of the mattress at the head of the bed.  This seems like a much more logical location for the plug.  I thought about just reversing the pad and putting the plug at the head of the bed, but then you would feel the plug under the pillow and touch it with your fingers.

2.  Because the plug is at the foot of the bed you have to stretch the power cord from the foot to the head so you can set the temperature controls on the nightstands.  This takes A LOT of cord.  To make it worse you can't put the cord between the mattress and the box spring, it has to go on the floor.  I keep a lot of stuff (aka junk) under my bed, and it seems that every time I pull something from under the bed the power cord gets snagged and this in turn yanks the temperature controllers from the nightstands.

3.  If you have a bed skirt on the box spring the location of the plug causes another problem.  To get the power cord under the bed you have to cut a hole in the bed skirt and fish the cord through the opening.

4.  The temperature controller is another issue.  You need two hands to turn the dial and set the temperature.  There is an easy on/off switch, but changing the setting on the dial takes a bit of effort.  Not good for the elderly or someone with arthritis.

5.  The temperature controller is also a weird shape, and won't sit flat on my nightstand.  The lighter, narrow end with the on/off button is always elevated about a 1/2 inch.  See picture in gallery.  The controller doesn't topple over, but it just looks a little odd.  Almost like a little mouse sitting next to my bed.

6.  You run your hand across the top of the pad you can feel the wires, but when you lay on it they are hardly noticeable.

So if your only concern is keeping warm at night, then this is the mattress warmer is a great choice.  But if you don't like the thought of your stretching toes touching the power plug, then look for a warmer with the plug on the side of the mattress.

PS: If your controllers keep flashing that means the power plug is not pushed far enough into the plug on the mattress.  Push it till it snaps in place.  Took me a while to figure that out.  Duh, I know.
profile.summary: Keeps you toasty warm, but I can feel the power plug with my toes....

profile.description: The Tommy Floral Hard side Collection is a durable composite polycarbonate luggage. Complete with unique floral print, enameled metal logo plate, 8 spinner wheels and a fully lined interior.
profile.reviewText:
This is a well-made piece of luggage, with lots of accent trim that make it look very stylish.  I love the color and design too.  It is cheerful and eye-catching without being too loud, and the unique design makes it super easy to spot on the luggage carousel or in the stacks and stacks of jumbled of luggage after a cruise.

The case weighs 7.8 pounds empty, and it can hold a lot of stuff.  The leather handle is attached with sturdy studs that didn't budge when I loaded the bag with 30 pounds of stuff.  The spinner wheels work beautifully, and I was able to wheel it across some shag carpet, gravel driveway, and  hard flooring with it fully loaded.  The inside of the case is lined, and the lining is super thick and cushion-y.  Have you ever unzipped the lining of the case and looked at the stuff underneath?  There are a lot of sharp edges, and pointy things under there.  Sure there is tape covering the sharp edges but after awhile the tape falls off and if the lining isn't thick enough the sharp edges can poke through the lining and snag your cloths or your fingers.

The telescoping handle works well and pulls up and closes smoothly, and none of the zippers snagged when I repeatedly opened and closed them.  The telescoping handle does seem a little flimsy, but because you don't tilt the case back and roll on two wheels this is not a problem.

My only complaint with the bag is the lock.  For one there were no instructions on how to use it!  It comes locked, and it took me a few minutes to figure out how to open it (actually one of the kids had to show me).  I kept pushing the button down to try and release the lock when you actually have to slide it to the right.  After the fact I did notice that there is an arrow on the button showing you the direction to push, but I didn't have my glasses on at the time so I didn't see it (it is a pain getting old).

So really nice piece of luggage, they just need to include some instruction about the lock.
profile.summary: Well-made and pretty.  Easy to spot on the luggage carousel or the cruise terminal

profile.description: Experience true control and power with just a squeeze of your hand. The first hand blender with Smart Speed technology, Braun's MultiQuick 7, model MQ777, helps you prep meals easier than ever. The patented PowerBell system blends food in a flash without splashing or suction. This exclusive bundle for Bed, Bath and Beyond includes a beaker, whisk and 1.5 cup chopper attachments that let you whip up creativity.
profile.reviewText:
This is a powerful little kitchen appliance that can perform a lot of different functions.  So far I made Blackberry Jalapeno BBQ sauce with the immersion blender.  I used the masher attachment to turn potatoes leftover from a crayfish boil into spicy mashed potatoes, and the food processor easily shredded apples to make Apple Pie Cookies.

For the most part the Braun has performed well.  The squeezable power control is easy to use and it doesnt cause hand fatigue even after a few minutes of constant use.  And best of all the Braun immersion blender doesnt spit it you.  I bought a KitchenAid hand blender a few months back and I cant use it in an open pot because it kicks up too much food.

The only thing I don't like about this Braun set is that it doesnt come with an attachment suitable for mixing cake batter.  I was just making a regular box cake mix, and when I tried the Braun whisk attachment I found that it was just too fragile for even the thin Betty Crocker cake mix.  I switched to the immersion blender attachment, but again it just didn't work right:  the blender just doesnt beat the batter enough.

So a good tool that does double duty as an immersion blender and a food processor, but sadly it won't replace your hand mixer.
profile.summary: Good immersion blender and a food processor, but sadly it won't replace your hand mixer

profile.description: Feeding your wild birds with Birdola makes good sense. For the consumer, it is convenient. Simply unwrap the two-pound cake, and insert it into Birdola Products' specially designed feeder. No more heavy bags to lift and break in your trunk. No more storage hassles. The Birdola Big Ol' Kob equals 8 cobs of corn and provides a premium mix of corn, black oil sunflower seeds and peanuts helps keeps squirrels away from the bird seed. Give them their own feeding area and food. Use the grommet included to attach to the Birdola KOB Bungee.
profile.reviewText:
I didn't have a tree limb sturdy enough to hang the bungee from so I attached it to a plant hook that is nailed to the fence.  The resident squirrels found the food after only a day, and have now completely abandoned my bird feeder with its tiny seeds in favor of the chunky corn on the Kob feeder.  But sadly while the squirrels do love the food, they don't care for the bungee cord at all.  I was hoping to see them bouncing wildly up and down, but instead the squirrels hang onto the wooden fence and just reach out and grab the brick of food.

Oh well, it is still fun watching the squirrels do their Reed Richards impersonation and stretch, twist and contort their bodies to reach the food.  I will be buying more Kobs to keep the squirrels fat, happy, and away from my bird feeder.
profile.summary: Squirrels love the food but won't bounce on the bungee ;-(

profile.description: Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E902 Air Walk Trainer provides an aerobic workout, giving you all the benefits of stretching, walking, running, cross-country, skiing and aerobic dancing without jarring impacts or damaging movements to your body. This space saving Air Walker trainer folds to half the size, making it easy to put away in your closet or in a tight space. The striding motion delivers a slight twist to the midsection engaging both the upper and lower body. Youll get a total body workout every time you workout!
profile.reviewText:
After my 81-year old Mother's back surgery she was using the Gazelle walker at the physical therapy office.  She wanted to get one for home use, and while researching the Gazelle I found (and bought) this Sunny Air Walk.  It works just like the Gazelle but is about half the price!  Mom even said she like the Sunny better because it has the stomach cushion that gives her more stability.

The Sunny was a snap to put together.  It has a small foot print, and it is light enough to move/slide around when I want to clean the carpet under it.  The foot pads are low to the ground so Mom has no trouble getting on or off, and even though the resistance is minimal, it still gives her a good workout.  And best of all it is low impact so there is no jarring motion on her knees or spine.

So great piece of exercise equipment if you need a workout without any jarring impact to your knees or back.
profile.summary: Great machine for the elderly

profile.description: This stylish Seville Classics UltraSlimline Personal Tower Fan is perfect for the office, bedroom or any room that needs a breeze. The tower fan is equipped with three whisper quiet speed settings (high, medium, low) that will leave you feeling cool and comfortable on those hot and humid days. The oscillating (70 degrees) space saving compact design has a footprint of less than 0.2 sq ft and the black satin finish complements any dcor. This mini tower fan measures 4.9 deep by 5.4 wide by 12.25 high. Ideal for use on desks, counters and in small spaces.
profile.reviewText:
I put this fan in my teenaged son's room.  He has a lot of gadgets and computer equipment in there so even with the AC and ceiling fan going full blast it was still uncomfortably hot.  I tried regular circular fans but he complained that the wind blew all his papers away.  Then I tried this Seville Tower Fan, and I was shocked when he gave me a big, tight hug and said the fan was awesome.

Likes:

&#10004 Oscillates smoothly and silently (no ticking sounds like in other fans).
&#10004 Pushes "cool" air.  I was surprised that the fan sends out what feels like cold air. I guess with the tower shape the fan is able to pull in the cold air that settles near the floor and push it upwards toward the center of the room.  Makes it feel like a mini AC unit.
&#10004 The "Eco" mode is almost silent, but the noise level increase slightly as the speed of the fan increases.  I actually like the sound the highest level makes.  Very soothing in a "white/ambient noise" kind of way.
&#10004 The time is a wonderful energy saving feature.  You can set the time so it doesn't run all night long.  Saves energy and money.
&#10004 The remote is very useful and easy to understand.
&#10004 The tower shape and color is very sleek looking, and blends into the room dcor.  It doesn't stand out like the big, round fans.  Also takes up a lot less room than the round fans.

Dislikes:

&#10008 &#160The only thing I dislike about the fan is that it wobbles if you touch it.  It doesn't wobble during normal operation, but if you misplace the remote and have to use the control button on the tower the things feels like it is going to topple over.  The plastic base needs to be larger and heavier to keep the tower from wobbling.
&#10008 &#160I also don't like the control on the little mini fan that comes with this unit.  There is only one button that you must repeatedly press to cycle through on/off and all the different fan speeds.  An on/off button and a separate button for each speed would be much nicer.

So I'm very satisfied with the fan, it does the job perfectly.  And any non-computer device that a teenaged boy would call "awesome" must be very awesome indeed.
profile.summary: In my teenaged son's words---"This fan is awesome"

&#10004 The remote is very useful and easy to understand.
&#10004 The tower shape and color is very sleek looking, and blends into the room dcor.  It doesn't stand out like the big, round fans.  Also takes up a lot less room than the round fans.

Dislikes:

&#10008 &#160The only thing I dislike about the fan is that it wobbles if you touch it.  It doesn't wobble during normal operation, but if you misplace the remote and have to use the control button on the tower the things feels like it is going to topple over.  The plastic base needs to be larger and heavier to keep the tower from wobbling.
&#10008 &#160I also don't like the control on the little mini fan that comes with this unit.  There is only one button that you must repeatedly press to cycle through on/off and all the different fan speeds.  An on/off button and a separate button for each speed would be much nicer.

So I'm very satisfied with the fan, it does the job perfectly.  And any non-computer device that a teenaged boy would call "awesome" must be very awesome indeed.
profile.summary: In my teenaged son's words---"This fan is awesome"

profile.description: Hot Shot Flying Insect Killer Aerosol kills houseflies, mosquitoes & other listed insects by contact. It kills for up to 4 weeks against mosquitoes & houseflies on non-porous surfaces & leaves a clean, fresh scent. Can be used indoors and outdoors. Read the entire label and follow all precautions and directions. SHAKE WELL BEFORE USING. Do not use on surfaces that can be harmed or stained by water. Hold container upright and aim spray away from face and body. INDOORS  To kill wasps, hornets, yellow jackets and bees: Use in late evening or early morning when insects are at rest. Spray liberally into hiding and breeding places, especially under attic rafters, contacting as many insects as possible. Repeat as necessary. AS A SPACE SPRAY: To kill houseflies, mosquitoes, cluster flies, gnats, fruit flies and flying moths: Close all doors and windows. Point nozzle upward. Direct spray mist to all parts of room, especially windows and other light sources that attract insects. Fill room with mist, then leave treated area immediately. Keep room closed for at least 15 minutes. Ventilate room when treatment is completed. Repeat as necessary. OUTDOORS  For houseflies, mosquitoes, cluster flies, gnats and flying moths: For use only as an aid in reducing the annoyance from these insects. Spray outside surfaces of screens, doors, window frames or wherever these insects may enter the building. Also treat surfaces around light fixtures on porches, in garages, and other places where insects congregate. Repeat as necessary. To kill bees, wasps, hornets and yellow jackets: Use in late evening or early morning when insects are at rest. Aim spray at nest openings in ground, bushes and in cracks and crevices that may harbor nests. Saturate nest openings and contact as many insects as possible. Repeat as necessary.
profile.reviewText:
Mosquitoes love me.  In a room filled with a hundred people, every mosquito will zero in on me.  The problem is worse at night.  Even with my bedroom door shut, windows closed, ceiling fan running the mosquitoes will find and bite me.  Every night, sometimes two or three times a night.  My battle with mosquitoes is epic, so I was more than willing to give this bug spray a try.

Cons:  This flying insect spray smells horrible.  It is like a toxic cloud that burns your lungs.  You need to spray this stuff and leave the house for a few hours.

Pro: It works!  In fact it works really well, and it is effective for weeks.  I sprayed all the outside door jams, the door to my bedroom, and the corners of my bedroom.  I sprayed the back patio where the mosquitoes like to cluster around the potted plants.  I sprayed about two weeks ago, and I haven't had a mosquito in my bedroom since.  Amazing.

Im not sure if the spray will continue working for four weeks that is advertised, but even if I have to spray every two weeks or so I would be happy.  And I can tolerate the smell if I know it is going to work.
profile.summary: Fumes are choking, but keeps the mosquitoes from entering my bedroom

profile.description: Ensure an evenly baked cake using Ateco's Cake Heating Cores. Simply place the four stainless steel cores in the bottom of any cake pan before you pour in the batter. The cores will conduct the heat into the center of your cake while baking in the oven, resulting in an a perfectly baked cake. The cores also aid in even rising. Remove before serving. Since 1905, Ateco has supplied fine restaurants and bakeries with quality built, specialty baking tools. Ateco products are internationally renowned for their high quality. When you use Ateco products, you're not only enjoying quality craftsmanship, you're also enjoying quality design, the products are a result of over one hundred years and four generations of innovation and development.
profile.reviewText:
I bought these heat cores because I was baking a 12" cake for the first time and I wanted to make sure the center was cooked.  I used only one core in each of the pans, not realizing until too late that I was supposed to use (as per the instructions) 3 cores in each pan.  I only had 4 cores and 3 pans, so I just used one in each pan.  And the cakes baked perfectly.  The centers were cooked, the top was flat, and the edges weren't over done.  So it worked perfectly even though I didn't use the correct number.

But there are a couple of things I don't like about the heating cores: 1) I think they could be sturdier  they look a little flimsy, and 2) It is a little difficult de-panning the cakes with the cores sticking out like long nails.  It would be better if the pointy core/nail separated from the base so that go can easily flip it out onto a flat surface.

Other observations:  Make sure you spray the base of the heating core with non-stick spray before you pour the batter over it.  Or better yet if you are using parchment paper, put the base under the parchment and poke the nail part through the paper.  The paper will keep the base of the core from getting stuck to the bottom of the cake.
profile.summary: Helps the center of the cake bake evenly, but didn't realize I needed more than 1 core/nail per cake
