profile.description: Inspired by the wine glass, my Sight features a modern, elegant design that makes it an attractive addition to any room which will not be easily recognized as a security camera or recording device. It connects directly to your Wi-Fi network automatically and has a 120deg field of view to see an entire room all at once. It can detect motion and noise for an entire room or specific areas and alert you by sending notifications to your mobile device or email.
profile.reviewText: Update 6-12-16 (lowered stars from 5 to 3) - Camera does not work with dual band router. I changed my internet service recently and couldn't get the iLuv to connect to the new WiFi router. After much hunting I found out that my router is a dual band router with both 2.4 and 5.0g broadcasts, and apparently the iLuv camera can't connect to the dual service. I even set my phone to use the 2.4 band, but the camera still won't connect. Update 11-11-15 My 30 day free trial of Premium services expired recently and when I reverted to the Free service I noticed a change from how the Free service worked previously. As of this point in time you no longer get 24 hours of cloud storage with the Free service. Now when the camera senses motion/sound it will send an email alert and a snapshot taken when the event was triggered. The Free service no longer saves a 10 second clip for 24 hours. :-( Sad ** Original Review ** I've only been using this iLuv mySight camera for a few weeks, but I am very impressed. First off it is a breeze to setup. The Amazon Product Description lists an "Easy 60 second setup". 60 seconds may be a stretch, but I can honestly say it didn't take me more than 5-10 minutes from start to finish. It just takes a few steps: 1) Plug the camera into a power outlet, 2) download the iVideon app to a smart phone/tablet that is connected to your Wi-Fi, 3) create an account with iVideon, 4) enter your Wi-Fi password into the iVideon app, and 5) place your phone next to the camera (the camera read the QR Code displayed on the phones screen). That is it. The camera automatically links itself the Wi-Fi, and then starts recording. At this point you can see the Live Feed on the app. It is that simple. Really. For the last two weeks Ive been struggling to install some outside cameras that use a DVR and port forwarding, so I was amazed at how easy it was to setup the fully functioning mySight system. In addition to the iVideon mobile app, the iLuv mySight camera uses the iVideon cloud for video storage. The camera comes with a Free service that will send you alerts (email or push) when motion or sound is detected by the camera. With this free service you can look at Live Feed, but there is no long-term storage of videos (you do get 24 hours ((update: you don't get this as of 11-11-15))) and no export of videos to a file. You can pay a monthly fee (lowest level is around 10 bucks per camera) that will let you store video clips for 7 days. With the purchase of the camera you also get a 30 day free trial to the 7-Day Cloud storage service. And something that is really classy you don't need to give them a credit card number to try it out the premium service. It is a good way to test the storage service and see if you need it. So after my 5 minutes of camera setup, I positioned the camera high atop a kitchen cabinet that faces the back door of the house. The power cord is 10 feet long. This is plenty long enough for my needs, but I do wish the cable came in black instead of the bright white. The bright white cable sticks out like a sore thumb against my dark cabinets. As for the most important thing - picture quality - this camera does an excellent job. Under lighted conditions the image is sharp and clear, and at night the IR does a good job of showing details. (Note: make sure you remove the clear plastic film for the lens or the picture will look really, really grainy. My bad, at first I didn't notice the film.) Motion and sound detection works great and the sensitivity of the detection can be modified using the app. The motion detector picks up anyone moving in the vicinity of the camera, and the noise detector will pick up sounds (footsteps, voices, breaking glass). Both types of detection will turn on the recorder, and that recording is transmitted to the cloud. I actually had to turn off the sound detection because noise from the TV in the living room was causing too many recording events. Another cool feature is that you can get the software to send alerts (via email or push to your phone) when the camera starts recording. And so that you are not bombarded with constant email alerts, the software allows you to schedule when alert emails are generated. For each day of the weeks (Mon-Sun) you can specify times (broken down into 15 minutes intervals) that you want alerts sent. There is also an option on the phone app to turn on/off the alerts that that particular phone receives. In my setup I have the alerts turned OFF during the day when someone is home, and turned ON at night and when the house is empty. I really like the scheduling and I wish there was something similar to control sound detection. Like the alerts I would only turn sound detection on at night and also when no one is home. Of course you can manually turn sound detection on and off, but it would be nice to set it and forget it. In the sound quality category the MySight is a little meh. Recording and playback of voices is a little muffled and sometimes unrecognizable. Another issue is when using it as a two-way radio. Be aware that there is about a 5 second delay between when something is said and when it is broadcast. Even the Live Feed has this delay. If you watch yourself real-time on the Live Feed the delay is very obvious. But this is not a flaw in the mySight camera (my Sharx and Qsee cameras do the same thing); it is more an issue with the router and Wi-Fi. To manage the cameras and look at the videos, iVideon provides both a mobile app and desktop web based software (the desktop version uses Flash). While both work fine, I did find the layout in both to be a little non-intuitive. To me it was difficult finding and remembering where certain functions were located. Everything seems buried and hidden. There are also certain functions that can only be done using the phone app (ie changing the settings of the camera like noise & sound sensitivity) and other things that could only be done on the desktop version (setting up the times to send email notifications). It really gets confusing trying to remember which platform to use to fiddle with which function. And finally the design of the camera... well that is really nice. Kudos to who every came up with the wine glass shape. It looks very elegant and stylish. So overall this iLuv mySight system is a great home security camera. The video quality is excellent, and it does a great job of picking up motion and sound. It is a snap to install, and the cloud based services makes it super easy to view, store, and export the video clips. You do pay a little more for the cloud storage, but it is so much easier than messing with routers, IP addresses, and port forwarding. And while the software menu system could use some tweeking, it works really well. So this is a great product for a DIY security system. ** Camera provided by iLuv for review purposes **
profile.summary: Picture quality is great and setup couldn't be easier; Software has lots of useful features

Our easy-to-use, fast-acting insect, lawn disease and weed control solutions help you tame lawn and landscape invaders with incredible pest-punishing power. Take command with Spectracide brand. You hold the power. Spectracide Weed Stop For Lawns For St. Augustine & Centipede Lawns Concentrate is formulated specifically for use on all St. Augustinegrass varieties as well as centipedegrass. It kills the weeds, not the lawn when used as directed. This atrazine-based formula controls both emerged tough weeds and weeds from seeds. Use it to control established weeds, including dollarweed, sandspur and Florida betony, and prevent weeds from emerging in the lawn. Spray any time temperatures are below 90 degrees. The QuickFlip hose-end sprayer activates at the flip of a switch. Spray Spectracide Weed Stop For Lawns For St. Augustine & Centipede Lawns Concentrate when temperatures are between 60 degrees and 90 degrees  spraying in cooler temperatures may result in slower weed control. This formula can be applied during both dormant and growing seasons, but for best results, apply in early spring or in dormant periods when weeds or small or have not yet emerged. This concentrate bottle will treat 3,720 square feet of listed grasses.
profile.reviewText:
One day I noticed a patch of my centipede lawn was being invaded by dollarweeds and I almost cried.  Dollarweeds are invasive, destructive to lawns, and very hard to eliminate.  I tried a few non-pesticides remedies first, and then I tried this Spectracide HG-95684.  After I applied the Spectracide I waited and waited, and nothing happened.  Some of the dollorweeds had a little browning around the edges but they did not seem to be dying.  I waited a few more days and still no reduction in the dollarweeds.

And then today (about 3 weeks after application) I went out to inspect the patch of lawn, and found that 95% of the weeds were gone!  At first I was confused and thought I was looking at the wrong section of grass, but no, I was looking at the area that had been invaded by the dollarweeds.  When I looked closely I could still see a few tiny weeds, but they look sickly and distressed.  I guess it has been about 3 weeks since I first applied the chemical, so it does work but it takes a long, long time.  Spray the lawn, and then give it a few weeks before you look for results. Patience is required when you use this product.

FYI: the home remedies I tried first were vinegar and granulated sugar.  The vinegar spritzed on the area worked amazingly fast (1-2 days) but it killed everything: weeds and lawn.  The sugar was sprinkled over the lawn and then watered in.  Apparently the sugar changes the chemical makeup of the soil which eventually kills the dollarweeds.  The sugar did seem to be helping somewhat, but then I over-sprayed the same sugar-treated area with the Spectracide which eventually killed all the weeds.
profile.summary: Took about three weeks to work, but all the  dollarweeds (pennywort) died and the lawn was not damaged

profile.description: This Sabatier Digital Thermometer with Adjustable Head features a 2-in-1 digital instant read thermometer and timer. Thermometer has a temperature range from -20 to 500 degrees F, and an adjustable head for easy viewing. The 5-inch stainless steel tapered probe comes with a storage sleeve for protection. Includes one 2032 button cell battery; on off button protects the life of the battery.
profile.reviewText:
The first thing I tested the Sabatier Probe on was boiling water, and sure enough it registered 212 degrees (Im at sea level).

Next I tried the gizmo on a thin steak that I wanted cooked well done.  I made sure I positioned the probe in the center of the meat, and then placed the pan, meat and probe into the oven (preheated to 400 degrees).  The wire that attaches the probe to the digital device was nice and long, so I was able to stick the digital device to my overhead microwave instead of the door of the oven.  I programmed the device for Beef  Well Done, and watched the thermometer do its stuff.  But all too quickly the thermometer began to beep (very loud BTW), and indicated that the internal temperature of the meat had reached 170 degrees.  I also noticed that the Sabatier was showing an oven temperature of 325 degrees even though the oven was set to 400 and my secondary, inside oven thermometer was showing 395.  I pulled out the pan, and I could tell from just one look that the meat was not cooked to the well done stage.  The Sabatier was still indicating 170 degrees, but when I stuck a different quick read thermometer into the meat I got a reading of 145 degrees.  I cut into the meat and found it still bright pink inside.  More rare than well done.

Next I tried the probe on a very thick crab cake.  In this case the probe worked much better.  The reading was the same as my other quick read temperature probe, but the oven temperature reading was still off by 50+ degrees.

So it looks like the probe works much better if the item you are trying to cook is thick.  Maybe if the item is too thin the probe is registering some of the high temperatures of the oven ???  Dont know for sure what is happening, but I just don't find the device reliable on thinner cuts of meat, and the reading of the oven temperature is completely off regardless of the thickness of the meat.  The device is also very slow to react to changes in temperature.  This is definitely not an instant-read thermometer.
profile.summary: Probe reads too high when used on thinner cuts of meat, and reads ambient oven temp  too low by 50-75 degrees

profile.description: Love your team but hate those bleachers? Ever feel like you're the one who got tackled when the game's over? Now there's a better way!Watch the game from the comfort of your Ultra-Padded Stadium Seat. Compact and portable with a built in carrying handle and sturdy grip, this stadium seat is the lightest of its kind. Weighing in at a mere 7.6 pounds, this amazing seat can support up to 500 pounds without even breaking a sweat. With its padded back and 3 inch foam seat, you'll be so comfortable you won't want the game to end.Rubber strips on the bottom prevent the seat from sliding. A built-in bleacher hook provides added stability when sitting on wooden and metal bleachers and easily pivots out of the way to sit on the ground. Not just for game day, take your game day seat with you when you go camping, to the beach and outdoor concerts.
profile.reviewText:
This bleacher seat has a thick wedge of padding so it is very, very comfortable when sitting for a long period of time.  The construction is sturdy, and the back provides lot of support.  The seat worked great on both the open metal outdoor bleachers, and the closed wooden bleacher in the gym.  I couldn't use the hook on the indoor bleachers, but I didn't have any trouble with the seat sliding around.  I also used it in the living room movie night when I ran out of sofa space.  The person who got the short straw found it much more comfortable than sitting on the floor.

The only nits I have with the seat is the somewhat narrow width of the padded seat itself.  I admit that I am a little hippy (size 10-12) so the sides of my thighs flopped over the edge a little bit.  It wasn't uncomfortable, but just an embarrassing reminder that I need to lose some weight.  Also be aware that between the padding and the runners you are adding approximately 4 inches of height; so if you are short, your feet might not touch the ground when you sit on this seat.

So a nice, very comfortable seat that isn't just limited to the bleachers.
profile.summary: Seat a little narrow, but still comfortable  lots of other uses beside bleacher seat

profile.description: This Panasonic Cordless & Lightweight Upright Bagless Stick Vacuum Cleaner converts into a Hand-held Vac. It operates on DC 1.7V Ni-MH rechargeable battery.
profile.reviewText:
Ive had lots of stick vacuums over the years, and they all work pretty much the same: they clean up small messes with a minimum of fuss and effort.  But this Panasonic is a little different  it has this very cool and useful Edge Grabber.  My large vacuum has the Edge Grabber so when I saw this option on a stick vacuum I decided to buy the Panasonic over several other brands I was considering.

Ive been using it for a few weeks now, and Im very happy with it.  The suction is fine, and the charge last long a good 15-20 minutes at the High setting.  At 9 pounds this stick vacuum weighs more than my old stick, but it is easy to handle and almost effortless to use.  Even my 82 year old mother has no trouble pushing it around.  The vacuum is also attractive in a George Jetson, space-age kind of way.  The bright purple and sliver colors are bold, and the sinuous design is very eye-catching.

But my favorite thing about the vacuum is the Edge Grabber.  When you push the front of the vacuum against the wall (or furniture), the front bumper guard lifts up and allow the suction to reach all the way to the edge of the floor/carpet.  With this vacuum you don't need to run the crevice tool where the wall meets the floor.  The Edge Grabber is also great for sucking up those tiny spiders that like to live on my baseboards.  One nit with the Edge Grabber though is that it doesnt work as well against the shoe molding on the hard surface floors.  The grabber lifts much higher when you push it against something vertical.

So I like it.  It is probably my favorite stick vacuum so far.

Update 8-5-15: Dust bin is a little small and cumbersome to open.  You need to remove three pieces/parts to dump the dirt from the bin.
profile.summary: Love the Edge Grabber  great for getting spiders that hang out on the baseboards

profile.description: This yoga block from Gaiam is lightweight and provides the stability needed for optimal alignment, deeper poses and increased strength.
profile.reviewText:
I'm a newcomer to the art of yoga, and my normally sedentary body hasn't accepted the fact that I want it to twist, bend, and stretch.  On my own I cant even touch my finger tips to my floor, but with a yoga block I can essentially extend the reach of my fingertips and touch the floor.  The block gives this yoga newbie a great sense of accomplishment, and makes me feel more stable and secure in my poses.

As for this particular Gaiam Yoga Block, well it seems denser and a bit larger than the blocks I have used at the fitness center.  The Gaiam doesn't seem like it would flatten under my weight.  I also like the darker color because it doesn't show stains and dirt as much as the pastel colored ones.

The medallion embossed on the side of the block gives it an extra bit of flare and uniqueness.  But what is the design supposed to represent?  I looked online but couldn't find its meaning.  I tend to "see" strange things in abstract designs, so to me it looks like the upper body of a skeleton woman.  She has dots for eyes, nose and smiling mouth, a skinny neck, big, poofy hair, and she is surrounded by a field of leaves.  Strange.
profile.summary: The block gives this yoga newbie a great sense of accomplishment

profile.description: This cordless solder tool kit is great and offers hands-free operation. It has a safety switch that prevents inadvertant ignition and a fuel-level sight window. Use as a solder tool, heat tool or a torch tool. Kit includes: Soldering iron, conical tip 2.4 millimeters, chisel tip 2.4 millimeters, hot knife tip, deflector tip, sponge, wrench, and soldering wire.
profile.reviewText:
Stained Glass is one of my many hobbies so I have a few soldering irons hanging around my house, but this iron became the star of the shop because it was able to do what the other could not.  It saved a 100 year old stained glass window from crumbling away.  The window in question was in the attic dormer of a two story house with no electricity.  The window was too high for a ladder, and too far to safely reach with daisy-chained extension cords.

But with this butane powered soldering iron I was able to worm my way to the stained glass window, and quickly repair the failing solder joints.  The iron didn't get hot enough to do a proper bead, but it was hot enough to get a blob of molten solder onto the joints to keep them from failing completely.  Hopefully in a few months the window can be salvage and properly restored.

So thanks OTC, this butane soldering iron belongs in the tool chest of every handy-man.  It is multi-function, easy to use, and works great.
profile.summary: Great for an emergency fix to a stained glass window

profile.description: A quick installation and locking bar make the OC80T great for residential or commercial applications. Fits most 23 - 42 inch TVs and supports up to 80lbs (36.3 kg).
profile.reviewText:
I always thought wall mounted TVs looked dangerous, a hundred pounds of tubes, glass, and electronics hanging from an iron rod like a circus performer, but this OmniMount dispelled all my fears.  It took a little effort to install it on the wall (didn't have the right power tools so had to screw everything in by hand), but after it was up it wasn't going anywhere.  I even did a few (one) chin-up to prove to myself that the full extended arm would hold the weight of my ancient and very heavy Samsung 45" LCD.  And the OmniMount performed like a trooper.  It didn't budge under my 140+ pounds of dangling weight.  It didn't creak, groan or give any indications that it couldn't handle the weight.  After I was satisfied the TV wouldn't tumble off the wall and hurt my new hardwood floors, we attached the TV to the extended arm of the mount.  This was actually the hardest part of the whole process; it took three of us to lift the 95+ pounds of TV 7 feet in the air.  Don't try and do that part on your own.

After mounting the TV on the wall I played with the full motion features.  Pulled it out so the TV extended 18 inches from the wall.  Turn it left it could be seen from one room, turned it right to view from a different room, tilted it up and down to remove the harsh glare from the afternoon sun.  It was amazing how easy it was to adjust the TV to get the viewing angle just right.  In the end I just pushed the TV back so it was flush against the wall, but it is nice to know the maneuverability is available when/if needed.

So if you are the in the market for a TV wall mount, give this one a look.  It is sturdy, flexible, and will keep your high $$$ investment securely perched on the wall.
profile.summary: Rock Solid construction, sturdy enough to do chin-ups on

profile.description: Senior bodies are not all the same! Physical abilities can vary widely from one person to another, and even from day to day. This DVD has 3 complete yoga practices to meet the varying needs of people over 70. Level 1 (26 minutes) is done all seated in a chair, and emphasizes gentle movements to improve strength, range-of-motion, joint health, and posture, and works the body as fully as possible while sitting in a chair. Level 2 (40 minutes) alternates sitting in a chair, with standing alongside and holding onto a chair for stability. Level 2 works on developing strength and flexibility evenly throughout the entire body, and includes many easy movements to improve balance and increase foot, ankle and leg strength. Level 3 (55 minutes) also alternates sitting in a chair with standing, but is an overall stronger and longer practice than level 2, with more time spent on the standing and balancing poses. Level 3 is broken down into 6 shorter segments for greater choice. The goal of this DVD is to help seniors live fuller, more independent lives. Special emphasis is placed on working the muscles and joints most needed in everyday life and to prevent falls. All 3 practices emphasize good posture, full deep breathing, and end with a short relaxation and meditation for a more alert and relaxed body and mind. Filmed in the beautiful Bibler Gardens. Designed and taught by Jane Adams, RYT 500, a yoga practitioner since 1976 who specializes in yoga for healthy ageing.
profile.reviewText:
My 80 year-old mother had never done yoga so she was a little apprehensive when I gave her this DVD.  She was recuperating from major back surgery, and I wanted something gentle yet effective to supplement her sessions with the Physical Therapist.  At first she was fearful that this strange thing called yoga would damage her back, but to her surprise and relief Level 1 was filled with the same exercises that her therapist had her doing.

In Level 1 everything is done while sitting.  There are leg lifts and stretches, arm strengthening, neck and shoulder stretches, posture training.  All the exercises were perfect for her current abilities.  Being an avid gardener she was also delighted with the flowers and water feature that was the backdrop for the video. (She has added a visit to Bibler Gardens to her Bucket List!)  The cat wandering into the scene also gave her a chuckle.

We looked briefly at Level 2 & 3, but they are well beyond her current abilities.  But Mom is getting a little stronger every day, and I hope to ease her into Level 2 in a few weeks.

So thank you, Jane Adams, this DVD is a gem.
profile.summary: Level 1 is perfect for older seniors (the 80+ crowd), Levels 2 & 3 are perfect for us younger seniors

profile.description: The UV guardian roller shade lets your little passenger take in the view without the harsh glare. The opti-view mesh blocks over 85% of harmful UV rays, while protecting your baby's delicate skin. With adjustable clip attachments, it's super easy to have a perfect fit on nearly any window shape.
profile.reviewText:
This shade is great at blocking out the sun while still allowing you to see through it. It is also easy to attach to the window either with the suction cups or the clips that slide over the edge of the window. But there are a few things that I don't like about it. For one it is very bulky. The casing at the top (the part that the shade rolls up into) is huge, and unless your window is perfectly square you have to slant the casing at a weird angle to get it to fit. This can create huge gaps between the shade and the door frame that allows the light to get into the car. The casing also tended to tap against the window and the metal door frame creating an annoying rattle.

So this shade has some good points and bad points. If you have a car with square windows it will work great, but if your windows are sloped or rounded you might not be completely satisfied.
profile.summary: Bulky and tends to rattle. Works better on cars with square windows

profile.description: Perfect for dorms and apartments close to metropolitan areas, Mohu Basic 25 is the best value for a basic indoor antenna. The Mohu Basic 25 TV antenna can receive free broadcast High Definition TV signals from Over-the-Air broadcasters in crystal clear 1080 HD. It's a fast and easy introduction to the world of Free TV. Place the Basic 25 indoor HDTV antenna high on the wall, plug it into the back of your TV, and scan with your television. This digital TV antenna has a small design that delivers full 1080p HD to any digital-ready television. The combination of its unobtrusive design and powerful reception capabilities make the Mohu Basic 25 HDTV antenna a top choice in any home. There are no exposed or distracting television antenna parts. The Mohu Basic 25 HD antenna for TV can be easily hidden behind a bookshelf, or television. An ideal digital antenna for HDTV, Basic 25 is a great solution for those looking to cut the cable cord.
profile.reviewText:
Nothing sadder than hooking up an antenna and watching the No Signal notice float around the screen.  This little Mohu 25 antenna was easy to hookup and mount in a window, but it only picked up 2 of the 25 channels available in my area.  And strangely the 2 channels it did pick up weren't even from the closest towers.  All the towers are less than 20 miles away (closest just 3 miles away), and the terrine is completely flat with no tall buildings to obstruct the signal.  I even took the TV and antenna outside to test, and a while a few new channels did briefly flash, the antenna couldn't hold the signal.

I have an old TERK amplified antenna that works fine and picks up all the stations, but it is not very attractive.  In fact it looks like some kind of prehistoric creature with a spiny tail and long antenna spikes.  I wanted to replace the TERK with the smaller, sleeker looking Mohu 25, but no such luck.  Guess Ill keep my pet stegosaurus.
profile.summary: No Signal, No Signal, No Signal

profile.description: Performance micro solid gabardine straight fit plain front slack
profile.reviewText:
First off these Haggar pants were very nice.  The fabric is lightweight, and has a smooth, cool feel when you touch it.  Stitching is nice and uniform and the seam are expertly finished.  They look very sleek and professional.

And the garment care label was a learning experience.  The label has the normal stuff: wash in warm water, tumble dry low, yada, yada, yada, but then it has a blurb Do Not Use  Fabric Softener or Drier Sheets (yes they put Drier Sheets on the label and not Dryer Sheets).  I did some googling and found that fabric softener and dryer sheets are the enemy of microfiber fabrics.  Guess Ive been living under a rock because I didn't know that.  I know you are not supposed to use the fabric softener and dryer sheets on baby and kids stuff because if harms the fire retardant coating, but what does a dryer sheet do to microfiber?  Well apparently the fabric softener and dryer sheets reduce the ability of the microfiber to wick moisture and breathe.  It also clogs the pores of microfiber towels and keeps them from sucking up water and dirt.

You learn something new every day.
profile.summary: Learning experience in a garment care label  No fabric softener or dryer sheets

profile.description: Kids can create their own kitchen scenario-the kitchen island has a dishwasher on one side and room to sit and share a meal on the other! This kitchen is fully equipped with a double-open oven (and slide-out cookie tray), a cool fridge and a tray of food. Role play becomes even more real when little homemakers press the pendant light on the kitchen island to see what's cookin', then press the stove to hear the sizzle sounds and the bubbling sound of coffee brewing!
profile.reviewText:
This kitchen set is so cute.  It has a ton of features to keep a child (or an adult) mesmerized.

The kitchen island piece has a light that turns on when you press a button, the stove makes sounds like frying eggs and a timer going off when you touch the controls, and the coffee maker makes a few sounds when you press it (kind of sounds like a cappuccino machine).  The dishwasher door opens to expose a decal showing a dishwasher stuffed with things.  The counter top looks like granite, and there is a goose neck faucet.

The refrigerator/stove piece doesnt have any lights or sounds, but there are some moving parts.  The trash can opens.  The oven doors open and you can slide out two trays.  One tray has a turkey dinner on it and the other tray has cookies. The refrigerator and freezer doors open too, but I was a little disappointed with the interiors.  There are plastic objects inside (eggs, fruit, ice, eggs, etc) but everything is just solid white, no color whatsoever.

But other than a bland refrigerator interior this set is great.  And it fits perfectly in the Loving Family Dollhouse.
profile.summary: So cute, love the lights, love the sounds, love all the doors that open and close

top_5.description: Etta Says! Duck Jerky, From All Natural American Farms! These yummy Duck Jerkey treats will melt in yer mouth, so make sure your hoomans git plenty of em'. Tell your hooman that this Duck Jerky is made with whole Duck and preserved naturally, has no artificial fillers, coloring, preservatives, or by-products. I'm pure bred American dog, and 12 or so out of the 10 dogs I surveyed prefer home-grown treats. Paws down...imports stink! My treats are 100% natural. These treats are the perfect size for any pooch. Taste is in the tongue of the beholder. And I be holdin' the best treats this side of the Pacific!
top_5.reviewText:
I have a VERY picky Chihuahua, and she gobbles these things up.

I used to buy her Waggin Train's Duck Jerky, but I threw the whole bag away after reading the negative reviews on consumer affairs.  I was hunting for a new duck jerky treat, when I found this brand.

They arrived quickly from Amazon, but when I opened the package I was a little startled.  I was expecting flat pieces of meat, but these are shaped like round, thin tubes.  They remind me of Pup-Peroni(which my dog won't eat).

But Peanut could care less about the shape, all she cares about is the great taste.  And all I care about is that they are made in the US, contain no grain, and are made from healthy stuff.

The ingredient list is: Duck, Turkey, Potato Flour, Pea Protein, Chicken, Tapioca Starch, Glycerin, Pea Flour, Sorbitol, Pinto Beans, Pork Gelatin, Potato Starch, Salt, soy Lecithin, Phosphoric Acid, Potassium Sorbate, Citric Acid, Caramel Color, Mixed Tocopherols, Rosemary Extract.
top_5.summary: Look like sausages not jerky, but regardless of the shape my dog loves them

top_5.description: Quick Shipping !!! New And Sealed !!! This Disc WILL NOT play on standard US DVD player. A multi-region PAL/NTSC DVD player is request to view it in USA/Canada. Please Review Description.
top_5.reviewText:
I really enjoyed Season 1 of this TV show.  It was quirky, unique, and a lot of fun.  Parts of it were over-the-top, but it was funny in its outlandishness.  I finished watching the 10th episode, and was amazed that every story arc ended in a cliff-hanger.  What was going to happen to the people inside the bunker, and more important how were the people outside the bunker going to survive?  Is Jamie the Son of God, or is he a prophet like Moses (well Jamie did part the Thames).

After the last episode I went to find out when Season 2 would start, and much to my disappointment I discovered that the show had had been CANCELED.  There would be no Season 2.  The cliff-hangers would never be resolved.  If I had known that, I never would have watched the first season.

So now I am left with all these unanswered questions.  Maybe SyFi will pick it up and produce a Season 2.
top_5.summary: Canceled  there will be no Season 2, and Season 1 ended with monumental cliff-hangers

top_5.description: Pet the Hair Away! Great for all Dogs & Cats. Your pet will love the True Touch Five Finger Deshedding Glove! It mimics the loving touch of your hand for a relaxing massage and includes 180 soft silicone grooming tips to groom your pet with ease. The hair sticks to the glove, making it easy to peel and throw away. Minimize shedding and keep your house clean with the True Touch Deshedding Glove.
top_5.reviewText:
I have to say that this glove works really well at gathering the loose hair from my long-haired Chihuahua.  I never considered her a shedder until I saw what accumulated on this glove after just a few minutes.  Her hair is white and apricot so it is very noticeable against the dark blue and black of the glove.  Most of the hair accumulated on the finger sections of the glove, and it was easy to clean the hair from the glove by just pulling on section loose and watching the rest of the hair mat follow.

But as much as I like the glove, my Chihuahua doesnt seem care for it.  When I gently stroke her body with the nubby, rubber tips of the glove she turns and gives me a hurt look.  Eventually she will squirm to get away.  So if you have a larger dog with a thick coat, the stroke of this glove might be soothing; but for a 4 lbs dog with long fine hair and sensitive skin, this glove is a little too rough.
top_5.summary: Works really well at gathering hair, but dog gives me a hurt look when I use it on her

top_5.description: AmazonBasics brings you everyday items at a great value. An Amazon Brand.
top_5.reviewText:
I have a long commuter van ride to work, and this pillow makes sleeping/relaxing in the van a little easier.  This pillow is large enough to support and cushion my back when I lean against the window, and it puffy enough to support my head when I snag a bench seat to myself and can lay down flat.

The pillow is made of an airtight vinyl fabric shell that is filled with quarter-sized pieces of foam.  The foam moves freely inside the fabric shell, so the shape of the pillow can be twisted and flatted to suite your needs. When you want to store the pillow you roll it into a tight tube which forces the air out of the bag and creates a vacuum inside, rolling up the pillow also compresses the foam pieces to a fraction of their normal size.  To inflate the pillow you open the air valve which allows air to flow into the pillow and also allows the foam pieces to expand from their compressed shape.  It takes a little strength to roll up the bag and force all the air out, but the inflation process is effortless.

The fabric used to make it pillow is nice.  It has a soft, slick feel that reminds me of microfiber.  The fabric is also semi-waterproof.  If water splashes on the fabric the water will bead and roll off, but if the water sits for more than a few seconds the fabric will absorb the water (but the fabric does dry quickly).

The only thing I don't like about the pillow is that the fabric makes these crinkling, plastic sounding noises when you touch it.  A noisy pillow is not an issue when it is being used in a creaky van barreling 80 mph down the highway, but if you are covertly trying to catch a few Zzzs in your cubicle at work, a noisy pillow is a dead giveaway.
top_5.summary: Comfortable, but a little noisy  makes crinkling sounds when you touch it

top_5.description: The Perfect Solution for Households with Pets.
top_5.reviewText:
I was pleasantly surprised with the power and suction of this Dirt Devil Pet vacuum.  I have a small Chihuahua who likes to hide her dry kibbles/treats on the carpet and this vacuum had no trouble sucking up her hidden treasures.  The vacuum also did an excellent job picking up the hair.  I never knew she shed so much until I saw all the hair whirling around in the clear canister.  (With my previous bag vacuum the amount of hair was hidden from view.)

Things I like about the vacuum:

  Suction is great.  It had no trouble picking up dirt, hair, and cheerios.

  The Dirt Cup is easy to empty.

But there are a few things that I don't like about the vacuum.

  The vacuum requires a lot of assembly, and the instructions are missing some important steps.  Step 2 has you attaching the dirt cup, but my dirt cup just wouldn't stay attached.  Every time I attached it, it would fall off.  Finally I realized that I needed to install the filter and filter cover first and then attach the dirt cup.  The instructions never mentioned that part!  Step 4 is another "winner".  It has you securing the handle to the back panel of the vacuum using a long screw, but after attaching the handle to the body the "screw" has nothing to screw into!  The instructions forget to mention that there is another plastic doodad that straddles the handle and the front of the vacuum.  The screw gets inserted through the handle and back panel and INTO the plastic doodad.  I think Dirt Devil needs to spend a little more time and effort on the assembly instructions.

  The headlight is dim.  Half the time I can't even tell if it is on.

  The Pet Power Brush tool has a special clamp that allows you to store the attachment when not in use, but it keeps falling off.  The clamp is not strong enough to hold it in place when the vacuum is being pushed around.

  There is a little clamp on the handle that is supposed to hold the cord and keep it out of the way.  But like the Power Brush clamp is not strong enough and the cord keeps pulling free.

  The power cord and the hose are a little short.

  The On/Off pedal and the Handle Release Pedal feel a little flimsy.  I haven't had any problems with them yet, but I hold my breath every time I press them.

So this Dirt Devil has a few little flaws, but it excels in the most important feature: SUCTION.  This vacuum will pick up anything!

profile.reviewText:
I recommend this movie.  It deserves its four stars.

I was one of the thousands of reenactors who helped make the movie in 1992.  I'll give you a true story.  You'll see rows of cannons shooting.  That's real.  Did you know those cannons shot down the radio controlled helicopter that was used to carry camera equipment?  It was the third film take of the Confederate cannon barrage for Picket's charge.  The day was hot, long, and filming was not going well.  The helicopter flew down the line taking pictures of the cannons going off.  Instead of flying to the end of the cannons the controller put the helicopter right in front of the cannon muzzle as it went off.  The blast knocked the helicopter out of the sky.  So, in 1992 a Confederate cannon crew shot down a helicopter.

Facts, this movie is fairly accurate.  It's not perfect.  They could not show the fighting on Cememtary Hill nor the skirmishing on the forth day.  However, it's accurate and most of us extras spent nearly $1000 ('92 dollars) on getting the correct clothing and equipment.

The one fact that you'll like in this movie is it shows the desperate fighting on Little Round Top.  Yep, the only thing that saved this republic was a Union colonel who used to be a school teacher and his little regiment of Maine Infantry.  Did you know that the US Army considers this "small unit action" to be one of the defining moments in history?  I will not give away how it goes.  However, Jeff Daniels is in his prime and does a fantastic job of capturing the mood of the moment.

I did not like Martin Sheen as Robert E. Lee.  That costs a star.

The rest of the movie is pretty good.  Now, this movie isn't as good as the movie that defined the type: Glory.  Glory is a rare five star movie and it will go down as a classic of the age.  However, this movie is far better than the prequel, "God's and Generals".  You can get this movie for $6 on discount and you'll watch it every once in a while.  I would use this movie for school instruction on Civil War history.  Historically it's fairly accurate.  It only has a PG-13 rating.  If you used "Glory" some people may get upset over the very strong words in that movie.

I got this movie on discount.  If you look for a flying fence post at Picket's charge you'll see me, a small "reb" who is sprinting by the fence.

Help me justify my past excesses to my wife.  Buy this DVD :)

I hope you enjoy this DVD.
profile.summary: A very good Civil War movie

profile.reviewText:
Mr. McBride has written a book that nearly perfectly talks about what can be expected from a modern infantry man.  He talks about sniping, putting in a properly sighted machine gun, raids, and patrols.  Honestly, this book is so good that most Army ROTC and Marine Infantry instruction may want to have their future officers and NCO candidates read this book.

I will give you a story that really stuck me as being ahead of its time.  Now, this book was written in the mid-1930s.  However, Mr. McBride knows the problems of lugging ammunition.  A soldier with .303 British (about equal to modern NATO 7.62 ammo) could only carry about 200 to 300 rounds.  So, Mr. McBride thinks the armies should carry ammunition of about .27 caliber.  That is almost exactly 6.8 mm.  This is exactly the same solution the US Army discovered after 5 years in Iraq.

I liked this book.  Mr. McBride thinks both the British and Canadian Armies did much better with their training time than the US military.  Indeed, he thinks the US Army and military is overly tied up with paperwork.  And that observation was made in 1918.

This is a five star book by a soldier who knows his field craft.  Pay attention to his anti-sniper traps.  They are still useful today.  Also, the book is great for telling about how the Germans would leave abandoned grenades after an attack.  Some were rigged to go off if picked up.

As written before, this book is five star.  Mr. McBride writes a book about the birth of the modern infantry man.  Indeed, their is little difference between a Tommy of WWI with a Lewis gun and a Grunt in Vietnam carrying an M-60 machinegun.  In 50 years little had changed.

The modern professional soldier can learn a lot from this book.  Some university military history departments may want this book for an individual study of a hard infantry man.
profile.summary: Excellent book for the soldier's craft:  infantry

profile.reviewText:
I both scratch build models and study US Naval history.  This book gives excellent reasons why the US rebuilt its seapower after the 20 suspension of Naval building following the American Civil War.
One of the best parts of this book is Dr. Friedman includes are the "post civil war" monitors in the design history.  Monitors are not battleships in a proper sense.  However, Dr. Friedman's giving them a seperate chapter does show that he concluded, correctly, that the Monitors were considered capital ships up until the time of the Spanish-American war.
Furthermore, Dr. Friedman pulls no punches regarding the short comings of American ships.  In words, American ships are slow and were often 2rd class in design.  But, he defends the reasons why the US Navy kept the old triple expansion steam engine rather than going over to the HMS Dreadnought type steam turbines.  American ships had severe design limitations imposed by the US Congress and the operational requirements of having to steam far distances to the Southern Pacific area.  So, American ships were designed for long distances and economy, not speed.  No other navy in the world had such different design requirements forced upon them.  The fact of the matter is a small battleship, such as the c. 1910 era USS Michigan, had a greater range than most Royal Navy ships of the same era on much less tonnage.  But, the cost of this is the USS Michigan could only steam at 18 knots rather than the 22 knots the typical post Dreadnought Class British Battleship.
Dr. Friedman goes into detail about the problems of the last ten America battleships.  The North Carolina class had a bad vibration problem.  On paper they looked better than the British KGV class.  However, the NC class had vibration problems and powder handling would have been deemed unacceptable by the Royal Navy.  Indeed, the powder problems come to haunt America in 1989.  The Alabama class was excessively crampted by any standard and that class was seen merely as a war expedient.  The Iowa nearly failed as a design because the turret design was not reconciled with the hull design.  Bluntly, the turret almost didn't fit on the Iowa and this nearly led to the failure of the class.  Also, a torpedo hit on the North Carolina led the US Navy to nearly "blister" the Iowa class.  However, the fast battleship's speed would have fallen to 30 knots:  the US navy was unwilling to give up the speed for protection.
From a ship scratch building point-of-view, there are few other better publicans than this one.  Presently, this writer is working on the USS Kearsarge, launched c. 1900 and modeling fit will be from 1912.  Dr. Friedman give reasons for the Kearsarge's ununusual design (and why no other nation followed it) and then why the ship was rebuilt in the 1912 era.
This reviewer didn't mind the lact of follow-up to the end-of-the-battleships.  The battleships in 1980 were seen as an inexpensive way to bring back massive firepower into the US Navy.  However, the 1989 explosion in the US Iowa was caused by poor powder handling techniques.  Also, American logistics could not afford the maintenance costs of the battleships.  In addition, technology had passed the guns of the battleships.  Modular type warships using evolved US Army MRLS rocket systems may be the future of ship-to-shore attack (litorial conflict).  The US Naval Institute publication, "Proceedings" had an extensive article on the demise of return of the Battleship in 2000.  Dr. Friedman could only follow up the rebuilding battleships in the 1980s era with the nearly as quick exit of the battleship in the post Gulf War era.
This reviewer is not a US Navy Veteran.  However, I have done a fair amount of study of American sea power.  Dr. Friedman sets the standard for writing on American Naval Ship design.  This review owns four of Dr. Friedmans "Illustrated" series and has read every one of them.
No reader of Dr. Friedman will come away disappointed.  Dr. Friedman is an excellent writer.
My only wish to to meet the man in real life.  It would be a great honor.
profile.summary: A very fine addition to your library

profile.reviewText:
The American cruiser was an odd ship for the United States Navy.  The cruisers most Americans know of are the "Treaty Cruisers" which first started with the Pennsicola class (or egg shells armed with hammers) and the cruiser class ended with the USS Long Beach, the first and last true missle cruiser for the US Navy.
Dr. Friedman makes it clear the first cruisers were inspired by the old American civil war frigates.  The first cruisers were designed as commerice raiders, scouts, and minor capital ships.  This is not much different than the initial days of the US Navy in the 1790 era.
However, the US Navy takes a different view of the Spanish American war and produces a group of post-war cruisers that have interesting design characterists.  They are slower, more expensive, and have greater weight than foreign ships.
American cruiser design goes into a sort of hybernation from about 1906 until 1918 when the Omaha class is invented.  American cruisers in WWI were left over ships from the Spanish American war or oddly designed ships, such as the over gunned & over armored USS Pennsylvania & Tennessee class armored cruisers.
The Treaty cruisers of the 20s and 30s are the halcyon days of cruisers.  Actually, a proper technical term for cruisers are "small, light, very fast battleships".
Dr. Friedman writes that none of the Treaty cruisers are bad designs.  Yes, there is stability problems but that is from treaty limits on warship weight and not from bad designs from the US Navy.  Indeed, the Cleveland & Baltimore class cruisers are some of the most outstanding designed cruisers from WWII.  The incorporation of the Combat Information Center (CIC) was the point where the US Navy was able to integrate the full use of ships, weapons, command, and control and beat the Japanese navy in every battle post 1943.
The cruiser mission largely died after WWII.  Basically, most of the cruisers were either converted to missile cruisers, a job that was taken over by the later frigates.  Else, cruisers were used for shore bombardment.
Dr. Friedman takes a reader from the start of the New Navy, the 1900s era of cruisers, the treaty cruisers, the war production cruisers (basically, improved Brooklyns), the non-treaty cruisers which become the Alaska battlecruisers (the only new battlecruisers made during WWII), the post war cruisers, and ends the book on cruisers with a near chapter devoted to the Long Beach.
It's almost with sadness that Dr. Friedman writes that the augmented Spruance destroyer - the Ticonderga class cruiser - is a successor to the real cruiser.  The destroyer & the frigate have taken over the job of the cruiser.  And the true cruiser had been with the United States Navy since its inception back in the founding days of the republic.
Yes, this book is 10 out of 10.  A novice will go away with a understanding of Cruisers.  A Navy man will appreciate his roots.
Dr. Friedman is one of the best writers of technical material in America.  If you buy this book, like I did, it will start to show wear from constant use.
profile.summary: American Cruisers:  the designs from beginning to end

profile.reviewText:
Retribution is every bit as good as Max Hasting's previous book, Armageddon.  Also, a person gets the story that in 1944 the issue of the war against Japan was still somewhat in doubt.  Hastings breaks the book down into three main themes.  First, there is the two part American offensive against Japan by both the Army and Navy.  Second, there is the British action against the Japanese in Southwestern Asia.  Third, the last theme is about several different subjects.

As in the allied book Armageddon, Retribution can get to be a little ghastly.  The reader is given a small paragraph on the horror of war on about every fifty page.  Strangely, both the Americans and Japanese are just as barbaric towards one another as the Germans and Soviets were to one another in the Eastern front of the European war.  One British commander tells a soldier driving a jeep to remove a skull from it.  The reason is not empathy with Japan but the fact the British lost thousands in the great retreats in early '42 and the worry was it would be a British soldier's skull decorating the jeep.

Retribution does a fair job of explaining the scope of the US Navy's win during the "Great Mariana's Turkey Shoot".  In the intensive aerial combat during the Battle of Britain, perhaps 65 aircraft were shot down on both sides per day.  The US Navy destroyed well over 450 aircraft during the Battle of the Phillippines sea in just one day.  In the space of a few days Japan's carriers were made impotent by American air power.  With the exception of the debacle with Taffy 3, the US Naval operations are textbook .

The book pretty much follows this formula of British War, American War, and allied subjects.  The individual subjects covered in the book range from the poor Chinese military leadership, the basic ineffectiveness of the 14th Air Force (formerly the AVG), how Australian went from being on the front lines against Japan to an inglorious end to the war, the British Navy's setting in the sun, the very overdone US Navy's build up during the war, and dozens of other Pacific war related subjects.

What makes this book important is it shows that most historians fail to understand is it was the B-29 SYSTEM that lead to the nuclear bombing of the Japanese cities.  The atomic bombs were not the end all or be all of weapons.  The atomic bombs were merely a part of an arsenal of weapons to attack Japan.  These weapons ranged from plain bombs to fire bombs to very complex anti-ship mines.  The American taxpayer had put billions of dollars (1940 era) into the ultimate bomber system.  Max Hastings makes it very clear the B-29 was both an expensive weapons system and it was somewhat ineffective.  B-17 and B-24 bombers operating from Iwo Jima and Okinawa could have done the same job as the B-29 and at a fraction of the cost.  This fact is lost on the anti-nuclear weapons critics.  It was not the building of the bombs that demanded their use in war.  It was the making of the most expensive bomber system in the world that forced the B-29 owners to use any weapon to justify the extremely high cost of the program.

If a reader gets anything from the book it should be the understanding that it was the B-29 that begat the nuclear age.  So much money was spent on the B-29 program that the US Army Air Force had to use nearly any weapon to justify the huge cost of the project.

This book also explained why Russia and China relationships soured by 1973.  When the Soviets invaded Manchuria in August of 1945 their soldiers acted as barbarically to the local Chinese as they had to the Germans in '44 to '45.  The seeds of the Chinese/American pacts of 1973 were sown by raping and pillaging Soviet solders in 1945.

That is the biggest difference between Armageddon and Retribution:  Armageddon is the end of the story; the Great European war of 1914 to 1945 was over.  Retribution is actually the beginning of an era; the advent of an independent South East Asia.  From India to Vietnam, from China to the Philippines, all these nations can count WWII as the milestone on their road to independence or self determination.
profile.summary: Best End of the Asian War Book
