profile.description: Stevie Nicks, rock's superstar chanteuse, performs her signature songs with Rock and Roll Hall of Famer Fleetwood Mac and her acclaimed solo career on Live In Chicago. Recorded at her October 2007 'Soundstage' performance.
profile.reviewText:
"The Soundstage Sessions" is being tagged as Stevie Nicks' first ever live album, this is only partially true. The songs contained on the CD are the live versions (with some post production) from the live DVD, however all of the crowd noises have been removed making the songs sound like new studio recordings. The songs were all pulled from Stevie's 2007 Soundstage show recorded while on her "Crystal Visions" tour. There are a couple new songs on the set, both covers. The first is the Dave Matthews song "Crash" and Stevie sings it from a woman's perspective making it her own. The other cover is Bonnie Raitt's "Circle Dance" done here a duet with Vanessa Carlton.
 The stand out tracks for me are "Stand Back", "Landslide" (using a different vocal than what is on the DVD), "How Still My Love" and "Beauty & The Beast". All songs on the CD have a punch that is missing from the original recordings. The only song that I feel doesn't quite hold up well is "Sara", a Fleetwood Mac classic and a personal favorite but Stevie's voice just isn't able to handle the delicate nature of the song anymore. However "Beauty & The Beast" (another personal favorite) makes the set worth the price at any cost.
profile.summary: Powerful updates to her classics

profile.description: Dolly Parton Has Few Peers, And No One In Music Will Deny Her Powers As A Singer, A Storyteller And A Pop Star. From Her First National Hit In 1967, The Ironically Titled 'Dumb Blonde' (Nobody With A Lick Of Sense Ever Accused Dolly Of That!) And The Legendary '70s Duets With Porter Wagoner, From Her First Number One Single ('Joshua') In 1970 To Her 26th Number One In 1991 ('Rockin' Years,' A Duet With Ricky Shelton) And All Train Stops In Between, Dolly Has It All. 'To Know Him Is To Love Him' From The Fertile Three-Way Collaboration With Linda Ronstadt And Emmylou Harris, The Amazing Crossover Pop Smashes, Including The Heartfelt Duet With Kenny Rogers 'Islands In The Stream,' As Well As Revered Juke Box Staples '9 To 5' And 'Here You Come Again,' This 101 Track/4 Cd Treasure Trove Covers All The Bases. You May Never Have To Leave Home Again, But If You Do, Be Sure To Take Dolly Along For The Ride. First-Ever Multi-Label, Career-Spanning Box Set For Dolly! 4 Cds, Over 100 Songs Includes Her Biggest Hits, Rarities, And Duets From Monument, Rca Victor, And Columbia + Seven Previously Unreleased Songs Introduction Written By Singer-Songwriter Laura Cantrell, And New Liner Notes Written By Noted Dolly Parton Historian Holly George-Warren Features Never-Before-Seen Photos And Rare Memorabilia! All The Big Hits, Including Jolene, 9 To 5, Coat Of Many Colors, Joshua, I Will Always Love You. Rarities And Previously Unreleased Tracks.
profile.reviewText:
For years Dolly fans have been waiting for a definitive boxed set from her. "Dolly" comes pretty close to being just that. With 99 tracks spread across four CD's there is an awful lot to like here. The set starts off with her very first recording "Puppy Love" and goes up thru 1992's "Romeo". Along the way are her solo hits as well as her duets with Porter Wagoner. The set follows her career from the small GoldBand record label thru her stay at Columbia, the main focus being of course her long tenure with RCA. The set begins with a string of early singles recorded for Monument Records when Dolly was being pushed towards a Brenda Lee/girl group sound. The songs are catchy, but nothing like what she would eventually find fame with. After that and her connection with Porter Wagoner do the really great songs start coming. All of the hits are her from "Jolene" and "Joshua" to "I Will Always Love You", "Here You Come Again" and of course "9 to 5". Not to mention some great album cuts like "The Bridge", "Down From Dover" and many more.
 For as great as the set is, there are few complaints. First is the fact that it ends in 1992. Dolly has continued to release some incredible records since then (such as her fantastic bluegrass albums from the past decade). Another complaint is that the massively successfull "Trio" album with Emmylou Harris and Linda Ronstadt is not represented at all. Despite having tons of great tracks, it's a shame they couldn't find room for her 1983 song "Appalachian Memories" one of her masterpieces. Finally, disc four is the least interesting of the bunch, the songs on disc four have been reissued so many times over the past several years that the disc is pretty redundant.
 Complaints aside this is the best collection of Dolly's work out there. It's not THE definitive set, but it is the best there is. A treat for long time fans as well as those who may be just now discovering Dolly.
profile.summary: The best Dolly box out there, but still not definitive...

profile.description: From First Edition to his '70s and '80s pop and country smashes to his recent #1 Buy Me a Rose (with Alison Krauss and Billy Dean), here are 40 of Kenny's classics plus two new songs: his pop Top 10s Just Dropped In (to See What Condition My Condition Was In); Lucille; Coward of the County; Don't Fall in Love with a Dreamer (with Kim Carnes); Lady; I Don't Need You; Islands in the Stream (with Dolly Parton); We've Got Tonight (with Sheena Easton), and more!
profile.reviewText: This is a great collection with all of Kenny's hits in one nice package. The boxed set is great too, but you have lots of album cuts mixed in there. This is great if you just want the hits. Pretty much every song of Kenny's you could want is here. Kicking off with five tracks from his days with the First Edition then it goes into the slew of hits he had in the 70's. The duets are here, the recent hits are here. A great collection. Only one flaw, "Daytime Friends" is credited as a duet with Dottie West, it isn't, it never was. A typo so if you thought you were getting something rare, you're not. Other than that, a great collection!
profile.summary: Great collection with all the hits!

profile.description: Sandra Halliburton is a successful management consultant in the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries. Her interest in Ms. Nicks life grew not only out of a love for her music, but from the inspiration of Stevie's social contributions to heart disease research as both women lost their fathers to the disease, Sandra in 1995 and Ms. Nicks in 2005.
profile.reviewText: This book is one of the most difficult biographies to read. It's not written in chronological order, the chapters jump all over the place, subject matter changes without warning. It reads as if it was written by a junior high school english student writing a report the morning before it was due. ALL quotes in the book come from previously published interviews. Timelines and facts are wrong. Certain events get nothing more than a mere sentence at the end of a chapter. For instance Fleetwood Mac's induction into the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame in 1998 is mentioned in one sentence in the chapter about the "Say You Will" album from 2003. The author uses different interviews from different years to tell the stories and the result is often disjointed and confusing. The whole thing is a mess. Stevie's life story is interesting for sure, this book just isn't the one to tell it. If you know nothing at all about Stevie I suppose you might find something in the book, but if you've been a fan for any length of time, you will be very disappointed.
profile.summary: This book is a complete mess!!

profile.description: Raven presents the defining collection of ROSANNE CASH, an unstoppable force on the US Country charts throughout the 1980s and early 1990s. This unique, deluxe compilation includes all her big hits, key album tracks and rarities in a stunning career-defining, 21-track, 77-minute overview. Includes her Number 1 single-only version of the Beatles' I Don't Want To Spoil The Party, her Rodney Crowell Number 1 duet It's Such A Small World, and her stunning versions of Joni Mitchell's River and Doc Pomus' I Count the Tears. Her commercial and critical successes, deft commerciality and harrowing honesty are all included in this indispensable package.
profile.reviewText:
I first became a big fan of Rosanne Cash with her "Rhythm And Romance" album, an album that is still a big favorite of mine. Her "King's Record Shop" is also a big fav. Several years ago Columbia put out a Hits collection for Rosanne, it was good, but was missing one song in particular that I really love, her #4 hit from 1982, "Ain't No Money". This new import collection includes that song along with 20 others, including all of her #1 country hits. I'm surprised that Sony hasn't issued an "Essential" album for Rosanne yet, perhaps this album will give them the boost they need. This set is missing a track or two that should have made the cut, "Hold On" from 1986, but for the most part it's a nice upgrade from the previous "Greatest Hits" collection. It is the best collection of Rosanne's work out there right now however. It also has a 12 page booklet full of photos and info about Rosanne and each track.
 The track listing is as follows:
Right or Wrong, No Memories Hangin''Round, Anybody's Darlin', Seven Year Ache, My Baby Thinks He's A Train, Blue Moon With Heartache, Ain't No Money, I Wonder, I Don't Know Why You Don't Want Me, Never Be You, The Way We Make A Broken Heart, Tennessee Flat Top Box, Runaway Train, I Don't Want To Spoil The Party, If You Change Your Mind, It's Such A Small World, Dance With The Tiger, What We Really Want, Sleeping In Paris, River, I Count The Tears
profile.summary: The best hits package available

profile.description: This BLACK+DECKER PP610 10" corded pole saw offers a powerful 6.5 Amp motor for your most demanding cuts; motor is inline which allows for for direct pruning and clear line of sight . It also features a 10" premium bar and chain for improved cutting performance on larger branches. An automatic oiling system ensures constant bar and chain lubrication, and it has a clear oil window that allows the user to easily gauge the oil level. This saw also includes a sturdy 9.5' Extend pole for high hanging or hard to reach branches. At only 8lbs, the lightweight design of this saw allows for easy control and maneuverability.
profile.reviewText: The Black and Decker pole saw is very easy to use and actually kind of fun. Basically if you can use a weed whacked you can handle this pole saw. The poles extends out and retracts and then locks into place depending on how far you need it to reach. I was cutting three inch branches to try it out and had no problem at all. I didn't have any thicker branches to cut, so I'm not sure how it handles the thicker stuff, but it's pretty sturdy so I don't see a problem. The only limitation I found was the length of my extension cord. Other than that this is a great and handle little saw to have around.
profile.summary: Very easy and fun to use!

profile.description: From Michael Bay, the producer of "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre," comes the true story of Amityville. In November 1974, a family of six was brutally murdered. Now, a year later, an unsuspecting young couple, George (Ryan Reynolds, "Blade: Trinity," "The
profile.reviewText:
I was very much looking forward to this new version of "The Amityville Horror". I liked the original and was hoping that this would be better than that. It's not. The acting is much better but that's about it. I think the original was far scarier and seemed to hold together better. In this new version the last half of the movie seems to totally fall apart. It's also interesting to note that nearly every religious element of the movie has been stripped away. The original had many religious scenes in it, of which only one remains in this new take. As I said the acting is far better this time around. But the changes made to the "true" story are just stretched too far. The scenes that made the original so scary are no longer part of the story, the glowing red eyes, the red room in the cellar, the linking of George Lutz to Ronnie DeFeo, even the blood dripping down the walls, all are not part of this telling. Some elements are briefly touched on, but most are gone altogether.

 I was hoping for so much more. I loved how they updated "The Texas Chainsaw Massacre" and was hoping the same would happen this time around. Not so. No one is expected to believe that what you are seeing in "The Amityville Horror" is at all true despite was is claimed. I suppose for a modern haunted house flick it's not bad. The original was creepier though. Read the book though to be really creeped out.
profile.summary: Acting is better this time around.

profile.description: With the phenomenal success of her 1970 single Rose Garden, Lynn Anderson was launched into the ranks of country and pop superstardom. The Grammy Award-winning singer s string of No. 1 hits made her a chart fixture in the 1970s, and, indeed, one of the most successful artists of all time. Among her most beloved recordings is 1971 s The Christmas Album, which arrived on Columbia Records while Lynn was still riding high from the worldwide success of Rose Garden. Christmas Album, produced in Nashville by her then-husband Glenn Sutton, featured Music City s A-team of musicians on a festive collection of both familiar and original yuletide tunes. In addition to her spirited revivals of Frosty the Snowman, Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer, Jingle Bell Rock and Rockin Around the Christmas Tree, Lynn introduced Ding-a-Ling the Christmas Bell and Mr. Mistletoe, and in a classic three-hanky country weeper, insisted, Don t Wish Me Merry Christmas. The Christmas Album placed high on the Billboard Christmas chart in the year of its release, becoming a Yuletide perennial for her legions of fans. However, the album has only seen a limited CD release that came and went, and fetches three-figure sums. Now, Real Gone Music and Second Disc Records have come to the rescue with the first-ever expanded CD reissue of this Christmas classic. This new edition of The Christmas Album includes the original album as well as four super-rare bonus tracks, all of which make their debut on CD: the mono mixes of Ding-a-Ling the Christmas Bell, Frosty the Snowman,: and Don t Wish Me Merry Christmas (complete with spoken word intros/outros) that appeared on the special Christmas Seals promotional singles Lynn recorded in 1971 and 1972 as the charity s ambassador. It s all been beautifully remastered by Vic Anesini at Sony s Battery Studios, and Joe Marchese has written the liner notes placing the album in context of Lynn s groundbreaking career. Lynn Anderson was just 67 years old when she passed away earlier this year, but her original Christmas Album stands as a happy and spirited tribute to her enduring legacy.
profile.reviewText:
When I was little we had this album on both 8-track and LP, it wasn't Christmas without it. "The Christmas Album" is not only one of the best Christmas albums, it's one of Lynn Andersons best albums of her career. The album was issued on CD previously in a very small run by Sony in the 90's then quickly disappeared. As a result it became a high demand item on eBay and other sites. At long last though the album is back in print, sadly it was spurred by the passing of Lynn earlier this year.
 The album consists of covers of classic Christmas songs like "Rudolph The Red Nosed Reindeer", "Rocking Around The Christmas Tree", "Jingle Bell Rock" and others, all done beautifully. The other songs are originals, "Mr. Mistletoe", "Ding A Ling The Christmas Bell", "A Whistle And A Whisker Away", "Soon It Will Be Chistmas Day" and the highlight, the heartbreaking "Don't Wish Me Merry Christmas" which has always been my favorite track. What's interesting is as great as these songs are none have ever been covered by anyone else.
 Rounding out this reissue are promo versions of "Ding A Ling" "Don't Wish Me Merry Christmas" and "Frosty The Snowman". The album also restores the albums original artwork and includes an newly written essay about the album.
 One of the greatest Christmas albums, back in print for old fans and new generations alike. It's just not like Christmas if you don't have this in your collection.
profile.summary: Finally Back In Print!

profile.description: Three years ago, Alice and good friend Johnny Depp got together and decided the spirit of the Hollywood Vampires should live again. Alice and Johnny were joined by Joe Perry, producer Bob Ezrin and an amazing group of guests including Perry Farrell, Dave Grohl, Sir Paul McCartney, Joe Walsh, Slash, Robbie Krieger, Zak Starkey, Brian Johnson and Kip Winger
profile.reviewText:
Although he sings lead on nearly every track, "Hollywood Vampires" isn't an Alice Cooper album per se, it's actually a supergroup tribute to the original Hollywood vampires of the early 70's. A group of musicians who hung out and drank together. Alice Cooper, John Lennon, Harry Nillson, Mickey Dolenz, Donovan etc were "members". This album pays tribute to those guys and that era.
 Consisting mainly of covers (it has two new tracks) it's loaded with guest appearances: Paul McCartney, Slash, Joe Walsh, Perry Ferrell, Joe Perry, Brian Johnson and lots of others. It also features Johnny Depp on guitar and vocals through out.
  The album opens with a narration by Christopher Lee, his last appearance on an album, and goes thru covers of songs by The Who, The Doors, Jimi Hendrix, Bad Finger, Led Zeppelin and others. One of my favorite tracks is a an update of "Schools Out" which features a verse from "Another Brick In The Wall".
 Really great album, and if you like Alice Cooper, it's a must!
profile.summary: Sounds like classic Alice Cooper!

profile.description: EZ Slice Right Melon Slicer with instruction sheet. Easy as 1,2,3, Cuts and servers perfect slices every time in seconds.
profile.reviewText: I saw this advertised on TV, they make it seem like cutting watermelon is an extremely challenging task unless you have this handy dandy slicer. Well, I've never had an issue cutting up a watermelon, but I did find this gadget to be pretty slick. You use one side to slice down thru the melon, then flip it around and use it as tongs to pick the slice out. I found that it works best with the melon cut in the long direction, but either way works. It does get a little tricky if you cut down into the white part of the melon, but otherwise this is a pretty handy kitchen tool. Says you can use it for cake too, but I haven't tried that. So if you find cutting a slice of watermelon is a challenge, then you probably need this tool. For everyone else, this just makes it that much easier.
profile.summary: Slice And Serve In One Tool!

profile.description: Based on the original film by fright master Wes Craven, The Hills Have Eyes is the story of a family road trip that goes terrifyingly awry when the travelers become stranded in a government atomic zone. Miles from nowhere, the Carter family soon realizes the seemingly uninhabited wasteland is actually the breeding ground of a blood-thirsty mutant family... and they are the prey.
profile.reviewText:
Apparently there are no original ideas for horror movies anymore. Lately every one that is coming out is a remake of a low budget 70's flick. "The Hills Have Eyes" is the latest. Speaking of which a preview for "The Omen" was shown at the start of the movie, clearly being remade for the once in a lifetime release date of 6/6/06. Anyhow I didn't expect much going into "The Hills" and didn't get much either. The plot is the standard horror plot, happy idiots unknowingly stumble upon a group of weirdos and the trouble begins. I realize this is just a movie and if people did anything smart there would be no movie in the first place, but when you are traveling thru the desert and you come across a toothless yokel, why would you take his advice for a "shortcut". That's just the first of many eye rolling moments. After that the stupidity of the characters just gets totally out of hand. Rather than being shocked when they get killed you find yourself wishing they would just kill them and get it over with. The whole thing is a mess. The freaks in the mine look like a they all came from the same family as Sloth from "The Goonies".

 The crowd at the theater I saw this at seemingly liked the movie, cheering when one of the freaks was killed. Teenagers will probably like the movie. Everyone else will find it a huge waste of time. I much preferred the recent "Hostel" or "The Devil's Rejects" two movies where the innocent are trapped in a nightmare not totally of their own doing.

 They may have eyes, but there's no need to see The Hills.
profile.summary: No Need To Run To The Hills

profile.description: His self-titled, 1970 debut, with the hits Your Song and Border Song .
profile.reviewText: Back when Rocket re-issued Elton's catalog, I skipped this disc and "11-17-70" for the same reason, these were early albums and not up to par with say "Yellow Brick Road" or "Don't Shoot Me..." how wrong I was! "Elton John" is just as good, if not BETTER than "Brick Road". The songs are much more quiet than his later hits, and there seems to be this underlying sadness in them that is just so hard to describe, you have to hear them. Paul Buckmaster's orchestration nail that sadness home. The lyrics may not be up to par with "Candle In The Wind" or other later songs, but Elton was able to take Bernie's lyrics and turn them into early masterpieces. For me the best tracks are "First Episode At Hienton", "Sixty Years On", "The Cage", "The King Must Die" and of course "Your Song" but the whole album is just so ethereal. If you've avoided this album for so long like me, give it a spin, it may have come out 34 years ago, but it's a lot better than most of the "music" you hear these days!!
profile.summary: Pretty impressive for a debut!

profile.description: New product. Never used!
profile.reviewText:
Bruce Springsteen's "Wrecking Ball" is among his best albums. The album is closer to "Nebraska" or "The Ghost Of Tom Joad" than say "Born In The USA" or "Darkness On The Edge Of Town". The first single "We Take Of Our Own", "Land Of Hope And Dreams" and "Wrecking Ball" are actually the closest to the classic E Street sound. Elsewhere the album takes on a folky-Irish-almost country feel. For me the album is one of those that ends and you start from the beginning again. A few stand out tracks, "Shackled And Drawn" (with it's Irish pub feel), the very simple piano ballad "Jack Of All Trades" (one of my favorites from the album), the Irish funeral march "Death To My Hometown", the gospel/with a rap "Rocky Ground" and finally "We Are Alive" with it's "Ring Of Fire" trumpets. If you get the deluxe edition you get two more tracks, the plantive "Swallowed Up (In The Belly Of A Whale) and "American Land" which to me sort of sounds like a rocked re-write of Johnny Horton's "Sink The Bismarc" if done by The Dropkick Murpheys.
 Throughout the album Springsteen continues singing about the everyday Joe and his struggles to get by. The album is heavily influenced by Pete Seeger and Ireland. If you're a long time Springsteen fan you won't be disappointed, if you're looking for another "Dancing In The Dark", you won't find that here. "Wrecking Ball" will certainly be on several "Best Albums of 2012" lists.
profile.summary: One of his best!

profile.description: Dutch compilation featuring all their Billboard hits as well as a number of solo hits for Sonny and Cher. Tracks include, 'Baby Don't Go', 'Just You', 'I Got You Babe', 'All I Really Want to Do', 'Laugh at Me', 'But You're Mine', 'Where DoYou Go', 'What Now My Love', 'Bang Bang', 'Alfie', 'Little Man', 'The Beat Goes On', 'You Better Sit Down Kids', 'Gypsy, Tramps And Thieves', 'All I Ever Need Is You', 'The Way of Love', 'A Cowboys Work Is Never Done' and 'When You Say Love'. All original recordings.
profile.reviewText: I belive this is the first Sonny & Cher collection to combine the "I Got You Babe" era and the "Sonny & Cher" Tv show era. Mixed in are Cher's many solo singles as well. Pretty much everything you'd want is here. The songs are in chronological order so you can hear how Cher's voice matured and Sonny's...well Sonny sounds like Sonny throughout! The booklet inside contains photos of the duos single sleeves as well as a bio of the two. The biggest complaint I would give it is this, first of all it is NOT all inclusive as it does not contain the very last Sonny & Cher single, "You're Not Right For Me" from 1977. And the other big flaw, is that for whatever reason they cut off the last "I love you!" from "Classified 1A". The song had been a very rare track until recently where it has turned up on several collections, including "The Way Of Love ~ The Cher Anthology" and Cher's new internet only release "Not Commercial". If you're looking for all the Sonny & Cher songs you remember, here you go. You get the hits, "I Got You Babe", you get the solo hits "Laugh At Me", "Gypsy's Tramps & Thieves",and you get the just plain weird tracks "Sing C'Est La Vie", "Plastic Man". Altogether you get a great set. So until someone decides to put out a Sonny & Cher or even just a Cher boxed set, this is a great place to start.
profile.summary: Like the title says, it's the singles!

profile.description: From Wikipedia: Extravaganza: Live at the Mirage is the first live music video title by singer and actress Cher. Released by Sony BMG in 1992 , it contained footage from Cher's two Heart of Stone Tour specials filmed at Mirage Hotel in Las Vegas in 1990. It featured tracks from Cher and Heart of Stone albums alongside various covers. The show was originally broadcast on CBS as a Cher concert special in 1992. It was then released on VHS and Laserdisc in the same year. The CBS Broadcast version was finally released on DVD in 2005 with many extras and further bonus songs that did not make the broadcast but were included on the VHS version.
profile.reviewText:
Was happy to see that this concert of Cher's made it to DVD finally. However, for whatever reason this is the TV version of the concert and NOT the version that was released on VHS in 1992. All of the songs from the VHS are here, but as bonus tracks.

 Overall this is a great concert, Cher looked incredible back then and this is my favorite era for Cher. The concert was filmed during her Heart Of Stone tour in 1990 and unlike her later tours, the show is actually pretty simple. At that time she wasn't doing any of her previous hits, only focusing on her current material and cover songs.

 The best songs from this concert are her covers of Jimmy Webb's "Many Rivers To Cross" and my favorite Springsteen's "Tougher Than The Rest".

 She looks and sounds great. The only flaw is the show is not the complete VHS show. But the DVD does have commentary from Cher on a few of the bonus features. And the bonus features are pretty cool, in particular the multi angle feature that lets you switch from the Mirage show, the rehearsal and from another tour date.

 Cher at her peak.
profile.summary: Great concert, but the VHS was the complete show

profile.description: Shooter Jennings - Put The O Back In Country - Cd
profile.reviewText: Until this morning I had no idea what Shooter Jennings sounded like. I knew who he was but had never heard his stuff before. This morning though I heard a sample of his stuff and went out and picked this album up. This guy is good! The music on here sounds a bit more Lynyrd Skynyrd than pure country. The overall sound is a bit sloppy as well, but that is not a bad thing. The album sounds and feels very "real". It doesn't have the over polished sound that the stuff passed off as country today has. Everything about Shooter harkens back to the mid-70's hey day of his dad. In fact even the album cover has the look of a worn LP jacket. The album is just great, some songs are a bit better than others, but the album is honest and you can't argue with honesty. No question that Waylon is looking down and smiling. Jessi has also got to be very proud. If you like your country coming from some poster boy in a hat, you might want to pass on this, but if you like real country with a southern rock twist you'll love this album.
profile.summary: Waylon would be proud!

profile.description: DOLLY PARTON: LIVE AND WELL
profile.reviewText:
First of all this is simply a GREAT CD! Dolly's live show is a show worth catching. For years one of my favorite Dolly concerts was her long deleted "Dolly In London" video from 1983. At long last we have another live recording that equals that show. This concert recorded during Dolly's "Halos & Horns" tour from 2002 show she hasn't lost a single thing. Dolly jokes between the songs and you can tell she is having a blast, as such the audience is too. Something some of the newer artists might want to learn.

 The set list for this show is somewhat interesting in that there aren't really a whole lot of hits. "Coat Of Many Colors", "Applejack", "9 To 5, "Jolene" and "I Will Always Love You" are really her only "hits" included. There is an a capella medley of four other hits, but for the most part these are all newer songs from the Dolly canon. By the way, in the medley she and her singers do a sped up snippit of "Two Doors Down" that you have to hear to belive, it really does sound like she's on the wrong speed. She did this same thing years ago with "Do I Ever Cross Your Mind", so it's cool to hear her do it again on something new.

 Dolly today sounds just as fresh and vibrant as she did twenty or thirty years ago. Her jokes are corny but she knows that and has fun with it. If you're a Dolly fan you will love this album.
profile.summary: Dolly is still at the top of her game!

profile.description: OUT OF PRINT,RCA ISSUE PRESSED IN JAPAN
profile.reviewText:
The last of the 2fer import titles includes two of my favorite Dolly RCA albums. The first is 1983's "Burlap & Satin" which includes some of Dolly's classics. The first is the incredible "Appalchian Memories" which she has since changed to "Smokey Mountain Memories", same song, different title. This is the original version and one of her best. The album includes Dolly's pop hit "Potential New Boyfriend" which was a hit at the time but has since become somewhat forgettable. The album includes one of Dolly's tearjerkers in "A Gamble Either Way", it ends with the gospel number "Calm On The Water" which contains a chorus that Dolly would use again years later in her song "High And Mighty".

 The second half of this disc is Dolly's last RCA album, "Real Love". The album doesn't really sound like her other albums, she seemed to be on automatic pilot for this one, but it's a great collection either way. The overall theme for the album is clearly "love" as the word appears in four of the albums ten titles. It also includes "I Hope You're Never Happy" which was heard in her movie "Rhinestone", although not by her in the movie. This album also features one of my favorite Dolly album covers.

 A word about all of these reissues, all three feature notes and original album cover artwork, front and back, and liner notes. It also interesting to note that, although not intentional the album covers as paired together here all look similar to each other.

 Thanks to Stephen Munns for heading this project, perhaps we can get Dolly's 1982 album "Heartbreak Express" on CD in the near future.
profile.summary: Two favorites finally on CD!

profile.description: Before Johnny Cash was the Man in Black, he was just another musician struggling to make something of himself. 'Walk the Line' chronicles the extraordinary rise to fame of a musical legend. Overcoming early hardships such as the accidental death of his brother, Cash (Joaquin Phoenix) stormed Nashville with his innovative blend of rock, folk, blues, gospel and country. But even as his creativity blossomed, his heavy drug use took a toll, leading to a period of destructive behavior and the failure of his first marriage. It was June Carter (Reese Witherspoon), daughter of the first family of country music, who lifted Cash out of his emotional chaos and helped him to become the man and the musician he was meant to be.
profile.reviewText:
"Walk The Line" tells the story of Johnny Cash from about age 12 up thru 1968. The movie is very well done. During parts of the movie you feel like you're watching Cash home movies. Phoenix does an incredible job, not only in portraying Cash but in singing his songs as well. He nails the mannerisms right down to the sideways smile. At times you get chills watching his performance as the resemblence is uncanny. Not so much for Reese Witherspoon, although she also does her own singing and does a great job in her portrayal, I kept seeing Reese and not June. I really liked this movie. Although it doesn't drag it does seem like it's a lot longer than it is. Also as with most bio-pics they stop at a point when things seem to settle down in the career. The movie tells the story of the man in black and his start in the music business. It follows him as he tries to win the heart of June Carter. Along the way other various big names pop up, Elvis, Jerry Lee Lewis and Shooter Jennings playing his father Waylon.

 A great movie that is certainly Oscar worthy if for nothing else that for Joaquin Phoenix's portrayal. There's a lot of great music along the way! When June died in 2003 everyone said that Johnny wouldn't last long without her. He didn't. Seeing this movie you understand why.
profile.summary: Incredible film on all counts!

profile.description: HATCHET. unrated director's cut.
profile.reviewText:
You could almost call "Hatchet" "Gilligan's Island meets Friday The 13th". The story is simple enough, a group of tourists on a New Orleans Haunted Swamp tour end up lost in the woods with hatchet wielding maniac. What sets "Hatchet" apart from others in the genre is it's sense of humor. This probably the first slasher comedy. It's not a spoof however, there are some moments where you'll find yourself jumping and the gore level is high. Overall I liked the movie, it's bloody, it's gory, the plot has been used a hundred times, but it's fun.
 The disc also has several documentaries about the film with the filmmakers. Among them is the story of how 80's hair band Twisted Sister lead singer Dee Snider plays into the whole making of the movie.
 "Hatchet" is a slasher film that doesn't take it's self to serious and cuts right to the juggular.
profile.summary: A surprisingly good film

profile.description: Directed by the prolific Rob Zombie, The Devil's Rejects is the sequel to 2003's successful House Of 1000 Corpses, and picks up several weeks after House left off. The music featured on the soundtrack plays an integral part in the film, including the shocking ending featuring the Lynyrd Skynyrd classic 'Free Bird'. Hip-O. 2005.
profile.reviewText:
This CD, the soundtrack to Rob Zombie's "The Devil's Rejects" is a great summer album! The CD consists primarily of 70's classic rock and a pair of country songs from the 1950's and 1960's. There are two versions of the album out there, this one with soundbites from the movie, and another version without the soundbites. The soundbites for just sort of add a little bit more to the listening experience. Keep in mind though that the sound bites all contain vulgarity, in most cases the "f" word, that one word is spoken by every character in the movie in nearly every line of the script. But getting back to the music. We start off with The Allman Brothers' "Midnight Rider" which seems to set the mood for the whole album. I was very surprised to see the two country songs on there, "It Wasn't God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels" by Kitty Wells, and "Satan's Got To Get Along Without Me" from Buck Owens. These two seem somewhat out of place, but as I said in my headline, listening to this album is like a funhouse ride, so you just go along with it.
 "Rocky Mountain Way" was used to perfection in the movie with it's sleazy guitar riff, "Free Bird" works really well also. The three Terry Reid tracks are standouts. Hearing these songs back to back and with sound bites, you can feel the heat of the summer and the reckless abandon depicted in the movie.
 The album closes with a few tracks from Banjo & Sullivan who also have a complete album out (Banjo & Sullivan are the fictious country band in the movie). What's interesting though is that although they are on the soundtrack and have a "Hits" album, you don't hear any of their songs in the movie.
 I like this album, I liked the movie. If you're a fan of 70's classic rock you'll probably like this album as well. It's a great album to play while going for a summer drive.
profile.summary: A wild funhouse ride!

top_5.description: CD
top_5.reviewText:
If you're looking for a country album, you won't find it in Thomas Rhett's sophomore album "Tangled Up". The album actually is a new category, "twangy funk". Clearly inspired by Bruno Mars' "Unorthodox Jukebox" Thomas Rhett may lose some fans of his debut album. The lead single "Crash And Burn" is about as country as it gets here. The last song, "Learned It From The Radio" could be a single as well for country radio. Other than that the rest of the disc is varying degrees of funk/R&B. The song "Tangled" is almost a rewrite of Bruno Mars' "Treasure" complete with the late 70's disco funk feel. "I Feel Good" has a rap break in the middle by Lunchbox Lewis. "Playing With Fire" is a great duet with Jordin Sparks.
 "Tangled Up" isn't a bad album at all, it's just not the "bro country" album you'd be expecting from Thomas Rhett. I can certainly see how he may lose some fans with this album, he may very well pick up some new ones though along the way.
top_5.summary: This is NOT a country album!

top_5.description: The first significant overview of Dolly Parton's most prolific and creative period, "Mission Chapel 1971-1975" reveals the hidden songwriting gems of her 'pre pop' country years and features key tracks never before on cd. The album also features adeluxe color booklet with detailed liner notes.
top_5.reviewText:
First off, here are the tracks on this Australian compilation:
Coat Of Many Colors, If I Lose My Mind, The Mystery Of The Mystery, She Never Met A Man, Love Is Only As Strong, Will He Be Waiting?, Loneliness Found Me, Mission Chapel Memories, Comes & Goes, Oh He's Everything, He Left Me Love, Still On Your Mind, My Kind Of Man, Pleasant As May, Jolene, When Someone Wants To Leave, Living On Memories Of You, Lonely Comin' Down, Highway Heading South, Once Upon A Memory, Sacred Memories, The Bargain Store, On My Mind Again, When I'm Gone.
 Now you probably see that there aren't too many hit singles in this collection. What these are, some of Dolly's great album cuts from her early 70's period. Most of these songs have never been released on CD. The albums sampled are: "Coat Of Many Colors", "Touch Your Woman", "My Favorite Songwriter, Porter Wagoner", "Bubbling Over", "Jolene", "Love Is Like A Butterfly" and "The Bargain Store". This is all hard core Dolly, prior to here pop crossover success in the mid 70's. The majority of these tracks were written by Dolly herself, with a handful by Porter Wagoner and one by her Uncle Bill Owens. If all you know of Dolly is "9 to 5" or "Here You Come Again" you may not be too impressed with this collection. But if you remember Dolly when she was more known for her songwriting skills and plantive singing style, then you'll want to pick this disc up. These are some great rare tracks from albums that haven't seen the light of day in years!!!
top_5.summary: Finally Hard Core Dolly On CD!!!!!!!!!

top_5.description: This cassette is in GREAT shape!! Ships FIRST CLASS!
top_5.reviewText:
This album was originally released in 1982. Actually, it was the first Dolly album I ever bought, of course back then it was on vinyl. The album was a big success at the time. The original pressing of the album included 12 songs, one of them being "Hard Candy Christmas" from the "Best Little Whorehouse In Texas" soundtrack. That song was dropped once "Islands In The Stream" became a big hit. At the time "Greatest Hits" was the only Dolly album where you could find "Islands". The original LP also included a gatefold cover that opened up to show a bunch of Dolly photos from thruout the years covered on the album, roughly 1977 thru 1982. The back cover featured shots of Dolly from "Whorehouse". In 1985 the album was released on CD. It contained all the same elements of the original album (however as with all versions of the album at that time, "Hard Candy Christmas" had been replaced). The CD had all the photos and liner notes that LP had. RCA was among the first record labels to issue CDs, Dolly had four albums issued on CD at the beginning of the format. "Greatest Hits", "Real Love", "Rhinestone" and her Christmas album with Kenny Rogers. All of these went out of print very quickly. Only "Greatest Hits" and the Christmas album were re-issued later on. By then RCA was putting out "budget" versions of the albums, removing songs that were on the original LP's. "Greatest Hits" lost three songs and all of the artwork, except the cover. The Christmas album also lost the Kenny Rogers solo songs, as well as the lyrics and artwork, except the cover shot.

 Today original copies of these CD's can be found only on eBay, but the later re-issues can be found anywhere. Back in the day, this was the only Dolly album to combine "Here You Come Again" with "9 To 5", "Islands In The Stream" etc. Today these songs have been reissued many many times making this album redundant. If you're a collector search out the original 1985 CD version. Good luck!
top_5.summary: Her original Hits album

top_5.description: Digitally remastered two CD set offers either a complete career overview or extensive selections from the artist's most important years & will feature key hits, album tracks, extensive liner notes, credits, period photos, & more.
top_5.reviewText: This collection covers the years 1965 thru 1975 so Tom's cover of Prince's "Kiss" is not here. Honestly you won't miss it. What you do get are 42 killer tracks. All of his big early hits are here, "It's Not Unusual", "What's New Pussycat", "Thunderball", "She's a Lady" and "Delilah". For me though the first ten tracks on disc one can be skipped, it's not that they are bad songs, but for me they are just too dated and sound too much alike. For me things get fun with "This And That" a UK only single from 1966. After that is his killer take on the country standard "Green Green Grass Of Home". From that point on there isn't really a weak track. You get his covers of well known hits of the era, "Sixteen Tons", "The Witch Queen Of New Orleans", "Ain't No Sunshine", "If Loving You Is Wrong I Don't Want To Be Right" and "Pledging My Love" all done with that same bombast and over the top vocal that makes Tom Jones, TOM JONES! Oh sure, middle aged women find something else about Tom Jones that appeals to them, but for the rest of us this is just great music. This is a great collection and I think you'll find once you start playing it, you won't be able to stop, and you'll keep asking yourself why??? You may never know why so just sit back and enjoy!
top_5.summary: A great collection of the best of Tom Jones

top_5.description: 2009 compilation from Waylon and Jessie's son. In five short years, Shooter Jennings has gone from performing in the small club scene to playing for thousands, including music festivals like Bonaroo and Stagecoach to name a few. Bad Magick: The Best of Shooter Jennings and the .357's is an all encompassing listening experience of 13 fan favorites from Shooter Jennings' last four albums, plus two tracks never before released on CD. With one listen, fans get an idea of who Shooter Jennings is musically, with songs he has written about life, blending the sounds of Country, Blues and Rock 'N' Roll. This album has it all, including the ever popular '4th Of July' to his cover of his friend Hank Williams Jr.'s 'Living Proof'. This collection is for all Shooter fans, whether this is the first album they sink into or whether they've been with him from his beginnings.
top_5.reviewText:
I have to say I was surprised to see a Best Of out there already for Shooter Jennings, I didn't think he had enough albums out yet. I bought his debut album, Put The "O" Back In Country when it was released and thought that was a great disc. It's nice to hear that Shooter's music hasn't changed much since then. Shooter (the song of Waylon Jennings and Jessi Colter) does country music that is a little country and a lot of outlaw and southern rock. The music is sloppy, but that's not a bad thing. Much of today's country music is very polished and shines and ends up sounded very processed. Shooter's music is real, his lyrics are a lot like his fathers.
 If you're a fan of southern rock or Waylon Jennings you will really like "Bad Magick" if you're already a fan of Shooter's you probably already have these tracks (except for the two new tracks) but I think you'll like this compilation nonetheless.
top_5.summary: Sloppy country music, a beautiful thing

I received this as a Christmas gift, since I have wanted an immersion blender and small chopper both, so this was a great solution. Please be sure to price this particular item, since I am aware that the cost of the one I received was significantly less than listed at the time of my review.

When I first took it out of the box, I was shocked by how large both the stick and the chopper were. I was expecting something much smaller! But after experimenting a bit, I realized that what looks huge actually was quite comfortable. I was amazed at the flexibility of the speed, both in the dial and the two buttons.

My first experiment was pico de gallo in the chopper. Having used choppers before, I knew enough to power it way down and use pulses. I cut my onion in fourths and pulsed away. Once I had things pretty chopped up, I cut both ends off of the jalapeno, cut it in fourths, and dropped it in for more pulsing. Then I cut three Roma tomatoes in thirds and dropped them in with a few cilantro leaves.

I seem to have overloaded it a bit, since the tomatoes weren't chopping that well, so I took out half and pulsed the first half until it was properly chopped up, then chopped the second half the same way. Voila, me and my tortilla chips were very happy, actually a bit too happy, since it was a VERY spicy jalapeno.

A key thing I noticed is that there is a lot of speed and power in this blender, so I will be running it at the lowest speeds when I try new things, especially when I am working with hot liquids (I can soups and vegetables, which is why this is an awesome tool for me).

Obviously, I can't speak to longevity, but if I find a problem in the future, I will report it.
profile.summary: A gift I'm enjoying

profile.reviewText:
You might wonder why you would need one of these little devices?

Last summer, I attended a week long conference somewhere north of nowhere. I was in a dorm and had to hang out on top of the building to get the tiniest amount of cell phone signal. Our rooms were wired, not wireless! Fortunately, I had my laptop, but NO connection with my iPad or iPhone unless I walked across campus to the community center. I was NOT happy.

I can't live without wifi (well, I guess I survived, but only after going out and buying a router that would hook up to my computer and work off of it).

This little doodad would have solved the problem quickly and easily. And given the panic of others in the dorm, I probably could have sold tickets to connect. Similarly, I recently stayed at a hotel where ethernet was free - wifi commanded a price of $20 per night.

Essentially, you plug it into the ethernet using a cable and it is an instant, inexpensive , portable router. It can also be used as a mini router in your own home.

I plugged it in and was easily able to connect using the software provided (on a tiny cd disk). The one thing you need to do is write your password down off of the back of it before connecting to it for the first time. I couldn't find the code anywhere on the packaging for the router. It was only on the back of the router.

It is now traveling with me anywhere I go so that I no longer have to worry about wifi.

Another NICE feature is that it can be set up as your own network. Anyone who has struggled with connecting to a travel printer with an iPad or iPhone knows the impossibility. No wires ... This creates a network you can use to connect your travel printer (as long as it is wifi capable) and your devices while on the go.

I received a complimentary sample to test for my review.
profile.summary: Where were you when I needed you?

This arrived just in front of our second winter storm of the season. I plugged it in and charged it immediately. While we only had flickers of power outages, more than 33,000 lost power from the storm. Having it available made a huge difference in my sense of security, and if we had lost power, in the use of my iPad.

We have 3 iPads in our home, so the fact that this can charge 2 major items concurrently is HUGE. Most of the chargers I own have two plugs, one for smaller items and one for more major ones. But with this charger, you can charge two items at once, either two larger items requiring more power (like the iPad), or two cell phones, or any combination.

It comes with a USB cord and multiple tips. While you can use your USB port to charge it, I chose to plug it into a USB charger that I already owned. Once the power crisis was over, I ran down my iPad and it charged it nicely. It maintained the charge in my iPad so that I was able to use it not just to charge the iPad, but also as a back-up battery.

It is a high gloss black, and I was very grateful that it had blinking lights that showed when it was charging then showed how much charge remained in the battery.

This was sent to my by Yubi as a complimentary sample so that I could test and use it for a review. Whether you choose this one because of its features or another one, I strongly recommend keeping these on hand for hurricanes, tornadoes, earthquakes, snowstorms, or other emergencies where you want to stay powered.

In either case, once I removed the pan, I was able to wipe it down within a few seconds to clean it. And that is one of my favorite points - no baked on overflows! Food only cooks inside of the skillet! It uses a standard size outlet - no special wiring needed. It has four standard settings, Boil & Sear (hottest), and warm and slow cook. But you can adjust these using the temperature arrows up and down. Because this gets hot so fast, you will need to have your ingredients ready before you start - no cutting up the onions while you wait for the pan to heat. You WILL need to use induction-ready cookware. You can grab your cast iron cookware (perfect) or find magnetic stainless steel cookware. IF a magnet sticks, it works. Just to be safe, Big Boss sends you a magnet for you to check your cookware. I looked pretty silly walking around my local stores trying to stick a magnet to the bottom of pans, but I figured that was the price of using Induction cooking. Actually, I did not find a set I could use locally, which is why I purchased on Amazon. This heats up to 475, which is about the top temperature I want to cook at. In case you aren't aware, you should never cook with nonstick cookware above 500 degrees, since it will release toxic fumes. It begins to beep if you remove the pan. At 10 seconds, it shuts off automatically. No problem, since it instantly heats back up when you turn it back on. All in all, a practical item at a good price. Now that I have it, I will be looking for more cookware in the appropriate sizes to use on it. Very Happy!

Second, we added my daughter (and all of her wifi connections to our home). So when I had the opportunity to check this router out, I jumped at the chance.

First of all, set up didn't go easily. First, while it did connect wirelessly to my computer with the push of a button, I had to use the (enclosed) cable to connect to the router to set it up. Then, it didn't connect at first and I had to reset my modem and router - twice. Even then, while it seems to connect perfectly, it never completely set up. I figure if it works, don't sweat it, so am happy.

About the speed. When I took the old router down - it had a broken antenna. Gee, thanks cats! Could that have been the problem? Well, that and the fact that my old router wasn't rated for enough devices? We had an N router and have 2 printers, 3 iPads, 2 iPhones, and 2 computers using it.

I began testing my new speed, and it is now significantly higher - I was running at 1mg upload, and now get up to 20 mgs upload speed at the same time of day, even using all of these devices.

I took a star off because with the problems I had connecting it, I had to go online using my iPhone in order to get the manual to figure things out when it wouldn't connect the first time. Nothing worse than needing a manual from the internet - and not having a connection. Smart or not - give me instructions that I can use in the package in case the smart router doesn't do it right.

So, not an auspicious start, but pleased with the actual router. FYI - I have been using it for more than three weeks. Will come back and post if there are any problems, but there haven't been to date.
profile.summary: Not perfect, but it significantly improved MY speed!

profile.description: The Silhouette CAMEO is an electronic cutting machine for personal use. Like a home printer, it plugs into your PC or Mac with a simple USB cable. However, instead of printing it uses a small blade to cut paper, cardstock, vinyl, fabric and more up to 12" wide and 10 feet long.
profile.reviewText:
This version of the Silhouette comes with just about everything you need to get started except the supplies. Since it mentions two different numbers of "free patterns," I want to reassure you that once you hook it up to your computer, you have access to 100 free patterns that come with it. I have included a video of three of our early items. I love the slim look, and having the touchscreen available is awesome. I especially appreciate being able to do a "one touch" repeat of the design you just completed.

It has a CD with the software and manual, however I was able to download it from online directly to my computer, so don't worry if you don't have a drive, you are safe. It also comes with a written start guide, and something you will want to own, a cutting mat.

If you are wondering what the mat is for, it is a sticky mat that you place under items that are too soft to send through the cutting machine on their own - a quick example that I tried is ... paper. It shredded it trying to feed it through. Once I stuck it on the mat, it cut it perfectly, although it stuck onto the mat. (big learning curve here). I have used 65 pound card stock with few problems, but even it does better with the mat. EDITED: After discussing this with some people in comments, even the card stock works better with the mat. One of the commenters suggested using a cricut mat because they are cheaper.

You can make crafts with cloth, but you need to use a heavy fabric liner - although I noticed on Pinterest that fabric starch might be another solution. Because of the precision, after you use the fusing, you can precisely place it on the mat for cutting. So you can cut several different colors after separating the image and locating the colors where they are needed.

In addition to the 100 included patterns, this includes a "one month subscription" or $25 worth of patterns off of the Silhouette web site, which allows you to choose your own, plus if you search around on the internet, there are many other ideas you can work with and patterns you can get for free. Silhouette also offers a free pattern of the week, and discounted patterns and sales, so it is easy to collect quite a few if you aren't confident enough to create your own.

The basic software to run the machine is free, but you will need to pay a premium if you want to upgrade to fancier software that will do more. If you are familiar with drawing programs, you will be able to get started quickly, however if you are new to software, this will also be a large learning curve.

In addition to supplies (and additional cutting mats), Silhouette offers replacement blades. They offer one that is listed as for fabric. You don't need a special blade for fabric, but for sharpness, it is a good idea to use one exclusively for this purpose. If you are doing much, they have some special blades, hooks, and scrapers to more easily remove your cut out pieces. After pricing around, Amazon seems to have the best prices for these.

What impressed me is that even with my lack of knowledge, I was able to use one of the patterns and create a project right off, so I'm happy with this machine and looking forward to many more projects to come. Like most craft items, the more you use it, the more things you find that it can do. I have been checking multiple ideas online and have ordered the lining to make cloth projects using my quilting scraps.
profile.summary: My first project only minutes after I set it up

In addition to the outstanding sound (and trust me, it is outstanding), these over ear headphones are positively the most comfortable ones I have ever worn.

First, for the sound. I am NOT an audiophile, sorry. In fact, I have some hearing loss in one of my ears. But that makes all of the notes I can hear even more important. While for many years I settled for cheaper earphones, a couple of years ago I had a chance to listen to my first outstanding set. Suddenly, I could tell the difference in the kinds of music I had on my computer. Some was muddy, not up to par. Others were so clear that I felt like I was sitting in the orchestra. These are that good! In fact, while listening to some "rock," I actually was able to flirt with the drummer.

I tried several genres of music to push the limits, but I didn't find any. Every sound was startlingly clear. From Bach, to Billy Joel, to the Oak Ridge Boys, to Tennessee Bird Walk; Loud, soft, and in-between, not a single mushy note.

Second, the comfort. These do not have leather, they have plush. The ear section is plenty large for your ear to fit INSIDE the cuff, allowing the plush to rest against your head while your ears are not mashed, squeezed, or otherwise troubled. I could keep these on my head for hours without feeling like I was wearing headphones at all.

Speaking of which, I have a small head. One of the reasons I often use ear buds is that I can't get headphones to correctly fit. These fit. They are able to be shortened enough that the top just grazes my head. This, combined with the comfortable cuffs make these trouble free to wear. They are easy to adjust, almost too easy.

It may sound strange, evaluating comfort, but I have given up on many headphones and ear buds for the simple reason that they hurt. If it hurts, it doesn't matter how good they sound, I can't enjoy them.

Third, I have an iPad and iPhone. The cord included with the set I received is aimed specifically for this platform. When I tested, they worked perfectly in controlling the sound.

Fourth, these are not advertised (that I could see) as being noise canceling. But, the way they cup over your ear and hold the sound in makes them work well to keep out unwanted noise. I could still hear what was being said without the music, but once I was playing the music, all other sound disappeared.

Finally, these are nicely portable with a beautiful carry bag. They fold up and go with you. If you look at my fourth comment, because these isolate your ears, you should be able to hear your music or video better. BUT, even if you aren't interested in listening to music, these will effectively dim the noise of your companions and that baby in the row across the way. OR, by placing these on your ears and pretending that you are listening, you can keep the person in the seat next to you from starting an annoying conversation.

Top of the line sound, fierce comfort, wonderful choice.

It isn't going to replace the snow blower anytime soon, but given the size, it did a great job on the blob of ice on my patio. Video was cut - it actually covers about 2 minutes. You need to make certain that the attachments are firmly connected, when they are, there are no leaks or dripping. It has a very nice safety feature, you cannot detach the lid without pushing down firmly, which will keep children from accidentally spilling hot water on themselves. This is small, light, and easy to use, even with my small hands. I used it to clean my sink and was very pleased with the result. The best part about this is all of the attachments that come along with it - It has The standard long spray nozzle (needed for most projects) and also includes a flexible extension hose, a door/window nozzle as well as a squeegee attachment for the shower, and a bent spray nozzle to get under the edges of the toilet, as well as a round brush nozzle, very handy for scrubbing. The door/window nozzle can actually be used to steam curtains or any item that needs to have wrinkles removed, or it can also be used on beds to clean them. It has a towel sleeve for gentle purposes. Besides all of this it has a measuring cup and funnel for filling - which is kind of important because the top is so small. In fact, my key concern for this particular steam cleaner is that it would be impossible to clean the inside, meaning you really need to use filtered water if you are going to use it regularly so that you don't have lime build up

profile.reviewText:
A few weeks ago I signed up with Roolen to receive a complimentary one of these humidifiers to test for a review. I had no idea how important this would turn out to be.

While people living in areas of low humidity might count on these to make their home more comfortable, there is a second use to these as a cool mist humidifier. When my granddaughter was diagnosed with pneumonia the very same day this arrived, it became a key aspect to her recovery - it is sitting in her sickroom as we speak on high (instead of low or automatic). Having this available is one of the reasons we were able to keep her from being admitted to the hospital!

I have used cool mist before and it has always had a problem - it got everything around it wet. In fact, I am used to having to put a cool mist humidifier on a towel, just to abosorb the moisture. NOT SO with Roolen. It disperses the moisture into the air smoothly with only the tiniest bit of moisture around the humidifier, and gently raises the humidity in the room making it easier for you to breathe. Best of all, it is extremely quiet.

Beautiful, quiet, works VERY well. For normal circumstances, I appreciate having the automatic shut off which will turn it off when the humidity goes above a comfortable level. Once we get past the crisis, I will be using it to keep the humidity in her room at a comfortable level, especially as the heater robs us of the humidity in the air (we were below freezing last night).

My granddaughter liked being able to see the little cloud of mist above the humidifier (she called it a volcano).

Do be aware that you will need to be sure to clean this regularly as you would need to clean any humidifier.

Five stars from someone who never knew how important this little device would be!

EDITED - For those reading, my granddaughter was able to remain home instead of being hospitalized and is now completely recovered from the pneumonia. We have been keeping this set to automatic and while I don't have a gauge to measure the humidity, it does come on only part of the time, so I have to assume it is doing its job. In fact, when we went to 100% humidity with a storm passing through last week, it didn't come on.
profile.summary: Quiet - everything the doctor ordered

Even more, they provide a rich sound of excellent quality. I especially love the way they block external noise. The only thing I wished was that they would be iPhone compatible.

Voila, RHA has just come out with the 450 model which not only includes all of these wonderful features, but is also designed to answer the iPhone and handle my calls. I love the extra long cord, which will allow my iPhone to set on the seat next to me or in a holder. While I don't normally talk and drive, I do enjoy talking as a passenger, and having the plugs block out a great deal of ambient sound makes my experience even more wonderful!

The buttons are clearly marked, white on black, and the middle button is recessed so that those who struggle with seeing the markings can easily and intuitively use them. Like the 350, these have a classy and sturdy 1.5m fabric braided cable that really does keep the cord from tangling.

The design of these is intended to bring the sound directly into your ears, with the ear piece fitting against the ear canal to block external noise. Because of the design, they are comfortable to wear and I have slept with them in my ears on many occasions. Even more, since most earbuds are larger, these are the only ones I have been able to comfortably wear. they come with several sizes of plugs, and I personally use the smallest size.

I am VERY grateful to the manufacturer for providing me with a complimentary set of these earbuds to test, except for the fact that now that I am using them, I can never go back to the cheap ones I used to use. I am totally hooked on these!

profile.description: Exuding old-fashioned country charm, the 2-gallon drink dispenser features authentically-embossed glass. Metal screw top cover and removable tap make cleaning a breeze. Perfect for kombucha continuous brewing, Kvass or Borscht. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- How to Make 2 Gallons of Kombucha Supplies 1 2 gallon glass vessel, such as Palais High Quality Mason Jar Beverage Dispenser. 2 Cups organic cane sugar 10 Teaspoons Loose leaf tea 2 Gallons Distiller water 1 Scoby 2 Cups Starter liquid 1 ) Start by boiling 8 cups of distilled water. As soon as it starts to boil put Ito your glass vessel. 2) Take the loose leaf tea and add to the water. 3) Steep the tea for 5-7 minutes. 4) Add in the 2 cups of sugar. 5) Stir it up until its fully dissolved. 6) Add another gallon of distilled water to the mixture. 7) Wash your hands thoroughly and then splash some vinegar on your hands. Your scoby is sensitive! 8) Make sure that the water went down to lukewarm temputure. Test it with your hands. Take that beautiful little miracle (scoby) and add it in. 9) Put the 2 cups of starter liquid in. Your scoby needs a little help. 10) Cover with screw off lid, Put it in a dark place with open air. A good tempurture should be 73-80 degrees. Let this be for 7 days and leave it alone. No touching no peaking! Taste w straw. If too sweet give it another day- to tart less time next time! profile.description: Black Box G98S GPS Dash Camera - Super HD Wide Angle Zoom Car DVR - Zinc Alloy Body
profile.reviewText: I received this dash camera in order to examine and test it for my review. There are actually many features that I am unable to comment on, including the fact that this coordinates with GPS and is not only able to show the location where the video was taken, but also is able to record your speed on the video. If you look at my video, you will notice that since I did not have the GPS connected, it does not reflect my current speed. I did not update the date, so that is incorrect on my video as well. With so many on the market, the key elements I was looking for were the clarity of the images and the ease of use. In my video, I put clips of a drive over the course of the morning so that you could see how it works during different daylight uses. The first segment begins just after sunrise, at the ending, you are looking at full noontime lighting. For safety and visibility, I do NOT use the suction cup attachment - instead, I have a flat holder that can be used for multiple uses on my dashboard, from my iPhone, to a GPS, or in this case, a camera. This fit perfectly, and as you will see, a portion of my dashboard shows in the video. If you are using their suction cup connection on your window, you will not see this. This actually comes complete with everything you need, including a 16G micro SD card. The plug in cord for your car is amply long, my only complaint is that it is connected to the plug itself. Since I normally use my charger for multiple devices, a simple cord would have been my preference. Other than getting it set up, for the basic camera, you need only to do one thing - on a plug powered by your auto that switches on/off when your vehicle is powered up - you turn your engine on. The camera comes on. When you turn your engine off, it runs for a few seconds and switches off. The software is awesome, it breaks the video into short consecutive clips allowing you to easily isolate a specific segment. While there is some reduction in quality in my video in order to size it - and Amazon will further reduce the quality - this video cam is more than ample for any information you need when driving. In fact, since it videotapes through windows, it can be used from indoors to monitor a specific area of your home. Simply use a standard cord to connect it to a USB source and place it in a window. You are limited by space on the SD card, and without an accident (where it stores the information in a separate folder), it will rewrite itself. My trip of just over an hour took up 5.6 G of memory. There are features that you can use, including taking photos (good in case of accident to supplement the video), but I would recommend using a different camera for that and saving this for what makes it super - as a car camera - on hand to document what happened. The only thing I noticed was that sitting on my dashboard it did get very hot in the 90 degree sun ... Because this fits so well in my car, I will be using it regularly after I find a cord that I can use to connect it in my multiple charger.
profile.summary: Good Video - Easy to Use

profile.reviewText:
I have been following the James Becker series since the very first novel. In my opinion, the stories are only getting better. This was the best yet.

The book starts out slow as the author begins to develop a complex plot, but speeds up once the plot is set in place.
The Koreans send up a weather satellite that fails to stabilize. Or is it meant to look that way?
A meteor lands in a farmer's field, and later disappears from where he has hidden it.
A veterinary pharmaceutical salesman finds himself being pulled under in the economy.

As these stories interweave, Becker and Beth try to sort things out with the help of Gunner and Bull and the FBI who is always one step behind as they are stuck with actually following the rules.

Things come down to the wire as the story builds to a climax and the posed risks are imminent.

The characters are more real than ever, and there is compassion in Becker that shows in new ways, and brings the book full circle at the end.
profile.summary: Becker & Beth, better than ever!

profile.description: Who Moved My Cheese? is an amusing and enlightening story of four characters who live in a maze and look for cheese to nourish them and make them happy. Cheese is a metaphor for what you want to have in life - whether it is a good job, a loving relationship, money or a possession, health or spirital peace of mind. And the maze is where you look for what you want - the organisation you work in, or the family or community you live in. This profound book from bestselling author, Spencer Johnson, will show you how to anticipate change, adapt to change quickly, enjoy change and be ready to change quickly again and again. Discover the secret for yourself and learn how to deal with change, so that you suffer from less stress and enjoy more success in your work and in life. Written for all ages, this story takes less than an hour to read, but its unique insights can last for a lifetime.
profile.reviewText:
I read this book as a part of a management team a number of years ago, but have found it much more applicable to my personal life than I was able to use it in the corporate world.

The truth exhibited in this book is that change happens. Sometimes it happens rapidly, sometimes it happens slowly, but it happens to all of us. Whether you are facing a change in your corporate structure, a change in your job, a change because you have moved, or simply are growing older, you will relate to some of the context of this book.

The story is told about mice and humans who live in a maze. They find a source of cheese, and while the humans build their lives around the source assuming it will always be there, the mice notice when it is dwindling and seek a new source of cheese.

  Anticipate Change
  Get Ready For The Cheese To Move

  Monitor Change

  Adapt To Change Quickly
  The Quicker You Let Go Of Old Cheese, The Sooner You Can Enjoy New Cheese

  Change
  Move With The Cheese

profile.description: Fisher-Price 3-in-1 Bounce, Stride, and Ride Elephant
profile.reviewText:
In order to assemble this you will need a Philips Head Screwdriver, and a bit of patience.

You clip the green handle on then turn it over and put on the back wheels. The green handle actually clips in place helping to line up the screw holes. I suggest (from experience) that you don't tighten all three screws at one time, instead just start all three screws. On the first wheel I didn't follow those instructions and had difficulty with the third screw. The second wheel went much easier.

The two front wheels also have three screw holes which are much easier to put in, although all of the screws require a bit of elbow grease. Once the wheels are on, you insert the head into the slots, turn it over and insert two more screws. All of the screws are the same size, so you don't have to worry about mixing them up.

I'm not certain what caused it (maybe the problems I had with the installation), but the back wheel rubs slightly.

After assembling it, I did a bit of testing (with my hand) and discovered that bouncing on the elephant activates the sounds as well as touching the buttons. What a noisy little critter! BUT, it also has an OFF button! So that redeems it.

Besides the off button, I thought I'd mention the battery situation. Once you correctly place the head onto the body, the battery case is accessible by turning the elephant over.  The handle on the back clips into place, but also unclips from the top and clips under the body of the elephant.

Except for the problems with installing the screws for the back wheels and the draggy back wheel, everything went smoothly and this really is a very cute critter. From the soft ears to the easy to grab handles and fun lights and songs, I believe the age listed is very appropriate for this toy, depending on the size and ability of the child.
profile.summary: Fun once it is assembled.

profile.description: Flash is a lightning fast dice game. Players aim to rack up the most points as they race through 8 dice challenges. Best not blinkany player could score in a flash! profile.reviewText:
This intriguing dice game works for two to six players, however it is best with three or more for better competition.

In the standard game, each person has their own set of dice and rolls for a specific goal (EG 3 pairs). When they accomplish the goal they get the highest chip (in a game of six people it would be the six) and each person gains a lower chip for when they finish. The chips become your score, the top player would get six, the next five, etc.

You have a scorecard where you record the different challenges and when all are done, you add up the scores.

The one thing I really like about this version of the game is that everyone has a chance and gets a chip. I strongly suggest this for families and younger children.

However there is a more vicious form of the game, great for competitive adults and teens, where the last person to score on the challenge is out. In this progressive game there is a final winner and the rolling and challenge becomes more intense as the game goes on.

I received a complimentary sample to test for a review and am grateful to have had the opportunity to try out this challenging new dice game. If you are looking for a cool game to send your favorite soldier who is deployed, I recommend this one. Easy to play and comes in its own carrying bag.

profile.description: This new petite pie maker bakes four delicious pies in minutes!
