profile.reviewText:
TL;DR I have tried top of the line AMD ASUS boards for 3 years with nothing but bad luck. Customer service is bad too.

I have owned two of these Asus motherboards since 2012. They both lasted an average of six months. Asus's customer support is horrible and it takes hours to get through. Just do yourself a favor and say it never turned on. When they worked they worked great. I then I upgraded to a formula crossfire Z. That one lasted longer about a year.
Same problem, fried bios chip and other issues. I have a water cooled 9590fx, and before that a 8350 fx. My newest Sabertooth lasted three weeks, in a top of the line system. EVGA 1000W plat, Titan X water cooled, and my 9590fx water cooled.
I have heard nothing but good things about Asus, but they are a bad luck brand for me. Corsair, MSI, Kingston, EVGA, I have had great luck. Going the MSI board route. Not compatible with my 9590 fx, so that had to be returned too. So it is back to my old 6350 fx and try a company I have had great luck with.
profile.summary: Hey Asus. The Sabertooth went extinct.

profile.description: Get ready to be at the centre of the ultimate fantasy adventure. Enter the world of FINAL FANTASY XV, and experience epic action-packed battles along your journey of discovery. You are Noctis, the Crown Prince of the Kingdom of Lucis, and your quest is to reclaim your homeland from the clutches of the imperial army. Joined by your closest friends, you will take the wheel and experience a voyage like no other, travelling through the breath-taking world of Eos encountering larger-than-life beasts and unforgiving enemies. You will learn to master the skills of weaponry and magic, channelling the power of your ancestors allowing you to effortlessly warp through the air in thrilling combat. Fresh faces and long-time fans, fulfil your destiny and experience a brand new kind of fantasy.
profile.reviewText:
If you have always sat there and felt you really should try to get into final fantasy? This the game to do it as it provides the best combat yet for fans of all RPGs very Dragon Age  Inquisition like. If you are a final fantasy fan disappointed in this last entry in the single player series? For sure get this one. I myself have forced myself over the years to get into final fantasy without success something about it breaks my immersion.

 I mean I love RPGs especially ones that tell a in depth story with great characters so you would think I would be a big fan of Final Fantasy - no. Witcher 3 is another game you would think a RPG mega fan would love and played it countless hours. Again that is wrong for whatever reason it did not hold my attention and I can't explain it - great game though. Many of the Final Fantasy games are great, as a critic and open minded fan I can say this despite my dislike.

My Final Fantasy friends (one of who failed out of college back in the day due to the series) give this game the stamp of approval and consider it one of the best ones in years. I myself coming from a RPG fan point of view? Everything you expect in a good to great RPG is in here but cars and cell phones in any Fantasy except Urban Fantasy kills all immersion for me. I imagine Skyrim killing a Dragon and calling up your characters mom in game so she would be proud of you. Lots of laughs.

So why did I play this game even though I am not a fan? Well being a critic is a hobby, I got a copy for free, and I can play through a game I am not into but still see the value of it for people who do enjoy it. The characters are great, love the sworn brothers feel, the combat is very good and the scope of the art direction is beautiful. You don't need to be a mega fan to be impressed by all that and you don't need to enjoy a plot - to really like characters who exist in a story. Walking Dead is the best example of it - bored of the plot like some characters.

I just wish it was set in a more traditional setting without cares and sell phones. Not saying no tech but through some science fiction elements in there with the fantasy. Another thing is even though I love the combat. Like the last Dragon Age game it has the same weakness it gets old after awhile. Some combat aspects (like turn based or Skyrim action combat without a party) is fun regardless of time spent. Where you don't even think of the combat and enjoy the game. The story is also somewhat weak at it's conclusion in my opinion.

The characters, music and art direction make up for those issues mostly however. And the setting and story comes down to opinion really and isn't a universal flaw. Just something to keep in mind before you buy it.

Pros
+ Graphics
+ Combat
+ Music
+ Characters
+ Art Direction

Cons
- But Combat could get old after awhile compared to other Final Fantasy games
- Story is hit or miss
- Elements of the setting feels off

This is the best Final Fantasy in years but not without flaws and objective immersion issues. This is a great game for new players and old Final Fantasy fans to experience.
profile.summary: Best Final Fantasy in years. But not without flaws.

profile.description: Fox, Falco, Peppy and Slippy (and their original voice actors) are back in a new adventure. Players use the GamePad to control their Arwing spaceship and see the view from the cockpit, while the TV shows the overall context of the full battlefield. The game includes a new Walker transformation for the Arwing, a new Gyrowing vehicle and the return of the Landmaster Tank. The game is scheduled to launch during the 2015 holiday season.
profile.reviewText:
I really hate to fault Nintendo for making the most of their system. I mean to incorporate the gamepad controls and motion controls are seeing the Wii U's potential realized. But I can fault them for not incorporating the controls well sometimes. When the controls do work right it offers the best experience or as great of one you can play. When it fails it offers one of the worst controller experiences you can suffer. Let me use the Wii pro controller and this is a masterpiece. Make me use the motion controls and gamepad pro and it turns Star Fox Zero into a bipolar experience with various degrees of mania.

If you can gut out the controls (flying is fine in most cases and fun - though an acquired taste. But the walker controls are a nightmare!) there is plenty of fun to be had with this game and it's amazing. When is shines this is one of the best Nintendo games ever. When it fails? It plunges into trolling and chaos.

The voice acting is very Pixar and I enjoyed it - characters are great. I think many younger kids would struggle at this game with the controls. The game isn't hard, the controls make it harder and more frustrating than it would otherwise be. I could easily give it a three star grade, but there are so many brilliant moments I just can't bring myself to do it. I can't blame those who hate the controls but the controls work just as much as fail. So if you can gut some rough patches out - you will be rewarded.

Pros
- Characters
- Graphics
- Sound
- Great mission (mostly)
- Good story
- Great gameplay when it works.
- Captures Spirit of Star Fox 64
- Voice Acting

Cons
- Controls fail as much as succeed - and it is bad when they do - really, really, bad
- No memorable music
- Forced gamepad and motion control use
- No option for a normal controller

Grade
C+

Closing comment
I can only suggest people who love Star Fox and to give it a chance. I would even say I could suggest any fan of Star Fox to pick it up.
Anyone beyond that group, buy at your own risk of hating the controls. Don't get me wrong you could love them but you could also want a refund after an hour. No middle ground really.
profile.summary: Star Fox Zero shows flashes of being a masterpeice, but is soured by controls that hit as much as miss.

profile.description: During a manned mission to Mars, Astronaut Mark Watney (Matt Damon) is presumed dead after a fierce storm and left behind by his crew. But Watney has survived and finds himself stranded and alone on the hostile planet. With only meager supplies, he must draw upon his ingenuity, wit and spirit to subsist and find a way to signal to Earth that he is alive. Millions of miles away, NASA and a team of international scientists work tirelessly to bring "the Martian" home, while his crewmates concurrently plot a daring, if not impossible rescue mission. As these stories of incredible bravery unfold, the world comes together to root for Watney's safe return.
profile.reviewText:
Let me warn you in advance. This isn't Star Trek. It also isn't Star Wars. The book or this movie is not thrown together to cater to those with low attention spans. No advanced aliens come to save the day or to lay a larva in anyone's chest. There isn't any Mary Sue characters who seem to be perfect at everything they do. Nor are any problems solved easily or without trouble.

There also isn't extra filler here or added drama to appease people interested in anything else. I really admire the book and film for these efforts. Not to mention there are some really awesome Easter eggs. I wasn't expecting them due to my focus on the survival situation. That made them even more amazing and this movie has a great humor sprinkled within.

This is survival Science Fiction at it's best. It showcases the spirit of human beings at their best, against the odds, and how solving enough problems shows you can get past anything. To sum up The Martian as quickly as possible, I would call it Survivor Man meets Apollo 13. What makes this film so special is Apollo 13 was real and although this movie is pure fiction it feels real, because of the hard research the author did in regards to NASA.

Nobody looking for a movie with regards to what I wrote above could ever be disappointed with this movie overall. At least in my mind it offers everything you could ever want in this genre. You don't have to be a lover of science fiction to enjoy this movie about the true strength of the human spirit and mind.

Pros
The Acting. Damon was great but the support cast was also amazing. This could have very easily been the Matt Damon show with below average support actors to save money. Doesn't happen here.
Dialog
Characters
Authentic atmosphere
Pacing
Easter Eggs
Sense of Humor

Cons
Soundtrack. While I enjoyed the humor behind what music he was left with to listen too. The dramatic elements from the instrumental aspect of the more dramatic scenes and movie lacked. I felt more could have been added here and it could have been better. A small stupid thing I know but I had to find some fault with this gem.

Grade A+
profile.summary: Survivor Man meets Apollo 13.

profile.description: Johnny Depp and Armie Hammer star in THE LONE RANGER, from Jerry Bruckheimer Films and Director Gore Verbinski. It's a wild ride of high-velocity action, explosions and gunfights that brings the famed masked legend to life through brand-new eyes. The Lone Ranger (Hammer), the last of his kind, teams with Tonto (Depp), a dark and mysterious vigilante, to seek vengeance after justice has failed them. It's a runaway train of epic surprises, as these two unlikely heroes must learn to work together before the ultimate showdown between good and evil explodes.
profile.reviewText:
It tries to be funny, slapstick at times, wink at you one in awhile, attempting to be fun. It fails most of the time and comes off as just very stupid.
It tries to be "The Crow" of the west, a gritty revenge tale, seeking vengeance and justice against those guilty. It fails, as the Lone Ranger himself, comes across as a goody two shoes, who can't stomach guns and has a laughable sense of justice. So you will never like the very hero the film is about.
It tries to be a action movie, but it fails, as the over the top action is anything but entertaining, it's laughable.
The only character we care about is Tonto, but without Depp's performance, his tale, would have lacked as well.
It can't decide what it wants to be, and because of which it breaks immersion time and time again.
Want to enjoy the comedy? A dude's heart gets cut out. Want to enjoy the action? A horse is in a tree with a cowboy hat on. Want to enjoy the drama? Oh, well the Loan Ranger, pretty much acts like Shaggy from Scooby do, with a Captain America sense of justice. Want to enjoy the love story? Well guess what, there is no chemistry and not to mention his brothers wife.
This is a jumbled messed of a film, that has very brief moments of something entertaining.
I rented it, and I almost feel like it was a rip off and I didn't get my money's worth but I guess it's close to the value.
Sometimes I like movies that get negative press, and people don't like. This isn't one of them.
Glad I rented it, which is the best I can suggest for people to do, because it stinks.
Gets two stars for Depp's performance. A bit captain jack sparrow of the west, but it's fun to watch.
profile.summary: Fails at nearly everything it attempts to do.

profile.description: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom  [VHS]
profile.reviewText:
This isn't the popular opinion but Temple of Doom is the best of the Indiana Jones movies. The reason is with the other two films typical Nazi's are the bad guys and it is surrounded by Christian history. But Temple of Doom dared to be dark, unforgiving and focus on gods from India. This is a very dark film compared to this others by far but there was also a great ending filled with hope. Indiana Jones chosen by a good god from another religion was just so original compared to the others.
There were a few mistakes, Alligators down at the bottom of the river instead of Crocodiles as an example. But this film is just amazing and my personal favorite. I have had some people tell me they hated the dark nature of this film and even liked Crystal Skull better, but that is just bitter crazy talk.
I liked the fact there were two side kicks, and both were very original. One a sissy showgirl and the other a wise cracking kids found on the streets during a World War. The annoying aspect of Willie's personality was on point and Short Round was perfect. I never considered them annoying.
The other two films are great as well of course and I don't consider Indiana Jones Kingdom of the Crystal Skull a Indiana Jones movie.
This easily makes my top 20 movies of all time and still holds up today, I can watch this film a few times a month and never get bored.
profile.summary: Temple of Doom is the best Indiana Jones.

top_5.description: NVIDIA's flagship GeForce GTX 1080 is the most advanced gaming GPU ever created, powered by the new NVIDIA Pascal architecture. The GeForce GTX 1080 comes with ultra-fast FinFET and high-bandwidth GDDR5X technologies, plus support for DirectX 12 features to deliver the fastest, smoothest, most power-efficient gaming experiences. Get the power to drive VR, ultra-high-resolution, and multiple monitors. Plus, bring more realism to every game with NVIDIA GameWorks technologies that deliver a true cinematic experience, smoother gameplay, and amazing new image-capture to share your game. All with the lowest latency and plug-and-play compatibility with leading VR headset.
top_5.reviewText:
This card is amazing. But it isn't beyond incredible like many tech reviewers are saying. The reason for my lack of awe; I only game in 4k and because of which I am not as impressed after Nvidia's questionable presentation that portrayed as just short of something that produces liquid gold. At 1440p I already got 60+ performance with my AMD Nano and my Titan X. So I am not impressed or surprised at all the 1080 manages to do this with ease - it should.

1440 benchmarks mean little to me, and anything lower than that is a joke for this card. If 1440 is the resolution for you buy this card without a thought. A single GTX 1080 can manage 50+ frame rates at 4k but games like Total War Warhammer- it drops in the high 40's. That is amazing for sure but not all that amazing compared to my Titan X which can manage high 30's on average in all games at 4k and the 980ti is just as good as the Titan X.

The price makes this card much more impressive, it is cheaper than both the Titan X and 980ti. But lets be honest reference cards are only great for two kinds of people. Those who want to rip off the cooler right away and water cool it and those who don't care about overclocking - who just want a little tank that will run forever without worry. It also dumps hot air out of your case which is nice but be prepared for a lot of hot hair with the founders cooler.

What is amazing to be is not many reviewers are talking about the heat for the reference cards, 67c is not even close to correct and Nvidia did little to clear it up. This card will easily run about 80c if you let it and it will idle down quickly when it does. So you really have to adjust the fan profile to make sure it does not idle and adjust temp limit. You may even have to go as high as 60%-80% fan speed to get the results you want. The card isn't too loud when adjusted that high either which I was surprised.

I have tried to look at the founders card being priced so high from a balanced point of view and I just can't see how it is acceptable. I see it only as a "need to have it on release day" tax which is hardly different (but cheaper) than what scalpers do on ebay with new tech.
The non-reference cards will be better fit for my needs towards 4k. I can overclock them and get better performance and maybe even max out 4k frame rates.

Plenty of amazing cards to chose from that will be coming out soon, ASUS, EVGA and ZOTEC look to be the best. Some could sell 100 dollars less than the founders, so could sell as much or slightly more. Regardless those are the cards that seem worth it. Assuming you are the kind of person who can wait slightly longer.

The non-reference cards allow for more power, they will cool much better for those don't want to water cool, EVGA will make a hybrid version, and honestly there is no downside. It makes no sense no to wait a few hours, days, week longer (sorry there are conflicting reports). Unless you want to watercool them yourself, or run in SLI.
Founders chips aren't cherry picked as the best ones, nothing about them is really different than no reference. So again the extra money makes no sense.

Pros
- Overall performance especially at 1440p
- reference design
- fan runs quiet even at high %

Cons
- reference model runs very hot
- 100 dollar got to have it now extra tax.
- Will be able to get one soon that runs cooler for the same price or cheaper
- Probably will need to overclock to get around 60fps for 4k

Grade
A- (Founders) A+++++++++++ (non reference/hybrid/watercooled)

Conclusion
A no brainer card for 1440p (honestly it is probably even too much but hey future proofing), for VR it is amazing too but for those of us who play only at 4k it is probably best to wait for non-reference models unless we want to watercool it ourselves or slap a hybrid on it (even still you are overpaying and voiding your warranty). It could use a overclock for some games at 4k.
I imagine the 1080ti and this generations Titan will be able to max out 4k easily with one card. Which is probably why this card can't max out frame rates for 4k resolutions for many games. Nvidia wants big spending pc gamers to look at those two beasts when they come.
top_5.summary: Amazing card! But consider waiting for non reference... I mean, sorry; "non founder" models.

top_5.description: Sapphire Radeon R9 295X2 8GB GDDR5 DVI-D / Quad Mini DP PCI-Express Graphics Card
top_5.reviewText:
The only thing keeping this card for being a perfect 5-star rating is the crossfire aspect and the fact 4 gigs of memory per card does not equal 8 gigs total it still is only 4 gigs. But that only really matters if you are running 4k. Crossfire is hit or miss some games will love it and some games will hate it.

I have gotten some games to run great with crossfire off. Which is the same thing as switching to a single card (which some have said) and it is nice to switch back to crossfire for games that will use it.  The cooling is great and worth the price compared to two reference 290xs.

So why take this card over a 980? Have you seen the benchmarks for windows 10? So my advice if you are upgrading to windows 10? Try this card out and or a 290x. See if you get better performance.

Even with the rumor that te 300 series is out in June. The 200 series will be cheaper and the better deal if it offers great windows 10 performance.

This card performs great right now if I have problems I turn crossfire off. I run it fine on my EVGA 850 gold. Hell, I even tried to run Tri crossfire thinking I couldn't do that but that worked fine too. Affordable upgrade options in the future at the very least. I think a lot of people's problems is they are running this card on their sparkle power 500 w power supply that is 10 years old. Or not disabling crossfire for some games. Disable crossfire if you are not using it. It's simple.
top_5.summary: The only thing keeping this card for being a perfect 5-star rating is the crossfire aspect and the fact ...

top_5.description: Wii U is the revolutionary console from Nintendo, featuring high definition graphics and the innovative Wii U GamePad controller. Play great games in all new ways, only on Wii U!
top_5.reviewText:
Video games are my greatest hobby. They inspire my writing, help me relieve stress and have given some of the best memories of my life. I am also a PC gamer. My PC costs more (built it myself) than many college student's cars. I laugh as I play my games flawlessly at 4k while Playstation and X-box One fans fight to the death in comment sections.

I have my HTC Vive set up at my desk, that costs more than a X-box One and Playstation 4 combined. So you understand I am a hardcore gamer and use my computer for everything, from work to games, I fully embrace the idea of PC gamer master race. I love my PC more than what it considered healthy. But I love Nintendo too. I play my Wii U and 3DS just as much. Currently I use them more than my HTC Vive and my 4k gaming rig.

I can play games like Halo on PC and do it better. Any game X-box offers as a non exclusive I can buy on PC and run it better. Playstation 4, I already have VR so that doesn't interest me. I may not be able to play Uncharted and it is a great series but I can play something almost like it on PC. I can watch Blu rays at 4k and I can do everything those boxes offer media wise and more.

I can't duplicate that with Nintendo unless I use emulators but that robs from the industry and Nintendo. There is only one Mario from my childhood regardless what game he is in, there is only one Zelda, Metroid and that is to name just a few. Nintendo offers experiences that nothing can match or duplicate. Even having a powerful PC with the best of everything can't duplicate it.
The Wii U is a great console and the hardware is amazing. I say this as a PC snob. It has some great games too and offers a experience that blows the other two consoles away.

The criticisms of the Wii U are fair however and I admit that as a fan. It lacks graphic power and so many titles wouldn't come to the system. It's slightly on par with or above a X-box 360. So the Wii U missed out on many gamers. On top of that they confused the hell out of people with the tablet controller, the name and the PR wasn't casual friendly.

The lack of games complaint is also fair. Now the games the do have are typical Nintendo quality and are amazing. But they do lack in number. The worst offense is the lack of a Zelda game - a new Zelda game. Plenty of people bought the Wii U just for a new Zelda alone and instead nothing for years. Yeah we got some amazing remakes AMAZING but that isn't enough for any real Zelda fan.

Nintendo also claims they want to cease production of this console by 2018. There will be a lack of titles even more from this point forward. The new Nintendo system will come out in 2017 and the Wii U will be quickly forgotten with focus on the NX. The most forgotten console ever for Nintendo without a doubt. The 3DS will slowly get killed off in favor of shifting their games to mobile and seems will go the way of the Wii U apart for the fact the 3DS was much more successful. Wii U sales wise pooped the bed regardless of it's quality.

All of that said? I do not regret my purchase for a second. Because I still have my original Nintendo, Super Nintendo, N64, Game Cube and Wii. I play them years later. They all have something to offer. Wii U games aren't going to stop being amazing just like the games made for other systems. Nintendo games age like fine wine when they are good or great. I still play Bases Loaded, Black Bass, and Contra to this day - Mega Man 2 my favorite game of all time - tied on with Castlevania.

Keep in mind you will still be able to buy Zelda Wii U next year if you pass on the NX. The 3ds will still play all the games it does now and I have a windows phone so I won't get to play any of the mobile Nintendo games anyway (not supported) and even if they do become supported the phone sucks for games.

The final reason for my lack of regret is very simple. My niece, playing Mario Cart or Zelda her eyes just light up. She plays all of my PC games, and has seen the best gaming has to offer tech wise. But nothing gets the reaction Nintendo does. I look into her eyes as she lights up and smiles playing Zelda and I see myself as a young kid. That same spark and excitement that made my childhood magical - that got me through good times and bad.

No way will I regret my purchase for that reason alone and even after all these years at 36 that sense of wonder, along with excitement still lives in me the same way it did as a little kid. I'll end up giving my niece my Wii U when I get the NX and hopefully her spark and sense of humor never fades either.
top_5.summary: The forgotten console, that offers the most to gamers.

top_5.description: Rainbow Six Siege is an intense, new approach to the first-person shooter experience. Choose from a variety of unique Counter-Terrorist Operators and master their abilities as you lead your team through tense, thrilling, and destructive team-based combat.
top_5.reviewText:
PROS: If you have a full team of friends? There is no better shooter this year.

CONS: If you don't? You can't rely on strangers who may or may not talk to provide an enjoyable experience. If anything this breeds toxic behavior. So if you are a solo focused multiplayer type person. This game is an easy pass.

I have a gaming system and it isn't for everybody but I find it useful. I expect a dollar an hour for my time invested in any game (yep I have heard all the trolls in regards to the dollar an hour comparisons - so funny kek).
A game like Skyrim? I put in over 300 hours and it is safe to say I made an outstanding purchase even at 150 dollars for the collectors edition at the time. But I have also bought many games where
I lost money on paying triple A price only to manage a handful of hours. Even some indie titles I think five dollars is a great deal on a game I am mildly interested in and then I never play it even though
it is a great deal I lost money.

Enter in RainbowSix: Seige. I have been a fan of these game for years and you can imagine when I found there to be no campaign I was very disappointed. Then I looked at the price tage and scoffed. That much for a non campaign game?
Insane! Typical Ubishit tricks again. But then I looked at it differently because when anyone is overractive they are rarely intelligent. I tried to remember the campaign from the other games and I couldn't. By saying that I could not remember I mean I couldn't even remember the smallest detail of any of the other games.
The book I could easily recall but not the stories told in games. Then I started to consider how many other campaigns I beat in other shooters and I could think of very few. When you think about it? Not really a big deal. Yes people have a right
to be disappointed but it certainly isn't the end of your gaming hobby either.

Then you look at the launch price and many felt it is too high for a multiplayer only game - especially with the season pass. At first I felt the same way but after playing it I can tell you I will easily get the money to time ratio I explained above because I enjoy it.
I compared it to battlefront the ulimate edition. Then I looked at the Black Ops III deluxe edition. Both over 100 dollars, Both with no campaign or a short one and I started to realize it might seem high but it is cheaper than other offerings - outside of Halo which is a
aquired taste and only on one system. And even then it is only 60 dollars in some cases. I just wanted to get those points out of the way. All that matters is how the game is and what it offers.

Believe it or not this could be the best multiplayer shooter of the year with on big IF. You have Halo 5, Battlefront, Call of Duty Black Ops III and then Rainbow Six: Seige. Sadly it does not take a genius to figure out Christmas wise what game people will
probably pick out of that group. It is just not a household names compared to those giants.

But here is the reality. While it might not be able to compare in name. It blows all of those others away as a game. While the others seem like easy choices to make you would be wrong.
This is a real shooter and runs in the same vein as the great shooters in the past and the destructable environment is amazing. Yes battlefront has some of that but nothing like this where it is part of the gameplay and strategy. That is
where this game shines. Another amazing aspect is you really feel incentive to progress in this game. The maps are amazing. The weapons smooth the whole concept is so well done.

I'm as shocked as anyone the start of this year I thought this would be the worst shooter of the year and that you could almost bet on it. While Battlefront or Halo would be the best. Now you could argue Battlefront is the worst and Rainbow Six is
the best. Any fan of multiplayer shooters owes it to themselves to give this game a try but just know this game is unlike other shooters. It is team based. No not a team death match team. Not a zone out a lone wolf it team.
This is a team shooter where you will need to talk with other people. So it is best to have a bunch of friends who want to play this game.

The one down side to this game is just how people are in general. You throw some random stangers together to play a game and you probably won't get the best results. In fact people who are part of an organized team will probably farm teams like that
for hours on end. So if you are going to invest in the game? Do so with the knowledge you shouldn't bother if you have no intention wanting to be social. I can't exactly punish a game that requires teamwork when there are so many other offerings on the market
where you can ignore everything solo or with a friend and have fun.

Grade B+
top_5.summary: If you are a solo player? Look elsewhere.

top_5.description: Platform:Xbox One | Edition:Legacy Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare - Xbox One Legacy Edition
top_5.reviewText:
If you enjoyed the last game? You will enjoy this game. How much really depends on how fast you get bored. Because everything will feel somewhat the same after awhile. This is a very safe play by Activision and one that I am not convinced pays off. Yes it will sell millions of copies. No doubt making a ton of money but it is hard to imagine this won't be deemed the most bland game of the series.

Multiplayer feels infinitely the same. Now the campaign is amazing, and I love the modern warfare remaster I can't save how much I loved those. But let me ask you something? How many people do you know buy call of duty of the campaign? How many people do you know finish the campaign? I know some do but lets face is this game is all about the multiplayer. That is where it truly lacks.

I know I gave Battlefield 1 game of the year, narrowly beating out Dark Souls III but not by much. But that has nothing to do with this average review, I try to be as fair as possible. My friends love Call of Duty on their impression are largely the same was mine - it doesn't do anything different enough and feels the same.

Pros
- Graphics
- Sound
- Gameplay
- Campaign
- Modern Warfare remaster

Cons
- Feels infinitely the same as the previous title
- Plays it too safe
- Lacks where it counts which is multiplayer

Grade
C

Conclusion
While not a bad game, it isn't a good game either. With Battlefield 1 and the surprisingly amazing Titan Fall 2 (still working on my review) I can't make the case for anyone to pick this up. Unless your love of COD is the campaigns and you really want the remaster. The end result is a multiplayer that offers Infinitely the same warfare.
top_5.summary: Infinitely the same warfare.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "1.0" for a product with description "The Wink HUB allows your diverse collection of smart products to speak the same wireless language so you can easily control them-and customize their interactions-from the Wink App. The Wink app is a beautifully designed mobile app that keeps you connected to your home-no matter where you are. Available free on the Apple App Store and Google Play. Products that are Wink App Ready have Wink technology built in and can connect directly to the Wink app without the assistance of the Wink HUB. Wink App Compatible products require the Wink HUB to connect to the Wink app. The Wink HUB allows them to speak the same wireless language, so you can easily control them- and customize their interactions-all from the Wink app. No monthly fees or contracts, EVER. Get help from a human anytime. Download the Wink app and connect your HUB. Wink app available for free at Apple App Store or Google Play. Wink HUB connects in minutes. Blinds, lights, locks, and more, from anywhere in the world! The Wink Hub will not automatically reconnect, since you've changed the credentials that the Hub currently knows. In order to update those credentials, power cycle your Wink Hub by unplugging it and plugging back in. Wait for it start flashing purple (may take several minutes). Then, go to the Wink app Wi-Fi Settings menu under Wink Hub Settings. Enter the new Wi-Fi credentials, tap "Update," and your Wink Hub should connect to your newly updated network! Why isn't my Hub connecting via my Android device Android phones (specifically Samsung Galaxies) have a default setting which causes the phone to jump between Wi-Fi or mobile data, depending on which connection is strongest. Disabling mobile data allows the phone to successfully pair the Hub.". The summary of the review text is "Won't update firmware on fast internet connections with strong routers.  You have to use a hotspot and some distance.".
output:
Avoid this product.  It has serious problems with updating firmware which I think I've finally gotten to the bottom of.

First off, if you're having the problem with the hub not updating and you come across some advice to change the DNS servers on your router to some wink set up to fix the hub, that's for an old problem and the servers are no longer there.

So here's the situation.  If you have a very fast internet connection and the device is too close to the router, it won't update.  My theory is that since the original wink hub had a very slow cpu, and I'm betting they use an 'unreliable' protocol with limited or no ability to ask for retransmission of missed data, that in setups where the firmware update is coming in fast, the hub can't keep up.  Moving it further away from the router drops the connection rate, so its more likely to be able to keep up.  However, even at the periphery of my routers ability to maintain a connection it still wouldn't update.  I even wrapped the hub in a space blanket (sorry Chuck, that doesn't work) and aluminum foil to attenuate the signal while the hub was 100' down the road and at the end of my large collection of extension cords.

Eventually, I hooked it up to the at&t wifi hotspot in my car, which had 1-2 bars of LTE and then placed the hub about 25' away from the car, where I had 1 iffy bar of signal from the hotspot.  My home internet is 240/12.  The car in that signal level was about 15Mb/s down, and at that distance the hub was probably in the single digits for Mb/s download rate.  It failed the first time, was good the second!

So I triumphantly went to hook the hub to my schlage deadbolt, only to have it ask for another firmware update!  And apparently they still haven't fixed the update issue by moving to a reliable protocol or having the server spoon feed the device with a delay loop as it took longer and tried more than one time but still wouldn't complete an update in the house.  Back to the car and extension cord, and it did again update.

Save yourself some and buy the newer wink2 or a smartthings hub, this POC isn't even worth the $25 I paid for it used.

Oh and if you buy a used one and it mysteriously won't work when setting up, you have to email wink support with a photo of the label with the mac address and proof of purchase, and they'll release it from its former owner.  No error message on why it won't set up, I had to figure it out.

profile.description: Dogswell Happy Hips Jerky - Lamb & RiceDogswell Happy Hips Jerky - Lamb & Rice helps your pet maintain healthy hips and joints with glucosamine and chondroitin. It's made from real lamb jerky with added nutrients.
profile.reviewText:
My dogs like these treats well enough.  My question is regarding the amounts of glucosamine and chondroitin that they incorporate.

According to what I'm looking at, you need around 300-500mg of each per 25lbs of dog, per day.  The bag ingredients says 2000mg/kg of glucosamine and 1000mg/kg of chondroitin.  So that means my 100lb dog would need to eat 2lbs of this treat every day to get a satisfactory dose, since a kg is 2.2lbs.

Reading the reviews of the various versions of this treat, I'm also wondering how much of the perceived results are scientifically due to the supplements.  I see a lot of people noting improvements and results in a week or two, yet glucosamine and chondroitin are supposed to take 4-6 weeks before they produce a noticeable benefit.

For our big, fat, old dogs, we've had good luck with the vetrin chewable aspirin for dogs.  They like them, they're inexpensive, and they do a nice job of taking the squeak and creak out of the dogs.
profile.summary: Not enough glucosamine and chondroitin

profile.description: Intel NUC NUC5CPYH, 4K Support via HDMI, HD Graphics, SATA3 for 2.5-Inch HDD/SSD BOXNUC5CPYH
profile.reviewText:
I managed to pick one of these up on ebay for $160 with an already installed ssd, stick of ram and windows 8.1.  That was a pretty decent deal.

Its quite slow for regular windows usage.  I made a little htpc out of it with Nextpvr, which turned out to be quite a fiasco to set up.  For that purpose the performance is acceptable.  I also installed OpenElec on it and that went smoothly with the standard install working fine for 4k video and all the capabilities of the recent cpu/gpu working fine.

On windows in 4k with windows media center, it slowed to a crawl.  It'd play video okay but response to the mouse and keyboard was a little slow and jerky.  In 1080/60 it was fine.

I found that usb wireless devices with the tiny little receivers were having problems.  Once I disabled the internal bluetooth and wireless lan and put the receiver on a 2' usb extension the poor response problems went away.  I've seen explanations that the usb 3 ports aren't fully compatible with the tiny receivers or that the other devices in the box cause interference, but since I didn't need bluetooth and the box is wired I just eliminated all possible sources of problems.

In reading a lot of reviews for the box, it became pretty clear that many problems were caused by using the wrong memory.  This requires a 1.35v stick and won't work properly with regular voltage ram and its picky about which 1.35v ram it'll work with.  I have a ripjaws 1.35v 8GB stick in there.  A little overkill as I rarely saw any app require more than 2-3GB, but the price differential between 4 and 8GB isn't that much.  Intel did the same thing with a few of their other chipsets and I'm not sure why as it tends to cause a ton of customer problems.  I think a lot of people figure they'll throw in that old stick of memory they have on the shelf and that's why there are so many bad reviews.

There is a small fan in the box which you can hear if you put your ear to it and I can feel a very very minor vibration when touching the case.  I've never heard the fan go any louder even when the box is going full blast.

Nice feature set for the price, especially if you can get one used or already assembled.  I think lots of people get one of these setup and are disappointed by the performance, which is pretty weak.  So there is a good secondary market for them  Unless you get full gpu hardware accelerated software, you won't get much out of this.  My former htpc/pvr machine was an older pentium dual core 2.7GHz machine with a 7770 video card.  That was sluggy with 4k video but other than that it was way faster than this.  A gtx 960 would have solved the 4k issue, but those cost more than this whole machine did.

For some performance figures, when this box is recording two shows from my silicondust tuner, its running ~25% cpu load.  When playing back 1080 without hardware acceleration its 80-100%.

Its a perfect little kodi box with openelec and that installed and ran with no problems.  I didn't load it up with 1000 shows, I just tested it with the standard stock openelec installed themes and zipped around all the options.  I didn't see any slowdowns or weak performance like I did with Windows 10.

There's no way I'd have paid ~$300 for one of these, a stick of ram, an ssd and a windows license.  Its not worth it.  However for half price its a decent deal and exactly what I needed.
profile.summary: Nice feature set, weak performance with windows, runs openelec perfectly

profile.description: Whirlpool GU2300XTVQ Full Console Dishwasher with 6 Automatic Cycles, 14 Place Settings, Auto Soil Sensor, 2-4-6 Hour Delay Wash and Quiet Partner III Sound Package: White
profile.reviewText:
You would think after decades of designing and building dishwashers that at least the simple things would be pretty well worked out.  Not so.

Right after buying my house, I turned the 20 year old dishwasher on, empty, to run a cycle to clean it out as the house had been sitting for quite a while.  When I got back from my shopping trip, the house was full of smoke.  Yes, I got a box full of water to catch on fire.  I'm a wizard.  My guess is the prior owner (the second cheapest person on earth) never turned on the heated dry option...ever...and I hit all the buttons when I turned it on.

So the home warranty company rolls out and offers me two models.  The cheapest dishwasher on earth or I could cough up an extra $150 and get this whirlpool gold model.  I opted for the whirlpool and of course got denied by the local utility company for a rebate for paying extra for an energy star unit.  Anyone ever get a utility rebate for anything?

This dishwasher won't clean dishes unless you rinse everything off of them first.  I end up just filling the sink with water in the morning and dumping dishes into it and leaving them there all day to remove anything sticky, dried on, or the usual hard to remove stuff (mustard, chocolate, egg yolks, etc).  If you put anything taller than 4" in the bottom rack in the front it'll block the detergent door from opening, the detergent will turn to a largely unused slurry, and if you're lucky you won't put half the dishes away before you realize that they aren't clean and have bits of detergent clinging to them.

Your next engineering surprise is the absolutely and completely horrid silverware holder.  You can put it on the door where your silverware won't get clean, or you can try to hang it on the end of the bottom rack.  Where it will take 5-6 tries to get it to drop into the slots and not just fall off.  Which gives you the second special effect of popping open, dumping all the silverware into the bottom of the dishwasher.  You see, it has a handy little lever that allows the rack to completely open, and it takes next to nothing to make that pop open.  Really.  It'll pop open while you're dropping spoons in it.  I ended up having to drive a screw into it after the 300th time I took it out to put the silverware away and it popped open and dumped my sort-of clean stuff onto the kitchen floor.

I'd go on, but I think you get the idea.  I've had 1970's dishwashers that cleaned better, used less energy and water because I didn't have to prewash, run loads twice when the detergent door didn't open because a spoon or a tall bowl blocked it, and I don't have to half empty it and then reload it and run it again because half the dishes have bits of food stuck to them.  Run away.  Don't buy this product.  If you buy a house that has this dishwasher in it, surrender hope.

Its rare that I wish daily that a major appliance would explode so I could spend $500 and replace it.  Sadly, I can't make this one catch on fire.
profile.summary: I hate this dishwasher

profile.description: Hungry Dog Value Pack 2lb Bag 1 bag: The Hungry Dog Value Pack is an assortment of Merrick treats that did not quite make the team to receive the Merrick 5star brand. They are great quality treats made in the USA, just slightly mis-shapen or undersized.. All Natural. No artificial coloring or flavoring. Made in the USA with ingredients sourced in the USA
profile.reviewText:
This is a nice bag of random crispy critter parts.  Most of them are potato chip poofy texture and disappear pretty fast.  There were a few of what looked like pork hide rolls that took them a few minutes to work through and some hoof-like items, and what looked like some pig ears with a portion of the rest of the pig attached.  Those were highly prized.  Most of the two bags I got looked to be dried lung...the brown stuff with the crosshatch pattern.  Not a whole lot of crunchy chewy items that would take a while to eat, so I was a bit disappointed.  Mine didn't look much like the ones in the other review photos, so it seems to be a bit of a crap shoot as to what you'll get.

Both dogs (Sammy Destroyer of Toys and Ben Who Must Have His Harness Removed First) like everything in the bag.  Nothing is tiny or seems odd or deformed despite the description that says its odds and ends that didn't meet their standards.  The price is very good for what I got but I down rated it due to the repetition and not getting some of the yummier looking, longer lasting stuff that others showed in their bags.

Still worth what I paid, I might try a few more bags in a few months and see if I do any better.  See attached picture for a sample of what I received.  The two items in the top row in the middle were rarities.  Most of the bag was the brown crosshatched stuff and the poofy 'tail' pieces on the right.

Edit: I did get about 4 more bags over a few months period.  Curiously they all contained roughly the same exact items.  So either Amazon has a huge stock of the same shipment with the same items or Merrick standardized the contents.
profile.summary: This value pack is like a box of chocolates.  You never know what you're going to get.

profile.description: Everlasting Treats are made from natural ingredients without plastics or polymers. They are edible and digestible with an irresistible taste dogs love. Raised dental ridges safely scrub the teeth clean. Can be used as a snack anytime or inside the Everlasting Treat Ball for a chewing challenge.
profile.reviewText:
I'd have suspected that the vanilla mint wouldn't be the favorite between our four dogs, but it is with this barbecue version coming in close second! These treats fit into a variety of the everlasting treat balls. We have the large blue one that takes two 'dog hockey pucks' and two orange ones that take one each. These are about the density of bone, and are made of not particularly nutritious stuff but are excellent for cleaning teeth and giving the jaws a workout.

We have a very old, very big malamute, another pretty old pointer, a big...err...we're not sure what he is exactly, part rotty, part small bear, part cat...and a black lab puppy. Everyone loves the everlasting treats, but they really prefer this flavor and the vanilla mint. The malamute isn't much for chew toys, but he absolutely mauls this like he was 12 years younger. Everyones teeth look considerably better after a few weeks of these treats.

Update: The malamute figured out if he sawed away at one side until about 1/4" was demolished, that he could then pull the whole thing out and just eat it.  Takes him 5 minutes to eat three of them now.  Good while it lasted! :)
profile.summary: Our dogs second favorite everlasting treat

profile.description: Stores up to 100 CD DVD games or photo discsEach double-sided sleeve inside protects 2 discsOrganize titles with built-in disc indexStackable up to 3 unitsIncludes 12-CD portable wallet and online disc indexing software
profile.reviewText:
So I had a problem...my 7 year old and his wolf pack would be playing video games and I'd have 100 video game boxes and disks everywhere, and the disks were being scratched and everything stepped on.  I didn't want to clean it up and getting a bunch of small kids to be responsible is a journey, not a destination.

So I got this, put all the disks in it, and didn't index or organize a darn thing.  For two days I got asked for help finding a particular game, then they got their own system going with my one rule that disk comes out and goes in the box before the next one comes out.  Thats working.  A suspected side effect is that in looking through the case he comes across games he hasn't played in a while and pops them in, or cant immediately find the one he's played constantly for 3 weeks and just pops in a different game.  I appreciate the change in theme music.
profile.summary: Very compact video game storage

profile.description: This unique ball-within-a-ball design keeps pets on their paws and holds their attention for hours! The Teaser Ball floats for summertime fun and is made of an extra durable plastic!
profile.reviewText:
Very hard, thin plastic ball with some holes in it and a ball inside that can't drop out of the holes.  The inside ball can be squished by hand and removed.  So far my Shepherd can stick her nose in the hole but can't get the ball and I think she figured that out because she quit trying.  She likes picking it up by one of the holes and marching around with it.  My Lab/Pit mix can't get his nose in the hole.  The outer ball would likely last a fairly long time with a chewer, the inner ball is very soft rubber.  If the dog got the inner ball out, it wouldn't last long.  You can also stuff it with a bunch of other toys and let them dig those out, which they have fun with.

Some reviews say the hard plastic Jolly balls cause long term tooth wear or breakage, so make sure playtime is supervised and you rotate toys if your dogs don't do that job for you.
profile.summary: Large, very hard, difficult for larger dogs to get a nose in the hole, fun

profile.description: HP Slate 21 Pro 16GB Tablet - 21.5\" - In-plane Switching (IPS) Technology) - NVIDIA - Tegra 4 T40S 1.66GHz - Black F7U54A8#ABA 202
profile.reviewText:
Update:  HP finally released a 4.4.2 update to the Slate Pro 21 which resolves the sleep problem they've been saying was a hardware issue for over a year now.  I've heard it introduces some new issues but most of those are with the bundled HP apps that come with the device.  I don't use those, but people who rely on them may want to do a little searching.

To get the update, either wait until HP pushes it to your device or do a factory reset, wait about 20 minutes and then check under settings/about tablet/software update.  The reset seems to make the update available immediately, and I think its a good idea to start fresh with a major android update.

The HP Slate 21 Pro is a fantastic piece of hardware...except it has a problem that results in it not waking up from a sleep state on occasion.

This is a widespread and well known problem, but I heard in many cases it can be resolved by replacing the unit through warranty (new scalar firmware), not using a keyboard mouse, not installing the 4.3 security update, using a bluetooth keyboard, not connecting an external PC to the HDMI, etc.

I thought I'd be fine because I was going to use it without a keyboard/mouse, perhaps with a bluetooth keyboard and I wasn't intending to connect a PC to it.  Wrong.  My original had the sleep of death problem and nothing I tried that others said resolved it worked for me.  When I contacted HP they didn't respond to any questions, but promptly shipped a replacement.  Which had the newer scalar firmware (3.7) and had exactly the same sleep issues.  Again nothing fixes it.  The original device went on to work superbly for the 3 days after I reported the problem to HP, but it then recurred on the original and the new one.  I tried the original with and without the '4.3 security update' to no avail.  The replacement came with the update already installed.

This is a capable piece  of hardware, Antutu reporting it as being in the top tier of android performers.  It has a very good screen, plenty of ports, and the hdmi input is a great feature.  I figured after the android version was old in the tooth that I'd stick a micro form factor PC or a PC stick into the HDMI port and the usb from that to the screen.  In that configuration the screen passes through touch information to the PC, and I've tested this with a small form factor windows box I already owned.  It worked fine with Windows 7 and Windows 10 preview.

Sadly its got a bug that can only be resolved by leaving the device on all the time, or shutting it down and starting it up for every use.  I've had a few android devices with sleep of death issues, but they were all android related and fixed with an app or OS update.  In fact sleep issues are pretty common in the replacement firmware field, I get them all the time with new versions of CM that are still in the unreleased state.

Since I returned the original, I hope I either get another working replacement or an alternative product from HP that isn't bug ridden.  HP stopped responding to my case updates after shipping the replacement.  Nobody follows up on their customer forum as its "operated by volunteers that may or may not work for HP" and if they do, can't tell you anything,  They did however very promptly jump on my case when I was one day late returning the original product, hilariously threatening to charge me $600 for the replacement,  That end of things works like a well lubricated machine.

If you want a great huge touchscreen android device that'll most likely be stuck at android 4.3 for its lifetime, and you don't mind disabling the sleep capability and leaving it on all the time, or you're okay with turning it off and booting for every use...its a great little machine and a nice front end for a windows PC (or a tv stick like a chromecast or firetv or roku) with touch control on the windows end.

Otherwise, run away.  I'll update if anything changes.
profile.summary: Update to android 4.4.2 to solve the sleep of death problems

profile.description: MSI GTX 970 GAMING 4G: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970, 4GB 256-bit GDDR5, DL-DVI-D, DL-DVI-I, HDMI, DisplayPort, PCI Express 3.0 Graphics Card
profile.reviewText:
So far we're quite happy with this card.  I wanted to get a card to upgrade the R9-270x in the gaming rig and after a lot of research settled on the 970.  While I'd love a 980/980ti or the new high end Radeons, the cost was a bit prohibitive and the radeon's I can afford use more power than the Nvidia cards.  This MSI overclocked 970 actually uses less power than the weaker R9 card it replaces.  I paired it with the lower cost Asus 4k monitor, which is either the low cost 4k editors choice or #1 pick, and where its not the chosen monitor (usually the Samsung) uses the same panel.

I have this in an antec skeleton frame, which is open to the air so low sound is nice.  The old 270x sounded like a helicopter getting ready to take off when we loaded it up to full capability.  The skeleton frame has a huge fan positioned right over the card blowing down, so the fan in this really doesn't run that much unless we're running skyrim or minecraft with 4k mods/textures, and even then I have to look to see if its on.

About the only game we have that wheezes a little is Batman Arkham Knight, and I think the slowness is a game issue that should be resolved.  When we set it for 4k and turn everything on, its averaging around 30-35fps.  Playable but sluggish.  With a few of the settings turned down to normal or low, FPS goes up to well over 60.  Skyrim with everything turned on and STEP mods+ other HD textures runs flawlessly.  I've actually looked at the fans and saw them off while playing.  We've tried a bunch of recent and older titles, everything works.

We've also put Windows 10 on the machine, which is helpful for the 4k screen as you can adjust fonts/icons big enough to see them, much better than Win7 could.  After we upgraded we had to reinstall some of the games but that's probably because we had years of mods added and removed from many of them.

Its turned out to be a great combo.  I bought the card for under 300 on sale and picked up the monitor as a clean item from the amazon warehouse for under 400.  Not exactly a cheap upgrade but pretty reasonable for a very good looking and well performing 4k setup.
profile.summary: So far we're quite happy with this card

profile.description: Make Smart Investment Decisions, Save Time on Taxes
profile.reviewText:
I used to use quicken years ago and it was wonderful for tracking finances, automatically downloading my brokerage and banking data, and doing practically pushbutton taxes at the end of the year with turbotax.

I'd gotten away from it for some years due to the incessant forced upgrades and pushing for revenues.  I've just been using my couch potato portfolio and watching my bank account, and having an annoying tax day once a year.

I recently started using Mint, a free finance product that was bought by Intuit, the maker of quicken.  I was surprised at how quickly it could marshall up my current finances and transactions, sort the latter into categories with 98% accuracy and tell me what I was spending money on and how.  Very simple interface.  There were just a few more things I wanted, like for it to download more than 18 months worth of data, perhaps find the cost basis for investments, and do more processing on my Lending Club account.  I can see data to either 1993 or 1998 at my brokerage and they have cost basis information available for viewing.

So I tried Quicken 2015.  Which was a mistake and if I could give it back for a refund I would.  It actually does less than Mint in many areas.  Specifically it didn't label my accounts (ex: calling my Discover card 'credit card 123456789' instead of 'discover'), it failed to categorize a lot more expenses and transactions, it didn't download any more of the available data (which may be my brokerages limitation), and it didn't even download my Lending Club transactions while Mint did.

I know Quicken is very powerful and the ideal tool for people who like to get down in the weeds on their financial transactions, but I just expected it to be much more than Mint in every way and its not.

If someone has a way to screen scrape vanguard for all of my data and get it into a format quicken will import, I'd be appreciative.  All of my significant financial information is there and I can see it, but it has names of funds/stocks/bonds instead of symbols and what they report is erratic.
profile.summary: Unless you're an "in the weeds" finance person, just use Mint for free

profile.description: Netgear Mingle 778S Mobile Hotspot (Virgin Mobile) Aircard
profile.reviewText:
I bought this device from Freedompop as a refurbished Virgin Mobile device.  Surely a mixture doomed to some sort of disaster.  But its working okay for me.  Someone in the 'refurbishing' process crossed out the VM logo with a sharpie.  You can still see it though.

First off, this has gotten a LOT of firmware updates in the last year, so many problems you see from 2014 to early 2015 may have been fixed by those.  Second, this is a lot to set up for someone not familiar with doing manual setup on a router.

Once you have it set up and on, you can connect to it like any other wireless router from your phone or tablet and go to 192.168.1.1 and then log in with the default password (seems to be either 'admin' or 'password' or blank, depending on the device.  Once in, you can change all of the wireless settings like SSID, password, other wifi configuration, to lock it to use LTE only, etc.  Its got about a dozen pages of configuration stuff to tinker with.  I set mine up to use a hidden SSID so nobody can even see it unless they know the name and password, to show the SSID and password on the main screen, and to show how much data I've used.  You can reset the data manually from these setup screens.

First thing your device will want to do is gobble up about 140-150MB of firmware updates and I don't see any way to do that over another connection, but its possible.  Update your profile and PRL databases while you're in the menu, this will give you the latest information about Sprint's network, such as it is.

Here's the good.  This is a "Sprint Spark" device, in fact it was one of the first if not THE first.  Spark is Sprints latest triple band network enhancement, which is being rolled out but is still in limited availability.  One of the bands is particularly good at penetrating into buildings, so that Sprint "lost inside" effect is minimized if you're in one of the areas they've implemented the new network bands.  Its their intention to build out the Spark capability in the future, so the good news is LTE connectivity with this device should continuously improve, especially in urban areas and near major highways.  If I recall right, Spark is capable of realistic speeds in the 50-60Mb/s range.

The device has a good wifi capability, although my devices only connected with it at 65Mb/s which is okay because in a best case scenario I'm not going to get close to that in real world LTE throughput.

It has two external connectors for small to enormous antennas but be advised that while an antenna improves your chance of reception (download), it doesn't do a lot for transmission (upload).  If you look for 'netgear mingle external antenna' you'll see that there are models from $10-100 and up.  I don't think I'd spend a lot of money for a giant antenna, but a pair of smaller cheaper ones would probably improve fringe connections.  Two of the three Spark bands (and they may be all you get) don't do well with penetrating walls, so putting this in a window might help, especially if you can put it in a second or third story window facing the nearest tower.

It has a replaceable battery, so you can get a second or third one.  Nice feature.  The case itself is flimsy.  It has a ridge all around that enables you to pop it open very easily although so far it hasn't happened to me by accident.

The device also appears to have a GPS inside, giving you basic latitude and longitude and has a button to start and stop tracking.  There doesn't seem to be much about what this does or how to use it.  Perhaps when the device is tethered to a PC with a usb connection and in conjunction with a mapping app that supports external GPS devices it can act as a standalone GPS.  It might be my imagination, but the device seems to acquire an LTE signal better when GPS feature is turned on.  I'd bet that depletes the battery fast.

I've used this for a few hours here and there and it gave me decent email/web browsing even at one LTE bar.  I haven't seen it give me more than 1 bar, but I'm in a suburb and not a Spark area.  Freedompoop gives me .5GB of data a month for free.  My plan is to have my elementary age son keep this in a hidden pocket of his backpack so he can download a few books a week to his e-reader in class, since the school won't allow use of their wifi and his e-reader doesn't have a way of doing anything other than wifi.

What I wouldn't do is buy this as a tether for a general purpose computer like a Windows/Mac machine.  While a phone/tablet/chromebook sips data, a full feature operating system can gluck down a GB or two in short order, doing updates and all sorts of background stuff.  I've seen some people have Windows 10 background update over their hotspot/LTE device and run their bill up into triple figures, or lock them out if they hit a monthly cap.
profile.summary: Capable hotspot I got very cheaply, may be better now with updates to firmware and Sprint Spark network than early reviews show

profile.description: One Box - Two Digital Tuners - Anywhere on Your Network/Dual Digital Network Attached Tuner Device/Watch - Pause - Record Digital and HD Content from Over-the-Air and Cable from any computer on your home network system. Cross OS Compatible with Windows/MAC/Linux. Total Media DVR software included.
profile.reviewText:
In short, you plug your cable with unencrypted digital channels or a broadcast antenna in one port and your home network in the other and any PC on the network can then lock the tuner and record tv shows.  The silicon dust products are exceptional and without reproach in most regards, so its a great choice for basic tv watching, dvr and windows media center usage.

The trouble is that many cable systems have or are encrypting their signals, and this model lacks the cablecard needed to decode the signal.  There is a new model that has the cablecard ability.

But for those with an antenna that want to enable a dvr or watch live tv, these are excellent for the purpose.  Just be advised that you may be limited with some cable systems either now or in the future, and this won't work with satellite for any purpose.
profile.summary: Great product, but becoming more limited in usefulness

profile.description: Acronis True Image 2014 gives home users reliable full system backup, recovery and file synchronization. Back up locally and online using secure Acronis Cloud storage (5GB included).
profile.reviewText:
I abandoned Acronis last year after using it for many, many years without problems.  At that time I had taken a pair of backups of my girlfriends daughters computer with verification and both passed.  I wiped the computer and went to reload a backup and it failed to restore.  Turns out that if you have a corrupt partition Acronis will back it up and not be able to restore it but will verify it okay.  Fortunately in this case the partition wasn't necessary and by 2AM I was able to get her computer working so she could use it in school the next day.  Turns out this bug has been in the software for years.  I changed to Macrium Reflect free edition which has worked fine for me since.

I just bought a new SSD for my son's computer and it came with a code for the new Acronis.  I made a mistake that would cost me the rest of my day.  Instead of ~10 minutes to stick the new drive into a sata port, run an image and swap out the old drive for the new, this turned into a 12 hour fiasco.

I installed the drive and acronis, told acronis to image the old to new drive, it rebooted and gave me an error.  And it was stuck like that.  I could boot into windows after the error, but acronis had put a boot loader on there and for whatever reason it wouldn't boot into it or remove it.  I tried to use the software to remove the acronis bootloader but it told me I had to pay to upgrade the software to do that.  I put a windows restore/bootfix disk in made on another PC loaded from the same windows install disk and at the same patch level and it said "not the same version of windows".  I used Windows' automated boot fixer, it said nothing was wrong.  I pulled out the original windows 7 SP1 install disk I'd used on the machine, same 'not the same version of windows'.

To make a long story short, after looking this up and seeing that Acronis had been doing this since 2008, no support thread ever showed a resolution other than loading windows from scratch, and trying every little thing I could come up with to fix the boot loader, I ended up just restoring a Reflect image I'd taken a few weeks ago and having my son re-do all the installs and changes he'd made since.

Acronis.  Never again.
profile.summary: Gave up on this last year and I should have stuck with that

profile.description: SanDisk Ultra plus 32GB class 10 memory card with SD Adapter
profile.reviewText:
The product itself seems to have been pretty well reviewed...I just wanted to chime in with a customer service story.

These days most things don't have much of a warranty and even when they do, its made useless by the manufacturer forcing you to jump through hoops to get a product replaced, or by having you pay for return or both way shipping.  Which often costs more than buying a new product.

I've bought many of these same cards for use in android tablets and phones, and I had one that started flaking out a bit.  It was in a windows tablet which started reporting the device ejected when it wasn't, and I'd have to reboot to have it re-appear.  It did the same thing in an android phone.  I figured I had a doorstop for a teeny, tiny door.

Just on a lark I checked out sandisks warranty on it.  Lifetime.  They pay shipping both ways.  Just a little online form with my info and what was wrong with it.  Simple and free!  You don't see a lifetime free shipping warranty with no hoops to jump through.

I filled the form, got an approval and shipping label, packed it inside a ziploc baggie inside a tiny box and dropped it at the UPS store.  In a week I had a brand new retail packaged replacement including another sd card adapter.  Wow.  I expected some recertified or bulk pack product in a bag.

My hat's off to you Sandisk.  Way to stand behind your products and give zero compromise incredible customer service all the way.  I'll be buying only your products in whatever segment you sell them into from now on.  You've earned my loyalty.  The only other company that ever did it this well was Fiskars, when they replaced an entire ten year old pole saw because a clamp broke.
profile.summary: Kudos for amazing customer service and standing behind the product!

profile.description: Color Beige overall Size 38-inch W/27-inch L/62-inch H
profile.reviewText:
Just got this in earlier today.  It was missing its instructions, the manufacturer has a web site but decided not to post instructions there (???) and you have to ask customer service to send them to you.  So far customer service doesn't exist.

So I found a video on youtube of an Arby's employee putting one together.  Don't bother watching it.  She persistently puts it together wrong, has to take it back apart and redo it again.

Just looking at the picture and tinkering with it for half an hour, I managed to get it together without the instructions.  The particle board is very thin, it has very thin faux fur glued to it, there are exposed bolt heads, several of the fasteners (especially the screw hooks for the 'hammock') poke through the fabric if you screw them in all the way, and this is quite positively made for smaller cats.  I do have a very big, somewhat fat cat.  Were he half his size, he might fit into the enclosures.  No chance of him using that trampoline thing on the right that sticks out for anything other than a step.  I'm guessing a 10-12lb cat would be the absolute max, 8-10 is more likely.

In short, this is cheap and you get what you pay for.  It'll probably last some years as I can fix things pretty well and the cat may never even use it.
profile.summary: A fine expression of the term "you get what you pay for".  NOT for larger cats.

profile.description: High Back Blow Up Flame Inflatable Chair. Inflatable furniture is a great way to make any space look whimsical and full of life. These fun chairs blow up to be a really cool decor statement and best of all they are comfortable. These wacky inflatable chairs will bring years of use and fun to any room in your home. These chairs are great for company, if you do not have enough seating you can easily blow up a chair or two in minutes. They will be your favorite seats in the house. The chairs are perfect for children's bedrooms, play areas, living rooms, inside or in the out doors! The thick plastic construction is tough, resisting most punctures and is air leak resistant so you will only have to blow it up once, and rarely refill the air. Imagine your dorm room decked out in wild inflatable furniture! You will love it. And no matter what your thinking it will not look cheap or chinsey, instead it will be a permanent fixture in you home matching all your other crazy decor
profile.reviewText:
This chair is made of about the same quality and thickness of vinyl as your typical inexpensive inflatable pool toy.  It is most definitely not the same caliber as serious inflatable furniture, but its also a lot less expensive.  However my 7 year old and his video game playing wolfpack all agree that its one of the coolest chairs they've ever seen.  One was sitting in it while another used the back as a footrest and it was kicked around and jumped on by 45-100 lb kids for a few hours and remained inflated the next day.  I'll come back and report if and when it goes to the Great Inflatable Chair Place In The Sky.  In  the meanwhile its joined the Intex inflatable sofa for instant kid movable furniture anywhere in the house.

When people have problems with the valve not holding air or the product seams becoming damaged, chances are that you're overinflating it and not lubricating the valve.  Most inflatables of this type work best when fully inflated but still with a bit of give to it.  Overinflating it and then jumping on it or putting a heavy load on it will weaken the seams and cause leaks.  If you can push your finger into the chair and it moves across the floor before you push in a couple of inches, you put too much air into it.

Inexpensive vinyl valves also need to be lubricated before and after filling to make sure they aren't damaged and maintain a good seal.  If you're going to use an inflator, put the valve in your mouth to lubricate it with spit and blow into it a bit to open the valve and get it started.  Then use your inflator to about 75-80% more spit and inflate the rest of the way by mouth and seal the valve.  99% of non-defective products will inflate without a leaky valve this way.  Sticking a dry inflator nozzle into a dry closed valve, overinflating and then dry sealing the valve will lead to leaks a fair bit of the time.  If you're one of the 1% who still leak, try warming the valve with a hair dryer to soften it and let it seal, let it cool a bit, and try inflating by mouth again.

I'd throw a blanket or something over it to protect it, and its definitely not going to last in a household with cats or dogs with claws.

Edit: I've had as many as six kids up to ~140lbs punching, kicking and jumping on it.  Its still in one piece.  I had to put a little air in it once, but thats probably because it got cold for a few days.
profile.summary: Thin and not strong looking seams but decent...here's how to avoid leaks

profile.description: Immediately Block all - Robo Calls, TeleMarketer Calls, Political Calls, Survey Calls, ,Donation Calls, Junk Faxes You don't need to do a thing! You don't need to hear the spammer first and then block the number. SENTRY brings peace from the moment you plug in. No Setup Required No External Power Required 9999 Black/White List Requires caller ID service to work
profile.reviewText:
I tried a few call block products but found that they're incompatible with my uniden phone.  No caller ID is passed to the phone when its called no matter how I configure it.  Its just an Ooma Telo with a wire to the blocker and a wire from that to the phone.  Call Waiting ID passes, but not initial caller ID.

I also found that the first two rings on a call are 'eaten' by the telo/sentry combo.  In other words, when someone calls your phone won't ring until the 3rd ring on the callers end.  This made for some issues with Ooma voicemail picking up the call before my home answering machine did.  And I've had a few instances where Google Voice voicemail picked up the call when people call my GV number that's forwarded to the Ooma.

Deciding to live without callerID, knowing that only my whitelist calls (or persistent human callers) will get through, I kept the Sentry.

I've been running it in "off" mode for about two weeks, Everyone I know has called and been added to the whitelist.  I blacklisted a handful of numbers that were autodialers.  In another week or so I'll turn the device "on" so it'll block all non whitelisted calls with the voice recording to press a number to get through. I had such a setup built into a VOIP phone system from AT&T about ten years ago and it was extremely effective.  Not only did I never get a telemarketer or political call, once that system had been in place for a year they simply stopped calling.  I must have landed on a lot of "never answers" lists.

Simple, easy to use.  Mine came with no cords/cables which wasn't a problem for me as I have a hundred phone cords, but it seemed silly to save 50c and not include one.  The instructions sheet was also minimal, but a full manual is available online.

I'll report back once I've had a month or so of "on" operation.  Now all I need is one of these for my cell phone. ;)

Edit: I've had this in place for a while now and its awesome.  I've had two live telemarketers press the 0 key to get through and all I did was hit the reject button.  All autodialers have been defeated.  My phone only rings when someone I know calls.  I've had a few instances with confused doctors office and vacuum repair places calling and getting the 'no telemarketers' message but it was just 'hey man, your phone is weird!' stuff.  Never had anyone say they tried to get through and couldn't.

I now have all calls from people I know routed to my google voice number, which then rings this ooma telo phone, my cell, my tablet, and my computer running chrome.  Everything rings and I see the caller ID on the other devices but not the uniden phone.
profile.summary: So far so good!
