profile.description: SToK Caffeinated Black Coffee Shots delivers 40 Mg of caffeine per serving, which is equivalent to a shot of espresso. Its a black coffee shot that puts more caffeine in your coffee. Comes in a creamer-like container for portion control. Limit to 2 servings per day. Not for use by children under age 18, pregnant women or the caffeine-sensitive.
profile.reviewText:
I got this 264 count in May of 2014.  The ingredients are listed on the box and its basically corn syrup, brewed coffee and caffeine.  It doesn't taste at all like espresso, more like strong coffee with a little sugar in it.  Mixing it with about an ounce of milk gives you a vaguely coffee tasting beverage.  In other words, if you put this in a full 8oz or 12oz drink, you probably wouldn't even notice it.  So its not like adding a shot at a coffee bar, it won't really punch up the coffee flavor of a cup of coffee.

This kind of works for me because I'm trying to get off of drinking coffee because I like it with sugar and cream and its about 200 calories by the time I'm done with a very large cup.  I can add this to something else and get the caffeine zing without the extra calories.

After one, I had a caffeine zing that seemed disproportionate to the amount listed on the box.  Usually an 8oz cup of strong coffee will wake me up but not put me on edge.  This made me clean the kitchen and do the dishes and talk 20% faster.

I'd go with this vs an energy drink, as those are a huge waste of money.  I've read a ton of analyses on those and while the ingredients sound impressive, aside from the caffeine there isn't anything in them that will increase mental attention or energy levels.

BTW, before I saw the 'not for under 18' note I gave one to my 9 year old.  Seemed to affect him less than when he asks for a cup of coffee and this isn't much different caffeine-wise than a can of cola.

So it does what it says as far as improving the caffeine load of a drink, but doesn't really deliver much in the way of coffee taste.  I got them very cheap so I'm happy with them, and I offloaded a lot to a friend who works night shift and supplies k-cups to her employees.  But another friend who constantly complains about having to buy a second shot of espresso for coffee bar drinks wasn't impressed as it doesn't change the flavor anywhere near as much as that second shot of real espresso.

They're also just packed loose in a box, which of course the shipper launched off a wall or dropped from a good height as it had a crushed corner.  One cup burst and made the rest sticky and most of them were dented or dinged.  No biggie, I just rinsed them and put them in a clean box.
profile.summary: Good zing, doesn't taste like espresso

profile.description: LCD display Touch Screen Digitizer Assembly for Motorola Moto G XT1032 XT1036 with Frame Tools
profile.reviewText:
This is the first time I took a cell phone apart.  I've taken laptops apart with mostly good success, but with lousy vision and fat fingers, this was a test.

My kit came with 9 tools.  Two of them were the same plastic pry tool, two of them were the same torx screwdriver, there were two triangular plastic tabs, there was a keyring, a tiny philips head screwdriver and a little suction cup.  I didn't use the last 3 items.  I'm guessing they have one kit for lots of different repairs.  The tools were nothing to write home about, and I wish I had a better plastic pry tool, but they got the job done, none of them broke, and the torx driver fit the screws fine.

I'd looked at 3 different repair videos and read lots of reviews in preparation.  Another things I needed were a good bench light a razor cutter and a heat gun, but a hair dryer would have done nicely.

You'll need to apply heat to the ribbon connections, blow heat under the battery, and under the motherboard to get them to release.  If something doesn't want to come off as easily as it looks in the video, put some heat on it for a while and then try again.

Everything went fine except for the ear piece, which came apart when I did it the way they showed in the videos, which was to use a razor cutter or a tiny set of tweezers to pry it up from the inside.  This is a mistake.  I ended up with the grill still stuck firmly into the front case and the speaker with a little copper coil and the two tiniest little wires hanging coming up.  I didn't break the wires, but I had to apply a LOT of heat to get the grill to release and pushed it from the outside (where you'd put it to your ear) to get the grill to pop out.  I'd recommend applying tons of gentle heat to both sides, especially the outside at the top of the screen, and pushing it out from the grill side.  I managed to put it all back together but it didn't work when I finish assembled the phone.  The good news is that I don't need it, I always use the phone on speaker or with an earbud.  Which is good because its .50c plus $18 shipping from China or about $8 off of ebay.  Another case where the maker should have put the 50c earpiece into the frame and not required replacement of such a small delicate piece.

I'm confident that most people who are okay with fixing things, go slow and take your time especially with warming things up before removing them can do this.  My display ribbon cable needed a fair bit of heating before it came up.  They also remove a little bit of yellow film from the smaller connector before flipping it open and they don't mention doing that, you had to pay attention to see them doing it.  Its also almost completely irrelevant what happens to that cable as long as you don't damage the larger connector.  There's a new one on the new display screen/frame.  So if you rip or destroy the cable it doesn't matter.  You don't even need to do anything with the smaller ribbon connection unless you're only replacing the glass and didn't buy the full frame piece.

I can't compare the old screen to the new one, but it looks fine.

This took me roughly an hour including reassembly and putting the sim in.  Now that I did it once I could do it again in about 20 minutes.

If you get the tool set and you have one of the two pictured blue plastic pry pieces and one torx screwdriver that fits, that's really all you need.  I used the blue plastic triangles while removing the motherboard but anything slim and non metallic like a toothpick or a popsicle stick would do.  I just needed something to hold one side while prying the other.

And now I have all the tools I probably need to repair other phones and tablets, so if I break anything else I'll feel pretty confident in fixing it.
profile.summary: Good screen, got all the tools and they worked fine, and it wasn't that hard to do.  Wish they'd included the ear piece.

profile.description: Comoze Lamps Compatible Mitsubishi 915B455011 Lamp, Includes Housing
profile.reviewText:
Lets get a few things out of the way first.  What is advertised here is a Osram bulb supplied by Mitsubishi.  What I received is not that.  In fact there is no label at all on the product and just a few numbers stamped into the plastic.  Its a good looking knock off.  If you paid less than $70ish for the bulb you're not getting an actual genuine factory original type bulb.  Its that simple.  When I bought this there were two sellers; one at about $85 and one around $45.  The second seller is no longer listed as of this writing.

Does it matter?  Its like using expensive alkaline batteries vs the "Mighty Super Heavy Duty" ones.  You might not notice the difference at first, but you will eventually.  My original bulb in my 73640 went for well over 2 years of very regular viewing and still worked, but was dim.  Knock-off bulbs have a lower cost ($15-40) but might only last 3-6 months before dimming or popping.  It might not be as bright as a genuine high quality bulb.  It might be a bulb intended for another purpose that happens to fit in the housing suited to a set.  It might even be a fire hazard.  One of the cheap bulbs I tried smelled like burning electronics until it died.  The wire insulation on another cheap bulb didn't quite fully cover the wire.

I've tried many inexpensive knockoff bulbs, From $18 to $40.  The $40 bulb was dead on arrival.  The $18 bulb worked great out of the box but after 3 weeks it was so dim that even with every setting on the tv turned up, the picture was barely viewable.  I got a bulb that was allegedly right out of the same model set I have (smashed during delivery), but it had some extra cage pieces on it that while easily removed meant it didn't come from my model as it wouldn't have fit.  At least that one had the right markings and labels to show that it was a real factory bulb and it lasted another couple of years until I replaced it with this one, so I could hold the still decent one as a backup.

I was saved from any out of pocket costs by the wonderful Prime 30 day return policy.

My lessons learned from these experiences are to pay up for a real bulb from someone like Philips, Osram or another top maker.  Don't fiddle with <$50 bulbs or you're probably in for an hour of replacing the bulb and then putting it back in the mail for a return and waiting on another one.  Make sure you know the return/replacement policy before you buy.  A lot of bulb sellers want you to pay to return the bulb and even for them to ship you another one.  Make sure you keep all of the packaging for the 30 day Amazon return period.  If you do have to do a return, don't return the bulb in the small box it comes in.  Repack the bulb into that box and place it in a larger shipping box with more packing.  Otherwise Amazon might get a smashed bulb and not give you a refund.  When you get your bulb, check its markings against one of the many web sites that show you how to determine whether you have a fake or not.  Don't count on the bulb being real because it comes in the same box with the same markings...fraudsters even make boxes that duplicate the high end bulb makers boxes.  Every bulb I've bought came in the exact same box.

Bottom line is that you do get what you pay for.

As far as replacing the bulb, its ridiculously easy.  Make sure the set hasn't been on for about 30 minutes.  On the back of the set is a plastic door with a couple of screws holding it on.  Once you've removed that you'll see the bulb.  It'll have 1 or 2 screws holding it in.  Remove those.  Pull out the bulb.  Stick the new one in using the rails as a guide.  Do not touch any non plastic portion of the bulb as the oils/dirt/dust from your skin may cause the bulb to pop when its turned on or soon after.  Replace the bulb screws, put the door back on and put its screws back in.  Note that the set will not start without the door on, it has a switch that detects that.

If you can replace a light bulb or put batteries in a kids toy you can do this.  Replacing your bulb when it starts to dim (usually 2-3.5 years) is a good idea.  Keep the old one in the shipping box, remember to not touch the glass parts, and that makes a nice backup if your new one pops.
profile.summary: Don't get suckered in by cheap bulbs or fakes.  This one SHOULD be a real high end bulb

profile.description: The stylish Samsung Gear Live takes your wearable experience to the next level by combining Googles Android Wear platform with Samsung mobile innovation. Gear Live is compatible with any smartphone with Android 4.3, Jelly Bean or higher, so your app notifications and personal information come with you, like flight status and messages. And when you say OK Google, you can ask a question about anything, from turn-by-turn navigation steps to team stats-even find out your heart rate.
profile.reviewText:
Other reviews seem to cover the features and cons of the watch.  One thing though is that many reviews are from a year or more ago and the newer software has brought a lot of features and fixed a lot of bugs.

Almost every android smart watch has basically the same hardware inside (quad core 1.2GHz, 512MB ram, 4GB storage) using the same or similar system-on-a-chip, with the differences being the styling and the screen.  This has one of the biggest screens.  The cool part is once you resolve the update problem, it'll come up to the same level as most other smart watches, enable wifi capabilities, and be able to go toe to toe with watches that are twice the price.

First off, a lot of people buying these are getting an open box item that was supposed to be wiped back to factory state, and the box was resealed.  Many of them weren't wiped correctly and have a 'userdev' software load.  It works but it won't update to the newer android wear. The good news is that if you're modestly handy with computers you can fix this.  If your watch is current (as of 3/1/16) your build should be MEC23G or later.  You can find this by swiping left, picking 'settings', scroll to the bottom and click 'about'.  If you'red stuck at a lower build, click system update under 'about' and if it says there are no update, you have one of the flaky watches with the wrong firmware.

You'll need a windows pc, a usb to microusb cable (like the one you charge your phone with), v2 of the software (not v3, that has bugs) and about 20-30 minutes to resolve the problem.  I've included download links for the software and a link to the developers youtube video where he explains step by step how to do it.  The method he uses is very safe...if you mess it up you'll be able to start over again.

The tool you need.  Amazon removed the link, so search for 'rootjunkysdl' and then look on the site for the gear watch live restore tool, v2.

Once you've downloaded and unzipped the files, watch this video.  Read ALL of the instructions on the pc screen and listen to each portion of the video.  Its not hard at all.  Amazon removed the link so look on youtube for "Samsung Gear Live Super Tool", its a ~12 minute video.

Once you've finished the process of unlocking, reloading and a factory reset, the watch will be at its original factory state.  Pair it with your phone with the android wear app and when its complete on the watch go to 'settings', 'about phone' and tap 'system update'.  About 45 minutes later the watch will ask to be reset and you'll have a factory fresh, latest android wear version on the watch.

The coolest part of this is that this watch has wifi capability and this turns it on.  You can connect it to any private or public wifi and use that capability instead of bluetooth.  You don't even need to have your phone with you, as googles cloud capabilities will let you get messages, notifications, etc.

Since this watch has essentially the same basic hardware as much newer watches, you can expect continued support and updates and get the same sort of functionality.  The only things it doesn't have and can't do is take/make calls using the watch only with its own sim card, and it doesn't have a camera.  Which is okay because so far the cameras in smart watches are horrible, make the watch bigger, and take away battery life.

It actually has some features that other watches don't have, like heart rate monitor.  I have mine configured with a weather watchface (free) that shows my steps, activity, the weather, time and date and I can tap any part of that screen to get detailed information.  No more phone/watch/fitbit combinations, one device.  Nice.

Your notifications from phone apps will show up on it, so you can see who's calling, texts come through and you can respond to those by voice, you can send email by voice, and you can tell it to make a call for you through your cell phone, but you have to use the phone to talk/listen once its made the call.  There are hundreds and hundreds of apps that either run right on the watch or on the phone with a companion part on the watch.

The hardware inside is a quad core 1.2GHz arm chip with 512mb of ram and 4GB of local storage.  About the only way the 4GB will be a problem is if you decide to load music on it.  The watch apps are much smaller than most regular android phone apps.  I have a ton of them loaded and I'm still below 50% utilization.

Since this is such a common, almost generic platform for android smart phones, there is also a lot of android development going on.  So there should be a lot of interesting custom roms to load and continued development should if eventually get eol'd from google direct development.  Now that you learned how to flash it back to stock, you'll be able to use the same tool to flash custom roms.

The one flaw is that the charger thing snaps onto the phone and its cheap plastic. Eventually you'll break it although I see people who've had it for more than a year.  I guess it depends on how much care you take with it.  They're $6-10 to buy, right here on amazon.  If you search for "samsung gear live watchband" you'll find numerous 22mm watchbands from $10-100+.  There are some really nice looking choices in the $10-25 range.  I don't mind the stock band but I'll probably get a nice metal band.
profile.summary: How to fix the watches that come with the wrong software load

profile.description: Capture more photos, record more Full HD videos and play more music on your mobile phone with reliable SanDisk microSDHC memory cards. By adding more memory to your mobile phone, you can transport and store more photos, Full HD videos and music - so you can get the most out of your mobile phone. Do more with SanDisk mobile memory cards.
profile.reviewText:
Little known fact about flash memory cards...the 'rating' or 'class' figure is only for large long sequential writes like you'd get when recording high definition video with a camera.  It has no bearing on the chips general performance or its ability to read and write information in a more random scattered manner like a phone or tablet would need.

Sandisk products tend to excel in this area, and as a result can offer substantially improved performance in cameras, tablets and other devices that use a memory chip more like a disk drive and less like a recording medium.

As a result, you can buy a class 4 or 6 sandisk product and except for applications like HD video recording, it'll outperform many class 10+ cards.

Do a search for microsd cards and random read/write performance.  You'll see a variety of sandisk products in the upper part of the benchmark ratings.
profile.summary: Get sandisk for your phone and tablet memory needs

profile.description: This soft and comfortable Slumber Pet Thermal Mat works with a pet's body temperatures to maintain consistent warmth. Reversibleone side is soft plush in a leopard print, the bottom is Berber Innovative thermal interior layer uses a cat's body heat to keep them warm No electricity required See the Specifications tab for product details.
profile.reviewText:
We bought two of these based on good reviews.  We have a couple of cats that live in the garage and it gets down to 60ish out there at night. We also have a big fat old male cat that lives indoors.

The two girls out in the garage took to it immediately and even sleep together on it, which says a lot because they don't really like each other!

The male cat was a little concerned about it at first due to the crinkling sound.  But I put it on the table next to the window where he likes to sleep and then noticed about 3/4 through the day that I hadnt seen him.  Right on the pad.  He usually comes down and watches tv with me at night and sleeps on my head, but he decided to stay on his pad most of the time and sleeps there now.

Which is a major plus, since having a 20-something pound cat sleeping on your head isn't the greatest thing in the world.

I've washed them in our front loader on delicate/handwash and they came out clean but the fabric holds plenty of fur.  Hung them out to dry per the instructions, which didn't take long.

These are nice for reflected heat without electricity.  Perfect for indoors and milder climates.  While it'd be better than nothing for outdoor/feral cats during northern winter weather, I think you really need something that plugs in for those applications.

We have a pair of the 6 watt pet bed heaters on a big, thin cardboard box with a thick towel over them and the thermal mat on top of the towel in between the heated pet bed pads.  The girls switch between the electrically heated pads and the thermal bed.  Total of 12 watts to keep them warm and comfortable is a pretty low price to pay.

We'd been using a heating pad on low, but the thermal pet bed heaters use less electricity and have much thicker plastic covers so claws have a harder time penetrating.
profile.summary: Cant get the cat off of it

profile.description: One of our hottest selling computer speaker / subwoofer combination. Classic lines, timeless design, compact and efficient. The CA-3090 is a 2.1 sound system that offers you high quality audio in space saving form. The satellites allow for an optimal angled listening experience with amazing sound clarity and punch. The system control pod turns the speakers on and off, with an LED power indicator, master volume control, a 3.5mm auxiliary input jack and headphone output jack. Includes subwoofer mounted volume control. Designed for laptops, desktop PC computers, gaming systems, tablets, smartphones, DVD players, iPods and MP3 players. AC powered 110V only.
profile.reviewText:
Pretty darn good speakers for a variety of uses.  I'm going to use them to replace the audio on my flat screen tv, since it appears that by law the included speakers have to stink.  I'd rather the set was a little thicker and had usable speakers.  So far I've yet to have anyone show up to my house and whip out a micrometer to see how thick my tv is.  I'm also not interested in firing up a 300-500 watt sound system to watch the news or for my son to watch a kids show.

Anyhow, I've looked at a few of these in the same ~$30 price range.  This one has very long cables, longer than any other I'd seen, which is a plus if you're going to use them on a big tv.  The bass box is small and has the large vent on the side, not the bottom, which many other speaker sets had.  I have two places for it, a hard surface and a spot on carpet, so bottom bass port is bad.  On many of these there is also no cover or screen on the bottom bass port, just a bare speaker.  That's going to get ripped pretty quick if you aren't careful handling it.

This also has adjustable bass.  Not found on many 2.1's this size/price, and a volume control on a little pod.  The pod has a headphone jack and an aux 3.5mm input.  Really handy!

Sound is very good.  I'm not an audiophile but I've tinkered with small 3.5mm/bluetooth speakers that went from $12-100 and this sounds by far the best.  Good sparkling highs although you're going to need to lower the bass at full volume level.  It starts sounding rough until you drop it to below the halfway point.

If you want something to plug your phone/tablet into, replace a bad flat screen tv speaker, or put out great sound-on-the-cheap from your PC, this appears to be the winner.  The runner-up was the Creative 2.1 that runs around the same price, $30ish.  That has shorter cables, no bass adjust, bass port on the bottom, etc.
profile.summary: After testing a number of these, this one wins for longest cables, adjustable bass with port on the side, great sound

profile.description: Supports for LGA1155 2nd Generation Intel Core Processors/Touch BIOS delivers the innovative new way to modify BIOS/4X performance boost with mSATA Intel Smart Response Technology/Supports USB 3.0 with superfast transfer rates of up to 5 Gbps/High speed SATA3 storage interface with superfast 6Gbps link speed/GIGABYTE 3x USB Power with On/Off Charge USB ports/CrossFireX multi-graphics support for ultimate graphics performance/Hybrid EFI technology with DualBIOS for 3TB HDD support/HDMI graphics output for smoother HD video playback/XHD technology accelerating hard drive performance with ease/GIGABYTE DualBIOS technology delivering highest level failure protection
profile.reviewText:
I really liked this board as a very cheap budget z68 board, but its got some warts.  Gigabyte is certainly good about keeping up with bios updates and driver versions on their web site, but these boards have been plagued by problems with the board locking up if you use the power switch on the power supply.  They had a fixed bios out for it but as of this writing sent out another bios update that says it 'improves' the problem, which means it hasn't been solved and certainly not by the last 'this fixes it' bios update.  But that problem only affects some configurations.

The fast ram (that won't do you much good, at least not with sandy bridge), the usb 3 and the sata 6 are all appealing features.  But then you get a parallel port and a serial port and a TPM connector that you probably don't need or want.  Clearly a board made for a managed corporate type environment, but I cant think of many of those that are going to want an enthusiast z68 board.

There is only an hdmi port, no vga, dvi or display port.  Too much room taken up by the serial and parallel port.  No USB 3 header for a front panel mount.  Realtek network and sound, not the intel network chip.  More expensive boards will have more display options and a dual intel gigabit setup, but most people will be satisfied with the single hdmi port and single gigabit.  You won't be able to do dual monitor on this without a video card added in.

The z68 gives a lot of choices for overclocking and providing hdmi out for the onboard cpu graphics.  Other 1155 socket chipsets offer either overclocking or integrated video out, but the z68 does both.  The newer z77 boards are superseding these and will offer the same capabilities along with ivy bridge cpu support (intels next generation), and multiple full speed pcie 3 slots.  Since those are sliding in around the same price point as the z68 boards, you might look at those.  Other than odd features most z68 and z77 boards perform quite similarly so buy on features and price.  In the same feature set, a more expensive board will usually have thicker layers, a larger copper base for the cpu and generally more robust voltage regulation and power management.  But this cheap gigabyte is decent enough for basic overclockers or performance enthusiasts on a budget.

But maybe I just need to dust off an old daisy wheel printer and hook it up to the parallel port to really appreciate it...
profile.summary: I wanted to love this board, but I cant

profile.description: The bubba 20 ounce Classic Travel Mug feature the RealTree design is for personal use and is perfect for use in transit or at work. This travel mug is made of high quality food grade quality stainless steel and has dual wall insulation, made from high performance insulation to keep your drinks hot or cold longer. Designed to fit most cup holders, it has an easy-drinking lid and features a locking flap. Holding just three 8 ounce cups, its the perfect size to get you going in the morning without slowing you down.
profile.reviewText:
Edit: I have two bubba cups.  They say to hand wash them and they mean it.  One is this model for cupholders and the other is a regular shape.  When put in the dishwasher both have the bottom plastic part separating from the metal part in the middle.  I have lots of other insulated cups that do fine in the top of the dishwasher but these don't.  I won't buy more as I have little interest in hand washing stuff.

Original review:

My new car came with cup holders that apparently weren't well thought out because all they'll hold is a can.  Anything bigger like 98% of my go-cups are won't fit at all.  You'd think after making cars with cup holders for 50 years, we'd have that part of the design knocked out.

I saw this cup and liked it because it has a huge capacity and will fit in a can-size cup holder.  Unfortunately they also put all three cupholders in a row so when I use this, it blocks the one next to it.

Keeps things cold, easy to clean, very solidly made.  I'm going to buy another one.
profile.summary: Solid, high capacity, fits in small cupholders.  Not dishwasher safe.

profile.description: MIU France plastic pull string salad spinner, item # 487. This multi-functional salad bowl / spinner / storage bowl is a perfect addition to any kitchen. Both the lid and colander are removable for easy cleaning. The clear plastic bowl keeps the salad crisp and clean until ready to serve. Stores on the countertop or in the frigde easily. Can be used to clean vegetables, fruits, berries and herbs. Pull gently when using it with berries to retain the shape. Pull string retracts into the lid to avoid unnecessary tangling of the cord. The pull tab locks into place on top of the lid for storage. Dishwasher safe. Measures: 10" L x 10" W x 5.25" H
profile.reviewText:
I've had one of these for more than 20 years.  In that time, one of the plastic teeth that engages the bowl has broken off.  That will happen if you don't hold the lid down tight while pulling the cord.  After washing the salad, place the bowl on a towel on the counter, hold the lid down (and the spinner) firmly and pull the cord gently with the other until the salad is dry.

If you put the lid on and pull the string hard without holding the lid down, I can see how it would break.  And you don't have to pull very hard, which is probably how the string broke on some people.  You're just trying to get a little water off some lettuce, not start a lawn mower.

Never had a broken string and as mentioned, just the one tooth broken off because the lid wasn't properly seated.  The whole thing has gone in the dishwasher 100+ times with no problems (top shelf).  Untether the line after washing and let it dry, then turn the inside of the lid to re-coil it.
profile.summary: No problems with proper use.  Dishwasher safe.

profile.description: There is no drips or mess. Ants carry bait back to the nest where it destroys the entire colony. The active ingredients is permethrin.
profile.reviewText:
Actually you can't, but understanding the enemy will help keep them out of your house and perhaps off your property.

The small argentinian ant you're well familiar with if you live in California is different from most ant situations.  Most ants will fight with other similar type ant colonies, they live with one queen to a nest, and they'll often avoid repopulating a dead nest.

Not these guys.  Most of them came from a single colony and so have the genetic marker that makes them think they're all from the same nest/colony.  Multiple queens will inhabit a nest.  And they have no problems with moving right back into a dead nest.  So the whole concept of 'killing the queen' or being rid of them is out the window.  In fact, once the queen is dead they'll go through a process of converting a hatchling to a new queen.

They also maintain a scent trail that will last for many years, right into your kitchen, bathroom or other areas where they have previously found food/water and shelter from extreme weather.  They are very fond of driveways, crowns in the road and large concrete spans where they can be protected and avoid drowning in the rain.  When its hot out, your air conditioned house is a great place to be.

This is a war of attrition, but I've 'won' that war on many properties.

First thing you need to do is get rid of excess food and water sources outside.  I've seen them eat everything from fallen fruit to dog poop.

Next when you see a line of ants, follow that trail to the furthest place away from your house you can locate and put one of these baits down.  Set it on the ground, pull out the stakes and press the top.  Don't try to do this while you're holding it unless you like getting it on your hands. Cover it with something to keep the sun off, unless its already in a shady place.  Stake it if necessary.  Monitor each one you put out to see if the ants are still feeding on it, its empty, or its dried out.  Keep replacing until you stop seeing the ants.

I've tried every bait I could buy and frankly this is the only one they take to.  They've largely ignored everything else.  They certainly like proteins but aren't interested in protein baits.  I sometimes will put a little bit of pet food on top of the white crown, it does draw more ants in but they'll take the terro while they're there.

This is basically sugar, water and boric acid.  The boric acid acts as a drying agent but it takes time to kill the ant.  So it can bring it back to the nest and feed it to the queen and the ant larvae.  Given enough of it, you will kill the nest, but as described above it'll be repopulated.

I restrict using this to within about 15' of my house.  If you have lots of time, money and persistence you can drive them to the property boundaries.

In the fall just before the real rain starts (hoping to see that again soon after 4 years of drought) get one of those water hose-screw-on insecticides that kills ants and spray all around your foundation for a few feet away from the house and a foot or so up the side of the house.  Spray the edges of all concrete including big cracks and seams.  In the spring once the rain is over but before the serious heat kicks in, do that spraying again.  I have a 2500 square foot house on 1/2 acre and this costs me about $50-75 a year for Terro and the spray.

If they get into your house, resist the urge to vacuum them up.  Remove the food/water they were interested in and put a Terro bait at the nearest point of entry you can find.  I actually use these outdoor ones instead of the indoor ones.  Simpler and less messy, and they hold more.  Let them continue eating the bait until they're gone...which might take a week or more.  You'll see a pattern of lots of regular looking ants, then when those are all gone from the nest you'll see some burlier versions, about 1.5x the size and thicker.  These are the queens/nests guards who have come in search of food because the workers are gone.  You might even see the queen escorted to the food source, she'll be a lot bigger.  Then you'll see really small ones, these are the newly hatched and the last ditch effort to get food for the nest.

Our objective here is to reduce the population and make the area immediately around your house unfriendly, and to prevent them from entering your house.  When it rains they'll migrate to a dry warm place with food.  When the real heat comes out and things dry up, they look for cooler surroundings with a water/food source.  After a few years of keeping them out, their scent trails that keep leading them into the house will no longer be effective and the job gets easier.

After a few years I've found that they decide that my neighbors are less trouble than I am.
profile.summary: Defeating the Argentinian ant commonly found in California

The outer glove is built similar to our top sellign General Utility Plus. It features extensive non-slip reinforcement to provide excellent grip and lasting durability. It also features a supportive cuff, padded knuckle and soft terry cloth thumb wipe. The interior of the glove is completely lined with Kevlar fiber. The Kevlar greatly increases the cut and puncture resistance of this glove. The result is a glove that is extremely versatile and it has found its way into a wide variety of applications where next level protection is required. Many use this glove in general construction, utility field work, landscape work or for gardening pros. The puncture resistance makes the glove great for handling brush or thorns and thistles without being slowed down or poked. The glove is machine washable and it is recommended to air dry them. This glove is available in sizes Small thru XXX-Large.
profile.reviewText: Good fit, they run a little small so buy up if you're unsure, good and snug, good grip, and so far despite working with a lot of roses and sharp saw blades I haven't gotten a single nick or penetration.  Clearly you're not going to apply the tool directly to the glove, its not that strong but pokes and scrapes and errant cuts are a lot less likely with a pair of these on.  They're quite warm though, so if using them in a hot climate get two pair so you can switch off and let one pair dry while you wear the other.  In the winter, they're nice and warm for work gloves but you can still handle a nail or other small item.  Cant open a beer can when they're on, thats the only major downside.
profile.summary: I really like these gloves

profile.description: Don't let a simple job like vacuuming wear you out - the Hoover Self-Propelled Bagged Upright does the hard work of driving while you simply steer. Fabulous filtration with a HEPA media bag lets you breathe easy knowing dust and pollens stay trapped inside.
profile.reviewText:
This is a pretty good vacuum with decent suction and the self propel makes it easy to use.  My wife won't let me buy anything else ever again.

But there are two things you should know about.

The first is to never pick it up by the handle, but to use the recessed grab area just below the handle.  Its intuitive to pick it up by the handle, but you'll damage the on/off switch if you do that and it won't work anymore.  They tell you this in the directions and even put a sticker on it telling you not to do this, but I see my wife doing it all the time.

The second is that you can expect to put a new self propel drive belt in about every six months if you use the vacuum frequently.  The belt stretches and after about 6 months worth of use the self propel will either not work well or stop working altogether and you may get a yummy burnt rubber smell.  Good news is the belts are only a couple of bucks for a package of two.  Bad news is you have to take out four screws, wiggle off a panel and it can be a little challenging to get the old belt off the spindle and then work the new one on.  Comparing the size of the six month old stretched belt with a new one, you'll see that the old one is considerably larger than the new one.

You'd think they could use a belt thats a bit better made and would last longer, or use a different mechanism.  I see an awful lot of bad reviews from people saying the self propel quit working and the unit smelled burnt, so it seems its a common issue.

We've owned three of these and the latter two came with 3 year warranties, although if you bring it in for service with a bad belt you'll get charged for the service call.  Bad belts are the owners responsibility.  We still have two of them working but on one the wire that actuates the self propel forward and backward (you can see it once you lower the handle) is attached to a slim plastic part and that part broke off about 2 months out of warranty.

So with about 5 minutes of belt replacement a few times a year and a little care around how you pick it up and move it, you can get a lot of life out of one of these, and the self propel really makes light work of the job.

I only took one star off because I think Hoover could do a better job of designing it or making a heavier duty reinforced belt that would last at least a couple of years.
profile.summary: Two things you should know about this vacuum

profile.description: Dog waste management has never been easier! Our Grass Wire Rake Dog Pooper Scooper allows you to conveniently remove outdoor waste. Our ergonomic rubber grip and sturdy scooping wire will help you keep your yard clean without getting your hands dirty. This pooper scooper is rust resistant, so you can trust its durability with confidence! Intended for backyards, this dog poop rake works best on grassy and sandy areas.
profile.reviewText:
I've had one of these for about 16 years.  The handle broke off after a few years and I wrapped some duct tape around it.  On occasion the tines bend and I've just bent them back.  Its challenging to use in vine type grasses that grow along the ground, but once you get the hang of it, its no problem.

Easily the best scooper I've ever bought and it'll probably last me for the rest of my life.  I've left it outside in a bucket the whole time and I other than negligible surface rust its as good as new.

My methodology for using this is in conjunction with a small black plastic bathroom size rectangular garbage can with a plastic bag in it.  The one I have will take a plastic grocery store 'tee shirt' bag.  Scoop in one hand, plastic garbage can in the other.  Scoop, turn it upside down to dump inside the can and tap the scooper on the edge of the can to knock any klingons off the rake.  I even showed my 9 year old how to do it and he has no trouble with it.
profile.summary: Probably the last pooper scooper scooper you'll ever buy.  It lasts forever.

profile.description: The Acer C720 is small but powerful. It's easy to pop in your bag, yet packs the latest Intel processor based on the Haswell micro-architecture, plus up to 8.5 hours of battery life for smooth sailing all day. This exceptional Chromebook also boots up in seconds and resists viruses, so you don't need to wait or worry.
profile.reviewText:
My elementary school age son uses chromebooks at school, so I got him this one to use at home.  We were using his regular PC to log into both his school and regular google accounts, but chrome delightfully synchronized all of his bookmarks from his regular account to his school account, and his teacher thought he was playing minecraft at school because it was in his bookmarks bar.

So a little separation of the two seemed like a good idea.

This chromebook has the latest intel cpu so its fast AND has long battery life.  The ARM cpu based units have the battery life but not the speed, and models like the C710 have the older intel cpu with good speed, but short battery life.  One thing the C710 has is some amount of upgrade potential but it requires a pretty heavy disassembly process.  This unit can't really be upgraded.

Its thin, light, has a good enough screen and as long as you're okay with doing stuff in a chrome browser or with google apps, its a fully functional lightweight laptop.  Besides school work, it also functions well enough as a lightweight home theater PC with the USB3 port for an external drive and the hdmi output for a tv.  Wireless remote/mouse/keyboard or what have you, and you can stream netflix, hulu, amazon instant video and so on.
profile.summary: Pretty good option if you need a chromebook

profile.reviewText:
The M1 Gaming Mouse comes attractively packaged with an actual manual and a cd containing Windows XP/Vista/7/8 software.  The cd is a 'mini' disc, probably to allow packaging in a box smaller than would be required for a full size disk.  The manual is 10 pages in color and in readable English.  It adequately describes how to install the product, its software and how to operate it.

The mouse is extremely glossy, in fact you'll see my reflection in the photo I took of it.  In the photo it looks like the mouse is silvery, but its solid black.  I've also added a photo of the main menu of the configuration software.  It fits my hand well, and I have medium size hands.  My ten year old son has also used it and says it feels fine for his size hands.  Its rounded in the back and all angles from the middle forward.  I have an expensive 7000 series Microsoft laser mouse which cost around 3x what the M1 goes for.  The buttons on the Microsoft mouse seem a bit firmer and sturdier, but only when I have one in each hand.  Separately, its a minor difference.  The M1 has more raised surface for gliding on the bottom than the MS one.  The M1 is perfectly symmetrical, so it could be used right or left handed, while the MS mouse is right handed only.

Its a corded mouse, which is prized by gamers for being more accurate and with no wireless response lag or interference.  The cord is covered with a braided fabric cover, which looks a little better than a plastic one.  It has a number of LED lights, which can be configured for color and solid/slow pulse.

The mouse is plug and play with Windows 7, but you can load the optional software for configuration purposes.  You may change what each button does, assign macro's to each button, and there are multiple profiles so you can set up buttons/macro's for a particular game or app.  You may also cycle through the various profiles by assigning that function to one of the buttons, so within the same game/app where you'd like different capabilities depending on the circumstances, you can employ a different profile with a click.

There are also advanced settings that let you fiddle with polling rate, DPI, sensitivity and so forth.  Highly configurable.

We'll try this out with the usual load of games we play, like Skyrim and Arkham Asylum, along with every day app use.  I'll update if I find any issues or with any compliments about particular observations.  Otherwise, looks like a well priced, highly configurable, well functioning product.
profile.summary: Well priced, highly configurable, well functioning wired mouse

profile.description: From Winsome Wood's new Hailey line of modular furniture, this wood TV stand with 6 open compartments in Espresso finish is designed to stand alone or be paired with other pieces from the collection to create an entertainment, storage and display center.
profile.reviewText:
Not that hard to assemble (12 screws and some wood pins, then 12 small screws to put the back piece on) so it won't take you long.

Downsides?  Half the holes the wood pins go in are much too large for them, and the other half will require you to use a hammer to put them in.  Not as stable as if the holes were all uniform, very slightly larger than the pins.  Plus then you'd be able to use some elmers glue on them to really firm it up.  Holes are either too big for glue or wipe the glue off when you hammer them in.

One major warning, unlike most 'build it yourself' furniture companies, this one won't send you spare parts by calling.  They require you to mail them a hunk of the box it comes in and the invoice.  They do have a fax option without an 800#, but this being 2013 I haven't owned a fax machine for around ten years and have a VOIP phone that doesn't do fax.  So you're looking at 10-14 days from when you mail them the form to when they send you the missing parts, or ~7 days if you can fax it in.  Long time to wait to put something together, and you better check the product thoroughly before removing part of the shipping box as 'proof of purchase'.  There are zero extra/spare screws.  Fortunately I have a couple of big cans of leftovers and was able to make up for the missing parts.

Its a huge dust and hair magnet, mine was covered with dog hair by the time I was done building it.  Fairly sturdy.  Not fine furniture or super good looking wood by any means.  Lots of little scuffs and "funny" wood, but the funny parts are mostly on the back end of the pieces as the finish work was only done on the front.  So if you're looking for something particularly high quality looking, this isn't it.  If you want a piece of furniture to drop a tv on and don't much care about how nice the grain looks, its good.

The two middle shelves are good size for a receiver or dvr type box, the outside four cubbies are too small for anything except maybe a roku player or other fairly small items.
profile.summary: Good enough and easy to put together, but definitely not grade A wood.

profile.description: If you are looking for a device that can assist you in streaming content and media with ease, take a look at Nyko's Xbox One Media Remote. The device can turn on or off your console while having operating buttons such as play, pause, and channel changing. This remote requires 2 AA batteries.
profile.reviewText:
This remote allows you to turn the xbox one on and off, navigate the basic menu's, and control media playback.  I use my XB1 as a blu ray player, and its annoying to go to pause a movie and see that the controller has powered off.  I have a media remote for my 360 and PS3, so I figured I'd get one for the XB1 for non gaming purposes.

It fits in the palm of your hand and all buttons are within a thumbs reach.  Its not beautifully crafted from the finest Corinthian leather, its just inexpensive plastic.  It is an infrared remote so it has to be pointed at the xbox.  Xbox one controllers use wireless and this is different from that, so range and where you point matters.  I've found it reaches about 12' with a new pair of AAA batteries, which were not included.

Controlling the tv?  There aren't any facilities to train the remote, so I believe the tv control part works only if you have a Kinect, which the Xbox one uses to control channel and volume on a tv.  You'd press a button on the remote, the XB1 would see it and tell the Kinect to send an IR signal to the tv and that's probably how that works.  I don't have a kinect so I can't test it right now.

I found the buttons worked pretty much all the time and didn't require any special effort to work.  I've also seen the 'real' microsoft remote and it doesn't seem any fancier or better working than this one, but the 'real' one costs a lot more.

So if you want a cheap remote to basically hit pause and play and turn the XB1 on and off, this is well recommended.  I don't think I'd try to play Halo with it, but maybe that'd be a special challenge
profile.summary: Fine media remote for Xbox One

profile.description: VIZIO's 32" Class Edge Lit Razor LED LCD HDTV features 1080p Full HD resolution and Edge Lit Razor LED backlighting for brilliant color and contrast in a razor thin design. With an amazing Dynamic Contrast Ratio of 100,000 to 1, this sleek HDTV also delivers superior audio using SRS TruSurround HD and SRS TruVolume audio for advanced virtual surround sound and volume control. It has three HDMI ports so you can connect up to three HDMI devices to your HDTV. Also exceeds Energy Star 4.1 guidelines to reduce energy consumption and has built-in ambient light sensing technology, which automatically adjusts backlight levels to the brightness of its surroundings.
profile.reviewText:
As many have found, the questionable race to make the thinnest tv set has a major casualty: the internal speakers.  While I'm perfectly happy having a set thats 3-5" thick, you cant put a decent speaker in a 1-2" set.  I discovered this when I bought a beautiful looking 60" set that had thin speakers pointing down from the bottom of the set.  Unless I planned to lay under the tv while watching it, I couldn't even coax enough volume out of the set to drown out the dishwasher in the kitchen.

So with that in mind, when my sons bedroom tv started making "The Hum Of Impending Death", I went looking for a 32" replacement.  My desired features were an LED set so I don't have to get as annoyed when he leaves it on, 1080p so it could be used as a computer monitor or for some other high definition gui based device down the road, a good picture, good enough internal speakers to not require a sound bar, and as far under $400 as I could get it.

I spent 3 days touring every place that sells tv's, and checking online reviews of sets compatible with those requirements.  I couldn't find a set in the stores that didn't have low volume, tinny, kazoo like speakers.  Not even at higher price points than I wanted to go.  I even tried 37 and 40" sets hoping the larger size would net me better sound, but had no luck with those either.

I did come across this one set, which is sold widely under slightly different model numbers.  Look for a Vizio with an all black case, no silver speaker grills, and no front mounted speaker grills, 32", LED, 1080p, and you'll find one of the many variants of this television.

The internal speakers actually have a little bit of bass, nice volume levels - it can get to loud in a small room, great picture quality, eleven bucks a year to run if you get 12c/KWH electricity and use it 5 hours a day, a nice remote control and lots of useful settings.  It also has an ambient light sensor that turns up the brightness in a bright sunlit room and down in a dark room.  Thats a nice feature that I'm going to want on all my sets in the future.

After looking at a hundred sets in two days, this is the one to get.  I honestly couldn't even find a set with worthwhile speakers for under $400 even if I dropped the LED and 1080p requirements.  The (admittedly less expensive) cfl lit 720 sets also had horrible speakers.

Some day someone has to explain to me why a tv thats 1" thick is so much better than one thats 2 inches thick.  Or what exactly you're going to do with that tiny little space that the tv used to sit in that requires you to spend $200 to screw it onto a wall.  All of my tv's have dvr's, blu-ray players, game consoles and other stuff that has to sit in some kind of cabinet near the television anyhow.  I guess I'm just not as cramped for room space as everyone else is.
profile.summary: Only 32" set I could find that had usable speakers

profile.description: Training collar for dogs with patented humane design.
profile.reviewText:
I have a dog that I recently got from the shelter, and she was in there a very long time.  She has several problems.  One is that she treats cars as though they were an aggressive animal and she wants to leap at them.  She doesn't do this all the time, in fact she'll let 3-4 pass and then suddenly jump at the next.  She's also very aggressive with other animals.  She isn't even happy about a bird landing in the yard or a tree.

Other than those two problems, she's a wonderful sweet girl.  I took her on a few walks with my usual harness, but she almost wrenched the leash out of my hand while leaping at a car.  Even paying close attention I was a little concerned.  She also lunged at a few other dogs walking across the street and once I almost lost the leash.

She came with one of the metal chain pronged collars and I wanted something less bite-y.  I liked the look of this collar as it uses hard plastic instead of metal and the 'teeth' are rounded so the tighter she pulls, the more surface area the pressure is spread over.

The bottom line is she pulls harder with this than the metal prong collar.  Not hugely, but its more.  My biggest problem is the collar has a tiny little thin strap and you're supposed to use a second strap which has a metal ring on each end as a 'safety'.  I have very little faith in this assembly and its not possible to put it on without a leash as the 'safety' won't stay on.  So taking a trip to the lake or another area to walk means I have to get in the back of the car and put the safety and the leash on, I can't just open the door and snap the leash onto the collar.

So I went back to the metal one.  I've used a combination of mostly positive and some negative reinforcement and she's doing much better with cars, but she's still tough with other dogs.  We'll keep working on it.  I'm not happy about the metal prong collar and didn't want to use it, but its either that or she stays home all the time.
profile.summary: I wanted to replace a metal prong collar with this, but its too thin to trust

profile.description: Purigen is a premium synthetic adsorbent that is unlike any other filtration product. It is not a mixture of ion exchangers or adsorbents, but a unique macro-porous synthetic polymer that removes soluble and insoluble impurities from water at a rate and capacity that exceeds all others by over 500%. purigen controls ammonia, nitrites and nitrates by removing nitrogenous organic waste that would otherwise release These harmful compounds. Purigen' s impact on trace elements is minimal. It significantly raises redox. It polishes water to unparalleled clarity. Purigen darkens progressively as it exhausts, and is easily renewed by treating with bleach. Purigen is designed for both marine and freshwater use.
profile.reviewText:
Its supposed to be a good filtration product, but make sure you use it with the same manufacturers water conditioner.  When combined with several common chlorine remover/water conditioners it produces chlorine in great amounts.  I tried this in a test tank that was going pretty well and it killed 3 of the 4 fish before I figured out what was wrong, and it happened in just a few hours.

Otherwise the concept is good...the product shlorks up organic waste and when it turns black you soak it in bleach which kills off everything it sucked up, and then you treat it with the chlorine remover sold by the same company, then its good to absorb bad stuff for another month or two.  Just be careful to research which chemicals you're using and make sure they won't cause harm.
profile.summary: Be very careful with this stuff

profile.description: Crucial MX100 128 GB 2.5' Internal Solid State Drive
profile.reviewText:
Very good SSD that's frequently available at a very attractive price.  While you can argue about fine grains of performance, without a benchmark or some industrial/commercial grade application that reads and writes full blast 24x7, you'd never know the difference between this drive and any other top notch performer.

Crucial's parent company Micron makes the NAND (flash memory chips) that go into this, which is the key decision factor in choosing an SSD.  Companies that put their own NAND into their drives generally use the latest, fastest, highest 'bin' parts.  These are their best memory chips.  Other companies that make SSD's buy their chips from these companies but they're not always using the best.  If the NAND fails or has a short life, the drive won't be useful anymore.  Intel, Samsung, Crucial and some others make their own high quality NAND and put it in their drives.

This drive has a very good controller.  Lots of people will argue about this controller or that controller or to not use one that came out a couple of years ago because its "dated".  The thing is, 98% of regular users wouldn't be able to distinguish between an "old" controller drive and this one in everyday use without running a benchmark.

So this drive will be an excellent performer, should offer excellent reliability, and if you can get a great price on it I see no reason to go elsewhere.

But do yourself a favor and throw out the Acronis key.  Acronis has failed me big time on several occasions.  The software is clunky and bug ridden.  In the case of this drive, I took a chance on it and it put my computer into an unusable state, requiring me to restore a 2 week old backup to get it running again...using a different tool.  I've been using Macrium Reflect Free for over a year with zero problems.  I used to like Acronis and had good luck with it for years, but the persistent bugs and failures just kill the product.
profile.summary: Great drive.  Skip the included Acronis.

profile.description: Enjoy the freedom of wireless connectivity with Adesso's wireless mini Keyboard with Optical trackball. The keyboard and trackball allow you to work up to 100 feet away from the USB receiver connected to your computer. In addition, the optical trackball provides great accuracy with minimal hand movement due to its 800 dpi resolution. The lightweight and stylish keyboard offers mobility and comfort wherever you type. Take complete control of your desktop with hotkeys. The different hotkeys give you quick access to some of your most common tasks such as e-mail access, volume control, and launching your web browser - at the push of a button.
profile.reviewText:
Like others, I've had the problem where it doesnt pick up all the keystrokes.  Picking where to plug it into the HTPC and moving some stuff away from the computer seems to have improved it.  Doesnt eat batteries, but it does go to sleep so dang fast that you constantly have to wake the keyboard up if you aren't typing continuously.

Biggest problem I'm having is that the left mouse click buttons are already losing their spring and the left one is almost completely flat.  I checked adesso's repair procedure and not only is the customer responsible for shipping, they have 87,000 requirements including copies of receipts, packing it in its original box, etc along with all sorts of charges they'll levy on you if they think its been abused, a seal is broken, etc.  I don't feel like anteing up $15+ to ship it back, then have them decide they want to charge me extra for repairs.

I haven't really used this to excess (maybe 40-50 times watching movies and whatnot, typing for a total of maybe 10 minutes per usage.  Never had a keyboard start getting soft keys, even after far more substantial use.  This has taken no abuse whatsoever.

Cant recommend anything better, but I think next time I'll just buy the el cheapo wireless keyboard at the office supply store thats a third the price and if it stops working, who cares.  This one IS nice and compact and light weight, but theres no long term durability to it.

Update: at this point, the mouse left click button is completely flat and unusable and the ball is jerky or over sensitive.  Its close to heading for the junk heap.
profile.summary: Not thrilled with it

profile.description: The Kenney 1 Fluted End Cap Curtain Rod Set provides the perfect scale for todays larger rooms and higher ceilings. The 1 diameter rod supports light, medium, and heavyweight curtains. End caps provide a streamlined and sophisticated solution for versatile applications in the family room, dining room, bedroom, or home office. The telescoping steel rods are sturdy and easily adjustable from 66 to 120 inches to fit most larger size windows. Mounting brackets and hardware are included.
profile.reviewText:
Good luck getting this rod out of the package.  I had to use a pair of pliers on the staples, a box cutter and a diagonal cutter on the tie wraps.  Its quite beautiful in its slightly crushed box, but when it takes me 20 minutes to get something out of the box, its gone too far.  I'd have paid someone ten bucks to get this out of the box, and they probably would have felt like they got a bad deal out of it.

Then we have the instructions, which are a heady 'screw it to the wall and put your curtains on it'.  Gee, thanks.  Maybe you could have used the other 80% of the piece of paper to explain that the rod without the end cap on it is NOT the middle extension, that you have to remove the end cap from the smaller rod and attach it to the 3rd rod, and the thinnest rod becomes the middle extension.  I discovered this after spending 10 minutes trying to yanks one of the plastic plugs out of the 3rd rod hoping that was why the other two rods wouldn't fit.

The screws packaged with this are the same screws I get 90% of the time with window treatments.  The metal is soft, the heads will spin out in 5 seconds with a power screwdriver, and the heads will snap off in 1/4 second if you tighten them too much.  I got used to seeing these show up about 5 years ago, and I throw them out and replace them with actually good screws that cost 1/10th of a cent more than the worthless ones included.

Oh, and I should also mention that amazons "frequently bought together" got me to buy this nickel rod with a curtain that has antique bronze grommets.  The curtain didn't specify nickel or bronze, but apparently 'frequently bought together' also equals "frequently returned separately after being bought together because they don't match".

Its a lovely, sturdy rod ruined by excessive and unnecessary packaging, worthless directions, and unnecessary cost savings in key areas that weaken the products installation and longevity.

For those who think the rods are scratched, there is a thin clear protective plastic glued to the rod which you have to remove, and thats what appears scratched.

For those who note that the rods don't fit, mine had little white plastic sleeves about an inch long that slid into the rod end before inserting the other rod.  Those fill the gap and make the rod not slide apart.
profile.summary: Nice curtain rod ruined by the packaging and directions

profile.description: The Highland hitch mounted cargo carrier is made from heavy duty powder coated steel construction. The carrier will fit any 2 inch receiver style hitch and has a capacity of up to 500 pounds. The 60 inch x 20 inch x 2-1/2 inch platform adds additional and convenient capacity for your gear.
profile.reviewText:
I had to order this 3 times from the Warehouse before I got it.  The first one mysteriously disappeared at a ups depot after being checked in and out 3 times, the second one was the wrong product, third time was the charm.

Its cheap, its decently made, its a little floppy and you'd best center or distribute your load, because if you put it on one side or the other, this will bend at I'd say around 80-100lbs.  It came a little scratched and dinged, so it'll need regular spray painting.

Its also quite heavy compared to tubular or aluminum versions.  As much as twice as heavy.

Serves my purpose well, with the matching waterproof bag that the same company (Highland) sells.  I throw this on the back of the SUV when we go to the beach, and all our wet stuff, towels, inflatables, etc all goes into the bag.  When we get home, I can sort everything out and no mud or water in the back of the car.  It'll also be nice if I need to go grab 6-8 bags of mulch, I can load them on this instead of breaking out the trailer to avoid stains in the back of the car.

If you have a trailer hitch and don't have one of these, you're missing out.  From hauling messy stuff to throwing a few bikes on it, its handy.  Make sure you buy one of those nice little cylinder hitch locks to keep someone from stealing it, and put some extra reflective tape on it while you're at it.  One of my ditzy friends turned into a parking lot last week and cleaned one of these right off the back of a parked car.

Lastly, I somehow managed to assemble mine perfectly backwards so the reflective tape that does come on it is on the bumper end.  Doh!  I'd have had to take every bolt and nut out to fix it.  I didn't notice that in the directions they had flipped the thing over between the two diagrams.  Wasn't worth the trouble, as I have plenty of reflective tape and other than the Highland name printed, there is no difference to having the bed in reverse.  Plus I'm sure it'll be a real conversation starter.
profile.summary: Good if you can get it, especially for the price

profile.description: Thoughtfully designed for no-hassle daily use, the Jitterbug Flip takes simplicity to the next level with features like: big buttons, simple Yes and No navigation, a backlit keypad and a powerful speaker for clear conversations. profile.reviewText:
Enjoy the hidden fees.  There's a $35 activation fee, you have to pay an extra $3 a month for voicemail (who doesn't want voicemail?) etc.  These fees aren't readily disclosed.  $10 of the activation fee is waived if you sign up online instead of over the phone

I never enjoy starting off on a bad foot.  However its about what you have to expect from most cell providers, who do their best to obfuscate, add fees and charge extra whenever possible.

Its also the first Verizon network device I've tried.  I'm unimpressed with the vaunted Verizon coverage, or this phone lacks the band support for some of Verizons build out.  I get good, average to low average signal for T-Mobile and Sprint at my house and at my dads house.  The Verizon signal on the Jitterbug at my house was so low I had to go up to the 3rd floor and walk around until I got enough to activate the phone, then the signal level was 'poor' at my dads house.

Updated review:

Dropped to one star.  After 10 months of use the device goes "dead" and the only way to get it to work again is to pull the battery and put it back in.  When I called greatcall, they said its a known problem, had no explanation how a phone works for ten months and then doesn't and insisting it was not defective.  I was initially refused a replacement or refund, with an attempt to upsell me to the android smartphone.  Once I got a supervisor, they offered to replace the phone and said "no chance" at a refund.  It seems they've never heard of small claims court.

Oh and its not the weak verizon network, its the device.  Another verizon device at the same addresses gets perfectly good signal.

Steer clear of this giant piece of %@#^ and get a decent big button flip phone.  Horrible product, horrible service, just no.
profile.summary: Hidden fees out the wazoo, product dies after 10 months, horrible, horrible customer service.

profile.description: The Maxxima MLN-50 is the brightest plug-in Night Light available, with 5 White LEDs. This Night Light will turn on when it gets dark in your room and stay on until morning or until you turn on the main lights in your room.
profile.reviewText: Here's the basics: Its a very bright, very white light.  Quite stark.  They aren't particularly sensitive to existing daylight and will light up if they're put anywhere they won't be hit with pretty bright light from a window.  They'll light up a very large area well enough to see fine when walking through.  I have one in an area about 25x10 and its enough.  While both of them are on or partially on pretty much 24x7, the electricity usage is practically negligible.  If you're one of the types to put everything on a power switch and shut it off to avoid a 1w 'vampire' load you'll hate these.  If on the other hand you aren't into fiddling with everything to save a dollar or two a year, you'll be fine with them.  Well made.  They should last a very long time.

Four adjustable ultrasonic volume levels - test, low, medium, and high, with LED battery power level indicator. The device uses low-intensity ultrasonic, is silent to humans and not harmful. Any reason our product doesn't meet your standards, just send it back our way for a replacement or a full refund!
profile.reviewText:
This is a really nice leash.  Its 8' long, while many dual handles are 6.  This gives my dogs a little more room to roam which is nice considering I'm walking two large dogs.  The closer handle is about 18" from the clip.  The leash material is heavy braided nylon strapping and is at least 4x as heavy duty as the strap in my 140lb-rated retractable leash.  I have absolutely no worries about the quality or expected life span of this leash.  I've seen some reviews that say this is like 'ribbon'.  They must have gotten something different or reviewed the wrong product.  This would hold even the largest dogs.  Not really for a small dog, its too heavy duty.  Serious overkill.

Each handle has an extra perforated leather or leather like layer on the inside.  Its soft and comfortable.  I've seen reviews that said the handles cut into their hands when the dog pulled.  I'm not sure how that could have happened the way its made.  This is a very well made leash.

Should I have any problems with it, I'll update the review.
profile.summary: Solid, strong, well made leash.  Recommended.

profile.description: Western Chief was founded in Seattle in 1891 to produce rugged outdoor boots designed to meet the harsh conditions of the Alaska Gold Rush. Today, they are still committed to making the same high quality, rugged work footwear. Built with the finest materials to demanding standards, their footwear keeps people warm and dry, comfortable and stylish, safe and secure.
profile.reviewText:
I've bought these rain boots for my son before and he grew out of them before we had any sorts of problems with them.  They're heavy duty and thick soled.  Unlike other boots we've tried, the little 'handles' at the top don't tear off after 10 uses.

They are a little bigger than similar sized shoes, but most rain boots I've bought for myself and my son have run a bit big.  Put two pairs of sox on if they're just a bit big.  At the time of this writing my sons feet are pushing the limits of a 2.5 shoe but a 3 is too big.  I bought these in a 2 and a 3 and the 2 is just a little large on him.  The 3 is humongous.  Those will be next years boots I guess.

The only downside I can mention is that they're clunky.  Very heavy, thick and not super flexible in the sole.  So I wouldn't see walking a long distance in them.  But my prior and current experience is that they should remain intact and waterproof for at least one rainy season.

One thing I appreciate is that the soles don't have the type of tread that can hold a lot of mud.  We have that thick gluey clay soil and it can really cling to an aggressive deep tread.
profile.summary: Good looking boots, well made, a bit heavy.  Runs a little big.

profile.description: The Lux Egg-Per'Fect timer features the ability to insure soft, medium and hard boiled eggs as cooked perfectly every time. The EP100 sits in the pot with the eggs and changes color as the eggs cook to show when the eggs are ready regardless of egg quantity or altitude. The EP100 senses heat, not time for consistency eliminating over or under cooking. Egg textures and color are perfect every time.
profile.reviewText:
This makes boiling eggs simple.  Put your eggs and this in a pot of cold water, bring it to a boil, shut off the heat and when the egg turns from red to purple at the doneness level you want, pour out the hot water and fill the pan with cold to stop the cooking process.  Note that if you use really extra large eggs you'll have to overshoot the doneness, and if you use small or medium eggs, pull them when you're about one level below desired doneness, as this seems to 'time' for a standard large egg.

I've used one for over a decade, and its predecessor lasted quite some time before I forgot to turn the burner off while working on 3 projects at once and it melted to the bottom of the pan.
profile.summary: Perfect eggs every time

profile.description: This listing is for a two (2) pack of Broadband DECAs . Allows an internet connection to be distributed throughout the home through coaxial cable. The DECA network is a shared 200Mb/s, or the same speed as full duplex 100Mb/s Ethernet This kit includes the DECA II adapter, EPS10 power supply and DCFR0 DC to RF adapter Use this device in place of a Cinema Connection Kit or older Broadband DECA The power supply and DC to RF adapter may also be used with any DECA or DECA II Compatible with the following receivers: H21,H23,H24,H25, HR20,HR21,HR22,HR23,HR24,HR34/Genie,THR22/Tivo Standard Definition receivers and DIRECTV H10/H20 receivers require a band stop filter Any ethernet cable may be used to connect the DECA to your home network If you do not have coaxial cable in the same room as an ethernet connection, use the Wireless Cinema Connection Kit instead Can be used with HR34/Genie and Genie Clients Allows connection of a broadband router to home set-up Great for using right behind a router to pump internet over coax for a Whole Home DVR or Connected Home Setup This unit will connect to your router via an Ethernet cable, and then into an open port on one of your sws splitters to get the internet into the coaxial cable for the entire system.
profile.reviewText:
These are really great for extending your network over coaxial cable.  They do not work if you have cable television but will work if you have a point to point coax connection or directv already wired.  My house has coax runs from a central spot near my router to all of the bedrooms.  You need one to plug into your router and one at the end of each coax line.  You may connect many runs together with a splitter but more than 3 probably won't work.  Point to point connections will require one at each end of each run.  You can also put a switch at either or both ends.  A pair of these basically make a piece of coaxial cable work like it was a regular ethernet cable.  Full duplex 100Mb/s for a total of 200Mb/s send and receive.  Only a little more latency than an ethernet cable.  Only a few watts of electricity per unit.  Completely plug and play.  I've had a couple of these in service for years and have forgotten that they're there.  I have one bedroom that's just outside of good wireless range.  I wouldn't go over 150' of coax with it, but it might work.

It won't work with cable tv on the same wire as the frequencies conflict.  You'll need MOCA adapters for that, which are usually a lot more expensive.
profile.summary: Good cheap way to use the coax in your house for ethernet, whether you have directv or not.

profile.description: Propel yourself to new levels of agility and endurance with the ASICS Gel-Nerve33. Leather and textile mesh upper provides lightweight breathability. Lace-up closure. Cushioned lining and insole. Injected Solyte midsole is exceptionally lightweight. Rearfoot Gel cushioning system attenuates impacting shock and allows for a smooth transition to midstance. Memory foam lined PHF (Personalized Heel Fit) collar molds to the athlete's heel, creating a personalized fit.
profile.reviewText:
I find Asics gel-33 shoes to be very comfortable.  I bought a pair a couple of years ago and find myself going to those over my other sneaks.  Soft comfortable sole insert and a very generous heel padding.  But my old ones were wearing out and nobody carried that model anymore.  They were gel-33 type shoes though, so I took a shot at the 'nerve' version

Honestly they fit and feel exactly the same, although they're a bit lighter.  I wasn't entirely thrilled with the pictures but I like the style fine in real life.  I've worn them two days in a row, the break in took about an hour.  Its nice to know I can stick with the various gel-33 models and still get the comfort I like.  I have occasional arch support issues with some shoes, and find that the shoes with a weak outside toe box let me supinate a little on the right foot.  I don't have either problem with these shoes.
