profile.description: The VisionTek Radeon R9 270X graphics card is the cornerstone of a high-performance, yet affordable gaming rig. Its the fastest 1080p capable gaming card available at its price point, offering a 3DMark Fire Strike score exceeding 5,500. With support for the DIRECTX 11.2 graphics standard, you just need to add a 1080p display and instantly youll elevate your gaming experience with stunning 3D visual effects, realistic lighting, and lifelike imagery. With 2GB of 256bit GDDR5 memory, engine clock speed of 1030MHz, award-winning Graphics Core Next (GCN) architecture, and DVD-I/DVI-D/HDMI/DisplayPort outputs, the VisionTek Radeon R9 270X can run todays most popular games at 1080p resolution up to 49% faster than other brand GPU powered graphics cards. For peace of mind ownership, it comes backed by an industry leading lifetime warranty and free lifetime US-based technical support.
profile.reviewText:
I installed this in my son's gaming rig.  Mind you its an antec skeleton frame, which is open to the air.  Basically a couple of places to mount the motherboard, power supply, drives and two crossed arches with a huge 250mm fan blowing on the system.

So its not really a silent machine, but not particularly noisy either.

I thought it was odd that what I got came with two fans instead of one (as originally shown on amazon but since fixed), and thought they might have sent me a 280x by accident, since visiontek puts two fans on those.  Still, happy with the cooling setup as most of the one fan 270x cards are basic reference designs.  This one has a better cooling solution.

Are the fans noisy or make squealy sounds?  Not mine.  No problems with the drivers either, just downloaded the latest on the AMD/ATI web site, installed them and its worked fine since.  Cranked up the res on all his games, turned on all the special features, and it seems to max everything out at 1080p.  When we play Garry's Mod or Batman Arkham City on it with everything turned up to max, the fans do make some noise, like a desk fan on medium, but again this chassis is wide open and you can actually see the card just a few feet away from your ears.

I tried running it at ~20% overclock and it was fine, but we didn't need the extra performance and won't until I get him a higher resolution display.  Maybe next year.  But then again, the cooling on this is good and I have it sitting right under the main 250mm fan blowing down on the card, the cpu, the ram and the chipset.  Unless I really crank it up nothing is going to have a chance to overheat.

Nice card, got it at a nice price over the holidays, and I'm very happy with it.  More than 2x the speed of the 7770 that was in there, didn't break the bank.
profile.summary: Good card and they've fixed the picture

profile.description: Bonjour's chef's crme brle torch allows you to make restaurant quality desserts at home. Not only is the chef's crme brle torch an essential tool for preparing the classic crme brle, but it also has a variety of other uses in the home kitchen including browning meringue and melting cheese on onion soup gratine. Die cast aluminum body features a fuel level indicator window so you know when it's time to refill. Butane not included.
profile.reviewText:
I frequently need to apply direct heat and open flame in a variety of kitchen and workshop applications.  I've used this to loosen stuck metal pipes joints, put a little extra browning on something or even to lightly cook fragile items like scallops.  The trick to this torch and any other is to use good gas thats been filtered at least 4-5 times.  I tried it with a major brand name gas from the supermarket and it sputtered and didn't keep a regular flame.  When I purged it and replaced it with vector quintuple filtered gas, it worked beautifully.

Good little recipe from Alton Brown...get some fudge covered marshmallow cookies, torch the tops until the chocolate starts to melt and then sprinkle with a little kosher salt.  Fastest quick dessert to bring to a party and it'll be the first one gone.

The base comes off a little too easily for me, I've accidentally knocked it off a few times.  To use, you push down on a tab, it locks and then you push a button on the back.  This ignites the flame and it'll run as long as you hold the button in.  Besides the hold-and-shoot method, it also has adjustments to the flame and a lock that lets you keep the flame on without pushing the trigger.  Thats a bad combination with the easy to knock off base, so I don't use that.  Its not hard to hold the button down in the back.

You won't be soldering with this, but for the 1-5 times a day when I think "I wish I had something that'd throw a little flame...", this comes in handy.
profile.summary: Not just for the kitchen...

profile.description: Hamilton Beach True Air 04531GM Air Purifier TruAir Plug-Mount Odor Eliminator This Hamilton Beach TrueAir Plug-Mount Odor Eliminator does not mask odors--it eliminates them and its scented cartridge freshens the air. Its carbon filter traps and neutralizes odors in the kitchen, in the bathroom and in pet areas as well as smoking/tobacco odors. The quiet fan pulls in unwanted odors. Plugs into standard 110 volt outlet. It has a filter replacement indicator and on/off switch. It has a built in night light and a green meadow scented catridge.
profile.reviewText:
If you're looking for an air circulator/purifier/deodorizer thats small in size, quiet and inexpensive to buy, I'm pleased with this one.  Its about 8" tall and 7" on the sides, has two speeds on top, air goes in three of the four sides and out the fourth.  Each of those 3 intakes has a flat air filter with charcoal powder in it, they're keyed to fit so pay attention to which way you put them in by comparing the notch on the filter with the notch inside the filter drawer.  There is a small container of febreze similar to the ones that go into the home febreze 'holders', clear plastic with the oil inside.  You insert that and a bump inside the filter holder pokes a hole in it.

On either speed its pretty quiet and makes a gentle 'white noise' whirring.  It uses a "squirrel cage" type fan that moves a good bit of air without a lot of sound.  Even on high its a pleasant sound that you could easily sleep through and might even mask other noises.

As with any 'air purifier', the problem is getting the dust and stuff that needs filtering to the filter.  Thats a problem because most particles are heavy and sink shortly after becoming airborn, or are so light they stay up and away from the filter.  So I wouldnt expect a cleaner room or relief from a significant allergy problem by using this or most any other air filtration device.  What it does do is make the room you put it in smell better and it'll certainly filter out some allergens and dust that pass through it.  The charcoal and febreze definitely reduce odors.  I've tried this out in the 'cat room' that has our cat boxes and feeding area.  A blindfolded person would have no problems locating our cat room my smell alone, but after about 2 hours the cat room smelled no more.  I also tried it in a 3 car garage that has a couple of cars, lawn care gear, the furnace and water heater, plus a bunch of other stuff.  It usually smells like musty rubber, gasoline, wet grass and vaguely of dog poop since I pick plenty of that up on the mowers when I'm cutting the grass.  After having this little cube running on LOW overnight, all I could smell walking around was dry particle board in our cabinets.  If you've ever walked into a brand new house thats being built, thats the smell...clean, dry, wood sawdust kind of smell.

It did that with just the charcoal, I haven't put the febreze packet in yet.

The downside and expense with this filter is it taking 3 filter pads and a febreze unit probably once every month or so.  Most of your large room size models can go a few months without a change but the filters can be $50+.  These are less expensive but charcoal only lasts so long.  I may look for someone selling sheets of the filtration material and try cutting some to fit, see if I can keep the costs down.

But awesome little filter to put in the animal area, the kids rooms that never get cleaned, the garage/shop, next to a smoker or anywhere else theres a smell.
profile.summary: Small, effective, quiet and somewhat expensive over the long run

profile.description: Building upon the success of the SB6121, Motorola's SURFboard SB6141 enhances your personal media experience, at lightning-fast broadband speed. It harnesses the power of DOCSIS 3.0 technology to bond up to eight downstream channels and four upstream channels--providing you advanced multimedia services with data rates up to 343 Mbps download and 131 Mbps upload depending on your Cable Internet provider service. That makes streaming HD Video, gaming, shopping, downloading, working, high-quality voice and video conferencing, and peer-to-peer networking applications far more realistic, faster, and efficient than ever before.
profile.reviewText:
Right up front, there is a lot of confusion about modem color.  Black and white modems are identical except for when they were manufactured (older made modems have older firmware) and how they're packaged.  Both black and white modems are for sale new and used and refurbished.  Both are sold at retail.  Both are available as OEM product, which is boxed without instructions or cables.  Aside from that, every single 6141 regardless of color is identical.

A black modem does not mean its used, black doesn't mean OEM, nor does it mean it has older firmware.  It is entirely plausible to buy a white modem and get a used OEM product if that is what the seller described it as.  It is also possible to buy a brand new, recently made black modem at retail with current firmware.

If you buy the modem from an authorized seller, motorola will give you warranty service on the modem regardless of its color.  If you buy it from some random guy who isn't an authorized seller, your warranty (if any) is with that seller.

What IS a problem is that some ISP's decided to not update firmware on customer owned modems.  My only guess as to why this wasn't done is that it increases the dissatisfaction with the customer owned modem, making it more likely that the customer will give up on owning and go back to the highly profitable renting.

Comcast updates the firmware on the 6141.  I've had it for quite some time now with zero problems.  Any problems are with your ISP, not the modem and has nothing whatsoever to do with the color.  You can have the exact same problem with any customer owned modem if it doesn't have current firmware and your ISP opts to not update it.

Original review:  This is the best cable modem you can buy.

Cable modems take the analog signals on the cable system and convert them to digital signals that your computer can understand, much like old style telephone modems let you connect via the analog phone system.

Depending on your internet service provider and their local implementation, you may or may not have multiple 'channels' for downloading and uploading.  Like a tv channel, a network/data channel takes up a certain amount of space and allows for a certain amount of bandwidth for either up or downloaded data.

The problem with older docsis 2.0 modems is they can only bond one channel down and one channel up.  If your channel gets congested with data your internet speeds will slow down and throughput and quality of service can suffer.  You'll see video buffering, voice-over-IP calls with clicks and pops and delays, and slow performance in general.

This is a docsis 3.0 modem, and as such its principal advantage is that it can bond more than one channel.  Lesser variants like the 6120/6121 are limited to four downstream channels, while the 6141 can bond eight.  This is akin to driving on an 8 lane road instead of a one lane road.  You aren't quite as limited in speed on the 8 lane version, and you can change lanes if one has too many cars in it, while the docsis 2.0 modem is stuck with the one lane its assigned to, even if that one is congested.

In a longer term test, I evaluated up and download speeds and ping times, which is the time it takes for a short message to go from my computer to another one somewhere on the open internet.  The longer your ping times, the more problems you'll have with voice, video and other real time apps, including games.

The 6120 I used to have, which is docsis 3 and did bond multiple channels, slowed down and showed erratic performance, ranging from about 8Mb/s download to 25Mb/s, depending on the time of day and usage by others in my neighborhood.  When I installed the 6141, I then got flat 25Mb/s every single time I tested, and my ping times settled into a consistent number.  When comcast did a recent speed bump for free, my uploads moved to consistently 35Mb/s.

More channels are better, and the 6141 can often be had for the same price as a 6120 or 6121.

Couple of tidbits.  There are some reviews that say a black modem is used.  Not true.  I've bought 3 motorola modems at retail the last 5 years, all black, all new.  My old 5120 was white, but thats an OLD modem.

Some cable providers are not sending the most current motorola firmware, and the modem doesn't work very well without it.  So if you're having problems on some isps like time warner, its because your modem needs a firmware update and the isp hasn't tested or certified it yet.  Comcast in my area sent me the current firmware.  But do note that its a recent modem and some ISP's seem to be dragging their feet on rolling out current, stable firmware.
profile.summary: Modem color has absolutely no meaning whatsoever

profile.description: Totally different from your dad's old needle scale, the Fitbit Aria WiFi Smart Scale uses advanced technology to track weight, lean mass, body fat percentage, and body mass index, allowing you to see all the numbers you need to start living a healthier lifestyle. With room for the storage of up to eight users, this scale recognizes who you are, displays your data, and sends your stats straight to your Fitbit account through your home's WiFi while remaining totally private to you. The sleek polished glass surface looks classy while resisting the condensation from steamy hot showers.
profile.reviewText:
First off, no manual but a quick start card, so you'll want to go to the fitbit web site and read the manual first.  It'll simplify things.

Setup was a pain in the butt.  If you don't have a smart phone or a wireless laptop, you cant configure the device.  Both methods require going to a site on the phone/laptop, running some software, changing your wireless access point from your regular one to the scale, configuring the scale, then switching back to your regular access point.  Clearly a product designed by 20-somethings that grew up with facebook and smart phones, and are comfortable with jiggling wifi settings.  NOT a high touch install and setup.

For whatever reason, our one wireless laptop would connect to but not allow configuration.  I never tried to figure out why, just used the smart phone.  This induces a situation where the phone wants to look for the scale to configure it, and the scale must be in setup mode, but the phone process was cumbersome enough that the scale would sometimes time out of setup mode before I got to the part of the setup where the phone would look for it.  Then you have to remove a battery, wait ten seconds, go back to the phone and restart the setup and try to get it done before it times out again.

It was completely non obvious to me how to add other users.  But in reading the manual you set up the primary person, and then they go to their devices on the fitbit dashboard and from there they can invite up to 7 more people by sending them an email.  When they click on 'accept' in the email they're added to the scales users.  I didn't go far enough to determine how you would tell it specifically who was who if you had a lot of people on it.  It can tell the difference between people if there is a large weight discrepancy, say my wife being 120lbs and I'm 180.  So it knows which of us is which when we step on.  But if we had a teenager that was close to my wifes weight, you'd have to have a way to tell it.  Whatever that is!

Only other thing I noted from removing and replacing the batteries 57 times is that the springs that hold the battery at each end seem like they aren't the strongest or best made.  Hopefully it won't require battery changes that often.

Once set up, it worked fine.  The scale takes your weight and then extrapolates the fat % and BMI based on your sex, height, weight and so forth.  There is a 'lean' or 'athletic' option because this type of calculation doesnt work for people with low body fat content.  Each time you step on the scale it weighs and calculates the bmi and fat % and uploads it immediately to your fitbit dashboard.  The integration is nice, as I can weigh myself repeatedly throughout the day and have it pop up automatically.

I noted that like the fitbit ultra, the dashboard doesn't report the battery status of the unit correctly.  The laptop said the scale was down to 1/4 battery but they were brand new, and my other computer says it has nearly a full charge.

So a large amount of improvement on the setup polishing (this would have been a lot easier with a usb port on it and some software) and I expect they'll have some frustrated returns of the product until that area becomes push button simple.  Also looks like there needs to be a little more polishing around the user interface on the computer end as well, but I've already found a number of bugs in the fitbit web site.  Hopefully they'll get there.

My limited experience with fitbit support wasn't pleasing.  They're only open m-f during extended business hours, they do not do phone or chat, and they take a day or two to respond to an email.  Mine specifically noted that my fitbit ultra wasn't working at all and that I'd tried upgrading the firmware and resetting it, but it was dead.  Two days later I got the most unhelpful suggestion to upgrade the firmware, which I'd already said I'd tried.  So instead of trying to process a return with this 24-48 hour turnaround email support, I just returned the fitbit to amazon and got a replacement from them.

Very cool technology.  We have two ultras and the aria.  I've lost 60lbs so far, but most of it without these tools.  With them I have much better recording of my efforts and intakes and with most of it being automatic, its a huge facilitator in the effort to work out, lose weight and feel better.  Its just that my immediate reliability and ease of installing the fitbit products aren't quite where they need to be.

Lastly, I sure would appreciate it if fitbit would package their products more simply and reduce the price a bit.  The packaging is lovely, very well done and quite high end.  But since I'm a retired marketing guy, I know its expensive to package this way.

Edit: The scale has been working fine for us, but I think I found another problem.  I liked weighing myself 3-4 times a day with my old scale, just to see how different things affected my weight like hydration, workouts, etc.  But I'm hesitant to step on this scale aside from my first thing morning weigh-in because its going to transmit that data to the fitbit web site.  I'll have to look but I didn't see anything about a 'weigh only and don't report' option.

The other annoying thing is that I started this odyssey at 247 and I'm at 189 now, but the fitbit web site says I've only lost 51.5 pounds.  I actually didn't catch that, but my 7 year old was looking over my shoulder and commented that the math was wrong. I did have some problems with the fitbit web site taking weight input for dates in the future when I typed in the wrong info.  No limit checking apparently.  So there were some 'future weights' that kept messing up my charts.  Maybe thats still a problem.

These products really have enormous potential and I've used them extensively in the short time I've had them...but the setup and the web site polish needs a lot of work.

Edit #2:  Been using this for a few years now, problem free.  After about a year the Fitbit site finally 'awarded' me with the right weight loss amounts.
profile.summary: The setup needed more work before releasing this

profile.description: Hand-wash recommended with non-abrasive soap. Leave cap off and allow to air dry. Dishwasher safe, but the harsh environment may cause wear to the paint. For a more thorough cleaning, add 1 teaspoon white vinegar or baking soda to the bottle, fill 3/4 of the way with warm water, close and gently shake. Rinse and let your bottle air dry with the cap off.
profile.reviewText:
They're very tall and therefore easier to knock over.  Not as good as shorter bottles for school kids.

I see no problems with 'rounded bottoms' causing this to fall over on its own.  I've tried it with and without the sleeve, and its as stable as any bottle thats 10x taller than it is wide.

The snap cap is finicky.  If you set and seal it fully, its pretty spill proof.  If you just slap it down, it may or may not seat and if it doesn't and you turn it upside down, it'll leak in a slow small stream.

Cup holder wise, if your holders snug a can, this is going to be a tight fit.  My cup holders have removable inserts, and the bottles fit fine.  I think without the sleeve it'd fit in most cup-holders.

I hadn't planned to purchase these, but when I can buy a bottle with a lid and a sleeve for less than other companies charge for just the sport lid, and the sport lid lasts about 3 months before the little silicone plug disappears and it starts leaking.  Unless these turn out to be a major problem, that's too good a deal to pass up.

Update: after sending these to school with my 8 year old successfully (no problems with leaks, bottle well protected from drops by the included sleeve) the tall bottle tumbled out of his backpack bottle holder.  To be fair its a huge bottle wobbling about in a sleeve that's about can sized, and I should have put it inside the pack.  But the bottle and the top failed to survive a 3.5' drop to the ground.  Both are made of apparently easily cracked plastic, as the collar the top screws into was shattered and the bottle top itself was cracked almost all the way through and missing a chunk of plastic.  Of course that's the only part of the bottle unprotected by the sleeve, and the sleeve was doing great at preventing the daily scrapes, scratches and dents our old bottles accumulated.

So these are great unless you drop them top down, like when they roll over and fall out of a backpack!  I don't think the top would survive a fall of more than 2' onto concrete or asphalt. Change the plastic in the lid so it can take a drop!  Its not particularly 'green' if you drop a new bottle and the result is you have to throw it out.

Speaking of which, no comments about how its not the bottles fault, its the asphalt...please! :)

Further update: I contacted the company, expecting them to do nothing, but they sent me a new bottle at no cost!  So be careful about dropping them, but kudo's to the company for standing behind the product.  Not many do.
profile.summary: First impressions + updated longer term experience

profile.description: The netgear powerline av 500 adapter kit extends your internet access to any electrical outlet for the most demanding applications. it offers easy, plug-and-play setup and provides faster speeds for the most demanding applications. perfect for connecting hdtvs, blu-ray players, dvrs, pcs and game consoles to your home network and the internet.
profile.reviewText:
Powerline networking uses a signal over your regular house wiring, allowing you to connect devices all over your house with potentially higher throughput and reliability than wireless communications.  Its particularly helpful with devices that don't do wireless natively.

The first thing you need to know about powerline is that your real throughput in most homes will be around 1/10th to 1/5th of what the advertised speeds are.  Even on the same outlet, they won't perform to the specification.  The reason is that the specs presume ideal circumstances, a particular low overhead protocol you won't be using, the wind blowing in the right direction, and there is some stuff involving chicken bones and reptile blood that I just won't get into.  Bottom line is these will give you around 100Mb/s of real throughput, maybe a little more, in most homes.  The "200Mb/s" models could push maybe 40 or 50.

Powerline also can have poor "quality of service" in some homes and with some setups.  What this means is that the reliability of a stream of packets from one device to another can be uneven, or even some data dropped.  But this is also a big problem with wireless.

Powerline can be interfered with by devices that behave poorly on the wire.  Dimmer switches, microwave ovens, old vacuum cleaners and some fluorescent lights can drop throughput or put a powerline network out of service.  My early powerline stuff would all stop when my wife vacuumed the house.  The new stuff seems much less resistant to that, and I've used these particular products with great success.

I have one unit next to my router, one on the other side of that floor where we have a cluster of computers and printers, and one upstairs in my office.  We get 100-140Mb/s of throughput and the quality of service is good enough to run voice and high def video, two applications where quality of service are important.

In short, you can use these units to replace hard wiring of devices at a speed level where it actually works.  Anything that came before just wasn't good enough.

The configuration utility lets you secure the devices with an encryption key, but thats probably unnecessary for most people unless you live in an apartment building or cluster housing with some unusual wiring.  This signal probably won't pass a meter and if it does, its unlikely that a neighbor could get a connection from a device in their house to yours.  You can also configure the units to have the LEDs on or off, which is nice.

I highly recommend these for anyone who wants flexibility in setting up their home network.  You can hang a network switch (5 or more ports is common) and plug a bunch of stuff into one powerline adapter.  They all share one common 'bus' on your powerline, so consider that all of these powerline devices are themselves connected to a shared network hub that happens to be your electrical wiring.  A good place to read up on them is smallnetbuilder.
profile.summary: Finally a powerline product that can replace hard wires

profile.description: Mighty dog toys rethink durability and approach it from a new angle. Durability is created for each toy with multiple layers of flexible materials that move with the dog&rsquo;s teeth instead of tearing. Compared to other toys, Mighty dog toys have no hard edges. The result is these toys do not promote chewing &ndash; great when you&rsquo;re trying to discourage chewing habits. These toys may seem plush on the outside, but all the durability features are internal making these toys soft, yet MIGHTY strong. Please be a responsible dog owner and only allow your dog to play with the toy under supervision. Do not allow your pet to ingest any portion of the toy.
profile.reviewText:
This is a tough little toy and one of my shepherd and labs favorites.  It actually lasted over a year of them chewing on it (lightly) and pulling between them.  The little legs don't last long, but it held onto its stuffing after that.  The head came off in a major pulling contest and then it lost most of its stuffing.  The scrap is still a preferred toy to carry around and for pulling, but I bought another one and they're starting to work that into their toy routine.  For some reason, little scraps of old toys are still the most fun.  I have no doubt that a serious toy destroyer could chew this in half in short order, but they both seem to have decided not to shred this one.

Despite being labeled as a toy for smaller dogs, these two are 80lbs each.
profile.summary: Tough little toy and works great for larger dogs.

profile.description: Available only from Oceanic, the BioCube premium filter cartridges feature dual-action filtration. It features a woven pre-filter to clear debris and activated charcoal to remove odor and discoloration. Helps keep your aquarium water clear and healthy. For optimum efficiency, cartridges should be replaced every four-six weeks. Fits BioCube sizes 8, 14 and 29.
profile.reviewText:
My aquarium eats one of these about every ten days.  You can rinse/shake it out in a sink or bowl full of water drained from the aquarium but the cleaned filter will only last 3-4 days before clogging again.  Couple of things to be aware of...a large part of your aquariums ability to remove waste revolves around beneficial bacteria growing in your filter.  When you take the filter out, you remove a lot of organic waste from the ecosystem but you may also remove a lot of the bacteria that are clinging to the filter.

As such, when replacing the filter do not clean any other part of the filter assembly.  Do that a week after changing the filter.

I also do keep the last "full" filter and after rinsing in drained water I tuck it on top of the filter mechanism under the door so it stays damp.  When I do a water change I use that filter for a few hours after the change to catch all the junk that gets knocked loose in the water, then toss it and use a new one.
profile.summary: I wish these lasted a little longer but...

profile.description: Now when the power goes out, your garage door opener will still work. The Chamberlain Whisper Drive with MyQ Technology and Battery Backup allows you complete use of your garage during a power outage. The safety and security features will continue to operate as well, ensuring your family is protected in a power failure. As added convenience features the opener has a timer-to-close function that will automatically close the garage door in case you forget, and MyQ technology that allows your garage door opener to automatically control interior and/or exterior lights (with purchase of additional MyQ accessories) so you will never come home to a dark house again. The opener also features smooth start and smooth stop to reduce the noise of the garage door as it opens and closes perfect for homes with a room above the garage.
profile.reviewText:
I bought this opener roughly 7 years ago.  I was looking for a pair of new remotes and an outdoor keypad for my existing opener, then realized that those 3 things cost close to the price of this opener which was on sale with free installation.

Its much quieter than the 19 year old screw driver unit and opens/closes the door quickly.  That's the good part.  Now for the bad parts based on long term ownership.

The battery dies after about four years.  That's $25 to replace.  Then all of a sudden none of the remotes, including the keypad, would open the door reliably or at any sort of distance.  I tried changing the batteries to no avail, then looked it up.  Seems a lot of people have these problems and blame it on the remote losing power.  Since I had 3 remotes all suddenly not want to open the door, I knew it wasn't the remote.

Some fix it by extending the antenna wire out to the door or outside through a wall or vent.  But it appears that the internal circuit board has lost its sensitivity.  Chamberlain says it was due to voltage spikes and it needed a surge protector.  My other now 26 year old opener still works beautifully, and most of my neighbors still have both original 25-26 year old Genie's.  So either Genies are made to take a power spike or (much more likely) Chamberlain uses cheap capacitors to save a few cents.  Its $70 for a replacement board, although it fails often enough that there are a number of youtube video's that show how to replace it.

The sensitivity of the wall plate that senses motion and turns the lights on also fades when the remote control sensitivity does.

Nice quiet fast GDO, but you'll spend $100 on batteries and $240 on logic boards over a 20 year life span.
profile.summary: Fast and quiet, but it needs a lot of $$$ repairs.

profile.description: DisplayPort to HDMI Active Adapter 4K
profile.reviewText:
The little plastic cover swings down to protect the smaller microusb connection.  It works with windows, mac's and SOME android devices.

On the android end, you need a newer version of android, the hardware capability to do "on the go" connections and the drivers on your phone or tablet.  There are some otg compatibility testers and some otg helpers in the Play store that can tell you (a little unreliably) if your android device will work with an otg flash device like this and help you mount it.  I'll say again that the helpers and compatibility testers aren't 100% reliable.

If you have a brand spanking new flagship phone, it'll probably work.  Not any of the Fire devices I have will mount it, the phone, the fire 6 and the 7" hdx don't work.

There is also a form factor issue with this product.  On the underside where you can't see right under the swivel for that plastic cover is a little keychain ring. If you have a thick protective cover on your tablet or phone, this prevents the drive from getting all the way in.  You can either nip it off with a tool or make a little groove in your cover.  Most of the devices I have excepting a PC had this problem.

This was a bit of a disappointing purchase.  Its a well made product, the performance is good, the price is great.  But it doesn't work on half of my devices and won't fit in most of the rest without a field modification.  The OTG compatibility isn't the devices fault but the keyring thing is a real problem.  I'm betting someone wanted that feature thrown in at the end and it wasn't well tested.
profile.summary: Make sure your device is compatible with an OTG flash drive, and beware the keyring

profile.description: This exciting hybrid combines qualities of both traditional metal and non-stick cooking surfaces. Now not only can you brown, sear, and reduce sauces as the recipe intended, but you can also breathe a sigh of relief as you won't have a battle removing food and stains from the pan following use. How did this happen you ask? CALPHALON ONE INFUSED ANODIZED is manufactured with a revolutionary anodization process. Both interior and exterior surfaces are infused with an advanced release polymer which actually penetrates below the surface of the metal, into its very pores, offering superb durability and versatility. The intrinsic properties of aluminum ensure fast and even heating, as you've come to expect from Calphalon. Stockpots are ideally suited for cooking stock of course, but also for boiling pasta, steaming lobsters and crabs, and cooking bulky items like corn on the cob and potatoes.
profile.reviewText:
We have three aging dogs.  One has had both rear knees reconstructed and the other two are just fat and creaky.  Our vet prescribed some anti inflammatory NSAID's, basically doggy alleve.  But man, they're really expensive.  I saw these chewable aspirin and tried them out and the results are quite good.  No more painful settling down to go to sleep, no more creaking when standing up, no more limping after laying on a particular leg for a while.  And they're all a lot more playful and quite obviously feel better.

They take these like a treat, and I'm giving one tablet twice a day to each dog.  Thats below the dosage the bottle recommends by a good margin, so I advise starting low on the dosage and working your way up until you get the results you want.  The prescription meds are good for 12 or 24 hours, these only for ~6.  But even at the increased number of pills per day, this is about 80% cheaper than the prescription products.

So if you have an older dog or one with a bit of arthritis, give it a try.  Its working great for us.
profile.summary: Works as well as the prescription meds!

profile.description: This handy Ice Shaver makes snow cones, slushies, margaritas and other frozen treats quickly. Whether conquering the sweltering heat, hosting a party, or having fun with the kids, the Icy Treats Ice Shaver from Hamilton Beach will make frozen concoctions fast. Snow cones, slushies and icy drinks are all easy to make using soda, juice or fruit. This cool appliance uses ice directly from the freezer and will shave into either a bowl from home for snow cones, or into the included mixing bowl for other icy treats. Fun recipes are included for the whole family. Why not choose something refreshing like apple juice or strawberries to make a healthy treat for the kids? All removable parts are dishwasher safe and the bowl includes measurement markings so icy drinks will turn out great every time. Features Include: Make your favorite icy treats in minutes Make slushies, snow cones, margaritas, and more Add ice cubes from your freezer Shave ice into your own dish or use included mixing bowl Fun recipes included All removable parts are dishwasher safe
profile.reviewText:
I have this model and a couple of the ones that use ice 'hockey pucks'.  The latter all seem to be about the same.  The hockey puck models take a little bit of effort as you have to press down and tilt the motor end of it with the ice puck on the bottom rotating against a blade.  This hamilton beach model puts the motor on the bottom and uses some turned fan blades to push the ice against what looks like the same exact blade.

What you get out of this hamilton beach model is fine chunks of ice.  Fine for kids but really not shaved ice.  The hockey puck models turn out fine shaved ice just like you get from a larger machine, but its more work and the blade is pretty much shot after about 100 snow cones.  Ours lasted about a year with our son and his ever present wolf pack.

This is very easy to use and pretty hard to hurt yourself with unless you start taking the bowl parts out to wash them, then the blade is exposed.  The ice puck versions have the blade exposed when you remove the lid/motor.  So this one is a little safer for younger kids to use, and easy enough for them to make their own with just a little help.  The ice puck versions are for grownups or much bigger kids.

The ice shaver that takes more work but produces much finer shaved ice that I've used most recently is the Hamilton Beach Snowman, it looks on the inside just like several of the 'hawaiian shaved ice' models are, but the outside on some of those is slightly different.

So if you want quick and easy, get this one.  If you want real shaved ice and don't mind doing a little work, get one of the ice puck versions.  I found I was too lazy to use the ice puck model on a number of occasions, but this one is too easy to say no!
profile.summary: Comparison of this and other ice shavers

profile.description: Building upon the success of the SB6121, SB6141 and SB6183 Arris Surfboard Cable modems the SB6190 enhances your personal media experience, at lightning-fast broadband speed. It harnesses the power of DOCSIS 3.0 technology to bond up to thirty two downstream channels and eight upstream channels--providing you advanced multimedia services with data rates up to 1.4 Gbps download and 131 Mbps upload depending on your Cable Internet provider service. That makes streaming HD Video, gaming, shopping, downloading, working, high-quality voice and video conferencing, and peer-to-peer networking applications far more realistic, faster, and efficient than ever before. 2 year warranty.
profile.reviewText:
Edit: I've gotten some performance numbers and some consistency testing done.  My service is 75 down and 5 up.  I get 91 down and 6 up with this modem.  I've also performed extensive testing and have gotten the same results +/- a few percentage points even at peak usage times.  In practical use I'd occasionally get delays/echo in voip calls and streaming video would occasionally lose quality for a few seconds to a minute, especially between 7 and 9 in the evening.  No longer a problem.

-----------------------------------
Original review:

This cable modem offers 32 downstream 'channels' and 8 upstream channels.  Your download info gets spread over 32 'lanes' and your upload data gets spread over 8.  Like lanes in a road, not enough of them coupled with heavy traffic can result in erratic performance and loss of quality of service.

You share your local loop / node with other people in your neighborhood, and perhaps other neighborhoods if you live in a rural area.  What this means is that your data and everyone else's is on a single shared medium, split up into these 'channels'.  Your cable company will 'provision' or tell your modem which ones to use.  32 is realistically as high as they're going to go with this technology.  Many areas already support 16 or 32.  All will go to 32 before too much longer.

Most customer owned/retail modems support 4x4 or at best 8x4.  That means that you're cut out of using 28 or 24 download 'lanes' and up to 4 upload lanes.  The modem doesn't jump around if your lane gets clogged up, you're stuck with the ones originally provisioned to the modem when it boots.

The technology used has an acronym called "docsis" which handles modem/network management, encoding of your data, and channel handling among other things.  Docsis 2.0 is an old end-of-life technology that has minimal management ability, cant use lots of channels and it takes separate resources for the cable company to provide you service, which makes their costs higher, which makes your costs higher.  Docsis 3.0 is the current tech and what this modem supports.  It allows the cable company to remotely identify problems with your equipment and correct it, and allows them to look at whats happening when you call them.  It supports bazoodles of channels and offers excellent speeds and smooth quality of service.

Modems are rated for total speed which is based on channels, however this 'ideal performance' figure is rarely ever seen even in standard lab conditions, let alone on the 25 year old cable in your house and to the connection at the street.  These speeds also presume a completely uncongested network with nobody else using it and the full complement of channels the modem supports.  You won't be getting any of that.

Will this make your 50Mb/s connection go faster?  I wouldn't count on it but many people report getting higher than their paid-for rate with a higher channel modem when their area is provisioned for high channel counts.  What it'll do is give you a better shot at always having 50Mb/s and keeping your 'ping' times, gaming response times and netflix video quality consistent.

The Arris modem is also the stock rental modem most ISP's use, so they're familiar with it.  You can save a few bucks with different brands, but be prepared for more problems on activation and during problem situations.

Many ISP's have "end of life"d modems with docsis 2.0 and 4/8 download channel modems although they're allowing retail/owned modems to continue being used, even though it creates problems for them and those customers aren't getting always getting the most out of their service.

Docsis 3.1 will eventually show up next year and offer even better speeds, performance and manageability but these high tier docsis 3.0 modems will continue to remain in service for quite some time, perhaps 4 or even 5 years.  When you're looking at renting a modem for $70-100+ a year, its a no-brainer to buy one.  Unless you're subscribing to extremely high bandwidth services (400+Mb/s) you can get away with an SB6183 for a little less but I'm not sure that's a favorable economy since you'll be saving less than a buck a month over the life of the modem.

I looked hard at the Netgear CM600 and the SB6183 and decided to go with the 6190.  I bought an SB6141 a little over 3 years ago and its still offering me fine service.  However my area (which is a little rural on the edge of the suburbs) has been set up for 32/8 channel support and I'm seeing my speeds and quality getting a bit rough especially in the evenings.  One of my friends just upped their service to a high tier and got an SB6190, so now I have modem envy.

I'm looking forward to the same experience as when I went from a 6121 (4x4) to the 6141 (8x4), which was an immediately measurable and noticeable improvement in consistency and quality of service.

This modem, like many others, was a little mature upon its initial release late last year and it takes ISP's a while to process firmware updates and make them available.  So while earlier reviews have had some legitimate complaints, the modem is now pretty solid on Comcast and most other providers.

I'll update the review with some numbers once I have it installed.  I thought I'd give the benefit of my research on this to save others time.  Frequently modem choices get limited to "but what I have now works" (similar argument made for horses when cars came out) or "but I only have 75Mb/s service and my 5 year old modem will do 120 under ideal conditions" (my steam engine will get my car to 70MPH eventually").  Its a little more involved than that.
profile.summary: Get the most out of your service (regardless of speed tier) and a lot of future proofing for about a buck extra a month

profile.description: Puppia Soft Dog Harness The Puppia Soft Dog Harness is lightweight and made with soft durable material to provide your pet dog with excellent comfort. Pair it with the Puppia Two Tone Dog Leash to make a matching set. Features: Durable, soft and lightweight material Designed to fit comfortably around dog's neck and chest Coordinates with Puppia Two Tone Dog Leash (item#495153) Item Specifications: Size: XSmall Small Medium Large XLarge XXLarge Color: Beige Black Brown Camouflage Green Orange Pink Purple Royal Blue Red Sky Blue Yellow
profile.reviewText:
We had two problems we needed to solve.  One was our two older, very large dogs that love to walk but go so bananas when we get the harnesses out that its hard to get them into them.  Plus they all seem to have been made by origami experts and go on 5 different ways, 4 of them wrong.  We also have a smaller lab puppy that didn't really want to walk but my ex-wife dragged him around the neighborhood anyhow and the traditional harness scraped him up a little under the arms.

I was concerned about the sizing after reading the reviews, but the XXL size fits our 130lb mastiff/rotty/chow combination, our 75lb dalmation/pointer mix and the 50lb puppy.  Even with the big dog, there's some room to let out.  But the neck size is key, since that slips over the head.  One belt, one latch, only goes on one way and even if the dog is barking and jumping around you can slip this over their head and buckle it in 10 seconds.

Its soft, wraps around the head and neck, under the arms and chest, and it spreads the load out over a larger area instead of just a 1" strap.

Our big dog did at one point turn around, crouch down with his front legs and slip the harness.  He's done that with every one we've had.  Big body, big thick neck and a smaller head is the problem.  What was nice is that it took me no time at all to put it back on, and we had no problems walking in a forward direction!

Edit: Its been a while since I first reviewed this, so I thought I'd give it an update.  I've used this harness exclusively for all of my dogs since buying the first one.  All are still fully intact and in service for several years and I've bought more.  I resolved the problem of backing out of it by tightening the strap a bit.  Considering two of the dogs I use these on are the 130 pounder mentioned above and a young 80lb german shepherd, both pullers, they haven't done anything to damage these harnesses.  I still love how fast and easy they go on and the comfort they allow the dogs.
profile.summary: At last, the perfect walking harness
