profile.description: Fur kiddo not getting around like he or she used to? Add a daily helping of The Missing Link Original Superfood Hip & Joint formula to your pet's food. This powerful, powdered superfood supplement is chock full of joint and bone health supporting glucosamine and balanced Omega 3 and 6 fatty acids, as well as dietary fiber and phytonutrients to support your pet's digestive system and overall health and happiness. Add a spoonful to your fur kid's bowl and get ready to run  or at least go for a really long walk.
profile.reviewText:
I have four larger (60-140lbs) mixed breed dogs, three of which are very geriatric.  Some hip/knee and skin issues.

First off, this is easy to use.  It has to be refrigerated after opening.  Its a fine powder.  All four eat it plain right out of a bowl, I sprinkle it over the food and its licked off the food first, so they like it.  I even have some canned food they aren't that fond of, and they are more interested in eating it with this poured over the top.  I use a large deep scoopy soup spoon to dig it out and sprinkle it over the food rather than dump it from the bag.  This keeps the very wimpy ziploc channel in the bag from filling with the powder.  Its still not that great though, I'm amazed at how many food companies put absolutely crap ziplocs on their product packages.

With both older dogs and my own aging creaky body I've done a lot of research and trials with various joint compounds.  I use a glucosamine/msm supplement from Costco with very good results as far as alleviating pain in my neck, back and hip.  From what I've ascertained, the msm component is effective in the shorter term (2-4 days) and the glucosamine component takes about 4-6 weeks before starting to take effect.  If I stop taking the supplement, my aches come back within 4-6 days.  If I restart it, its about 3 days before I start feeling markedly better and after the 6 weeks there is further benefit.

I've taken both types of glucosamine (sufate and hcl), with about the same effects.  The hcl version is usually derived from plant sources and as a result can have much fewer contamination and allergic reaction problems as the sulfate, although in some studies the sulfate performed better.  Quite a few criticisms of those studies though, so they may be a canard.  In fact, most studies and science around this stuff is not particularly good, so its pretty much a case of try it and if it helps, great.

From what I've determined through talking to vets, human doctors and my own experiences, chondroitin does nothing or very little.  I see that most supplement makers have dropped it.

Omega-3's and their sources?  Well, its a good fat and its good for skin and coat but the most recent (and pretty good) science says that omega-3's don't reduce heart events or increase life span at all, regardless of their source.  The operators of the last major study done said they think the observed improvements from eating oily fish were likely that the fish was simply a better choice for a meal than other options, and that supplements are not effective whatsoever as heart helpers.  So the flax and rice bran act as a nice source of fiber and offer some oils that are beneficial to the system and the skin/coat, but I wouldn't get too worried about it being flax vs fish oil.

The rest of the ingredients either have limited or no solid science to support a major benefit, but they certainly don't hurt.  Would have been nice had they included a probiotic component, but you can't have everything.

I'm actually using this in conjunction with Phycox, giving essentially the maintenance dose of each instead of a double dose of one to 'ramp up', as both have glucosamine and msm.  Phycox seems to include some additional interesting ingredients like creatine. ala and turmeric along with some proprietary anti-inflammatory compounds.  So if they work I won't be able to tell which gave the relief or if it was the combination, but both seem inexpensive, are of good quality and both are eagerly eaten by all four so I'll probably continue to use both unless I see zero benefits.

If I see a benefit, I'll up the rating to four or five stars, if not I'll drop it to one or two.
profile.summary: So far so good, will update as I use it

profile.description: The Petmate Giant Litter Pan is suitable for multi-cat households and large cats with its extra large capacity. The extra large litter box is designed to hold more than 30 pounds of litter. The high walls keep litter contained and prevent litter scatter. The design break pattern of the huge kitty litter box provides a more durable base that won't tip over. The two side storage compartments on the side of the jumbo cat litter box allow for convenient placement of litter scoops and disposal bags. The Petmate extra large cat litter box also has an increased handle area for easier lifting and moving. Features Microban Antimicrobial Product Protection to help prevent the growth of stain and odor-causing bacteria in the litter box. Made in the USA.
profile.reviewText:
First off, this is the largest cat litter box I've ever seen.  You can pour a costco size container of litter into this and still have room

I got this for my very large, very overweight cat who stands in a normal box and shoots pee over the edge and onto the floor.  This has mostly solved that but it has one problematic area.  In the photo shown, the 'front' facing towards you dips inward and down.  I guess this was to facilitate entry, but if you have the same problem I have, that area is in enough and low enough to allow the cat butt to hang out.  To mitigate this, I bank the little against the three other sides to make a low spot.
profile.summary: HUGE!  Low dipped spot on the front could allow urine escapage

profile.description: The Char-Griller #3001 Grillin' Pro Gas Grill provides 438 square inches of gas grilling space; 438 square inches of primary surface and 192 square inches on the warming rack. The three stainless steel burner tubes generate a total of 40,800 BTU's. Also includes a 12,000 BTU side burner. The grill features heavy-steel construction, porcelain coated cast iron grates, dual stacks for even heating, a stainless steel thermometer, Stay Cool hood handle, and an electronic igniter probe on every burner.
profile.reviewText:
Big grill, high btu's, took me ~2 hours to assemble with 3 elementary school age helpers and the neighbors cat getting in the middle of it.  Could probably put it together in 30-40 minutes but the directions are a bit vague at times.  For example, some parts are helpfully labeled "this side inward", but "inward" is sort of up for interpretation.  Some bolts are different size in what you get vs the directions.  I have one long bolt with a wingnut on it leftover but nothing in the instructions seems to call for that.

As others have mentioned, you'll have a hard time turning the gas bottle off until the grill cools.  The knob is about 1.5" below the drip pan, which gets hot along with the grill.  No idea why people are reporting problems getting the gas bottle to fit, mine drops right in.  One igniter had no spark until I tweaked the distance between the tip and the burner, then all 3 worked fine.

Haven't cooked in it yet.  I'll report back if its good or not and if I have any problems with it at all.  If you see no reports of problems, I didn't have any!  Heated up to >600 in a few minutes, runs around 450 with all 3 burners on low.  I like the 'stacks' because you could cover one with an empty can or piece of foil to increase the heat retention inside (meaning one burner on low would give you some decent low and slow) and it looks like you could remove a portion of the right side of the lower casement and probably add on an indirect or smoker box to the side.

It does have a lot of gummy machine oil all over it.  I let it run to max temp for about 15 minutes, then low for 15 minutes, then shut it off.  I'll check tomorrow when its cool but that should have burned it off and helped 'set' the paint on it.  A high heat/off cycle like that heats the paint and then lets it 'stick' better, so there is less flaking or discoloration down the line.  Whole thing is matte black, so any black grill paint will dress up rust or scrapes.  Had a bunch of very minor scrapes and dings from the shipping process, its not really packed very well and lots of the parts are VERY close to the sides of the boxes, so if your box is bashed badly you might consider returning it instead of unpacking it, because you have about zero chance of getting all this back in the box once its unpacked.  Paid about $160 for it, can't really get anything this nice at that price point unless you're lucky enough to grab a clearance item at a B&M store.  Good luck with that.

Edit 2/14/15: I've used this for a little over a year.  The bottom of the 'barrel' under the grate collects grease and debris.  There isn't enough angle for it to run off.  So unless you scrape the gooey debris down into the lower collection tray, you'll have a grill fire eventually.  I don't have to do this very often, just once every few months.

The bolts all over it are also starting to rust.  Nothing serious yet but that's going to be the failure point of the grill eventually.  Its just rusting due to the paint coming off from the grill heat.  The worst are the four screws that hold the can exhausts on top of the barrel, but I can replace those with a stainless steel screw.  I'm guessing this to have about a 5 year life span.  I don't cover it, as I've had more problems with moisture buildup under a cover than I've had with a grill getting rained on.

Edit 8/10/2015:

The rust is setting in.  The grate has some heavy rust, one of the 'deflectors' is well rusted, and the bottom half of the 'barrel' is starting to rust.  I frequently spray the grill all over the inside with grill oil and its still going.  About what I've experienced with cheap painted metal grills before...good for 2-3 years and then they need enough parts replaced to consider tossing it and buying a new one.

Edit 5/31/2018

Finally ready to replace the grill although I could easily squeeze another year out of it.  The burners are rusty but still work, no blowouts.  The heat deflectors are pretty rusty but still in one piece.  I have the original grates but there's a 2"x2" section that's rusting.  Some rust on the bots but it still has structural integrity.  Home depot offered a nice 4 burner with ceramic infrared sear side burner for under two hundred, assembled with a free gas bottle exchange and I couldn't pass that up.  I'm going to scrape this old one out and leave it out in the yard should I need to cook anything really messy on it.

3.5 years with an easy shot at 4-4.5 isn't too shabby for an inexpensive grill.
profile.summary: Nice grill especially at the price.  Still going after 3.5 years

profile.description: The Foscam FI9821P is Foscam's first "Plug & Play" camera featuring the ability to connect via smartphone by simply scanning the QR code on the underside of the camera. Bypassing the need to access your router and setup port forwarding, the FI9821P can be set up effortlessly by anyone, even those with very little IT experience. The FI9821P also features 1280 x 720p video resolution, h.264 video compression, built-in DVR via SD card (upto 32gb), two-way audio, Wi-Fi-N capability, pan/tilt, remote internet viewing, motion detection, night-vision as well as network video recording capability. In addition, it is smartphone compatible (iPhone, Android - app required) as well as viewable over the internet using standard browsers on PC (Firefox, IE & Chrome) or Mac (Safari only). The camera functions well as a smartphone baby, pet or elderly parent monitor or as part of a complete home/office security system with remote internet monitoring ability. The FI9821P improves on the FI8910W by adopting high performance media and video processors capable of H.264 video compression which allows for ultra-smooth high definition video transmission, increased FPS and minimal bandwidth consumption. In addition, due to the small file sizes produced by H.264 video compression it has the ability to save tremendous disk space when doing video recording.
profile.reviewText:
Do not buy.  I've just removed them from my network and I'm throwing them out.

These have a peer to peer function that broadcasts locally on your wireless network looking for anyone who wants to connect to them.  They also go through your firewall and connect to numerous hosts, mostly in China.  There is an option to turn this off, but it doesn't actually do anything.  One user reported that the camera sent 600,000 packets of data through their router in 8 minutes.

The manufacturer will glad hand you about this, saying that its just for convenience.  I see that they've offered a special patch to resolve it, but nobody can confirm actually getting it.

Lastly, in order to get firmware updates you have to give them your email and agree to receive promotional mails.  No direct links.  They email you the links, which apparently change regularly.

Steer clear and buy another brand.
profile.summary: Do not buy.  Major security issues and a non responsive manufacturer.

profile.description: Ultra-thin design,High quality material
profile.reviewText:
Very good for the price, which was under $4.  It does make the phone a lot more bulky and heavier.  I switch between this and a super cheap clear case.  This offers good scratch resistance and some drop resistance, although the side/corners where the latch is are exposed and close to the edge.  It'll do as well as any minimal/pleather case for drops.

The one thing I don't like about it is that the inside of the left side where the pockets are has one pocket that is bright lipstick red while the rest of the case is black.  That makes it look cheap.  I tried to color it black like the rest but its not very permeable.  You can see the red on the edge without opening the case.
profile.summary: Very nice folio fake leather case for the price

profile.description: PlastiColor Plain Black Mud Guards are the most colorful and durable flaps with a patented, fiberglass backing that not only keeps them from cracking or splitting, but also adds " memory" to keep their shape. They are also made of a specially formulated PVC that will easily withstand sub-zero temperatures and extreme heat without cracking. These " Easy Fit" mud guards feature an easy-to-install design, and includes all the necessary hardware which facilitates easy installation.
profile.reviewText:
Edit: seems some folks are confused at the star rating and irate at my alternative usage and not as a mud flap.

My star rating on these is as a mud flap.  It has no reinforcement at the top and hence would have a short life unless you were to epoxy a metal overlay to it.  Additionally I used one as the floor of a home made feral cat shelter and the cat pretty well destroyed it in a few months.

However they're perfectly fine large, thick rubber pieces with a myriad of uses.  I happened to get a pair from amazon warehouse for <$10, and it fit the bill at that price for several alternative uses.

Original:

I bought these for the same reason as another reviewer: to use in a home made dog door.  I have three very large very old dogs that have trouble navigating a regular dog door, and ones that they can fit through run $700.  So I'm going to use this in a similarly sized wood frame and attach a $20 insulated foam panel to the top of it to fill a sliding glass door.

For this application i think I'm going to have to put a stick on cork sheet on one side.  One side is smooth rubber, the other is rough and bumpy...probably the side intended to go towards the tire.  Doesn't look like it'd be comfortable for a dog nose.  Its also pretty heavy and not very flexible, so I hope I don't have any problems with tail slap as it closes.

Its got several indents in the top to put screws or bolts through.  If I can make it work I'll be looking at about $50 for the door.  Not attractive or easily removed/reinstalled but it'll do the job.
profile.summary: Using it for a dog door

profile.description: NZXT presents the cutting edge Phantom Full Tower Chassis. Designed with sleek, pristine contours, the Phantom delivers high performance cooling advantages with 7 fan cooling options, dual radiator support, quad watercooling cutouts, and five 20W per channel fan controls. An innovative 5.25" screwless system vast space to encompass 7 hard drives, and five 5.25" bays enable smooth customization.
profile.reviewText:
Its huge.  Biggest case I've ever owned.  But it holds any motherboard, tons of disk drives, plenty of fans, and you won't scrape any fingers or knuckles on the inside because its both large and well made, with rolled metal edges.

I bought this and all the parts to build a computer, and put it together with my 7 year old.  The huge case made that easy, and we're sliding it beside a desk where we have plenty of room.

The case has a lot of nice features like painted interior, rolled metal edges, tool free design, etc.

Couple of things to note...one is that the lights to light it up the way its pictured on Amazon aren't included.  You get one fan on top in the back with the colored LED's on it that lights up most of the top mesh black panel, but no lights on the side or the front as pictured.  You have to buy fans from NZXT to make them fit as they used a non-standard size...for example the '200mm' fans they use are 192mm, so a 200mm from someone like corsair won't fit.

I also knocked a star off because their customer service is completely unresponsive.  One of the fans is clicky and I thought that maybe there was a way to light up the remaining panels that I hadnt found like a connection or switch, but I got no answers to my emails, so I might have to call amazon to fix these issues.  Its a shame that so many companies do such a poor job of customer service, then expect people to continue buying their stuff.  Oh well, thanks to amazon I don't have to worry about that sort of thing!
profile.summary: Arguably one of the best cases, if you have room for it!

profile.description: These butane cans are impurity-free, having been refined 14 times. For you that means it won’t impair the performance of your lighter. Each can is equipped with plastic adapter tips that are located conveniently in the cap. Features: Six (6) Cans Each can is 10.8 oz 14 Times Filtered Butane fuel Assures clean, clog-free fuel burning with most butane ligthers Comes with adapters to fit most butane lighters Please note: Due to FAA regulations, these items will ship via USPS Parcel Post and may incur additional delivery times.
profile.reviewText:
I have a kitchen torch that gets used for all sorts of stuff besides creme brulee, but when I got it I used a common gas that my supermarket carried.  It sputtered and smelled funny and just didn't burn well, so I complained to the manufacturer of the torch.  They suggested a short list of butane including the vector gas.  Sure enough, once I purged the supposed brand name gas out of the torch and refilled it with this, it burned great.

I guess butane is really dirty and most manufacturers just sell it unrefined or barely refined. It takes at least 3-4 filtrations to use in a quality butane lighter or torch.  This is filtered at least 5 times.

So far its worked out extremely well for me, and bought in quantity is cheaper than the supermarket canned butane.
profile.summary: Clean gas is crucial

profile.description: Augusta Sportswear Boys' Training Short S Silver Grey
profile.reviewText:
For the price, you can't beat these.  Considering my son loses 1-2 pairs of PE shorts each year I don't want to pay big bucks for them.

My primary concern was about the reviews saying they were see through.  Not really.  If you hold them up to a bright light, you get nothing through two layers and a little through one.  I had him put white undies on and put the shorts on.  Nothing.  Not at all see through.  If he's outside in the sun, you can see some sun through the very bottoms of the legs but you can't see the legs.

I almost didn't buy them due to those concerns, but glad I did.  The $25 shorts the school sells are not much better.
profile.summary: A steal, perfectly good for PE or regular sports stuff, not "see through" like people claim

profile.description: Rii Keyboard/ Mouse Combo
profile.reviewText:
Its small, lasts a long time on a charge, and the backlighting while not particularly consistent is nice when using it in the dark.

The keys are small, feel like those bubble contact keys, the backlight is much brighter on some keys than others and the trackpad is a little too small.

I think had they made these about 20% larger with a bigger trackpad that I'd have liked it a lot better.

Range-wise you can actually go pretty far with these but it sort of depends on how you're holding it.  I got easily 30+ feet away and if I held it with the large flat back (on the flip side of the keys) facing the receiver it'd do fine but if I held it horizontally with the narrow back facing the receiver and the keys facing up, it'd only give me ~10-12 feet.

I ended up keeping this and also getting a logitech k-400r.  I use the 400r unless its too dark to see the keys or I really just want one or two buttons to use one handed with my htpc.  Both seem to work fine together in the same pc with both receivers in the front usb slots about 3" apart.
profile.summary: I wanted to like this more than I do

profile.description: Take it to the next level with the Razor Pro XX Scooter. Designed and tested by Team Razor pro riders, for maximum durability and performance in mind. The scooter offers a 100 percent aircraft-grade aluminum body, a double TIG-welded deck for superior strength, and threaded 110mm compatible fork to sustain even the roughest conditions. The scooter also features freestyle rubberized grips to protect your palms along with Razors patented rear brake system. It is equipped with 14 spoke 110mm high grade urethane wheels and RZR Pro 20 bearings for a smooth ride. Recommended for ages 8 and older and comes in your choice of silver or red, the Razor Pro XX Scooter is sure to impress!
profile.reviewText:
I did quite a bit of research on scooters before buying one for my son.  Bottom line is that you get what you pay for...up to a point.

There are a load of inexpensive scooters that are often said to be "good enough".  Their limitations are smaller wheels that wear out or break faster or more easily.  They have weight limits that your child may exceed by the time they're 11 or 12.  The decks are smaller and the brake actuators are smaller and may be harder to use.  The whole scooter may break if they do some curb hopping or other minor 'tricks' or hard usage.  So you'll end up buying a second and perhaps third or fourth, making the bargain much less bargainy.

This is a solid scooter you can get for about 50% more than the cheapest available.  It has big heavy duty wheels that will take a long time to wear out and won't break unless your kid is doing tricks that would cause you to wet your pants if you saw them doing it.  It has a large deck with plenty of foot space for better balance and fewer foot slips.  Big brake pedal with raised markings which is easy to actuate and control.  Solid heavy duty welds, thick aluminum and a fixed handlebar, plus >200lb weight load limit.

In short, this scooter is safer than a $20 cheapie, will last longer, and you probably won't ever have to do anything with it like replace wheels.  Some folks that really beat on it report they need to change the grips on the handlebars.  They seem pretty tough to me.

Worst problem with these is everyone knows they're a good scooter, so it may get stolen more often.  My son was messing around with friends a few weeks ago and they all left their scooters on a lawn out of sight for a few minutes.  My son's pro was grabbed but not the others.  So make sure someone keeps an eye on this or its put away.
profile.summary: Solid, well made very safe scooter with a lot of good features that will last a very long time

profile.description: A cool combination of earth science and technology, this computer software and microscope kit turns ordinary discoveries into creative adventures. First, it's collecting specimens from around the house, backyard or even the school lunch tray. The microscope magnifies them up to 200 times the original size, and connects to your PC for viewing and downloading the image-whether it's a snapshot or time-lapse movie. The rest is up to your imagination. You can use the QX3 software to add special effects or manipulate the image. Create animated movies or use the image and video library to enhance your scientific presentation. Finally, print stickers and posters, or share your movie with your friends via email. Includes activity guide book and lab supplies: 2 specimen jars, 2 containment dishes, sample slide, tweezers, eye dropper and slide clip. Compatible with Windows 98, Me, 2000, or XP.
profile.reviewText:
Just so people understand the lack of support from Intel on this, it was discontinued twelve years ago and was made from 1999 to 2002.  In fact, its pretty impressive that Intel kept up with driver updates on it and that there is a good windows XP driver pack.  Windows XP released AFTER this was discontinued.

You should be able to get this to work by downloading Microsoft XP mode/virtual machine and installing the drivers/software within that.  [...]
It is actually a fairly good grade of equipment for its price point (in 1999) and very cool for kids.  You can often find one for around $10.  My son's school has two of them just stuffed in the back of an equipment cabinet where they've probably sat for ten years.  Newer usb microscopes will likely have better quality, but this does pretty well for windows 98 era technology.
profile.summary: Heads up for recent buyers

profile.description: Give your dog the taste of a home-cooked meal with IAMS PROACTIVE HEALTH Adult Wet Dog Food. Our wholesome dog foods are made with natural ingredients, such as beef and rice in a savory broth for a taste dogs can't resist. IAMS PROACTIVE HEALTH also is formulated with omega fatty acids to promote healthy skin and a soft, shiny coat. Plus, with added vitamins and minerals, you can feel good knowing that your dog's favorite wet food offers complete and balanced nutrition for adult maintenance. Make dinnertime special with IAMS PROACTIVE HEALTH Adult Ground Wet Dog Food.
profile.reviewText:
The ingredients aren't great and honestly, neither is the price for what you're buying.  Lets look at some ingredients and see why:

Water Sufficient For Processing (water isn't bad, but its not nutritional)
Chicken (standard trick of using fresh chicken before its been cooked/dried, after which it'll be much lower on the list by weight)
Meat By-Products (not even a named by product, so whatever was in the leftover bin at the meat processing plant that they couldn't make into pink slime)
Chicken By-Products (at least a named protein that was in the leftover bin at the chicken plant and couldn't be made into 'nuggets')
Brewers Rice (this is the leftover bits of rice from cheap beer makers who use fermented rice alcohol to boost their products alcohol contents)
Carrots, Sweet Potatoes (good ingredients)
Dried Beet Pulp (the stuff leftover from making beet sugar)
Flax Meal (the stuff leftover from making flax oil)

The rest isn't in amounts large enough to care a lot about, but several of those are also leftover items that aren't beneficial to a dog.

The tricks to watch out for, as illustrated above, is showing a fresh ingredient so its #1 or #2 when after processing it'd be 3rd/4th or later; breaking the same ingredients up so they're lower on the list, and coming up with lovely sounding names for leftover which can either be used as a filler in dog food or has to be discarded.

This is a can of 'meat' and chicken by products with leftover waste rice and beets and some vegetables.  They kept the corn, wheat and soy out of it, but this isn't much different from a lot of less expensive brands.
profile.summary: Not very good ingedients

profile.description: Give your dog the taste of a home-cooked meal with IAMS PROACTIVE HEALTH Adult Wet Dog Food. Our wholesome dog foods are made with natural ingredients, such as beef and rice in a savory broth for a taste dogs can't resist. IAMS PROACTIVE HEALTH also is formulated with omega fatty acids to promote healthy skin and a soft, shiny coat. Plus, with added vitamins and minerals, you can feel good knowing that your dog's favorite wet food offers complete and balanced nutrition for adult maintenance. Make dinnertime special with IAMS PROACTIVE HEALTH Adult Ground Wet Dog Food.
profile.reviewText:
All four of my various mixed breed large dogs like this food.

Ingredient wise, not that great.  You have the mystery 'meat by products'.  When a by product is named, like beef or chicken, at least you know it all came from one source.  Which is still not that great.  This is what is left in a vat after meat is processed and its the material that can't be legitimately used for anything.  Consider it about 3 generations below 'pink slime' in quality.  Generally when its not even named to a specific animal its about the worst quality product that can still be named meat.

Next there is brewers rice.  Rice isn't really that good for dogs and lately its been found to contain levels of arsenic.  Brewers rice is a byproduct of beer and rice wine manufacture.  Basically bits of rice that fell on the floor or weren't used properly or were leftover.  Many low end beer makers just produce a beer flavored product and then spike it with distilled rice alcohol to give it the kick.

No corn, no wheat, no soy and a couple of named proteins to go with the byproducts,  I've certainly seen much worse and honestly to get better foods (grain free, named proteins, no by products) you'd have to pay a lot more or make it yourself.  I'm somewhat picky about pet food and I'm okay with this for part of my pets feeding.

Three of my four dogs and both of my cats are over 100 in people years, and they've outlived their joints, teeth and hearing, so I'm doing something right.
profile.summary: Not the best ingredients but reasonably priced and well liked

profile.description: Harness - Soft SKY BLUE XS
profile.reviewText:
We had two problems we needed to solve.  One was our two older, very large dogs that love to walk but go so bananas when we get the harnesses out that its hard to get them into them.  Plus they all seem to have been made by origami experts and go on 5 different ways, 4 of them wrong.  We also have a smaller lab puppy that didn't really want to walk but my ex-wife dragged him around the neighborhood anyhow and the traditional harness scraped him up a little under the arms.

I was concerned about the sizing after reading the reviews, but the XXL size fits our 130lb mastiff/rotty/chow combination, our 75lb dalmation/pointer mix and the 50lb puppy.  Even with the big dog, there's some room to let out.  But the neck size is key, since that slips over the head.  One belt, one latch, only goes on one way and even if the dog is barking and jumping around you can slip this over their head and buckle it in 10 seconds.

Its soft, wraps around the head and neck, under the arms and chest, and it spreads the load out over a larger area instead of just a 1" strap.

Our big dog did at one point turn around, crouch down with his front legs and slip the harness.  He's done that with every one we've had.  Big body, big thick neck and a smaller head is the problem.  What was nice is that it took me no time at all to put it back on, and we had no problems walking in a forward direction!

Edit: Its been a while since I first reviewed this, so I thought I'd give it an update.  I've used this harness exclusively for all of my dogs since buying the first one.  All are still fully intact and in service for several years and I've bought more.  I resolved the problem of backing out of it by tightening the strap a bit.  Considering two of the dogs I use these on are the 130 pounder mentioned above and a young 80lb german shepherd, both pullers, they haven't done anything to damage these harnesses.  I still love how fast and easy they go on and the comfort they allow the dogs.
profile.summary: At last, the perfect walking harness

profile.description: WT Max PetPlus Bglss Upright
profile.reviewText:
With a household containing four large dogs and a variable number of 10-12 year old boys, a vacuum cleaner is an important part of the cleaning arsenal.  These are the voyages of my experiences with these items.  My 15 year mission has been to explore strange new products, identify bogus suction claims, and try to figure out why a $400 vacuum would be better than a $200 vacuum.  To boldly suck up clods of unidentifiable gloop like no man has ever done before.

For starters, there's a good chance that not just one vacuum will do it for you.  I have a handheld, a really small narrower one just the right width for stairs, which is super light and has great suction.  And a larger one that hopefully does both carpet and hard floors.

I've tried and tested numerous expensive main cleaners, from my gigantic whole house vacuum unit in my first mcmansion to the high priced boutique brands to the higher end mainstream brands.  The two big bogus things you'll encounter are "Doesn't lose suction!", which tests how well a cleaner draws up dirt when its full.  I'm not sure about you but I empty my vacuum when its full.  Whether or not it'll maintain suction while stuffing its innards with dirt after the cup overflows seems irrelevant to me.  The other is using your old vacuum and then re-doing it with the new one.  A $40 brand new vacuum with clean hoses, paths and a fresh motor will pick up some stuff that your 8 year old tired $250 vacuum could no longer pull up.

So I've developed a strategy of finding vacuums with good suction, good features, and either relegating them to secondary duty (upstairs) or just tossing them out after a few years.  I also don't buy a bagged vacuum.  I've tried that and spent more money on the bags than replacing the cleaner every few years.  But bear in mind my dirt load isn't exactly one person living alone with a short haired cat.  I have to empty a high capacity cleaners cup twice just to do my living room.

Best vacuum I ever used was a self propelled hoover.  It had the highest suction of any vacuum I've used except the whole house unit that was 4' tall and 2' wide, just for the suction part.  It had a few warts around how you used it which caused problems for some folks, and it was very heavy and non maneuverable.  But a vacuum that moves by itself and pulled the most dirt worked for me.

Problem is, those are expensive and do need some belts and whatnot, and the hepa replacement filters are spendy too.

My more recent foray was into a Hoover T series rewind bagless model that I got for a truly stupid price.  I was just going to use it for secondary purposes but it had plenty of suction, easily adjusted height, had a retractable cord, and wasn't that heavy to push around.  But its got a few years of use on it, so I figured something a little higher end might be in order.

Comparing this vacuum with the t-series.  This one tends to be about twice the price of my T series and they look remarkably the same.  Almost the same dirt canisters (but not quite, they aren't interchangeable...close though) except for the top part of the more expensive one shows the multiple 'cyclones' while the T series has one large cone.  Both have almost the exact same controls in the same places, with the only main exception being the more expensive model has more carpet height settings and a foldable handle.  Power, cord, cord retract, brush on/off and handle release are all identical.  The hose snaps off with a push of a button at the base, and wands and crevice/brush tools are easily deployed.  Can't imagine an easier setup there to switch from cleaning carpet to wand cleaning, although some reviews here see to suggest some kind of problem or inefficiency.  I'm not seeing that.  Cord is nice and long but the hose could be a foot or so longer for my needs, which involve lots of stair/small area cleaning.

It runs quieter than the T series and the brushes ruffle the carpet more thoroughly, so it looks like the primary delta's between this and the cheaper T series is a quieter slightly more powerful motor for the vacuum and the brushes, more 'cyclones' and the powered hand tool.  Its also about 1" wider and has a clear head so you can see if the brushes move or not.

Downsides?  The dirt cup is the same size among all these style Hoovers, which is to say it could be a good 30-50% larger for my needs.  I have to empty it a lot.  To do that you can use two methods.  The 'one button' bottom empty which I can't believe they still include because its about worthless.  You end up with a bunch of dirt still sitting in the 'bottom' and by the time you shake everything out and get the bottom reattached, you'll have dust everywhere including all over your hands.  I just unscrew the canister and turn it over, then tap the rest on the inside of the garbage can.  Outside.  Good luck dumping this out inside.  However now the canister has some wear points from unscrewing it and tapping it.  A plastic piece at the end of the cone on my T-series cracked, but some duct tape has held it together for six months now.

Last problem you have with both is considerable dust collection in the cyclonic area and one long job to take it apart and clean it.  Easy solution though, remove the filter from the top of the canister and rinse the whole assembly with hot water in the sink, take it outside and shake the excess water out and let it dry before reassembly.  I have to do this every few months.  Hoover took a step back with the hepa filter in the canister head.  It used to be easy to remove, now its round and rimless.  You'll have to dig a finger in between the rubber ring and the plastic housing to get it out.

Bottom line: inexpensive (if you shop carefully), great suction, good ease of use except for emptying, wide path, great carpet brushing, very good selection of tools, brush on/off is nice, very good vacuum for the price.  If you need a bag, want something with a ball or joint in it, want to vacuum with a full dirt cup or want to spend $400-700 on a vacuum cleaner...not for you.
profile.summary: Good vacuum, similar to its brethren, inherits some issues that Hoover really should have solved a while ago

profile.description: As dogs walk, run, jump and play, tremendous stress is placed on all components of ther joints. Years of wear and tear from exercise, normal aging, disease, injury or genetic conditions can break down cartilage, leading to instability and discomfort. Nutri-Vet bone and joint supplements are specifically formulated to support structural integrity of joints and connective tissues in dogs, and aspirin helps reduce pain in dogs of all ages, breeds and sizes. Liver flavor chewables minimize the potential of stomach upset and maximize taste and aroma. 300 mg per tablet.
profile.reviewText:
Most people know that dogs can use many of the same medications as we do, although they tend to eliminate them more slowly than we do so they last a little longer in the dog than it will in a person.

Aspirin and pepto bismol are two things we've used extensively at our house.  Grumpy tummies are often fixed up with a spoon full of pepto (I put it in a syringe and squirt it in the side of the dogs mouth), and achy joints and minor injuries are well treated with canine aspirin.  Once our dogs got really old we moved to prescription anti-inflammatories.

We used a variety of canine aspirin with good luck, then I bought four of these.  They work, but they're smaller in size and must have less tasty liver stuff in them, because our dogs just aren't fond of them and sometimes leave them behind.  But the idea is good, so look for canine aspiring your dog likes if they're starting to get a little older and creakier.  Its a low cost way to help them feel better, may have the same heart healthy benefits that aspirin does in humans, and there is very little downside other than a sore stomach if taken without food and to excess.
profile.summary: The idea is good, but this isn't as palatable as others

profile.description: A favorite "good bug" and alternative to chemicals, ladybugs have been a popular part of the Orcon line of beneficial insects for over 20 years. When released at sundown (because they don't fly at night), ladybugs eat aphids, mealy bugs, scale, leaf hoppers, various plant eating worms and other destructive soft bodied pests. And they keep on eating until the bad guys are gone, laying their own eggs in the process. When new pests arrive, fresh ladybugs will be waiting. Each container includes approximately 1500 live ladybugs. Restricted State: Hawaii
profile.reviewText:
Ladybugs hatch and are quite active in the spring and early summer, lay their eggs and migrate away in the fall.  So its preferable to buy them early in the season if you want them to finish off the aphids on your roses, but okay to buy them late in the season if you want hatching ladybugs the following year.  I've tended to buy some early and release them once the first frosts are over, and again when they're on sale in the fall.

This has worked out well for me.  This year I don't think I need to buy any, as its hard to pick out a square foot of flowers or ivy in my yard that doesnt have at least 4-5 ladybugs on it, feasting away on the nuisance bugs.
profile.summary: What time of year you order these matters...

top_5.description: Dogswell Happy Hips Jerky - Lamb & RiceDogswell Happy Hips Jerky - Lamb & Rice helps your pet maintain healthy hips and joints with glucosamine and chondroitin. It's made from real lamb jerky with added nutrients.
top_5.reviewText:
My dogs like these treats well enough.  My question is regarding the amounts of glucosamine and chondroitin that they incorporate.

According to what I'm looking at, you need around 300-500mg of each per 25lbs of dog, per day.  The bag ingredients says 2000mg/kg of glucosamine and 1000mg/kg of chondroitin.  So that means my 100lb dog would need to eat 2lbs of this treat every day to get a satisfactory dose, since a kg is 2.2lbs.

Reading the reviews of the various versions of this treat, I'm also wondering how much of the perceived results are scientifically due to the supplements.  I see a lot of people noting improvements and results in a week or two, yet glucosamine and chondroitin are supposed to take 4-6 weeks before they produce a noticeable benefit.

For our big, fat, old dogs, we've had good luck with the vetrin chewable aspirin for dogs.  They like them, they're inexpensive, and they do a nice job of taking the squeak and creak out of the dogs.
top_5.summary: Not enough glucosamine and chondroitin

top_5.description: Intel NUC NUC5CPYH, 4K Support via HDMI, HD Graphics, SATA3 for 2.5-Inch HDD/SSD BOXNUC5CPYH
top_5.reviewText:
I managed to pick one of these up on ebay for $160 with an already installed ssd, stick of ram and windows 8.1.  That was a pretty decent deal.

Its quite slow for regular windows usage.  I made a little htpc out of it with Nextpvr, which turned out to be quite a fiasco to set up.  For that purpose the performance is acceptable.  I also installed OpenElec on it and that went smoothly with the standard install working fine for 4k video and all the capabilities of the recent cpu/gpu working fine.

On windows in 4k with windows media center, it slowed to a crawl.  It'd play video okay but response to the mouse and keyboard was a little slow and jerky.  In 1080/60 it was fine.

I found that usb wireless devices with the tiny little receivers were having problems.  Once I disabled the internal bluetooth and wireless lan and put the receiver on a 2' usb extension the poor response problems went away.  I've seen explanations that the usb 3 ports aren't fully compatible with the tiny receivers or that the other devices in the box cause interference, but since I didn't need bluetooth and the box is wired I just eliminated all possible sources of problems.

In reading a lot of reviews for the box, it became pretty clear that many problems were caused by using the wrong memory.  This requires a 1.35v stick and won't work properly with regular voltage ram and its picky about which 1.35v ram it'll work with.  I have a ripjaws 1.35v 8GB stick in there.  A little overkill as I rarely saw any app require more than 2-3GB, but the price differential between 4 and 8GB isn't that much.  Intel did the same thing with a few of their other chipsets and I'm not sure why as it tends to cause a ton of customer problems.  I think a lot of people figure they'll throw in that old stick of memory they have on the shelf and that's why there are so many bad reviews.

There is a small fan in the box which you can hear if you put your ear to it and I can feel a very very minor vibration when touching the case.  I've never heard the fan go any louder even when the box is going full blast.

Nice feature set for the price, especially if you can get one used or already assembled.  I think lots of people get one of these setup and are disappointed by the performance, which is pretty weak.  So there is a good secondary market for them  Unless you get full gpu hardware accelerated software, you won't get much out of this.  My former htpc/pvr machine was an older pentium dual core 2.7GHz machine with a 7770 video card.  That was sluggy with 4k video but other than that it was way faster than this.  A gtx 960 would have solved the 4k issue, but those cost more than this whole machine did.

For some performance figures, when this box is recording two shows from my silicondust tuner, its running ~25% cpu load.  When playing back 1080 without hardware acceleration its 80-100%.

Its a perfect little kodi box with openelec and that installed and ran with no problems.  I didn't load it up with 1000 shows, I just tested it with the standard stock openelec installed themes and zipped around all the options.  I didn't see any slowdowns or weak performance like I did with Windows 10.

There's no way I'd have paid ~$300 for one of these, a stick of ram, an ssd and a windows license.  Its not worth it.  However for half price its a decent deal and exactly what I needed.
top_5.summary: Nice feature set, weak performance with windows, runs openelec perfectly

top_5.description: Whirlpool GU2300XTVQ Full Console Dishwasher with 6 Automatic Cycles, 14 Place Settings, Auto Soil Sensor, 2-4-6 Hour Delay Wash and Quiet Partner III Sound Package: White
top_5.reviewText:
You would think after decades of designing and building dishwashers that at least the simple things would be pretty well worked out.  Not so.

Right after buying my house, I turned the 20 year old dishwasher on, empty, to run a cycle to clean it out as the house had been sitting for quite a while.  When I got back from my shopping trip, the house was full of smoke.  Yes, I got a box full of water to catch on fire.  I'm a wizard.  My guess is the prior owner (the second cheapest person on earth) never turned on the heated dry option...ever...and I hit all the buttons when I turned it on.

So the home warranty company rolls out and offers me two models.  The cheapest dishwasher on earth or I could cough up an extra $150 and get this whirlpool gold model.  I opted for the whirlpool and of course got denied by the local utility company for a rebate for paying extra for an energy star unit.  Anyone ever get a utility rebate for anything?

This dishwasher won't clean dishes unless you rinse everything off of them first.  I end up just filling the sink with water in the morning and dumping dishes into it and leaving them there all day to remove anything sticky, dried on, or the usual hard to remove stuff (mustard, chocolate, egg yolks, etc).  If you put anything taller than 4" in the bottom rack in the front it'll block the detergent door from opening, the detergent will turn to a largely unused slurry, and if you're lucky you won't put half the dishes away before you realize that they aren't clean and have bits of detergent clinging to them.

Your next engineering surprise is the absolutely and completely horrid silverware holder.  You can put it on the door where your silverware won't get clean, or you can try to hang it on the end of the bottom rack.  Where it will take 5-6 tries to get it to drop into the slots and not just fall off.  Which gives you the second special effect of popping open, dumping all the silverware into the bottom of the dishwasher.  You see, it has a handy little lever that allows the rack to completely open, and it takes next to nothing to make that pop open.  Really.  It'll pop open while you're dropping spoons in it.  I ended up having to drive a screw into it after the 300th time I took it out to put the silverware away and it popped open and dumped my sort-of clean stuff onto the kitchen floor.

I'd go on, but I think you get the idea.  I've had 1970's dishwashers that cleaned better, used less energy and water because I didn't have to prewash, run loads twice when the detergent door didn't open because a spoon or a tall bowl blocked it, and I don't have to half empty it and then reload it and run it again because half the dishes have bits of food stuck to them.  Run away.  Don't buy this product.  If you buy a house that has this dishwasher in it, surrender hope.

Its rare that I wish daily that a major appliance would explode so I could spend $500 and replace it.  Sadly, I can't make this one catch on fire.
top_5.summary: I hate this dishwasher

top_5.reviewText:
This is a nice bag of random crispy critter parts.  Most of them are potato chip poofy texture and disappear pretty fast.  There were a few of what looked like pork hide rolls that took them a few minutes to work through and some hoof-like items, and what looked like some pig ears with a portion of the rest of the pig attached.  Those were highly prized.  Most of the two bags I got looked to be dried lung...the brown stuff with the crosshatch pattern.  Not a whole lot of crunchy chewy items that would take a while to eat, so I was a bit disappointed.  Mine didn't look much like the ones in the other review photos, so it seems to be a bit of a crap shoot as to what you'll get.

Both dogs (Sammy Destroyer of Toys and Ben Who Must Have His Harness Removed First) like everything in the bag.  Nothing is tiny or seems odd or deformed despite the description that says its odds and ends that didn't meet their standards.  The price is very good for what I got but I down rated it due to the repetition and not getting some of the yummier looking, longer lasting stuff that others showed in their bags.

Still worth what I paid, I might try a few more bags in a few months and see if I do any better.  See attached picture for a sample of what I received.  The two items in the top row in the middle were rarities.  Most of the bag was the brown crosshatched stuff and the poofy 'tail' pieces on the right.

Edit: I did get about 4 more bags over a few months period.  Curiously they all contained roughly the same exact items.  So either Amazon has a huge stock of the same shipment with the same items or Merrick standardized the contents.
top_5.summary: This value pack is like a box of chocolates.  You never know what you're going to get.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "Male nurse Greg Focker (Ben Stiller) is poised to propose to his girlfriend Pam (Teri Polo) during a weekend stay at her parents' home. But here's the catch... he needs to ask her father first. Alas, the fur flies as Jack Byrnes, Pam's cat-crazy, ex-CIA father, played hysterically by Academy Award winner Robert De Niro, takes an immediate dislike to her less-than-truthful beau. Greg's quest for approval gets seriously sidetracked as Murphy's Law takes over an d a hilarious string of mishaps turns him into a master of disaster and total pariah in the eyes of the entire family... all except his shell-shocked girlfriend, who can't believe she still loves her one-man wrecking crew. Meet the Parents, from the director of Austin Powers, is an uproarious blockbuster hit that bombards you with one laugh after another, as true love tries to conquer all, against all odds.". The summary of the review text is "Still good for a laugh".
output:
Anyone who's felt the stress of meeting the future in-laws for the first time can relate to this movie.  Though it's been out for a long time now it's still a fun movie.

Ben Stiller gives a super performance, as expected, and Deniro is outstanding as the now retired and ever stiff and humorless CIA officer who refuses to leave the clandestine life behind.  The interaction and play between the two is hilarious.  The series of unfortunate events that befall Stiller's character as he meets the in-laws is never ending.  If there's a weakness to the movie, it may be that those never ending events get a little over-the-top sometimes, but the hilarity of it all far overshadows that minor point.

If you're looking for a fun and lighthearted comedy one evening, I recommend this one.

When starting this book I'd have never thought Scrooge would come up with a quotable line, but through the power of Dickens and the three Spirits, even Scrooge was a changed man!

Of course just about anybody who celebrates Christmas and has paid attention to the world around them as they've grown up is familiar with the story of Ebenezer Scrooge as written by the genius Dickens.  And most of us have been exposed to at least a few different versions of some animated or Hollywood version of the story.  But anyone interested in a simple and short read at Christmas time would do well to treat themselves to the Dickens classic in its original written form.  You'll likely not be disappointed as long as you're willing to understand that it's Dickens and it's written in his classic Victorian style, i.e., not a simplified Hollywood script.  This was great fun to read and there are some very good points presented by the three Spirits that just about any of us - not just Scrooge - might be able to infuse into our lives at the Christmas time of year.
profile.summary: "Men's courses will foreshadow certain ends, to which, if persevered in, they must lead" - Scrooge

When I had to read this book in my adolescent years, it was literary torture.  Today, reading with 25 more years of life behind me and greater appreciation for literary art, it's a great story.  I never would have picked this story back up had it not been for the review/referral from a friend.  In retrospect, I'm not really certain this story is best read, comprehended and appreciated by an adolescent.  The story, and the seedy sides of life exposed, might be better processed by an adult.

In addition to the story woven by Dickens, I think what I appreciated most about this writing was how Dickens used the novel as a commentary on life in England at the time of the writing, e.g., society's treatment of the paupers and impoverished, the caste system that existed and condemned a pauper child to destitution at birth, and the judicial system with its corruption and brutality, to name a few.  Even as a mature adult reader I winced at how Oliver and the young paupers were brutally treated by "the system" in the first half of the book.

I loved how in the end all the characters, excepting Nancy, received their just rewards and ends in accordance with how they had lived life.  The only mild criticism I have was the almost too remarkable coincidence of the relationships of Oliver, Brownlow, Rose and Monks, and how life had brought them together prior even to the discovery of the existence of their relationships and ties from the prior generation.  Nevertheless, it's a feel-good ending and the story kept me turning the pages with anticipation.
profile.summary: Now it's worth a read

profile.reviewText:
I've only listened to this album for a few days now, but it didn't take long to realize how good it is.  The music is good, the vocals are good, but where Gaines stands out is in his songwriting and lyrics.  He is a master lyricist!  As a person who pays particular attention to the lyrics of a song - how well the words capture life's emotions, feelings, events - I really appreciate this album and Gaines' obvious capabilities.

So, while I'd heard of Gaines before, and I understand he has contributed lyrics to some fine artists in the music world, I am very glad I took the time to heed a dear friends advice and give this album a listen.  Many thanks...

profile.description: Unusual book
profile.reviewText:
I'm not prone to spending my spare moments of free time reading about the radicalization of Islam from the 1930's and how that lead to the destruction of thousands of people on 9/11. From an intellectual stand point I think it's very important to understand the processes and belief systems that make up a certain part of the world's population, and to get a grasp of how those beliefs affect me and my family in my western world today. But I don't generally look for some level of "entertainment" in that learning process.

I undertook this reading on a referral from a friend and has hugely gratified with the outcome. The book is a fascinating narrative, incredibly well researched and written for "the average man on the street," so to speak. It's full of fact but reads like a novel as opposed to some kind of dry history lesson. It seems that Wright has access to sources, both primary and secondary, that give this book great credibility. Being myself somewhat familiar with Islam, the radicalization thereof, how some of those more extreme in their beliefs tend to think, and the Arab culture in general, I understand how such cultural and religious differences can be quite confusing to many in the "West", i.e. the US and Western Europe. So I was very impressed with how well Wright was able to make the nuances of Islam and the Arab cultures accessible and understandable to the reader. For example, reading through material that is heavy with middle eastern names can quickly become very tedious and confusing at best, given that "we" have little experience navigating the naming conventions utilized by the culture; the non-Arab reader cannot relate to the names, thereby causing the reader to lose interest. But Wright was able to introduce many different characters as he followed the history of one of the fathers of radical Islam in the 1930s to the final moments of the execution of the 9/11 plot, and he did so without confusing the reader with excessive and tedious cultural nuances, etc. That is but one example, but Wright's command and understanding of the subject matter have made it possible for him to bring this material on the whole to the reader who is otherwise inexperienced in such material.

People should read this book if they are someone who: is concerned about the world in which we now live; desires an understanding of what the struggles are that western nations now face against a radical element threatening a way of life; maybe seeks an answer to the question of "Why do they hate me and my family and my country? And why do they want to kill us?", or; just wants to read a fascinating narrative on modern history. This is not a book for just Americans, but for anyone from any country that faces similar threats from Al-Qaeda, whether it be in New York, London, Madrid, or anywhere else.

I could go on about the strengths of this book and its important historical perspectives, but I won't. Just go read it.
profile.summary: How we got to where we are

profile.reviewText: The story is not particularly anything to write home about, though it is fun and light hearted.  But what really makes this movie worthy of the time to watch it was Ricky Gervais and his great Brit sense of humor juxtaposed against the New York City setting.  And I must say, NYC looked beautiful as parts of the movie were shot against the autumn colors of Central Park.  But Gervais was, I thought, the key to success in the movie.  He was brilliant as his character developed from a dull, antisocial and disagreeable British dentist displaced in NYC and bent on avoiding contact with about everyone around him, to a wonderfully funny and love-sick single man who realized a life of service with an ingredient of love will get him much further than his lonely existence.  Tea Leoni was also super and very beautiful as his targeted love interest.  While the movie is a comedy, the more romantic elements of the film certainly provided a bit more depth to the story and Gervais and Leoni played it beautifully together.  Definitely a movie worth the time.
profile.summary: Gervais and Leoni are great in this fun film

profile.description: The Millenium Triology on blu-ray discs.
profile.reviewText: Much - if not most - of the extraneous subplots found in the books were removed from the movie adaptation.  Despite that, each of the movies captured the essence of and was true to the main storyline.  Consequently, this was an extremely well done book-to-movie adaptation.  It also seemed that each of the characters were well acted; however, given that I don't speak Swedish, it's difficult to make such an assessment because the language barrier doesn't allow for a true assessment of the authenticism each actor gives to the respective character through the delivery of the diaologue.  Though each of the movies has omitted much of the story found in the books, they are all over two hours long.  Nevertheless, the time travels quickly because the movies do draw-in viewer.  Overall, the Swedes have done a fine job in the silver screen adaptation.
profile.summary: Well done in capturing the essence of the books

profile.description: Told with deadpan humour and bitter irony, Kurt Vonnegut's cult tale of global destruction preys on our deepest fears of witnessing Armageddon and, worse still, surviving it ...Dr Felix Hoenikker, one of the founding 'fathers' of the atomic bomb, has left a deadly legacy to the world. For he is the inventor of 'ice-nine', a lethal chemical capable of freezing the entire planet. The search for its whereabouts leads to Hoenikker's three ecentric children, to a crazed dictator in the Caribbean, to madness. Felix Hoenikker's Death Wish comes true when his last, fatal gift to mankind brings about the end, that for all of us, is nigh.
profile.reviewText:
Sometimes one of the elements of the spice of life is to break out of one's box and try new things.  Thus, in terms of literature, I decided to try a little bit of Kurt Vonnegut just to "mix it up" a little bit.  While I certainly had heard of him for many years, I had never read any of his works.  I recently read about his real-life experience of being an American soldier at the Battle of the Bulge in Belgium during WWII, where he was captured and taken prisoner of war.  I then researched more about him and read he considered 'Cat's Cradle' to be one of his best books.  Intrigued by the story line, I chose this as my first foray into Vonnegut's world.

The book is an easy read.  The Kindle version I had was 287 pages and chapters are but a few pages at the most.  The story flows and, if one's interest is maintained through the story, the book is read quickly.  However, even as the story captured my interest at the beginning, by midway through the book it was becoming quite odd and I had difficulty staying committed to finishing it.  Granted, I'm admittedly a Vonnegut novice but I am aware he's a satirist who's not afraid to voice his opinions and disagreements with many social and political issues from his time period.  In terms of my perception of Cat's Cradle, I think - but am not entirely certain - the oddities of the story, it's characters, the backdrop of the story on a fictional island nation, the influences of a fictional religion made up by an old man considered an "enemy of the state" (in a tongue-in-cheek sort of way), and a few other subplots, all seemed to have passed me by and I failed to understand the significance of what Vonnegut was trying to get across to me.  Perhaps one must be more studied in his style, his life, him as a person, and the social climate and issues of his times to ultimately understand the morals of his stories.  Would I read Vonnegut again?  Yes, but I'm in no hurry.
profile.summary: It's just kind of odd.

profile.description: "Rock of Ages" tells the story of small town girl Sherrie and city boy Drew, who meet on the Sunset Strip while pursuing their Hollywood dreams. Their rock 'n' roll romance is told through the heart-pounding hits of Def Leppard, Joan Jett, Journey, Foreigner, Bon Jovi, Night Ranger, REO Speedwagon, Pat Benatar, Twisted Sister, Poison, Whitesnake, and more.
profile.reviewText:
I notice this movie has garnered a broad variety of opinions and star ratings that run the gamut.

But seriously people, let's not take this movie too seriously.  If the viewer is searching for an intellectual or spiritual experience, a movie that inspires instrospection, or a movie that will stand the test of time, Rock of Ages is probably not what you're looking for (unless you're a child of the 80s and are still quoting lines from Fast Times at Ridgemont High and Porky's).  However, it the viewer understands this movie doesn't offer elements of intellect, thereby having a more realistic expectation of the movie, then this is a downright fun flick to watch.  And if the viewer is a child of the 80s who grew up listening to the cassette tapes of some of the era's greatest Glam Rock Hair Bands, then this movie is nothing less than a grand trip down Memory Lane, singing along with great oldies (No Way!!  Oldies??  Say it isn't so!) from groups like Def Leppard, Journey, Foreigner, Joan Jett, Pat Benatar, REO Speedwagon, Guns 'N Roses, The Scorpions, and so much more.  And in addition to the music, the directors have mixed in some type of simple love story played out by characters with combined IQs of maybe a 100 - but that's okay, cuz this movie wasn't made for the story (or the intellectual viewer) - it's all about the MUSIC.

So be realistic about this movie and simply enjoy it for what it is - a 2 hour retreat from the world to the nostalgia of a great music era gone by.  Do that and you just might find yourself being simply entertained as you sing along to some great tunes that helped define the era.  Expect more than that, and you'll probably be disappointed.

P.S. Some of the lip syncing is pretty bad too, but just go with it!

P.S.S. Having said all that, in the interest of fairness across the generations I am obligated to report that my teens say this music makes their ears bleed...but what would they know, they're just teens - though they do seem to have all the answers to life's mysterious questions, or so they tell me, their stupid old man.  But I'm grateful they allow me to soak up their wisdom...really.
profile.summary: Seriously, let's not be too serious here...

profile.description: Following in the footsteps of his father and uncle before him, Albert Pierrepoint (Timothy Spall) joins the 'family business'. He becomes the most feared and respected executioner in Britain, hanging over 450 people before his sudden resignation in 1956. Living a double life as a master craftsman hangman, and as a grocery deliveryman and loyal husband, Pierrepoint's obsession with becoming the 'Number One' executioner in the country results in a fate he could not have chosen.
profile.reviewText:
A British film about the story of Albert Pierrepoint, the "last hangman" of Britain before the death penalty was abolished in the UK.  I came across this one and decided to watch simply because it captured my curiosity.  I thought it might be interesting to see the perspective of an individual working in the hidden profession of government executioner.

I thought the movie was very well done and the acting superb, which, I think, made the rest of the film work.  The theme and content certainly gave me pause to stop and think about the issues presented to those who have been/were/are called upon by their governments to carry out the sentences of execution - the impact on the individual and their family and their society.  Are they presented with a moral dilemma?  How do they reconcile the act of execution, particularly when it is voluntary?  Does is preoccupy or disrupt the other aspects of their lives?  How do they keep it secret, and if they don't, then what?

Because of the thematic content of the story this is not really a movie one watches simply to be entertained.  Certainly the theme deserves more thought, attention and open-mindedness from the viewer.  Despite the movie's theme and whether the viewer is pro- or anti- death penalty, the story of Albert Pierrepoint is worth watching and knowing, if for nothing else than to understand the position not of the condemned but of he who is in the position of carrying out the condemnation.
profile.summary: Really kind of fascinating

profile.description: The first holiday album from super-star Faith Hill, 'Joy To The World' is a joy to behold, featuring beautiful new versions of ten traditional and modern classics, complete with horns, strings, woodwings, percussion and chorales, much like the big-band orchestras of the 40's and 50's. One of the most popular music stars in America, Faith Hill celebrates the joy-and faith- of the season with 'Joy to the World.'
profile.reviewText: Every year I buy one new Christmas album for the season.  This year I bought Faith Hill's Joy To The World.  When it comes to Christmas music I'm pretty much a traditionalist, preferring the Christmas classics presented in their traditional renditions and arrangements.  I don't want to hear Silent Night in a Blues rendition or The Little Drummer Boy with a country twang.  Faith Hill, though she's a country music star, really did a nice job of staying traditional in this album.  The arrangements are traditional and she's not infused them with elements that might be more indicative of the country genre.  In some of them she's used the backing of choirs and the accompaniment of orchestras and symphonies.  In another song she performs a beautiful a capella arrangement of the Little Drummer Boy accompanied by only background vocals.  So I'm overall very pleased with this year's Christmas album purchase and look forward to enjoying it for years to come.
profile.summary: Good, traditional style Christmas classics

top_5.summary: "Men's courses will foreshadow certain ends, to which, if persevered in, they must lead" - Scrooge

top_5.description:
LIKE NEW, LIMITED EDITION FRANKLIN LIBRARY LEATHER BOUND, 22 CARAT GILDED PAGES. In like new, unread condition, not price clipped, not library edition, not remainder marked.
Seller is a lifelong book collector and each edition comes directly from his 35,000+ volume collection! All orders are shipped every business day using USPS Media Mail for all U S. orders. Orders shipped from Grover Beach, California. 93433-1585, Thank You, for your business!!
top_5.reviewText:
When I had to read this book in my adolescent years, it was literary torture.  Today, reading with 25 more years of life behind me and greater appreciation for literary art, it's a great story.  I never would have picked this story back up had it not been for the review/referral from a friend.  In retrospect, I'm not really certain this story is best read, comprehended and appreciated by an adolescent.  The story, and the seedy sides of life exposed, might be better processed by an adult.

In addition to the story woven by Dickens, I think what I appreciated most about this writing was how Dickens used the novel as a commentary on life in England at the time of the writing, e.g., society's treatment of the paupers and impoverished, the caste system that existed and condemned a pauper child to destitution at birth, and the judicial system with its corruption and brutality, to name a few.  Even as a mature adult reader I winced at how Oliver and the young paupers were brutally treated by "the system" in the first half of the book.

I loved how in the end all the characters, excepting Nancy, received their just rewards and ends in accordance with how they had lived life.  The only mild criticism I have was the almost too remarkable coincidence of the relationships of Oliver, Brownlow, Rose and Monks, and how life had brought them together prior even to the discovery of the existence of their relationships and ties from the prior generation.  Nevertheless, it's a feel-good ending and the story kept me turning the pages with anticipation.
top_5.summary: Now it's worth a read

top_5.description: Jeffrey Gaines ~ Jeffrey Gaines
top_5.reviewText:
I've only listened to this album for a few days now, but it didn't take long to realize how good it is.  The music is good, the vocals are good, but where Gaines stands out is in his songwriting and lyrics.  He is a master lyricist!  As a person who pays particular attention to the lyrics of a song - how well the words capture life's emotions, feelings, events - I really appreciate this album and Gaines' obvious capabilities.

I really believe the stories his songs tell are universal.  Just about anyone anywhere could relate in some way to what he has to say, whether about love (in love or broken love), society and social issues, or self.

So, while I'd heard of Gaines before, and I understand he has contributed lyrics to some fine artists in the music world, I am very glad I took the time to heed a dear friends advice and give this album a listen.  Many thanks...

"...Your smiling face in a photograph, Remember how I made you laugh..."
top_5.summary: "I was dreaming of the last time we lie together, Seems whenever I need you you're across the sea..."

top_5.description: Unusual book
top_5.reviewText:
I'm not prone to spending my spare moments of free time reading about the radicalization of Islam from the 1930's and how that lead to the destruction of thousands of people on 9/11. From an intellectual stand point I think it's very important to understand the processes and belief systems that make up a certain part of the world's population, and to get a grasp of how those beliefs affect me and my family in my western world today. But I don't generally look for some level of "entertainment" in that learning process.

I undertook this reading on a referral from a friend and has hugely gratified with the outcome. The book is a fascinating narrative, incredibly well researched and written for "the average man on the street," so to speak. It's full of fact but reads like a novel as opposed to some kind of dry history lesson. It seems that Wright has access to sources, both primary and secondary, that give this book great credibility. Being myself somewhat familiar with Islam, the radicalization thereof, how some of those more extreme in their beliefs tend to think, and the Arab culture in general, I understand how such cultural and religious differences can be quite confusing to many in the "West", i.e. the US and Western Europe. So I was very impressed with how well Wright was able to make the nuances of Islam and the Arab cultures accessible and understandable to the reader. For example, reading through material that is heavy with middle eastern names can quickly become very tedious and confusing at best, given that "we" have little experience navigating the naming conventions utilized by the culture; the non-Arab reader cannot relate to the names, thereby causing the reader to lose interest. But Wright was able to introduce many different characters as he followed the history of one of the fathers of radical Islam in the 1930s to the final moments of the execution of the 9/11 plot, and he did so without confusing the reader with excessive and tedious cultural nuances, etc. That is but one example, but Wright's command and understanding of the subject matter have made it possible for him to bring this material on the whole to the reader who is otherwise inexperienced in such material.

People should read this book if they are someone who: is concerned about the world in which we now live; desires an understanding of what the struggles are that western nations now face against a radical element threatening a way of life; maybe seeks an answer to the question of "Why do they hate me and my family and my country? And why do they want to kill us?", or; just wants to read a fascinating narrative on modern history. This is not a book for just Americans, but for anyone from any country that faces similar threats from Al-Qaeda, whether it be in New York, London, Madrid, or anywhere else.

I could go on about the strengths of this book and its important historical perspectives, but I won't. Just go read it.
top_5.summary: How we got to where we are

top_5.description: NOTICE: Polish Release, cover may contain Polish text/markings. The disk has English audio and subtitles.
top_5.reviewText: The story is not particularly anything to write home about, though it is fun and light hearted.  But what really makes this movie worthy of the time to watch it was Ricky Gervais and his great Brit sense of humor juxtaposed against the New York City setting.  And I must say, NYC looked beautiful as parts of the movie were shot against the autumn colors of Central Park.  But Gervais was, I thought, the key to success in the movie.  He was brilliant as his character developed from a dull, antisocial and disagreeable British dentist displaced in NYC and bent on avoiding contact with about everyone around him, to a wonderfully funny and love-sick single man who realized a life of service with an ingredient of love will get him much further than his lonely existence.  Tea Leoni was also super and very beautiful as his targeted love interest.  While the movie is a comedy, the more romantic elements of the film certainly provided a bit more depth to the story and Gervais and Leoni played it beautifully together.  Definitely a movie worth the time.
top_5.summary: Gervais and Leoni are great in this fun film

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "America’s Test Kitchen is well-known for its top-rated television shows with more than 4 million weekly public television viewers, bestselling cookbooks, magazines, websites, and cooking school. The highly reputable and recognizable brands of America’s Test Kitchen, Cook’s Illustrated, and Cook’s Country are the work of over 60 passionate chefs based in Boston, Massachusetts, who put ingredients, cookware, equipment, and recipes through objective, rigorous testing to identify the very best. Discover, learn, and expand your cooking repertoire with Julia Collin Davison, Bridget Lancaster, Jack Bishop, Dan Souza, Lisa McManus, Tucker Shaw, Bryan Roof, and our fabulous team of test cooks!". The summary of the review text is "The folks at ATK don't disappoint!".
output:
I'm a fan of their PBS show but I tried to be unbiased on the book review. Is it a fine cuisine book? I would not think so. Does it have delicious home cooked meal recipes? I think so.
