Their recipes are well explained with mouth-watering pictures. The book is organized in several chapters that should appeal to different types of make-ahead cooks. There are recipes that will be ready to eat once you get home the next day (either waiting in the slow cooker or ready to quickly warm up/cook), to grand(er) Sunday recipes that will provide for some leftover-inspired recipes. I also liked the 3 dinner recipes that share many of the ingredients to speed up grocery shopping.

Each recipe starts with a "why this recipe works" section explaining the experimenting (if any) that went into the recipe as well as reasons for ingredient selection/prep. This is followed by ingredients and prep/store/serve instructions and an occasional useful tip. These tips as well as the introductory section of the book make it a fairly self-contained book that would do well to get a new cook started.

profile.description: Letter Factory Adventures: The Rainforest teaches and reinforces life science concepts for children ages 4-7 years old. Through action-packed gameplay, children develop their knowledge of life science, animals and ecosystems. Letter Factory Adventures: The Rainforest also helps little explorers build fundamental scientific inquiry and critical thinking skills as they learn about the exotic animals and plants that call the four layers of the rainforest their home. Children join Leap, Tad and Lily on a colorful journey through the rainforest, where they encounter diverse ecosystems and an array of amazing life forms. Using their styluses, children move Tad's magnifying glass or Lily's light for a closer look at the many unique plants and animals. There's no shortage of fun in the abundant Amazon! Players climb up vines, bounce off mushrooms and trek through the canopy in pursuit of fascinating creatures to feature in Leap's journal. Letter Factory Adventures: The Rainforest contains more than 200 fascinating facts! Young adventurers will meet the world's loudest monkey, the largest freshwater turtle and a bird that mimics human speech. They'll discover that coffee, chocolate and bananas all grow in the rainforest and explore plants used in important medicines and chewing gum! After completing in-game missions assigned by The Chief, kids may find themselves still in observation mode and thinking like a scientist in the real world! "This learning game gives children opportunities to explore flora and fauna in a unique ecosystem. Children build classification skills by learning about animal characteristics and plant life cycles, which can help them learn to think like scientists."-Elizabeth B., LeapFrog Learning Expert Works with all LeapPad learning tablets and Leapster Explorer and LeapsterGS game systems (sold separately). Internet connection may be required for cartridge.
profile.reviewText:
It's a fun, informative game for the little ones. At the base is a platform-type game with ladder (i.e vines) to climb, "enemies" to jump on top to get rid of, and with the addition of small interruptions in game play when a creature of interest is found. That's where the informative, learning part comes in.

The rainforest is explored in stages from the ground up all the way to the canopy. At each level various animals, insects, and plants are encountered and kids have the opportunity to learn different facts (as well as answer some questions) about them. In addition, as points are gained during the game, one can "buy" extra fun facts about the creatures encountered.

The game play is reasonably hard for the age group it targets so it should be neither easy nor frustrating.
profile.summary: Learning while having some fun

profile.description: Restyled for 2014, the Weber Q 140 is now the Weber Q 1400. The grill has the same great performance and sleek styling, but adds new aesthetics that are both functional and fun, including larger grip handle and control knobs, ergonomic side handles, sturdy front and rear cradles plus the familiar Weber Q logo branded in the lid. The Weber Q 1400 Electric grill raises the bar on flavor expectations and performance of an electric grill. Sear burgers, steaks and chops; grill chicken, fish, vegetables and fruit on the porcelain-enameled cast-iron grates. Youll be amazed at the authentic grilled taste of foods cooked on this electric grill. The Weber Q 1400 grill is fully featured, yet space-saving and portable  just the ticket for grillers living in condos or any residence where restrictions govern gas and charcoal grill usage. May be used with Weber Portable Cart model #6557. Weber Q 1400 is for outdoor use only.
profile.reviewText:
The grill was quick to assemble. It has few parts and the materials seem to be of good quality (which should bode well for durability).

Size-wise it's good for grilling something for a family meal or maybe at a campsite but don't expect to entertain many guests with it (unless you have plenty of beers for the down time). I've only grilled burgers so far on it and it can accommodate well 4 Costco burger patties. You could squeeze in a couple more but then the cooking probably won't be as even.

I like that the grille does not have any opening right above the burner thus preventing grease and other debris from falling onto the latter and clogging it.

I wish that it came with a built in thermometer but I think that using the grilling guide that was included can be a reasonable substitute.

Lastly even fully assembled it fits in its original box so it makes it easy to store away when not in use.
profile.summary: A neat little grill

profile.description: ZAGG Rugged Folio Case, Durable, Hinged with Detachable Backlit Keyboard for iPad Mini & Mini Retina - Black OPEN BOX
profile.reviewText:
It's very nice and functional! It's almost as having a mini laptop.

I got this for my father-in-law and he loves it. His main complaint about the iPad was the onscreen keyboard being not as nice to use as a real keyboard (and I agree with him). This has solved his problem and also added some much needed safety to his iPad as the grandkids are bound to drop it.

The keyboard does need a bit of getting used to as it's not full size but it's not too bad. It has a good typing feel to the fingers. Once the shell is closed both iPad and keyboard are very well protected. Setting up the Bluetooth connection was a cinch and it seems to work reliably.
profile.summary: I wish they made this for the Kindle Fire!

profile.description: The Lenovo MIIX 310 is a 2-in-1 detachable Windows tablet designed for on-the-go webaholics who need data all-day, every day. Featuring an optional Full HD IPS display and detachable keyboard, it gives you the flexibility to be productive anytime, anywhere.
profile.reviewText:
I really wanted to like the Miix310. I liked that it had 64GB built-in storage when most low-end notebooks usually just have 32GB. With Windows being a disk space hog 32GB is hardly enough it you want to install a few apps. Yes, you can attach an SD card but some programs refuse to install there and when they do they are much slower because of the SD card performance.

I was hoping that it would be a bit smoother in operation than my HP Stream 13 mainly due to 4 CPU cores vs 2 cores but it's a wash. Neither are the GPU or the SSD significantly faster. So at least from a price point the $200 HP is better. Also I had forgotten the keyboard trade-offs when using a 10" keyboard: PgUp/Dn are located awkwardly and the function keys F1-F12 are only accessible by pressing the Fn key.

The magnetic hinge connecting the tablet and the keyboard works quite well but snaps in with quite some force so watch out for your fingers. Also if using it on your lap while wearing shorts watch out for the hinge pinching your leg skin/hair when opening it up.

Pros:
- battery life : more than 8 hours easily
- 64GB SSD storage : lots of room left after Windows and its updates
- nice sharp screen : I'm not a fan of matte screens
- good keyboard and touchpad : not excellent but no complaints either
- full size USB ports on the keyboard : allows you to connect USB drives, mice

Cons:
- sharp edges on both the tablet and keyboard parts make it not comfortable to hold
- a bit top heavy : for most laptops/notebooks the part holding the keyboard is heavier than the one holding the screen. Here things are reversed so it makes holding and walking around with it a bit more difficult
- power plug hard to insert, harder to remove
- power cord rather short : it's only 5 feet long
- overall quality impression marred : a screen issue and some impurities on the outer shell paint are not inspiring
- need specialized tool (provided) to open SD card slot : or at least must find a similar thin hard metal rod
- battery slow to charge : Win10 estimates 3 1/2 hours from a fully discharged state, after 2 hours it was at 68%

Finally the one that I got has 15 or so bubbles under the top level screen layer. I called Lenovo and will have to send it in. Stay tuned.

UPDATE: more than a month after sending it in for repair it's still "in-progress" due to missing parts. Also no communication from the repair department with updates, you need to check on it yourself. Downgrading rating to 2 stars.

UPDATE2: it's been 2 months new and I still don't have the unit back. 0 stars would be in order but I can only give it a minimum of one.

UPDARE3: finally Lenovo sent me a new unit after just having too many things to fix on the original one and taking way too long. However, it has the exact same issue with the screen: dust trapped under the top layer protecting the screen.
profile.summary: Works in a pinch, horrible support

profile.description: The highly anticipated family comedy The Smurfs 2 is now a video game! The evil wizard Gargamel has created the Naughties, who kidnap Smurfette from Smurfs Village and imprison her in Paris. It's now up to the Smurfs to travel from the Enchanted Forest, through the busy streets of New York, into Paris, and everywhere in between to save the day and bring Smurfette home safe!
profile.reviewText:
Having watched the kids play the game for a while and having played a level or two myself I can say that the game is quite fun. Don't expect any earth-shattering gameplay but if you like the type of game you'll definitely get quite a few hours of play out of it. The levels are engaging with quite a bit of imagination in the enemies and structures encountered. The backdrops are also well designed and improve the look and feel of the game. The controls are simple and intuitive so you'll be up and playing in no time. You can select different smurfs and use their different abilities to your advantage.

One complaint I had (but not the kids) is that perhaps the characters/elements in the game are a bit on the small side which makes it a bit difficult to follow what's going on at times.
profile.summary: Good ol' "platform" game

profile.description: Boston Acoustics MC100 Blue is a wireless Bluetooth music system for your home or office. Simply stream your favorite music wirelessly from your smartphone, tablet or other Bluetooth-enabled device - without the need for a network connection. Boston engineered and designed, the MC100Blue will fill your room with great sound, and thanks to its modern, minimalist design it will blend easily into your surroundings. The MC100 Blue also features aptX which allows for CD-quality sound when streaming from a Bluetooth device that also includes aptX. In addition, NFC (Near Field Communication) allows for simple, tap-to-pair connectivity from mobile devices that are NFC equipped. You can literally place your NFC-enabled device near the top of the MC100 Blue and it will initiate pairing. Many of the latest mobile phones and tablets include NFC functionality built-in. There is even an auxiliary input for connecting devices that do not have Bluetooth capability.
profile.reviewText:
I got this for playing some music in the bedroom at night. I have it sitting on the nightstand for now as I could not figure out a good way of turning it on/off if places behind the bed's headboard even with the remote. The design is sleek and subdued enough that I can be on the nightstand without attracting too much attention.

The speakers manage to put out a decent sound (quality- and quantity-wise) with sufficient bass. While trying it behind the bed headboard I could see that bass was dramatically improved in that position.

The sound quality over Bluetooth is the best of the 4 Bluetooth speaker and speaker adapter that I have used. It has a longer range than my Belkin Bluetooth speaker adapter. I could be in the house and about 25ft away and I still get a good connection even with intervening walls.

I have not tried NFC as none of my phones have it but it sounds as if connecting would be even easier.
profile.summary: Great sound, great range

profile.description: Lift and Go gives you powerful pick-up for every corner of your home. Cover couches to stairs to floors with the Lift and Go Carry Canister Mode and On-Demand Cleaning Wand.
profile.reviewText:
The vacuum handles and cleans well. In canister mode, I think that the reduction in bulk is more significant than the reduction in weight, since the vacuum is already pretty light. I also like that the handle converts into a wand that can be used to reach tight or high spaces and there's one less accessory to stow.

I would also like it if it had a self-retractable cord but I guess that would have increased the bulk in the "canister" mode. Or at least add a notch that would hold the cord to a certain length when the full cord need not be unwound.

I briefly tried the swipes feature on the tiles in the kitchen. While it works I probably won't use it very often since I find the pre-moistened wipes (the Swiffer Sweeper kind) easier to use for my small space. However, for cases where more hair and such winds up on tiles or hardwood floors I think this would work quite well.
profile.summary: Lightweight, fairly quiet, good suction

profile.description: Microsoft Designer Bluetooth Mouse
profile.reviewText:
This is one sleek mouse. Some might find the low profile less ergonomic but I think it works just fine. Then again I use the keyboard much more than the mouse.

Much like any other Bluetooth mouse it was a breeze to setup and get going. It seems to connect faster than the Microsoft Sculpt mouse and to keep a steadier connection. The battery compartment has a magnetic latch that just needs a gentle push to pop open but fits securely when back in place. No need to fumble with the tip of the nails or a coin to open the compartment.

Perhaps the only point that I'm less than satisfied with is the wheel. It seems a bit stiff to rotate and press and it has an abruptly rising profile. This means that I can't just glide the finger from the left button to the wheel but I have to raise the finger just a bit to bring it to the wheel's height. A rounder, wider side profile would have made this easier but perhaps look less minimalistic and modern.
profile.summary: Sleek, functional, middle buttom might be the only weak point

profile.description: Tommy Hilfiger jeans for men featuring a skinny fit and five pocket styling. These skinny jeans for men create an ultra-fitted look from waist to ankle. Mens skinny jeans with mid-rise waist. Button closure with fly zip. Flag logo at coin pocket. Inseam: 30/32/34/36; Leg opening: 13.75"; Front rise: 9.5"; Back rise: 14.5". Create a trendy look with these Tommy Hilfiger mens jeans. These skinny stretch jeans for men will keep you feeling comfortable and looking cool. By Tommy Hilfiger Denim Men.
profile.reviewText:
The jeans are stylish and made out of nice materials. I think that the color (dark blue with a very light purple tinge) is nice but that's subjective. The stitching is well done and should last a while.

I usually wear 32x32 jeans but for this pair I got the 32x30. This seemed to work well as the tighter trim does not need to reach as low as baggier ones.

Where I'm having a bit of trouble is the girth of the pant leg. I do have fairly muscular legs and, in my case, the pants are tight around the calves and also around the thighs but a bit less so there. As a result, on me, they don't look as loose as on the guy in the product picture. This means that while they're relatively OK for walking around they are not so comfy for sitting down. I'm also concerned at how they will be after the first wash. So perhaps skinny is a bit out of my range :)
profile.summary: Nice but a bit tight on the pant leg

profile.description: Q Marshal is our everyday digital display watch that connects seamlessly to your phone. Strapped in sleek silicone, the tech-savvy dial with touchscreen functionality includes the all-new Wear OS by Google's interactive dials (for info at a glance), user-friendly messaging, customizable watch faces and automatic activity tracking. Smartwatches built with Wear OS by Google are compatible with iPhone and Android phones. Wear OS by Google and other related marks are trademarks of Google LLC. Touchscreen smartwatches built with Wear OS by Google require a phone running Android OS 4.4+ (excluding Go edition) or iOS 9.3+. Supported features may vary between platforms.
profile.reviewText:
At first I did not think that I'd like or find this watch of much use other than to tell the time. However, I quickly realized that it made looking and dismissing notifications a cinch. No longer did I have to reach into my holster to see what's making that racket. It also allows me to control music and podcast players right from it's screen. I think of it as a "remote" for my phone and as such it adds quite a bit of ease of use.

I like that the styling of the watch is rather simple and not betraying its digital provenance.

Some small things that did not quite work as expected for me

1. The watch detects when you move your forearm as if you'd be looking at it's face. However there are times when that detection misfires and then accidentally touching the face of the clock results in a command being sent to say the music player (if it happened to be active) to, for example, skip to the next track. This doesn't happen too often but often enough to be noticeable.

2. I wish that the display would automatically turn off when the phone is put in do-not-disturb mode. I place the watch to charge on my nightstand and its light (even when dimmed) is strong enough to be bothersome. This means that I need to work through the menus to turn on "Theater Mode" so the screen is turned off.

Finally, a minor inconvenience, it does need to be recharged pretty much each day but the contactless charger does make things as simple as possible.
profile.summary: A stylish "remote" for your smartphone

profile.description: The GPS watch and activity monitor to track runs and daily activity. This lightweight GPS watch/activity monitor features highly-accurate GPS to track your runs while also measuring daily steps and calories burned, providing insight into all your activity.
profile.reviewText:
Given the health monitoring craze I thought I'd give this a try. I was always curious to see how much walking about I do day-to-day. The only mode that I used in was the have it track activity 24-7. I did not use the GPS feature nor the workout tracker. As such activity tracker will record how many steps you've taken since midnight (?) and report the corresponding amount of kcal used. I think that 1kcal is one of the better known calories but I'm not sure. I wish the watch would allow one to change these units. As far as accuracy of recording steps it's a mixed bag. Sometimes it seems to miss steps when walking just a few steps. Other time a ride in the car registers as steps.

In the mode that I have used it the battery seem to last about 5 days (a bit shorter than the advertized 7) but still a reasonable amount of time.

The watch comes with a cradle for charging but I really wish that instead it has a microUSB port. This way I could using my phone charger when on the road instead of having to carry yet on more charger.

Aesthetically the watch is quite alright. I wish however that all the button wording was not there. It spoils the presentation. After all one should be able to remember what four buttons do. One thing that was a bit of a surprise was the fact that the plastic hand band is not impervious to dirt. So don't go on gardening like I did if you like the green to stay clean.
profile.summary: Good device but with limitations

profile.description: 100% SAMSUNG SDI Li-polymer battery cells only, top quality 5,000mAh power bank with digital LED power level indicator, ultra high charging speed 2.4A Max, triple safety protection, for smartphones, tablet PCs, Digital Cameras, Gopro and more (Metallic Silver)
profile.reviewText: Having used it for a few weeks now I think that I like this portable battery. I own a Motorola Moto G and this battery is about the size of two MotoG's sandwiched together and just a bit heavier. It seems to provide enough power for about 3 1/2 full charges which seems to be a bit less than the advertised 10,000mAh but still plenty of power on the go. There's an LED charge indicator (from 0 to 100%) that's cleverly hidden behind the silvery top cover. There are two USB ports providing 1A and 2.4A at 5V so you can pick how fast/slow you want to charge things. A full charge of the battery takes about 3 hours with my Kindle Fire charger.
profile.summary: Sleek, plentiful backup power

profile.description: POOF Door N Floor Rebound Basketball is an indoor/outdoor mini basketball game that grows with your child. When assembled, the product measures 15.75in. L x 25in. W x 26in. H (40cm x 63.5cm x 66cm) and stands on the ground as your little one learns how to shoot baskets with the included 4in. (10cm) foam ball. Under the hoop, there's an angled nylon ball return, which sends the ball back in the direction it came from. As your child gets bigger, or masters the low net, you can hang the set from a door or fence. The ball return is attached to the hoop, so whether it's standing or hanging it will always send your ball back! The set includes backboard, foam ball, 2 door hooks, connectors, tubes, nylon ball return, rim, net and easy instructions. Adult assembly required. Recommended for children 5 years of age and older.
profile.reviewText:
I got this for my 5 year old that seems to be interested in basketball. He played with it a bit but complained that, when placed on the floor, it's too low and thus doesn't quite feel like basketball. So I said: "Let me hook it onto the door". However all our doors do not have enough clearance between the door frame and the actual door to allow the hook to be placed on the door frame and the door to then close properly.

Installation was pretty easy and the instructions were clear. Installing the panel on the frame was the toughest but if you like each side properly on the channels and push both left and right sides in sync the panel will slide in fairly easily.
profile.summary: Reasonably fun, will work on doors with reasonable clearance

profile.description: The MOTO G has the sharpest 4.5 HD display in its class, all-day battery, quad-core speed and the lastest version of Android! What youll notice first about Moto G is the sharp HD display. Its edge-to-edge display stretches to all four corners of the phone. Watch, read and browse on a big, brilliant display. Youll get a sharp picture and then some.
profile.reviewText:
I got the 16GB global GSM version direct from Motorola instead of Amazon as they were shipping faster but here it goes anyway. The phone feels well built, of quality materials and it handles well (can almost be use one-handed). I would have preferred the power button on top but it still better than having it on the left.

Pros

  - good quadcore processor handles tasks easily given the 1GB of RAM
  - not much fluff on top of Android4.3 and guaranteed update to 4.4
  - good looking screen with vibrant colors and great resolution/DPI
  - built-in FM radio (yes, I'm old-fashioned but it was a must for me)
  - camera is decent for a phone
  - LED is powerful enough and makes a good spot for using as flashlight
  - built in compass is fairly precise and does not jump around much

Cons

 - no SD card (this is more of a fault to me since I like to put loads of music on my phone and thus only 4 star rating. You get ~12GB free with the 16GB version)
 - no 4G (I get 8Mbits/second in San Jose, CA using 3G though which is sufficient to watch Neflix without a hitch)

Update to cons: the new LTE version of the MotoG fixes both these cons with the slight caveat that SD card capacity is limited to 32GB. I think 64GB should have been a minimum.

Edit1: despite what the description says in San Jose, CA using T-mobile prepaid I am not limited to 2G service. Actually 3G speeds are quite good as noted above. More than enough for me.

Edit2: reordered cons from my point of view

Edit3: as of 12/25/2013 firmware was updated to Android 4.4.2.

Edit4: as of 06/07/2014 firmware was updated to Android 4.4.3.
profile.summary: Great phone for the money

profile.description: Breathe new life into your bedroom decor with the Traditions by Waverly Antalya 6-Piece Comforter Collection. This beautiful ensemble features an updated damask pattern in warm jewel tones on a light tan ground. Comforter set includes one comforter, one tailored 5-box pleat coordinating bed skirt, two coordinating pillow shams and two decorative pillows. Queen set measures 88" x 88" with two 20" x 26" pillow shams and a 60" x 80" bed skirt with a 15" drop. King set measures 104" x 88" with two 20" x 36" pillow shams and a 78" x 80" bed skirt with a 15" drop. 16x16 pillow features light tan pleated face and solid light tan reverse, 12x16 pillow features a damask face and light tan reverse. Comforter, shams and bed skirt are machine washable. Wash in cold water on the gentle cycle and tumble dry on low for long lasting beauty. Pillows are spot clean only. 100% Polyester.
profile.reviewText:
A stylish set with a lovely pattern. The pillow covers are quite nice, the small accent pillow is nice but I'm not a fan of the striped one. Somehow it does not look as nice as the one in the picture. Perhaps it needs a little ironing. The feel of the comforter is a bit rough but I expect it to soften somewhat after a wash or two.

Two things to complain about
1. It is made of polyester. I like the feel of cotton and knowing that it is naturally grown.
2. The color of the set that I got are darker (at least to me) than what is shown in the picture. The darks are a tad darker and the creamy background is a tad yellower. Probably not a show stopper though.
profile.summary: Nice for a guest bedroom but a tad darker than pictured

profile.description: Lightweight design with superior performance. 9X multi-cyclonic, suction channel technology for increased suction & better cleaning. Dirt lifter power brush for a deep down clean. Swivel steering for easy maneuvering. On/off brush for scatter free hard floor cleaning. 27' power cord, multi-level filtration. Includes turbo eraser tool, crevice tool, telescopic extension wand & extra febreze filter. Lightweight design with superior performance 9X multi-cyclonic, suction channel technology for increased suction & better cleaning Dirt lifter power brush for a deep down clean Swivel steering for easy maneuvering On/off brush for scatter free hard floor cleaning 27' power cord, multi-level filtration Includes turbo eraser tool, crevice tool, telescopic extension wand & extra febreze filter.
profile.reviewText:
Overall the vacuum looks decent. It seems to clean well, the swivel mechanism works well in guiding the vacuum around. I would have preferred if the power cord was internally stored with a spring-loaded mechanism instead of the manual wound around version it has.

Finally I think that my particular vacuum has a defect: it makes a loud whining noise. It seems that the noise comes from where the canister attaches to the body. If I press the canister in with my hand then the noise goes away but I can't go around vacuuming that way. The noise level of the vacuum is quite higher than our current Panasonic one (and I'm not even including the whining noise in the comparison).

Update: I've contacted Bissell about the noise. Let's see how it goes.

Update: After some attempts at debugging the noise issue Bissell customer service replaced the unit. This new unit does not make the same noise and actually seems overall quieter than the first one. Kudos to Bissell for handling this well. As such I've upgraded the rating to 4 stars.
profile.summary: Makes loud whining noise (but see updates)

profile.description: The Zinus Modern Studio Collection is an ideal combination of function and style. The 4-Shelf Bookcase is an economical storage solution for books or decorative items. The sturdy, black square steel tubing and high density panel with rich brown wood grain finish will add an elegant touch to any decor. Easy to assemble. Worry free limited 1 year warranty.
profile.reviewText:
I already have the night stand from the same collection so I knew what to expect. It has clean, modern lines and the faux wood panels are a pleasant reddish-brown color with good texture. It is easily assembled (and comes with the needed Allen wrench) but be careful not to scratch the legs as it will show. Fully assembled the shelf is 38 inches which is pretty tall.

Two things that were less than satisfying:

1. I would have preferred if the legs were made out of one piece: the line where they come together is still visible (especially if you know it's there)

2. Some of the parts had a bit of rust damage. Luckily I was able to assemble those areas on the bottom shelf and facing back.
profile.summary: Easy to assemble, stylish in a modern way

profile.description: Our black colored 3 device universal remote is easy to set up and easy to use. This remote works with over 350 brands, and programming is a breeze. It can even control your digital converter box. It is perfect for today's DVR's and DVD players, it includes large keypads for easy navigation, and the partially backlit feature allows you to see the keys in the dark.
profile.reviewText:
I use this to control a TV, a DVD player, and a Roku. It works well with all of them but some of the key mappings are not obvious. For example it took some experimenting to find out that the "Back" key on the Roku is equivalent to the UP key on the remote. Also, there is no key (that I could find) for close captioning on the TV/DVD player. Perhaps one of the red/green/yellow/blue programmable buttons at the bottom can be set to it but I'd prefer a dedicated key.

The remote is comfortable to hold and operate. The common buttons (volume/channel/etc) are well placed for easy access with one hand.  There's one glow-in-the-dark button that turns on backlighting and also makes it easy to locate the remote in the dark.
profile.summary: Works well with my devices

profile.description: IlluStory Junior is the perfect introduction to hands-on creativity and storytelling for young readers and writers. Children write and illustrate their story using the materials provided and receive a full-color, professionally bound and printed 5.5"x8.5" paperback book. With up to 14 book pages, a dedication page, a title page and an "About the Author" page, young children can put their first stories into a book that will be treasured for years to come. The production and delivery of the finished book is included in the price of the book-making kit. From the makers of Illustory, My Comic Book, and My Awesome Book.
profile.reviewText:
So, what's in the box? You get is a set of markers, a set of "pages" for your book, some forms to fill out and a prepaid envelope. You write and illustrate, and number the paegs then off they go in the mail. My daughter would have preferred some pages with just text (i.e. no placeholder for drawings) but I guess she's on the upper end of the age group that the product is targeted for.

She has just finished her book so we've just sent it out in the mail to be printed. However, she didn't want to use the included markers so we'll have to see how the print comes out since it wasn't clear what happens if not using the included ones.
profile.summary: A fun activity for kids that like to illustrate and write

profile.description: Crafted with premium laminated safety glass and round edges, the Incipio PLEXTempered Glass Screen Protector is designed to provide impact and scratch protection for your device screen while enhancing the user experience. The ultra-smooth surface is polished with a unique anti-smudge finish to repel natural finger and face oils to provide perfect clarity. Incipios PLEXScreen Protector also includes a snap-on installation bumper to ensure accurate application right out of the box.
profile.reviewText:
Installation instructions were clear. The screen fits well on my wife's Moto G4. It comes with a frame that you place around the phone thus making alignment of the screen before placement quite easy. Getting rid of all the dirt on the screen was quite a challenge though. Even after using the sticky tape there was some left (which resulted in tiny bubbles) but since it was out of the way at the edges it was not intrusive. So, make sure that you clean the surface well.

Finally putting the phone case back on was not a problem since the screen protector is just a bit smaller than the actual screen. Touch screen performance did not seem to change at all.
profile.summary: Easy install, works well

profile.description: The Scotts Easy Hand-Held Broadcast Spreader is the perfect spreader for small yards. It comes fully assembled, so you can begin treating your lawn immediately. You can use it to apply seed, fertilizer, ice melt, or other products on small areas.
profile.reviewText: So I tried it with some lawn fertilizer. I was hoping that the other reviews were too critical but it does turn out that it's not easy to use. I first loaded it about 1/3 and it seemed to work but it still pulverized some of the fertilizer pellets. But upon reloading it, it started jamming and the small crank made it even more of a problem. I'm not a wimpy guy but I still could not get enough torque to rotate it while still maintaining it in a working position. I might give it another try the next time I need to fertilize the lawn but if it still does not work it'll have to go into the recycling container.
profile.summary: It's very hard to use

profile.description: COMPACT DESIGN WITH A GUIDE NUMBER OF 20 AT ISO 100 M 28 AT ISO 200 M SIMPLE MODE DIAL OPERATION OFFERS P-TTL WITH PRE-FLASH TO ASSURE PROPER EXPOSURE FLASH EXPOSURE COMPENSATION CAN BE SET TO -0.5 and -1 EV IN P-TTL MODE THROUGH DIAL  FULL MANUAL MODE FOR MORE CREATIVE CONTROL  FLASH COVERAGE FOR FOCAL LENGTHS AS WIDE AS 28MM IN THE 35MM FORMAT BUILT-IN, FLIP DOWN DIFFUSER COVERS FOCAL LENGTHS DOWN TO 24MM IN THE 35MM FORMATSHIPS IN A PLAIN WHITE BOX
profile.reviewText:
I ordered this but returned it as I found the vertical grip to be too narrow for a comfortable hold. I have fairly big hands so that might have something to do with it. If Pentax could add some bulk to it then it would be perfect. It did however make the horizontal hold quite a bit more comfortable (especially with large heavy lenses).

Otherwise the build is great (just like the K20D I tried it on) and it's well designed. The "green" button is placed a bit off from its position on the camera and since I use it very often I found it a bit hard to get used to. The extra battery and remote/SD card storage are good to have as well.
profile.summary: Vertical grip not that great

profile.description: Our Manual Lawn Spike Aerator has four 3-inch spikes penetrate and loosen compacted soil. Spike aeration loosens soil and thatch to let air, water and fertilizer down to the roots. Spike aeration also stimulates root growth by separating the roots. Your lawn will look better with less water and fertilizer. For best results water your yard thoroughly before aerating. Works well in rocky, highly compacted, root-bound or very sticky soil, such as due to high clay content. Yard Butler guarantees all Yard Butler tools for life against any defects in manufacturing or materials.
profile.reviewText:
I have used it on one area of my yard where the grass is a bit unhappy. I have clay soil and compaction is indeed a problem. The tool works as advertised but

  1) make sure the soil is moist otherwise, at least in my clay, it was quite difficult to drive through. Here's where I wish the foot rest was a bit wider so I can place both feet on when pressing down

  2) you're up for quite a bit of sweat as, even when the soil is moist, it does take quite a few "diggings" to cover even a small area

I have not yet figured out if it's OK to just leave the little soil pellets (that are the byproduct of using the tool) just on the grass. My 3 year old son warned me to watch out about walking on the goose poop. We'll that's pretty much what they look like. In about 3 weeks since I've used the aerator the pellets are still visible on the grass.
profile.summary: Works but for large areas it's a lot of work

profile.description: This strength hand grip features a durable steel coil and strengthens muscles in your hand, wrist and forearms while the cushioned foam handles provide a comfortable nonslip grip. A just able resistance levels from 20 to 90 lbs.
profile.reviewText:
I have used other strength grips before but this was the first that I've seen that was adjustable so I jumped at the occasion. After trying it out for the past few days I think that I like it and will continue to use it at work a couple of times a day.

The one that I received did not come with any instructions on the package but it should not be difficult to figure out how to use it. The green knob is used to adjust strength (although the 90-20lbs inscription seems to be in reverse). The curved handle wraps nicely against the muscular base of the thumb while the straight one is easily gripped by the rest of the fingers.

About the only concern is how well the knob will last as it is already a bit wobbly.
profile.summary: Comfortable to use, adjustable resistance a plus

profile.description: This 2.1 speaker system features the Creative Image Focusing Plate (IFP) design which improves sonic directivity and imaging while preserving tonal accuracy. You can also fine-tune your audio preferences by accessing the wired remote control and bass cont
profile.reviewText:
The build and sound quality is good. I don't think it's at the audiophile level nor do I expect it at this price point. But as a set of speakers for a PC it is more than adequate on treble/bass for casual music/gaming sound.

What I like is that is seems well built and it is easy to use. The fact that the cord holding the wired remote is long enough makes it easy to place within arms reach. This allows volume control from either PC or remove. I also like that the speakers can be turned off from the wired remote unlike another pair of speakers where I have to crawl under the desk and press the power switch. Since I don't always use the speakers when I use my PC this allows me to save some energy by making it easy to turn them off.
profile.summary: Good sound and easy to use

profile.description: First wide-angle to standard zoom lens to achieve a large aperture of 1.8   Due to the very shallow depth of field (DOF) of fast glass and focus variation between the cameras, users may experience focus shift and inconsistent AF. This can be fixed by using the AF fine tune ( For Nikon System)  or AF Micro Adjustment( For Canon System)  in the camera’s Menu to calibrate the lens to specific cameras. Also shooting at smaller aperture values will increase the DOF which reduces “focus issues” as the result of the variations and decreases the amount of fall of (Vignetting).
profile.reviewText:
Yes, it's big but if you want it for it can do there's no way around it that I know of.

I did not want the f/1.8 just for its light gathering capability (although it doesn't hurt to have it) but more for the narrow depth of field it allows. For "environmental" portraits (i.e. not just a head shot but also including a good deal of the background for context) with that "full frame" look I don't think that there's a more versatile lens for APS-C cameras. Add in the fact that it's just about as sharp (if not sharper) than similar prime lenses and you've got a winner.

Update: I forgot to mention that the build of the lens is great. I have some other EX DG Sigma lenses which were well built but this is a notch above those. The materials look like high quality, both the focus and zoom rings move smoothly and without any wobble.
profile.summary: Beauty and the beast! All in one.

top_5.description: Letter Factory Adventures: The Rainforest teaches and reinforces life science concepts for children ages 4-7 years old. Through action-packed gameplay, children develop their knowledge of life science, animals and ecosystems. Letter Factory Adventures: The Rainforest also helps little explorers build fundamental scientific inquiry and critical thinking skills as they learn about the exotic animals and plants that call the four layers of the rainforest their home. Children join Leap, Tad and Lily on a colorful journey through the rainforest, where they encounter diverse ecosystems and an array of amazing life forms. Using their styluses, children move Tad's magnifying glass or Lily's light for a closer look at the many unique plants and animals. There's no shortage of fun in the abundant Amazon! Players climb up vines, bounce off mushrooms and trek through the canopy in pursuit of fascinating creatures to feature in Leap's journal. Letter Factory Adventures: The Rainforest contains more than 200 fascinating facts! Young adventurers will meet the world's loudest monkey, the largest freshwater turtle and a bird that mimics human speech. They'll discover that coffee, chocolate and bananas all grow in the rainforest and explore plants used in important medicines and chewing gum! After completing in-game missions assigned by The Chief, kids may find themselves still in observation mode and thinking like a scientist in the real world! "This learning game gives children opportunities to explore flora and fauna in a unique ecosystem. Children build classification skills by learning about animal characteristics and plant life cycles, which can help them learn to think like scientists."-Elizabeth B., LeapFrog Learning Expert Works with all LeapPad learning tablets and Leapster Explorer and LeapsterGS game systems (sold separately). Internet connection may be required for cartridge.
top_5.reviewText:
It's a fun, informative game for the little ones. At the base is a platform-type game with ladder (i.e vines) to climb, "enemies" to jump on top to get rid of, and with the addition of small interruptions in game play when a creature of interest is found. That's where the informative, learning part comes in.

The rainforest is explored in stages from the ground up all the way to the canopy. At each level various animals, insects, and plants are encountered and kids have the opportunity to learn different facts (as well as answer some questions) about them. In addition, as points are gained during the game, one can "buy" extra fun facts about the creatures encountered.

The game play is reasonably hard for the age group it targets so it should be neither easy nor frustrating.
top_5.summary: Learning while having some fun

top_5.description: Restyled for 2014, the Weber Q 140 is now the Weber Q 1400. The grill has the same great performance and sleek styling, but adds new aesthetics that are both functional and fun, including larger grip handle and control knobs, ergonomic side handles, sturdy front and rear cradles plus the familiar Weber Q logo branded in the lid. The Weber Q 1400 Electric grill raises the bar on flavor expectations and performance of an electric grill. Sear burgers, steaks and chops; grill chicken, fish, vegetables and fruit on the porcelain-enameled cast-iron grates. Youll be amazed at the authentic grilled taste of foods cooked on this electric grill. The Weber Q 1400 grill is fully featured, yet space-saving and portable  just the ticket for grillers living in condos or any residence where restrictions govern gas and charcoal grill usage. May be used with Weber Portable Cart model #6557. Weber Q 1400 is for outdoor use only.
top_5.reviewText:
The grill was quick to assemble. It has few parts and the materials seem to be of good quality (which should bode well for durability).

Size-wise it's good for grilling something for a family meal or maybe at a campsite but don't expect to entertain many guests with it (unless you have plenty of beers for the down time). I've only grilled burgers so far on it and it can accommodate well 4 Costco burger patties. You could squeeze in a couple more but then the cooking probably won't be as even.

I like that the grille does not have any opening right above the burner thus preventing grease and other debris from falling onto the latter and clogging it.

I wish that it came with a built in thermometer but I think that using the grilling guide that was included can be a reasonable substitute.

Lastly even fully assembled it fits in its original box so it makes it easy to store away when not in use.
top_5.summary: A neat little grill

top_5.description: ZAGG Rugged Folio Case, Durable, Hinged with Detachable Backlit Keyboard for iPad Mini & Mini Retina - Black OPEN BOX
top_5.reviewText:
It's very nice and functional! It's almost as having a mini laptop.

I got this for my father-in-law and he loves it. His main complaint about the iPad was the onscreen keyboard being not as nice to use as a real keyboard (and I agree with him). This has solved his problem and also added some much needed safety to his iPad as the grandkids are bound to drop it.

The keyboard does need a bit of getting used to as it's not full size but it's not too bad. It has a good typing feel to the fingers. Once the shell is closed both iPad and keyboard are very well protected. Setting up the Bluetooth connection was a cinch and it seems to work reliably.
top_5.summary: I wish they made this for the Kindle Fire!

top_5.description: The Lenovo MIIX 310 is a 2-in-1 detachable Windows tablet designed for on-the-go webaholics who need data all-day, every day. Featuring an optional Full HD IPS display and detachable keyboard, it gives you the flexibility to be productive anytime, anywhere.
top_5.reviewText:
I really wanted to like the Miix310. I liked that it had 64GB built-in storage when most low-end notebooks usually just have 32GB. With Windows being a disk space hog 32GB is hardly enough it you want to install a few apps. Yes, you can attach an SD card but some programs refuse to install there and when they do they are much slower because of the SD card performance.

I was hoping that it would be a bit smoother in operation than my HP Stream 13 mainly due to 4 CPU cores vs 2 cores but it's a wash. Neither are the GPU or the SSD significantly faster. So at least from a price point the $200 HP is better. Also I had forgotten the keyboard trade-offs when using a 10" keyboard: PgUp/Dn are located awkwardly and the function keys F1-F12 are only accessible by pressing the Fn key.

The magnetic hinge connecting the tablet and the keyboard works quite well but snaps in with quite some force so watch out for your fingers. Also if using it on your lap while wearing shorts watch out for the hinge pinching your leg skin/hair when opening it up.

Pros:
- battery life : more than 8 hours easily
- 64GB SSD storage : lots of room left after Windows and its updates
- nice sharp screen : I'm not a fan of matte screens
- good keyboard and touchpad : not excellent but no complaints either
- full size USB ports on the keyboard : allows you to connect USB drives, mice

Cons:
- sharp edges on both the tablet and keyboard parts make it not comfortable to hold
- a bit top heavy : for most laptops/notebooks the part holding the keyboard is heavier than the one holding the screen. Here things are reversed so it makes holding and walking around with it a bit more difficult
- power plug hard to insert, harder to remove
- power cord rather short : it's only 5 feet long
- overall quality impression marred : a screen issue and some impurities on the outer shell paint are not inspiring
- need specialized tool (provided) to open SD card slot : or at least must find a similar thin hard metal rod
- battery slow to charge : Win10 estimates 3 1/2 hours from a fully discharged state, after 2 hours it was at 68%

Finally the one that I got has 15 or so bubbles under the top level screen layer. I called Lenovo and will have to send it in. Stay tuned.

UPDATE: more than a month after sending it in for repair it's still "in-progress" due to missing parts. Also no communication from the repair department with updates, you need to check on it yourself. Downgrading rating to 2 stars.

UPDATE2: it's been 2 months new and I still don't have the unit back. 0 stars would be in order but I can only give it a minimum of one.

UPDARE3: finally Lenovo sent me a new unit after just having too many things to fix on the original one and taking way too long. However, it has the exact same issue with the screen: dust trapped under the top layer protecting the screen.
top_5.summary: Works in a pinch, horrible support

top_5.description: The highly anticipated family comedy The Smurfs 2 is now a video game! The evil wizard Gargamel has created the Naughties, who kidnap Smurfette from Smurfs Village and imprison her in Paris. It's now up to the Smurfs to travel from the Enchanted Forest, through the busy streets of New York, into Paris, and everywhere in between to save the day and bring Smurfette home safe!
top_5.reviewText:
Having watched the kids play the game for a while and having played a level or two myself I can say that the game is quite fun. Don't expect any earth-shattering gameplay but if you like the type of game you'll definitely get quite a few hours of play out of it. The levels are engaging with quite a bit of imagination in the enemies and structures encountered. The backdrops are also well designed and improve the look and feel of the game. The controls are simple and intuitive so you'll be up and playing in no time. You can select different smurfs and use their different abilities to your advantage.

One complaint I had (but not the kids) is that perhaps the characters/elements in the game are a bit on the small side which makes it a bit difficult to follow what's going on at times.
top_5.summary: Good ol' "platform" game

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "Keyshia Cole is the real deal. Like many young people raised in tough neighborhoods, the 21-year-old songstress endured a tumultuous childhood in Oakland, California, and has fought all her life to keep her dream of a music career alive. Now she's realizing that dream on her own terms with her first album for the A&M label, 'The Way It Is'. It's been a long road for Keyshia, but it's her powerful voice, a belllike instrument whose soaring clarity is topped off with a tantalizing touch of soulful grit that's carried her through, not to mention the diminutive singer's personal combination of sugar, spice, sass and sex appeal, along with a solid-steel spine. With production by Kanye West, Krucial Keys, Ron Fair and Chink Santana, Keyshia's dreams have been realized. Universal. 2005.". The summary of the review text is "The Way R&B Should Be!".
output:
That's right people, you heard me! In a world where female mainstream R&B is generally ruled by hot-looking songstresses who rely on infectious, club-ready production and sub-par lyrics, Keyshia Cole easily stands out amount amongst the growing female R&B surplus with her raw, soulful vocals. Seemingly more inclined to following the examples of artists like Alicia Keys, Faith Evans and -more specifically, and most noticeably- Mary J. Blige, Keyshia Cole's mind-blowing debut album "The Way It Is" is an uncompromised R&B classic that mainly puts a betrayed female's wrath into crystal-clear perspective.

While there may be virtually NO synthesizer-heavy mainstream club bangers on this album, Keyshia clearly doesn't need any, as her compelling lyrics & soulful vocals do a much better job at telling the story. In fact, the Jadakiss-assisted "Guess What" -a bluntly aggressive power ballad where Keyshia furiously gives her man the boot after catching him out- is as close as you'll get to anything remotely danceable, boasting some loud horns & nice bass on the production board.

There are plenty of highlights to go around on the album. Produced by Kanye West, lead single "I Changed My Mind" is a powerful ballad which has Keyshia giving up on a lover who's unwilling to appreciate her for the great woman she truly is. Alicia Keys also lends a helping hand on the horn-driven R&B/Soul anthem "(I Just Want It) To Be Over", a dramatic power ballad where Keyshia reminisces on the good times of her relationship, and how she wishes that her now-rotten relationship would just end. The best heartbreak ballad, however, is "I Should Have Cheated". With stellar lyrics, funky guitar riffs & smooth harmonicas, Keyshia Cole's powerful vocals are drenched in sorrow & regret as she confesses to her paranoid ex-lover that although she didn't cheat on him like he constantly accused her of doing, she wished she did. Nowhere else on this album (or any other album, for that matter) will you find confrontational subject matter put into such a creative viewpoint, nor will you find any other songstress of this new generation who can do such a song with better results (well...maybe Alicia Keys, and possibly Beyonce, but probably not too many others).

However, Keyshia Cole still knows how to love like any sane female. A perfect example of this is the self-penned "Love", an amazing ballad where Keyshia exposes her vulnerable side that longs for love from that special somebody over beautifully smooth instrumental arrangements. The vocal melismas on the sweet chorus also add a very nice touch to an unavoidable standout. "We Could Be" also makes room for emotional tenderness, where Keyshia ponders the thoughts of being with another man. Although some people may be less attracted to the sensuous misfit ballad "Down & Dirty", it gets its fair share of props for its instrumental experimentation, Keyshia's seductive vocals & the cheesy metaphor-free lyrics that come with it.

Everyone will be bound to love many tracks over others (the Chink Santana-assisted drama ballad "Situations" & the R&B/Soul ballad "Superstar" should score the "skip" button more than anything else), but ultimately, Keyshia has come out with a stunning debut. 5 STARS!

Best 5 Tracks:

"Love"

"I Should Have Cheated"

"We Could Be"

"I Changed My Mind"

"(I Just Want It) To Be Over"

profile.description: Take the best songwriters & the best singers, add the most exciting performers & the best all around personalities, throw in the hottest looks & the sexiest smiles, mix them all together & the finished product would probably sound a lot like CIARA.
profile.reviewText:
As the First Lady of Crunk'n'B and a multi-talented individual with 3 consecutive smash hit singles (the Crunk'n'B female independence anthem "Goodies", the pulsating R&B/Pop club banger "1, 2 Step" & the grimy, street-edged anthem "Oh", featuring Petey Pablo, Missy Elliott & Ludacris respectively), I had high expectations of Ciara's debut album. Unfortunately, I was left rather disappointed.

Don't get me wrong...I absolutely love everything about Ciara -from her sweet vocals to her almost-unparalleled dancing skills to her beautiful looks and physique (although the vicious rumours questioning her true gender leave me rattled and bewildered)- but the album title says it all. The album's GOOD, but not GREAT! As a lot of people know, there's more to music than commercial success, looks and money, but this album doesn't seem to reflect Ciara's knowledge towards that. Ciara still has a nice voice, but when you put it next to other newcomers & veterans, you can see that she has a long way to go vocally, as it is entirely indistinctive.

However, there are still some other great tracks on the album (excluding the first 3 singles). "Thug Style" is a beautiful, mellow guitar ballad where Ciara angelically croons one minute before breaking out into a hypnotic lullaby the next. Not only that, but "Thug Style" also has some slow-dance appeal to it, which makes it a clear highlight. "The Title" is also another smooth slow jam dedicated to her lover, which also has an unusual old-school feel to it.

While the aforementioned tracks are delectable treats for every listener, there is also some inevitable musical sabotage. The boring-as-s*** "Other Chicks" clearly proves that fact, as does the overly generic and diluted dance tunes "Lookin' At You" & "Hotline", which lack the energy and distinctiveness of "Goodies", "1, 2 Step" & "Oh". It also pains me to say that the soothing ballad (and failed fourth single) "And I" is also a letdown, considering the fact that Ciara wrote the lyrics earlier on in her youth. Unfortunately, Ciara's emotional closeness and sweet vocals, combined with the beautiful acoustic guitar in the background, cannot redeem the overly clichd lyrics. Honestly, if you listen close enough, it'll make lyrically troubled singers like Ashanti look like poets (or at least better writers).

As I said before, Ciara's album is good, but not great. Nonetheless, it's worth your money, but I hope she steps her game up on her 2nd album. Best wishes to you Ciara.
profile.summary: The title says it all :(

profile.description: 50 CENT THE MASSACRE
profile.reviewText:
Wow, I can't believe I almost considering buying this over Alicia Keys' sophomore album back when I was younger. Sure, Alicia Keys isn't as radio-friendly, offensive or "gangster" as 50 Cent, but I can easily appreciate the musicality, substance and personality of her music more than this "Pop-(c)rap(-tastic)" offering from 50 Cent. Long story short, "The Massacre", 50 Cent's multi-platinum sophomore album, is essentially a "Get Rich Or Die Tryin'" remake.

Once again, star-studded producers (Scott Storch, Eminem, Dr. Dre, etc.), pounding beats, addictive hooks, typically narrow subject matter (misogyny, materialism, etc.) and 50 Cent's aggressive rapping delivery are back in full force. And just like before, the guests are kept to a minimum, allowing the spotlight to shine (or the darkness to fall) on 50 Cent. There's long-forgotten R&B singer Olivia (pray to God she sees some kind of stardom this year) who is employed as the sexy support hook singer on the dreadful single "Candy Shop", a shameless, Scott Storch-produced slab of sleazy come-ons relating to typical sex fantasies and 50 Cent's physical self (I'm not going in-depth, you should know what I mean); her other appearance on "So Amazing", one of many pieces of worthless filler, is no better; Jamie Foxx completely belittles his own extraordinary singing talents on "Build You Up", a cheesy, literally unbelievable, bulls**t-feeding ladies joint; and rapper Tony Yayo sounds as useless as ever on the lacklustre "My Toy Soldier". Thankfully, he strikes gold with Eminem once again on "Gatman & Robbin", which is much like "Patiently Waiting" (from his debut album) - lacking substance, but lyrically/verbally complex and sonically thrilling, partially because of Eminem's solid, haunting production.

Unfortunately, 50 Cent isn't much better when he's by himself either. Registering the pitiful "Piggy Bank" as a legitimate diss track is insulting in its own self; the Dr. Dre-produced "Outta Control" and the Cool & Dre-co-produced lead single "Disco Inferno" are two misogynistic club cuts that put perfectly functional, appealing beats to complete waste; and practically everything else, especially the Scott Storch-produced, Middle Eastern-inflected third single "Just A Lil' Bit", fails on nearly every level. The only solo track where 50 Cent really shines is the laid-back "Ryder Music", where Hi-Tek's R&B-leaning production works surprisingly well with 50 Cent's more laid-back flow and (partially) substantial lyrics.

In conclusion, 50 Cent and "The Massacre" are essentially and structurally the same - you love it or you hate it. In my case, I choose the latter, hands-down. 1 star!

Best Tracks:

"Gatman & Robbin"

"Ryder Music"

"Hate It Or Love It (G-Unit Remix)"
profile.summary: "The Massacre" - What An Appropriate Title!

profile.description: BARKLEY GNARLS ST.ELSEWHERE
profile.reviewText:
DJ/Producer Danger Mouse & rapper/singer/songwriter/producer/ex-Goodie Mob member Cee-Lo, collectively known as Gnarls Barkley, have joined forces to craft one of 2006's best and weirdest albums! What confuses me, however, is why their music is being labelled as Pop music.

Understandably, there are talented and creative forces in the world of Pop (Pink, Nelly Furtado, etc.), but the genre's generally the household of superficiality, mainstream predictability, talent-challenged Pop tarts and temporary heart-throbs. Unlike most run-of-the-mill Pop stars, Cee-Lo's vocals are strong, powerful, soulful and slightly raspy - the type that are easily capable of equalling, if not wilfully overpowering, Danger Mouse's insanely unconventional, upbeat production (see album opener "Go-Go Gadget Gospel", where Cee-Lo unsubtly wails with maddening passion over Danger Mouse's boisterous horns). Then of course there's the UK-record-breaking #1 smash hit "Crazy", where Cee-Lo contemplates mental insanity over a dark, eerie beat.

Speaking of contemplation, it's obvious that Cee-Lo & Danger Mouse put a lot of effort into this stellar collaborative effort. From the crazy production to the singing to the rapping to the thought-provoking lyrics to the diverse subject matter, Gnarls Barkley manage to successfully throw all of their wacky ideas into a rather brief 37-40min.-long album and balance everything out to perfection. This type of album sure as Hell wasn't meant to be tailor-made for the pre-teen set.

On "Necromancer", Cee-Lo pervertedly details his sickening love for necrophilia over suitably haunting production, while "Just A Thought", "Smiley Faces" & "Who Cares" -all three of which talk about depression, pain and/or contemplative suicide- best exemplify the album's lyrical complexity. On top of all this, there's an infectious cover of the Violent Femmes' "Gone Daddy Gone" - complete with bouncy xylophonic sound effects and electric guitar strings- and the schizophrenic "Transformer", where Cee-Lo rapidly raps and loudly sings the hook with the help of a few random (but different) vocal samples and/or effects, as well as Danger Mouse's super-fast production.

Well, does this album have any weaknesses? Believe it or not, this album really has no weaknesses. The comparatively short running time prevents the set from getting monotonous or self-indulgent (thanks for pointing that out AMG), and with just about no filler in sight, Gnarls Barkley have crafted a perfect debut album.

Only God knows what the f*** possessed these two nut-bags to create a concept album of such brilliance (though I doubt it was from "Feng Shui", as they stated on the track of the same name), but "St. Eslewhere" definitely a classic example of what can happen when artists motivate themselves enough to push musical boundaries in search of something more. 5 stars, easily!
profile.summary: "St. Elsehwere" - A Great Place For Music To Be!

profile.description: STONE JOSS MIND, BODY & SOUL
profile.reviewText:
As Joss Stone's debut album "The Soul Session" indicated, she is a phenomenally talented singer - with those soulful, throaty, gritty, powerful vocals of hers, it would be perfectly normal to be shocked that such a beautiful voice could come from the mouth of a 16-year-old teenage "white" girl from London ( hate that "white"/"black" categorization stuff). Sure, "The Soul Sessions" was just an album full of cover songs, so originality was naturally dire, but that was not the point - the point of that album was to establish Joss Stone for the truly gifted artist she is, as well as her vocal skills. And much like "The Soul Sessions", "Mind, Body & Soul", the follow-up album and Joss Stone's first album that consists of entirely original material, serves the same purpose in a different way.

Apart from appearances from Betty Wright and Steven Greenberg and others, the list of producers is relatively superstar-free, and the guest list is completely empty, further emphasizing the fact that this album is all about Joss Stone. Then there's the fact that she co-wrote over half of the lyrical content on this album, including the first portion of the whole album that elevates this album into greatness.

"Right To Be Wrong", the album-opening track, is easily the best track on the album. The strong lyrics, which obviously relate to the song title, are just as captivating and penetrating as Joss Stone's vocal delivery, and the minimalist piano-guitar production add to the raw appeal of the song. Naturally, highlights are still abundant - her youthful energy and powerful vocals enliven tracks like the summery retro-70's/80's-pop anthem "Don't Cha Wanna Ride" and "You Had Me", a funk guitar-driven kiss off to a negligent, money-scabbing, dope-sniffing ex-lover; "Jet Lag" is hypnotic and mellow ballad with its smooth instrumentation and Joss Stone's smooth vocals; piano-driven R&B/Soul ballad "Spoiled" is drenched with emotion and regret; and "Less Is More" is a semi-brutally honest ode to a lover doing too much to please her, the song's heavy sentimentality pleasantly lightened by Reggae-flavoured production.

Unfortunately, by the time we're past the cheesy R&B/Gospel ballad "Security" and the contrastingly beautiful ballad (and late-album highlight) "Young At Heart", the album's quality heavily wavers. "Snakes & Ladders" is ridiculously original with its metaphorical lyrics about a complicated relationship, and the song's slightly catchy, but the weak production brings the track down; "Don't Know How" feels lifeless, formulaic and devoid of the passion that Joss Stone usually (and naturally) brings to some of her other tracks; and album closers "Killing Time" and "Sleep Like A Child" are two dreary ballad that wear out their welcome well before the 5+ minutes are fully up.

Another fault to this album is its substance. Apart from "Right To Be Wrong" and hidden track "Daniel", a passionate ode to her previously incarcerated criminal brother of the same name, it's all about relationships - the typical cycle of love, hate, like, etc. in typical relationships.

Nonetheless, "Mind, Body & Soul" is a pleasing album that shows more promise from a truly talented individual. 3.5 stars!

5 Best Tracks (IMO):

"Right To Be Wrong"

"You Had Me"

"Jet Lag"

"Young At Heart"

"Spoiled"
profile.summary: Promising, But Not Fulfilling!

profile.description: Includes 2 UK bonus tracks.
profile.reviewText:
Considering Frankie J's immense musical talent, Mexican/Latin roots, beautiful falsetto (unlike many other male artists), the multiple comparisons to multi-talented mega-superstar Usher & the massive success of his Baby Bash-assisted smash hit single "Obsession (No Es Amor)", I was expecting a mind-blowing, stellar sophomore effort from him. Unfortunately, Frankie J does not fulfill my expectations. Instead, he delivers a formulaic set of music material to his fans consisting of a few spectacular tracks hidden under sweet -but ultimately forgettable- filler.

As minimally inspired as "The One" is, there are a few bright moments here & there. The smash hit single "Obsession (No Es Amor)" is a song that everybody should know by now, and explains the situation of being being lovingly obsessed with another girl. Baby Bash takes the time to drop an unnecessary verse, but it doesn't hurt or help the already-amazing track. Relatable subject matter, great vocals, a tiny bit of Latin, nice beat...enough said, the track's great, and it's global success testifies to that fact.

"How To Deal", Frankie J's minor second hit single, talks about the struggle of choosing between staying with the love of your life or leaving to pursue your dreams. Couples & lovers will be able to strongly relate to this song to a certain extent, and everything about the song pieces together effectively (vocals, lyrics, beat, emotion, etc.). "The One" is also another sweet ballad, pairing Frankie J & 3LW, and has hit single potential written all over it. The song's sweet, simplistic & laid-back, making it perfect for any occasion of love.

"Story Of My Life", the album's compulsory autobiographical ballad, is undoubtedly the best track on the album. Accompained by nothing more than some introductory violins, a guitar & some hand-clapping/clicking sound effects, Frankie J connects to his audience with soft, emotional vocals & universally relatable, inspiring, touching lyrics. Not only does Frankie J manage to portray his life story in a colourful manner, but he simultaneously manages to help heal the wounds of a hurting heart. You'd have to be majorly shallow to deny a track as masterful as this.

Every other song on this track is a take-it-or-leave-it affair. As good as "On The Floor" is, the song feels like something forcefully added in for the sake of variety. Not only that, but it looks bad on you when you have to get a materialistic C+ rapper like Paul Wall to do the more hard-edged portions of musical material. It's good to know that Frankie J isn't trying to sound full-on gangsta, but unfortunately, "On The Floor" reveals one of his biggest weaknesses...versatility. With his stupid pretty-boy looks, neo-soul/pop music & God knows what else, this leaves Frankie J in a limited space for creativity.

If you enjoy a sweet, simple listen, then this album is for you. If you're looking for something unpredictable, stellar & ambitiously driven, then skip this at all costs! "The One" is far too formulaic to satisfy those who look for something more revolutionary or incredibly creative.
profile.summary: This isn't "The One"!

profile.description: There's nothing like the warm spirit of the caribbean, to re-energize a dry, stale season of the same old song & dance. Introducing Rihanna, a stunning 17-yr-old from barbados who's poised & positioned to take the music world by storm. Already on teen peoples's hot list, Rihanna's powerful singing voice conjures up feelings & experiences way beyond her years....while still maintaining her youthful spirit. Besides ripping traditional reggae tracks like a seasoned dancehall Queen, she exudes the kind of energy that solidifies her as one of 05's top emerging artists. Her debut album Music Of The Sun, includes the mega summer hit 'Pon De Replay' as well as the sultry ballad 'last time', & the track masters produced 'If It's Lovin That You Want'. Island. 2005.
profile.reviewText:
Now-18-year-old Bajan beauty Rihanna, America's newest R&B/Pop & Dancehall sensation & 1 of 3 of Jay-Z's latest proteges, debuts with "Music Of The Sun", a great album full of moving ballads, emotional heartbreak songs & irresistible club bangers, all infused with Rihanna's native Carribean music style. To top it off, "MUsic Of The Sun" is released than none other than Def Jam Records, lead by the legendary multi-tasking rapper, Jay-Z himself.

Rihanna makes an impressive solid debut with "Music Of The Sun", a record full of irresistible club bangers & emotionally moving ballads, along with guest artist support from Sean Paul ("Rush"), Vybez Cartel ("You Don't Love Me {No, No, No}") & Elephant Man ("Pon De Replay Remix"). Standouts on the album include the lyrically mesmeric & creative "Music Of The Sun", the R&B/Pop/Dancehall club-banging smash hit "Pon De Replay", the light-hearted dance numer "If It's Lovin' That You Want", the emotionally moving guitar ballad "The Last Time" & the Vybez Cartel-assisted ballad "You Don't Love Me (No, No, No). Although there are no bad or disastrous tracks on the album, the weakness of Rihanna's debut lies in its lack of lyrical originality & subject matter. "Music Of The Sun" is entirely an exception to the album's weakness, but 1 track cannot redeem an entire album's worth of predictable subject matter.

However, Rihanna's beautiful, stunning voice & her burning desire to place her native Carribean flavour into the vast majority of her tracks prevent this album from becoming a disaster of any kind. That's what I like about Rihanna...she keeps it real with her music & her fans. Instead of creating generic Bubblegum pop & soulless R&B, she adds her own flavour & puts a part of herself into each of her tracks, increasing the overall quality of her songs & saving them from being dismissed as album filler.

"Music Of The Sun" may not be perfect, but it's a solid debut that shows potential in this promising talent. If Rihanna can put some more originality into her subject matter, she will ensure herself longevity in the music industry. Her latest hit single "S.O.S. (Rescue Me)" & her upcoming single "Unfaithful" from her sophomore album "A Girl Like Me",  are already displaying her growth as an artist & as a person.

On a final note, I wish nothing but the best for Rihanna. Nice job with your debut album, and I'm sure your sophomore set will be even more amazing than this.

Rating: 3.5 Stars
profile.summary: A Solid Debut From A Promising Talent...She's Obviously Hot Too :D

profile.description: Teairra Mar, Roc-A-Fella Records' new young princess steps onto the scene with a smash....The Detroit native, representing 8-mile, is also a former student of Detroit's DSA high school for the performing arts which Aaliyah also attended. 'Make Her Feel Good' is Teairra's first single. 2005.
profile.reviewText:
I seriously don't understand why everyone's hating on her so much. Wow, she's a 17-year-old teenage girl who uses some inappropriate language on widely relateable, yet -hardly-talked-about subject matter...GET OVER IT! Teenagers, especially girls, go through many of the song topics Teairra Mari sings about. She's not a gimmick, she's not a fake, she's not a sellout & she's DEFINITELY not a stupid girl! Teairra knows where she stands in the music industry & what she represents, whether it be as a proud Detroit native or one of the standout voices of a young female generation.

Although this great album is mainly aimed at the young female audience, guys will be able to learn alot from this album. Lyrically strong & truthful lyrics in songs like "Make Her Feel Good" (1st hit single that samples from Eric B. & Rakim's "My Melody"), "No Daddy" (2nd single that unfortunately flopped), "Confidential" & "Get Up On Ya Gangsta" really make you think...if you can get past the energetic, club-ready beats blasting in the background. "Phone Booth", the album's best track (IMO), depicts a powerfully descriptive, lyrically colourful, emotionally heart-wrenching story of a young woman having a life-changing argument with her mother before heading off to a "phone booth" to ask her boyfriend to pick her up. Long story short, it's nothing short of spectacular. The album's only other ballad, "Act Right", is a simplistic, yet relaxing love song dedicated to her man. Lyrics are pretty well-constructed, and vocals sound beautiful.

If you're more blunt & aggressive on love gone wrong, there's always room for giving your love-rat the boot on "New S**t", bragging about your female independence & superiority with "MVP" or telling playas & gangsta-wannabes to back off with "Stay In Ya Lane" & "Lala"...the latter one moreso about staying true to your current lover, rather than leaving every guy bitterly rejected.

If you simply couldn't care less about life's thought-provoking issues, there's always the joyful club banger "Get Down Tonight", which has a disco-like, girls-night-out feel to it. Definitely not for the guys unless you're trying to rip off or sample the beat.

Altogether, this is a great set which can teach alot to everybody who listen to it. However, as good as the club-ready beats are, they tend to overshadow the actual meanings & lyrics of the songs if you don't focus carefully. I understand that club bangers tend to be catchier & more attention-grasping, but sometimes it's not always a good idea to add thumping beats to such sensitive subject matter. I'm betting "No Daddy" in the 1st song to come to mind at that point, but the song still leaves a positive message of growing more independent & stronger beause of her father's absence, so stop hating on the song. I'm surprised at how unsuccessful that song was, considering it was a great track.

4.5 stars...GREAT ALBUM! "No Daddy (Remix)", isn't so bad either :D
profile.summary: ALL YOU HATERS BACK OFF!!

profile.description: With the hit single 'All Because Of You', 'Do It' Featuring the Ying Yang Twins. 'Naked' and 'Everything' the album displays Marques's vocal maturity. It is evident that he ahs taken his writing and producing abilities to a new level with the release of 'Naked'. CLEAN VERSION. Universal. 2005
profile.reviewText:
Wow, I never thought I would've found an R&B album worse than Omarion's debut until I finished listening to this album's samples on Amazon. "Naked", Marques Houston's spohomore effort, is undoubtedly the worst R&B album I have ever heard in a long while.

I apoligize for sounding harsh, but think about it. Where's the talent? Where's the skill? What about the heart & soul? Where's the musical ambition? What about meaningful lyrics & nice beats? Where's his dignity? Where's hist artistic growth? I'm betting he threw all that & so much more out the window along with his tacky clothes. Marques, take this into account...YOU'RE NOT USHER AND YOU NEVER WILL BE, SO STOP TRYING!

I honestly tried really hard to force myself to like his song "All Because Of You", but I just couldn't convince myself to do it. There's not a single song on this entire album that has any true emotional depth. His other singles, "Naked" & "Sex Wit You" are absolutely pathetic attempts at explicit sexuality, with egomaniacle, ridicuously retarded videos to boot. As if the cheesy, sexual come-ons & emotionally devoid ballads were hard enough to bare, you have miserable club tunes to complain about here & there.

Marques Houston is a perfect example of why R&B goes downhills nowadays. Anybody with a slight fraction of a brain would be aware that he has no talent, and relies on his ugly mug & flabby gut to seek the attention of ditsy tween girls worldwide. Skip this album at ALL COSTS (AND I MEAN THAT LITERALLY)!
profile.summary: Omarion's Cheaper, Less Talented Alternative

profile.description: On December 14th, Ashanti proves again that there is power found in her musical phenomenon. On this, her trinity release, CONCRETE ROSE. This is a creative combination of her freshman and sophomore albums. Ashanti merges her profound writing abilities, the stellar production of The Inc. Records CEO Irv Gotti and Seven, and collaborations with Ja Rule & Lloyd to create this masterpiece. The first single, 'Only U' is a high energy R&B/rhythmic crossover mix and impacts the first week in October.
