Ashanti is back to once again prove why she is by far one of today's most sought after and intriguing female entertainers of this decade.
profile.reviewText:
After 2 #1 U.S. multi-platinum albums, numerous accolades, strong -but not overpowering- appearances as a well-known singer for rap hooks & a bunch of hit singles, the one & only The Princess of The Inc. known as Ashanti returns with her 3rd album, poetically titled "Concrete Rose". Such an album title is obviously a creative metaphor, which describes Ashanti's music as a combination of Hip-Hop ("Concrete") and R&B ("Rose"). I personally thought it was a metaphor for combining strength & solidity ("Concrete") with beauty, elegance & vulnerability ("Rose"). Unfortunately, this album does not live up to its title. Instead, Ashanti delivers us another CD full of tracks generally revolving around love, heartbreak & tearing the club up!

The album kicks off with an intro explaining the title of the album & why she thinks it's the best album of her career. I am one of many people who disagree with this, but I'll explain why towards the end of the review.

Once the intro is done, the album enters the 1st song, "Still Down", a laid-back love-song where Ashanti is basically asking her man if he's still down for her. Self-proclaimed "King of the South" T.I. drops some nice rhymes to accompany Ashanti's smooth crooning on this track, making a great song & an even greater way to officially start off the album.

"Message to the Fans" is simply a skit where Ashanti spares a few seconds to thank her fans for helping her pull through all the ups & downs of her career. If you thought that was sweet, wait `til she backs her thanks up by getting into the next track...the love-addiction-based R&B/Rock gem "Only U". Loud guitar riffs & dark, heavy bass strongly intensify Ashanti's seductive vocals & the dark vibe of this addictive, empowering club banger, making this the best track on the album! Although this song became a hit, a song as musically  creative (no, NOT LYRICS) & addictive as this deserves the #1 spot much more than a lot of songs that tend to grab the top spot on the Billboard Hot 100. Throwaway trashes like "Laffy Taffy" & "Grillz" have nothing on a track like "Only U".

"Focus", the 5th track to "Concrete Rose", is another bouncy R&B club joint, but fails to sustain the loudness & boundless energy of "Only U". Although the song itself makes a decent album cut with its catchy, dark beat, Ashanti's decent vocal efforts & the inspirational theme of moving on after a love gone wrong, it's just not the right kind of song to follow a track like "Only U". The lyrics aren't exactly creative either.

Thankfully, "Don't Let Them" -a smooth, emotionally chord-plucking ballad about not letting everyone around you tear apart your love for that special someone- picks up the slack that "Focus" left behind. Surprisingly, this is Ashanti's favourite track off the album as well as my main favourite, and with good reason. Ashanti manages to croon with a sense of soul & emotional captivation -something considered highly uncommon when it comes to Ashanti's music & how the general public perceive it. There is the occasional clich? here & there, but Ashanti's soulful vocals compensates for those minor flaws. The accompanying beat strengthens the emotional grip this song has, making this song -along with "Only U"- a standout. Maybe the review on this song sounds misleading, but everybody has an opinion, and I think this song is something special. It's hard to believe this song didn't become a success.

Once "Don't Let Them" concludes, "Love Again" -another love ballad- follows. Considering how well her vocals work with the easy beat & the dreamy, sensual vibe, it's a shame that the song's predictable rhymes & clich?s drag this song down. Lines like, "And when you put your hands in certain places/Boy I can't help but make them silly faces/'Cause what you doing to me should be a sin/It feels so good that I can barely hold it in", are examples of sinful depravity in its own self, and although it blatantly shows how deeply in love she is with her man, it makes Ashanti sound nothing like a lovesick individual. I never really liked this song anyway, so I consider it filler...half-creepy, half-bland filler.

Things don't get much better with yet ANOTHER love ballad, "Take Me Tonight", a duet between Ashanti & R&B artist Lloyd. This song is nothing but pure filler because the song is devoid of passion, originality, lyrical creativity & most importantly, believable chemistry between the 2 artists. Considering how well they worked together on Lloyd's "Southside", it's a shame that this song failed so miserably. You should definitely skip this track.

Things don't get much better with the following track "U", which sounds more like a darker, redone version of "Love Again". Ashanti's vocals sound lacklustre & dragged in this song, while predictable rhymes once again paired with a few dirty lyrics here & there, which add both power & indignity to the track. I dislike this song slightly more than "Love Again", so I consider this filler.

Thank God hope returns when ANOTHER love ballad comes along by the name of "Every Lil' Thing". Vocals are mesmerically sweet, music in the background plays beautifully & the lyrics dip in & out of clich?s like "Don't Let Them". The song itself is refreshing compared to the 3 disastrous ballads that preceded it, but unfortunately, love songs & balladry have been worn out thin by the time listeners reach this track.

Luckily, "Turn It Up", an anthem-like, girls-night-out club banger featuring Ja Rule, comes out from the middle of nowhere, drawing listeners in with its thumping beats, boundless energy & Ashanti's joyous vocals. Ja Rule's 16 bars add a little flavour to the track, making this song a definite standout!

Hope slowly begins to slide away from the minds of listeners again when a meaningless skit by the name of "Buck 3000" pops up. Only God knows why this waste of space was added! This obviously needs skipping, and is undeserving of anybody's time.

ANOTHER ballad, titled "So Hot", begins to play at the end of the "Buck 3000" skit. With its relaxing beats & instrumentals combined once again with the mesmerically sweet vocals used in Ashanti's "Every Lil' Thing", "So Hot" turns out to become a strong album cut. Even the occasionally clich?d lyrics play a stronger role than usual, painting the scenes, thoughts & emotions of the track into the minds of listeners. This is a job well done by Ashanti.

"Don't Leave Me Alone", another ballads featuring 7 Aurelius, is another refreshing standout. Passion, soulfulness, beats, instrumentals, love & purity shine brightly on this amazing ballad. Ashanti manages to belt out the overused lyrics with feeling & soul, while 7 Aurelius adds the icing to the cake on the chorus.

Following this track is another skit, but to my surprise, it was surprisingly good. Ashanti & her sister display their vocal chops in this short-lived skit, and once again, Ashanti sounded amazing to my surprise. No instrumentals, no beats, no digital magic on the vocals...just 2 sisters belting out a few lyrics with strength. One part of me wishes they made this into a single, while another part of me is thankful this is just a skit, otherwise the potential song could've been violently butchered!

The album is concluded with "Freedom", a song addressed to the doubters & haters. This song is yet ANOTHER standout with excellent lyrics, simplistic instrumentals & good vocals. Not only does this song state the facts to the haters, but it also manages to inspire the people who really look up to her. There is nothing but realness on this track. When she sings at the average noise level, she sounds calm, collective & in-control. When she belts those high notes, she sounds passionate & determined.

The "Wonderful" remix is added as a bonus track at the end of the album. It's not much different to the original, but the original version was great anyway, so it's a good bonus track. I didn't consider it to be the conclusion to the album itself.

Verdict:

Ashanti has come out with another satisfactory album, but like her previous 2 albums, she is still cursed by her biggest weakness - originality. With the exceptions of certain songs, this album is filled with loads of forgettable ballads & riddled with misplaced skits. "Sister Stories" should've been placed before "Focus" because both songs relate to relationships gone wrong in a certain way ("Sister Stories" could've made "Focus" look like a story instead of a misplaced track). She has the looks, the dancing skills, the voice, mainstream success & street credibility...all she needs now is some inspiration & creativity. If she can make songs as unconventional as "Only U", soulful as "Don't Let Them" & "Don't Leave Me Alone" or as lyrically wise as "Freedom", she will easily be able to catapult herself back into the R&B elite. Her career is diminishing with her creativity, and if she doesn't begin to grow as an artist, it won't be long before she's forgotten. Also, she needs to cut down on the excess ballads & add some more club bangers or soul ballads. They suit her voice & her style very well.

Rating: 3 Stars

Top 5 Tracks:

"Don't Let Them"

"Only U"

"Turn It Up (feat. Ja Rule)"

"Don't Leave Me Alone (feat. 7 Aurelius)"

"Freedom"
profile.summary: If Ashanti cut down on the ROSES & added some more CONCRETE tracks, she'd have a respectable album!! Average at best

profile.description: DMX, the legendary Ruff Ryder who's sold 20 million albums, is back in the saddle with his eagerly-awaited sixth solo outing, Year Of The Dog Again, his previous album, 2003's Grand Champ, made him the only artist in the history of the Billboard Top 200 to have his first five albums debut consecutively at #1. Beyond iconic, DMX has been the voice of the hood since he first burst onto the scene as a representative of the street movement and record label Ruff Ryders. As hip-hop is assimilated into the cultural mainstream, it's time for the long overdue and much needed return of rap's prophetic visionary, DMX. The groundbreaking new album Year Of The Dog Again includes the single "Lord Give Me A Sign," as well as the blazin' track "We In Here."
profile.reviewText:
Whether DMX's sixth studio album (and debut offering on Sony) is his best album to date is questionable, but one thing that remains unquestionable is whether DMX can create great music. Enlisting helps from the likes of Swizz Beatz, Dame Grease and others on the production board, as well as plenty of guest artists from established veterans (Busta Rhymes, Styles P, Jadakiss, Amerie, etc.) to talented newcomers (singer Janyce, rappers Big Stan and Kashmir, etc.), DMX has come swinging hard with more hardcore raps on "Year Of The Dog...Again".

Personally, I haven't listened to any of his 5 previous albums, but if their lead single were anything to go by, I suspect many longtime fans of DMX's music will be disappointed with this release because DMX doesn't bother trying to do anything new in his music. As a man who's lived a very hard knock life -whether it be in the courts, behind bars, on the streets or with his inner demons- it's always nice to know that one of Hip-Hop's dopest rappers is still coming strong with uncompromised Hip-Hop that all real gangsta can either relate or ride to, but this studio effort brings nothing new to the table.

Nonetheless, highlights (standout just isn't the right word for any of these songs) can still be found if listeners are willing to look. On lead single "Lord Give Me A Sign", DMX's compelling rhymes asks for guidance from Jesus in a vulnerable (and almost preachy) manner over guitar-driven production, while also making room for some soulful choir background vocals towards the end. The piano-driven "Goodbye" has DMX wisely bids his farewells, sounding fully aware in his powerful lyrics and his almost-sing-rap-esque hook popularized by 50 Cent that anyone can die anytime, anywhere. "Blown Away" is another introspective moment where DMX breaks down the story of his life while Janyce's soulful vocals bless the lyrically confessional hook (Like the wind/ God will take/All my sins/ Blown away) in a Mary J. Blige-esque manner. The only highlights that don't have DMX showing any shades of vulnerability are the wildly pulsating "Come Thru (Move)", where the braggadocious rhymes of DMX & Busta rhymes are forcefully blasted over Dame Grease's addictively electric production, and "Walk These Dogs", which revels in it's awesome combination of faint rock guitar riffs, royal horns & swift, lively, hardcore rhymes from DMX & female guest rapper Kashmir. What makes the latter track special in its own way, however, is the way DMX & Kashmir brag in such a way that they do sound like real leaders who, like the title suggests, can (and will!) "walk these dogs".

Unfortunately, like I mentioned earlier in this review, DMX brings virtually nothing new to the table with the release, as exemplified by many of DMX's remaining tracks. "We In Here" & "I Run S**t" sound like bland retreads of previous hits, while "Give `Em What They Want" just plainly sucks due to stale rhymes. "Dog Love", DMX's "ode to the ladies", would've been an incredible track if he put more time and thought into his lyrics (And it was aiight, shorty was a thoroughbred/Like Billy, she ain't f**k, she just gave me he*d), especially considering the fact that guest vocalists Amerie & Janyce put their beautiful, soaring vocals on display on this otherwise disappointing track.

Ultimately, the highlights outweigh the disasters, which is why I gave this album the 3.5 it deserves. Not only that, but despite a lack of re-invention, DMX remains to be of one the realest rappers in the game right now! If you're a newcomer, cop this album. If you're long-time fans, either check the samples, read the lyrics sheets or download the tracks I suggested (a Bonus Behind-The-Scenes DVD should also be included).

5 Best Tracks:

"Lord Give Me A Sign"

"Goodbye"

"Come Thru (Move) (feat. Busta Rhymes)"

"Blown Away (feat. Janyce)"

"Walk These Dogs (feat. Kashmir)"

5 Worst Tracks:

"I Run S**t"

"We In Here"

"Dog Love (feat. Amerie & Janyce)"

"Give `Em What They Want"

"It's Personal (feat. Styles P & Jadakiss)"...COME ON JADAKISS, STEP YOUR GAME UP!
profile.summary: Unfortunately, 2006 Doesn't Belong To Dmx! :(

top_5.description: Take the best songwriters & the best singers, add the most exciting performers & the best all around personalities, throw in the hottest looks & the sexiest smiles, mix them all together & the finished product would probably sound a lot like CIARA.
top_5.reviewText:
As the First Lady of Crunk'n'B and a multi-talented individual with 3 consecutive smash hit singles (the Crunk'n'B female independence anthem "Goodies", the pulsating R&B/Pop club banger "1, 2 Step" & the grimy, street-edged anthem "Oh", featuring Petey Pablo, Missy Elliott & Ludacris respectively), I had high expectations of Ciara's debut album. Unfortunately, I was left rather disappointed.

Don't get me wrong...I absolutely love everything about Ciara -from her sweet vocals to her almost-unparalleled dancing skills to her beautiful looks and physique (although the vicious rumours questioning her true gender leave me rattled and bewildered)- but the album title says it all. The album's GOOD, but not GREAT! As a lot of people know, there's more to music than commercial success, looks and money, but this album doesn't seem to reflect Ciara's knowledge towards that. Ciara still has a nice voice, but when you put it next to other newcomers & veterans, you can see that she has a long way to go vocally, as it is entirely indistinctive.

However, there are still some other great tracks on the album (excluding the first 3 singles). "Thug Style" is a beautiful, mellow guitar ballad where Ciara angelically croons one minute before breaking out into a hypnotic lullaby the next. Not only that, but "Thug Style" also has some slow-dance appeal to it, which makes it a clear highlight. "The Title" is also another smooth slow jam dedicated to her lover, which also has an unusual old-school feel to it.

While the aforementioned tracks are delectable treats for every listener, there is also some inevitable musical sabotage. The boring-as-s*** "Other Chicks" clearly proves that fact, as does the overly generic and diluted dance tunes "Lookin' At You" & "Hotline", which lack the energy and distinctiveness of "Goodies", "1, 2 Step" & "Oh". It also pains me to say that the soothing ballad (and failed fourth single) "And I" is also a letdown, considering the fact that Ciara wrote the lyrics earlier on in her youth. Unfortunately, Ciara's emotional closeness and sweet vocals, combined with the beautiful acoustic guitar in the background, cannot redeem the overly clichd lyrics. Honestly, if you listen close enough, it'll make lyrically troubled singers like Ashanti look like poets (or at least better writers).

As I said before, Ciara's album is good, but not great. Nonetheless, it's worth your money, but I hope she steps her game up on her 2nd album. Best wishes to you Ciara.
top_5.summary: The title says it all :(

top_5.description: 50 CENT THE MASSACRE
top_5.reviewText:
Wow, I can't believe I almost considering buying this over Alicia Keys' sophomore album back when I was younger. Sure, Alicia Keys isn't as radio-friendly, offensive or "gangster" as 50 Cent, but I can easily appreciate the musicality, substance and personality of her music more than this "Pop-(c)rap(-tastic)" offering from 50 Cent. Long story short, "The Massacre", 50 Cent's multi-platinum sophomore album, is essentially a "Get Rich Or Die Tryin'" remake.

Once again, star-studded producers (Scott Storch, Eminem, Dr. Dre, etc.), pounding beats, addictive hooks, typically narrow subject matter (misogyny, materialism, etc.) and 50 Cent's aggressive rapping delivery are back in full force. And just like before, the guests are kept to a minimum, allowing the spotlight to shine (or the darkness to fall) on 50 Cent. There's long-forgotten R&B singer Olivia (pray to God she sees some kind of stardom this year) who is employed as the sexy support hook singer on the dreadful single "Candy Shop", a shameless, Scott Storch-produced slab of sleazy come-ons relating to typical sex fantasies and 50 Cent's physical self (I'm not going in-depth, you should know what I mean); her other appearance on "So Amazing", one of many pieces of worthless filler, is no better; Jamie Foxx completely belittles his own extraordinary singing talents on "Build You Up", a cheesy, literally unbelievable, bulls**t-feeding ladies joint; and rapper Tony Yayo sounds as useless as ever on the lacklustre "My Toy Soldier". Thankfully, he strikes gold with Eminem once again on "Gatman & Robbin", which is much like "Patiently Waiting" (from his debut album) - lacking substance, but lyrically/verbally complex and sonically thrilling, partially because of Eminem's solid, haunting production.

Unfortunately, 50 Cent isn't much better when he's by himself either. Registering the pitiful "Piggy Bank" as a legitimate diss track is insulting in its own self; the Dr. Dre-produced "Outta Control" and the Cool & Dre-co-produced lead single "Disco Inferno" are two misogynistic club cuts that put perfectly functional, appealing beats to complete waste; and practically everything else, especially the Scott Storch-produced, Middle Eastern-inflected third single "Just A Lil' Bit", fails on nearly every level. The only solo track where 50 Cent really shines is the laid-back "Ryder Music", where Hi-Tek's R&B-leaning production works surprisingly well with 50 Cent's more laid-back flow and (partially) substantial lyrics.

In conclusion, 50 Cent and "The Massacre" are essentially and structurally the same - you love it or you hate it. In my case, I choose the latter, hands-down. 1 star!

Best Tracks:

"Gatman & Robbin"

"Ryder Music"

"Hate It Or Love It (G-Unit Remix)"
top_5.summary: "The Massacre" - What An Appropriate Title!

top_5.description: BARKLEY GNARLS ST.ELSEWHERE
top_5.reviewText:
DJ/Producer Danger Mouse & rapper/singer/songwriter/producer/ex-Goodie Mob member Cee-Lo, collectively known as Gnarls Barkley, have joined forces to craft one of 2006's best and weirdest albums! What confuses me, however, is why their music is being labelled as Pop music.

Understandably, there are talented and creative forces in the world of Pop (Pink, Nelly Furtado, etc.), but the genre's generally the household of superficiality, mainstream predictability, talent-challenged Pop tarts and temporary heart-throbs. Unlike most run-of-the-mill Pop stars, Cee-Lo's vocals are strong, powerful, soulful and slightly raspy - the type that are easily capable of equalling, if not wilfully overpowering, Danger Mouse's insanely unconventional, upbeat production (see album opener "Go-Go Gadget Gospel", where Cee-Lo unsubtly wails with maddening passion over Danger Mouse's boisterous horns). Then of course there's the UK-record-breaking #1 smash hit "Crazy", where Cee-Lo contemplates mental insanity over a dark, eerie beat.

Speaking of contemplation, it's obvious that Cee-Lo & Danger Mouse put a lot of effort into this stellar collaborative effort. From the crazy production to the singing to the rapping to the thought-provoking lyrics to the diverse subject matter, Gnarls Barkley manage to successfully throw all of their wacky ideas into a rather brief 37-40min.-long album and balance everything out to perfection. This type of album sure as Hell wasn't meant to be tailor-made for the pre-teen set.

On "Necromancer", Cee-Lo pervertedly details his sickening love for necrophilia over suitably haunting production, while "Just A Thought", "Smiley Faces" & "Who Cares" -all three of which talk about depression, pain and/or contemplative suicide- best exemplify the album's lyrical complexity. On top of all this, there's an infectious cover of the Violent Femmes' "Gone Daddy Gone" - complete with bouncy xylophonic sound effects and electric guitar strings- and the schizophrenic "Transformer", where Cee-Lo rapidly raps and loudly sings the hook with the help of a few random (but different) vocal samples and/or effects, as well as Danger Mouse's super-fast production.

Well, does this album have any weaknesses? Believe it or not, this album really has no weaknesses. The comparatively short running time prevents the set from getting monotonous or self-indulgent (thanks for pointing that out AMG), and with just about no filler in sight, Gnarls Barkley have crafted a perfect debut album.

Only God knows what the f*** possessed these two nut-bags to create a concept album of such brilliance (though I doubt it was from "Feng Shui", as they stated on the track of the same name), but "St. Eslewhere" definitely a classic example of what can happen when artists motivate themselves enough to push musical boundaries in search of something more. 5 stars, easily!
top_5.summary: "St. Elsehwere" - A Great Place For Music To Be!

top_5.description: STONE JOSS MIND, BODY & SOUL
top_5.reviewText:
As Joss Stone's debut album "The Soul Session" indicated, she is a phenomenally talented singer - with those soulful, throaty, gritty, powerful vocals of hers, it would be perfectly normal to be shocked that such a beautiful voice could come from the mouth of a 16-year-old teenage "white" girl from London ( hate that "white"/"black" categorization stuff). Sure, "The Soul Sessions" was just an album full of cover songs, so originality was naturally dire, but that was not the point - the point of that album was to establish Joss Stone for the truly gifted artist she is, as well as her vocal skills. And much like "The Soul Sessions", "Mind, Body & Soul", the follow-up album and Joss Stone's first album that consists of entirely original material, serves the same purpose in a different way.

Apart from appearances from Betty Wright and Steven Greenberg and others, the list of producers is relatively superstar-free, and the guest list is completely empty, further emphasizing the fact that this album is all about Joss Stone. Then there's the fact that she co-wrote over half of the lyrical content on this album, including the first portion of the whole album that elevates this album into greatness.

"Right To Be Wrong", the album-opening track, is easily the best track on the album. The strong lyrics, which obviously relate to the song title, are just as captivating and penetrating as Joss Stone's vocal delivery, and the minimalist piano-guitar production add to the raw appeal of the song. Naturally, highlights are still abundant - her youthful energy and powerful vocals enliven tracks like the summery retro-70's/80's-pop anthem "Don't Cha Wanna Ride" and "You Had Me", a funk guitar-driven kiss off to a negligent, money-scabbing, dope-sniffing ex-lover; "Jet Lag" is hypnotic and mellow ballad with its smooth instrumentation and Joss Stone's smooth vocals; piano-driven R&B/Soul ballad "Spoiled" is drenched with emotion and regret; and "Less Is More" is a semi-brutally honest ode to a lover doing too much to please her, the song's heavy sentimentality pleasantly lightened by Reggae-flavoured production.

Unfortunately, by the time we're past the cheesy R&B/Gospel ballad "Security" and the contrastingly beautiful ballad (and late-album highlight) "Young At Heart", the album's quality heavily wavers. "Snakes & Ladders" is ridiculously original with its metaphorical lyrics about a complicated relationship, and the song's slightly catchy, but the weak production brings the track down; "Don't Know How" feels lifeless, formulaic and devoid of the passion that Joss Stone usually (and naturally) brings to some of her other tracks; and album closers "Killing Time" and "Sleep Like A Child" are two dreary ballad that wear out their welcome well before the 5+ minutes are fully up.

Another fault to this album is its substance. Apart from "Right To Be Wrong" and hidden track "Daniel", a passionate ode to her previously incarcerated criminal brother of the same name, it's all about relationships - the typical cycle of love, hate, like, etc. in typical relationships.

Nonetheless, "Mind, Body & Soul" is a pleasing album that shows more promise from a truly talented individual. 3.5 stars!

5 Best Tracks (IMO):

"Right To Be Wrong"

"You Had Me"

"Jet Lag"

"Young At Heart"

"Spoiled"
top_5.summary: Promising, But Not Fulfilling!

top_5.description: Includes 2 UK bonus tracks.
top_5.reviewText:
Considering Frankie J's immense musical talent, Mexican/Latin roots, beautiful falsetto (unlike many other male artists), the multiple comparisons to multi-talented mega-superstar Usher & the massive success of his Baby Bash-assisted smash hit single "Obsession (No Es Amor)", I was expecting a mind-blowing, stellar sophomore effort from him. Unfortunately, Frankie J does not fulfill my expectations. Instead, he delivers a formulaic set of music material to his fans consisting of a few spectacular tracks hidden under sweet -but ultimately forgettable- filler.

As minimally inspired as "The One" is, there are a few bright moments here & there. The smash hit single "Obsession (No Es Amor)" is a song that everybody should know by now, and explains the situation of being being lovingly obsessed with another girl. Baby Bash takes the time to drop an unnecessary verse, but it doesn't hurt or help the already-amazing track. Relatable subject matter, great vocals, a tiny bit of Latin, nice beat...enough said, the track's great, and it's global success testifies to that fact.

"How To Deal", Frankie J's minor second hit single, talks about the struggle of choosing between staying with the love of your life or leaving to pursue your dreams. Couples & lovers will be able to strongly relate to this song to a certain extent, and everything about the song pieces together effectively (vocals, lyrics, beat, emotion, etc.). "The One" is also another sweet ballad, pairing Frankie J & 3LW, and has hit single potential written all over it. The song's sweet, simplistic & laid-back, making it perfect for any occasion of love.

"Story Of My Life", the album's compulsory autobiographical ballad, is undoubtedly the best track on the album. Accompained by nothing more than some introductory violins, a guitar & some hand-clapping/clicking sound effects, Frankie J connects to his audience with soft, emotional vocals & universally relatable, inspiring, touching lyrics. Not only does Frankie J manage to portray his life story in a colourful manner, but he simultaneously manages to help heal the wounds of a hurting heart. You'd have to be majorly shallow to deny a track as masterful as this.

Every other song on this track is a take-it-or-leave-it affair. As good as "On The Floor" is, the song feels like something forcefully added in for the sake of variety. Not only that, but it looks bad on you when you have to get a materialistic C+ rapper like Paul Wall to do the more hard-edged portions of musical material. It's good to know that Frankie J isn't trying to sound full-on gangsta, but unfortunately, "On The Floor" reveals one of his biggest weaknesses...versatility. With his stupid pretty-boy looks, neo-soul/pop music & God knows what else, this leaves Frankie J in a limited space for creativity.

If you enjoy a sweet, simple listen, then this album is for you. If you're looking for something unpredictable, stellar & ambitiously driven, then skip this at all costs! "The One" is far too formulaic to satisfy those who look for something more revolutionary or incredibly creative.
top_5.summary: This isn't "The One"!

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "Vincent H. ONeil brings a wealth of life experience to his writing. He has worked as a private consultant to a software development firm, managed risk in a major corporation, created marketing campaigns, and worked as an apprentice librarian. His critically-acclaimed debut novel Murder in Exile was followed by three more books in the Frank Cole / Exile series: Reduced Circumstances, Exile Trust, and Contest of Wills. He has also published a military science fiction novel entitled Glory Main, under the pen name Henry V. O'Neil, as well as a horror novel entitled Interlands featuring his first female protagonist. He holds a bachelor of science degree from West Point and a master's degree from The Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy. You can read reviews and sample chapters of all his books at www.vincenthoneil.com". The summary of the review text is ""The Play's the Thing..."".
output:
In this book, the play's the thing indeed, and impresario and director Jerome Barron of Jerome Barron Players has developed an unusual twist on community-based theatre. He contracts with communities to write and perform a unique mystery play set locally and using local legends and stories in the plot. His writers arrive months before the performance and live openly in the community, absorbing the local atmosphere and soliciting stories and suggestions from residents as they write the play.

Other staff arrive on irregular schedules, surreptitiously planting clues to the mystery which are hotly debated on the  troupe's website forum. The actors rehearse several different endings, and no one but the director knows which one will finally be used in the sole performance.

Jack Glynn had been the first writer for the troupe, leaving only when fellow writer Ryan Berencourt stole his lover, actress Allison Green. Two years later, Ryan apparently commits suicide following a performance in California which resulted in the suicide of a real descendant of the murderer Ryan wrote into his play. Barron persuades Jack to finish writing the new play in progress despite the misgivings of private detective Wade Parker, the troupe's front man, who is suspicious of Ryan's 'suicide'. When Jack nearly dies while cross-country skiing, Wade is sure something is wrong.

The characterization was a little generic and the motive for the crimes seemed farfetched and weak; but the complexity of implementing the unique performance of this "traveling magic mystery show" and the town's wholehearted participation more than made up for these flaws. An unusual and interesting story!

profile.description: Paperback. Pub Date :2013-07-18 Pages: 330 Language: English Publisher: Macmillan Hardback Omes A rainy night. an Amish father returning home with his three children. a speeding car hurtling toward them out of nowhere What at first seems like. a tragic. but routine car accident suddenly takes on a more sinister cast as evidence emerges that nothing about the crash is accidental. But who would want to kill an Amish deacon and two of his children He leaves behind a grieving widow and a young son who clings to life in the intensive care wing of a hospital. unable to communicate. Desperate to find out who killed her best friends husband and why. Kate begins to suspect she is not looking for a reckless drunk. but instead is on the trail of a cold blooded killer in the heart of Painters Mill. It is a search that takes her on a chilling journey into the darkest reaches of the human...
profile.reviewText:
Amish Deacon Paul Borntrager is returning home one rainy evening with his three young children. Without warning, a pickup truck roars out of a blind intersection and smashes into the buggy, killing Paul, the horse, and two of his children. The truck does not stop.

When the dying Paul greets Painter's Mill police chief Kate Burkholder by name she realizes in horror that this is the family of her closest childhood friend, Mattie. When Kate tore herself away from her Amish family and community as a young woman, beautiful Mattie had stayed in the Plain Life, married Paul, and bore his children.

It was a curious accident scene. There were no skid marks from braking, and no debris from the vehicle except for a side-view mirror and part of a metal cotter pin. The vehicle must have blown through a stop sign at 80 miles an hour to have scattered the bodies and buggy debris so far. After painstaking reconstruction, the police finally conclude that it had not been an accident, but deliberate murder. Was it a hate crime, or something personal?

This is the fifth in the author's Kate Burkholder series, but the first I have read. Consequently, I don't know if the body found in the old grain elevator is a surprise to followers of the series; but it added a whole second thread, which remains unresolved, to the story. The story moved nonstop, and the histories of these two remarkable women and the secret burdens they each carry dwarfed the rather weak murder mystery. The book is written in the first person from Kate's perspective and in the present tense. While I often find this annoying in a novel, this one moved so fast that I quickly forgot about it. I genuinely wish the motive had been better developed and explored; there is a harrowing tale there.
profile.summary: Fascinating characters completely overshadow the story line

profile.description: M.K. Coker grew up on a river bluff in southeastern South Dakota. Part of the Dakota diaspora, the author has lived in half a dozen states, including New Mexico, but returns to the prairie at every opportunity. Website: www.mkcoker.com
profile.reviewText:
Bored and clicking around for a new police procedural, I happened on Dead White and was intrigued by the description. Among the many first novels I have read, no first book by any author ever took my breath away quite like this one did. It was assured, polished, and well plotted. The voice and setting were authentic and unusual. From sublime to ridiculous - I also really appreciated the lack of grammar and spelling errors so common in first efforts.

The story is well set up in the Product Description, so I won't rehash it. The newbie sheriff's insecurity and resentment of her more experienced uncle sometimes left me wanting to shake her (LISTEN, Karen!); but she and the relationship improve over the course of the book, while still leaving issues for the sequel. The weather is a major factor here, and the fierce Dakota winter was a vivid and welcome relief from the steamy New Jersey summer.

An astonishing new voice and story from the Heartland. Very well done!
profile.summary: Best first novel I have read

profile.description: The contemporary Lava coat rack is both sturdy and functional. The dark color marble base is heavy enough to hold multiple things and the first hooks are a kid friendly 42" high. profile.reviewText:
Nearly everyone in my house uses the back door, and the nearest closet is (gasp) twenty steps down the back hall, with the result that no one ever hangs coats up. They get piled on the furniture - or the floor! I looked at many coat racks before selecting this one, and am glad I found it. Assembly was easy - DH and daughter had it together in about half an hour. It was buried under coats, hats, and scarves within a few hours, and even the umbrellas I regularly knock down and trip over are safely stashed. So far, the tree is sturdy and stable under our none too gentle, real-world use. My only minor quibble is that the drip pan for the umbrellas could be a little larger. Still, if they do drip, it will be on the marble base, not the hardwood floor.

I may order another for our bedroom, for those "can be worn again but shouldn't be put back in the drawer with the clean clothes" items. A very good product at a fair price. What will they think of next?

profile.reviewText:
I've been interested in photography for a long time.  Movie making, however, has always been a challenge for me.  Think of your average home movie, simple recording of a vacation trip, including where you dropped the camera, or cleverly left it running in the back seat of the car.  Pinnacle Studio 18 is going to help, but at a price.

The price is the learning curve for the program, capacity for your computer, and patience with yourself and your clips.  Do not expect to make a feature length film over the first weekend.  Now a "SmartMovie", that, is a different story.

The benefits are the sense of accomplishment. The extra dimension of "film at eleven."  Creating tid bits to amaze the world of You Tube.  The family will actually enjoy seeing what the trip looked like.  And your popcorn bill may increase.  (definite sign of audience enjoyment)

The program is B I G.  The box says 5.8GB of HDD space for full installation.  Another way of saying that is it took my machine (brand new ASUS desk top)  a little better than half an hour to load the program from disc.  There are additional size, and time, requirements for training material.  Read the requirements if you have any question at all.

There appear to be four ways to learn the program, and I suspect you will wind up using bits of all four. The four that I saw were:  1 Explore, poke buttons get frustrated have another cup of coffee.
2. Users Manual identifies the major buttons to poke.  3. You Tube clips  4. Studio Back Lot.
Methods 2 and 3 are accessible through the help button which takes the form of a Question Mark ?  High left on the screen.  Select the "?" then select "User Manual" you then have access to You Tube "Pinnacle Studio Pro" with Maliek Whitaker and a PDF of a "paper" User Manual.  Studio Backlot with Paul Holtz, I suspect hopped out of the box with the program.  Both 2 and 4  are internet based.

You want to stay active with the program for the first couple of weeks.  While I don't fully understand the requirements yet, it appears that "Warranty" after the first two weeks from registration is an additional charge.  The same way with Studio Back Lot but after a longer period of time (45 days I think).  This may not be as bad as it sounds as long as you work to understand the program in the first couple of weeks.

If you haven't kept up with the changing world of video resolution there are some new definitions to learn.  The program does have some fail safes to get you going from the files that you have or that you create now.

I followed Studio Back Lot through the first three chapters and learned a lot.  I also allowed me to create my first "SmartMovie" a 30 second wonder complete with titling, scene selection, a sound track, and included a couple of still photographs for good measure.  It was fun and met with great "Critical Acclaim."  That means both Charming Wife and Daughter said "Hey dad, That's pretty good!"  I didn't mention that all I did was push the button that said Smart Movie.

I've looked at the first few Chapters of Studio Backlot and have gained a lot.  Learn about "Watch folders" and your sanity may be preserved.  I've looked at the first couple of Pinnacle Studio Pro and gained a better overall view of the program.

Nutshell, big program, looks like a lot of fun to be had, Be patient, and you can amaze your friends, neighbors and the You Tube community.

top_5.description: Paperback. Pub Date :2013-07-18 Pages: 330 Language: English Publisher: Macmillan Hardback Omes A rainy night. an Amish father returning home with his three children. a speeding car hurtling toward them out of nowhere What at first seems like. a tragic. but routine car accident suddenly takes on a more sinister cast as evidence emerges that nothing about the crash is accidental. But who would want to kill an Amish deacon and two of his children He leaves behind a grieving widow and a young son who clings to life in the intensive care wing of a hospital. unable to communicate. Desperate to find out who killed her best friends husband and why. Kate begins to suspect she is not looking for a reckless drunk. but instead is on the trail of a cold blooded killer in the heart of Painters Mill. It is a search that takes her on a chilling journey into the darkest reaches of the human...
top_5.reviewText:
Amish Deacon Paul Borntrager is returning home one rainy evening with his three young children. Without warning, a pickup truck roars out of a blind intersection and smashes into the buggy, killing Paul, the horse, and two of his children. The truck does not stop.

When the dying Paul greets Painter's Mill police chief Kate Burkholder by name she realizes in horror that this is the family of her closest childhood friend, Mattie. When Kate tore herself away from her Amish family and community as a young woman, beautiful Mattie had stayed in the Plain Life, married Paul, and bore his children.

It was a curious accident scene. There were no skid marks from braking, and no debris from the vehicle except for a side-view mirror and part of a metal cotter pin. The vehicle must have blown through a stop sign at 80 miles an hour to have scattered the bodies and buggy debris so far. After painstaking reconstruction, the police finally conclude that it had not been an accident, but deliberate murder. Was it a hate crime, or something personal?

This is the fifth in the author's Kate Burkholder series, but the first I have read. Consequently, I don't know if the body found in the old grain elevator is a surprise to followers of the series; but it added a whole second thread, which remains unresolved, to the story. The story moved nonstop, and the histories of these two remarkable women and the secret burdens they each carry dwarfed the rather weak murder mystery. The book is written in the first person from Kate's perspective and in the present tense. While I often find this annoying in a novel, this one moved so fast that I quickly forgot about it. I genuinely wish the motive had been better developed and explored; there is a harrowing tale there.
top_5.summary: Fascinating characters completely overshadow the story line

top_5.description: M.K. Coker grew up on a river bluff in southeastern South Dakota. Part of the Dakota diaspora, the author has lived in half a dozen states, including New Mexico, but returns to the prairie at every opportunity. Website: www.mkcoker.com
top_5.reviewText:
Bored and clicking around for a new police procedural, I happened on Dead White and was intrigued by the description. Among the many first novels I have read, no first book by any author ever took my breath away quite like this one did. It was assured, polished, and well plotted. The voice and setting were authentic and unusual. From sublime to ridiculous - I also really appreciated the lack of grammar and spelling errors so common in first efforts.

The story is well set up in the Product Description, so I won't rehash it. The newbie sheriff's insecurity and resentment of her more experienced uncle sometimes left me wanting to shake her (LISTEN, Karen!); but she and the relationship improve over the course of the book, while still leaving issues for the sequel. The weather is a major factor here, and the fierce Dakota winter was a vivid and welcome relief from the steamy New Jersey summer.

An astonishing new voice and story from the Heartland. Very well done!
top_5.summary: Best first novel I have read

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "The multi-talented Belkin Family RockStar provides an enormous 5.4 Amp total charging power across four USB ports. Thats enough power to charge two tablets and two smartphones, all at the same time. Any port can charge any device thanks to an intelligent smartchip, which recognizes the connected device automatically. For tablets that means optimal charging at 2.4 Amps. Wall-mountable and boasting a ten foot cable for convenient placement, this charging hero will make power struggles at home a thing of the past.". The summary of the review text is "a bit pricey but may save you some money on family therapy bills...".
output:
I like this Belkin Family Rockstar (4-Port).  When I read their product description "this charging hero will make power struggles at home a thing of the past" I could relate to that with a chuckle because earlier that day my 13 year old son had just thrown a fit before school when he grabbed his school ipad from a random charger and saw that it had barely charged overnight...he then proceeded to rant about how his little sister took his ipad charger and he had to then find some other crappy charger that didn't work.  Well to be honest he had a point - alot of older chargers are 1 AMP output and tablets these days along with some other devices take 2.1 AMPs.  For the layperson it's hard to tell what charger has what AMPs...I'm actually contemplating getting rid of my various 1 AMP chargers that aren't original equipment just to reduce this type of "charger rage".  Technology is great but it's a bit of work to keep up with the dynamics...

Enter this Belkin Rockstar.  Really the key here is this thing has 4 ports and 5.4 AMPs total power...its got "SmartChip" built in to provide the right power to various devices.  ie, most tablets currently can charge at 2.1AMPS - you can charge 2 tablets at the same time on this Belkin and also charge a Smartphone at ~1 AMP.  Or you could charge 4 smartphones at 1 AMP each, etc, etc.  That capability is really key to reducing family charger rage and increasing peace, love, and happiness in the family (well at least a little bit).  So I set this Belkin up in a central location, plugged it in, stuck a note on it that said "you move this & you die" and there has been no drama since then (at least on this topic).  This thing charges my son's ipad faster than any other charger in the house.

Build quality is excellent - 4 port unit is on the physically larger side but that also helps keep the charger from sliding around.  Cord plugs into the charger and wall outlet - I do wish it had a "flat plug" instead of standard full profile plug which would make it easier to plug in behind furniture.  The Belkin brand has been pretty reputable based on my experiences which makes me feel a bit more confident about the "SmartChip" not being Dumb and frying all my devices.

In conclusion, Belkin Family Rockstar 4-Port is a welcome addition to my humble abode - works well for my family's needs and potentially saves on therapy bills for whomever down the road.  At current price of $51 a bit on the pricey side relative to other chargers out there but also lives up to its billing by being able to accommodate family usage better than most other chargers that I have used in the past.  Overall rating from me of 4-STARS in consideration of price/value.

profile.reviewText:
I've got these Panasonic wireless earbuds in red.  I've got quite a few Panasonic earbuds & headphones - in my experience they are a very reputable brand in this space.  For these newest wireless earbuds I sum up my feelings by saying "good but not great".

What I like:
 ++Lightweight = Comfy.  Both a plus and a minus (covered later).  On the plus side these are one of my lightest weight wireless bluetooth headphones...hence they are very comfortable to wear because it doesn't feel like I have any fishing weights dangling from my ears.
 ++Battery life pretty decent for being tiny/lightweight.  I'm getting about 4 hours battery life which I can live with consider the light weight that I like.
 ++Bluetooth was easy for me to synch.  Intuitive to connect and worked on the first try (yes this should be expected but I've had some difficult experiences before...particularly on some generic brands).

What could be better:
 --Lightweight = A Bit Flimsy.  The wires are skinny...not sure how long they will hold up.  Being lightweight and not ruggedized they don't work well for me when working out...they tend to bounce around during physical activity.  I've got some other wireless hybrid earbuds that grip my ears better and more effective for working out.  What I like to use these Panasonics for is at my workdesk...the lightweightness makes then very comfy to wear and since the most exercise I ever get at work is spinning my chair 180 degrees I don't have to worry about the headphones getting jostled.
 --Sound quality not that great IMO.  Certainly suitable to listen to music but sound is a bit "tinny"...maybe also a byproduct of lightweightness.  I've got some other earbuds (Panasonic wired included) that sound much better (but most cost more too).

So in summary at current price I think these are "good not great".  The best feature is the lightweight wireless aspect.  Sound quality ok, durability concerns.  3-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: The best feature is the lightweight wireless aspect...

profile.description: This Product is Ultra bright LED's. Screws onto valve stem like a valve cap. Motion activated. Extra batteries included .Made in China.
profile.reviewText:
Bought this on Amazon and have been using for a few weeks.  I usually put on lighted valve caps on the family bikes when getting near dark (in addition to standard lights).

These valve caps are motion sensing which means they only turn on when they are in motion which is nice in theory from a battery saving perspective.  But in reality, my specific item purchased does not always light up when we are cycling down the road...therefor not very useful and frustrating as well.  Expectation is that it should work all the time when my wheels are moving, not some of the time or only if I bunnyhop the bike...otherwise no point in buying.

I bought a generic version on ebay for 1/3 the price and that item has always lighted up when cycling/ wheels spinning.  Hence, 1 star for this item I purchased on Amazon.  I hope you found my review helpful.

profile.reviewText:
With laws these days requiring hands-free cellphone in cars if you are yapper you should have some kind of hands free device.  Alot of newer cars have built-in blue tooth hands free but if you're car doesn't then you should get this type of device.

I compared my use of this Parrot Minikit(+) and about $80 to my other hands-free unit which is a Jabra Freeway (about $120).

Overall, the Parrot met my basic needs but I still prefer my Jabra Freeway.

Good:
 -The Parrot synched easy for me with my Android cellphone, contacts downloaded.
 -Small size is nice to fit on car vizor, build quality seems good.

Not So Good:
 -On/Off button not the best ergonomics - user has to find the smaller button instead of the larger.
 -Sound volume too low for me - if the windows are closed it is fine but if any are cracked it gets difficult for me to hear.
 -My least favorite is the voice recognition and I stopped trying to use it - "Accept" vs "Reject" doesn't work to well for me (I think it is because the end of the words have similar "t" sound).

In conclusion, if this Parrot was my only hands free then I find it serviceable.  However, I like using my Jabra Freeway more (none of the gripes) - worth the extra $$ IMO.

I bought this Mintek DTV-265-D 26" this weekend because I liked the price, the built-in DVD, and the styling (in that order).

Initial Reaction:  I was immediately disappointed when I hooked the Mintek up at home, especially when I compared it to my 2-year old Sony WEGA LCD 23" runnig in another room.

Picture:  The non-HDTV cable picture I tried on the Mintek is not very good...no comparison versus my Sony.  The picture was just not that sharp or bright compared to the Sony...it was dull to watch.

Sound:  The sound on the Mintek is incredibly bad...my 13" old TV has better sound.  The sound is very "tinny" and weak and detracted from enjoying TV show (especially MTV).

Built-In DVD:  The Mintek built-in DVD player takes very long to load and makes all kinds of weird noises.  When the movie finally did play the picture was very good/sharp so I'll give them credit for that.  But later on it was again difficult and lengthy to switch back over from TV to DVD.

I fiddled around with the Mintek throughout the day but was unable to make any improvements on my issues.

Conclusion:  I'm packing up the Mintek and returning it to the store this week.  I'm going to spend the extra money and get a brand with higher end quality/performance (probably the Panasonic or Sony 26").  The biggest eye opener for me was comparing the Mintek side-by-side with my older Sony...no comparison and makes me appreciate the Sony more.

I gave the Mintek 2 stars instead of 1 star since it was the lowest price TV so you can't have too unrealistic of expectations.
profile.summary: You get what you pay for

profile.description: ZAGG Rugged Folio Case, Durable, Hinged with Detachable Backlit Keyboard for iPad Mini & Mini Retina - Black OPEN BOX
profile.reviewText:
My family has been using this ZAGG Rugged Folio Case for iPad Mini for about 1 month now and this is a very nice product.  My son primarily uses it for school with his ipad mini - the school permits the kids to bring their tablets for school purposes and as a matter of fact alot of the kids have this type of keyboard case for their tablets.  Pop you tablet in and presto - pretty much a laptop.

I would say this ZAGG is a premium-type keyboard case - the price is on the high side (currently $138) relative to some other options out there but the good news is the quality and features are also on the high side (as you would hope for higher priced products).  Some things I like:
 +Most importantly the case fits an ipad mini very nicely and offers good protection for the ipad when closed (ie, a necessity to survive the chaos inside a kids school backpack).  Side note - I've also used this keyboard case with a few of my 7 inch android tablets which are slightly smaller than the 7.9" ipad tablet - not an exact fit for my other tablets as a protective place but the screens do stay in place for typing and the bluetooth connectivity works with them as well.
 +The keyboard is a premium/high quality keyboard.  The keys are nice to the touch and have backlighting (I wish more of my computer stuff had this).  The keyboard has a battery that we charged on first use but haven't need to charge since (the instructions say the battery lasts up to 2 years between charges - hey if I get one year out of it I am still very impressed).
 +Build quality excellent/ premium as I mentioned.  Has held up well thus far with my son toting this thing around school.
 +Usability is plug-n-play.  Turn on your bluetooth and good to go.

On the "cons" side the only things I would note right now are the higher price (currently $138) relative to some other keyboards out there and the fact that it makes your ipad weight alot more (keypad+keypad battery) - but if you would like a keyboard there is going to be extra weight from that and you can always take your ipad out of the case for reading, etc.

Overall a quality product that does a good job fulfilling its mission of making it faster/easier to type with a tablet.  4-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value (at lower pricepoint I would give it 5-STARS).
profile.summary: a quality product that does a good job fulfilling its mission

profile.description: The World's Smallest Cup Inverter, the 180-Watt 12-Volt Cup Inverter from Energizer will allow you to power your mobile devices in your car, boat or RV. This cup inverter is ultra compact, plugs into your vehicle's cigarette lighter socket or attaches to a car battery and fits securely in most vehicles' cup holders. With 4 USB ports and 1 standard North American outlet, you can run and charge up to 5 devices at once, keeping you connected wherever you go.
profile.reviewText:
I've put this Energizer cup inverter (aka, personal device power supply for your car) through some real life tests and I like this device.

First off the form factor is awesome - it fits in a car's cupholder which gives it a nice secure spot instead of sliding around.  Second, it's not just the 4 USB's that are nice, the key is the actual electric outlet so you can plug in your laptop PC that doesn't run from USB...this part is key for my family roadtrips (eg; kids able to use laptops hence less effort spent on fighting).  Third, since it's got multiple outlets more than one kid (& parent) can charge their phones/tablets at the same time) - resulting of further reduction of squabbling while on the road.  Build quality and durability seem good (I will update my review if this changes).

The only con I see thus far is the fact I noticed the USB doesn't charge up our phones/tablets as fast as their dedicated chargers (not sure if it is because multiple outlets are being used or overall energizer not optimized to each device as much).  At any rate, for me the pros far outweigh the cons and at $35 dollars I think this energizer is a good value.  My overall rating is 4-stars (I deducted one star for slower usb charging) and a big help to making the family vacation roadtrip a bit more relaxing (note: my comments apply to "roadtrip" vacation phase only, not "shared family hotel room" phase which is a story for another day).
profile.summary: Makes the Family Vacation Roadtrip a little more bearable

profile.description: Bring music to your adventures with a compact, rugged and easily carried speaker that can be strapped to any bag. Anti-clip technology gives better sound for its size. When you want more just pull it open. Music lasts for half day.
profile.reviewText:
Search "bluetooth portable speaker" on Amazon and there are currently 80,000 product listings - this Philips Flex BT2000B joins a very crowded field.

In my usage of this Philips Flex - it's competent enough for a small portable bluetooth speaker - probably too pricey at current $40 relative to many other competitive offerings.

Here's a couple of specs I dug for that aren't currently listed in the online details:  Rated Output power is 2W (Watts) RMS.  Internal battery size is 500 mAh (Lithium Polymer).

My user notes:
 +I do like the form factor.  Small, collapsible, good build quality.  I won't hang it around my neck like Flavor Flav but my daugher will.
 +I like the usability.  Simple, intuitive controls.  Easy bluetooth synch on my HTC One phone.
 +The output sound is clear but probably slightly underpowered at the 2 watts output (5 watt output is not uncommon in this range).  But just to keep reality in check - no speaker in this class is going to bump the walls during your house party.
 + The battery did last me 10 hours+ which is surprising because it's pretty small at 500 mAh - probably related to lower side watt output - ie, better battery life.

In summary, good quality and usability, competent sound if not slightly underpowered which helps the battery life, at current $40 price not best bang-for-my-buck.  Overall 4 STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Competent but not best bang-for-my-buck...

profile.description: 360 of rich, balanced sound with Ring Radiator Technology, Multiroom Compatible, Bluetooth, OLED Display, Tap and Swipe Speaker Top for Easy Control
profile.reviewText:
My review is for the Samsung WAM5500 speaker - better known as the "R5".  There are R1, R3, and this R5 speaker - the bigger the R means the bigger the size of the dedicated woofer (R5 the biggest of the three).  This R5 speaker is touted as "omni-directional" sound from the two speakers contained - this means the sound quality benefits most when placed centrally in a room (as opposed to placing in a corner where the sound loses some of its impact.

I've invested in a pretty nice Sonos multi-room setup and this Samsung R5 reminds me of the Sonos concept - load up your house with speakers and then control them all with an app (love the concept).  I currently only have one of these Samsung's but I still put it through the paces.  Samsung app easy enough for me to download/use/play...also bluetooth option available which was easy to get up and running.

The actual R5 speaker is very attractive/sleek with good build quality.  One feature this R5 has that my Sonos do not have is a nice LCD display at top of speaker for easy access to some basic features.  I think the overall sound quality of this R5 is very good - on par with my other similar priced speakers - the omni-directional sound does sound very good (if you are able to place the speaker more centrally in your room)...this R5 also has very good bass/punch due to the decent sized dedicated woofer.

What would be nice that this speaker does not have is a built in battery so you can take it with you when some decent portable tunes are needed.

At current price of $398 this Samsung R5 is not cheap (check around for pricing - I saw some lower sales pricing out and about on the web).  Pricey but inline with this type of wifi whole home setup trend these days.  Ultimately the true benefit from these type of speakers comes from procuring multiple units and spreading them around your house - then controlling them with your app - ie, have them playing in a few rooms or "party mode" - all rooms.  From what I've seen this Samsung is a decent enough choice to build out your "whole home" system - particular if you're already invested in alot of other Samsung equipment (extra connectivity with Samsung TV's, etc) - this is assuming that Samsung continues to invest in and expand the ecosystem (I imagine they would as they are a very large company).

So in conclusion - attractive looking speaker, easy to use via app or bluetooth, sounds great with good bass/punch (especially if  location kept away from room corners), nifty LCD screen on top, expandable as part of "whole home" system.  A tad pricey at $398 relative to some other very good competition out there such as Sonos but all in all the R5 is a solid choice...4-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Samsung R5 - solid option in the "whole home system" arena...

profile.description: Give yourself a power boost! BoostTurbine4000 from Eton is a durable back-up battery with a hand turbine power generator that provides power when you need it most. For everyday or emergency use, BoostTurbine4000 enables you to charge your mobile device anytime, anywhere. Fast and efficient, in one minute the hand turbine power generator can produce enough power for about 4 minutes of talk time and a few critical texts. When fully charged, BoostTurbine4000 fully charges most smartphones twice. BoostTurbine4000 is made of tough but lightweight aluminum and with its sleek and elegant design it's compact enough to fit in your pocket. BoostTurbine4000 features a Micro-USB DC input to use with most smartphone chargers and a high output (2.1A) USB port for charging most mobile devices, including tablets. Press button to see LED indicator of battery charge level. BoostTurbine4000 is completely self-contained and it's all you need for an on-the-go-power solution.
profile.reviewText:
I brought this Eton rechargeable battery pack with me on a recent business trip along with two other smaller (and lighter battery packs).  Of the 3, the Eton provides me the most extra juice - fully recharging my Samsung Galaxy S4 from an almost dead starting point (my other two battery packs can't do that).  Of course I certainly hope the Eton provides me the most juice - this thing is big and heavy almost like a brick...too be honest probably a bit too heavy for me to tote around in my backpack on my biz trip for something that I only needed a few times.

The hand crank is the bonus feature on this Eton.  If I had been stuck in the wilderness this is the only one of my 3 battery packs that would have saved me.  It's hard to quantify the handcrank effectiveness but I did try it out when the Eton was dead and I did muster some juice after 5 minutes of cranking (plus a good wrist workout).  One other thing that happened with my Eton on my biz trip - the micro USB receptacle on the Eton became slightly bent somehow...I have to lean the Eton a certain way to get it to recharge.

Overall, a big brick of a power source - if you need extra power then this could fit the bill (eg; the beach, hiking, etc).  A bit too heavy to tote around for daily use.  At $90 a bit pricey (my other two smaller power sources run $30 each and also have dual functions).  Overall I rate this 3-stars in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Big like a brick, provides lots of juice

profile.description: New NEAT Widget B Desktop USB Microphone that has a clear, full-range 96kHz/24 bit audio is a must have for anyone and everyone.
profile.reviewText:
My family has been using this Neat "Widget A (the green one)" microphone and we have to say it is pretty Neat.  What do these type of microphones get you beyond the cheapie plastic free microphone that comes with some PC computers?  The answer is much better recording clarity...so if better recording clarity for whatever reason then you'll want to step up to a PC mic such as this.  I use this thing for work/podcast-type recording stuff but who really hogs this mic is my 9-year old daughter to lay down some singing vocal tracks (aspiring American Idol contestant - lord help me).  Notables on this product by me:
  ---Good brand.  This brand called "Neat" is a division of the famous Gibson Guitars...so if it sounds like a random startup brand there is a bit of assurance by having it backed by a well known brand in music with the assumption they will want to build products that keep within their good reputation.k  These Neat Widget microphones were released for sale in the November'2015 timeframe so these are a pretty new product.
  ---Good design, quality, and usability.  This Neat Widget is advertised for Windows and Mac PC's.  I use this on a Windows7 laptop - I'm glad to say this was plug'n'play for me.  I plugged it in and it worked great right off the bat.  One of the big selling features of this Widget is the design aesthetics...they certainly look whimsical and not boring on your desk.  Choice of Widget A/B/C looks is up to you.  The quality of the mic is excellent...nice materials, appears durable, and very substantial in size sitting on your desk (large mic area easy to talk in to).

I'm a bit unclear if there are actual usability differences in the Widget A/B/C versions beyond the physical looks/colors.  Currently it doesn't specify any of this info on the Amazon site...I did see a few articles on the web that mentioned each Mic version was slightly tuned more for podcasting or singing vocals...hopefully they can clarify this point in the future on the product info.  My guess is even if there was slightly different tuning for each that the average person (such as myself) would still not be able to tell the difference when listening to actual recording results.

In summary, if you're looking to upgrade your PC Mic then this Neat Widget is a good choice.  At current price of $99 this seems a good value when perusing other offering out there in the same price range.  This Neat has the legacy of a good brand (Gibson) behind it.  The design is attractive with good build quality.  Most importantly the mic is easy to start using in my experience and the recorded results are good.  Overall 5-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: (Widget A) -Interesting look, well made, easy to use, good recorded results...

profile.description: This DJ-inspired headphone creates powerful sound and bass. With the rotating and soft cushioned ear shells, you will get a perfect listening experience on the go.
profile.reviewText:
I've been slowly getting to appreciate over-ear headphones more - maybe it's to block out the sound of my screaming kids (and/or wife).  Anyway, these Philips SHL3060's (I refuse to say "DJ Style") are a welcome addition to my over-ear headphone collection and they've done a pretty decent job thus far at providing me a little sanctuary amidst the chaos (as long as I keep my eyes closed).

Pricepoint-wise I noticed these Philips seem to be all over the map - I've seen them as low as $25 and as high as $44 depending on the retail outlet, the color, and timing (note:  Target currently has them for $25).  My assumption is these are headphones in the $25 pricepoint range thus somewhat comparable to a very good value-priced headphone Sony MDRZX100/110 (~$20).  To my layman ears the sound is pretty comparable to my Sony's which is good - crisp sounds, decent bass.  Comfort-wise these Philips are slightly less comfortable than my Sony because the Philips rattle around more due to the extra "fold flat" joint.  The extra fold-flat joint is both a blessing and a curse.  It's a blessing when you need headphones that fold extra compact if you don't have much space in your bag - I think you do pay the price for this option though because the headphones rattle around a bit more because of this extra folding joint - my preference would be to do without the extra fold so I have the extra rigidity.

So to summarize in a nutshell - these are a competent offering in the $25 pricepoint range - they are pretty comfortable although they could use a bit more rigidity, the sound quality doesn't dazzle me but is good for this pricepoint, they are fairly attractive (I have the black color though my first choice would be the white), they do a pretty good job of blocking out outside sound such as screaming wives & kids.  Overall 4-STAR rating for me in consideration of price/value at $25 (3 stars if you pay $40+).
profile.summary: Pretty good value headphones (if you don't overpay)...

profile.description: Go for the ultimate trophy! Deer Drive: Legends takes you to the far corners of the earth where you will go after wild animals rarely seen by the human eye, some even believed to be extinct! profile.reviewText:
I've actually played some decent hunting games - there is a fun one at Chuck E Cheese that my son play once in awhile that has some interesting challenge levels and team play.

But for a hunting game Deer Drive Legends is dull.  Not alot of moving around in the game - more like target range shooting gallery.  I wasn't that impressed with visual quality - kinda jerky and nothing compelling.  Control movements are clunky.  Repeatable fun factor is low and this is the most important thing - my 10 year old son played it for about 20 minutes and then no interest to try again (even though 10 year old boys usually love anything to do with guns and hunting).

Overall 2-stars - price way too high at $25+ relative to the competition and the complexity of the game, from what I can tell the repeat play factor is very low for most gamers.
profile.summary: Hunt for a better game

profile.reviewText:

profile.description: Toaster Pro wirelessly connects smartphones, tablets, PCs and Macs to easily share, stream and transfer content. It can be used as a portable travel router, can act as a Wi-Fi repeater to extend the reach of your wireless network and even recharge your mobile devices through its built-in battery.
profile.reviewText:
I stay in overseas hotels once in awhile that only have a wired internet connection - very frustrating since you can't use your phone/tablet wifi while in your room.  Last year I actually got so frustrated that while at the hotel I purchased a top selling ranked travel wifi router on Amazon UK and had it overnight shipped to my hotel room - it was well worth it and I still use that travel wifi (TP-Link Nano @ $19 USD).

So I was very happy to add this Alpheus Toaster Pro to my collection since it actually lists more features than my basic TP-Link Nano.  I used both overseas within the past one month and I'll share my observations on the Alpheus Toaster Pro:

What I like about the Alpheus Toaster Pro:
 +Advertised Features.  On paper it has lots of sexy features - kind of a swiss army knife of travel routers.  Not just a basic wifi router (like my TP-Link).  Beyond basic wifi the Alpheus has ability to stream for your small group including from SD Card slot.  Alpheus has a built in battery to provide emergency juice for your mobile device - always needed at some point while traveling.
 +Build Quality.  The Alpheus does appear to be well built and solid.  It's small but still at least 2x bigger than my TP-Link Nano (because of the card slots, battery, etc).
 +Easy wifi.  The Alpheus wifi was easy for me to get up and running - plug in, recognize that wifi connection, put in password written on bottom (recommend to change password to your own).  The wifi provided good enough speeds in my hotel room - pretty comparable connection vs my TP-Link from my usage.

What Could Be Better about the Alpheus Toaster Pro:
 -Usefulness of features.  In reality - the key feature of the Alpheus is the wifi router - for me I use this about 95% of the time and the other features about 5% of the time.  The streaming network is fairly slow and I don't really use it that often.  The battery is small capacity (1250mAh) - I have a few dedicated recharge batteries that are 2500mAh (around $20 each) and they still don't fully recharge my phone or tablet - the 1250mAh is for brief emergency power.
 -Price.  $99 is steep price for travel wifi - my TPLink Nano is just as good of a travel router and smaller form factor - for $19.  The second most valuable feature is the recharge battery - larger dedicated battery can be purchased for $20.  The other features will rarely be used by most people.  So for $39 total I can get a good travel wifi that is smaller and a larger backup battery - it is up to you if the rest of the features are worth the extra $60.

Overall - I have used this Alpheus Toaster Pro (mainly for wifi) and it has worked fine for me.  Current price too high relative to other options available - 3-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Decent enough but are the additional features beyond WiFi worth the extra $80?

profile.description: Goggles with facial soft silicone which ensures perfect adaptability to a wide range of facial profiles. Ideal for swimming, swimming, triathlon and water sports for all. I really like these Cressi Skylight goggles for casual swimming - I can't go au naturel because I wear contact lenses.  What I really like about these things is that they are like a comfortable Muumuu for my eyes which is a good thing.  I'm not sure if my eyeballs have gotten fatter as I've gotten older (probably) but the old school tiny goggles dig into my eye sockets and hurt worse than ever.  Enter these Cressi's - ahhhh.

I really like the fit on these Cressi's as well - the straps are very adjustable around your noggin and they create a very good vacuum seal that stays on when I swim casually (I can't speak for competitive swimming). profile.description: Enjoy fresh coffee every day with this elegantly designed French coffee press. Product features a no-drip spout and the large size accommodates 2-3 standard coffee cups.
profile.reviewText:
I've been using this "Francois et Mimi" french press for about a month now and I like it.  First off, I like the stainless steel as opposed to some glass french presses that I've had in the past and broke pretty quickly...the stainless steel on this "Mimi" seems like it should hold up better for me.  The stainless steel also looks attractive and the overall design of this "Mimi" is a good blend of contemporary and traditional that will look good in any home.  Double-wall is always a great feature to provide insulation to keep your coffee hot for longer and its worked well for me.

I've always preferred french press coffee to drip.  French press is less of a hassle to make for me (just add coffee, layer in water, press down to separate coffee - drink and enjoy).  Plus french press usually tastes better to me and this Mimi is no exception to my experience - minimal coffee grain leakage after using separator - a good cup of coffee to get my day started right.  At $50 I think this is a good value - 5 stars from me.
