profile.description: Everybody loves a bright white smile. Safely enhance your smile every day without giving up the foods and drinks you love! The Philips Sonicare HealthyWhite+ rechargeable toothbrush is proven to remove up to 100% more stains for whiter teeth in only 1 week versus a manual toothbrush.TROUBLESHOOTING STEPS :If the electric toothbrush does not power up, Ensure the correct button is being pushed (power button vs. mode button). The mode button will not turn the handle on. Reinstall the brush head as it is shown in your toothbrush users manual If there is not a brush head on the handle it may not be easily heard. Try placing a brush head on the handle and turning it on. Place the handle in the charger and charge for 24 hours before turning it back on
profile.reviewText:
Any preventative investment for dental care is almost always worth it - any dental work required will require more $$ and more time (not to mention good old fashion pain & suffering) - multiply that by Total Cost of Ownership over your life for tuneups, replacements, emergencies for cracked fillings, etc, etc, etc.  So at current price of $105 this SonicCare HealthyWhite+ is well worth it in my book - just for the fact that it gets my 9 year old daughter brushing her teeth more.  She tries her best but her penchant for secret late night (notso)Jolly Rancher candies (as evidenced by crumpled wrappers under her bed) has resulted in some unfortunate dental work for her (and hundreds of $$ out of pocket for Dad even after dental insurance coverage).  Besides the fact that sonic toothbrushes are clinically proven (if what I read is accurate) to do a better job than the old fashioned elbow grease toothbrushes - the timers are also useful for my daughter (who tends to rush) - total timer alert after 2 minutes, 30 second "quad" timer to alert change location in mouth...these timers really help my daughter brush better and hopefully that will show in her future dental checkups.

As for me, I use the Sonic too - my dentist is a great guy and is a great source for local fishing tips but the less I see of him and his drill the better.  You may be thinking "gross, this weirdo man is sharing a toothbrush with his daughter" - well I'll have you know that I use the adult diamonhead brush and I bought her a separate kidshead brush which also fits onto the same base - so shame on you for ass-uming.  The actual soniccare unit is great - lighter than my old one, easy to operate, battery life better than ever - several weeks.  This model comes with nice travel case.  This toothbrush has multiple modes but from what I've read "clean" mode is the most effective mode you should be using (which also means a soniccare model next pricepoint down would be fine as well if it still has quadtimer feature).

Overall, a no brainer.  If you're not dentally gifted and you're subjected to dental work - what have you got to lose by using a better toothbrush (sidenote - your manual toothbrush was in use before man invented flight).  I'm amazed by the range of model #'s in the Sonic lineup - really for me the key features to have are "clean" mode and "quadtimer" which I've noticed are features offered (as of now) on next model down with lower pricepoint.  Still - whatever the model# - a very worthwhile investment if it helps reduce your dental work.  5-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Are you still using the same manual toothbrush technology in place before man invented flight!?

profile.description: Smash, bash and battle with the fast and furious Air Hogs Smash Bots! Go head-to-head against your friends in an epic two-player face-off in the Smash Bots arena. profile.reviewText:
These Air Hogs Smash Bots were put the test by my 9 year old daughter (and then her 13 year old brother had to jump in to challenge her).  The concept sounds cool, the reality ok but not quite as cool.

Once batteries loaded and units operational my kids headed into battle. What could be better:

  -Replayability - my kids got pretty bored of this pretty fast - they quit playing after an hour and haven't tried again since.  Thus I'm going to say ideal ages are younger than 9.

In summary - good build quality, takes too many batteries, limited ability to control robots, replayability probably best for kids under 9.  At $50 current price kinda pricey considering all these factors though around the same price of  a new release video game if you think of it that way - overall rating from me is 3-STARS in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Probably best for ages under 9...

profile.description: You can power up both now with the newest Cobra JumpPack CPP 8000. Small enough to carry it with you anywhere you go, easily stowing it away in a handbag, briefcase, or even a pocket and weighing in at just under 10 ounces, it is one of the most-compact and portable power packs while offering dual capabilities of mobile-device charging and vehicle jumpstarting, including a range of cars, SUVs, motorcycles, outboard boat engines, etc. multiple times. With a form factor that is 40 percent smaller than its predecessor, the CPP 8000 model is the perfect companion for travel, outdoor, safety and multi-purpose use. The sleek and attractive new model now offers added built-in protection circuitry including short circuit protection, reverse charge, over-charge and reverse polarity protection. The unit holds approximately 85 to 90 percent of its charge for up to eight months.
profile.reviewText:
I think everyone should have one of these types of devices in their car as a backup battery if your car won't start.  This Cobra JumPack is not much bigger than a smartphone so it fits easily in the glovebox.  It comes included with jumper cables and car charger so all inclusive for emergency needs...it even has a mini LED flashlight bulb built in as well in case you need it.  This a high quality lithium cobalt battery that is advertised as holding its charge for several months - but be sure to recharge it regularly because if/when you need it that means your car battery will not be available to recharge the JumPack.  Not to mention it's just handy to have a backup battery charger for your (or your fighting kids) mobile devices like smartphones/tablets - and this Cobra JumPack recharges at higher 2.4Amp speeds which is great.  I just took an overseas business trip a few weeks ago and this battery recharger was incredibly handy many times in the trains/planes/automobile phases of my journey (note to self to make sure I put this Cobra back in my car glovebox).

Quality-wise I am impressed with the build of this product - well made and appears durable.  Design wise very easy to use - just hit the button to turn on the power and there is auto shutoff after use.

Battery capacity:  For the non-techies the "6000mAh" is the capacity of the battery (the higher the number the bigger the charge held).  To put the 6000mAh size in perspective most smartphones are around 2000mAh.  6000mAh is not that big for a backup battery - there are many batteries out there with 10000+ mAh but the Cobra JumPack 6000mAh is big enough to do the job - it's advertised as being able to jumpstart your car at least several times before needing a recharge...and while bigger mAh capacity is good it also comes at the expense of bigger/heavier physically...so I think this Cobra 6000mAh strikes a good balance of having sufficient capacity in a reasonably sized form factor.

The only knock as of now I can mention about this product is the current price of $89 is on the higher side (up to ~$20+) relative to some similar spec (jumpstart capable) competitive options I see on Amazon (albeit many are from brands I have never heard of).  My experience with Cobra Electronics is that it is a reputable brand with good quality and design - which is important for a device such as this that you may be counting on should the emergency need arise.  All things considered this is a nice product and I'm glad I have it - overall 4-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Good to keep one of these things in your car - on the pricey side but good quality from reputable brand

profile.description: Ideal Mega Magic Show Kit contains everything your little magician needs to put on a big mysterious magic show! Let professional magician Ryan Oakes teach them his 220 easy-to-learn tricks, which can be performed with the included 62 piece magic set. Its a great kit for beginners and even illusionists with some experience can learn a few new tricks and play with some new props. Abracadabra! Includes, magic wand, 3 purple cups, 4 fuzzy balls, 2 blue tubes, 2 bottles, 2 bottle decals, 2 clear cups, crazy coin cap, 6 multiplying rabbits, thumb tip, disappearing card box, deck of cards, cloth handkerchief, magic magicians deck, 10 changing food cards, changing food card box, magic fruit box, fruit cube, levitating tool, handkerchief vanisher, 4 magic envelopes, 6 number card sheets, magic hat, magic lunch box, magic thermal bottle, 3 pc. spoon and fork trick, holey sandwich, clean and dirty knife, 2 plastic rings, rabbit token, double stick tape and Secret of 220 Magic Tricks instruction booklet. Recommended for children 7 years of age and older.
profile.reviewText:
Standing almost 2 feet wide and over 1 foot tall, the box for Poof Slinky "Mega Magic Show" certainly looks quite impressive at first glance.  Like the art of real magic, this is an illusion because upon opening the overly thin cardboard box there is mostly empty space and the actual contents could fit in a smaller box (and magically create a smaller carbon footprint).  The Mega Magic Show box boldly shouts "Perform 220 Tricks!" but if you notice the box also screams "64 Pieces!" which means many of the pieces are relied upon for multiple magic tricks - on a positive note the magician's deck of cards is only counted as 1 piece when a less scrupulous magician might have advertised it as 50+ pieces(!).  The set is advised for ages 7+.

The actual 64 Pieces! are mostly very basic and cheap - paper, cardboard, thin plastic, etc.  The magic trick book is also fairly flimsy and since this is the true heart of the magic set a more ruggedly constructed magic book would be the #1 improvement I would suggest.  The nicest quality piece in the set is the magician's hat.  Given the 220 tricks, my kids did find a wide variety of tricks to mess around with and they have had some fun thus far messing around with the set and showing off their magic tricks to me (I can see their slight of hand most of the time but they look so cute I don't want to tell them and rain on their magic parade).  With minimal use some of the 64 Pieces! have already been torn/broken although to be honest I can find/make comparable replacement items fairly easily if need be.

When I first saw this set it was selling on Amazon for $50 which I would say is definitely too pricey for the value.  Now I notice the set is $35 - divided by 220 now we're talking about less than 20 cents per magic trick - it doesn't sound too bad when its put that way.  Still the secret sauce is the book - if you have that you could pretty much rustle up the items you need to do the tricks and that is why it would be nice if the book was higher quality.

Overall, kids seem naturally drawn to magic tricks and it is good clean interactive fun compared to video games.  I noticed on Amazon that Poof Slinky sells many other magic sets that are smaller than this 220 mega box - a couple of their other sets are 100 tricks (which have a subset of alot of the same tricks this 220 does).  To be honest, I would spend less money and get a 100 trick box - if my kids love it and use it alot and still want more then I would consider adding the 220 box (plus the spare pieces would also be needed by then).  Overall for this 220 mega box I rate 3-stars out of 5 in consideration of price/value - try a smaller set first.
profile.summary: 1 Pound of Magic in a 10 Pound Box

I've got all kinds of electronics chargers strewn all over the place - in my house, in my kids rooms, in my cars, at my work desk, etc.  A few years ago I had an epiphany when it dawned on me that, most of my electronic devices were starting to have USB plugs into the chargers - could it be that I could start consolidating?

profile.description: Restonic's Brio mattress features open-celled latex for cool, breathable sleep - with a bit of bounce. Additionally, we use a layer of high density, breathable memory foam to cradle your body. The support is delivered by a 6.5" our True Comfort, high density, pre-compressed for longer comfort life, (No Suggestions) polyurethane core. Our designer cover has spandex, so you can immediately feel the comfort of our specialty foams. Best of all, this Restonic Brio mattress is 100% made in the USA!.
profile.reviewText:
We've been using this Restonic Brio Mattress (full size) for my 10-year old daughter's bed and I (Dad) have been sleeping well on it.  Why am I not sleeping in my own bed you ask?...daughter likes to sleep with Mommy...Daddy swaps places and falls asleep peacefully on a couple of pillow pets.  I wasn't complaining in having a new mattress in my room..err...my daughter's room since this was replacing a 25+ year old mattress with some lumpy spring that seem to poke in all the wrong places.

So back to the Restonic Brio mattress.  First off I was very impressed with the shipping. The last mattress I had delivered to my house was a coil/spring king size mattress...it arrived sealed in a plastic bag but was fairly scuffed up from the travel...the sealed bag had some rips and some of the actual mattress had scuff stains and tears.  Not this Brio - the beauty of memory foam is that this thing came compressed/sealed in a cardboard box that was maybe the size of a dishwasher.  I opened up the mattress and it uncompressed to full mattress shape thus prompting my wife to say "you will never ever get that mattress to go back in that box - trash that box, rake the leaves, put away the dishes, blah, blah, blah, etc, etc".

I was impressed with the actual mattress quality - nice fabric, durable stitching, sleek euro type look.  But bottom line___ mattresses are for providing a comfortable night's sleep...my daughter and I have both logged some nights on this mattress and I'm happy to report that we both get a good night's sleep on this puppy.  This is the only memory foam mattress in our house but I've slept on other memory foam mattresses.  I would say that this memory foam/latex combo is a bit firmer than typical memory foam mattresses I've slept on but still in the "medium" range of firmness...ie, my king bed spring/coil mattress is a bit firmer but I don't have any back problems (yet) so either works fine for me.  Temperature-wise this mattress stays cool enough for me...no issues there.

So overall, I like this Brio mattress (especially compared to the 25+ year old one it replaced).  I like the way it came nicely shipped.  Good quality.  Attractive design.  Comfortable night's sleep and doesn't overheat.  Tonight I will sink into my mattress to be cradled the way only memory foam can do, I'll snuggle up with a couple of pillow pets, maybe even eat a couple of rolls of Smarties from the night stand drawer and wash it down with a half drank Capri Sun that is still lying next to the bed.  At current price of $725 not the lowest price relative to various competition but a solid good quality choice - 4-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Ships Well - Sleeps Well (cradles you the way only memory foam can do)...

Because you tie it behind your head it fits my daughter's 9-year old child noggin just find and it fits my adult male mid-sized (so I've been told) noggin just fine.  My daughter ties this thing on and it stay and same for me.
  ---Material - this is a nice quality material - soft to the touch yet thick - almost spandexy to the touch.  This is not like the Dollar Store bandannas that are almost translucent and will most likely tear after a few uses.  These colors don't tear (or run).

Well, that's about all you can say about a headband / bandanna.  This Junk is good - nice material, easy to use, good fit, can't go wrong with the red-white-and-blue.  At current price of $20 a bit on the pricey side but you do get more than typical.  Overall 4-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Pricier than typical but better quality than typical...

profile.description: Plenty of room. 7 pocket expanding file with color tab inserts offers lots of space for all your school papers. Get organized! 6 pull up tabs to help you remember. The tabs easily pull up to serve as a reminder as to whats filed and where. They also help you with prioritization and organization. Its sturdy. Durable plastic outer shell with secure zipper closure protects those important papers, while reinforced gussets prevent sides from tearing. Personalize it. Its front cover has a clear pocket, so you can display a personalized cover sheet or use for storing more school papers -- class assignments or homework due that day! Convenient storage for pens. 2 loops on the outside of the file are for pen storage. Overall size of 13-3/4 x 10-3/4.
profile.reviewText:
I remember using Mead FIVE STAR  products back in my high school days (decades ago).  Good products stay in business and now all these years later I find myself buying various FIVE STAR school supplies for my two kids (especially for my son who manages to destroy things very quickly).  Mead makes plenty of regular branded office products - 5STAR is their premium brand focused on more durability - extra reinforcements in high fail areas such as tougher plastic, reinforced bendable areas, etc.  This 7-Pocket expanding file (docket) is no exception - tougher than a normal docket and has good functionality.  Serendipitously my son has just entered 7th grade and his school requires that each student procedure a docket with at least 7 folders.

What I like:
  + #1 is the build quality of course.  Sturdy and will outlive a standard docket.
  + Simple design.  Tough but simple.  Just a zipper and 7 folders inside - not overly complex.
  + I really like the clear cover that allows the owner to slide a piece of paper in to customize the front.  Too many times I've seen my kids reject folders because they don't like the cover (the stars are a girls color, nobody watches that show anymore, etc).  Problem solved - printout whatever you want and stick it in the front of the folder - now do your homework.

What could be better:
  -Really for me the only showstopper might be price.  A similar docket base model might run you $8.  I thought this red 5STAR was pricey at $18 - kind of a toss up vs just owning 2 base model dockets (1 spare).  But I also noticed that there are plenty of colors offered in this 5STAR at $11 - with that low premium over base model it's a good value.  My recommendation is to stick to the colors that offer a better price (as long as they aren't too wacky) - see my early comment - your kid (or you) can always insert a custom cover sheet to tailor it closer to your aesthetic preference.
  -Minor nitpick but the file tab labels are hard to get at to write on and hard to put back - maybe if they protruded a bit from the sleeve it would be a bit easier (can always make your own).

Overall, I'm a fan of Mead FIVESTAR, I've seen plenty of this product line field tested by my kids and they really do last longer (even for my son).  For this particular 7-Pocket folder if I had to buy it for $18 I would only give it 3 or 4 stars because the price premium is just too steep vs a base $8 docket.  But if I buy this MEAD FIVESTAR at the $11 price I see listed for some colors then I give it my own 5-STAR rating in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: 5-Stars for FIVE STAR (if the price is right)

profile.description: TPX Louisville Slugger BB12Z -3 Z-1000 Composite High School/College bat meets BBCOR bat standards.
profile.reviewText:
My official baseball days are behind me but that doesn't mean Ole' Dad can't take Son to the park once in awhile to show him that Dad has still got It.  This Louisville TPX 33/30 is a good fit for me (5'10", 195lbs-ish).  I headed off to my sons idle little league field to take some swings with my son serving up the BP.  The control group is my old Easton aluminum bat clocking in at about $19.99 retail, vs this Louisville TPX composite clocking in at $300+.  Yes, even with the Easton this Ole' Dad can still put on a show (at least for my naive son) by launching some shots over the homerun fence (peewee league 150 foot fence).  But with the TPX, this Ole' Dad took it to the next level with higher percent of swings sailing over the fence and with more distance.  Definitely a bigger sweet spot and added benefit of composite materials.

 So, overall I give this bat a thumbs up.  Do I need a bat this expensive - no.  Am I glad I have it - yes.  Will I get an expensive bat like this for my son to improve his/my changes of a college baseball scholarship - absolutely (especially in the little league arms race where alot of other kids already have these types of high end bats).  If I had a bat like this when I was growing up would I have made it to the big leagues - I'd like to think so (at least that's the story I've been telling my son and I'm going to stick with that).
profile.summary: Maybe Money Does Buy Happiness

profile.description: Genius introduces its new innovative Energy Mouse, that combines a power bank function with a mouse. It's perfect for charging your smartphone anytime, anywhere. The Energy Mouse combines a 1200dpi mouse with a 2700 mAh power bank feature, bringing you the best of both worlds. Embedded in the mouse is a Li-polymer battery for excellent charge control and four LED lights to indicate battery capacity as well as charging status. Don't worry about the power bank used up all the battery. A special battery reserve feature is dedicated just for mouse operation. The bi-directional 2.4GHz anti-interference technology ensures a reliable working distance of up to 10 meters. Enjoy responsive cursor control and effortless scrolling. The two-in-one function saves travel storage space making Energy Mouse your mouse of choice when you're on-the-go.
profile.reviewText:
I've been using this Genius Wireless Energy Mouse for 1+ month now and I have to say I love it.  I actually have quite a few cordless mouses but now I realize the dual function as a battery pack is the way to go.  Not only do I never have to replace batteries in this mouse (because it leverages the battery pack source) but the combo just makes sense.  I recently brought this mouse on a business trip.  On the airplane my smartphone/mp3 player was running out of juice - I plugged it into this mouse (using mouses USB plug receptacle) and it gave me enough juice on the flight.

As an actual mouse I like using this product.  It's comfortable and very responsive - it behaves the same as my other cordless mouses.  Bottom line - at $27 this Energy Mouse costs about the same as some other cordless mouses I own...to me it's a no brainer and next time I'll buy the mouse that also functions as a supplemental battery pack for my portable electronic devices.  5-stars from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Love it, why buy an ordinary cordless mouse

profile.description: Clip light w/ built-in speaker / Plays iPod, MPS-compatible w/all other AUX audio sources / AC adapter included, works on 4 AA batteries (not included)
profile.reviewText:
I've tried out this Vibe clip-on speaker for about a month....

The good:
  -It's a decent desklight for kids and the speaker sound is ok enough (better than most cellphone speakers).
  -The battery power is a plus for the kids to bring on a car trip as a reading light.
  -It uses LED bulb which is good.  I pretty much only buy products with LED bulbs now (uses less power, lasts longer).
  -The latest price I noticed is $10 which appears like new lower discounted price.

What could be better:
  -Combining a desklight and a speaker makes this light too bulky.  The head is big and the unpluggable wire can get messy.
  -The clip on the light could not clip to a thicker desk that I have (it couldn't open wide enough).
  -The light brightness is not adjustable.

Overall I rate this 4-stars...it's an ok desklight, it's an ok speaker.  I was going to rate overall 3-stars for price/value but with the $10 selling price I bumped up to 4-stars for price/value.
profile.summary: OK but jack of all trades is master of none

profile.description: NEW DESIGN with a gift box! The Killerspin JET200 table tennis paddle is one of the best sellers on the marketfor good reason. With 5 layers of premium wood and performance rubbers, the JET200 is a step up from comparable rackets in terms of power, control and spin. The equal-weight distribution and quality construction is engineered to cater to the all-around players game with a focus on precision shots and finesse. Superior feel with power to spare allows you to utilize all aspects of your game for precise placement and hard-hitting shots when needed. The green/black rubber combination will add style and flair to your game as you hone your skills with the JET200. The product comes with a 30-day limited warranty.
profile.reviewText:
This Killerspin JET200  is a very nice paddle for current price of $24.  The Company I work for recently setup a new table tennis room so the battling has begun.  I'm decent at ping pong (yes I call it ping pong)...decent but not great.  So I need to capitalize on every advantage to assert my ping pong dominance over my various random loudmouth coworkers (some of whom spend way too much time in the ping pong room).  Hence, I shunned the company provided ping pong paddles (which are dirty, sweaty, and half busted) in favor of this JET200.

What I like:
 ++The overall quality and attention to detail.  First off this thing was packaged like an Apple product - very nice packaging and box swings open to reveal this gleaming paddle.  The box is nice enough that I keep the paddle in the box (plus it intimidates my coworkers when I unsheath my ping pong paddle while they sadly look down at the grimy loaner paddles that they are clutching in their sweaty hands).  The actual paddle has a nice hefty weight to it and the rubber surface is incredibly thick and gripping (especially when comparing to standard cheapie paddles).

But most importantly this JET200 plays great.  Indeed my ball spins are better with this thing.  I'm undefeated thus far (6-0) using this paddle (but of course I only play coworkers that I know I can beat).  At current price of $24 this is great value for what you get...5-STAR rating by me.
profile.summary: Great quality, playability, overall value!

profile.description: The Big Boss Grill was created to make your life easier. This one appliance makes cooking any meal quicker, cleaner, and easier. Each plate is removable for an easy clean in your dishwasher. The storage rack makes it easy and convenient to store and access each plate whenever you need it. You will also receive the "Cooking With The Big Boss" recipe guide, with amazing recipes that can be made quick and household ingredients that you can cook into delicious meals!
profile.reviewText:
Back when I was in college I don't think they had these type of grills, but I think I would have loved it back then (3am snack breaks).

Now that I am married with kids this "Small Boss" proves too small - probably works best for one college kid.  I made myself a decent grill cheese sandwich on the grill but it was promptly snatched from me by one of my kids forcing me to ponder if I should go through exercise of grilling another one.  Also with a family I now prefer items that produce less clutter and the Boss just has too many little parts and accessories than I like to track and store.

In terms of Quality it has worked fine for me so far but I haven't had it that long (will post an update if I experience any quality issues).

So overall, the college-version of me would give this 5-stars.  The married-with-children version of me gives this 3-stars for my current lifestyle needs.
profile.summary: Would Have Used More Back In College

profile.description: Bring your art studio on the go! Faber-Castells Do Art Portable Easel holds all of your art materials in 2 tidy drawers. Recommended by art educators, each easel is stocked full of premium quality Faber-Castell art supplies including Mini Colored Pencils, Beeswax Crayons, Markers, Chalk, Dry Erase Marker, Eraser, Pencil Sharpener and Sketch Pad. Lock the easel in place and secure your paper using the attached clips and create art on the go! Fold the easel back up and youve got a convenient lap desk. This 37 piece art set is great for ages 4+.
profile.reviewText:
I'm a fan of this Faber-Castell Tabletop Art Studio!  Yes the current price is $58 for this quality art set...which is about the same price of that new release video game "Zombie Baby Slaughter 9" for your zBox.  Which investment feels better?

The cleverest aspect of this set is the actual box...a fairly nice versatile wood box that stores your stuff...it folds as an easel or a magnetic whiteboard or just a  plain old drawing surface (handy for car rides).  Then of course there is the good stuff that comes inside the box for all your kids basic art needs - paper, crayons, paint, etc etc and it's always easy to restock/buy more (if you're feeling really wild you can restock some with different brands).  Faber-Castell is also a well-known / reputable brand.

So overall I'm a fan of this Tabletop Art Studio...it just feels better giving this to your kid or as a gift to another kid instead of Zombie Baby Slaughter 9 (plus they already have ZBS 1-8 anyway).  I think this is good/healthy value at current price of $58 - 5-STAR rating by me in consideration of overall price/value.
profile.summary: Nice set and the same price as 1 new release video game...

profile.description: A fun and exciting way to get fit. Just roll the 12-Sided exercise Dice and perform exercise and repetitions that appear on top. Exercises include burpees, push-ups, Russian twists and many more.
profile.reviewText:
I'm all for anything that promotes more exercise so hence this exercise dice.  I was surprised how big this die was - the size of a couple of softballs.
 --Made of a soft foam material so you can toss it around in the house without breaking anything (may tear over time though)?
 --12 sided dice so 12 exercises to choose from.  Actual numbers (reps) for each exercise may not be appropriate for all people (like me) so what I have done is "divide by 3"...maybe later I'll graduate to "divide by 2".  What would be really cool if the exercise descriptions/reps could be customized/edited by the user.
 --Color scheme of dark red on black is a bit hard to read but still manageable. Still, orange or yellow on black would be better.

In summary, decent enough prop to get you moving (my kids like it).  At current price of $20 a bit pricey for what you get - you can always get your own 12 sided standard die and make your own hit list.  3-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: I can only do 5 Burpees (so I divide by 3)...

profile.description: The ONE Smart Piano 61-Key Portable Keyboard White. This portable keyboard is an ideal instrument for beginners and experienced players alike. It is an excellent learner's tool, and a fun way for more experienced players to learn new music. There are 61 backlit keys that light up with sheet music through The ONE Smart Piano app. The ONE Light is portable, so you can take it with you anywhere. You can select from over 128 different instrument sounds. Carry the piano around anywhere with 6 AA batteries or use the power supply. It is available with a black or white chassis (select from drop-down menu). One key component of The ONE is the included app, which lets you take private lessons with top online instructors. Each lesson is integrated with light-up keys, so it's like having a teacher with you any time. The ONE Light comes with built-in speakers, so you can play any music through third-party apps such as Spotify, YouTube, Pandora, and more. Play your own renditions on top of the music. Your house can become a live music party-central. In addition to the external player input, the rear panel includes a mic input, pedal input, USB and an audio output for patching into larger amplification systems. This is a fun, versatile and satisfying keyboard that can help you grow as a musician. Whats not to like? NOTE: iPad pictured is sold separately.
profile.reviewText:
This keyboard replaced a less expensive Casio we had that my daughter trashed over the years (keys missing, etc).  So happy to upgrade to "The One".  Mainly used by my 12-year old daughter who loves music but only dabbles with various instruments before her attention span moves on to the next thing.

What we like:
 ++The speakers.  The speaker sound/quality is definitely much better than the old Casio (though The1 cost more) and the speakers are physically pretty big size relative to the old Casio.
 ++The connectivity.  Getting up and running on the iPad app was fairly painless and the app works well with the keyboard.  My daughter has taken the concessional piano lesson (at $100 per) and she learned some new things on the keyboard using the app...so that alone is kind of worth it compared to the cost of live lessons.  Light up keys also very cool to follow along and help accelerate learning (before attention span runs out).
 ++Overall build quality and design.  They're going for the minimalist design here which works well because alot of the interface is through the app.  Our old Casio had buttons everywhere (and we didn't know what half of them did - it did not have app connectivity).  The keyboard appears sturdy enough for the pricepoint and no issues with broken keys or anything so far.

What could be better:
 --Keys are a bit light but too be expected at this pricepoint.
 --The app connectivity is a pro and a con.  Reliance that this company will continue to invest and maintain the apps else the keyboard becomes mostly a brick with the minimalist design.  But from what I see The One has alot of products out there with good reviews and they appear to be a reputable company committed to building and supporting good products.

Overall at current price of $279 I think this is a pretty good value relative to other options out there if you're looking for some features to accelerate your learning (app guided and lighted keys) along with pretty good speaker sound at this pricepoint.  Some thought went into this product.  4-STAR rating by me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Some well thought out features to accelerate your learning...

profile.description: With its sleek, stainless-steel door and base and stainless silver body, the powerful Panasonic Microwave Oven NN-SD945S Countertop/Built-In with Inverter Technology and Genius Sensor makes a stylish and convenient addition to any home, apartment or condo kitchen. This exceptional 1250-Watt, 2.2-cubic-foot capacity stainless steel microwave with 16-1/2-inch turntable evenly heats and cooks breakfast foods, after-school snacks, dinners, appetizers and more, making it ideal for singles, busy professionals and on-the-go families. This innovative microwave oven includes patented Inverter Technology which, unlike traditional microwaves that rely on pulse-on, pulse-off power at lower temperatures, delivers a constant stream of cooking power at every temperature for more evenly cooked meals - edges to centers - every time. With the touch of the Genius Sensor cooking button, this microwave takes the guesswork out of creating a great meal by automatically setting power levels and adjusting cooking or defrosting time for added time-saving convenience. The sensor measures the amount of steam produced during cooking and signals the microprocessor to calculate the remaining cooking time at the appropriate power level. A selection of 18 auto cook options enable you to quickly prepare your favorite foods, such as pizza, popcorn, pasta, soup, oatmeal and other dishes. This Panasonic microwave oven externally measures 14-inch (H) x 23-7/8-inch (W) x 19-15/16-inch (D).
profile.reviewText:
I got this Panasonic NN-SD745S 1.6 cubic size to replace my older version which is Panasonic NN-SD797SS.  Once I saw the new Panasonic still used the same built-in kit I was sold.  I just pulled the old one out and slid the new one in...done.

I would give my old Panasonic SD797 4-STARS (minus 1-Star for reliability).  I liked everything about it but the reliability.  Mine stopped working after a few years use but I got lucky...I removed it from built-in, turned off power, removed a bunch of dust/ dust-bunny build-up from the vents and it started working again (no new problems for 1+ year).  A friend bought this microwave for their house based upon my endorsement...it broke within 1 year (door latch broke due to abuse from young kids).

So, having read generally more favorable reviews about this new SD7455S model (including reliability) I figured I should take advantage and swap it out.  The new microwave looks & works alot like my old one which is a good thing.  Very easy to use (twist knob, hit on button) but has more complex features if you want to use them, display easy to read, looks attractive, I like the 1.6 cubic size (not too small, not too huge), and of course most importantly the food turns out good (and fast).

At current price of ~$197 I think this Panasonic SD745S microwave is a great value.  5-STAR rating by me in consideration of price/value.  If I have any issues with this microwave within the next year I'll add an update to my review and adjust my stars rating.
profile.summary: Looks Good, Cooks Good

profile.description: The Oral-B PRO 3000 provides a clinically proven superior clean vs. a regular manual toothbrush. The professionally inspired design of the Cross Action brush head surrounds each tooth with bristles angled at 16 degrees, and 3D cleaning action oscillates, rotates, and pulsates to break up and removes up to 97% of plaque from hard-to-reach places. The pressure sensor lights up if you brush too hard to prevent harmful over-brushing and there are 3 modes, plus an in-handle timer to help you brush for a dentist-recommended 2 minutes. Best of all its brought to you by Oral-B  the #1 brand used by dentists worldwide.
profile.reviewText:
This is the first high powered sonic toothbrush I have used, up to now have always used old school toothbrushes.  I've been meaning to get one and finally got around to it.  My dentist really sings the praises of these types of toothbrushes.

After using this Oral-b 3K for a few weeks I really like it so far.  The first few times using it were a bit jarring because it sort of feels like a jackhammer on my teeth.  But, my teeth feel much cleaner than regular brushing and it's easier to clean a few plaque-prone areas.

My pros:  seems superior method to regular toothbrush, good handle size in my hand, good brush size in my mouth, holds a good battery charge, base has spots for extra heads for other family members, pressure sensor light works for me, timer is good.

My cons:  my only con so far is that I don't like how the base charger cord is long...this sits on my bathroom vanity so has unsightly cord bunched...would like shorter cord or hide it in the base somehow.

I can't speak to durability so far since only been using a few weeks...if anything notable happens I will update this post.  I have a dental cleaning in a few weeks so I'm curious to see if my dentist notices anything different!
profile.summary: I'm A Sonic Rookie But Liking It So Far

profile.description: The Unwind Bedside Alarm Dock is a full-function dual alarm clock with gradual wake that also charges and plays iPhone, iPod, and iPad devices. The auto-set clock has six nature sounds - Waterfall, Brook, Rain, Forest, Ocean, and Summer Night. A passive subwoofer provides expanded bass profile and excellent sound. The digital tune FM radio has 10 station presets, and a USB port for charging your devices. Plus, it has an aux-in for connecting non-Apple devices. The Unwind features a customizable color-changing mood light and includes a convenient remote control.
profile.reviewText:
I put this HMDX bedside unit through the paces and found it does a little of everything but nothing super well.  The physical design of it is pretty good but a little on the large side.  Larger size is ok with me if the purpose is to accommodate better speakers but I found the music sound to be underwhelming compared to a similar pricepoint Philips that I have.  The actual controls setup is ok - I figured everything out eventually but could be more intuitive.  The mood lighting and nature sounds are kind of cool add on gimmicks but not really necessary and the kids become bored with them after a few days.  Docking works fine for old Apple connections - for newer Apple connection you can use the Aux input which is also what I use for any Android devices.

So net/net like I say in my title I thought this unit does a little bit of everything but nothing stands out.  At $50 pricepoint there is alot of other choices and for my personal preference I would focus on sound quality first.  This HMDX is a good candidate for my daughter's room since the mood lights and nature sounds are also something she can play around with.  Overall, I give 3-stars for price/value.
profile.summary: Jack Of All Trades, Master Of None

profile.description: In-Ear Apple Control talk green
profile.reviewText:
First off I have to confess that when it comes to ear buds I'm not a snob and usually order various versions <$15 that are well rated on amazon.com.  That way if the headphones stop working, get smashed, my kids cut the cord, etc I don't get overly worked up about it.  And also I'm not really a highly tuned audiophile so I always felt that headphones 10x the price might only sound 1.2x better.

So that brings me to these Monster Isport headphones; in detail:  At $99.99 they are definitely pricier than my usual headphones.  First off I think $20 of that might be in the fancy decadent packaging these things arrived in - fancy to look at but hard to open although I survived with no papercuts.  The actual headphones look cool in monster green - I'm a fan of sporty looking headphones.  3 ear sizing choices included - turns out I am a Medium.  The way they fit in your ears was unusual to me but once I figured it out I liked it - I'm often actively doing something when I have my headphones on and I hate it when headphones can jostle off - these things stayed very put.  I also noted the solid fit results in less outside noise - good for higher quality listening (but bad if you are jogging and can't hear traffic as much).  The actual sound was very good to me though could use a bit more base (some boss headphones I recently tried had much better base).  Sound versus my $10 Colby earbuds - Monster sounds much better.  Not $89 better but I did noticed the sound was a bit crisper (probably also related to more outside noise blocked out).  I also like the fact that these earphones are built to be weatherproof/durable since I do tend to be hard on my headphones.

So in summary, I like these Monster headphones and they fit my lifestyle needs for the reasons I describe above.  Overall, I give 4 stars for price/value (I would give 5 stars if priced $40 or less).
profile.summary: These headphones work well for me but pricey

profile.description: Versatile maxTowel with towelDT (Dry-Tech) technology absorbs twice as much and dries twice as fast as standard cotton. Sized longer and wider for full coverage, and the hypoallergenic microfiber resists odors. Geared for hot yoga and traditional practices, this is also a great gym towel for strength and conditioning workouts. Machine wash separately in cold water. Dry flat. 88% Polyester, 12% Nylon, Exclusive of decoration. 30"W x 84"L.
profile.reviewText:
I've been using this Gaiam Yoga towel for about 1 month.  My observations/comments:

What I like:
 +This is definitely a larger than normal size yoga towel.  Good for draping over your floor mat - not as good for non-bulky gym towel.
 +You get alot of Microfiber material for the money  at current towel price of $29.99.  I prefer Microfiber for athletic type towels since for it's weight it dries faster (ie, no stinky gym bag).  I don't usually see such big microfiber towels at this $30 price point.
 +Product quality appears good.  I've washed this 10+ times and still looks great - built to last.
 +I like this grey color.  Kind of a blue-ish grey that goes with everything/ everyone - doesn't over commit you to a color scheme but still looks good / more timeless.

What could be better:
 -The microfiber feels a bit harsher than typical on my skin.  Just a bit abrasive/ sandpaper-ish but still livable - this is probably due to trying to slide around less on a floor mat.  There is a bit of slide on my floor mat but when I tried a normal/ softer microfiber towel it slide even more - so there is a method to the madness.

So in summary:  big towel, a lot of good quality microfiber for the money, good quality, good color, slightly abrasive. profile.description: Meguiars Heavy Oxidation Scrub is an excellent surface preparation solution for removing chalky oxidation, staining, rust, and mold to allow for optimized gel coat restoration. This water-soluble formulation rinses easily!
profile.reviewText:
I'm a fan of Meguiar's brand - good reputable brand and always performs well for me (car soap, etc)...which is good when it comes to this M77132 Heavy Oxidation scrub because I like having a trustworthy brand for this stuff (to reduce my fear of damaging my stuff).

This Heavy Oxidation Scrub is not the type of cleaner you use daily - this is for the occasional "big clean" projects on your RV, Boat, or any general similar surfaces (test in a small spot first).  I found this scrub easy enough to use and good results for me so far - apply, scrub, rinse (water soluble/easy rinse clean which is nice)...it does take a lot of elbow grease to to get surfaces clean - but that's the nature of this type of cleaning.

Amazon current price of $25 for 32oz seems competitive right now - Walmart has this product for pretty similar price.  It's one of those cleaning supplies you won't use that often but you're really happy you have it when the need comes along.  5-STAR rating by me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: one of those cleaning supplies you won't use that often but you're really happy you have it when the need comes along...

profile.description: Chrono Bomb is a super secret spy mission where kids use the included clamps and 27.5-ft. string to create a "laser" field to crawl through. At the end of the maze is the bomb, counting down. Tick, tick, tick! So, you have to hurry, carefully, and make it to the end to defuse the bomb and be the hero! Play over and over again, building new courses each time or trying to beat your or your friend's time! Includes free app for more play value! Requires three AAA batteries, not included. For ages 7 and up.
profile.reviewText:
My kids (13 & 9) find this Chrono Bomb game fun.  Coincidentally my kids had just recently seen the Big Bang Theory rerun episode where the guys played a similar concept type game where they had to navigate a real laser alarm field to retrieve their pizza.  So my kids were a bit disappointed at first when they opened the Chrono Bomb box to setup their course and realized that the alarm "laser beams"  were just actual strings you connect to sensors.  It's not as cool but at the end of the day it still does the job - don't touch the "lasers" or you fail in your mission (and I guess real lasers could very easily strike some eyeballs).

What I like about this game is that the kids (and one time even Dad) actually have to move their physical bodies - not their avatars or whatnot.  My 13 year old son is realizing that his videogame pot belly is not so handy when trying to crawl through lasers to collect gear cards, complete your mission, and most importantly try to beat your 9 year old little sister who is skinnier and more agile.

The game also has high repeatability play (until the kids tangle all the strings and break all the sensors eventually) - kids setup their own creative obstacle courses (that they think plays to their strengths and their opponents weaknesses).  At current price of $25 I think this is a pretty good value for the overall concept it provides - new PS4 game  is $50+ and they get bored of those pretty quickly.  In summary - interesting/ different than norm concept that gets this kids actually physically moving/engaged, good repeat play - overall 5-STAR rating from this Dad in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Kids actually have to move their physical bodies - not their avatars

profile.description: This decorative, magnetic combination board is the elegant way to post messages and photos in one convenient location. The 3-in-1 collaborative system gives you a trio of messaging options. The dry-erase surface makes writing notes a breeze and wipes cleans fast. The magnetic surface lets you post pictures fast and the natural cork section holds important papers in place with just a push pin. This stylish 17" x 23" two-tone, blank and silver framed board looks great in any occasional use, small or home office. Hangs horizontally or vertically with the included self-stick pads. Comes with dry-erase marker with eraser cap and two magnets.
profile.reviewText:
I've been using this Quartet combo board for about one month now and it's a good product.  My family has already been using another similar Quartet except the whiteboard and corkboard are split 50/50 down the middle...I like the layout of this new combo board because in actual use we use the whiteboard more so this wins over our old version.

What I like:
+good size.  Not too small, not too big - so easy to find a spot for it.
+ 3-in-1:  I really like the whiteboard, corkboard, and magnetic all available.  We use all 3 of these features - corkboard and magnetic handy for posting up pictures, sport schedules, etc.
+Overall good quality product - even our existing Quartet is still going strong with no parts falling off.

What could be better:
 -Hanging options - this is the key area for me that would bump up my rating +1 star.  For my personal preference, I don't like the tape hanging strips - I don't like to stick tape on my walls that sometimes peels off my paint, etc.  I like to hang my stuff on small hooks and this Quartet does not have an option on the back for hooks - so I jerry-rigged my own hanging wire on the back so I could then hang it in my preferred style.

profile.summary: Good size, good whiteboard/cork ratio

profile.description: VTech Kidizoom Smartwatch, Blue
profile.reviewText:
My 8-year old daughter has been using this VTech Kidizoom Smartwatch for a few weeks and I've got to say its a pretty cool gadget.  Dick Tracy's "time" has almost arrived.

What I like:
  +Easy to use & alot of entertaining features.  My daughter strapped this thing on and had it up and running herself.  She messed around with the games including her favorite which is a voice recorder that modulates her (singing) voice.  She's a bit on the older side for the games included - what she really uses the watch for now is as an actual watch to tell time (she enjoys changing the face style), taking pictures and videos, and of course walking around singing into her watch like a crazy person.  How developed the ecosystems becomes remains to be seen (ie, new games available to load, etc).
  +Build quality & design (mostly).  The actual watch is well made and durable and comfortable on a wrist.  Design is good in terms of usability except for very tiny on/off power button on the backside where even my fingernail is too fat to turn it on/off (a safety pin does the trick for me).
  +Battery life is good enough to get through the day with occasional usage then plug in for recharge at night (like everyone does with their cellphone).

What Could Be Better:
  -Number one thing is the cursed nano-on/off switch (see above).  Also my fingers are evidently too fat to remove the recharge plug (I have to use tweezers).
  -No WiFi - one extra step to plug the thing into PC with a cable, etc (at least it is both Windows and Mac compatible).
  -Small memory size.  According to the specs the watch comes with 128MB of internal memory which VTech says is enough to store about 800 photos or six 1-minute videos.  This is not alot of memory these days (especially since kids like to shoot video) and moving files off the watch to make room for new ones is not as convenient due to lack of wifi (and also involves more help from mommy or daddy).

Overall I think this is a decent kiddie smartwatch for around the current $60 pricepoint.  It's definitely for kids on the younger side (my 8-year old daughter is probably just becoming too old for this watch).  Something else to think about is that alot of kids (including my daughter) have some generation of ipod touches which generally blow this out of the water for usability by older kids (WiFi, sharper pictures/video, way more storage, infinity more robust app ecosystem, still fits in your pocket).  But still for tiny tikes this is a cool gadget that helps them learn to tell time, take pictures of bugs and what not, and generally make them feel like big boys and girls.  At current $60 pricepoint, I rate this between 3 and 4 stars overall in consideration of price/value.  I hope you found my review useful.
profile.summary: Dick Tracy's "time" has almost arrived

profile.description: Mepra's The Luxury Art' is upmarket brand for an upscale audience, is a truly unique range of flatware and tableware. It is made of Stainless steel. It is Dishwasher safe. It has greater control over cooking temperatures. It allows gentle cooking with little water and fat for more wholesome and flavorful food. It is suitable for all types of hobs except induction hobs.

profile.description: The Tacwise Heavy Duty Combi Cable Tacker/Staple Gun is truly versatile and one of a kind. It fires two different sizes of cable staple in 3/16 inch and 1/4 inch in diameter without the need for adjustment. The all metal construction makes the Combi Cable Tacker/Staple Gun a robust, heavy duty professional tool. It is ideal for the installation of telephone and alarm cables with the CT45 staple. With the CT60 staple (T18 type), it is perfect for installing coaxial, satellite, CAT5 & CAT6 cables and other low voltage cabling applications. No need for adjustment when changing staples, just load the required type and size and you are ready to go. This unique cable tacker is loaded with all of the necessary features including pull out handle lock, impact power adjuster, bottom loading magazine and full length cable guide. Tacwise is a new brand of rugged tools and accessories for the professional tradesman. The professional, Tacwise brand has evolved from 40 years of power tool know-how to best reflect the powerful and durable nature of the new products -which are high quality, feature packed and hard wearing with a robust and practical design.
profile.reviewText:
This Tacwise Heavy Duty Combi Staple gun is a Manly staple gun - I say that because this thing is built like a ww2 sherman tank and my wife complains that it's too heavy for her to use (which is fine because she shouldn't be messin' with my tools anyway).

Main objective of this stapler is to run/keep cables in place and takes two sizes of staples (CT45 and CT60) intended for cables up to 6mm in diameter.  There is a pressure adjuster you can tinker with to make sure your staplin' doesn't crush your wiring.  Based upon my experience, this Tacwise works great - easy to use (load'n'go) - I was tidying up my wiring around the house in no time.

And just because this says it's a "cable" staple gun don't forget that it's still a "staple gun".  aka, lots of other uses for it - fixing screens on doors, sprucing up any loosened furniture fabric by retacking, littering your neighborhood with garage sale signs that you tack up on every telephone pole but forget to take down afterwards, etc.

So at around $22 current price, I think this is a very solid staple gun for your Manly tool kit.  I venture to say this thing may outlive me.  Plus you get a great bicep workout when using.  The only bad thing I can think of to say about it is if you are stapling something above you and you drop it  and it lands on top of your head - you might knock yourself out (I'm actually not kidding about this and its probably happened already and posted on youtube).  Overall 5-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: Built like a WW2 Sherman Tank...

profile.description: The Ankuoo NEO Wi-Fi Wall Switch lets you turn lights on and off from anywhere at any time. The NEO Wi-Fi Wall Switch uses your existing home Wi-Fi network and provides wireless control of lights. Simply download the free NEO app and replace your existing light switch with the NEO Wall Switch. You will be able to control your home lighting using your smartphone. You can set schedule timer, countdown timer and anti-theft timers to fit your life style. You can add multiple switches to your home to control your lighting using one single NEO app.
profile.reviewText:
I've had this Ankuoo Neo wi-fi outlet switch for about one month now.  For my personal preferences, I don't like to be an early adopter Beta tester - I like the kinks worked out before me, software refined, etc.  The Ankuoo is a nicely built device but does appear to be early in its life cycle - when I downloaded the Android app it said the app had been downloaded one hundred times (compare that to Flappy Birds downloads of bazillions)...point is this Neo is still a new product.  I also have the Belkin WeMo which is a similar WiFi outlet switch.

What I liked:
 +Neo Build quality and design are good.  Smaller than my WeMo plug which is good.  I find Neo design attractive in a contemporary way.  Neo build appears pretty rugged.
 +Neo does work.  It was a bit of a hassle for me to get working (see other comments in section below) but once I got it working it does work.  I plugged my wifi nanny cam into it and I use the Neo to turn the cam off/on remotely from anywhere with my phone.  Then view the nanny-cam video with my phone.  I'll probably also use Neo when I go on trips for security by controlling on/off lighting.

What could be better:
 -Initial setup was not smooth for me.  Neo broke my streak of 5+ previous wifi setups that went quick / smoothly.  I read the Neo instructions and attempted to continue my setup winning streak - no luck, streak broken.  I couldn't get Neo working so after a few tries I had to roll-up my sleeves and start troubleshooting.  First I went googled Ankuoo Neo and went to their website - notable that 2/3 of the homepage real estate is dedicated to a banner that says "Quick Troubleshooting Guide"...I read up on various FAQ and then returned to my attempted setup.  I still could not get Neo working with my primary router - based on some FAQ I believe I think it may be because I've got so much other wifi stuff connected to that router (ie, my Sonos stereo system, wireless printer, laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, probably all my neighbors stuff, etc etc).  So then I switched over to using my secondary router which covers some weaker signal areas in my house and doesn't have alot of wifi stuff hooked up to it - Neo then worked right away for me...only tricky thing was when I finished install the App had some weird red message that read like an error message but upon more careful reading it was more of a warning message and I did finally notice my Neo icon was now visible.  Neo was then up and running for me - easy to turn on/off the outlet with a click of the button from the app.
 -Potential long term support.  I don't know much about Ankuoo/Neo but this does appear to be a new product for them (ie, 100 downloads on Android app, etc).  I believe start-ups / new products help make America great but if the venture does not work out then no more app support down the road. The similar product WeMo is made by Belkin which is a pretty mature / large company.  I'm not saying larger companies should always get the business but I also think consumers should make fully transparent / informed decisions.

Overall this Neo is working well for me now (on my secondary router) and very similar usability for me as my Belkin WeMo.  The Neo is currently price at $40 which is similar to a WeMo.  My overall rating for Neo is 3-stars...I deducted a few stars for my initial setup issues and android app not fully mature yet.
profile.summary: Works well for me now after start-up kinks...

profile.description: Five Star Locker Shelf Extender, Berry Pink/Purple (72892)
profile.reviewText:
I remember using FIVE STAR products back in my high school days (decades ago). Mead makes plenty of regular branded office products - 5STAR is their premium brand focused on more durability - extra reinforcements in high fail areas such as tougher plastic, reinforced bendable areas, etc. This locker shelf is no exception - strong build quality and has good functionality.

But I use those hooks you say...you'll see in the picture of this product it still gives you back your beloved two hooks below the shelf so chillax my friend.

So be sure to check the colors and be a bit flexible on the color to save some money (though trying to convince your son in junior high school to live with a pink shelf in his locker to save $6 may be pushing it too far). profile.summary: Great Product If Extra Locker Space Is Needed (pricing can vary by color so be sure to check)

profile.description: This Farberware Fresh collapsible bowl has a unique collapsing design for compact storage. Durable and sturdy, the bowl is perfect for preparing and mixing ingredients while cooking. Holds 1-1/2 quartz. Dishwasher safe.

profile.description: Screwpull Pocket Model Corkscrew, Black

I bought this Corkscrew in Aug'08 from Amazon.  One of my favorite things about Amazon is the ability for me to enter a generic product description (such as "corkscrew") and then sort by "best selling".  Often times this has given me visibility to good products I had never heard of before.  I believe the collective wisdom of a group is (usually) greater than that of an individual (I call it GroupThink, also note that Al Gore actually got more votes than GW Bush). profile.description:
Our best indoor FM Antenna that also works wonders with HD Radio.

A quick and easy way to improve the FM reception of your portable radio or stereo receiver is with an affordable FM Reflect Antenna. The FM Reflect can be bent and shaped to get the best reception from the circular polarization now used by many FM stations. If you've made the leap to HD radio, the FM Reflect is also one of the few antennas that tested well with the new digital signal.

Compared to other indoor FM antennas, the FM Reflect achieves a high signal-to-noise ratio and is less susceptible to interference from surrounding objects and people. The dipole design is more powerful than a standard dipole antenna, and delivers maximum gain across the entire FM broadcast band. Unlike ordinary dipoles, with the FM Reflect Antenna there is no fall off near the end of the FM band. In other words, this is a good FM antenna.
National Public Radio Labs has performed some HD Radio reception tests using the FM Reflect and other FM antennas

Size: 54" all-copper element with an 8-foot feed line. Weight: 8.5 oz. Comes with "F" connector, balun spade connector and alligator clip. Limited Lifetime Warranty.
profile.reviewText:
Let me preface by saying that I am a radio layman.  I can't tell you the science behind radio waves, I can just tell you if my radio sounds better.

I purchased this antenna via Amazon for my Bose wave radio.  Prior to this, I had added a dipole type antenna to my wave radio and I still was not getting clear sounds on most channels (bits of static, etc).  I have now switched to this Crane Reflect Antenna and my radio reception has improved across the board.  I still have a few channels with static but many of them come in clear now with no static.  My old Dipole was thin cable while this Crane Reflect looks more like the type of round cable that you connect to your TV.

Anyway, mission accomplished for my needs.  Minus one star because this antenna is pricey for what appears to be.  I hope you found my review helpful.
profile.summary: Improved my radio receiption...

profile.description: Rapid Supreme SuperFlatClinch is more than your normal desktop stapler. They're designed to staple up to 250%* more sheets. Patented SuperFlatClinch technology flattens the staple reducing paper stacks by 40%. And with an ergonomic design, get a superior performance regardless if you use it in-hand or on a desk. *250% based on 50 sheet capacity stapler
profile.reviewText:
"They switched from the Swingline to the Boston stapler, but I kept my Swingline stapler because it didn't bind up as much, and I kept the staples for the Swingline stapler and it's not okay".  -Milton Waddams (Office Space)

Sorry, whenever I hear the word stapler I think of Milton.  I may not love staplers as much as Milton, but I'm a fan of staplers.  I've got a stapler on my desk at work and I've got piles of paper on my desk at work - I staple stuff, it's handy.  My kids love staplers, they staple stuff all the time that shouldn't be stapled, just for the fun of it (for them,  not me).

My current stapler I've had for years (now that I actually read the model# after all this time) is a "Stanley Bostitch B440"...still shows available on Amazon currently priced just below $7.  Actually, the reason why I've had this so long is because "Stanley" (as I call him) has been a very faithful stapler - he's reliable, he's low drama (never jams)...before Stanley I did have a string of unperforming staplers that I had to let go (usually Swinglines).

So now along comes this sexy new model "Rapid S17" dressed up in black with a little grey trim (I like the red trim better).  She's lighter but still well built, she's easy on the eyes with curves in all the right places (Stanley is kind of frumpy).  Rapida (as I call her) also staples very well - just a light touch and the job is done (I have to bang down on Stan) - she knows her way around a stack of paper. profile.description: Kill snails and slugs with the easy-to-use Ortho Bug-Geta Snail & Slug Killer. No mixing or spraying required; simply spread the indicated amount of product around your vegetables, fruit trees, citrus, berries, ornamentals, shrubs, flowers, trees, or gardens, and control snail and slugs for up to 3 weeks. Remains effective even after rainfall. And, you can use Ortho Bug-Geta Snail & Slug Killer around pets and wildlife.
profile.reviewText:
I live in the Bay Area, Calif...10+ years ago when I moved into my home I quickly learned I had quite a snail/slug infestation...anything I planted was quickly riddled with leaf holes.  So I declared war and I will say that these days I don't have alot of snails/slugs left in my yard.  There's many ways to wage wars against snails - my son's favorite is "night stomping".  I however am more civilized and prefer to poison my snails and slugs - that way I don't get my shoes dirty.  Before you say I am cruel I will point out that alot of snails/slugs in California are considered "invasive species" that found there way over here from Europe...plus they kill my plants.

So this "Bug-geta" from Ortho is one of my preferred war tactics.  Just sprinkle the granules around problem areas...snails/slugs eat them...snails/slugs go bye-bye and help fertilize your soil.  These types of granule poisons generally advertise that they are safe to use in yards and around plants, etc...this is the  type of situation where it's better to go with brand names such as Ortho since you can generally trust their claims more (though do your homework - don't blindly trust the Big Corporation).  I will point out per the Ortho ingredients label that the active ingredients is "sulfur" and I believe it used to be "metaldehyde"...sulfur is generally regarded as safer so that is a positive...though from what I've read it might not be as effective as metaldehyde.  Thus far this latest Bug-Geta does appear to be helping my yard to stay fairly snail/slug free so I'm all for the safer formula.

At current price of $10 for 2-lbs (similar price as Home Depot)...a bit pricier relative to some other brands I used but does the job without any crazy poisons.  4-STAR rating from me in consideration of price/value.
profile.summary: This Bug-Geta active ingredient is "sulfur"...used to be "metaldehyde"...

profile.description: We've packed high-powered cleaning into this deceivingly small canister vac. Cut around obstacles and corners while the cyclonic filtration lets you roll through any mess.
profile.reviewText:
There are Upright People and there are Canister people.  Much like the Hatfields and McCoys - a person's predilection most likely comes from their upbringing.  My mom and my wife have always been Uprights (uptights) so I guess I am an Upright.  But I try to keep an open mind hence my family has been using this Dirt Devil SD40050 Canister for about one month now.

Overall, I like this Canister thingamajig.  Growing up I never heard any positives about the Canisters so I read up on both sides and found that they both have their strengths and weaknesses.  The main advantage of the Canister family is that they are lighter weight for carrying up/down stairs and easier to maneuver under furniture such as tables - but you are towing a trailer behind you which can be a bit awkward.  The Upright family is "grab & go" - roll out of the closet and start vacuuming - but  they are heavy and bulky (harder to carry on stairs, harder to vacuum under furniture).  So for me I've found a place for both in the world - Upright kept upstairs, Canister kept downstairs.

What I like about this Dirt Devil Canister:
 +Easy to take out of the box, assemble, and get up and running.
 +lightweight yet powerful suction - does a good job for me.  Decently quiet.
 +great for hardwood floors - long wand/hose and lighter weight make it easier to vacuum my hardwood floors vs upright.
 +Power cord is nice and long and auto retract button works well.

What could be better:
 -The attachment tool needs a redesign.  For starters my wife and I had a "debate" on which ends goes in the nozzle - by appearance it could go either way (but only one way fits so I am right again).  Converting the attachment tool to different modes is difficult when trying to slide up/down.  The attachment tool constantly falls off it's location on the hose.
 -Emptying the container/ filter is easy enough in theory.  But the first time my wife had it in pieces and the instructions appeared to be for an older version that wasn't totally applicable (could be because I have an early product release version).  We eventually figured it out by sticking all the pieces back together based upon "best fit".
 -Storage - canisters are lighter weight but the long hose actually makes storing this vacuum in the closet more unwieldy than storing our upright.  I may install a bracket in the closet to hold the canister hose up so it doesn't flop around everywhere.

Overall, I'm glad I took the chance in getting to know the Canister family.  I now have learned (in my opinion) that the Canisters are better fits in homes with lots of stairs or lots of hardwood.  Conversely the Uprights are better suited for no stairs and lots of carpet.  Hopefully my Switzerland-like stance is not offending any Uptights or Canisters but I believe there is a place for both in this world.  At current $91 price tag I think this DD Canister is a pretty good value - 4 STAR rating from me.
profile.summary: An Upright's venture into the Canister family

profile.description: Theres no reason to search for shade, when you can bring it with you. Use the Versa-Brella for all of your outdoor adventures. Whether its time for your favorite player to run down the field, or youre spending your day at the beach, youll be confident in your sun protection with this quick set up canopy. The UPF 50+ protection, and 99.5% protection from UVA and UVB light will keep your skin safe. We even include eye safety tips, and an underneath silver coating so youll have everything you need. With a compact carrying case, and weighing only 1.8 lbs. this offers you a hassle free set up and easy transportation. When open, it spans 3.4 x 3/5 and when folded down its 3.5 wide and 36 high. The connector attaches to both square and tubular surfaces and it has two push button hinges for easy adjustment, so you can get the perfect angle. Use the Versa-Brella by Sport-Brella for all your favorite sports adventures. Cheer on your favorite player as they hustle down the field, or give them a cool snack during half time under the shade. The Versa-Brella will never let you down.
profile.reviewText:
I've got elementary school age kids and I live in California = lots of sports games in the sun.  This umbrella appeals to me.  My wife & I have an assorted collection of various portable chairs for soccer viewing - a few of these chairs have built-in umbrellas.  But, I've found the built-in umbrellas make the chairs bulkier to lug around and more of a complex chinese puzzle trying to figure out how to fold them back up properly.

Enter this Sport-Brella.  A portable umbrella you can clip to any chair.  I used this a few times and loved it - it was pretty easy to clip to any chair I was using and block the sun so I had decent spectator view of my kids games.  The umbrella comes in it's own carry sheath and is nice and lightweight.  I found it easy to clamp on to whatever chair I needed to.  The actual umbrella is fairly small but very adjustable and also swivels so I found I could always position it block the sun from my eyes.

So I really like this umbrella.  The unfortunate thing is the third time I was using it when I was trying to adjust the umbrella the top tube portion snapped off at the joint.  So technically the umbrella is now broken (the plastic is snapped at the joint) but I have managed to jerry-rig it to still work with some strong masking tape.

Overall, I love the concept but wish it has been a bit more durable for me.  At $20 I may actually buy another one and see if it holds up with a bit more caution from me.  Overall I rate 3 stars in consideration of price/value.  If it had not broken on me I would have rated 5 stars.
profile.summary: I liked it but it broke after a few weeks

profile.description: Oral-B Glide Pro-Health Original Floss helps remove plaque between teeth and below the gum line. The silky-smooth, shred-resistant texture slides more easily in tight spaces vs. regular floss.
profile.reviewText:
Not sure what is going on with Crest.  The Crest name has always been synonymous with dental care for as long as I can remember but in recent years I've had bad experiences.  First there was the Crest Pro Health brown teeth incident, now my Crest Glide floss is not what I remember.  Glide used to be my favorite floss - it glided easily through my teeth and was my floss of choice.
