profile.reviewText: This is a GREAT tri-ply stainless cookware set that will last you a LIFETIME if properly cared for. This set has every pan that you would need. Included in the set is: 8 inch Fry Pan 10 Inch Fry Pan with lid 3 Quart Saute Pan with lid 1.6 Quart Sauce Pan with lid 3 Quart Sauce Pan with lid 8 Quart Stockpot with lid Steam insert that fits on both the 3 quart sauce pan and the 8 quart stockpot 2 Pot Holders Each of these pans is weighted nicely. These aren't the pans you'd find at Walmart. If you've never cooked with stainless steel cookware before...it's a bit different than cooking on that non stick teflon stuff that you don't need oil or anything in the pan (unless you want it there) With stainless steel, unless you're cooking something like bacon where your the fat being cooked off becomes the oil you then cook in.... for the most part .... you'll need some sort of butter, margarine, or oil. It'll help keep the food you're cooking from sticking to the pan. If you're having an issue with food sticking a lot... your heat is often to high. That's another thing, with stainless steel cookware like this that has the whole clad construction....the WHOLE PAN sides and all is very conductive for heating and heats rather quickly. It's because of this nature that you never want to really use a heat seating above medium. You can boil water at medium-high. This cookware is dishwasher-safe; oven-safe to 550 degrees F and Freezer-safe for food storage I personally recommend using either wooden or plastic utensils when cooking otherwise...if using metal ones you run the risk of scratching your cookware (and scratches caused by that are not covered with warranty on these pans) The lids fit the pans nicely...not too tight so that if you've got the lid on the pan won't be able to vent. I've cooked several meals already using these pans and I will say this... the handle can get warm so please make sure to keep a potholder or towel handy so you don't burn yourself Speaking of the handles.... that's one of my favorite aspects of these pans. The handles are riveted to the pan.... no more worrying about handles coming loose, or needing to tighten a screw or anything of that sort. This really is a nice set of cookware and it's the only set I'll need for the rest of my life. I received this product for free in exchange for an honest and unbiased review. profile.reviewText:
I was immediately sucked into this teenage angsty world right from the start. This author did it again with her very developed teenage characters and story line.

I wasn't able to read it fast enough to get to the bottom of it all. I wanted to know every secret and mystery surrounding the characters and their lives. I also love that the two main characters had known each other nearly their whole lives and that their "meet" wasn't a traditional one. Pen pals that live 30 minutes from each other and never cross paths until one night that changed it all.

Ryen isn't who I thought she would be from the shield she wore to fit in. Like any other kid all she ever wanted was to fit in and she did, even though she lost who she really was along the way. But she had her pen pal Misha that she could use as an outlet to who she really was until she didn't anymore. Her character was such a contradiction from internal to external. I really connecter with her inner person, but hated her outer person. The one she projected to everyone for the sake of fitting in. I hated her "friends" and the way she compromised her true self to keep their attention and "respect". But by the end I was so in love with her character and her ability to change for the better.

Misha oh what a hand he was dealt. I felt for him and all the stuff he had been through in his 18 years. I both loved and hated him (which is a common occurrence with this authors male characters) for the way he treated Ryan and that he kept the huge secret from her for way too long. I loved that even though he wanted to hate her for the person she projected he couldn't help but keep coming back to her. He couldn't leave her alone. I love that he pushed her at every turn and that it eventually broke the barrier she had in place.

This book has some surprises and some pretty heavy emotional parts. It is angsty and teenage drama filled. I was sucked in though right off the bat.

I have been dying to read this book since it released, but I wanted to wait until I could read book two as well.

Well, that time finally came and I really dig me some Xavier Cold.

When we meet Anna she has just left the only life she has ever known and is flying across the country to start fresh. She is a wreck and the only saving grace is that once she lands she will be with her cousin who she thinks of as a sister and her aunt who is kooky but loving. She doesn't expect to meet an alpha male on her flight that will consume her thoughts and insert himself into her life.

When we meet Xavier, he is every bit the alpha male just looking for a good time. All those dirty things he said to Anna made me with that she would have given into him on that plane, but I am so glad that she didn't because the build up was worth the wait. It also helped me fall in love with X and see that was capable of something more. I really loved  the small changes that X began to show in this book and that Anna seemed to be just what he needed.

Although at one time he really crushed my heart, but at the same time I know that a man has needs and can only resist so much temptation, but still he broke my heart and he really had to redeem himself.

He did.

Xavier Cold is one of those BBF's that you will eventually compare others to. He is strong and caring (even when he thinks he is evil personified). He is protective of Anna from the very beginning and I love that he realizes that she is different and that she is someone that he needs in his life.

We find out some of X's secrets in this book, but so much is left unanswered and will leave you wanting to so much more from these two. At the end of this book I kept swiping looking wanting it not to end where it did, but luckily I had book two waiting to be read ;)

profile.reviewText:
I vow that this a 5 STAR READ!!!

**I received an ARC for an honest review.**

This is most definitely one of my most favorites of 2015. I LOVED this book!

Mia Sheridan does an amazing job with this story. I felt the heartache and pain as well and the happiness and love. She makes sure that everything gets it ending and leaves no stone unturned. She has an amazing way with word that draws you into the story and it's characters. Her characters are so well written and easy to love or hate.

Grayson Hawthorn is kind of an ass, but he his an ass that will still make you swoon and root for him. I couldn't help but fall completely and utter in love with him. Although there were times when I wanted to reach into my kindle and smack him around a bit, but after getting into his head and knowing his full story you can help but understand him and the reason he guarded his heart. When all of the truths finally come out and everything is laid bare, I think I fell in love Grayson a little bit more.

So, when Kira is concocting her plan I really didn't see it coming. I though about quite a few things that she could possibly proposed to Grayson to help each other out, but what she actually did was ballsy and after getting to know her totally made sense. I loved her personality the more I got to know her. Especially after knowing her past and relating it to the person she became. She is such a genuine and loving person. I loved that not only did she want to make Grayson's life a little bit better, but she made everyone's lives better in the process.

Her coming into his life allowed him to open up as well as the people around him. I loved all of their interactions even the ones that broke my heart, but I loved that they both started to trust each other enough to open up. I really liked when Kira brought out a side of Grayson that had never been present. I loved that her presence made slowly brought him back to life and let him start to mend the scars of his past. Of course there had to be some pretty awful things have to happen before the mending could begin. And this awful things just about gutted me.

This is a MUST READ!!!

The author did an amazing writing the characters in a way that made it easy for me to connect with them, even the ones you want to hate. I loved that this book was so much more than just a romance, but about two people finding themselves in each other. Both Holt and Maddy had pasts that defined who they were in the present. Pasts that haunted them and made it difficult to move on, but I loved that when they both recognized it that they went for what they wanted. There was no lying and denying for these two. They both realized that the other is what their lives where missing.

There are a lot of aspects to this storyline that kept me reading for more. There was some mystery, suspense, sweet, funny and sexy...oh was there some sexy. What I really loved was that the sexy didn't overpower the storyline, the sexual tension was there and you felt it throughout the book, but it was built and executed in a way that made the anticipation worth it.

Holt is that perfect book boyfriend that makes you swoon and fall in love. He is such a strong male character and I loved his personality. Maddy is the perfect leading lady for Holt. I loved all of their interactions right from the beginning and that Maddy had Holt second guessing his assumptions of her right from the start. I liked that she confused him and that he was trying to figure her out from first meet.

Maddy is just one of those heroines that you fall in love with and root for. The one that you hope finds her way and finally gets a good break in life. Her character grew so much from the first page right until the last page. She deserved every bit of goodness that came her way.

There are a few surprises along the way and they made this story so much better. I loved that when all things were out in the open that it made these characters stronger.

I absolutely LOVE this book! I loved Skylar in Jake Undone and I really LOVE her is this book too.

When we first meet Skylar in Jake Undone you can not help but love her for her snarky personality and sympathize with her situation. I love that this book starts with a Prologue told in Mitch's POV and you get immediately sucked in by his actions and the way he is telling his side of the story. I am not usually one for books that go back in time, but it really made this story so much better to go back to the very beginning of their friendship/relationship. Even as a 10 year old little girl Skylar was immediately lovable and you could tell that she was very wise beyond her years.

The characters in this book are so well written that I easily connected with them. Even though when we first meet Mitch he sounds a little stalkerish you can't help but be sucked in by him. Their relationship was never easy even from the very beginning. They had to go through so much at such young ages that I couldn't help but root for them to eventually end up together. Their tale is not easy and it is very heart wrenching right from the beginning. When they met as kids you could instantly feel the connection that they shared and I just couldn't wait to see how it developed. Their teen relationship really showed what kind of person Mitch was and made him even more lovable. You could feel the love that he had for Skylar in every thought that he had and the same goes for Skylar.  When it gets to the root of why they aren't together in the present I was completely blown away. I really did not see it coming at all. I was a shocked and couldn't really make full sense of it until the other POV from HER.

After the book gets back into the present and we get to see how their relationship continues to grow I just fell even more in love with the both of them. Mitch for trying to be respectful of Skylar's life and also for the man that he turned out to be when he was so afraid of becoming his father. I sympathized with Skylar and her need for safety after she felt so broken. Their relationship is filled with sexual tension and you can definitely feel it. The only thing that I will give away is that their steamy sex scenes are just that...super freaking sexy and super freaking steamy.

I love this book. It is not your everyday romance, but it is so much better. It is filled with raw emotion, love and even some angst. I couldn't help but feel the same emotions that they were going through. My heart raced when I knew something bad was about to happen or even when I could feel something good about to happen. I got he horrible sinking feeling in the pit of my stomach when both Mitch and Skylar shattered because of the actions of another. I cried when Skylar sacrificed her own needs for what she though Mitch would want and need later in life. I was choked up when Mitch showed such devotion to Skylar during one of the most challenging times in her life. I could go on and on and practically give away the whole book, so I will cut my review off now. This book is a MUST read. It is just awesome!

5 EMOTIONALLY SINFUL STARS

**I received an ARC for an honest review.**

This book is by far my most favorite of Penelope Wards, ever. I think I have said that about each and every book that I have read, but this one takes the cake. It is filled with so much more than I thought it would be and it definitely surpassed all of my expectations going into it.

This book contains so much emotion right from the start. It is just packed with so much that I don't even want to mention because I do not want to give any spoilers. But I will say that I am in love with Sevin Montgomery. I will say that he is so much more than the man we meet at the beginning got this book. I will say that it has been awhile since I have connected so fully with a male character and he takes the cake.

As I write this review, I am still reeling a bit from the ending of this book. I can still feel the lump that was lodged there pretty much the entire second half. I am still going through everything that happened and still processing it and keep loving this book more and more.

This book is definitely one of my most favorite reads of 2015 and I can pretty much feel the book hangover coming on.

If you are a Penelope Ward fan then this is a MUST READ. If you have never read a Penelope Ward book before, then this is a MUST READ. If you have never read a book before, but love an emotional and satisfying story then this a MUST READ. So, in my honest opinion Sins of Sevin is a MUST READ.

top_5.reviewText:
I was immediately sucked into this teenage angsty world right from the start. This author did it again with her very developed teenage characters and story line.

I wasn't able to read it fast enough to get to the bottom of it all. I wanted to know every secret and mystery surrounding the characters and their lives. I also love that the two main characters had known each other nearly their whole lives and that their "meet" wasn't a traditional one. Pen pals that live 30 minutes from each other and never cross paths until one night that changed it all.

Ryen isn't who I thought she would be from the shield she wore to fit in. Like any other kid all she ever wanted was to fit in and she did, even though she lost who she really was along the way. But she had her pen pal Misha that she could use as an outlet to who she really was until she didn't anymore. Her character was such a contradiction from internal to external. I really connecter with her inner person, but hated her outer person. The one she projected to everyone for the sake of fitting in. I hated her "friends" and the way she compromised her true self to keep their attention and "respect". But by the end I was so in love with her character and her ability to change for the better.

Misha oh what a hand he was dealt. I felt for him and all the stuff he had been through in his 18 years. I both loved and hated him (which is a common occurrence with this authors male characters) for the way he treated Ryan and that he kept the huge secret from her for way too long. I loved that even though he wanted to hate her for the person she projected he couldn't help but keep coming back to her. He couldn't leave her alone. I love that he pushed her at every turn and that it eventually broke the barrier she had in place.

This book has some surprises and some pretty heavy emotional parts. It is angsty and teenage drama filled. I was sucked in though right off the bat.
top_5.summary: I was immediately sucked into this teenage angsty world right from the start

top_5.reviewText:
I have been dying to read this book since it released, but I wanted to wait until I could read book two as well.

Well, that time finally came and I really dig me some Xavier Cold.

When we meet Anna she has just left the only life she has ever known and is flying across the country to start fresh. She is a wreck and the only saving grace is that once she lands she will be with her cousin who she thinks of as a sister and her aunt who is kooky but loving. She doesn't expect to meet an alpha male on her flight that will consume her thoughts and insert himself into her life.

When we meet Xavier, he is every bit the alpha male just looking for a good time. All those dirty things he said to Anna made me with that she would have given into him on that plane, but I am so glad that she didn't because the build up was worth the wait. It also helped me fall in love with X and see that was capable of something more. I really loved  the small changes that X began to show in this book and that Anna seemed to be just what he needed.

Although at one time he really crushed my heart, but at the same time I know that a man has needs and can only resist so much temptation, but still he broke my heart and he really had to redeem himself.

He did.

Xavier Cold is one of those BBF's that you will eventually compare others to. He is strong and caring (even when he thinks he is evil personified). He is protective of Anna from the very beginning and I love that he realizes that she is different and that she is someone that he needs in his life.

We find out some of X's secrets in this book, but so much is left unanswered and will leave you wanting to so much more from these two. At the end of this book I kept swiping looking wanting it not to end where it did, but luckily I had book two waiting to be read ;)

top_5.reviewText:
I vow that this a 5 STAR READ!!!

**I received an ARC for an honest review.**

This is most definitely one of my most favorites of 2015. I LOVED this book!

Mia Sheridan does an amazing job with this story. I felt the heartache and pain as well and the happiness and love. She makes sure that everything gets it ending and leaves no stone unturned. She has an amazing way with word that draws you into the story and it's characters. Her characters are so well written and easy to love or hate.

Grayson Hawthorn is kind of an ass, but he his an ass that will still make you swoon and root for him. I couldn't help but fall completely and utter in love with him. Although there were times when I wanted to reach into my kindle and smack him around a bit, but after getting into his head and knowing his full story you can help but understand him and the reason he guarded his heart. When all of the truths finally come out and everything is laid bare, I think I fell in love Grayson a little bit more.

So, when Kira is concocting her plan I really didn't see it coming. I though about quite a few things that she could possibly proposed to Grayson to help each other out, but what she actually did was ballsy and after getting to know her totally made sense. I loved her personality the more I got to know her. Especially after knowing her past and relating it to the person she became. She is such a genuine and loving person. I loved that not only did she want to make Grayson's life a little bit better, but she made everyone's lives better in the process.

Her coming into his life allowed him to open up as well as the people around him. I loved all of their interactions even the ones that broke my heart, but I loved that they both started to trust each other enough to open up. I really liked when Kira brought out a side of Grayson that had never been present. I loved that her presence made slowly brought him back to life and let him start to mend the scars of his past. Of course there had to be some pretty awful things have to happen before the mending could begin. And this awful things just about gutted me.

This is a MUST READ!!!
top_5.summary: I LOVED this book

If you're into hardcore, rock, and post-hardcore type music, I highly recommend checking these guys out. They are worth while.

Sci-fi, action, and epics are the movies to get in high def, because they'll give the best viewing experiences in high def.
profile.summary: Pretty Cool Movies Overall!

profile.description: This critically acclaimed epic trilogy follows the quest undertaken by the hobbit, Frodo Baggins, and his fellowship of companions to save Middle-earth by destroying the One Ring and defeating the evil forces of the Dark Lord Sauron.
profile.reviewText: If you're a Lord of the Rings fan and want the best set of the movies to buy, the extended cuts are definitely the way to go. If you have Blu-Ray capability, then it's even better because you'll get the best picture and sound that way, but these are of course also available in DVD if you don't have a Blu-Ray player. These are some of the most epic movies ever, based on one of the most epic fantasy novel series ever written! I think of any book to movie adaption, these are definitely some of the best I've seen. You won't always get every little detail from book to a movie because of time restraints and what have you, but these are definitely the best adaptions I have ever seen. I can hardly wait until Peter Jackson's 2 part film adaption of The Hobbit comes out...you can be sure that will be epic as well! He's also the mind behind some other pretty good films too, like District 9 [Blu-ray], King Kong [Blu-ray], The Frighteners [Blu-ray], and The Lovely Bones (Two-Disc Special Edition) [Blu-ray]. He also has 3 films on the way based off the graphic novel series The Adventures of Tintin, which he is working on with Steven Spielberg, and as a fan of those graphic novels growing up, I am very excited about them. Still, as great as all of those movies are & such, I don't think any other thing he works on will ever measure up to Lord of the Rings, spare maybe The Hobbit, but we shall see what the future holds. These films are truly epic, and everyone should see these films at least once, as I believe most everyone has. Bravo Peter Jackson and crew!
profile.summary: Awesome Edition Of These Epic Films!

profile.reviewText:
I have loved the past Assassin's Creed games, and I was super excited when I heard that an Assassin's Creed III was on the way...and taking place during Colonial times no less!  I had a copy reserved as soon as it was available for pre-order...and the limited edition steel case I received with my pre-order was pretty awesome too!  It's displayed up on the top shelf of my bookshelf alongside my Skyrim collector's edition stuff and the Assassin's Creed III stuff that came in this great limited edition set!

With very few exceptions, I'm really not one for snagging these limited edition sets like this...I'm usually more interested in just playing the games, and many of the collector's sets I see aren't really anything to write home about, not to mention that most of them are pretty expensive.  The only other games I've ever gotten the collector's editions of were Skyrim (because Skyrim is epic), God of War III, and The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time way back in the day...the gold edition with the soundtrack and t-shirt, which I still have to this day.  This particular limited edition I had to have though, because I love the Assassin's Creed franchise and this limited edition set's contents were pretty awesome.

The statuette of Connor that came in this set was detailed and very awesome looking, a great piece to adorn the top of my book shelf along with the collectible AC belt buckle and George Washington's journal that came with it too...both of which are pretty cool little collectibles.  The flag was actually bigger than I was expecting...like just about full size.  I was expecting it to maybe be half that size.  Totally cool though...adorns the wall within my "man cave" very nicely.  All this neat stuff was totally worth the extra $60 in my opinion!

As for the game, well...the game was overall pretty freakin fantastic!  I was sad to see Ezio's journey end, but it was also cool to see a new character come into play in the Assassin's Creed franchise.  I'll always have the past Assassin's Creed games to play whenever though, so no worries there.  Although Connor is not as flamboyant and occasionally comical like Ezio was, he's still a very strong character whose concern lies mainly with his people and protecting them...at least half of what Connor does in the game is to the benefit of his people, and the other half basically to see the Templars schemes put to a stop...even if it means putting an end to his father, who happens to be a Templar.  I don't want to say anything else beyond that...play the game!

The Pros:  The gameplay is fun and addictive, and the control mechanics are tightened up pretty well and it is overall pretty easy to control Connor.  Some classic weapons were brought back into the game in different manners and more suited to the time period.  As an example, a mace from back during the Ezio games is now in the form of either a big club or big hammer of sorts.  All the weapons are pretty neat.  Of course the hidden assassin blades are still in the game.  For secondary weapons, you have the flintlock pistol and various other neat pistols at your disposal, as well as bow and arrow.  The poison darts are back in this one too, a classic and enjoyable assassin weapon.  The rope dart was fun to use too...it can be used to pull enemies closer to you or, which I enjoyed the most, used from above to hang enemies...great fun!  The environments are very pristine looking and I hardly noticed very many glitches with them.  The environments are also suitably large, especially the frontier...plenty of exploring to be had and side quests to complete!  A form of the tower taking side quests from Brotherhood is back in this game as well, which was something I very much enjoyed in that game...in this one, you actually capture British forts for the Colonials...there are about 2 per area and really very fun to capture.  I won't go into too much detail about all the side stuff that you can do and everything...just play the game and find out for yourself.  It's really very awesome.  And the naval stuff...oh man, wicked cool!  I very much enjoyed the naval commandeering and battles...a quality edition to the game!  I hope there is more of that in future Assassin's Creed games as well!

The Cons:  You start out playing Connor's father in the game, leading up to how Connor came to be, and aside from a little action here & there the game did start out noticably slow with not a whole lot of action and very few side things at the time.  However, don't let that hinder you because there's some good background story involved there and it's only for a little ways into the game.  Once you begin to start playing as Connor and he seeks out the retired assassin Achiles and becomes an assassin, then things pick up very nicely.  There were a few of the standard Assassin's Creed glitches within the game too, though it does seem that they have really tightened up on that and those glitches were fewer and further between, (as an example, when you're running across buildings and you're pushing forward for instance and all of a sudden when you jump, the character decides to jump in a different direction...or like when you've synched with a viewpoint and you're trying to jump the character into a hay cart or something and he instead decides to jump off to the left or right and you plummet to your doom).  These little glitches are a bit bothersome and rather annoying, but don't let that deter you...only once in a while did I encounter these glitches within the game.  And then the only other one thing I did notice was near the beginning when you're on a ship as Connor's father, there's a small cut scene in which you're talking to the captain and his mouth is not moving at all, but that's one of those things that Ubisoft will likely fix with a patch in an update, so not a big deal.  There are these few little minor things in the game, but really not enough to put off the enjoyment of the game.

As for the parts involving Desmond, there is some cool stuff involved within that and the end with him was rather interesting, but some of those parts I could honestly take or leave.  It'll be nice to see them finally do an actual game though as Desmond as the main assassin...like a modern day assassin's creed game.  Maybe one day, but I'm also up for Ubisoft exploring other time periods and other assassins as well, not so anxious for the Assassin's Creed franchise to end just yet.  However, there may not even be a Desmond game depending on what happens in the end, after the end of the game, but I'm not going to reveal anything to anyone...find out for yourself.

All around, Assassin's Creed III was a very enjoyable game and the collector's items that came in this set are all very cool and worthwhile trinkets.  I will definitely be keeping this and I plan to play that game again in the not too distant future, along with all the Ezio games.  (I have played the 1st one but was honestly not real into that one, but I love II, Brotherhood, Revelations, and III!)  If you like open world action adventure games or are a fan of past Assassin's Creed games, then I highly recommend at least just picking up the game and playing it...it's worthwhile!
profile.summary: A Must For Assassin's Creed Uber Fans!  4.5 out of 5!

profile.reviewText:
I have enjoyed these movies ever since I can remember!  I grew up between 2 homes, my dad and step mom and my mom and step dad, where action and sci-fi movies were played often, so needless to say I grew up on a lot of the classics such as these films, Star Wars, Die Hard, Terminator 1 & 2, etc, etc.  These ones were a popular watch at my mom and step dad's house.

I think the first one I ever saw was 2 back sometime around 6th grade or something like that, and from there I went on to eventually see 1 and 3...and then 4 when it eventually came out.  2 was the favorite movie until 4 came out, but we enjoyed all of them!  I have loved these films ever since!  Some of the best buddy action comedy movies ever!  Mel Gibson and Danny Glover are awesome together in these films, and their chemistry together on screen just flows well.  LoL, I love the chief too dealing with the 2 of them, and Mel Gibson's exchanges with the precinct shrink...classic!  Acting is all around pretty superb.

As far as humor in action movies, you don't get much better than this, and they get funnier with each passing film!  The exchanges between Mel Gibson and Danny Glover are often pretty comical.  Then throw in Joe Pesci in LW 2 and his shennaigans, and it just adds to it.  Then you throw Chris Rock into the mix in 4 and it's all a riot...4 is probably the funniest one of all of them.

Action wise, it's off the hook!  Quality car chases, lots of shoot em up moments, explosions, all that action packed goodness!  Again, 4 probably takes the cake in this department too, having probably the most action of them all.  All of them are great though as far as action.

As far as the packaging is concerned, I like it!  And a whole lot better than the DVD copies I had too, which were in what I like to call the stupid cases...those taller ones with the plastic bars on the top and bottom, and the plastic bar that you open on the side to open up the DVD, and you have a hard time fitting them into your shelves next to other DVDs because the stupid plastic bars snag on the other DVDs.  Yes...those kind of stupid cases!  I'm glad I finally have this Blu-Ray set because it meant that I could get rid of those stupid cases, LoL.  I'd been trying to upgrade to the Blu-Ray set for a while now and then my wife finally got it for me for Valentine's Day, (she's awesome like that), and I was glad to finally sell of the DVDs.  I'd say the only thing that I thought was funny about the packaging is that there's 5 discs, LW 1-4 plus a bonus disc, but the casing had 6 disc slots.  Why on earth would they make a 6 disc case for only 5 dics.  Seems kinda funny to me, but not really a big deal.  What matters is that I have some of my favorite action films of all time in high definition and in a set that fits much more nicely in my movie collection than the DVD copies, and I'm super excited!  :-)

For any of you action lovers who have not seen these movies yet, what are you waiting for?  To any of you who love these movies and are looking to upgrade to Blu-Ray, do it!  Choice material!  I've marathoned these movies many times, and I'm looking to do so again very soon!  Choice viewing!
profile.summary: Great Movies, Great Set!

I very much enjoy the Guitar Hero titles, as well as even a few of the Rock Band titles, but I always enjoyed Guitar Hero a little more.  This one takes a bunch of the most favorite songs from between Guitar Hero 1 and World Tour and combines them together, and the majority of those chosen are great songs! profile.description: Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter explores the secret life of our greatest president, and the untold story that shaped our nation. Visionary filmmakers Tim Burton and Timur Bekmambetov (director of Wanted) bring a fresh and visceral voice to the bloodthirsty lore of the vampire, imagining lincoln as history's greatest hunter of the undead.
profile.reviewText:
After seeing the trailer and reading a little bit about this film, I thought it looked like a cool watch but I really wasn't sure if it would wind up being the caliber of movie I'd want to pay theater prices to see...maybe more like a rental or something.  A little hope was restored when I saw that Timur Bekmambetov was directing and that Tim Burton was producing...I am a long time fan of Tim Burton, and I very much enjoyed Timur's movies Wanted and 9.  There were other bigger movies around that time that I was wanting to see in the theater, so I decided I'd compromise anad wait & see this at a local dollar theater instead, which I finally got around to doing.

Though I think a couple of things were over done and there were a couple of kinda cheesy parts, I must admit that this movie was actually better than I had expected it to be...a great blending of history and fantasy/horror!  The characters were, for the most part, pretty believable.  The special effects were overall pretty well done, spare maybe a couple of parts, and the concept was actually pretty neat.  I do understand that this movie was based off the book of the same name by Seth Grahamme-Smith, and it makes me hopeful that maybe they'll actually make a movie based off his other popular book Pride Prejudice and Zombies...and I'm not even a Pride and Prejudice kind of person, though I do love zombie films.

In any case, if you've enjoyed any of Timur Bekmambetov & Tim Burton's movies in the past, I would highly suggest checking this movie out, because it was honestly pretty good...not, I would say, my absolute favorite movie of the summer, but still pretty dang entertaining.  Give it a watch!  I for one will probably be picking this one up on Blu-Ray!
profile.summary: Better Than I Expected!

profile.description: Garrett, the Master Thief, steps out of the shadows into the City. In this treacherous place, where the Baron's Watch spreads a rising tide of fear and oppression, his skills are the only things he can trust. Even the most cautious citizens and their best-guarded possessions are not safe from his reach. As an uprising emerges, Garrett finds himself entangled in growing layers of conflict. Lead by Orion, the voice of the people, the tyrannized citizens will do everything they can to claim back the City from the Baron's grasp. The revolution is inevitable. If Garrett doesn't get involved, the streets will run red with blood and the City will tear itself apart.
profile.reviewText:
I had highly anticipated the release of this game and I really wanted to like it, but in the end I found it to just be rather mediocre.  I played about 4 chapters into this game before deciding to trade it in on something else.  I didn't hate the game necessarily, but it left a bit to be desired.

Breaking into places and picking locks & sneaking around & thieving valuables etc was fun at first, but eventually just got rather monotonous and lost it's luster.  Traveling around the city & squeezing through crevices etc got to the point where it seemed like a chore...became repetitive and/or tedious, and was sometimes confusing.  I personally had a hard time deciphering the map as well and was hard to distinguish where to go when I was trying to find certain places again or the merchant to buy materials etc.  I even got rather confused trying to find my way to the area in the 4th chapter.  Some people might have had no trouble there, but I am among many people whose navigational skills aren't always that keen, and having a confusing map to look at did not help matters.

Graphically Thief was not all that impressive, it seemed more like mid era PS3 graphics to me than eye popping PS4 graphics...and the frame rate was certainly not PS4 quality, compared to what I'd seen with games like Assasssin's Creed Black Flag or Tomb Raider Definitive Edition etc.  Graphically it was often somewhat choppy as well and character movements were sometimes choppy as well.  There were parts where character mouth movements didn't exactly match words being spoken, or was just a monotonous up & down motion.

Some of the environments in the game seemed fairly interesting and gothic, which I thought was neat, but much of the area left a bit to be desired, especially when gazing off across the city or a large expanse of space...much of the distant horizon seemed somewhat broken up & choppy.

The story seemed fairly interesting, but with all the many faults if this game I just simply could not bring myself to continue on with the game.  Just another attempt to profit off of an otherwise classic game.  I've never played the original PC game before so I can't attest to what it was like, but I have read reviews by others who have said it does not do the classic game any justice, and I believe it, judging from what I experienced myself on this PS4 version.

There are some who I have read enjoyed this game, and there may be others of you who do too...to each their own.  However, I felt it was a feeble attempt on PS4 and I would recommend renting it before buying and see for yourself whether or not you are going to like it.  Even though I gave it a 2.5, I did give click the upper end of the spectrum at 3 because it's not exactly a terrible game, but it's definitely not a very good game.
profile.summary: Fell Short, 2.5 out of 5

profile.description: Since 2005 Saving Grace s ever-growing fan base and dedication to touring has earned them the reputation of the most successful spirit-filled hardcore act downunder. Saving Grace was born in a small coastal beach town in New Zealand, a sleeping beginning to a band that would become a metallic hardcore powerhouse, playing music in the 90s hardcore style of Earth Crisis and Arkangel mixed with the classic metal bands like Slayer and Sepultura. Saving Grace have toured the US, New Zealand, Australia, and Mexico and there is no end in site for touring in support of this new album.
profile.reviewText: I fell in love with this band after having first heard some stuff off of their debut album Behind Enemy Lines on Harvest Earth Records. I don't know if Harvest Earth Records later shut down or what, but a physical copy of Behind Enemy Lines is hard to find anymore, at least for any less than $20-$30, though you can easily get it on digital download of it on Amazon for $8.99. Anyway, ever since then I've absolutely loved Saving Grace and have not missed a release by them yet. Unbreakable (Dig) is also a fantastic album, and was their debut album after having signed on with Facedown Records, who is or at least was affiliated with Harvest Earth Records. Then, later on, they released their next metal masterpiece that is King Is Coming. King Is Coming is an absolutely brutal death metal ride full of lyrics containing both warning of impending judgment and more importantly, a message of hope. My kinda dudes, my kinda metal! \m/ If you love modern metal & death metal, than friends...I very highly recommend checking out this album, or the band's entire works for that matter! They are absolutely fantastic! Quality face melting material! Love it!
profile.summary: Absolutely <3 This Band!

profile.description: 2012 album from Italy's greatest musical export. The album was recorded with acclaimed producer Don Gilmore (Avril Lavigne, Linkin Park, Pearl Jam) at the famed NRG Studios in Los Angeles. Dark Adrenaline is another huge step forward in the band's continuous evolution and marks their first full-length since 2008's Shallow Life and promises to be well worth the wait.
profile.reviewText: My wife and I both really like Lacuna Coil, so of course when this new offering by them came out, we had to snag it.  We had heard a few songs off of it before it's release and loved them, so I went out on the day of release and picked up the CD/DVD version of it for us, which came with some cool stuff...a guitar pick, a poster, and a sticker.  We have not yet watched the DVD, but I'm sure there is some cool content on it.  We sat and listened through the whole album that afternoon while we ate lunch and were blown away.  Amazing album all the way through...probably their best album yet in our opinion!  We have listened to it multiple times and just simply love it!  If you're a rock/metal fan, I highly recommend checking these guys out...at least this album if nothing more.  Great stuff!
profile.summary: Their Best Album Yet!

profile.description: In this sequel, the G.I. Joes are not only fighting their mortal enemy Cobra; they are forced to contend with threats from within the government that jeopardize their very existence.
profile.reviewText:
*SPOILER ALERT WITHIN THIS REVIEW...FYI!*

My dad and I were both interested in seeing this movie because we enjoyed the first one, so I decided I would treat him to a viewing for his birthday.  We both really enjoyed the movie, it was action packed and a lot of fun! I enjoyed the movie overall, but my favorite of it was seeing what developed with Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow.  I don't want to say too much on that account, just watch the movie for yourself.

The actors all did a good job in the film, and it was a joy to see Dwayne Johnson as Roadblock and Bruce Willis as General Colton.  I was glad to see Flint and Lady J in the film too, as I'd wondered why they were not included in the first film, though regardless, I did really enjoy the first film.  And as always, a joy to have Ray Park back as Snake Eyes and Lee Byung-hun as Storm Shadow.

Now for the aspects of the film that I did not really care for, mainly involving the characters, or lack there of.  *SPOILER ALERTS* Firstly, although I know the director had or might have a purpose for it, I didn't like that they killed of Duke, especially considering he was a primary character in the cartoon series...just didn't sit well with me.  Secondly and primarily, what the heck happened to some of the characters from the first film?  I.e. Ripcord, Baroness, etc.  They all seemed fine and dandy at the end of the first movie?  Why did they just suddenly drop out of the picture, without us knowing what became of them?  I imagine that some of it had to do with the fact that they couldn't get some of the actors back to play the rolls again, but c'mon...give us something!  It was kind of annoying to me that they suddenly weren't involved in the 2nd movie, without even so much as an explaination on what become of them.  I don't know, maybe they'll make a return in the 3rd film, because you know they'll make a 3rd one, and then maybe we'll get some answers.  Growing up loving GI Joe and being a bit of a fan, this just kind of bugs me.

All that aside though, with that exception, the movie is awesome and action packed and should suffice most action movie fanatics, whether you grew up with GI Joe or just a big time action movie fan, which I am both.  Check it out, but decide for yourselves whether to pay to see it while it's still in the theater, or to buy it or just rent it down the road.
profile.summary: 3.5/5 Action Packed And Fun, But Unhappy About A Couple Of Things...

profile.description: 2009 sophomore release. In the two short years since the release of the band's full length debut Genesis, Job For A Cowboy JFAC) has progressed from the band with the different name to one of the leading lights for heavy music in the 21st century. Ruination sees JFAC advance by leaps and bounds; the record is a concentrated hotbed of astounding dexterity, scorching attack, sleek arrangement and thundering musical muscle. Infectious riffs, keen dynamics and the assertive vocals of rising star front man Jonny Davy combine to produce an album that is at once powerful, expressive, confident and commanding.
profile.reviewText: Admittedly, I had not yet heard this entire album before writing this review, but I have heard enough to know that this is an amazing album...ever so much better than Genesis was.  My first taste of Job For A Cowboy was via Doom, and I simply loved their debut EP.  I had bought it about the time that Genesis was out.  However, later I bought Genesis and that album, in my opinion, wasn't so good...it kinda put me off Job For A Cowboy for a while because it lacked some of Doom's luster and they had dropped much of the technical and grindcore elements that really made me like their music in the first place.  That's neither here nor there now though.  After Ruination had been out for a while, I finally took a listen to a couple of tracks off of it and realized that the Job For A Cowboy I had loved previously were back!  As I write this, I haven't yet picked up a copy of this album, (in fact, I was just about to pop over and order a copy as I write this), but I did go right on and pick up Demonocracy upon it's release, and it's pretty freakin amazing!  After I get Ruination, I will have the albums I care to own by Job For A Cowboy.  I don't know what happened with Genesis, but they must have learned from that album, because they got much better again after that.  To my fellow metal heads out there, I highly recommend Doom, Ruination, and Demonocracy.  Judge Genesis for yourself, but I highly recommend listening to a little of it before deciding to buy it.  But yeah, Ruination is pretty legit!  Shred on!  \m/(^-^)\m/
profile.summary: Bad@$$!  So Much Better Than Genesis!

profile.description: STAR WARS EPISODIO III:LA VENGANZA DE LOS SITH. ltimo captulo de la saga de Star Wars, en el que Anakin Skywalker definitivamente se pasa al lado oscuro. En el Episodio III aparece el General Grievous, un ser implacable mitad-alien mitad-robot, el lder del ejrcito separatista Droid. Los Sith son los amos del lado oscuro de la Fuerza y los enemigos de los Jedi. Ellos fueron prcticamente exterminados por los Jedi hace mil aos, pero la orden del mal sobrevivi en la clandestinidad.
profile.reviewText: As most Star Wars fans would agree, the original Star Wars trilogy, episodes IV-VI, are and will always be the best Star Wars films ever!  Episodes I-III weren't quite the same.  However, that being said, they are still pretty epic...especially episode III!  If you're a Star Wars fan, the original trilogy is definitely the best, but the prequel trilogy is still awesome and fills in the story of what came to be quite well I think.  The only part of episodes I-III that I honestly did not care much for was Jar Jar Binks.  What a waste of space & budget, I'm sorry to say.  I did find it rather enjoy it when he got his head caught in the pod racer beam in episode I though...that was pretty funny.  Otherwise, I thought he was absolutely worthless.  Despite that, I still couldn't bring myself to give these films any less than 5 stars, because they are still pretty epic and worthy to be in any good sci-fi movie collection.
profile.summary: Not Quite Up To Par With The Classics, But Still Awesome!

profile.description: I AM LEGEND
profile.reviewText:
I loved I Am Legend the first time I saw it!  I loved it even more when I saw the version with the alternate ending, and that's pretty much the way I prefer watching it because I hated what happened to Will Smith in the end of the original version.

When this movie had first come out onto DVD and Blu-Ray, I initally picked up the DVD because I did not yet have Blu-Ray capabilities, but eventually I bought myself a PlayStation 3 and among one of the first movies I upgraded to Blu-Ray after a handful of classics was I Am Legend.

I'd been familiar with the ultimate collector's editions of the film but never bought one at the time, mostly because money was tight and they were a bit more expensive back then.  However, I finally broke down and decided to buy one of them.  I already owned the Blu-Ray copy, and for the longest time I had seen a DVD ultimate collector's edition set sitting up on top of a cabinet containing movie sets at a local entertainment store I frequent, and I would always eyeball it when I was in there.

Eventually the set hit $14.99, and a while later I had happened to have some Christmas movie & finally broke down and decided to buy it.  I loved that movie and I couldn't stand to see that cool set sit there and collect dust.  Having the Blu-Ray, I will always watch that, but I bought the set if nothing other than for pure nostalgia.  It has some cool collectibles and I just like owning it.

So yes, this is a bit more of a story as to how I came across this than an actual review, but review wise...if you are a fan of this movie, this collector's set, whether Blu-Ray or DVD, is pretty cool and it would be a cool collectible for anyone who enjoys this movie.  I think eventually I'm even going to try and incorporate my Blu-Ray copy into it, if I ever come across a slim enough case.  But yeah, totally cool set...I love it!
profile.summary: Great Movie, Great Set!

profile.description: Get mixed up in the mob underworld of a fictitious late 1940's and early 1950's! Developed by Illusion Softworks, creators of the original game, Mafia 2 embraces the elements of the first game while bringing an all-new experience fans have been waiting for, featuring a mobster narrative packed with both behind-the-wheel and on-foot action. Players will easily become engaged in the game's cinematic Hollywood movie experience with strong, believable characters in a living, breathing city. By fusing high octane gunplay with white knuckle driving and an engaging narrative, Mafia 2 looks to be the industry's most compelling Mafia title to date.
profile.reviewText: If you're going into this game expecting another version of GTA, think again...though it's open world to a degree, it's nowhere near as open as say GTA IV, and there really isn't much in the way of side missions.  You can kind of explore the city and screw around a little bit between missions if you want to, but it really follows a more linear path and has a pretty set storyline to it...your a war hero returned home who, accompanied by a close friend, work their way into the Mob and work their way up the latter...lots of hand to hand combat and stealing stuff and shooting thugs.  Those are the primary 3 things you will be doing in your missions on this game.  While it's not as open, in depth, and big as GTA IV, this is still an enjoyable game, and if you're into gangster & crime games, you should still at least give this game a play through.  It really ain't too bad.
profile.summary: It's No GTA, But It's Still Enjoyable

profile.description: Django Unchained (2012)
profile.reviewText: Knowing Quentin Tarrantino I knew this movie would probably be a bit brutal and bloody in parts and a bit racy, and boy was it ever!  But it was great!  A very well made and directed film, one of Tarrantino's best I'd venture to say, alongside Pulp Fiction and Inglorious Basterds.  He is very keen on dialogue, and there's some great dialogue in this film, plus his love for spaghetti westerns definitely shows in this film.  I will likely buy this on day one!  To any of you Tarrantino fans out there or that like a really well made film and don't mind gore and racial stuff & a bit of brutality, then I highly recommend this film.  If you are sensitive to any of the following...racial issues, brutality, violence & gore, or strong language...then I suggest you avoid it.  Otherwise fellow movie lovers, I say watch it!
profile.summary: Brutal But Very Well Done!

profile.description: Thor: God of Thunder
profile.reviewText: If they had made this game back on Playstation 2, it might have passed for a kind of sub par title on that system that might have gotten some play for a little while, but this game really isn't all that great, especially for being a new gen system title. The graphics are so early Playstation 2 and, even for Playstation 2, the game play is not all that great at all. Thor got jipped on this title in my opinion. I played maybe a level of it and said screw this. Play it if you really want to, but I recommend renting it. It was very disappointing. Captain America: Super Soldier was so much better! I think they learned from this one and got their act together in making Captain America. My prognosis is to skip this title.
profile.summary: More Like A Mediocre Ps2 Title

profile.description: Darth Vader (Death Star)
profile.reviewText: I love Legos...I received several sets during my adolescence and loved building them and having little wars with them.  Now I'm an adult...still a big kid at heart and major geek, and I collect some novelty Lego sets here & there to build and just collect.  It is a hobby!  I have unfortunately been unable to acquire as many of the sets as I would have liked to, Star Wars or otherwise, partly due to lack of funds for them, but I have acquired a few pretty awesome sets.  I never did acquire a set including Darth Vader, and I had really really wanted a Darth Vader Star Wars Lego figure.  I searched around here on Amazon and found myself one for about $15, which is kind of expensive, but Legos tend to start getting rare after they have been out for so long, because once the sets run out, that's it.  I have some Lego figures, though, worth a lot more than that...and I figured I may as well get the figure now while I can, instead of down the road when it becomes worth more.  This little figure sits proudly atop one of my book cases in my wife and I's living room...totally worth the price I paid for him!
profile.summary: A Must Have Lego Figure For Geeks Everywhere!

top_5.reviewText:
I still think the first movie is my favorite of the 3, but I enjoyed all of these movies pretty well...I felt they were good modern movie takes on a toy & cartoon I actually grew up with.  It was cool that they got the same guy to do the voice of Optimus that di it in the original cartoon too...cool that he's still around.  I think one or two of the others may have had the same voicework too, but not entirely sure.

Anyway, though I thought perhaps maybe a few things could have been done better throughout the course of the 2nd & 3rd films, I felt none the less that they were awesome and action packed, with a good amount of appropriate humor mixed in throughout them as well.  I own each movie on DVD, but I'm thinking about upgrading them to this Blu-Ray box set sometime soon, so as to get the full high def experience on them, because these are some of the kinds of movies that I like to have in high def because action packed movies like this sound the best...and these types of movies are also my favorite types of movies, other than comedies & certain family movies, but I'm content just getting DVDs of those types of movies.  Sci-fi, action, and epics are the movies to get in high def, because they'll give the best viewing experiences in high def.
top_5.summary: Pretty Cool Movies Overall!

top_5.description: This critically acclaimed epic trilogy follows the quest undertaken by the hobbit, Frodo Baggins, and his fellowship of companions to save Middle-earth by destroying the One Ring and defeating the evil forces of the Dark Lord Sauron.
top_5.reviewText: If you're a Lord of the Rings fan and want the best set of the movies to buy, the extended cuts are definitely the way to go. If you have Blu-Ray capability, then it's even better because you'll get the best picture and sound that way, but these are of course also available in DVD if you don't have a Blu-Ray player. These are some of the most epic movies ever, based on one of the most epic fantasy novel series ever written! I think of any book to movie adaption, these are definitely some of the best I've seen. You won't always get every little detail from book to a movie because of time restraints and what have you, but these are definitely the best adaptions I have ever seen. I can hardly wait until Peter Jackson's 2 part film adaption of The Hobbit comes out...you can be sure that will be epic as well! He's also the mind behind some other pretty good films too, like District 9 [Blu-ray], King Kong [Blu-ray], The Frighteners [Blu-ray], and The Lovely Bones (Two-Disc Special Edition) [Blu-ray]. He also has 3 films on the way based off the graphic novel series The Adventures of Tintin, which he is working on with Steven Spielberg, and as a fan of those graphic novels growing up, I am very excited about them. Still, as great as all of those movies are & such, I don't think any other thing he works on will ever measure up to Lord of the Rings, spare maybe The Hobbit, but we shall see what the future holds. These films are truly epic, and everyone should see these films at least once, as I believe most everyone has. Bravo Peter Jackson and crew!
top_5.summary: Awesome Edition Of These Epic Films!

top_5.description: PERFECT CONDITION. FACTORY SEALED WITH NO RIPS OR TEARS.
top_5.reviewText:
I have loved the past Assassin's Creed games, and I was super excited when I heard that an Assassin's Creed III was on the way...and taking place during Colonial times no less!  I had a copy reserved as soon as it was available for pre-order...and the limited edition steel case I received with my pre-order was pretty awesome too!  It's displayed up on the top shelf of my bookshelf alongside my Skyrim collector's edition stuff and the Assassin's Creed III stuff that came in this great limited edition set!

With very few exceptions, I'm really not one for snagging these limited edition sets like this...I'm usually more interested in just playing the games, and many of the collector's sets I see aren't really anything to write home about, not to mention that most of them are pretty expensive.  The only other games I've ever gotten the collector's editions of were Skyrim (because Skyrim is epic), God of War III, and The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time way back in the day...the gold edition with the soundtrack and t-shirt, which I still have to this day.  This particular limited edition I had to have though, because I love the Assassin's Creed franchise and this limited edition set's contents were pretty awesome.

The statuette of Connor that came in this set was detailed and very awesome looking, a great piece to adorn the top of my book shelf along with the collectible AC belt buckle and George Washington's journal that came with it too...both of which are pretty cool little collectibles.  The flag was actually bigger than I was expecting...like just about full size.  I was expecting it to maybe be half that size.  Totally cool though...adorns the wall within my "man cave" very nicely.  All this neat stuff was totally worth the extra $60 in my opinion!

As for the game, well...the game was overall pretty freakin fantastic!  I was sad to see Ezio's journey end, but it was also cool to see a new character come into play in the Assassin's Creed franchise.  I'll always have the past Assassin's Creed games to play whenever though, so no worries there.  Although Connor is not as flamboyant and occasionally comical like Ezio was, he's still a very strong character whose concern lies mainly with his people and protecting them...at least half of what Connor does in the game is to the benefit of his people, and the other half basically to see the Templars schemes put to a stop...even if it means putting an end to his father, who happens to be a Templar.  I don't want to say anything else beyond that...play the game!

The Pros:  The gameplay is fun and addictive, and the control mechanics are tightened up pretty well and it is overall pretty easy to control Connor.  Some classic weapons were brought back into the game in different manners and more suited to the time period.  As an example, a mace from back during the Ezio games is now in the form of either a big club or big hammer of sorts.  All the weapons are pretty neat.  Of course the hidden assassin blades are still in the game.  For secondary weapons, you have the flintlock pistol and various other neat pistols at your disposal, as well as bow and arrow.  The poison darts are back in this one too, a classic and enjoyable assassin weapon.  The rope dart was fun to use too...it can be used to pull enemies closer to you or, which I enjoyed the most, used from above to hang enemies...great fun!  The environments are very pristine looking and I hardly noticed very many glitches with them.  The environments are also suitably large, especially the frontier...plenty of exploring to be had and side quests to complete!  A form of the tower taking side quests from Brotherhood is back in this game as well, which was something I very much enjoyed in that game...in this one, you actually capture British forts for the Colonials...there are about 2 per area and really very fun to capture.  I won't go into too much detail about all the side stuff that you can do and everything...just play the game and find out for yourself.  It's really very awesome.  And the naval stuff...oh man, wicked cool!  I very much enjoyed the naval commandeering and battles...a quality edition to the game!  I hope there is more of that in future Assassin's Creed games as well!

The Cons:  You start out playing Connor's father in the game, leading up to how Connor came to be, and aside from a little action here & there the game did start out noticably slow with not a whole lot of action and very few side things at the time.  However, don't let that hinder you because there's some good background story involved there and it's only for a little ways into the game.  Once you begin to start playing as Connor and he seeks out the retired assassin Achiles and becomes an assassin, then things pick up very nicely.  There were a few of the standard Assassin's Creed glitches within the game too, though it does seem that they have really tightened up on that and those glitches were fewer and further between, (as an example, when you're running across buildings and you're pushing forward for instance and all of a sudden when you jump, the character decides to jump in a different direction...or like when you've synched with a viewpoint and you're trying to jump the character into a hay cart or something and he instead decides to jump off to the left or right and you plummet to your doom).  These little glitches are a bit bothersome and rather annoying, but don't let that deter you...only once in a while did I encounter these glitches within the game.  And then the only other one thing I did notice was near the beginning when you're on a ship as Connor's father, there's a small cut scene in which you're talking to the captain and his mouth is not moving at all, but that's one of those things that Ubisoft will likely fix with a patch in an update, so not a big deal.  There are these few little minor things in the game, but really not enough to put off the enjoyment of the game.

As for the parts involving Desmond, there is some cool stuff involved within that and the end with him was rather interesting, but some of those parts I could honestly take or leave.  It'll be nice to see them finally do an actual game though as Desmond as the main assassin...like a modern day assassin's creed game.  Maybe one day, but I'm also up for Ubisoft exploring other time periods and other assassins as well, not so anxious for the Assassin's Creed franchise to end just yet.  However, there may not even be a Desmond game depending on what happens in the end, after the end of the game, but I'm not going to reveal anything to anyone...find out for yourself.

All around, Assassin's Creed III was a very enjoyable game and the collector's items that came in this set are all very cool and worthwhile trinkets.  I will definitely be keeping this and I plan to play that game again in the not too distant future, along with all the Ezio games.  (I have played the 1st one but was honestly not real into that one, but I love II, Brotherhood, Revelations, and III!)  If you like open world action adventure games or are a fan of past Assassin's Creed games, then I highly recommend at least just picking up the game and playing it...it's worthwhile!
top_5.summary: A Must For Assassin's Creed Uber Fans!  4.5 out of 5!
