But for some reason the Rascal decided to ignore the pheromone collar or it's lost it's effect to help keep the peace with the rascal and he's picking on the bigger cat again starting this past winter. So ran into this calm coat. The idea has merit but so far it's not working with our little meany me. Actually he's been caught going after the neutral kit the last two days? That's making it appear the stress relief coat is making the dynamics worse. So will give it a few more days try. Leaving it on him most days from 9 a.m. to 10 evenings. But he wants his evening brushing and we remove it then for the rest of the night. The size is off also for our little guy. He weighs right close to 12 pounds at the vets. He has a funny build with very narrow shoulders and a kind of bullet shaped body that's fatter on the back end then the front but a lot of it is FUR. I think the coat needs to be a good 2 inches longer to fit better so I may add an extention to the arm that wraps around the body to achieve that. The front chest wrap is plenty big. I suspect it might fit a short hair kit better than this particular long haired one...his fur actually sticks straight up along his sides when he sleeps....like a little bush. I am not willing to give it 3 stars because I do think it has merit and probably will work with some cats as the reviews show. But unfortunately our little beasty is as stuborn as ever. .........Something that might be helpful to those folks who have trouble using the pheromone collars and have this item you could sew a small narrow pocket on thte upper back area with a velcro closed/open end where you could push half a collar cut in two into it and the cat could wear the collar that way. Yes they would too benefit from the collar. Keep the second half of collar in fridge closed up in ziplock bags until you see signs it needs replaced on kitty coat. Pockets for collar or half or quarter collars could be placed in other places on this coat too. Overall...if worse comes to it I may try that myself since this being the bad kitty we hate to punish the victim cat with the collar but this is not all that out of the norm too. Like this the pheromone collars do not always work the way we expect or on the cat we expect. This bad kitty we tried the collars the orginal on the cat as sold and it lasted two days before it took us three years to discover where he lost it. (Cleaning up a sewing room more than usual...finally found it under an old portable tv used for work and show and tell on the road video and microscope work. So relieved we did finally find it and cat didn't eat it. But there was no keeping the collar on this cat. So we turned to the other cat and he is not happy with it...it clearly does temper his personality which has it's good points but it's down side too. Anyway this wrinkles up badly on this kitty and suggests it needs to be a bit looser too I think. He is a bit short bodied though. Like I said a funny shaped kitty compared to the normal range.
profile.summary: I so want this to work. So far it isn't doing it. He tolerates it kinda....we know..we know. We love our kits even the bad boy!

profile.description:
XLC Rear Trunk Cargo Box Deluxe - Hardshell with Carrier Handle !
 Locking hardshell Case with Ergonomic Carrier Handle !
 Quick Release, Removable at the push of a button, Includes Removable Adapter Pkate !
 Cargo Weight Capacity 22 lbs. Volume Capacity 17 liters !
 Dimensions: 40 x 25 x 17 cm. Weight: 1727g.
profile.reviewText:
Just got back from 2 day bike trip & this box worked out great as a trunk. I carried food & 2 water bottles that don't leak of course. I carred two apples, a pound bag of carrots, a bag of carmel corn, the water, small camera, rain jacket which kept everything from jumping around. The last day I lost half those contents on the ground and didn't realize until others noticed what happened. OOPS! Not box fault mine. I have a bad leg & have to dip bike all the way over to step my foot to other side these days. And I hadn't clipped the box shut.
I suspect the plastic could fail in a crash and definitely would scuff. Top got scuffed up when we attached the release plate to the bottom. A towel placed on ground or table before hand would prevent this.
The silly keys I'll never use. Really what good is the key/lock system when anyone could just remove & walk away with the entire quick release box? Meantime it held a decent amount of stuff for a day trip & did well on a fairly rough trail. Hiawatha Railbed converted Bike Path look it up on Google:))) Coming down is the bone shaking part. We enjoy the bottom up approach then get to coast back down instead of the more popular top down then shuttle bus back to top. Put box through some stress and held up well.
Box is light weight yet study. I will make a cushioned liner with 3/8" closed cell foam so that fruit among other things don't shake around so much. Also I'm thinking a bag with a pull cord closure might help with that too and less likely to spill contents again. Still should be able to slip a rain jacket or pants inside on top of everything. Some helmets might be too high to fit inside or too long. Mine would fit but I wouldn't do that. I wish it had a full flattened end on back narrow side so that I could set it up for both storage & when I need to carry it. As is the hinge prevents that from being steady on it's end. Husband has soft side competition of this trunk & likes it alot. We share in what we carry on rides together. All in all we thought it handled well & held up fine. The bigger boxes that this is cousin to are too large for bicycles in general. We have folding full size bikes so need the quick release trunks and handlebar bags so we can slip the bikes into their carry/storage bags for transporting.
I think it's a personal choice as to if you prefer the soft bags or this hard trunk or even the inbetween harder soft bags out there. Husband is thinking he'll cut the lock out and plug the hole. I'm thinking how to make a shoulder sling for it. And  make one for his soft bag that didn't come with one not even a handly handle like this XLC Cargo Box has. Oh yeah color beige can't be beat. And I could put one of those small cargo nets across the top and sides over it to hold any clothing overflow if it was needed...so carried the net inside too but never used on this trip.

UPdate a year later. Still like this trunk. Use it all the time and though it can rattle with contents inside a thin foam insert sheet slit on the corners to fit nicely into the bottom and sides of this box do a lot to help with the noise. Also usually just throw in a light rain jacket which helps most of all I think to prevent items from jangling around. Have had no problems and no breakage on this box in a years use. My only wish for it still is to be able to be set on it's side or backside so it's foot print when you remove it from bike and or carry it in travel off the bike is smaller. I'm amazed at how much really we can put inside this gem.
profile.summary: Worked well for me.

profile.description: The TheraBand Stretch Strap was designed to facilitate both static & "contract-relax" stretching, making it a versatile tool for patients & athletes. The Stretch Strap is as effective as contract-relax partner stretching at increasing flexibility without the need for a partner. A step-up from a traditional elastic resistance band allows for more targeted stretching. The elastic stretching device delivers a more effective 'dynamic' stretch vs. static stretching or static stretching devices. A dynamic stretch is an active stretch that moves the muscle in it's full range of motion and isn't associated with a loss in strength or performance like some studies may have shown with static stretching. TheraBand makes a variety of similar products designed to facilitate rehabilitation, recovery, and strengthening, including elastic resistance bands and tubing, large exercise balls, Flexbars, soft weights, and countless other useful home workout essentials.
profile.reviewText: In very small print on the last and third section of the fold out informatin and excercise sheet provided finally there it is...Contains Latex......darn it! That means I must get rid of it. Sellers and Amazon sellers need to realize they MUST TELL the consumer if it contains latex just like they warn consumers about peanut or peanut oil etc. It's a very dangerous allergy/sensitivity. 3M once sent me 20 in cash and 80 free products when I had a latex reaction to one of their products that they labeled as latex free. I wanted to know what was in it not get the freebies which was a real joke because they also sent a box of the very item that I had a latex reaction too....and said sometimes someone like me does react to it or a batch of their adhesive. SOOOOO Thera who does sell both latex straps and latex free straps and usually tells the buyer that...this SELLER DID NOT. This Description fails to warn you. Also the way it's wrapped you have to unpack the strap and pull out the direction sheet and on the third and last folded up and at the very bottom of the left panel there it is..CAUTION Contains Latex. So Seller and Thera? You can and should do better. This is not one of those fad diseases of the month things it is quite serious. And sellers who don't disclose often have to eat the shipping both ways and pass the cost onto the future consumers increase of items. So it's a non win situation for the company and the buyers. Unfortunate for me my neighbor who often has recieved many a product from me that contains latex will get this newest one because in the same order I had 4 other items of same thing and their boxes clearly said contains latex so quickly arranged to return and that box was already packed and tag from Amazon labeled so it would be very awkward to arrange yet another return for yet another product from same order with yet the situation. Amazon insist your sellers describe or disclose if it contains latex...or peanut. What I can tell you about the strap is it's not like a rubber one those stretchy band like ones at all. It reminds me of a nylon dog leash but more cotton feeling. I really think it would be comfortable to use in comparison. I would have loved to use it in fact. So for those without allergies to latex it looks like a good sturdy strap with potential for long lasting use. The folded up pamphlet is sort of cheesy with person sitting on ball doing different stretches. I hate the balls myself and would use a chair if sitting is needed but didn't intend to follow it's instructions perse anyway....I've got my own routine for using strech bands to help promote strength training. I looked forward to using something a bit different and now can't. My neighbor so far has been given compression socks, bandaids, ice-bags, that I can think of of the top of my mind..oh yeah rugs with the rubber like latex non slip backings. If they start to break up after they start to break down they become powdery and I've had quite the problem with those. So now buy non-backed carpets. Quit using latex.
profile.summary: Warning IT DOES CONTAIN LATEX !!!!

profile.description: The mark of the perfect pen. The performance of a Sharpie permanent marker meets pen-like precision: that's the signature of the one-and-only Sharpie pen. profile.reviewText:
I bought for art work and nice writing with sharp black ink. We do love the Sharpie brand and original pens and markers. Love their hard tipped fine ones that we use to mark garden stakes and photo's and just everything. Discovered they make it in a more permanant industrial quality for a few pennies more...we like them even better. But these pens just don't cut it for our needs today...and dang it for tomorrow too. profile.description: Coolaroo exterior Roller shades combine unique knitted fabric & classic design. Unique, knitted HDPE fabric in traditional shade styling blocksup to 80% of damaging UV rays. Breathable fabric allows air flow, substantially reducing temperatures & savingup to 40% on energy costs. Light filtering knit reduces glare without darkening a room's interior. profile.reviewText: I bought 4 of these many years ago. They work well. BUT my husband did not like not being able to see through them when they were down. So evntually I purchased some 10 yards of the mesh screening that could be cut to fit these rollers. I then proceeded to remove the coolaroo fabric and replace with the new screen. Not only does it block as much heat and sun but they can be seen through really well. If you get the darker colors of the shade screen. Ok so why give this 4 stars. Because nothing is wrong with it. Except a husband who wasn't happy with the vision imparement. I am very happy with how well the switcheroo of fabrics took place. Also I did sew on some pieces on both ends of the bottom of the shade to stablize the panels when down to prevent wind gusts from messing  with them. Their tie down was not as good as I would have liked. I would buy these again and yes I might even buy to remove and exchange with the vinyl mesh which comes in a variety of colors and weights and wind and UV varitions too. We have one large 6 foot wide window and three in a row 4 foot wide so a 12 foot wide overall picture window and all have the same length alll over five feet. Luv them and the bonus when hung outside the windows is during bird migration spring and fall both it prevents birds flying smack into the windows. Which by the way was my number one reason for buying them in the first place. Second to sun/shade on south side of house. I've made the rest of my vinyl mesh into single rectangles with grommets set on each corner to hang on windows on the rest of the house where birds often smack into them too. This also allows us to see out when they are on but we put up and take down between the migration periods. I plan to use the coolaroo fabric now to make a hang down curtain on a long narrow covered patio to help keep it cooler during the hottest days. I already put up 2 by 8 foot panels of insulating bubble where one side up is aluminum and the other side down is white. Looks great but does not work as well as I had hoped. So now to figure out how to hang curtains or curtain rods on a slopiing celing. I have some ideas though. And these panels will be ideal. And I can move them to the interior by a few feet so my hangng plants are still out in full sun and not touching the curtains. Love thinking outside the box and DIY projects. OH YEAH it's summer and lots to get done before the snow flies again.
profile.summary: I did buy years ago and not from Amazon. They work great but I did remove the coolaroo fabric and replaced with vinyl shade mesh

profile.reviewText: It took the seller a while before shipping these off to me. Just when I was about to contact them they came that very day. I've used them for a couple of days now. I think for my purpose they will do fine. I am allergic to latex and some latex is worse than others. I never know when something will trigger a problem or give me a slide. But this is the soft type product that seems to be dangerous for me at times. They warn you if you are allergic to latex and I've been diagnosed since 1953 when the doctors could not use any tape products to hold bandages on my head wound following being hit by a car at 3 years old. (It's been an interesting life since....soles of keds shoes burning the skin off my feet, latex backed throw rugs drying out and turning to powders that make me ill and when in contact with my skin triggers sores, and of course no latex gloves and I worked in a lab...nitral to the rescue. And more.) So these seem sturdy and as far as I can tell pretty much the same as the latex models. Perhaps a wee bit less stretchy as the firmness goes up or as it's called here heavy rating increases. I want to use for resistance excercises and occasionally need to go through some wrist and elbow excercises for past injuries the physical therapist taught me years ago. These look to be every bit as good perhaps even better....non of that powdery substance I have to watch out for on latex bands.
profile.summary: Finally arrived and they look good!

profile.reviewText: I enjoyed the pan. Cake batter does not make it up to the rim so you can not see the detail of the train going around...cakes fault not the pan of course. Then again if details were recessed deeper leaving room for the cake to rise above.....but my only complaint is neighbors don't realize it's trees not a castle. profile.reviewText:
I'm use to one inch width so bought this 1.5 inch size and it's nice. I like being able to use this as straps not only to contain loose wires and cords but in the sewing department and bike department. I will add this to the bottom of a bag I'm making for a trip to hold a thin travel blanket. The straps will stick to themselves to stay out of the way and yet be there when I need them to hold the blanket. That would work even better on the side of a bag so might switch that around. I'm working on a way to hold a travel pillow tightly compressed with this item too. I've got several possiblities. One is an expanding pillowcase that's part of the pillow. The Velcro banding would actually remain covered when the pillow is expanded. I know what I'm doing...but see I'm having trouble describing it here. This one wrap velcro can be flipped over and still catches on itself. You can sew it into things and that's the beauty of it too. No adhesive here that limits it's use. Or leaves residue on sewing needles and hard items when you need to remove it.

Update. I'm ready to give this 5 stars now. Have found many uses. Also the same goes for the smaller width one wrap...now the 3/4 inch comes in colors. You can find it in half inch size too but so far only in 75 foot or 25 yard rolls..in colors that is. I like the 3/4 inch, one inch which I've not found here on Amazon today and this 1.5 inch. Several items I use it for are to hold a yoga mat rolled up. To secure our sleeping mats and with a larger piece you can let them breath and roll less tight for storage yet compress down small to carry on back. Hold a jacket rolled and to your bike rack. To compress a bike box I made to prevent the soft sides from getting into the wheel or rubbing on them. And to prevent gear from moving around. I can use it for straps without having to sew hardware onto them and they are adjustable which I find a wonderful thing and helps keep things flexible. They hold a water bottle to the bottom of my totes that carry a travel blanket and travel pillow. This allows for different sized pillows as well due to the flexible size of the strap. I sewed a full length sized 1.5 inch strip of normal plush velcro to the inside bottom of the totes I designed. And they have sides that prevent things from slipping out but this tape allows me to insert water bottles empty for flying to be filled once through inspection and also filled for train and car travel. The flexible straps can compress travel pillows down to the smallest size and so you can use larger pillows or the smaller ones. All said and done. It beats elastics and so far seems to be durable and long lasting. I've used up most of the first roll so here to buy another today and add a few of the new colored 3/4 inch ones too my stash too.
profile.summary: Good stuff lots of uses. Can sew it too.

profile.reviewText: Binders as expected and we make our own family cook books for over 40 years. Husband decided to print on computer. Over my dead body but so far he's gotten away with that. Meantime same size 3 ring binders half page he has used and before my choice orignally too. The difference is for some reason he's into two books now and more divider categories and the binder pockets help keep track of recipe notes and new ones I'm in the development stage with. We just use several in each of the books for that. I am famous for making a great dish or recipe both baking or cooking styles and if I do not repeat often enough it's loss for ever. :))) Only time I've ever regretted it the most is I can not for the life of me recall how I made a nut (pecan or walnut) based pie crust shell for creme pies. I've tried to repeat it numersous times with no luck not even close. When I first developed it I made about a pie a week for one summer. Was putting in a dash of cinnamon. I'm allergic to it and husband did not want the pies without so about 5-7 years later he wants the pies again sans the spice...but the recipe was in my head and now refuses to surface. :))) Anyway he's after me to write down what I do all the time. He hounds me and no kidding !!!! These little pockets help me keep a new idea or trial one from vaporizing in my head. I kid you not. (PS I do the same with sewing patterns. profile.description: Our Four Paws Magic Coat Instant Dog Mat Remover works to remove mats and tangles from your dog's coat quickly and easily. This dematting brush features a double row of sturdy stainless-steel pins that helps eliminate stubborn, unmanageable mats efficiently. At the same time, this mat remover brush doesn't damage the coat and maintains its length. This essential at-home dog grooming tool helps achieve a healthy, smooth coat.
profile.reviewText:
Disclaimer. NOT FOR ALL CATS. NOT FOR SHORT HAIRED CATS. BUT if your Kit has Mat's this might be just the tool if you use it with a light touch and often to prevent build up of mats.

All claws & meow complaints when we get after the BIG boys. One super huge long haired Siamese mix with blue eyes & an attitude to match but turns ice blue not cool kitty when he has major knots & us humans are after them. But out of so many different products this rake works the best on 2 of our long haired Boys. One is a Maine Coon classic gray fella & neither he nor the Siamese like brushing. Almost all our cats have learned to enjoy it but not these two heavy weights. Our other long haired fluffy boy asks that we bring it on. Only trouble is he doesn't mat and he doesn't have much to shed but he still rolls all over even tummy up for a faux brushing with this or other brushes. We never seem to have this rake as we refer to it handy in all the places that present themselves for us to snatch a mat or two on the go. They let us rake them outside in summer time a little bit if you don't get too aggressive & stay away from those pantaloons. Oh my those pantaloons are not to be touched or messed with....the Siamese has the widest nose and big bone structure of any kitty we've known.(A rescued kitty chosen to match the size of our difficult Maine Coon & ended up weighing 2 pounds more.) Siameses his claws are the sharpest, his paws wide at the end of super strong arms. You don't want to get on the bad side of him. But both the big guys are warming ever so little to this rake and even begging just a wee bit now and again for some raking down their middle backs where they arch their backs and stick up their butts in the air as if to say more please. But will take off if you attempt those lower sides and forget the belly region. Once in a while mats get out of hand and one pet parent holds the kitty while the other attempts to get a knot or 2 without losing their arm in the process. Nice thing about our kits are they all seem to forgive us...forget not on your life. But they have forgiving natures. So we don't declaw. Life would be a little easier but we don't believe in maiming a pet for our own selfish satisfaction. Husband said get more rakes so we can keep one outside and at the back door handy when we need it and not have to go searching. We have the similar item in the wood handle but the metal teeth are not as sharp yet perhaps then more comfortable to the kit's skin it doesn't seem to get at the mat's like this one. I check how sharp it is by running it across my bare arm to get a feel of how light a touch I should use with it. Also the kits in their way give good feedback on this. If you have a short haired kitty this one is not for you. Find a good comb or the slickers seem to have been favored by all our short haired cats over the years. They like the dog slickers more than the cat slickers even the petite tiny kitties. Ah heck they used to line up for their turn at being slicked and if you stopped to give one a quite little brushing....it must give radar signals because you would hear all the kits from around the house jumping off the couch, bed, computer desk around the house and come running for theirs too. Every time. So our big longer haired fellas are a surpise or perhaps they have more nerve endings on their fluffy britches. They are so too worth it! Even the now and again snag by a claw...it wasn't personal.
profile.summary: Have 1 buying 3 more. Have fussy Long Hair Beasts!!!

profile.reviewText:
I like this. It would be better if you could have a low and high setting but it has it's virtues. I bought primarily to use camping in a tent with power banks and maybe sometimes a solar generator inverter with a usb port here at home under a covered patio that doesn't have AC outlets but we
sit out under a lot in the summer. I thought it was lacking air movement until I realized the USB port I was trying it out on was faulty...and would make contact some of the time but with variable results. Once I thought to try a different charger device oh my we had much better air movement.

profile.description: NOW Pets L-Lysine Powder helps support a healthy immune system, normal respiratory health, and also helps to maintain ocular health. NOW Pets L-Lysine Powder is recommended by renowned veterinarian Dr. Barbara Royal, DVM, CVA, founder of the Royal Treatment Veterinary Center. For use in Cats only. Perfect for multi-cat households and boarding.
profile.reviewText: Bought this when in a panic to find something for our sick kitty. Vet has no idea what's wrong nor do we really. But this order was delayed due to bad weather across the USA this winter. Meantime I started using people pure L-lysine no additives in 500mg capsules. Just opened up one and poured half into small amount of canned kitty food twice a day. Until this arrived. surprised it is a lot coarser than the human capsule contents. If kitty eats it no problem but not sure he will accept it. Overall I think it would be a better product if it was a finer powder. Kitty has been on the Lysine for just about a week today. He's not gotten worse but he's not getting better. May not be fault of product because no one knows or understands what is causing him to be ill. He is eating and drinking but he's weak and has congestion in throat and eyes both. We are carrying him to his food twice a day and he's now got other water dishes around the house to help make sure he's getting enough liquids. Scary to say the least for a pet parent who like people parents the kids or the cats can't tell you what is wrong. He's had a full blood work up and he's had a full x-ray. Nothings been found nor sets off any alarms other than he is sick.
profile.summary: For a pet product it would be nicer to be more of a powder form than a larger crystal formulation.

profile.description: Quickly provide comfort and shelter to any outdoor party with the Coleman Swingwall Instant Canopy. In three minutes and three easy steps, this 10-foot by 10-foot canopy tent sets up to create 100 square feet of shade. The versatile Swingwall can be set up as a wall for added protection from sun, rain, or wind, or it can be put up like an awning for an additional 60 square feet of shade. Ergonomically designed comfort grips allow you to set up and lock the lightweight telescoping poles supporting this outdoor canopy without having to reach over your head. Welded steel feet on the poles provide stability on hard surfaces. Made of heavy-duty UV Guard material, this instant canopy also delivers 50+ UPF. The canopy quickly folds down into a compact size for easy transport and storage.
profile.reviewText:
See further down about how Coleman dealt with a missing part for this tent. Since we have fixed this problem ourselves but with NO HELP from COLEMAN or it's Customer Service center it is no longer an issue nor was it ever a detraction for this Swingwall Canopy which we love still. The orginal we love...the second NOT.
This is the updated review to say we would give the first Swingwall canopy ten stars it is that good. We love it. That's the problem when I ordered it for my camping uses primarily I also knew to order one for my husband but he insisted he did not want the swingwall version but the LED lighted canopy instead. So I obliged. The thing is the moment he saw the swing wall he decided it was HIS and he's never once used the lighted version. I even purchased him two sun wall protector add ons and an insect screen set up for it. NO he likes the SWING WALL period. Ok so now and again our dates of use crosses paths. And I usually cave and let him have it. Since I love my ten by ten foot straight wall tent that is made to fit under these canopies and frames I have little to no use for the LED lit version where the tent would cover it completely. I love the swingwall because not only does it provide a lovely little covered porch in front of the tent door but it's without any other poles or guy lines to trip over too. And when you leave your campsite for a day of hiking/biking etc. you can slip the door down over the tent door adding an extra level of security. It also provides a lot of extra shade and probably why this tent set up stays so much cooler when it's hot and sunny compared to classic nylon tents today even with rain fly's and added dome canopy covering them for more shade to help with the heat load. So yeah we love it and both want it.
In 2015 suddently the price dropped on the Swingwall enough if I added in my Amazon CC beanie points I would only pay less than 90 for a second one. I jumped at the oportunity to get the second one. And only two years after our first so I wasn't expecting any kind of quality issues between the new and older one. It arrived. We inspected it and I took it up to set up along the river picnic arrea a few days later. But dang within minutes one umbrella corner collapsed. I didn't bring a step stool so went home to get one. Husband came back with me. We all stood over by a picnic table and watched now two umbrella corners collapse and right after that the front legs buckled on the wall side and landed over breaking at least one of the umbrella arms beyond repair. And bending a third foot pulling it out of the ground as a slight breeze caught the canopy up and it took me a full hour to untangle the whole works guy lines and all. The canopy itself had a small but significant tear too. None of us could believe it? Clearly the metal and welds to feet were no longer the same quality as the original Swingwall we never had a problem with. So dang it !!!!! Lucky I'd insisted we save the two outside boxes for return shipping and was within the return 30 day grace period. With no problems from Amazon or Seller we returned it the next day and repacked it that same day. I was traumatized enough I refused to set up our original one all of that summer. But husband has continued to use it and it's never had a problem with the umbrella arms or the feet bending and collapsiing the legs.
Within a few weeks of having bought the second one Amazon had a number or reviewers claim almost identical damage and circumstances. So I figured at first Coleman must have a bad batch of materials and welding. BUT it's now two years later and those negative reviews continue to add up. Mind you when we bought the first one this model had been out a few years and there weren't any of these negative reviews. NOW I ADVISE you to look at the photo's of those posted and the negative reviews. You can select just the negatives by clicking on the bar showing the 1 and 2 star reviews. So I would gladly trade our brandnew never used LED lighted canopy that cost more than the swing wall did both times...for at least a 3 to 4 year old swing wall even well used if it was cared for and doesn't have problems. But clearly COLEMAN needs to evaluate their production plants of this item..and probably if one frame is not being well made other models will have similar problems too. Even though a tent under the LED canopy blocks that feature it might pay for me to figure out a way to attach my own DIY version of the canopy swing wall. Probably have to use adjustable tent poles to hold up the corners when set up but it could be done just not as nice as the original. I carry PARIA tent poles as spares and now use those as lantern poles too both inside tents and at the camsite outside but this way I also have them for spares if any tent poles fail or you want to set up a canopy cover over a hanging hammock. It just provides a lot more options and covers a lot of what if's both. So I give it three stars with reservations..the three is because we still love the original but would not recommend buying one made after 2015 unless you see a few years without these horror stories happening when the canopy is brand new like ours was. I think a clear sign is when the umbrella arm fails or two. It might tell you this is a newer model that's not made well and the feet can collapse without even any wind or gusts of wind. A light breeze should not cause problems at all. Bottom line...less than one star for the newer ones because they basicaly are useless if they become trash.

Below took place with the first canopy when the cross pole on the canopy swing wall was lost:
Coleman states THEY DO NOT SERVICE or offer REPLACEMENT PARTS for any of their canopies. I understand that. I do. So I ordered a tent pole kit after the life chat line clerk told me that the poles were 5 all 30 inches long. Came the kit and all poles were a variety of sizes from 29 inches on down. And only two ferrules that connect 2-3 poles at most together. Not going to reach the 116 inches straight length I need to fix/this problem as in DIY. So I called Coleman via phone this time..and the man kept saying I MADE A MISTAKE AND BOUGHT THE WRONG ITEM. Should have bought a POLE REPLACEMENT KIT not the Pole Repair kit and the replacement kits come with the 30" poles all 5. OK....But NOT MY MISTAKE Coleman's CHAT Fault. So he told me they were sending me out free of charge the POLE REPLACEMENT KIT because of this mishap etc. Very nice of them I thought. And yes I did get it two days ago. I ordered and needed the 12.7 diameter pole they shipped me a 6.7 I think it was..the smallest diameter pole they have. We decided to give it a run and cut the one pole down we needed to fit the 116 length we needed and threaded the shock cord and voila...inserted into the canopy sleeve and it sank...no strength and bowed because it needs to be the bigger diameter. So SAD and so frustrating. I decided IF I'm going to get this right and have to order yet another replacement set...that is going to work closer to perfect...then the least Coleman can do is give me the diameter of the pole that was lost. SO I wrote the following which answer came today and I am copy pasting it so there is no missunderstanding as to what I requested and how they answered:
COLEMAN:
Thank you for allowing us to be of service to you.
Subject
What is the diameter of the canopy pole on the swing wall canopy? I need to replace a lost one by making one since Coleman does not support them or sell spare parts.

 Discussion Thread
 Response Via Email (Michael) 05/19/2015 03:15 PM
Hello Leslie,
I sincerely apologize for any inconvenience with our product and would be more than happy to assist you.
Unfortunately we do have this item as a replacement part. I could not even find the pole dimensions to get you a diameter.
I apologize again for the inconvenience this may have caused. Thank you for contacting Coleman, the outdoor company. Have a nice day.
Thank You,
Michael
Well Michael......YOU COULDN'T send someone some where in the world even Wal-mart or Costco or somewhere you retail these out to measure with a caliper the diameter of the pole? REALLY? SHAME ON COLEMAN. We loved the swing wall canopy. We bought different Coleman Canopies at the time. One the LED lit one and this one. Turned out everyone wants this one. And the Ham people good folks they all are...too many helping hands one day and somehow the pole bag that holds them was missed being put into the case upon return. When we discovered the missing pole we attempted to call the Chamber of Commerce and the Rail-museum where they had used this canopy for local events and they did not have one turned in as a lost item. SO....here we are almost a full year round and Coleman doesn't have the respect for it's customers to at least measure the pole. I wonder if they know how frustrating and annoying this has been. I honestly try to be honest. But due to their lack of CARE or Customer Support...I would if I could..we live (100 miles away from any possible store that might actually carry this canopy item.) But yeah...some people are going to get frustrated enough after attempting to do the honorable thing here and pick up a canopy at a store....the Swing Wall one and remove the pole bag with pole and return the whole works sans the poles to said store for full refund saying...the poles are missing !!!!!! Now as much as I may think and agree that is a bit dishonest...hey!  COLEMAN GET YOUR ACT TOGETHER and stop playing your customers. The old saying what goes around comes around...as far as I am concerned Coleman would be getting what they deserve. And folks the canopy WAS great. But really why can't they just know the size of the pole so we can order that kit and on their web page when you click on the pole kits state clearly what is contained in them. Turns out the web page via several links to "IS THIS THE RIGHT POLE FOR YOUR TENT" nonsense you do find kinda a photo and statement which in two places is wrong...what is in either of these sets. SO by the time I am done getting the right pole replacement kit here...I'll have spent about 50 dollars not counting the freebie 10 dollar wrong size set they shipped out and that is almost 1/3 the replacement cost of a whole new canopy. Shame on Coleman.  This is a great example of what happens when a company that used to be Great several decades ago gets bought up and merges too many times and turns it's back on the customers which make it what it was.
UPDATE on this. We made a pole that worked...then someone actually returned the lost bag of poles !!!! The orginal was definitely better than our DIY that did work. Now we have like three sets of poles that aren't all that useful. I perfer the aluminum Paria adjustable tent poles to carry for any possible pole failure. I probably need to sell these other poles but one of my newer Alps tents came with fiberglass style heavy poles not the aluminum ones I like with my Kelty. So one of the kits might work to repair the Alps poles if one ever failed. Meantime I am looking to replace them with aluminum poles to lighten the weight of the tent itself. When I went through the Coleman pole situation it was difficult to find any reasonable priced pole replacements or DIY poles. Since then you can find lots of options and sizes. And in many cases the prices are more reasonable too. And you can choose a vareity of materials from steel, aluminum, or fiber. I love aluminum for it's weight and non rusting and less likely to break too. My husband might disagree but he's not the one who camps I do he was one of those who played me...I recall gals who played the guys back in college years that they joined the climbing/caving groups to please a boy friend etc..but hated it themselves...I was the gal who loved it and looks like the boy friend played me:))) LOL...it's been 45 years so can the violins you are about to pull out:)))) I go camping when I want to...he tends the house and pets and sometimes I stay home so he can travel to visit friends and relatives. A win win pretty much...so funny his Mom used to say the oddest thing to me that it's your thing camping/hiking/skiing etc. not his. And I was like no way...young and naive comes to mind. My dear precious Mom in law was right.

FOLKS get this canopy if  you can find a used one in good condition. Keep in mind COLEMAN offers no repairs or parts. But the canopy could be repaired or remade sewn etc. if need be. As long as the frame is good. We will continue to use it. I will look this year into making a wall that can be attached to one side of the LED canopy and start putting it to use even though I have no desire to use the LED's. Coleman's rechargable battery pack that is suppose to fit this canopy or you can use lots of batteries...my husband insists he can
configure one of the small deep cell 12Volt battery packs he's made for me to run the lights on the LEDs too. Colemans battery recharge battery pack is notorious for failure. So I also have a 800W deep cell solar/generator inverter system that might be able to be wired with a plug to it too. (The two small 12 volt battery boxes he made for me will run my portable DVD player for two full nights of TV or approx 5-6 hours each. It holds a charge itself for about 2 hours. So I can watch a week of Great Course lessons after dark when I'm camping by myself. The 800W solar chargeable system would no doubt work too as it has AC/USB/12V outlets. Happy camping and summer everyone !!!!
profile.summary: UPDATE # 3 : Our original 2013 Swingwall is great. Had to return the 2015 Swingwall when it collapsed & broke on first use.

profile.description: The Cuisinart Chef's Style Stainless Tabletop Grill is a powerful combination of raw grilling performance and great design. This grill goes from box to burgers in less than 10 minutes with no tools required. Once set up, two stainless steel burners combine for a total of 20,000 BTUs of meat-searing heat sparked by a simple TwistStart ignition system. profile.reviewText:
I read the one review here on Amazon. Searched for others over the net but nope none could be found. So I debated and then up it came at 50 off from another on line site. So we ordered it. It arrived with the grill lodged tight down into the box and burners. Broke a cross bar on the far right of the grill right off. So much for spot welds. And there are three dents into the right side where the grill had attempted to poke through. So I bought from a site that doesn't take returns and it's hard to figure out even how to contact them. I'm most unhappy. We inspected the thing inside and out. Decided there wasn't any obvious damage to the gas intakes and burners etc. So we put an LP tank on and cooked a New York Steak. SO SO. For some reason it didn't heat as hot as one would expect. Yes we heated the unit up before following instructions. Now that we used it once..I'm tempted to close it up and put it away and forget I made this buy. BUMMER.
For those who think they would like this grill look close at the dimensions. You'll need a pretty good sized cart or table to put it on. We have an aluminum outdoor cart it happens to fit to a T. Just luck but I really want my cart back for all the things we use it for summer time. And that means this chunky fat boy is going to be a pain in the...to put away after it cools every time. The grill despite it's lost cross bar is too heavy too big to handle with any amount of ease. A grill that came in two equal sizes would be far more intelligent for people friendly handling. And I also think a lighter weight one. I tried to talk the husband into using our old grill that is half the size and did fit on one side but he was afraid it would move enough to slip down. I'm certain I could avoid that but he was taking over the BBQ at the time...being MANLY so to speak. His conclusion is he was not impressed and thinks we should get rid of it ASAP. I so agree. One of the Coleman Portable grills and Cuisnart makes a few of similar ones that come with cases and wheels on stands ready to roll is a better deal. Really to cook a couple hamburgers or chicken parts or dogs...this is way over kill. Maybe it would impress a few people but it's terrible. I contacted Cuisnart by the way with a question before we bought it and they sent me an email telling me nothing as they don't handle these someone else does but they didn't bother to link me to or give me the url or web page etc. So much for customer support. That should have been a big enough hint don't buy this. Sometimes we all have to learn the lesson we need to pay attention to our gut instinct...I wasn't listening. It's too late for us maybe it's not too late for you. (PS no wind up here and temps in low 70's so that's not why the meat wouldn't heat up enough to cook right.)
profile.summary: WOW not what I expected at all.

But I couldn't locate a source for the black 1 inch which I have a little left of. I also go through the 1.5 inch black pretty fast. But I needed a narrower tape for a customized and flexible cart box I made for our bike trailer..and this was all I could find...in colors was cute. So went aheand and splurged on all of them. It's got lots of uses as means to hold together or rolled up yoga mats and my two nail-bed mats and this also allows me to hold the two nail mats to my leg to help with edema I have. A video showed using one mat to do that but didn't show how one was to keep it rolled around the leg. One Wrap to the rescue. Good stuff....it's unclear if this is true Velcro but it works pretty much the same.

Wrap yoga mats, sleeping mats, sleeping bags, quilts, throw blankets traveling. Holds cart box to bike cart and did I mention it's all adjustable everytime a perfect fit. Not just for wires around the house. And an extra plus our cats don't seek it out like they do rubber bands. I've sewn with it too. And it's just good stuff. And comes now in these colors...oh how fun.
profile.summary: Wish it came in one inch width otherwise it's great still.

profile.description: Oxine Animal Health (AH) has been tested and proven effective against a variety of bacteria, fungi and viruses, including E. coli, Salmonella, Staphylococcus, Parvovirus and more. Utilizes chlorine dioxide chemistry to eliminate odors and kill the bacteria that causes them. May be used everywhere in animal care facilities and confinements, plus it can be used for fogging or spraying. Effective as a feed-water and premise disinfectant. With an ultra-high activity level, it should be used in low concentrations, making it economical to use. It is completely soluble in water and has long-lasting bacteriostatic activity. Oxine has been shown to be more effective than other common sanitizers, including quaternary ammonia, lodophors, Peracetic acid, and sodium hypochlorite (chlorine). EPA registered and organically approved through Organic Materials Review Institute. Made in USA.
profile.reviewText:
Easier to follow directions and examples might be helpful or even a link to an on line site would help on how to attempt to use this product. There are a lot of uses that are not shown on the product bottle. I'm attempting to get rid of 50 years of oil and coal furnace and perhaps some cigarette smoking by past owners of our house. The walls are all wood from 8 to 16 to 25 feet high floor to ceiling walls throughout home. I'm allergic to flax oil cleaners like Murphy Oil soap which cleans them great but makes me ill for days even when we hire someone else to do the cleaning the fumes bother me. We also intend to use this in a fogger to clean the inside of the old furnace duct work. We had professionally cleaned but all they did was vacuum it out and then not a great job of that either. So could use more insight and specific directions on how to apply the activator (Vitamin C.) And what all precautions one needs to use to avoid poison gas and fumes it gives off. When is it safe to come back into house and do you need to re-apply to make sure all areas of the duct work are treated when it's a large system like ours. (Great original duct work but many
different cut off's to it and travels through four stories of house. Replaced the oil furnace converted from an old Majestic Coal furnace when we moved in too...with a high energy efficient LP furnace. Just wish these sellers would post a blog on how to use this and where others who use it outside of the norm could post what they did and who successful it turned out. How to handle it in active formulation is our biggest concern. Otherwise I intend to use it on the walls mixed with castle soap and olive oil for the walls. And may or may not add citrus turpentine's to it.....will have to check out if they change the Oxine AH into active formulation being they are citrus products.
profile.summary: Needs to have more directions with it.

profile.description: Bring along a perfect relaxation spot on your next camping trip with the Coleman Pack-Away Camping Cot. Ideal for sitting, reclining, and sleeping, this versatile camping cot features an extra-wide design that provides ample resting room. It also comes equipped with a convenient removable side table with a cup holder, where you can easily keep drinks, magazines, and other personal items. The steel frame can support up to 300 pounds and is built to withstand season after season of rugged use. Thanks to its folding, portable design and included carry bag, this camping cot fits inside most car trunks and is easy to transport. The Coleman Pack-Away Camping Cot accommodates most people up to 6 feet 6 inches tall.
profile.reviewText:
Bought two. One is on it's way back as an exchange. One was perfect no wobble, The side/tray fit both sides as should. The thing though heavy is what I was looking for. I'm upgrading to a cot and will make a mattress foam pad to use with these too. Well insert a space blanket on one side of the foam...bottom side and make the upper side you sleep against out of 100% breathable cotton sheeting. And the rest sides and bottom out of nylon pack cloth and sew a few strips of soft rubber like shelf liner on the bottom too to prevent it from shifting. I may or may not add corner ties. But put a zipper in the side and you can pull out the foam and wash the covers when needed. Or remove the sheet of space blanket too. But as a kid I abandoned cots because I always freezed on them....they let the cold air just come right through your bottom side. And since have used all kinds of wonderful ground mattresses and been happy. UNTIL I reached 65 and decided I prefer to be higher off the ground. Anyway second pack-away cot the tray had one hook made too narrow and would not fit and would be difficult to widen to work without damage to the metal and paint. Not enough to return...but one end of the cot two legs were damaged. The vinyl inserts to protect the floor and tent floor from damage both feet were either worn through or someone had hammered them in too far until they split and were now in deeper than they should be cutting off one side and leaving the sharp metal edge showing. SO Amazon sent return tag and just this one cot went back same day it arrived for a full exchange. Lets hope second one is as good as the first one. I do not plan to use them in the house but with all hardwood floors the feet wouldn't be right. And not sure I could find replacements that would fit either. But they would definitely cut through a tent floor. but all the other four feet were right. Meantime these are nice long cots and wide enough should accomodate most tall folks six to six 2 at least. And the tray is a nice touch and may end up using. Didn't think so when ordered but now that they are here and I can see how they are in person and oh yeah very helpful. I'm s till making a hang off bag for hubby's eyeglasses though and one for me to stuff a few tissues in. I have allergies. Anyway a few pockets would be nice. And yes they do not have locking legs like ALMOST ALL COTS. But once they are fully extended properly and you sit on them you weight by physic's and the cots design holds them in place. I doubt anyone has collapsed using one of these if in the weight limit and also lighter due to non locking legs. HOWEVER they are not designed for small lighter kids or teens or even some adults to just bounce or jump and push them about. They are not for physical activities other than normal cot use and I did check them out for side sitting. I sat along all the length of each side and no tipping at all. Perfect...well almost I'm the short person and could be a wee bit lower but is ideal for 6 foot tall long legged hubby. These will fit our 10x10 foot straight wall tent to a tee. They also fit our currant 4 and 6 person tents with a slight slanted wall and another with a more dome style wall. And they leave lots of room to move around and I intend to make a few storage bags to fit under
the cots when camping for a week or two. Overall I can't wait for the hopeful GOOD replacement to get here. Camping season is almost here in the Northern Rockies...and cabin fever is raging:))) Happy camping everyone. PS thanks Amazon for exchange system too.
profile.summary: Gottal luv it for height, length, Able to sit like bench. No locking legs most cot designed w/o locks. It's called physics!!!!

profile.description: The Fold-To-Go is a compact, sturdy, light weight portable toilet designed for field use and emergency scenarios. It has an integrated handle, making it easy to carry. It also boasts an innovative leg locking system, making it one of the sturdiest portable toilets around. The system is lightweight, dependable and easy to use. When not in use, it folds away in a plastic carrying case for easy storage. The Fold-To-Go has an impressive weight capacity of 300lbs and is great for camping, hunting, field use, boating, and emergency preparedness. This unit is ideally suited to be used with the Double Doodie waste bag bagging system.n-up.
profile.reviewText:
What else can you say it's a portable loo. And it's lower to the ground than might be comfortable for some but fine for us. And it's plastic but holds a lot of weight so also not a concern for us but could be an issue for others or guests along for a trip outdoors. And you have to fiddle with the bags and all but all do able as long as you take care to begin with and pay attention to details of all. I do buy the pre-double bag made up systems. I have only used regular sized ones not the over sized ones that also fit in your at home toilet during water problem emergencies. An idea that caught my eye but we now have this loo so in a pinch in our home it would do for our family.
What I like best about this loo is it's fold up small size bundle. It's easy to bring along. Keep clean * even hide it in a bag or large pillow case or small sheet if you feel the need to do that to keep it out of sight during actual travel. You don't have to drag along a big ole bucket with a comfy seat attached. However the 5 and 6 gallon buckets are a lot more higher and maybe more comfortable for really tall people or compromised physical needs. This works and it's on it's way out the door as we speak. Summer you know...gotta go...we live where 80% of our area is wilderness...I know I know you guys own this place...you really should come visit it. Taxes and all....

PS for those who enjoy making their own....you can fashion your own double bagged bag systems using disposable diapers and 2 gallon ziplocks for out side bag and firm 20-22 quart garbage bags for the innner system that holds the torn apart diaper and maybe some extra baking soda for odor control. Also I'm sticking a charcoal filter to the top underside of the lid on my loo. Don't know if it's needed just thought it might help out as a bug detractant by reducing any day time odors.
profile.summary: It's a lux-loo for camping!

profile.description: The 2PL has a sturdy acrylic base, machine riveted to a heavy vinyl coated, steel wire back brace for continuous firm tension. Being 4 3/4" in height, 5 3/8" in length and 3 7/8" in width make the 2PL ideal for displaying serving trays, plates, tiles, artwork, framed photos and much more! The 2PL is adjustable, lightweight and compact for easy storage and mobility. This product aids in promoting point of purchase sales and increases visibility of any item.
profile.reviewText: So many love these. I first looked at a larger size version I believe the 3PL but after reading the reviews and asking a question or two that some buyers were so kind to answer I settled on this size for my purpose. I make flip books with or without laminated pages. These can be only a few pages all the way up to over 50. And most are about half a normal sheet of paper size but the covers often made of fabric run a wee bit larger and of course using lamination sheets it can add up to 1/4 to 1/2 inch more width and length too. So around 6x9 inches but again I create them for various reasons and sizes so I wanted to make sure the stand would work with a 5 inch size width. I am very pleased. They seem sturdy enough to hold the largest of my creations to date...even full sized sheets of paper. Often I relied on the books themselves to act as their own stand but that at times is an iffy project. SOmetimes it works well not always though. This solves that. And since all my projects are gifts not sold this is not so expensive I can include one even if the person is getting 2-4 different books one stand would work for one or all. Say an excercise book with various poses...or types of yoga etc. They would only use one book at a time and if for some reason if they did want or need another stand they could find one themselves or even ask me for one. Happy happy happy. Not super strong in terms of materials but just right..light weight and not obtrusive. Kinda neat. I may need to think about making a small case to hold the book/books in as gifts along with a pocket on the outside of case that holds one of these protected inside that too.  This list of the type of books I make is limited only by imagination...and putting it all in motion:)))
profile.summary: These really are kind of cool. I'm using for homemade flip books..photo display books, excercise positions such as yoga, recipes

profile.description: Westcott Titanium-Bonded Scissors are lighter, stronger and sharper. Lightweight yet durable enough for any cutting job. From the Manufacturer: Scissors feature high-performance, titanium-bonded blades that provide three times the strength of stainless steel and resist corrosion. Scissors are ideal for paper, cardboard, lightweight line, fabric and other materials. Straight handles have a contoured soft grip
profile.reviewText: Bought these about 3 years ago. No problem with them at all. I was going back to buy another set and there they are here on Amazon. I think I got mine before from another site. Anyway these are the same exact model the 8 inch straights. And I've had trouble keeping them at hand because I'll take one to the bathroom to open those pesky bubble packed items when new....like toothbrushes come sealed in these days. And I'll take a pair to the sewing room despite having a lot of different scissors from tiny snips to full size fabric shears I'll grab this one a lot for carrying about a project from the cutting table to the ironing board to the machine to clip errant threads etc. It's always on the move. And then there is my computer room where they are suppose to be...and where are they off to this time...So here I am back to get two more sets of two because with luck I'll keep at least one in the computer desk and book making area. They cut fabric well and I've had no complaints with nicks on the blades or quality of the pair I have owned. I assume these will be just as good and though I have four pairs of scissors for the kitchen tasks of opening packages and what have you and more bubble packs which are the red dot mundials which I originally got at under 3 a pair and they have somewhat tripled since. I may eventually add a few of these to the kitchen's collection to. I grew up in a household without enough scissors. My father and brother both took turns ruining my sewing scissors including breaking one tip off using it as a screw driver and then the other tip went by the other GUY which actually ended their use all together as scissors because it snapped about 1/4 of the way down the blade not just the tip this time. I then got in trouble with my mother for taking such poor care of my things. WELL.....I actually before the last event was hiding them in my room to prevent anymore injuries to these expensive gems.....and who ever tossed my room looking for it. So I made a promise to myself at the age of 12 that when I grew up I would never be short of scissors at hand or for the task. And as far as that goes keeping a drawer with two sizes of Phillips and straight ende screw drivers and some shorts of the same along with regular pliers is a must too. It all helps when it comes to scissor protection. Meantime it's not how much fabric you have that wins when you die it's how many pairs of scissors you own:))) Never have too many. I've never had any rust issues by the way...but we live in a dry dry dry climate with little humidity ever. Having lived in higher humidity zones such as IA I suspect it could be a problem there. But for us it's not one and that includes the pair that seems to enjoy sitting in the extra tooth brush holder hole in the bathroom these days. At least I know where that pair is.
profile.summary: Buying more of these little handy shears.

profile.description: An ultra-portable cooking companion for camping trips and picnics, the Coleman Fold N Go Propane Stove, 2-Burner, delivers powerful, consistent heat output for efficient outdoor cooking. This camping stove produces up to 20,000 total BTUs of heat across 2 independently adjustable burners, giving you enough cooking power to prepare hot meals in two 10-inch pans at once. PerfectFlow pressure-control technology delivers steady heat output while cooking, while PerfectHeat technology ensures efficient fuel usage that allows this propane gas stove to last more than an hour with both burners on high on one 16.4 oz. propane cylinder (sold separately). The Coleman Fold N Go Propane Stove folds up compactly for easy storage and transportation.
profile.reviewText: Haven't used it much yet. However it's much smaller than we expected when it's all folded up for storage. That was a pleasant surprise. Had looked on youtube to see reviews and it always looked much larger than it is. Anyway opened it seems big. In part I compare it to our very small one burner gas burner that we've used for some years now and rarely use the original gasoline Coleman two burner camp stove. We still have it and it still works great but these LP systems are kind of edging the old school out. This item would benefit with a wind-foil. I think Coleman could or should sell something for these stoves maybe one that fits several of their smaller LP stoves and all in ones they offer. Anyway something tall enough not a back packing wind foil aluminum folding one but say a foot high and folds up to no more than 10 to 12 inches wide and pretty flat but goes around the whole back and sides so you can place closer in or further out depending on conditions. They are missing the boat and could be the first to offer a portable wind foil for these items. Meantime we are trying to figure out how to make one ourselves and keep it lighter than the steel panels I have suggested to husband. Aluminum would be the lighter move but it's hard to come by in sheets and expensive too. I'm even thinking about making pockets that are joined together or fold up that have some stiffening in them made of pack cloth to make a stand up gate around the stove..but being fabric would have to be placed far enough away to prevent melting or catching on fire. They also make heat resistant and iron clothes in gold and silver both quilted or not in sewing departments and maybe that along with the heat insulating batting for oven and hot pads would be interesting to experiment with. But these need a wind foil a lot of the time and would be far more efficient if they had them.
profile.summary: Nice Small Storage than expected.

profile.description: Originally filmed and aired in 1974, Ridin' the Rails is a nostalgic look at the history of the American railroad through the song and story of the legendary Johnny Cash. Reenactments of historic railroading moments are movingly narrated by Cash and superbyly embellished by his inimitable music. Track Listings: Ridin' The Rails, Tom Thum, Collage of Yesterday, Night They Drove Old Dixie Down, Legend of John Henry's Hammer, Shave And A Hot Bath, Train Robbers, Satirical Aire, Casey Jones, Crystal Chandeliers and Burgundy, Doesn't Anybody Know My Name, City of New Orleans, The L&N Don't Stop Here, Anymore, These Hands
profile.reviewText:
Despite loving trains and JC both this didn't move me that much. I found the staged gold-silver spike scene stilted and would have enjoyed it more if they had JC singing and just showing the trains and telling the history instead of trying to re-create it in little episodes. Usually I love documenteries too. No I don't think it's because it was over 30 years old either. It was the staged or the way it was staged scenes yet not stills that didn't work for me. I also didn't like the John Henry set up either pretty much for similar reasons. Poor fella swinging that hammer hope they didn't take too many takes to get the shots they finally used. Whew!

But the redeeming quality of this was how much we miss JC and his wife June Carter Cash....may they be in the heaven as they believed together and happy....and perhaps riding the rails as it was once done.
profile.summary: I love Johnny Cash and I love trains but????

profile.reviewText: I think it's going to work out just fine for what I purchased it for. Take along camping to use inside tent when it's rainy out and or later at night and want to work a jigsaw puzzle in the tent. Camp chairs are too relaxed and difficult to bend over the table to work a puzzle. Have plastic folding chairs for outdoor use but this is smaller in size for packing and bringing along. profile.reviewText: It's OK....BUT directions on how to use it with various size edges and styles would be really helpful. Photos and or drawings showing just HOW IT DOES ADJUST as they claim on their sales sight and product would be very HELPFUL and customer friendly. This comes with a few less photos on the card stock than the sales page on Amazon provides. NO directions at all. I see where some folks are most frustrated and I now understand. I have a vareity of different style tables from standard picnic ones to the plastic folding tables. Those with solid edges work best that are over an inch thick. But for those that are hallow behind the edge and an inch or less there is no way I have found to stablize this bracket to feel firm and solid even may drop off. So since the SELLER states it is adjustable please make a video showing a variety of edge depths and styles both and just how one makes the so called adjustment for the slimmer ones. I will make good use of it just the same because it does fit some of my tables fine used outdoors and at Ham Radio events when they have an outdoor weekend global event. BUT more info CLEARLY provided is most helpful. Maybe reference a YouTube site or link to it once the Seller puts something Clear together. SELLER I hope you read this. I think you can find it cheaper than it seems to sell here on Amazon but I wanted the Amazon protection 30 day return just in case it didn't work at all. It does just not as well as one would like and is led to believe.
profile.summary: OK maybe a bit more. It lacks insight and directions on how to adjust it to fit a variety of width edges on different tables !!!

profile.reviewText:
This is our second order. Roofers used up our first rolls by accident and we decided to re-order for our other areas they weren't doing. We intend to use it on a small little play house we use as a storage area for hoses and plant supports over winter. It needs a new roof and the old one is covered with moss too. Only northi side of property had moss except for this small tiny little over fifty year play house that original builders had for their kids.
It'll be interesting how it works on that too. Meantime it's going on our north side of house on the new roof too. But got too cold before the rooffers finished the job. So we thought we'd better get some more even though it's expensive not so much if it works well. We are hoping it also helps prevent the moss that's developed on the patio's under the porches..it appears to be worse right at the edges of the roof overhangs. Suggesting it's caused by the run off from the roof. It'll take a year bfore we know for sure about that.
profile.summary: What we wanted and have bought several times now.

profile.reviewText: Ok I don't own it but searching for a TREE TENT it came up do to it's name. Wenzel this is not a TREE TENT...as in a tent that hangs from tree limbs or even hammock style tents that you hang between trees from the tree trunks. Change the name of this Wenzel...I'm sure you meant a nice backpack tent for one to two that is great to have on hiking trips among the trees. profile.reviewText: These aren't quite what I expected. But they are unique and interesting. I orginally intended to use on an automatic/machine writer to bring out & add depth to written words already through the writer. However they are too thin lined for that purpose. Perhaps as an outline around a bit thicker written font leaving area inside the outline as the original font color. But not as a cover over the entire print. I probably will be using these on their own via hand to eye to paper the old fashion process a& skip the machine all together. I played with the pens and they don't show much on light to white paper on their own. And they don't show at all on my metalic cover stock but they do show quite sparkly on black velvet cardstock I have. I like the effect on the black but they aren't made to be used on their own they are made to go over and bring out the pre-written or print already. A highlight of sorts if you will. Which is what I wanted but due to the thin point they just fall short of my desired effect. Can't take off for that or fault the pens. I had a wee bit of skipping early on with some trials and that's the reason I dropped off a star. I checked out if they would write straight up and down and they do seem to hold their own as well as a normal slant to my hand's way of holding most pens. I can see lots of interesting potential for the scrapbooker and the card makers as to add a sparkle here or there even as small as a dot effect or dash....say shine in a corner of an eye or glimmer around the ribbon. Look forward to playing but doubt it'll become one of my reach for items. Never know though...just need the right project for the creative juices to flow and start tapping into this product. This dual package will last me a while. I'm going to see if sakura has something like it in a wider point for my initial purpose. I do like that sparkle but think 'subtle look'.
profile.summary: Interesting pen & ink.

profile.description: How often have you forgotten to turn off your holiday lights and/or decorations? Do you dread stepping out into the cold, damp night to fiddle with the switch? With the Woods 32555WD Weatherproof Outdoor Outlet Remote Control Converter Kit, youll be able to switch your lights (or other outdoor electronics) off without having to leave the comfort of your home. You can simply attach the remote to your keychain so its always handy when you need it. The kit is a breeze to install and can make a fantastic gift.
profile.reviewText:
This is going to be my wee bit of security system for camping this summer. I found a work/spot like light not a big hefty number but one that has enough light to see about the campsite if some furry or human is rummaging about. The light turns on and off with a switch and even has a remote itself but this I can keep inside the tent with me. Folks the past two years at my favorite campgrounds have been driving in after dark arriving late looking for a campsite. Those folks do not bother me. I usually can peak out the tent window and take stock of what's what and determine sure enough and by then they are usually backing their vehicles out. But last year took the cake...already at least 3 times folks had driven down...and
each time I could see out and relax. But winds took out my first tent and I switched to one that had a rain fly that covered all the windows and one night soon after....someone drove in 5 times over a 24 minute time period starting at 3 in the morning. First two times they drove in and pointed their high beams on my tent? Did not back out too fast. ???? Third time in someone got out of the vehicle and walked up to my tent and was walking about it...with a high beam flashlight. ??????? This was followed by another drive in....and finally a second repeat of walking up to my tent with a high beam flashlight. I couldn't see anything and I didn't dare step out of the tent to be blinded by their light. I was totally vulnerable. Also not knowing who or what...I didn't want to give away that I was a female 65 year old camping alone. Wouldn't take someone long to evaluate the situation and know they were in control. So I suspect this was the sheriff. For two reasons...one it happened a year before where the sheriff arrived searching the whole campground on other side of river every morning for a week. They caught who they were looking for over a hundred miles no where near the campground...but they came in day light early morning but light out just the same. I also had a camp guest with me that year who was however 78 years old and tiny little thing. Anyway this past year the next morning after the disturbance here is a sheriff's car speeding past the campsite on the main road above one way then back the other and finally taking off in as much a hurry on another loop up to the lake. But of course I have no idea if it was the law because they didn't announce. However some folks who drive in park with their high beams smack on your tent so how rude. I figure it might help to have a light set up on the table..which is metal and I can tie the light down to it...so I can look out the tent window...if they are not backing out as fast as most do...and or set their high beams on my tent...I can turn the light on to let them know...and see there is not another campsite and to retreat. Also not sure what the sheriff would do if that ever happens again...if it was them...but it should deliver the same message...go away and come back at a more reasonable hour...really. (I told my husband when I got home..what would happen if I sprayed the sheriff with bear spray under those condtions and they didn't announce themselves? As much as I'd feel it was justified...no doubt they would claim...did too call out..she said he said...but I did have my little tape recorder on...which I keep to catch bird sounds at night. Owls being my favorite. It would have held up my end of the story I'd hope. But oh yeah...by the fifth visit I was on edge enough to have the can of pepper spray in one hand and the tape player on. Silly old lady some might say. Humor me I'd probably say. I did put an end to all driving in after dark by parking the car up to the top of the entrance drive every evening.  And never again for a tent without windows to see out. I also invited a couple who kept asking me how long I intended to stay to share the campsite. It's big with plenty of room for more...they had a small camper and can't say it was ideal. I felt invaded and taken advantaged almost right away. But no doubt a bit of a knee jerk move on my part.) This year..armed with this tiny little remote system I am going to be prepared for night intruders.....pepper spray is my last resort but don't mess with this lady!  I take my camping seriously. Outdoors is to relax and enjoy and not for encounters that go bump in the night so to speak. Boy Scouts say....be prepared. Wonder what girl scouts say...get a box of cookies:)))
profile.summary: Setting up a wee bit of security at campsite to see any animal rustling about and two footers intruding after dark too.

profile.description: The first heat resistant silicone food trussing tool designed to replace kitchen string and toothpicks in the prep and cooking process. Use thefoodloop to hold small stuffed, rolled, bunched and wrapped meats, fish and veggies. Pack comes with six, 15 loops. Use individually around a bunch of asparagus or join together to make a longer tool. Use thefoodloop in any pan on the stove, in the oven, microwave or in the freezer. profile.reviewText: These work but with some issues. They like to slip and sometimes without little provocation they will slip apart. In otherwords the design ends and nubs that are meant not to allow slipping doesn't always work. For a roast in oven they will hold pretty good but for chicken to keep wings from flapping as they turn on a spit they don't always hold well and can be hard to set. A hint is to actually tie the ends over and tuck them into the bands on either side so you night also need to put two together doing the same all the way around the larger band tucking in all the ends. They wash great. I just wash by hand and dry with paper towel or set to dry on one. Then tuck in it's little mesh bag and drop into drawer we store it in. You can also place in net bag that comes with it and wash through your dishwasher on top rack. We don't bother with that. We hand wash dishes more than dishwasher. So I give it 3 stars because the concept is great and we can use them but almost prefer to reach for the old fashion string because of the slipping issues and where they just don't always hold when you need more tension. Hope they make an improved model soon.
profile.summary: Works but slipping can cause problem.

profile.description: Eliminator goggles are our most popular motorcycle riding goggles. Soft airy foam, and side-venting prevent wind incursion and lens fog.
profile.reviewText:
Bought to use when I spray underside of patio ceilings once every spring with concentrated bleach and water to kill a specific black mold that develops over winter up here. profile.reviewText: I bought for a 12 inch fry pan which is about 2.5 to 3 inches deep. Use for camping only but no lid and some of my lids for other pans large enough would seal too tight and just awkward to carry too. So had hopes that this would work with  12 inch pan.
