profile.description: 2.1 OZ, Whiskas Cat Temptations Hairball Control. Good quality product. The product adds a great value. Manufactured in China.
profile.reviewText: I thought another lady seemed to turn on this product unfairly. Shame on me. My kitty which has for 7 years suffered from extreme hair ball issues...he's a huge long haired fluffy cat with hair we've never seen the likes of. But his upchucks have lead to dental and gum problems which is threatening his quality of life too. We try to get the malt sticky glues down him and nope he's super good at rubbing said mess off his paw and leaving veneers of it around the house. So yes Vet puts him on antibiotics a few times a year too and it helps but only a little. So this is the third brand of food type treats that treat hairballs we've tried.  Kitty ate the first two I gave him...three more.....and the full 10 in all. Within seconds of the last one swallowed...he was getting sick...all over the house...he sent every single one up. I think he forgave me later that night when he showed up for his brushing which he loves. But he choose my husband to cuddle with and purr fest with through the evening letting me know I got the cold shoulder treatment for feeding him treats that made him get sick..the very thing we want to prevent or cut down on.......OK to be fair to all of you who use it and kitty's who benefit from this product...yes it may be fine for you and your beloved felines. I suspect there's a small popluation that doesn't get along with it. My huge fluffy ball is one.  So here's a hint. If you suspect a cat may not tolerate it or worry about that start with just one or two nibbles at a time and no more for at least another day. So each day maybe increase by one or two pieces until you are satisfied kitty can tolerate them. It could be our kitty has such a bad hair ball the 10 at once caused him instant misery. Hard to say..no hair came up just a lot of phlem and sticky mess along with the bites...none of them had been chewed by the way kitty scarffed them whole...maybe it's not a cat maybe it's one of those little fluffy yip yaps and we mistook it for a dog all these years. ????? But he tolerates another similar product and we have another one to test too but will use more caution in the future for any type of this product when it's new. By the way this product has a lot of ingredients and a few are questionable as to their usefulness. This is more a fiber oritented product than a lubricating one that most of the malt goo's are. (Laxtives can be fiber or lubricants for humans too.)
profile.summary: Poor kitty upchucked all 10 pices of food one by one all over the house seconds after eating last one. Not for this feline.

profile.description: Keep your food cold while traveling with this deluxe and spacious EdgeStar FP630 Portable Refrigerator Freezer. profile.reviewText:
Bought ours from another dealer than Amazon because they offered a 4 year extended warranty. And this is the kind of item that likes to fail. Of course if it fails on our way to Alaska or Camping out on the San Juan Islands we'll not be happy campers but at least once home we'll get some money back. It's the type of warranty we'll get full refund on cost of item so would be out of the insurance which was around 80 dollars for 4 years or average of 20 per year. We don't expect it to fail however. We are taking good care of it. We used it this summer as both a freezer and a fridge on several occasions one amounted to about a week. Always plugged into house electricity not 12 volt or battery back up. We'll get a battery for using it next summer camping. And since it's 180 miles round trip to shop for major groceries it'll come in handy to take in the car.
It weighs a lot. I would not be able to lift it when it's full. And it's pretty big despite paying attention to the size given. I'm thinking of making a case like they sell for them to help keep it clean and maybe add some insulation. The cases have cut outs for the vents and plugs so well do the same. We chose this size over the smaller one because it wasn't that much bigger in foot print and same height and width. A few inches longer. But the next larger size is much bigger for some reason. We have a small SUV and it's back seat is split in two so we can remove or just pop out one seat and set this in it's place. With the top hinges to the inside and the opening facing the door we can access the freezer/fridge real well. We prefer it in this position for side door access than in the back where it seems to take up almost the whole back end. We didn't think it was too loud. It got close to the temp setting really quick we thought and held it well. It may fluctuate a little up and down from your set temp but it's the way it's maintaining it. Once it reaches temp however it does not run a lot. Didn't have cord problems others mentioned but didn't use it on the go traveling either. If the 12Volt plug becomes a problem we'll fix it by getting a plug from Radio Shack as others who are handy have mentioned doing. It's a keeper and have had it for approx 6 months. If there's a problem I'll come back to post an update.
profile.summary: We like it !!!

profile.description: These mini clips feature great holding capacity and have a multitude of uses. Each clip opens wide to hold layers of fabric and the clip base is flat for easy feeding to the presser foot. They make a great alternative to pins. Perfect for making quilts, handbags, and more. This package contains 50 wonder clips. Each clip measures 1 by 3/8-inch. Imported.
profile.reviewText: The clips are interesting and lots of OUT OF BOX USES come to mind too. I tested them out for a camping clothes line pin and voila they are perfect little gems for that use. Putting away the camping gear for this year as tomorrow is Sept 1 and the weather has flipped to wet and well wetter. COOL temps too. Anyway sewing well I found these after I managed to stick my fingers multiple times recently on a major sewing job. By the time I was finished with it I felt like I had been sacraficed to the Sewing GODs as a human pin cushion. These gods are not forgiving. I'm an experienced sewer from fancy gowns to outdoor heavy duty gear including sleeping bags and tents. And my favorite fabrics are coated nylons of every weight and upholstery tapestries. So pins have always been a must but never so many pricks. If I disappear my husband might get charged with cutting me up and carrying me out with the mattress covers I just made there is so much DNA left behind. Ok too many The Closer re-runs. I'd give these 5 stars but the price kept jumping. I finally was forced to skip off to another site other than Amazon to purchase without seeing the price jump after putting in my to buy box. Really jumped as much as 8 dollars up then back down a bit then up. Today at this moment they are down. I just gave up and bought two boxes of 50 each. The one in pink and the one in Red. Why both...because sometimes it helps to see a direction or one color might be seen better than another on different fabric backgrounds. These remind me of mini chip bags. I am sure some well too find their way to that use. Actually might be great for sealing up bags of sewing hardware such as D rings and tiny buckles too. Though they do have their limits and in all reality can't be compared to a PIN for placement say in the middle of the fabric....I've been known to handle yards at a time where everything has to be lined up perfectly...and these will work with my pins. They don't make your fingers bleed. I think they might be hard to use for people with joint problems or weaker hands. I like them so far. I've got three major sewing projects to get through this next week. And one they won't be a help with and pin's it'll have to be. Sewing two XL twin upper and bottom covers together with a 184 custom cut zipper run before going into just the simple seam to sew the rest all around the middle. The seam they would be fine but not the zipper at least not the way I sew them. I use zippers in my work a lot. So I've looked at these twice now trying to figure out an approach but haven't found one. So really I look at these as a newbie tool to my life...to enhance sewing with and without pins. And maybe add some extra things it can do to...like tiny clothes pins next summer. I can't wait and when someday I get a tiny camper these can come along in their box and be the cutest little pins ever. I honestly think they could hold up a mens pair of wet blue jeans. I am now a fan.  PS better hide from HUBBY if he sees them he'll have to get his own. So far I haven't seen them in mens colors...yet !!!!!
profile.summary: Zipper installing no go. But lots of uses w & w/o pins. Gentler on the fingers. Tiny little clothes pins. Recommended !!!

profile.description: With This Handy Immersion Heater, There's All Kinds Of Things You Can Do On The Road Or On A Camping Trip. You Can Use The Car Lighter Socket On Your Dashboard To Heat A Cup Or Pan Filled With Water. This Can Be Useful For: Tea, Instant Soup, Instant Co
profile.reviewText: Honestly we usually use the AC ones. The ones we are using now are 10 years old. No problem we are always careful to insert in liquid before plugging in and unplug before removing from liquid which prevents blowing their system. BUT there have been a few times we didn't have AC on a car trip and have been going to get one for those. And finally it's here. I understand the same set of principles applies to this one as to the AC version about keeping in contact with liquids at all time while plugged into power. We also have a small 800watt deep cell battery solar generator/inverter system for camping which has a 12Volt cig port too. And we thought it might work with it better than the electric model though it has two AC outlets too. Cord's could be a bit shorter but that's all relative and nit picky. I carry these tucked into a silicone covered metal travel mug which we use with these....the AC's have been used on long train trips, In motels and hotels and gas station restrooms and rest stops if there's an AC outlet...you can plug them in. The 12V has a ways to go to convince us of it's full potential and if it can live up to the AC brothers I'll return and change it to five stars. End of summer we'll know.
profile.summary: Look forward to using this summer on camping trips with generator and 12Volt port as well as occasional car trips.

profile.description: Lift-Away. Press a button to lift the canister away and easily clean hard-to-reach areas. Anti-Allergen Complete Seal Technology + a HEPA filter. Traps 99.9% of dust and allergens inside the vacuum. Powerful and lightweight. Portable and versatile at only 12.5 lbs Brushroll Shutoff. Deep carpet and gentle bare floor cleaning. Swivel Steering. Excellent control for maneuvering around furniture.
profile.reviewText:
I can not recommend this machine at all. It reminds me of a plastic lighter weight vacuum stick trying to be an actual vacuum cleaner in all seriousness and pricing itself twice as much. A wanna be a big guy. GO TO A STORE TO VIEW THIS before buying first. I'm so serious.

Bought this for a few bucks less & free shipping after checking out the reviews here. It's so plastic and so cheap & so not what I would expect for a 150 vacuum cleaner today. I mean please read carefully those who gave it 2-3 stars tossing out of course those who's complaints have nothing to do with the vacuum. I've used it 5 times so far. A big house with mostly hardwood & hard floors on three levels. So this sounded great & light weight to carry up the stairs as well as grab the nozzle & attachments to take on those stairs.

Pros: Light weight, small, smaller footprint than standard upright for same bucks so takes up less space in closet, does get pet fur up, hardfloor & carpet switching via easy to reach button that turns the rollers off or on. Interesting assortment of attachments. Dust cup stays closed until release button pushed. (Not all models have a 24 inch wand the one I have has the shorter 11 inch one. The Sharp site sells the model with the 24".)

Cons: Over priced. Cheapest of Plastics. Head has no reach under most furniture. Plan on getting out attachment wand frequently to reach under and beyond. Flex hose to bottom roller head comes out all the time dumping dirt everywhere. May need to tape it on or figure out someway to prevent this from happening. Can not use glue because you switch out this roller for other heads. The video suggests this has sort of a rolling ball any directional machine but it's not....has some tiny wheels underneath that are sort of multi directional that kinda can turn any which way. Instead these wheels get full of dirt & hair. Ours is a multi(3) long-hair-cat home. The first time I used vacuum I spent 10 minutes half way through tweezing out the hair from the very small brush wheel before freeing them up so one could continue. (I'd just picked up most of the hair ahead of time as I normally do so as not to fill the bag or bagless cups depending on vacuum cleaner I'm using. A dog grooming tool we have works great for this on throw rugs.) And yes we constantly comb/brush the cats too...one rescue kitty just sheds a lot. I've knocked both the attachment tools the machine is suppose to carry off mulitple times already. I haven't had it fall over like some report but can see how that could be an issue. The cup as some complained does get full fast & does stop working if full of hair so expect to dump it more frequently then you may be used to. I'd say about 3 to one normal dumping when compared to our old Dyson. And this one is much dirty to dump. It's nice that the dirt cup comes off machine enclosed to hold dust to carry to garbage-can which thankgoodness ours is in the garage. I then release the contents messy as that is. Not sure what people do without the option of an outside place. Take a paper sack outside with them & try to release in that. Which brings the next negative.....one side of this cup never dumps completely as others mentioned. That means I have to take a stick or hand up into it to pull out the debri that's stuck there. Really stuck there sometimes. For years I had this feather duster that allowed me to once I released the Dyson's cup which always fell out I'd use the feather duster to clean up static clinging dust. Even with the feather duster technique & turning it around to stick it's handle up to try to snag & drag the dirt caught down.....then turn it back around to dust out the cup inside & out...the dirt just clings to the whole thing. I mean I really want to take it all to the utility sink each and every time we dump the cup & wash the whole works iside and out. So instead since there is much more vacuuming to do...gotta put it dusty back on. I'm going to try using a baby wipe or two next time. They say you need to wash the sponge filter every month and change the felt every 6-12 months. I'm ordering 2 new sets of filters for the machine so I can wash two & change them out twice during the use of this machine each time. (Machine needs dry filters.)

Bottom line had I seen this machine in the store or a demo in person I would never fork over 100 bucks plus. I can see how someone who can't handle or has special needs and a very small apartment could feel this machine is good enough. Not great but good enough. But all the plastic all the mess with the filters and the small cup that clings to the dirt and dust makes me suggest you need to Pass on this item. Or at least go look at one first. (We live 90 miles from nearest town that may or may not have one on display. So we depend on the internet and thank you Amazon and Reviewers. Most of the time you are right on.!!!)

The good thing about this machine is it does seem to pick up the dirt off the barefloors and throw rugs both. But on throw rugs it attempts to eat it when you get to an edge so watch rugs with fringes. Also I hated the Dyson so this was actually going to be it's replacement. Foiled again? Have a canister that's good but hard to get up and down the stairs. Looking at the Bissel Smartclean Rewind upright...bagless and more machine for the bucks. Eventually I might use this Sharp to replace an old stick vacuum in sewing room...where you don't want brush heads getting clogged with threads. The vacuum stick definitely falls over and holds very little so this Sharp is a very expensive vacuum stick.
profile.summary: Wanted to like but doesn't roll out for the price.

profile.reviewText: Plan to do dual duty. In house as a small water tower/cooler/heater. And bought a pump that fits into the top to use during camping in summers. I like the smaller size especially in the house scene. The 5-6 gallon bottles at the store freaked me out. Way to big to have sitting on a bathroom counter even if you have good room on it and it's in the guest bath room. This was what I wanted. I rinsed it out with hot water and some soda too and after that filled with well water from the tap. Our water is good but hard. My only worry is the build up of water scale in the dispenser. If I didn't need hot water source I would have chosen a simple crock dispenser but we have some sort of issue with a new water heater causing some distaste in that bathroom and I use my water pik and need warm water for it due to sensitive teeth. So carrying water from the downstairs every day got old. This well work out much better. See no issues with this bottle either. The lid is the screw on 48 mm size for those who may need that info but don't see it listed.
profile.summary: A bit thin. But seems to be fine for my needs so far.

I have two lanterns that do that too and function pretty much same way. One quite expensive does not dim enough though for tenting. Folks who tent know what I'm saying here. Want a light that you can turn on but not disturb others in the tent if you need to get up in middle of night. Also dim way down for changing clothes etc. so the rest of the world isn't getting a shadow show!!! These lights are great for that and also good in general for power failures. I use sometimes with puzzle lampshades too. For some reason these didn't work the first day they arrived. But a day later they did? I left a review but it was taken down? Don't understand why. I sometimes question Amazon for how that happens. Not the first time. If they don't want you to leave a review they need to remove them from your leave a review page when you re-visit. Because if this one makes it I'm pretty sure it's the third time.

profile.reviewText:
WOW these would not come on when first tried with three different Power banks. Two 7500 and one 10,000 all freshly charged and yet no matter how many times I pushed the button or tried to push it did it come on. It's a touch type button which at times can be TOUCHY.

I wrote the company and did not get a response but it was on a weekend. Meantime...next morning I just couldn't get over it wouldn't come on. So I took them downstairs to a wall charger and when I put the first plug into the USB port...and turned the wall chargers switch to on voila just like that it came on. I could turn it off and on and dim without any problems what so ever. So went and collecte two of the power banks that did not work the night before and OMG it lit right up same story. Checked the other bulb out but with the power bank first and it came on too.  So this one has my head scratching and then some. But once they lit they seem fine and very responsive without having to press on the button as it is just a touch pad basically. (I have some experience with these touch pads and a lantern with one that is quite fussy for turning off but it's dimmer also works the same and works well.)
So I changed my review to 4 stars...as much as I like it...I am confused by both their initial problem to turn on. They were aclimated to the house having arrived a few days earlier and had yet to plug them in to try. I love on the other hand the regular rocker switch day light and warm light bulbs which I have bought about a dozen now. I prefer the day light to the warm light but have both for possible power outages in case you want to read and the book or print does better with a warm glo. I recommend the rocker switch bulbs a lot. I can go almost a week on a 10,000 full charged battery pack but also have a solar 800 watt generator that has usb ports and I have a converter for a 12 Volt port that runs another two USB ports too. So I have the option of running these lights on the generator via AC/Wall chargers or the USB ports when camping for a week or two at a time. I usually top off both the generator and my power banks full by AC before I pack up so I have plenty of power. I am concerned that these might become a bit touchy again so I am thinking I will always bring the regular rocker switch bulbs for primary use just in case. I like the idea of being able to dim the light however a lot. It dims down really well at least today it did.
I guess it's just a fluke that both bulbs refused to turn on yesterday via Power Banks but today they worked fine.???? I've given about 8 of the rocker switch bulbs away as gifts this past summer. Along with puzzle lamp shades for difusers and 10,000 power banks per bulb. So far no one has used them? A few have used the power bank but no one is using the bulbs nor are they making the puzzle lampshades. I was told that's a winter project. I mean I gave them the first week of July? I guess my mind works different than others. I had mine out on a back covered patio in use all summer which has no AC power so this is the first year in 15 that we had light in the evenings out there. It was really good and good enough to read by even. And then of course the number one reason I bought my first ones was for camping and also back up lighting for power outages. We don't have a lot of outages but from time to time they do happen. I have one power bank set on side of a small stand up freezer pretty much out of sight but easy to feel for. It's attached to a smaller but super  bright LED/USB light similar to these with push button switch and all one has to do is walk up to it and feel for the switch and turn it on and voila you have lots of light which is instantly portable too and nicer than any flashlight or most lanterns being light weight. I can go then to the utility closet and
find these lights the other power banks and set them up around the house for pretty good light. One we hang from inside an antique floor lamp that's over my husbands easy chair so it provides good enough light to read by. I wish I'd found these years before but think they have only hit the market over the past 3 to 4 years or I was slow to discover them. I also have two solar powered higher wattage bulbs that also can be charged with USB ports and have built in rechargable batteries. Those are sold by aother vendor here on Amazon too. I tried a cheaper version that has a plastic bale but these are by far my favorite ones.
profile.summary: Pretty much delighted with these bulbs and the variety of uses one can find for them.

profile.description: Put on your own mystery dinner theater: murder's on the menu, and everyone's a suspect in this grownup game for 6 to 8 players. The game includes everything you need to serve up mystery, murder, and fun: a shopping list, menus, recipes by cookbook author Sandra Gluck, eight party invitations and envelopes, place cards, secret clues and, best of all, a murder mystery to solve. The annual wine-tasting festival in California Wine Country is in full swing when the body of local vineyard owner, Barry Underwood, is found hidden beneath his wine cellar. Barry has been missing for six long years but with the discovery of his body comes a wealth of new clues to solve the mystery. It's a vintage murder and you may be a suspect. Just invite your friends to dress up and play the roles of the devious suspects (each with his or her own character booklet with roles and background info): Otto Von Schnapps, Tiny Bubbles, Papa Vito, Marilyn Merlot, Ralph Rottingrape, Hedy Shablee, Bonny Lass, and Bud Wizer. Serve up a meal or light snack, play the included CD with its introduction, summary of events, and solution to the crime. Find out who killed California vineyard owner Barry Underwood, and why. In 1985, University Games introduced the Murder Mystery Party to the world as its first game. 31 years later, these parties-in-a-box still include everything players needs to solve a murder during an evening with friends. Ages 18 years and up.
profile.reviewText: Gave it as a gift. Person was over joyed but has yet to hold the party. If one is careful with it you could change the story line and improve upon the twists and turns of the plots and re-do the party over and over about once a year without investing in yet another expensive item. I thought it was a tad expensive for the too dark printed material and pictures on invitations etc. Lots of room for improvements here. As to how it works I would rather see a game where the hostess does not have to orchestrate or know in advance the who did it and nitty gritty story line. Perhaps just telling the host what gender and type of character without revealing whole plot would work better over all. They sell books on how to write your own version of these party games too. I suggest looking here on Amazon for one. I think we'll get one for our neighbor for next year instead of another pre-boxed game.
profile.summary: A gift to neighbor who loves this kind of toy.

profile.description: Designed for flawless brewing of loose leaf iced tea and tea bags, this fine mesh Tea Infuser fully circulates hot water over the tea leaves and provides ample room for the leaves to expand, unfurl and release their full flavor. It's pretty much like science. Twists easily onto any 2 QT TAKEYA Iced Tea Maker or Pitcher.
profile.reviewText:
Fits my Teavanna pitchers too. Looks like the Takeya and Teavanna are pretty much identical. I have 5 of the Teavanna pitchers but thought I'd like the larger infuser. However now that I have it I might have not needed it so much. This infuser the bottom screen part is only 1.5 inches longer. With the coupler or extention upper part it's a full 10.5 inches long. The orginal screen with the Teavanna pitchers are 6 inches long. Also I could just substitute the 6 inch screen with this extention tube as the screens look identical and the screw threads pretty much match.
Teavanna and probably Takeya orginal normal screens with the 2qt sized pitchers = 6 inches in length.

The 7.5 inch screen plus the extention tube top no screen part makes for a full 10.5 inches long.

All before screwing into the lid.

profile.description: Spattered dishes in the microwave, stove top or oven are no more with the Orka Silicone line of lids. profile.reviewText: Buying 3 get 4 deal so picked up an extra set of these for a total of 6. I will use the smallest one the most often....but wanted something I could not only use here at home and in microwave and fridge but take along on camping and backpack trips. I kinda wish they laid more flat to use as coasters too...or hot pads...but can kinda get by with some pans that way with them. Also on the flip side I wish they had a better handle raised up on them which then wouldn't allow them to be used as a coaster at all...so can't have it both ways. Like all silicone it can be hard to keep clean and dust free. Static clobbers these. And I recommend both washing machines and dishwashers when they get beyond decent enough to use or stained. I haven't used these a long time yet. They are difficult to find a place to stash them in drawer or cupboard. I'm working that one out as we speak. One Con is they do not always stay sealed or vacuumed sealed I should say as you might think they should. Some brands do a better job others worse. Overall if you can get past the expense they can help with microwave dishes that don't have lids etc. I do wish they made several rectangled sizes too...especially for say loaf pan sizes. I've got several casserole dishes and loafs that I use a standard sized loaf pan...old Corningware full size loaf pans are ideal but finding them with lids is rare. The smaller sized loaf pans corningware used to make do often have a small glass lid...but a spare silicone would be nice as back up and as coaster too. More colors would be nice too. (If it held the suction...or vacuum better I'd give it 5 stars.)
profile.summary: Expensive but bought set of 3 plus another via buy 3 get 4 deal.

profile.reviewText: Works as it should. Wish I could get this in a longer version...we have an unusual situation in our house. profile.description: The Foodpod is a cooking vessel designed as an easy and convenient way to quickly remove and drain foods that are cooked by boiling, blanching or steaming. Great with all foods; the Foodpod fully contains food for even and easy removal from hot water. The flexible silicone compresses to fit any size pot and for easy storage. The top of the Foodpod clips to the pan edge for easy removal. All materials are FDA food safe and BPA free. Foodpod is top rack dishwasher safe. 6-inch diameter and 5-inch tall.
profile.reviewText:
Basically this item needs a hero...that's YOU to think outside of the box and work out how it might enhance your life.

Ok I read the reviews saying it wasn't good for pasta as it's holes are too large. I agree and it would be nice to have one more netted like with tiny small holes all over so one could grab the top handle and pull it out of pot letting it drain immediately.

ARE YOU LISTENING Fusionbrands? Great concept but you aren't quite there yet...lots of room for improvement or at least another model or two.

But on the other hand it's cute and does a great job with hard boiled eggs & small batch of potato's whole or small ones...green beans and baby carrots not cut up too small or sliced carrots chunkier sized. Cauliflower, Broccoli, Brusselsprouts that sort of veggie. I'm wondering if I could line it with a gauze & develop a simple boiled bread or rice type stuffing with this...where you don't put it down into water but set it up in a deep steamer or even set it on a crumpled bed of foil that sits in water and holds this slightly above the water so essentially using it as a holder for steamed foods...including veggie's as described above. I wouldn't say it is a true 9 by 9 inches like another reviewer complained. So super long veggie's aren't going to fit well either or poke out the strange holes.

Best thing Fusionbrands could do is invent a better food pod that works for most salad and elbow macaroni style pastas......because right now this is no more than an extra draining device for eggs. I like it for eggs but I also use my 10 year old egghead also sold on Amazon more often then not....I gave it 4 stars for it's ability to work my mind and challenge my imagination. Trying not to complain in my head about what it isn't and work out what it could do as is.....Always think outside the box it'll help keep you young.  PS read the postive reviewers here that give you suggestions on what they do succeed in using this. Another improvement would be a way to let you boil/with stirring a pasta that when it's done you just grasp the top it pulls it alltogether and you yank it out to drain.....under cold water when needed too. I'm planning on taking it backpacking and camping to see if I can find an off the wall use.
profile.summary: Great to boil eggs in. Not so for some pasta. Never Rice !!!

This piece is also light in weight and has a glass lid to monitor your food as you cook. Complete with a limited lifetime warranty for worry-free cooking. Make the right choice, choose Lima!
profile.reviewText: Bought for camping so I could pop corn without oil. I'm now afraid to pop corn without oil for fear of chipping the nonstick surface etc. But as far as decent nonstick pans go with the new ceramic safe non stick coatings go this pan seems as good as any...having said that. I have very little nonstick cookware. I prefer stainless with aluminum bottoms or not and enamel clad cast iron and straight up cast iron. Also some enamel ware too. Teflon coated pans of lore I am not sure they even make that any more...was dangerous and never held up over time. Glad to see it go having a pet occupied home...the teflon gases released could harm even kill pet birds not sure what effects on us humans and other mammals is. Anyway the so called ceramic non stick coatings are all over the map for quality and holding up over time. Since this pot if for camping only and it's not part of my daily household cooking I've had no issues with it to date. But I am looking to try a thinking outside the box approach to make non-oiled popcorn camping....they now sell a microwave popper that folks rave about...lots of makers out there selling these almost identical silicone bowls for that purpose. I tent camp so no microwave. BUT I know silicone holds up against pretty high heat. High enough to be placed inside another pot and that pot heated over an open flame. So will see if it works and if I need to add a light crinkled layer of aluminum foil to the bottom of the pan before adding the silicone bowl of corn kernels and that lid. It's an experiement remember. It's one of those the logic to try is there but once in a great while or actually perhaps way to often it still fails. So won't try until next summer but once I do I'll return to update. It's now Feb 2017 so it's a 4-6 month wait. Always thinking outside the lines. (PS the folks using the silicone poppers in microwaves some say no oil is great others say they spray a little oil others use a lot of oil. I'm not opposed to oil and actually love butter and coconut oil for popcorn but when camping do not want to deal with oil messes and cookware. I can flavor the popcorn with butter or butter/grains which I have never tried btw...while still warm after it popped.)
profile.summary: Using for camping gear but hoped to pop corn in it without oils. I chickened out on the popcorn popper idea though.

profile.description: Perfect your abdominal crunches with the Perfect Crunch. The Perfect Crunch reduces strain and supports your head, neck and shoulder so you can focus on targeting your abdominal muscles. Perform crunches comfortably and effectively. Flip over for pushups, dips and a total body workout. Perfect for all fitness levels.
profile.reviewText: It is a bit large. This will work fine for my purpose to use when camping in non maintained campgrounds/sites. Not always have a solid picnic table to help with some excercises let alone a safe chair even. So this item handles uneven ground pretty well..not if it is super rockie. We have ROCKS here in the extreme NW rockies but usually can find a little bit of a flat spot. I am dissapointed in how long it takes to ship. Most of their other products do not have this warning may ship 3 to 5 weeks. Why this one does and the others even as large an item seems odd. My own fault for not catching this as the seller plainly even in RED print at the top of page states this. But still it escaped me. So that is on me. Otherwise once together one does not want to mess taking it apart. It's to big in my mind to leave in the house all year...it'll get stored out in a protected shed with other camping gear...but not the item itself fault. I hate to lay on the floor. I reject yoga and many other excercises due to floor is required. Yes I know a foam pad helps...just some folks have a difficult time with that. Call me mental I can handle the name. This item does help me avoid all floor work. Dips and in my case I do deep knee bends too and this allows me a sturdy enough handle to achieve that when at a camp. A sturdy picnic table though may do same this does it inside the privacy of my tent if I prefer. I look forward to making personal improvements such as better bar padding for better hand gripping. And maybe a cover to keep it dust free during storage. I would give it 5 stars if it came apart easily to fold or folded for storage and travel. But once together it really is meant to stay put together not taken apart. It's size is awkward to throw into the RAV4 to travel with all the other camping gear. Still a tent camper though looking at mini campers but can't get my head around them just yet...and items like this could prove almost impossible to store in them...size and awkward shape. After reading about rust on one reviewers report I will treat and keep up with treating the exposed metal with products that help prevent that..including washing it well and spraying with acrylic clear coat. That ought to help...we are not very humid here so may not become an issue even. Just a simple prevention step.
profile.summary: Pro's outweigh the Con's. Size being the biggest Con. Non folding the Second CON.

profile.description: A CLASSIC MUG FOR COZY MORNINGS. A nostalgic look-alike, this insulated version of the iconic diner mug is just as inviting as the original.
profile.reviewText: Bought 2 one in pink...not what I wanted a very raspberry hot pink top and liner. And one in Pebble a very gray or more than taupe cover and liner which is fine. Wish they offered it in this white so as to avoid pink..but bought on half sale via another seller. I was looking for to use when traveling and camping. We make coffee and tea both using tea like bags for both and one of those hot water heaters in a metal lined silicone travel mug. Love that. Even make coffee on the train in the loo. Carefully to avoid spills with hot hot water. Meantime...these will work great via microwave in motel rooms etc. Had no way to do that with the metal lined other mugs. And so will carry these with some extras stucked inside when traveling but have available when needed to take advantage of the microwave. Wash with mild sponge and they seem to stay pretty clean without staining so far. My white tea...stains worse than any black tea ever has. Not sure why but it's White Peony and it even turns blackish when I make sun tea after a day or two in the fridge even though the tea has been removed. But I can't give it up...so glad so far these mugs haven't been effected.  Do wish they came in about 20 ounce size too. Yes bigger but it allows one to cook a special method of eggs in the microwave that I developed. Or well lets put it this way I discovered on my own and since see there are similar recipes out there. Like I say nothing is ever a true orginal idea...someone else has thought it up too:)))  Oh one reason they don't stain is the color linings help with that. BUT this ALL WHITE one...might be a different story. I'd love to trade off the pink one..but ordered two different to keep our tea vs. coffee separate.
profile.summary: YES PLASTIC MUGS and YES just WHAT I WANTED. Camping and travel. Holds temps well too.

profile.description: You'll be the life of the party when you take along the Coleman 20 Can Party Stacker Cooler to your next event. Not limited to canned drinks, it's tall enough to hold 2-liter bottles upright, so you can easily pack something for everyone. No matter what you bring, the bail handle will make it easy to get it there. To add even more variety, grab a few coolers in different colors and organize your fun. Use one color to chill the adult drinks, another color for the kids, and keep food warm in yet another, so everyone will know where to find their favorite treats. When the fun is done, the specially designed base fits in the lid of other Party Stacker items, making them simple to stack and store until the next glorious get together.
profile.reviewText: I have two this size along with the flat cooler and the 2 gallon water bottle all in same color tan/grayish color. Anyway the upright ones seem to condense on the outside. Made a terrible mess in a friends camper we were sharing for a bike/camp trip at the time. Not happy at all with the condensation problem as well as it tends to not hold ice even 1 to 2  six to eight pound blocks frozen in containers to prevent leakage..and still these condense and water puddles underneath them. I've had them now for three years and though on occasion we use them I didn't call the police when someone stole one of the flat ones even though they didn't condense as much they were pretty limited in their use too. (Actually theft was probably used as a box to carry the brandnew planters out of the garage which was the only items taken. BUT 400 in planters and 20 cooler?) I would not recommend this cooler. Had it not condensed I would love them for their shape and ease in transporting. Instead we just don't use them. We bought them from Pamida before they went out of business and merged into Shopko. Where you buy them I doubt matters. Unless they have improved their insulation capacity or we got 4 coolers all bad insulation I would skip this one. Maybe a day event here or there but not a weekend or more than that.
profile.summary: Condensation issues which appears almost like it's leaking but it's not. Ice is contained in plastic bags but water forms under.

profile.description: Compatible With Nikon: CoolPix S1000pj / S610 / S610c / S620 / S630 / S640 / S70 / S710 / S8000 / Coolpix S1100pj / Coolpix S8100 / S9100 / S6100 / P300
profile.reviewText: This should have been included with the Nikon S8000 but what was Nikon thinking? profile.description: Digital Party Animal Dancing Speaker- Brown Fury Cat - Move to the beat of your favorite music and hook up to mobile devices and stereo systems. - Adopt Me!
profile.reviewText: Ok this was a whimsy gift for older relative...adult but child at heart one. And they loved it and it was just so fun. We presented on a family picnic so out doors and connected to a Sandisk MP3 Player Fuse....and did it's wiggle, jiggle and get down boogie moves. Very cute. People say do not bend it's arms. On line on YouTube it said you could. On a site for Party Animals it said you could adjust the arms but so many people say no matter never grab it's arm when it's dancing...so we are a bit paranoid. It's made very cheap...love the contrast of words telling you how top quality the fur and the speaker is..no it's not folks. This is a whimsical item and it's not made super well. Wish it was...on the other hand it can delight. If it works that is. First Dancing Kitty arrived dead as a door nail...no music from speaker no wiggle or boogie. ZIP. So it went back but knowing the reviews saying sometimes this happens due to poor quality...we ordered a second. We told ourselves this would be the only second chance it got and it delivered. So WHEW. Do I recommend...no...but wouldn't say don't buy either. Why because it's over priced for it's lack of quality but it makes up for that when it works and fit the situation we wanted it for. So...right it's all up to you or your needs. We saw it on a TV commercial on mute and I went oh...that would be perfect for our relative. And went on line searching for dancing kitty and just like that found the very kitty as in the commercial lady sitting in a car...and viola was able to get it. Amazon had the best price but even Amazon had other sellers charging more. So do some searching first. The site on line said they were under 20 and you could get 25% off but I never went far enough to find out the cost of shipping. Also right after I did look into it there...my credit card was compromised. COULD BE? So glad I stuck with Amazon...for original purchase. I was just trying to help someone else out that day who wanted one after seeing ours. Now if only they would upgrade the plastic and working parts and yes we also had to work at keeping the plug connected to the foot like other reviewers on the second kitty. So a lot of what other reviewers said good and bad...we experienced too.
profile.summary: It was a hit...the 2nd one anyway:))))

profile.description: Grafix white chipboard .057 thickness 8-1/2-inch-by-11-inch, pack of 25 lets you add dimension and strength to any paper craft project. profile.reviewText:
I thought I was getting WHITE chipboard and it's more a creme color. Yes it says white. And only one side is finished in white the other is natural. The board is what I wanted but I also expected a slicker surface on at least the one white side. I didn't expect both sides not to be finished in white even though often you get one side that is more rough that would have been fine. It doesn't state two sided finished so guess it's on me. I ordered this same board in the black and the natural too. Natural and white came in same box...so far not the black. So I'm bracing for the black to also be only finished on one side. So they will work for book ends and calander supports for standing up etc. But not for the plans I intended..which were to cut into 3.5 or 4 inch squares for thick Zentangle squares...not unless I figure out how to glue good quality water color paper to the tiles finished or not yet. And also have not found a great source of black paper that's smooth for doing tangles in silver and white inks. I wanted a pure white for both black and brown ink work without having to re-surface or cover. It'll get used up...we make a lot of books and print off our manuals that come on disks so often these days too.
Also do have a pazzle cutter so will use some for cut outs. I might even make my own version of
a french curve for use on my tangles by cutting it via the pazzle and small enough to carry along
with my supplies. I know they make minature french curves but haven't located one recently. So perhaps I can spray paint the edges of my own cardboard version here to help hold up and stay smooth to use during drawings.
profile.summary: Not white on both sides only one side.

Kyra Sedgwick headlines a sizzling 4-disc, 15-episode Season 5 of the series that combines heart, humor and homicide into a show thats equally compelling as a police procedural and a personal drama. profile.description: A must-have for restaurants, this versatile and durable 18" by 26" aluminum sheet pan can be used to prepare just about any food. Designed for professional use, this bakeware product is made with 18-gauge heavy duty 3003 aluminum.
profile.reviewText:
Well cover with acrylic clear or maybe colored paint not sure yet. It is going to be used to turn a kind of camp sink into a table/counter. The sink is 30 inches high but the bottom is 6 inches down from that as it's a canvas sink...(Item sold as a instant/portable planter of all things and is 18 by 36 inches. I was planning in just setting a cookie sheet or melmine large tray into the bottom on one side but that's too incumbersome to use as a table to hold say your coffee mug etc. So the light bulb moment hit me as to what light weight item would work and oh yes an aluminum cookie sheet. A big one. And voila here it is the ideal one. It's 18 and still leaves 10 inches at one end. The plan is to make a ultra tight sling across the top of the sink to rest this sheet on. Only reason I haven't got the project done yet is I'm trying to figure out if it makes sense to make corner sleeves into the sling to fit the sheet into or an elastic band for the corners to hold it in place. Just in case wind comes up not so much to protect it from people knocking it about. Meantime the sling well also reinforce the canvas sink part which improves the sturdy frame to begin with. It could use a little help though the feet are like those you see on the portable camp chairs all the rages these days that
kind of spread out accordian like. The center needs two tiny pins to stop it from over extending and that's where the taught cover well help hold it firmer. I'm so excited I could almost go camping right now...oh wait it's still winter for a couple more days. Darn it! Pouring rain up here but it's washed all the lower valley snow away....so spring and camping is in the air. I'm so happy with the cookie sheet as a DIY item I might buy the shorter 22 inch version to drop to the bottom of the sink to use too...and the cool part is I'll be able to use the under side of the canopy through the 10 inches left open for storage for towels and maybe even dishes or paper goods. And I've already ordred through Amazon a tiny dish sink that's perfect for the open end too...and I could use this on top as a counter to dry the dishes etc. The sink it'self is meant to hold big weight as a planter think wet earth 18 by 6 by 36 inches so this should also hold a three gallon jug of water with a pump or spigot. All kinds of light bulbs are going off....Thanks to the gal who said she paints them and uses them to marble and do other craft projects. That sold me.
profile.summary: Just what I wanted.

profile.description: So what makes these bottle easy to squeeze? Our plastic squeeze bottles with caps are made from LDPE (Low-density polyethylene) plastic recycle code 4. This plastic has a lower density which makes it more pliable and easier to squeeze, but yet just as durable as a more rigid bottle made from high density plastic. They are great for kids or people with a weak hand grip. LDPE can also withstand cold temperatures very well but are not ideal for heated liquids. These bottles are strong and have very good impact resistance. The dispensing spout already has a precut hole in the tip, you can easily cut the tip to increase the hole size to accommodate thicker liquids and prevent clumping if your liquids have larger solid particles such as minced onion or garlic.
profile.reviewText: Like and recommend within in limits. They do leak air along their lids not the caps the screw on lids leak. Not bad and if careful not product probably but yes a source of leakage especially oils. Having said that we still like and wanted this style cap. Can trim the nozzle down to open for wider or chunky foods like pickle relishes or not so chunky salsas. Bought eight ounces and their brothers the 16 ounce size both. Lids are same size for both so could be interchanged if you like. Did not want the attached cap because I find they can get in way of use. If I place out on picnic table or for a group of folks I will keep the lids in the house in a small bowl until done and putting back in fridge. This way I don't lose a cap by a misplaced one by guest who isn't paying attention so to speak. I would recommend having stated the obvious and expected problem for us. Screw on caps do not seal prefectly...most of these however do not. Not the narrow mouthed variety either. We wanted the wider mouth version..even could be wider but did not find any to choose over these.
profile.summary: Pretty much what we expected. A bit high priced but plastic's have gone up as of late. Recommend with limits. Have 16 ounce too.

profile.description: Now you can make your very own books right at home, and it's so easy! Make notebooks, recipe books, journals, reports, calendars, albums and more! The Cinch binds your project in 3 easy steps: punch holes in up to 20 sheets of light weight paper, thread sheets, and cinch wire. It also features a large, easy-to-empty waste bin for catching all those punched holes, a handle clip so the Cinch can be stored easily, a sliding measurement guide for perfectly centered holes every time, and rulers in inches and centimeters. The easy to use lever means no batteries or power supply needed! This package contains 1 Cinch Book Binding Tool (5" x 8-1/2" x 11-1/2") and instruction sheet. The Cinch binds 3/4" to 1-1/4" and uses double O wires or spiral binder. Book covers, binding wires, binders, and paper sold separately.
profile.reviewText:
I like square or rectangle holes for the wires over the round ones. So Zutter has the square angled ones. Just in case you miss reading that among the fine print on this item. Some of you it might matter. This has some good qualties. It says that some coils fit these holes too. I have a 4 to 1 coil system but haven't checked to see if those coils fit these holes yet. The 3 to 1 coils and wires might match up but these are suppose to be 2 to 1. Which reminds me google binding wires or double wires to locate prices much better than the small craft sized packages of 3-6 come sold for these systems. Also a few craft places not just the office binding shops like Office Depot sell the wires in bulk of 50 to 100 and nice colors to choose from.
This machine is a lot bigger than the Zutter...other reviewers on other sites said they like this better than the Bind It All. I can't say one is any better or easier myself. But the foot print this takes up is huge compared to Zutter the holes are round not square and so it comes down to individual taste as much as anything. Amazons prices in Sept 2010 was the best for this unit at the time I could find which included shipping total.
What I wish is that either or both Zutter and Cinch would come out with a 3 to 1 punch model too so that the smaller diameter wires would be available to take advantage of....both priced cheaper and give us more options.
Also for those who do lots of binding check out the small office punch systems available on office binding sites that cater to all sorts of binding. Many machines available from 100 to below 300 dollars.
Happy Binding....and stay away from Plastic Comb machines...they are such a thing of the past:)))) Coiling or wires are the only way today!!!!
profile.summary: Round Holes Not Angled.....

profile.description: 1 - 8 Oz Bottle, 1 Microfiber Cloth (terry style) And 2 Instant Detailers
profile.reviewText:
Be careful when using this solution. A little goes a long ways. Also not sure how one gets it off but we had to remove it after using it on our counter and marble topped table. Why because it polished it alright & everything & I mean everything slipped right off it. Any magazine or piece of paper would just go gliding off. For those who have bars & want to show off throwing a mug of beer down to the end for someone to catch...just make sure someone is prepared to make a quick catch. This stuff glides..wonder what would happen on a bowling alley? Anyway what happened to us is we had older kits...yes I know they have no business walking on our counters let alone a table top. They do anyway & at their ages this was a problem. Jumping from the counter to the marble table top & then just slide right off the other side of the table. I kid you not they had no way to stop so not cool. In fact cruel. After waiting for this stuff to wear down or off naturally within a few days..it did not. We eventually got out fresh cleaning cloth & clean sponge filled with dish soap & went at washing the stuff off the counters & the table top. We hated to do it as we thought it was just the greatest. It made our black marble & green marble items & table top shine. Brought it back to life wasn't the word for it. However kitties were too old for this ice skating rink polish & we took reverse action with the soap which worked. Meantime our cabinets are a formica type material so we ordered the larger 32 ounce spray bottles to bring them back to new. There is a slight rough texture to the surface but that is why we like this material it still cleans it & brings it back to life. Seems to help keep static and dust and grease from building back up as fast too. If you have a wood cabinet that is finished this material does a nice job keeping them polished too. Do be careful not to get it on the floor.....or you'll be doing a number keeping your own paws I mean feet under you. And even though I use poly type finishes on my wood & vinyl floors both giving them a nice wet look. I do not want people including ourselves to fall. I've used it to help bring back life to a huge marble nut bowl and other polished marble products & faucets and stainless products around the house. I haven't used it at all on LCD, Computer or TV screens. Have cleaned my phones with it. Have never tried it on CD or DVD disks. It does not appear to be very abrasive....we have no idea what is in it. But it makes one think of silicon only I believe it states it does not contain silicon. Have not tried their speciality cloths since I have 24 or more micro-fiber and detailer cloths already. Most are still new. I cut the larger ones into fourths and finish their edges to stop ravel and make it easier to use in smaller projects & clean into corners if need be. Try a small bottle first then decide yourself. Amazon doesn't seem to carry the larger 32 ounce sizes or the gallon size just yet that sells for under 30 through other sources. Very interesting stuff this Brillianize !!!

Update after several years of use. For some reason the larger sized bottles seem to loose strength over time. So we are no longer buying it in bulk...a little goes a long ways.
profile.summary: A little dab will do you !!!

profile.description: Working in conjunction with its carbon washable filter system, our air purifier pulls in unclean air from the rear, first passing through the carbon filter which removes airborne particles as small as 0.3 microns. This filter also acts to deodorize any unpleasant odors. Air then passes through the inner PCO cell, further filtering airborne contaminants as small as 0.2 microns. The anion emitters, now moved forward of the fan to the front panel, release trillions of negative ions into your home, attaching themselves to dust particles, and dropping them straight to the floor. This advanced function is ideal for eliminating dust, animal dander, and other harmful particles that float in the air. Left behind is fresh oxygen rich air. The sterilizer function turns on the units blue UV lamp to incinerate viruses and germs. When you need to eliminate strong or offensive odors in your home, the Purifier/AWAY mode creates activated oxygen (ozone) based upon the square footage of your home. Perfect for eliminating tobacco smoke odors, cooking odors, chemical/cleaning agent odors, paint odors, etc. The activated oxygen will also sanitize pollution embedded in walls, ceilings, floors, carpets, furniture, clothing, countertops....all surfaces in your home. Use Purifier/AWAY mode (ozone function) when home is unoccupied on units built in timer. Ozone reverts back to oxygen after approx. 30 to 45 minutes. Return home to fresh, clean, oxygen rich air....provided only by the 4 advanced technologies of the Green Air Machine!! 2 year warranty.
profile.reviewText:
Update: I see many people thought original review rambled & said nothing. Reading it today they have a point but the information was definitely there. So the update...
I'd give this purifier only 2 stars today. A comment asked for an update.
Three issues I have against this air purifier is #1) No thumb screws on front cover just the back cover to the filters. So screw driver is needed. The blades seem to need cleaning every 2-4 weeks. I mean it builds up with a lot of dust as much as 1/4-1/2 inch beyond the edge of the blades. #2) Gave up on auto settings due to the many power interrupts in our area and the occasional person unplugging or turning unit off. Unit does not hold it's settings if loss of power. #3)Not enough air pull to utilize filters. Little build up of dust or anything on filters. I've checked & rechecked the filters to make sure they are configured & placed correctly. No idea if it helps with odor as I doubt it pulls enough air through the charcoal filter.

I need to look for replacement thumb screws to make the process of removing the front cover easier. I wipe the blades & inside area in front & the cover down with a slightly damp microfiber cloth. I don't know what would happen if I didn't clean it often. I check the back filters when I clean the blades. I do love the small foot print of this unit but performance and maintenance brings it down.  I've invested in several larger units by Rabbit Air for 2 living areas and placed this little unit in utility room approx 12' x 13' with 1 outside back door & multi-cat litter box. Basically no more hair or dust on blades in this location than occurred in more open area of house.

*** To sum it up.....The fan doesn't appear to have enough pulling force to actually pull air through the dense multi-filters & I suspect most of the dust on the blades is entering through the front of the unit. I would not recommend it if you have allergies as I think it's under engineered to pull enough air through the filters.***

I may somewhat contradict since I continue to use it as it does seem to reduce dust build up on open shelves & table and counter tops. (Perhaps the ozone generator is helping with that. But I have no way to evaluate/measure it.) Good luck everyone and hope this makes more sense than orginal review.
profile.summary: Expensive but small foot print sort of.

profile.description: Premium Steel Straight Blade for CARL DC-210N/220N/238N/250.
profile.reviewText: I don't think Love it is quite the word for five stars but we have the 15 inch trimmer and now and again it needs new blades. Especially if you are cutting lots of photo paper. For some reason it'll start to drag on photo paper before it does other kind of card stock or paper? I used to buy sets of 4-5 I think it was but can not find them any longer. Its small size makes it ideal for protecting laptop computers, projectors and other portable electronics. A Protected LED illuminates to indicate that adequate surge suppression is available. profile.reviewText:
Used this on a train trip recently. Have used it other places too but basically the train has me worried and the motels for plugging in our mini PC. And we also brought along a coil heater unit the kind you place in a cup of water and plug directly into an outlet and it heats up to the boiling. Well this Tripp Lite held up and seemed to protect the PC and the heater coil just fine. At least we didn't loose either and they worked great with no signs of power surges. profile.description: TIKI, the brand trusted by millions, helps create a paradise in your backyard. This charcoal colored torch stand secures torch poles up to 1-inch in diameter and is made with 7-pound of cast iron to ensure torch stability. This torch stand is a must have accessory and gives you the flexibility to place your TIKI(R) Brand Torch anywhere in your backyard
profile.reviewText:
OK I DO NOT use with Tiki Torchs but they hold spare tent poles with lantern arms for LED lights perfectly.
Have bought two now. I spray painted both with Rustoleums CLEAR MATTE spray paint because many reviewers claimed this style of pole holder rusts. The two I bought look well painted but to make sure I did two top coats on the upper side and three on the bottom. This paint dry's fast and I did it outdoors on the lawn and let dry between coats of paint. Looks just slighty shiner than it did to begin with despite paint being matte. Would do it again because it'll get used in the tent camping and outside tent both and this way I do not have to worry. about rust marks developing on my tent floor.  It supports my Para adjustable tent poles which I use as lamp poles with two to 3 pig tail style arms each and hang light weight Camp lanterns and or Puzzle lamp shades with LED/USB powered light bulbs. I can hang the power bank on one arm using a small fabric basket/sling I made to hold the power bank while the other arm holds the hanging lamp or a USB/LED lantern with dimmer switch. I bought the tent poles for spares for a tent that's got fragile built in tent poles as in the day will come the tent poles will fail.. So now why not put the poles to use otherwise.  BUY THE WAY it clearly states on the tag on the stand when it arrives NOT FOR UMBRELLAS. OK it does not say no tent poles:)))) I live my life coloring outside the lines and thinking outside the box. I may need a bit of a shim for the poles are approx. 3/4 inch diameter but to date haven't bothered with shimming. These are small enough I can actually put just one to two pole sections on it and set it on the picnic table middle or side to cast light over the table much like a table lamp. Love the poles and love the stand. I would consider using it with a sunbrella style camping/beach umbrela but probably is a bit light weight for a full market umbrella and a lot of negatives by folks who THOUGHT despite saying Not for umbrellas that it should too hold their Market or Yard umbrellas with or without a table center hole to help support it. NOT the fault of the seller or the item it's the fault of the folks who wanted it to work for which it was clearly not designed for...Spray paint it to prevent rusting if that's a concern you may have.  I'm still happy with these stands and also use as a coat tree inside the tent using the pig tail like pole arms or lantern arms and sold on Amazon and Ebay alike. I bought from both and all pairs are a bit different sized but all work out for my needs. I cut out coated pack cloth to make a case for these to tote to campsite and keep from sliding about the back end of car or pickup. They don't exactly stack perfectly on top of each other but with a piece of fabric between them it seems to balance out much better. So I am a happy camper. Wishing you all a long and happy summer season of fun outdoors.
profile.summary: My second one!!!. States CLEARLY NOT FOR UMBRELLAS for all those who get mad when it's too light weight for that.

profile.description: TIKI, the brand trusted by millions, helps create a paradise in your backyard. This charcoal colored torch stand secures torch poles up to 1-inch in diameter and is made with 7-pound of cast iron to ensure torch stability. This torch stand is a must have accessory and gives you the flexibility to place your TIKI(R) Brand Torch anywhere in your backyard
profile.reviewText:
I got a good laugh at the do not use with umbrella. Many sites who are selling this reviews mention they use with umbrellas and most of those hate this. It's a wee bit small and light weight for a full sized umbrella. However I could see how some manage to make it work if they use a table with an umbrella hole. I don't intend to use with any style of umbrella so I can skip that warning LOL
I picked up some CLEAR MATTE Rustoleum Spray paint this past week to use to cover this stand especially the underside. I've read lots of times where someone had rust develop. My husband thinks I'm a bit too nervous since he thinks it's painted very well. I tend to agree to a point. If others have complained with similar if not identical items a small bit of precaution seems warranted. I intend to use mainly inside a tent but now thinking about a second to use outside too. I carry Paria tent poles..a pair of them to have for back up poles if my favorite tents very fragile attached poles break. They will sooner or later break. The first tent they sent me had one inserted backwards and arrived busted. The replacement has yet to break. BUT I also fear using it because they are so fragile. But I love the tent. I also discovered only a year ago the wonderful LED/USB light bulbs with on off switches and that plug into power banks that charge phones. WE don't have a cell phone living in a dead zone means no tower service most of our area up here. I don't do tiki's torches either. But picked up two lantern arms and will pick up two more and I also picked up two other stick in the ground with nails umbrella pole holders to use with the paria poles too outside the tent of course. Those are proving to be quite the challenge as they will need inserts of PVC pipe or a wood rod that fits better and had been drilled out for the poles to slide down into. Basically a round shim of sorts. This tiki stand may need some extra support as the poles are smaller than many umbrella poles maybe up to about half. I enjoy outside the box DIY challenges so this will not be that big of a problem. I do recommend painting this stand..it is iron and it might rust or maybe not if you have it inside. I intend to use inside the tent and outside sometimes at home. If I have two I could set them up to two poles with a rod or rope between them to hang up a privacy wall inside the larger tents too. Overall. I'm happy with this item and for what I intend to use it for. Though not light weight it's a do-able size for car camping. Or oh yeah really glamping as they are calling it these days for when you go over board for the comforts.
profile.summary: Will use for Paria Adjustable Tent Pole & two lantern arms while camping etc.

profile.description: Proven to effectively treat behavior problems in dogs and cats that are caused by stress, anxiety and phobias, such as separation anxiety, travel, new environments and social interaction. Provides superior, longer-lasting delivery of pheromones than any other pheromone product and goes where the animal goes to provide round-the-clock pheromone release. This is a safe and effective first-line treatment that often eliminates the need for powerful prescription medicines. Can be used on dogs and cats of all breeds and ages and without side effects.
profile.reviewText: Even though we divide these collars in to four pieces...and sew those into tubular shoe laces/webbing...to make up four quick release collars for our cats...because these on their own do not hold up and our cats well not only chew through one within a day or two but the other fellow cats help the one wearing it chew through it too...little rascals. It works...doesn't seem to be a problem it is inclosed in a tubular lace and as active if not better than the orginal. Any of the powdered residue that is left sitting on the table or sewing machine after making up a group of four of these at one time...we smear and rub into these new collars to make sure each has an approx...portion of the good stuff. And the bonus....it goes 3 sometimes 4 times longer than the orginal one collar does. Cats do not chew off...they do scratch at it...one must not use nylon webbing like they make leashes out of because they can become forshortened enough it starts to strangle kitty. We found out the hard way. Kitty is fine...lucky though. Back to shoe laces though they look ratty and fuzzy we can re-use several times by opening up one end of the collar and taking off the buckle on that end...pulling out old plastic piece and inserting new. Must find 1/2 inch flat tubular laces. Possible you could make out of fabric folded and made into a strap but not sure how it would hold up...the laces we use are cotton. Cat that needs it is not the cat that gets to wear collar. As others have noted sometimes it's the victim of the bully that wears collar to calm down the house. And so our kitty is the victim and has to wear the collar too...poor kitty. Meany ME ME kitty is smallest bully ever...but BULLY in caps for sure. Relentless little guy...but so happy these collars work. Saves on vet bills and injuries too.
profile.summary: Been using for years...like the ones without the perfumed scent...so does kitty.

profile.description: The songwriting genius' multi-label highlights on one CD! The first of its kind, this unique collection gathers 21 tracks released between 1968 and 1999, including Newman's greatest hits, album cuts, and soundtrack classics.
profile.reviewText: Lets get this straight...I AM A SHORT PERSON AND I LOVE "SHORT PEOPLE" of course I don't have grubby little fingers...but first time I heard this piece was eons ago when Scott Hamilton ice skated to it as one of his competitive programs pre-olympic days. Yes it's that old. He hit the ice in a long black trench coat but started out in a squatt down pose as super short. And eventually was skating standing tall.....Scott's not that tall himself and so another short person was totally delighted in Randy Newmans fun.....ya gotta have self esteem to make it in this world. You get your confidence from your parents and Randy is not your parent...He's an entertainer. Randy is the guy who would write songs that kids would sing to drive their parents nuts in the car. One very delightful and talented guy come music classical as well as funny! Thanx Randy may all your hate mail just dry up and blow away.....you'll get the last laugh anyway as CD's will out last us all.....hurray! If you can afford it someday buy the 30 year package. Meantime enjoy this one or any CD's by Randy Newman.....and he doesn't care if you are short or tall....as long as you have grubby fingers afterall.
profile.summary: IT's RANDY NEWMAN What's more to say:)))

profile.description: Back to Basics Nut Roaster makes glazed nuts in just 10 minutes. Fun-to-use, the stove-top Nut Roaster's unique design gives consumers the ability to create this favorite snack at home. Ideal for glazing Almonds, Pecans, Walnuts, and more.
profile.reviewText:
This is something of a gimmick item. I was looking for a nut roaster 3 years ago and
this kept coming up as the only one to get. So finally I bought it and it basically is for
using pre-made bottled flavorings full of sugar and spices and this thing sort of mixes them all around the pan so that the flavorings get applied well to the nuts. I don't want that. I want a nut roaster period. Yes I tried to use it for that but Almonds especially bunch up and you have to reverse directions with the stir handle and when you do that the handle sometimes unscrews itself and there you are. And when the nuts get caught up under the stir rod they can also burn before you can manage to unstick. I found it does not do a good job of keeping all the nuts evenly in contact and turning to avoid contact with the heat instead many of the nuts on the bottom do not get stirred up and around either. Basically if you want to sugar coat nuts maybe this works. But for me I do a better job doing small batches of nuts in a cup in the microwave than trying to manage small or larger amounts in this thing. I've given up trying to make this pan work out. It doesn't cut it as a nut roaster any way which way you turn it.
profile.summary: It doesn't just roast nuts well.

profile.description: Shark Motorized Floor Brush Hose - NV350 series including NV350, NV351 & NV352
profile.reviewText: Just what was needed to replace a broken one. Torn on end nearest rotator head. So we are not easy on our NV350 and more rough treatment than some households probably. No doubt attributed to the orignal one failing. But replaced with this and it's now as good as new. Unless you notice the scratches over the years of hard use overall. Happy customer and would recommend if yours needs replacing too. Not all second dealer products work well. I have yet to find a charcoal filter that matches the original or even is charcoal. Lucky for me I've kept the original foam one and just use swiffer like sheets cut to fit to filter the outter side and it works great. Replace every 4 to 6 uses with new cut to fit piece over the black foam. I wash the black foam 3 to 4 times a year too. Every according style replacement filter tried falls out. They do not stay in the machine. That is using their replacment casing too. So happy I kept the original until we had given the new one a trial or two or five. And again I tried and again the next one by another seller still fell out. So the orignal stays in the new ones are not made to have the fiber filter removed so could not tear it out and apply to the original case that stays put. But washing the original black foam filter and cutting out prefilters from swiffer sheets or similar dusting sheets works just like the new one. If the white cut outs show grey to black it is time to replace them. If you skip it once too often you will notice the machine is not working as well at picking up and seems to over heat a bit too. SO we make a pile of white cut out prefilters which are easy to replace and just keep going. Sharp makes the best vacuums these days. Makes all others shameful especially Dyson..and YES I own one...and plan to give it away at a garage sale this summer but if no one wants it I'll take it to the good will. So need to weed out the old vacuum cleaners. I would like to have a sharp on each floor. We have three stories and a 12 foot deep basement. So far one is handling the whole house. But I'm looking at a new one...and you can find good used ones on Ebay so maybe for the basement and for the attic too a used one would be handy to leave those places. Meantime one is doing it all and we have long haired cats.
profile.summary: Exactly perfect replacement for torn original one. Would buy again if needed.

profile.description: Oral B Cross Action Power Battery Toothbrush Soft bristle (Pack of 3)
profile.reviewText: Husband uses the expensive & forever failing & changing models Sonic Care rechargable brushes. I found these in 04 & couldn't be happier. I left him to play with the Soniccare items on his own. I find this as good as it gets. No timing & no fancy gimmicks but I get great feed back & results when I go in for cleaning. I'm always told...once a year is quite enough for an annual check up & cleaning not twice or more. What I also love about these toothbrushes is you can travel with them. Not itty bitty mind you but they aren't bad either. The battery life seems reasonable & I can tell when they need changing because it does slow down but still keeps going. Maybe someone else wouldn't notice so then change them on a scheduled basis like every 4 or 6 months. I suspect 6 is plenty of time for that. I change them no more than twice a year it seems. I have two tiny toothbrushes I carry in my purse when on travel or camping or biking and one is a snoopy kids model that's nice and short and has a nice cover for protection on the head. It fits in a side pocket so no one ever notices my tooth brush. Also the other is skinnier and though an adult size it has a small soft head & slim size is great to travel with too. No head protector so I bought one of those that slips over just the head. A sandwich Zip Lock bag works great and holds the travel tooth paste and floss all together. If I could change anything it would be the noise any of the electronic tooth brushes make both battery or electric. I take my Oral-B along for travel to convention or extended road trips. I change the brushes about 2-3 times a year but make sure in between time they are kept clean & not building up toothpaste in any way so as not to prevent good performance. The only thing that could be better is sometimes you catch the bristles in the cover wrong and it bends them out of shape. So I'll replace a head when that happens. I've learned to be more careful and inspect it when putting the cover on most every time as an automatic thing. I never worry about batteries on travel. If I'm going for a long time like trip to NZ for two months I'll put in a new set so no problem. I always use the soft brushes as recommended by most dentists.
