profile.description: Vellum Bristol paper, 67 lb Bristol, 92 bright, Size 8.5" x 11", 250 sheets per pack,.resealable clearwrap package, Acid free, Lignin free, Laser Inkjet and copier guaranteed
profile.reviewText:
This is exactly what it is a nice bright white THIN cardstock. It might show through printing so not great for double sided work. I find it too light for a booklet cover but I might use it to make say a notepad or post it note cover.....as it would be easy to fold to make those. I suggest you look at the Wausau 90 & 110 pound cardstocks if you want to make the classic tags and crafty cards with a white background. I use this paper a lot and it prints well through inkjets and copy machines...but I turn to the 90 and 110 pound versions both heavier weight and thicker paper for cards & gift tag making. And it stamps well too. But this paper is the lightest weighted of the vellum hand cardstocks by Wausau's common line here.

NOTE VELLUM DOES NOT IMPLY IN ANYWAY TRANSLUCENCY in the paper industry perse. The crafters began calling some of the translucent vegi based papers as vellums and the term has stuck in their small world but has yet to make the industry on the whole throw out the term of Vellum as in hand or style of surface on the paper out. It was in the industry before cafters came along and it will remain long after the fads too. As to the vegi based paper the crafters are looking for there are a number of kinds and most tend to curl when run through inkjet printers. But they do make specialized ones and slightly heavier weight ones that are made for use in home and office inkjets without much curling. I've got beautiful reds and deep blue and even a soft mossy green in these translucents all chosen for their inkjet compatiblity. I found a wonderful metalic soft gold too. Most are sold in 500 sheet bulk packages or full reams.
profile.summary: This is Vellum in the paper industry...not the crafters world.

profile.description: Add extra weather protection to your sun canopy with the Coleman Instant Canopy Sunwall, Accessory Only. Designed for use with 10 x 10-foot straight-leg Coleman Instant Canopies (sold separately), this canopy wall is made of UV Guard fabric that provides UPF 50+ sun protection. The heavy-duty material can also help block wind and rain, creating a sheltered wall for your instant canopy.
profile.reviewText:
Love no...so funny. Have white version from another seller that does same but wanted to give this one a try to perhaps help keep a Canopy straight wall tent cooler when the sun and heat intensifies during summer up here. I lost a brand-new swingwall canopy last year. Now this year...I missed the canopy straight wall tent with it's full 10 by 10 foot print so hope to try again this year but move it away from any wind. We have another three to four year old swing wall as well as a LED coleman canopy both bought the same time that have never given us problems. The new one just collapsed last year after first 2 of the upper arms wouldn't stay up then we were standing away from it over by the picnic table and it just went right over bending the feet even. We were all in awe you might say. . OK wish it was silver one side at least to reflect the heat away. BUT UV protected or so it states. I think a lot of us expect this to be silver on one side.
Important info for those shopping for other than coleman canopy's. This has a couple of hooks that fit around the legs on each end/side and three stakes to help hold it down to the ground. It also has at least one hook or two at the top middle areas that you can wrap around the top side beam. These are all metal flat small hooks on elastics some. Ok...if you don't have a coleman with the exact spaces to attach the hooks this is one idea I ofter. Buy about 50 yards of 1/4 or even 1/8 inch diameter shock cord here on Amazon pretty reasonable in any of your favored colors they seem to have a lot of them to choose. Anyway cut into strips double the size strips and a bit more to go around your pole size. Close the open ends together via a figure eight knot. Pull each side very tight to make sure it won't undo. Wrap these around your poles working them up the pole to match where the Sunwall side hooks appear. You can now hook onto these elastic mini wraps which is better than say rubber bands and can maybe even stay with your leg or removed depending on your choice and the way your brand of leg collapses. Take a tiny beaner to hold/store all the little bands you made to keep with the sunwall in it's case if you want. You could do this at the top I suppose too or to wrap one of the hooks around the top. The white sunwall we have uses velcro and it just happens to match up like the other brand of four sided sun room too pretty close to Colemans hook velcro like patches at the top of the canopy and beams so we actually could sew on velcro to help close up any gapping for this or for another style of canopy. Since I am not familiar with any others nor the slant wall versions I assume most folks can think outside the box for other fixes on their own too.
profile.summary: This is heavier & more opaque to block the sun better than our white version from other maker. But may absorb more heat too!

profile.description: Sergeant's good behavior pheromone collar helps cats in fearful or stressful situations (separation anxiety, visitors, other household cats, Loud Noises, new baby, vet Visits, traveling). good behavior pheromone collar provides a convenient alternative to diffusers- the collar goes where your cat goes!
profile.reviewText: Bought these again...only because they were 1/3 cheaper than the brand that's not scented. I HATE THE SMELL OF THESE. THE CAT HATES THE SMELL OF THESE. The non smell variiety is identical in everyway to these but the no scent is a plus. But cheap hubby wants to save money so we bought the stinky version. Poor kitty. Poor me when kitty gets close up to my face say when he visits a moment in bed or on couch. He's not a big lap sitter...he's a BIG MAINECOON. A sweety with the collars on not so sweet without. Another much smaller newbie came to live here three years ago and one or both needed intervention...thus the collars seem to work and seem to keep on working. But only on the Mainecoon not the little bully. But the Mainecoon wasn't going to take it off the little fella so we feared vet bills etc. and gave the collars a trial run. They need severe modification however. These things are plastic that is brittle and breaks up easily. Cats will chew through them also including our third cat would help chew through them on the other cats who were chewing and scratching at them so we'd be lucky to get one to stay on a kitty for even a week...usually within 3 days and it was off. One we've yet to find after 3 plus years...so some major DIY know how has come into play. WIDE TUBULAR shoe lacing works the best. We open a new packaged collar. Take it out and cut it in half. Then we cut up the middle the fulll length of that very carefully with strong scissors so you have a narrow half as long piece and approx 1/4 of the orginal collar. We insert this into the shoe lace pre cut to the size we'll need to fit the cat after we sew on the quick release plastic buckles. (100 in a package and all re-usable well last forever.) And we also recycle some laces others get too frayed during the use. Best just to keep looking for ones that work. We tried tubular nylon cording 1/2" but when kitty scratched at it...it ended up for shortening it...until collar actually became too tight and was strangling him. So the nylon webbing is out for our cats at least.) Shoe laces are not easy to come by that work well. Tubular and 1/2 inch are the key. So we make 4 collars out of the one. The cool thing is we get on average 5 months out of one collar. I kid you not. The quarter collar lasts longer. The interesting thing is there is a half life going on however. So we make a note on our calendar when he gets a new collar and if it's number 1 through 4. So as it goes the first lasts 4-6 weeks. Second 3-5 weeks the third 2-3 the fourth 2 with luck. How do we know it' not...suddenly our lovely Mainecoon is no longer trying to avoid the rascal bully and well have a show down instead. Also we have tried collars on both kits but like others with multi cat families noted sometimes a collar doesn't work on a cat..that seems to be the case with the little monster. I'd love to collar him and just him as we miss our fiesty independent Mainecoon but we do love the mellowed out fellow just the same. We probably would continue with the collar for him even if we didn't have the rascal who's the bully anymore because it seems to help with some of his anxieties. He can become a big spook of dark corners and what have you. The collar seems to help him with that. So the third kit needs nothing he's loved or not buy the other two. The rascal it doesn't work with if anything might make him a bit more agressive by reducing his anxiety in the other direction but does work on the BIG fellow who could use some slight mellowing out. And is better than big vet bills too. But requires modifications with benefits. Oh by the way they say the powdery stuff that flakes off the collars contains the active ingredients I sweep it up and rub that in equal parts right into the freshly made shoe lace collars before re-sealing the three spars into the orginal foil pouch. I date the pouch when I started the new 4 collars to not just the calendar so I've got a record to consult if I forget to write it elsewhere. Hope this helps anyone else who has had trouble keeping these things on their pets.
profile.summary: Works with modifications. But hate the scent.

We hope he didn't eat it. He chewed it and another cat that we adopted at same time chewed it on him too. They say it's safe but plastic solids probably not..chemical maybe. profile.description: Wenzel Smartshade canopy turns into a screenhouse using the Smartshade Screen Walls. Easily attach them to the Smartshade canopy to provide ventilation and insect protection.
profile.reviewText:
With some modification it FITS our Coleman Swing Wall frame and the Coleman LED frame canopy both. [Numbered highlights at bottom for those who want to skip all the details and majority of longer text here.]
Though if frames are set to the fullest height it can be a tad short so we set it to the middle height peg and it fits
as pefect as you'll ever get. We intended to go all the way around the outside of the poles like it shows in this picture with the Wenzel frame. You can do that with the LED canopy but not the Swing Wall. The swing arm mechanism gets in the way with that. So one side it fits just fine on the outside the Swing Wall side we have to attach inside the poles because it can't wrap around them. Also the coleman canopy cover material doesn't have the matching hook velcro where they appear on the Screen Walls we will add some via sewing the hook to the canopy canvas to mate up with the already sewn loop on the screen. It's easy to match up without even marking the canopy because it's almost directly under the coresponding Coleman's velcro wrap to attach and secure to the frame. So we will add 5-6 inches of 1.5 - 2 inch wide hook velcro to the lower inside edge of the canopy cover and voila this shade will fit perfect as if it's custom made. (Which by then it is.)This will do the same for the LED canopy and I would assume the regular straight leg version of Coleman Canopy systems too.
Now why didn't we purchase the coleman screen house instead? Because it has bad and I mean BAD reviews as being made with such poor screen materials it falls apart as well as snags and often looks used upon opening the brand new package. So REVIEWS count. The EZ-up brands said a lot of their walls are only 80 inches and are too short for Coleman frames. I offered to sew on a 6 inch strip of fabric to the inside of the screen wall all around to & divide into pockets for storage of small items but more to add water bottles or weighted items to help hold it down to ground & in place. I was told not to bother. I may do it because really I bought it for someone else to use primarily but it's also mine & I can see where it might be helpful. I got that hint from an EZ-up sun wall where they have a pocket that helps hold it down against flapping in the wind. True not everyone is going to have an access to a sewing machine so think outside the box and ask a relative or friend that sews or would let you use their machine or help you out with the project. Or better yet call a few church-cummunity-sewing bee groups & or the local fabric shops who often maintain a list of sewers who hire out for work. Tell them this material is not heavy duty & all sewing machines should be fine & cause no harm to sew. Just must be able to handle velcro hook or loop depending. (Buy the velcro for them in advance.) I can add a few more velcro patches around the upper areas on same plane as the already patches to secure it a few more places to make sure there is no gaps where pesty bugs can fly in. (But we found the gaps weren't there if we wrapped it around the poles on the outside verses in the inside so for the Swing Arm canopy we'll need to do that to just one side.) I was going to make a floor but everyone involved in the use of this for their ham radio camp agree it won't be needed and may even prefer not having to mess with one. (If I do make a floor it will be optional to use or not. It will be bucket style with an edged wall of about 5-6 inches all around and of course that wonderful invention of velcro along the bottom of screen material...USE pile/loop on the screen wall unit only and reserve hook on on all other parts including the canvas of the canopy. So nothing would grab or scratch the netting of the screen while stored or otherwise in use.
I didnt' find any feedback if this Wenzel Smartshade fit Colemans so I came back to make sure people know it can. The slight dropped down pole position does not cause much height loss and you really don't notice it at all. Many of the fellas who will be using this in the future are 6 feet tall as is my husband but assure me it's still plenty high. I like that it folds up small & will make a light weight nylon bag to store because the plastic it comes in will not last for years as I expect the screen will with good care & proper storage.
Why a star off? I think the zipper could be better. But will be easy to repair/replace if ever it does fail. I don't grasp the ties half way down along the poles both inside & outside. It's like just string hanging there but if there had been another line next to it you could tie it to the pole inside or outside pole position. We don't like the hook/elastics they provide for corner etc. use. We are not fans of or like the metal hooks on elastics that help attach to the corners and sides while hanging up. There are several designs that might be better. And then there are zero instructions. Not even a picture or cartoon style drawing. Pretty easy to figure out otherwise but something should be included for those who have no experience with this kind of thing. Locate the tabs with metal clips/hooks and the velcro on the wider white end and that IS the TOP to help you get it positioned in the right direction. Loved the fella who said he had it upside down at first:))) I get it!!! You would maybe think the wider white would be down.
1) Fits coleman canopy frames. Regular/LED pretty well but won't match the velcro patches...however if wrapped around the outside of the poles not to inside most gapping will be pulled taught at top.
2) Lower the height of frame to middle selection of holes on all four poles to reach the ground completely.
3) Coleman Swing Wall Canopy will need some modification to the inside poles on swingwall side but can work with some effort.
4) Metal hooks/clips that help hang it to the upper frame doesn't fit well over metal frame but corners you attach to one another around the upper pole by hooking one clip to the other or one to the elastic loop on the other. Maybe you could remove the clips and use a self wrapping strip of velcro inside the elastic loops or ignore the metal hooks and add a self hook velcro wrap 3/4 to 1 inch wide would be ideal and these are not expensive and sold on Amazon in variety of lengths even colors besides black.) I would not place hook velcro however in with the screen for fear it could snag the screen. But a few strips of it would be useful and you could just place in a zip lock baggy and keep it with the screen just not where it could come in contact during storage and remove them as you take them off the frame and as you remove the screen each time.
profile.summary: Fits our Coleman LED & Swing Wall Frames !!

profile.description: Stanley Marianski is the author of eleven books which include topics on meat smoking, pickling and making alcoholic beverages. Stanley actively participates in many forums and conferences related to meat smoking; he is a regular participant of the Wedliny Domowe National Conference in Poland where purveyors of meat products get the opportunity to showcase their goods. His main objective in writing his books which always contain diagrams is to help the reader "understand the sausage making process" and then "create his own recipes." His passion for creating unique sausage blends have been handed down from generations and he looks forward to continue sharing this passion with sons who also co-authored most of his books.
profile.reviewText: Though experienced canners and Kraut makers for going on more than 4 decades we were interested in the airlock hints for small mason jar use. I'd been making kraut in mason jars for over 40 years. Been happy with it but hubby was fighting the technique. The idea of the airlocks will help with his problems. And I picked up four airlocks with attached rubber plugs already set up and good to go. Have both plenty of metal and plastic Ball jar lids both regular/smaller size and the widemouth variety. Husband also intends to make his own items to hold the slaw down when the lid is screwed in place. Thus protecting the top from air decay so to speak. And by the way...it's a great DIY project going airlock. Amazon offers a number of pre-made sets both plastic and metal but all large widemouth lid size and I've always used regular pints and quart jars so the shoulder acts as an aid to keep the slaw down below the air field and prevent problems with that. So at 35-55 and even higher for just a few jar lids...with airlocks pre-attached...hey hey hey make your own. Plus hubby has beer making airlock supplies so we are good to go. By the way to save even more check out beer making suppliers for airlock supplies. Sometimes local stores have the plastic ball lids in both sizes cheaper than mail order but can be cheaper on Amazon. Worth shopping around. The book has a number of good ideas and information. I was going oh Bok Choy only to realize it's considered iffy as it's thin leaf makes for a difficult product to use. Goodluck and happy sour krauting. There are better books and recipes out there but this book covers a lot of basic information I am glad I gave it as a gift to his silly stocking stuffers..the airlocks this year. Also save your mayo jar lids they fit regular mason sized openings well and come in colors besides white too. Great to use in fridge or jelly jars after you open and remove the metal lids that can cause metal scent or corrode in the fridge such as pickles and acid products might.
profile.summary: Slow to arrive but what we hoped for.

profile.description: You'll see improvements in your personal organization with these Mini WorkSaver(R) Insertable Tab Dividers. At 5-1/2" x 8-1/2", the dividers fit perfectly into smaller binders to add a boost of efficiency to your day planner or other small notebook. A durable, reinforced edge and Rip-Proof(TM) tabs resist tearing to provide you with lasting organization. Customize the included tab inserts with your computer, printer and free templates at avery.com. These dividers are big on convenience.
profile.reviewText: Been using these for over 20 years and when need more we buy more and will continue. I started my own family cook book just before getting married over 43 years ago and sometime around 20 years ago hubby decided to behind my back take over my personal recipe book and computer/print it out and do his own idea of divisions. We had already been using these tabs for categories in original hand written. He RUINED IT. The whole purpose and special feel to my original recipe book was lost. I kid you not he has yet to grasp just how far he over stepped here. I recall a story when my parents put in new counters and cabinets in a house they bought and the workers were two elderly gents who had been partners for some 40 plus years. The one had finally made himself a set of all wood cabinets. He had finished them in a natural finish that brought out the beauty of the wood. He was sent off to visit a distant relative by his daughter and while he was gone the daughter entered his home and PAINTED these cabinets white. She thought it was a mass improvement. He came home and was crushed. Daughter never forgave him for being so non accepting of her attempt to improve Dad's life. My husband is this daughter. Gone are the special pages in my late mom's hand of special shared recipes...or friends too no longer here of hand written recipes. All others were written in my own hand and corrections or changes noted. Recently one he had typed up 20 years back...but had a side note for double the recipe as that is how I make it...he went off and re-typed just with the double directions. It literally throws me off balance. He refuses to get it and he also has refused to stop doing this to me. So as sad as it is.... IT IS. And as Dr. Phil would say do you want to be right or do you want to be happy? Actually Dr. Phil I want my cake and to eat it too. MY RECIPE BOOK MY WAY and for the well meaning or not hubby to stay out of it :))) It really is NOT HIS to mess with. He doesn't realize that one of the reasons he's attracted this project and book with his so call improve on my book is based on the preciousness & work & even details as fussy or clarifications even fuzzy as they might be. He came along and listed for example recipes I had labeled Mom now appear as MRS. Carpenter. WHO the H is Mrs. Carpenter...who did not become Mrs. Carpenter until I was married myself as an adult and our family recipes passed down from generations to me were touching and I want them back the way they were. In all their precious and rights and wrongs. When a page may get soiled during cooking I would re-write and replace it. But in my hand and Mrs. Carpenter or Mrs Springer a grandmother who the heck are they? These insertable dividers do what they need to do. But they also create a whole other battle as to what belongs where. I often have to work out now where did the jerk put my Chicken salad recipe? It's not under salad or chicken...oh it's under combination dishes. I did not have combination dishes. I had casserole but the chicken salad would not have been found there..it's a salad. Dr. Phil...I want it both ways. RIGHT and HAPPY !!!! Us women do get tired of compromise.  LOL...maybe even ROFLOL I'm sure you have had similar stories:)))) And yes I see the humor. Thankful for that. This purchase today goes along with a new white notebook that fits this in half page size and is to replace one of his that the vinyl is starting to crack. He may never understand the special or the esthetic preciousness of my original book I do understand his need to be a part of it. Just it would have been nice if he could have understood how important this was to me and at least understood I was fine with his making it to share with others or making his own version...but to destroy and to insult that which was precious to my heart and soul will never be fine.  So why support him? Kill them with kindness is my motto. !!! Complain but do not let them mess with who you really are. I also love a good challenge. My heart and soul are not crushed...annoyed yes...crushed no. :))))
profile.summary: They work well...hold the tabs usually without out slipping out. But why we buy these behind the scene the battle goes on.

profile.description: This versatile egg white substitute is better than real egg whites for making meringues for a tart lemon pie or cookies that won't fall flat and smooth royal icing that dries to a hard, glossy finish.
profile.reviewText:
Ok here's the deal: I have searched high and low for an ideal meringue powder. All have their virtues and some con's too. This one can be too sweet. It contains too much cornstarch and can alter some recipes negatively. SOOOO I searched for how to make my OWN powdered meringue. Here it is and very simple but does have negative virtues of it's own...just not the same as the purchased stuff.
Mix 3/4 cup powdered sugar with 1/4 cup of powdered egg whites. Add slight 1/2 teaspoon of creme of tartar and 1/2 teaspoon of cornstarch.
Sift all four times going back and forth between two glass or metal mixing bowls. Store in air tight jar in fridge for up to 1-2 weeks and resift to use. Also can extend time in fridge by adding a new dessicant packet or ceramic dessicant round. But it only extends it about double. This should make a full 9 inch meringue pie.
OK this is not an egg substitute. Note it contains EGG for those allergic as do all other commercial made meringue powders too.
Con's. Has lots of sugar more than a regular meringue does made with fresh eggs. So could like Wilton's Powder push the sugar over the top.
Does not have much perservatives once made and thus has pretty short shelf life even in the fridge. Maybe would do better in the freezer but might clump have not tried that.
It would work well in some of the cookie frosting recipes that call for meringue powder but hey why make all of  this up when you can just add some powdered egg. Which is where I'm heading right now to experiment with. Also as a child into my early adult years I always made plain old cookie frosting with approx 3-4 teaspoons of milk per pound or 4 cups of powdered sugar and some flavoring like almond or peppermint or vanilly depending for some of the milk. Mixed with fork and thinned if need be with more milk or thickened with more sugar. Sometimes if I wanted a richer creamer frosting on my cookies I added up to a tablespoon of real softened butter. No fancy eggwhites or egg powder or meringue powder to make it more into a royal frosting. But over the years I found myself making thie egg white frosting and not sure why I drifted into that. Bottom line I think nothings wrong with using it but Wiltion's is too sweet for many recipes. And I think they need to change the wording that it is not an egg substitute because it contains eggs. Also folks remember it is a meringue powder associated with making pie and meringue pastries. Some folks are expecting something else. Also for those who used to buy smaller batches of H & H powdered meringue the CK I hear is the same product also sold here on Amazon but starts at around 20 a pound. Todays price anyway. If you try this for it's purpose it's made and like the results then by all means write a review for Wiltion's. But keep in mind these Meringue Powders vary in the ratio and ingredient contents quite a bit. Some like the recipe above to make your own start with sugar. Others start with egg white like CK and others start with cornstarch like Wiltons. SO hard to determine as a cook what a product is going to shift your recipe when you don't know the actual ratio. If used in a mouse for example this one might add too much cornstarch or thicken it too much. There is virtue in meringue powders but it's hard to pin them down to just one brand and also has a lot to do with your intended use and recipe. However in my conclusion of continued use and only use of these powders as an additive to cookie frostings or royal frosting sub's I can't justify the cost any longer and worse they just don't keep as long as I would need in the pantry and fridge space is limited when it comes to a year long can sitting in there even to the back. From now on I plan to just add a pinch of powdered egg white if I think it will enhance the frosting otherwise I make a mean four egg lemon meringue pie that's way to beautiful not to continue to use the real egg whites left over from the pie filling as the meringue and a whole lot less sugar too and no problem storing anything else. I suggest some of you with time and or resources try to make your own version of less sweetened meringue powder for recipes that you don't want the added sugar. Otherwise experiment with just the use of eggwhite powder with or without cornstartch and creme of tartar going easy on the last two ingredients. So bottom line to date is Wiltion Meringue Powder is about the only one I can find 100 miles from our rural home. None is carried in our town any longer but it was Wilton's. And CK is probably the best and the others all have merit but all pretty much for frosting additives only. As far as meringues themselves go it's iffy. Also google on line for recipes that use your brand specific powder of choice. I find this very helpful and helps figure out ways I might apply the powder to use it up faster too when needed.
profile.summary: This is not an EGG replacer for those who fall for the egg substitute wording. Wilton has it's virtues though.

profile.description: Make your favorite fresh ravioli tonight. Easy to use and simply attaches to the hub of your stand mixer. Recommended for use with the KitchenAid Pasta Roller attachment (KPSA, sold separately).
profile.reviewText: Beats the hand crank version but lazy on this end getting the mixer out to attach it to. So not it's fault at all. Didn't get the other attachments that make ravoli. Just wanted to make simple noodles period and even then sheets of noodles is fine as I can cut my own. Hint for newbies to making your own noodles. For years I've just taken the noodles and piled each long noodle onto itself sort of making a nest out of it placed on a clean cotton dish towel or wax paper and let them air dry. Then pick these nests of noodles up and store in air tight jars or canisters. Works and keeps well for me but we live in more dry climate in Montana. Didn't make noodles in IA when we lived their in part because of the humidity. You can do as many recommend and store in freezer but we always have to many other needs for freezer space when they keep just fine in a gallon jar or even heavy duty plastic zip bag. Oh jar works better as once they are dry they tend to want to break up easy. Freezing while still pliable helps prevent breakage. We don't mind either way with some breakage. We also make noodles to enjoy fresh more often than not too. Think outside the box and use your noodle often:)))
profile.summary: Works as long as you aren't lazy!

profile.description: We love our cats, but when they stop using the litter box and have messes it's time for serious action. No product works faster to get cats back to using the litter box and remove messes from urine, vomit, hair balls, feces, marking scents and cat spray. You do not wipe this product up after applying. Let it air dry. Do-Not add more liquid before five to seven days after initial application. Adding more Dumb Cat liquid before this period will stop the product from working. Dumb Cat is the most effective cat urine remover available. Retrain cats to use litterbox while using Dumb Cat. Cover treated area to prevent cats from returning until issues are removed. Do not allow cats to roam free until their scent confusion or behavior issues are corrected.
profile.reviewText: I've used this for over 10 years. Off and on though. Depends on if we have marking issues or not. For the past 3 and half years we haven't had a problem. But for some reason a cat we've had this winter is his fourth has decided to mark. I'm not always convinced it's something we humans can control in the animal world of thinking. Us against them isn't always the answer we just do the best we can and try to figure out the best approach. For a Psycho kitty our vet nicknamed years before this product helped a lot. I used a lot of products to clean up carpets and floor problems and not so much this one as described. What I found and still find is I spray the litter box area ours is a huge deep box set into a closet floor that's ceramic tiled and slightly a step up. Anyway the walls are lined in full wood panels and not always does an extra litter box solve this problem in multi cat houses. The kitty with the problem now has never gotten along with one other cat. That cat has worn a pheremone collar for the past 3 years and helped resolve the hostility issues from the other guy. The bad kitty doesn't accept the collar himself so the targeted kitty instead wears it and it works very well until now. So the little bully cat goes about sniffing where ever the other cat has laid even and often takes over a spot that the other kitty had been sleeping. So that is where Dumb Cat comes in as an anti-marking spray. I use it to mask all these kit's smells. I spray the ottoman and their kitty mats or pads they like to sleep on we keep all about the house in living room areas as well as on beds with this spray once a week. Maybe twice. And once before going to bed at night I spray the litter box area around all the walls that's pretty much right up against the box as well as lightly across the litter itself. We used clumping liter so we don't want to saturate the litter. Just target the sides of the box well and lightly mist the top of the liter itself. As well as mist the sides of the wood walls. For some reason that helps a lot. I also put some on a microcleaning small rag and wipe down some of the areas the cats rub their cheeks on that scent those corners and legs of furniture as their's. And this I hope cuts down on the pheremones these little guys have been spreading about making war with each other. The funny but not so funny in our house is the BIG Maincoon kitty is being bullied by the little much smaller nermal character. Big Kitty tries is hardest to avoid little kitty. While another bigger yet fellow gets along with both cats just fine. Well until the marking started up...I'd noticed for a couple of weeks the little bully had been jealous of any attention shared with the middle kit....and that was unusual. So out comes the Dumb Cat. I don't pretend to understand all cats behavior when it comes to marking. Psycho kitty was a beautiful cat but showed signs of problems before her eyes were open as a kitten. And the real problems happend when she didn't like an across country move. That summer she growled and ran down the halls or up the stairs refusing any kind of attempts to calm her and give her love. She didn't want any. She was mad at us. She shredded a brandnew set of sheets on a new king mattress set and lucky only shred the sheets not the mattress. That in itself is a type of marking and anger. Over the years she adjusted to the new home and loved the fenced back yard but we'd go around and around with the marking. That's when I discovered Dumb Kitty..which is what I call it...and it works with the cats. I find a product by Bissel works far better as an enzyme active product in removing or helping to remove really bad situations where say a cat's pee has run into floor boards on a hardwood floor or along the edges or under a counter in a kitchen or floor boards. In some cases you can remove the kick boards or side boards and refinish and or clean behind those. But sometimes you can't get to those areas that the pee may have run or absorbed into or under. I pour the Bissel product directly into the same spot the cat has done damage of course having cleaned the surface area well. I repeat this sometimes as many as a dozen times over that many weeks or more. One area of floor that was refinished even still starts to smell in the spring when the front of the house heats up due to sunshine. And I get out the Bissel and pour it right into and over that area again. A Vet friend had problems from a past kit peeing into his furnace registers and couldn't seem to get out all the scent. I suggested he try pouring the Bissel and then spraying alternately a week or two aparth with the Dumb Cat down into the duct work. And he said it was a success. Anyway we love our kits and these products work or not. It seems not all products work the same for everyone. We all have individual expectations and vary in our needs too or situations. Which is why I carried on about how we use this product. Another product I use is an enzyme active one also that you pour heated up in your microwave directly onto carpets. Then you saturate that carpet with the hot product and use a few utility towels to soak up the product after it sets for a few minutes. This helps with carpet that you can't afford to replace. But in all cases I've had to re-apply sometimes going on several years later again going through the same steps. Actually there are two products I use on carpets first is for stains: Folex Instant Carpet Stain Remover but it can lighten the fabric so some care is needed with it. The other described above is called of all things : Get Serious. All three of these other items are sold here on Amazon. The Bissel pet odor additive or concentrate as a 2X product that's been renamed since I started buying it but I use it undiluted. And these other two all sold here on Amazon. All pretty decent prices compared to stores. For us stores are 90 to 200 miles trips one way to the metro shopping areas. Up here we are in a remote low populated area so Amazon is a big help to us. There are lots of products out there. Some we've found are quite good too but these four are our return to basics with our feline pets. Good luck to all of you...you need it if you're looking on this page at this item. I know!!!!
profile.summary: Works for marking problems. But I use it off label for better results.

profile.reviewText:
Love this brand but really a pack of 20 with 8 dollar shipping? Google for this product or other brands which are as good if not better...yes there is better and there are other thicknesses too. So don't be a slave to higher costs of shipping here today. Sometimes Amazon changes vendors and so the prices of products and shipping cost or not changes out too.

With this over priced shipping you could pick and choose a better product for not more. But google laminate pouches to find other brands and so many more products and sizes and as good a quality or even better some times. Think outside the box....color outside the lines:)))

profile.reviewText:
These are novelty Erasers and they fit standard sized pencils just fine. Firm enough to stay on and do the right thing. The questions about is it a fun toy and educational value and durablity is kinda off the mark here. It's an eraser first and for my purpose it helps prevent pencils from falling off the desks of kids when their pencils are round not angled with flat sides to prevent that. aged kids.
profile.summary: Not really a TOY perse so odd questions.

profile.description: HP Everyday Photo Paper, Glossy
profile.reviewText: I'm giving it the same rating I gave the 50 size packages of the same paper. BUT NOT HAPPY CAMPER with finding out I ordered both the 50 and the 25 size packages of the SAME EXACT PAPER. Only I paid approx 20.00 dollars per two 50 packs and 20.00 for three 25 packs thus making the 75 sheets 25% more expensive. You could not tell from the descriptions given that these were the same paper but they came and it was clear they were. So that's shameful on the sellers or HP perhaps for not making it clear these are basically the same paper only in different size boxes by number of sheets contained. As far as the rating for the paper goes. It does a great photo quality on both my old HP printer now 12 years old and my new EPSON R2000 printer almost a year old. So that's fine. What I do not like is the ghosted printing on the nonglossy photo side. I bought this paper to save weight and thickness in layering different medias together...and when I can't print text on the flip side that sort of undoes what the whole idea of thinner paper is about. So I like it and I probably will use it again but will also look for other paper that competes and does not have a ghost print on the flip side...preventing it's use when needed or wanted by the consumer that's me. So it lost a star and then some over that. I hope HP is listening but really most of us do not need help with this paper anyway figuring out which is the photo side. I didn't and rarely have ever. SO STOP DOING THAT...or offer us a choice and I bet you soon find that most consumers or customers prefer the advantage to using the flip side too. It's thinner and unfortunately my design of a 6 panel card this year did not prevent me from having to add that exttra 20 cents onto the cards for postage. I had hoped as last year I used thicker and heavier paper for an 8 panel card and still it was only 20 cents more too. At least it wasn't more:)))) But I suspect I would have saved the 20 cents extra charge had I not been forced to glue on 4 extra sheets for the flip side of the cards for my printing and text materials. It certainly undid the whole reason to go with lighter weight photo paper this project.
profile.summary: Get rid of the Ghosting on flip side of paper. Prevents printing any text.

profile.description: 10 ft Offset Patio Umbrella

profile.reviewText:
Have an old almost all wood interior house. We were struggling with an over sized plant or two that are hung and wanted to move it to another window too. So went in search for a longer bracket and this does the trick. However we hang the plants outside in summer and so would be nice to be able to  swing the bracket to the side or even like we do other brackets we have swing them to one side or the other as slight adjustments to where you want it to hang in front of or to the side of the window.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "An exciting twist on the adventure RPG genre build your skills and amass loads of cuddly monsters to become the ultimate Plushkins Master". The summary of the review text is "Sailor Moon meets Pokemon".
output:
Take a clueless magical girl, throw her into a world populated by critters that kinda resemble Pokemon, then add a few staples like dungeon crawling, and you might end up with Moco Moco Friends.

The basic gameplay is pretty simple. Go explore dungeons, fighting and collecting Plushkins. The dungeon part of the game reminds me somewhat of Rogue, but at a very basic level. The overworld consists of a shop which I've yet to use. There's a garden to grow materials you'll need for various upgrades. The sewing shop turns those raw materials into necessary components, and you'll use those in a third building to train, evolve, etc, your Plushkins. The towns "people" will sometimes give you quests, and over the course of the game, you'll unlock other NPCs.

As simple as it is, I find it charmingly addictive. I'm up to chapter 20 now, and I think I'm getting close to the end. The difficulty slowly ramps up once you get into the higher teen chapters. There are a few things which I could point out, but they don't reduce my score. Mainly the repetition and tedium of doing the same thing again and again. Go into a dungeon, which so far, typically consists of no more than 6 rooms and I've yet to see anything bigger than three floors. Fight some Plushkins on your way down to the boss, and collect materials Once you beat the boss, you're taken back to the overworld, where you'll repeat the process. Some dungeons are story-based and some are special timed dungeons that give bonuses to material collection or experience.

The game keeps the original Japanese voice acting but there is English text and there are a few funny anime-style references thrown in. Some of the interactions are genuinely funny. One of my favorite reactions is Moco's face when her Plushkins are hit in battle. The Plushkins don't die. They're just stuffed animals and you kinda beat the stuffing out of them during the battle (yes, you can actually see the stuffing popping out as they take damage). When the Plushkin faints, you might have a chance to befriend them once the battle is done.

Given the nature of the game, it makes me wonder why the original publisher didn't team up with some plushie manufacturer to create some unique tie-ins.

profile.description: Harvest Moon: The Lost Valley - Nintendo 3DS
profile.reviewText:
Since the game came out less than 24 hours as of my review, it's hard to make an in-depth review. But since I see non-helpful reviews lashing against this game because "it's not the real Harvest Moon", I thought I would share my experiences based on my current 6 hours of play-time. I'm quite aware that this is a Natsume-developed game and this might be considered a variant of Harvest Moon rather than a main series game.

Those who decry it as a "Minecraft meets Harvest Moon" probably have not played either this game or Minecraft. The blocky terrain is the only similarity to Minecraft. The concept of the terrain is interesting, and it gives you a broader style of gameplay. The terrain shape also seems to have implications in how your crops grow.

Unlike the most recent Harvest Moon, A New Beginning, there is very little hand-holding. You spend about 30 minutes with the first harvest sprite who teaches you basic terrain and crop management. After this, the sprite gives you a fairly easy first quest, then you're kinda on your own. Explore, plant, and do the normal things. I don't know what triggers some events, but there seem to be some events that are triggered based on what/how much you've planted so far.

Terrain management takes a bit getting used to. You trigger management mode by pressing Y, and then using A/B/X/Y to dig, raise, etc. Once you trigger terrain management, your screen is highlighted with a 3x3 selection, but only the differently colored selection is the one you operate on. You'll find yourself moving around quite a bit, either to position your selection marker, or to move terrain blocking your view. You can press the L and R shoulder buttons to rotate the camera, and press L+R simultaneously to place the camera directly behind you.

Tool selection is somewhat context-sensitive. After you've used terrain mode to prepare the field, you press A to choose an operation. Facing a prepared section of field, that will allow you to plant seeds. Approaching trees will let you chop them down. So it seems like you don't need to manually select your tools any more.

There are plenty of Harvest Moon features, beside the farming. You have stamina which you need to be mindful of, but you get lots of it. I've not been at risk of fainting yet. Time passes rather fast, about 1 real second is 1 in-game minute. I'm suspecting that as the game progresses, you'll need to make standard Harvest Moon types of time-management decisions. I've only met a few NPCs so far, but they kinda plant themselves in my yard, rather than a town proper like HM:ANB. Since I've not yet woke up the Harvest Goddess, which is a key plot element to unlocking the rest of the seasons, I'm hoping that a real town will eventually open. There are stairs to the left of your house, but they're blocked off and only NPCs can use them.

The 3D in the title is a bit of a misnomer. Most (if not all?) of the game is in 2D mode (you can tell because the 3D status light is off), so I suspect the 3D part of it is rather from the view of the character, which is something isometric view: that is, the camera floats behind the character, and as you walk around the world, the camera can (and will, of it's own) rotate to view different perspectives.

The camera... This is why the game gets 3-stars. It moves on it's own. You'll be walking in your field, and it'll rotate around. It doesn't appear that you can modify the camera behavior, and hopefully this is something I can learn to deal with. Natsume used a similar technique in their recent game Hometown Story, and altho it is not as disruptive, it is still somewhat unnecessary.

I've been anticipating this game for a few months now, and will definitely be playing it more. I'm not 100% certain I am enamored with the game, as I've yet to hit that "sweet spot" which tells me "Keep playing!".
profile.summary: Harvest Moon: The Lost Valley

profile.description: Lord of Magna: Maiden Heaven is a brand new strategy RPG adventure set on a colorful island in the tropics. Bestowed with a mysterious bracelet called the Lachryma, Luchs is fated to trade in his days of peaceful inn keeping for chaotic combat as he reunites seven compelling heroines and pieces together their mysterious pasts. The unique strategy battle system encourages players to line up their attacks in order to bowl over the frontline enemies into others, causing collateral damage.
profile.reviewText:
Since I've seen this asked various places, this is not a Rune Factory game, and it's not even a "spiritual successor". It's a strategy RPG with a bit of harem. I guess the best comparison would be with something like Fire Emblem Awakening.

The game is heavily story driven, and that makes it a slow game. There's tons and tons of dialogues you have to work thru. I vary between just wanting to get on with the game to forcing myself to slow down and read the story. This slow pace is the only reason I give 4 stars instead of 5. I'd actually give 4.5, but since we can't half-star things....

It's also a very linear game. It's not an open-world game where you can go off to explore as you wish. You'll be taken from main event to main event, but there are side-quests to help break the pace. The side quests also take place in fixed locations and seem to be unlocked based on previous events. If you want some mats for crafting or maybe a bit of grinding, I guess the side-quests would be it.

The artwork and music are very nice. There are options within the game to view various heart events and still images of key points. The copy I got has the OST; not sure if there are different editions or if all will come with the OST, but since the music is good, I'd make sure of that if you like to collect those kind of things. The art is kind of mixed what you see in the world-view (chibi style characters) versus when character portraits pop up during dialogue, which are in standard anime styles.

Combat is turn-based but took a bit getting used to, mostly just because it's a different style than I'm normally used to. Not so much the turn-based system, but the AOE (area of effect) style attacks. All your attacks are a type of AOE and you get bonuses based on how many enemies you can knock out in one turn. Even if you have a single enemy targetted, if you knock it back into a group of enemies, it may take out additional units, which also add up. Displays and controls help you aim attacks to get the most hits.

The game throws huge numbers of enemies at you, usually in groups that consist of trash mobs with seemingly one HP and a "generator" that will repeatedly respawn its entourage, so take them out first. There are other bosses and mini-bosses, and they'll vary. I felt emotionally overwhelmed during one particular event due to the number of enemies. Even ended up losing my entire party but I was able to restart without any seeming consequence.

There is a StreetPass function, but since I've had the game less than 24 hours (and have about 6 hours played so far), I haven't really ran into anyone yet. Seems to be mostly some kind of farm where you can harvest stuff.

Other than these things, I don't want to write a huge review. The game has the typical RPG elements, such as upgrading skills and the like. There seems to be multiple endings which you can unlock depending on your relationships with the other girls, but like any other harem, you don't really "marry" or "date" one of them (at least not that I've seen so far). I'm enjoying the game so far, and it's been the first game to be able to rip me away from SoS since SoS was released...
profile.summary: I guess the best comparison would be with something like Fire Emblem Awakening

profile.description: Welcome to the greatest farming simulation ever made! Farming Simulator invites you into the demanding world of a modern day farmer with BRAND NEW content and vehicles. Take on all the challenges of farming life. Breed animals, harvest and sell crops, and advance in your career as you manage your own farm in a huge open world! A brand new American farming environment in addition to the pre-existing European farm Loads of challenges representative of a true farmer's life New animals to breed and crops to grow Large tractors and farming machines faithfully modeled after true farming brands such as Case IH, Deutz-Fahr, Lamborghini, Same, and Horsh The ability to create your dream farm in an open world full of possibilities
profile.reviewText:
I've never played a game in this franchise, but it appears there are several versions for various platforms. The 2014 version seems to be a stripped down version of 2013 adapted for mobile devices (3DS, PS Vita, iOS, Android). This review is for the 3DS version. The closest comparison would be the PS Vita version. The Android version may be cheaper, but contains the dreaded "in-app purchasing".

This is a farming simulation, and that's pretty much what it is. You plant seeds and grow three basic crops. This is not a social game like Harvest Moon. This is a good game if you just want to drive tractors and manage how to most efficiently tend and sell your crops. When I say "tend", that's usually a matter of trying to schedule everything so you don't have any idle machinery. Once you plant and fertilize, you just play the waiting game.

It's a fairly fun game with little depth. You can set it down and pick it up at will, watch TV or do other stuff while waiting for harvest time. As a sim, there's no ultimate goal, altho there are trophies for various deeds, things like how many hectares you've harvested. There are easy to finish timed missions, usually in the form of "find the lost something".

There are a few things in the 3DS version which could be better addressed:

It could use information on the types of equipment available. You're presented with the name of the equipment (Krone Big-X) but no idea what it's for. Have a device nearby with internet access so you can search the wiki's, which is almost mandatory.

Hiring workers is nice, and allows you to move on to other tasks, but you do need to keep an eye on them. They'll get stuck on fences or rocks. When you want to sell a harvest, you have the manually drive to the point of interest. And let's not even talk about how hard it is to backup a tractor! Seems like it all these should be a matter of course to adapt the AI for these things.

Cars are eye-candy and serve no purpose. Roads, too. You just drive the shortest route and traffic be damned. I like to park my tractors in the road to create massive road jams, which seem to periodically clear up automatically. You can bump into cars and force them off the road. Sometimes it's fun to play a bit of Mad Max with the cars, but they'll eventually get back on track. Maybe an option to disable traffic would be helpful.

There is no multiplayer, StreetPass or SpotPass, but there is a Miiverse community. But in all seriousness, I'm not sure what they could present for those types of scenarios anyways.
profile.summary: Farming Simulator 2014 for 3DS

profile.description: Christian Cantrell is a science fiction writer and software developer living in Northern Virginia.
profile.reviewText:
Good hard science fiction is when the author invents plausible technology without resorting to "magic". The author does a good job with this, but it could really use a wee bit less technical detail.

The protagonist wakes up from an operation with a "what just happened?", and in the first half of the book, the author alternates chapters of prior events (what leads up to the operation) to the present (what happens after the operation). profile.description: Create your own worlds staged in the medieval fantasy world of Dungeons and Dragons. Gold Edition contains "Neverwinter Nights" and "Neverwinter Nights: Shadows of Undrentide Expansion Pack". Can be played online with up to 64 friends.
profile.reviewText:
I like this game a lot. Forgive the length of this review - this is a long game, which has a lot of elements.

For starters, the sounds are excellent. The voice-overs are a little goofy; I get a little tired of Tomi's "hokey-dokie!", but the sound effects are very nice. The music is simply outstanding, and very well written. I especially like the musical trigger, which changes the soundtrack when you are going into battle.

Visuals are outstanding as well. There should be enough eye-candy to satisfy most critics (weather effects, shadows, and a wide range of item art).

Game control is generally straight-forward. There is a tutorial which walks you thru the basic game mechanics. But really, most RPGs have the same generic features - character development, inventory management, maps and notebooks, and so on. It's not too hard to figure out to press "i" to bring up your inventory screen, or to click on an NPC to talk to them.

Camera control is a bit tricky. There are three modes - chase, top down and driving mode. The game defaults to chase mode, which automatically rotates the screen. I found myself getting a little queazy, as the screen would rotate, so changed it to top down mode. All that means is that I have to spin the screen manually.

You might need to spend some time in screen rotation and zooming, due to the way the game sometimes puts plot items right underneath another object. I often end up clicking on an avatar and getting a dialogue box, rather than examining the item I want.

As a small side note, there are WAY too many crates/barrels/boxes in the game, in places you don't expect to see them. A lot of them are locked, and a lot of those are trapped. It gets to be tedious, because you really want to search all the areas, in case there is a signficant plot item.

The campaign is pretty big. It's divided into four "chapters", but they're fairly longish. I've finished the OC (official, or original campaign) and the SoU expansion pack. I really don't know how long it took me to finish. I found the SoU expansion to be a little more fun in some areas, even tho it was a lot shorter. The SoU adds visual effects to plot items, and henchie inventory control, among other things.

It is kind of linear in play, and personally, I like that. In most non-linear games, I have a tendency to dawdle around or simply get lost without knowing what to do. The main storyline is fairly straight forward, but there are still a lot of side-quests you can tackle along the way, if you get bored of the story.

Others have said the game is too much hack-n-slash, but I like that. In all my RPGing, I always select the generic fighter type.  So in this game, I chose a half-orc barbarian. I don't choose my character types based on lazyness. I know a lot of people would say choosing the big dumb brute is the easy way. But when you think about it, if you have to wade into five or six mobs with just your brute force, taking direct blows, it's just another style of strategy, which is the style I've been playing since the old C-64 Bards Tale games.

In any event, there are a huge number of items to find in the game - weapons, armor, magic items. Gold abounds. I was a little worried at the start of the game, trying to hire a henchman for 250gp, when all I had was 50gp in my pocket. But as soon as I started adventuring, that turned into a non-issue. The game-world is big enough that it does take a bit of time moving around from place to place.

I haven't played online yet, and am franky probably not going to even try. My online gaming experience was spoiled years ago thanks to Diablo, Battle. Net and wide-spread cheating. I know these newer games have methods to control stuff, but honestly, quite a lot of people I meet online are just plain jerks. I guess anonyminity tends to make people less polite to strangers which they'll never meet personally.
profile.summary: hack-n-slash maybe, but still great fun!

profile.description: Shows some signs of wear, and may have some markings on the inside. 100% Money Back Guarantee.
profile.reviewText:
I've been re-reading this book for at least 15 years. My copy is well dog-eared and the spine is cracked. Each time I read it, I read it from cover to cover, and it captures me each time. I can't even number how many times I've read this.

I personally have no problem with the enormous amount of personal or geological names presented here, altho it did take me at least two false starts to finally read this. I've read the Bible from front to back many times, also, and if you can keep up with that pace, the Silmarillion won't hold any special challenge.

With the spate of interest in JRR Tolkien, especially regarding the movies, I figure a lot of people may pick this up and hope to find more about hobbits and Gandalf. I think those casual readers may be disillusioned.

But I hope that even those who are casually intereted in the Hobbits will find press on and read this book in it's entirety, and learn what sheer brilliance lays beyond Peter Jackson's cimematic interpetation.

This is an entire mythos of creation, mainly as seen from the Elves perspective, from the beginning of the world to the end of the War of the Rings.

I could go on and on, about the lingustical matters, and the author's denial of allegory, but other reviews and other books will talk about those...

It's just as important to note that this was edited by his son, after his death, and a question often occurs to me - which is pure JRRT and which is CJRT? CJRT was working with a huge amount of materials and did the best he could with what he had. If you'd like to see the real-life cronological creation, the "History of Middle-earth" volumes are a good place to start. But you still need to read this book first, as the HoME series are the (unedited) versions of the "final" stories in the Sil...
profile.summary: Read it, and re-read it, and read it again

profile.description: One Full Face Shield. This Face Shield meet all ANSI regulations. Meets ANSI Type 1 z89.1-1989. Front and back adjustable headgear with soft lined front strap for comfort, Shield covers 100 percent of face and neck area, Clear Shield provides un obstructed field of vision, Shield is constructed of super tough lightweight polycarbonate
profile.reviewText:
As an electronics hobbyist, solder splashes are a real and dangerous concern. I wear prescription glasses, and have yet to find a pair of safety glasses which I can wear comfortably over my glasses. But even more so, I recently had a slash which struck my chin, so even if I was wearing safety glasses, they would not have helped.

Hence, a full face shield. For the price of this, you really can't beat it. If you are a professional, or otherwise need to wear a face shield during a full working shift, this is probably not the product for you. For an hour or so, during a project, this is a great thing to have.

While I can find no real complaints, a few nitpicks come to mind, but not enough to reduce my rating.

Apparently my head is smaller than most people's, so even at the smallest and tightest straps settings, it's marginally loose. I might try to pad it with an old sock or something.

As shipped, it was simply placed into a box with no shipping material. Be VERY careful when you open the box, do NOT use a knife or other box cutter. The actual shield was directly below the packing tape, and while I tried to be careful, even then I slightly scarred the shield while opening it. The protective coating ate most of the scarring, and what is visible will be in my extreme periphery vision, but even so.

There is protective coating on both sides, one side being tinted, so make sure you peel both off before use. The shield is detachable, which implies it could be replaced, but I don't know if there does exist a replacement.

Even given these, for $10, for the added safety, 5 stars is right.
profile.summary: Can't beat for the price

profile.description: Prepare yourself for some Irken yuletide goodness as Zim concludes its triumphant DVD release. Featuring the highly sought after "unaired" season two episodes, ZIM fans will finally get what they've been waiting for. Watch ZIM eat waffles while a pair of backseat drivers make trouble from beyond the stars. See Mortos steal souls as a Fry cook appears from all that space. Yes boys and girls, there is a Santa... and he's bent on world domination!
profile.reviewText:
For some reason, I tend to hook onto television shows which are just too progressive for the majority of drones out there. Does anyone remember the (original British) Max Headroom in the '80s? After the pilot, they produced about 8 shows, and it was prematurelly cancelled. When they tried to bring it back, it totally lost the edge.

So the same thing with Zim. But at least Zim was just cancelled before Nick tried to sugar it up. I still find it amazing that Nick even aired the show. These are the kind of cartoons to which none other can stand against.

From the commentary, the people involved give the impression that a lot of the work was half-baked, and I shudder to think what would happen if the producers were give total creative freedom, rather than being dragged down by the masses.

In any event, Zim is a brilliant creation which was deemed unworthy by Nick for further production.

If you've not seen Zim, you need to seriously buy all three of these DVD's and have a blowout weekend just watching them. You'll find yourself a better person.
profile.summary: This has nothing to do with jelly!

profile.description:
A fictional story about rabbits trying to find safety. 
"One fine evening, in the beautiful heart of the English countryside, a group of rabbits emerge from their warren to feed.  But as the sun sinks behind a hill, one of their number - Fiver - has a terrifying vision of the warren's destruction at the hands of man."
profile.reviewText:
This is one of those movies which can stand the test of time, almost 30 years after it was released.

For those of us who saw this movie when it was still considered new, in the late 70's and even into the early 80's, this may bring you some feelings of nostalgia, as you ponder over the possible messages of this movie, and how things have changed since those possibly carefree days.

By today's modern animation standards, the hand-drawn animation in this movie might be considered crude or rough. The style of animation seems to be deliberate, and even seems to bring a little more life to the story.

I'd also say that in today's 'touchy-feely' society, this movie might not be considered appropriate for children under the ages of 10.

If I have a single complaint about this DVD, it's with the sound production. The audio track is extremely poor quality. I had to max the volume, and even ended up turning on sub-titles.
profile.summary: Some movies are ageless

Travel pouch

profile.reviewText:
I purchased these specifically to use on my Kindle Fire, whose built in speakers I find to be too low in volume. I don't like to use headphones, so I was looking for active speakers, something small, if possible. The price is ultimately what caught my attention.

top_5.description: Harvest Moon: The Lost Valley - Nintendo 3DS
top_5.reviewText:
Since the game came out less than 24 hours as of my review, it's hard to make an in-depth review. But since I see non-helpful reviews lashing against this game because "it's not the real Harvest Moon", I thought I would share my experiences based on my current 6 hours of play-time. I'm quite aware that this is a Natsume-developed game and this might be considered a variant of Harvest Moon rather than a main series game.

Those who decry it as a "Minecraft meets Harvest Moon" probably have not played either this game or Minecraft. The blocky terrain is the only similarity to Minecraft. The concept of the terrain is interesting, and it gives you a broader style of gameplay. The terrain shape also seems to have implications in how your crops grow.

Unlike the most recent Harvest Moon, A New Beginning, there is very little hand-holding. You spend about 30 minutes with the first harvest sprite who teaches you basic terrain and crop management. After this, the sprite gives you a fairly easy first quest, then you're kinda on your own. Explore, plant, and do the normal things. I don't know what triggers some events, but there seem to be some events that are triggered based on what/how much you've planted so far.

Terrain management takes a bit getting used to. You trigger management mode by pressing Y, and then using A/B/X/Y to dig, raise, etc. Once you trigger terrain management, your screen is highlighted with a 3x3 selection, but only the differently colored selection is the one you operate on. You'll find yourself moving around quite a bit, either to position your selection marker, or to move terrain blocking your view. You can press the L and R shoulder buttons to rotate the camera, and press L+R simultaneously to place the camera directly behind you.

Tool selection is somewhat context-sensitive. After you've used terrain mode to prepare the field, you press A to choose an operation. Facing a prepared section of field, that will allow you to plant seeds. Approaching trees will let you chop them down. So it seems like you don't need to manually select your tools any more.

There are plenty of Harvest Moon features, beside the farming. You have stamina which you need to be mindful of, but you get lots of it. I've not been at risk of fainting yet. Time passes rather fast, about 1 real second is 1 in-game minute. I'm suspecting that as the game progresses, you'll need to make standard Harvest Moon types of time-management decisions. I've only met a few NPCs so far, but they kinda plant themselves in my yard, rather than a town proper like HM:ANB. Since I've not yet woke up the Harvest Goddess, which is a key plot element to unlocking the rest of the seasons, I'm hoping that a real town will eventually open. There are stairs to the left of your house, but they're blocked off and only NPCs can use them.

The 3D in the title is a bit of a misnomer. Most (if not all?) of the game is in 2D mode (you can tell because the 3D status light is off), so I suspect the 3D part of it is rather from the view of the character, which is something isometric view: that is, the camera floats behind the character, and as you walk around the world, the camera can (and will, of it's own) rotate to view different perspectives.

The camera... This is why the game gets 3-stars. It moves on it's own. You'll be walking in your field, and it'll rotate around. It doesn't appear that you can modify the camera behavior, and hopefully this is something I can learn to deal with. Natsume used a similar technique in their recent game Hometown Story, and altho it is not as disruptive, it is still somewhat unnecessary.

I've been anticipating this game for a few months now, and will definitely be playing it more. I'm not 100% certain I am enamored with the game, as I've yet to hit that "sweet spot" which tells me "Keep playing!".
top_5.summary: Harvest Moon: The Lost Valley

top_5.description: Lord of Magna: Maiden Heaven is a brand new strategy RPG adventure set on a colorful island in the tropics. Bestowed with a mysterious bracelet called the Lachryma, Luchs is fated to trade in his days of peaceful inn keeping for chaotic combat as he reunites seven compelling heroines and pieces together their mysterious pasts. The unique strategy battle system encourages players to line up their attacks in order to bowl over the frontline enemies into others, causing collateral damage.
top_5.reviewText:
Since I've seen this asked various places, this is not a Rune Factory game, and it's not even a "spiritual successor". It's a strategy RPG with a bit of harem. I guess the best comparison would be with something like Fire Emblem Awakening.

The game is heavily story driven, and that makes it a slow game. There's tons and tons of dialogues you have to work thru. I vary between just wanting to get on with the game to forcing myself to slow down and read the story. This slow pace is the only reason I give 4 stars instead of 5. I'd actually give 4.5, but since we can't half-star things....

It's also a very linear game. It's not an open-world game where you can go off to explore as you wish. You'll be taken from main event to main event, but there are side-quests to help break the pace. The side quests also take place in fixed locations and seem to be unlocked based on previous events. If you want some mats for crafting or maybe a bit of grinding, I guess the side-quests would be it.

The artwork and music are very nice. There are options within the game to view various heart events and still images of key points. The copy I got has the OST; not sure if there are different editions or if all will come with the OST, but since the music is good, I'd make sure of that if you like to collect those kind of things. The art is kind of mixed what you see in the world-view (chibi style characters) versus when character portraits pop up during dialogue, which are in standard anime styles.

Combat is turn-based but took a bit getting used to, mostly just because it's a different style than I'm normally used to. Not so much the turn-based system, but the AOE (area of effect) style attacks. All your attacks are a type of AOE and you get bonuses based on how many enemies you can knock out in one turn. Even if you have a single enemy targetted, if you knock it back into a group of enemies, it may take out additional units, which also add up. Displays and controls help you aim attacks to get the most hits.

The game throws huge numbers of enemies at you, usually in groups that consist of trash mobs with seemingly one HP and a "generator" that will repeatedly respawn its entourage, so take them out first. There are other bosses and mini-bosses, and they'll vary. I felt emotionally overwhelmed during one particular event due to the number of enemies. Even ended up losing my entire party but I was able to restart without any seeming consequence.

There is a StreetPass function, but since I've had the game less than 24 hours (and have about 6 hours played so far), I haven't really ran into anyone yet. Seems to be mostly some kind of farm where you can harvest stuff.

Other than these things, I don't want to write a huge review. The game has the typical RPG elements, such as upgrading skills and the like. There seems to be multiple endings which you can unlock depending on your relationships with the other girls, but like any other harem, you don't really "marry" or "date" one of them (at least not that I've seen so far). I'm enjoying the game so far, and it's been the first game to be able to rip me away from SoS since SoS was released...
top_5.summary: I guess the best comparison would be with something like Fire Emblem Awakening

top_5.description: Welcome to the greatest farming simulation ever made! Farming Simulator invites you into the demanding world of a modern day farmer with BRAND NEW content and vehicles. Take on all the challenges of farming life. Breed animals, harvest and sell crops, and advance in your career as you manage your own farm in a huge open world! A brand new American farming environment in addition to the pre-existing European farm Loads of challenges representative of a true farmer's life New animals to breed and crops to grow Large tractors and farming machines faithfully modeled after true farming brands such as Case IH, Deutz-Fahr, Lamborghini, Same, and Horsh The ability to create your dream farm in an open world full of possibilities
top_5.reviewText:
I've never played a game in this franchise, but it appears there are several versions for various platforms. The 2014 version seems to be a stripped down version of 2013 adapted for mobile devices (3DS, PS Vita, iOS, Android). This review is for the 3DS version. The closest comparison would be the PS Vita version. The Android version may be cheaper, but contains the dreaded "in-app purchasing".

This is a farming simulation, and that's pretty much what it is. You plant seeds and grow three basic crops. This is not a social game like Harvest Moon. This is a good game if you just want to drive tractors and manage how to most efficiently tend and sell your crops. When I say "tend", that's usually a matter of trying to schedule everything so you don't have any idle machinery. Once you plant and fertilize, you just play the waiting game.

It's a fairly fun game with little depth. You can set it down and pick it up at will, watch TV or do other stuff while waiting for harvest time. As a sim, there's no ultimate goal, altho there are trophies for various deeds, things like how many hectares you've harvested. There are easy to finish timed missions, usually in the form of "find the lost something".

There are a few things in the 3DS version which could be better addressed:

It could use information on the types of equipment available. You're presented with the name of the equipment (Krone Big-X) but no idea what it's for. Have a device nearby with internet access so you can search the wiki's, which is almost mandatory.

Hiring workers is nice, and allows you to move on to other tasks, but you do need to keep an eye on them. They'll get stuck on fences or rocks. When you want to sell a harvest, you have the manually drive to the point of interest. And let's not even talk about how hard it is to backup a tractor! Seems like it all these should be a matter of course to adapt the AI for these things.

Cars are eye-candy and serve no purpose. Roads, too. You just drive the shortest route and traffic be damned. I like to park my tractors in the road to create massive road jams, which seem to periodically clear up automatically. You can bump into cars and force them off the road. Sometimes it's fun to play a bit of Mad Max with the cars, but they'll eventually get back on track. Maybe an option to disable traffic would be helpful.

There is no multiplayer, StreetPass or SpotPass, but there is a Miiverse community. But in all seriousness, I'm not sure what they could present for those types of scenarios anyways.
top_5.summary: Farming Simulator 2014 for 3DS

output:
