profile.reviewText:
My guppies are weird. They do not like changes in diet, or at least they don't take to them quickly. The first time I tried to give them blood worms, they turned up their collective noses. I've never before met fish that didn't like blood worms. I kept feeding those to the frogs, and finally the guppies came around.

This, the first time I fed it, the guppies were uninterested, but the neon tetras went nuts for it. The guppies showed an interest on the second attempt, and now they are an absolute favorite. Keep in mind, this isn't for any fish that must eat meat. Betta, for example, won't do well on this. I'm not letting it be a staple food for my guppies and tetras, but I serve it once a week as a treat and they love it.
profile.summary: Tetras and guppies love it.

profile.description: The best thing about cool weather? Cool cable knits. Warm up to our new assortment of chunky knits, classic cables and much-loved infinities. The eternity knitted infinity scarf is here to stay. This cowl is perfect for the evening chill or for daytime out and about. This scarf is beautifully cable rope knit patterned with modern look and sophisticated. This beautiful scarf will keep you warm during the wintertime and light up your day. The scarf material is made from 100% acrylic. The scarf is smooth and soft, great for the cold winter.
profile.reviewText:
It's really soft, not at all scratchy, and very warm. You can wear it doubled, or as a hood and scarf.  Either way, it is extremely warm.  Alternatively, you can leave it as a single loop which is still warm, but less so.  Good if you (or your meteorologist) misjudged the temperature.  I wouldn't say it's ever going to be a fall weather scarf. It's too warm for that.  But it's perfect for anything from mild to severe winter days.

It's a high loft fiber, more on the black than the red which leads to it being very squooshy, visually interesting (the contrasting texture of the two yarns gives it more character than is clear in the photograph) and good at trapping heat, so it will keep you warm.  The trick to a warm garment isn't that it is dense, but that it can hold in the air warmed by your body.  A high loft item like this will do an excellent job of that with limited excess weight to carry around and make you feel too bundled up and overburdened in the cold.

I've been trying to dissect the pattern.  There is a seam in the inside, so it was done flat.  The seam looks like it was joined by chain stitch, which is unusual in a machined piece.  The inside looks like it alternates between one knit one purl one row in red and then two rows knit one red purl one with a thicker black yarn that leads to the image of red windows surrounding a black background.  But not quite that. There is something else going on with the black stitches and I'm not sure what.  On the front it looks like the same K1P1 rib in red, followed by a row of yarn over red, knit one black, then knit one red, knit one black. Except the yarn overs lead to long stitches, not holes so something else is going on.  I'm going to be fascinated by this all winter.  Your knitting friends will love this just to figure out the puzzle.

I found one knot in the yarn, and the instructions say dry clean only.  Those are the only faults I could find with it.  I received a sample in exchange for review.
profile.summary: Soft and very warm

profile.description: Learn about the wonder of robotics with the 4M Table Top Robot. The Table Top Robot is a hands-on science kit that teaches the basics of robotics by constructing a working robot crab. When activated, the robot crab scuttles under its own power and changes direction when it encounters an obstacle. Place it on a tabletop and watch it perform acrobatic tricks. No special tools or knowledge required; the kit contains detailed instructions and all the necessary parts. Requires one AAA battery (not included). Recommended for ages 8 years and up.
profile.reviewText:
It's not a hard project -- it should take about an hour to put it together and will be entertaining for about that long. In terms of difficulty, it's well-suited to kids maybe 10 and up.  It scores low on education value.  You won't learn anything about robotics not even the simplest elements from this, and it doesn't do very much, making it a toy likely to move quickly to permanent residence in the back of the closet.

Three things you should know:

1- You will require a AA battery and a small cross head screwdriver.
2- The robot avoids edges most of the time, and usually doesn't fall off the table, but at least once every five minutes it will find an edge, often near a corner or coming at a side at an angle, turn incorrectly, and go flying off the side and crashing to the floor.
3- When it crashes to the floor, the legs fly off, but are easily reattached and the robot continues to function.  So it's sturdy at least.

I'm disappointed it can't actually avoid edges and that it seems likely to move quickly from novelty to clutter.  I'm dinging it a star for each of these points.
profile.summary: Short term entertainment, and does a poor job avoiding edges

profile.description: The flutter balls set is a teasingly tempting pair of soft balls with enticing feathers that offer an irresistible prey substitute for your cat. Flutter balls promise great fun with an emphasis on safety. This toys are designed without potentially hazardous beads, buttons and decorations that are common in many cat toys but are meaningless to your cat. Includes two balls per pack--style may vary. Measures 1-3/4-Inch length by 5-Inch width by .07-Inch height.
profile.reviewText:
When I first put it in front of the cats, the nine year old had no interest at all.  He went off to find an old catnip bird to play with.  The 1 year olds were amused for maybe an hour.  Now, they sometimes go over to it, and sometimes, if I put it in front of them, they play with it, but overall they just seem a little bored with it.

It's sturdy -- my cats always pull the feathers out of toys in minutes, but this one has held together very well.  It does bobble back up, if the cat knocks it down, which is kind of cute and surprised the cat the first time.  None of them seemed very impressed the second time it did that.

Overall, kind of cute, kind of fun.  Definitely something good for short-term amusement.  I'd very strongly recommend this to pet stores and adoption centers, because it encourages more of a sweet, batting the toy play than a pouncing or attacking behavior.
profile.summary: The cats were amused, but easily bored

profile.description: Hang this magnetic notepad in your locker, on your fridge, or any metal surface you see on a daily basis. At 3 x 7.5 inches it fits just about anywhere and it perfect for jotting down notes throughout the day. Three pre-printed headers help you organize your tasks. Each easy to tear away sheet is lined to keep your handwriting aligned. Paper is white, top binding is black.
profile.reviewText:
Each sheet is really three perforated segments for things to do, things to buy, and things to remember.  Most of us write our lists one item per line, because the human brain can more rapidly parse it that way.  The layout is easiest for us to work with.  Because these are so small, for all but the most trivial lists (the kind you rarely need to write down) there is only room to write items in a paragraph format.

Ie:  Milk, eggs, juice, bread

as opposed to:

Milk
eggs
juice
bread

It makes it harder to scan the list.

The hard back is nice, and makes it easy to write on, even standing up.  The strap on the bottom keeps the pad closed, and the pages need.  In terms of number of sheets, it is a very generous pad.
profile.summary: Very small sections to write in.

profile.description: Enjoy superior sound while easily steaming music with built-in Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and AirPlay. With 7.2 channels & 165 watts of power, driven by the largest capacitors and transformer in its class, its legendary Sony sound that really connects. Featuring 4K resolution pass-through and upscaling, high-res audio compatibility, 10 HD inputs and support for 2 separate powered zones, this receiver is the ultimate high resolution sound stage for your music, Blu-ray movies, games and more
profile.reviewText:
The sound quality on this machine is amazing.

It is kind of hard to set it up.  You use a microphone (included) to get the acoustics of the room.  This is pretty normal.  Then you have to set the sound field to match the source video or audio.  That's not so standard.  Denon, for example, can automatically detect what the source is putting out and adjust automatically. It took a while to figure out what lined up with what, but once I had it all sorted out, I was a very happy camper.

The range of audio, high to low, is very impressive.  The bass is amazing.  Naturally your speakers will play a role in this, more so than the receiver will, but with the right speakers this unit is pretty amazing. 7.2 strikes me as odd.  There is only one audio channel that goes to the subwoofer, so the same sound is sent to both.  Humans can't audiolocate subsonics, so there isn't much surround quality involved.

It supports both WiFi (with a good antenna that sticks up from the back) and Ethernet.  As with any device, Ethernet will give you the more reliable connection.

It supports Blutooth, which is kind of cool.  I use it to stream Audible books from my Kindle Fire.  It's very easy to set up.

It supports passive HDMI, which is really nice.  You don't have to have everything turned on if you don't need it.  When the system powers itself down, which it does if it is inactive for two long -- say if you leave a video or disk paused -- the screen barely flickers.

It does not yet have support for Sirius, which is disappointing, but it supports other services, such as Pandora and, of course, Sony's own Music Unlimited service.
profile.summary: Great sound quality; a little complicated

profile.description: Enhance your gaming experience with the Afterglow Prismatic wired Controller, Officially Licensed by Microsoft for Xbox One. With new dimmable Prismatic LED lighting available through full color range LEDs, gamers can set their favorite color, cycle through the Rainbow, or turn off the lights completely. Take a peek into the controller's clear polycarbonate housing, which reveals the controller's inner circuitry, and enjoy the red action-pulse lighting for enhancement of in-game rumble events. The dual Multi-Function wheels on the back of the Controller allow gamers to customize up to 6 different actions, so you can keep your thumbs on the analog sticks while engaged in the action. Additionally, the included 3.5mm headset jack will support game and chat audio. The onboard audio controls add a hassle-free way to access and adjust audio levels without interrupting gameplay.
profile.reviewText:
My only complaint is that I could not find the mentioned App on the XBox One.  Perhaps with the Windows 10 update.

You can change the color, and it goes through the entire spectrum, right from the controller.  It has a very long (I think ten feet), very stable, not prone to tangle cable.  It is responsive, has good rumble features and works well on both the XBox One and the PC.  I've been using it to play Halo: Master Chief Collection and I've yet to find it lacking.  On the PC side, I've played a little Splinter Cell: Blacklist and so far it is perfect.  Definitely the best controller I've ever tried on PC. I'm running the game in Steam on Windows 10 if that matters.
profile.summary: Great for PC and XBox

profile.description: Slim Stand Case Fire HD10 Navy
profile.reviewText:
It's sturdy.  Destructo-cat took a try at ripping into it with her claws (which I really must trim this weekend) and she was not able to do damage.  She was also unable to open it and get to the kindle inside, which is more a measure of how secure the case is than one of how dumb the cat is.  This nut figured out a trick to open the refrigerator, don't ask me how, but once in a while I used to see her run in the kitchen and then the fridge light goes on.  I had to get a child safety lock to put a stop to that.  Books? She opens them. And then eats them. iPad?  Must live in a sleeve or she will open it and activate Siri.  I'm kind of scared she'll start ordering cat treats online.  The cabinet said treats used to live it?  There's a reason they don't live there anymore.  But this one has her stumped, at least for now.  If she figures it out, I'll update.

It can hold the kindle up in a low horizontal position by placing the spine to the top (good for videos) and in a more upright position by placing the spine to the bottom as is in the photo (good for reading).
profile.summary: Stands up to abuse by cat

profile.description: Experience a new level of comfort on the PlayStation 4 with the Siberia P100 Lightweight Gaming Headset. The enjoyable, relaxed fit is built for hours and hours of gaming. Next-generation SteelSeries speaker drivers let you hear PlayStation 4 games like never before thanks to the helpful positional audio, incredible immersion and crisp details. This member of the iconic Siberia line brings you breathable, soft-padded earcups on an over-ear design that rests easily on your head. The 3.5mm plug easily connects to your wireless DualShock 4 controller and also works great on mobile devices and other platforms for a new level of audio fidelity no matter where you listen.
profile.reviewText:
This looks identical to their H series, sets up much the same and performs much the same, so if you are familiar with that, you know what to expect.

Unlike the H series, this is XBox specific.  It works on the 360 and the One (and of course as a regular set of headphones with the included audio cable).

You set it up by plugging the optical (or analog) cable from the console into a small box that serves as both relay station and battery charger.  That will, of course, need to be plugged into the wall as well.  You get two batteries with this so when one dies, just swap them and charge the dead one while using the fully charged one.  The headset is then wired into the controller.  The adapter for the One is included.

The sound quality is excellent and the balance of chat and game sound is exceptional.  You have a mute button on the headset proper, but I'm lazy and just push in the microphone to mute it.  They are supremely comfortable.  They will swivel fully to lay against your chest when not in use.  They don't grab my hair, which is always a concern for me and headsets.

I would say it isn't as good as their H series only because it is so specific, but it is better in terms of sound quality and range.
profile.summary: The sound quality is excellent and the balance of chat and game sound is ...

profile.description: The Belkin Air Protect Case for iPad Air provides reliable, cart-compatible iPad protection without unnecessary bulk or weight.
profile.reviewText:
I'm torn on this one, and I think it has a lot to do with how it is meant to be used.  It is absolutely the best tool for certain types of situations, not so much so in others.

It wraps around the back of the iPad (the iPad Air in my case), and while it is a little difficult to get the iPad in, it holds extremely firmly.  It is like a bumper system on all sides, so it adds a bit of bulk, but that can't be helped given the intention of the design.  While there are cut outs for the controls, the thickness of the case makes getting to them, in particular volume down, a little difficult.  In the hand, it feels like a foam toddler's toy.  I would imagine wrapping something like a handheld game system in this type of thing.

There is no coverage on the front, so it cannot be used in a briefcase or tote bag without an additional screen protector.  The case extends forward of the screen a little bit (that is to say, once in the case, the screen is sunken in) so even if it falls face down on a smooth surface, the iPad should be fine -- it offers substantial padding -- however, if it falls face down on a rocky or uneven surface, or if something drops on it, it's more than likely going to break.  Basically, for day to day use commuting to the office, look elsewhere.

Now, say you put a good screen protector on it and you want to take it into a more challenging situation.  You're putting it in your backpack to go camping or hiking, and you need something that can well and truly cushion the blows.  In that situation, this is your case, absolutely.

Say you want to let your small child play with it, but you're worried about the kid dropping it on the dining room floor.  You want something easy to grip, and something that can keep the device safe from the kind of mishaps the kid is likely to get into.  In that situation, this is again, absolutely, the right case for the job.
profile.summary: Either the best case or the worst case,depending on how you mean to use it

profile.description: Fluffy, delicious waffles are even better when cleanup is this easy! The BLACK+DECKER Removable Plate Waffle Maker quickly delivers 7" round Belgian-style waffles. The nonstick, extra-deep grids make thick, fluffy waffles with plenty of room for your favorite toppings. Plus, the dishwasher-safe plates are so easy to clean that the waffle possibilities are endless. Try out cinnamon rolls, brownies, hash browns and even grilled cheese sandwiches!.
profile.reviewText:
It's easy to use, and especially easy to clean.  That's not true of most waffle irons (the easy to clean part).  You plug it in, the red light comes on.  When it goes out and the green comes on, it's ready to go.  There is no "done" indicator; the green light will go on and off as it regulates temperature, so I just go by time or by steam. When the steam stops coming out, the waffle is done.  The waffle hasn't stuck to the plates yet, and the plates pop out to just put them in the sink for easy cleaning, which is wonderful.  It's tricky when you want to be thorough with the plates, yet protect the electronics from getting wet.

It comes with some nice recipes to get you started.

There were some small things I didn't like.  The first, and I'm not dinging a star for it, is the instructions for for a little too little batter.  This makes for waffles that don't form full circles.  It takes a bit of trial and error to get them right (true of any waffle iron) but once you learn to eyeball that, you're golden.

The second, and I am dinging a star here, is the latch that keeps it closed.  I've never seen such in a waffle iron before, and I'm not convinced it's an improvement.  After two waffles it becomes very hot and very hard to safely latch and unlatch it.  I'm not convinced it brings enough to the table to warrant the risk.

The third is that it has no hinge.  Most irons I'm used to hinge, so you pour the batter on one side, then turn it, and it evens it out for cooking.  Not a big deal (I'm not dinging a star for that either) but a common enough feature it seems odd to exclude it.  Still, it's not that hard to distribute the batter without it.
profile.summary: Very good, and easy

profile.description: Bandai created and continues to dominate the character model kit market around the world, most commonly represented in the billion dollar Gundam franchise and Gunpla model kits. Bandai brings over 30 years of model kit experience to the all-new SpruKits line of articulated figural model kits. With SpruKits, kids and adult fans can build their favorite action figure characters and have their creation look like a great collectable action figure without needing any glue, paint or scissors. Fans of action figures, collectors and model builders will absolutely love the exciting innovation and detailed SpruKits figures they are able to easily build, pose and display. Fans of action figures, collectors and model builders will absolutely love the exciting innovation and detailed SpruKits figures they are able to easily build, pose and display. What makes a hero? YOU DO!.
profile.reviewText:
I'm fast becomg a fan of SpruKits.  They make excellent models that are easy to put together.  You don't need any tools, but there are a bunch of rubbery top hat like pieces that seem to be common across the SpruKits snap together kits, and those are much easier to handle with a pair of tweezers.

The detailing on Batman is quite amazing, right down to the scowl.  It doesn't look like a kit when it is done.  It looks like a really good action figure.  The photo is a perfectly accurate representation, except you also get a stand (that isn't really needed as it balances well enough on its own), a few extra hands to select from, a bat-a-rang and a gun. profile.description: Paper Mate Arrowhead Pink Pearl Cap Erasers, 144 Count
profile.reviewText:
They fit well enough if you really push them on the pencil, kind of dig the end in because are kind of tight.  Otherwise they pop off.  They erase about as well as any eraser of this type would.  Nothing out of the ordinary here.  Same as the one that comes built into your standard pencil.

I'm dinging it a star because the box came open, the erasers were spilled out all over the box, and one was missing (yes, I sat there and counted 143 erasers).  I paired them with the Amazon branded pencil for a quick sketching pencil and that's good enough for my purposes.  I would say I'd buy them again, but I think the odds are a bit slim that I'll ever run out.
profile.summary: Box came open and one was missing but otherwise ok

profile.description: 29882 Features: -3 Easy steps: Add ingredients, select cycle, start. -Prepare healthy whole-grain bread - control the nutritional content of your bread. -Homemade bread without preservatives or trans fat. -Recipes included: Gluten-free to French bread. -12 Cycles including jam and cake. -Great for dough prep. Dimensions: Overall Height - Top to Bottom: -12.2". Overall Width - Side to Side: -10.43". Overall Depth - Front to Back: -14.13". Overall Product Weight: -11.9 lbs.
profile.reviewText:
It couldn't be any easier.  You just put in the ingredients, push the right buttons, and let it work.  The instructions warn that the shaking of the machine causes it to walk, but I haven't seen it move, and it's heavy enough I rather doubt it ever will.  Clean up is a snap.  The trick is, as stated in the manual, take the pan out before adding ingredients and put it back full.  I thought it would fall doing that, but so far, it has been perfectly stable.  Then all you need to do is clean out the baking pan and give the inside a quick wipe from whatever stray flour might have gotten kicked up in the mixing cycle.

It comes with recipes for all sorts of breads: french breads, corn breads, chocolate loaf, pizza dough, cakes, whole grain and more.  There is even a recipe for making jam with the machine.  It has a cycle for gluten-free breads as well.

For the simple breads, the recipe often calls for less yeast than is typical.  I thought this might be a machine thing -- previously I've only made bread by hand -- but the lower yeast content results in a dense, hearty bread.  This is awesome for winter, and I can't think of anything better to dip into a rich stew on a cold night.  I put a little more yeast in for a lighter bread, or a little less flour.  As with anything else, experimentation is the key.

If you want to really impress your friends, grab a pint of heavy cream, add a pinch of salt (or not, it's to taste) and agitate it, either by shaking it up (in the original container or in a jar) or with a hand mixer.  It'll turn into homemade butter to go with your homemade bread.  The leftover liquid is buttermilk, which can go into a nice buttermilk bread, and this machine comes with a recipe for that.  Incidentally, the heavy cream will become whipped cream before it becomes butter, and that is one really nice whipped cream.
profile.summary: Very easy to use, makes great bread

profile.description: H Wireless cuts the cord on their highly successful H Series headset line to deliver exceptional audio in a brilliantly designed wireless headset. Crystal clear audio and cutting edge performance on all your platforms. Dont settle - go wireless and limitless. H Wireless is continuously frequency-hopping to preempt and circumvent interference. Most other headsets wait for interference to be detected to change channels - these just avoid it completely.
profile.reviewText:
It's set up differently, depending on which console you want to use it with.  For PS3, you plug both the AV and USB cables into the base, and then.  You  need to go into the settings menu on the PS3 to activate the headset.

For XBox 360, you plug both the AV and USB cables into the base, and the small audio cable into the controller.

For the PS4 or Wii U, you plug the standard audio cable into the controller.  That means if you are going to use it for the PS4 or Wii U, you do not need to set up the base, except as a battery charging station.  This setup is also used for any portable electronic device that uses a standard headset or standard headphones.  Vita, 3DS, MP3 player, Kindle whatever.

For the PC, you plug the USB cable into the base.

I have my base connected to the PC, and often plug the headset into the PS4.  It swaps between those two setups dynammically.

The audio quality is exceptional.  These are excellent noise cancelling headphones. A yeshiva two blocks away from my house is using an old air raid siren as a shabbos alarm.  Imagine how loud that is.  When I have these on, and have my game set to a comfortable volume (I do not like it too loud) I can easily hear the game over the air raid siren.
profile.summary: Extreme noise cancelling; high quality sound

profile.description: A pocket-sized (3" x 5") flip notepad with a protective pink cover makes it convenient for quick and easy note-taking on the spot. Livescribe smartpens only work with Livescribe dot paper
profile.reviewText: It's not obvious, but the card in the top flap is reversable, and there is a calculator in the back. I tend to use that more than the controls. Some of the controls on the back are printed on the bottom of each card, specifically: Nav Plus Paper Replay Jump forward and back The controls on the card that are not on the bottom of each card are: Playback speed Bookmark Jump to a specific location Date Time Battery Storage Volume. There are three major negatives to this pad: 1- There is no storage pouch for cards you've already written on. Granted, with the technology that's not necessarily needed, but it would have been nice. 2- There are no dots on the back of the sheet. Wasteful and inconvenient. 3- There is no home button. For something designed for quick notes, it should have a home button at the very least, and ideally, the three shortcut buttons found on the Livescribe Sticky Notes There is no pen loop, but given the size of the pen, it wouldn't have made sense.
profile.summary: Missing a few things

profile.description: Connects to your iOS and Android devices via Bluetooth Smart (Low Energy) to sync everything you write or draw to the free Livescribe+ app.The quickest, simplest way to bring valuable information from paper onto your tablet. Easy to use.
profile.reviewText:
LiveScribe seems to reinvent their ideas rather than simply upgrading.  The current offering is hard to place.  It's kind of like writing on your tablet with a stylus (in fact, one end is a stylus) and kind of not.  You write on their special dot paper with the pen while the writing simultaneously shows up on the table.  Unlike prior pens, this is not asynchronous.  You don't store the writing in the pen, then sync it later.  It transmits via bluetooth smart as it goes.  So it's hard to see the value of the pen over simply writing to a note taking app on the tablet, except the value of an extra print backup.

There are some compatibility issues.  It doesn't work with all generations of iOS devices.  Only those that can run iOS 7.  So make certain your device is on the list.  It doesn't work with Windows tablets.  It doesn't work with Android, though support is supposed to come in 2014.  There was plans for adding Drop Box, Facebook, Google Drive, and Mail support to their last pen in 2013, and that never materialized, so take the plans for Android support for this pen with a grain of salt.  Android or Windows users would be better served with their Echo or Sky smartpens. The ink for this pen is not compatible with prior Livescribe pens.  The app, when I could finally find a device it would run on, was a little flaky and crashed quite often.

It's a good concept, overall.  It needs some time to become stable enough for day to day use, and it needs to work against a greater range of infrastructure.  As a pen, it writes very smoothly, and is a pleasure to hold.
profile.summary: Bleeding edge -- beware compatibility and stability issues

profile.description: The Clef du Vin enables you to instantly reveal the qualities of a wine. 1 Travel size and 1 Service size Cles du vin. It works effectively on all types of wine: white sparkling, rose, red and naturally sweet wine With the Clef du Vin, you can adjust the balance of a wine to your personal taste and enjoy it straight away. Accurately gauge how your wines will develop so that you can manage your wine cellar efficiently.
profile.reviewText:
I tried it with a few wines, and the results varied wine to wine, which I think is part of the point.  With Bartenura, for example, I didn't notice much difference at all.  Before and after were much the same.  The impact on Baron Herzog Late Harvest Zinfandel, on the other hand, was astounding.  It went from a fruity, sweet desert wine to a more complex wine.  A bit sweeter, and a bit richer.

I did not find any wines made worse by this tool, and I did not find a dramatic improvement outside of the Zinfandels.  However, the effect on those alone makes it worthy of five stars.  It's hard to describe, but I'd say it breaks up the flavors, layers them.  One wine went from impact to finish with very little variation in taste before the tool, but after took on quite a few variations in tone.

From what I'm seeing, the impact is most on Zinfandel, then white, and red shows the least change.

The impact on the legs confused me, and I had to repeat the test a few times to be certain of what I was seeing.  The wine before using the tool had better legs than the wine after.  Legs are caused by alcohol in wine evaporating, then the leftover water and wine condensing on the sides and running down. The greater the alcohol content, the more the legs.  Some say the sweeter the wine, the greater the legs, but that seems to be in debate.  Certainly the tool isn't removing alcohol, and at least to taste the wine after is generally sweeter, so it must be having some other impact on the wine.  Researching it, I found that covering the glass impacts legs (no, I didn't do that) and that there are many interesting myths about the legs, but nothing that would explain what I'm seeing.  Shouldn't be a problem, unless you or your guests like swirling the wine and holding it to the light.  It had no impact on the nose in any of the wines I tried.
profile.summary: Results vary from wine to wine

profile.description: This is an economical way to supply your chess team, desk, or office with the basic essentials of the chess worlda board and a set of pieces. The Analysis pieces have a 2 1/2" king and the board is 12" x 12". The small size of the set is ideal for places where you don't have a lot of storage and/or playing room.
profile.reviewText:
I did not expect to like this nearly as much as I do.

I signed up for the Chess University Lite program, and I needed a small analysis board with which to work on the problems provided in the videos. This was meant solely for that purpose. It is the perfect size for a quick game with my roommate, and even though we have a great number of other boards, from time to tournament size, this is the one we keep pulling out. It's small enough to play anywhere, and big enough to play comfortably. I love it so much, I bought another one in blue.

The board folds into quarters to stick in the bag and lays flat when pulled out.  I tend to rest it on a small drawing board when playing on the couch.

The chessmen are sturdy enough that they have taken a tumble or two onto the floor without damage. They seem of a kind with the roll up tournament boards.
profile.summary: Small enough to play anywhere; large enough to play comfortably

profile.description: Titanium Bonded blades stay sharper longer, features auto sensor shut off, includes EZ-view shaving reservoir, innovative new design, winner of the Good Design Award, manufacturers limited one-year warranty
profile.reviewText:
The one thing that surprised me is that it is outlet only.  You can't run it off batteries.  That seems kind of last century, but then pencils are a bit last century.

I tried it with a host of art pencils from 8B to 5H and it was able to handle them all.  The points came out clean and did not break in the process, which can be a problem with the very hard ones as they can run a bit brittle or the very soft ones as they are, well, very soft.  This was able to deal with all of them.

The automatic shut off is a great feature.  No pulling the pencil out to check if its done, just press it down until the sharpener stops.  It's good to know I'm not the only person who wants an idiot proof pencil sharpener.
profile.summary: Convenient, but no batteries

profile.description: This crafty DIY electronics kit contains everything kids need to create a snuggly trio of light-up forest friends. The circuit is complete when the friends holds hands, making the plushies glow. Each Sew Science kit comes with a plastic needle and precut felt pieces to stitch together, making assembly easy, safe, and fun. Sew Science kits also include the LED lights, batteries and conductive thread needed to complete the circuit. Sew Science is a super cute way to teach kids about electricity and circuits, and makes STEAM learning adorable and fun.
profile.reviewText:
It's not that hard, but you need to follow instructions closely and some things are not intuitive.

First, the electrical thread comes doubled all the way through the bobbin but you use it singly.  There isn't a lot of it, nor can I find any information on what thread to buy should it run out.  Mine barely made it.

Second, the embroidery thread does not come on a bobbin, and there is enough of it that it needs it. If it were wound as it would be when sold for needlepoint, that would be all right.  This looks like someone wound it around a few fingers then tied it off.  It will tangle.

The double sided tape is a pain, and is more prone to come off the component than off the paper.

You need a scissor, and a lot of patience.  That said, there is something insanely cool about a project that teaches something of electronics and sewing in one.  The stitches taught are whip stitch and running stitch, and the felt is marked and perforated for guidance.  The felt is clearly marked as to where the components go, but be careful not to let wires that should not touch actually touch as that will kill the circuit.  A child who can do complex Lego projects should have no trouble with this.  Certainly if they are up to the Technic level they will be fine.
profile.summary: Not perfect, but the blending of sewing and electronics is awesome.

profile.description: The MotoCare Variable Temperature Heat Gun has multiple temperature settings that take the guesswork out of the most common applications. This heat gun allows the user to choose the correct temperature for the application, such as refreshing headlights and trim, deactivating adhesives or drying touch up paint. The included glass protector and flare nozzles help direct the airflow for various projects.
profile.reviewText:
I use it for embossing.

What I like is that it has two heat setting and very little blowing.  I've yet to see a heat gun that doesn't blow air a little -- it's not a hair dryer, but it does have to move the heat somehow.  But some are more prone to scattering the embossing powder than others, and this one is good for that.

It has two settings, and for my purposes low works better.  That's in line with single-setting heat guns marketed specifically for the purpose.

I don't like that it doesn't have a stand to keep it from touching the table.  The metal part doesn't touch the edge, so I guess it's okay, but I would have preferred a stand.

I like that it sheds heat fairly quickly when it's turned off.  I made the mistake of tapping the metal with the side of my pinky soon after use and it left a small blister.  My older gun would have done far more damage, but this had shed a substantial amount of heat in a few minutes making it not as bad.

Overall, I like this much better than my old Darice.
profile.summary: Two settings, low air movement, good for embossing

profile.description: Philips A19 LED light bulbs with Warm Glow Effect provide 800 lumens of soft white light, equivalent to 60-Watt incandescents with 80% less energy use. These bulbs fit standard medium base (E26) fixtures with the look and feel of a classic bulb. Not for use with Philips HUE products. Warm Glow dimming offers flicker-free, silent dimming that works with more dimmer switches than any other LED on the market. The more you dim, the warmer the light--from 2700- to 2200-kelvin just like traditional incandescent light bulbs. These best-in-class, Energy Star Certified Philips LEDs provide steady, natural lighting at 1/4 of the energy of incandescents, 1/2 the energy of halogens and with 10X and 4X the lifespan respectively. Philips LEDs are mercury-free so they don't contribute to harmful hazardous waste. Classic A19 soft white light bulbs are perfect anywhere you need a balance of clarity and warmth with the flexibility of dimming. The E26 medium base fits standard fixtures on pendant, vanity, and bare lamps, providing soft white light with warm dimming. This 2-pack of A19 LEDs is expected to deliver a lifetime of up to 25,000 hours and over 20 years based on standard usage of three hours per day, saving you the cost and hassle of frequent bulb replacement.
profile.reviewText:
First, these will not work in a host of situations.  If you have a timer on your lights, a nightlight, an indicator light, or home automation -- pretty much anything other than the most basic of switches -- the slight power that remains active in the system, even when the switch is "off" is enough to cause these to glow bright enough to read by.  I tried them in a home automation setup using Z-Wave and a dimmer paddle and had no luck getting them to shut off.

I found the light to be too warm, so much so as to throw off colors in the room a little bit.  I know artists talk about light quality impacting color, but I never noticed it before trying these.  I've never been aware of the warmth of a bulb before,but with these it was pretty striking.  They dim to a decent semblance of the orange of dimmed incandescent bulbs.
profile.summary: Does not work with dimmable home automation solutions

profile.description: BulbZ is a Z-Wave Controllable Fully-Dimmable Instant-On LED Screw-In Light Bulb Equivalent to a 60 Watt Wirelessly Control the Bulb Z-Wave App Required
profile.reviewText:
I hooked this up to a Nexia bridge without a problem.  Activate it as other Z-Wave lighting.  It's weird because that only displays switches, but it handled the bulb no problem.

You can control it from the switch, which I feared would be a problem.  The light switch must remain on at all times, otherwise the bulb won't get power.  You turn it off and on quickly to turn  the light on.  Turn it off, on, off, on quickly and wait about 5 seconds and it will fade and turn off.  I don't know why the on is instant and the off has a momentary delay, that could be related to my setup,  It works every time.

It provides a clean, white light.  It's dimmable even if the switch isn't, which is a nice feature.
profile.summary: Easy to set up; easy to use

profile.description: This kit introduces you to programming in a fun, step-by-step way. An Arduino-compatible gamepad connects wirelessly to your tablet. Using the gamepad and four interchangeable sensor modules, you play through a video game app on your tablet. In each level of the game, you have to learn a piece of the Arduino programming language and how to use it in order to solve puzzles and challenges and move forward in the game. In this way, you progressively learn the basics of coding. Soon you will be able to write programs on your computer using the four sensors and invent new applications. Following instructions in the 64-page, full-color experiment manual, you can create cool projects. Learn to code by playing a video game Gaming: Use sensors to control the game with this innovative gamepad Coding: Solve puzzles and challenges in the game to learn the Arduino programming language Making: Write your own programs and develop new applications for the sensors Includes Arduino-compatible microcontroller (with Bluetooth), cable, rotary control wheel, circuit board, gamepad housing, two push buttons, motion sensor, temperature sensor, sound sensor, light sensor, parts for projects, Code Gamer App. Requires a tablet or smartphone running iOS or Android. GAMING Connect the physical and digital worlds! Use the gamepad to play through 15 fun game levels on your tablet. Plug one of the four sensorbots into the gamepad to activate its special powers. Level Editor: Design and create your own game levels, share them, and access other players' levels. CODING Level by level, learn the basics of the Arduino programming language! Discover which program commands make the LEDs on your gamepad blink and the sound module activate. Learn how your gamepad works and how you can configure it yourself. Use the light sensor to count how many times a drawer is opened or program an alarm system that sends you messages. Enter the digital maker's world and unleash your creativity.
profile.reviewText:
It's a little tricky to assemble this.  Not that hard, but a bit.

Do not remove the wrapping on the battery.  Or at least, it will work if you don't.  It wasn't clear.
Do not remove the plastic covering the contacts for the buttons.
Both of those points confused me.

The thing I'm dinging it a star for is that the track wheel is sticky.  You start to move the character a little, let go, and it keeps moving.  It's clicked in properly, but once in a while it over responds.

The thing I like best is that you're first coding Arduino on the app.  It lets you pull bits of code, more and more, into the correct place.  You learn gradually in a gaming context.  You ultimately move onto PC and real Arduino programming.

The thing I like least is that it is mostly repetition for so long.  You memorize what line is where and fill it it when it goes blank.  So it's the same code every time (it blinks the LED) and the first time one line is missing and you have one code monster.  Second time that same line and another are missing and you get the old code monster and a new one.  Lots of repetition.  Why start with a header for a function called startup?  Because that's the line missing and the only code the monster has.  It doesn't explain at that point even what a function is.

And yet it pulls a person in, is compelling, and is a weirdly effective way to learn at least a little.

Embedded systems like this, IoT, is the future of technology.  We are facing a pending crisis of too many jobs with too few skilled people in this field, so this is a huge step up for any kid, and it's creative, educational, and plain old fun.

You will need a cell phone or tablet with Bluetooth to play with this and complete the early lessons and a PC for the later part.
profile.summary: Great way to get into IoT projects

profile.description: An Amazon Brand.
profile.reviewText: I like the feel of this, and that the cat can't destroy it.  I can store a 10" Kindle Fire, with the keyboard case, in this and stuff it in my bag with no fear keys or coins or other scratching things will get inside the case. profile.description: Old Leather Mini Journal

profile.description: This cookware set is an exceptional value, including all of the pans needed to equip your kitchen with the most used cooking pieces. As the set contains only basic pieces, you'll really use each and every pan. It includes saucepans for whisking a homemade sauce or cooking your morning oatmeal, a big stockpot for soups, stews or boiling pasta, and skillets (probably the most used pan in any kitchen) that will help you turn out perfect crepes or a simple grilled cheese sandwich. The set also includes a saute pan, a wide, straight-sided pan that can perform many of the functions of a skillet but features deep sides for extra capacity, perfect for one dish meals. Start your dish in this pan by sauteing onions and browning meat, then add your liquid and other ingredients into the same pan to finish on the stovetop or in the oven.
profile.reviewText:
I should start by saying, I am, by and large, inept in the kitchen.  Mostly I burn stuff, then spend an hour scraping burned food out of the pan.  I am probably the last person you'd want near a cookware set this good.  These pans actually help.

The metal heats evenly, and the lids fit snugly, so food cooks better.  We made blintzes in them, and the middles heated up perfectly before the outsides browned too much, which normally is not the case.  The outsides browned evenly, no matter where the blintz was in the pan.  I used to have to shuffle them around to give each a turn in the hottest part.  Omlets routinely come out better.  Usually they're a little darker on the bottom than the top, and darker in the middle of the bottom than on the edges, but with these, they come out even.

The non-stick coating is no joke.  Food just slides right out of these.  I've melted butter in them, enough to coat a tub of popcorn, and there was no problem cleaning even that kind of greasy mess.  No scrubbing.  No struggling.  Just fast, easy clean up.  I love that.

The handles are riveted on.  They don't come loose, don't swivel, and hold very securely.  They stay cool, and are comfortable to use, even on the stockpot. Have I mentioned I don't own potholders?  These just feel good to use.  The pots in pans gerenally feel solid and well-made.  They're a pleasure to use.

Even the manual is useful.  It includes helpful tidbits like don't spray them with a cooking spray--that ruins the non-stick coating, and don't scour them or use metal implements in them--that can crack the non-stick surface and make them unsuitable for use.  This is true for all non-stick cookware, just not something I'd known before.

I never thought I'd love cookware, but I love these. They might make a homemaker of me yet.  If you have as much trouble in the kitchen as I do, you're going to love how much these can make cooking so much better, and cleanup so much easier.
profile.summary: They make cooking (and cleanup) easier

profile.description: Lightweight, versatile, portable and travel-friendly. Sculpt and tone your lower body. Durable flat latex bands help increase shoulder flexibility and range of motion. Three resistance levels to meet your needs. Includes exercise guide.
profile.reviewText: One of the things I wanted these for was to do the supported one handed pull up progression in Convict Conditioning: How to Bust Free of All Weakness-Using the Lost Secrets of Supreme Survival Strength. No, I'm not up to those yet, but I was worried I wouldn't find something easy enough to grip and strong enough it won't rip. The book uses a towel, but I didn't think that would work for me. The grey one (the heavy one) is exactly what I was looking for, sturdy, easy to grip, and not so elastic if held reasonably close to the bar as to interfere with the workout. It comes in three resistance, not marked, but easy to figure out by touch. Purple is light. Blue is medium. Grey is heavy. I would have liked them to be marked, but after a time it won't matter. You can adjust your workout not only by the band but by how long a tail you leave past your hands. The longer the tail, the shorter the working band. The shorter the working band, the greater the resistance. So you get a lot of flexibility here. Marking them to your grip position might help measure progress over time. I highly suggest keeping a journal and measuring that progress. Nothing motivates better than seeing steady improvement over time and beating any kind of personal best. It comes with a nice, short workout, including a warm up. Do the move empty handed 3-5 times as a workout, which is similar to weight lifting where you lift the empty bar. In weight lifting you'd then go through the lighter weights to the work set, so here I'd say work through the lighter bands 3-5 times each to the work set as well if you'd like a more thorough warm up (I would on a cold day when muscles are tight). The workouts are: Side Raises -- hands out to either side, Arm Extensions -- hands behind you from behind the head to overhead, Lunges -- Lunge with the band as resistance coming up, or as I like to say "bwah ha ha, they have got to be kidding (lunges are my weakness). Front Raise -- hands go from just under the waist palms up to straight out in front of you palms down. Arm Curl -- Looks like a bicep curl, acts like a bicep curl. Turn it sideways if you want a hammer curl. As you can see there is a lot here for the arms, almost nothing for the legs, and I'm not sure it's providing enough of a challenge for the core. Yes, any time you're lifting under resistance, you're working your core, but I'm not sure the resistance here is sufficient It might be, I just have doubts. I barely smell the latex unless I hold my nose to the bands. They stink if you do that. Don't do that. They store nicely enough in the box they came in. They take up very little room.
profile.summary: Not bad, but could stand more exercises.

profile.description: Hamilton Beach Single-serve Blender With Travel Lid; Red; 51101r; New
profile.reviewText:
I was nervous at first with this because when I first opened it, I wanted to clean it out, so filled it with soapy water and shook it vigorously for an initial rinse.  It spilled all over the place.  I was using it at the office and rather than have chocolate peanut butter lean shake sprayed all over my desk, I took it to the kitchen, where my colleagues stood back ... way back ... and I debated changing to a gym T-Shirt just in case.

Turns out it blends perfectly, no splatter, no mess, no fuss.  For something as simple as a powdered drink mix (the reason I bought it) it's perfect.  For powder drink mixes like Muscle Milk and diet shakes and the like, the general thinking is thus.  Spoons are highest convenience and lowest quality.  Shake bottles are medium convenience, medium quality.  Blenders are least convenient, highest quality.  I'm greedy.  I want high quality and high convenience, and I feel I have that with this.

I would, however, not trust it not to spill.  It's about as spill resistant as a lidded coffee cup.
profile.summary: Convenient, effective, not entirely spill proof

profile.description: The powerful EX5230 Pro ensures professional presentations in virtually any setting, even in large venues with ambient light. Offering high brightness and XGA resolution, this powerful performer ensures engaging presentations with sharp detail. And, it features fast wireless connectivity, making it easy to project content from laptops, smartphones, and tablets (optional wireless LAN module required). Builtin HDMI delivers digital video and audio with just one cable, while Epson's Simple Setup Suite enables flexible positioning and rapid setup. It's the ideal projector for busy professionals whose presentations demand proven performance.
profile.reviewText:
It was very easy to set up, and very easy to use.  The only thing that confused me was the pointer.  I was trying to wave it around like some sort of WiiMote.  You need to use the arrow buttons to move it.  If you plug it in via the serial cable to an Ubuntu box, it shows up as a second desktop.  If you plug it in via the serial cable to a Win 7 box, it mirrors the desktop.  Of course, this is fully configurable for both.  That's the default behavior.  If you plug it in via USB, it installs drivers first.  You can plug in multiple sources and switch between them at will with the included remote control.

What I like.  The picture clarity.  It looks like a 720p HDTV.  It's not quite 1080, but not that far off, and that's pretty remarkable for a projector.  The color clarity trumps that of my netbook. To test it I connected my netbook via HDMI to the projector and projected a movie.  At one point there was a distant view of a crowd with pink glow sticks.  Where there was a haze of pink lights, all the same shade, the projector showed tiny dots in hundreds of similar shades of pink.  I was very impressed.

The speakers are well place, and produce a full range of sound at full range of volumes.  You could use this for showing a film to a classroom with no issues. Run through the image options to find the right one.  It looks horrible if it is on the wrong setting, but fantastic on the right one.  It can adjust the lens to account for uneveness in the surface. That just about everything is included.  You need an HDMI cable.  The serial cable is included.  The USB cable is included.  The case is included.  The case looks flimsy, but it holds up very well.  The ability to freeze frame if you want to do something on your machine, say to set up the next slide or next presentation, without showing it to the room.  The pointer controlled by the remote control.  It's just one less little thing to forget.

What I did not like.  It gets hot fast.  The driver install is a little clunky.

This is the best projector I've ever used.  I love it.
profile.summary: Beautiful image, fabulous color saturation

profile.description: BLS2K8G3N169ES4 is a 16GB Kit containing (2) 8GB DDR3 modules that operates at speeds up to 1600 MT/s and has a CL9 latency with extended timings of 9-9-9-24. It is Performance and is non-ECC. It conforms to the industry standard SODIMM layout of 204 pins and is compatible with computers that take DDR3 SODIMM memory.
profile.reviewText:
This review is for the Crucial Ballistix Sports XT 16 Gig DIMM kit.

I was a little concerned with the DIMMs as they were a little fatter than normal, but they snapped easily into my Dell desktop computer.  Both Windows 7 and Ubuntu recognized the memory at once, with no issues, which really was to be expected.

Often, I'll run multiple VMs at a time.  I do software development, so often I'll have one VM running Windows Server 2008, hosting SQL Server, while a second acts as a development box, and a third, which is frequently wiped out and recreated (or really, cloned from a blank copy) acts as a testing machine.  Each of these machines gets 4 gig dedicated ram, and I leave the last 4 for the host OS.  This RAM has held up to that kind of intense use without any problem.  I am delighted.

I also use this machine for intense gaming, and again, this RAM does an awesome job.  The memory, left at default configuration, is fast, fast, fast.  Again, I'm a happy user.

Overall, I think the product is an exceptional value -- a top performer at a sensible price.  The best I can say is, after a while you won't notice it.  It will give you solid performance with no problems, and will just become invisible as you.  I will definitely be using them again next time I'm in the market for memory.
profile.summary: Sport XT 16 GIG DIMM pack

profile.description: Build and program robots with this compete robotics engineering system. Using sensors, motors, a core controller, and hundreds of snap-together building pieces, you can follow the instructions to assemble 12 different robots. The versatile parts also allow you to make robots according to your own designs. This fun robotics curriculum starts out with instructions for building simple robots, teaching you how the sensors can be used to control the robots. Build an ultrasound robot that can avoid obstacles, a line tracker robot, a touch sensor robot, and a doodling robot. Move on to more complex robots that have multiple functions, such as a ball-manipulating robot, a crawling robot, and a grabbing robot. Finally build some functional, helpful robotics including an automated door-opening robot and a protected robotic safe to store your valuables. After you have mastered all of the robotic models in the instructions, you will have the tools and knowledge you need to go on and build and program your own amazing robotic creations. The robots can be controlled directly in real-time and programmed to perform series of commands using an easy-to-use, free downloadable app on tablets and smartphones. The app wirelessly connects to the core controller using a Bluetooth low energy connection. You can create more complex programs using the open source visual block programming editor "Google Blockly" on a PC with a USB connection to the core controller. The app requires a tablet or smartphone running iOS or Android. A 96-page, full-color manual features step-by-step illustrated building instructions and instructions for how to program and operate the models. Using the core controller, the ultrasonic sensor is able to detect an object and measure its proximity. Core Controller Your robot's brain! The core controller features a Bluetooth connection to tablets and smartphones and a USB connection to a PC. You can download programs from your devices to the core controller.
profile.reviewText: I found this kit surprisingly frustrating. You're going to need a very small screwdriver to open the battery case. Yes, the instruction say slide it off, but no, it's held in by very small screws that took a while to discover. Just want you to know so you'll have one handy. The size in an eyeglass repair case is about right. Also, have six AA batteries at hand. They are not included. Forgive me if this review sounds a little technical. You're here because you're interested in a tool to learn programming, so I'm guessing you'll be okay with a little discussion of the inner workings of that. You can't really program it with the computer. You need to keep it tethered to the computer while the program runs. The thing it, it uses Snap as a programming language. Not a bad choice. It's what's used in Hour of Code and a great variety of introduction to programming projects. There are versions of Snap that are interpreted and versions that are compiled, and they chose an interpreted version, which, in my opinion, was a very bad choice. Interpreted means the interpreter looks at the code one line at a time and translates it into machine code, which is then executed. Which means it needs to send each line, one at a time, carry out the instructions, then interpret the next line. Compiled means the compiler looks at all the code and translates all of it into machine code, which is then stored to be executed at will. Compiled code could be downloaded to the robot, so you could detach and run it over and over again. Robolink Codrone Programmable and Educational Drone Kit for Beginner/Arduino Learners with Video Tutorials for example, uses compiled code. You could use the tablet app (it suggests a 9" screen tablet for the IDE (Integrated Development Environment) to present clearly) and connect via Bluetooth, but I could find no way to make that connection on the PC. The robots themselves are cute and easy to assemble, and it comes with a tool to take them apart easily to reassemble the next one. These are best done by following the guide in sequence, as the skills build on each other. There are some charming features to what this can do, especially if you're comfortable programming on a tablet. I would suggest any Arduino kit over this for any but the most newbie of newbies. For those I would suggest Thames & Kosmos Code Gamer Coding Workshop and Game (iOS and Android Compatible) first, and then any Arduino kit.
profile.summary: It you program it one the PC, you need to keep the USB cable attached while it runs around.

profile.description: This strength hand grip features a durable steel coil and strengthens muscles in your hand, wrist and forearms while the cushioned foam handles provide a comfortable nonslip grip. A just able resistance levels from 20 to 90 lbs.
profile.reviewText:
This is a very quiet hand grip.  No squeaking.  No clicking.  There is a very slight noise of the coils rubbing against each other, but not much at all.  It's perfectly fine for using while watching tv and it won't be heard over the television.

On the easiest setting it's very low resistance.  I'm new to strength building and I can do it easily.  At the hardest setting I can't move it at all.  So it feels like I have something I can do now, and a lot of room to grow.

My only concern, and I'm not sure if this is particular to this grip or typical of adjustable grips in general (I've only had very simple grips with no way to adjust the difficulty) is that the resistance is confusing.  If the spring is at the 90 pound mark, you get minimum resistance.  If it it at the 20 pound mark, you get maximum resistance.  There are no interim markings.  It is controlled by the green knob at the head, which turns easily and gives you fine control over the angle, at the expense of it taking a while to go from one end to the other, but ideally it's a set it and only adjust it a bit at a time kind of tool.

There is no information sent along with it (the device is pretty self-explanatory) but if you want information on reps and sets and all that stuff, there is abundant data online.  I'm going to do 3x10 in each hand then turn it one rotation on the next go and keep that up until I can't do it anymore, then back down as much as I have to and work on that until I can up it again.  Seems as simple a plan as any.
profile.summary: Quiet and quite adjustable

top_5.description: Assassin's Creed Unity - Limited Edition - PlayStation 4
top_5.reviewText:
When you first start the game prepare for a long install.  This game has been patched, re-patched, and patched again to knock out the bugs, and there are still bugs.  In the first section, before even the welcome screen (which is granted something like an hour into the game) I managed to crouch behind something only to have a clipping error trap me there.  I had to go in the world map then back out again to refresh the screen layout so that I can move.  But that's not that bad.  Most of the bugs are gone, and those clipping issues are a running part of the franchise.

There is a companion app with a whack of micropay transactions that is pretty much a required part of the experience.  Many chests won't open until you solve a ridiculously easy puzzle in the app.  Easy, because the things you're looking for don't move, so you can just remember where they are for the next try.  That's a little worse, especially because not all mobile platforms are supported.  At the time of this writing Windows Phone (tiny install base, granted) and the Kindle Fire (very large install base) are not supported.  If the thing is mandatory, it should work on all platforms.  The app also allows you to send out your assassin's on assignment, similar to what Ezio was doing in Brotherhood, except it made sense for Ezio to do that.  He was pretty much leading the assassin's at that point.  Arno isn't even an assassin when he starts.  Also, the forgot the initiation rite from Ezio's time or else it changed past all recognition.  The new one is really weird.

Also required is the multiplayer element built right into the single player story line.  I mean, you can ignore these things but not if you want to fully complete the game to 100%.

The upgrades are tied to helix credits that you can buy, more microtransactions, which can get kind of annoying especially since they start at $20 and go up to $100, but are, at least, optional.  Really optional.  Like if you don't buy air assassination, you can still perform an air assassination, you just have to guess when it will and will not work as the option doesn't show up in the UI.  It's as if they made the decision to implement the "you have to buy this" feature late in the development cycle, so the programmers just hid it from the interface.  You can also do leap of faith before Arno learns it.  In fact, you have to do it before Arno learns it.

If anyone was wondering if we lost the modern era stuff in this game, worry not.  It's still there.  Pretty interesting stuff too.

Arno is wanted, so much so that if he is seen in a restricted area, no matter how many other random people are loitering around, he'll be pursued.  So with this in mind, he walks into a police station and randomly offers to help with the crime problem.  The only cop on duty isn't all that concerned, neither with a most wanted fugitive standing in front of him, nor with such an odd request, but a bored prisoner sets him to solving murder mysteries.  Why?  Because they wanted murder mysteries in the game.  They're not bad murder mysteries.  They just don't fit in at all.

The worse part, is that Arno is the single wimpiest assassin in the entire brotherhood.  Eagle vision wears off in a few moments, and needs to recharge.  He can't escape battle and heal over time.  Like Ezio, he needs healing bottles. Unlike Ezio, he can't find doctors all over the place.  He can't counter and do an instant kill.  He just gets some extra blows in and if he does it wrong he's off balance instead.  His attacks do a lot less damage than any prior assassin.  What he gets instead is...he can crouch.  Yep, we're giving up unlimited eagle vision, healing over time, and a deadly counter-attack for crouching.  Oh, and he can pick locks.  So basically we're trading in an assassin for a cat burglar.

If you can, bypass this one and try Rogue instead.  Rogue is the real A.C. game out this year, a true successor to Black Flag.  This one...had potential for true greatness and gave in to mediocre gimmicks instead.
top_5.summary: They wimpified my assassin.

top_5.description: With write speeds of up to 150MB/s, the SanDisk Extreme Go USB 3.1 Flash Drive lets you quickly copy and go. Up to 35X faster than standard USB 2.0 drives, so you can transfer a 4K movie to the drive in less than 40 seconds. The design keeps the retractable connector protected when not in use, and the included SanDisk Secure Access software provides password protection of your private files while leaving the rest of the drive available for sharing.
top_5.reviewText:
Fast, fast, fast.  It came formatted FAT (I think for Mac support), which means no support for files larger than 4 gig.  I changed mine to NTFS to use in Linux and Windows.  In Windows, the easy way to do that is with the convert command "convert <drive letter> /fs:ntfs"  In Linux, it depends on your distro, but then, if you're only using Linux, you won't be using NTFS.

I built an Ubuntu Virtual Machine on the drive, and have been running it across multiple machines, as swiftly and easily as if the VM were stored locally.  I can't think of a rougher stress test on performance, and it meets the challenge easily.  It's rugged, reliable, and comes with built in drive encryption for your protection.  Every OS I plug it into --Win 7, Win 8, Red Hat, Ubuntu, Debian -- recognizes it and mounts it with easy.  It's so convenient.  It holds my entire toolset.  I never go anywhere without it.
top_5.summary: Super fantastic flash drive

top_5.description: WD Blue WD10JPVX 1 TB SATA 6 Gb/s high-performance 8 MB cache 5400 RPM 2.5-inch 9.5mm internal mobile hard drive. SINGLE PACK
top_5.reviewText:
I used this as an upgrade drive for the PS4.  It caused one reboot on installing a lot of software over a slow Internet connection (it was during the upgrade of the software, and might have been caused by that) but it has been running flawlessly ever since.

It is stable, reliable, and quiet.

Don't let the speed be an issue here.  Sony bullt at 5400 into the PS4 originally, so it will not need faster, and a faster drive could cause overheating. Two things to keep in mind when downloading the Sony firmware though.  First, the folder names are case sensitive.  PS4/UPDATE not ps4/update.  If you are going to use this to upgrade the PS3, a thing to keep in mind when installing the system software is that the PS3 has trouble reading larger thumb drives.  This nailed me when I tried a 120 gig drive.  I had to roll back to an 8 gig, that did the trick.

For a laptop or netbook, I would favor a faster drive, but for the budget conscious, this one is excellent.
top_5.summary: Excellent for upgrading the PS4 hard drive

top_5.description: The Alex Toys My First Sewing Kit will introduce children to the creative world of sewing. It's a skill that lasts a lifetime and can be used to make adorable stuffed animals,notebook covers and more. All the materials you need come in the charming carrycase that closes securely and has a handle for sewing on-the-go. Includes 28 pre-cut polyester felt shapes, 8 colors of embroidery floss (26ft/8m each), polyester stuffing(0.4oz/11g), fabric cloth (65% polyester/35% cotton), polyester ric rac(24in/60cm), scissors, measuring tape, 40 straight pins, 2 needles, thimble, cotton/polyesterpin cushion, polyester ribbon (12in/30cm), 6 buttons, pom pom strip (12in/30cm)and easy instructions. Recommended for children 7 to 12 years of age.
top_5.reviewText: This possibly isn't the best starter kit for a child who has never sewn before. The instructions aren't that good. If the child has done any other sewing, or has anyone who can help (can be another kid) then this will provide a great deal of practice, which is where this really shines. There are quite a few projects here. There is a draw string bag, a stuffed cat, a stuffed dog, a stuffed elephant, and a book cover with pencil holder wrapper. For supplies, it has everything - scissor, tape measure, pins, pin cushion, button, even some extra stuff, like pop poms, that you won't need for any of the projects. There definitely is not even close to enough stuffing. It did not quite fill the cat, which is the first, and smallest, of the stuffed animal projects. You'll want to pick up something like Fairfield Poly-Fil Premium Polyester Fiber, White, 1 Bag, 12-Ounce. Any fiberfill will do, but this is a good one, similar to what is in the kit. While on the topic of stuffing, a double pointed knitting needle, or better http://www.amazon.com/Little-Foot-That-Purple-Thang-/dp/B001ELBCFG/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1464647654&sr=8-1&keywords=purple+thang will help get the stuffing into the tight areas, like the tails. Both the fiberfill and the thang will be useful items in a variety of sewing projects. For the embroidery floss, it says to cut the skein on one side to make lengths. That works, no issue, but it might be better to make a little yarn butterfly (really simple; instructions are online) so that you can pull the length you need for each section and the leftovers, and there will be plenty, can be used to make friendship bracelets. There is an excess of embroidery floss here.

profile.description: I was born in 1942, so I'm an autumn rather than a spring chicken. I live outside of Tampa, Florida with my fabulous wife Anita, and one remaining son at home, Montana. I have three older boys, Mark, Gary, and Anthony, all of whom have married and presented us with terrific grandchildren. I read hundreds of books by the science fiction greats growing up, and thousands of fair to not so greats in dual novel paperbacks and magazines. My education gravitated to science, starting out as a physics major and my depression era folks told me I'd never make a living as a theoretical physicist (probably right, and Cosmology wasn't a career field then), so I moved to Electronics Engineering. I did most of that in the aerospace field for MacDonnell Douglas Corp, in St. Louis, Mo. I worked on the F4 Phantom project, and briefly on Manned Orbiting Laboratory (MOL), before the fickle fates of government finance forced contract cancelations. I devoted (read: I was drafted into) two years' service for the US Army from 1965 to 1967. A great two years, and the Army, caring not a whit for my electronics background, offered this draftee a job as an Air Traffic Controller. Cool! After discharge I spent a short time back at MacDonnell Douglas before the contract reductions laid me off, and was hired by Emerson Electric (1968), working on the design of a neat heads-up fire control system for the Army's new Cheyenne Helicopter (to be a 270-knot hybrid fixed wing/rotor craft). Never heard of it? The fickle fates of Army finance is why this time, plus Lockheed didn't keep the airframe part from crashing and burning at a crucial point in development. I taught Electronics for about eighteen months (near starvation wages after the high pay), and finally decided to try my hand at actually supporting my family again. I hired on with the Federal Aviation Administration as an Air Traffic Controller in 1970. Thanks Army! I spent exactly forty years in federal service, deciding in 1979 to use my technical background to work on writing features for the software of the FAA's Terminal Automation Systems (for 28 of those 40 years). Retired, I now work as a consultant/contractor for the FAA, supporting a software system I helped create. In anticipation of more free time in the future, I finally decided to try my hand at writing what I love to read, Science Fiction. Thanks for reading my books, Steve Bennett
profile.reviewText:
Stephen Bennett's Koban series is absolutely great, the perfect blend of hard sci-fi and space opera. I read at least the samples of all the new sci-fi that Amazon lists, and Koban is by far the best that has been written for many years. I especially appreciate the length of these books, as I don't want the story to end. I hope the series goes on for a long time.

In this third book Captain Mirikami makes what to me are errors in judgement that are very costly to his people. I expect his leadership to be shared more fully by others in future books.

I encourage other fans to mention the Koban books on the Amazon science fiction forum as well as the combo fantasy/sci-fi forum, so more people can be made aware of this great series.

http://www.amazon.com/forum/kindle%20fantasy%20science%20fiction/ref=cm_cd_ecf_sap?_encoding=UTF8&cdForum=Fx3HM4WU2RDYE3B
profile.summary: Best sci-fi being written

profile.description: Directed by Sam Mendes. Starring Ralph Fiennes, Javier Bardem, Judi Dench.
profile.reviewText:
Yes, it's a totally different Bond movie. But that's OK. I like the more cerebral Daniel Craig Bond movies, with less emphasis on high-tech, underscored hilariously by Q's outfitting of Bond with a pistol and a radio transmitter, period. "Not exactly Christmas, is it?"

This is a thinking man's 007 movie, harkening back to the original Sean Connery films. And I swear, I thought the movie was over at the island, but there was still an hour to go. Then came the best part. The second half probably left a lot of people flat, those who appreciate the super-gadgetry of the Brosnan and Roger Moore Bond movies especially. But I found it deep and emotional, and Bond really had to try to stay alive.

I hope they keep doing these type of Bond movies with Daniel Craig. You can believe in this James Bond.
profile.summary: Two Bond movies in one.

profile.reviewText:

profile.description: Life for John and Lara Brennan (Russell Crowe, Elizabeth Banks) is miserable after she is convicted of a murder she says she did not commit. Three years later while struggling with the demands of work and raising his son alone, John is still trying to establish her innocence. When her final appeal is rejected, Lara becomes suicidal, forcing John to exercise the only option he has left: Break her out of prison.
profile.reviewText:
As many reviewers have noted this film is filled with implausible events but the one that ruins the suspense is when the detective finds a piece of Crowe's Prius  tailight plastic which leads him IMMEDIATELY to Crowe, which leads him immediately to Crowe's breakout location, which leads him immediately to a garbage can full of Crowe's notes and maps for the scheme. Dude should buy a lottery ticket he's so lucky.

The rest of the weak points can be smoothed over by a suspension of disbelief but to go from a jagged piece of plastic to IDing it as a piece of plastic from a Prius that is registered to Crowe's wife as the FIRST GUESS just ruins the whole thing. From that point on every step the detective takes is directly in line with Crowe's plan. He even runs around crowded downtown Pittsburgh and just happens to see Crowe and his wife in the split second they are visible in a subway tunnel.

You will agree with everyone else that her conviction would have been impossible in the first place. Really, it's a weak story held up by implausibilities and a waste of your time.

Every company has a keystone product around which their image builds and MH's foundation is solid. This all-time bestseller is soft on skin and unflappable in the wind.
