top_5.description: Professional cooking torch for all cooking needs. Use only with Iwatani gas cylinder, Bu-5 and BU-6. Become a professional Chef and make Creme Brulee and other fine foods to impress and make for friends and family. Perfect for caramelizing sugar atop your creme brulee, glazing a baked ham for the holidays, searing a steak, roasting bell peppers, melting cheese and toasting bread crumbs.
top_5.reviewText:
The attached photo shows that this torch fits easily onto any standard size asian hotpot tank.

This is my third blow torch, and thankfully, it's also the end of my search.  I've had it for 3 years now and it still works great.

I first tried one of those torches that come with creme brulee kits.  Those suck.  They have weak flames, meaning it takes so long to get the job done that you'd better have 2nd dinner planned because your guests will be hungry again by the time you finish with your first pot of creme.  They are also a pain because you need to buy specialized canisters to refill the torch.

I then went to the hardware store and got a soldering torch.  It was definitely far more powerful, but 1) I thought I was going to torch the whole kitchen, the flame was so large, and 2) the model I got didn't seem to handle being tipped very well and would go out.  The canisters were also way big and heavy.  I felt like I was holding a mini fire extinguisher, which knowing me I probably *should* have had on hand.

Then, I found this torch.

And I tell you, I'm in torching bliss.

I love that it's powerful enough to brulee things quickly and evenly.  The flame is adjustable so you can have a wide, even flame or a tight targeted one.  Most of the time I just leave mine on a wide flame, which works best for creme brulee to have that even finish.  It also seared my prime rib roast nicely (I cooked my roast low and slow and wanted to finish the roast with an even crust.)  The browning of the gristle smelled so good I'm getting hungry thinking about that roast and I'm writing this review in the AM.  I've used it to finish a lot of my sous vide dishes and it's consistently worked great.

The unit is compact (it comes with just the top), but it fits on top of any of the standard butane canisters you'd find at Asian grocery stores.  Just ask for the canisters for hotpot.  It means refills are cheap and relatively easy to find.  I hate the other type of blowtorch where you have to refill it into a little compartment in a handle.  Those were such a hassle.

One thing is that the tip of the torch changes to a copper colour with use, which my previous torches didn't  But hey it doesn't hinder performance so who cares.  It looks well used as a result and you get more cred for being a hard core torcher.

Can't wait to use this to sear the top of some pressed sushi as well.

Yum!
top_5.summary: Powerful enough to brulee the heck out of everything

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "Your kitty will love the Catnip Chaser by Petstages! This fun toy combines the catnip scent cats love with fun movement and play. Adjustable vents let you determine the strength of catnip scent, and the center securely closes to hold catnip. Includes bonus catnip! Non-skid pads on bottom ensure it stays in place.". The summary of the review text is "Is it a toy or a puzzle?  Depends on the cat. Either way, it's a hit!".
output:
This catnip "toy" is a hit in my two-cat household but for very different reasons (see below). In general, the catnip chaser keeps my cats entertained and occupied while delivering cat happiness. There is one design flaw, but there's an easy workaround. The top of the chaser has a catnip reservoir and an adjustable lid. The lid is designed a bit like the top of a Parmesan cheese bottle - there's a wide opening and a perforated opening. Twist the lid to align the wide opening over the reservoir to fill, twist again to place the perforated section over the reservoir to release the catnip scent. Adjust as desired. The cat smells the nip, gets worked up and bats the ball around the track. However, the lid is pretty loose so batting at the ball also twist the lid to either completely cover or completely expose the reservoir (turning it into more of a catnip feeding station). I adjusted the lid to have about 1/3 of the perforations over the reservoir then taped the lid in place. I have to remove the tape to refill, but that's not a big deal. Now, for the different cat experiences. Also, the toy is lightweight so it moves around a lot. Rubber feet might help keep it in place, at least on smooth floors.

Heres' how my cats reacted. Cat 1 sniffed the catnip, and got animated, batting the ball around, flipping herself on her back, rubbing her chin on the chaser, and pushing it across the floor. Cat 2 sniffed the catnip, rubbed her head all over the lid, and drooled uncontrollably until the whole thing (and the cat's face) were covered in spit. She didn't understand the toy function at all. At first I thought she was just dumb. Then I turned my back and she flipped the chaser over so that a bunch of the catnip fell out of the holes and onto the floor. She moved the chaser out of the way and rolled in the catnip until she was covered in it. She looked fully seasoned and ready for the soup pot. Who's the dumb one now?

So, lesson learned. Now I keep the chaser locked up and bring it out for supervised play. I know if I leave it out, chaos will ensue. This way, everyone is happy!

profile.description: Paperback. Pub Date :2013-07-18 Pages: 330 Language: English Publisher: Macmillan Hardback Omes A rainy night. an Amish father returning home with his three children. a speeding car hurtling toward them out of nowhere What at first seems like. a tragic. but routine car accident suddenly takes on a more sinister cast as evidence emerges that nothing about the crash is accidental. But who would want to kill an Amish deacon and two of his children He leaves behind a grieving widow and a young son who clings to life in the intensive care wing of a hospital. unable to communicate. Desperate to find out who killed her best friends husband and why. Kate begins to suspect she is not looking for a reckless drunk. but instead is on the trail of a cold blooded killer in the heart of Painters Mill. It is a search that takes her on a chilling journey into the darkest reaches of the human...
profile.reviewText:
Sheriff Kate Burkholder's latest case hits close to home. A buggy carrying an Amish man and his three children is involved in a hit-and-run accident that leaves all but one child dead. Kate's called the scene only to discover that the victims are the husband and children of her childhood best friend. Dealing with an important person from her past gives us a chance to learn more about Kate's formative years; we get to learn more about who Kate was before a personal tragedy forced Kate out of her Amish community. In the last book, there was plenty of movement in Kate's relationship with Tomasetti. This time out, we're doing little more than marking time. But, I'm already looking forward to finding out what happens next.

If you haven't read any of the others in the series, you should be able to pick this book up and have a good idea about what's going on. Castillo does a nice job of providing expository narrative to bring you quickly up to speed on prior key developments.

I love that Linda Castillo teaches me something new about Amish people or culture in every book. This book is now exception - now I know a bit about non-farming options and the genetic issues of their closed cultures. And because I used to be a medical librarian, I did a little follow up research and discovered there's even an Amish, Mennonite, and Hutterite Genetic Disorders Database. Who knew?
profile.summary: Kate's formative years revealed

profile.description: Tackle all your daily tasks with an affordable laptop that comes packed with the features you need.
profile.reviewText:
It is hard to write a review on a laptop; besides the physical characteristics you are pretty much left reviewing the software, how easy it is to set up, and how fast you perceive it to be running. Regardless, here goes.

The laptop weighs in at 4 lbs 10 oz with dimensions of 10" x 15" x 1" as advertised in the product specs. It is equipped per the product specs on the Amazon page. The screen is large, vivid, and clear although it does have the usual contrast problems in bright sunlight. The screen is not touch sensitive.

The biggest drawback to the laptop is that the top and bottom surfaces are plastic and quite slippery. I can easily see this laptop slipping out of your hands if you are not extremely careful.

The keyboard has chiclet style keys that have nice stiffness and are spaced like a regular desktop keyboard. There is a separate numeric keypad.

The left side of the laptop has the following: 2 x USB 2.0, 1 x HDMI; 1 x Ethernet; and 1 x Power. The right side of the laptop has the following: 1 x SD Card slot; 1 x USB (unsure if USB 2.0 or 3.0); 1 x DVD drive; and 1 x Kensington lock.

The power supply input is 100-240 VAC 50-60Hz at 1.4 A; the output is 19.5 VDC at 2.31 A. The power supply is rated at 45 W. The power supply brick is also extremely tiny: 3.5" x 1.5" x 1". The brick connects to the computer by a 6' cable with a proprietary connector; this cable is attached to the brick. The brick connects to the wall using a 3' long cable using a standard three prong connector; this cable can be removed from the brick. You will need to check with HP to see if there will be a problem with an ungrounded power supply should you take the laptop overseas.

I started work on this review at around 7:30 AM with the laptop fully charged. It is now 9:30 and the battery charge is at 35% showing 1 hour and 24 minutes remaining. Battery performance not that great.

Missing from the top of the computer are indicators for disk activity or computer sleep/hibernate. Not a deal breaker but if you are used to them you will definitely miss them.

I downloaded and installed the following software without any problems: Symantec Endpoint Security, Microsoft Office 2016, Matlab, and LabView. All installed software worked without a problem.

I ran several graphics routines with Matlab and had no noticeable performance issues; i.e. hit go and the graphics were done before I blinked. For basic users looking for document editing, email, and web browsing the computer processor is faster than you need.

The Wifi network performance is acceptable; regardless, I am not happy with it. I use a Luma surround WiFi network of three routers. The Luma trio is distributed around the house and establish a proprietary mesh network operating between 300 and 500 Mbps. Each router then provide a standard WiFi network all with the same SSID and passphrase. Basically they guarantee 100% WiFi coverage throughout the whole place with no dead spots. When I check network status at all of my other devices I see connection to my WiFi network at speeds of 300+ Mbps - full speed in and out of my routers. When I run [...] on these computers I get the rated performance of my ISP - 10 Mbps up and 100 Mbps down. When I check the HP laptop I get status less than 72 Mbps and 6 up/36 down. Definitely not the same performance. This is still adequate for typical home applications but you want full performance regardless of the computer. I need to double check its configuration on my network.

I did not test the wired Ethernet connection. I did not test the Bluetooth connection.

Upshot. Good basic low-cost general purpose laptop for web, email, document editing, and basic calculations. Not for high power users.

Downshot. Battery performance not that great. It is slippery - be prepared to drop it unless you are extremely careful.
profile.summary: Slippery, battery, WiFi - Things to consider

profile.description: Classic Brands 6-Inch Memory Foam Mattress is the perfect solution for getting a better night's sleep. The memory foam layer conforms and supports your body so that you can get the rest you deserve. Only the highest quality foam is used and it is CertiPUR-US Certified so it is naturally antimicrobial and resistant to allergens, mold, bacteria and dust mites. This mattress is an excellent choice for bunk beds, kids rooms, dorms, and even boats and recreational vehicles. It's a value priced solution to other expensive branded memory foam mattresses Look for more innovative specialty sleep products from Classic Brands.
profile.reviewText:
Our old mattress was showing signs of wear after 15 years and we knew it was time to find a new mattress. But, mattress shopping is the worst. When I had the chance to try this mattress out I figured I had nothing to lose. I'm so glad I ordered. It's almost perfect.

I had slept on a Tempurpedic mattress once in a hotel and didn't care for it - it was too soft and sitting up reading in bed resulted in my backside making a big dent in the mattress that didn't quickly regain its shape when it was time to lie down. I have also heard they can be too hot. But, the reviews for this memory foam mattress were largely position so I took my chances.

The queen mattress came vacuum packed in a box about the size of a footlocker or hope chest. It was too heavy for one person to drag upstairs, but two of us made it easy. When we opened the box and cut the plastic wrap, it quickly (but not alarmingly) started to magically puff up. We let it air out for about 3 days before putting in in our bedroom, and although there was initially a slight, plasticy odor, it wasn't too bad and went away quickly.

Overall, we really like the mattress. The foam does contour to your body, but is firm enough not to leave a body-shaped indent when you get up. With no pocketed coils, it doesn't transfer movement so it doesn't disturb my partner when I shift around. And it doesn't sleep hot at all. All in all a great deal. Easy delivery, comfortable sleep, great price.

The only awkward thing about the mattress is its thickness. Our old spring mattress is about 10" tall. Putting this mattress on top of the box spring made the bed too short for our foot board/head board. Putting it on top of the old mattress makes it too tall. I'm still not sure what we'll end up doing about that. For now it's on top of the old mattress. A 6" mattress is also too short for our sheets which are all made for an old school pillow top coil one. We bought sheet corner straps to keep the sheets pulled tight, but will probably end up buying new sheets that fit better.
profile.summary: Better than a Tempurpedic

profile.description: Portable platform helps turn your tablet into an interactive presentation tool. Folds flat for easy portability. Ideal for tablets 7" to 11" diagonal. Download the Belkin Stage App to turn your IPad or Android Tablet into an interactive whiteboard and document camera, available on Apple App Store and Google Play.
profile.reviewText:
Bottom line: You can already use your tablet's camera to view stuff, you can already purchase or acquire the software/hardware needed to display your tablet's image on a monitor or through a projector, you can already download the Stage app (free or Pro) if you want to interact with the image that's displayed. How much more are you willing to pay for this stand to rest your tablet on? As far as a tablet stand goes, this Belkin gets the job done. I'm just not sold on its value.

Bigger picture: To get the most out of this product you'll need additional software (and potentially hardware). What Belkin provides is basically a stand to position your tablet. I used the Stage with my iPad 2, but any tablet with a rear-facing camera should work. The Stage is sturdy and it lets me position the tablet at any needed angle. Putting items on the Stage base allows me use the iPad as a document camera, displaying the item on my iPad screen. Doing anything more requires software.

Belkin offers a Stage app that can be downloaded to your iPad or Android device. The free version lets you draw on the screen to annotate either the live version of the document camera display, or you can take a photo of the item you are viewing and draw on the still shot. All additional features of the Stage program require you to pay-per-feature-use or to download the Pro version of the software for $5. It is mind-boggling to me that the "Pro" version doesn't come with the purchase of the Stage. Without the software, the Stage is just a fancy tablet stand.

If you want to use the Stage to display the iPad screen to a group of viewers, you'll need to hook your tablet up to a monitor or projector. This requires additional software or cables. It might be too much to ask for the Stage software to include the ability to send a wireless image of your tablet's screen to another device, but for me, it's just not useful without the ability to project.

It's important to understand that the Stage is just one (small) piece of the puzzle needed to make your tablet into a fully featured teaching or display device.
profile.summary: Decent stand with limited additional functionality

profile.description: The SMART1300LCDT SmartPro LCD 120V, 1300VA/720W Line-Interactive Uninterruptible Power Supply provides battery backup and AC power protection against blackouts, brownouts, power surges and line noise that can damage electronics or destroy data. Ideal for backing up your desktop computer or audio/visual components, this line-interactive UPS switches to battery backup mode in milliseconds to keep your connected equipment running long enough to save files and shut down safely with no data loss. While all eight NEMA 5-15R outlets protect against surges, four outlets also provide up to 64 minutes of UPS battery support for a basic desktop PC and LCD monitor and up to 10 minutes of support at half load (360W). Automatic voltage regulation (AVR) corrects undervoltages as low as 92V and overvoltages as high as 150V without using any battery power. EMI/RFI noise filtering improves your equipments performance and prevents damage. A 650-joule surge suppression rating protects your equipment from harmful power surges. NEMA 5-15P plug with 6-foot cord connects to any NEMA 5-15R socket. Large LCD screen shows real-time input voltage, overload, AVR, remaining battery runtime and battery statuses at a glance. Alarm sounds to indicate power loss or low battery. With Tripp Lites free PowerAlert software (available via free web download), the SMART1300LCDT enables safe unattended system shutdown and file saves in case of a prolonged power failure.
profile.reviewText:
I recently installed a 12 TB RAID FreeNAS server for computer backup, photo storage, and video playbacks. Also added a custom Untangle firewall. High reliability systems of this type require continuous power and in the event of a power failure need to stay on long enough to gracefully shutdown. This UPS fits the bill. I have suffered 4 power outages at home in New Jersey since installing these systems. I also have three additional Tripp-Lites for desktop computers. During the power outages all the computers have stayed powered own throughout. In fact the only way I have known that there has been a power outage has been the clocks on the microwave and oven resetting and the UPS have beeped during the outage, The power outages have never been long enough for the computer auto shutdown feature to initiate; typically less than 1 hour.

I have built satellite ground stations and developed a passionate hate for APC UPSes. In my experience when the power goes out on an APC UPS and the backup battery begins to discharge, the first thing to lose power is the USB communications card connecting the UPS to the PC being protected. Losing the communication cards then triggers the computer to shutdown well before the battery is discharged. I have never had that problem since I switched to Tripp-Lite UPSes.
profile.summary: Tripp-Lite UPS - So good that I have never noticed it being there

profile.description: Kit includes four commonly used adapter plugs
profile.reviewText:
First, this is an adapter NOT a voltage converter. This adapter solves the problem of having a two prong US plug (say off a computer power brick) while facing a two hole European plug in a Norwegian hotel room. It does not convert the 240 VAC European voltage into 120 VAC US wall voltage. These days most power supplies can automatically accept 100-240 VAC making a voltage converter unnecessary - all that you need is an adapter to match your plug to the wall socket.

Second, this unit is ungrounded. If you plug a three prong power cord into the adapter only the hot and neutral lines are passed to the wall outlet. This may or may not affect you. Check the Users' Manual on your equipment.

That said, this is a cool little unit. It has a slide/pushbutton switch to select USA/Australia plug, European plug, or British plug. Sliding to the US/AUST position the familiar two blades pop out; using your fingers you manually rotate the blades between the angled AUST and parallel US positions. You then slide back to the Europe position and the US/AUST blades retract. Pushing the button in then causes the European prongs to partially pop out. You must manually flip the prongs into the fully extended position; this took more force than I expected. You must manually close the European prongs before you are able to slide to either the US/AUST or UK positions. You then slide the switch to the UK position and the thick prongs pop out. Between the prongs is a plastic "wedge" flipping that up creates the insulated 3rd pin for European outlets.

The adapter is small but not small enough. Depending on its orientation it may use up the space over one or two US wall or power bar sockets.

The unit also provides two USB charging ports. I sacrificed a USB cable and was able to confirm that a regulated 5 VDC at around 2.4 A was provided by the adapter.

This adapter will be in my travel gear for all future trips.
profile.summary: Well Thought Out Travel Adapter - Already On My Must Pack List

profile.description: Super-slim form factor provides the benefits of a folio/desk-top case with no extra bulk
profile.reviewText:
Now that I've had it for a couple of months, I'm looking for a replacement alternative to Apple's iPad Smart Cover. I want something that protects the back of my device, folds into a stand, and covers the front without leaving the weird fold lines the smart cover does on the glass. The Case Logic folio meets my requirements, but I'm still not quite happy with it.

The case snaps firmly around the aluminum body and definitely feels secure. The front flap covers the glass, but doesn't stay in place. I knew it didn't have the magnet feature to turn the unit off and on automatically (which I didn't think I'd care about but found I missed) but would expect there to be some other mechanism to keep the flap closed. There isn't. When I'm using the iPad that's fine, but when I put it in my purse, it's problematic that the cover opens and leaves the glass exposed.

I didn't find the cover conducive the way I primarily use my iPad (propped up in landscape mode for typing, viewing documents, web surfing). Although the cover folds back to make a stand, it doesn't really stay in place. Standing it up vertically, the flap fits nicely into the lip on the back and gravity keeps the two pieces interlocked. However, when I prop it up in the direction I usually use it (i.e., slightly elevated for typing), the flap slides out of the lip too easily. As soon as I start touching the screen, the flap slips out of the lip and the iPad falls flat. The elastic band you can slip your hand through is oddly placed, at least for the way I hold the iPad. It's only helpful in portrait mode and since it's as wide as the case, your hand slips around inside it. I can't imagine any situation in which I would find it useful.

This cover performs as promised and does everything thought I was looking for in a cover. But, it doesn't do it as elegantly as I would like and I'll keep looking for that perfect cover.
profile.summary: Gets the job done

profile.reviewText: The Fish Basket is a quality product. The frame and basket are well attached and the clamp on handle holds the basket securely. profile.description: The Altec Lansing IMW255 Mini H2O Blue Waterproof Bluetooth Speaker is an ultra-thin and portable waterproof speaker. profile.reviewText: Very cool. Extremely compact Bluetooth speakers with good (not super fantastic great) sound that can take a dunking. Opened up the packaging in images attached. The speakers are about the size of the original handheld transistor radios or the size of two packs of smokes. Plugged them into USB and let them charge for about an hour then went to laptop (Lenovo L430) and enabled Bluetooth pairing mode. Turned on the speakers and held the power button for about 2 seconds. The speakers then speak and let you know pairing is in progress. Speakers also tell you when they are paired and connected. Announcing Bluetooth status changes is perfect for me; no more frustrating guesswork. Went to Win v10 Sound settings and selected the speakers as default. This is probably my biggest concern, having to select between Bluetooth and regular speakers on whatever device you are using; no really easy way to switch on laptop, you have to change playback device in Win control panel. I tested with my laptop. Anyway, set Bluetooth speakers as default sound output and turned on and turned up the Rolling Stones (Title 5 remains awesome as always) using iTunes. Loudest volume could be heard across the upstairs of the house with no noticeable distortion or clipping. Picked the speakers up and walked downstairs; speakers dropped in and out when there was about 20 feet and a wall between me and the laptop. Walked into garage, directly under the laptop, speakers picked up and played loud and clear. Can now listen to iTunes in the garage; excellent. Brought the speakers upstairs and dropout repeated until I was back in office. Sound picked right back up. Carried speakers over to the bathroom; three walls and 20' to laptop so sound definitely dropped out. Ran a sink of water and tossed the speakers in. They float. Unfortunately no sound to see what they are like in the water; too lazy to reconfigure for that test. Picked up the speakers and shook the water out of them. LED was still lit so power was on. As I approached the office the speakers announced that they had reconnected to the laptop and music happened. They speakers continue to operate in a little puddle of water on my desk. Going canoeing in the morning; I have a waterproof pocket for my mobile phone and will have these speakers clipped to my PFD. Play a little Wagner.
profile.summary: Good sound for your next trip to the beach - and they float

Lionel is expanding beyond model trains with the introduction of Mega Tracks, a revolutionary rail system where kids can use their imagination to design and build their own race courses! Utilizing a new clamp and construction system, kids can build anywhere, including on the floor or attaching to furniture, to create one-of-a-kind race courses. In addition to building their own track, kids can also create their own stunts by twisting the TwisTrack, a new flexible track system. Once the layout and stunts are built, kids can send the rail racer vehicle into high speed action, using a handheld RC controller to adjust the speed of the vehicle and keep it on the track. This master set includes 20 feet of TwisTrack, 55 construction pieces to build customized track layouts, Rail Racer vehicle and charger, handheld RC controller and includes track clamps and connectors, Red and green engines are sold separately and are on different frequencies. Set includes: 20 feet of TwisTrack 55 construction pieces to build customized track layouts Green Rail Racer vehicle and charger Handheld RC controller Includes track clamps and connectorsFeatures:Enjoy the flexibility of MegaTracks and experiment using your imaginationCreativity to build the track of your dreamsHours of endless funDimensions: 22.5 Inches x 5.25 Inches x 5.25 InchesRecommended Age: 8 - 15 years
profile.reviewText:
Lionel Mega Tracks - Corkscrew Chaos Red Engine

This review was handled by the biggest kid I know; my husband.

"Lionel is expanding beyond model trains with the introduction of Mega Tracks, a revolutionary rail system where kids can use their imagination to design and build their own race courses! Utilizing a new clamp and construction system, kids can build anywhere."

To translate. Revolutionary = monorail on flexible Hotwheel-style ......track. Imagination = learning curve. Race courses = 20 foot one-man circuit. Anywhere = anywhere you have a huuuuuuge table top or floor space.

Mega Tracks requires a lot of table space and you need to be able to walk around most of the table. Why? Because the pieces are huge. The Red Engine is huge. I think the problem started with the Red Engine. The motor, gear train, or track grippers set the size. That defined the weight of the car. The weight of the car set the track weight and stiffness. The track set the size and weight of the support arms. Somewhere in there they had to add spacing margin so that there was room for the large car to not run into things as it went around the track. It is big. The example track used in the instructions is about 3' x 5'.

Second, don't get me wrong, this is great fun but it is not something casually whipped together out of a child's imagination. The box states "Ages 8 to Adult"; I think an 8 y.o. will get fed up pretty quickly. Number of reasons.

The parts are difficult to assemble and disassemble. In order to get the rigidity necessary to hold the track in place the joints between parts are very tightfitting. This adult struggled to get some parts apart when changes were called for. Very tight. Too tight for 8 y.o.

The beam parts are two different sizes. Instead of being interchangeable you have to know the differences in functionality between the two in order to pick the right one. Why not put in a little more design, be clever, and have a single part?

The only way to "hold down" the track is to use one of the clamps; at the edge of your table or piece of furniture of clamping thickness. Any other support structures just sit on the table top or ground and are free to slide around wherever they like. This causes problems when you have to worry about track clearance so that the car doesnt run into another track or wall when it is on its way by. Other support structures must be made of beams and joints that could have been used to better support the track. What they need is a mid table support with suction cups to keep it in place. Otherwise you are using books to weigh things down and hold supports in place.

The play set comes well packed in a sturdy cardboard box. Inside the box is the product packaging with the usual clear circular stickers; I cut them with a precision cutter just because I may want to keep the box. The controller and Red Engine are cable tied in; I flipped them over to cut the cable ties from the bottom to avoid damaging the hardware. The construction parts were provided in a separate flat inside the product packaging. I strongly recommend having a parts bin available to dump all of the joints, couplings and track supports into; I am in the process of organizing my office and had a 2 gallon plastic tote available. The instructions are in pretty fine print; I ended up using a magnifier and guessing in a couple of places. I tried building the demo from the instruction sheet but it was just too large for my desk; I used my imagination. I placed clamps around the edge of my desk and stabilized them with some blue beams but eventually realized that every single part was necessary if I wanted a complete circuit. When I started attaching the track I realized exactly why kids will not have the patience for this toy. There are two types of track supports; a holder that attaches to the middle of a track segment and just holds it in place, and a joint that connects two track segments and holds both track segments in place. The set comes with 5 pieces of track, 5 track joints and 5 holders (actually a couple more but I am not counting) which should be enough to connect and support everything. Only there is nowhere near enough parts to build all the necessary support structures. Not perfect but you can not support some holders and that makes it all better. Right? No. Because joints must be supported AND joints must be exactly one length of track apart; if not, there is a gap in the track or there is curve that is not the desired radius or a curve that sags. This explains why you have all the unanchored supports; you have to slide things around a bit. And while you are sliding it around you have to worry about the length of the next segment of track, the clearance between all the track (particularly the stuff that is sliding around), the angle of the track, the radius of curvature, etc. Kids are either going to get this immediately or will not understand why the car keeps dragging on the floor around the second turn. A couple of different track lengths and more parts for support structures are needed here.

The handheld controller requires a 9 V battery. Before you start assembling track you should plug the Red Engine in. Looking nose on at the vehicle there is a switch on the top left marked ON/CHG; on the top right is the DC power input jack. When you plug it in a bright red LED will light up. Once charging is complete, approximately 2 hours, the LED will turn green.

The end result is a bit ... I don't know ... the little Red Engine definitely could. The long blue track sorta could. The weight of the car is a lot for the track. Even supported in the middle of each track segment it was flopping around like a long circular al dente lasagna noodle. The Red Engine can move; I got my reflexes tuned to slow it down before it flew off into the walls.

Lionel has a little plastic widget to attach your mobile phone to the top of the controller. They point you to their website which gives a little stopwatch app. Now if they had made the train set at half or third scale of what it is, a few more support ideas, different track lengths, controlled the car via Bluetooth, and placed a video camera in the nose of the car. That would be cool.

Upshot. A lot of effort. Not enough pieces to properly anchor track; check Lionel website videos for examples. No way to anchor supports in the middle of a table. Pieces can be difficult to disassemble; quite a bit of strength necessary. Need track pieces of various lengths. Car is WAY too heavy and large. WAY. I would say this is more for 12 y.o. to adult. This adult had fun and will be reconfiguring his desk every week or so; reminds me of a start up where we had slot cars, a ping pong table, and free Red Bull. Talk about the little engine that could.

UPDATE: the packaging shows a little Red Engine and a little Green Engine. Unfortunately the box only contains one engine. The second is in an add-on kit that must be purchased separately.
profile.summary: Very flexible (in a good way; in a bad way)

profile.description: From Gourmet Basics by Mikasa collection. This 3 tier Rooster hanging basket features a beautiful traditional design and allows you to maximize space in any room of your home. This 3 tier basket is great for storing or displaying food or other items. Crafted from carbon structured steel for long-lasting beauty even under rigorous use. Wipe clean with damp cloth. Measures 17-1/2 inches high x 6-3/4 inches wide x 10 inches long.
profile.reviewText:
This hanging basket set is good stuff. I was worried that it would be lightweight, tippy, wobbly, covered with sharp edges, ill-fitting and use cheap materials. I was wrong on all accounts except for a couple of slightly minorly sorta sharp edges and a little bit of wobbliness; keep reading for details. It took me about 15 minutes to assemble.

The concerning edges are on the hooks holding the handles to the basket. They are sharp enough that you would have to take a running start and jamb your finger in just the right way and you will either get a minor scratch or break your finger; i.e. they are not a big deal.

The base is substantial steel. It will hold the thing upright unless you seriously seriously add too much weight over one side of all the baskets. Key words are over the edges - the weight would have to really be trying to tip the thing over. If everything is weighted vertically this thing ain't gonna tip.

Wobbiliness. The base on mine is not perfectly flat; it wobbles with two corners slightly higher than the others. We are using ours in the carpeted dining room to hold place settings (napkins, placemats, tablecloths) so there is no problem for us. You might need shims; small strips of duct tape would be hidden under the frame or use rubber feet to protect a wood or tile floor. I don't consider this a big deal.

All parts are solid metal or close to it. The parts fit well and like the base are substantial; it would take a lot of effort to bend one. The risers are solid, square steel. At the top there is a slightly larger hollow square tube. The risers drop vertically down into the hollow tube. Screws are tightened through the hollow tube to hold the riser in place. Do this at base/riser 1 then riser 1/riser 2 then riser 2/top piece. Total of 12 screws.

An Allen Key is provided to tighten the screws; once you are done you can throw it away. The Allen Key is 5/32" and can use any generic Allen Key in your toolbox (I use a Sears Craftsman 46701 Allen Key set - well worth the money - get the metric one while you are at it - Craftsman lifetime guarantee and mostly made in America). My screw thread gauge has gone missing so I cannot help there.

The finish is a deep burnished copper color. It looks like a powder coat but I am not an expert to say for sure. The finish is well attached and shows no sign of chipping or scratching without the application of a knife or tool.

The baskets are deep about 10". Perfect for storing puppies, kittens, and small children.

Upshot. This is a solid, well built, good looking, storage unit for kitchen or bath. It will serve our needs perfectly. I like it.
profile.summary: Solid, well-built, good-looking, storage for kitchen or bath - I like it.
