profile.description: Feel the Groove Good Looks, Great Texture Shield your iPod from damage, without sacrificing style. The flexible silicone sleeves feature a unique textured design that looks and feels great. Protection that Fits: The thin, yet durable material is a stylish way to keep your iPod's surface free of scratches and scuffs, without adding extra bulk.
profile.reviewText:
Really, I suppose for those who have a propensity to drop their mobile devices, these covers might provide an easily measurable benefit. The silicone textured case offers a sure grip and thus far fits snugly. The access holes are appropriately placed to accommodate access to all jacks and rear positioned lens. To this point, I haven't encountered any problems mounting the iPod to any of my speakers with docks either.

I prefer the black case as I suspect over time the translucent one will begin to show the effects of age and become soiled if even from only transferal of body oil secretions in the course of normal handling. It might be my imagination but it also has a less tacky feel to me.

The cases material composition is similar to another case I own for an older generation iPod and over time that case has expanded to the point control wheel functionality on the iPod has become inconsistent because the case no longer remains in direct contact as I attempt to change settings. I suspect the same thing will occur here in the areas of the power button and volume side positioned volume controls.

However, as was my observation when I purchased the previous cover, it seems ironic that the cover packaging actually provides more protection for the covers than the covers provide for the area of the iPod most likely to be damaged or scratched, namely the screen. So once again, after securing the iPod in the cover, I cut a face plate out of the plastic packaging and used that to protect the screen

Now for those who use the iPod for a multiplicity of functions, touch sensitivity might be impacted somewhat but for me it's just a portable music player and for my purposes is a lot cheaper than buying dedicated screen protectors...with the added benefit I don't feel like a dunce acquiring a cover that fails to protect the part of the device I am most likely to damage.
profile.summary: Another night at the improv

profile.description: The new Life Play 2 succeeds its predecessor, powered with a new 1.3 GHz Quad Core processor and upgraded 8GB Internal memory. Also included is 1GB RAM and the latest Android 4.4 Kit Kat which offers users the most up to date performance. 8MP Camera with features such as LED Flash, geo-tagging, and 1080p HD Video Recording.
profile.reviewText:
Yeah, I know. I'm a compilation of contradictions. This is my first extended foray with an android device and I have to say, I'm impressed if not swayed. I do not find it as easy to navigate as Windows 8.1 on a mobile device (although I detest the touch screen optimized interface with a PC) but 4.4 does seem to have more user built in conveniences and services for the user than the IOS 8.0.2.

Now, all of that has to be tempered with the further admission if circumstances allowed I would be satisfied to use my basic, dumb flip phone but my most significant personal contacts seem to be allergic to voice calls, obsessed with texting, Skype and Facetime.  Yet, for anyone contemplating a move away from Apple, the distinctions in navigation should not be all that much of a problem. The most significant challenge for me was remembering not to accidentally toggle between screens by touching the directional and menuing keys at bottom of the front panel on this device. And, it would have been nice if those three had been backlit.

Obviously...or maybe not so obviously...there is the pachyderm of the absence LTE capability in the room (HSPA 4+) but as a less than prolific user of mobile devices, that is not a major factor for me any more than the absence of NFC, which I have gotten along without pretty well with my current iPhone 5c. The device does support Bluetooth tethering and WLAN hotspot. Some may have reservations regarding the lower tier processor but I didn't encounter any significant issues with delays or skipping during streaming over Wifi thus far. I also don't spend a lot of time gaming either, so I suppose there might be the potential for issues for mobile device gaming fans.

The first thing that got my attention is the dual SIM card feature as I frequently travel internationally (okay, Canada but still...) and the ability to have two lines is a winner. The phone is configured for a nano and a mini although with an adapter the mini slot could be used for a micro card as well. While this version is represented to be limited to 8GB internal storage, in real terms I couldn't see where the user could actually access for than around 4.5GB. However, storage capacity is expandable up to 32GB with an SD card. The battery life is superior to my iPhone at around two days of moderate use and according to manufacturer specs, competitive with the Samsung Galaxy 5s. Brightness auto adjust left me unimpressed especially with the dark background in daylight conditions, but with the brightness set manually at the highest setting, it was usable.

The Life Play 2 Package is pretty good, including the phone, battery,  color coordinated hard silicone cover, screen protector, USB charging cable, AC jack, and ear plugs. The cover isn't going to do much for drops but it is better than nothing and based on my cursory investigations in local b/m stores and initial on line searches, there isn't a lot out there presently for protection of BLU devices. The phone has two external buttons, one for power and the other for volume (and also can be configured for the camera shutter release), a USB port and 3.5mm earphone jack. I was surprised to discover how much larger the display appeared in comparison to the iPhone 5c although in actual terms the screen is only negligibly larger. I don't watch a ton of video or movies via a mobile device and I don't expect to change my preferences with this one but the 1080p streaming impressive despite the somewhat less robust pixilation of the display.

The rear facing 8MP camera is...okay. There are a relatively wide range of camera settings available along with a zoom capability and flash but the Neanderthal in me still says if I intend to shoot photos or video, there's a specialized piece of equipment for that, not a mobile phone. If I didn't have a house full of devices specifically designed for Apple product compatibility, I probably would switch as there didn't seem to be a great deal of drop off from my 5c in a device that is comparatively speaking a price performer for a less intensive user of mobile device services.
profile.summary: A Rave and a Rant

profile.description: Portable 7" TFT LCD portable DVD, 16:9 widescreen, Plays DVD,DVR+R,DVD-R, MP3, CD, Play your favorite movie or listen to you favorite MP3 music or even look at your jpeg picture photos fany time or any place. Has an up to 2 hour rechargeable battery and comes with car adaptor and ac power supply. Simple and easy to operate, built in stereo speakers allows you to enjoy your movies and music wherever you are.
profile.reviewText:
And you better find an electrical outlet if you have any hopes of finding out what happened.  Most recently the screen collapsed to black while watching "Unstoppable," thus the title of this review. It's not the first time the battery lost its' luster at an inopportune time but in defense of the manufacturer, it was never represented to have more than a maximum 2 hour capacity. And admirably, after 3 years of regular use, battery degradation has been minimal.  The rub is 2 hours just isn't sufficient for a wide range of films. Philips has an upgraded model with much more reasonable battery life.

That said, this 7 - inch display portable DVD player has been a dependable performer when I was in situations where an outlet was available or the car adapter was sufficient(e.g. hotels, office, park shelters, road trips) and I wanted to watch a movie, music videos or play mp3's or CDs.  Unlike newer models the screen lacks a swivel feature but the picture remains precise and clear.

Excluding powering on and off, the remote control can be used for all features and I have yet to replace that battery.  Not surprisingly, audio reproduction  is only passable but external systems can be used via the a/v  or headphone jacks.

It would not be my first choice in today's market but if one is available at an attractive price, it's worth the money...as long as your viewing window is under two hours.
profile.summary: The locomotive barreling toward the curve carrying way too much speed...

profile.description: Innovative design of the Case Logic Kontrast DSLR Zoom Holster makes it easier than ever to access your camera with zoom lens.
profile.reviewText:
Another thoughtfully designed product from CaseLogic, this time with a feature I haven't seen before with DSLR cases. The padded interior also includes a hammock system for insertion of the zoom lens and secure suspension of the attached camera body. The velcro locked hammock will not only accommodate full size DSLRs but also allow this case to be used with smaller body hybrids and bridge cameras that have a changeable lens feature.

In addition to three exterior pockets and one interior pocket for smaller form factor accessories like cords, additional batteries, SD cards, filters, etc. the water resistant case also has a hard shell base providing free standing stability and also adds another degree of protection for the lens from those inadvertent bumps and bruises that couldn't possibly happen yet always seem to occur.
profile.summary: A glorious hole...in the hammock.

profile.description: Universal waterproof phone case dry bag fits all smartphones up to 6.0" diagonal size (Certain big screen phones need to remove protective case); Credit card wallet money waterproof dry bag for beach, fishing, swimming, boating, kayaking, snorkeling and water park activities Clear Window on both front and back sides, perfect for taking pictures, videos and checking emails 100 feet IPX8 Certified waterproof; Offers waterproof / snowproof / dirtproof protection for your device while maintaining full touch screen functionality Compatible with devices up to 100mm x 170mm (clear window 70mm X 140mm); Comes with a neck strap for convenient carrying Features a simple snap and lock access, easy to keep out water, snow, dust, sand, and dirt
profile.reviewText:
This case proved to perform a lot more impressively than I expected when I opened the thinner white plastic case it came in, although if you were caught in a bind the clear front plastic packaging with the zip lock seal would probably get the job done as well, it just doesn't appear to be as durable over the longer term, but it's better than a freezer bag...

The Kindz Waterproof case enclosure is large enough to accommodate an iPhone with an otterbox defender case. I'm still not sure I would want to go as far as proclaiming it waterproof; highly water resistant is probably the more accurate description. It works as represented but I'm sure how well it would stand up to severe conditions like going down a water slide. Why you would take the phone with you on the slide to start with is another discussion.

Manipulation of the device touch screen is degraded due to the thickness of the clear front cover of the protective case but I don't see that as a significant issue since I think the objective is to protect the device from water, sand or dust in outdoor conditions and removal from the case when necessary is not an inconvenience. This Kindz case package also includes a lanyard with a removal snap clasp providing a couple of different options for usability and transportation.

I didn't want to place my iPhone in peril immediately, so I tested permeability with a less precious (to me) 5.0 in. display mobile phone it in a bucket of water. It turned out I forgot about it and it stayed in the bucket for 24 hours without any indication of seal failure, so naturally, I tried the same thing, this time intentionally, with the white plastic bag the product case came in.

It didn't fail either although I admit if placed under stress the vacuum seal would be more likely to fail than the clasp lock of the actual product.

I received a sample for evaluation.
profile.summary: A case and a spare.

profile.description: High-end high-resolution monitor headphones that reproduce even the most subtle nuances of the source sound. In addition to mixing and recording in the studio, the HPH-MT7 headphones are perfect for mix monitoring in live performance applications thanks to their high sound pressure levels and durability.
profile.reviewText:
No BS review:

Preferences for headphones will vary, often based on genres the perspective purchaser most frequently listens to. I think this is a very good set of headphones, but I really couldn't say how well they might meet the needs of potential buyers who do intend to use them for mixing. They perform well across the spectrum, however, if one is seeking heavier bass tones, an equalizer /device/app/program is going to be required. I'll be using these at home and only using the higher price point yet IMO lesser performing Bose QC25's for travel.

Start of an all BS review (before I wondered why):

So, after a couple of weeks of use and comparison to other closed back headphones I have (most notably a set of Bose QC25s and a decent set of inexpensive Sentey Thorx headphones), switching off and replaying the same tracks (among them Herbie Hancocks Headhunters, Audra McDonalds Build a Bridge, Al Jarreaus Roof Garden, Miles Davis Tutu, Alicia Keys If I Aint Got You,  RTFs Sorceress, EWFs Reasons, Weather Reports Black Market , Traffics Low Spark, and a handful more) with splitters, in some cases from multiple formats (CD, MP3, M4a, .aiff, FLAC, SACD, Vinyl, Streaming), sourced from laptops, full blown A/V receivers, iPhone, Hi Resolution music player, I finally felt prepared to sit down and write a review of my evaluation of these Studio Monitor (as opposed to  reference) headphones.

I got all my audio review clichs cleaned up for use (harmonics, pitch, frequency range, colorization, timbre, mid-range response, separation, clarity, static, reverberation, bass enhancement, flat tonality, brand consistent tuning) because in the end, its all about the sound.

Yes, overall build quality is very good, including larger than customarily used 45 mm drivers. The headband is adjustable for inflated audiophile noggins, the faux leather earcups fully envelope my ears and tend to provide a degree of noise isolation. Over several extended sessions of an hour or more, while the headset is noticeably heavier than my Bose headphones, I didn't feel any discomfort or any degree of pressure, although I should be noted, I haven't with most headphones Ive owned.

The package includes two quality cords (1.2m Coiled cable, 3.0m Straight cable)  with 3.5 mm connectors and a convenient  adapter as well as a draw string closure soft faux leather case.
profile.summary: Just an unsophisticated music lover, I suppose.

profile.description: 2011 collection from the three-time Grammy-award winning singer/songwriter, New York Times Best-selling poet, and critically acclaimed actress. This compilation contains previously unreleased tracks that Jill recorded during her time with the Hidden Beach label.
profile.reviewText:
I don't know how many times I looked at this album but couldn't pull the trigger or more accurately, press the mouse button because in my psyche to purchase it felt like a violation of a  - unilateral and unknown to her - covenant  with the irrepressible Ms. Scott, a betrayal. Yet, not having it in my collection left a vacuum that I had to confront whenever I decided to open my Jill vault and that occurs with a frequency not duplicated with nearly any other artist.

I'm glad I finally relented. As she swoons at the fade out of Running Away, resistance is futile...I listen to 'Collaborations,' 'The Real Thing' and to a lesser extent, 'The Light Of The Sun.' All have selected tunes that bring a glow to the visage but in totality, none of those releases lift me in the same manner as `Who is...,' `Experience' and most especially, `Beautifully Human.' These are the missing tracks from Experience. I have no idea why Jill and Hidden Beach decided to keep these cuts in mothballs because all of them soar. This is the Jill who brought butterflies the first time I heard her and continues to do so with that silky, sensuous voice.

Really, there isn't a weak track here and when you give a listen, you'll know the best feature of audio equipment is the repeat loop option.
profile.summary: Thank you and damn you, Hidden Beach...

Unbox it, and then OtterBox it with the tough and rugged Defender Series case for iPhone 5c. OtterBox Defender Series for iPhone 5cView larger View larger Multi-Layer Protection Three layers of rugged protection come together in the Defender Series case for iPhone 5c, enhancing every innovative feature and complementing the design language of this device. From a drop onto the asphalt to a toss across the living room by a temper tantrum-throwing toddler, we thought of all of those 'worst-case scenarios' you may encounter when we designed this case. A Case Made For Everyone The Defender Series consumer has an active lifestyle, works in harsh environments, is rough with his or her phones, or is just plain clumsy. For anyone who's broken a phone and wants the most protection possible '” the Defender Series
profile.reviewText: While the overall quality of this case may not be up to the standards I have come to expect from Otterbox, it remains a good value and prominently recommendable option for protection of a relatively pricey piece of electronics. The one major criticism I have of it is the screen protector is near to worthless as it provides very little resistance to dust accumulation and may serve as a annoyance for many users when keying on the phone. In fact, I am so underwhelmed by the level of screen protection provided in the built in protector that I also use a pressure sensitive protector underneath it. It reduces the sensitivity to touch even more, but is a trade off I'm willing to make since I would find a damaged screen even more of an aggravation.
profile.summary: Frustrating me screen protection

profile.description: GreenWorks G-24 24V cordless compact drill with 1/2" keyless Chuck & 2 Speed operation - tool only. The GreenWorks 24V system offers durable & versatile handheld tools ranging from outdoor power equipment to power tools. If you're building a deck, clearing debris from your yd or tackling overgrown weeds & hedges, there's a tool for every task.
profile.reviewText:
About quite a few things:

- The manufacturer. Although it has apparently developed a degree of visibility on this site, the products do not appear readily available in the usual suspect brick and mortar national Home Improvement stores.

- The price. Measured against comparable models from manufacturers I am familiar with this drill seems reasonably priced with consideration to features and promoted capabilities but I still wonder if it is really a lesser quality product with an inflated price depending on buyer subliminal acquiescence to environmental consciousness.

-The lithium ion batteries. This is my first power tool with something other than NiCad (or a cord), and the thought the package includes two 24V 2.0 Ah batteries at the current price point because you are going to need them to do anything substantive.

- Long term durability of the tool. It feels lightweight and thus far comfortable to use but I haven't dropped it on the driveway yet so we'll see.

I haven't placed any significant demands on it yet, only using it to drill a couple of holes in some drywall and attaching a sanding wheel to it to brighten up some plastic headlight covers and really I could have accomplished either of those tasks with a screwdriver, hammer and a sanding block, hopefully not getting the order reversed. Maybe I'll loan it to an acquaintance roofer who does real work but he might get the snazzy green body dirty.

Like most drills today, this " keyless chuck compact drill makes changing bits a simple task. It also has a 24 position clutch and is rated to deliver up to 498lbs torque from the higher of  two available speed settings. As noted, thus far I haven't needed to crank up the torque or even ramp up the speed to anything near the published maximum rate of 1700rpm. The built-in base positioned LED light, which is not a  feature with any of my present tools will come in handy in tight locations where manipulating a flashlight or getting sufficient illumination can be frustrating.

The batteries, delivered with a partial charge, are easily attachable to the bottom of the drill or the included battery charger, when necessary.  As noted a full charge did take about 45 minutes. It should be noted conventional wisdom indicates lithium ion batteries should not be fully depleted before recharging but recent studies have suggested they may in fact have similar memory tendencies as NiMH and NiCad so I suppose for the time being, the user has to make the call. They should not be stored in locations susceptible to either extremely high heat or cold and can be expected to last for two to three years under moderate use and charge cycles. It is also represented these batteries will not drain significantly if left sitting unused for extended time frames.

The Greenworks deal also includes an attachable metal belt clip, a dual head screwdriver bit that can be stored on the body of the drill and  a carrying/storage case that will accommodate the drill, the charger, both batteries and has enough room for me to include medium sized drill bit and screwdriver bit sets.

In any event, presently I'm quite pleased with the drill and dependent on the course of future experience, this review will be updated accordingly.
profile.summary: Just a tinge of doubt

profile.description: Mepra's The Luxury Art' is upmarket brand for an upscale audience, is a truly unique range of flatware and tableware. It is made of Stainless steel. It is Dishwasher safe. It has greater control over cooking temperatures. It allows gentle cooking with little water and fat for more wholesome and flavorful food. It is suitable for all types of hobs except induction hobs.
profile.reviewText:
While I like this pot and I realize a segment of the potential market for it will be effusive in praise of it, I cant say that I have noticed any features that lead me to believe it is so demonstrably superior to our primary use stainless steel cookware (Anolon Nouvelle Copper) that I find the price of this pot (at the current price point) to be fully justifiable. Including the cost of a lid, this single pot is more expensive than a 10 piece set of the comparably performing Anolon.

 I also readily admit Im metrically challenged so with the pot listed as 20cm casserole size, I didn't have a firm idea of the actual size of the pot until I got it. I associate centimeters with inches so with a skillet it may have meant more to me but a pot I  relate to liters or minimally, milliliters.  Its about the size of a 3-quart pot, suitable for sauces and the like for us but not large enough for most casserole dishes we typically serve.

Whereas our Anolon stainless steel pans have a base construction of a copper core encapsulated by two layers of aluminum and a stainless steel cap, the tri-ply Mepra pot has an aluminum core surrounded by two layers of stainless steel. Both designs seem to heat equally as well, can be used at lower cooking temperatures and are suitable for use on multiple heating surfaces.

The Mepra pot is visually appealing in what I would consider to be a traditional shape however the lip or rim isn't particularly convenient for pouring sauces. The pot feels somewhat weighty but not to the extent it is challenging to use.  As with most stainless steel cookware, heat is transferred to the riveted handles and use of oven mitts or gloves is incumbent. The pot is dishwasher safe for those who wish to cleanse in that manner. One minor concern for us is how susceptible the interior of this pot tends to be to scratching with the use of metal utensils.

Another thing I am somewhat ambivalent about is the stainless steel lid (not included but available from Mepra for around ninety dollars). It is form fitting and provides a tight seal but definitely seems overpriced to me. The lid handles are welded rather than riveted although Im not sure that will make that much of a difference with appropriate care.
profile.summary: Must be what the leprechaun keeps his stash in.

profile.description: Luxurious Geoffrey Beene 100% pure silk charmeuse pajama pant features an elasticized waist with silk drawstring, two side seam pockets and covered button thru fly. Give the gift of comfortable luxury.
profile.reviewText:
These bottoms are nearly nice enough to encourage me to wear pajamas to bed. Almost.

They are fantastic for lying around reading before bedtime or to don once you decide to drag yourself out of bed the following morning. Theyre comfortable and extremely lightweight, so much so it feels like your walking around nude.

The finish is good, I haven't noticed any fraying around seams or flaws in stitching. Typically, a large size denotes a waist size of 36 to 38 inches and this pair, with an elasticized waist and drawstring, corresponds to those dimensions. However, they are also high rise (about 13 inches) so despite a typical inseam of 30 in, as far as effective length is concerned, they may have to be worn above the natural waist by shorter purchasers.  If worn lower, the single button fly becomes somewhat of a joke.

Like many silk products, hand washing is suggested although thats not going to happen with me. Well see how well they hold up after being subjected to the washer delicate cycle and line drying.
profile.summary: Half an elegant ninja

profile.description: The DEEBOT DM82 is a powerful floor cleaning robot that replaces your broom for bare-floor cleaning and helps out with routine carpet vacuuming. It is easy to operate, lasts up to 150 minutes per charge, and cleans up with a powerful suction motor that includes a Max mode for even deeper cleaning. The DM82 has intelligent standard features such as stair safety technology, obstacle detection technology, 4 cleaning modes, automatic recharge, and daily scheduling.
profile.reviewText:
The grown up around here refuses to allow me to have a drone copter because she says Im not responsible enough. If I get an R/C car or boat, she says I have to give it to the grandkid, BUT I can play with a robot vacuum and theres not a heck of a lot she can do about without subjecting herself to some mundane tasks. This is our first robotic unit.  Actually, Ive been curious about them for a while but not so much that I was willing to pay full price for one so it was propitious when this one sort of dropped onto the flooring surfaces.

Now, assuming I would have been willing to lay out my money for any of them, with consideration of my tendency to research a product until all the joy in acquisition has been squeezed out of it, based on consumer resource reviews of other models from this manufacturer I came across, Im pretty certain Deebot models would not have made my short list. After playingI mean usingthe DM82 for about a month, Im happy to say overlooking it would have been an egregious error.

Obviously, I cant really speak to the utility of Roombas and Neatos, among numerable competitive models in the same price range or beyond, but after observing the performance this unit if the others are significantly superior, good on them.  Unquestionably, there are a few quirks with the DM82 but the benefit gained far outweighs the shortcomings.

It didn't take long to determine we would need to 'vacuumproof' the level of the house where it would be most often used.  My cord management system has been 'If cant see it so its not a problem' and, 'if that area rug slipped, its because you walk funny.' Both of those scenarios can typically bring this unit to a grinding halt. It is not a replacement for a deep cleaning vacuum, particularly with deep pile carpeting but when set to a regularly scheduled daily routine- assignable via the included remote - it will obviate the need to regularly sweep or vacuum other floor surfaces.  Im also not sure it would stand up to the challenges presented by pet breeds that are heavy shedders although for this type of appliance it has a convenient, spacious, easily removable dust collection bin. The replaceable dual stage filtering system housed within the collection bin is also easily accessible.

 Primarily, we have hardwood floors, tiled areas with low pile area rugs or runners scattered about, and our canine resident is not a major shedder. Under those conditions, we haven't had the need to pull out another vacuum unit for the pertinent coverage area since the Deebot was placed into operation.  In comparison to other vacuum types (and from what I have seen published regarding other robot units), it is comparatively quiet.

 While not measured by me, I would speculate under the normal setting, it has a noise level of less than 56db. Even at the higher cleaning power setting, the increase in noise is minimal. I think potential buyers who live in multiple unit environments would find this model to be a good choice in that regard since as far as I can tell no matter what mode it is set to, the unit is going to continue to run until it is shut down by the user or in auto cleaning, the battery is drained to the point it needs to shut down itself and return to the charging station.

The Lithium-ion battery housed in the unit is represented by the manufacturer as being capable of providing up to 150 minutes of cleaning time on a charge but I have watched the vacuum putter around for up to 165 minutes over hardwood and lower pile area carpets before attempting to find its way back to the charging basewhich can be an epic adventure. The charging base is lightweight so the vacuum tends to push it around until it is wedged against a wall (or in our case, the very less frequently used stick broom style vacuum that now sits behind it) in the attempt to mount it.

 The unit can be assigned variable cleaning modes (automatic, single room, spot cleaning, edge cleaning) via the infrared remote, however,  beyond the spot cleaning  this thing doesnt seem to have a consistent cleaning pattern, most often wandering around like an underage drunk freshman on the last leg of a pub crawl in haphazard search of his/ her dormitory. I suppose in open floor plan homes, it might be less of a quest but if it is outside the room where the charging unit is located, getting back to the base seems to be like the search for Jimmy Hoffas body.  One minor aggravation is, although the instructions illustrate how to disable daily scheduling via the remote, my remote cannot be set to 00:00 so to preclude the vacuum starting up at a set time period, it has to be powered off on the unit itself. Fortunately, the device will continue to recharge while mounted on the charging base and powered off.

 The unit seems least effective in picking up weightier particles such as gravel or grit.  Thus far, we haven't had any unfortunate incidents at a staircase although it has on occasion struggled to climb a one-inch door sill into another room. Our solution is to_close_the_door since despite what you might think the single room setting in actual operation means the Deebot has to be confined to a single room.

In spot cleaning mode, the unit automatically adjusts to maximum power and circles around like a dog chasing its tail (maximum power can also be initiated in any mode via the remote).  The DM82 with a combination of optical sensing and light touch bumper is very good at negotiation around obstacles like chairs, desks and efficiently navigates under beds and raised furniture. In corners or other locations where dust may accumulate the two front mounted spin brushes (extra set included) work very well.
profile.summary: If all else fails, it could serve as a beverage caddy

profile.reviewText:
As one of the idiosyncratic crowd  who cant seem to fall asleep without a duvet or something pulled up to my nose, even in the heat of summer flannel sheets are a welcome compromise with the other person in the bed who prefers to sleep with a tornado strength fan blowing all night. These Ashley sheets also work as a compromise for the frilly versus subtle argument that also seems to dominate our discussions of bedroom dcor. profile.reviewText:
When you feel the anticipation growing for receipt of a rather commonplace decorating item, it just might be time to take personal inventory. I had a defined plan for this understated, tasteful flat black composite wood frame. The build quality is good and overall the product impresses me as a reasonable alternative to more expensive customized art shop merchandise.

With space for a photo array of three 4"x 6" prints, the matted backgrounds of slate, sea mist green and white should work with most decors. The kit includes spacers that give the layout depth and somewhat of a 3D effect. As a result of the use of spacers, mounted prints have to be taped.  Based on design and configuration of the photo slots, I thought landscape prints would work best for me, with the frame hung in vertical orientation. I also noticed the distributor has compatible frames in other shapes and I intend to purchase a couple of them as well.

Yeah, I know we shouldn't talk about shipping issues or damages in a review but I'm going to anyway. Actually, the first thought I had when I started unpeeling the cocoon encasing this frame was the old egg drop science project. It seemed to have more layers of protection than CDC isolation lab so of course by the time I managed to liberate it I discovered a hairline fracture in the glass pane. In my opinion, with the amount of thought that went into packaging, this one had to have been damaged beforehand and the damage was inadvertently overlooked.

Anyway, I now have what I consider to be a placeholder frame because I like it so much I decided to hang it with cracked, super glued glass pending receipt of a replacement frame from the distributor, which they graciously offered.

And, they have a new customer.
profile.summary: Time for me to get a life

profile.reviewText:
If it seems like the marketplace is saturated with compact Bluetooth speakers, it's probably because it is,  but this is one shouldn't be overlooked if you can find it for a reasonable price. No, it isn't the most impressive in terms of audio quality or overall functionality however it has some relatively attractive features.

First of all, it is a water resistant rather than waterproof device so usage in the shower area, at beaches, or around pools is less of a concern if you happen to be as clumsy as I seem to have become. While the speaker is capable of floating, it is not fully immersible as the 3.5mm jack outlet doesn't appear to be sufficiently sealed to block all substances in the event of longer term immersion. With the attached suction cup the speaker can be somewhat securely mounted on non-porous although I did have a few instances where adhesion failed and it went tumbling down. To my surprise and relief, the hard plastic outer shell was not damaged.

The Bluetooth function works well. I didn't precisely measure streaming distance but I'm sure the proclaimed effective range of 10 meters was easily surpassed with loss of signal. I wasn't particularly impressed with sound quality; I have other single speaker units of similar size and specifications where tonality is better but I can't plop them on the bathroom tiles either. Overall playtime between charges is pretty good and recharge time isn't intolerable coming in at right around three hours. I do wish there was an AC option in addition to the USB cord which BTW, has a 3.5mm RCA plug rather than the micro USB connectors many similar units feature. The speaker also supports mobile phone calls and SIRI for IOS devices.

I received a sample for evaluation.
profile.summary: Despite what you might believe, Singing in shower doesn't make you sound better.

profile.description: Tiny tear bottom DJ. Pages are clean and bright and binding is tight. Solid Book.
profile.reviewText:
I think the best science fiction compels you to contemplate the possibilities. With THE LIGHT OF OTHER DAYS, Arthur C. Clarke and Stephen Baxter have written a book that is terrifying.

My humanities-based education does not offer the expertise to determine if the 'hard sci-fi' component of the book is adequate or accurate enough for those who focus on that aspect of the genre. My primary concern is not to have my luggage suspended in the time/space continuum. OTHER DAYS is speculative social commentary in the most classical sense, set not too far in the future. It poses the question of the exigencies relating to the elimination of all privacy, where the only security from your peers' inquisitiveness is non-verbalization of one's thoughts and considerations. It looks at a world where the very basis of everything we believe about religion, morality, government, politics and any other aspect of man's existence past or present, is open to intensive scrutiny, by anyone with the initiative to look. A society where trust is no longer an issue, it is an irrelevancy because truth is the only realistic alternative.

Neither the premise nor the story are flawless. The characters are not well developed; the vision is that of Clarke and Baxter and represents but one possibility. Devout Christians may be troubled by some sections. Yet, for me this is a tale of the human spirit, a story that must be considered in the context of existent technological advances that inexorably adjust our values.
profile.summary: Who is watching me write this...and why?

I picked up these gloves specifically for use with a snowblower so I haven't given them a fair workout yet but if they are as magical -and I fervently hope they are -  as the snowblower proved to be in warding off snowfall when I received it as a gift a few years back, I will not be returning to update this review. Regardless, this heavyweight set is also a great choice to leave in the car for potential emergency situations.  The gloves are constructed of a quality grade of cowhide and all of the seams appear securely stitched. The seam running the length of the glove along the index finger is thoughtfully double stitched as that is a prime point for stress.

I received the large size which fits snugly yet comfortably. While surprisingly flexible for a leather product geared towards outdoor work in colder conditions, I think with a short break in period the gloves will eventually fit...like a glove. profile.description: Working-class Alice (Academy Award nominee Alfre Woodard) and wealthy Charlotte (Academy Award winner Kathy Bates) are friends and mothers who have supported each other through all that their families have gone through over the years. But now their families are embroiled in new turmoil  with each other. Can the two women save their children from the dark secrets and dirty deeds that threaten to destroy them all?
profile.reviewText:
Because it is also pretty obvious he's putting out exactly the type of superficial movies that will not stand up to any amount of incisive consideration but will appeal to his targeted audience. Granted, compared to the majority of his movies that I have seen, this one is probably the best of a mediocre mix, but that doesn't make it worthwhile.

This time out, you have two family matriarchs, portrayed by two very talented actors, Alfre Woodward and Kathy Bates, from appreciatively distinct social, cultural and economic backgrounds who have nevertheless forged what appears to be a committed friendship over nearly 30 years.  Alice, Woodward's character is the `salt of the earth,' deeply religious, forgiving and non-judgmental which is fortunate since she is also the mother of a manipulative, self-absorbed thirty-something daughter (Sanaa Lathan) who is willing to do whatever she deems necessary to achieve her aspirations of upward mobility, including emasculation of her ambitious but patently nave husband (Rockmond Dunbar) by entering into an adulterous relationship with her employer (Cole Hauser) who conveniently also happens to be the back-stabbing, self-serving son of  Bates' character, Charlotte.

It is feasible that Perry intended to subtly comment on historical objectification of Black women by white oppressors because Cartwright, at his lecherous best also shows more than passing interest in Robin Given's character, a no nonsense COO brought into the company by his mother as direct threat to her son's quest to usurp the corporate chairperson position, but that's way more credit than I am willing to proffer.

Also in the recipe there are the strong-willed, family oriented yet curiously childless other Woodward daughter (Taraji P. Henson), wife of the grounded, dedicated hard-working, secure in life, Ben (Tyler Perry), and the introverted, non-confrontational wife (KaDee Strickland) of  Houser's character... and a homeless guy. It is made clear Charlotte doesn't trust or conceivably even like her son and she has no use for her ex-trailer trash parvenu daughter-in-law. It's a mystery to me why these two women, (Charlotte and Alice) are friends because although how they met is eventually brought to light, the friendship does not appear to have been particularly deep or reciprocal. Alice seems to know a great deal about Charlotte and her travails in life but at the same time, Charlotte isn't even aware Alice is a teetotaler.

Those factors and many others are revealed during  the girl buddy road trip Charlotte convinces Alice to take with her in a classic Coupe Deville, leaving the foibles of the homefront to take care of themselves, one of which is the nave husband trying to get funding from his employer (and his wife's lover) to start his own construction company, when it seems to me, unless one was cognizant of his spouse's intimacy with the potential benefactor, playing upon his mother-in-law's relationship with Charlotte, the actual owner of corporation, would have been a better course of action, or maybe applying for an SBA loan. I'm not even going to address why Lathan's character who clearly had little respect for her husband and is supposed to be a financial expert would choose to place her slush fund in a joint account. Those are at the bottom of the this doesn't make sense totem pole but to mention the more confounding issues would probably constitute spoilers.

In the end, this is a typical Perry movie. If his work has entertained in the past or if you're looking for a movie with an ostensibly uplifting message that in reality will not survive any contemplative scrutiny, you're in the right place. So, my five star rating is measured against other Perry films, not a wide range of films of similar plotlines, where my real assessment would be two stars.
profile.summary: I know, it's me, not Tyler Perry
