I have only minor complaints with frequency separation as I regularly have to drive in areas where significant interference is likely and it is rare I have to adjust the station signal. While sound reproduction is basically good, there are instances where I will encounter static however that might be a function of sourcing for the music files I created. Location memory is limited meaning when the car is turned off, the device will not remember positioning in the music track but will restart at the beginning of the track. During daylight hours, the digital readout is near to impossible to read and with consideration to size and character space, most often not really worth the effort but in my opinion that is a small trade-off. The remote is IR line of sight and seems like it has to be within inches of the device before signal transmission is recognized, another annoyance that you simply have to learn to accept. After all this time, muscle memory lets me hit the right keys on the remote without thinking about it, anyway. Thus far, even with what I consider to be extensive use, I haven't had the need to replace the unit's fuse, the battery in the remote or more critically from my perspective, replenish my supply car fuses as this device is dependable.
profile.summary: What? no color screen. This is unacceptable...

profile.description: Expand wireless coverage throughout your home or connect a wired device.
profile.reviewText: I would have found more enjoyment and lasting benefits wasting two unrecoverable hours of my life smoking than trying to get this thing to work. Yes,it's running and I'm sure my wireless devices can connect through it but beyond pure speculation I don't have any idea how it was eventually recognized on my network. All I know is I sacrificed every pawn I had on the board. The only aspect more useless than the CD setup program is the user manual on the very same CD. Well, that's somewhat inaccurate as the Linksys website must have been designed by a lover of Russian nesting dolls. It is consistent though. Both the copy of the manual on the CD and on the website open to pages that appear to be written in Arabic (I'm not being facetious) and your best bet is to scroll though the multiple copies until you identify a language you have some familiarity with, so long as the language you seek is not English. BTW, the quick launch pamphlet is pretty straightforward, it just has little relationship to what you're likely to encounter, so in reality it is truly best suited for fireplace kindling. For purposes of full disclosure (and fairness) I will admit I didn't follow step one to the installation procedure - placement of the device in close proximity to the router - opting to attempt installation with the extender located on another level and opposite side of the house, plugged into a surge protector next to a wireless doorbell. Yeah, guess what. The extender was recognized in under ten seconds and connection to the router D-Link Wireless AC 750 Mbps Home Cloud App-Enabled Dual-Band Broadband Router (DIR-810L) was initiated. I was prompted to enter my network password...and ten minutes later I received an error message installation could not be completed with the suggestion to check the Linksys webpages. So I duly copied the error code, pulled up the website and allowed my frustration to percolate. Failing to identify ANYTHING on the website that was remotely related to what looked to me to be an encumbrance a healthy percentage of users might encounter, I decided to press on, commencing with depression of the reset button. Naturally, there's no information about what to do anywhere but realistically, I'm sure many of us have been required to pull off the highway a fix a networking flat tire before. Start over. And yes, I am stubborn so I still didn't relocate the extender. This time, it cannot be recognized. Reset again. Okay, now it's recognized but only available signal is 5ghz which really isn't going to do much for the majority of my devices which remain at 2.4ghz. What the heck, let's do it anyway. Input network password again. And we're back to the error code that is not searchable on the website. See ya tomorrow. Okay. Let's color inside the lines. Move the device to near proximity to router. Check. Reset again just in case. Check. Commence installation. Same result. Well, there's an Ethernet cable, let's try that. Nothing. WPS button? Yep, another crash and burn. One more reset attempt before you give in and call support (which I will go to any lengths to avoid. I've had the experience of Cisco's call center before and I was not enthused). Start the setup program again. Wait, it doesn't see the 2.4 broadcast. Refresh...refresh...refresh...there it is. Oh, wait, it's asking for an ID AND PASSWORD FOR THE EXTENDER. No one said anything about that...OR PROVIDED ONE. Admin/Admin maybe? Well, that didn't work. Device still taking too long to respond... Okay, last attempt. What? Installation successful? Problem is, after all the courting, the marriage isn't all that exciting. Checking signal strengths via the router address, accessibility in a couple of challenging areas in my house is actually better without the extender and it seems some other devices on 2.4ghz like a microwave and the aforementioned wireless doorbell negatively impact this extender more so than they affect other devices in the same generalized area. I'm going to have a smoke... Oh, yeah. The MAC address hidden under the plug doesn't match what is appearing via security program network mapping or on the router device info pages. Figures... Maybe one day I'll have the inspiration to figure out how to set it up with dual bands...right after I complete my Arabic course.
profile.summary: The only range really extended is your patience.

top_5.description: Old Mother Hubbard Fruit Ins Natural Dog Treats, Honey Apple & Bacon Recipe are wholesome, all natural dog treats made in USA only and made with two unique textures
top_5.reviewText:
So, I sampled three varieties of the Old Mother Hubbard treats:

-Old Mother Hubbard Gourmet Goodies Crispers Parmesan & Bacon Natural Crunchy
-Old Mother Hubbard Gourmet Goodies Soft Bakes Carrot & Pumpkin Natural Soft
-Old Mother Hubbard Gourmet Goodies Fruit'ins Honey, Oatmeal & Blueberries

No, really.

It should be noted with the 3rd listed treat, I was expecting to receive the Honey, Apple and Bacon (which I was personally looking forward to) but stuff happens. Anyway, I cant depend on the mutt to be a credible evaluator because so far as I can recall the only things hes ever turned down are green beans (classic cut), and pork or kidney beans. Hes not a big fan of salt and vinegar potato chips either, but he will reluctantly accept them if followed by a bowl of ice coffee, but I digress

As it turns out, just about the same time as I received the treats, my owner was also trying to convince me to substitute my normal breakfast fare of powdered donuts with some Belvita blueberry biscuits so it also seemed like the perfect opportunity to compare ingredients. She wasn't real pleased when I pointed out if you look at the sugar content of the human intended biscuit as contrasted with the absence of the same in the dog variety, the canine product is the winner of the healthier product ribbon by a wide margin.

Individually, the Parmesan & Bacon treat isn't bad, kind of reminiscent of a Zwieback teething biscuit (oh, come on. I got grandkids) but the bacon is not very discernible. The soft bake carrot and pumpkin however, is another story. Its neither soft nor is it all that tasty.

Now, the Honey, Oatmeal & Blueberry cookie; that one might become a regular. It looks like a fig newton with a considerably harder crusty exterior. It isn't particularly sweet which should be expected as apparently dog consumption of sugar is a bigger deal than my ingestion of sugar is for Belvita.

Doesnt seem to matter, though. Whichever treats I toss into my pocket as we (me and the mutt) go on our excursions, he lopes off to do what dogs do, then comes galloping back to await his reward.

Most of the time by the he gets back, I still have some of his treats left.
top_5.summary: Um, that's not the cookie jar.

top_5.description: Challenge friends and family to a friendly game of Atomic Jumpball Basketball Shootout. Including four mini basketballs and an inflating air pump, this game includes electronic, infrared eyes for accurate scoring and a timer for two players. The 1 " steel tubing offers stability. The Atomic Jumpball Basketball Shootout measures 106" L x 45" W x 89" H.
top_5.reviewText:
No, not to cover it but to protect the car it has displaced in the garage, or it may serve as an entirely specious reason to move. For any indoor space with less than 10 foot ceilings, this thing is a no go. Needless to say, theres intellectual comprehension and then theres reality.  I looked at the dimensions, I knew there was no way it would work with low ceiling basement but all I thought about was my grandson would love ithe does and Id like him to love it at his mothers house where there is even less space to accommodate it.

 It is too cold right now in our garage to have any marathon arcade style competitions unless we also want to see how well the players do while attempting to beat the opposition and the clock under the effects of vehicle induced carbon monoxide oxygen deprivation but summer isn't going to a marked improvement for game play indoors because the overhang of the open garage door blocks shooting angles as well. But enough of my shortsighted problems

The game itself is loads of fun, although I do wonder how long the euphoria will last before I decide to deconstruct and restore the rightful fossil fueled occupant to primacy.  It took a while to put it together because its really a two person job and the only other immediately available body in my household was too busy carping about the silliness of it to offer any assistance (I guess I wasn't finished with my personal issues) but with some creativity in stabilizing it (think bungee cords) I got it done. Its actually sturdier than it appears when you first look at the configuration and support tubing and at this price point appears to be a good alternative to some pricier comparable models.

 The electronic controls are located on the rear panel which is somewhat of an inconvenience, especially for younger future hoop stars as a chair or step ladder will be required for resets/ restarts and I do have some concerns over that if they are allowed to play unmonitored. Youll probably need an extension cord which in some situations like mine might be an additional safety hazard, but obviously not the fault of the game. The set comes with four balls and an air pump but I would like to see if I can get a few more to reduce the jockeying to grab returns.
top_5.summary: It should come with a tarp

top_5.description: We love all things Scandinavian, from chefs to naturalists to cookbooks. The Modern Farmhouse collection evokes the best of modern Scandinavian design in rustic but sophisticated colors and a smart shape for easy stacking. Dishwasher-safe, microwave-safe and oven-safe. Service for four includes four 10.5 dinner plates, four 9 salad plates, four 6.5 (16 oz) all purpose bowls and four 12 oz mugs. Includes a booklet of Food & Wine favorite recipes.
top_5.reviewText:
Upon unwrapping, I was mildly surprised and at the same time pleased to discover the product page description of the porcelain flame colored dinnerware had planted an image in my mind not borne out by the actual color of the product. This set is much closer to my idea of a coral hue so I suppose if the comparison is to a malfunctioning natural gas flame, yeah, it is flame colored.

 Another misconception, this time brought about by sneaking a peek at other reviews, was the plates might present some dishwasher loading problems. Again, for some that might prove to be an issue due to the high lip on dinner and salad plates but I didn't have any problems as it appears the wider spaced prongs on our dishwasher rack allow for easy loading. It should be noted, the pieces are also microwave safe.

The plates are substantial, both in circumference and heft. Evidently, we lucked out again as our kitchen cabinets have  just barely  enough depth to accommodate these 10.5 dinner plates.  I don't think anyone will have to worry about having to overfill as your loading up for a holiday buffet dinner. We can easily substitute the salad plates for most meals. Another thing I like about this set is the 12oz. mugs were designed with real coffee drinkers in mind. With most of our china sets, the cups are good enough for a lungo shot but not nearly the size I need to get myself together most mornings.

The only minor negative Ive noticed thus far relates to the cereal bowls. Im sure for most potential buyers, they are sufficiently sized but if your morning routine includes half a box of frosted flakes sopping in whole milk, you're going to have to stick with a mixing bowl or adjust to having several refills of these bowls.
top_5.summary: Are you dieting? Your plate looks so empty.

top_5.description: End the day as strong as you started in Carhartt fastest-drying, odor-fighting gear.
top_5.reviewText:
Yeah, I know. I need to re-tool my thinking. But, I will not be wearing this hooded sweatshirt when I use a wrench to turn the requisite bolts. Ive always associated the Carhartt brand with quality made, dependable and durable clothing items you can wear into a crawl space and not worry about a wayward nail grabbing onto it and requiring a search and rescue team to free you.

This hoodie is fine, for the white hardhats standing at the perimeter gathering information to write you up later. The blended polyester fabric is soft and feels somewhat luxuriant. The hoodie impresses me as accurately sized and comfortable to wear. It seems to continue the Carhartt tradition of meticulously crafted merchandise but this one is not intended for those who anticipate getting in some dirt, beyond carrying around a leaf (electric) blower on a cool autumn morning.

 Well have to see what happens when some motor oil is inadvertently smeared on a cuff.

top_5.description: Fashion Unisex Computer Glasses- Anti-reflective ,Anti-glare ,Clear Lens, Uv Protection (Amber)
top_5.reviewText:
Despite a barely resistible urge to go down to the borough building and apply for a name change to Poindexter, I find myself mildly surprised to admit these glare reducing computer glasses have helped with eye fatigue after spending extended hours in front of a monitor. input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "TANDY LEATHER FACTORY-Split Key Rings. Spring steel split rings are perfect for using with leather shapes and key fobs. This package contains ten 1 inch nickel rings. Made in USA.". The summary of the review text is "Excited about... key rings. Seriously.".
output:
I never thought I would write a review about something as trivial as a key ring, but that was before I discovered how nice a key ring can be.

We've all seen them. We've all used them. Up until buying these, I can't recall EVER buying key rings. They've always come with the key. Whether it's a car, an apartment, a set of handcuffs: I've never been handed a key a la carte.

But this brings me back to the ubiquity of the key ring: we've all been disappointed with them. I don't know how many times I've cursed a bent key ring for losing an important key. The thing was that I always had another key laying around that I wasn't using so I could scavenge, what I assumed, was the only kind of key ring out there: sucky ones.

Then one day I mauled my car's key ring and I thought, "somebody should sell key rings, not just things that come with keys with rings attached."

Like all things I think should be sold, I looked it up on Amazon... and key rings be boughteth.

These things are built very strong and I doubt I'll be bending them like all the other junky rings I've suffered for more than thirty years. They're chromed, and like anything else I can see myself in, they just look good.

Do yourself a favor and replace all those junky sucky key rings you've got laying around with these things. I never appreciated how nice a simple strong ring of metal containing unknown levels of Chinese carcinogens could be. Not only will your keys be securely ringed, but you'll be able to attach rings to all sorts of things.

Thumb drives? Check.

Water bottles? Check.

Three ring binders? Why not four? F-it and check it.

At this price, every key in my house will have it's own ring.

profile.reviewText:
This is a fine case for traveling with your tablet. It is constructed of quality materials with plenty of high quality and heavy duty protection, and it is large enough to store a Samsung Note 8.0 tablet in the main compartment and a full-size folding Bluetooth keyboard in the pocket. Not quite enough room to also store a charger, but I've never found myself using one while traveling, anyway.

The case firmly holds the tablet in a landscape perspective, and if your turn the case over you have multiple viewing angles... pretty slick. The anchors for the tablet are thinner than the bezel of the Note 8.0, so it doesn't interfere with any of the functions of thhe tablet. All keys are readily accessible, the screen is stable enough to use the S-pen, and the viewing angles are comfortable in any situation from using it on a table, in bed or on an airplane's folding tray table.

Another bonus is that the case amplifiies and deepens the sound coming from the Note 8.0's speakers a little bit. I usually wear headphones, so this is a minor bonus, but I thought it was pretty cool.

That capacity and protection also contributes to the case's main fault: it's just too big for most daily users. This is a case for traveling: throw it in your suitcase or backpack and go to your flight without much concern. You can toss it on the x-ray machine without worry. You can drop your luggage without concern. You could probably even throw your tablet like a Frisbee and come out golden as long as you weren't playing against a wall or on concrete.

But it's too big for an office person, and the brown tweed is not that attractive in professional settings, unless you're a college professor with suede patches on the elbows of your 1972 sports jacket.

That being said, I LOVE suede elbow patches, worn fedora hats and even houndstooth. My problem with the fabric is that it's not the gray illustrated in the photos, but rather a very brown brown. If you know how to wear suits, you know that gray goes with everything: it's the complete absense of color.

Brown, on the other hand? It's too casual unless its leather, which this is not.

Traveling or carting your tablet around in a backpack: A+

Professional environments or keeping your tablet in a well-organized attache that already provides good protection: C-. Wrong color. Wrong size. Overkill protection.

Overall: a solid B performer.
profile.summary: While the color is off, the quality is good.

profile.description: This is the maintenance product manufacturers recommend most! Only '303' beautifies as intensely, protects as powerfully or lasts as long. This provides powerful UV screening protection for colored gel-coat fiberglass, inflatable boats, vinyl, clear vinyl windows, rubber, plastics and leather.? Just spray on and wipe dry!? Treated surfaces repel dirt, soiling, staining, water spots, salt water and mildew. Note: Each bottle of 303 is sold separately.
profile.reviewText:
PROs

- Great product for a good price.
- Painlessly restores exterior black plastics.
- Doesn't smell horrible.

CONs

- Attracts a lot of dust.
- Doesn't smell good.

THE REVIEW

After reading and hearing about 303 for quite a while, I finally caved and purchased it. The first thing I noticed is that it applies and works in a very similar way to the "nano" line of Turtle Wax products that were available a few years ago. The best way to describe how plastic looks after application is to say it resembles freshly exfoliated skin.

It just looks healthier.

Part of the benefit is that the plastic is clean and free of dust. The other part of the benefit is that 303 actually penetrates the plastic and restores it's chemical properties that are slowly eroded by the sun, pollution, and the elements. I was a skeptic of this claim initially since it seems to "science" to be non-fiction, but 303's claims are true. The black plastic on my cowl was severely oxidized and damaged from the previous owner's use of Armor All (HORRIBLE!!!). One application of 303 brought back the deep rich black and it has lasted through two months of 100+ heat and rainy days in the 50s.

This is a fantastic product.

I use it after cleaning my plastic with a mixture of Simple Green diluted with distilled water. Forget the combination cleaner/conditioner sprays. Outside of smelling good, they offer no real lasting benefit. The stuff that cleans weakens the stuff that conditions, and vice versa. I clean with Simple Green once a week and treat with 303 once a month. I treat the exterior plastic whenever I wash my car. This schedule has restored my car's interior and maintained her exterior... and I don't care that it will never be considered on a collector's list!
profile.summary: This stuff works great for making plastic pretty and attracting dust.

profile.description: What's Better than a quart of luscious homemade ice cream, sorbet or frozen yogurt? Two quarts! The fully automatic Cuisinart Pure Indulgence makes 2 quarts of your favorite frozen desserts or drinks in as little as 25 minutes. It's easy - an intergrat
profile.reviewText:
I love my little Cuisinart ice cream maker!

If you've ever used an old-school ice cream machine with ice and salt, you are going to flip the $%&# out with how easy it is to make ice cream with a frozen cylinder. All you do is freeze the tub, assemble the machine, turn it on, slowly add your batter, and hang out.

While the newer models of nearly all brands offer separate settings for frozen yogurt and sorbet, you really don't need more precise equipment than your own eyeballs to make really good frozen deserts. For the price, this thing is a great device, and the extra half quart over the older models is awesome.

One complaint I have is that this adds a little too much air to the batter for my taste. This is intentional because the recipes in the book call for fairly lower-fat options (this is ice cream: "lower" fat is a relative term), where I prefer my batters to be closer to frozen custards. The extra air with all that fat gives the results a slightly chewy, almost taffy-like quality.

My guess is that this machine rolls in about 40-50% air into the final mixture if you let it run long enough, which is totally fine. The extra air helps your flavors escape sooner, leading to very good desserts using modest amounts of extracts. That makes homemade ice creams less expensive, and definitely way better than store-bought varieties.

I prefer my air content to be down around 15-20%. This leads to a denser, richer ice cream that satisfies my sweets cravings with far smaller servings. And I'm a total ice cream machine. I usually can't get enough of the stuff during the summer, and have been known to smash prodigious amounts during the winter, too. Anything I can do to keep my portions down is good.

How I solve the air problem is simple: I don't let it churn as long as the directions call for. I'll let my custard chill in the fridge overnight, then move it to the freezer (in a thin-walled brownie tin) for about an hour before churning it. This allows for the temperature to drop just above the point of crystal formation, so when it hits the frozen cylinder, it freezes almost instantly.

This is also why I like to turn on the machine before adding the mixture: otherwise I'd end up with a custard slushy.

Churning takes about 9-12 minutes, depending on the butterfat content of what I'm making. Then I transfer the soft serve rapidly into a pre-chilled container and let it hard set for a few hours. Easy as pie, and the final result is always awesome.

I use the same technique for making sorbets, though I prefer higher air contents in frozen yogurt for some reason. Regardless of what I'm making, or how I want it to come across while consuming, this machine always gives me great results. You just have to use your peepers, and after watching a few batches transform in the rotating cylinder, you'll know exactly what to look for when conducting your own tasty experiments.

Buy it. Play with it. Get fat. It's fun.
profile.summary: This thing makes the @&#$! out of ice cream!

profile.description: Minisuit's new Classic Stand Case with Handstrap jacket cover, case, and stand is perfect for trendy tablet users. This lightweight accessory case provides the smart executive style without clashing your wardrobe. The animal-friendly PU Leather cover protects your tablet, and is a 3-in-1 case cover that is a combination of two unique features. First, as a case: Sturdy, compact folio case. Second, as a stand: Versatile cover design transforms your case into a stand. Third, smart handstrap feature lets you carry your new electronic toy in confidence. Finally, the encasement is lightweight, compact, and portable. Take a stand, and accessorize your tablet with the perfect Minisuit case while commuting, working, and entertaining!
profile.reviewText:
First of all, I purchased this case to satisfy a curiosity as to how good a case I can get for $4.

Verdict: quite a good case, so why did I review it at two stars?

First: the many pros to this case.

The construction is excellent. While nobody will confuse this for genuine cowhide, I didn't dock any points for this becauseI don't care. 98% of what's on the market is pleather. The padding is also a little thin. I would like to see thin foam reinforced with cardboard to give a little squeeze to the screen's cover, but the main danger with tablets is torsion or punctures to the screen, causing breakage. This cover will provide good protection to both of those kinds of situations because those situations are due primarily to user stupidity.

Also: this case is $4!

The fit is also exceptional. I like that the MiniSuit case provides 360 degree protection to my Galaxy Tab Note 8.0, with cutouts to the case that perfectly match the camera, navigation buttons, IR blaster, power and volume buttons, S-Pen and USB hub. I dig the fact that the bezel is protected, and it fits the screen perfectly as long as you know how to tuck in sheets to make "hospital corners" with the flap that tucks under the Note to secure it in the case (with Velcro for added stability).

The only thing that isn't accessible is the microSD card, but I don't care about that. When 64GB cards are less han $50 and OTG cables are $5, there really isn't a practical reason to access the physical memory Samsung wisely allows their users to add.

Also, when laying down the tablet to work while standing at a counter or bar, this case has the best viewing angle of ANY case I've used (not only do I like standing up and writing, but I bring my work to happy hour... and sometimes my work happens AT happy hour)!

Now for the bad:

Magnets. The threat of magnetic damage to the S-Pen sensors is very VERY real. While these are weak magnets that don't activate the auto-wake feature of the GT-N51xx line of tablets (which is idiotically redundant: between the massive home button and being able to program the Note tabs to wake up by voice command, there is no reason for an auto-wake function using magnets. If Samsung wisely eliminated this feature, case manufacturers would stop using improper magnets that cause damage to the sensors trying to exploit the auto-wake feature), I am very concerned by their placement, and the fact that they're in constant contact with the bezel of the Note 8.0.

However, I didn't dock the MiniSuit any points because of these magnets. First of all, I don't know where Samsung places their sensors. Second: I don't know what the tolerance is for magnetic interference/damage to those sensors. Finally, i have no way to measure the magnetic force of the magnets embedded in the case, nor determining whether the case bodyor the flap contains the magnets. For all I know, the magnets are harmless.

However, from a design perspective, I would like to see some kind of strap that buttons shut like an old-school steno pad. Not only would this completely alleviate any concern over magnetic damage, but it would be cool in a retro-bow-tie-and-fez-Matt-Smith's-Dr.-Who-sort-of-way.

So what could possibly be responsible for causing a negative three star hit?

It is completely unusable when standing up in the verticle position. It is far too upright, making it stable and prone to face-planting any time it is used while seated. What's the point of using a tablet if you can't use its touch screen because the case seems to be balancing it as precariously as balancing a barstool on your chin?

If the MiniSuit's tab that secures the cover and allows it to stand upright was to be moved as far to the edge as possible, the cover would be 100% stable, 100% usable and 100% five stars. I absolutely love this case because it provides all the protection I need in a sleek package at an outrageous price... I just can't use it.
profile.summary: One inch away from being five stars.

profile.description: Samsung 830-SERIES 256GB 2.5in SATA III Mlc Internal SSD Hard Drive - Samsung MZ-7PC256B/WW.
profile.reviewText:
I learned this the hard way: I saw that the 256GB was on sale and I couldn't resist making the move to SSD. Upon getting my order, I realized that it was the bare drive, no software besides Samsung's Magician, no spacer, and no transfer cable.

Before I get into this, let me say this: the Samsung drive is the best one out there for laptops, even better than the Crucial M4. It is totally worth the extra $20 because you'll earn that back in extra working time with every battery charge.

And don't even consider the new Intels: they suck power, even when they're idle.

What I found was that the Norton Ghost "included" is not at all included in the bare drive package. You can download a 30 day trial from Samsung's software server through Magician, but it won't let you access the features needed to clone an OEM drive per Norton's protocol... so the trial is useless. No big deal: a transfer cable is $10, including Apricorn's software (which has worked well for friends), and I needed to buy one anyway. Also, because of the way my laptop's mount is designed for the hard drive, I don't need the spacer thanks to some sweet flat machine screws.

However, at the time I opened the box I was disappointed because I was expecting an hour long job for the swap, and a box that included all the goodies.

Was I in for a rude awakening! First off: the clone failed because of undiagnosed bad sectors. I should have run chkdsk before trying to clone. Everyone should. Even after a thorough cleaning with CCleaner and Defraggler, combined with doing some work with HDDRegenerator, my drive remained unable to have the partitions moved adequately for the clone to a smaller SSD.

Because my laptop came with Windows 7 pre-loaded, I couldn't do a fresh install. Upon trying to move partitions, my drive had bad sectors and was rendered useless by the cloning software. After debating spending another $100 on the software package of Windows 7 for a fresh install, I decided to read up on Linux. Had I done this when I ordered the drive, I would have never even bothered with the clone in the first place! What I did was copy all my personal files to a 16GB card, yank the old drive, install the Samsung, and install Mint from a MD5-verified Live DVD (always verify, especially when downloading over WiFi).

I have an older Acer i3 laptop with 8GB RAM and SATA 2 connections running Linux Mint 13 64bit. After a few tweaks to the fstab file and I/O manager, my laptop cold boots in 20 seconds! To compare, my system took nearly four minutes to load before with a 5400RPM hard drive and Windows 7 Home Premium 64bit. I know I'm comparing apples to oranges since Linux is streamlined, but WOW! What a difference!

The first thing I noticed was how fast the drive ate the files I transfered over from my old drive. What took an hour and a half to load onto a class 10 card took less than 10 minutes to write onto the new drive... and writing is where SSDs lag! The read times are fantastic, and I'm only getting half of the performance because of my dated motherboard.

With SATA 6gb/s I'd be booting in around 10 seconds and sitting at idle more often, extending battery life even more! If you have a newer laptop, you're going to be blown away.

As for the Magician software, I can't review it at this time because Samsung doesn't support Linux. I could load it through Wine, but I don't expect it to do much outside update firmware without having to burn an ISO disc. For the Windows user, though, you're going to get a lot of mileage out of it. Samsung makes some of the best electronics right now, and I doubt their software is held to any standard less than great.

Even though my experience led me to nearly pull out my hair a few times (I'm a noob at all this stuff) and curse a blue streak, it worked out for the best. I'd suggest that everyone try Linux before either cloning or purchasing a retail package of your proprietary OS of choice to do the job right. Cloning won't, and not because it didn't work for me. Cloning simply won't get the most performance out of these drives.

Think of it this way: you can "clone" an old record by holding up your cell phone to a speaker using a voice recording app. But compared to buying an mp3 version of the same song, the quality of the clone will be subpar (though still recognizable).

And you wouldn't be looking at a Samsung drive if you expect anything less than the best.
profile.summary: Be careful what drive you buy!!!

profile.description: Classic meets modern in this International Silver American Bead Flatware Set. Features a teardrop shape with embossed bead chain border. Expertly crafted from 18/0 stainless steel, this set is designed to complement any tabletop decor. This 53-Piece Set, service for eight, includes (8) each: dinner fork, salad fork, dinner knife, dinner spoon, teaspoon and steak knives, plus a 5 piece Hostess Set, which includes (1) each of: tablespoon, pierced tablespoon, cold meat fork, sugar spoon and butter knife. Dishwasher safe.
profile.reviewText:
The Good:

- It's cheap in price and manipulates food (+5 stars).

The Bad:

- It's cheap in quality and feels very flimsy (-2 starts).

The Review:

My girlfriend and I bought this as a second set of silverware to help out around the holidays and for dinner parties. The quality is lacking, but it does the job we need it to. This isn't a big deal because we only host six to ten dinner parties a year, so we can reserve these for the children, the deranged or the developmentally disabled... also known as the in-laws.

Are the in-law jokes back in?

Not really that great of a bargain considering the deals club stores offer multiple times throughout the year.
profile.summary: You'll only consider it an heirloom if you're homeless.
