profile.description: The Marlin stapler  a hardworking, practical addition to any desktop. This traditional full-strip, top-loading metal stapler features an ABS top cap for ease of use and a full rubber base for stability. This durable stapler is backed by a 15 year Guarantee and has a capacity of 25 sheets (20lb paper)
profile.reviewText:
Rapesco is a British company, and its products are the most popular there and in Europe. I'd never used one of their products before here in the US. But I wanted to try a flat clinch stapler, where the staple is crimped close to the paper rather than in a curved loop that sticks out on the bottom.

That turns out to be a nice feature when you have to stack several stapled documents together. The staple does not create a gap between documents (it's only about a 1/16 of an inch, but that can matter) and does not dig into the paper of the document below it. It's a small thing, but I do prefer it. Xerox machines with automatic staplers do it that way. Now I can too.

Perhaps because this stapler does bend the staple in a flat clinch rather than a loop, it seems to take more pressure to staple than my usual stapler. Not excessive force, but more. The stapler seems fairly solid, but feels a little cheaper than my usual stapler. The color's nice, though. Better blue than basic black.

The stapler takes typical 1/4 inch staples. The bottom of the stapler says it takes 26/6 or 24/6 staples, which are hard to find in the US. That's because it's the metric measure: the 6 is 6 mm, which is about 1/4 inch. The 26 and 24 are the gauge of the wire used, with 24 gauge being slightly larger and thus stronger wire. The 24 gauge staples require more force to use, since you need to bend the thicker wire into the flat clinch, which itself requires more force than a curved clinch.

All in all, it's a good stapler for the price, and I now use it for all my stapling needs. I do have to say, though, that I am not a heavy stapler. I often go three or four days between stapling, and rarely staple more than a few documents at a time. Those who staple more might want a heavier stapler that can be placed on a desktop and pushed down more easily with force.
profile.summary: A nice stapler for casual users like me

profile.description: Logitech C930e 1080P HD Video Webcam - 90-Degree Extended View, Microsoft Lync 2013 and Skype Certified
profile.reviewText:
This webcam is designed for business use, in conference calls and the like. My use is a little different, so my experience may not be as helpful.

I found the webcam to produce a very high definition picture, and when stationary it worked fine. But if I held it in my hand to take a picture of a moving object, it did not work as well. It seemed to take a while to get the picture in focus.

Although the webcam has software that allows it to zoom, pan and tilt, the interface to the program is hard to use. You have to use the mouse to control some buttons on the screen. It's hard to do that when trying to watch the webcam picture at the same time.

All in all, this seems to be a great webcam for those who want to just put it in place and leave it there, as with a conference call. The picture is perfect, and if you adjust the webcam's characteristics in advance and don't need to change them, you will be fine. The two microphones work well for that too.

But if you want to use the webcam for other things, you will be stretching its abilities. It won't work as well.
profile.summary: Good picture, but a little hard to use

profile.description: Nitrogen is the new black. Miracle-Gro Natures Care Organic Blood Meal brings life and vitality to your flowers and veggies for abundant harvests that are full of color. Because who wants pale, sickly, lifeless gardens? This is the luscious way to feed your plants for bodacious blooms and vibrant color. Just grow for it.
profile.reviewText:
This fertilizer is made of pig's blood. That's not an appealing thought. But it does seem a good source of nitrogen to invigorate the soil and make plants grow. Particularly, the leaves need nitrogen to make them green. The other elements of fertilizer -- phosphorus and potash -- are not in this product and will need to come from another source.

This Nature's Care labeled product comes from the makers of Miracle-Gro, which is the Scotts Miracle-Gro company, with the Scotts, Miracle-Gro, and Ortho brands of yard products. This is their organic line, apparently, since pig's blood -- or porcine blood meal -- qualifies as an organic fertilizer whereas Miracle-Gro does not.

The package this comes in contains the rather unusual smell of its contents, and the spout and built-in handle make it easy to apply. I just sprinkle it around the flowers that need it, and don't work it in the soil. It's a little early to tell how well it works yet. But 12% nitrogen should give the plants a big boost.

Too much is as bad as too little, though, so go easy on the application. And peas and legumes have bacteria in their root systems that fix nitrogen from the air, so they don't need any extra.
profile.summary: Great packaging and a solid 12% nitrogen (but the vampire eggplant on the package is a bit goofy)

profile.description: Marine life planet wide is dying off in staggering proportions, and if adventurer Dirk Pitt can't find the solution--ALL life is in danger! So what's he doing looking for the answer in the middle of the Sahara desert? Just trust him. Good cast in a movie that was done better last summer as Flight Of The Phoenix.
profile.reviewText:
Clive Cussler's books featuring Dirk Pitt have always been a favorite of mine.  That's a bit of a guilty pleasure.  Cussler's characters could better be called caricatures.  His plots are also larger than life -- no one could suspend disbelief enough to think that the things Cussler dreams up for his hero Dirk Pitt could ever happen in real life.

But that does not stop me from enjoying the books.  Cussler's lively imagination captures me in his make-believe world for a time.  And his almost self-parodying characters always entertain as an escape from real life people.

The movie Sahara is the same way.  It's just as fun to watch as the book Sahara is to read.

Yes, it's true that the movie does not follow the book.  That's probably a good thing.  Cussler's novels would not translate well to the movie screen if the translation were too direct.  Cussler's intricate plotting, his attention to detail (as in his detailed description of each classic car that appears in any book), and his rather cartoonish dialogue work in his books.  They would look foolish in a movie.

As a movie, Sahara works best as a family picture.  Adults will probably find it entertaining enough.  Children will find it easy to understand, with enough humor and surprises to keep their interest.

Definitely not a must-see film.  But everyone in our family liked it.  Both adults, and both children.  Everyone thumbs up.  That's pretty rare.
profile.summary: Different from the book, but just as fun to watch as the book is to read

profile.description: Furinno JAYA Simple Design TV Stand is a perfect fits into your modern simple lifestyle. There are open display shelves to hold your entertainment equipment and two storage bins for your loose stuff such as CDs, DVDs and games. It is easy to assemble, lightweight and space saving. The manufacturing process complies with the green rules of production. There is no foul smell, durable and the material is the most stable amongst the medium density composite woods. The PVC tubes are made from recycled plastic and is tested for its durability. A simple attitude towards lifestyle is reflected directly on the design of Furinno Furniture, creating a trend of simply nature. All the products are produced and assembled 100-percent in Malaysia with 95% - 100% recycled materials. Care instructions: wipe clean with clean damped cloth. Avoid using harsh chemicals. Pictures are for illustration purpose. All decor items are not included in this offer.
profile.reviewText:
If you need a television stand that looks reasonably decent and holds together reasonably well, but not something that you will keep for a long time, this will work well for you.

At least, that is my experience. The stand is built out of basic materials, and the construction is solid enough to put a heavy television on it. But the design is pretty pedestrian, the workmanship and finish of the materials is poor, and the stand does not seem like it will wear well. Moving, for example, may be a chore not worth the effort.

The stand comes pretty much broken down and you need to assemble it yourself. The box is about 40 pounds, so it's not light. It takes about 30 minutes to assemble, mainly because you need to do a lot of figuring on your own since the instructions are little help.

But for the price, this television stand is a versatile piece of furniture that may not get many compliments but will certainly serve its function.
profile.summary: A good choice for basic, functional furniture

profile.description: High quality flat clinch, top-loading personal stapler with 25 per cent less stapling force required. The flat clinch mechanism flattens the staple legs on the reverse side of the paper to avoid sharp edges and achieve neat paper stacking. Full rubber base and personalization window. Made from quality materials it uses 26 and 24/6mm Rapesco Staples for up to 25-30 sheets.
profile.reviewText:
Rapesco is a British company, and its products are the most popular there and in Europe. I'd never used one of their products before here in the US. But I wanted to try a flat clinch stapler, where the staple is crimped close to the paper rather than in a curved loop that sticks out on the bottom.

That turns out to be a nice feature when you have to stack several stapled documents together. The staple does not create a gap between documents (it's only about a 1/16 of an inch, but that can matter) and does not dig into the paper of the document below it. It's a small thing, but I do prefer it. Xerox machines with automatic staplers do it that way. Now I can too.

Perhaps because this stapler does bend the staple in a flat clinch rather than a loop, it seems to take more pressure to staple than my usual stapler. Not excessive force, but more. The stapler seems fairly solid, but feels a little cheaper than my usual stapler. The color's nice, though. Better blue than basic black.

The stapler takes typical 1/4 inch staples. The bottom of the stapler says it takes 26/6 or 24/6 staples, which are hard to find in the US. That's because it's the metric measure: the 6 is 6 mm, which is about 1/4 inch. The 26 and 24 are the gauge of the wire used, with 24 gauge being slightly larger and thus stronger wire. The 24 gauge staples require more force to use, since you need to bend the thicker wire into the flat clinch, which itself requires more force than a curved clinch.

All in all, it's a good stapler for the price, and I now use it for all my stapling needs. I do have to say, though, that I am not a heavy stapler. I often go three or four days between stapling, and rarely staple more than a few documents at a time. Those who staple more might want a heavier stapler that can be placed on a desktop and pushed down more easily with force.
profile.summary: A nice stapler for casual users like me

profile.description: The First Alert Onelink Wi-Fi Touchscreen Smart Thermostat connects to your Wi-Fi network and is designed to work with your smartphone or tablet using the Onelink app. This programmable thermostat lets you control the temperature from anywhere--even when you are away--to save you money while increasing energy efficiency. The thermostat can also be controlled from your Amazon Alexa-enabled device, using your voice to adjust interior climate settings. The Wi-Fi Touchscreen Smart Thermostat tracks your energy usage and displays the power consumption of your system over the past seven days. It also features a full-color touchscreen with a user-friendly interface that can showcase up to 100 images.
profile.reviewText:
This thermostat is the only one I've tried, so I can't tell you if it's better than Nest or any other competitor. But I can say that this one works well. Depending on your thermostat setup, it installs easily and you're good to go. The unit can be programmed either using its touchscreen or over Wi-Fi using an app. It's pretty straightforward to handle.

The only drawback I see is that so far I have used none of the features of this unit beyond its basic programming ability. So my old programmable thermostat was just as good as this one. I really have no need to change the heating remotely, or to use the screen of the thermostat to display a text message to someone else. Nor do I need to get weather forecasts, check our energy usage, or put pictures on display.

In short, if you want a thermostat with a variety of functions, this will do you well. If your needs are more basic, like mine, you're paying a lot for things you will not get.
profile.summary: Good, but too many features that I pay for and don't use

profile.description: Design unique crafts and standout projects with quality and affordable u create arts & crafts products. The 9" x 12" sketch book is the perfect art pad for doodling, designing or creative note taking. Features include perforated sheets and 75 lb. Premium drawing paper.
profile.reviewText:
This sketch book has 75 sheets of drawing paper that is 12 inches by (if you tear the sheet out) about 8.6 inches. The paper is wire bound, and the binding is a little sketchy. When the book was shipped to me, it was thrown in a box with some plastic air bags for cushion and it has a little wear (though no tear yet) from bouncing around the box. I imagine as I use it the wear will get worse. Another sketch book I have has a sturdier cover and binding, which I like a little better.

That said, the paper quality is weighty (75 pound, compared to 20 pound for typical printer paper) and good, and the binding gives good access to each sheet as I draw on it. So this sketch book should serve me well.
profile.summary: Good quality paper, but binding is a little sketchy

profile.description: Maisto Rock Crawler Extreme Remote Controlled Vehicle, Colors May Vary
profile.reviewText:
If you want a remote-controlled toy that will give some fun for a while, this one fits the bill. It's fun to take out and give it a spin. But if you want to use it more than a few times, you may want to get something better. This vehicle takes normal batteries, not a rechargeable battery pack. And it only has one speed. If you want to do any kind of sophisticated driving, you need better control.

But a toy vehicle with a rechargeable battery pack and better control will also cost more than this toy. Most children play with a vehicle like this a few times, and then tire of it. So at this price this vehicle may be a better buy than a more expensive, higher-quality vehicle.
profile.summary: A good, cheap toy for fun while it lasts

profile.description: TP-LINK's Archer D7 AC1750 Wireless Dual Band Gigabit ADSL2+ Modem Router is a combined wired/wireless network connection device with integrated wireless router and ADSL modem, reducing hassle of configuration and saving space.Featuring a variety of features and rich functionality, Archer D7 is the perfect hub of your home or business network. It works with top ISPs - Verizon, Fairpoint, WindStream, AT&T. It is not compatible with FiOS, AT&T U-Verse, or VDSL. ( as stated on the box.)
profile.reviewText:
This router combines a DSL modem with a high-end router to give you a good combination. It's quite compact, even with the dual function. It gets a little warm when running, but no more (and no less) than other routers. It has a built-in stand so you can put it on its edge to save desktop space. I like the design, and the external antennas.

The problem I have is that we use AT&T Uverse for our Internet service. When this box arrived, it had a sticker on it that said it does not work with Uverse. And indeed it doesn't. I tried it, and could not get Internet access by plugging the DSL phone cord into the modem/router.

But I can still use the router. It's a little hard to reconfigure it to accept an Internet connection from my Uverse modem. I first had to connect my computer up to the TP-LINK router and access the setup screen at 192.168.1.1. Then I had to find the "Operation Mode" screen and set operation to "Wireless Router Mode" from "DSL Modem Router Mode." Then I saved my choice, and waited for about 5 minutes for the router to reboot. Once it finished rebooting, I connected the LAN/WAN jack up to the output from my modem.

None of this is explained in the Quick Installation Guide. The User Guide for the Archer D2 AC750 available at the TP-LINK support website does explain the process, but it's a little hard to find there as well. It's under Section 4.4 Operation Mode.

Once I got the router set up and working, I found that the 5 GHz band does not have very good range in my house. The 2.4 GHz band works fine, though.

All in all, this modem/router works fine as just a router, but I'd be a lot happier with it if I could junk my AT&T Uverse modem/router and just go with this one. But I can't.
profile.summary: Good router, but doesn't work with AT&T Uverse and a little hard to reconfigure to use as just a router

profile.description: The latest in contemporary design, these deadbolts are the first of their kind, featuring a half-inch projection off the door and the latest version of Kwikset patented smart key security. Uptown, a round slim deadbolt is the latest in contemporary design and a perfect accent for the style-conscious consumer.
profile.reviewText:
This deadbolt lock looks nice on the door, with the "satin nickel" color being understated and classy. The deadbolt makes a larger circle than most, but is thinner in profile. The inner mechanism works a little differently, allowing the lock to be under the latch instead of directly to the side of it. I'm hoping the design will not be a problem in terms of durability.

The deadbolt comes with instructions that make installation easy. I was replacing a 25 year old deadbolt, so the hole in the door was much smaller than the 2 1/8 inch standard now. But a hole saw soon solved that problem.

I did have a more difficult problem with the plate in the door jam that the latch fits into. The deadbolt comes with a plate that takes 4 screws, 2 of which are 3 inches long. I took off the existing plate with its 2 small screws and drilled guide holes for the 4 new screws. Trouble is, I got the plate just off where it needed to go, so that the latch bumps it as it slides into the hole in the door jamb.

So now I need to move the plate about 1/8 inch, but there's no room to put new screw holes that close to the ones I just made. (I should have measured more carefully!) I'll have to plug up the previous screw holes and drill new ones. Meanwhile, I'm just using the old plate, which works just fine.
profile.summary: Nice look; easy to install

profile.description: The OREI Mini Boom II Bluetooth Wireless Portable Speaker provides a convenient source of audio listening of just about anywhere you wish to locate it. It can connect wirelessly to your smartphone, laptop or other Bluetooth compatible device and produce high-quality sound as it streams your music or game audio. The high bass technology produces powerful deep notes. Its compact shape allows it to easily be placed on a desk or a shelf. It can be operated with either AC or battery power.
profile.reviewText:
This speaker looks nice and, more important, sounds nice. It's more powerful than I thought it would be, even compared to speakers much larger. Bluetooth pairing was no problem, and I was able to use it a telephone speakerphone. All in all, I was impressed.

The only drawback I found was the controls on the top of the device are hard for me to use. They seem to be delayed a bit, so that I push them, wait a bit, and push them again just as the previous action is working. Maybe I'll figure out how to use the controls better as time goes on. So far, though, they work but not well.

Even with that fault, I like the speaker. It's a good one.
profile.summary: Nice look, nice sound

profile.description: A fully balanced acoustic profile, combined with wireless Bluetooth technology lets you experience every layer of your music in a sleek, sophisticated design.
profile.reviewText:
While I'm not a constant user of headphones, I do prefer them over earphones and frequently use them when I don't want to bother others with my music. This pair of headphones works very well for me.

The headphones are light and fit well (though the balance is a little tricky -- if I'm not careful and move my head quickly, they will shift their position). They feel good on my ears (though they do get tiresome after a few hours, but all headphones do and these are definitely on the comfortable side).

The headphones look elegant and come in a nice soft pouch of a case. The material looks and feels somewhat like leather, but it is not leather. They seem well made and I think will last for a long time.

The bluetooth pairing with my smartphone was quick and easy. I do occasionally get some breaks when I am streaming music from the internet, but I doubt that those are due to bluetooth problems with these headphones.

As to sound -- the most important quality -- I was impressed. Volume is easily adjustable, and loud enough. The range of sound is good, with the bass notes being particularly well done for a pair of headphones. There is a little distance to the sound, compared to earphones, but that is not a problem for me.

All in all, I'm very pleased with these headphones, which look and (most importantly) sound fantastic.
profile.summary: Look and (most importantly) sound fantastic

profile.description: A19 LED smart bulb, 800 lumens, 60W equivalent, color app Tunable. Simple whole home control - start with one ilumi or outfit your whole home. Only ilumi has robust & long-range Bluetooth mesh to control 1 to 50+ ilumi at a time. No hub or Wi-Fi required - plug and play setup without bridges, routers, or other hassles. Your ilumi will be up-and-running in seconds. Enhance the switch - unlike any other, ilumi allows you to set and store your own "power on" default for light that's just right whether you use the switch or the app. Long lasting & energy efficient - the most energy efficient smart bulb, , ilumi will pay for itself! with high quality LEDs, you can enjoy up to 20 years of beautiful light. Discover a world of color - create the perfect atmosphere. Only ilumi with hyper lux technology shines brightly with every vibrant color under the rainbow. Light your routine - with a clock inside every ilumi, enjoy the exact lighting you want on your Schedule. Convenient absolutely. Custom lighting experiences - Jam to your favorite tunes while ilumi dance to the music, automate your lighting before you head out on vacation, or enjoy a perfect home-cooked meal under ilumi candlelight. ilumi can even detect your presence when you walk in the room. With ilumi, you'll never see lighting the same again. 2 year limited warranty.
profile.reviewText:
This 10 Watt bulb puts out a lot of light. You can pick any color too, using the 0 to 255 RGB scale. The Ilumi app lets you use your smartphone's Bluetooth to pick the color from a color chart. You can also use the app to generate a variety of effects, like Stars and Stripes (which cycles through red to white to blue).

Frankly speaking, the app could use some work. I had a lot of trouble downloading it, and when I finally got it to work, I was unable to do some of the promised operations. I've used another similar bulb that cost half as much, and though I complained about that app as well, at least it does more than the Ilumi app.

So while I think these colorful bulbs are an interesting new technology, and this one works very well at putting out different colors, I'm not sure why I would ever buy a $60 bulb like this, or what I would do with it.
profile.summary: Interesting technology, but pricey and still not ready for prime time

profile.description: THE NATIONAL MUSEUM OF AMERICAN HISTORY collects and preserves more than 3 million artifacts that explore the infinite richness and complexity of American history. It is one of the Smithsonian's most popular and frequently visited museums. Contributors include HARRY R. RUBENSTEIN, WILLIAM BIRD, LISA KATHLEEN GRADDY, and BARBARA CLARK SMITH, curators at the National Museum of American History,and GRACE COHEN GROSSMAN, a former Goldman Sachs Fellow at the National Museum of American History.
profile.reviewText:
I like this book. Like the exhibits at the Smithsonian's American History Museum that the book is a companion to, this book has no political agenda to preach but instead largely presents history through pictures and items that speak for themselves. A little preaching does creep in, and a book limited to 200 pages is inevitably going to give spotty coverage to almost 250 years of political history. Still, it's fascinating to see history come alive in a way that a textbook or a class cannot duplicate.

One thing that struck me from the book is how we tend to simplify our history and mythologize some heroes. George Washington, for example, rarely gets mentioned today except in praise. Yet in his time he had been a divisive figure as well as a unifying one, and was no great fan of democracy in politics. Should Americans see the founding as a complete, perfect, sacred event led by a great patriot?, the book asks. Or was it part of a wider, unfinished movement for liberty -- deeply imperfect but with sacred aspirations? Good questions.

Our lives today will be history tomorrow. But while we are caught up in the experience of the present, we often have a tough time trying to experience the past. If we are not careful, it is easy to forget that as Will and Ariel Durant said, "Most history is guessing, and the rest is prejudice." When we can, better to learn history from primary material, like that presented in this book, than from secondary material that is mainly someone else's guessing and prejudice.
profile.summary: Great chance to look at historical artifacts rather than just a textbook interpretation of history

profile.description: The Kichler Lighting 12393WH30 120V TaskWork 27-inch LED Under Cabinet Fixture allows you to quickly and easily add useful light to a variety of workspaces throughout your home making it perfectly suited whether you're a crafter or baker, weekend workshopper or hobby enthusiast. The plug-in design means you can install light in minutes, and the interconnect capability allows you to outfit your entire space with multiple fixtures and plug into one standard outlet. The slim profile shows its versatility when it tucks cleanly under cabinets in kitchens, baths, craft or laundry rooms, workshops, garages, offices and more. The portable design also makes them great for dorm rooms. The 12393WH30 features LED technology, which is highly efficient yet extremely bright, bringing you consistent working light without draining energy. Plus, LED lights run cool - meaning no extra heat is generated on workspaces below. Color Rendering Index of 83 keeps colors accurate - essential in kitchens and craft rooms, and the 3000K light creates a pure, white light with no blue cast. The included interconnect cable allows you to link multiple fixtures and power them from a single outlet. Different length fixtures can also be linked as long as the combined total wattage does not exceed 100W. When linking fixtures, leave at least 2.5 inches between fixtures. Two mounting screws are preassembled on the light, easily installed using a Philips screwdriver. The 36-inch power cord, supplied with the fixture, comes with two mounting screws and three white adhesive clips, allowing you to secure the on/off switch and the power cord to the wall. For optimum attachment, the mounting surface needs to be a minimum of .5 inches thick. The quality aluminum construction is built to last and the long-life Nichia LEDs never need to be replaced. All fixtures are designed and manufactured by Kichler - a lighting leader for more than 75 years -- and come backed by the Kichler 3-year warranty.
profile.reviewText:
This under-the-cabinet light works well for us. The light fits under a cabinet near the sink where some extra light is handy. The light is heavy-duty but not heavy, so it was easy to install and looks like it will stay in place permanently. And we were lucky to have an empty power socket close by to plug the light's fairly short cord into.

So all in all the light fits our needs. But the price seems awfully high for what you get. And I'm a little worried about the screws for mounting. There are two screws each for the light and the switch. I'm afraid we may have stripped the screw heads on one or two of them during installation.
profile.summary: Works well for us

profile.description: The HAMMERHEAD Compact Impact Driver/Auto Hammer is two tools in one, giving you the ability to drive screws and hammer nails with ease. The right-angle design is perfect for gaining access in tight spaces, especially where swinging a hammer is not possible. Included with the kit is a 30pc impact bit assortment for increased versatility and convenience. Kit includes: (1) Impact Driver/Auto Hammer, (1) 12V Charger, (1) Auto Hammer Adaptor, (1) Standard Impact Bit, 2 Bits: (1) PH2, (1) PH3, (1) SQ2, (1) SQ3, 1 Bits: (1) PH1, (8) PH2, (3) PH3, (4) SQ2, (2) SQ3, (1) T15, (1) T20, (1) T25, (1) T30, (2) SL6-8, (1) Magnetic Bit Collar, and (1) Magnetic Insert Bit Holder.
profile.reviewText:
Very handy tool for power driving screws and pounding nails. The tool is a bit heavy for one-handed use, so it can be a little tough to hold a screw or nail in place and still hold the tool with precision. But I'm getting used to that.

At 12 volts the tool is a little underpowered, so it probably will not do the tougher jobs. I've not tried drilling with it, since you need to buy special drill bits with a hexagonal base. So far, it's done everything I've tried it for.

The battery pack is integrated into the tool, so you can't have extra batteries. If the battery needs charging, the tool is out of commission until it is charged.

The tool came with two bits, one a screw head and the other for holding nails. But I also got a set of bits -- 30 of them, although there are several of the more common bits so there are only about 14 different types of bits.

I like the light that comes on to shine on where you are working. That helps.

I've got nothing to compare this tool to, and I suspect those who need something for heavy use will pick something else. But for those like me who are using a tool like this to replace hand tools and an electric drill, this is a very handy tool that does a lot of different things.
profile.summary: Very handy tool that does a lot of different things

profile.description: The Jabra speak 510 Bluetooth speakerphone lets you take audio conferencing to a whole new level as you turn any room into a conference room. You can join the conversation anytime and anywhere with a slim, compact design, outstanding sound quality and a plug-and-play solution for all your devices - connect and dial-in, that's it.
profile.reviewText:
This speakerphone does a good job when needed. It has a rechargeable battery, so it does not need to be plugged in during use. The battery has a good charge -- it seems to last for several hours. You can connect any device that uses Bluetooth or USB to send out an audio signal, and it will work with this speaker. (There is no "audio in" jack, so you cannot plug in a simple audio line.)

That makes this speakerphone very handy for a variety of things where you want an external speaker bigger than that on a smartphone or the like. The sound is better on the speakerphone (although the volume seems lower at its maximum than it should be).

The main disadvantage I have found is that the microphone is not that great. People on the other end of telephone calls have remarked that my voice sounds a little distorted. More so than with a cellphone. This speakerphone does work well for calls where more than one person needs to talk. But we seem to get by without pulling out this speakerphone even in those cases. In fact, it's hard to think of a time when this speakerphone would be a whole lot better than the easier alternative. So it's more a gadget than a necessity.
profile.summary: Handy, but pricey for the limited use we make of it

profile.description: Slow down and appreciate the experience of expressing your thoughts and ideas on paper with the PARKER Jotter Bond Street Black ballpoint pen. A style icon for over 60 years, the Jotter has a fresh, streamlined design. It features a stainless steel barrel in a sleek black finish, linished stainless steel cap, high-shine trims, and an arrowhead clip. The Jotters stunning details make it a refined gift for graduates, first-time job seekers, or anyone who appreciates the art of fine writing. This Jotter pen's name is inspired by the city of London. It arrives packaged in an elegant gift box.
profile.reviewText:
It looks like this pen sells for around $25. While it is a nice pen, in that it feels good in the hand when writing and writes well, it seems overpriced at that price. It is quite lightweight and looks a little cheap to me. The gift box is a nice touch, but is nothing fancy and in fact has a plastic container that holds the pen in so securely you have to pry it out.

On the other hand, it does look like this pen will last a long while, and it seems to be made with typical Parker pen quality, which I have always found to be excellent. I was a little surprised to find it writes in blue, when I was expecting black. The ink cartridge is easily replaced, but costs about $3 for a single refill.
profile.summary: Not impressive, but certainly adequate

profile.description: Scotch(R) Multi-Purpose Fasteners are great for mounting items on walls. Grip and Release. For indoor use.
profile.reviewText:
These velcro fasteners work well to put things up on walls. You put one piece on the wall, the other on the thing you want to hang, and then you can put the thing up and take it off as many times as you want.

Two problems. One, you can only use them for light things. Two, they only make sense for things you want to put up, take down, put up, take down, time and again. I tried them just to test them out. But so far I cannot think of anything I really want to use them on.

Maybe someday they will come in handy. I hope when, and if, that day comes, I can still find these fasteners in the drawer.
profile.summary: Work well to put things up, as long as they are not heavy

profile.description: These Triangle Bulbs brand Dimmable LED 100 watt equivalent everyday household use only 16 watts of energy, and replaces your traditional 100 watt light bulbs, providing an 84% reduction in energy usage. Designed to deliver everyday value and effective, consistent light, these light bulbs provide a soft, comfortable light. Use them throughout your home in table and floor lamps and open pendant fixtures. They are ideal for use in any room in your home, including kitchens, living rooms, hallways and bedrooms. These LED light bulbs provide a beautiful light and because they are so affordable you can use them anywhere and everywhere around your home. These LED bulbs are built to last up to 20000 hours or 18 years and they are mercury free with no ultraviolet (UV) light. These LED A21 bulbs give you instant light output with just a simple flip of a switch. These bulbs provide soft white (also known as, warm white) color temperature (3000 Kelvin), which gives off a warm full glow ideal for living rooms, dining rooms and recreation rooms. Based on 3 hours average daily usage.
profile.reviewText:
The LED lights seem well made and put out a lot of light. Since they only use 14 Watts but put out the light of a 100 Watt bulb, you can put them in a socket for a 60 Watt bulb and get a lot more brightness. I tried that in a bedside lamp, and it works really well.

The light the bulb puts out is a little too much on the white side for my wife, who prefers more yellowish tint than these bulbs offer. But I like the tint just fine. Tastes differ.

The bulbs are a little oversize compared to both incandescent and fluorescent bulbs. They also put out little light downward, making them not suitable for a floor lamp that we have in our living room. Too little light shines on the couch for me to read there. The packaging for the bulb says it puts out light across 270 degrees, but it doesn't seem that way to me. Closer to 180 degrees.

I was surprised to see how much heat the base retains. The bulb portion doesn't get hot, but the base gets quite hot.
profile.summary: Works well for me, but my wife likes a more yellow light

profile.description: SkyBell is a Wi-Fi enabled video doorbell that allows you to see who's at your door from your mobile device - whether you're at home, at work or on the go. When a visitor presses the button, SkyBell sends you a live video feed so you can see, hear and speak to the person at your door from iOS and Android mobile devices. SkyBell helps you stay connected with your home, feel safer about answering the door on your terms. SkyBell has an advanced motion sensor for sending alerts and video even when a visitor doesn't press the button. SkyBell is the only video doorbell with an on-demand feature that allows you to see out of the SkyBell camera at any time. You can even turn off your home's doorbell chime from the app. SkyBell features a contrast setting for more favorable lighting, Wi-Fi capability (b/g router required), invisible night vision for viewing after dark, and is Made the USA. SkyBell replaces your current doorbell, attaches to your transformer for full-time power, connects to your home's door chime and securely connects to your home's Wi-Fi network. Motion sensor activation: receive alerts and video feed even if visitor doesn't press button. On-demand access allows you to see out of SkyBell's video camera at any time from the app. Multiple users are able receive the video alerts anyplace that has cellular or internet connection on your mobile device (Connection times vary due to WiFi, 3G or LTE video upload/download speeds). Compatible with b/g routers. Requires 2.4GHz band, b/g mode, 20 MHz bandwidth and 1 mbps upload speed at your front door. You must connect your smartphone to the 2.4 Ghz network before syncing to SkyBell. It requires upload speed of 1mbps at SkyBells location.
profile.reviewText:
SkyBell has done a great job putting together this video doorbell. Combining video, audio, and wi-fi communications into the small circle of a doorbell takes some doing, and they did it well. The outer covering is a metallic-looking plastic, and it looks fine on our house's wall (and I suspect it would look good on most walls as well).

Installation did not take too long, although there's not much space to work with in attaching the wires of the SkyBell to the two existing wires. The button mechanism is easy to push, and the whole thing runs off the current, transformed down, that most houses have running through their doorbell setup.

Our doorbell is a little offset from our door, but the wide angle of the SkyBell captures enough of the person standing at the front door for me to identify them. We originally had it set up to trigger on motion, but found that impractical and turned that feature off.

Like most devices like this, it took a while to get everything working. You have to download an app (your smartphone has to be compatible, but mine was), make sure your wireless router lets the device get an address, and register. Even with it working, it takes a while to get the image up on my smartphone. So I'm not sure how often I'll use this device. Maybe more as time goes on. But I think my wife will continue to just peek out the front curtain to see who's there.
profile.summary: Great design, but maybe a little too feature-full for us

profile.description: Luceco's LED bulbs offer an 80% energy savings over their incandescent counterparts, at an average energy cost of just $1.14 per year. With a color temperature of 2700K, they produce the same soft, warm white glow of a traditional bulb, making them as easy on the eyes as they are on the wallet. These bulbs are a direct replacement for a standard A19 65-watt incandescent light bulb - no rewiring is required to upgrade your lighting. The mercury-free LED bulb also stays cool when lit for a safe, environmentally and family friendly lighting option. A 15,000 hour lifetime means less time and money spent on replacements. Backed by Luceco's 3-year warranty.
profile.reviewText:
These LED bulbs are priced lower than any others I have seen, and perform just as well. The light is not as warm as incandescent bulbs, but it is less bluish and more warm than many LED bulbs. These LED bulbs work well, and seem to be of high quality, although that is hard to tell. Of course, having used them only a few days, I'm not sure how long they will last. That will be the test.

Like all LED bulbs I have purchased, the light portion of the bulb does not get hot, but the base portion does. Since the base does not emit light, these do not work well in a light fixture with an upright bulb that is above a sitting person. Otherwise, it works quite well as it is not as heavy as many LED bulbs.
profile.summary: Great price and reasonable quality

profile.description: Sunlite 88102 LFX/TP/15W/PC 15 Watt 120-277 Volt LED Wall Packs Fixture, Bronze Finish, Polycarbonate Glass.
profile.reviewText:
This light fixture looks nice and works well. It puts out a lot of light for 15 watts. It says that it replaces a 60-watt bulb, but it seems to be brighter than that. The LED lights are in a bunch that takes up about the same amount of space as a light bulb. But the LEDs don't get as hot, so the whole fixture is somewhat smaller than the old fixture it replaced. It sticks out from the wall a lot more than it looks in the picture, though -- about 5 inches.

This light fixture is not going to win any design awards, and looks more cheap than chic. It's made out of frosted plastic and bronze-colored plastic, with a metal back. The LEDs cannot be replaced, but are supposed to last for many years.

The light fixture comes with some foam adhesive strips and a foam backing to keep water out. I added some caulking since I put the light fixture in an exposed location where rain falls directly on it. Installation was easy since it replaced an existing light fixture.

All in all, I like the light. I don't use the light-sensing on/off feature, since the light is only useful when someone is in that area and we don't need it on more than about 1% of the time. I wanted to use it as a porch light, which is on a lot, but my wife likes our existing porch light fixture better than this one, so I did not get my wish.
profile.summary: A pretty basic-looking light, but works well

profile.description: The Belkin Wireless USB Multimedia Keyboard sets up quickly, with no software necessary
profile.reviewText:
This wireless keyboard from Belkin works fine. Plug into your computer the USB adapter that you will find hidden in the compartment on the back of the keyboard, and you are set to go. No driver to install from a CD, or any other fuss. Just plug and play. (Although you do have to add a couple of AA batteries first.) I was a little surprised that the keyboard had no "on" or "off" switch, or any light or other signal to indicate that the keyboard has power and is ready to go. It seems like it just uses power when keys are pressed, and the rest of the time it's just waiting in "off" mode without draining the battery.

The keyboard has no frills, but you do get a fairly full keyboard. You get a full number keypad, but some of the other buttons from my full-size keyboard are missing (like Insert, Delete, Home, Page Up, etc.). The keyboard is light but solid, and the keys have a nice feel to them, making it easy to type. I have not had any problems with the keyboard not keeping up with my typing, like some other reviewers have reported. I typed this review using the keyboard, and had no problems at all. (Perhaps I'm just a slow typist.)

All in all, you get a good, solid, if rather plain, keyboard that is worth the price you have to pay. I like it.
profile.summary: No frills, but solid

profile.description: Hard to find
profile.reviewText: A fascinating story about people and our food. Not a diet book, and not a medical book, The End of Overeating falls somewhere in between the two. Written by the former head of the Food and Drug Administration, the book reads very well. David Kessler still works in the medical field, apparently, and is now at the University of California, San Francisco. I'd say he will have a pretty good second career as a writer. Some doctors (like Michael Crichton, Tess Gerritsen, and Robin Cook) have done that, making the transition to best-selling fiction writers. But how many doctors, let alone former government bureaucrats, can write compelling and entertaining nonfiction? Like the chapter on Cinnabons, that had me salivating and smelling those wicked treats just by reading the words David Kessler wrote? Not many. The title did seem overreaching, though. David Kessler tells how many of us become "conditioned hypereaters." That is, we eat foods laden with fat and sugar even when we are not hungry and even though we are desperate to lose weight. We hate ourselves for it, but still we eat. David Kessler does offer some suggestions on what to do. From other reviews it seems like those suggestions have helped some readers. But I did not see anything in the book that pointed out how to Take Control of the Insatiable American Appetite. Or that foreshadowed the End of Overeating. I learned a lot about why we eat what we do, and that was interesting. But even David Kessler admitted that he struggles with his own weight. The End of Overeating does not provide any big secrets on how to win that struggle. Just why it is a struggle. That story it tells very well. [For a possible answer on how we might win the struggle with weight, take a look at Why Diet and Exercise Fail: How Current Research Contradicts Conventional Wisdom about Weight Loss. David Kessler's book has been heavily promoted and written about in the press. But I was more impressed with the thinking and suggestions in Why Diet and Exercise Fail.]
profile.summary: Title overreaches, but interesting

profile.description: Save water by eliminating the wait for hot water to reach the faucet. Simply tap into the water line and install the heater directly at the sink. No need for costly recirculating lines and pumps. And when you want to eliminate the wait for hot water but need more volume, install the Eco smart heater in-line with a larger hot water source, such as a thankless heater or a storage tank heater. Lightweight and compact, these units plug into a standard 110 volt outlet.
profile.reviewText:
I like the convenience of having hot water available immediately at the faucet. This unit provides enough hot water to do anything we need it to do. It won't last for a shower, but our hot water tank handles that. For washing a few dishes at the sink, this unit works wonderfully. It seems nicely made, and was easy to install.

There are a few drawbacks. First, it takes up quite a bit of space in the cupboard under the sink where we put it. We used to use that space for a variety of things. It's valuable space, most of it now dedicated to this unit.

Second, I'm worried about water leaking in that space. Several people have noted that these small tanks don't last too long, and when they do spring a leak, it can be a disaster. With a big water heater, it's important to have a way for leaking water to drain outside. Seems the same for this. But we don't have any way to handle that in this space. It's a worry.
profile.summary: Convenient, but . . .

profile.description: Samsung's SL-M3320ND ProXpress 35 ppm monochrome laser printer provides fast, professional quality and lower operating costs.
profile.reviewText:
For a laser printer without other functions like copying, faxing and scanning, this printer seems bulky and heavy. But if all you need is good, reliable, and cheap black-and-white printing, this printer will fit the bill. It works well. One pro is that it prints on both sides of the page.

A couple of cons. First, it is a network printer but not a wireless printer. If you want to use it wirelessly, you need to attach an access point device. Second, the toner appears to be expensive. I have not purchased any toner yet, but am not looking forward to having to do that. The replacement toner is priced on Amazon at a higher price than the printer!

On sale, this printer seems good value. At list price, perhaps not so much.
profile.summary: Good quality, but a couple of cons

top_5.description: The FlexFit Classic Wristwrap from Harbinger Fitness features a new technology that takes fitness gloves to a new level of performance and responsiveness. The innovative Tri-Flex Palm provides three dimensional movement to your hand, mimicking the hand's natural motion for the best possible fitting glove. The benefit of the Tri-Flex Palm is that it allows the hand to move naturally and comfortably when training, maximizing control and feel of the training surface. It's the perfect union of comfort and performance. The patented graduated WristWrap with Fit Lock, insures a customized fit while maintaining the proper positioning of the glove, wrist and hand during lifting. A Close Contact design minimizes bulk, supporting and protecting hands for maximum feel on the bar. The ergonomic curved finger design fits the natural shape of the hand increasing flexibility and comfort and the extended  finger length maximizes hand protection. Exclusive Wash & Dry leathers and Comfort Tech fabrics stay supple, breathable and last longer. Improve your workout with the latest advances in fitness gloves from the #1 workout glove manufacturer, Harbinger.
top_5.reviewText:
I'm not a hardcore weightlifter, but I do like to get to the gym at least two or three times a week. Weightlifting gloves help keep the calluses on my hands from getting too thick. (Of course, that the gloves make me look a lot more like a hardcore lifter has never entered my mind, and has absolutely nothing to do with the fact that I wear them.)

These gloves are a great pair. They are comfortable, give good support, protect my hands, and look good. The only complaint I have is that the wrist straps (what they call wrist wraps) do not work well for me. It's hard to get them wrapped right. Sometimes they dig into my hands. Sometimes they pinch hairs. Sometimes they are hard to secure with the velcro.

I'm sticking with these gloves. Their problems are minor -- I can live with them. But if the wrist straps were a little better, they would be perfect.
top_5.summary: Good gloves. I really like them. If the wrist straps were a little better, they would be perfect.

top_5.description: Lacoste men's 3-pack 100 percent essentials cotton trunk boxed
top_5.reviewText:
These briefs look good and feel good. They are very comfortable, made with 100% "supima" cotton. Supima cotton is apparently "superior" Pima cotton grown in the United States. The cotton has longer, more durable fibers than normal cotton, thus making it the "cashmere of cottons". I am not sure I would go that far, but it is noticeably different from other cottons in feel.

The price too seems superior too, in the sense that it is higher than what I would normally expect. Part is probably the Supima cotton, and perhaps part the Lacoste brand (each pair of briefs has a little alligator on it). But I think the price is fair for what you get.

Be aware, though, that these briefs do not have a fly opening in front, like most briefs do. So they are not as convenient at the urinal.
top_5.summary: A cut above normal briefs

top_5.description: The Machine That Changed the World: The Story of Lean Production-- Toyota's Secret Weapon in the Global Car Wars That Is Now Revolutionizing World Industr [ The Machine That Changed the World: The Story of Lean Production-- Toyota's Secret Weapon in the Global Car Wars That Is Now Revolutionizing World Industr by Womack, James P. ( Author ) Paperback Mar- 2007 ] Paperback Mar- 01- 2007
top_5.reviewText:
The title sets the tone the authors carry throughout the book. A little too much glorifying. A little too much hype. Yes, what Toyota and others did was impressive. But no, they did not change the world. In my opinion, not even close.

And this book is dated. In fact, though written in the early '90s, it reads more like many of the books written about Japanese management in the early '80s. Books like "Japan As Number One." Or "Trading Places." At the time, the Japanese were thought to be able to do no wrong.

Now, of course, we know that Japanese executives and managers are mere mortals too. Toyota has certainly done better than most Japanese companies over the last 15 years. And part of the reason -- a big part probably -- has been the effectiveness of their management in areas like lean production. But even without the benefit of the hindsight we now have, the authors of this book should have realized that their unstinted praise was not warranted. Even for the brains behind Toyota.

Still, this book is the best I have found on the history of the "Industry of Industries." It traces the history of the automobile industry from craft production to mass production to lean production. No other book I have read has done that so well.

And for an academic book, The Machine That Changed the World is easy to read. It keeps a careful balance between informing the reader and keeping the reader's interest. Most writers, particularly of works like this, tilt too much one way or the other. Either too dry and pedantic or too light and entertaining. A happy medium is hard to achieve.

Where does the auto industry go from here? Lean production is no longer exceptional. It has become the rule. But it seems to have run its course.

The future of the automobile industry may lie in "collaborative production." Major automakers concentrate on sales and service, not production. Suppliers develop specialized skills in technologies from hybrid power trains to drive-by-wire control systems. And everyone sells to everyone else. Technology becomes less important than brand.

If that is the case, Toyota may still lead the pack. In Business Week's list of the top 100 global brands, Toyota leads all carmakers at number 7. No one has caught Toyota napping on the increasing importance of brand.

Even so, Toyota fiercely defends the idea that is a motor company, not a sales company. Innovative technology and excellent manufacturing have been much more of a focus than sales. Will it be able to adapt if the industry does change?

An interesting question that we should see answered in the next few years.  Like many good history books, The Machine That Changed the World gives us hints as to what that future will be.
top_5.summary: Excellent book, but dated and perhaps a little too fawning
