NFC cuts the pairing process to a fraction of a second and is as easy as putting your Android device on top of the ARCTIC S113BT. Powerful Bluetooth 4.0 connectivity gives you true stereo sound far superior than what the tiny speakers from your mobile device can ever produce even with your device is 30 feet away from the ARCTIC S113BT! ARCTIC S113BT supports the same high quality Advanced Audio Coding (AAC) digital audio format popularized by YouTube, iPhone, iPod, iPad, Nintendo & PlayStation 3 and delivers better sound quality than MP3 at similar bit rates. ARCTIC S113BT is also compatible with aptX digital audio codec compression technology that brings you high quality audio virtually identical as wired speakers with an impressive dynamic range and crisp clarity. Standard 3.5mm audio cable is provided if you prefer wired connection. Dual full-range drivers & two bass radiators deliver excellent sound indoor and outdoor. Built-in rechargeable battery provides up to 8 hours of playback in a single charge. ARCTIC S113BT has a rubberized protective casing in a petite footprint of only 7"x3"x2" that weighs only 14 oz. A padded nylon carrying case keeps it safe and dry wherever you go. The integrated omni-directional microphone in ARCTIC S113BT turns it into your portable speaker box in the car or in conference room. ARCTIC S113BT supports NFC and/or Bluetooth-enabled devices running iOS/Android/Windows. Feel free to pair ARCTIC S113BT with your smartphones, tablets, e-reader, MP3, laptop and even desktop enjoying full stereo audio without tangling speaker wires. ARCTIC 113BT comes with a 2-year limited warranty and there are 6 different colors to choose from for different lifestyles. Contact arctic.us@arctic.ac for services.
profile.reviewText: ...the Arctic S113BT delivers surprisingly big sound from a very compact speaker. In addition, operation for Bluetooth connectivity is intuitive and was issue free. In the box are the speaker, a zippered storage/carrying case, two cables (a 3.5mm aux stereo cable for wired input and a micro USB cable for charging its battery) and a user guide. The speaker enclosure is covered with a non-slip rubberized material. It has three control buttons on the front panel (for volume up/down and one for BT pairing). On the right side are a separate on/off switch and the micro USB and aux in ports. This speaker was immediately recognized by both a HTC Evo 4G LTE and an iPod Nano (7th gen) in traditional Bluetooth pairing. My phone and this speaker have NFC capability (which I did not test). The sound was excellent across highs and midrange. Don't expect to rattle windows or annoy neighbors with the bass response, but for filling a room with crisp sound from your Bluetooth source, this speaker does a great job (and with an 8 hour battery life,should get you through most parties or workdays). Select with confidence. Note: this item was provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Surprisingly big sound from a very compact speaker...

profile.description: Dock up to two 2.5in or 3.5in SATA SSDs/HDDs in a stylish black docking station with an integrated 2-port USB 3.0 hub,SATA Hard Drive Docking Station,USB to SATA Docking Station,HDD USB Docking Station,UASP Supported,80mm Fan,SATA 6 Gbps
profile.reviewText: This dual-bay docking station for 2.5" or 3.5" SATA hard drives (HDD or SSD) works well and has a number of features that increase its overall utility. I've used many different external enclosures over the years, most often as part of either a system or hard drive upgrade process (and less often as part of a data recovery effort, usually following a major OS or hardware hiccup). The "SDOCK2U33HFW" was readily recognized by both Windows 7 and Window 8 machines. I tested with one 2.5" SSD and one 3.5" HDD. After a brief initialization period, both appeared as standard lettered drives. Among the features that add to this device's usefulness are a front data port (that can be set for charging only) and a a control wheel on the back for adjusting the fan speed (or turning it off). Considering that it was running an uncased mechanical drive and a fan, overall operation was generally quiet. If you have a recurring need to rapidly access the contents of SATA drives, this is a good choice for that task. Note: this item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Good option for those who need rapid access to multiple hard drives...

profile.description: TerraMaster F2-NAS 2 is a private cloud, it not only makes your file storage and sharing easy and convenient, but also realizes low cost data sharing and storage for families and small sized offices. TerraMaster F2-NAS 2 adopts silver all-aluminium material. Its anodized and frosted process makes it look stable and high-end, and ensures better heat dispersion under long time working hours; Removable hard disk, accumbent working brings safer and more stable performance when rotating with high speed. Specific handle design is a humanized concept, it makes NAS convenient to move and carry. It's every detail can embody the design concept of considerate and best service. It processes mighty Marvell 1.6 GHz imbedded CPU and 512MB DDRIII, supports two 3.5 inch SATA hard disk, and can keep high speed work with low power consumption. Its powerful system provides single disk, JBOD, RAID0, RAID1, and mirror backup protection, which ensures safety of data storage.
profile.reviewText: The Terra Master TM-F2-NAS (F2) networked attached storage (NAS) device offers a strong hardware environment for adding up to 8TB of storage capacity accessible via a variety of physical and services options. Like other NAS devices, this is not for the technically timid. Those already familiar with NAS devices won't find many surprises. Users who are generally comfortable with the basics of multiple disk (especially RAID) management and common network service/data transfer should also be fine. Those who like their SOHO computing to be totally plug and play (or nearly so) can expect to be frustrated without assistance from a reliable alpha geek (which seems to be common among all NAS products). Pros: -Hardware. The F2 has a self-contained 1.6GHZ processor and 512 MB of RAM. -Storage capacity: accommodates up to 8 GB total storage (via 2x 3.5" SATA drive bays). -Abundant network service options: all the usual suspects, plus a few that were new to me (see "Cons" discussion below!) -Powerful configuration options through a detailed browser-based user interface. -Large data storage capacity (up to 4 TB redundant and 8 TB non-redundant) -Multiple connectivity options (ethernet, eSATA and USB 3.0 ports are all available). I have not tested connecting either a USB or eSATA device to the F2. Cons: -"China-centric" defaults (including Shanghai as the default time zone, and a great possibility of content on the Terra Max website appearing in Chinese. I don't have an automatic bias against "made in China", but since these are being marketed in North America, defaults to this region would be better. -Similarly, the quick start guide, user guide and user interface could benefit from additional work by editors with stronger English language skills. The contents aren't profoundly bad, but are often non-informative due to their awkward usage. -Even though a more current firmware version was available on the Terra Master website, the only firmware upgrade instructions I found were in Chinese. I'm pretty confident in figuring out computer tasks like this, but would *not* risk attempting something that could brick my system without the assistance of instructions in English that I confidently understood. -Bumpy integration with Windows: I got there, but had to do some digging (who knew that Samba services had to be enabled for Windows networking integration...not me, until I dug into the user guide). -Fan sound levels: the F2's fan can be manually set to either low (500-900 rpm), medium (900-1600 rpm), high (1600-2000 rpm) speed or to an automatic "smart mode". At the medium or high speeds (and when the auto places it in this range), fan noise is very noticeable. None of these are show-stoppers for users already comfortable with the concepts addressed at the the start of this review. Just be aware they could present problems for those with reduced levels of networking, disk management and general SOHO computing kung fu. I used two WD Red 1TB 3.5" SATAIII hard drives --specifically designed for the "always on" 24/7 demands of NAS-- as the storage hardware for the F2. I set these up in a RAID 1 (mirrored) configuration, resulting in slightly less than 1 TB of fully redundant storage. The F2 also offers "JBOD" (just a bunch of disks) and RAID 0. These two options do not include any redundancy: lose one drive and lose all your data. Users whose overriding needs are sheer volume or slight gains in performance (and who have another backup strategy) will want to consider the JBOD and RAID 0 choices. Initial set-up took about 15 minutes as the browser interface walked me through basic configuration options. After that, it took about 2 hours for the F2 to have the disks prepared for RAID 1 service. The browser-based interface for the F2 is generally very good. Options are deep, and similar ones are managed categorically (some via a tabbed interface, some on their own pages). I was able to rapidly integrate this into my existing backup software via both Windows file management and FTP options. Windows integration is slightly awkward as the F2 inconsistently displays as both its device name and IP address; I'm continuing to work through understanding this behavior. Overall, this is a strong NAS device. It would be stronger if it assumed less about users' overall technical expertise (common among all NAS units I've worked with) and with stronger attention to the language needs of North American customers (on the website, in the user guide and --occasionally-- within the user interface options). Note: this item was provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Solid hardware; like most NAS devices, not for the technical novice....

profile.description: Full HD 1080p two channel compatible dash cam with 140-degree viewing angle. Equipped with a Road Safety Warning System  FDWS, LDWS. Built-in Wi-Fi for easy video playback and device configuration through a compatible iOS or Android smartphone. Built-in GPS for Red Light and Speed Camera Alerts, and embeds data (speed, time, and location) to video recordings.
profile.reviewText: ...but even with its self-proclaimed "premium" price, it's a strong perfomer that will serve both first time and experienced dashcam users well. Note: This review originally included sample video from this camera. However, amazon's processing (compression for streaming) rendered the source HD with so much pixelation that I have since removed it. The original video was very high quality, and the video degradation from the processing did not provide a good example of the camera's video quality. The Thinkware M750 product description and packaging call it a "dash cam". Such a description falls short of what it really offers, which is windshield-mounted, GPS-enabled video capture and aftermarket vehicle safety features. While there's no doubt that the F750 is in a premium price range for a dashcam market that is awash in lower priced commodity items, as the price of competing products decreases, they also start to shed features and usability. Users will have to decide for themselves if the F750's combination of features and pricing provides the functionality and value they need. One thing I'm sure of: its default performance and documentation will run circles around most less costly options. The M750 arrives with some strikingly obvious pros and some downsides that are design choices I may not agree with..but that in no way are show-stoppers. Here's what it does real nicely: -Video quality: Wow. The 1080p HD video captured by this camera is easily the best I've seen from any dashcam. Awesome clarity and faithful color rendering. -Interface options: this camera does not have an on-camera display (a choice that I prefer). On-camera buttons provide options for major functions (power, WiFi, audio enable/disable and manual recording). All other settings are accessed either via a smart phone or desktop computer app. -Overall, mostly intuitive operation. -Outstanding documentation: the best writing and illustrations (in both the included print start guide and the .pdf full manual available from Thinkware's support website) that came with any dashcam I've used to date. If you've used a dashcam with bad documentation, you'll know why this is important. -Extra feature 1: Lane departure warning: If you drive a late-model vehicle with lane-departure notification, you probably already know that most of these work through video analysis of roadway lane markings. When you first set up this camera (which I did via an Android phone using its onboard WiFi), the app will display the vertical and horizontal sensing lines for the centerline and front edge of your hood (respectively). Once calibrated through positioning of the camera (hint: work this out BEFORE you mount it with included window adhesive or you'll be in for some heartache with later adjustments to the centerline; the front edge (horizontal) is easily corrected through rotation of the lens mount), I found the lane departure notifications (two audible beeps) to perform similarly to the OEM function in late model cars. If you already have a factory installed warning system, you probably won't care about this. -Extra feature 2: Forward collision warning: This works just fine. While I found it to be somewhat more concerned about following distance than the OEM system on a 2014 GM vehicle, it's a nice aftermarket solution to cars that don't have them. -Very good support information on the Thinkware website. -Overall good user interface with both the Android and PC apps (with two exceptions noted below); great flexibility for managing video between the camera's storage and your phone (note: recording stops when you are connected to an Android device via WiFi). -Included 16GB microSD card (supports up to 64GB). -Love the .mp4 video capture choice; much smaller file size than many other format options. Note: Any pixelation/graininess in the accompanying video are a product of Amazon's processing of the source HD video (compression for streaming). The original video is very high quality, and any video degradation seen here is an artifact of Amazon's processing, not the fault of the camera being reviewed. Why four stars instead of five? If you've never used a dashcam before, none of these might matter to you. Further, I readily agree that some of these are design options that aren't inherently better or worse than the alternatives (but: I know what I like). These are not showstoppers in any way, but some things you need to prepare for as you make the commitment to the premium pricing category of dashcams): -Adhesive tape windshield mounting. To its credit, Thinkware explains in its support FAQ why it chose adhesive mounting over suction cup mounting (less vibration and more security in the event of crash). However, even with two mounting brackets included, this limits the portability to two vehicles. I prefer the unlimited portability of a suction cup mount. -Overall mass/size: this is among the heaviest and bulkiest dashcams I've used. This comes as a particular surprise in the absence of an on-camera display. -microSD for recording media: I have an irrational hatred of this form factor. This a is a camera large enough to easily accommdate standard SD card. They are easier to insert/remove, and far less likely to take a spring-loaded trip into the neverland between the seats of a car. -Date-time inscrutability: To correctly get local time read into the camera (for both displayed data in the video and file names), the only setting are to provide input for your GMT offset and daylight savings time status; the camera then converts based on time input from GPS data. I know my GMT offset..but many users may not. -The PC program for viewing this camera's video and geographic/g-force data overall is very strong...with one notable exception: the Google maps display represents a very small portion of the Thinkware application. Unfortunately, it can't be detached or resized. I'm hoping Thinkware will correct this in a later version. The F750 comes at a price that may cause frugal shoppers to pause. It brings a lot to the table for that price, and the things it does well, it does very well. The things that may not be quite perfect aren't so bad as to interfere with the goodness of the things it does right.
profile.summary: Full-featured and full-sized (and yes: a price to match both)...

profile.description: Samsung LEVEL-On Premium Stereo Headphones for Smartphones - Black
profile.reviewText:
...as somebody who is notoriously tone deaf and has had confirmation in blind testing that I can't differentiate a full range CD from a compressed .mp3 source, perhaps high end headphones are wasted on me.

However, after many years of listening to my most favored tunes through many types of speakers and headsets, I can tell when a device is adding value to my listening experience. This is particularly true of headphones, and I expect good headphones to bring presence and clarity to music. They should not only convey what is familiar after many listens, but should leave me with new appreciation for subtleties in voice and instrumentation that I've not noticed before.

The Samsung LEVEL headphones were wide of this mark. Overall I can only describe their sound as flat. I don't mean flat as in neutral, where the sound is clear but there's no overemphasis on high, mid or bass tones (which I consider a good thing), but I mean flat as in distant and subdued. I tested these with both .mp3 and CD audio sources, and noticed the overall lack of presence and clarity across multiple music genres.

While the sound is generally acceptable, you can get acceptable sound from headphones costing a lot less.

The fit and finish are nice, as is the detachable cord and the hinged earpieces that permit storage in the semi-hard case. The only jack is a 3.5mm. Users planning to use this with the standard 1/4" jack on many A/V components will need an adapter, which I also consider a shortfall on a premium headset.

I've had decent experiences with other Samsung products, but this one delivers average sound at an above average price.
profile.summary: Average sound at a premium price...

profile.description: Wireless Gateway Brown Box Kit
profile.reviewText:
This is an updated version (same model number) of the Internet/telephony modem Comcast originally provided four years ago as part of the solution to an indoor/outdoor troubleshooting effort. Finally, after looking at the $10/month  "rental" (alternate spelling: "gouging") that Comcast charged for this hardware, I decided to eliminate that fee by bringing my own device. This is one of about two dozen on Comcast's "supported device" list (even though under the DOCSIS standard, we should be hardware-agonostic...we're not). Be sure to visit your provider's support site for a list of supported devices (which will vary by both provider and your level of service).

This arrived with detailed instructions for a self-installation and provisioning in Comcast's network. It took less than 30 minutes (including network recognition and device updates) after providing account number/telephone number login.

Pros:
-DOCSIS 3.0 compliant.
-Integrated 4-port wired LAN and 802.11 wireless router.
-Accommodates two phone lines.
-I set it up "upstream" from my existing wireless router (coax into this device and the router connected from one its four wired ports); now I have the flexibility of two wireless networks  and 8 total wired points (well, seven really, but you get the idea). Very nice.

Cons:
-None noted. The predecessor was going strong after four years, so I expect this to take me to 2020 (and to have my monthy "rental" savings recouped in 16 months).

The backup battery (for phone service) charges slowly. It arrived at 42% charge indicated (via the router's internal web-based interface) after eight hours had charged to 80%. It was fully charged sometime in the first 24 hours after setup.

Select with confidence.
profile.summary: Rock solid Internet and telephony data delivery...

profile.description: Did you know deep down dirt and pet stains can get left behind by vacuuming alone? Well the Bissell PROheat 2X Pet can help. Bissell is the only brand with a hot water heater, continuously heating water and solution to maximize cleaning effectiveness. And the PROheat 2X Pets dual rotating PowerBrushes help agitate and remove deep down dirt so you have powerful pet clean-up at your fingertips, anytime you need it. Also included are EdgeSweep brushes for full width cleaning, Surround Suction for full coverage cleaning around baseboards and furniture, and a ready-to-use hose and hand tool for use on carpet, stairs, upholstery, and auto interiors.
profile.reviewText: I selected this machine specifically to remediate some of the long-term effects showing on a light-colored Berber carpet in our basement. Installed five years ago, it has endured the cumulative effects of three geriatric cats (who often had trouble keeping their dinners down), three rambunctious dogs, the comings and goings of several crowds of autumn party-goers, a sweet 16 party, a couple of New Year's Eve soirees and some on-again, off-again jam sessions with groups of teenage and young adult musicians. Bottom line: we had an excellent 800 square foot test track to work with. Overall, this cleaner did an excellent job. Pros: -Easy assembly. Three screws for the handle, one for the upper hose reel and you're done in less than than 10 minutes. Everything else slides/snaps easily and relatively intuitively into place. -Detailed user manual and full color quick start guide. -Good water management system. The water tank consists of an exterior hard plastic tank with an integrated soft inner bladder. You fill the bladder with hot top water, and the cleaning process returns the dirty water into the hard exterior tank (which you empty). -Cleaned very well. Look: in real life, the difference is never going to be as dramatic as in the marketing pictures. But we had some definite problem areas that showed residual staining even after multiple treatments with various cleaners and spot removers. This machine took care of those, as well as some ground-in soiling from where an HVAC crew had worked to replace a heat pump two years ago. -The cleaning tool extension worked well on carpeted step treads. Keeping this machine from five stars: --no real good way to tell when the fresh water bladder is empty (and several times it was empty before I noticed). So you'll need to check often as your work proceeds. --the tool hose is for use with both furniture and stairs. As a stair tool, it's only long enough to reach about halfway up/down a typical 13-step staircase, so you'll have to plan your work accordingly. Expect to either carry it over your freshly cleaned --but not yet dry-- treads (or carry it all the way around the exterior of your house if you have exits at both levels). Finally: this ships with enough Bissell 2X concentrate cleaning solution to fill the reservoir (in a water/cleaner mix) one time. My local Wal-Mart doesn't carry this, but does carry a 2x concentrate for carpet cleaners by Resolve; the Resolve brand is marked for use with Bissell cleaners and works just fine (even though the user guide says "Bissel brand cleaner only). Just make sure you have enough hand when you start. I got about 800 square feet of carpet cleaning with a single reservoir fill-up. FYI, the Bissell product has slight citrus scent when first applied; it rapidly dissipates.
profile.summary: Cleaned up five years of fun from our carpet very nicely...

profile.description: Add a splash of sound with the Splash SoundBox. This Marine Grade Speaker comes equipped with Bluetooth wireless technology and brings audio wherever you go. Easily stream and play music from virtually any Bluetooth enabled device quickly and easily - that includes your smartphone, MP3 player, tablet, computer, etc. Rugged splash proof and shock resistant design makes this portable speaker perfect by the pool, visits to the beach, hiking and just about any outdoor activity. Features include built-in rechargeable battery, easy-push button controls, impressive bass output and plenty more to add some audio to any occasion.
profile.reviewText: The PWPBTA70BKA provides very nice sound for sub-$100 speaker. In addition, it can accept input from a 3.5mm aux cable (included), and is splash and shock proof (the "splash proof" is standard-defined, the shock proof is claimed). This speaker is charged from a powered USB port via an included cable. It accepts audio inputs from both Bluetooth sources or a wired 3.5mm aux input on the speaker bottom. PROS: -Very nice sound. Mids and highs are clear, and the bass is very well defined without being muddy or over-emphasized. You won't entertain the entire garden party, but this will do for a pool or deck area. -Wireless (Bluetooth) and wired (3.5mm aux) input options. -Tough rubber exterior and metal grills -Includes a hook for a tie-down or hanging CONS: Nothing significant, but be aware of the following: -I question the placement of the aux jack on the bottom of the speaker. -The packaging includes a picture of the speaker semi-submerged in water. Be aware the specification for liquid ingress is IPX4 ("water splashing against the enclosure shall have no harmful effect"). Pay attention to the speaker's name ("Splash") and resist the temptation to place it in water as shown on the box. Overall, this is a decent speaker for outdoor use with Bluetooth sources. Note: This item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Tough portable speaker with decent sound, multiple input options...

profile.description: The HD 180-Degree Wi-Fi Camera (DCS-8200LH) with 180-degree Wide Eye lens keeps a vigilant eye on your home and provides crisp HD 720p video to watch your kids or pets with wall-to-wall coverage. Night vision allows you to see in total darkness and you can be notified whenever sound or motion is detected. With the microSD card slot you can record video directly from the camera so you never miss a moment. Stream live HD 720p video to your smartphone or tablet with the free mydlink Lite app for remote monitoring.
profile.reviewText:
This camera is an overall disappointment.

Initial set-up using an Android device (Galaxy S5) was relatively problem free. The essential item NOT included in the quick start guide is that both the camera and the phone need to be connected to the same WiFi network. Camera controls (settings and video.still capture) were relatively intuitive via the Android app. You will need to provide a valid email address to set up a "mydlink" online account.

This camera simply failed in it's ability to access its services via a PC:
-First,  D-link uses a browser plug-in  (instead of a dedicated Windows program) as the PC interface between the camera and D-Link home account This was problematic to install (took several attempts on a Windows 10 PC), and this will be a MAJOR  problem for non-technically savvy users. It also appears that the plug-in is limited to the Firefox browser. It was unclear to me how users of Chrome, Edge/Internet Explorer are to interact from a PC.

-The bigger problem: once installed, the plug-in and D-Link camera yielded an "unsupported device" message (screenshot shown), and invited me to remove the camera from my shiny new D-Link account. That this is a show stopper needs no further explanation.

Very disappointing performance in  a camera at this (or any) price.
profile.summary: Worked fine with an Android device, but not at all in PC browser...

profile.description: DEWALT UTC (Ultimate Trim Compressor )
profile.reviewText: I am an admitted newbie when it comes to air-driven tools. I am also not likely to ever use this for any large scale interior construction work (without a major upgrade to my DIY skills). But: I'm slightly obsessive about the fuel economy of the cars we drive. After choosing a vehicle and establishing driving habits, the next most important factor for fuel economy is properly inflated tires. Even knowing this, I have been in self-exile to gas station and convenience store air pumps. As a group these are of questionable reliability, and seem far better at making noise than quickly adding a couple of PSI to the hooptie's tires. This compressor has changed all that. In concert with 50 feet of 1/4" hose and a pneumatic tire inflator, maintaining the proper tire pressure (and keeping the garage free of blown-in debris!) is now a painless process. Bonus for my fellow citizens: they are no longer subject to images of me squatting in front of the place where they are trying to get a tank of gas and some to-go nourishment. At 75 PSI, I can add a pound or two to my tires in just seconds. This is a compact compressor that will run two hoses (I've only used it with one). Pressure regulation is via a single large regulator knob. Operation is relatively quiet and pressure is nearly immediately available. Overall, typical DeWalt quality of construction and attention to detail is obvious. Expert users of air tools may find my use case rather uninteresting...but this has elevated my care car environment immeasurably.
profile.summary: Many, many PSI of sweet pneumatic awesomeness clad in ebony and maize...

profile.description: A game for fans of Checkers and Cupcakes! Madd Capp Checkers a new way to play a classic game. Madd Capp Checkers adds a strategic twist, more risk and more fun. It's checkers with a POP! What's the twist? A unique dice popper means you can move your own cupcakes and even your opponent's cupcakes. The challenge is maddening. Cross the Madd Capp checker board and get "kinged" with what belongs on every special cupcake. A candle! Capture all of your opponent's cupcakes and you win! It's time to celebrate, so let's party! Come play!.
profile.reviewText:
Take a standard 8x8 checkerboard...
...change the checkers into opposing forces of chocolate and strawberry cupcakes.
....add a 3-dice popper that changes the gameplay from old-school back-and-forth to a variable chance to move either your or your opponent's pieces (to either your or your opponent's disadvantage.
...wrap it all up in a whimsical cupcake theme

...and you have a nice board game that you might want to toss in in the trunk as you head off for summer vacation (or keep on standby for the next wintery storm).

Who will like this game?
(1) Fans of checkers who should enjoy the variation brought on by a dice popper that directs you to move up to three pieces in a turn (in any combination of three that the strawberry/chocolate die faces can turn up)
(2) Fans of cupcakes. As it turns out, some people collect things that are cupcake themed...and this is such a thing.

It gets points for changing up checkers and cupcakey-ness.
profile.summary: Shake up your old school checkers with dice and cupcake theme...

profile.description: Bolse 300Mbps Wireless-N mini Router
profile.reviewText: The Bolse 300Mbps Wireless-N mini router provides a relatively inexpensive expansion of a current wired router's functionality (to add wireless LAN services) or to expand the connectivity/configuration options of a current wireless network. Pros: -Nicely packaged (router is cradled in a conformal foam cusion -Rapidly detected by existing networks -Easy browser-based configuration -Good signal strength Cons: -Proximity to AC outlet AND existing wired router required (if using included 1 meter ethernet cable; this goes away if you use a longer one of your own). This device was immediately detected as an attached wired device when connected to my current router. Windows 7 wireless networking tools then immediately detected its default SSID and made it available for connection. Within five minutes I had change the SSID and applied encryption. Internet connectivity was indistinguishable from my normal Netgear router connection. Data from this router was available everywhere in the house where I access data wirelessly from my regular router. As I am already running a wired/wireless router, I don't have a specific use for this. But if you want to establish a separately configurable wireless network for gaming, guests or or other specialized purposes, this would make a perfectly acceptable choice for doing so. This could be a good choice if you currently have a wired-only network, and wanted to expand to a wireless environment. This could also be used when traveling to overcome limitations on laptop placement that can result from the location of wired-only connection. Arrives nicely packaged and with a good multi-color user guide. Note: This item was provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Good basic router functionality...

profile.description: Sanyo SanDisk 8GB Class4 MicroSDHC / TransFlash Card w/SD Adapter cell phone . This SanDisk 8 GB MicroSDHC / TransFlash Card w/SD Adapter is for you to expand the memory capacity for your compatible device like cell phone, PDAs, digital camera, music players, and more cool device that is with a microSD card slot available.It is ideal for storing media-rich files such as music, videos, and photographs. FEATURES: High storage capacity for storing essential digital content such as high quality photos, videos, music.
profile.reviewText: This card was installed as an upgrade the 2 GB card that shipped with an HTC EVO Shift 4G Android Phone Not so long ago, 2 GB may have seemed voluminous storage capacity, especially for a *phone*. But with a 5 megapixel still/video camera and the ability to suck in a wide range of multimedia content (and use your phone to listen to your digital music), a 2 GB storage volume quickly fills up. If you have a large digital music collection or are a prolific photographer/videographer/sound recorder, having the extra capacity lets you focus more on capturing or using your content, and worry less about data file space management. Data cards tend to either work right way or not...this one worked immediately. The additional storage space was immediately recognized by the phone, and the phone's Android operating system files, settings and data (which I copied to the card prior to the install) were similarly recognized without missing a beat. 8 GB cards are very affordable right now, making a removable media storage upgrade for your smart phone about as expensive as a cup or two of your favorite designer coffee:-) Check your product specs to make sure it will recognize the full capacity of this item.
profile.summary: Excellent upgrade from original capacity card in HTC EVO Shift 4G

profile.description: Enjoy nutritious, fast and flavorful cooking with the Elite Platinum 10 Qt. Digital Pressure Cooker. The unique process of pressure cooking allows you to trap steam during the cooking process, thereby, cooking food evenly, sealing in nutrients, and, most important of all, retaining flavor. With a 24-hour delay timer, and a 10 quart inner pot you can cook a wide variety of meals for the whole family. Use the preset functions to cook delicious risotto, vegetables, meat, chicken, and much more with this versatile and elegant pressure cooker. Note: There will be steam coming out from top. The steam escapes from the unit to avoid the item building pressure and exploding. The vent provided is meant to allow steam to escape.
profile.reviewText:
...time will tell as we see how it stands up to regular use.

Until this arrived, I had never cooked with a pressure cooker, and I've been cooking for a long time. I have a vague memories of my grandparents cooking with one when I was a kid, and vague memories of it being regarded with a mix of wonder and worry whenever it appeared in their kitchen.

Overall, this cooker is very easy to use. The included instruction guide is well written and thorough. Because this is a device that cooks with water and steam under pressure, I can't  recommend enough that you spend some time with it before you start loading the cooking container with stuff.
The recommended test run is with water (I used the soup setting), which will verify the cooker's overall functionality and familiarize you with its controls.

This is generally very easy to use, and the included recipes offer many starting places if you are new to pressure cooking.
Also for those new to pressure cooking: the time it takes for the pressure to build and the cooking countdown to begin will vary. Also variable is  the time for the cooker to be safe to open when the timer is finished. Expect at least five minutes if using the "quick release" option, and considerably longer (up to 30 minutes) if using the "natural release" option (which extends cooking effects).

It's not without quirks, however.
If you don't use the "delay start" timer, that portion of the digital display will show animated LED segments to indicate that pressure is building before the default cooking timer begins counting down on the right half of the display. This is somewhat hidden in the user guide (and is really the guide's only deficiency).

The cooker has a browning function (via the "Fish & Vegetables" menu item used with the lid off). Overall, some browning might be more easily accomplished in a separate pan on the stove.

As of the time of this review, the web site shown in the user guide was not available. I was able to find a .pdf version of the user guide elsewhere, but should there be a future issue, I hope the toll-free number works...because the web site doesn't.
profile.summary: Four stars out of the gate...

profile.description: HP ScanJet 3970 Digital Flatbed Scanner
profile.summary: Terrific performer for about $100

Goal Zero's Portable Solar Power Essentials Kit is the ultimate solution to keeping your handheld electronics charged up anywhere you go.  Use the Nomad 7 solar panel to charge up your cell phone, GPS and iPods directly using the USB port. Store your solar power in your Guide 10 Plus Battery Pack. Use the Guide 10 Plus to power up your cell phones, Tablets, GPS, iPods, Cameras and really anything that can charge off of the 1 amp USB port. The Guide 10 also includes a built in LED light that lasts up to a 150 hours. You can also charge up your AA and AAA batteries as well through the Guide 10 Plus. Plug in the Luna USB Light into the Guide 10 Plus or your laptop to brighten up your night. The Nomad 7 has a built in pocket to store your Guide 10 Plus or cell phone and folds up to be lightweight, compact, and weather resistant.

    Keep your power hungry phone juiced and ready for you to use
    Power up your tablet for 25% longer
    Recharge up the AA or AAA batteries right from the sun  
    Small and compact enough to carry with you always and power up anywhere  
    Handy built-in LED flashlight in the Guide 10 Plus to help you search in your dark backpack or purse  
    9" bendable cord lets you secure the Luna USB Light around objects
    Kit includes:
    - Nomad 7 Solar Panel  
    - Guide 10 Plus battery pack  
    - 4 AA and 4 AAA rechargeable batteries  
    - Luna USB LED light
profile.reviewText: The Goal Zero solar essentials kit is a collection of products also sold separately by Goal Zero that will answer a variety of solar charging needs for many mobile devices and electronics powered by AAA or AA batteries. The kit includes: -The "Nomad 7" a bi-fold solar panel (with zippered mesh storage compartment); this will either provide direct charging to devices during daylight or charge the included NiMH charging pack (for both AAA and AA batteries) -The "Guide 10 Plus" NiMH battery recharging unit; includes 4 AA batteries and 4 AAA batteries (can also be charged via a USB input) -The "Luna" 10-element USB LED -Cables for connecting to a 12v auto adapter, direct output to a USB port and for charging the battery pack. All of these fold into a 7" x 9" self-contained package that weighs slightly over 1 pound. If you're going to be outdoors in the daylight and can't live without your mobile devices, this is a good option for helping get past the limitations of their normal battery life.
profile.summary: Multiple solar-powered charging options...plus!

profile.description: Penclic B2 utilizes Bluetooth technology. Having Bluetooth technology available in a mouse allows for a fast, safe connection to your device, as well as not requiring a USB port. Penclic Mouse B2 changes a little bit from our other mouses by being available in white, instead of the black associated with Penclic R2 and D2. But don't worry. Penclic B2 still maintains its smooth and stylish looks!
profile.reviewText: Mouse-assisted computing has come a long way since the days of dust-filled mechanical models able to operate only within the confines of a mouse pad and in wired proximity to an appropriate motherboard I/O shield. Every iterative improvement in mousing, whether adding more buttons, removing wires, adding software configurable options or an evolving array of ergonomic developments has served to improve our relationship with this iconic device of the human-machine interface experience. When offered the chance to test and review the Penclic B2 mouse, I particularly looked forward to the opportunity because of recent workplace experiences with a coworker with limited hand strength and motion issues that prevented nominal interactions with traditional mice. While the B2 is not offered as a piece of adaptive technology for the physically limited user, its packaging proudly claims "designed to prevent RSI" (repetitive strain injuries). Even after 30+ years of mousing, I have not experienced this, but know many who suffer painfully from such effects...and therefore welcome any chance not to join them. The Penclic B2 arrives flamboyantly packaged (some may consider it over-packaged) in a two-piece plastic cylinder nearly 3" taller than the unit it houses. The additional volume holds a retractable USB charger for the (included) AAA rechargeable battery, a quick start guide and a cloth storage pouch with a drawstring closure. While charging the battery I was able to easily pair the mouse with a Bluetooth-cabable netbook running Windows 8. And even though the Penclic arrived with a friendly note from the supplier indicating "a mouse like this can take some time getting used to after years with a traditional mouse", The Penclic and I did not become fast friends. Its overall user experience sent me hurrying back to a more conventional pointing device after several days of repeated frustration (unmitigated by increasing familiarity). The Penclic website claims "(the) Penclic Mouse is so responsive and intuitive that it almost feels like the mouse itself predicts where you are planning to move the cursor." My user experience was much different. Even after adjusting the mouse properties in the Windows 8 control panel, I found the pointer movement erratic. Pointer movement is controlled by the base, and it was generally imprecise (whether guided by hand on the base or moving the base with the cylindrical pen-like control unit. There is a considerable learning curve in mastering the five buttons. I found this learning curve so steep that I eventually resorted to labeling them with a Sharpie. The set of buttons that perform left, middle and right mouse functions are housed in a shield that presents with a very noticable gap between it and the pen body. This gap is noticeable enough that I thought it may have been a flaw or become unseated from the body. For all the obvious investment in style, this came as a surprising design element. Overall, this mouse delivers what it promises: Bluetooth mousing in a non-traditional form factor. This will probably apeal to the same users who (for whatever reasons) choose to use a trackball, a vertical mouse or other alternative pointing device technology. But they must prepare for a relatively steep learning curve in order to master this mouse. It may also appeal to those who value esthetics over utility in their peripheral devices. PROS: -Bluetooth connectivity (leaves USB ports available for other devices) -Multiple power options (rechargable or disposable AAA) -Included retractable recharging cable (permits use as battery recharges) CONS: -Learning curve to master control button functions (will vary among users; I found it steep) -Gap between mouse buttons shield and pen body looks shoddy -Imprecise mouse pointer positioning -Premium pricing for what is normally a commodity-priced item -Right-handed configuration only; southpaws will have to adapt -Probably over-packaged, but the big plastic tube should be recyclable. Note: This item was provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Form overtakes function, or: design in search of a problem to solve...

profile.description: Successor model for MDR-EX55  change to new hybrid silicone type earbuds for better sound, more comfort, and secure fit  three sizes (S, M, L)
profile.reviewText: Santa brought an iPod nano last week. Apparently my ears are asymmetrical, because I could not get the left earbud to stay in place. So, off to a nationwide brick and mortar store to look at aftermarket options to Apple's OEM earbuds. Alternatives ranged in price from $10 to $79. The cheapest were no-names, and the most expensive were "noise cancelling". I selected this product because: (1) it fell pretty much in the middle of the price range for available offerings at this store (2) It came with three different sizes of rubber inserts. One of the sizes was a perfect fit. Sound quality is excellent. The package includes a cord winder to manage slack in the cord...and a fabric case that can also hold the Nano.
profile.summary: Great alternative to iPod OEM earbuds

profile.description: The NETGEAR R6250 Smart Wi-Fi Router with AC dual band Gigabit delivers AC1600 Wi-Fi speeds. It offers the best wireless coverage for large homes and is ideal for homes with 8 or more wireless devices. It also provides the best connectivity for dual band wireless devices like iPad and iPhone5.
profile.reviewText: The Netgear R6250 AC1600 router offers a complete set of features that should satisfy the demands of most SOHO, family, home theater/entertainment and gaming users. Using its default configuration, I had wired and wireless devices connected to it and sharing both Internet connectivity and the contents of a USB hard drive in less than 10 minutes. This router is at the higher end of the price range for similarly performing routers. At that price is should be nearly perfect in every respect. I encountered some minor issues with my user experience that keeps this from five stars. These don't detract from its basic data delivery and sharing functions. PROS: -Front panel indicators for power, Internet connectivity and wireless transmitter operation -Pushbutton wireless on/off button on side panel -Dual 2.4 GHZ and 5 GHZ operating bands (independently selectable) providing 802.11 ac/n/g/b operation (collectively) -Home and guest network options (for both 2.4 GHZ and 5 GHZ bands) -USB 3.0 port with data sharing capability (via Windows networking settings or FTP) -Relatively easy set-up with basic default security enabled by default -Parental controls (by time or domain), port forwarding/prioritization (for gamers) and log/activity email notifications -DLNA server services for streaming content from an attached USB storage device CONS: -Some quirks in user interface; did not consistently display assigned IP address of all connected devices (even after manually assigning them) -No wired port connection/activity indicators in front panel. This may not be an issue for everybody, but I regularly use three or four wired devices, and like immediate visual feedback about which wired ports are connected. -"Constant on" backlit Netgear logo. As far as I could tell, there is no way to turn this off. If you need total darkness in a room, this will be an issue for you. -Wired port jacks are in a fairly confined space between the router base and its rear cover; users with large hands will notice this, especially when trying to remove the ethernet cables. These are relatively minor items. While they keep this router from five stars, its overall functionality and features are excellent, even at what I would consider the upper end of consumer wireless router pricing. This router recognized my (Comcast) Internet connection immediately. Its browser-based user interface immediately notified me that a firmware update was available. I accepted the prompt to proceed with the update, which took less than two minutes to complete. By default, this router initially connects wireless devices with WPA-PSK (AES) security using a factory configured SSID and password. 10 minutes after applying power to the router, I had the following devices connected: -Windows 7 laptop (wired) -Ubuntu desktop (wireless) -Two Android phones (wireless) -Kindle (wireless) -USB 3.0 external hard drive (for DLNA media streaming and remote data access) -A Sony TV The packaging for this router claims "best wireless coverage for large homes". While unscientific, an examination of signal bar meters on connected wireless devices showed this router was at least as strong as the existing one that ran at the same time. At the farthest point inside my house from the router, its RSSI was slightly stronger than the older Netgear router. While "best" is a subjective claim, I experienced a consistently strong signal throughout the house from this router. I'm a little picky about my network configuration, and always add hardware (MAC address) access controls to my network in addition to wireless encryption. The R6250 allowed me to easily capture the MAC addresses of attached devices and add them to the access control list. In addition, I like to reserve IP addresses for devices that connect regularly, and this router has easy to use options for doing this. Users new to router/network configuration will find enough acceptable default security options to be quickly up and running. Experienced users should find sufficient options to fully exercise the control they need. Other than sometimes not identifying the assigned IP address of attached wireless devices and the lack of wired connection LED indicators, I had no issues with any of this router's functions. profile.description: The innovative Rowenta Pro-compact IB9100 is the most compact ironing board when folded for easy transport and perfect storage. Pro-compact provides perfect stability and efficient ironing with an extra large ironing surface when open to iron faster large pieces of cloth. The thick branded cotton cover offers perfect ironing results without any prints left on the fabric. This is an easy-to-use, easy-to-store and easy-to-transport ergonomic product. To ensure long-lasting ironing board, metallic mesh platforms are treated against corrosion and robust materials provide durable high quality boards. The ironing surface is 54'' x 18 ''. The height is adjustable from 27 '' up to 37 '', the cover & pad is Extra Thick - 5 mm. In addition, it is feature with hanger rack, extra-Large steam iron & steam stations rest, integrated wheels and aluminum legs and feet.
profile.reviewText: ...you'll have to decide for yourself if Rowenta's premium pricing is worth it. Ironing is a weekly (and sometimes more often) event in our house. To be quite honest, we haven't been challenged by the performance of "standard" ironing boards over the years (and I couldn't tell you on a bet what the brand is of the ironing board we were using before this one arrived). The Rowenta IB9100U1 displays many obvious upgrades from a standard board. The legs that hold the rear base in place are doubled (and all three legs are rectangular rather than tubular). The ironing surface is substantially greater. Integrated into the board are a hanger rack and a storage shelf (the latter is specifically designed for Rowenta steaming products). The board is stable and the oversized ironing surface speeds up many ironing tasks. I can almost close our standard board with one hand. Both closing opening this Rowenta board are definitely two-handed operations, and not for the mobility impaired. The included user guide is printed on oversize cardstock and contains pictographs only; overall, I'm neutral on its effectiveness, especially since this is a three latch ironing board (one for the ironing surface extension, one for the main hinge raising/lowering, and one for the forward leg catch/release. If this board has a flaw, it's with the fit of the included cover. It does not secure as tautly on the board as I like, which causes wrinkling under your ironing work. One year warranty. It's not quite perfect, but should provide long service.
profile.summary: Good, big and sturdy (with big, sturdy pricing to match!)...

profile.description: The SunBell Solar Lamp and Phone Charger offers a unique all-in-one design. It works as a reading lamp, a ceiling lamp, a flashlight, and as a mobile phone charger. The rechargeable LiFePO battery requires only 3-4 hours of good sunlight to be fully charged. The dimmer switch lets you choose between 3 levels of LED light intensity and operating time. A 9 foot cable is hidden inside the solar disk, so the panel can be placed outside while the lamp or mobile phone can be stored safely inside a house, hut or tent while charging. Features & Benefits:  An all-in-one solar lantern and cell phone charger  Task light  when the lamp shade serves as a table stand  Ceiling light / lantern  when the lamp head is inserted into the lamp shade  Portable light / neck light  when the light unit and battery pack is detached from the lamp  High quality DC/DC USB adaptor that can be used with any mobile phone with a USB charging cable  1 LiFePO battery, 1.400 mAh / 3.2V with 2.000+ cycles (5-7 years)  3 High quality LEDs with adjustable light from 5 to 50 to 150 lumen, 5.500-6.000 kelvin  SunBOOST3 Technology for Max Powerpoint Tracking / battery protection  1.8 W Solar panel with 3m/9ft cable rolled up in solar disc  UV resistant ABS plastic housing  Splash proof covers for plugs  Shade can be used as a sound amplifier for mobile phone speakers  High light output: 150 lm for 4.5+ hours  Medium light output: 50 lm for 14+ hours  Low light output: 5 lm for 130+ hours  LED lifespan: 50,000 hours  Automatic dimming to lower modes at low voltage  Charging time PV: 3-8 hours depending on how much sun is available  Battery protection: self discharge, reverse polarity, trickle charge  Materials in housing: polycarbonate, ABS plastic, steel gooseneck  Dimensions (with lamp unit stored inside the shade): 16x16x16 cm or 6.3x6.3x6.3 inches. Weight 21.2 oz
profile.reviewText: The solar-powered Bright Sunbell is a combination LED (lamp and flashlight) and USB mobile device charger. It offers a lot to like. The things it does, it does well. Lighting: -As a solar-powered LED, lighting is provided via a 3-element LED with a 3-level switch that cycles the output between 5, 50 and 150 lumens. The lighting element can be stowed in the "bell" for lamp-like functionality; it can sit on a horizontal surface or be hung. -As a flashlight, it can be carried, worn around your neck or fixed to other objects as a snakelight (while retaining the three level capability). When fully charged, this light easily met its published spec of more than 4.5 hours of operation. Mobile device power: -When fully charged, it consistently delivered 5V output to USB devices. I'm not sure why Bright chose a separate charging dongle instead of just using a USB port. At first I wasn't completely sold on the design of the solar panel and charging cable. The panel snaps into the bottom of the bell, with the solar panels facing the outside, and the 3 meter cable is tucked inside semi-rigid flaps ion the reverse of the solar panel. This seemed to be an invitation to damaging the surface of the solar cells. However, in viewing the Bright Products website, this design becomes more understandable: this product was designed for developing areas of the world as an alternative to more expensive (and hazardous) kerosene lanterns. This allows separation of the the solar panel from the device. However, I'm still not a fan of the stowage of the charging cable inside the panel. The process of removing the cable caused some of the insulation to be superficially stripped. There's no way to assess this product without addressing the price. The market is crowded with small, solar-powered charging/lighting options, and many cost less than this. If price is your only criteria, this may not be for you. But in looking at both the company's stated design goals of helping those without ready access to a reliable electrical grid and the overall utility of its functions, I feel that it is worth the sticker price. Select with confidence; you don't know when your next power outage is coming! Note: this item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Lots of utility and a couple quirks...

profile.description: In Brooklyn, we know a thing or two about being bold and when we say this coffee is bold you betta believe it's bold. To get a perfect dark roast, the beans are removed from the roasters right before they get to their peak roasting point. This helps them retain their sharp floral notes and all the smoky goodness without any of the burnt aftertaste. When these beans with big-time flavor are brewed through our patented tension- based filters, they create a Cup of Joe that will delight lovers of good strong coffee. The Bold Variety Pack includes: Boardwalk Blend, Corner Donut Shop, Cyclone, Express-O, French Roast and Fuhgeddaboutit.
profile.reviewText:
Over time, I've come to prefer my coffee (and especially the first cup or two of the day) to be on the lighter side of flavor. I consider this a sign of a maturing palette after believing that the midwatch coffee served during my US Navy days was the standard; now I know it was just overcooked and overpowering.

To me, one of the true tests of a light roast is the flavor it delivers without being overbearing.

Brooklyn Bean Roastery's Light Roast Breakfast blend gets this perfectly right.

The flavor is rich with a clear presence without being overpowering or bitter.

It's a crowded market competing for your first morning cup.

This is well worth considering for that (or for that cup you might enjoy at the end of day).

Select with confidence.

Note: this item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Proof: light roast doesn't have to mean light on flavor...

profile.description: Black Box dashboard cameras feature stunning 1080p HD video and audio recording, night vision capability, and unmatched reliability. The 2.7 high resolution LCD screen is easy to navigate and lets you playback recordings directly on the camera anywhere. Our Black Box dash cams are a breeze to setup; the included suction mount allows you to attach it to any glass surface in seconds. Insert a formatted Micro SD card, plug the camera into your cigarette lighter and start driving. The device automatically starts whenever your car does. To ensure that you are always protected your camera will record indefinitely via loop recording, overwriting the oldest footage recorded with the newest.
profile.reviewText:
The BlackBox F1S is a relatively low cost HD dashcam that provides captures video in high definition.

I've been very impressed with the quality of the video. However, the user experience is diminished by some rather inelegant points in the user interface, inadequate documentation, apparently missing viewer software and the somewhat cheap appearance resulting from the a large amount of chrome-colored plastic.

What's good:
-Excellent video quality; true HD (1080p @ 30fps).

What's not so good:
-The captured video format is .MOV. These are significantly larger than .mp4 files used by other HD camcorders, decreasing the recording capacity on like-sized media.

-The included user guide requires some significant parsing.

-There is no viewer software included. The user guide references installing a video/gps data viewer from a .exe file...but none was noted on the camera or included in the box. An email to BlackBox asking about this went unanswered.

-There is a a non-removable Chinese character (apparently one of several standard regional prefixes that go in front of plate numbers) that appears both on the display and the captured video files.

-As far as I can tell, there's no way to get the time display to anything other than GMT, a DST offset for Chinese time (GMT + 8 hours) or one of three Asian time zones.

-The large amount of silver-colored plastic gives it a cheap appearance while calling attention to its presence in the windshield. All black would have been a much better choice.

Records video just fine. Everything else is cludgy.

Note: This item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Excellent video, but cludgy interface, missing software and flimsy appearance...

profile.description: One of the most used pans in any well-equipped kitchen. Skillets have sloped sides so that foods slide out easily. Used for cooking omelets, pancakes, quesadillas, sauteing vegetables, searing steaks, fish and poultry. The nonstick surface makes cleanup effortless.
profile.reviewText:
As a rule, I'm not overly impressed when celebrity cooks add their names to a line of cookware or other kitchen tools. In many cases they are simply adding a name, and doing so does not indicate to me that they have been involved in any way in creating something they would use themselves (or want others to use). And the list of celebrity cooks who get on my nerves is way longer than those who don't...

As for these skillets: Out of the box they have performed excellently. Their non-stick characteristics are excellent. No issues even with dishes that sometimes are challenges (egg-based or refried beans, for example). Of course, the true test of cookware comes over team, and how these will stand up to years of use can't be known yet,

Read the use and care instructions carefully. These are NOT dishwasher safe, and the instructions contain multiple cautions against using these over high heat on a glass-top cooking surface...who knew that ceramic cookware could fuse to a glass cooking surface. Not me, until I read the instructions for these skillets. In addition, don't use any non-stick sprays, which can interfere with the non-stick at the molecular level. Wow.
profile.summary: Good enough out the box; excellent non-stick performance and reasonably priced...

profile.description: Your photos and videos, with you wherever you are. Make quick photo edits, create movies in minutes, add artistic touches like a pro, or transform your photos and videos to show your vision. Share them virtually anywhere, and access them on the go. And always find any photo or video, fast.*
profile.reviewText: Note: the accompanying video is to demonstrate how Premier Elements 13 successfully imported multiple video and still image file formats (in this case, for output to a .mpg file). The review content is written, and follows below... In the world of marketing, you probably have attained success when your product name has become a verb. "Photoshop" is used as a verb because of its place in the technology world as the tool of choice for using digital technology to enhance and manipulate digital images. I've used most versions of Photoshop Elements (PSE) since version 3. After some hiccups in the middle of this series, Version 11 (released in 2012) returned Adobe and PSE to the position of standard bearer for non-commercial image editing software (while it's pricier cousin Photoshop remained arguably one of the two top contenders for fuller featured commercial use products). Because of the strength of version 11, I totally skipped version 12 until the recent acquisition of a new computer created a natural reason to transition to version 13. Users familiar with the versions 11 and 12 interface won't be confronted with drastic changes, since most of the changes in version 13 have been made behind the interface. The biggest improvement for Windows users is that (as with version 12) version 13 is now available as a 64-bit program, which allows it access to more than the 3 GB of system RAM resources access. Other changes include tools that are likely to be noticed mostly by advanced users (some have migrated from Photoshop, others are enhancements to earlier PSE tools). -Download and installation: Users who have purchased via download have a little more work to do than those who purchase it on a DVD. After purchase (and, in my case, verifying educational version eligibility), I experienced some browser dependencies in completing the download (I received an error message in Firefox but was successful using Internet Explorer; be prepared to try both. The download process will deliver four files: a smaller (about 1.5 MB) executable for each of PSE and Premier Elements (PE) and a larger (1.6 GB for PSE and 1.7 GB for PE) zipped (.7z compression) for each. At installation, you'll be prompted to either accept the default (Desktop) or navigate to a folder where you want the files extracted to (I created a subdirectory in the folder where I retain all of my downloaded executables). Once the download is complete, you'll repeat the extract-and-install process separately for the two programs. In my case, on two relatively capable computers (one desktop, one laptop), the extraction process took less than 10 minutes and the installation process took between 13 and 20 minutes. When the extraction is complete, you are automatically prompted to run the installer. If you don't already have one, you'll have to create an Adobe ID and use this in concert with your product serial number (separate for each of PSE and PE) to complete the installation. The bottom line for users of the downloadable version: you'll want to set aside ample time for the entire download, extraction and install process. PSE 13 retains an image indexing system ("Organizer") that identifies and creates links and thumbnail views of your images; you can limit or expand the range of drives/folders that it indexes. It took slightly less than four hours to index the 62000+ images in the locations I specified for it to work in. -Function and features: The interface, function and features of PSE 13 remain familiar to users of recent PSE versions. Its .psd files are still manipulated using layers and selection tools. The complete range of image effects ("filters"), image enhancement and editing tools are essentially unchanged since version 6. Still present are options to open, edit and save in wide range of file formats. -Perhaps the biggest new feature is one that trickled down from Photoshop: Photomerge. Photomerge Compose offers a highly automated way to move selected content from one image into another (with varying degrees of automation). -Output to the printers on my system was trouble-free. Accepting the default printing options yielded fine results, but advanced options for those who like to tweak are readily available. PSE 11 successfully offered options to print to the two physical (laserjet, inkjet) and two virtual (Acrobat and Microsoft Document Writer) printers attached to my desktop. Issues: -PSE 13 and Adobe continue to assume plenty about user connectivity. All of the help files for PSE 13 are online. Select "Help" in the menu bar (or press the "F1" key), and you are not taken to local help files...you are taken to adobe.com. This is fine if you are connected to the Internet, but less fine if you are not (and some people are NOT connected at all times). You can optionally download a 16 MB, 316 page .pdf help guide. This is an option you'll want to exercise if you anticipate needing help while not online or if you have bandwidth constraints where you work. Conclusion: -PSE 13, like all of its predecessors is extremely feature dense. Even power users of earlier versions will benefit from additional help. In addition to widely available online forums (hosted by Adobe and elsewhere on the web; search popular video sites for step-by-steps on even the most advanced functions), a reference book will improve your user experience. Remember: technology is complicated, and you're not a dummy! Rather than something in yellow and black that calls you names, consider the PSE 13 version  of the "Missing Manual" series (also available in a Kindle edition). About Premier Elements: Premier Elements is one of many entry level video editing tools. It accepts video and still images in many formats, allows you to compile and edit them in projects, adding text and effects to create videos content in many additional formats. If you don't have another video editing tool you are using already (and as a Windows user, my basic video editing needs are met with the free Windows Movie Maker product), then this is as a good a choice as any. Like PSE, PE is feature dense, but many of the interface elements will be familiar to you if you are a PSE user. Similarly, its help content defaults to online, but can be downloaded as a .pdf file (9 MB and 250 pages) from Adobe. Be prepared for the many associated project files and folders that PE13 creates while preparing and rendering your video. While I don't find may of it's features especially intuitive (especially output menu options when you are trying to constrain final file size), as the accompanying video shows, it successfully handled every video type I threw at it. Overall, both are strong performers for hobbyist/prosumer users looking to expand control over the imagery they have captured.
profile.summary: Remains the standard bearer for photo hobbyist and "prosumer" image editing...

profile.description: Wrangle up all that unsightly hose with this Suncast Smart Trak Hideaway with swivel base. This unique base provides an easy way to unravel hose in your lawn or garden. The hose reel will swivel to your direction and allow for a smooth unrolling motion. This hose reel also boasts a large capacity of hose storage at 225 feet!
profile.reviewText:
In short, this is an outstanding hose reel.

It easily holds the 150 feet of 5/8" garden hose I stowed in it. Nice reel gearing makes reeling far easier than other similar form-factor reels (even when the hose is charged). The winder evenly distributes the hose on the reel. The box swivels on the fixed base to allow easy repositioning of the hose feeder. Although I did not do so, the base includes holes for securing the entire until with stakes. The top is hinged for easy access to the hose compartment.

It arrived fully assembled. All I had to do was attach the feeder hose to the the exterior and wind my hose onto the reel.

Little things matter in taking care of business outside the house, and the ease of use of this product pay dividends every time you turn on the faucet.
profile.summary: Real nice hose reel...

profile.description: Roadhawk Car Vehicle Dash Cam Blackbox DVR (Lighter Socket Power Lead)
profile.reviewText:
...which is one of four separate Road Hawk accessories that appear under this ASIN.

My original 12v/24v input - 12v output power cable that plugs into what was once known as a cigarette lighter socket (these days; so many power-hungry devices, so few smokers in cars...I'm not sure what the neologism should be) to power the Road Hawk DC-2 failed.

What's not to like ?

profile.description: Provides Battery Backup Power that allows yu to work through power outages and protects your data and equipment. Green features to include outlets that turn off idle peripherals resulting in reduced energy use and saving money on electricity
profile.reviewText: 18 month update: After a desktop computer that freed up a USB port, I finally installed the included APC "PowerChute Personal Edition"software that shipped with this unit. This is an excellent, easy to use power/backup power management utility. Upon installation, it disables "Windows Native Power Management". Its interface is simple and easy to use, providing real-time updates on your power draw, reserve capacity (battery time and current loading and power usage/interruption history). Next time I come home to flashing displays on electric clocks, I can get the mystery of how long the power was out solved! ----- Although the electricity in my neighborhood is underground, the wires don't go deep until about 400 feet from my house. Before getting there, they are fed by two miles of above ground poles and wiring that pass under *MANY* trees between here and the closest substation. Any severe weather that includes high winds puts our power at risk...usually not for extended outages, but for frequent flickering during the dance between the trees and the above ground run of power lines. The flickering is mostly an annoyance, except for the effects power interruptions can have on a desktop computer and its most important peripherals. I connect a desktop computer,a network attached storage device and dual monitors to four of the five battery-powered UPS outlets. This provides a safety margin to let me work uninterrupted during flickers...or do an orderly shutdown during a no-kidding power loss. It also has five additional surge-protected outlets (not part of the UPS). Both banks of outlets include two outlets with wide spacing to accommodate plugs that may be part of a large "wall wart"...very thoughtful. I did not install the included utility software, mostly because I didn't care to tie up the USB port required for the interface. I'm writing this review on the fringes of Hurricane Irene, where I've been able to work uninterrupted during several hours of intermittently interrupted power (many episodes of 30 seconds or less). Without the luxury of the UPS, I would have shut down for the safety of the data and the computer long ago. Plug your important computing devices into this device: it will save your data and keep you from recreating your work.
profile.summary: Reliable when your power source isn't...and now hurricane tested...

profile.description: G-Force GreenDrive line of external USB and eSATA disk drives feature the latest advances in power saving technology and ROHS (Restriction of Hazardous Substances Directive) compliant materials and process. The G-Force Green Drive gives the consumer the ability to minimize his or her carbon footprint without sacrificing performance. Fantom Drives GreenDrive USB 2.0 Hard Drives are a power conscious step forward to provide maximum capacity and performance while reducing power consumption by up to 40%. The G-Force GreenDrive USB 2.0 Hard Drive family feature sturdy aluminum casing to provide maximum durability, fanless design for silent operation, and could be placed horizontally or stand vertically to allow maximum deskspace. Fantom Drives GreenDrives yield average drive power savings of 4-5 watts over competitors' drives while maintaining solid performance. That power savings equates to reducing CO2 emission by up to 60 kilograms per drive per year - the equivalent of taking your car off the road for 14 days each year.
profile.reviewText:
The Fantom 1TB GreenDrive is a good choice for relatively inexpensive external storage.

PROS:
-1TB *plus*: When connected to Windows machines, most external drives end up yielding slightly less capacity than what's on the box (not due to deceit, but due to binary/decimal capacity measurement differences between the drive and the operating system). When connected to a Windows 7 machine, this drive showed 1.3 GB. Nice!
-Multiple interface choices, USB and eSATA. If you have a computer with eSATA, this option is excellent for freeing up USB ports...which I never seem to have enough of.
-Power on/disk activity LED.
-Silver color; not a dust and fingerprint palette!
-Even though an external hard drive hardly needs one: a very nice user guide (printed on glossy paper) was included. A welcome change from either no guide, or one written in hieroglyphics.
-No marginally functional backup software; apparently they trust that you already have a plan for your backups, and didn't add utilities that often add little value to the hardware.

CONS:
-Surprisingly noisy for a fan-free machine. Clearly audible when working in a quiet environment (and the difference between four and five stars for this drive).
-Super-sized "wall wart" power adapter. It's REALLY big!
profile.summary: Some nice features; surprisingly noisy for a fan-free unit...

profile.reviewText:
Unlike some other reviewers who make candles/soap or work with lead, I don't have a recurring use case for needing a accurate, non-contact temperature readings.

Which doesn't mean this isn't great fun, and potentially very useful.

Here are some remotely measured temperature values (all Fahrenheit from around the house):

Freezer compartment (kitchen refrigerator/freezer): -10.3 degrees
Freezer compartment (garage refrigerator/freezer): 2.0 degrees
Refrigerator compartment (kitchen refrigerator/freezer): 38.8 degrees
Refrigerator compartment (garage refrigerator/freezer): 43.3 degrees
Dog's back (short hair, indoors): 88.1 degrees
Dog's belly (exposed skin): 92.3 degrees
Own cheek (interior): 98.4 degrees
Own skin (forearm): 91.2 degrees
Grass at dusk (ambient air temp: 77 degrees): 64 degrees

Select with confidence.
