profile.reviewText: Our 18-month old rescue Weimaraner has a full-grown body and a brain that is still on the march from "puppy" to "adult". He loves to chew, and left to his own devices, the shoes of any member of the pack are probably first on his hit parade. For him, the the laces, tongue and heel tab/Achilles notch are particularly delectable. When he appears in the room with a shoe, this is a great distraction that makes him forget about human footware. We don't play tug games with him, but he has fun with simple chewing on this as well as energetic flinging. Keeps his attention nicely. He frequently alternates between this rope and the always-popular antler chew. Good choice for a dog who needs his attention re-focused.
profile.summary: Great fun for active dogs...

profile.description: Get blown away by your games AND movies in Dolby Digital Surround Sound with the Turtle Beach Ear Force PX4. With up to 15 hours of uninterrupted, crystal clear wireless play, the PX4 not only dominates for PS4, PS3 and Xbox 360 games, but lets you experience Netflix or Blu-Ray Disc movies in cinematic surround sound. Don't settle for less; get the Turtle Beach Audio Advantage today.
profile.reviewText:
Although I have ready access to Xbox 360, I am not a regular gamer myself. I watched these headphones get put through their paces in being connected to an Xbox 360. Connection and pairing was fast and relatively easy, requiring just a quick visit into the Xbox's settings to complete pairing and hookup.

These are very comfortable headphones, and if you like the sensory deprivation of real world events that comes from an immersive gaming experience, these are a good choice. The sound was vibrant in the high and mid ranges. Some may find bass tones are overemphasized, but I felt like this added extra pop to game effects that include bass tones.

This headset also paired easily with an HTC EVO 4G LTE, ensuring that the outside world wasn't totally cut off when worn; both incoming and outgoing phone audio was fine.

Good sound overall; if you are ready to undertake what I consider a premium expenditure for a gaming peripheral (adding "gaming" to a product description is like adding "wedding"...it shoots the price up considerably) these will be a good choice.

I remember Turtle Beach fondly from the days when I built my own PCs and included a separate sound card as part of the hardware package. TB delivered solid hardware and audio output then, and nearly a generation later are doing the same with these headphones.

Select with confidence.
profile.summary: Really nice sound; worked well with both an Xbox 360 and an Android phone...

profile.description: Create an external dual 3.5in HDD SATA RAID array, connected through either USB 3.0 with UASP or eSATA - Multi Bay Hard Drive Enclosure - Dual Bay SATA Enclosure with RAID - Black 2 Bay SATA External Enclosure - 2 Bay HDD RAID Enclosure
profile.reviewText: The StarTech S352BU33RER is a dual-bay external hard drive enclosure (for 3.5" SATA drives) with multiple connectivity and disk control options. It permits hot-swapping of installed drives. Interface attached devices is either via USB 3.0 or eSATA connectivity. Installed disks can be used either as independent drives (separate drive letters, or JBOD: "just a bunch of disks"). Additionally, it has a front panel switch for a hardware-only RAID setup (RAID 1, RAID 0 or both drives spanned into a single disk configuration). I am using this device via the USB 3.0 cable, and have the two installed drives configured as separate lettered drives in a Windows 7 environment (the "standard" position on the bay's function switch). The disks slid easily into the bay; torque from the right side of the bay door when closing seats the disk to the connectors at the rear of the bay. It was instantly recognized by Windows 7, and the two drives become available for use immediately. This is a heavy unit (more than 6 pounds) that feels solid and well made. Although it includes two RAID and a non-RAID multi-disk spannning option, I did not test these features. There is no software RAID or disk management interface, and I'm simply not comfortable managing my RAID configurations without one (presumably this is what separates this device from other NAS devices). Excellent performance as a dual-bay enclosure for back-up or maintenance needs. Why four stars instead of five? Primarily because of the lack of a dedicated user interface for RAID management and fan noise. Yes, I know Windows disk management tools allow management of mirrored/striped hard disks. But if you've used them, you'll know why a dedicated RAID control UI is a better choice:-) The fan noise isn't unacceptable, but this enclosure is louder than either the PS/graphics card fans on my PC and the fan on a (separate) desktop RAID device. There are no show-stoppers here, but you should be aware of them. Overall, this is a strong performer if used in the correct way (and for me, this with each disk working independently). Select with confidence. Note: this item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Excellent dual-bay system; limited RAID control via your OS

profile.description: Create batches of fun, consistent cookies with the OXO Good Grips Cookie Press. The large, contoured lever is easy to grip and the non-slip base keeps the Press steady while dispensing dough. The clear cylindrical barrel shows how much dough remains and disassembles for easy loading and cleaning. With 12 Stainless Steel Cookie Disk patterns included, you'll be prepared for any occasion.
profile.reviewText:
When it comes to making cookies from scratch in my house, this is not exactly a place where Martha Stewart would feel the crush of competition...because it's pretty much a couple-of-times-a-year proposition (around the holidays, plus another time or two when a big snowstorm  heads in).

As a baker, my skills are at low journeyman level. I can follow the instructions of a not-too-complicated recipe. And I fully realize that cookie making has plenty of its own tricks and tips that are the result of experience and not always shown in the recipe itself.

With those disclaimers out of the way, about the OXO cookie press:
-If you start exploring cookie recipes, you'll discover a whole family of cookies that are unavailable to you without a cookie press...so this closes that gap.

-The cookie presses my parents (and grandparents) used fed their dough through metal supply cylinder that did not provide you with anything other than a gut feeling about how much dough remained. The clear reservoir on the OXO press solves that problem.

-A case holds twelve disks for ending the boredom in the shapes of your cookies.

-Large lever shows typical OXO design consideration.

This is a took we use a handful of times each year in our kitchen...and it does the job nicely. The cylinder is not dishwasher-safe, which is the only thing keeping this from five starts. You can select with confidence anyway.
profile.summary: Typical OXO quality and thoughtful features...

profile.description: The Weather Direct WD-3103U features Daily Forecast for 60,000 locations, 4 Day Forecast with daily sky conditions, HI and Low daily Temperature Forecast, Indoor Temperature, Wireless Outdoor Temperature
profile.reviewText:
April 2010 update: I received an email saying that there were "temporary" server problems and that the forecast service would be restored soon. This lasted about two weeks, turning the device an overpriced wireless thermometer.

--------------

Original December 2008 review:

"Internet-powered" is mostly a marketing ploy to convince you to subscribe to weather alert services...that you can already receive online from National Weather Service at no cost (you pay for customizing forecast elements you are interested in).

Since these subscription services require broadband and you can get the data for free (direct from the National Weather Service) the "weatherdirect" value added is presumably for tailoring the data and provides an audible alert for conditions of concern to you (delivered via the device even when your PC is off).

You might find this item deeply discounted at big box stores. Configuration is picky (you must register the local transmitter --the one that connects to your router-- first), but not impossible. If your "gateway" device losses Internet connectivity, you have to go online to re-register the deice.

Agree with another review suggesting that there should be an option to constantly display the outside air temp.

This works at the fundamental level...but it wide of a great user experience on several marks.
profile.summary: Works fine...."Internet powered" is primarily a ploy....

profile.description: This SanDisk microSD High Capacity (microSDHC) flash card offers high storage capacity for storing essential digital content such as high quality photos, videos, music and more; optimal speed and performance for microSDHC compatible devices. SanDisk microSDHC 4GB card ships with Bonus MicroMate USB 2.0 SD/SDHC Reader, to ensure compatibility when downloading pictures or other digital content. Easily transfer files between your digital devices and computer.
profile.reviewText: Overall, the microSD form factor would never be my first choice for solid state storage. But, when that's what some products require, we don't have any options. This was purchased specifically for use in a Garmin GPS (a nvi 1490LMT and a nvi 1390LMT) in order to accommodate Garmin's periodic updates. Inexplicably, even though I have never installed any of Garmin's "extra" content on these GPS devices, their internal storage capacity has been insufficient to accept full US and Canada map updates since they were new. As a result, I limited updates to the lower 48 states only, one of Garmin's update options. Garmin's updating software also offers an option to install updates to a microSD card (which then must remain in the GPS to use the data). Once installed in the Garmins, both devices accepted the full update package on the microSD card. Thoughtful extra: The SD adapter allows you to read/write to the microSD card from a standard SD port if you need to. GPS updates complete, so let's go driving in Canada!
profile.summary: Works just fine in a Garmin GPS;  very reasonably priced...

profile.description: The Spider Monkey is almost more art than it is function. Offering the ultimate in ease and comfort while securely raises your tablet to the exact position you require. Eye-level hands free tablet bliss! Works will all iPad models (even the iPadPro 12.9"), Galaxy Tab, Surface and Kindle devices. This Kit includes two components, the Spider and the MonkeyTail. The tail is incredibly strong but very easy to bend and adjust. With a single press of the button on the patented Spider, it flies open and then ratchets down to securely hold your device. Works with larger smartphones like the iPhone Plus. Wrap, curl, or tuck it in place in bed, on the couch, and elsewhere. Its flexible steel skeleton will hold a wild variety of shapes. No longer bound by gravity, youll find futuristic and previously impossible tablet uses. Get out the popcorn, and get your hands back. There is something incredibly rewarding and magical about the feeling as if your tablet is floating right in front of your eyes while your hands just tap swipe or relax. Watching movies has never been so comfortable. The Spider Monkey is a transformer and can adapt from a wobble free table stand to a bed levitation tool. It quickly coils up to get out the way or slide in your bag for use on the plane or by the pool. With a focus on quality, design and agility all of Octa's products stand out. Octa's customer service is on call to help you get the most out our your products and we respond very quickly to any emails.
profile.reviewText: Even though I have a tablet, I'm not heavy tablet user. Most of my computing tasks at home are in productivity tools that need a keyboard and large display. As a result, most of my tablet use is for watching cat videos, following Twitter on a second screen during live sports events (and the Oscars: great fun!) or other non attention intensive tasks. Until now I've been satisfied with a simple folding stand that enables rotating a tablet between landscape and portrait views. For users who use their tablets more extensively, or might have specialized placement needs (perhaps referring to an instructional video or documentation while taking on a DIY project, or engaging in extended video conferencing), the Octa TabletTail Spider Money is an elegant solution. This is also an excellent solution for displaying multimedia to multiple viewers in a conference room or office environment. In order to understand this product, you'll have to understand its specialize nomenclature: -the tail is the semi-rigid tubing that forms the base and holds the connector interface for the other part of this device -the spider is round device that holds gripping "claws" that secure the tablet, and the mounting interface that secures itself to the tail (while allowing 360 degree rotation). The claws are extended via a spring-actuated button, and squeezed to secure the tablet. Once secured, you can freely rotate the tablet, or slide a locking collar on the end of the tail to fix it in place. The fundamental operation is very intuitive; this is accompanied by a very well-written use guide. In short, you attach the spider to the tail and the tablet to the spider. You can flex the tail to adjust the height. It is most stable when the tablet is centered over inside of the tail's horizontal arc. This device adds flexibility to extend the height or shift the viewing angle. Three things deserve addressing to help manage your expectations: (1) Expect some give/wobble when you interact with the touch screen; I found this to be reduced by using a stylus. (2) The total volume of this is obviously much larger than a small portable stand; users who are space constrained should be prepared for this. (3) This is not an inexpensive accessory; however, I feel that both the build/engineering quality and tablet display flexibility will be returned on this price (and especially for those who use their tablets a lot). Select with confidence. Note: this item was provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Excellent design and display flexibility for tablet users...

profile.description: High quality gaming mouse pad features durability and reliability with smooth surface to ensure precise in-game movements.
profile.reviewText:
...this is a good choice.

Mousepads are truly a commodity item. Many of us are happy to use the ones we acquired for free as giveaway items. Whether received as freebies or purchased, we probably don't pay too much attention to them until they reach the end of their life, and start to curl as the facing separates from the base.

Even though I'm not a gamer, I spend major parts of my workday interacting with productivity applications and web-based services. Mousing is part that interaction, and a good mousing surface is part of that cumulative interface experience.

This is a nice big mouse pad (350mm x 250mm x 3mm or 13.7" x 9.84" x 0.1") that offers a smooth mousing surface and a base that is nicely resistant to sliding and appears to have quality construction joining the base to the mousing surface (time will be the test of this...but Amazon only gives me 30 days to prepare this review).

Neither the Lenovo branding or the stylized red detail add any functionality, but neither do they seem to add to the price: for its size, the price seems reasonable.

If you have a small or cluttered desk this may not be your best choice because of its large footprint; otherwise, select with confidence.
profile.summary: Not just for gamers: good choice if you like a big mousing surface...

profile.description: G7 Power introduces the only 830 lumen, dimmable, omnidirectional LED bulb with a lifetime guarantee. At 830 lumens, it will replace a standard 60-Watt incandescent bulb in nearly all fixtures. A 60-Watt incandescent puts out approximately 840 lumens. Like an incandescent or CFL, this LED bulb distributes light in all directions. Its warm white color temperature falls between incandescent light and pure white light. It is constructed with a shatter resistant hard plastic lens and its nickel-coated copper base is uniquely designed to effectively dissipate heat. Rest assured knowing this bulb is UL certified, contains no mercury, does not emit UV light and is RoHS compliant. LED Light Review scores the G7 bulb higher than the Philips Ambient LED and the GE Energy Smart LED in quality of light. This bulb will pay for itself in energy savings after approximately one year when compared to a 60-Watt incandescent used eight hours a day at the rate of $0.12 per kilowatt hour.
profile.reviewText: This is the first LED light claiming to be dimmable that has actually dimmed successfully for me without any flickering. So: believe the "dimmable" claim. As the accompanying video will show, this bulb has the general shape of a traditional incandescent or enclosed CFL, but much of the similarity ends there. There is actually a four-section lighting element; each quadrant is enclosed with a metal frame. Between the lighting element ('bulb") and the base are what appears to be metallic radiator fins, which I assume to be for heat dissipation. The lighting tone of this bulb is warm and much more pleasant than what is emitted by a CFL. One thing to note is the weight. The shipping weight of the bulb is 6.6 ounces. This is a noticeably massive bulb. In the ceiling receptacle I placed it in for its permanent home definitely deflected slightly under the load of the bulb. When I tested it in a fixture in a hanging, 3-bulb fixture in our kitchen, its weight definitely affected the horizontal level of the fixture globes (so: replace all of them!). Almost $20 may seem like a lot for a single bulb. However, G7 offers a lifetime guarantee, and the energy cost savings will make up this amount eventually (when depending on your use and electric rates; check out G7's site for excellent online and downloadable Excel calculators that can help you bottom line this). Customer service note: The original G7 bulb I used failed after four days. After emailing G7, they crossed-shipped a replacement to me, and offered to refund my shipping costs via PayPal. Like many things that run on electricity, it went DOA early in its life. The replacement they sent is soldiering on for rest of its own lifetime service. Disclosure: This product was provided to me by the manufacturer for review purposes.
profile.summary: Way better than CFLs; full illumination instantly, truely dimmable...

profile.description: This TomTom Start 55 TM 1EF001704 GPS features a 5" touch-screen display, so you can easily view your route. Lifetime traffic and map updates help simplify travel, while spoken street names let you keep your eyes on the road for safety.
profile.reviewText:
As a basic GPS, the START 55M provides good driving directions. I tested this unit going to several known destinations within 50 miles of my house, and generally agreed with the routes offered by the 55M.

Online registration is required in order to activate the lifetime services (and to receive one year of a fuel-price service). Registration codes are required for both, and requires you to enter codes included on the few pieces of literature included in the carton (so don't throw anything out right away!). Other included documentation consists of a glossy quick start poster. You'll have to go to TomTom's website to download the full .pdf user guide.

The user interface is not the best I have used on a touch-screen GPS. The screen sometimes us not immediately responsive to the first touch of either a menu item or the on-screen keyboard. In addition, some optional settings --such as changing the the vehicle indicator icon-- do not show the changes in an entirely intuitive way; you may think they have not been accepted...and then the new settings appear in a later screen.

This unit ships with a windshield mount, an option I don't care for (and which at least two states --California and Minnesota-- no longer permit). Consider a dashboard mount instead.
profile.summary: Good basic navigation; minor interface issues...

profile.description: he Rexing V6 dash camera is a wide-angle midrange dash camera packed with surpisingly solid features. With a WDR wide dynamic range specialized night-time sensor and a humongous 170 degree field of view, the V6 produces full HD footage.
profile.reviewText: The Rexing V6 is an excellent choice for those new to automotive video capture. It it simple to operate and captures HD video (1080P) in .mov file format (or still images in 12MP resolution (4032x3024 pixel image size). Initial setup requires charging via an included USB cable so allowing access to camera menu settings (for date, time and recording/still image resolution options). The camera mounts easily via a suction mount. Video quality is excellent (altough the quality in the accompanying video will be degraded by amazon for its streaming delivery). Output is very simple: just locate the .mov files in the "movie" directory created on the microSd card. Because this camera doesn't include any GPS data (there is a port for an apparently optional GPS module), no specialized playback software is needed to extract or view such data. The camera ships with a relatively well-written user guide. Why four stars instead of five? (1) Choice of microSD media. This camera body is large enough that it could accommodate the more user-friendly full SD media (which would have been much appreciated given the deep indent of the microSD slot on this camera. (2) The unneeded metallic trim. The textured plastic on the face of this camera would totally improve the look if used instead of the chrome around the lens bezel and camera body. The chrome feature cheapen the appearance of this camera. Good camera overall; select with confidence. Note: this item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Easy operation, high quality video...

profile.description: The Bionaire Micathermic Console Heater offers a slender design, this heater does not take up a lot of space and heats up quickly. Heats through the process of convection. The micathermic heating panels are made of the mineral mica, which resists breakdown and has excellent stability. Adjustable thermostat control and heat mode setting let you set the heat just right for you.
profile.reviewText:
Let's face it: many times we have to turn to portable heaters because builders went the minimum distance when they installed heating systems or ductwork (and any builder north of Richmond, VA who chooses an electric heat pump should be summarily punished...maybe by forcing them to spend a winter in a house heated by one of these barely adequate systems).

The choices are many (fan? oil filled? radiant? convection?), but ultimately limited (in the U.S., anyway) by a national code to 1500 watt maximum power consumption value (which is going to cost you about $0.12 per hour of operation if your electricity costs $0.08 per kWh).

I placed this in a finished basement space approximately 900 square feet in area. When first turned on, the outside air temperature was 37 degrees (F), and the room temperature was 67 degrees. 90 minutes later, the room temperature was 70.5 degrees when measured by a thermometer approximately 3 feet from the heater. Perceptibly warmer air could also be felt as you ascended the steps out of the basement.

This heater is silent and easy to assemble: the handle snaps in the front, the two base legs fit intuitively into the bottom and are secured with winged screws, and the two large, hard plastic wheels snap easily onto the rear base leg.

The thermostat is marked with arbitrary tick marks; you'll have to determine your own comfort level over time.

Having to use a space heater is always a compromise, but this is a good choice.
profile.summary: If you must use  a portable heater, this is a good choice...

profile.description: AC15 comes with the next generation 11ac Wi-Fi standard, offering total data transfer speeds up to 1.9Gbps. With 1.3Gbps over the clearer 5GHz frequency, and 600Mbps using two wireless chips to maximize performance over the 2.4GHz frequency, your whole home will get excellent wireless coverage. Ultra-fast 1GHz dual-core CPU function as a great 'heart' for fast, stable and responsive performance with Wi-Fi, Ethernet and USB devices. The outstanding Gigabit WiFi and Gigabit wired connections are ideal for bandwidth sensitive applications like streaming With AC15 you get a super-fast, high performance connected home.
profile.reviewText:
The Tenda AC15 dual-band (2.4 and 5 GHZ) router has plenty to like...and a couple forgivable (but noticeable) shortcomings.

First, the good:
-Set-up was typical for wireless routers, and it was providing wireless connectivity to multiple Windows, Android  computers, phones and tablets (plus two dedicated WiFi  music streaming  devices) within 10 minutes of unboxing.
-In addition to the dual-band capability, it offers a guest network capability
-Strong signal throughout the house. Operating on the ground level of a two-floor (with basement), the AC15 provided strong coverage in the most distant corners of the house (and a deck).
- Good set of subtle (bit visible) external LED status buttons (including for the wired ethernet ports, a feature that is often omitted on many routers).
-The internal configuration server is mostly intuitive for those who have configured other routers.

Next: the neutral:
-From a design standpoint, I'm not a fan of the big external antennas, which essentially double the routers vertical profile. I understand that in theory movable external antennas should deliver better transmit/receive performance, but for household use in a modestly size home, I have had satisfactory coverage from the more subtle appearance of routers with internal antenna(s). This is not a drawback, unless you share your space with somebody who is sensitive to the encroachment of technology devices into his or her interior design (I'm on thin ice in this area!).
-I'm also not a fan of the very shiny black plastic case; even with its slightly undulating surface, it is a strong fingerprint magnet (and yes, once up and running a router is not something that needs to be touched often...but be prepared)

Finally, the items which are forgivable, but are the difference between four and five stars for this router:
-Three instead of four wired ports. Four pours are the typical standard for household routers, and I was surprised to find only three in the AC15. I have three wired ports permanently in use (for an NAS, an MFD printer/scanner/fax and for a desktop PC). I like to have the fourth port available for connecting other devices (for temporary use or testing). While this is an issue for me, if your use case doesn't require a fourth port, then it's a non issue (but most routers at this price...and below...offer four ports).
-Documentation: no user guide is available on the Tenda website. It ships with an installation/quick start guide, but after that you are more or less on your own. This comes in to play with the final item that follows.
-No capability to reserve internal IP addresses. While it's possible that I simply overlooked this in the configuration options, I'm fairly confident that this was absent. If you have a need to to reserve your internal IP addresses (it's something I do as part of a never ending desire to always understand how my router is providing services...and to what), then this is something you could be aware. It's also something that might be addressed in a user guide...if there were a user guide.

Overall, the positives outweigh the shortcomings, and many users might not ever be aware of them. If you don't need four wired ports or reserved IP addresses for your connected devices, then select with confidence.

Note: this item provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Excellent wireless coverage and easy set-up...

profile.description: Pioneer's SC-1523-K AV receiver utilizes the latest in audio, video, and networking to deliver the ultimate home theater experience with 9.2 surround sound.
profile.reviewText:
Nine month update:

While the fundamental areas of attention (both the positive ones and those that are not so much) in the original review (below) remain intact, the selling price of the this receiver has dropped considerably since it arrived on the market. These make its obvious shortcomings less glaring. Assuming the price stays in the three figure range, I'm bumping this from three stars to four stars. While you could never go wrong selecting this receiver, you'll need to reinvest some of the resulting savings from recent discounting into add-on hardware if you want either Bluetooth or WiFi capability.

-----

Original review:

When offered the opportunity to review the SC-1523-K, I couldn't wait to try it out. I've been on an audio (and later, audio/video) upgrade trajectory since Jimmy Carter was president, and have delighted in the incremental changes that arrived with each upgrade process. And even though my electronics budget has grown over the years, the price of this receiver is still several times more than I would normally consider spending (even if I can afford a little extra extravagance now).

Here's what quickly became apparent about this model: while long on functions and features, serious gaps are apparent in the user interface (and at least one absent input) that will come as a big surprise to anybody parting with the premium price of this receiver.

The issues begin as soon as you open the box. The enclosed documentation consists of a quick start guide, a guide to avoiding speaker wiring shorts, a generic safety sheet and warranty information. Conspicuously absent: a printed user guide. Yes, it's downloadable from Pioneer as a .pdf. The user guide is 131 pages long, the features are many, and this should have been included has a hard copy in the box so users aren't forced to refer to a display device. This is an unacceptable omission for a device this feature dense and this pricey.

The SC-1523-K arrives "network ready"; it can be connected directly to a wired LAN out of the box. Want to connect wirelessly? Fine, but according to Pioneer you'll be doing so *only* via the Pioneer AS-WL300 adapter, and you'll be adding almost another Benjamin (plus!) to your purchase price. You can also add Bluetooth connectivity. Of course, this will also require *another* proprietary Pioneer adapter, and you'll get to part with another Benjamin to do so. Please not that some users have had success with non-Pioneer network/Bluetooth adapters, so your experience could vary (but don't look to Pioneer for a list of supported/compatible adapters from non-Pioneer sources; you'll have to locate this on your own).
Many inexpensive electronics components arrive with either WiFi or Bluetooth (and in some cases, both) integrated , and I can certainly find less expensive AV receivers with *both* types of connectivity built in. That one of these capabilities was not included in this device --which touts interactivity and network capabilities-- is surprising.

Want to provide input from a standard 3.5mm stereo output adapter (like you might use from an iPod or a smartphone?). You won't be doing so with this receiver. My current 2-year old Sony A/V receiver, which cost a fraction of what this model has such an input...

The SC-1523-K includes a claimed "interactive" set-up (Windows CD included; Mac users will have to download for their systems) as part of its "AVNavigator" software package. Be prepared. The software is not especially intuitive, and you'll still be referring regularly to the user manual (on your display device, since it's not available as a printed document).

The components I hung from this machine are very basic compared to its full capabilities (a simple 2.1 (stereo with subwoofer) audio system, cable/DVR and Blue-Ray player inputs, all feeding a single HDMI output to a television.

Both the front panel controls and the remote are overly complicated and very non-intuitive. The remote has more than 60 buttons (some mulch-functional, all the same color and most the same size) crowding its surface, and you won't be figuring it out without frequent trips to the user guide (remember...it's a .pdf...so I hope you haven't turned off your display device yet!). Neither will you be reading the miniscule labels in the light of room dimmed for movie watching.

The volume display is in an arcane dB scaling. Why Pioneer chose this instead of a progress-level minimum/maximum indicator is anybody's guess.

Users of surround sound speaker systems will get to use an included calibration microphone to balance the levels of their speakers (a use case I was unable to test).

Once you get past these deficiencies --and for me, some are deal-breakers when it comes to long-term usability--you'll find many features: up to 9.2 speaker inputs, speaker bi-wiring, supplementary amplifier integration, HDMI inputs aplenty (9!), USB inputs, RCA inputs, optical inputs and 3 HDMI outputs. It will provide power to deliver sound worthy of whatever source or speakers you place in the stream.

Finally, when you're ready to move this into place: bring a strong friend. It weights 39 pounds...much more than even vacuum-tube analog HF transceivers I used in the navy in the last century. This is not a criticism, but a heads up: some people may need help carrying or moving this.

In short: Lots of features and capability, lots of mass, and some surprising gap areas in a premium priced A/V receiver.

Finally: this item has dropped in price considerably since its release. The usability issues that nicked it two stars remain, but its faults seem less grievous when the pricing is displayed with just three figures.
profile.summary: Feature rich, excellent sound and some surprising gaps...

profile.description: These Triangle Bulbs brand Dimmable LED 100 watt equivalent everyday household use only 16 watts of energy, and replaces your traditional 100 watt light bulbs, providing an 84% reduction in energy usage. Designed to deliver everyday value and effective, consistent light, these light bulbs provide a soft, comfortable light. Use them throughout your home in table and floor lamps and open pendant fixtures. They are ideal for use in any room in your home, including kitchens, living rooms, hallways and bedrooms. These LED light bulbs provide a beautiful light and because they are so affordable you can use them anywhere and everywhere around your home. These LED bulbs are built to last up to 20000 hours or 18 years and they are mercury free with no ultraviolet (UV) light. These LED A21 bulbs give you instant light output with just a simple flip of a switch. These bulbs provide soft white (also known as, warm white) color temperature (3000 Kelvin), which gives off a warm full glow ideal for living rooms, dining rooms and recreation rooms. Based on 3 hours average daily usage.
profile.reviewText:
As LED bulbs keep journeying into the mainstream of household lighting, I've noticed two things in the four years that I've been gradually shifting to "LED everywhere":
(1) They have continued to get more affordable. While the sticker price on these remains nominally more than incandescent equivalents, even those who couldn't be bothered to the LED total cost of ownership in the past should now realize that the expected 20000 hour life of one of these bulbs is a great result for the $8 per item cost of this bulb.
(2) The actual illumination is improving from a sometimes off-putting, overly cool and blue-shifted light to warmer shades that illuminate in ways we've grown up expecting from incandescent bulbs.
(3) More versatile, *especially* in dimming applications.

These give fine, warm and energy efficient 1600 lumen lights. I should have a few years to wait before I assessing their life, but out of the box they light nicely and look great.

Select with confidence.

profile.description: Thundershirt applies gentle, constant pressure that has a dramatic calming effect for most cats. Great for vet visits, travel anxiety, grooming, general fearfulness and much more. With its patent-pending design, the new Thundershirt for Cats applies gentle, constant pressure to the torso. This pressure has a dramatic calming effect for cats if they are anxious or fearful. Thundershirt has already helped many tens of thousands of dogs around the world, and is recommended by thousands of veterinarians and dog trainers. And the early results for cats look just as impressive. Cat owners and veterinarians are amazed by the positive impact a Thundershirt can have with cats.
profile.reviewText: I purchased this for a nearby family member whose cat is fundamentally nice enough, but has some rather noticeable issues. To protect the cat's anonymity, we'll just call call him "Fitz" (OK, "Fitz" is his actual name, but I have it on good authority that he doesn't read amazon reviews...). Fitz is a conflicted soul. On the one hand, he enjoys being where the people are (people he shares the house with and those who come to visit), so he is delighted to hang out where the humans have gathered. He is concurrently demonstrably territorial. He is vocal when you come to close to his personal space, and sometimes his vocalizations extend to attempts at scratching or biting. A recent trip to the vet resulted in a near total meltdown. The vet basically said: "well, I can't hear his heart with all that screeching, so let's update his shots, assume he's healthy and get him on his way". Which meant that Fitz will go another year without a good listen to his heart. His issues are obvious enough that one of his regular visitors has dubbed him "Meowzelbub". The Thundershirt has brought a measure of relief to both Fitz and his pack. He tolerates being enveloped in it, and mostly assumes the "freeze and flop" response. But it clearly has diminished his agitation and he is now posed for success when company comes and when visiting the vet. What's not to like?
profile.summary: Turned a tiger into a pussycat...

profile.description: Save yourself monthly rental fees and enjoy reliable Wi-Fi in your home with the TC-W7960. The 2-in-1 device works as both a cable modem and a router, replacing your ISPs rental modem while also creating strong Wi-Fi for your home. The TC-W7960 sets up easily, and its 8x4 channel bonding keeps your connections reliable so you can game, watch movies, and download files without slowing down your network.
profile.reviewText:
The TP-Link TC-W7960 modem/wired and wireless router is a good choice for users looking to shed the monthly donation to your cable provider that comes when you rent its modem. This model appears on Comcast's list of supported devices for DOCSIS 3.0 on its network (where I tested it).

Plan on spending about 30 minutes for Comcast "provisioning" of the router (which is basically a process of getting its MAC addressed recognized by Comcast). I was able to do this without a telephone call to Comcast, but this won;t be true for everybody. Be prepared for that eventuality.

I installed this modem/router "upstream" from my exisiting wired/wireless router (coax into this device and the router connected from one its four wired ports). This resulted in the flexibility of two separate  wireless networks and 8 total wired points (well, seven really, but you get the idea).

Note: if your Comcast/Xfinity service includes bundled landline telephone service: this modem does *not* have the telephony ports; you'll have to look for a model that also accommodates those lines.

Pros:
-compact footprint (no external antennas)
-integrated 4-port wired LAN and 802.11 b/g/n wireless router (2.4 GHZ)
-separate guest network.
-Decent user interface for router/network setup options.

Cons:
-No front panel indicators for wired port connections/activity.
-Fixed base means vertical standing only.
profile.summary: Inexpensive solution for shedding montly rental fees...

profile.description: This year, showcase the magic of Christmas with The Polar Express train set. Witness the childrens shadows as they sit in the passenger cars drinking steaming mugs of hot chocolate and chattering excitedly about Santa. This train is sure to make your home glow with Christmas spirit this season. You can operate this train using six conventional C batteries (not included)! The set also comes with an easy-to-operate RC remote control (requires three AAA batteries). With this Ready-to-Play set comes an exclusive track system which allows you to create; a circle, a rectangle or an oval layout. As this track system is exclusive to Ready-to-Play set, it is not compatible with Lionel G Gauge or other G Gauge track systems.
profile.reviewText: I first read The Polar Express in its 1985 release year. Both the book and the later film were extraordinary evocative...so Lionel had its work cut out for it in bringing a three-dimensional version. For both train fans and Polar Express fans: Lionel nailed it. The engine, coal car, passenger car and observation car are crisply detailed. The remote control controls the audio: train sounds increase with speed, and you can add whistle, bell and "all aboard the Polar Express" announcement. Included track allows either a circle, squared circle or oval layout. Controller requires 3x AAA batteries, and the engine requires 6x C batteries. My only quibble with the design of this beautiful train is the decision to secure the battery compartment with screws. Otherwise: I dare you to watch it in motion and not smile. Even on 90 degree August day, it made me think of the the holidays.
profile.summary: Should charm the Scrooge out of anybody...

profile.description: The Motorola Roadster 2 wireless in-car speakerphone is a simple solution for responsible driving. Hands free calling and texting keep your eyes on the road, and the convenient motion-activated on/off sensor saves battery life. The sleek and compact design looks great in any car, and the powerful 2-Watt speaker with HD audio packs a punch. Dual-mic CrystalTalk noise canceling technology helps you hear more of your call and less of the road, and voice prompts let you know when you’re connected, muted, or low on battery. And with 20 hours of talk time and three weeks on standby, you battery will last on even the longest road trips.
profile.reviewText:
I live in a state where hand-held calls while driving is now an invitation to have a conversation with Mr. State Trooper. Even if your normal driving environment is someplace where the law hasn't caught up with technology, a Bluetooth-enabled hands free solution is just a good way to keep your focus where it belongs...on the road.

The Roadster 2 paired easily with two separate HTC Evo phones. Incoming call quality through the integrated speaker was satisfactory, and callers reported good quality via the Roadster 2.

If you get tired of losing aux audio input cords (or drive a car without one), you can use the Roadster 2 to stream audio from your phone's apps through an integrated FM transmitter to your car's radio. This wasn't always a strong or steady signal (and I'm not sure if it's because of a crowded FM spectrum where I live or signal strength through the cars root to the antenna above my rear windshield). You can also stream music through the integrated speaker in the Roadster 2, but I'm not sure why you'd want to (what's fine for a phone call doesn't do justice to music you like...).

This device recognizes when you enter or leave the car (perhaps by the noise of the car door closing??, and battery life is quite long. No AC adapter is included, but a 12v DC adapter for the car is). A very detailed user guide is included.

We've been using the earlier version of this model (the Roadster) for 16 months, and it has worked very well. Assuming the changes to the Roadster 2 are actual improvements, we expect to get long and useful service from it.
profile.summary: Stay hands free...stay-legal (and add options for your audio apps)

profile.description: Spain released, Blu-Ray/Region A/B/C : it WILL NOT play on regular DVD player. You need Blu-Ray DVD player to view this Blu-Ray DVD: LANGUAGES: Spanish ( Dolby Digital 5.1 ), Spanish ( DTS-HD Master Audio ), English ( Subtitles ), WIDESCREEN (2.35:1), SPECIAL FEATURES: Deleted Scenes, Interactive Menu, Making Of, Scene Access, Teaser(s), Trailer(s), SYNOPSIS: Carlos (Antonio de la Torre) works as a tailor in Granada, one of Spain's sleepy southern cities where time seems to have stopped - and where things that lurk in the shadows can remain unnoticed. Carlos lives alone and rarely interacts with anyone beyond his clients. No one would imagine that this shy and respectable tradesman is actually a murderer and a cannibal, remorselessly targeting Eastern European women who have no papers and filling his freezer with their flesh. Then the truly unexpected occurs: Nina (Olimpia Melinte), the Romanian twin sister of one of his victims, appears at his front door, and love slowly creeps in. SCREENED/AWARDED AT: San Sebastian International Film Festival, Toronto International Film Festival, ...Cannibal (2013) ( Canbal )
profile.reviewText:
...Hannibal Lechter would not approve.

"Cannibal" begins with almost four minutes of a nearly static opening scene, showing the transaction of the driver of car at a remote gas station late at night. It is shot from a great distance, and there is almost no dialogue. Distance from its characters and lack of exposition (through actions or words) are the downfall of this film, despite its provocative premise.

Carlos is a maker of handmade suits in Granada. He lives an ascetic, ordered life, with his apartment and studio situated across the street and within view of each other. His only apparent joy is in restocking his refrigerator...with the products of the female victims he targets, kills and then butchers in a remote mountain cabin.

This routine is toppled with the intrusion of upstairs neighbor Alexandra into his world. A Romanian immigrant whose actual job is one of the film's areas of ambiguity (legitimate massage therapist or something else....you be be the judge) who has recently arrived in Granada after working in a "spa" in Zaragosa. Vaguely threatened by another Romanian (is he a pimp? you decide), Alexandra ends up missing. This sets the stage for the arrival of her sister Nina, her former spa partner (played by the same actress). Against his own sense of control, Carlos engages with her on a personal level. It's not a spoiler to say that what ensues is not a madcap romp, and neither does the outcome --while tragic-- track entirely with the film's title

This movie is nearly two hours long. Its impact could be greater without the repeated, lingering camera shots of the small --if macabre-- world that Carlos haunts. Similarly, the plot is interspersed with many distractions: the well-heeled client of Carlos that is going to get him an invite into a fraternal organization, his side work on a piece of fabric with religious significance, the strained relationship with an relative of indeterminate connection (aunt? cousin? who knows), Aurora.

Enter with caution. When you're done, you might wish you were on top of Carlos's preparation table instead of in front of your video screen.

Note: provided for review by Film Movement.
profile.summary: Plodding pace and too many red herrings...

profile.description: nvi Advanced Series automotive navigators do not rely on cellular signals. nvi is available with your choice of 5, 6 or 7display. profile.reviewText: This is the fifth Garmin model I've purchased for either myself or family members since 2008. I've enjoyed both long service and good user experiences with each, so I am an admitted Garmin fanboy. With that acknowledged: Garmin exceeded my expectations in almost every way with the navigation features in the Nuvi 2589LMT. The interface is intuitive and refined and navigation performance is outstanding. Voice commands (both "fixed" commands for GPS functions --which display on the screen so you don't have to memorize them-- and searching for addresses) worked very well. It offers great flexibility in getting destinations input (QWERTY touchscreen keyboard, searches in its internal map database and voice commands each yielded excellent results). Add Bluetooth connectivity (very useful of you have a primitive vehicle without integrated Bluetooth), and included lifetime traffic and map updating for North America, and you get a lot for your money. Out of the box, you're presented with a "ready to operate" sticker. Nevertheless, I connected this to a PC and checked for updates using Garmin's "Garmin Express" software. Initially this process was balky, and I was presented with an apparent "update and restart" prompt series by Garmin Express Eventually I removed the old version of Express from my Windows 7 machine, downloaded the current version from Garmin. This cured the update issue (and it took less than 15 minutes to backup the other two Garmin units previously being managed by the Express software). Also be aware that it ships with only a quick start poster. The full user guide is a downloadable .pdf from Garmin. Why four stars instead of five? Every Garmin GPS I've purchased prior to this had a matte screen. Garmin inexplicably built this model with a glossy screen...simply not a good choice for a screen that may often be used in direct sunlight. I have purchased an aftermarket matte screen protector to mitigate this. Finally, I'm sad to report the always-pleasant Australian female voice has disappeared from both the integrated options and Garmin's support site. Even with these minor stumbles, this is a fine GPS; select with confidence.
profile.summary: Good navigation, excellent interface and puzzling screen surface choice...

profile.description: Remote Weather Access Platform: Get your home weather data from anywhere! Know real-time weather conditions at the preset locations with your mobile devices via broadband Internet connection. Now you can monitor your own microclimate from afar. Avoid freezing pipes and flooded basements and project your plants when you are away. You can also track the historical weather data to share with your friends online. The Remote Weather Access Platform uses traditional wireless frequencies and a hub to convert that data into uploadable information from your own personal website or via smartphone (iOS, Android) application. Features: Display real-time and historical weather data on your mobile devices or personal website, Compatible with web-based & mobile apps, User-defined push alert via mobile apps, Uses GPS to locate and collect data from the nearest weather Internet hub, Data sharing via weather community with other Remote Access users, Backwards-compatible with many current Oregon Scientific weather station sensors (check website for details), Includes wireless temperature/humidity, rain gauge, and wind sensors. *Includes the following sensors: THGR800 Temperature and Humidity sensor, WGR800 Wind Sensor, RGR800 Rain Gauge Sensor.
profile.reviewText: ...all combine to make this a very disappointing product. With patience, you can eventually get your weather geek on...sometimes. But first you have to overcome issues likely to challenge all but the most patient and resourceful users. And when you're all done with that, it's a roll of the dice whether or not the Oregon Scientific site that holds *your* weather data will respond. It's difficult to believe that this product and its companion online interface was sent to market with any significant user testing. If it had, tech savvy users would certainly be squawking (my squawks are below) and tech-challenged users are certain to bail on the overall user experience, which is glitchy and unpredictable. Eventually I was able to get the sensors running (sometimes) and data delivered (sometimes) from this weather station. After doing so, a month of operation revealed substantial issues in the following areas: (1) Hardware/sensor performance: --the barometric data (the sensor is integrated with the indoor receive unit) shows significant variance from reliable settings from three other sources (an analog barometer, a known reliable digital barometer and National Weather Service data from a nearby airport at approximately the same elevation). --the temperature/humidity data intermittently fails to send to the receive unit (even though placed well within the claimed range of the sensor). --the anemometer intermittently fails to send to the receive unit (even though placed well within the claimed range of the sensor) --The design choice of the receiver and network interface device as separate instead of integrated can only be described as "baffling". --Even though located well within the recommended placement area, each of the outdoor sensors has established a track record of spotty communication with the indoor components. As a result, the "live" data option frequently displays dashes instead of data, and exported historical data is rife with gaps in readings (sometimes many hours long). (2) Software/documentation: - The user guide correctly describes *only* accessing data from this station is via a smartphone (nope, there's no amazon store app for your Kindle Fire, and no program to directly access data from your local computer; everything is online). But wait: -Right there on the user guide table of contents, it says "View Readings on a PC" (page 10). Hooray! But what do you find on page 10? How about: "View Readings on a Server"....with Oregon Scientific main corporate site URL shown. However, some search engine time revealed a *dedicated" Oregon Scientific's Anywhere Weather site (the domain is "osanywhereweather" ). There you can register your device and change its settings..even if you don't have a smartphone. That this URL is shown *nowhere* in the user guide has a word..and that word is "fail". Once you find the site and register your device (via its MAC address, a registration number and an email address), your current data becomes viewable, and you can access your historical data as either a coarsely scaled chart or via export to a .csv file. Note that .csv is the only data export type, and that you can only export single data types (temperature, wind, etc) into any single .csv. The data does easily copy/paste into Excel if you want to work with multiple data sets at once. If you are not a hardcore Excel geek, just save the resulting .csv file in an Excel format (.xls, .xlsx) and it will work fine. In addition, even though the .csv file resulting from a history request will include a cell that says "All data are in 5 minute block", the exported data actually arrives with one-hour demarcations. In addition, if there are any gaps in data (my temperature/barometer data has frequent drop outs), the .csv file does not add null values for those time fields. The result can be graphs that require careful interpretation to reveal you are looking a gaps in data rather than dramatic changes in weather conditions. -The "location" of my station as shown in the "Anywhere Weather" application was derived from an unknown source, was miles from my actual location and could not be adjusted via either the Android or web-based client. (3) Interface: -For data available via an Android application (and no, you won't be finding it the Amazon store for your Kindle Fire...hope you like that small screen on your phone), the display contents are fixed in size. You can't zoom in on them and they won't change orientation with your phone. The fonts on the data history charts are not going to be read by mere mortals. -For the data available via the web interface, the data fields are non-customizable (so, if you don't have a UV sensor in your kit, you get to stare at a blank "UV" data field). -The Oregon Scientific website used to access the data from your weather station is often unresponsive (you can tell when it rejects the password you have entered correctly). -Even though I have my display preferences set to receive barometric pressure data in in/Hg, the exported data files delivered from "osanywhereweather" only provides results in mm/Hg (yet is clearly labeled "in/Hg" in the exported data file; go figure). Overall, this product has as many disappointments as strengths: less one star for each of the hardware, software user interface and data availability deficiencies. It works, but it's not easy getting it to do so. You not only have to get used to its ways, but also get over the idea that your data will be consistently and readily available (because it will not). Attempts to get assistance from Oregon Scientific have been marked by non-responsiveness.
profile.summary: Hardware, software, user interface and data delivery/access issues...

profile.reviewText: The Brainwavz M2 sells for a price where you start to worry about misplacing them...or making a poor selection at purchase time. profile.description: Lota mesh back task seating from HON has all the features expected from a quality office chair, and a few that are unexpected. Lota is equipped with an intuitive weight-activated tilt that uses body weight as the tension control. It eliminates the need for confusing chair adjustment such as levers or paddles. As you recline, your lower back support remains constant throughout the range of motion. Counterbalance tilt also makes Lota ideal for conference rooms where people of all shapes and sizes can easily get comfortable. In addition, Lota offers three-way pivoting arms that support your shoulders, elbows and forearms in virtually any position, and a cooling mesh back that looks contemporary and feels great. The upscale design is surprising at Lota's approachable price.
profile.reviewText:
The HON Lota is priced somewhere between the lower end of chairs you might find in an office supply store and the potentially stratospheric cost of offerings from Herman Miller and Steelcase.

Assembly was relatively easy:
-attach casters to base (they are friction mounted, and slid easily on
-attach gas cylinder to base
-screw arms to seat bottom
-screw back to seat bottom
-place assembled seat onto gas cylinder.

My unit shipped with the hardware (10 screws and an Allen wrench) missing. A three-minute toll-free call to HON and FEDEX had them at my door in two days.

One person can assemble this chair, but attaching the arms and seat will be slightly easier with an assistant.

The chair has one lever for height adjustment, one lever for seat-back tilt adjustment (and locking), and buttons on each arm to adjust their height.

Overall this chair very comfortable, and won't break the bank to get your bottom placed in it. The polished aluminum has an excellent look, and is brushed enough to avoid being a total fingerprint magnet.
profile.summary: substantial office chair that ducks under premium pricing...

profile.reviewText: This is a dimmable LED bulb with an 600-lumen output comparable to a standard 50-watt incandescent bulb. The light is generally softer and more diffuse than an incandescent and with much less heat than an incandescent bulb. As the accompanying video will show, this bulb has the general shape of a traditional incandescent or enclosed CFL globe light when viewed from the top to the base. When viewed from the side, you will notice that about half of the bulb's body consists of heat-dissipating radiator fins between the glass and and the base. The lighting tone of this bulb is warm and far more pleasant than what is emitted by a CFL. One thing to note is the weight. The shipping weight of the bulb is 10.4 ounces. This was not an issue for me since I placed it in a ceiling "can" receptacle. If you plan to use it in a hanging, multiple bulb fixture, you'll want to replace all with the same model bulb, as it its weight will affect the horizontal level. Almost $20 may seem like a lot for a single bulb. However, G7 offers a lifetime guarantee, and the energy cost savings will make up this amount eventually (when depending on your use and electric rates; check out G7's site for excellent online and downloadable Excel calculators that can help you bottom line this). You might also consider a price comparison direct from G7's own website. Note: This item was provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Nice light; cool, energy-saving operation and lifetime gurantee...

profile.reviewText:
...and it probably exceeds the routine needs of most household users.

The 2T2R first functions as a rather typical wireless/wired router (4 wired ethernet ports plus 802.11b/g/n wireless).

Its advanced functionality comes in a variety of user permission capabilities for both guest access and administrator logging of guest use status and history. Be prepared: while these functions are flexible and advanced, you'll need a strong comfort level with either already knowing or being prepared to learn the ins and outs of both router configuration and WAN setup options.

This device essentially offers three levels of access to the connectivity it provides:
-adminstrator (to five users)
-"employee"
-"guest"

Administrator users set up a wide range of access options for the other categories of users (by either time or sites). "Guest" options are further advanced by the presence of a one-touch button that generates and displays a 1-hour guest SSID and WPA2 password.

This is a device that probably exceeds the wireless access control needs of most household environments, which should be well served by the nearly ubiquitous availability of guest networking options. However, if your household includes a large number of visitors with recurring wireless access needs, or you are a small business owner trying to manage your own network (and you are comfortable with LAN/WAN configuration  options), then this is when this device will really shine.
profile.summary: What it does, it does well...

profile.description: Even more power with the home charger 4500 you can fast charge four of your USB devices at the same time. With four ports, all up to 2.9a (combined 4.5a), and the support of USB 3.1 your devices are fit for service in a blink. Charge your devices fast - the two black ports are able to fast charge smartphones of every major manufacturer (Apple, Nokia, LG, Huawei, Blackberry, Samsung, Motorola, Sony, HTC, Lenovo). The configuration of the orange ports enable tablets of the new generation such as iPad, Xperia, Nexus, Slate etc. Change into fast charge mode. Older devices can possibly be charged only at the black ones. The home charger 4500 charges Samsung Galaxy tab, Samsung Galaxy note, Hyundai t7s, LG Optimus 7 and Odys Xelio only with max. 1a. Samsung Galaxy tab and Samsung Galaxy note are not showing that the device is charging. Led lights - every port has its own led light that shows you if a device is being charged and how fast. Another led signaling the function of the charger if a total load of 4a is exceeded. More than enough power - with a total output of 4500ma, you can fast charge a combination of four smartphones and tablets without overloading the home charger 4500. 86% efficiency does not just save you electricity cost; it also keeps the adapter's temperature low and makes it live longer. Worry-free charging thanks to its thermal, short circuit, over-current and over-voltage protection, you can rely on this wall USB charger to charge all your USB gadgets worry-free.
profile.reviewText:
The Arctic 4500 home charger is a four-port USB charger for mobile devices well worth purchasing...but with some design choices that keep it from being a true five star product.

The pros:
-4 available charging ports with 4000mAh total output.
-2 of the ports are fast charge ports for tablets (so, if you have a shiny new Kindle Fire HD but passed on the aftermarket charger: this will decrease your charging time).
-LED charging status indicators (see the CONs below).

The cons:
-USB ports are placed on the short side edge of this charger.. For easy access to the USB ports, you'll have to mount this in the top plug of standard vertical 2-plug outlet. Not a problem, unless you wanted to use that plug for something else (which I do in the place where I am most likely to use this charger). While you could plug it into the bottom outlet, this will then remove the top outlet from use. This design choice should have been considered.
-The LED flashing sequence indicating variations in charging load/power output are indicated by the speed of flashing, and are not intuitive.

As a charger: five stars, but less one star for design choices that limit its flexibility around already crowded outlets.

Note: This item was provided for review purposes.
profile.summary: Good multi-device charger (with some quirks)...

profile.description: Penclic Mini Wired Keyboard's comfortable Quiet-Touch keys minimizes noise and provides good tactile feeling while you are working. Only small keystrokes are needed and minimal pressure is required when typing, creating a relaxed and efficient time in front of the computer. - Black
profile.reviewText: The Penclic C2 is wired USB keyboard with a significantly smaller footprint than a standard 104-key Windows PC keyboard. The savings in keys (and therefore, area) comes from eliminating dedicated keys for a keybad and the standard set of 11 navigational keys (and combining several others onto a Function (FB) option with another character. This keyboard was immediately recognized by a computer running Windows 7 Professional. The keys are full size and spaced slightly closer than full-size keyboard. They provide good tactile feedback. Since this is a wired keyboard, users will enjoy dedicated LED indicators for Caps Lock (standard key), Numbers lock (a FN option on the F11 key and Scroll lock (a FN option on the F10 key). The keyboard contains two legs and two USB ports. Users who key numbers in using a the dedicated numbers keys on a standard keyboard will probably not care for the numbers integrated with other keys on this keyboard. Wired keyboards are essentially commodity items, and the cost-conscious may not want to spend what this keyboard costs. Note: this item was provided at no cost for review purposes.
profile.summary: Nice keyboard with smaller footprint...

profile.description: Oakland A's general manager Billy Beane's successful attempt to assemble a baseball team on a lean budget by employing computer-generated analysis to acquire new players.
profile.reviewText:
As a confirmed baseball junkie, I really wanted to see this movie when in was in theaters, but had to wait for the DVD release. I was generally familiar with the back story (although as I watched it wondered how I had managed to forget the improbable winning streak that takes this film towards it climax), and I'm also familiar with some of the criticism for the liberties this movie may (or may not) have taken with actual facts.

Forget about all that. If you're a baseball fan, you will almost certainly love this movie...and you'll love it even more if you're the fan of a small-market team that's not the Yankees or the Red Sox (and are exhausted with the adoration of those franchises as staples of prime-time TV offerings). If you're not a baseball fan, you can still expect to enjoy this story of Billy Beane (Bradd Ptt), former big-leaguer and, in 2001, general manager of the cash-strapped Oakland A's. How cash-strapped are they? The players have to pay for sodas from a vending machine in the clubhouse (and during a later trade, Beane asks for soda supplies in partial compensation for a player).

After the A's lose in the playoffs to the Yankees and three major players leave, Beane must find a way to rebuild his roster. An encounter with a new Cleveland Indians employee and Bill James statistics disciple Peter Brand (Jonah Hill) sets the wheels in motion for Beane to adopt a stat-based approach to finding the best players.

The metrics create tension with his current scouting staff, most of whom are played by themselves and who are shown frequently including many other "intangibles" (including the attractiveness of a player or his girlfriend) in their calculations of player potential. It also creates tension with field manager Art Howe (Philip Seymour Hoffman, whose range is rapidly making him one of my favorite actors).

Pitt as Beane shows us a man who is alternately cutthroat, competitive, calculating, superstitious...and then suddently contemplative as he gains buy-in and attention for the unlikely success of his low-budget approach to managing major league talent (and opportunities to to move on to other opportunities).

As the film closes and Brand and Beane are contemplating their system, Brand shows Beane footage of one one of their minor league players who is under-regarded because of his weight and apparently scared to death of running beyond first towards second base. If you watch this scene without a lump in in your throat: well, you might be a human being, but your are certainly NOT a baseball fan.

Good baseball movie grounded in real wold events. Enjoy!
profile.summary: Not perfect, but a great Opening Day appetizer...

profile.description: Capture video or photos from your cars dashboard. The CMP212 friction dashboard car mount holds all small digital cameras or video recorders with the standard 1/4-20 camera pattern, including the Sony 4K, PowerShot A2500, and NEX-3NL/B, Fujifilm X-T1, Samsung NX1100 Smart, Olympus OM-D E-M1, Panasonic LUMIX, and Nikon COOLPIX. This mount includes Arkons weighted mini friction (bean bag) dashboard mount with optional adhesive safety anchor, and Travelmount deluxe mini suction car mount and camera adapter. The 2-pound friction (aka bean bag) design features an anti-skid bottom surface, and keeps the mount secured to any deep, slightly slanted, or flat dashboard. The adhesive safety anchor is optional, but when hooked to the mount, provides an added level of stability. The suction mount attaches easily to the bean bag mount with a one-touch lever. For the ultimate flexibility in positioning the camera at any angle, the mount arm adjusts vertically and provides 360 rotation. To install the camera, just screw it onto the mount and secure with the tightening ring. The Travelmount suction car mount can also be used as a windshield mount.
profile.reviewText: ...and it turns out the suction cup assembly can be used directly on the windshield too. Too make a long story short, I was in need of an alternative to using adhesive on my windshield to mount a Car Black Box -Timetec Road Hawk DC-2 vehicle recorder. Using this friction mound was my Plan A...until I discovered that the DC-2's tripod mount point was on the top of the camera. However, the suction cup assembly that fits to the weighted (beanbag) area of this mount secures to the windshield perfectly, and it's male tripod fitting allows use of the camera's tripod mounting point. No adhesives on the windshield and the camera can now be moved easily from car to car. Nice; select with confidence.
profile.summary: Excellent choice for my needs...

profile.description: Keep your data safe and mobile with the Antec MX-100 portable hard drive enclosure, the latest entry in Antecs prestigious VERIS line of home PC components. With a stylish black finish and sturdy but lightweight aluminum, the MX-100 is easy to set up and easy to use  the ideal lightweight hard drive enclosure. Just set up the drive, connect it to your computer, and start transferring your data at blazing speeds over USB2.0.
profile.reviewText:
This is a a fine, reasonably priced SATA hard drive enclosure.

Installation of the hard drive is straightforward:
(1) Slide out the mounting tray from the enclosure.
(2) Mate the fixed SATA/power plugs on the hard drive to their partners on the mounting tray.
(3) Secure the hard drive to the mounting tray with four included screws
(4) Slide the tray back in most of the way
(5) Attach the three-pin power/disk activity LED connector wire
(6) Slide the mounting tray in the rest of the way
(7) Secure the rear panel with two more screws (also included).

Included in the box:
-Stand for vertical placement (or it can sit horizontally on four small rubber feet).
-Power cord (with the *biggest* wall wart you've ever seen!),
-USB cable
-Driver disk for Windows 98 (it works natively with newer versions of Windows; I checked it with machines running both XP Home and Windows 7 Professional).

As with anything electronic, time will tell about its durability (but its always a good sign when they work out of the box as mine did).

Why not five stars?

Three things:
(1) BEWARE! The "wall wart" for plugging this in to your AC power source is HUGE (1.25 inches thick and approximately 2.5 x 3 inches in area). Even on a power strip with wide gaps between outlets, expect to give up two outlets to accommodate this. Surely this bulk could have been worked into the case instead, or simply made smaller.
(2) The power switch is on the rear of the case. It would be better placed in front, easily accessible to users (although the rear placement seems to be the norm for most enclosures).
(3) Included instructions are silly, Ikea-like pictograms. While they are clear enough, their content will probably be obvious to those experienced with other enclosures while remaining inscrutable to  technical novices.
profile.summary: Reasonably priced; nice fit and finish. Beware: GIANT wall wart!!!
