profile.description: Filmed as Angel Heart, by Alan Parker, a crime novel in which a New York detective becomes embroiled in a nightmare of voodoo and black magic when a missing-persons case he accepts develops into a mysterious murder investigation.
profile.reviewText:
Set in late 1950's New York City, FALLING ANGEL is the story about a private detective named Harry Angel who is recruited by mysterious client Louis Cyphre to find a long lost big-band crooner named Johnny Favorite.  Angel's search for Favorite leads him through a bloody trail that involves jazz musicians, sideshow performers, and Satanic voodoo cults.  To further complicate matters, the closer Angel thinks he gets toward finding Favorite, the more dead bodies turn up that appear to have Angel written all over them.  And closer to a truth that Angel won't want to know.
I'm not going to spoil the plot for you, even if some reviewers already did.  What I can tell you is that this is a splendid atmospheric novel.  Hjortsberg does such a good job bringing about the feel of 1950's New York City that you can almost hear jazz playing somewhere in the background.  The plot is intricate without being confusing as well.
If you haven't read this masterpiece yet, I suggest you do so PDQ.  But before you read it don't let anyone tell you how it ends.  If they persist, RUN!!!  Discover this fine book for yourself.
profile.summary: Great combination of mystery and horror

profile.reviewText:
I have yet to hear Cave-In's earlier albums, from what I gather have more of a math-metal sound to them.  So I decided to start with Jupiter.  I must say I'm really impressed with this.  I usually don't care much for when a band makes a transition from a non-trendy form of music such as metal to something that already gets more than enough media attention (like alternative or emo - whatever it is called).  You can read my review for Metallica's wretched Load as an example.  Yet, I find a lot of enormously compelling things about Jupiter.
Cave-In's Jupiter comes across as being heartfelt, jaw-dropping, and hypnotic wheras Metallica's Load comes across as being uninspired, underwelming, and just flat out boring.  Load was just a sickening attempt (with suggestive coercing from the eMpTyV/radio consortium)to gather a Gen-X audience at the expense of their loyal fanbase.  Jupiter sounds like a group playing what THEY (not a record label exec) believe they should be playing.  But enough bellyaching.
Jupiter is just a great album from start to end.  I'm reminded of a great 1990's alternative band named Failure, another group that never received their deserved success.  The cosmic guitar textures and effects have to heard to be believed.  Stephen Brodsky's vocals fit this type of music perfectly.  And his lyrics are pretty nifty too.  If I was a songwriter, I'd give up my movie star (OK, I admit the star is Godzilla) looks just to come up with lines like "You're another coat of red in Hell".  It just makes you wonder how unoriginal lameness like Nickleback and Puddle of Dumm sell millions, while most music fans remain ignorant of Cave-In's existence.  Why is that?
profile.summary: By Jove, Cave-In's got it!!!

top_5.description: WIDESCREEN VHS TAPE.
top_5.reviewText:
This movie is the epitome of excess: budget, explosions, melodrama, "cuteness", in-jokes.  LAH is one of those films that thinks its a lot more hip and clever than what it really is.  It claims to be a spoof of the action movie genre when all it really does is shake its own hands.  The jokes are not funny and yet you get the feeling that the people responsible for this cinematic atrocity are sending a subliminal message that translates as, " That skit was pretty cool, huh?".  The action sequences, intended to be absurd, only elicit yawning.  The child, who was intended to be cute, is annoying.
The only saving grace, if you can call it that, LAH has is Arnold Schwarzeneggar's performance.  His (non)acting is just as good in this movie as it is in THE TERMINATOR or TRUE LIES.  If the only good thing about your movie is Schwarzeneggar's acting, then your movie is in serious trouble.
I like a good spoof movie as much as anyone, as long as it is funny like BLAZING SADDLES or THE NAKED GUN movies.  But I think this movie was best described on an episode of THE SIMPSONS.  On that episode there was a fancy party in which all the beautiful people of Springfield attended.  There was a character at the party inspired by Arnold Schwarzeneggar named Rainier Wolfcastle.  Police Chief Wiggum walked up the Wolfcastle and said, "Magic ticket, my a**!".  My sentiments exactly.
top_5.summary: Excessive on all counts except quality

top_5.description: The highly-acclaimed sequel to H G Wells's The Time Machine, from the heir to Arthur C. Clarke. Written to celebrate the centenary of the publication of H G Wells's classic story The Time Machine, Stephen Baxter's stunning sequel is an outstanding work of imaginative fiction. The Time Traveller has abandoned his charming and helpless Eloi friend Weena to the cannibal appetites of the Morlocks, the devolved race of future humans from whom he was forced to flee. He promptly embarks on a second journey to the year AD 802,701, pledged to rescue Weena. He never arrives! The future was changed by his presence! and will be changed again. Hurled towards infinity, the Traveller must resolve the paradoxes building around him in a dazzling temporal journey of discovery. He must achieve the impossible if Weena is to be saved.
top_5.reviewText:
Like many people, I see H.G. Wells' The Time Machine as being a classic save for one major flaw.  It is too short.  While it was mastefully written, much more could have been accomplished within the confines of the story.  So a century later, Stephen Baxter took it upon himself to write the sequel to what can only be described as possibly the most important science fiction work of all time.
The story picks up directly after The Time Machine left off when the Time Traveler and his Machine left his workshop.  The guilt-ridden Traveler attempts to rescue his beloved Weena from the fiery predicament he left her in when he traveled to 802,701 A.D.  Instead, he winds up about 150,000 years short and on an Earth populated only by Morlocks.  The Traveler is taken to the sphere (which not only encases the sun, but has a surface area 300 million times greater than that of Earth) where he is observed by Morlock scientist Nebogipfel.  The Time Traveler learns that these Morlocks are not of the flesh-eating variety, yet he feels this distant future has no place for him.  So he concocts a plan to return to 1891.  He succeeds in taking back his Machine, with Nebogipfel riding shotgun.
Without giving away too many plot details, The Traveler and Nebogipfel visit several time periods.  First, they visit a younger version of the Time Traveler in the 1870s.  Secondly, they end up in a 1938 in which England and Germany have been at war for 24 years, with no end in sight.  Their third visit is 50 million years into past, where (or should I say when) the Traveler and Nebogipfel aren't alone for long.  Finally, they arrive in an 1891 in which not only the remnants of the human race do not resemble anything human, they also do not resemble anything that can be cosidered Life.  Their visits not only change the course of human history, they also change the very fabric of the universe.
Baxter, whose work I'm largely unfamiliar with, is one of the leaders of the Hard SF vanguard.  When someone says "Hard SF", it's easy to think of an overly technical writer who writes material that is unreadable.  Baxter proves here to be extremely readable.  The only real flaw, which is minor at worst, is that he tends to oscillate between 19th and 20th Century narrative  styles.  Still, he does a commendable job continuing a story that finished far too early.
Overall rating: 4.5 stars.
top_5.summary: It HAD to be written.

top_5.description: Back To School
top_5.reviewText:
Having recently turned 34, I decided to go back to college.  These last few weeks have brought back memories such as standing in long lines, worrying about financial aid, exorbitant book store prices, finding my way around campus, entrance exams (which can be quite challenging if your math is rusty like mine), and trying to find classes that best suit my work schedule.  All of this has to happen before the first minute is actually spent in class.  Being an older than average college student prompted me to write a review on this comedy classic about a college freshman much older than myself.

The sorely missed Rodney Dangerfield plays Thornton Melon in perhaps his greatest performance ever.  Melon is a wealthy self-made sixty year-old entreprenuer whose massive retail chain specializes in clothes for large men.  What Melon lacks in formal education, he makes up for by being hard-working and having a solid business know-how that is not taught in the economics classes.  Two things happen that bring his life to a crossroads.  First of all, he catches his no-good wife (played with perfect bitchiness by Adrianne Barbeau) making time and a half with another man.  Secondly, his awkward, unhappy son Jason (played by Keith Gordon) calls him to say he wants to drop out of college.  So, what's a rich over the hill fatcat to do?  Enroll at his son's college, what else?

Thornton initially has a good thing going at school with partying, cutting up in class, and lots of beautiful female students.  His wealth and fun-loving personality make him a hit with most of the other students.  He doesn't just throw parties; he IS the party.  His popularity even begins to rub off on Jason - which is a mixed blessing since he wants to succeed at school on his own merits.  But soon his partying and the fact that he has paid consultants to do his homework  illegally begin to catch up with him.

As I mentioned earlier in the review, Rodney was at the top of his game here.  He was cleary having a good time making the movie, and that good time works its way to the viewer.  The supporting cast is also excellent.  Paxton Whitehead is perfect as an aloof Economics professor who serves as Thornton's diametrically opposed antagonist.  Robert Downey Jr, an actor who normally annoys me to end, is hilarious as Jason's punked-out diver-heckling best friend.  The late Sam Kinison is especially memorable as a psychotic History professor/Vietnam veteran.  You even have a cameo by Kurt Vonnegut Jr (yes, the same Kurt Vonnegut Jr who wrote _Slaughterhouse Five_).  Back to School is a textbook (bad choice of words) example of how great comedy films used to be before the comedy genre became hijacked by disgustingly unfunny toilet humor mavens like Rob Schneider and bland rom-com chick flicks.

Not only is Back to School great for those times when you just need a good belly laugh, it also has a great message about the importance of both having to work hard and also having a good time.  Thornton was having a hard time with college because he partied too much.  Jason, on the other hand, was unhappy because he worked too hard and didn't take time to smell the roses.  Both of them needed to find a balance. Everyone going to school (college, high school, etc.) should take that lesson to heart. I certainly intend to.
top_5.summary: I hereby dedicate this review to...Myself!!!

top_5.description: Quick Shipping !!! New And Sealed !!! This Disc WILL NOT play on standard US DVD player. A multi-region PAL/NTSC DVD player is request to view it in USA/Canada. Please Review Description.
top_5.reviewText:
Nowadays, the American horror film is raking it in at the box office.  Or so it would appear to the casual observer.  Truth be told, the genre is under siege at all fronts.  It seems like every horror film coming out anymore is a sequel, an inferior adaptation of a J-horror hit, a far inferior remake of a 1970s classic, or just plain garbage (_Godsend_ anyone?).

_Evil Dead 2_ from 1987 was guilty of none of the above.  It wasn't even a sequel so much as it was a complete reworking of the 1983 underground cult classic _The Evil Dead_.  While at times the 1983 version suffered because of its extremely low budget, it was undeniable that it possessed a fire and energy that is absent in just about every $100 million (or more)  produced film out there.  Not to mention director Sam Raimi was only 24 years old at the time.  _ED2_ was the version that Raimi and actor Bruce Campbell wanted to make since they had more money to their disposal.

The end result turned out to be unquestionably one of the greatest horror films of all time.  It is a wild thrill ride from beginning to end that was wholly unlike anything that came out before it, including its predecessor.  While the combination of horror and comedy was nothing new at the time, it was almost never done with such pinache.  The viewer was treated with dancing demon zombies, Campbell being thrown around like a baseball during spring training, and an epic battle between Campbell and his right hand.  All of which has to seen to be believed.

The 1993 film _Army of Darkness_ was the first true sequel of the _ED_ franchise.  It takes the lesser chosen route of sequelization by continuing the story instead of recycling it.  It saddens me to think that that may be the last _ED_ film because of Raimi's success with _Spiderman_.  Don't get me wrong here, I enjoy the _Spiderman_ films.  I'm not going to call Raimi a "sellout" or anything else derogatory because I believe that he dreamed of making such films his entire life.  I feel his success couldn't have happened to a better director.  It's just that in times like these when originality and energetic filmmaking is lacking in modern horror (well actually any genre today), we need another _ED_ film.  Until, that happens, I'm just going to hope I'm wrong.
top_5.summary: The right hand of darkness.

top_5.description: The hauntingly prophetic classic novel set in a not-too-distant future where books are burned by a special task force of firemen. Guy Montag is a fireman. His job is to burn books, which are forbidden, being the source of all discord and unhappiness. Even so, Montag is unhappy; there is discord in his marriage. Are books hidden in his house? The Mechanical Hound of the Fire Department, armed with a lethal hypodermic, escorted by helicopters, is ready to track down those dissidents who defy society to preserve and read books. The classic novel of a post-literate future, 'Fahrenheit 451' stands alongside Orwell's '1984' and Huxley's 'Brave New World' as a prophetic account of Western civilization's enslavement by the media, drugs and conformity. Bradbury's powerful and poetic prose combines with uncanny insight into the potential of technology to create a novel which over fifty years from first publication, still has the power to dazzle and shock.
top_5.reviewText:
I'm not going to waste a lot of time describing _Fahrenheit 451_.  There's over 1,000 reviews on Amazon alone.  I'm sure most people know that it tells of a dystopian future in which books have been banned, and how firemen are employed to start fires instead of fighting them.  Even some of those who have not read the book have at least that superficial idea.

What makes _Fahrenheit 451_ so nightmarish is how this society came to be.  This was not the result of a totalitarian dictator or government, it was the will of the people.  Somewhere along the way, people tired of being challenged, both intellectually and morally, by books.  Bland, inoffensive, and mind-numbing  forms of recreation dominated the cultural landscape.  Commentators on the ailments of the human condition became enemies of the state, while the true disease itself went unchecked.  There are quite a few out there who think something like this can't happen in these "enlightened" times.

It's already happening.  The cirriculum throughout the American school system is being dumbed down far below the capabilities of the average student.  Public libraries are being underfunded, and in many cases, closed down completely.  Authors and intellectuals are given far less reverence than celebrities who hold on to their fame through idiotic publicity stunts rather than through talent and hard work.

So, I might not have told you anything you don't know already.  I won't be offended if you choose to brush off everything I mentioned previous  to the point I'm about to make.  Read _Fahrenheit 451_.  Take a good look at the cultural and intellectual climate of society today.  Ask yourself if this is what you want our future to be.

Me neither.
top_5.summary: Truth wearing the guise of fiction.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "Digitally remastered two CD set containing a quartet of albums from the '60s Pop combo - Herman's Hermits, Both Sides Of, There's a Kind of Hush and Mrs. Brown You've Got a Lovely Daughter. These four albums were originally released on EMI's Columbia label, dating between 1965 and 1968. All albums were produced by Mickie Most and feature UK and US hits such as 'I'm Henry the Eighth I Am', Mrs. Brown You've Got a Lovely Daughter', 'Listen People', 'No Milk Today', 'There's a Kind of Hush', 'Dandy' and 'You Won't Be Leaving.". The summary of the review text is "Essential supplement to "50th Anniversary Anthology"".
output: This excellent sounding re-mastered BGO (Warner Music UK) 2014 release (2 discs (60 & 53 minutes) containing their 1st 4 U.K. albums in a secure hinged jewel case) is a must-have supplement to the Hermits Bear Family 2 disc 50th Anniversary Anthology.  With 17 of 45 songs not on the 50th Anniversary release, this collection nicely fills in gaps from that period (those 17 are tracks 1, 2, 5, 6, 17, 18, 21, 22, 23, 36, 37, 38, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44); all tracks are mono except #s 37-45 (most of their 4th album). As an added bonus, the playback level is the same as the 50th anniversary release so I was able to make my own chronological playlist via my computer without having to worry about volume spikes. Also has a very informative 20 page booklet. This British Invasion band is much better than I remember them back in the 60s  they had some excellent songs for a 2nd tier band. Amazingly, in 1965 they were the top selling artist in the U.S.!!

profile.description: Digitally remastered six CD box set. Originally released on the small White Whale label, the Turtles' original albums have remained stubbornly out of print for many years, leaving fans with various greatest-hits collections that only scratched the surface of the band's deep and rewarding catalog. The Turtles' label FloEdCo, in association with Manifesto Records, celebrates the band's 50th anniversary with the release of The Complete Original Albums Collection, a CD box set containing the six albums that the Turtles released between 1965 to 1970, plus a wealth of rare bonus material. Each of the band's first three albums - It Ain't Me Babe, You Baby and Happy Together - is presented in it's original mono and stereo mixes, while each of the remaining three - The Turtles Present the Battle of the Bands, Turtle Soup and Wooden Head - provide a generous assortment of rare bonus tracks, including some previously unreleased material. Meticulously researched and prepared from the original master tapes by renowned engineer Bill Inglot, and contains detailed liner notes by noted writer and archivist Andrew Sandoval. The resulting package offer a unique insight into one of rock's most misunderstood bands.
profile.reviewText: A great Turtles anthology with just a few complaints. All 6 of their albums feature nice gatefold covers, the sound is excellent through headphones, & the playback volume level between albums is very nicely consistent (fabulous for making even sounding playlists thru Windows Media Player I filled two 79 minute CDs of just my favorite songs in their chronologically recorded order (thus Wooden Head became their 3rd album in my personal collection). Its also nice to have the mono/ stereo versions of each of their earlier songs that were available in both  no need to have the which is better debate  everybodys happy. The only cons I found are only 2 of the discs are encoded w/info (artist/ album/ song, etc.), some of which is wrong, like song titles, 3 discs have absolutely no info, & 1 has about  of the songs listed. Even though the booklet is quite informative, the printing is very large so they wouldve had enough room to have included more Billboard & UK chart info about the songs, what songs ended up as B-sides, etc. (there is SOME of this info included, but far from inclusive). And lastly, there are 4 songs missing from this complete collection: 69s Lady-O (included on an earlier reissue to Turtle Soup); 70s Teardrops (released by White Whale as The Dedications as artist); Who Would Ever Think That I Would Marry Mary Margaret (a horrible single thats been on a Rhino comp & More Golden Hits); and a quite good song, We Aint Gonna Party no More (was on a reissue of Wooden Head, & was also on More Golden Hits). Also a minor quibble w/the packaging - the outer box is 1/2" taller that a standard jewel case, so it will not fit on my CD library shelves - all they had to do was slightly shrink the inside album covers down a bit (to the size that come w/Rhino's Original Album Series), & everything would've fit better, including the overly loose CDs inside the jackets.
profile.summary: Some things are missing, but the Turtles are a 5 star band

profile.description: CD
profile.reviewText:
Thru 2016, straight-ahead jazz guitarist, grounded in bebop & blues, Kenny Burrell has released about 75 albums as band leader, & MANY dozens more as a sideman. This great sounding (w/headphones) box set presents 8 of his albums in chronological release order on 4 discs, but unfortunately, playback volume is uneven (1st album is lower than everything else, & 7th album is louder than everything else, although not so bad that youve got to race to the volume control, but a bummer if you want to make your own playlists).

Disc 1: 81:24 minutes; Interplay for 2 Trumpets & Two Tenors (1957; mono) & Blue Lights vol. 1* (58; stereo).

D-2: 82:29; Blue Lights vol. 2* (58; stereo) & The Cats (58; mono; band is Flanagan, Coltrane, Burrell, Sulieman).
* Blue Lights 2 volumes are mixed up from original release, although the re-release, which these may be, were released in different song order.

D-3: 79:10; On View at the Five Spot Caf (59, wrongly labeled 60 in booklet; stereo; Kenny Burrell & Art Blakey) & A Night at the Vanguard (60; stereo; Kenny Burrell Trio).

D-4: 71:79; Weaver of Dreams (61; stereo; Burrell vocals on 10 of 12 tracks) & Kenny Burrell & John Coltrane (63, not 62 as booklet states; recorded 3/58; mono).

Discs are securely held by plastic teeth in a dual hinged jewel case, which in turn slides into a cardboard outer box w/flap, normal jewel case height & depth for good shelf storage size. Back of  both box & case list song titles & lengths, & the fronts of both + booklet show pictures of the album front covers; 8 page booklet has a minor 1  page bio; 1 page w/song titles, lengths & composers;  page w/album titles & release year; 4 Burrell photos. No personnel listed. Each album is complete. If Interested, Windows Media Player correctly identifies all song titles and composers.
profile.summary: music 5 stars; uneven playback volume level 3 stars

profile.summary: His music 5 stars; ding 1 star for uneven playback volume.

profile.description: 8CD set w/all 8 original albums remastered: Bachman Turner Overdrive (1973) Bachman Turner Overdrive II (1973) Not Fragile (1974) Four Wheel Drive (1975) Head On (1975) Freeways (1977) Street Action (1978) Rock N Roll Nights (1979)
profile.reviewText: Another amazing Caroline Records release  all 8 1970s Bachman-Turner Overdrive (6) & BTO (2) albums, & like their April Wine boxset, with great remastered sound THAT ALL PLAY BACK AT THE SAME LEVEL (much unlike way too many of Rhinos 5 disc Original Album Series releases)  I find this extremely important for making group playlists of my favorite songs, or putting the discs in a carousel for playback  no running for the volume control. Like the Rhino series, each disc slips into a cardboard replica of just the front/ back of the original album sleeve (no gatefolds included), but these sleeves are a bit thinner than the Rhino packages. For storage info, the outer box is 5/16 taller than a standard jewel case & 1/2 less in width. The only song I found missing is 76s Down to the Line ( a non-album #43 hit) which was on 03s Head On reissue. Comes w/a 20 page relatively informative booklet. BTW, Randy Bachman & Fred Turner now tour as Bachamn-Turner & have released 1 studio EP, 1 studio album in 2010 & a live one in 2012.
profile.summary: Excellently even playback levels between albums

profile.description: Five CD set containing a quintet of albums by the veteran rocker housed in mini LP sleeves. Features the albums Get It (1977), Tracks On Wax 4 (1978), Repeat When Necessary (1979) and Twangin'... (1981), plus Love Scuplture's Forms & Feelings (1970).
profile.reviewText: Second Original Album Series Dave Edmunds collection, 2015 European release (this one from Warner/ Rhino) containing his albums # 3 (Get It, 1977), 4 (Trax on Wax 4, 78), 5 (Repeat When Necessary, 79), 7 (Twangin..., 81) - (Im considering his 6th album to be Seconds of Pleasure by Rockpile, basically the same group, only a different name), plus his 2nd album w/Love sculpture from 1970. As usual w/this series, just 5 mini LP front/back thin cardboard cover replicas, slipping inside a slightly larger box (height of a standard jewel case, but  less in width), w/no booklet/info of any kind & no extra tracks. Edmunds music is great, as is the sound, but the playback levels suck  lots of variation between discs, so forget about using your computer to make a level-volumed playlist of your favorites.
profile.summary: Edmunds' music 5 stars, playback levels 1 star

profile.description: EU-only four CD set containing seven classic albums by the Jazz great. Includes the albums Lets Cook, Kessel Plays Carmen, Some Like It Hot, The Poll Winners, Barney Kessel's Swingin' Party, Workin' Out and Bossa Nova.
profile.reviewText:
Barney Kessel was a much in demand session guitarist of the 40s-50s jazz bop scene, playing on many dozens of albums, & was a member of the famous 60s Wrecking Crew (fascinating history to look up if you're not familiar); as band leader, he recorded over 30 albums between 53-88. This box set features 7 full albums of his as band leader, spread over 4 discs (so individual albums are not confined to the same disc): Lets Cook (1957), Kessel Plays Carmen (58), Some Like it Hot (59), Exploring the Scene (4th release of 5 from 1960 recording sessions as trio The Poll Winners, released in 63), Barney Kessels Swingin Party (60, live in studio w/audience), Workin Out (61, as the Barney Kessel Quartet), & Bossa Nova (61, as Barney Kessel plus Big Band, mis-identified as a 62 release).
Sound (w/headphones) is great, although album #1 plays at a slightly higher volume level (not too bad that youve got to run for the volume control). All tracks are in gorgeous stereo. Disc 1 = 70 minutes/ Windows Media Player mislabels all tracks; D-2 = 73/ WMP correct for all tracks; D-3 = 75/ WMP all wrong; D-4 = 57/ WMP correct except many tracks misspelled.
Discs are held securely by plastic teeth in a double hinged jewel case. Do not expect much from the 8 page booklet (6 inner pages are devoted to a VERY extensive list of this labels jazz box set releases)  the front you see on this Amazon page, the back shows a nearly complete list of personnel for each album (misses a few people for Carmen, Swingin & Bossa  can find info on-line if needed). Back of jewel case lists album/ date/ song title & length. No song composers listed anywhere.
Considering what some of these individual albums go for on line, this set is an amazing value.
profile.summary: exceptional stereo sound of jazz guitar master

profile.description: UK five CD set containing a quintet of albums from the British Rock outfit led by guitarist/vocalist Bill Nelson: AXE VICTIM, FUTURAMA, SUNBURST FINISH, MODERN MUSIC and DRASTIC PLASTIC.
profile.reviewText:
Kudos to Warner Music/ Rhino for this new addition to their Original Album Series, containing the Harvest label  British release versions of all 5 of Be-Bop Deluxes studio albums from 1974-78.  For those not familiar with this critically acclaimed, but not overly commercially successful band, their sound was a mix of glam, prog & straightforward rock, led by Bill Nelson (who at the time was considered one of the finest guitarists in England).  Their first album, Axe Victim, was inadvertently quite Bowie-esque (Nelson so disliked the comparisons that he dissolved this first group to pursue less commercial paths of expression) ; 3  years later, their final album, Drastic Plastic, skirted the new wave of the times (several of the songs wouldve fit comfortably on playlists w/ Roxy Music, The Cars, or The Stranglers).
This European Union release has each cd album (as is standard with this series) slipped into a cardboard sleeve, a replica of the front/ back cover of the original release, which in turn are housed in a slightly larger box (about the size of a double cd jewel case).  Bare bones: no booklet/ info; no non-LP tracks.  Sound is excellent (remastered??  no info is listed).  And as is not always the case in this series, the volume playback level between albums is remarkably even, so I can make an even volume playlist of all my favorites for my portable device.
profile.summary: very nice even playback levels between discs

profile.description: Five CD set containing a quintet of albums by the Swedish rockers housed in mini LP sleeves and packaged in a slipcase. Contains the albums Europe, Wings Of Tomorrow, The Final Countdown, Out Of This World, and Prisoners In Paradise.
profile.reviewText: Europe started out as a prog rock band, but switched to a more melodic pop-metal/ big hair sound by their 3rd album (which worked  their most well known song, The Final Countdown, was a worldwide hit - #1 in 25 countries  now you can see them perform it in a funny GEICO commercial).  This 2015 Sony release of their 1st 5 albums from 1983-91 before their 92 break-up (they would reform in 03 & release 5 more albums  so far  thru 15) has each album housed in a mini cardboard replica of the original vinyl release, which in turn all slide into a slightly larger box (typical of these 5 albums box releases), w/just song titles listed on the back cover underneath a picture of the album; no bonus tracks, song credits or track running time  just bare bones (considering the price for 5 albums, not a big deal). The 1st album (initially released only in Japan & their native Sweden before their Epic Records contract, as was their 2nd) is muddier sounding than the others, but overall sound for all albums is very good (re-mastered???, no info given). One major complaint for me is the playback level of the 5th album (Prisoners in Paradise) is very much louder than the others, so making a level sounding personal playlist is not an option (the 1st 4 are fine together).
profile.summary: Music 5 stars, playback levels 3 stars.

profile.description: 6CD set. Collects every studio album from their initial era fronted by David Lee Roth! Features "Van Halen" (1978) ; "Van Halen II" (1979) ; "Women & Children First" (1980) ; "Fair Warning" (1981) ; "Diver Down" (1982) and "1984" (1984).
profile.reviewText: I love picking up these kinds of box sets to make my own playlists of just the songs I like, but too often the playback volume varies greatly (especially w/ Rhino boxes)...not so w/this set: the excellent (re-mastered??) sound quality of these discs play back at a consistent level between discs. Similar to Rhino's 5 album "Original Album Series", this inexpensive 2013 Warner Brothers box has Van Halen's first 6 albums (before the band line-up started changing; IMHO, their best) w/each disc slipped into a cardboard front/back cover replica of the original vinyl album, which are all housed in a larger, 1" thick box (5 mm taller than a standard jewel case for those of you w/limited height storage space). Totally bare bones w/no bonus tracks or info of any kind (other than song titles listed on the back of the box next to a picture of each album); for me, not a big deal if it keeps the price low since you can find all the info you need online.
profile.summary: even volume playback levels

profile.description: American Jazz Trumpeter, Frederick Dewayne Freddie Hubbard, born April 7th 1938, was known primarily for playing in the bebop, hard bop and post-bop styles from the early 1960s onwards. His unmistakable and influential tone contributed to new perspectives for modern jazz and bebop. In his teens Hubbard worked locally with brothers Wes and Monk Montgomery, and with bassist Larry Ridley and saxophonist James Spaulding. In 1958, at the age of 20, he moved to New York and began accompanying some of the best jazz players of the era, including Philly Joe Jones, Sonny Rollins, Eric Dolphy and Quincy Jones. In June 1960 Hubbard made his first record as a leader, Open Sesame, with saxophonist Tina Brooks, pianist McCoy Tyner, bassist Sam Jones, and drummer Clifford Jarvis. In December 1960, Hubbard was invited to appear on Ornette Coleman's Free Jazz after Coleman had heard him playing with Don Cherry. Then, in May 1961, Hubbard played on Ol Coltrane, John Coltrane's final recording session with Atlantic Records. Later, in August 1961, Hubbard made one of his most famous records, Ready for Freddie, which was also his first collaboration with saxophonist Wayne Shorter. Hubbard joined Shorter later in 1961 when he replaced Lee Morgan in Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers. He played on several Blakey recordings, including Caravan, Ugetsu, Mosaic, and Free For All. Hubbard remained with Blakey until 1966, leaving to form the first of several small groups of his own. This 4 CD set collects together Freddie Hubbard's first 6 albums as leader, alongside 2 of his finest collaborations (with Oliver Nelson and Curtis Fuller), plus a bonus cut - the delicious 'Take Your Pick', from the classic Hank Mobley album Roll Call, which Hubbard featured on to quite startling effect. All cuts come from the era 1960 to 1962, when, although not at his best known or most celebrated, most would agree this titan of Jazz was certainly at his most creative, experimental and, crucially, satisfying.
profile.reviewText:
Description on box is misleading. There is only 1 bonus track (not plural)  Take Your Pick from Hank Mobleys Roll Call, & 1 album is not complete (The Blues & the Abstract Truth by Oliver Nelson on disc 4 of this set {Hubbard was on this session}) is missing 1 song - Hoe-Down. Plus a big thumbs down to the 2nd album on disc 4, Getting It Together, by Hubbard/ Curtis Fuller/ Yusef Lateef  unfortunately it plays back at a lower volume than everything else in this box, so it is very distracting if you make yourself a playlist of different tracks, or play the discs in a carousel. This aforementioned disc 4 runs 79 minutes.

The first 3 discs are 79, 83, & 81 minutes long (HOW do they cram that much on a disc without using some kind of compression  all the music in this set sounds great w/headphones, so I don't think anything is compressed????), & all songs are stereo. Hubbards first 6 albums are chronologically arranged on the first 3 discs: Open Sesame, Goin Up (both 1960), Hub Cap, Ready For Freddie (both 61), The Artistry of Freddie Hubbard, Hub-Tones (both 62).

Discs are securely held by plastic teeth in a hinged jewel case, which in turn slides into a cardboard box w/album pictures on front, songs + length on back; minimal 8 page picture booklet w/1  page devoted to a limited bio w/some personnel info, 1 page repeating back cover info (title+ length) but adding song composers last name, &  page listing album name/date/label/catalog #. One mistake in this listing: the song Arietis on disc 2 is not on Hub Cap, but rather on Ready For Freddie. If of interest, Windows Media Player correctly identifies song titles, but leaves a lot of song composers blank.
profile.summary: Hubbard's music 5 stars, ding 1 star for uneven playback volume

profile.description: UK five CD box set containing a quintet of original albums packaged in mini LP sleeves and housed in a slipcase. This set from the American Rock 'n' Rollers includes the albums Best Of, Nightmare And Other Tales from the Vinyl Jungle, Live Blow Your Face Out, Hotline and Monkey Island. Rhino.
profile.reviewText: I love to pick up these inexpensive Original  Album Series Rhino releases to make easy playlists for myself of just the songs I like. Unfortunately, once again, Rhino has done a great disservice to listeners by the very unequal playback levels between discs. One disc will play back at 11 (a nod & a wink to Spinal Tap), the next at a 6, so you need to be close to your volume control. Other than that, the sound for each disc is good, crisp cd quality. As w/all this series releases, this is totally bare bones: 5 original albums, each housed in replica mini LP cardboard sleeves (original gatefold album covers are now just front & back covers) with absolutely no extra info or tracks (so any re-mastering is unknown), all slipped inside a slightly larger cardboard box (nice that it only takes up about as much shelf space as a double cd jewel case). Also, including a Best Of disc is lame; if there were non-album tracks on this disc, that would be different, but everything here is on another studio album (either in this box or the prior box set release). I assume they did this in planning for a future release of the final 5 J. Geils albums (they had 15 albums: 11 studio, 3 live, 1 greatest hits) before splitting up. BTW, if you are interested in this newest box, get it soon; I assume it won't be around long, since their first 5 album Rhino box from 2010 is already out of print & quite pricey on the market.
profile.summary: horrible playback levels between discs

profile.description: Includes five full albums: "The J. Geils Band," "The Morning," "Live: Full House," "Bloodshot," and "Ladies Invited."
profile.reviewText: This Japanese Rhino box set of the J. Geils Bands first 4 studio albums (1970-73) plus their 72 live album Full House is, for me, well worth the higher than normal price for other sets in Rhinos 5 album Original Album Series because, IMHO, their first 3 studio albums were there best:  more grounded in their rawer blues/ R&B sound.  I subtract 1 star for the volume playback levels: the 4 studio albums play back at even levels (great for making a personal playlist), but unfortunately the live album will blow your ears out compared to the rest.  There is no re-mastering info listed anywhere, but all the songs sound very clean & crisp.  As is standard w/these Rhino releases, each disc slips inside of a cardboard mini replica of the original vinyl album (front/back cover only; any gatefolds are absent), which in turn all slip inside of a slightly larger  thick box, nice for taking up limited shelf space; the back of this box has a picture of each album & lists all songs on each; & as usual, absolutely no frills, such as bonus tracks or written info (other than the original tiny print on the replica covers).  If you buy this set, look for their next set in the Rhino series (not a Japanese import, so much cheaper) containing their next 3 studio albums, next live album, & the unneeded greatest hits album.
profile.summary: music 5 stars, volume playback levels 3 stars

profile.description: UK five CD box set containing a quintet of original albums packaged in mini LP sleeves and housed in a slipcase. This set from the British Hard Rock legends includes the albums Phenomenon, Force It, No Heavy Petting, Lights Out and Obsession. Warner.
profile.reviewText: I love picking up these inexpensive "Original Album Series" 5 disc sets (Rhino imports) as an easy way to make a playlist of just my favorite songs by an artist, but too often, the playback levels of these collections between discs are all over the place, making an even volume playback set not possible via computer. This UFO set gets it right w/the levels!!  Since these sets are always bare-bones - no extra songs or info of any kind - I do not know if the albums are re-mastered, but the sound quality is excellent. Each disc slips inside of a cardboard mini replica of the original album, & all 5 slip inside a box about the size of a double jewel case, nice for taking up minimal shelf space. This set includes UFO's studio albums #'s 3-7 from 1974-78 when guitarist Michael Schenker was w/the group the first time (IMHO their apex). I did notice that the tracks on Phenomenon are in a different order than my original vinyl (didn't check any of the others) and "Too Young to Know" is incorrectly listed as "Too Young to No" on this set.
profile.summary: great sound; even playback levels.

profile.description: Five CD box set containing a quintet of albums from the Psychedelic rockers all housed in mini LP sleeves and packaged in a slipcase. Includes the albums I Had Too Much to Dream (Last Night), Underground, Mass in F Minor, Release of an Oath and Just Good Old Rock & Roll.
profile.reviewText: The first 5 albums, 1967-69, from the Electric Prunes; all in true stereo & sounding great; all 5 discs play back at an even sound level (nice for making your own playlist of the best tracks); as typical w/the Original Album Series, each disk slips into a cardboard replica of the original vinyl album, w/no extra tracks or info of any kind (no big deal considering the affordable price & how easy it is to find info on the web).  Most people will only know this band from the garage/psych classic (& by far their best song) I Had too Much to Dream (Last Night). This 5 album set is actually 2 different groups, the only commonality being engineer/manager/record procucer David Hassinger.  The first 2 albums have a few interesting psych songs, a few w/Stones-y influences, a few Monkees-like. The next 2 albums (played by studio musicians) are basically curiosities:  religious rock written & produced by David Axelrod (Kyrie Eleison from the 3rd album was used in the movie Easy Rider). The final album, using most of the same studio musicians, is a very 1969 sounding, not-very-good bar band type of music (I hear echoes of much better period bands like Sugarloaf, Bloodrock, Moby Grape, Country Joe & the Fish).
profile.summary: Nice to see a re-release of relatively obscure music.

profile.description: 2014 five CD set containing a quartet of albums from '60s legends Manfred Mann and one solo album from the band's original vocalist, Paul Jones. Contains the Manfred Mann albums THE FIVE FACES OF MANFRED MANN, MANN MADE, MANN MADE HITS and SOUL OF MANN plus the Paul Jones album MY WAY.
profile.reviewText: Manfred Mann were a very underrated British Invasion band which brought a heavy jazz influence to the blues/beat/R&B they played in the early 60s London clubs. If you are a fan of 1963-65 era Rolling Stones or Animals, you need this box set. The Manfreds were more musically proficient, & this incarnation of the group had Paul Jones as vocalist - he was a genuine U.K. rival to Jagger at the time. This very reasonably priced 2014 5-cd European Union release from Warner Music/Rhino features that era Manfred Mann w/their albums #1, 2, 3 & 5, released on the British HMV label (The Five Faces of Manfred Mann, 9/64; Mann Made, 10/65; Mann Made Hits, 9/66; Soul of Mann, 1/67 - missing is the 4th album, 1966's As Is on the Fontana label) plus the throwaway Paul Jones solo album from 1966. Albums 1 & 2, plus Jones' album, are in true stereo, as is most of album 3 (tracks #4, 12, 13 are mono - see back of box Amazon picture for songs).  Interestingly, the Soul of Mann album (a collection of mostly instrumental tracks recorded by the original band before their 4th album release - As Is {the group changed members by this 4th album}) is in mono, but 6 of these songs (#'s 1, 3, 4, 6, 10, 14) are also (originally) on the first 2 albums where they are in stereo. The Mann Made Hits album is a comp of early hits & B-sides which were not released on the first 2 LPs, & contains their most well known songs for the casual listener.  Typical w/the "Original Album Series", each disc slips into a sturdy cardboard front/rear cover replica sleeve of the original British release, which all slip into a slightly larger box, roughly the size of a double cd jewel case. Totally bare bones: no booklet/info or extra tracks.  Sound is excellent (I assume re-mastered; no info given on box).  What I love is playback level is very even between discs so I can make a consistent level playlist for my portable playback unit (this series is often not too good in this regard). Since it wasn't unusual at that time, singles, B-sides, & 4-song EP releases often did not end up on albums, so an excellent supplement to this box is Ascot/EMI's The Best of Manfred Mann: The Definitive Collection (25 tracks, 14 of which are not on this box) - as an added perk, this Definitive Collection has a playback volume level just a tad lower than the box, so I could make a relatively level sounding chronological playlist.
profile.summary: excellent sound; consistent playback volume levels between discs

profile.description: 2009 UK five CD box set containing a quintet of albums from the Southern rockers: Seven Turns (1990), Shades of Two Worlds (1991), An Evening with The Allman Brothers Band: First Set (1992), Where It All Beings (1994) and An Evening with The Allman Brothers Band: Second Set (1995). Sony/BMG.
profile.reviewText: The early 90s saw The Allman Brothers band making a remarkable sounding comeback, harkening back to their early years, so this is a very nice package w/ 3 studio albums (1990, 91, 94) & 2 live albums (1992, 95).  Unfortunately, once again, Sony screwed it up by not having a consistent playback volume level between discs, so if you are playing them in a carousel or in a playlist youve burned for yourself, you will need to keep changing the volume; the sound quality non-the-less is excellent.  Of the studio albums, disc 1 is very low, disc 2 a bit higher, & disc 4 is very loud; the first live album is quite low, the second quite a bit higher.  Although its nice to have all 5 albums in one package, when will these studios get it right?  My 5 stars are strictly for the music.
profile.summary: Lousy playback volume level between albums.

profile.description: UK five CD box set containing a quintet of original albums packaged in mini LP sleeves and housed in a slipcase. This set from the Rock guitar veteran includes the albums TWICE REMOVED FROM YESTERDAY, BRIDGE OF SIGHS, FOR EARTH BELOW, LIVE and LONG MISTY DAYS. Rhino.
profile.reviewText: Former Procol Harum guitarist Robin Trower's first 4 studio albums (1973-76), plus his 1976 live album. An inexpensive European release from Rhino's "Original Album Series", each disc slips inside of a front/rear cover cardboard replica of the original vinyl album, which in turn all slip into a slightly larger box (about the size of a triple disc jewel case) which is nice for taking up minimal shelf space. No bonus tracks or additional info of any kind (thus I do not know if it's re-mastered, but sound quality is excellent). Since info is easily found online, I don't mind no booklet if it keeps the price of these boxes low. My only gripe (thus 4 stars instead of 5) is the playback volume level is a bit lower for albums 1 & 4, so making a playlist of my favorite tracks is a bit compromised (this box isn't too bad; some of the Rhino boxes are disasters in this regard). If you are not familiar w/ Trower's playing, often compared to Jimi Hendrix because of his bluesy/psychedelic, Fender Strat-fueled playing style, listen to some soundbites at Allmusic.com, and buy this box!!
profile.summary: Fantastic guitarist; playback levels not even.

profile.description: Import-only four CD set containing eight albums from the Jazz legend. Includes the albums Hank Mobley Quartet, Tenor Conclave, Hank Mobley All Stars, Hank, Hank Mobley Quintet, Hank Mobley Sextet, Soul Station and Roll Call.
profile.reviewText:
This selective box set of 8 1955-60 era albums of American hard bop and soul jazz tenor saxophonist and composer Hank Mobley is a very strong introduction to his music for anyone not very familiar with his work. I wasnt, and Im VERY impressed with his music, and amazed at the talent he surrounded himself with (Horace Silver, Art Blakey, Coltrane, Zoot Sims, Red Garland, Milt Jackson, Doug Watkins, Donald Byrd, Art Farmer, Freddie Hubbard...).
I am quite pleased with the sound quality (listened to all through headphones) and had no playback problems with any track, unlike some reviewers here. Unfortunately, his Hank Mobley Quintet album (1st  of disc 3) plays back at a lower volume than all the others, not good for making a uniform sounding playlist.
Disc minute lengths are 69, 75, 79 & 79. All are mono except for 2nd  of disc 4, his 1960 Roll Call album, which is in glorious stereo. Box set securely holds each disc in place w/plastic teeth inside of a tri-fold cardboard case. Back of box lists album/ year/ song/ length; inside has the same along w/recording info (where, when), personnel and instrument played, and song composer  no other info. Windows Media Players song tagging is mostly wrong.
profile.summary: Hank's music 5+ stars; un-uniform playback volume 3 stars

profile.description: UK five CD box set containing a quintet of albums from the Classic Rock legends. Features the albums The Doobie Brothers, Livin'' on the Fault Line, Minute By Minute, One Step Closer and Farewell Tour.
profile.reviewText: As is the case w/most Original Album Series releases, each of the 5 cds is housed in a replica of the original vinyl albums front & back cover (original gatefold covers are not included), w/no extra tracks or info of any kind (no big deal considering the affordable price & how easy it is to find info on the web). Sound is excellent, & all 5 discs play back at an even sound level (nice for making your own playlist of the best tracks). This is the 2nd Doobie Brothers release in this series; kind of strange since this set contains their 1st album (1971) plus studio albums 7-9 (1977-80) & their 1983 Farewell Tour album (live from their 1982 last tour), whereas the prior series release had their 2-6 studio albums (1972-76); why wasn't their 1st album part of the initial series? I guess this isn't a big deal since if you're a fan, youll buy both sets anyway just for the great (re-mastered??) sound.
profile.summary: Great sound; nice even playback levels.

profile.description: 2016 Original Album Series collection with the first five albums from the sixties sunshine pop harmony group. Includes the albums: And Then... Along Comes the Association (1966), Renaissance (1966), Insight Out (1967), Birthday (1968) & The Association (1969).
profile.reviewText: 2016 Rhino/ Warner Original Album Series release of the 1st 5 Association albums (1966-69), w/(typical for this series) cardboard front/ back cover replicas of the original albums, fitting inside a slightly larger box (standard jewel case height but  less in length) w/a picture of each album & a list of songs on each. There are no bonus tracks or booklet, but for this price, no biggie. Time for each album is about 30, 32, 32, 34 & 38 minutes. All tracks are stereo & I think it sounds great w/headphones, & of particular importance to me, the playback level between discs is very uniform (unlike many releases in this series)  I like to compose my own playlist of only the songs I like (hard to do w/greatly fluctuating levels between albums).
profile.summary: Playback levels are nicely even between discs

profile.description: At long last, all 5 of the sticky sweet studio albums by bubblegum pop icons The Archies gathered together in one sugar high inducing box set! Features the groovy classics "Sugar, Sugar," "Bang-Shang-A-Lang," "Jingle Jangle" and more! Each album comes in its own individual sleeve replicating the original LP artowrk, and includes a full-color booklet with extensive liner notes!
profile.reviewText: Reading TomAzons excellent must-read review here titled Everythings Archie, But covers pretty much everything, but I wanted to add a bit about the packaging. The needlessly over-sized box (5  x 5 ) will not fit on my CD shelves, & results in the album sleeves inside flopping around (these album sleeves are the normal size (5" x 5") that come in Rhinos Original Album Series)  I just rolled up paper towels to keep them snug  its bad enough that the discs move around inside the jackets.  Each album has 12 tracks, ranging from 27-31 minutes. Even though info is easy to find online, the booklet couldve been more informative & accurate than it is. It is, however, nice to hear all five albums again  for me, the sound was fine w/headphones, but it couldve been better; all tracks are stereo w/quite varying degrees of separation. For those who like to record their own favorites comps for portable play, all 5 discs have nice, even playback levels.
profile.summary: nice to have, but lacking

profile.description: 2016 six CD set. This box from the Canadian rockers contains the five albums the band did for Capitol between 1978 and 1984 as well as a BBC in concert from 1980. It was remastered by Andy Pearce and contains notes by Classic Rock's Malcolm Dome, all put into a 20 page booklet and clam shell box. April Wine formed in 1969. Originally based in Halifax, Nova Scotia, the band enjoyed international success in the 1970s and 1980s, releasing more than 20 albums since 1971. 1979 saw continued Canadian success, and the beginning of international success. The band's seventh album, First Glance, had an immediate impact and the first two singles were both successful on Canadian radio. First Glance also found an audience in the U.S., staying on the Billboard album chart for many weeks, making it April Wine's first gold record outside of Canada. Following on the popularity of First Glance, April Wine released Harder... Faster. "Say Hello" and "I Like to Rock" were popular hits and Harder... Faster proved to be yet another multi-platinum release for the band. The Nature of the Beast was released in January 1981, and riding on the popularity of the smash hit singles "Just Between You and Me" was the first April Wine album to reach platinum status internationally. In July of 1982, April Wine released their tenth album, Power Play. The album included the singles "Enough is Enough", "If You See Kay" and "Anything You Want, You Got It". Animal Grace followed but the band was put on hold for some time after that with member releasing solo albums. The band has since reformed and still plays all over the world to this day.
profile.reviewText: This box set contains 5 of April Wines 16 studio albums (1978-84, their most successful international years) and one live in London 1980 album. Canadas arena/ hard rockers April Wine were one of those bands most critics lambasted but the fans loved. I was very pleasantly surprised by this box  listening to radio in Wisconsin & as a fan of the genre during that time, I know only some of their songs, but I never realized just how good their album music is  they definitely shouldve been much bigger than they were. These albums are full of should've-been-hits, & I can't understand how their few U.S. hits didn't chart higher - this band should've been just as successful as Foreigner or Loverboy. The Nature of the Beast album adds 2 bonus live tracks from 1981. Caroline Records did a great job w/this release  remastered sound, & unlike a lot of these multi-album reissue series (are you listening Rhino), the playback volume between studio discs is very nicely even (fabulous for making CDs of just my favorites  I compiled two 78-79 minute playlists of just my favorites). The only con for me is the box is 1/4" taller than a standard jewel case & doesn't fit on my shelf. Also, booklet info is incorrect about the release date of First Glance - it was March '78, not 1979. Hopefully they will release their 1st 6 studio albums in another box!
profile.summary: Much more than a singles band! Not heard enough in the U.S.

profile.description: UK five CD collection from the R&B belter, containing a quintet of his finest albums housed together in an attractive slipcase: In The Midnight Hour (1965), The Exciting Wilson Pickett (1966), The Wicked Pickett (1966), The Sound Of Wilson Pickett (1967) and I'm In Love (1968). When one thinks of the sweaty and raw Soul and R&B of the '60s, there was no one more raw and sweaty than Mr. Wilson Pickett. With a powerful voice, sex appeal, energy to spare and great tunes, Wilson's memorable output created the musical blueprints that every Rock/Soul/R&B crossover act has followed ever since. Warner.
profile.reviewText: Sadly this could've-been-wonderful inexpensive Rhino re-release of R&B legend Wilson Picketts first 5 major label studio albums (1965-67; his 1963 small label debut is missing) is marred by some horrible sound quality and wildly varied playback levels between discs. Even though album #2s cover says stereo, the first 2 mono albums are a mix of boomy/muddy lows & (sometimes) screechy/distorted highs w/too loud playback levels. Album 3 (showing mono on the cover) is a horrible stereo mix, w/muffled/very muted bass & not-bad-sounding backup vocals on the left, and everything else not-very-crisp on the right (although its not as bad as fake electronically simulated stereo of that era). The last 2 albums sound good: crisp, clean, w/nicely separated stereo. Although most of Rhinos 5 album Original Album Series are European, this one is from the U.S.; as usual each album comes in a cardboard mini replica of the front/back cover of the original LP release, w/all 5 albums slipping inside of a lightweight box about the size of a double cd jewel case (nice for taking up limited shelf space). Set has no bonus tracks or additional info of any kind, other than song titles on the back of the box, & what was/is on the covers of the original albums. Read Luigi Facottis review above & follow his suggestion for the more expensive release to buy if you want better sound than this disappointing box. W/shipping, I picked this up for about $19, so I don't feel too bad since the last 2 albums sound great.
profile.summary: disappointing sound 2; Pickett's music 5.

profile.description: Quick Shipping !!! New And Sealed !!! This Disc WILL NOT play on standard US DVD player. A multi-region PAL/NTSC DVD player is request to view it in USA/Canada. Please Review Description.
profile.reviewText:
Space Rangers, CBS, Jan. 1993, aired 4 of 6 episodes out of order (which made the series nonsensical, just like Fox did to Firefly); all 6 aired overseas.  Great stereo sound (I only listened w/ headphones; ending credits state episodes are recorded in THX surround, so that may be the case, but there is no such info on the box); no subtitles; very good picture quality (although often times seems quite soft of focus; no dropouts); effects by Industrial Light & Magic; no dvd extras.  Menu has episode selection, and each episode is broken into 5 chapters.  Music by Hans Zimmer (notable for MANY movie soundtracks, such as Lion King, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, several Batman & Pirates of the Caribbean movies, Inception...).  Created by Pen Densham (Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves; Outer Limits & Twilight Zones revivals...).  Disc 1 has the six episodes, disc 2 combines 2 episodes (such as Fort Hope + Banshees) to make 3 "movies".  Great casting of Clint Howard as the science guy in his usual comic relief role, and Linda Hunt (I so loved her in Silverado).  To me the show has a vague feel and/ or look of a mash-up of Babylon 5, Firefly, Brisco County Jr., and The Last Starfighter.  Following is a list of the episodes (I beta taped the original episodes when they aired, and all of the episodes were shorter than on the dvd release, especially the pilot).
Pilot (a.k.a. Fort Hope), air date 1/27/93, 47:08 minutes (dvd episode 49:45).
Replacements, 1/6/93, 45:15 (dvd episode 45:45).
Banshees, 1/13/93, 46:47 (dvd episode 47:30); IMHO, the best episode.
Death Before Dishonor, 1/20/93, 46:20 (dvd episode 46:45).
The Trial, unaired, vhs released episode 46:20, dvd episode 46:45.
To Be or Not to Be, unaired, vhs episode 46:48, dvd episode 47:20.
profile.summary: A fun, early 90's sci-fi tv show

profile.description: SHARE YOUR MUSIC BassBoomz have been designed with maximum compatibility. They can be used with all Bluetooth enabled devices such as laptops, smartphones and tablets as well as non-Bluetooth devices like MP3 players via AUX input (cable included). The wide level of compatibility makes BassBoomz attractive to all customers. Once connected, BassBoomz provide listeners with an explosive sound experience. Simply twist to release the Bass Expansion System, which gives deep, rich bass tones and crisp trebles. With its durable, solid aluminium construction, vibration dampening and high grip base there is minimum interference when used on hard surfaces. Users listening to music, audio-books or movies shouldn't find this high quality sound from any competitor within this price range. Portable and pocket-sized, BassBoomz create an impressive volume-to-size digital amplifier and are designed with a Li-ion rechargeable battery that lasts 5-6 hours at 70%, so they can be used while on the go. BassBoomz are perfect for every season - they can be taken on holiday, used at a picnic in the park with friends, or simply around the house.
profile.reviewText: This BassBoomz speaker is VERY disappointing. I bought 2 different colors for $60 total (a good price considering how much they normally cost) for convenience, to use with my Sansa Clip mp3 player or a personal cd player for when Im working in the garage or basement; since a full charge supposedly lasts up to 4 hours, Id have a second speaker ready to go. Unfortunately, it takes so much power to drive them that I can barely hear them from 10 feet away w/the Sansa volume ON FULL (compared to about  volume if Im using headphones or earbuds); if I use the cd player, I can get the volume of the speaker higher but it distorts pretty badly. I tried w/a small kitchen tv, & sound is ok if you are sitting w/in a few feet of the tv. Save your money & pick up an Altec Lansing iM227 Orbit MP3 Speaker (available @ Amazon) for MUCH less... the sound is about the same, & it runs for about 25-30 hours on 3 AAA batteries... I've been using mine for going on 3 years w/our kitchen tv with no problems.
profile.summary: Very disappointing; needs too much power to drive!!

profile.description: Add class to the looks of your production with simple CD Sleeves! These low-cost paper CD Sleeves makes it handy and cost efficient to place CD's in.
profile.reviewText: These disc sleeves are adequate. Ive used about 80 so far, & none of them have become unglued & the plastic film stays intact. They are, however, a bit smaller than other sleeves Ive used. The width is snugger than normal, which is ok because there is still room for 2 discs if needed. The height is a problem. The flap fold is slightly below the level of the top of a stored disc, so you have to make a new fold, and thus the thickness of the disc kind of keeps the flap flapping, & since there is no usual cut half moon slot on the back of the sleeve to hold the flap, I had to use a small piece of tape to hold it down. No biggie, but an extra 1/8 on the initial pre-fold wouldve been helpful. BTW, no problem w/the seller.
profile.summary: slightly too short but useable

profile.description: VARIOUS ARTISTS - 75 BEST JAZZ TRACKS OF THE 1960'S - 6 CD SET
profile.reviewText: Chrome Dreams label really cheaped-out on this compared to their 100 Best Jazz Tunes of the 1950's, which included a great booklet with each track info and date. This 60s set has no dates listed nor any artist song info - it was quite time consuming finding dates on the internet for those I wanted info on. And not all tracks are from the 60s - I found 3 (there probably are more) from the 50s, including The Modern Jazz Quartet's "Vendome" (1956), plus at least 1 track ("Moanin'" by Art Blakey,1958) that is also included on their 50s set. Now the positive: tracks sound great with headphones, and both box set releases (50s and 60s) are all at basically the same playback volume, so I was easily able to use my computer to make 7 CD playlists of just the songs I wanted to listen to repeatedly without having to worry about playback volume levels. And whereas the 50s set comes in paper sleeves, this set has a single swing-hinged jewel case (discs are secure) that is slid inside a thin cardboard box.
profile.summary: Great companion to label's 100 Best Jazz Tunes of the 1950's

profile.description: 2014 five CD box set containing a quintet of original albums packaged in mini LP sleeves and housed in a slipcase. This set from the Welsh rockers includes the albums Man, Rhinos Winos + Lunatics, Slow Motion, Do You Like It Here Now, Are You Settling in Alright and Be Good to Yourself at Least Once a Day. Warner.
profile.reviewText: A totally unexpected release from Rhinos (European import) inexpensive Original Album Series: the relatively obscure (in the U.S. at least) Welch band Man, who incorporated a mix of West Coast psychedelia, progressive rock, blues and pub rock. Of their 17 studio albums from 1969-2009, this 5 album collection has albums #3, 4, 5, 7 & 8 (missing album #6, their double 1973 release Back into the Future).  I don't think their first 4 albums were originally released in the U.S., so the first 2 albums in this box may be new to most U.S. listeners. As is typical of this Rhino series, each of the 5 discs are housed in mini cardboard replicas of the original album (missing would be original gatefold covers; this series only has a front/ back cover) which slip inside of a larger cardboard box about the size of a double cd jewel case (nice for taking up limited shelf space). No extra tracks, w/no info of any kind other than the tiny printing on the original album art, although the back of the box gives a track listing of each album. W/no info given, I have no idea if anything is re-mastered, but sound quality is very clean & crisp, and hallelujah (!!!), the playback levels between discs is quite even (unlike way too many in this series) so you can make your own playlist of the songs you like & have a consistent playback volume.
profile.summary: surprise release of obscure band's early 70's albums

profile.description: DAVE EDMUNDS - ORIGINAL ALBUM CLASSICS - 5 CD SET
profile.reviewText: First Original Album Series Dave Edmunds collection, 2013 European release (this one from Sony/ Arista) containing his albums # 2 (Subtle as a Flying Mallet, 1975), 8 (D.E. 7th, 82), 9 (Information, 83), 10 (Riff Raff, 84) - (Im considering his 6th album to be Seconds of Pleasure by Rockpile, basically the same group, only a different name), plus his 1st live album (I Hear You Rockin, 87). As usual w/this series, just 5 mini LP front/back thin cardboard cover replicas, slipping inside a slightly larger box (height of a standard jewel case, but  less in width), w/no booklet/info of any kind & no extra tracks, except for Subtle..., which has 2 bonus tracks that were on the 06 reissue. Edmunds music is great, as is the sound, but the playback levels suck  lots of variation between discs, so forget about using your computer to make a level-volumed playlist of your favorites. This is also true of his next 5 album collection (Warner/ Rhinos 15 release).
profile.summary: Edmunds' music 5 stars, playback levels 1 star

profile.description: Rock Collections ~ Living In Oblivion : The 80's G
profile.reviewText: This is part an absolutely fabulous 5 cd series (even though liner notes say there are 6 volumes) of mostly new wave mid-level chart hits from mainly early-mid 1980's (a few reach back to the late 70's or into the later 80's).  If you listened to and enjoyed radio from that era, you definitely need to pick up this out-of-print set, even though you may not know all the songs.  Recording levels are consistent through all 5 discs of the series which is great for making your own playlists so you have level playback, and quality of the sound is top notch.  Each track has artist info/ photo, top chart position and release date for both the U.S. & U.K., what album(s) it appeared on, time, composer & producer.  19 tracks; time: 76:17.
profile.summary: MUST HAVE mid-level 80's hits

profile.description: LOU DONALDSON - 1959-63: COMPLETE ALBUMS COLLECTION (WITH BOOKLET) - 4 CD SET
profile.reviewText:
American jazz alto saxophonist Lou Donaldson (born 1926) is best known for his soulful, bluesy approach to playing, & was heavily influenced by Charlie Parker. From 1952-99, he recorded 50 albums, plus 17 more as a sideman, mainly w/Jimmy Smith. All songs in this set are stereo (liner notes state re-mastered; sound great w/headphones).

Disc-1: 73:57 minutes; LD + 3 & The Time Is Right (both 1959).
D-2: 78:00; Sunny Side Up (61, not 60 as booklet states) & Here Tis (61).
D-3: 82:54; Gravy Train (61) & The Natural Soul (62).
D-4: 73:06; Good Gracious & Signifyin (both 63).

Discs are securely held by plastic teeth inside a dual-hinged jewel case, which in turn slides into a cardboard box w/a closing flap, same height/ length as a normal jewel case for optimal storage. Front cover of box, case & booklet all show pictures of original albums front covers; back of box & case list songs + lengths; minimal 8 page booklet: 1  page of a limited Donaldson bio w/very incomplete song personnel listed;  page w/album names + release year; 1 page w/songs + lengths + composers last name; 5 pictures. If interested, Windows Media Player correctly identifies all song titles & lists composers full names on all songs. Albums are in original release song order & are complete (except for Jump Up on 1st album, which is 1  minutes shorter than original length).

Now the bad news: playback volume levels between albums suck  not good for playing in a carousel, or making personal CD playlists of favorites via computer! There are 4 loud albums  1, 3, 5 & 8; much lower are 4, 6 & 7; album 2 is kind of in the middle. I was able to make 3 full non-chronological CD playlists (kind of alleviating the loudness spikes) by starting out w/tracks from the 3 lowest albums, which are a good fit together since they are his 3 organ-heavy releases, followed by the middle volumed #2, followed by the 4 loud albums, which are very much in the style of #2.
profile.summary: Music 5 stars, very uneven playback levels 2 stars

profile.description: ART BLAKEY - 1957-60: COMPLETE BLUE NOTE COLLECTION - 4 CD SET
profile.reviewText:
AMAZON HAS THIS TOTALLY SCREWED UP - this review is for Blakey's 1957-60 box set, but Amazon automatically posts it for all of his box sets, so if you are reading this review under one of his other collections (like 54-57, or 60-62), stop, because this is wrong. I'VE POSTED A REVIEW FOR 60-62 UNDERNEATH THIS ONE.

Prolific American hard-bop jazz drummer/ bandleader Arthur "Art" Blakey whose famous technique - frequent, high volume snare w/bass drum accents - recorded 76 albums as leader or co-leader of the Jazz Messengers, 10 studio albums, 3 live albums & 4 compilation sessions, along w/appearing on dozens of other artists albums. This box set features 7 albums w/the Jazz Messengers and 1 album, On View at the Five Spot Caf by Kenny Burrell & Art Blakey, which is also included in Burrells 1957-62 box set. Sound (w/headphones) is great; all play back at a uniform volume level between albums.

Disc 1: 80:25 minutes; Ritual: The Modern Jazz Messengers (1957; mono) & Art Blakey & the Jazz Messengers (later known as Moanin; 1958; stereo).
D-2: 72:37; (1 carryover song from D-1 2nd album); Holiday for Skins, vols. 1 & 2 (58; stereo).
D-3: 78:02; At the Jazz Corner of the World, vols. 1 & 2 (59; stereo; live) (not to be confused w/1961s Meet You at the Jazz Corner of the World contained in Blakeys Part Three 1960-62 box set).
D-4: 81:21; On View at the Five Spot Cafe (by Kenny Burrell & Art Blakey; 59; stereo) & A Night in Tunisia (61 {not 60 as box states}; stereo) (this is Art Blakey & the Jazz Messengers, not to be confused w/the same titled 1957 album attributed to Art Blakeys Jazz Messengers).

Discs are securely held by plastic teeth in a dual hinged jewel case, which in turn slides into a cardboard outer box w/flap, normal jewel case height & depth for good shelf storage size. Back of  both box & case list song titles & lengths, & the fronts of both + booklet show pictures of album front covers; 8 page booklet has a minor 1  page bio; 1 page w/song titles, lengths & composers;  page w/album titles & release year; + 4 photos. Some personnel listed in bio. Each album is complete & in original release order; 1 song from the 2nd album carries over to disc 2 (otherwise each disc has 2 albums).  If Interested, Windows Media Player correctly identifies all song titles & most composers (a few are wrong).

END OF 57-60 REVIEW; NEW REVIEW FOR 60-62 FOLLOWS.

This box set has:
Disc 1; 78:26 min.; The Big Beat (1960) & The Witch Doctor (61).
D-2; 82:05; Meet You at the Jazz Corner of the World, vols. 1& 2 (61, live).
D-3; 74:01; The Freedom Rider & Mosaic (both 61).
D-4: 81:03; 3 Blind Mice & The African Beat (both 62).
All tracks are stereo & sound great through headphones, plus discs have a uniform playback volume between them. Discs are securely held by plastic teeth in a dual hinged jewel case, which slides into a flapped cardboard box, height & length of standard jewel case for optimum shelf storage. Box & case back & front are the same, w/original album front covers pictured; song titles + lengths are listed on the back, & again on 1 page of booklet along w/composers; 8 page booklet has limited 1  page bio w/most song personnel listed;  page w/album name & date; 4 photos. Windows Media Player DOES correctly tag every song, & most song composers.
For the price this set cannot be beat, but unfortunately (I think) the artists estate no longer receives any royalties on this now public domain music. And can anyone tell me how they cram 82 minutes of music onto a CD without using compression technology (I thought the limit is 79.8 minutes)?? These tracks do not sound compressed.
profile.summary: uniform playback volume level between songs/ discs

profile.description: The 120 classic Rockabilly tracks on this box set, performed by artists ranging from it's leading exponents to the most obscure performers of the genre, present classic Rockabilly in all it's glory and formats. Today, Rockabilly, a genre that was commercially viable for only a couple of years, has endured the support of it's fans for over 50 years and the fan base is growing. Hearing Elvis Presley perform his brand of Rockabilly on record influenced a whole host of other artists who would soon emulate him, many are included here. This set is compiled and annotated by acknowledged expert Adam Komorowski.
profile.reviewText: An extremely good buy for the price: British import w/120 digitally remastered rockabilly classics from 1955-56, most being quite obscure (including B-sides), w/a couple tracks each from well knowns like Presley, Orbison, Perkins, G. Vincent, Johnny Burnette, Charlie Feathers. These really great sounding tracks are all recorded w/a very even playback level (important for making your personal comp favorites). Each disc runs between 67-70 minutes, & each slips inside of an individual cardboard cover which all slip into a slightly larger box which also contains an excellent 66 page booklet with a history of every artist & the songs, along w/pictures. Each disc's songs are grouped into categories related to song titles, such as the "Swing Bop Boogie" disc where songs have "bop" and/or "boogie" in the title. If you like this, check out  Not Now Music's 2-cd sets: "The Roots of Phychobilly" & "The Godfathers of Psychobilly" with 100 more rockabilly classics, covering a slightly later 1957-61 era (all available on Amazon or ErnieBReggae).
profile.summary: 1955-56 rockabilly must-haves w/excellent sound

profile.description: Allah Las met while working at the biggest of all the L.A. Record stores, but they became a band in an even more rare and special space--a California basement, dug out somewhere between the mountains and the beach. They began gigging shortly after their conception in and around Los Angeles in the later part of 2008. It wasn't until three years later that they would find the proper environment to record their first single ''Long Journey'' which now bookends their self-titled release. These were the kind of songs that bounced between London and Los Angeles, the kind of thing that could have come from Mick Jagger or Arthur Lee or both at once, with crystalline guitar and slow-mo drums that recalled the way the waves take big bites of the beach at night. This was mystery music from the strange and ancient-modern California fringe, more Night Tide than Easy Rider. Allah Las were a reflection of a reflection, an echo of an echo, a band that was psychedelic not because of reverb or shredding through pedals but for the simple way their songs seem to extend to infinity.
profile.reviewText: Combining sounds of mid-60s folk rock, garage & psych (a touch of Love, The Chocolate Watch Band, mid-period Quicksilver Messenger Service), power pop jangle (hints of Beau Brummels, & Jimmy Silva, especially the vocals ), w/a healthy dose of early 60s surf guitar, the L.A. based  Allah-Las first album contains their first 4 songs (A/B sided singles) plus 8 more mostly mid-tempo songs with a loping pace.  AllMusic says it  sounds like it came straight out of a Midwestern garage or from the stage of a West Coast teen club in the mid-60s; perfectly layered guitars (with plenty of chiming 12-string), a chunky but fluid bass pulse, a tinny but tough drum sound, & just the right amount of reverb on the vocals.
profile.summary: Power pop fans take a listen

profile.reviewText: This is part an absolutely fabulous 5 cd series (even though liner notes say there are 6 volumes) of mostly new wave mid-level chart hits from mainly early-mid 1980's (a few reach back to the late 70's or into the later 80's).  If you listened to and enjoyed radio from that era, you definitely need to pick up this out-of-print set, even though you may not know all the songs.
