profile.description: 2012 two CD collection. Del Shannon made an instant impact when his debut release, the startlingly innovative and much-loved 'Runaway', went to the top of the charts on both sides of the Atlantic. He went onto score another six UK Top Ten hits in a career that encompassed jukebox classics, dramatic minor key ballads, definitive cover versions, raucous garage-punk, beautifully arranged psych-pop, Nashville country and a late career revival with the aid of celebrity fans Tom Petty and Jeff Lynne. This is the most comprehensive overview of his body of work to date: 52 tracks that include all his hits alongside hard-to-find rarities, album tracks and b-sides that chronologically span his thirty year recording legacy. Music Club Deluxe.
profile.reviewText: A chronological, inexpensive British 52 track, 134 minute essential Del Shannon collection, with 33 of his 44 U.S. released single A-sides from 1961-91, starting w/his first, the #1 Runaway, to the fabulous (posthumously released, sadly non-charting) Walk Away, written will Jeff Lynne & Tom Petty, along with non-U.S. A-sides, rarities, B-sides & a few album cuts (including stereo mixes of his Needle & Pins cover and the great I Go to Pieces (his own song that he regrettably gave away to Peter & Gordon, since covered by many artists) .  His Lennon/McCartney cover of From Me to You charted before the Beatles hit the U.S. (he was the 1st U.S. artist to cover a Beatles' song). Shannon wrote A LOT of his own stuff, relatively rare for an early 60's artist. Sound is quite acceptable (I guess re-mastered, from reading reviews here).  The stereo tracks (21 mono, 31 stereo) vary greatly; much of the earlier stuff has center vocal, organ/strings on right, & a fairly muddy/boomy low end including sax on the left; at least it's not the crappy electronic rechanneled "stereo" not uncommon for the time.  Surprisingly, there are mono tracks extending all the way up to 1974, although most of them are in the '63-'66 era; the 1965-66 mono songs are quite muddy).  Too bad there isn't more, since the 2-disc set has 24 minutes of time left; it would've been great to have a few more tracks from his last album, like his redo of his classic I Go to Pieces, or his '86 remix of Runaway for NBC's fantastic Crime Story. If of interest to you, the mono tracks are: disc 1: 4, 8-11, 15-20, 22; disc 2: 2-5, 7, 10, 18, 20, maybe 14 (it's not quite mono; more like a very extremely narrow stereo). If you need a good overview of this artist, this is the one to buy.
profile.summary: He would've made a great Traveling Wilbury!

profile.description: Much more than the charm of its attractive design, the Rio headphone offers high performance audio. Get ready for the Rio's state of the art Hi-Fi audio performance and incredible comfort that includes various ear adapters that maximizes ambient noise reduction and offers the ultimate fit for your individual style. With a built-in cable microphone, you get crystal clear hands-free calling with your phone or other mobile device.
profile.reviewText: I picked up a pair of these with a great on-line deal.  These RIO in-ear headphones sound as good as my $300 on-ear Bose or over-ear noise-cancelling Able Planet phones, with remarkable full range sound reproduction and great passive noise cancelling (assuming 1 of the 3 supplied sizes of rubber tips fit well for you).  The phones are quite heavy compared to other in-ears, but that does not affect their comfort.  Unfortunately, I can only use these when I am passive, such as sitting and reading, or just sitting and listening to music;  I cannot use these with any kind of activity.  The 4 mm wide, 4 foot ribbon-type chord GREATLY amplifies any movement, such as rubbing on my beard or shirt/ jacket collar; many headphones have this problem, but never to this extreme extent (and I have over a dozen different kinds of good quality headphones).  This can be pretty much mitigated by using a couple of small spring-type paper clips securely clamping the chord against clothing... actually this is a good idea for any headphone chord since this cuts down on wear movement on any connections that could break from use; just be sure not to clamp the clip's feet on the cable as that could damage the cable.  Two problems still remain though.  I tried using them for walking, but any breeze/ wind hitting the phones is quite amplified; this is usually only a problem with on or over-ear phones and is why I like to use good in-ear phones on windy days.  Also, maybe because the seal is so good, the sound of my feet hitting the pavement is conducted through my bones and drowns out the music.  This negates the benefits of good outside noise cancellation, keeping the music volume to a level where there is no possible hearing damage.  For a very similar list price, I would suggest the BassBuds w/ Swarovski elements (available on Amazon).  I find the sound and passive noise cancelling nearly identical to the Rio's with none of the associated problems.  Also, both the RIO and BassBud phones do not work out of the ear canals with body movement; both have built-in mics for use with cell phones, but the BassBud also has an mp3 playback control for use w/ cell phones.
profile.summary: 5 stars for sound, zero stars for chord

profile.description: 2013 five CD box set containing a quintet of albums packaged in cardboard mini LP sleeves and housed in a slipcase. This collection of Ratt's first five albums covers the years from 1984 to 1990 that saw them have significant commercial success. Tracks such as 'Round and Round,' 'Wanted Man' and 'Lay It Down' helped define the Glam Metal genre, while their later output such as 'Way Cool Jr.' and 'I Want a Woman' featured heavily on MTV. Originally hailing from San Diego California, Ratt were a key figure in the formation of the 80's Los Angeles Hard Rock and Glam Metal scene.
profile.reviewText: Being in my mid-30s back in 1984 when Ratt (a huge influence for L.A.'s glam metal scene) first hit the radio, I enjoyed their radio hits but never bought one of their albums. This new Rhino (European) "Original Album Series" release of Ratt's first 5 major label studio albums (of their 8 total w/a new one planned in 2014, plus a 1983 small label EP) from 1984-90 is an excellent, inexpensive way to pick up (for me) unheard tracks from one of the era's better hair metal bands.  As is typical w/this series, each album disc slips inside of a mini cardboard replica of the original LP front/back cover (original gatefold covers, if any, are missing), all housed in a box about the size of a double cd jewel case (nice for limited shelf space); there are no bonus tracks or additional info of any kind. Sound is clean/ crisp (since there is no info given, re-mastering is unknown), but unfortunately the final album plays back at a little higher level than the first 4, so making an even volume playback playlist of favorite tracks is compromised.
profile.summary: Ratt 5 stars; playback level 3 stars.

profile.description: Renowned for his unique playing style that drew influence from the likes of Ahmad Jamal and blended them with his own sense of swing and syncopation, Red Garland was one of the most influential musicians to rise to prominence during the hard bop era. Having performed and recorded extensively since his discharging from the Army in 1944, Garland's career had reached a zenith as the 1950s drew to a close. By 1959, Garland has already appeared alongside many esteemed jazz artists, including multiple albums with the likes of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, playing on such undisputed masterpieces as 'Round About Midnight (Columbia, 1957) and Soultrane (Prestige, 1958). Garland's attention by the end of the decade was equally divided between his high-profile collaborations and his own projects as band leader, which had at this point borne considerable fruit. With the new decade came one of Red Garland's most remarkable albums. Red Alone (Moodsville, 1960), was the first of a number of solo jazz albums Garland recorded throughout his career, capturing his profound technique in a new and uninhibited fashion. His use of block chords, unlike that of previously renowned users of the style George Shearing and Milt Buckner, utilised three notes with the right hand and four with the left whilst maintaining the same rhythm in both harmony and melody. This boxed set, containing over five hours of music across four discs, demonstrates the depth of Red Garland's artistry during this transition period of his career. Housed within are eight fully-remastered albums which show quite clearly the astonishing development of the pianist over such a short period, bringing in his own trademark style alongside influences from all corners. If this compilation manages one thing, it is to leave no doubt in the mind of the listener the importance of Red Garland's music to modern jazz, and the thoroughly deserved legacy he managed to build.
profile.reviewText:
American jazz pianist William McKinley "Red" Garland, Jr. (1923-84) was known for his trademark style of block chord playing (he also had a short-lived career as a welterweight boxer in the 40s, w/more than 35 fights, one being an exhibition bout w/Sugar Ray Robinson). During 1946-55, he worked steadily in New York & Philadelphia, backing Charlie Parker, Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, & Roy Eldridge, but remaining fairly obscure. That changed in 54 when he became a member of the Miles Davis Quintet. He formed his own trio in 58; as leader he recorded about 45 albums, & about 2 dozen as a sideman, mainly w/ John Coltrane & Miles Davis. This Enlightment box set is, so far, the 2nd of 3 of Garlands 8 album collections. THIS SET IS NOT COMPLETE (missing final song  Mr. Wonderful  from album #8). Everything else is complete w/original song lengths & track order.

Disc 1: 79:03 minutes; Coleman Hawkins w/the Red Garland Trio (1959; stereo) & Soul Junction (recorded 57, released 60 {not 59 as booklet states}; mono).
D-2: 83:17; The Red Garland Trio + Eddie Lockjaw Davis {aka Moodsville vol. 1} (60 {not59}; [very narrow] stereo) & Moodsville 6  The Red Garland Trio (60; stereo).
D-3: 78:49; Halleloo-Y-All (60; stereo) & Red Alone {aka Moodsville vol. 3} (60; stereo).
D-4: 77:09; Alone w/the Blues (60; stereo) & ROJO (61; stereo; missing final song).

The re-mastered songs sound great w/headphones, but bad news alert, the volume playback levels are very uneven between albums (lousy for making personal playlists via computer or playing in a carousel (albums 3, 4, 8 are even; 2, 4, 6, 7 are louder; 1 is lower). Discs are securely held by plastic teeth inside a dual-hinged jewel case, which in turn slides into a cardboard box w/a closing flap, same height/ length as a normal jewel case for optimal storage. Front cover of box, case & booklet all show pictures of original albums front covers; back of box & case list songs + lengths; minimal 8 page booklet: 1  page of a limited Garland bio w/very limited song personnel listed;  page w/album names + release year; 1 page w/songs + lengths + composers last name; 5 photos. If interested, Windows Media Player correctly identifies all song titles & lists composers full name on all songs.

On a personal note, Ive collected dozens of these 8-album jazz boxes  Garland is the only artist so far that kind of annoys me - in so many of his arrangements, there are extended (1-2 minute) stand-up bass solos. To each their own, but I find them very boring/ distracting, but w/out the bass solos, I do love his music.
profile.summary: Music 5 stars; uneven playback volume levels 2 stars

profile.description: The lustrous Chicago blues scene of the 1950s was predominated by great pianists, and Henry Gray was one of the finest. His rolling two-fisted keyboard work graced countless Chicago blues recordings during the '50s, and Henry spent twelve years as pianist for the legendary Howlin' Wolf. This session, recorded in 1988, marked something of a comeback for Henry who had recorded only sporadically in the previous two decades. Long out of print on LP, Blind Pig is proud to issue these classic sides by a true blues master at the special budget list price of $9.98.
profile.reviewText: Louisiana born (1925) blues pianist Henry Gray, unfortunately, is not as well known as he should be, since he was very influential to the post-war Chicago two fisted piano boogie woogie playing style, playing for 12 years in Howlin Wolfs band starting in 1956, & as a session player w/such  blues giants as Jimmy Reed, Bo Diddley, Jimmy Rogers, Little Walter, Billy Boy Arnold, Sonny Boy Williamson, Muddy Waters, Otis Rush, Lazy Lester, Buddy Guy, James Cotton, Hubert Sumlin, & Elmore James (he played w/him on the night James died). This, his 1988 stateside debut release, recorded in Chicago, features him on piano & vocals w/a tight band on guitar, bass, & drums.  An equal mix of slow & rockin blues, there are 12 songs (35:29 minutes); 6 original, & 6 covers of songs by J. Rogers, Big Maceo, Little Walter, J. Reed, J.B. Lenoirs Mojo Boogie,  & a nice rockin blues version of Fats Dominos My Girl Josephine.  Any fan of Chicago style blues definitely needs this in their collection! Search out his other stuff too, and btw, he is still touring in his late 80s!!
profile.summary: An overlooked Chicago style blues gem

profile.description: Garland began his musical career studying clarinet and alto saxophone under the tutelage of Buster Prof Smith, who had previously been an early mentor of saxophonist Charlie Parker. Having been drafted into the army in 1941, Garland began to learn piano whilst stationed Fort Huachuca, Arizona, practicing relentlessly until his playing quickly became proficient. It was also around this time that Garland undertook a short-lived amateur boxing career, racking up 35 professional fights in total which would include facing a young Sugar Ray Robinson in the ring, although he would go on to lose this particular bout. Fortunately, his time spent as a welterweight seemed to have no negative impact on his performance, and after being discharged from the army in 1944 he immediately began playing small venues all over Texas. By the turn of the 1950s, Garland's stature as a musician had increased incalculably, having performed with a plethora of jazz greats including Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, Ben Webster and Sonny Stitt, as well as leading his own trio. Garland embarked on without a doubt his most famous collaboration in 1955 when he was invited to join Miles Davis' band, which at the time also featured Coltrane, Philly Joe Jones and Paul Chambers. Garland would remain in Davis' band until the summer of 1958, recording such classic albums as Miles: The New Miles Davis Quintet, 'Round About Midnight and Milestones. Quite astoundingly, Garland would somehow also manage to produce numerous highly-regarded albums of his own during this period. Following his debut A Garland Of Red, he went on to record such classics as John Coltrane With The Red Garland Trio, further building on his previous work with the renowned saxophonist, and All Mornin' Long, with critic Ira Gitler describing the epic 20 minute title track as a many-splendored, deep-dish demonstration of feeling, mood and melody.

profile.reviewText: An excellent mid-tier 60s British invasion band from Liverpool, this 58 minute, 2002 re-mastered disc features their only 2 UK album releases from 1963 & 1965 in full stereo (pay no attention to the Amazon listing). Their 1st albums stereo mix (tracks 1-14), although not that god-awful simulated stereo of the era, has most of the lead vocals on the right channel; this album was released in the U.S. scattered over their 1st 2 albums (on the 4 album set listed below, but they are all in mono on that set  - you will need this U.K. release to get the songs in stereo). The 2nd - Ferry Cross the Mersey - has fantastic stereo sound; since this is a soundtrack, there are only 9 (of 12) songs by the group. Unlike their 1st album, Gerry Marsden wrote most of their songs on here, and it contains several songs that rank among the upper echelons of Merseybeat (Its Gonna Be Alright, Think About Love & Ill Wait for You  the last 2 rank right up there w/the best of the Beatles catalogue of that era).  If you remember this band from the 60s, you will be missing a lot of their hits since many more of their songs were on U.S. albums, so you will need to supplement this w/the BGO (Warner Music UK) 2015 2 disc release w/4 U.S. albums (Youll Never Walk Alone/Second Album/Ill Be There/Girl On A Swing). If you love the Merseybeat era, you definitely need this in your collection (even if you have the original vinyl, you must have the re-mastering). Comes w/a 6 page booklet w/reproductions of the original front/back album covers, but unless you have 20 year old eyes, you will need a magnifying glass to read the tiny print (there was a lot written on the back of those albums!).
profile.summary: Must-have Merseybeat British Invasion

profile.description: For many, the story of Weather Report begins with the late 1970s albums that featured the addition of electric bassist Jaco Pastorius (as documented on 2011's box set, Weather Report: The Columbia Albums 1976-1982, which celebrated the 40th anniversary of the band's formation). Yet what the six albums that make up this comprehensive collection prove beyond a shadow of a doubt is that the early to mid 1970s saw some of the most adventurous and satisfying work of Weather Report's entire lifespan. In fact, it's these recordings Weather Report, I Sing the Body Electric, Live In Tokyo, Sweetnighter, Mysterious Traveller and Tale Spinnin' that established Weather Report as one of the seminal fusion ensembles of the era, alongside such brethren bands as the Mahavishnu Orchestra, The Headhunters, and Return To Forever. With remastered sound and authoritative liner notes by Bill Milkowski, Weather Report: The Columbia Albums 1971-1975, is also noteworthy for the inclusion of the complete Live In Tokyo, (a handful of whose tracks had appeared on I Sing the Body Electric) which captures the band at a peak performance in 1972.
profile.reviewText: Re-mastered, excellent sounding, inexpensive Sony European Union box set of Weather Reports 1st five studio albums, each w/bonus tracks, plus the Live in Tokyo double 3rd release.  Each disc is in a cardboard sleeve replica of the original album, all housed in a side-flip-open 5 W x 5  H x 1  thick box.  Comes w/a 23 page highly informative booklet chock full of band & individual song info (such as personnel on each song, recording date), album chart info, etc.  As a bonus for me, the volume playback level between discs is quite even, so I was able to make a consistent sounding playlist w/only the songs I like and even better, the next box set, The Columbia Albums 1976-1982, are also of the same volume level, so buy that one up too.
profile.summary: consistent playback level between discs

profile.reviewText: Not exactly a Whirlpool part but it works fine (original replacements cost 3X more). The coils are a little thinner than the original, and the "arm" under the burner front doesn't "clip" into and under the notch in the drip pan to hold it flat and in place, but it fits flat non-the-less since the contacts easily fit into the plug-in on the stove. I think this may be a little better made than the original since the first (smallest) coil is held in place by a notch in the arm (as you can see in the picture). The original burner had no such holder and that part of the coil kind of popped up so pots would not fit plat on the heating surface.

profile.reviewText: This replacement pump for my Petmate Deluxe Fresh Flow drinking fountain, although the same model #, is slightly different but it works well. The white flow control lever on the old pump (which stuck through the hole in the fountain between the pump compartment & the water "bowl") has been replaced by a tiny sliding control nub on the face of the pump, only accessible before the fountain is assembled for operation (I would suggest setting it in the low flow position for the first time since it seems more powerful than the replaced pump). The ac/dc adapter power cord is about 14" long (note: 2 prior pumps I owned broke where the hard, very thin plastic power cord meets the cord "collar" on both ends... I suggest reinforcing this flex point w/electrical tape). The cord from the pump to its female end (where it plugs into the adaptor cord male end) is at least 4' long (I didn't stretch it out to measure) but is missing the dial power on/off switch of the last pump (although if you need it this is very easy to re-install onto the new cord if you are at all handy). If like me you are using this for the pet fountain, 2 things: make sure to keep the cord "clamp" from the old cord (the black piece that holds the cord in place where it exits the fountain's rear); and twist out the plastic 1/2" (outside diameter) "pipe/ nozzle" sticking out the top of the pump & replace it w/the smaller 1/4" nozzle (packed loose in the pump box w/no instructions w/it so you at first wonder what it's for) which fits into the water flow tube of the assembled water fountain. This is a cheaper option than buying a new Petmate fountain. After a few hours of use so far, seems more powerful & quieter than previous pump.
profile.summary: a bit different than earlier model/ works for Petmate fountain

profile.description: Heavy-duty zip ties are hard-wearing and designed for rugged industrial, automotive, and farm/ag applications demanding high levels of tensile strength and large bundle diameters. Permanently secured until you cut them off GB ties lock tight without stretching or sliding. The thick nylon 6/6 material and patented one-piece, injection-molded construction eliminates failure due to parts working loose or breaking off. Raised ridges on the cable ties bent tips are designed to provide a secure grip while requiring minimal effort to close and the strong locking head ensures the increased tensile strength you need. Ideal for ducts, temporary fencing, heavy equipment, and vibration prone areas in both electric and non-electric applications, including home repairs, remodeling, kitchen, or bathroom renovations in residential and commercial locations. When you've got a big job that demands a strong tie able to handle a large bundle diameter then count on Gardner Bender heavy-duty cable ties. UL Recognized component. Ultraviolet black (UVB) ties resist harmful light rays - primarily for outdoor use.
profile.reviewText: One star strictly for the false product description - package is labeled for "indoor use" only, & they ARE NOT UV resistant (even though the product # contains UV - most GB different sized cable ties are no longer made w/UV resistance); also labeled for only 32 degrees, so if you do happen to use them outside somewhere you have a cold winter, they may snap if they have any kind of load on them. On the plus side, they are pretty heavy duty (1/4" wide) - package lists them as 120 lbs. tensile strength, but I kind of doubt that - I think it would snap w/that much pull, but I've yet to have one fail on me by snugging it too tightly.
profile.summary: NOT UV resistant; for indoor use only.

top_5.description: Digitally remastered six CD box set. Originally released on the small White Whale label, the Turtles' original albums have remained stubbornly out of print for many years, leaving fans with various greatest-hits collections that only scratched the surface of the band's deep and rewarding catalog. The Turtles' label FloEdCo, in association with Manifesto Records, celebrates the band's 50th anniversary with the release of The Complete Original Albums Collection, a CD box set containing the six albums that the Turtles released between 1965 to 1970, plus a wealth of rare bonus material. Each of the band's first three albums - It Ain't Me Babe, You Baby and Happy Together - is presented in it's original mono and stereo mixes, while each of the remaining three - The Turtles Present the Battle of the Bands, Turtle Soup and Wooden Head - provide a generous assortment of rare bonus tracks, including some previously unreleased material. Meticulously researched and prepared from the original master tapes by renowned engineer Bill Inglot, and contains detailed liner notes by noted writer and archivist Andrew Sandoval. The resulting package offer a unique insight into one of rock's most misunderstood bands.
top_5.reviewText: A great Turtles anthology with just a few complaints. All 6 of their albums feature nice gatefold covers, the sound is excellent through headphones, & the playback volume level between albums is very nicely consistent (fabulous for making even sounding playlists thru Windows Media Player I filled two 79 minute CDs of just my favorite songs in their chronologically recorded order (thus Wooden Head became their 3rd album in my personal collection). Its also nice to have the mono/ stereo versions of each of their earlier songs that were available in both  no need to have the which is better debate  everybodys happy. The only cons I found are only 2 of the discs are encoded w/info (artist/ album/ song, etc.), some of which is wrong, like song titles, 3 discs have absolutely no info, & 1 has about  of the songs listed. Even though the booklet is quite informative, the printing is very large so they wouldve had enough room to have included more Billboard & UK chart info about the songs, what songs ended up as B-sides, etc. (there is SOME of this info included, but far from inclusive). And lastly, there are 4 songs missing from this complete collection: 69s Lady-O (included on an earlier reissue to Turtle Soup); 70s Teardrops (released by White Whale as The Dedications as artist); Who Would Ever Think That I Would Marry Mary Margaret (a horrible single thats been on a Rhino comp & More Golden Hits); and a quite good song, We Aint Gonna Party no More (was on a reissue of Wooden Head, & was also on More Golden Hits). input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "2010 sophomore release from the Alt-Rock/Pop outfit. Congratulations is a collection of nine individual musical tours de force sequenced to flow with sonic and thematic coherence. Produced by MGMT and Sonic Boom, the album was recorded throughout 2009 in Upstate New York, Malibu and Brooklyn and features the band's core duo (Andrew Vanwyngarden and Ben Goldwasser) performing with Matt Asti, Will Berman and James Richardson, their live band.". output:
You know, I didn't realize how many morons were out there until I started reading the reviews of this album.

profile.description: iBank manages checking, savings and credit card accounts... tracks loans and investments... analyzes income and expenses... and plans your financial future with powerful budgeting and reporting tools.
profile.reviewText:
We wasted $60 on this software, hoping that it would be a replacement for Quicken 2007.

While iBank can do the bare-bones basics well (like balancing a checkbook), it has literally HUNDREDS of bugs in the product... and it can't even do BASIC REPORTING like Quicken could. Here we are, at the end of the year at tax time, and we can't even get the reports that we need out of iBank to get our tax data to the IRS.

If you like your data being held hostage, then this is the app for you.

If you don't believe our complaints, check out the IGG Software Forums on their websites for THOUSANDS of complaints from other iBank users, that have gone UNANSWERED by iBank's technical support team.

iBank's technical support is incompetent & clueless at best, and completely unresponsive for weeks on end at worst.

iBank will NEVER be the product that people want it to be.

Our best advice would be to wait until Quicken 2007 is updated for Lion in a few months, and use that instead.
profile.summary: Think twice before buying this software

profile.description: RETROSPECT 8.0 DESKTOP 3U MAC
profile.reviewText:
As of December 3, 2009, this product is STILL not ready for primetime yet.

profile.description: Protective Suede Case & Stand for iPad
profile.reviewText:
I read several of the negative reviews here about this case, but I am just not seeing the same sorts of problems on my end.

I have owned this case for over a month now, and I absolutely love this case.  I think that this case is *SIGNIFICANTLY BETTER* than the Apple case because the Apple case has sharp edges that makes it difficult to hold for long periods of time while you're reading a book, along with many other disadvantages which I will describe below.

BTW, I also ordered other cases as well, but they all paled in comparison to this wonderful case from MacAlly.

I have to admit that I have always been a MacAlly fan, and I think that they live up to their high standards with this iPad case as well.

Some of the advantages of this MacAlly case over the Apple case:

1. This case has soft edges, so it is very easy to hold for long periods of time while you are reading a book. (The Apple case has sharp uncomfortable edges.)
2. This case lets you easily snap your iPad in & out in just a matter of seconds. Don't want to use the case so you can show off your beautiful iPad's hardware to your friends? Simply pop it out. Want to use the case again? Just pop it back in. If you've tried to use the Apple case, you know that it takes minutes upon minutes of pulling and stretching and screaming and pulling your hair out to try to get the iPad in and out of that case.
3. This case allows for much better control of your iPad than the Apple case because this case lets you insert your iPad in either direction: home button on the left or home button on the right. This is sooo much better for me than the Apple case, which REQUIRES you to put your iPad in with the button on the left... which means that the volume controls are smashed into your lap and difficult to adjust.
4. This case is much more ergonomic than the Apple case because it has a much larger incline than the Apple case. This makes it sooo much easier to type on. While the Apple case gives you a tiny bit of an incline, the iPad is still pretty close to being flat in your lap with the Apple case. The MacAlly case really gives you a nice incline to work with, so you have a much easier time when typing.

Some slight disadvantages to this case:

1. Cosmetically, the grey color is not that pretty to look at. I would have rather had this case in black, but when I purchased it, grey was the only color to choose from. MacAlly, please make this case in black or any other color!!
2. Cosmetically, the leather strap isn't really that pretty either, but it is functional.
3. Sometimes the leather strap can be a little difficult to slide in & out of its holder, but its not a deal-breaker for me.

In regards to people's claims that the construction of this item is poor, I have to admit that I am not seeing this problem. I feel like this is a really solid case, and I am very happy with my purchase. Granted, I've only had this for a little over a month, so maybe my opinion will change over time.

Hope this helps!
profile.summary: My favorite iPad case!

profile.description: The WarioWare team took an idea so wacky, it could only be made with the latest technology: the Wii Remote controller! Wario stumbles into an old building called the Temple of Form. Inside, he finds a mystical treasure called the Form Baton. There are many ways to hold and move the baton (called "forms"), and legend has it that if the holder follows the forms, he can overcome any challenge. With this discovery, the form craze spreads and soon everybody is doing their best to master the moves. Features: • Revolutionary Fun: With hundreds of microgames, this game is just as wild as you'd expect from the name WarioWare, but the gameplay has been revolutionized. Under Wario's tutelage and with the help of the Wii Remote, players will swing, spin and squat their way to victory. • Tons and Tons of Microgames: With more than 200 lightning-quick microgames and controls that range from scribbling to flailing, WarioWare: Smooth Moves takes interactive gaming to a whole new level. All players need is confidence, a Wii Remote and their best moves. • Off-Screen Party: With games that are as much fun to play as they are to watch people play, WarioWare: Smooth Moves brings the party to its feet. It's hilarious for players and audiences alike.
profile.reviewText:
This game is perfect for the Nintendo Wii, because it shows off how much fun the groundbreaking Wii remote can be! You have to twist & shake & turn & bend the remote in all sorts of fun ways in order to play this game.

In fact, I feel that this game should be the very first game that all new Nintendo Wii owners should add to their collection. I actually feel that Nintendo should have included this game for free with the Wii instead of the built-in sports package -- it's more fun than the Wii Sports collection.

Fun for kids of all ages, WarioWare Smooth Moves is actually the PERFECT PARTY GAME! This is probably the most fun Wii game you could whip out for a group of drunk or party-minded adults... as well as the most fun game you could whip out for your 6-year-old kid as well! My adult friends are all hooked on this game, and so are their young kids as well! How many games can you honestly say entice both kids & adults? This is one of them. WarioWare Smooth Moves is fun & frantically paced.

There is really no storyline at all, although they do try to squeeze in some ill-placed plot elements which simply don't make any sense at all. Luckily, you can skip through the weird & annoying storylines which add absolutely nothing to this game, and skip straight to the important part: the hundreds of very short, 3-second long MICROGAMES!

Yes, that's right -- MICROGAMES! You don't even have any time to think about the game you just finished, because you're already halfway through the next game and you only have 3 seconds to win each game! THREE SECONDS to win a game! At first, you don't even think your brain can handle information coming at you that quickly, and then as you continue to play the game & get better at it, you actually start speeding up your thinking so much that you actually feel like time is moving in slow motion during those 3 seconds.

Some of the microgames include: save the woman from falling off the skyscraper; shake the flies off the banana; spin the pizza; deflect the balls that are flying at you; reunite the lovers on a desert island; find the missing kid in the dark; close the grocery store for the night; swat the fly; don't fall off the beachball; drink the glass of water; turn off the alarm clock.

The games get more furious & more fast-paced as you play, and it just keeps building up to explosive fun & laughter amongst you & your friends.

If you are a Wii owner and want to add a fun & unique game to your collection, absolutely add WarioWare Smooth Moves to your collection. At the time of this writing, this is currently my favorite party game in my entire Wii collection.
profile.summary: Very fun game! Perfect for the Wii!

profile.description: Wheat Belly Plan
profile.reviewText:
I discovered this book because it was recommended over 20 times by John McLean in his excellent book "Low Carb Revolution". So I read "Wheat Belly" from cover-to-cover, based on John McLean's recommendation.

It turns out that "Wheat Belly" is mostly fantastic & an excellent read & an almost-perfect book, with a few problems that bothered me:

1. William Davis gets way too technical in multiple chapters throughout the book. Therefore, I highly recommend reading John McLean's "Low Carb Revolution" FIRST before reading "Wheat Belly", because McLean explains (in simple & easy-to-understand & layperson terms) the roles of insulin & glucagon & other hormones in the body. Unfortunately, William Davis assumes that you have a technical background in medicine for many parts of his book, and doesn't grasp how to explain things clearly to a layperson. On the other hand, John McLean excels at this, so luckily, if you read McLean's book first, you'll at least be able to understand what Davis is talking about during the technical portions of this book.

2. William Davis goes on & on & on about how to live a healthy lifestyle, but then he ends the entire book by telling you to use a **MICROWAVE** for most of his recipes!! Um, what, William? Are you kidding me?!?! I stopped using a microwave 15 years ago, and the terrible effects that microwaves have on food molecules & the body have been widely documented. How do you expect us to take you seriously as a health expert if you're advising everybody to use a microwave?? Not a great way to end your book, after taking us along for an entire journey that was pretty outstanding. I would NEVER advise ANYBODY ANYWHERE to EVER use a microwave for ANYTHING. Absolutely poor way to end the book.

3. William Davis gives sugar a "get out of jail free" pass throughout the book to focus solely on wheat. In reality, the perfect diet isn't just a wheat-free diet, but actually a "low-glycemic diet", which eliminates modern society's 2 evils: BOTH wheat AND sugar. The effects of sugar on the bloodstream & human health are ALMOST as bad as wheat, but Davis chooses not to point any fingers at sugar. If you just eliminated wheat from your diet but continued to drink coca-cola every day, you're going to be in SERIOUS SERIOUS trouble. So Davis is about 80% of the way there, but he really needed to come down harder on sugar, too.

Besides those 3 things, "Wheat Belly" is a very fast read, it is very informative, and it will be life-changing to just about every single human being that reads it. I highly recommend "Wheat Belly", but be sure to give yourself a well-rounded education by supplementing this book with other books advocating low-glycemic & low-insulinemic diets. Then, you will have the complete picture!!
profile.summary: Mostly excellent (with a few flaws)

profile.description: In the tradition of The Player and Swimming with Sharks, comes this biting comedy about Hollywood sycophants and schemers that fuel its increasingly vacuous ideas. Kevin Taylor is a young screenwriter with a dream, but his unfortunate reality is fetching coffee (and hookers) for a washed-up producer and listening to his blowhard colleagues
profile.reviewText: This film is a modern-day spin on "The Emperor's New Clothes", and it is extremely well-written & well-done.  It is smart, biting, relentless, and funny.  This is the movie that "The Player" was trying to be... but this movie is actually effective at breaking through to the audience, while "The Player" alienated itself from its audience by using too many "inside jokes".  I was lucky enough to catch this fantastic movie while it was in limited release in Los Angeles, and went back to see it 3 times because I enjoyed it so much.  I'm excited about this DVD release of "New Suit", because I want to hear the commentary track with the writer, who seems particularly astute at knowing what really happens behind-the-scenes in Hollywood. profile.description: The NGP Matte is an ultra thin, soft and impact resistant carrying solution. Made from a next generation polymer, this carrying solution is tear and elongation resistant. The NGP Matte will not fade or become sticky.
profile.reviewText:
This little $20 case may be the best purchase I've ever made!! I wish I could give this product 10 stars!!

Let me tell you a brief story:

I previously never had a case on my iPhone 4 before, because I thought the phone was too beautiful to mar with a case. Well that was a huge mistake, because 2 weeks ago, I accidentally dropped my iPhone 4 on the sidewalk and the screen shattered into about a million pieces, the sides of the iPhone were completely crushed in, and it basically looked like my iPhone had been run over by a tank.
