profile.description: Recently widowed Karen Tunny and her two daughters, Sarah and Emma, move to a remote mountain home which Karen has inherited from the family of her late husband. However, she is unaware that the home is situated near an old mine, the site of an early 20th century tragedy in which many children where buried alive..
profile.reviewText:
It's never a good thing when you're laughing midway through a horror movie...There was alot of predictability in the story - which seemed liked it had been a preteen horror book or an extension on one of those urban legend short stories for preteens. The idea has been done in other movies and even on t.v shows. A group of children die in a mining accident in the early 1900's and wander the now deserted forest up in the hills at night as little zombies with axes. A mother and her two daughters move in after inheriting their dead father's family house. I could have done without the beginning back story on the miner kids and how it all began - that's what finding newspaper articles is for... Of the two daughters, one is about 7, and very devoid of personality. Scout Taylor-Compton is the teenage sister, the best thing in this long movie. The family never stops to wonder why they are the only people on the hill besides a crazy woodsman, why everyone else lives in the town below them. In a Hide & Seek ripoff idea, the young daughter goes out to play with invisible friends and disappears. People start to die, farm animals disappear...
This movie has to have the lamest killers EVER seen. They attack robotically with their little pick-axes and the first image in my head is of the 7 dwarves gone mad. This is the part that inspires laughter. Now be very glad you only rented this and you never have to see it again.
profile.summary: The 700 zombie dwarfs...

profile.description: Persona 4: Dancing All Night "Disco Fever Collector's Edition" is a North American exclusive set and the ultimate collector's edition for Persona fans! Persona 4: Dancing All Night is a story-driven music game of the cult hit RPG Persona 4, developed by ATLUS. Replacing the RPG elements are dance battles that challenge players' dexterity and accuracy, as they tap out re-mixes of fan-favorite themes and brand new music tracks. The storyline continues from after the events of Persona 4, when the teenage mega-idol, Rise Kajikawa, returns to the city to re-take her show biz career. During that time, a strange video appears on the internet and the unfortunate people who watched it have gone missing! Members of Kanamin Kitchen, Rise's junior idol group, have disappeared and it's up to the Investigation team to mount a rescue mission - only they discover the same monstrous Shadows from the Midnight Channel. To make matters even worse, their Persona abilities are rendered ineffective, and the Shadows in P4D can only be defeated by dance, so bust out powerful dance moves to save the day!
profile.reviewText:
I love the Persona series, and I am never tired of new stories in the series, no matter the premise or style.
 I think the people who will buy this game  will fall into either the hardcore Persona fan category, or just like dance/rhythm games.
Since I fall into the first category, I have the Special Edition, which consists of a heavy golden Teddy keychain, a plastic Disco Teddy zip bag, Vita skin, soundtrack, and some download codes for costumes and songs in free play mode. Not since P4 Golden have any Limited Editions in this series been sold out or hard to find,  with even prices dropping months and months later, but any Persona fan will need to have these things regardless whatever value the flippers place on them.
The game. The game takes place sometime after the events of Persona 4 Golden, I suspect likely before Arena because the Shadow Operatives are never mentioned. It has kind a new midnight threat, a new Shadow world, a new villain, and a new threat to the town. In the last spinoff game, the Investigation Team couldn't battle with their Personas and were forced to compete in a fighting tournament in another Shadow world. Here the Investigation Team enter a world where no one can hurt anyone else, and can't battle with their Personas. An new Shadow world, new midnight broadcast over the internet,  new villain, and new threat to the town.
Instead of having them taken against their will and entered in a dance competition where they must dance to survive, escape, or move on, this time they go in willingly. And dance willingly. It might be the strangest thing about this game. Already learning dance routines to support Rise in her comeback, the team are preparing to be her backup dancers in this comeback performance at a sold out idol festival.
In the middle of rehearsals, a bizarre over the top parody group of new idols disappear-minus their leader- amid already existing rumors that going to the festival website at midnight results in a dead idol pulling you into a another world or putting you into a coma. Yu, Naoto, and Rise test this rumor and find themselves pulled into another Shadow World where they are unable to battle. They are kicked out just as they find out that the missing girls are inside, and gather the team to go back in. Here a hypnotic song plays and then Shadows try to tie them up and ribbons and pull them under to a mindset where they decide to hide their true selves and instead give the world what it wants to see in order to form bonds and be accepted. Not too different. The only way to escape being dragged in? Play your own music and...dance to it to express your feelings to the shadows trying to drag you under. Then you are free to move to the next point in the world or the next stage created for each missing idol. The idols themselves are not very likable and don't really have much in the way of personalities- however hard the game tries to give them some.
The game focuses on having you perform rhythm dance routines, like DDR but with your hands, as a way of battling your way through the shadows to the next area, and then as a way of defeating the monsters the girls turn into. Instead of having them forced to dance, they seem excited to tak turns, and some aren't so great (Naoto, Teddie, Yukiko) while others excel (Rise, Kanji, Yu). The game is essentially a visual novel that stops and has you complete dances to keep going. It even splits the team in half, and then goes as far as showing you what's going on with Nanako, Dojima, and the group's leader back in the real world. Read. Dance. Read. Dance. Is it a little cheesy? Yes. Is it just great to be back in the Persona world? Yes! Is the dancing more fun than you thought it would be? Yes again. Most of the songs you will remember from Golden, just remixed.
Overall, it won't kill you to play a few rhythm games to familiar music to keep the story going, and it's highly likely you'll have fun doing it.
The only sad part, is that if you sit down and dedicate two nights and 8 hours to playing this, it'll be over before you know it.
I just hope they can come up with another way or reason for the cast to jump into another mystery. Persona Racing? I'm in.
profile.summary: Visual Novel with Dancing Stages Continues the Persona 4 Story into a New Chapter.

profile.description: After ten years of marriage, Do-il (Kim Jin-geun) and Mi-sook (Shim Hye-jin) live a seemingly happy and secure life together. Unable to conceive, they decide to adopt Jin-sung (Moon woo-bin), a young boy that Mi-sook is drawn to after seeing his Munch-like paintings. Quiet and introverted, Jin-sung spends most of his time playing underneath the Acacia tree in their backyard, away from the family. When Mi-sook becomes miraculously pregnant, he becomes even more detached. As the once-dead Acacia tree in the backyard begins to bloom, terrible accidents begin to tear the household apart. Is it Jin-sung, or something far more sinister?
profile.reviewText:
I should have known better! The reviews on Asian movie review sites were consistantly bad, but I guess people really just HAVE to see it for themselves right? This Korean "thriller" isn't poor quality or low budget. The acting is believeable. The little girl next door is probably one of the scariest faces you will ever see of a child cast. The story starts out interestingly enough,  a couple adopts a boy because the woman can't get pregnant, only to become pregnant shortly after the adoption. Then everything becomes grey as the new baby arrives and resentment builds on all sides. One night the boy  disappears over being banned from playing with a tree he obsesses over in the backyard as well as hated of the new baby. Now the story turns on it's side and changes the characters completely from what they were. Some domestic-abuse scenes that'll make you go "what?"... Accidents and a death start happening mysteriously. All in all the secret of the movie is really something that everyone but you knows all along!
The movie is unsettling in a unwatchable and sickening way rather than being scary.
There are scenes where the child tries to kill the baby and the baby is constantly neglected; if things like that bother you (not the case with me), skip this movie altogether.
I wish someone had bothered to write a detailed review before I wasted my time with this sick, twisted, plot-hole movie.
profile.summary: Didn't listen to reviews... Here's my detailed review -avoid this

profile.description: Every culture has one - the horrible monster fueling young children's nightmares. But for Tim, the Boogeyman still lives in his memories as a creature that devoured his father 16 years earlier. Is the Boogeyman real? Or did Tim make him up to explain why his father abandoned his family? The answerlies hidden behind every dark corner and half-opened closet of his childhood home - a place he mustreturn to and face the chilling unanswered question does the Boogeyman really exist?
profile.reviewText:
This sounds familiar...
No, not because it's a remake. Because it follows the whole paranoid, death of a parent on his own vein that Darkness Falls did. Only the story falls flat. It starts out as the beginning chapter of a new life for a man with childhood trauma. A unsupportive,useless, and whiny girlfriend who has no on-screen chemistry at all with him. Why was she even in the story? Well, it all "starts" when his mother dies, the "girl" doesn't get it, and he leaves to check out the house. This is all sketchy. The trailers and previews make you think there's more here - like a plot- but there isn't. FINALLY the movie has started and the search is on for the truth. Another useless and confusing scene involves that stupid girl again when she comes to get him, they leave and go to a low budget motel...she disappears. :) :) :) :) He steps into a closet and finds himself back in his old house. No sense. So that and the idiot "girlfriend", they kind of ruin the movie along with that empty plot thing.
profile.summary: falls flat, stays empty

profile.description: The One Missed Call curse has become an urban legend in Tokyo. Your cell phone rings with a chilling tone. Your violent demise is heard on the other end. Moments later, you die a horrible death. However, the curse has mutated to fool a wiser public and reach a broader audience. The curse indiscriminately infects anyone who answers and then works its way through every number in your phone book. Trying to solve the mystery, a couple of friends and a journalist trace the lineage of the curse to Taiwan. Once the origins are discovered, it's a race against time to put an end to the horror.
profile.reviewText:
As everyone knows, Takashi Miike directed the first movie. He's kind of controversial -but he didn't bring any of that into the movie. You need to see that movie first.

The movie brings us back with that familiar cell ring that makes you want to hide, a new option of taking someone's call for them, and news that the girl from the last movie - she's in a mental hospital. It picks up fast, with a knowledable detective and scared friends. The difference this time is no candy ball. Investigation leads them to a completely different place, with a new source seeming to have teamed up with the old one. It's not so suspenseful, not as scary as the first, but definitly worth the viewing.
profile.summary: Very different from the first

profile.description: An Epic Tale of Love and Honor  Learn about Chizuru and her many companions, as well as the secrets and political intrigue behind the Shinsengumi and the mystery of her missing father.
profile.reviewText:
What do fans of Hakuoki need to know? This game is the same story as the PSP version (Demon of the Fleeting Blossom) released in 2012. There is an extra mini section of story from the viewpoint of the men, but just a mini bonus. If you have that...you have this. It seems that every single reviewer is new to this series and doesn't seem to realize that there was ever a PSP version.
What do other people need to know?
This is a visual novel. Which is essentially the same as a choose your own adventure book. For those unaware, those are the books from your childhood where you get to the end of a chapter and it lets you decide between two or three different actions. Each choice leads to a different arc and there are good endings and bad ones where you suddenly die. That's what this game is. No walking around, no fighting. Just reading a story set in ancient Japan, and then making choices that lead to story changes. Reading.
It's also kind of a dating game. You have a group of guys to choose from. The story centers around a young girl whose father disappears. She goes looking for him and ends up in trouble, and suddenly she is living with a group of soldiers.
If you love to read, if you love ancient Japan, and if you have not played the first game, this may be for you. If you hate reading, hate japanese culture, and hate dating sims...this is not for you.
profile.summary: Same game as PSP Hakuoki: Demon of the Fleeting Blossom

profile.description: DanganRonpa: Trigger Happy Havoc is a revised and revamped edition of a title originally released on the PlayStation Portable in Japan in 2010. You'll take on the role of Makoto Naegi, a desperately average teenager who somehow finds himself accepted into Hope's Peak Academy, a prestigious high school normally reserved for the nation's" ultimate" students. But when he arrives, he and the other students soon find themselves trapped in a battle for survival against a twisted mastermind who has taken them all prisoner. You'll have to unmask the villain and uncover the secret of the school, or die trying.
profile.reviewText:
Who is this game NOT for? Anyone under 18. The official website requires you to enter your birthdate.
Why? It's stuffed full of extreme violence in the form of  torture style executions and regular murders, blood, suicide, extremely perverse adult humor, explicit language (every swear word in the books), and what games call "adult situations". The violence is often mixed in with the humor, and at least one of the torture scenes is so over the top brutal that it is hard to watch. The creator admits the game was inspired by "Saw".
Who else is this game NOT for? Anyone who does not like to read. The game consists of NO battling, NO fighting. It's all walking around and exploring, talking to other students, looking for clues, and then finally figuring out the mysteries with those clues in a court room dungeon. Hours of reading dialogue. If you didn't like 999 or Virtue's Last Reward, you probably won't like this.
The game has the horror, mystery, and visual novel aspects of 999 & Virtue's Last Reward, the trial based mysteries of Phoenix Wright (and these comparisons have already been made by at least 2 separate game review sites), and the unsettling, disturbing feel of Corpse Party.
That said...
What's the game about? You start the game as Makoto, a very plain, average, boring Japanese high school student. That point is emphasized over and over.
He, along with a number of other students, has been selected to attend a prestigious boarding school for highly skilled "Ultimate" students that guarantees success upon graduation. This may be due to the fact that the students selected to attend are already pretty much set for life. For example, there is an Ultimate Affluent Progengy (aka the rich heir to a fortune born to one of the most powerful families in Japan), the Ultimate Programmer, Ultimate Gambler, Ultimate Baseball Star, Ultimate Swimming Pro, Ultimate Writing Prodigy...and so on. Makoto is the Ultimate Lucky student. Not because he is lucky, but because he is so ordinary that he is lucky to have been chosen. There are also a few that don't make much sense to be attending such as the Ultimate Fan-fic Writer and the Ultimate Biker Gang Leader...
You go to your first day of school and the school is empty. The next thing you know, you are waking up in a secure building with metal sheets over the windows and a bunch of other students who have no idea what's going on.
That's when a little homicidal bear -Monokuma- walks in and tells you that you are trapped in the school forever. Unless...you murder another student and get away with it. There are cameras everywhere and a set of rules, and of course a trial. If you murder someone and are caught, you are executed. If you are not caught, you go free and everyone else is executed.
The game consists of NO fighting, no battling, no leveling up. Just walking around the school, exploring with point and click, finding clues, and solving murders. During "free time" you have the option to get to know other students and give them gifts to max out your friendship and earn skills. Kind of like Persona social links, but less involved.
Once you start the game, every day you will wake up, explore, and talk to other students. Occasionally Monokuma pops up to threaten you, make jokes, give you clues, or try to push you into murdering each other. Once a murder occurs, you collect clues and go to trial.
The regular gameplay is very similar to 999 or Virtue's Last Reward minus the escape the room puzzles meets Phoenix Wright. The trial gameplay only mirrors Phoenix in the way that you need to find the evidence in your file of clues that proves why certain statements are false. The difference is that words stream across the screen and once you elide which are false, you need to shoot them down with the correct clue or statement. It can get confusing to know what exactly the game wants you to combine, and when. The rest of the trial consists of a rhythm game of shooting down statements to a beat, and a fill in the scene graphic novel. The last game comparison is Corpse Party that also has a similar unsettling horror and dread that builds in inside you and can't quite believe you are seeing during the executions.
The entire game switches from extreme violence to strange humor in the blink of an eye. It is very heavy on Japanese culture, and the humor reflects this. There is constant sexual innuendo due to characters constantly mistaking innocent statements for dirty ones, and some of it gets pretty explicit. Monokuma at one point talks about his white stuffing exploding out.
Overall, if you love to read, love mysteries, love Japanese games, and can get past some of the grotesque over the top execution murders, you should love this game as much as I do. 6 days in, I am at the final chapter, but in 6 to 7 months, the seconds game will release.
My only complaint is that the controls are not always responsive. There seems to be glitches where no matter how many times you press the correct statement, it does not register. This can result in time running out 12 minutes later, and failing the case. It has happened to me on more than 3 occasions, with it taking as many as 15-20 tries to get it to respond. Which means playing the same thing over and over 15-20 times or more. EDIT: I would suggest setting the difficulty on average or easy, ask it isn't really "gamer skill", but instead it gives you more chances to make mistakes in the trial. Mistakes are easy to make when you have to tap words that are semi-responsive while there are other words criss-crossing across them that you need to avoid tapping, and also when you just aren't sure what the game is asking. You know WHY the stement is false, but not exactly what words they want you to use and in what order to PROVE that.
profile.summary: A Violent Japanese Murder Mystery Point & Click Visual Novel

profile.description: Includes cards in handsome carrying case with latch.
profile.reviewText:
I didn't get this when it was selling for 50% off in toy stores nationwide because I was a fan of the original Japanese series and thought the American dub was incredibly childish and annoying...
Anyways, this one is the American made version not the deluxe Japanese version.
The cards are thin and shiny laminated paper, but exactly accurate to the anime in artwork. The "book" itself is a laminated with plastic paper box with a plastic latch on the outside that holds it shut. I wouldn't be opening and closing it and expect it to be durable enough not to wear away and break. The cards have a slot dug out of, yes - plastic.
Overall it's cute and nice to have if you like the series, but original retail wasn't much more than $12, and I found mine for $7 in a used book store. It wasn't an amazing find; they had price-checked it and put it in the glass display case to protect it from children, but not marked it up because it honestly isn't worth that much.
profile.summary: WAY over-priced, but nice to own....American version

profile.description: Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth: The Wild Cards Premium Edition is a North American exclusive set and the ultimate collector's edition for Persona fans! This special set contains the Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth game, a colorful groovy Persona Q-themed protective case for your Nintendo 3DS system previously only available in Japan, the "Sounds of the Labyrinth "music CD from Japan, an exclusive art book, and eleven Persona Tarot Cards (Part 2 of the card collection)! All of the items are contained inside a collectible outer box.
profile.reviewText:
Persona Q Wild Card Edition includes the second part of the tarot set, a 3DS XL case, a mini soundtrack, and a mini mini art book.
If you are a fan of the series, a must have.
This game is a lot different than the last few games in the series, or last 2 and portable variations. It is first person view and seems very similar to the Etrian Odyssey. You explore dungeons and as you explore, you draw your own map, adding walls, icons, doors, etc.
You choose to play the game as either the Persona 3 or 4 cast protagonist with his team, and at the first boss, the other team shows up to team up. Familiar people and things include Margaret who shows up to run the nurses office, the workshop, and the Velvet Room- for a price. Eventually Elizabeth and Theo come along to take over the Nurse's Office and Weapon Shop respectively.
Missions pop up and some involves mini games, collecting objects, or getting to know your team better.
 The Persona 4 story starts off in school during a festival. Suddenly a clock tower appears and they find two strangers names Zen and Rei wandering in the dungeons. That's when they realize it's a different worlds of some sort.
What are the differences from previous games?
As the protagonist of 3 or 4, you can only control 2 personas now, instead of multiples. You can still carry several, but can't assign more than 2. This can be frustrating. Your team each gets two personas as well.
You also have to choose your teammates here, and can have 5 but in rows; three in front, two in back and each character is meant for one or the other slot.
When all enemies are knocked down, it DOES NOT give you the combo or group attack option; instead it seems to happen randomly.
 You don't get cards after battle aside from the occasional and very repetitive Persona ones (Slime shows up almost exclusively). the Velvet Room fusion format has a new option where you can dissolve any persona into another to gain skills.
 There are shortcuts that either are completely one way, or allow back and forth travel.
There are new enemies called FOES, that you have to find ways to maneuver around on the path.
It definitely takes some getting use to. The story is still the same casts you know done in chibi form, the same humor, the same enemies/shadows. On normal, 11 hours in I was still on the first level grinding to get strong enough. 42 hours in? Level 3.
I am still getting use to all the new things, and will update as I continue. So far, so many things are familiar and others are new, but overall it seems like a great addition to Persona.
Any Persona fan will be able to overcome the changes after playing for a few hours, and just having characters we have grown to love in a new story is enough to keep me playing. Like any Prsona game, you dread the end coming.
profile.summary: Must Have For Persona Fans

profile.description: Kor, a young man living in a small village by the sea, is enhancing his sword fighting skills under the careful supervision of his grandfather. Impressed by Kor's growing skill, his grandfather bequeaths to him an unusual weapon known as a Soma. Soon afterwards, while watching the house in his grandfather's absence, Kor meets a young woman named Kohaku who has come searching for his grandfather. Kor is enchanted with the young woman, the first girl he's ever met from outside his village. However, a mysterious witch soon appears who casts a spell on Kohaku's Spiria, the embodiment of her heart and soul. Kor attempts to lift the spell by connecting to her Spiria through a technique known as a Spiria Link, but while doing so he accidentally shatters her Spiria Core, the source of her emotions. Kor, armed only with the Soma given to him by his grandfather, must now set out on a journey to find a way to make Kohaku's Spiria whole once more.
profile.reviewText:
*This review is for the NORTH AMERICAN release...*

I picked this game up on release Tuesday at 12 am and have been playing it everyday for the past 6 days. I am 24 hours or so in and so far I love the game.
Know that teh game is in original Japanese language, with English subtitles. The gameplay animation is smooth and streamlined, (and the characters don't look robotic in movement or construction) more so than Tales of Xillia. The story is solid, interesting, adn it starts up right away. There is no waiting 20 minutes for the story to build. A boy named Kor meets a girl named Kohaku and her brother who are fleeing from a murderous witch android, and when her core spiria is shattered and the pieces rain down over the land, Kor vows to track down each feeling crystal -anger, fear, sadness, etc. The three of them can all use mystical weapons called somas and powers called artes, and along the way they pick up more misfits to add to the team. Each core feeling ends up inside another human and ends up affecting them and/or others around them. There is adventure, suspense, and lots of humor between the squabbling team members. As the story unfolds, more villains emerge. About 22 hours in it seemed that the story was at it's close and there was betrayal and tragedy and chaos. And then the story continued with a new objective for the characters- save the world (of course)! I am not as impressed with how the first half of the story ended but am still sad to think the game will end soon. The gameplay is also seamless. Characters wander from town to town and field to field much like Tales of Xillia, and battles are free instead of turn based as well. The difference is that you can't avoid enemies in the field by sneaking past them- instead they are invsible and you randomly end up in battle much like walking through grass in Pokemon. There is a learning curve with using artes magic attacks, putting them into shortcuts for easy access, leveling up your magic in categories (much like TOX here too) and learning special attacks. But it becomes second nature with the shortcuts. Each team member is playable and able to level up in level, soma, and artes, and you can even travel as any of them. The map has blue and red dots that represent towns, etc, and act as a guide when you get lost. It does not tell you where to go but it shows you where you are and where you can go. Some of the towns and areas have puzzles and only one made me so frustrated I needed to look it up.
As of now I love the graphics, the story, the gameplay, the humor, and some of the characters. If i had to find anything negative it becomes very tiny such as Kor's stubborn naivete, the endless focus on Kohaku(which adorable Beryl also brings up), and some of the unexpected tragedy mid game in the form of one death that seems unnecessary.
One more things I did hate that was also very tiny, was during a trip to a small village in the second half of the game, all of the villagers have odd accents and since the game dialogue is in Japanese, the translators choose -POORLY- to communicate this by using odd symbols and spelling. It seems to parody the stereotypical Canadian with "oots and aboots" but it becomes completely impossible to understand the text when they use the symbols and the odd phonetic spellings together. The second half of the game overall is also slower and a little messy, but overall a solid title that has more pros than many games out there. The story never drags in the beginning, it pulls you in. A must have RPG!
profile.summary: I am 24 hours or so in and so far I love the game

profile.description: KINGDOM HEARTS HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue is a compilation that brings the popular KINGDOM HEARTS [Dream Drop Distance] to the PlayStation4 computer entertainment system platform remastered in high definition. Originally released in 2012, KINGDOM HEARTS [Dream Drop Distance] HD is a full-HD remastered version of KINGDOM HEARTS 3D [Dream Drop Distance]. Series protagonists Sora and Riku take on the Mark of Mastery exam in preparation for coming threats. The signature action of the KINGDOM HEARTS series has evolved, allowing players to experience faster-paced battles and exploration at a blistering pace.
profile.reviewText:
This game was scheduled to come out on January 24th. It was released at 9 pm on the 23rd however at Gamestop.
The limited edition comes in a paper box with a Disney pin. It's the same price as the regular edition, and only difference is that paper box and pin. Since Gamestop had 6 copies and only 5 were pre-orders, I picked up this last copy.
This game consists of 1 new 2 hour game, one 3DS port, and one movie. I'd caution people to be careful when reading reviews by people who admit that they have only played the game for an hour, but that the new content looks amazing. The only new content is a very short almost demo like epilogue to a past PSP game. Once you finsih that, it leaves you only with a port and a movie. More on that in my review.
The first game is an HD port from the 2012 of 3DS game called Dream Drop Distance. Not new content.  If you've already played it, unless it tops your list of all time favorite games,  chances are that you'll skip it. For those that have not played it, it's a kind of side story from the perspective of Sora, and it doesn't play all that differently from the first or second games.
The second game is a beautiful, but extremely short mini game. A short continuation of the story in the PSP game Birth By Sleep. It's called a Fragmentary Passage,  and at just under 2 hours of gameplay, it's an accurate title. Birth By Sleep is possibly my favorite game in the series, and this continuation has beautiful graphics. The controls are responsive and accurate, the camera view has no large flaws, and the gameplay is fun and engaging. But it's too short to count as a real game. It feels like the first two levels of a game that then skips to a hasty cliffhanger ending. Just as you're really starting to enjoy it, as you are looking forward to the story unfolding, it's over. It also ends unresolved, with a cutscene that ends in a silent "to be continued". The average jrpg? Two hours into one, and you haven't even cracked the surface.  You're still in the beginning of the story, nowhere even near the halfway point, with anywhere from 20 to 40 hours being a full game. Because I enjoyed this so much, I was left feeling cheated. I'd enjoy a remake of the full game, and I'd enjoy this epilogue being expanded into a full game.
The movie Back Cover covers some untold history of the series which is apparently told in an upcoming mobile game.
Overall, unless you're a diehard fan, I don't think that a handheld port plus a two hour epilogue of a game, plus an unplayable movie is worth $60. Just to clarify,  I loved the Birth By Sleep partial game, but on its own, I could see it sold as(because of the short gameplay time), lower priced downloadable content. Unless Dream Drop was your favorite game of all time, I'd suggest waiting until you can buy it pre-owned for $17.99.
It's a nice time filler, but it doesn't stand on it's own. And looking ahead to Kingdom Hearts Remix in March, it's 6 games at $49.99. Why is this 1.5 games for $59.99?
profile.summary: A fragment of a game at full price

profile.description: After the space faring antics of Saints Row IV, many fans asked what we could do next… the answer?  Shoot The Devil in the face.  Play as either Johnny Gat or Kinzie Kensington as you tear apart Hell in a quest to save the leader of the Saints’ soul.  Historical icons, old friends, older enemies, a talking gun, a full length musical number, and a whole lot of other shenanigans all await you in the open world standalone expansion playground that is Saints Row: Gat Out Of Hell.
profile.reviewText:
I bought the digital version of this game only because i wasn't aware that there was a physical copy. I advise getting the physical copy.
I have not finished the game yet, but much of what you may have loved about the last game is carried over here.
You are Kinsie or Johnny and you are in hell, trying to bring back your leader who was kidnapped to marry Satan's unwilling daughter (even as a female leader, it does not change).
The civilians are lost souls that looked like grey skinned zombies. The goal is to disrupt Satan's world enough to get him to come after you- much like the last game but with aliens.
I love the ability to fly. You no longer defy gravity and leap and soar with super-powers, but instead, you have demon wings that have a harder learning curve, but end up being just as useful at getting around once leveled up.
There are a few cons, one being that some of the mini games are downright unfun- and some of them are required to progress. The soul catching game for example.
Overall, partway through, it's fun and humorous, and I'm glad I bought it.
profile.summary: From Aliens to Demons...

profile.description: Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair, the sequel to the highly popular mystery adventure game Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc, will be making its way to the PlayStation Vita in North America and Europe this fall in both retail and digital form. As in the first game, players will take on the role of a high school student as they are thrust into a life-or-death situation, and must use their wits and teamwork to survive. Each student was chosen for a special ability they possess, making them the "ultimate" example of something. Characters in this title are also designed by Rui Komatsuzaki for a unique and darker take on the anime style.
profile.reviewText:
This game is the second in the series, so if you have not played that one, pick that up first or parts of this game especially the ending  will spoil that one.
Like the last one, a group of students from Hope's Peak wake up trapped in a place they cannot escape- this time it's a deserted tropical island. This time they are brought here by a magical pink bunny named Usami who only wants them to live on the island until they bond with each other. Instead, Monokuma shows up and overthrows Usami, changes her appearance, and renames her Monomi. Once again the student's memories of their school life have been taken away. Each retains the memories from before they started school, as well as their Ultimate status- the talent that makes them unique enough to attend Hope's Peak. Once again there is a "traitor". Once again, if they want to escape, they have to kill someone in secret and get away with it. Once someone is killed, an investigation starts, and then there is a trial. Pick the wrong killer or make too many mistakes and it's game over and everyone dies. Except the killer. Guess right and the killer is executed.
This is very heavily a visual novel, so if you hate to read or find that boring, skip this game. It's reading, walking around and talking to other characters, investigating new places on the island as they unlock after every trial, and getting to know other students in your free time. Spend enough time with them to max out your relationship and get a completed crystal. Once a murder occurs, you investigate the crime scene and other locations for clues. Then you head to the court room to solve the crime by pointing out false statements.
What's new? Differences...
*New location. A tropical island instead of the school.
* The addition of a second mascot- a magical girl rabbit who is a good character and not a villain- Usami/Monomi
*Variation from the first person view. When traveling between the attractions on each area of the island, you know run left or right across the screen to your destination.
(Your character looks kind of strange with exaggerated long legs, and at fist I hated this new feature, but by the second case you are use to it.)
*Trial changes allow you to agree with statements instead of just disagreeing/contradicting.
*A new mini game that I personally thought was annoying where you...snowboard on light beams and avoid drops and choose the side with the right answer. This is not fun, but tedious.
*There is also a character that immediately emerges as an insane villain pretty early on and hides things from the group. The first game does a much better job of motivating the group to kill, making them desperate to escape- this one does not offer much motivation at all.
*The ending twist.
Although I really enjoyed this game, and I got used to the new running from point to point, there was one other thing i did not like.  Trying to keep this from being a large spoiler...The ending has a huge twist that makes you like the characters much less, and the one character I really liked ends up dying through no fault of their own. It made the "game" seem very unfair to the created "rules" and almost feels like a betrayal. In a game where there are executions, we want the killers to deserve to be executed, we don't want them executed for an accidental killing, a set-up, and so on. So up until my favorite character dying undeservedly, and then having a huge twist tossed at us, I was really loving this game. That it what prevents me from giving 5 stars.
The old cast also makes an appearance at the end and that's interesting.
profile.summary: Story twist not nearly as good as the first, but some new elements that are alot of fun!

profile.description: Persona 5 is a game about the internal and external conflicts of a group of troubled high school students - the protagonist and a collection of compatriots he meets in the game's story - who live dual lives as Phantom Thieves. They have the typically ordinary day-to-day of a Tokyo high schooler - attending class, after school activities and part-time jobs. But they also undertake fantastical adventures by using otherworldly powers to enter the hearts of people. Their power comes from the Persona, the Jungian concept of the self. The game's heroes realize that society forces people to wear masks to protect their inner vulnerabilities, and by literally ripping off their protective masks and confronting their inner selves do the heroes awaken their inner power, and use it to strive to help those in need. Ultimately, the group of Phantom Thieves seeks to change their day-to-day world to match their perception and see through the masks modern-day society wears.
profile.reviewText:
I did not get my game a few days to a week early from Amazon like some did. Amazon released the majority of copies on release day. Gamestop had a 9 o clock release the night before.
Just a note. This edition was taken off preorder on Amazon and in store at Gamestop as early as 3 weeks before release, but it remained up for pre-order via Gamestop and at least 3 other online stores up until release. The reason it was taken off early was due to the con artists on ebay who were buying them and selling them 10 months before they released. One such con artist bought and sold 160 preorder for almost a $50 profit each. Preorder of these editions need to be restricted to 3 each.
Anyways.
I'll be reviewing the edition, and then the game. I have played every single Person game besides #1, from 2 to Q. That's 8 games. For anyone who enjoys this, I can't express how vital it is to actually play the rest of the series.
Box - the box is huge. It's a laminated shiny flip top with a magnetized cover.
Artbook- the Artbook is a smaller hardcover book featuring art from the game.
Soundtrack -music from the game
Bag - A small canvas zip tote. Kind of flimsy, and I don't recommend heavy use. But it's a really great addition.
Plush - A tiny palm sized Morgana, aka the best part of the game.
That wraps up the review of the collector's edition itself. TBC...
profile.summary: Harder to find due to scalpers buying over 100 copies...

profile.description: Gurumin: A Monstrous Adventure takes you into a vivid fantasy world, with a colorful cast of characters. A strong-willed girl named Parin is sent to live with her grandfather in a small mining town while her parents are off excavating an ancient ruin. No other kids live in town, so Parin is shocked to see a young girl tormented by a stray dog. The girl is actually an invisible monster that only she can see. Parin is invited to Monster Village -- just when Phantoms invade. Only the Legendary Drill can beat back the Phantoms, and Parin sets off to find it.   Mini-games galore
profile.reviewText:
I bought this game via the Playstation store for my PS Vita.
It's an action JRPG/ platformed that is a little bit like a Zelda game. There is no leveling up, just a weapon that can be expanded with new attacks and power-ups.
You play as a little girl gone to a small village to stay with her grandpa. There are no other kids in the village, but she ends up meeting a little girl who is actually a monster. Another little village of monsters lives through a crack in the wall in town, and she becomes friends with them.
One day the village is attacked by enemies and her new friends and some of their belongings are kidnapped. She ends up being able to wield the legendary drill in town and goes on a mission to get her friends - and their stuff- back.
It reminds me a little of the free range of Dark Cloud 2. Being an action RPG, battles are not turn based but in real time.
You learn a range of different attacks and powers ranging from fire to ice, and you also complete challenges- some of which a re completely frustrating and stupid. Take for example climbing the jungle gym in the park, which is trial and error and very careful planning. Also playing a soccer game against a pro player.
The graphics are surprisingly good, and it's adorable. it does get harder the further you progress, and like any platformed, you aim to collect- in this case, all the treasure and enemies in each level for a better level rank.
I wish there were more games like this out there, especially now days. It feels like a throwback to the Ps2 era.
I highly recommend it to fans of platformers, action JRPGs, fans of Zelda, and fans of anything cute!
profile.summary: Fun & Adorable Action JRPG platformer

profile.description: After the horrors have ended at Hope's Peak Academy, society is on the verge of collapse and violent anarchy has engulfed the whole world in despair! Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls is the pre-sequel to the highly popular mystery adventure game Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair. Unlike the first two games, players will take on the role of two heroines, Komaru Naegi and Toko Fukawa, as they are thrust into a despair-ridden Towa City with one goal-escape. Komaru Naegi, little sister to Makoto Naegi, has been imprisoned inside a mysterious apartment for over a year. One day, she is rescued by Byakuya Togami of Future Foundation, but the rescue is derailed by a sudden attack of hundreds of Monokumas. Komaru soon discovers that the city has been taken over by a group of children calling themselves the Warriors of Hope. Their leader, Monaca, declares that the city will be the site of a Children's Paradise, and to accomplish this, all the adults will be exterminated. Komaru teams up with Toko Fukawa to try to survive the rampaging Monokumas, escape the crafty Monokuma Kids, and uncover the secrets of the city.
profile.reviewText:
This game just game out, but I wanted to give it a preliminary review to encourage other adults to pick it up! Yes, adults. The subject matter tackled in this game goes beyond just violence and murder. It goes into some heavy topics not for children.

Danganronpa Another Episode is not another visual novel murder mystery like the first two games. Will playing this before the first one spoil you? Yes. Absolutely. It's a continuation of the story, that takes place in between 1 and 2. There is also a tiny spoiler for the second game, in revealing a bad character.
Kormaru Naegi is the little sister of the first game's protagonist Makoto. This game starts with her trapped in a two bedroom apartment that she is locked in after being kidnapped by unknown assailants a year and a half ago. The animation and voice over as Kormaru tells her story draw you right into the story, and it's very well done. 5 stars right there, instant immersion. You're already invested in what happens next. That's when a Monokuma robot comes to shred down her door, and she runs into the Future Foundation led by one of the last game's survivors. He hands her an electrical megaphone gun type device and tells her to run. She leaves the apartment building to find chaos, mayhem, and murder. The Monobots are killing everyone, and they're led by an insane band of children out to eradicate all adults. Her gun is eventually stolen and downgraded by a guest appearance form a sinister character from game #2, and she must try to escape town, killing Monobots, and leveling up her gun. She is joined by yet another familiar character from the first game, Toko, and together they must survive the murderous robots.
There are differences. Originally this was advertised as a shooter. It is and it's not. It's more like survival horror in an anime environment. The gameplay animation is fully 3D and you have free run around town. There is no immediate comic relief, just bleak and horrific chaos. (Occasionally something like Toko tumbling face first down the stairs will happen, but humor is few and far between.) Monobots murdering everyone with the trademark pink blood everywhere. Some of the cut scenes channel the execution scenes from the previous two games, the almost sketchbook anime style that is dark and nightmarish. The music you know from those games also makes an appearance in these scenes during cut scenes, but during the game it plays an odd soundtrack of faint pop music.
About an hour and a half in, I couldn't find anything to dislike, other than Toko's bizarre and somewhat dirty fantasy scenes, and a hatred of the villains. Chapter 3 and after is when the game loses a star.
SPOILERS
The game really pulls a frustrating move and cheats you out of getting to see the villains killed after you defeat them, which is almost a core element of the series. I, for one, was dying to see the villains executed. These sick kids refer to adults as demons and have made a game of hunting them down and killing those they see adult, as well as ordering their bots to kill everyone else. Lucky adults with tie-in's to the first story are part of a hunting game complete with exploding bracelets, should they actually make it out of town. There are also Monokids; kids in Monokuma masks hanging around playing with dead bodies that they won't let you even fight. Probably because they are kids, which is a weak excuse.
This is where I explain why I took a star off. There are tiny frustrations that are not a big deal. Camera angles in boss fights, and so on. Those will be mentioned in the cons list. The children villains are Insane, and it's frustrating to be cheated out of their executions. Very frustrating. The children are insane for a reason, but this is where it goes too far. (It goes so far into the adult realm that you could not possibly explain this to your kids)
MINOR SPOILERS (just a boss spoiler, but you can skip to the section where it ends to read on)
 One of the girls was a child prostitute/rape victim. Rented to pedophiles. The game is very clear about this and takes it pretty far in Chapter 3, instead of leaving it vague. Not enough to take off a star, but enough to make you a little uncomfortable. How far?  This leads to her building a rape/molestation machine. Yes. You read right. This inclusion is so extremely over the top inappropriate that I had to remove a star. After the rape machine is destroyed, the game tries to cover what they know was going too far with humor. The little girl says it would be inappropriate, but she's a child, so it's okay. She then goes on to say, as her clothes fall off in the fight, that it's a good thing she's 18. Which she clearly isn't. This humor in the form of admitting they went too far doesn't really fix the damage of a rape machine. The other kids suffered some bad abuses as well that contribute to them being soulless monsters, but those don't delve very far into them, not like this one does. And again, it's not a problem that the subject was used, but how they tried to make it...funny?
END SPOILER
Another huge issue I have with the game? Bugs. The biggest issue comes when you spend time figuring out a Monobot maze, execute it perfectly, and the game refuses to recognize this. You kill them all in one shot, celebrate...and then you get the rejection screen. It acts as though you have failed, which lowers your score at the chapter end. You can reload if a save point was near, but if not, you need to decide if a higher score is worth replaying 20 minutes of gameplay, and possibly 20 minute of tedious gameplay. Tedious gameplay is known as spots where you must defend another character from hordes of monobots, sometimes as many as 3 or 4 waves of them, running past laser beams that trigger hordes of bots if tripped...and so on.
Some save points are very reasonably placed, while other times it may seem like it's been eons since you saw one.
Who will like this game? Fans of anime, survival horror, the Danganronpa series in general, and don't mind a game filled with despair and murder. There isn't a ton of the reading dialogue or mystery solving from the last game that those with short attention spans can't sit still for. There is no clues gathering, no courtroom mystery that requires trial and error of figuring out the what the clues mean, in the order they want you to figure them out, and what evidence to present. There is so trial and error shooting truth bullets at words to reject them or select them. NO rhythm mini games to catch the killer in the end. No mini games to collect points. The story unfolds on it's own in front of you. There are small riddles and puzzles.  Figuring to how to kill all of the Monobots in a room at once, and figuring out the password to get through a room, which is a little reminiscent of 999 or Virtue's Last Reward, and those add to the game experience. It's great to see this story continue from another angle, and Kormaru is very much a everyman type protagonist in the way her brother was, and in the style that many JRPGs/visual novels/puzzle games go in order to let the player be able relate to them on some level. There are two new types of Monokuma brought in, and helpful Shirokuma is absolutely adorable.
Overall, I recommend this to everyone who loved the first two games,  anyone who loves unique Japanese games,and anyone who wants to give something new a try. I give it 3.5 stars. Minus one and a half stars for (MINI SPOILER) including a rape machine built by a child rape victim, but still being afraid to have the children villains executed, which is a huge deviation from the story. It feels cheap. Way to go out of your way to offend people one way, but be scared to offend them in another. (END OF MINI SPOILER)
Yes there are some bugs and control issues, but overall the beautifully done graphics and ongoing story are enough to get you through all that.
THIS GAME IS NOT FOR CHILDREN. Contains rape and murder.
Still not sure about the game?
Pros:
-A solid story. It fills the blanks of what happened in between games 1 and 2, and spins off a new story at the same time. It's not just a mindless shooting spree.
-Great design and visuals. The game itself is just as good as the cutscenes, and the opening scene pulls you right in.
-Suspense & mystery. A real story unfolds as you progress.
-Billed as a FPS, it's actually not. It's more survival horror.
It's like playing a story. It's like a visual novel with gameplay beyond point and click and puzzles. Nonstop action to keep those with short attention spans busy.
-Puzzles/riddles are not so challenging that you usually can't figure them out, or find a way around them.
If you can't figure out how to solve the room puzzle of taking out all monobots at once, you can kill them all and still open the sealed door. You will get a lower score however.

CONS:
*Puzzle bugs!! Spend time figuring out a room puzzle to take out all Monobots in a single strike, and sometimes the game refuses to credit you and acts like you failed. If you are 20 minutes from a save point, you have to decide whether to let it go or replay 20 minutes and hope it doesn't glitch again
*The camera angles in boss fights flip so rapidly that you find yourself headed in one direction to get a power-up, and then suddenly it spins, and you're facing the wrong direction. This sucks.
*Some really long load screens in between...
*Sometimes Monobots will run at you and you are forced to run in circles to have enough room to aim and shoot.
*When you need to aim at a specific Monobot -such as an alarmbot, the aim flips instead to the nearest bot thanks to an aim powerup. This can get you killed.
*Sometimes you don't have enough power-ups/bullets to complete a puzzle or enough batteries for Genocide Jack to make it past a tough spot..
*Grades for the levels are based on how many puzzle mazes you complete by solving them instead of brute force, how many hidden villain icons you find, and how many retries you make/how many times you die instead of reloading.
*Save points are put either reasonably close together OR far enough apart that you must run backwards to save- if you can- to avoid having to reload and replay 20 minutes or a particularly difficult part. If the game bugs on a puzzle...
(SPOILER)*The story strays from it's roots where teenage killers & accidental killers are executed & teen victims are brutally murdered, and refuses to execute child killers. You can also kill robot bears, but not murderous kids in robot bear masks who are playing with dead bodies. Execution scenes end with them being carried off. It feels cheap and cowardly. Especially in light of other controversial things not left out. Going into detail about a little girl's history of being pimped out and raped which turns her into a sort of rapist herself is okay apparently. There are jokes made about how inappropriate it would be for a video game.
*The molestation/rape machine.
*Kormaru's change in attitude and lack of common sense in Chapter 4, in order to keep the story going. Let me tell you, I would be gone. To get help and bring help back, but GONE.
profile.summary: ADULT game series Danganronpa's spin-off is different, but just as much fun! Beware of some bugs & extreme ADULT content.

profile.description: A chilling film in the style of THE RING, and THE GRUDGE. When a group of teens starts receiving a "One Missed Call" display on their cell phone screens, they hear terrifying voice messages documenting their very own anguished death throes with the exact
profile.reviewText:
The original Japanese title for this movie is "Chakushin Ari" It's the first movie in a trilogy that was hugely popular in Japan. Thee is also a T.V series DVD based on just the first movie's events with different actors, some different characters, same story. Despite drawing comparisons to The Ring and ORIGINAL Ringu, the only thing they have in common is: a vengeful ghost and the use of cellphones. These types of stories are both common and popular in Japan in the same way that slasher flicks once were here and Saw/Hostel type of films currently are here as of the end of 2007. The best thing about this film is the terrifying ringtone that is the theme. The plot unfolds as people start receiving phone calls from their own cell phone numbers from a time and date in the future - about a week or so.. When you answer, you hear the last few seconds of your life. If you don't answer, you will get a voicemail or photo. Changing your number doesn't work, and if you throw away the phone, it mysteriously comes back anyways.
A US remake has a January 2008 release date. It is unknown as of now whether it will shame this movie like The Ring did with Ringu, but the previews make it seem likely. See the original version now!
profile.summary: THE ORIGINAL must see

profile.description: Relive the complete first season of ABC's ONCE UPON A TIME, the hit series that boasts unforgettable characters and a tangled web of romance, action and enchantment. Immerse yourself in the magic and mystery of Storybrooke -- a sleep little town where every fairytale character you've ever known is frozen in time and trapped between two worlds, victims of an evil curse. On her 28th birthday, Emma Swan (Jennifer Morrison) meets Henry (Jared Gilmore), the son she gave up for adoption 10 years ago. Henry believes Emma is the daughter of Snow White (Ginnifer Goodwin) and Prince Charming (Josh Dallas), prophesied to break a powerful curse. Unconvinced, Emma returns Henry to Storybrooke, where she encounters the enigmatic Mr. Gold (Robert Carlyle) and clashes with mayor Regina Mills (Lana Parrilla) -- the boy's adoptive mother -- who Henry insists is none other than the Evil Queen! Start your epic collection with all 22 captivating episodes, including never-before-seen bonus features, in this spectacular 5-disc boxed set.
profile.reviewText:
You know that thing they do in soap operas where things drag on for episode after episode and although the audience knows exactly what's going on, the characters don't seem to be able to figure anything out? Time after time, they almost figure something out or they get a tiny piece of the puzzle...and something thwarts them at the last second? You watch the villains hatch and carry out scheme after scheme on the clueless victims, or sometimes the "good" characters bully the "villains" into becoming what they are. You just want the story to progress instead of almost progressing over and over? You start to feel almost angry that the "heroes" are so clueless or frustrated that they can't catch a break. You keep watching because you really want to see how interesting and dramatic it gets when everything is out in the open...but it doesn't happen...That's how this series gets in Season 1.
I started off really liking this. Until I just got frustrated.
It's about a woman, a bounty hunter who gets tracked down by the kid she gave up for adoption. He takes her back to a town cursed by an evil queen where fairy tale characters from another world have lost their memories and are living out new lives. It's addictive and suspenseful. Fairytales are re-spun and re-told. Some good, some not.. Snow White and her Prince have a very different version of the story here, that is interesting and unique. Snow White is a thief and a bandit that tries to rob the prince and then...but in the cursed world, the Prince (without his memory) is a complete tool. He lies to Snow White and breaks her heart over and over, dating two women at once. The main character refuses to believe in the curse no matter how much proof she gets. Beauty and the Beast is turned into a farce with Belle falling in love with old evil man Rumplestillskin. The episodes story switches between the cursed town in present time, and telling background stories from the past fairy tail land to introduce new characters and reveal more of the background on them. Which is very well calculated and enjoyable to watch.
However...
Time and time again both villain characters control every aspect of things so that just when you think the truth is coming out...something happens and it's back to everyone being in the dark and clueless. It happens in the present time and in the fairy tale past and it gets old fast. Example...after Snow is about to go to the Prince(in fairy tale past), the king convinces her to lie to save his life and walk away. After several more JUST misses, it is beyond annoying. It is building a story about how they have overcome so much to be together, but after it keeps happening over and over, it stops being believable. AGAIN? Really?
FORTUNATELY I was able to skip from episode 8 or so to reading episode summaries and then straight to the season finale where the truth is revealed. Now that the truth is out I can watch season 2, but the middle episodes just drag on and make you want to bang your head against a wall in frustration! Here is hoping they don't make the same mistake twice! Just as the pay-off comes...no, sorry guys back to the beginning and 3 more episodes going in circles until they might almost figure out a clue to go forwards.
If you dislike soap operas, and you like the show and the story, try the same route I did, but maybe a little sooner. Had I done that, I might not be trying to get over a huge dislike for the Prince who they made into a cheater and liar, and then magically morphed him into a hero again in the end. But if these characters are part their fairy tale selves and part the new modern cursed versions with no memories...it still makes the Prince a tool afterwards.

UPDATE: I really liked Season 2. Struggle through and keep watching!
profile.summary: A little too "soap opera" for me.
