profile.description: Ten people, strangers to each other are invited to a lavish estate on a remote island. Through a recording their mysterious host accuses each of his 'guests' of murder and proceeds to exact 'justice'. The tension mounts as, one-by-one, the number of people are reduced through the ingenious plotting of the unseen killer. Prepare to play the 11th character in the video game based on the best-selling murder mystery of all time!
profile.reviewText:
This is a GREAT game! We started the game Monday night and finished it last night (Wednesday). It's a hard game to stop playing and I loved the clever mysteries within the story. Tha narration is also well done ,creepy, and intriguing. There is absolutely NO need fo a strategy guide or a walkthrough if you have enough intelligence and/or patience for puzzles. Clues are all over the house for codes & you can't get stuck if you talk to everyone and explore all areas. Your actions trigger the next actions. Search an area, talk to everyone, then search again. Easy enough. The only point we got stuck at was the second to last chapter when we couldn't find one of the guests. 10 minutes later we talked to everyone in a different order and were feeling stupid for our oversight.
I DO NOT recommend this game for inexperienced, casual, or impatient gamers however! Like Silent Hill & Resident Evil, advancing depends on figuring out how to put items together, where to use them, and who to talk to -but on an easier scale puzzle-wise. The controls are easy to use with the Wii remote and includes things like turning doorknobs and digging with a shovel, which adds to the interactive intrigue of the game.
It is also made by The Adventure Company who are known for their excellent puzzle/mystery games. If you can't sit still for a few hours to read a book, you would probably be better off playing Super Smash Bros or something similar. Also, it is impossible to die playing this game so you can really enjoy the story unraveling. To those who love only survival horror with constant enemies and battling crazy zombie/demons, you may be bored. I love many survival horror games but find an overdose of enemies around every corner to be distracting...
A final warning to people familiar with the book -the ending has been changed to suit a video game and to insert a playable character, but at the end you are treated to the end of the original story as a bonus in the form of a voice-over letter.
I can't wait to get the next 2 games!!
profile.summary: Clever, Underrated, and Fun!

profile.description: The finest odor-fighting litter box on the planet. Turn it on, odor’s gone! The Odor Grabber Air-Cleaning Litter Box from Bionaire automatically removes embarrassing and unwanted litter box odors. It continuously eliminates odors in the litter box while sending fresh, odor-free air into the room. A built-in electronic air purifier with advanced filtration quietly circulates the air without disturbing the cat. A pre-filter also removes harmful litter dust, dander and fur flowing through the filter. Activated Carbon and Zeolite target odors directly from the litter box and reduces ammonia odors better then the tested competitors. Does not emit ozone-producing ions. Electronic LED count-down indicator lights and reset button simplify filter replacement. Roll-top lid reduces scatter and rolls up for simplified cleaning. Contoured scoop eases scooping throughout the corners and an integrated holster permits litter to fall back into pan. Includes 12-ft power cord and 2 sets of filters. Superior, contemporary style that fits all areas of the home. Patent pending.
profile.reviewText:
I bought one of these on sale and while it didn't make any difference in the smell, the cats loved the design. When it broke- the motor just DIED, I ordered 2 more directly from the company because the cats really liked them and the litter STAYED in the box for once as the plastic around it keeps litter from flying out when they throw it around... Kind of how those tacky clear boards at ice skating rinks keep the hockey pucks in...
Those new ones lasted a few months and then also broke. This time both cords just wouldn't connect right and thus the filter system didn't work.  The cats still loved them for the design. I e-mailed the company to complain, and they said they would replace them. I only got one, e-mailed them again, and got the second one.  It's been about a month and they are still functioning, but again, no improvement on the smell. I'd say they should just manufacture these @ $25 each and forget the "odor grabbing" feature since it doesn't work. YOu also have to order filters to put in the boxes, and that is more expense for something that just doesn't work.
profile.summary: Interesting design, but no "odor grabbing". Just like a regular litter box!

profile.description: Get your floors clean deep down with the Eureka AirSpeed Bagless Upright Vacuum, AS2011A model. This vacuum is engineered to move more air and remove more dirt than comparable machines, so your home can get cleaner faster. The on-board upholstery turbo nozzle even allows for deep cleaning on stairs and upholstered furniture, while the on-board crevice tool and dusting brush make cleaning odds and ends easier. The Eureka Airspeed Bagless Upright Vacuum also has a lightweight design that moves easily with you from room to room with less strain than heavier models. Even better, this Eureka Airspeed Vacuum Cleaner requires no bags, so you can wash the filter and container again and again, without the need for replacements.
profile.reviewText:
My biggest concern with vacuum reviews is that they usually come from people that use them once or twice, or maybe for a week, and then rush to write a glowing review. The majority of vacuums are decent in that timeframe. That's why many boxes will claim "never loses suction". I think that for things like this, the reviewer should be required to use it for at least 4-5 months, if not longer before reviewing.
I shudder to read these reviews from people who have no clue on the quality of the vacuum. They review it and then when it fails, they return it or throw it away, and forget about it.
This is my SECOND AirSpeed. The first one was the pink model that also came in yellow. Amazon did not have the pink listed so I reviewed the yellow. It was sold at Walmart for something like $38.
I got it home and it felt like a flimsy kid's toy vacuum, sounded like a lawnmower, but had amazing suction! It even pulled itself along which was scary at first, but really nice.
Until one day, a month and a half or so later...it just stopped picking up every tiny fiber, and slowly got worse.
I returned it and was going to try a new one, as maybe it was just defective, but they were not sold there anymore. Discontinued.
Instead there was a $59 version that they said was the exact same thing but in a different color, with a longer cord, and possibly slightly more powerful. They let it go as an even exchange.
I got it home, and it was just a tiny bit more sturdy than the last one, but not by much. It's a little bigger, and the cord is long enough that it doesn't pull itself out every few minutes. it still sounds like a lawnmower, but it still had that excellent pull and excellent suction. In under a minute, my 8X10 rug and 5 feet of kitchen was spotless.
Cut to about 2 months later. I was using it and it started turning itself off and on. I got a video of it doing it once, then it stopped. Next time I used it, it was fine.
Last night, I turned it on and started vacuuming my tiny rug. That's when I noticed that it was dragging what looked like dust bunnies across the rug into giant caterpillar shapes. I went over them again and again with no luck. As I got to the edge of the rug, the edge became covered in these dust-pillars. As I dragged the vacuum of the rug, it deposited dust smears all over the floor bordering the carpet edge. Each time i went over it, it left it there or picked it up and deposited it behind it. I took it into the kitchen on the floor setting and little pieces of dirt, etc I could hear being picked up, but some of that was deposited behind it.
Now there are these giant smears of dust,grime,dirt, and hair on the edges of my rug and on the edge where the floor meets rug. Whisps are on the floor, and upon running my shoe over the rug, those whisps are BURIED IN MY RUG all over!
I have always been very gentle with this flimsy vacuum for fear of breaking it. I vacuum my tiny kitchen twice a week at most, and a 6X8 rug twice a week at most. I run it over the bathroom and bedroom and hallway once a month or less and just pick up dust bunnies and hair. This is not heavy use. I always empty it before it's full, and I check to make sure my hair is not stuck in the bottom. Often dust would be stuck up in the part that you can't reach and would need to be pulled out with a stick or such. I always tapped it lightly after dumping to get out the dust and grime.
This vacuum is going back if they will still take it, as I believe it is within 90 day return period, but i may have waited before opening it, worried about getting another lemon.
As my second AirSpeed and third Eureka (Oh Pet that has a design flaw in a filter that gets so clogged it just shuts off) that stopped functioning, I am moving on.
profile.summary: Stops working after a month or two. Second Airspeed that was amazing to start, then useless.

profile.description: The ReTrak retractable Micro USB cables are the perfect way to connect to any USB Micro device. The retractable cable is great for travel yet easily expands to the desired length without the clutter of unwanted cable. It has 3.2' total expanded length and a transfer data rate at up to 480 Mbps/sec.
profile.reviewText:
Terrible terrible product. It extends to a certain length and then it's supposed to stay that way until you need it to retract. This is apparently done by stretching it taut which sets it, then tapping it when you want it to retract. When you tap it, it whips the ends back in.
Unfortunately, many times it does this on it's own, yanking the charger out of the phone completely. If you place it down on the table and it thinks you are tapping it, and rips the charger out the phone. If you nudge it slightly with your arm, or even sit down next to it, it can apparently mistake this for you tapping it and then rip the charger out of the phone. So you can't put it down, nudge it, sit next to it, or at times, even look at it without it retracting out of nowhere. Ripping the charger end out of your phone not only stops it from charging, but is also bad for the connection on your plug. It doesn't always rip the charger out however. Sometimes it retracts back and instead drags your phone right off the couch or coffee table. Right onto the floor. Which could break it.
And that's not all. The cord is on a circular pulley, and it tangles regularly, refusing to retract at all. Which leaves you with an ordinary charger.
Maybe I got a defective one?
The idea here is great, but it is so poorly made that I would not recommend this to anyone!
It is also a dollar less at Half Price Books.
AVOID!
profile.summary: Retracts by itself ripping the cord out of the phone OR dragging the phone to the floor. Also tangles. AVOID!

profile.description: Proven to effectively treat behavior problems in dogs and cats that are caused by stress, anxiety and phobias, such as separation anxiety, travel, new environments and social interaction. Provides superior, longer-lasting delivery of pheromones than any other pheromone product and goes where the animal goes to provide round-the-clock pheromone release. This is a safe and effective first-line treatment that often eliminates the need for powerful prescription medicines. Can be used on dogs and cats of all breeds and ages and without side effects.
profile.reviewText:
The clinic where I work sells these for $16 or $17 and we don't get a discount on products, so I ordered from here.
The cat I ordered it for is very shy and nervous about everything in the world. He may actually think the sky is falling. He was a 6 month old feral kitten that I decided would be very unhappy living in a cage at a local rescue for the rest of his life. Luckily no SPCA or "humane" society got their hands on him or he wouldn't even be here...
He's pretty happy when left to himself sleeping on the bed, but everything else scares him including people and noises and movement. It took me a few days to catch him and get it on him, but he has had it on for over two weeks with no change in his attitude or behavior at all. He is still terrified of his own shadow and constantly hiding except for when he is alone on the bed purring happily by himself or sporadically when he thinks whatever imagined danger in the world isn't after him... I don't know if maybe I got a defective collar, or if just doesn't work on all cats, or on tough cases. I see one of the reviews says that the collar they got from their vet worked and the one they got from a seller on Amazon did not. The collar itself is a pretty purple color and made of a rubbery plastic. It is covered in flakes of powder that fall off when you open the package and by the time it gets on the cat, it is just a film of powder as the big pieces crack and fall apart or disintegrate into the air. He is an expert at getting off all his safety collars in the past, but this is still on him.
Again, I am not sure if this is a defective collar or old collar, or just a product that does not work.
I decided to try this brand instead of Feliway because i have tried Feliway diffusers in the past and those did nothing for my shy cats either; one non-shy cat even peed on it.
profile.summary: Didn't do a single thing...

top_5.description: A multimedia messaging powerhouse! The LG enV Touch has a bright, external 3" touchscreen and a full-size QWERTY keyboard. Revolutionary Dolby mobile sound brings a deep, rich, engaging listening experience. Plus, a 3.2-megapixel camera offers built-in flash, video, and much more. Touch it and believe!
top_5.reviewText:
I have had TWO of these die. Also, LG has horrible customer service.
The first one I had didn't even last a year. After a few months, it started freezing, randomly shutting off, the screen would get stuck on rainbow-colored static...Then it got worse and just shut down. I took it to a local Verizon where they told me it was over-loaded and dying, and talked to me like I was a very slow child. They said there was nothing they could do and they couldn't get my information off. They told me to take it home and transfer all my info to the card. On the way home it died. I called the LG rep and he told me they had no idea what they were talking about and that what they said was not possible. I went to a different Verizon and they said that they COULD have gotten my information out (which i knew), but it was too late now. I was still under warranty, so they ordered me a refurbished phone- they said I could NOT get a different kind of phone, just the exact same one. Unless I wanted to pay full price, of course. I contacted LG, and they said that while they COULD fix it and get all of my information out of the phone after they fixed it, they wouldn't. They would instead fix it, wipe the information clean,and sell it to someone else. And give me someone else's refurbished phone.  Yes, they admitted all of that.  I lost ALL my information and got the refurbished phone from Verizon.
Cut to another few months later. No warranty and SURPRISE! It starts again. Freezing, shutting off, getting stuck...
Then one day the touch screen just stopped working. I took it to yet another Verizon. This guy had no idea what was wrong and said I would have to call the national line if I had other questions about what was actually wrong with it. He said that the phone was clearly going to die, there was no way to fix it, and I would have to wait 4 months until my contract was up for renewal to get a working phone. 2 hours later...it unfroze and the touch screen starting working again. For the next 4 months, the phone continued to sporadically lose all my photos except 8, then magically find them minutes later, change my background photos, freeze randomly, static, shut off...then...it died.
Let me just say that I will NEVER EVER get another LG phone. I will never let any friends or family get one either.

Aside from the problems I had with the phone being a complete POS, when it was working, I was constantly having my purse, my pockets, even my arms (when I was carrying a bunch of bags,etc) dial random numbers in my phonebook.
Why didn't I lock it you ask? The lock function,if you want to call it that, doesn't actually "lock" the phone and require a password to get back in. I'm not quite sure what the actual function is.
The touch screen is impossible to use to text; even with my tiny little girly fingers, the screen would constantly choose the wrong letter or number. The voice dial is just as bad, if not worse. You have to scream at the phone, sometimes more than 5 or 6 times and still nothing- or worse- it dials the wrong person.

On to the camera-
Don't bother taking photos unless it's something LESS than a 1/2 foot away- there is no zoom. Even my cheap Motorola Razr had zoom. You can't take photos from across the room and crop them later- it will make them blurry.
Don't bother taking photos unless you are in broad daylight with no shadows. Indoors, you better be directly under light- but not in the glare. 9/10 times the flash goes off, you get a completely white screen. Without the flash, you get a black screen.
I can't tell you how many times I missed something, or how many times I stood somewhere trying 8 or 9 times to get a photo to be visible. I don't know about you, but I'm embarrassed asking someone to hold still for 8-9 re-takes, and admitting I still didn't get it.
I may make it my mission in life to make sure no one I meet ever buys this POS- or anything LG!
top_5.summary: WORST...PHONE...EVER!! Horrible camera, bad customer service...

I have this figure, and I recommend it... if you can get it for a good price. Over $30 is not a good price. I pre-ordered mine online and it was only about $15. Unfortunately, many people tend to order  as many extras as they can and then flip them for double...or more.

top_5.description: BOOKS
top_5.reviewText:
Initially, I almost stopped reading in Chapter 7 once the family corruption was revealed. Her father is a politician and her sister is a typical rich brat. She was sent away at a young age when she showed witch powers and then she changed her name and the family has spent time and money into hiding the relation...Not much detail is given besides that, but it made me a great deal less sympathetic to her. The reason i almost stopped reading is that her father is politically active in a group AGAINST supernaturals, yet this group uses magic and her sister is secretly a witch too. Too much soap opera style drama in the background overshadowing the actual story is something I am not a fan of.
Other than the "heroine" being the typical supernatural heroine with an over-inflated attitude that everyone else finds to be spunky, I didn't dislike her. However, she doesn't seem to know what she wants and shows no backbone whatsoever when it comes to men. This leads to my biggest issue with the book. Right in the middle is a tedious and BORING scene of graphic bookporn that I could have done without that seems to span an endless number of pages. I don't know why every author of supernatural books feels compelled to throw that in at some point, no matter if it fits or not, but I am getting very tired of it. If I want something trashy, I know where to find the romance section in the library or bookstore. I don't like it being snuck into books.
The last complaint is a spoiler I will not ruin. But in the end of the story, like in seemingly every supernatural story, the heroine is found to be something no one knew she was- including herself, and to have more powers than anyone thought that suddenly make the average character all the more important to everyone else.
I may pick up the next one at the library if I can't find anything better to read...and in today's world of supernatural fiction it isn't looking good...
top_5.summary: Undecided...but your typical supernatural story...

top_5.description: TALES OF XILLIA 2 IS SET A YEAR AFTER TALES OF XILLIA, AND REVOLVES AROUND LUDGER KRESNIK, A RUN-OF-THE-MILL MAN WHO LIV ES WITH HIS BROTHER AND CAT, AND ELLE MARTA, A YOUNG AND DEPEND ABLE GIRL WHO LUDGER MEETS BY CHANCE. THROUGHOUT THE GAME THE PL AYER WILL HAVE TO MAKE DECISIONS FOR LUDGER THAT WILL CAUSE THE
top_5.reviewText:
I got this for $19.99 on Black Friday, and I really really WANT to like it...
I loved Tales of Hearts. I really liked Tales of Graces. I liked Tales of Xillia. I am hoping for Tales of Innocence and planning to get Tales of Zesteria.
I was a little hesitant to play a continuation, a part 2, and thought at first that it may be a different story labeled as 2, the way Americans sometimes label series...and that is actually kind of the case. But I don't like it as a Tales game. It's kind of the way some people feel about Silent Hill. They love the ones Team Silent worked on with the Japanese feel of building dread, and they WOULD like the new Americanized ones better if they were a completely different series in name. That's how this feels.
A new protagonist, Lutger, and instead of being a kind of bland everyman, or over-noble and annoying (TOH,TOG), he is silent and somewhat brooding.
The younger brother of a very successful sibling named Julius, he recently failed his test of powers, and instead of starting a promising career, if off to his first day working in the cafeteria. He boards a train and everything falls apart when rogue soldiers take it hostage. This is where he meets Jude from TOX and they pick up a bratty little girl to the party. It all comes to a head when the man behind it is revealed to be a glowing creature that looks and talks just like brother Julius. He wakes up in debt to a shady and sleazy young doctor who saved the trio and expects Lutger to pay off the debts of all 3 of them. Which is ridiculous and makes no sense why he should shoulder the debt. He sets off on a journey to get back home, find out what happened to Julius, and repay the debt.
Instead of the usual sword era with green countrysides, there are modern towns and cell phones. The feel is completely different, which is why I say it does not feel like a Tales game. The protagonist is silent, but during certain parts of gameplay, cut-scenes, two choices pop up. Some are timed choices. You pick the trigger button that corresponds with the choice on the left or right. Many of them are dialogue choices that determine how close you are to your companions, etc. Choose to make your special tomato omelet OR  make the bratty little girl something without tomatoes. I think this is put in place to make the game feel more modern and more interactive, and I don't dislike it. I don't dislike the very different modern and gritty look to the towns either. What I do dislike, is the always changing battle system, and the always changing level up powers method. In every game it changes. Xillia added more than just basic sword and magic attacks, it adding partnering. This adds more partnering but it doesn't feel the same.
The system for leveling up magic and power was perfect in TOH and I would be happy with that method for all the games. Even TOX had a web that was not as user friendly, but not such a pain. This system is more complicated and not fun. What IS the same as TOX is the fields. No changes. In between chasing story events, you can choose missions in town such as gathering supplies or defeating enemies.
Major gripes?
The map. The icons are so teeny tiny that you can't read them anyways even with the map open to full view. There is. No. Zoom. It doesn't always tell you what is where, so memorize it over time, or go with trial and error. The power up grid. No wheels, no webs, but instead a new web.. evolution...
The debt repayment stalker. You owe a ton of money. It restricts movement. First you can't take the train, then you can't cross certain borders. But once you earn a larger amount of money from battles, fields, and missions, you cannot take more than 6 steps without being assaulted by the pop up reminder that you owe money. How annoying is it? It's the face and voice of the annoying way too happy debt collector girl popping up on your screen in the form of some kind of futuristic video surveillance. Pay us. Or I will never go away. You can pay her 50 a time out of spite for her annoyance, but paying her more will get her to go away.
Overall, I find myself unable to read a map I can't see, the background feels foreign and too modern for Tales, the power ups system is annoying, and the connective battle elects I didn't love in TOX are amplified here.
I want TOH's battle, Artes, power ups, villages, field travel, maps, town identification on maps...and applied to future games. It's suppose to be smoother, not harder. I would like this better if it had been given a different name and been named as a spin-off. I will finish the game one day, but right now there are too many other games out there.
top_5.summary: I WANT to like it...A Dark & Gritty Modern Tale That Doesn't Feel Like "Tales"

top_5.description: Ice Age 2: The Meltdown takes you back in time for a great adventure! The world is melting and your Ice Age pals need help escaping from the rising waters. Swim, splash, scamper and scurry through all the action and adventure from the new Ice Age 2 movie and unearth fun, laughter and surprises along the way!
top_5.reviewText: You get to BE Scrat! Now if you're a huge Scrat fan like I am, this should be enough for you... I rented this also worried that it would be another kid's game with no real gameplay. I saw on the back that Scrat is a playable character- and it turns out that aside from a Sid mini-game, Scrat is THE character you play as through the whole game!!  I think the review above pretty much covers all the game details, but I have to agree that it's fun, not just for kids - you have to figure things out. There's the collecting element for Spyro fans. Back to Scrat. He has a range of little attacks and motions that you can prance around doing forever! Kicks, sniffing, jumping. I was sad when the game came to an end, because I would have loved to keep running through levels as Scrat, defeating animals, swimming, squeezing through trees, playing games like bowling and playing dead, and just being adorable!
top_5.summary: BE Scrat! Must have for Scrat-fans..

profile.description: TP-Link ANT2405C 2.4GHz 5dBi Indoor Desktop Omni-directional Antenna
profile.reviewText:
I had a Graupner MX20 laying around that I haven't used in a few years (Great Radio, when it was new and still to this day..  stopped using due to having a Futaba 18MZ, Graupner MZ24 and MC32) So I threw them MX20 in a FPV Hexa setup and flew to fail safe/RTL kicked in.. I did the test in 4 different areas and each area I went straight North, South, East and West so 4 different areas and 4 different paths in each area.. with the stock antenna I got a best of 2.6 kilometers and a worst of 1.3 kilometers (the 1.3k was in a heavy WiFi environment so that's dang good) with an average of 1.92K then I came home installed this 8dbi antenna with a Pci to Rp-sma adapter drilling out a spot close to the stock antenna at install the adaptor.. the next day was nearly identical weather so that had no effect on the test... With the new antenna installed I did the same 4 tests at the same time of day in each location and the results are amazing. My best was now 4.1 kilometers my worst in the heavy WiFi area was 3.2K with an Average of 3.7 kilometers... Not only a huge range boost BUT my signal was FAR stronger then before in the middle of those ranges... What I mean is normally when I would get out about a mile my signal would be around 15 to 25% but now at a Mile my signal is 85 to 90%... The packet error rate is 1/100th or what it is with the stock antenna at 1 mile (1.6 kilometers) out.. my signal would stay nearly 80% or higher until the last 15 to 20% of the max range, dropping off much quicker over the last 20% of the max range then it does in the first 80% of it.. these ranges are with a 6 channel signal antenna receiver.. in most cases a duel diversity receiver doesn't increase range a lot but I believe in this case it would add about 30 to 40% more range with this antenna mod do to signal being blocked by items on the quad shadowing the signal that I can't get around with a single antenna receiver. Going much more then 8dbi on a 100mw transmitter won't gain you much more other then bulk.. if you want to increase to a even higher dbi antenna then you will need a signal booster to really gain the max from the upgrade. The over all huge range gain to me is not the best part.. the massively increased signal density and hugely lowered packet loss at 80% of the max range is the part I care mostly about... It will allow you to safely fly in highly contested WiFi areas safely.. you will have much lower chances of having signal block out when flying around powerful WiFi signals even at VERY long ranges. Penetration through trees also is hugely increased...

That's very important to us racing FPV quad guys....I had a friend walk the quad in the woods swapping the pci back to the stock antenna and when I got to 20% rssi I stopped him, he was about 140 meters back in some fairly thick trees and under growth, I swapped the pci back to this antenna and was at 95% rssi... He started walking again and when we was about 1.2k back in the woods and I still had 60 to 75% rssi it was pointless to go any more... Your fpv system would not reliably get 1/4 that distance in that thick of mother nature. Would I drill a hole on my new high dollar units to install this antenna NO unless the stock antennas wasn't giving me what I needed reliably however they do... But now I have a med long range 2.4 system that I will use... However if you use a module based 2.4 system then this is 110% a must upgrade that cost hardly nothing AND will GREATLY improve the performance of your systems range and reliability and it's as easy as unscrewing one antenna and installing this antenna as most modules use a rp-sma antenna connection. If size is a concern then going to a quality 5dbi antenna will not to much larger then the stock antenna but will provide about 50% increased signal density and about 40% increased range over the stock 2.5 or 3dbi unit in/on your transmitter... If you have a Flysky I6 radio then get two 5dbi antennas (VERY IMPORTANT NOTE, ONLY USE A HIGH QUALITY ANTENNA NOT CHEAP CRAP UNITS) I have now done 3 I6 radios for friends, it's a cheap 50 to 60 USD radio that works well for newbis or just guys that are on a tight budget... You will need two 4 to 6 inch PCI to rp-sma connectors and two 5 to 8dbi TP link or other HIGH QUALITY 2.4ghz antennas I would go with 5dbi just for the fact of size as it needs two.. you then drill out two holes for the rp-sma connectors on top the radio case (use the front half it's wider and easier to mount the jack) pop off the two pci connectors to the stock antennas you can leave them in its fine, then after you have mounted the sma in the radio pop on the two pci clips and screw the radio back together... Screw on the two antennas (do NOT power on the radio without the antennas installed you will cook your 2.4ghz transceiver) and power on the radio.... Your range with the normal 6ch park flyer receiver will be in the 1.5 mile range vs stock it will be about 600 to 700 meters before the packet loss is so high you are getting glitches and signal drop out... With the full range 6ch or 10ch receiver we tested it out to over 4 miles and stopped and the packet loss was fair and safe at 4 miles I would say 5 to 5.5 miles vs stock 1.4 miles would be the max range in a clean 2.4ghz area or 3 to 3.5 miles in a heavy 2.4ghz area with FAR LESS packet loss then stock... So for less then 70 bucks with the cable and antenna cost added they now have radios that they can safely fly their fpv multirotors very long range on a safe and easy to use 2.4ghz system with very very good reliability and very very good range... Sorry for the long post just trying to help out anyone looking to greatly increase the range and signal density of their 2.4ghz radio system for not much money and easy to do... Well this is how to do it...
profile.summary: Great 2.4ghz radio control range booster! For R/C plane

profile.description: Crossman Corporation is an American designer, manufacturer and supplier of products for the shooting sports. The company has a long-standing presence in air gun design and a tradition of producing pellet and BB air rifles and pistols.
profile.reviewText: I mainly shoot High end PCP and high end Springers with a few high end Co2 and duel fuel guns in there as well. H&N and JSB are my main stay in pellets but Crosman Brown box .177 and .22s dome/field target pellets have a place in some of my guns to. Now here's where the review for this pellet comes in, in 95% of my high end pcp and springers these pellets will shoot decently in BUT when you compare groups with these vs high end pellets the difference is night and day in most guns BUT... I have a Gamo Bull whisper bone collector that I got in a trade that was new (i HATE gamo guns, plain and simple they are trash unless they are the BSA built Gamos then they are nice guns) so I had no use for the BC but wasn't gonna waste my time to try and sell it SO I found a 65lb gas strut that fit and had a friend that owns a moulding shop custom mould me some piston seals and some high pressure breach seals that would stand up to the pressure. That would fit perfectly and handle the 65lb strut that was doubling the chamber pressure.. I could not find a pellet (I went through roughly 70 different pellet brands, makes and weights with this gun) that would group within 4 inches at 15 yards so another words really horrible accuracy.. I knew part of it was because the gun was massively over powered lol and the other part was it was a gamo and that says it's pretty much craps! Then I came across a few tins of these that I had in a different pellet case and tried them.. I was shocked, number one this pellet is way to light for that much horse power but it was shooting .30 inch center to center 5 shot groups at 25 yards with these and doing it over and over and over some more.  It is shooting 1360fps average at 32.4ftlbs of energy.. that's WAY AND I MEAN WAY to fast for accuracy but some how and some way these are very very accurate at insane speeds and stupid amount of energy for a break barrel .177, heck powerful .177 pcp guns don't break 35ftlbs very often.  I can say how these pellets stand up to that much velocity but they do it in spades and imho rarely shoot really good in any highly accurate gun, they shoot decently in a lot of guns but rarely even close to what the gun is capable of.  On high speed scope cam video I can see they start De-stabilizing after about 60 yards but fly very well until they start to cork screw but they don't do it until they are about 25 yards past falling sub-sonic as where most super sonic pellets start tumbling when they cross over from super to sub sonic. This gun/pellet combo is capable of 3/4 inch groups at 50 yards however that opens to 8 inchs at 65 yards lol, 3/4 inch groups at 50 yards are nothing to write home about in pcp or high end spring guns BUT in a 32ftlb gamo that's massively over powered it is something to write home about... Heck it's something to write you guys on Amazon about lol. The shots are loud, really .22lr loud or very close to it, as it's totally in the super sonic range not just right there close to it.. and this is a 7.99 grain pellet that's way super sonic and not a 4 grain pellet thats as good for your gun as dry firing and the super hard alloy they are made from are really hard on barrels. The 65# gas ram was 47.99 the seals 15 bucks and you have a 32ftlb .177 break barrel lol that's a monster of epic proportion.. it shoots so smooth with the hard custom seals but a lot of recoil but it's not the jump all over the place normal springer recoil rather a hard solid "thud" and a super sonic crack. The gun shoots amazingly well for what it Is.. if it shot H&N baracuda series pellets as accurate as it does these it would be sub sonic and likely 40ftlbs of energy, it just doesn't shoot them accurate. When I find a heavy pellet it shoots well this thing will be a 150 yard coke can capable gun.
profile.summary: Decent pellet in a lot of guns but rarely a highly accurate pellet

profile.description: 1x charging cable
profile.reviewText: To the people who don't understand how this works. If you have a 600 mah charger and charge one 600 mah  pack it will take an hour for a fully depleted battery (do not run lipos below 20% remaining IE, 1000 mah pack run 800 or less mah out of it 50 mah pack run 400 mah out of it ect ect.) Now if you connect 5 600 mah packs to a 600 mah charger it will take 5 hours to charge. Now if you have a charger that has adjustable rate charging you would set the charger for 1c charge rate... meaning if you are charging 5x 500 mah packs you would charge at 2.5A and charge all batteries in 1 hour if you charged 5x 200 mah packs you would charge at 1A for 1C charge rate.. 5x 1000 mah packs you would charge at 5A to charge at 1C meaning you would complete all 5 packs right at 1 hour of charging. Good packs have no problem being charged at 1/10th there C rating meaning a 15C discharge rated pack can handle a a 1.5c charge rate a 20C pack can handle safely 2C charge rate 30 discharge rated pack can charge at 3C ect. I have been in the hobby over 20 years and have flew lipos since they first came out. 1c charge rate is not a rule it is safe and will make packs last the longest but charging at or below 1/10th the discharge rating is very safe and packs will last plenty long. I use a 5x jst jumper to charge 1s 150 mah packs for micro combat wings and with 30C 150 mah 1S packs that are high quality I charge them at 2.25A finishing 5 packs in roughly 18 to 20 mins charge time some packs have 200 cycles on them and fly almost as good as new packs so if you have good quality packs the 1/10th the discharge C rating is a very safe charge limit. On cheap or no name packs do not charge at over 1C.
profile.summary: explaining how this unit works.

profile.description: Want your shot to travel further? Super Point .177 caliber pellets get the maximum distance for your airgun. 500 per tin.
profile.reviewText:
If you have a gun that most pellets fit a little loose in then these may be the pellet for you. The front drive band on these are larger then most pellets so the will fit a looser bore pretty tight but if it's a tight bore they won't fit.. you will damage the pellet trying to push it in if your chamber is on the tight side, but if it's on the loose side these may be 50 yard and in tack drivers. In most guns they don't shoot well at all and that's in top end PCP guns that shoot almost anything pellet on top of pellet.. however I have a Benjamin Armada .177 that shoots these with the best of them. They are a 50 yard max pellet, they will start to De-stabilize at about 55 yards in any gun I've shot them in. If you have a break barrel that most pellets fit losse in then try these you may just be shocked.

5 stars for loose chamber guns, 3 stars for all else.. they will not shoot good in 90% of guns. If you have a rifle barreled Co2 pistol that has a slightly larger dia barrel for mag feed reasons these will likely shoot well.
profile.summary: Very VERY tight fitting pellet but thats not always a bad thing.

profile.reviewText: The people saying they can't get a scope (be it stock or after market) to adjust high enough to bring to point of impact up to the point of aim.. its called Barrel droop A lot of break barrels have it , it's part of the monster that is break barrels (i have two brand new Air Arms guns one in .177 and one in .22 that both have barrel droop and they are 700 dollar rifles.) You need to shim the scope if its just mild droop, if it's morn then you can shim out then you have to by a drop compensation rail or adjustable dove tail mounts.. Gamo guns are over priced and poor quality as the norm. The triggers are DANGEROUS as the gun can be half shot (IE: pull the trigger right to the fire point but don't shoot the gun and the feel how long the first stang becomes.. it's not safe and it's a horrid trigger to start with, yes I have a Bone collector I got brand new in a trade) the guns are super hold sensitive and really pellet PICKY. Now that's not saying they can't be accurate, if you find the right hold and right pellet the can be accurate guns.. the amount of time it takes to find a pellet it likes and to learn it's wildly hold sensitive nature is just to much. You want a super mag break barrel that doesn't have much barrel droop and rarely if ever needs a compensation mount, is far more accurate with many more pellets and carries more ftlbs of energy? At the same price or less get you a Beeman Mach 12.5 (much better trigger as well) make 29 to 31ftlbs in .22 and 27 to 28 ftlbs in .177. That's a good deal more then this gun, it's not nearly as hold sensitive and likes most some type pellets you feed it and it's deadly accurate in its price range. I have videoson YT of shooting 12oz soda cans at 165 and 200 yards with a 85% hit to miss ratio.. the BC couldn't do this with its best pellet on its best day. Plus they made the twist rate to slow (IE: made to shoot sub 8 grain pellets) and the gun is to powerful for sub 8 grain pellets so it's to fast a twist rate of the 9.5 to 11 grain pellets that at it's power level needs to be shot. All in all stay away from gamo they make poor quality products and greatly over change for them.. that's putting it plain and simple.
profile.summary: Stay away from Gamo if you want accuracy and quality

profile.reviewText:
Update 12/20/15
I must have gotten one good one out of 5 yes you read that right 1 out of 5. The first one I got for the contest gun was great, now we ordered 4 more for other contests and give a ways. It's sad, EVERYONE having the same issue (except for the first one) all have decent glass for the money it's great glass..the issue with the other 4 scopes (one from Amazon , 3 from a sponsor optics retailer) the adjustments, they have ONLY 45moa elevation and windage (the first had A LOT MORE) then within a few rounds down range the adjustments are ALL OVER the place like REALLY REALLY BAD, windage tracks in a arc across the whole adjustment range that turrets turn 4 whole turns past when the adjustments actually stop moving on elevation and windage it will move ten whole turns but only move 47 to 51 moa (that's between all 4 scopes) at what should be 7.5moa per full turn you get 6ish whole turns from the bottom of adjustment then the next 4ish turns don't move anything.. the adjustments aren't even close, on turn 1 off the bottom of adjustment range will move very close to 7.5moa then the next turn will move between 3 and 4moa then the next full turn will move it to 22.5moa likes it should be then turn 4 will move roughtly 2 to 3moa then the next full turn will catch up to where it should be.. the adjustments are so bad that shooting past 400 yards using elevation adjustment to dial in bullet drop is pointless it is in fact impossible because the adjustments move so poorly that you won't even be able to get close. And then the windage ( centering the turrets meaning the turrets move ten full turns so maxing out then centering at 5 down on elevation and windage) moves either way in a arc going from about 6moa up down to level then back up to 6moa of elevation included in the wimdage adjustment.. these are simply not worth 30 dollars, yes the glass is good for the money BUT the adjustments are total trash.. now if you get a good one like the first one I got then you will be shocked at how good they are for the money BUT right now that's a 20% chance of getting a good one and 80% chance you will get one that isn't even close to usable. Plain and simple AVOID THIS SCOPE OR YOU ARE WASTING YOUR TIME AND MONEY AND AMMO COST .. it's a shame how bad they are, I mean if the adjustments was even decent this scope would be a steal but with how bad they are even at 20 or 30 bucks you are getting ripped off.. IT REALLY IS THAT BAD.

This is the scope we ended up with on the sub moa at 1k for less the 1k project/contest on YT give away rifle. We went through a total of 9 scopes (each scope we used a total of three replacements on to make sure it wasn't a one off problem before giving a poor review and removing it from the contest list), starting with the junk CVlife 6-24X50 front parallax and side parallax versions (the side parallax version is a much nicer scope just lacks in total elevation moa range for what we needed but other then that it is a decent scope with decently clear glass, but the adjustments aren't even close to being consistent and the mildots are not true at any magnification so it's just a poorly made rectical) then to the tasco world class 6-24 mildot just couldn't handle the recoil (read my review) of the sub 11 pound .300rum shooting very close to a absolute max charge with Molly coated 210 VLD's for sub 35 ftlbs of recoil guns it would make a awesome choice as it's under 60 bucks... Then we went through a good bit more scopes and none being capable of giving what we needed, we thought it would be the optics that made the project a failure.. a friend of mine has a Barska 10-40x on a .17hmr that he showed me and asked me after I looked through it what I thought it costs... I guessed in the 300ish range and he said 75 bucks... I was shocked (i shoot for/sponsored by Night Force, DPMS, Lazzeroni, Barnes and a few others. I make my living shooting looooong range and have for 15 years now so I know and only use high end optics) so I called Barska and asked if they would supply one of their scopes for the contest as a 1 time advertising deal if the scope was good the said no and wanted to have an ad in at least 3 videos if they gave me a scope.. I laughed... So I hopped online and bought one from a sponsor Optics planet for a few bucks but with no need to run an ad.. so here's the scope review, glass awesome at all mags (exit pupil is small at max mag and will strain your eyes but that's to be expected with budget high power optics) at 20x and below it's Leupold VX2 or slightly better clarity but no where near VX3 clarity but still well above its price point clear and crisp all the way to the edge, at max mag it does loss some crispness and image quality but still the best I've seen for a scope below 4 bills.. The eteched glass rectical is AWESOME for this price point and dead on true mils at the correct power another rarity for a scope of this price.. adjustments are dead on 1/8th moa with plenty of elevation for on to 1200ish with out a built in moa rail, we are using a 20 moa rail because we want to be able to reach out 1400 and we still have 10 moa left at 1400 yards with the .300rum shooting the Molly coated 210 vlds out a 26 inch tube. It has plenty of elevation and windage for extreme long range shooting on cals that are capabled of extreme L/R. We are capable of 8.5 to 9.5 inches 3 shot groups at 1k yards so the scope and rifle did it's goal and only just breaking 1 moa at 1400, now this combo can NOT DO this with factory ammo... Not even close, it's doing it with very very dialed in hand loads that the rifle eats up.. this scope did put us over budget, if bought at Amazon's cost (I got it from a sponsor for hardly any cost but I'm counting the Amazon cost in the rifles price) the price this setup can be bought for is 1028.82 now but that's with the 80 dollar 20 moa rail and to shoot 1k yards this scope has enough elevation that the rail is not needed so it really is under 1k.. if you know how to dial in really good hand loads and properly break in the rifle and don't get one of the few "bad" rifles that slip by with this scope, a well built hand load and you know how to shoot long range you can do 1 moa capable rifle at 1k yards for 1k us dollars. Just to know this rifle is printing consistently .5 to .6 moa out to 600 yards opening up to .8 moa consistently out to 800 and staying sub 1 moa to 1200.. this scope is absolutely a bargain at its price, it's built like a Leupold and will hold up to heavy recoil for a long long time, it is a heavy scope but that's a good thing as it's built like a tank .. holding up to 57 ftlbs of recoil on the sub 11 pound non-muzzle braked rifle. You shoulder will not be happy at all but the scope handles it in spades.  The parallax markings are pretty close to what the say also, again rare for a budget priced optic. I'm a huge fan of this scope and would say it will stand up to scopes 4x it's price and beat most of them in every facet except for max mag clarity and that's not saying its max mag clearness is bad it's just not as crisp as it is at 20x and less but will still beat ANY sub 400 dollar scope at max mag clarity and size of exit pupil, most budget high mag scoped have a exit pupil so small it will strain your eyes to the point of a head ache, this one is small but more then fair and if you are placing your head on the stock where it should be then  it's not bad at all.. Will this scope compare to my cake and eat it to Night Force N series and bench rest scopes? Absolutely NOT... not even remotely close... But it shouldn't as it's 14 to 18x less money then they are.  I'm sponsored by NF and they may not like me saying this but oh well, would I rather have one NF scope  if I had ten rifles or ten of these and plenty left over for ammo... Sorry Night Force I would take the 10 scopes rifles... As would the CEO so don't rip up my contract lol... This scope preforms FAR beyond its price point.. BTW we are giving the contest gun away to a lucky sub on Dec 31st, along with 300 rounds of the hand loads and a data and reload chart for the gun, Night Force is generously giving the winner a option for any NF scope at 25% off street price coupon that's valid for 365 days from the drawing date... DPMS is giving a 15% off street price coupon to the winner as well good for any DPMS rifle. If you like L/R shooting and give a ways you need to Sub to me, lots of fun videos and lots of sponsor give a ways..

Edit 12/2/15
I'm still overly impressed by this scope, I'm absolutely shocked at the optical quality of the this scope at this price point it is mind numbingly good, one again this coming from a scope snob, that has shot world class optics for 22 years of my 33 years of life. After close to 1500 hot 190 and 210 .300rum loads the scope is rock solid.. there is no better for the coin scope I've ever seen it blows away scopes of its power level at 3x the cost.. they aren't even near the same level of all around build quality nor optic quality. After roughly 1500 rounds the tracking is still exact 1/8th moa, turrets are good feeling at its price point and have stayed feeling good and we are turning those turrets no stop when shooting between 800 and 1400 yards.. the only grip I have with this scope is no height hash marks so you have to remember how many turns you made, on a zero resettable scope this is absurd.. with it being 1/8th moa 2 whole turns is the same as one whole turn on a 1/4 moa scope so some times you are making LARGE elevation adjustments and you have to remember how many turns back to zero its silly that is the only knock I can give this scope as everything else performs well above it's price point by far. Scope is clear enough to see .30 cal hole out to about 800 or so that tells you the scope is crisp, I prefer to use it at 22x as you get a high quality image and it degrades ever so slightly at max. Parallax markings are very good and accurate that is a shocker in a budget scope.. still the thing that shocks me the most is after a lot of heavy recoiling rounds the tracking is still perfect, I haven't seen tracking on any sub 500 dollar scope (except for SWFA SS scopes) be so true through out it's whole range of movement. This thing is amazing for the cost.
profile.summary: These scopes are beyond JUNK they would be a rip off at even 30.00

profile.reviewText: These are a good field pellet that is 0.7 cents per shot... These are not pellets that will shoot tiny groups in our PCP guns and match grade spring/gas piston guns... I do not shoot these in my match guns and pcp match guns that's what JSB and H&Ns are for... If you weight sort these pellets and have a faster twist barreled gun they may very well shoot well for you.. I wish they was 8 grain.. what I use these for and they work very well in all 4 of my guns in my highly built up bulk filled two being highly modded 2300KT's (both 450.00 pistols with all the mods) and 2 built to the max 2300S's (both being close to 500.00 pistols) if weight sorted after a good wash and de-lube then re-lube slick 50...These in all 4 of them are absolutely capable of 10 shot .20 inch groups at 20 yards.. These pistols are all bulk filled and built with Lother barrels and the best of the best upgrades making them all match grade tack drivers.. they are all power adjustable as well and these pellets do not like breaking 580fps unless you are shooting very fast twist barrels and most stock/box store quality guns have slower twist barrels.. out of all my top end pcp rifles the only one that will shoot these well is a FX, due to the smooth twist barrel that gun shoots any pellet well.. I would never use this light a pellet in my rifles anyhow and do not buy them for that... I buy them for my 2300 builds... They are a lower mid grade pellet but if weight sorted they will shoot well in 2300 series.. my 2300 series pistols are capable of driving these pellets at between 805fps for the 10 inch barrel pistol and 910fps for the 2300s carbine ... However if I break 600 with them they will spray all over at 25 yards to give you an idea at 560 to 580 they will shoot .20 to .25 at 25 yards all day long in all 4 of them... The carbine will allow me to jump to 600fps and hold 1/2 inch out to 40 yards with little to no wind... But if I push them to  650 or more my groups will open up to 3 inchs at 25 yards and from there the hotter I push them the more they open up... At 800fps 25 yards will open to 5 inchs or so.. and that's out of sub 1/4 inch capable guns... I've watched slow mo's of these in flight through my scope cams and it has to do with the CG of these pellets.. as long as you don't break 600 they stay stable and no wobble in flight.. above 620fps they start to wobble in flight and the faster you run them the worse it gets... At 700 they will key hole 30% of the time at 25 yards... At 800 they key hole about 85% of the time at 25 yards... They just can't handle high speeds without a very fast twist to lock the skirt in place in flight... They are to light for 90% of break barrels and way to light for any pcp rifle... They are a budget pellet that shoots extremely well in every 2300 series pistols I've shot them in or seen them shot in no matter if they are totally stock or modded through the roof like mine are.. the key is if they aren't stock you really have to have a power adjuster if you did power mods and bulk fill as you will easily be breaking 600, if you max power mod them on Co2 then at max power you will be in the low 800s and can't use these pellets but with a power adjuster just dial them down to 580ish for insane accuracy and increase you shot count per fill massively.. crank up the power and sling them all over... Do not expect itty bitty groups in break barrels as 99% of them will vastly over power these pellets.. a rifled barreled pump gun may shoot these very well to just keep them under 600fps... You absolutely can not shoot these over 600 without a fast twist barrel or a FX smooth twist barrel.. They are some of the best pellets out of stock 2300 series guns as they won't break the 580 threshold stock and they are insanely cheap to shoot and absolutely tack driving pellets from those pistols. If your 2300 series is power modded then buy a power adjuster if you don't have one and dial it down to 580 and smile each and every shot.. the super low cost per shot of these pellets will pay for the power adjuster in one box if you normally shoot premium pellets as 1500 top line pellets will be close to 50 bucks... These are 10 for 1250 and a poet adjuster is 20 for a cheap one and 45 for a top end one. So yeah you will easily pay for the power adjuster shooting these pellets vs top shelf stuff with just a few tins of them... And at 560 to 580 these pellets will out preform the top end pellets I'm 2300's almost every time.
profile.summary: These pellets are only good in fast twist barrels.

profile.reviewText: This is a great deal on a remote coil, it's stiff when charged with HPA but no more so then others, it handles 4500psi tanks reg'ed to 2000psi perfect.. I have a few of them and I haven't had one blow out at 3600psi of pressure in the line so I know they have no issue holding 2000psi very safely, so that means Co2 will never blow out the line even on really hot days.. very impressive quality for the cost... I'm gonna test one at 4500psi in the line and see if it blows out, I know they will safely hold 3600 psi but no idea above that... I believe 4500psi will not blow it out but I do believe it will be so stiff that it will be tough to move around as at 3600psi it's already super stiff adding almost 1000psi more is gonna make it rock hard but that's expected and nothing gets taken away for that as all coils get harder and tighter as the pressure go up... some ever get very stiff at Co2 pressures on cooler days and super stiff with Co2 on hot days... this line stays usable (stiffness/flexibility wise) up to about 2600psi past that it gets really stiff and the more pressure past that the stiffer it gets... now at Co2 pressures it only gets a little stiffer and tighter then it does with no pressure and that says it's a quality line.. as off right now it's the only remote coil I will buy for HPA converted Co2 air rifles, for Co2 I use Micro lines and love them but they aren't capable of handling HPA pressures so that's a no go and when 3000psi capable micro lines come out I will be a happy camper..
profile.summary: Awesome quality for the money.. one of the better coils out

profile.reviewText: What can you say about the slow stick other then its perfect, it flys amazing and is one of the most relaxing just plain fun planes to fly. Very high quality, can't hardly destroy them beyond rapairvwith some foam safe CA and kicker or hot glue (careful with hot glue it adds weight quick and the lighter it is the better it flys). Do not buy the version with power system, the brushed motor does work and will fly it but its a PIA when you can do a brushless system for cheaper, get longer flights and never have to mess with it and have more power with less weight. 400 class BL motor that's 800 to 1100KV with a 9x3.8 or 10x3.8 SF prop and you have one powerful plane that climbs quick and is a ball to have combat with to me combat with SS's is more fun then with flying wings. No need to do an aileron mod, rudder and ele only work perfect and with a lot of throw will snap it around really good. With a 3 axis gyro they make a very good and very floaty AP plane as well. The 3 axis unit will give you super smooth video when you have the plane way out there and can't tell exactly what its attitude is up close if your a good pilot you don't need a gyro to do AP but if it's really far out the gyro will help you keep the plane where you want it and not allow it to drift around when its so far out you can't really see the drifting to correct for it. I have made some stellar flight videos in the Fl keys with one that are nearly as good as with a high end AP multi rotor not as good but nearly as good. This plane flys best if it's built light, I want mine to be 400 to 420 grams AUW without cam that puts me well under 500 with an action cam. With a 400 class 1100kv blm and a 3s 1800 you will get 25 mins or more depending on how you use throttle and have unlimited vertical that's space shuttle climb out quick lol. I have gotten 40 mins on a 3s 2200 30c pack carrying a Gopro with a 9x4.7 APC SF prop. Want beautiful video from a very easy to fly and cheap plane to build you can not beat a BL Slow Stick. They also make awesome FPV planes that have very good duration and performance.. Don't think it has to be slow because its called a slow stick, I've built these with straight wings and ailrons and with a 10x7 prop and a 450 class 1650kv motor and they are dang fast planes, but that will kill you duration and AP stability if you want to use it for that.
profile.summary: One of many new and long time RC pilots favs.

profile.reviewText: I own this model and the  8.5-25x50 and love them, I also have 4 of the Mark 4 8.5-25x50 IRs. The VX3s are AWESOME scopes for the money.. yes the Mark 4s have slightly nicer glass but over all not really worth nearly 2x the cost of these. I have the 6.5-20 on a  Custom .300rum and the 8.5-25 on a Lazzeroni .257 Scream jet (imho the best 1000 yard cal. Out there, shooting a 120vld at 3940FPS and holds true 1/2moa  groups out to 800 yards and will stay sub moa out to about 1300 yards.) These scopes have dead on parallax markings on the side turrets and absolutely accurate 1/4 moa adjustmests they are dead on 1/4 moa that is a big deal and if the scopes are ever so slightly off on the adjustments it means little out to about 600 yards but past that is the adjustments are slightly more or less then the stated value it will wreck havoc on you sighting in correct adjustments and it becomes really a problem when you reach past 1000 yards. The glass is awesome and super bright and crisp at all mag settings.. I love these scopes in fact will be putting one on a Christian arms Carbon .338 lapua mag for a 2000 yard capable rifle. All in all yes the Mark 4 is a better scope but not nearly twice the cost better.
profile.summary: The best deal in a truly high end optic on the market.

profile.description: Medium-weight, accurate pointed pellet for plinking, hobby shooting and co2-pistols at medium ranges. Aerodynamic design for flat trajectories and high-impact. Ribbed.
profile.reviewText:
Update 2/6/16 @ 9:41PM EST.
Simply put I can not find a gun that won't shoot these. I have ran them through all my high end PCP and high end Break barrels and not one don't like them ( 14 pcp and 11 springers in .22 is my fleet and a bunch of High end pcp and break barrel .177s gotta get some of these to feed the .177s and see how that plays out) so outta 25 guns everyone shoots these very well, only one shoots these the best of any pellet and it's the Air Arms I was telling about in the review, but they all shoot them very well and better then any other pointed pellet I've ever shot. For a pointed pellet the B.C. is very good (of course not as high as high BC domes but very high for a pointed pellet) they shoot much flatter then any pointed pellet I've ever shot and buck the wind better due to the higher BC. I shot a large Farrel car due to it fighting with my much smaller cat out of a 75ftlb Air Force gun and it laid it down like nothing I dialed it back to 35ish ftlbs with these pellets and a double lung pass through was instant death.. not a movement after impact and that was a 65 yard shot so the pellets will do very well on game as well, shooting them past 47ftlbs will blow the head off the pellet leaving the skirt in the barrel I forgot to dial the guns power down and it happened to me.

These pellets are TACK DRIVERS, pointed pellets in high power guns are rarely super accurate (in lower powered guns they can be very accurate but rarely in magnum level rifles) I shot these today in a Benji Armada/Hawke Sidewinder 30 8-32x56.. getting sub half inch 5 shot groups at 55 yards and they shoot flat, stay extremely stable @ 33.5ftlbs and was printing 5 shot 110 yard groups on the sub 1.5 inch range, this gun with H&N baracuda match can go in the .85 inch range at 110 yards but for a lighter weight pointed pellet these did very very well in that gun. Next I shot them in a Daystate Wolverine/Leupold VX-3 8.5-25X50 30mm tube Mildot combo and was again shock at them shooting as well as dome pellets out to 55 yards and shooting 5 shot  groups in the 3/8 inch range @ 55 yards and staying right below 1 inch at 110 yards and the Big Wolv is shooting the WAY fast.. Next I shot them in a Air Arms S510 and that gun ate them up inside of 75 yards but was loosing stability after about 80 yards.. however they shot the tightest 55 yard groups that gun has ever shot multiple 5 shot groups in the .25 inch CtC.. I shot them in a few highly tuned extremely powerful break barrels to and was very surprised with how well they did. Needless to say these pellets have outshot ANY pointed pellets I've ever shot.. out of the 7 PCP and 4 BBs I shot them from today all shot them extremely well.
profile.summary: The most accurate .22 pointed pellet ever!
