profile.reviewText: Awesome thread lock gel , it's at a fantastic price and works better then loc tight, as it cures faster and  holds just as tight if not a little tighter but still breakable to remove bolt if need be. I used this on all my high powered competition long range rifles for scope mounting, as well as my PCP and break barrel air guns. I know it holds well as I'm mounted a VX-3 8.5-25x40 leupold on a HW97K that has a massively over powered spring (gun makes 46ftlbs with H&N Baracuda match pellets so it's a very powerful high recoil Springer) I haven't had one base screw or ring screw break loose on this gun with this thread locker yet unless I wanted to remove a screw.  This gun is a power house of a Springer and kicks like a mule so if it can handle the G load that gun puts out and the vibs then it will stand up to anything.
profile.summary: Awesome thread lock, super value! Cures faster the brand names do!

profile.description: Medium-weight, accurate pellet for plinking, hobby shooting and co2-pistols at medium ranges. Enhanced aerodynamics through englisch form (round head) for flat trajectories. Ideal for knock-down targets. Ribbed.
profile.reviewText: This are fantasticly accurate pellets, they are not very high BC for domes my fifty yard avg B.C works out to .0210. They are very very accurate out to roughly 65 yards but the mid range BC will cause the pellet to drop quickly and be affected by wind and scrub energy off fairly quickly.. If you need a very accurate in a lot of guns pellet for a max of 65 yards these are worth a try. I have a custom built 47ftlb double Disco that is built on a laminated thumb hole TARGET stock, custom cut LW barrel W/11 degree target crown to fit the custom CNC-ed multi shot breach (it uses Mrod mags) with full shroud, custom polished and tuned Mrod trigger and a leupold VX-3 8.5-25x40 scope. This gun will shoot with any FT gun out there, it's as accurate as a 4800 dollar full custom .22 based on a Air Arms gun I had built that's 4800.00 without scope. And this is it's pellet of choice, it will out shoot any other pellet I've ran through it (about 55 different pellets) with the Hammers. The H& FTTs will out shoot these in the Disco past 75 yards but inside of 70 these things are magic in that gun. On a calm day it will shoot 65 yard 10 shot groups in the .35 to .40 CtC range staying sub MOA 10 shot groups at 100 but with the FTTs, the Hammers will group in the 1.5 moa range at 100 and drop about 10 inches more then the FTTs BUT the Hammers are absolutely tack drivers inside of 70 yards. Air Arms guns like them very much to but none of my Daystates shoot them very well.
profile.summary: Superbly accurate pellet! Daystate guns don't like them tho.

profile.description: If you prize accuracy over anything else, you'll appreciate the consistent quality of H&N air gun pellets. H&N Barracudas are heavyweights designed to provide maximum energy for magnum springer's and pre-charged pneumatics. Copper coated, reduces the amount of contact with lead.
profile.reviewText: These along with baracuda and baracuda match are my fav pellets In all my pcp guns for shooting at 125 yards and longer. They have the highest BC and fly well even at 60ftlbs, no cork screwing and at that kinda velocity not many pellets can do that.. I love these.. the review is for all 3 Baracuda lines, power, match and plain baracudas. It's gun dependent as to what one I like best I have guns that prefer each one.. the power is only really liked in a few pcp guns I own, the match is liked by most of the as well as the normal ones.. the match are a little more consistent and shoot slightly tighter groups but not by much. These are the pellets to shoot if you have a 25 and over ftlb rifle and really want to push the range way out there.. I shoot coke cans at 200 yards with these with about a 85% hit ratio. No other pellet I've shot is the hit ratio that high, the next closest is H&N FTTs but that's if there is hardly any wind then I have about a 65 to 70% hit ratio with them. A 100 yards and in the FTTs are the more accurate pellet in most guns.
profile.summary: My fav long range (125-200 yards) pellets, the Baracuda series by H&N

profile.description: Remington express pellets round nose 22 caliber, 250 CT (89310). optimized for use with Remington airguns.
profile.reviewText:
These look exactly like H&N Field targets, they may not be H&N made but they look very good and shoot the same point of aim as the FT shoots out of a FX extreme and a Daystate big wolv. So I believe they are H&N FT at 30% the cost per shot as the H&Ns.. I believe they are the usable but not up to H&Ns standards to put in their tins so they sell the slightly outta spec pellets to remington at a super cheap price.. if these aren't FT they sure as hell shoot just like them as well as look just like them.. I need to get a scale,out and see if they weigh the same or very close to the same. Outstanding value in a pretty accurate 50 yards and in plinking pellet.

Update, these are NOT H&N made pellets as the weight is different then the Field targets and they are longer.. they do look just like the H&N field targets but what really tells them they aren't other then the weight is H&N pellets are made of a fairly hard lead and these aren't they are in fact JSB lead soft so pure lead not a lead with antimony to harden it up. Never-the-less they are a very good accurate 50 meter and in pellet.. I calculated the B.C from muzzle to 60 yards in 3 guns then averaged out the overall B.C and it was .0162 so they are in between wadcutter and pointed pellets B.C wise, deff not no flat shooting pellets and will scrub energy off fairly quickly but for a cheap and high accurate pellet these are very good at that.. I've shot them only in PCP guns  (7 total) and not one shot them badly and all shot then pretty well. Are they going to shoot with H&N or JSB pellets... Likely not but some guns may eat these up but on average they are not going to shoot with premium pellets HOWEVER they are 1/4th the cost of premium pellets.. as back yard paper punchers or pest removing or plinking pellets these will be hard to beat... just remember these are not going to do a very good job on pests out past 50 yards as the lower B.C scrubs energy quickly... if you aren't shooting these at 25ftlbs or more I would limit my shots on fur game to 30 yards and 50 on game with feathers. In 15 to 18ftlb guns I would not shoot furs at anything more then 20 yards with 15 being more realistic however the pellets are accurate enough at 40 to 50 yards for head shoots in good PCP guns the energy shaving off at a very fast rate is not fair to the animal to shoot them at extended ranges... and yes that's even head shots. They make a awesome rat pellet in 20 to 30 ft lb guns... rats I will say your max range is however far your gun holds 5 shot groups that all shots are within the vitals.. the shape does deff put a wallop on whatever it hits and digs in well.
profile.summary: Very good value for the coin.

profile.description: Medium-weight, extremely accurate competition pellet with flat trajectory for medium ranges. Exceptional aerodynamic design for high impact and penetration. Tightest shot groups. Lowest rate of lead fouling and consistent shot spreads thanks to special alloy.
profile.reviewText: H&N FTT's in .177 and .22 are my 1# fav pellets followed closely by JSB Exact series pellets. The FTT shoot well to extremely well in 95% of high quality springers and pcp guns.. they are very very consistent with weight, head and skirt size and because they are a harder pellet then jsb pellets you will have very few if any bent skirts or deformed pellets that's a big plus over JSB pellets that have on avg 20 to 30 out of 500 pellets with damaged skirts due to how soft they are. These are among the highest BC .177 and .22 pellets on the market in there respected weight class.. These pellets shoot extremely flat, retain energy and buck the wind with the best of them and much better then most. I've got a HW97K in .22 and .177 both fully tuned and with heavier springs, the .177 is a 20.5ftlb (with the FTT's @ 1040fps) gun with the heavy spring.. it's tuned very well and shoots smooth as silk for a ultra mag Springer. With a 35 yard ZERO these pellets drop only 23 inches at 130 yards, they are the flatest shooting pellets in .177 and .22 I've ever shot and extremely accurate at very long range for .177s I've worked out the avg B.C over 130 yards to be 0.0310 that's higher then any .177 pellet I've ever shot.. These pellets are not the absolute best hunting pellet due to them being hard and don't mushroom/deform at impact on game and will have full pass throughs on most game with mag power guns resulting in not a lot of energy transfer but if you need penetration these will do very well.. If you need an extremely flat shooting extremely accurate in most guns long range TARGET pellet these are hard to beat.
profile.summary: One of the if not the best long range pellet in .177 & .22

profile.description: If you prize accuracy over anything else, you'll appreciate the consistent quality of H&N air gun pellets. H&N Barcudas are heavyweights designed to provide maximum energy for magnum springers and pre-charged pneumatics.
profile.reviewText: Some of the most accurate high power gun pellets on the market.. plain and simple if you have a power PCP or break barrel this is the first pellet to try with the JSB 10.34s a close second.. if you have a really high power break barrel this is the pellet to try first as it has a skirt strong enough and thick enough to handle how hard high power break barrels are on pellet skirts.. these pellets are stable at 1025fps and less, breaking 1025 will likely have stability issues but that's no matter not many guns out there can anyhow, my Condor has no issues pushing these to 1200fps with a heavier hammer spring, but I tune it down to push them at 1010fps and the gun is superbly accurate, like .25 inch ten shot groups indoors at 50 yards and 1.25 to 1.5 inch 10 shot groups at 100 yards with a lot being very close to MOA but I've never broke MOA 10 shot group at 100 yards with a .177.. 3 or 5 shot groups at a 100 yards with these in the Condor I go sub MOA all the time but never with a 10 shot group, even with head sizing the pellets and weigh sorting never broke Sub MOA 10,shot group at 100, at 50 yards Sub MOA 10 shot groups are pretty easy indoors. These are my FAV .177 and .22 pellets with H&N Sniper right behind and then JSB heavies. This pellet is almost assured to be a very accurate pellet in any PCP.. some don't like them but not many, most will shoot them lights out. The 10.34 JSBS have a higher BC but rarely will they out shoot the Baracudas at extreme long range, the Sniper line will out shoot the Baracudas at extremely long range if the gun likes them just for the fact of less wind drift but the Baracudas are easy get and in Stock anywhere you can buy premium pellets as where the Snipers aren't so easy to find.. and you can get the Baracudas in different head sizes for choked barrels and barrels that aren't choked, not something you can get with the Snipers or the JSB heavies. For me in .177 it's 4.51mm head size for choked/Match barrels and 4.53mm head size for un choked barrels. The 4.53mm Baracudas most times shoot well in choked barrels BUT you will have flyers and with the 4.51s you won't have flyers hardly ever.. the 4.51s normally don't shoot well in un choked barrels. If you have a big box store type break barrel then get the 4.53s not the 4.51s ask the seller what ones they are selling as you will likely be unhappy if your shooting a un choked barrel and get the 4.51s NOW that is not always the case your un choked barrel may shoot the 4.51s lights out good.. I'm talking on average, on average un choked barrels shoot the 4.51s poorly or at least not as good as it will the 4.53s.. that goes the same if you have a pcp gun that doesn't have a match grade barrel, match barrels are choked.. if you have like let's say a Benjamin Discovery then you will want the 4.53 head size as well but have a better chance of the Disco shooting the 4.51s well then if you tried the 4.51s in a big box store break barrel. In fact I have tuned a lot of Discos for friends and I have yet to see one that don't like 4.53 Baracudas, JSB 10.34s and Sniper 8.5 and 15 grain. The Baracuda normally being the most accurate pellet at 100 yards followed very closely by the 8.5 grain Sniper medium. I hope this helps, it's always wise to try different head sizes in your gun as one head size of the same pellet design will deff shoot better then the rest.. but you can use this guide so you don't have to buy all the head sizes, 4.51 for choked barrels and 4.52 or 4.53 for un choked. IMHO the 4.50 and 4.55 head sizes are useless but that's only in my tests, I've never had a gun shoot the 4.50 or 4.55 good, it's always the 4.51 or 4.53s... same goes for .22 as well.
profile.summary: One of the best long range pellets made, its a must try in your gun

profile.description: Beeman pointed pellets 177 caliber 500 count per box. Follow all state and local laws about the purchase, ownership and use of air guns.
profile.reviewText: This are VERY GOOD PELLETS FOR THE COIN, are they as consistent as JSB or H&N well of course NOT... BUT they are well made? With fairly consistent head and skirt sizes? Yes are they decently close in weight between each other? Yes and they clean? YES they coating on them will not rub off on your fingers and keep direct contact with lead down... now I'm a elite high end PCP kinda gun and 90% of my air guns are PCP but I do have a special place in my heart for a high quality and very well tuned break barrel and I'm not much of a .177 gun but I do have 3 .177 break barrels, 2 RWS and 1 BSA .177 Break barrels... and what's funny is in the two RWS guns, one tuned to 20.5ftlbs with H&N 8.66 grain 4.51mm head size FTT's and the other 26ftlbs with JSB Diabolo Exact heavies and these pellets in both those guns shoot lights out... they are the MOST accurate 40 yards and in pellets I've ever shot in those guns and I've shot just about every pellet out there through them.. Now they open up QUICKLY in both guns after 45 yards, they are capable of 10 shot groups on the .4 to .5 inch range from 10 to 40 yards, at 50 yards those half inch and under groups are now 1.5 inches and at 75 yards they are over 6 inches.. in those guns 40 yard half inch or less center to center groups in over sprung (over sprung meaning putting more powerful Springs in them) magnum power level .177 break barrels and as we all know powerful break barrels are not easy to shoot well and overall not the most accurate guns in the world... these pellets have shocked me that they shoot that we'll and like I said at 45 yards max and 40 and under being where they really shine these pellets at the cost they are become a phenomenal value.. the Super mag BSA that we tuned out and put a silly strong spring in is a powerhouse shooting these at 1090fps (just ever so slightly under super sonic and every now and then pushing one super sonic)  is dang accurate with these as well and that gun only likes H&N Baracudas in the 4.50 head size, with the Baracudas it is a 5 shot group in the .75 to 1 inch range at 50 yards and that's as good as that gun will ever shot just due to the over whelming power and recoil being almost uncontrollable but fun to shoot never the less. And with this pellet shooting 5 shot groups at 35 yards it's a 1.5 inch gun AND that in amazing for this gun keep in mind 1.5 inch 5 shot groups at 35 yards for THIS gun is super good! However those groups at 50 yards are in the 10 inch range due to pellets becoming unstable... these pellets have more then proved they are a well made and very consistent "very consistent when you factor what they cost in to the equation" pellet that is exceptionally accurate in 2 magnum and 1 super magnum level .177 springers.. I really believe these are deff a pellet you should give a try as the cost is very low and the quality of the pellet is beyond the price point and likely will be accurate to very accurate... needless to say I'm very impressed with them period and when you factor what they cost in I'm beyond impressed. Just do not expect them to be much more then a 40 yards MAX pellet as they scrub energy quickly and groups open up super fast after 40 yards... I believe in a less powerful gun they may stay stable for longer and may give you a decent accuracy out to 60 ish yards in good guns... I haven't tried them in any PCP .177s, I do own a few high end .177 pcp guns, so I'll run some through them and ideas be willing to bet inside of 50 yards they will shoot very well. The reason I haven't tested them in any pcp guns yet is any of my .177 pcps will shoot them well over super sonic as they set so I'll swap some hammer Springs and lower fill pressure and get them sub sonic and see what they will do... I'll update with that info soon.. just remember this if you are in need of long range pellets these are NOT going to fill the bill for that, there calculated B.C over 40 yards ranges between depending on how each gun reshapes them 0.0125 and 0.0133 so just slightly higher then Wad cutter B.C's when good High B.C Domes are in the 0.0280 to 0.0320 B.C. range.. so yeah they are gonna really get thrower around by the wind and scrub energy and drop like a rock very quickly... with that said when if these shoot well for you then when you zero your scope at the max range these pellets hold accuracy, don't zero at 10 yards and then try to make 40 yards shots as even in powerful guns these pellets are going to be dropping quick past 25 yards... in a 15ftlb gun if you zero at 40 you will never be more then one mildot hold over or under from 10 to 40 yards... if you zero at let's say 15 yards you will be 3 mils low at 45 in a 15ftlb gun and 1.5 mils high at 25... that's to much hold over and under to deal with... when you get zero at 40 and be just plus or minus 1 Mildot over the whole 40 yards. This is a paper punching pellet OR VERY CLOSE RANGE small pest pellet like small rats or small birds being all you should shoot with this pellet and even in a fairly powerful gun at no more then 20 yards due to the massive energy loss... a 15ftlb at the muzzle gun with this pellet will be at less then 7 ft lbs at 50 yards...so a 12ftlb gun at 50 yards will have less on target power then a Crosman pump master 760 at the muzzle... keep that in mind... this pellet in a 15ftlb gun is not going to be able to put a squirrel down quickly at anything more then 15 yards at the ABSOLUTE max and that's with good shot placement. A 20ftlb gun may extend that to 20 yards with good shoot placement and remember if you made a bad shot at 20 yards with a 20 ft lb guns on a squirrel that's gonna be a slow painful ordeal from the animal... so be respectful of the animal you are pesting... and ONLY short range pesting with this pellet... it is by no means even a decent hunting pellet even tho it can be very accurate at closer ranges. Deff no shots on crows at more then 15 yards in a powerful gun and as we all know crows are NOT letting you get that close... so don't even think about it...
profile.summary: Can be an exceptionally accurate SHORT range pellet (40 yards and in)

profile.description: Mendini violin is completely hand-carved with a solid spruce top and maple back and sides. profile.reviewText: I bought this for my wife's birthday and just gave it to her today as today Is her bday.. we are extremely disappointed but since I bought it and wrapped it on Nov 4th 2015 waiting for her bday today I can't send it back.. the strings are crisscrossed causing the E string to break during tuning cutting the crap out of my wife's finger.. the thing should at least come strung without the wires being crisscrossed causing you to not be able to tune it and causing UN-needed stress on the wires that are under the top wire and causing high tension breaks... An E wire will cut the crap out of you on a break if it hits you as it breaks and lash you open pretty good.. anyone that's ever had a thin wire cut knows they hurt like crazy. This was all around a disappointing gift I gave her and I'm stuck with it. I would give it ZERO stars if I could...
profile.summary: Poorly setup and strung with crisscrossed wires just all around poor quality.

profile.reviewText:
Update 1/26/2017
I just shot these pellets in my FX Royale 400 .22 and my Impact with the .22 barrel.. the .Royale 400 pushing them them a little to hot at 39.5ftlbs but they still shot lights out out to 85 yards and started to open up quicker then I like but inside of 80 yards they are crazy good in that gun.. in the Impact I dialed the power down to push them at 35ftlbs or 930fps and holy well they are amazing.. at 100 yards I shot 10, 10 shot groups and my avg was 1.3 MOA groups with two being slightly under 1 MOA.. that's amazing, the most accurate gun I have ever shot is my Impact with the .25 barrel pushing 52ftlbs with JSBs.. my .30 Boss, my .30 barrel for the impact neither will shoot 10 shot groups at 100 yards as tight as my .25 barrel on the impact... these pellets stunned me in the Impact at 35ftlbs.. they honestly shoot almost as tight as the .25 will and honestly it's easier to shoot the .22 barrel with this pellet and hold those groups.. the .25 fights wind VERY well, but honestly this pellet at 35ftlbs fight the wind imho a little better then the .25 and shoots slightly flatter. If I sorted these pellets by weight and head size I believe I could get very close to MOA avg 10 shot groups.. this pellet needs to come out in .25 in a 29 and 33 grain weight.. that may very well be the most accurate pellet made for 100 yard shooting in any Smooth Twist barreled gun. I would absolutly LOVE this pellet in .25 in a 28 and 30 or 31 grain to be able to push in the 52 to 60ftlb range.. that would be a pellet long range airgunners dream of, a BC in the .0400 to .0450 range due to the shape of the pellet and weight.. so it would be a lot higher then any normal wasp waist Diabolo style pellet... that would fight wind super well and shoot super flat.. honestly this would be a bench rest long range guys dream pellet... come on H&N I buy a dang many tins of pellets from yall and JSB every year... make all us .25 smooth twist guys happy.. bring us this pellet in .25 pleaseeeeeee, if the Die work is to hard to make multiple weights just make a 29.5 grain and we will come in groves.. you won't be able to make enough.. these pellets in .177 and .22 are lights out accurate so long at yoy don't break 1020fps in every FX gun I own... if you have a smooth twist barreled FX gun in .177 or .22 buy these in any grain weight adjust the gun to push them between 920 and 990fps and I can bet money on it that you won't be buying any other pellets for that gun. I have a total of 4 FX Smooth Twist .177s and 3 .22s, plus my Impact and my Boss... so 4 in .22  and 5 in .177 counting the Impact as I have all 4 barrels for it the .177, .22, .25 and .30 barrels.. so in nine Smooth Twist barrels these pellets in the 3 weights in .177 and 2 in .22 these pellets are absolutely magic in Smooth Twist guns... I'm going to say so long as they aren't pushed to hot they are the most accurate pellet in every one of those guns, with JSB 10.34s in .177 being seconds most accurate and JSB 18.13s in the .22s. Oh yeah and I will tell you this I had to push the .22s to right around 1160fps to get them to destabilize and the .177s to around 1200fps to get them to destablize.. I have never seen any pellet that can be pushed faster then 1040fps and shoot ten pellets and not have one destabilize.. I could push these at 1100fps and have 1 in 50 sprial... it's flat amazing how good these pellets fly when pushing them super hot.. at 50 yards I was still putting 10 .177s in under 1 inch group when pushing them at 1170fps from the impact. Bet you can't find another pellet that can do that at that speed... please H&N give us these pellets in .25..
 I will eat up the long range bench rest comps for a while until they catch on if they make a .25 Sniper.

If your looking for a super high B.C pellet this may very well be your best bet. My calculated B.C. over 75 yards is between 0.0385 and 0.0412 depending on what gun I shoot then from as how the barrel reshapes them changes the overall B.C. I have never shot any other .22 pellet that breaks 0.0390. These happen to be accurate in every PCP gun of mine I've shot then through and that's 14 and every one of them shot then very good. If you want a awesome pellet for busting cans at 200 yards these will get you out there with the least wind drift and less drop then anything I've ever shot before. One of my Heavily Moded Air Force guns with the power backed down to 41ftlbs was smacking cans yesterday at
255 yards (video on YouTube search 125ftlb Air Force .22 backed off to 41ftlbs shooting at 255 yards) and as seen in the unedited video I hit 15 out of 15 coke cans with 17 shots using this pellet. My overall drop was 13MOA less then JSB 18.13s and that is a flat shooting pellets so that speaks tons about how high the B.C of these pellets are, and I have to dope for wind less with these as a result of the higher B.C... easily my fav pellet for that gun when shooting extremely long range with Diabolo type Airgun pellets. With the super high B.C spitzer type projectile. 257s and 7mm in super high power guns 255 isn't long range anymore.. just remember this is with a Diabolo type projectile at 41ftlbs then hitting cans with great precision at (for this type of projectile) extreme range says a lot about the pellet and the rifle and the shooter but a really good gun and really good ammo can make anyone look REALLY good and this is the ammo part of that equation!
profile.summary: Some of the best long range pellets on the market!

profile.description: The Bushnell Rimfire optics 6-18x40 riflescope provides peak performance for precise shot placement, these Rimfire rifle scopes designed by Bushnell tout adjustable objectives for excellent aim with distant targets. With an impressive bullet drop compensating turret system and side Parallax focus, you're bound to be impressed by the Bushnell Rimfire optics 6-18x40mm side focus scope.
profile.reviewText:
I'm a sponsored ELR rifle guy to start with being sponsored by a top tier optics company as well as major name custom bolt gun company and many others and have been since I was 16 years old I'm 29 now. This scope was bought for my 9 year old little girls Air Arms S510 .22 pcp girl, I'm big in to extreme long range rifle shooting (ERL) and as much so pushing the limits of Air rifles at the very edge of what high end pcp rifles are capable of. I shoot only top tier glass on my air guns just as my center fires I could not justify putting a 2000 dollar scope on my daughters AAS510 even tho it's a top tier rifle she's not ready for glass like that just in case she knocked it off the bench ect ect... so really nice gun for her and a usable optic, that's my back group and the need for a decent budget scope explained (I'm not some Joe blow just running his mouth I know my stuff and I'm sponsored on a national level for competitive long range shooting) the glass on this scope is nothing to write home about by any means but for 130 bucks it's usable but tough on people that are use to extremely high end optics, parallax can NOT BE used to range targets as its not close to stated value however that's to be expected in a scope of this cost and it has nothing to do with the diopter setting as its all the way in where the parallax markings are set for at the factory as we both have perfect eye sight.. but it does focus decently and remove parallax just as it should, light transfer is horrid but once again I'm used to top tier stuff so I won't go in detail on that, glass wise the scope is usable just don't expect to much and remember it's price...
Now for where the scope has issues, number 1 is I had the first one replaced due to really bad tracking.. I set up my tracking chart at 100 yards to test it and I laughed I gained one moa for every 5 I dialed in, so if you dial in 10 moa you get 12 and on elevation and windage was even worse I was getting 13.5 moa when I dialed 10 minutes. So I got it replaced and the next one was a little better but still BAD BUT it's repeatable so you just dial in remembering that each click value is X and not really 1/4 minute when shooting 150 yards with a Air gun at tiny targets dead on turrets are even more important then centerfire at 600 yards so that is a hard one to deal with due to having to think about it and not just dial the turrets like I normally do as I expect perfectly accurate tracking turrets not 20% off stated value turrets...

And here's the next issue and to long range airgunning it's even a bigger issue then the first one.. the first scope had 31 minutes of elevation yes you read that right THIRTY ONE minutes... that is horrible in a 28ftlb .22 with it shimmer to be zeroed close to center on adjustment range I was left with 17 moa and that's not enough to get her out to a 100 yards with out hold over... the replacement was better but not much at 42 minutes..

I had a Oculus 4-16x42 LR with MOA reticle and matching 1/4 minute adjustments moa/moa scopes are great for air gunners I love them... that's a 250 dollar scope and a excellent one at that... glass would be luppy VX 2 quality or nice Nikon so the glass is very good for the price range it's parallax is close enough to range you with in 10 yards it's got a TMR style ret and it's moa/moa all for 250 bucks... this coming from a self admitted optics snob that is a very good scope for the coin... without a doubt the best sub 400 dollar scope I've ever seen... it tracks almost perfect you may gain a 1/4 minute here and loose one there but that's to be expected and you don't get absolute tracking units 2000 dollars in a scope so it's very good.. in a 1in tube scope but has a honest 70 minute of adjustment so more then usable and with a 20 moa base that's a 1000 yard capable scope in .308 for 250 dollars... so she now has that mounted on her S510 and is ringing 6in steel plates at 180 yards with a 85% hit to miss ratio... not bad at all for a 9 year old with a med power .22 air gun.

In a nut shell this scope will cause more pain then it's worth. Always buy the best optics you can afford plain and simple... that oculus is a hidden gem for people looking for a excellent budget scope that can and will get the job done.
profile.summary: Many problems, 2 scopes both had same issues.

profile.description: The Gamo bone collector Cone pellet trap allows shooters to practice safely practically anywhere. The Cone design disassembles for transport and can be shot freestanding or can be mounted to a wall. The heavy duty steel construction keeps pellets where they're meant to be-provided the shooter does their part
profile.reviewText:
This trap handled my two Sub 12 FT pcps just fine.. I shot a few 100 rounds from both my FT sub 12 .177s and it looked good. That's my only two low power PCPS. I shot my FX Impact at 38ftlbs with the .22 barrel and within 10 shots it was eating it up, I slapped the .25 barrel on the Impact to see what it would do it with with JSB Kings at 52ftlbs and I had holes through it in 6 shots.. I grabbed my FX Boss tuned to 110ftlbs on high power and it had the whole back blew out in 3 shots.. I mean yeah it's a 110ftlb .30 cal lol and I knew the Boss would destroy this target no problems at all... BUT I did not expect the .22 and .25 to eat it up like that, the .22 at 38ftlbs would have ate a hole through it with in 30 shots... the .25 just did it a little quicker.. the .30 Impact barrel and my Boss would have holes in a new back stop with in 5 shots.. I know this isn't a big bore target and wouldn't have used the .30s on it if it held up to the small bores, problem is if your shooting a .177 or .22 at 15ftlbs or less you are going to have a lasting target, if you are at 20ftlbs or more it's not gonna last long, if your over 25ftlbs don't even waste your time you will have a ate out back stop within 100 shots. I finished it off with my Haley .257 airgun shooting at 410ftlbs blowing it all to heck and back in a few shots at 300 yards.
Here's the run down, if you have a 10 meter target rifle or pistol it will last forever as those guns are shooting at 4 to 5ftlbs. Any gun at or below 15 to 16ftlbs will be fine .177s at 15 to 16ftlbs are going to beat it up more then 15 to 16ftlb .22s due to the much high velocity the .177 is reaching to hit those energy levels but both will last a long time at the energy level, this targets are really suited for 10 meter type guns and Field Target sub 12ftlb guns and I bought another for that purpose, if you are over 20ftlbs don't even waste your money because it's not gonna even come close to lasting a full tin of pellets. There is no reason that this target should be sold without them stating that it can't handle guns shooting hotter then 16ftlbs at the absolute max.. that needs to be stated, if you take a stock .177 Benjamin Disco that gun at 19 to 21ftlbs depending on pellet will eat this target out in 50 shots a .22 Disco at 23 to 24ftlbs may get you a 100 shots before it's ate it out.. once again because the .177 is shooting much faster to hit the same energy levels it will tear through the metal faster. Point is a Disco is a low power PCP gun and a very well priced gun that is a lot of people's first PCP and most of those people are looking for a target like this and waste their money because Gamo don't list what is a safe energy level this trap can stop. The side plates on the one I destroyed I set up at 50 yards and shot them with a .22 highly tuned and moded Condor that at max power shoots at 80ftlbs but I was shooting Baracuda copper coated lead at 52ftlbs out of it and that gun would shoot slap through the side plates like it wasn't there... I dropped the power and shot again at 35ftlbs it still shot right through it, it finely stopped it at 27ftlbs but I shot the spot again at 27ftlbs and it blew right through it.. so two shots in the same spot at 27ftlbs and there's a hole in the trap, given the side plates aren't made to be shot head on at 90 degree angle but never the less it looks like they would have made this target be able to safe stop 50ftlb guns. The Crosman Target trap stops my .25s that run from 46 to 65ftlbs safely and without being beat up to bad.. the Crosman trap will stop any small bore Air rifle and last a while.. my crosman trap that I use for .22 has prolly 25 thousand shots on it and those guns run from 30 to 50ftlbs and it's still going strong. The Crosman target I use for the .25s has prolly 12 thousand rounds on it with guns that run from 46 to 65ftlbs and it's beat to heck but not no blow through and will likely go another 2000 to 3000 rounds before it has holes in it.. the one I use for my Impact. 30 barrel and FX Boss in .30 both guns making over 110ftlbs the Crosman trap held up to about 700 rounds before it had holes in it.. the Crosman trap costs twice as much but it's a 50 times better product for high power guns.
profile.summary: 5 stars for 15ftlb and less guns 1 star for above 25ftlb guns

profile.description: Advecta II for Cats (over 9 lbs.) contains the same active ingredients used in Advantage II for Cats. Advecta II is a convenient, easy-to-apply topical solution for the prevention and treatment of fleas on cats 8 weeks of age and older. Kills fleas on cats within 12 hours of application and continues to prevent reinfestations for up to 4 weeks. This is a waterproof, fragrance-free formula. EPA REG # 2596-181-91384.
profile.reviewText:
This stuff did make the fleas leave her, however my 4 year old very healthy Pom died two days after I put this on her, the day after I put it on her she acted not so playful and the next morning I found her dead... I don't know if this did it or not.. I have no idea all I do know is less then 48 hours after putting a few drops on her she was dead..
 I'm totally broken hearted she was our baby and we loved little Foxy very very much... I'm so sick to my stomach about it I can't hardly stand it... and the only thing I can go off of is this was the cause... I mean she was perfect and went the the vet every 3 months to be checked up (last check being 1.5 months ago and she had a clean health check up) she didn't act sick after I put it on her she just wasn't playful like normal the next day then the following morning roughly 40 hours after I put it on her she was dead laying on her pillow.. omg it's sickening and I'm going to find out if this caused it, the vet has blood samples from her and if this is the cause of my dogs death I will be suing the heck out of them... I'm disgraced in every possible meaning of the word...
profile.summary: 4 Y/O Pom died 40 hours after putting this on her, not sure this was cause or not but likely so

profile.description: This.22 caliber air pistol features an improved bolt design for easier cocking and loading. The rifled steel barrel provides greater accuracy and CO2 power provided by the 12 gram Power let provides 460 feet per second of power. A great pistol for target and plinking or small pests. Ergonomically designed ambidextrous grip fits the hand for perfect balance and comfort with checkering and a thumb rest on both grip panels. Rear sight is open and fully adjustable.
profile.reviewText: I bought this for the air tube mainly, 26.5 in barrel, custom wood stock, Prod trigger group, left handle long steel breech, custom cut, opened up, polished valve, 16 inch long Disco air tube, Leupold VX3 6.5-20x40 scope, Lother barrel cut to 26.5 inches and turned down and drilled, custom Flow through bolt, 4500psi carbon wrapped bottle reged to 1875psi... this gun is capable of shooting with any 1500 dollar .22 air rifle out there, on indoor range at 50 yards it's .25 ctc capable with JSB monsters and H&N Baracudas in 5.51 head size, with the Baracudas I'm shooting it 45 ftlbs and is capable of 55 ftlbs with the JSB Monsters, it's also superbly accurate with H&N Sniper mags 18 grainers at 43 ftlbs...6.5 inch TKO on her and she is quiet and but long as it's 26.5 inch barrel plus the LDC but it looks awesome.. it's a power house.. I'm building another in .25 cal just the same other then with a Baker Airguns Big Bore breech and a Lother .25 barrel that I will cut, turn down and drilled it will be exactly the same as the .22 just in .25 and 75 ftlb capable.. this is what makes these guns awesome, they are absolutely build able to your hearts content.. stock they are fun and cheap, however rarely do they stay stock.. I may so a 3000psi capable tube on the .25 and use a 3000 psi reged 4500psi tank with remote line as I do on the .22 and up to to 100 ftlb capable but drastically reducing shots per bottle.. the .22 on at 45 ftlbs on a 4500 psi Ninja bottle reg'ed to 1875 psi is good for 140 shots, the 16 inch tube filled to 2000psi is good for about 12 shoots untethered from the bottle but I never do that as the remote line and tank are light and easy to handle and lots of extremely consistent shots. A 100 ftlbs in .25 makes this a 100 yards yote capable gun that will likely hold sub MOA groups at 100 yards with solid rounds and retain tons of energy and with pellets will still be a 50 yards capable yote gun that will absolutely drive tacks.. with this gun a 400 dollar investment in upgrades will build you a gun that will compete with guns costing 2 to 3 times the 400 dollar total investment..
profile.summary: Amazing pistol that is not made to stay stock!! I love them

profile.description: The Graupner GR-12L HoTT (Hopping Telemetry Transmission) 2.4GHz 6 Channel receiver is designed with Graupner's unique telemetry technology, supporting bi-directional data transmission to give the user real-time sensor data. The use of up to 75 frequency hopping channels ensures extreme operating reliability and immunity to external interference. By utilizing the receiver's telemetry functions, telemetry data such as input and output signal strength, receiver temperature and voltage are transmitted real time in-flight to the transmitter for onscreen review and post flight analysis. Featuring a versatile one-chip integrated RF design and MCU (Microcontroller Unit) chip, the GR-12L receiver is lightweight, has a small form factor and is exceptionally affordable. Its small size, low weight and high quality make it ideal for use in small or low channel models. Other Graupner telemetry sensors can be plugged in through the Ch 5 port via a Y-lead for passing further real-time, in-flight data to the transmitter.
profile.reviewText:
Yes this receiver DOES support PWM and digital serial protocol SUMD, the description is incorrect stating the support analog PPM SUMO and SUMI as they DO NOT they are SUMD and PWM only that isn't any issue what so ever as all modern multirotor FC and Heli Flybarless units accept SUMD serial protocol. These are an incredible value for what they do with built in telemetry and ROCK SOLID link at longer distances then any other system ive used. I fly a  Hott MZ24 and a MC32 and a Futaba 18MZ. I prefer the Hott systems to the Fasst/Fasstest system. The Hott systems have the longest range of any 2.4 system I've ever see or used. Also the Hott systems are very fast, they keep up with my thumbs no problem when flying competition level 3d heli flights, systems with 20ms total latency I can notice and feel the lag, with the Hott systems on 10ms its more then fast enough, you will feel no latency at all if your a world class 3d heli pilot. I'm totally in love with my MZ24 and MC32 Hott systems. Plus the 3GX receivers as flybarless units on my 600, 700 and 800 size helis and they are as good as any stand alone FBL unit, they fly as good as my GY750s.

I have been flying Graupner HOTT since the MZ24 first hit USA shores and I will tell you this still to this day even with the single antenna non diversity GR-12L receivers I have never had a failsafe or glitches that I didn't force.. What I mean by force is leaving line of sight behind something at extended ranges.. I have took a plane that I had setup with a Eagletree system and return to home and flew out over 1.5 miles and still have 60 to 70% rssi value on the GR12L and on the GR24L on the same rig was out over 2.5 miles 380 feet AGL and still had around 55 to 60% rssi values no matter the orientation of the plane and in antennas. That is with the stock 2.4 antenna on the mz-24 the range on the hott systems is absolutely incredible for a 2.4 system and no antenna mods... I have been out over 4 miles LOS on the GR24L with just a simple windsurfer made from paper and foil on the transmitter antenna and avg 70 to 80% rssi.. my 18mz with a full range FASSTEST RX never had usable safe rssi values past 2.5 to 3 miles depending on area with a windsurfer.. the HOTT systems are Superior on latency range and system link nothing else on the market right now compares in the 2.4 Spectrum.
profile.summary: Hott systems are the best

profile.description: Crosman Lead Airgun Pellets - Per 1250 - Made in the USA
profile.reviewText: These are silly accurate pellets so long as you keep them sub 1100 fps, spring and gas piston guns will have a very hard time pushing these much past 1000. My pcp guns that have adjustable power I dial back to push these 1075fps and they will shoot with my all around fav .177 and .22 pellets JSB exact series and H&N FTTs, they aren't as accurate as the H&Ns and Jsbs but they are half the cost per shot and will hang with them 60 yards and in, after 60 the premium stuff will show the accuracy difference. I shoot these in the 7.9 and 10.5 grain versions and love them for everything except trying to shoot the smallest groups possible or shooting long range then it will be JSB Exacts, H&N FTT or Baracuda match that goes for .177 & .22. When you can get 1250 for under 20.00 they are a awesome value but they do have limits, so long as you understand those limits these are great pellets as are the 10.5s and shoot well in the vast majority of rifles and high power pistols out there.. if you can't dial the Fps down below 1100 with these the go with the 10.5s, these really do best in the 900 to 1075 range.. avoiding the trans-sonic and super sonic range is an absolute must for accuracy.. keep them 1075 or less and it's 9 outta 10 odds your gun will shoot them well to very well.
profile.summary: Awesome pellet so long as you understand its limits.

profile.description: This High Pressure Air Fill Whip device allows you to fill high pressure compressed air/nitrogen tanks from scuba tank. It can also work with ALL 3000psi Aluminum and Carbon Fiber wrapped Tanks. Extremely easy to use. All you need is RENT or BUY a scuba tank and your all set and ready to fill your own paintball tanks.
profile.reviewText: This is the best deal on a Scuba Fill Station for paint ball and PCP air guns on the market. It's cheaper then the Ninja unit and this one comes with a Fill whip included and the Ninja doesn't so it's less then half the cost on the Ninja when you factor the cost of the needed fill whip.  The gauge is dead on accurate and the whole unit whip included is very very high quality, it doesn't leak one bit and the whip has a female foster fitting attached so it will fill most pcp guns that don't use a proprietary fill probe, it will fill all crosman and Benjamin pcp guns and 85% of others on the market. Most importantly it handles over 4500 psi safely and that makes it be able to fill ANY pcp guns on the market as you aren't stuck to 3000 or less psi fill pressures, when the meter on this unit reads 3k the high accuracy manometer on my rifles read exactly 3k and that's very important so you can fill only watching the meter on the fill station instead on having to watch the meter on the tank/gun very important for safety. The foster fitting is of high quality and not some crappy cheap fitting, the hose is of high quality as well and shows,ZERO swelling on a 4400 psi fill and that is something that cheap hoses will do is slightly swell once they hit about 3200 psi and this hose shows zero swelling even at 4400 psi telling me it's a good quality hose and not some cheap hose they slapped on to save a few cents and cause safety issues, low quality stuff is a mega huge NO NO when dealing with then insanely high pressures this guns no days run on. I have already used it with compressed air and compressed nitrogen  and it's well worth the money and I will buy 6 more some I have one for each of my 2 3000 psi tanks and 4 4500 psi carbon wrapped tanks and one 4500 psi piggy tank I own so I don't need to swap them around as each tank will have its own station attached. I can not stress how good the value is with this unit, it's less then half of the other stations when you factor the included with this unit but not with the others fill whip and less then one forth the cost of the major brand stuff that is just rebranded Ninja units. This unit is 95% the same as the Ninja unit but this one feels like the machining is a little better on this unit and that's saying something as the machining on the Ninja unit is very good to begain with.  You have to be silly to spend double or 4x as much for the Ninja or Crosman/Benjamin units when this is of better quality. I have been in PCP for a long time and this is simply one of the best values in a very expensive hobby/sport.
profile.summary: Best value in a very high quality fill station on the market!!

profile.description: If you prize accuracy over anything else, you'll appreciate the consistent quality of H&N air gun pellets. H&N Crow Magnum is a very accurate pellet and hits hard with a lot of energy.
profile.reviewText: This is a devastating pellet on flesh, leaving the barrel at 34 ftlbs to 36 ftlbs this pellet is a monster on any small game inside of 75 yards... the B.C on this pellet I have calculated an average of .0248 and that's REALLY good when you see the gaping cup on its nose so they don't scrub energy to quickly and shoot fairly flat for what they are!! This pellet holds 1.5 moa groups at 75 yards in a gun that is known to shooting .40 moa at 75 yards so they fly decently at extended ranges and hold energy decently at extended ranges and at absolutely devastating on small game from 10 to 75 yards.. these would be excellent pellets even in a 20ftlb gun inside of 45 yards and at 35ftlbs that is a easily capable 75 yard pellet on small game if you and the gun can hold 1 to 1.25 inch groups at that range.
profile.summary: Devastating pellet on flesh, accurate and deadly

profile.description: Package : 2 pair 9443 Propellers
profile.reviewText: You can use these on 5mm prop adaptors if you find the right size prop adaptor... These are dang nice props I'm using on a 450 size flame wheel and they are awesome super thin and super stiff super good acro props... Decent AP props... These props ARE NOT 9 INCH PROPS they are 9.4 inch props so keep that in mind they will lift weight better then 9in props will but will shorten your flight times... Normal tear drop 9x4.7 props are not nearly as fast as these props are, they will GO they are very fast props... Very quiet to as they don't flex at all and at very thin.. I'm sure because they are thin they will not hold up to impact at all... Thin props fly better and are much quieter but the down side is they will not take abuse. The thin props are more efficient as well so a thick bladed 9.5 in prop of the same pitch will get shorter flight times vs a thin 9.5 of the same pitch.. These are way outta balance when you get them do not fly with out balancing them first its bad enough it will confuse your flight controller.. But for the quality and price these are fantastic acro props and decent AP props but IMHO just to stiff for a good AP prop. If I'm trying to get fluid smooth video even with a highend Gimble I do not use carbon props for that a quality set of composit props will make for much smoother video as they are a little less responsive then carbon props do to flex so they feel a little more spongy, that's BAD for acro and great for AP IMHO.  Overall these are a great value for a high quality nicely finished carbon acro prop and they are quiet so as not to disturb the people that are around where your flying.
profile.summary: they do their job well for the cost... very thin very stiff acro props that are finished well but way outta balance.

profile.description: To balance your prop simply make sure the prop balancer is placed on a level surface and the holder is level. Then place your prop in the holder and tighten them. Then use small pieces of scotch tape to add weight to the high blade until the prop sits level. That's it you now have a balanced prop!
profile.reviewText: This balancer is very nice quality and looks sweet with the carbon and anodized alum. Problem the collets are poorly balanced throwing off your balance then the magnets are not of equal power so when you balance it one way then flip it you have a completely different balance. The shaft doesn't rotate as freely as it should you can forget about even trying to balance a 4.5x4.5 it will sit and not move usless it's crazy outta balance. But even then being the mags hold at different levels of power and the collet are way outta balance it not moving makes no difference anyhow because your balance will be incorrect and truthfully not even close. It looks sweet it feels of high quality and for something of this quality to not make it work correctly is just bad business... I have bought 4 so its not just I got a bad one... Everyone have the same issue.
profile.summary: looks of great quality BUT thats where it ends.

profile.description: The distribution of weight makes this pellet extremely accurate at any distance. It also features higher penetration. Dome style 177 caliber pellet made with lead comes in quantity of 750.
profile.reviewText:
Update 11/03/16
I reported the issue with the pellets I order to Amazon for a refund and always Amazon was absolutely awesome at fixing the issue and refunding my money for a unusable product. As always Amazon gets 5 stars.. heck 10 stars as the best company in the world.. the product and Gamo as a whole get 1 star for allowing pellets of this horrid quality to reach the end user/Customer. Thank you Amazon for being the first rate stand up company that you are. You have truly brought back retailer/etailer quality to the market place and for that reason I buy from your amazing company almost exclusively and it would be totally exclusively if every product I needed was on prime and handled directly by Amazon.

Update 10/30/16
Yesterday I recieved a large order of pellets consisting of 5 tins of these from PA along with a case of H&N Sniper Magnums 18 grain and a case of JSB 18.13 as well as a case of JSB .22 Monster, a Case of .30 44.5 grain JSBs and a case of .25 JSB kings.
The 5 tins of these that I received are absolutely horrid... mold lines that are huge on every pellet in all 5 tins and little spikes of lead from the molds on the edge of the skirt on 95% of pellets in all 5 tins.. it's a shame, some tins are usable and those tins shoot really well in the guns I own that shoot them well but omg these 5 tins are literally a joke and in guns that shoot then very well normally shoot these all over the place and I shot then from every tin to check and ten shot groups that with these pellets are normally quarter inch center to center at 25 yards are grouping at close to a inch out of these tins, I'm sure it was a bad batch that PA got and all 5 tins I got are very likely the same LOT #  (Gamo doesn't label their lot number on the packaging so no way to know for sure, but I assume because normally they aren't nearly this bad they are never really good quality but some how shoot well.. but the normal poor quality compared to this would make the normal quality as good as H&N or JSB ect ect.. this are just horrible) so I assume I got all 5 tins from the same lot that are just really really bad, like a said the normal poor quality is MUCH better then these, I can't even believe these wasn't melted down and remade that are THAT bad..
My custom 1377 hybrid that normally shoots these lights out good will not group these under 3 inches for a 10 shot group at 50 yards and normally that would be sub half inch with the normal Pro mags I get. These fit the same so it's not the different molds it just no flashing was removed and the little spikes on the read of the skirt and throwing the balance off causing severe pellet sprial and this is not a guess, I was shooting with my scope mount and in slow motion out of the 137u hybrid, I shot some at only 600 fps so I can see them real good on the slo mo videos and the tins . Already had showed no sprial/corkscrewing at all out testing 10 pellets each out of 4 tins I already had, I then tested 10 pellets from each of the 5 new tins and EVERYONE severely corkscrewed/sprialed and the spiraling started with in ten feet of leaving the muzzle, that's something I never seen before.. normally pellets that sprial will not start the sprial until around 40 yards and then it will become more and more pronounced the farther they go but would not start until at least 30 yards but most times not until at least 40 yards... I hope this isn't the super bad quality that is going to become the normal with these pellets as I do have some guns that shoot them extremely well, even tho I don't understand how because the normal quality is still very poor but some how some way some of my guns shoot them super tight but if this is what you can expect to be normal now you can forget about it.. no gun is going to shoot them well, I tested the new tins in every .177 I have, and out of every PCP, multi and single pump pneumatics, world class break barrels including a super accurate TX200 and out of EVERY GUN pellet sprial happened some where between 5 feet to 15 feet from leaving the barrel, some guns it started a little farther out say 15ish to 20 feet out and some guns was spiraling as soon as it came in to view of the scope so within 5 feet.. once again NEVER before have I seen a pellet sprial that quickly.. even when playing around shooting RWS 7.0 grain wad cutters out of a Air Force Condor using a .25 valve and a .177 barrel (that .25 valve tuned to push JSB Kings from 40ftlbs and adjustable up to almost 80ftlbs with heavier solid projectiles) so I tuned the power down to low that would push a .25 JSB kings at 42ftlbs, mounted a .177 barrel and the 7.0 grain wad cutters and shot them at almost 1600fps and slow motion video via the scope cam to see how the pellet reacted and even those at 1600fps and being a wad cutter designed to fly no faster then 600 fps and that massive blast of Air severely deforming the skirt they still didn't start to sprial out until about 35 yards... so these starting to sprial almost as they leave the barrel and a speed slow enough that you almost can't get a pellet to sprial at that speed is truly a feat in its self lol.. point is I order 2 tins from a online auction site store seller, 2 from airgun Depot, 2 from Amazon and PA is replacing the 5 tins I got from them so I will test and see if it was a small issue with a shipment to PA or if it's a wide spread issue with this pellet now. The normal normal pellet quality is low and the mold lines are easily noticed on all pellets but not nearly as big as they was on these 5 tins and some small skirt issues on about 10% of a normal tin but on 95% of these 5 tins, so the bad quality is much worse and easily noticeable on these 5 tins.. if you order these and you look at then and there is a little point on one side at the end of the skirt and the big mold lines that almost look like wings then you got the bad batch that I did, if there's no point on the end of the skirt and the mold lines are easily noticeable BUT don't have flashing that runs down the side of the pellet from tip to end of skirt then you got the normal pellets that some how do shoot good in a lot of guns.. normally I don't buy anything but H&N, Air Arms, JSB, Crosman Brown Box Premier domes and some RWS pellets so pretty much only shoot top quality pellets but like I said I got a tin of these for free a long time ago and just tried them in a few guns because I had them and was shocked they shot lights out in some guns, I'm a person that preaches only buy high quality pellets but these for some crazy reason are the only non premium pellet that I will recommend because they do some how shoot good to extremely good in a lot of guns so I always keep a bunch on hand because they are cheap and good to great accuracy for plinking, when I'm trying to shoot the tightest groups possible then I deff don't use these for that (most times that's what I do, punch paper trying to shoot as close to 0.00 center to center 10 shot groups but do plink some times and that's where these at .005 cents per shot when bought at online airgun stores or .009 cent per shot on amazon) but for plinking at short distance they rock, and in some guns you can reach way out with good accuracy with these, that's gun and barrel dependent tho, if you have a tight choked barrel that stretches and reshapes these a lot they can be a good long range pellet but in non choked barrels that don't stretch the pellet much the BC is to low to be a good accurate pellet at long range (I say long range for a .177 is between 75 and 150 yards) the BC is high enough out of 15 or more ftlbs guns to shoot 50 yards no matter how the barrel reshapes the pellets, out past 75 these pellets really start to open up quick even in guns that shoot them lights out good at 50 or less yards. I'm very upset that a good highly accurate pellet in some of my guns may very well not be able to be bought any more... so I will be buying every tin I find at stores that I can see are of the normal quality.. easily seen because the tin lid is clear and so is the packaging and the seams and what not are so bad on these pellets that it's easy to see while in the packaging so it can buy the tins that are clean.. after the orders I made to check and see if they are the same from other etailers if they are all bad, I will send them back and never buy them online again, just what I can find and see in person at local stores buying up what I can find. A normal airgun weekend for me between all my .177, .22, .25 and .30 Air guns I normally shoot between 4 and 7000 shots on a weekend when we are having a Air gun shooting weekend and that's normally 2 a month (my beautiful young wife and I both love Airguns so when I say we I'm talking about her and i) between the two of us on a Airgun weekend we will go between 6 and 10,000 shots over a weekend.. so when I buy 3 or 4 thousand of a pellet some people think that's a lot of pellets and will last a long time, but for real airgun enthusiasts husband and wife a 10,000 shot weekend is a normal thing. I know family's that have 2 kids and the husband and wife that will go 25,000 shots over a weekend. Heck I've got 40,000 shots on my FX Impact when yoy combine all the barrels .177, .22, .25 and .30 and mines only 5 months old, my wife's Impact is 1.5 years old and has over and has over 100,000 shots on it in .22 and .25 (she doesn't use the .177 barrel never and just got her .30 barrel and hasn't shot it yet) she's went through 6 cases of .22 JSB 18.13 heavies at 20 tins per case and 500 pellets per tin in the last 8 months and 2 Cases of JSB Kings in .25. So gamo ruining these pellets is deff gonna cost me money because how I gotta go back to 4.50 head size H&N FTT 8.66 grain at 14 dollars a tin for 500 as the replacement for these, that's nearly 3x the cost per shot of these for no more performance over these out of the guns I have that like these... so it will now cost me 3x more to shoot our .177s that really liked these pellets because Gamo has really crappy QC.... that REALLY REALLY SUCKS... thank God I don't shoot a ton of .177 anymore anyhow so it's not that big a deal anyhow I guess... .177 still holds a special place in my heart tho, .177s are how I got in to the sport and how I God my super prissy, hot little young wife in to liking airguns as much as I do (not something you expect to see at airgun meets and shooting weekends is a 26 year old, perfect bodied beauty in a tiny mini skirt, halter top and showing her perfect tight little belly, heels of some sort be it normal high heels or boots with high heels, sexy makeup on and hair done perfectly, with her bench rested target gun and eye looking down the scope and her shooting ITTY bitty little groups that make most guys look bad.. the Airgun guys love her, the wife's of the airgun guys absolutely hate her because all the attention is focuses on her, talk about having a big head on your shoulders... well any time I'm at the range she's there with me and EVERY GUY OUT THERE wants to be me... so yes I have a huge head on my shoulders as a result lololol)
Update 10/22/16
I built a Crosman 1377 with a 24 in Lother barrel, MK-177 pump tube, B&M multishot breech (all of my 13xx and 22xx builds I use the B&M breech on, it's the best most solid barrel mounting system for the Crosman pump and co2 bolt pistol builds and it uses Mrod mags) Crosmods two stage match trigger and grip and their full shroud and custom low stress 4 screw machined barrel band, this gun is running a Mac1 Moded MK-177 valve it's been faced/flat topped and a Crosmods flat top piston. The value is moded for pump efficiency, fully ported and polished by Tim at Mac1 I cut an extended front end to the valve on the lathe as well as a titanium valve pin and derlin valve seat/check valve and custom made wife open transfer port that is very well sealed
The way the gun is built it's making 24ftlbs with H&N Sniper magnums 15 grain at 19 pumps thanks to the longer pump tube and flat topped valve and piston, the gun is an absolute monster for a pumper (I have another I'm building in .25 that should push 35ftlbs it's moreless the same build without the LW .177 barrel, I will be using a Baker Airguns .25 drop in barrel and it fits the B&M breech perfectly so I can use .25 Mrod mags in it to) anyhow I'm proud of the gun and that's why I'm rambling about it lol now to the pellet, this pellet shoots awesome in that gun at 16.8ftlbs thats 985fps and the really awesome part I build 16.8ftlbs at 9 pumps! The Sniper mags and JSB monsters both making 24 to 25ftlbs at 19 pumps, Baracuda Match 10.65s are 18ftlbs at 13 pumps and JSB 10.34s at 18ftlbs at 13 pumps as well all 4 of those pellets are capable of .25 inch groups at 50 yards when shooting at my range in my back yard that I built over time to 50 yards with 6 foot 1x6 fence on on both sides 10 feet apart so it blocks 95% of wind, in an open area 50 yard groups will open up to .35 to .45 inch 10 shot groups.. now these pellets are bang on shooting at 985 fps at 7.8 grains that's 16.8 ftlbs, I get an ES shooting a ten shot string with quality pellets of between 1.5 to 3.5 fps depending on the pellet and a SD of .5 to 1.5 fps again depending on pellet, with these the ES over ten is 7 fps and the SD is 3.5fps, so no where as consistent as high quality pellets but not bad and,for the price they rock the gun is shooting them to .5 in the closed 50 yard range for 10 shots and in a open area that opens up to about .8 to .85 of an inch ten shot groups.. these pellets shoot Lazer flat at 985 fps, it's 14.5 MOA low at 100 yards with a 20 yards zero and 10 shot groups are roughly 3.5 inches at 100 yards. But when a sub 8 grain pellet is stable and Flys well to 100 yards when shooting them WAY HOT at 985 they are doing something right, cheap pellets that perform extremely well in some guns.. the gun will group 10 Sniper mags 15 grainers at 100 yards around 1.5 to 1.75 inch so twice as tight as these but 3 times the cost per shot.
These are fantastic rat pellets, getting 1500 pellets for 15 dollars is a lot of rat shooting for hardly any cost, I have no issues taking large rats and 100 yards and in on calm windlass nights with more then enough retained energy to put them down quick even at very long ranges, my longest rat kill with this pellet from that Franken gun is 124 yards, it was a perfect lung shit and full pass through and it was a large rat, so plenty of energy at range, I would not take that shot on other pests but I hate rats so badly that if I didn't make a near instant kill I wouldn't feel to horrible however , do try my best to make every shot a super quick kill and anyone should even if it is on rats. Every time I try this pellet in a new gun I get a shock that how can a pellet that is as poorly made and inconsistent as these shoot as well as they do, it shocks me over and over again.

Updated 12/22/15 in a fully tuned Stainless HW97K with higher power spring it's fav pellets are Beeman Kodiak match 10.65 grain and it makes 27.1ftlb at 1071fps and at will hold sub half inch 50 yard 10 shot groups 90% of the time and every now and then throw a flier opening a ten shot group to 3/4 to 7/8 inch but that's one out of ten groups... with THIS pellet in this gun is making 22.7ftlbs @ 1130fps (thats REALLY fast for accuracy) but some how some way these pellets when weight sorted will shoot groups in the 3/4 inch ten shoots @ 50 yards and under 1 inch @ 50 yards UN-weight sorted... These pellets are not high quality by any means BUT some how they are impressively accurate at closer ranges and in a few guns fairly accurate out to 65 yards (most guns will not shoot them tight past 25 to 30 even high end pcp guns I guess it's the way the HW97 reshapes them massively upping there BC and keeps them shooting flat out to 50 and fairly tight out to 65 past that the groups open up VERY quickly and they scrub Ftlbs/fps SUPER FAST) these pellets are a rip off when Amazon breaks the 8.50usd per 750 of them but when they are 8 bucks for 750 they are worth a shot as they shoot well in a lot of guns they just don't shot flat at all and wind beats them up bad all due to the super low BC, but if your gun reshapes them just right they do shoot pretty flat and do decent in wind.. Will these replace JSBs, H&Ns, Beemans or Ein Juns HECK NO they won't replace CP magnum 10.5s or the lite 7.9s.. these pellets ARE of low quality, very inconsistent head size and weight, flashing all over the rear of skirt and big seam lines ect ect.. they just aren't of high quality BUT some how they shoot well up close they just aren't by any means a long range pellet as the BC is almost wadcutter low (it's amazing it's so low because the shape should have a fairly high BC) at the 14.xx Amazon is selling them at now it's a joke as you can buy 500 H&N FTTs for 13.xx shipped yes it's 250 more for 1 or 2 more dollars BUT the H&Ns will make these look worse then daisy Wadcutters. Anyhow Amazon has them for 8 dollars on prime for 750 and they are absolutely worth a try at that cost just due to the fact they shoot so well (remember up close) in so many guns once again I can not understand how.. it's just poorly executed molding on a very well designed pellets, if they molded these really well, kept weights close (within 3/100th a grain over a whole lot#, they are 6 to 8/100ths a grain off over a pack) and the sizes was within premium pellets head size consistency these would be some really good performing pellets for shooting ITTY bitty groups at 10 to 25 yards.

These pellets are ok, if you want accuracy then weight sorting is a absolute must as they are all over the place in weight.. the sizing is all over to, but some how they are accurate in a lot of guns of mine be it springers , gas rams, pcp and pcp pistols .. however there is a big stink in these pellets and that is they are sold as a long range pellet LOL the BC of these pellets are just slightly better then wad cutters it's 0.0120 and after the gun reshapes them it will jump up to a calculated avg of 0.0133 that is horrible for a "long range pellet plain old crosman wad cutters have a BC of 0.0100 and after being shot and reshaped by the gun it will have a avg BC of 0.0118 and that's a wad cutter.. a pointed pellet having a BC that is very close to a wad cutter is crazy lol.. these things drop like a rock they loose velocity and Ftlbs of energy at a rate that is hard to believe when it's a pointed pellet.. they are massively affected by wind because the stupid low BC and all around a pellet that is worthless past 30 yards and really it's happy even in a 20 ftlb gun at 20 yards max being 30 to 35 that's in very powerful guns.. now they are accurate is most guns I've shot them in inside of 30 yards.. they slow down so quickly and become unstable VERY quick so accuracy will fall off very quickly as it slows down... These pellets drops twice as much a Crosman premiere Lites 7.9g domes at 50 yards and 6 times as much at 100.. in a 20ftlb gun they they have lost 89% of there muzzle energy at 55 yards.. I can shot a crosman 7.9g domes out of a 12ftlb gun and these out of a 20ftlb gun and at 40 yards the crosmans have more energy then these even tho these started out with 8ftlbs more energy... It's crazy how bad the BC on these pellets are outside of wad cutters I have never seen a pellet of any design have a BC this poor. These are priced well per shot and do preform well in most guns and will do a great job at pest control in 15ftlb or higher guns at a MAX of 25 yards.. past that they scrub energy to quickly and won't kill effectively. I would NOT shoot a squirrel with a 20ftlb gun with these at 30 yards 25 would be my max and that's with a 20ftlb gun if it was a 15ftlb gun I would limit to 15 yards max.. I take small game with a fully tuned Berman R9 with a after market spring that is making it a 24ftlb gun and it eats up HN Baracuda match 10.65g at 80 yards with total efficiency in killing squirrels (a tough vermin to kill).. I laugh at how poor Gamo is at labeling product it's such a shame.. These pellets should he labeled as accurate in many guns to 20-30 yards and worthless for anything else.. If you want a close range accurate in many guns cheap pellet then this will fill the bill BUT if you use these to take animals and do so at any range you will be sorry and you will have wounded animals left to die a slow painful death.. btw penetrating ability of these rounds is extremely poor due to the fact the scrub energy at such a high rate they can't dig in deep.. they do mushroom well in mag power guns but only at close range.. would be a good low cost rat pellet in 15+ftlb guns inside of 15 yards but once again no more then that.. just understand you will hurt animals trying to hunt at any distance at all with these don't let the label fool you.. I know I said it many times like a broken record but I want anyone that reads this to understand they will harm and not quickly kill if used to hunt at distance.
profile.summary: Used to be decent pellets, Gamo products have literally went to garbage
