profile.reviewText:
I am editing my previous review on this little guitar after taking the time to properly set it up, dial it in and play it for a while.  I edited yet again as someone didn't appreciate my "gloating" over other guitars I own.  Sorry to offend YOU.
I made a knee jerk review (again) right after I got this.  But in all fairness I received my Gibson Les Paul on the same day, buying IT from my local music store and professionally set up, ready to go.  I was comparing apples and oranges, so to speak.  But now, even after comparing them to each other, they really aren't that far apart.
The Gibson is the best guitar I've ever owned and made my previous comparison based on it.  But this little baby is now my second favorite.
My other review was NOT FAIR!!!!!!  I paid a lot more for the Gibson and 149 bucks for this Epiphone.  Dollar for dollar this little Ephiphone is a steal!!!!  WOW!!!
I must honestly admit, the edge goes to my Gibson, but not by as much as you'd think.  This little Epiphone is an outstanding guitar, regardless of price.  If I were to play them each blindfolded I would never guess one was $149 guitar, ever!  The tone of the Epiphone is much like the Gibson Les Paul.  It's easy to play, comfortable and has a sweet sound.  I can either rock out with it or mellow out and play the blues or classic rock.
To be honest, I will probably play this Epiphone a LOT more than the Gibson.  After all, if I ding this one up I haven't broke the bank.  I think I'll tend to use this one a lot more than the other.
I am very happy with this Epiphone Les Paul and will proudly play and OWN it.  I am amazed they can make this thing for the money they charge.  I may purchase another one and put it away as I'm sure the price won't stay this low.  PLUS, I'll get another one in a different color!!  You can never have too many guitars..  I am going to an a pickguard to this one.  The finish on it is outstanding and I'd like to keep it that way.
If I were thinking of learning to play the guitar, this one is a no-brainer....BUY IT!!!
If you're an established player looking for a really nice practice guitar, I'd buy this one is a heartbeat.  I was shocked at how sweet it sounds, how good it looks, how comfortable and light it is and how well it plays.  Sure it was way out of tune and required a few height adjustments but now it is FANTASTIC.
New rule for me, no writing reviews until I own the product for at least one week!!!!!
profile.summary: After a proper set-up 5 stars  Damn nice guitar

profile.description: The Dean Boca 12-String Electric Guitar is great for that jangly classic rock sound.With the full twelve strings, a semi-hollow body with arched top, dual humbuckers, Grover tuners, adjustable bridge with stop bar tailpiece, and rosewood fretboard with dot markers. A sweet-playing axe that gets that Roger McGuinn sound to perfection.
profile.reviewText:
UNBELIEVABLE QUALITY AND VALUE.  I own many guitars, electric and acoustic, including one 12 sting acoustic but no 12 string electric.  I wanted a 12 string Electric guitar to experiment with just to see if it would be something I would actually use.  I do own a Rickenbacker 6 string and considered buying the Ric 12 but asked about and a good friend of mine who is also a luthier recommended I give this Dean a try.
I found a brand new one for an unbelievable low price so ordered it, a Trans Cherry Burst exactly like the one pictured here.  First, let me say the photo doesn't begin to do the guitar justice.  The paint is vibrant and the fit and finish is outstanding and flawless, better than you'd find on a guitar costing 5 times what this one sells for.  She is a bit neck heavy but there are 12 tuners so it has to be so I put a nice padded strap on and tuned it, then plugged it in......and WOW.  The sound brought me back to the early days of rock and roll.  NO feedback whatsoever, just pure 12 string harmony with a LOT of tone range from jangly to a deep throaty sound.  I am so impressed by this guitar and am 100% positive that I will play it often and it will be my go-to guitar for many songs that would benefit from that 12 string harmonic tone.  Another thing that surprised me was how well this thing stayed in tune, which is important when you're talking about 12 strings to adjust...  I could not be happier with my purchase.  I have NO plans on purchasing another 12 string, this one is perfect for what I need it for and I plan on using it well.  Sure, I love my Ric and would love to have a Ric 12 too but just can't see paying $2500+ for it when this $300 guitar sounds just as nice and looks as good too.  The ONLY reason I can see that anyone wouldn't buy this one opposed to a Ric would be for status.  I own too many Gibsons, American Fenders and other high end guitars to count but some of my favorites are the less expensive models, this being one of them.  If you are in the market for a 12 string Electric and unsure about what to buy, I give this one two thumbs up and highly recommend it.
profile.summary: UNBELIEVABLE QUALITY AND VALUE!!

profile.reviewText:
I was using the 350L bullets on my Strats but they just were not lasting long.  They showed wear almost immediately, requiring a string change every week.  That gets old in a hurry....
I didn't notice that these weren't bullets when I bought them, I wish I had bought the bullets as they just seem like a better fit for a Strat.
But, what I did like about these as that they are color coded for installation.  The ends are just the right size too.
These are just a bit heavier than the 350's but have the same sound.  So far, no notice of wear yet either so I think I finally found my perfect Fender Electric string.  They sound fantastic, bend well and were easy to install.  I have 3 Strats and 1 Telecaster, these will be my strings of choice for all of these.  I like buying the multi-packs.  They are inexpensive and each set is packaged individually.  I change strings often too, so always want plenty on hand.  Strings can make or break a guitar.  Put bad strings on a good guitar and it sounds bad.  Put good string on a cheap guitar, and it sounds better.  Put these on a high end guitar and you have the perfect formula.  Everyone has their own personal reference when it comes to strings, this is my choice for Fender Electrics.
5 stars.  The search is over

profile.reviewText:
I am revising my previous review on the 3250L's...
I have now only had these on my American Stratocaster for two weeks.  I loved them so much at first that I ordered 5 other sets and restrung several of my other Strats and other guitars.
BIG mistake.  Why am I so impatient?
These were unbelievable right out of the box, bring my Strat to life, giving it an unbelievable feel and sound.
But, with every positive, there's usually a negative....and wait for it.....wait for it...yup, there was.
I changed pickguards only two weeks after installing this on my Strat and noticed all three smaller strings. G,B &E were all flat on the fret side.  They were already worn out.  I suspected something as the sound had changed already too, becoming flat after only about a week.

Now, I'm so disappointed.  I'm going to step up to the 250's, then the 150 if I have to.  I love the sound but don't want to change strings every week.

profile.description: A calibrated three pickup set for Stratocaster players who are seeking that bright vintage tone from their modern set-up instruments
profile.reviewText:
I purchased these for my first custom build Stratocaster.  I own a Chinese Fender and an American Fender, the difference is night and day.  I considered purchasing Fender pickups for this build but after reading reviews decided to go with this Seymour Duncan trio of pickups.  I must say I am very happy I did.
After taking my time and building an unbelievable (I think so anyway) custom Stratocaster with the best of everything, I soldered in these pickups.  After filing, sanding and buffing the frets all level and adjusting everything right by the book I tentatively plugged it in.  To my surprise, silence....  no humming feedback as with some guitars.  I touched a string and had sound.  After going through all the switch selections and tone adjustments to make sure everything was working properly, I started playing.
The very first thing I noticed was that it sounded smooth and toned down a bit from my other Fenders.  Going through the pickups I noticed they had great range, reminded me of my Gibson Les Paul a bit.  I could make it twang and bark, but could also bring the blues and rock mellow tone in easily.
I prefer this OVER my Fender American HSS.  It looks better (maybe that's a stretch) and sounds superior to either of my other Stats or my American Telecaster, although the Telecaster is still one of my favorites.
I like these so much that I am going to purchase another set for my Chinese Fender and make a few other upgrades to it as I love the fit and finish of the guitar, it just doesn't sound and react like the American Stat.  For 130 bucks, that's a lot of bang for the buck.  I plan on upgrading a few other parts as well with it.
I am working on a Les Paul build and already have a set of Seymour Duncan Humbuckers ready to install in it, hoping for the same results.  I have another cheap off-brand Strat done up in red, white and blue (I'm a flag loving disabled veteran) and I hope I can do a few upgrades to it to make it sound as good as it looks.
I am excited about this product and won't hesitate to install these in any of my future projects.  Personally, I don't know how anyone could say anything bad about Seymour Duncan's except "you can't please all of the people all of the time".  I think 9 out of 10 people would probably agree with me.
I'd like to mention a few more things about the product.  I got the Seymour Duncan covers and installed them over the pickups, made them look awesome.  The also came packaged VERY well in a nice plastic container with the pickups set in foam molds, making it impossible to damage them in shipping.  I'm going to use them to store old pickups in.  These came with plenty of wire to make connections and great installation directions for soldering too, for use in any application.  I am very happy with the product.  I wish I could post a photo of my guitar, I'm so proud of it.
5 stars all day long and I will and already have bought more of these for a future project.  I wish they were a bit cheaper, but you get what you pay for.  It's a small price to pay to make a $400 guitar sound like a $2000 guitar.
profile.summary: Bought these for a custom build, glad I did

profile.description: .011-.052 Custom Light Gauge Acoustic Guitar Strings, Phosphor Bronze
profile.reviewText:
I will keep this short.  The price is unbelievable, it's nice to have three sets in a box and these are the best acoustic strings on the market.  That's only my opinion and everyone has one......so many will disagree.
I have an regular acoustic and an acoustic electric and strung both with these strings.  It made each guitar sound like a 3 thousand dollar guitar.  I find that most inexpensive guitars have cheap strings, most can be vastly improved with something as simple as new strings.  I really believe in these strings.  When I find a good thing, I am hooked and I will not use anything BUT these on anything acoustic.  On a guitar, strings are everything.  The tone feel and bend is what's important.  These are very light and VERY easy on the fingers, unlike clunky stock strings on most acoustics.  I guess they think you need big, think strings to produce volume....not so.  Some will disagree saying they break if they're too thin.  I would rather have a shorter life with strings, getting a pure beautiful, rich sound than have a long lasting flat string.  My thick stock strings were killing my fingers.  These are effortless to play and sound so sweet and mellow, just like an acoustic should sound.
Again, someone will chime in and bash me for saying this...but I would put my inexpensive Yamaha up against guitars costing 10 times what I paid.  I have no plans of changing brands now I've made the string switch.  Some say thin strings break easily, but you should change strings often anyway.  I can do a string change-over in about 15 minutes on a bad day.  It's worth the effort.  I don't plan on hammering my acoustic anyway.  That's what the Fender is for.  AND it's not that I'm cheap either.  I own 18 guitars, 16 of which are electrics.  3 Gibson Les Paul's, 2 Fender Strats (one American) a couple of Dillions (another great find) and some other nice guitars.
My Acoustic is just an inexpensive Yamaha 700 but is a very nice guitar for the money.  But after changing the strings it sounds like an expensive Martin.  It didn't take me long to throw a set of these on my acoustic electric and got the same results.
5 stars in my book, more if they'd allow that.  There are no other options unless someone gives me a set that blow me away.
profile.summary: IMHO the best acoustic strings sold at any price

profile.description: Seymour created this classic humbucker combination while in England in 1974, and it remains his favorite today: an SH-4 JB for the bridge and SH-2n Jazz Model for the neck. Together they provide one of the most versatile humbucker combinations available. The JB owes its popularity to over-wound coils, which provide high output with just the right amount of sustain and distortion--perfect for searing leads. Seymour matched the JB with a Jazz Model in the neck for calibrated output and a clear, bright sound--perfect for articulate rhythm playing. This set is great for everything from hard blues to heavy rock. It comes with four-conductor cable for trick switching options. A wiring diagram and mounting hardware are included.
profile.reviewText:
I have been building a custom Les Paul (from scratch), working many weeks on it, over a month.  After getting the body and paint just perfect, I did a silverburst finish, the pickups were a no-brainer.  I put the best pots and switches in it and this set of Seymour Duncan Humbuckers.  I put single coil Seymour Duncans in a Stratocaster I built and was totally happy with my selection.  I'm even going to upgrade a few Strats I own with them,
I finally plugged into an amp yesterday with my Les Paul and was blown away with the tones and sound these pickups generate.  100% thrilled that I chose these for my project.  So much so that I am considering purchasing a few extra sets for some other Pauls I own.
My only concern with these are that I was surprised how tiny the wiring is for the pickups.  I would have thought it would have had thicker gauge wire coming from the pickups but I'm sure there must be a good reason for it.
Also, the side cover wrap that covers wiring doesn't completely hide the wire wrapping around the pickups.  I would have thought pickups of this price and reputation would have had a bit more attention to detail.
But, when it comes right down to it, it's all about the sound and that's where these shine.  I haven't heard anything better and won't use anything but Seymour Duncans for builds or even upgrading.
Spend the few extra bucks and go with Seymour Duncan.  Pickups are not the place to try to save a few bucks.  Make sure you use quality pots as well, 500K are my recommendation.
5 stars and rockin' already!!!
profile.summary: Seymour Duncans....What more is there to say?  The BEST

profile.reviewText:
I own many practice amps and a Fender Mustang IV, none of which gave me the sound I wanted.

WOW...  THIS IS THE ONE  This amp is unbelievable.  100 Watts of power with a tube amp sound.

This is the greatest sounding amp I have heard or used, bar none.  I like the incled foot pedal, good for drastically changing the tome from pure to distorted rock in any increment you want.
I love the simplicity of this amp!!!  It look great too.  I knew I couldn't afford an expensive tube amp and didn't want a full stack to lug around and take up space.  This gives you both in a decent sized package.  She's still a big girl but you will not believe your ears when you hit the first note with this.

profile.description: Bone bridge saddle and nut 6 string acoustic guitar
profile.reviewText:
After reading many review on my Yamaha 700 acoustic guitar I have owned and played for 4 months, I finally took the advice of other consumers.  MANY people suggested changing the stock plastic nut and bridge saddle to improve tone.
This guitar is an incredible deal and piece the way it was.  I did put a light set of D'addario strings that made a world of difference.

profile.description: A formidably modified classic, the Modern Player Stratocaster HSH gives you a singing Strat middle pickup flanked by the powerful voice of humbucking neck and bridge pickups. Other features include a mahogany body, maple neck with "modern C" profile, 9.5"-radius rosewood fingerboard with 22 medium jumbo frets, five-way switching, three-ply black pickguard and black plastic control knobs, and two-point synchronized tremolo bridge with block saddles. Available in Charcoal Transparent and Crimson Red Transparent.
profile.reviewText:
First, the reason I didn't give this Fender a 5 Star review.  I love everything about this guitar except that it was in a box that was not padded or protected by bubble wrap or anything else to keep it from suffering any damage in shipment.  I thought the pickups were also a bit weak.
Now I've given the ONLY negatives, I will tell you what I REALLY think about this.
The pictures in no way do justice to this, it's a masterpiece!  I am so happy I chose this combination of wood, color, etc.  It is stunning!!!  The workmanship is flawless.  It fits my body like a glove, almost wrapping itself around me.  I love all of the controls of volume and tones on the guitar as well, making it possible to do most adjustments for sound choice on the guitar itself rather than constantly going to the amp, although at times you have to do that anyway, depending on what sound or effect you're looking for.
As a beginner, owning an acoustic first, let me tell you this thing is so much easier to play.  I can reach all of the chords with ease, the playability is so much easier than the acoustic.
I tried other electric guitars at my local music store before ordering this one here on Amazon and ordered this one because it fit me.  I am so anxious to get GOOD at playing this.  They say you can't teach an old dog new tricks but I'm 57 and just learning to play and loving every second.  I play until my fingers HURT!!!  I'm told that will go away but playing this makes me feel GOOD.  AND I actually sound good too.  I LOVE this thing.  So, I would HIGHLY recommend this to anyone but would also ask the manufacturer to pack it a bit better and an instruction manual would be nice as well for those of us who are beginners with electrics.
Time for a quick edit:  I loved this little Strat so much that I bought an American Strat to go with it.  WOW, what a difference between the two but it's cost a LOT more!!!  I've been playing for about two months and OMG, give me a music book and I'll play along.  Practice, practice, practice.  I'm into doing riffs and playing complete songs.  Still use this little Strat too, but use the American and I have a Gibson Les Paul.  I know, getting carried away.
I would still buy THIS guitar all over again, it's the nicest looking one I have.  My only complaint is that the pick guard already looks like crap but I have a new multi colored red one coming, it will really spice it up.  UPDATE...one year later and I own more guitars than I can count and will always have this one.  I now own quite a few American Strats as well and the difference is substantial...but so is the price.  I have modified this one a bit since buying it, adding a custom pickguard, changing a few external components and it still looks brand new.  This guitar is a great purchase.
profile.summary: Really a 5 star guitar but just a bit short of perfect

profile.description: The fret flattening kit used to find and level high frets to optimize your guitar's set up or remove fret buzz. The kit is composed of a hardwood sanding block crowned to fit most frets , a 3, 2 and 1-1/2" straight solid steel pins ( flat to within .001") to check for high frets, a piece of 220 and 400 grit sandpaper, and a small piece of steel wool. The pins are used to check flatness of the frets relative to each other. The 2 pin is for frets 12- 20 and the 1-1/2" dowel is for frets 21-24 where they are closer together. Place the pin across three frets and try to rock it back and forth. A clicking sound will reveal a high fret. Mask off the fingerboard with tape and lightly sand down the fret using the hardwood sanding block starting with 220 and progress to 400 grit sandpaper. Check for flatness with the pin again. When level, polish with #0000 steel wool. The sanding block can be easily modified to fit almost any fret wire. Place the sandpaper rough side up on the fingerboard over the fret. Rub the concave groove on the bottom of the block on the sandpaper on the fret until the shape mimics the fret. If the groove becomes too deep just sand off some material from the bottom, enough to keep it from touching the fingerboard, and you are ready to go! Kit is not used for neck flattening.
profile.reviewText:
I bought this to complete a few project guitars I am building and to check frets on my other guitars.
Yes, it works.  But, honestly folks...a couple tiny pieces of sandpaper and a piece of steel wool the size of a quarter doesn't cut it.  I guess you're paying for the two metal rollers used to rock back and forth on the frets, checking for being level.  A couple of sheer pins would work the same.  The piece of wood for wrapping the sand paper around to sand the frets isn't anything to write home about either.  This could have been something more ergonomically designed for the job.
Someone is making a killing selling these.  Probably cost 3 busks to put together the package and sells for 23 bucks.  Maybe I will design a GOOD alternative and sell them....
I give it 3 stars because it does get the job done, kind of.
profile.summary: It does work but WAY over priced

Philbrick's story telling is reminiscent of docudramas. He never leaves the documentarian-voice, and when expanding on material and leaving the main storyline of the Essex, it's for good reason...

I'm a slow reader, but I couldn't put this one down... The maps were helpful. I also kept my Kindle handy with a world-map atlas, as sometimes Philbrick refers to other ship-stories that are similar to the Essex's tragedy.

Philbrick has put visiting Nantucket on my bucket-list, and this book is the first of many Philbrick books on my shelf, I'm sure!

profile.reviewText:
After Kirk Cameron's Left Behind movies, there was a daunting fear over every Christian every time a faith-based film comes out. And in many cases, those fears were realized when watching the movies. But every now and then, few and far between, a good one comes out. This is definitely one of those times.

If non-believers get weird feeling around people who close their eyes and seemingly talk to "no one," and get together and sing songs about "someone who doesn't seem present," I have no idea why movie makers who seek to evangelize via media think it'll look better on the screen. God's Not Dead does a good job of bridging that gap between the non-believers perception and the believer's perception.

The scientific battle that the move plot centers on is nothing new, however perhaps if non-believers give the movie its duration time, perhaps like the audience in the movie will be somewhat moved to realize that God's existence is at least testable. The other subplots of the movie also show case real-life situations.

If I could, I would might take a half-star off, because is it just me, or is every couple presented in this film (okay, besides the Duck Dynasty clan) have one good, lovable person, and another broken, complete jerk? profile.summary: A Long-Needed Improvement in Faith-Based Movies

profile.description: Shot in HD with stunning footage from NASA and packed with state-of-the-art CGI graphics, this epic series explores the celestial skies to reveal the beauty and mysteries of the cosmos. The program delves into the catclysmic events that set the stage for life, visits sites where Earth's birthing process is still in evidence, portrays colliding celestial bodies and collapsing suns, and describes how the universe is awash in all sorts of strange liquids, from oceans of methane to blobs of alcohol floating in space to iron rain. This 17-DVD boxed set includes all 55 episodes of the series' first four seasons plus the feature-length documentary Beyond the Big Bang.
profile.reviewText:
My recollection of this series first coming out was better in the past. I've come to find that this series isn't really a series of facts. All it is, is a bunch of educated guessing, and furthermore, what you didn't expect: a bunch of non-educated fear-mongering. I swear, every show has an out-there theory: "What if the moon gets hit by an asteroid and hurls through space and wipes out a planet earth by first landing on an orphanage of innocent children?"

I kid you not, for whatever sick, demented reason, every show's punchline happens to be a "what-if" theory that planet earth is threatened? These are all way-out-there speculations that have so many factors to make the usually twisted scenario even half-way possible. Some of the shows go the whole way and tell you what they are, there are a few shows about possible apocalyptic occurrences. But when I'm watching a show about supposedly the moon, or the sun, and the show's punchline is about the people of earth dying because we didn't hug enough trees or look at the stars enough, this isn't a show about facts and the universe anymore. If this is what astrologers and scientists sit around and think about, I grieve over their families, if they have them.

Do yourself a favor, buy a telescope, or maybe a picture-book with a few anecdotes of what scientists DO know, don't waste your time on fear-mongering, sad, depressed scientists, and movie-makers that use both educated and very uneducated guesses about what they haven't figured out yet. Just like Americans to pretend they know when they really don't because, believe it or not, we don't have the ability to, yet.
profile.summary: If you're looking for facts, you won't find it here

profile.description: The Christmas Candleis a timeless holiday film for the entire family. Deep in the heart of the English countryside lies the enchanting village of Gladbury. Legend has it every twenty-five years an angel visits the village candlemaker and touches a single candle. Whoever lights the Christmas Candle will receive a miracle on Christmas Eve. But in 1890, at the dawn of the electric age, this centuries old legend may come to an end.When David Richmond (Hans Matheson), a progressive young minister from London arrives in Gladbury, the villagers discover a new formula for miracles; good deeds and acts of kindness. Now with a skeptic in the pulpit, the fiery candlemaker Edward Haddington (Sylvester McCoy) must fight to preserve his family's legacy. When the Christmas Candle goes missing the miraculous and human collide in the most astonishing Christmas the village of Gladbury has ever seen.
profile.reviewText:
I reviewed the book, stating that I liked the book better.

What I will give the movie is this:

+ The plot is "fleshed out" better, than it may be in Lucado's.
- However, the differences in character(s), and backstories that the movie has done, does, I believe, detriment to the story. The book is better.

+ Susan Boyle is a great singer... Just a great singer. Her first acting job capitalized on her great singing, because she didn't have great acting.

+ I watched the special features, and Lucado said, "We were glad to showcase the great work of the Salvation Army in this film," as the Reverend is working for them at the beginning. It reminded me that they were not show-cased in the book, and thus caused me to wonder, "Okay, sure, kudos to the Salvation Army, but it seems a rather unrelated plot point," and it truly is.

The movie adds a plot line that isn't in the book, and that is the community's aversion to electricity. It seems rather unrelated and unnecessary.

The book's character development of the Reverend, to me, is much more preferable than the movie's character development, especially the book Reverend's "dark past" compared to the movie's version of it.

I felt like the Christmas Candle movie was just hoping to capitalize off of Downton Abbey-esque motif, and settled with, I think, a sad treatment of Lucado's rich book. I am surprised to see Lucado's kudos of the story.

It sits on my shelf, and occasionally comes out around Christmas to remind me of how cheesy it is, and how I should probably just be rid of the movie and be content with the book.
profile.summary: The Book is Better

profile.description: Prepare to go behind the scenes of one of the nation's most tragic and inexplicable murders. By allappearances, Scott and Laci Peterson were the perfect couple - until Christmas Eve 2002, when 28-year-old Laci went missing while walking her dog. After an agonizing almost four-month search, her body, and that of her unborn child were found in the Richmond marina at Point Isabel. As the investigation and the media frenzy came to a shocking head, Scott was arrested for the homicide. Now, as the nation stands in wait, and Scott stands accused, The Perfect Husband tracks the events leading up to Laci's disappearance and deaththrough the people who knew them best.
profile.reviewText:
I was just 12 years old when this story hit the news channels. I was already watching bio channel's true crime shows at the time, and thus seeing this unfold in real time was sometimes scary as I realize that what I see on the bio channel is what this story of the Petersons were for many families and nations before.

As I grew older, this case imprinted on my mind as it did for many Americans. What I didn't do, is sell my soul to the thing, and read in a frenzy everything I could on it. However, this movie I caught at age 13 on TV was always on my mind too... Now older, I ordered it just to see it again, as well as read Scott's sister's book.

I found that the movie, as most movies do, took a few liberties, never the less it captured the "spirit" of the time, with wanting to believe a man is innocent, until - like the constitution says - is proven guilty. And boy is that proven.

 Maybe the makers did it out of convince or respect, or who knows - maybe they were forced. But I think authenticity would've given it another star on my review. Reading Anne Bird's book will fill in the blanks where this movie left them. But a few events, times, places, and even names were changed. There is one fictional prominent character in the movie that I think was supposed to be Anne Bird. And the movie changed sexes. Maybe that was Anne's personal wish. But if not, I always question movie-makers intent when they seek to make a move "inspired" or "based" or simply crediting it as "a real story," knowing full well it's not entirely true or real.
profile.summary: The Imperfect Representation of the Laci Peterson Story

profile.description: A young boy learns that he has extraordinary powers and is not of this Earth. As a young man, he journeys to discover where he came from and what he was sent here to do. But the hero in him must emerge if he is to save the world from annihilation and become the symbol of hope for all mankind.
profile.reviewText:
So I watched this twice in theaters... and it was that second time, and definitely that third time when I watched it home that I began to realize that 45 minutes or more of just pure fighting... literally... is just too much for a person to sit through. It was a good first viewing (obviously as I watched it again)... but it quickly becomes a long sit for anyone to just watch a bunch of fighting.

If you prefer watching MMA or fighting, okay, all the more kudos.

It is, by far, probably the best Superman movie on film, but at the same time, I feel like Man of Steel was just competing against Avengers in terms of "How do we make this epic?" And apparently, that was to completely copy the alien-invasion story from Avengers, and throw in a Neo vs. Smith from Matrix 3 fight sequence with the names of Superman and Zod and call it epic. That formula worked and people bought it... but at the same time in retrospect it is a let down that the makers couldn't come up with something a little more original.

I'll be interested in seeing how Batman vs. Superman tops it, and hope that it enjoys the success of sequel-toppers of the Nolan Batman franchise instead of joining the sad category of sequel-letdowns...
profile.summary: Hits Like a Ton of Bricks, Then Turns into a House of Clay...

profile.description: Lewis and Clark are joined by John Ordway and Patrick Gas in their expedition to find the Pacific coast. Players will take on the role of the famous explorers as they plot new routes, negotiate with American Indian tribes and record their adventures in their field journals. The more exciting your journey, the more points you'll earn at the end of the game. This dice rolling strategy story builds on Lewis & Clark The Expedition. Combine your dice to complete objectives or steal your opponents' dice and use them for your goals.
profile.reviewText:
I have been getting in the habit of playing board games more often, probably since I discovered Dominion. I am a history buff, and live in an area that Lewis and Clark traveled through. I find this to be a fun game. It takes awhile (like a good game-play, or maybe 2 games played) to learn the ins, outs, and hows to play this. But once learned, it is a VERY fun game.

My wife doesn't really care for it, because it's really involved. But if you're a game-player, you'll like it.

I don't play LOTS AND LOTS of board games, but this game is unique for me, in that it utilizes dice (with pictures, not dots or numbers), and includes many different factors to bring about the completion of the game...whether it be "activating" actions with dice, or getting special rules through help-cards (called tribal cards) in this game.

I would encourage potential buyers to check out a review on Youtube (such as gameboygeek) and then make the decision. Then, like I did, when you have the board in front of you, watch the review again to get a visual help on how to play the game.

PROS -
+ Very original, I think
+ Great combination history, strategy, and fun
+ Great artwork and aesthetics... there are even clips of journal entries in the instruction booklet

SETBACKS -
+ LONG learning time
+ Not for the "causal" board gamer
profile.summary: Great Combination of Board-game playing, History, and fun!

profile.description: Dustin Kensrue, the frontman of the critically acclaimed alternative rock band Thrice, who have sold 1.4 million albums, is teaming up with Mars Hill Music and BEC Recordings to release his first full length solo album The Water and the Blood. Kensrue, now the Worship Pastor of Mars Hill Church's Bellevue location presents 11 songs with robust gospel centered lyrics to rally and encourage the church.
profile.reviewText:
There is something incredibly unique about Kensrue's music. It took awhile to grow on me. At first listen I was disappointed, because since Mars Hill's release of the Citizens, I've anticipated every release. However, after second listen, I was immerses in Kensrue's truthful, and rich theological lyrics. My favorite is "God is Good," followed closely by "Come, Lord Jesus." His remake of Rock of Ages, and Suffering Servant -- many of his songs get in your head for hours, as well as become anthems to praise God with no matter where you're at.

It feels like a new breed of worship music that the Christian music scene desperately needs. It's as rich and filling as the theology of old hymns finally mixed with the creative power that music today can bring. I highly recommend it over the names of contemporary praise music today.
profile.summary: It Feels Like a New Old-Fashioned

Okay. Matthew's dead. My favorite reason for watching Downton Abbey: the romance of Matthew and Mary. But Don Stevens wanted to go, and he felt like there's nothing left to tell, and he couldn't be put into the position of being out of the spotlight perhaps.. With Matthew around and the other events that took place in Season 4, it would've been better... however...

This season just grew darker. As people may've mentioned. profile.description: Gathering together today's most respected Christian artists and songwriters, Jesus, Firm Foundation: Hymns of Worship offers a fresh perspective on timeless hymns such as "Blessed Assurance" and "Turn Your Eyes Upon Jesus" re-imagined by favorite artists Casting Crowns, Newsboys, Brandon Heath, Matthew West and many more! The title track, "Jesus, Firm Foundation" featuring Mark Hall (Casting Crowns), Mike Donehey (Tenth Avenue North), Steven Curtis Chapman and Mandisa, releases to radio January 2013.
profile.reviewText:
These were good rearrangements of classics.

However nothing jumps out such as when a Passion CD or Chris Tomlin or Matt Redman puts out a re-vamped classic.

Nevertheless I do listen to this CD, some favorites are "Nothing But the Blood" by Andy Cherry - which I will probably purchase his CD next thanks to this one.

"It is Well" by Brandon Heath, his additions are nice.

And "Blessed Assurance" by Matthew West.

Newsboys "Jesus Paid it All" is good, but it's nothing new or different from Newsboys.. which could be advantageous to say their sound is distinct, or could be considered disadvantageous because they cannot branch out. I give it four stars because it delivers good, but I don't believe it's the best these musical artists could deliver.
profile.summary: A Little Above Typical

profile.description: The CSI franchise continues to thrive with the second season of CSI: NY, which aired on CBS during the 2005-2006 season. The kickoff episode is filled with lots of drama--but not much suspense--as the investigators delve into the death of a jewelry designer who is found wearing an $8 million diamond bra. The other case involves the shooting of a thrill seeker who is killed while climbing up a skyscraper. Though neither crime is particularly challenging for the viewer to solve, it's the little things that make the series an enjoyable viewing experience. A mosquito, for instance, provides more data on a potential killer than fingerprints or witnesses. And in a later episode, a discarded coffee mug provides the evidence to convict someone of killing a plastic surgeon. There is drama within the department as well: One of the investigators, who gets too caught up in a rape case, tampers with the forensic evidence and is told to resign from the department. While the chemistry between the main characters isn't as strong as it is with the cast of the original CSI--starring William Petersen and Marg Helgenberger--Gary Sinise (Forrest Gump, Apollo 13) makes a strong presence as lead investigator Mac Taylor. And Detective Don Flack (Eddie Cahill) gets to show more dimension in a storyline where he's trapped inside a panic room. All 24 episodes are included on this 6-disc set, which includes audio commentary on five episodes, as well as a handful of behind-the-scenes featurettes. This season also includes a little stunt casting, with David Caruso (playing his CSI: Miami character Horatio Crane) in a compelling crossover episode that involves the kidnapping of a young girl. Both strong silent types, Horatio and Mac make for a wonderful team, despite their different methods. --Jae-Ha Kim
profile.reviewText:
Why do good shows feel like that in order to be watched in successor seasons feel like they need to beef up their sexuality? CSI: NY will hit a string of shows every now and then that feel like every show has either a modeling-studio, or deals with prostitutes, or people going above and beyond PDA in public places. Granted, you are DEALING with the slums of NY, but I definitely know it's intentional in trying to sell with sex.

CSI:NY has good story lines, and I like it's shows it's just I feel like season 2 is a leap into more sexuality that it really did extremely fine without. The raunchier scenes are perhaps fewer and farer between, so you're still more about the CSInvestigating itself, but still. I just felt like this was not as prevalent in season one, I could be wrong, and just didn't notice it.
profile.summary: Sill a CSI Fan, but....

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "Thanks for reading! I hope you enjoy the Nichelle Clarke series. output:
Nichelle Clark is back and has the Jimmy Choo shoes to prove it.  She is doing an interview as a favor for a friend.  Co-worker, Grant Parker has asked Nicey to interview legendary football player Tony Okerson.  It is an exclusive for the Richmond Telegraph.  So why isn't Nicey thrilled with the story?  First - the story is about the suicide death of Tonys son TJ.  Second  Nicey is under the weather  this ace crime reporter can hardly breathe.

Nicey drives all the way to Mathews County to the Okerson home located on Gyynns Island.  The family couldn't have been nicer.  They answered all Nichelles questions.  However, something seems to be missing from the story.  Niceys inner Lois Lane is telling her this might not be a suicide. Her gut feelings are rarely wrong.  She will be walking on egg shells during this investigation.  Nichelle wants to find the truth  but does not want to bring more pain to an already grieving family.  When the sheriff calls Nicey and tells her there has been a second death, she knows that she will have to step up her game.  Nichelle had better be very careful, she could end up shoeless.

Things to ponder:  Was a murder made to look like a suicide? Could a jealous teammate also be a murderer?  Was there a copycat suicide?  Are you Team Joey or Team Kyle?

LynDee Walker has done it again.  She has written a compelling mystery that kept me glued to the pages of the book.  I could not put this book down.  It was a page-turner right from the start.  Dealing with a sobering issue like teen suicide can be rough.  The author has injected plenty of humor and a hunk that cooks to keep the story light.  In my opinion, this is by far the best in the series.  LynDee has given our intrepid reporter a bad sinus infection and rivals that either want her story or her job.  I cant wait to see where Nichelles next investigation will take her.

Peggy Lee is back.  She has a new lead into the death of her husband John.  Her internet friend Nightflyer teamed her with Harry Fletcher. Oh he calls her all right  bring the bolt cutters.  He forgot to take them with him.  So Peggy gets them out of the car.  She hears a wheezing sound.  So she high tails it for Unit 34.  She arrives to find Harry is not there.  Soon after, the police arrive and take her down to the station.  Good thing she knows many of the police on duty or she surely would have been booked on breaking and entering charges.  She still has to explain all this to her husband Steve Newsome.  You know Steve is not going to be thrilled to find out what Peggy has been up to with Harry.

There is peace in Peggys household and she gets a lift from neighbor Walter. She does plan on stopping at Harrys motel before going to the auction.  Walter is not happy to be driving his Bentley to such a seedy area.  Peggy tells him not to wait  she and Harry will take a cab to the auction.  This is not to be.  There is no answer to her knocking and Peggy tries the door knob.  The door opens and Peggy still does not see Harry.  Last place to search is the bathroom. Peggy had better be very careful tracking down the murderer or she could end up with dead roots.

Things to ponder:  What is in Storage Unit #34?  Was the buyer the same person Peggy heard wheezing the night before?  Where is the bottle of scotch?  Is Harrys death connected to Peggys late husband Johns murder?

The authors have thoughtfully included a yummy recipe and some gardening tips.  So if you like a mystery that gets your hands dirty, then you should be reading Lethal Lily.

profile.reviewText:
The village of Mount Penn was not the quiet friendly town everyone thought it was.  Drugs were being sold by Carl Lewis right up the road.  Patrick Goody and Jerry Foster were arrested when the police found a box of illegal drugs in the flatbed of Jerry's pickup truck.  Roger Ballard looked like he had been in a fight.  Worst of all Lillie Mae Harris found a dead body on her first hike of the season!  Before you know it Charlie Warren, a part of the Antioch Police Force, has Lillie Mae with him as he questions the citizens of Mount Penn. Will the ladies of the Thursday Morning Breakfast Club be able to figure out whodunit? Things to ponder:  How did the drugs get into Jerry Foster's truck? Who did Roger fight with?  Where is Roger?

I hope the author is busy plotting and writing the next in the series so I don't have to wait too long to find out what is going on in Mount Penn.  So if you are like me and love finding a new mystery series, then you should be reading the Thursday Morning Breakfast (And Murder) Club.

profile.reviewText:
Former psychologist and now image consultant Allison Campbell has taken on the job of reinventing Congressman Hank McBride's 15 year old daughter Maggie.  The Congressman is throwing his hat in the ring to run for the Senate with an eye to a future presidential run.  Maggie will need to fit his idea of the "perfect" daughter.  Allison agrees to work with Maggie.  She sees a frightened girl underneath all the Goth makeup.

 A phone call from police Lt Mark Helms gets Allison involved in the Main Line Murder of divorce lawyer Arnie Feldman.  Not only was his wife Sasha one of her clients but her ex mother-in-law Mia had threatened Arnie during her own divorce proceedings.  Allison's assistant, Vaughn, found out that this was no ordinary murder - Arnie Feldman was tortured to death during the ritualistic deed.  When Maggie McBride becomes the prime suspect of the police, Allison has to help prove her innocent.

Things to ponder:  Will helping Maggie help Allison come to terms with her own past?  Could Mia's threats to Arnie have festered into his murder? Will Allison be able to help Maggie?

This debut novel from Wendy Tyson has me saying - I can't wait to see where she will go from here.  This first Allison Campbell mystery takes you on a journey into the lives of the Main Line rich of Philadelphia.  This is not a cozy mystery but much more of a thriller. I liked that the story is told from several points of view.  It is very well plotted and will keep you guessing until the very end. This book will not let you put it down.  You will be riveted to the edge of your seat.  I loved this fast-paced page turner.  All I can say is that Henery Press has found another winning author. So, if you like your mystery written by a wonderful new voice, then you should be reading Killer Image.

profile.reviewText:
Tina Shaw finally has her first job as a professional organizer for her friend Rachel Palmer. Tina has her hands full since Rachel seems like more like a hoarder. Finally, they have some boxes to move and Rachel suggests the nursery. However, it doesn't look like there will be enough room there to store the boxes since they find Rachel's sister Crystal dead on the floor.

The police determine that Crystal was killed with a 22 caliber gun. They have a few more questions for Tina including does she own a gun? Well she does own a gun and it is missing! The police also know about an argument that Tina had with Crystal the week before. Tina is starting to look like a primary suspect in the case. This was a fun fast-paced read. A real page turner.  In addition to finding out whodunit, I needed to find out about all the secrets that kept popping up in the book.  This book had more twists and turns than a ball of yarn my cat has gotten into. So if you are a little disorganized like I am, then Organized To Death is a book you should read.

profile.description: Barb is a freelance writer, corporate minion, over-scheduled parent and connoisseur of fine chocolate. A second-generation journalist, her work has appeared in the Chicago Tribune and its affiliates as well as Mom.Me. profile.reviewText:
Mattie Ross writes a column for the Chicago Gazette.  Her column, The Plate Spinner, gives advice about parenting and juggling all your other commitments.  She is not a wife or mother.  The pictures in her office are of her sisters family.  Mattie is in major debt due to the wedding that never happened.  Her almost groom never showed up at the church.

Now her boss has given her a new assignment that will reap a big bonus and a raise.  She has ten months to train and compete in the Chicago Marathon.  Known as Fatty Mattie at school, has this woman with self-doubts reeling.  Worst of all her coach is none other than the twin brother of her ex-fianc.  Mattie has never liked Nick.  She sees no reason to start now.  Can these two people who have been kicked to the curb learn to trust each other and go the distance?

A new author and a charming new series - it is like having a second birthday with all the goodies. Romance readers will be thrilled to find a new voice and a delightful new series.  It is a well-plotted page-turner that pulled me in right from the beginning.  I am looking forward to reading many more books in this new and appealing series.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "Samsung 27" Curved Monitor". The summary of the review text is "Very nice monitor, but some problems for me.".
output:
When I first got this monitor I thought I wouldn't be able to use it. It was so big I felt I'd never get used to it. I went from running a 19/17" monitor pair to running a 27/19" pair of monitors. The difference was enormous. Luckily it didn't take too long to get used to the larger screen, though a month later I'm still not optimally set up or adjusted.

The monitor has a great picture, game mode does make things brighter and yes, it's 27". It's huge. Once I was connected my computer did recognize it properly and it did select the proper native resolution. The best resolution doesn't use full screen but leaves one inch or so on all sides dark. You can get full screen but it isn't a great resolution.

Now for the issues I experienced. My video card is dvi out only, so I had to purchase a dvi to hdmi cable(dvi to DP oddly didn't work for me). Also using the hdmi cable I have found that the audio in for the built in speaker doesn't seem to work. Makes sense as the monitor likely expects hdmi to deliver both audio and video. Result my audio is coming from the speaker on the smaller monitor which is a little odd. My final complaint is relatively minor, game mode does not stay on. When the monitor goes to sleep and you wake it up the next morning game mode is turned off again.

If I hadn't had these issues this would be a 5 star monitor for me. Huge size, great picture. Lots of input options but sadly not the one my video card had.

profile.description: HEADPHONES WITH MICROPHONES HD Dolby(R) Digital Plus enhanced sound via exclusive Jabra(R) sound app; In-line controls for easy music & call management; Tough, shatterproof & constructed for ultimate portability; Lightweight & flexible with steel hinges & aluminum frame; Foldable design for quick & easy storage; Premium comfort for extended wear; Memory foam ear cups & padded headband; White
profile.reviewText:
3.5 stars

Since my original iPhone ear buds gave up the ghost I haven't had a set that had controls on the cable, a feature I really missed. Since then I have gone through many sets of earbuds and they all fell to the same flaw, the cable wearing out where it connects to the iPhone. So I was really excited to get these headphones and see how they worked.

The cable is thick and covered in fabric, as a bonus the connectors to the headphones and the iPhone are encased in hard plastic. No cable bending and wearing out at these critical junction points. This should last for quite some time and not fail due to the wear and tear of the cable bending at these two places. The on cable controls work well though perhaps not intuitively. There are three buttons. The top button for volume increase, the bottom button for volume decrease, the middle button is a multi-function button where one press will pause/resume the song being played or answer the phone, two presses will skip forward to the next song, three will skip back. The buttons work as described without issue.

The controls also feature a microphone enabling you to answer the phone and speak "hands-free", I had someone call me and they told me they heard me loud and clear using the built in microphone.

The sound is very good. Even using the normal iTunes player it is good. Using the Jabra app it is even better, though much louder. The app imports your iTunes library and playlists and allows you to use them, even with shuffle with a few extra options, a dolby sound function, a surround sound function and a variety of equalizers to play with. The dolby funcion does give a fuller, deeper sound and I enjoy using this. The surround sound function also gives a fuller sound though I opted to disable this. I prefer to hear the stereo mix the artist designed rather than have the app mixing things up. The equalizers are fun and I've settled on the "rock" equalizer. Some caveats do exist though, the importing of the library/playlists is slow, though a shuffle does exist you must first select a song to play then skip forward, no random from the start, using the app the volume is loud, in fact when I'm sitting home alone I use iTunes at the lowest volume because the headphones are so loud and using the Jabra app the volume even at the lowest setting is too loud.

My main issue is the fit, maybe my head is freakishly shaped, maybe it is to thin but I have a real problem keeping the headphones on. If I bend my head forward to look down at something, bend over to pick up after my dog the headphones will almost always start sliding off. If my hair happens to be underneath the headphones over my ear they slide off very quickly. As great as the sound is if the headphones can't stay on my head without issue then they become a less viable solution. My primary use of the headphones is for walking my dog, and reading in bed, using the headphones and music to lessen any noises from my wife blasting the television. It does the second very well, the first less so. I'm thining jogging or running in these headphones would be completely out of the question, at least for me.

In conclusion these are really ruggedly built headphones with great sound and controls on the headphone cable that work really well, the sound app is really good at enhancing the music you play but for me the fit is hampering the ability to wear them to do things I might like to do.
profile.summary: Great Sound, Poor Fit

profile.description: Make the Most of Your Mobile Lifestyle. Sleek, slim, and stylish - the PowerPack CC1800 rechargeable battery extends the life of your smartphone by up to one full charge. The ultra thin design resembles a credit card. The included Micro-USB cable plugs in to keep your Android smartphones charged, and also lets you easily recharge your Power Pack. iPhone users have the benefit of using their existing Apple charging cable for connection to the Power Pack. Know when it's time to recharge with the simple LED indicator, which uses four lights to display the Power Pack's battery level status. Stay charged and stay in touch. Varies by device
profile.reviewText:
This is a nice compact reserve tank for your phone, more compact if it isn't an iPhone.

Though the battery comes mostly completely charged, I charged it to full before use to see just how much of a charge it would give my iPhone 6. It took 1 hour to drain the charger fully and that 1 hour gave me 53% of a full charge on my iPhone 6(2% to 55%). So I was charging at close to 1% a minute. A 50% charge isn't a full tank, but it's pretty good and should be able to give you at least a few more hours of full use or a longer time on idle.

Myself, I want this for my Disney trips, when I'm at the park for a full day of 12+ hours I like to take photos and post them to facebook at each attraction to make my friends jealous. Taking pics, uploading and location services do eat battery so the idea of a pocket sized charger is very appealing. Something you can keep in your pocket and snake a small cable out to the phone to charge it up after it has been drained. This is credit card sized and does fit in the definition of pocket sized, and for a non-iPhone you could just run a cable to it. However, to charge an iPhone you must use the USB to iPhone cable the iphone came with along with a dongle attachment to let your USB cable attach to the battery. This is where it gets a bit precarious. The dongle is about 1x2 inches and I'm worried that just keeping it in my pocket and walking around charging might end up with it being snapped off.

Also, instructions must be followed. Plug the dongle into the battery last. That is, plug your iPhone into its cable, plug the USB end into the dongle, then plug the dongle into the battery. Only then will it charge. Plugging the dongle into the battery then plugging the cable into the dongle will not result in your iPhone being charged.

The battery comes with two cables, one USB cable to charge itself, and one cable to charge and Android phone. Brief but sufficient instructions are included on the use of the battery but the only real instruction necessary was what I mentioned above, complete your circuit by connecting the dongle to the battery last.

Though with the dongle it isn't as safely small and portable as I'd like it is still a nice solution to rescue your battery with a half charge when you are out for a day. It is definitely worth the $20.00 to have this reserve power available when you need it.
profile.summary: iPhone 6 Review-Compact Reserve tank with a caveat

Built to toast 50% faster than previous BLACK+DECKER models, this toaster delivers efficient performance with a variety of shade options. The extra-wide slots make it easy to fit any type of bread, and the extended lift ensures you retrieve toasted items safely. Bagel and frozen functions let you customize the toaster for special tasks, delivering perfectly toasted results every time. Start your day out right with the trusted name in home appliances, BLACK+DECKER.
profile.reviewText:
3.5 stars bumped to 4, but really, 3.5 stars. This isn't a 4 star toaster.

The good: It has a small footprint, the slots are wide(ish) and has a temp control of 1-7 and buttons for bagels and frozen items. It does make toast much faster than our previous toaster.

The bad: The toast is not cooked evenly at all, the outside of both slices is most definitely less cooked than the sides facing the interior of the unit. The recommended setting for toast is 4, and I found that 4 is actually much too high. I think for non-burnt toast you'll want to use a 2, 3 at max. If you like your toast very brown to black though, you can go nuts with 4 and above.

It does the job and it makes toast quickly. Even though the temperature is high for my taste the range of settings allows you to select a toast level you should find appealing. The big problem is that the sides of the bread facing the interior of the toaster get more cooked than those facing the outside. It is a very noticeable difference.
profile.summary: Small footprint, fast toasting, but uneven.

profile.description: Andrew Harlan is an Eternal, a man whose job it is to range through past and present Centuries, monitoring and, where necessary, altering Time's myriad cause-and-effect relationships. But when Harlan meets and falls for a non-Eternal woman, he seeks to use the awesome powers and techniques of the Eternals to twist time for his own purposes, so that he and his love can survive together.
profile.reviewText:
There once was a time when authors could write books about important subjects with a short page count, and the books were good, and the stories were complete. This work is an example of the past which has changed.
  This book has thematic similarities to both his Galaxia/Gaia of the end of Foundation, as well as with Clarke's City and the Stars and Childhood's End. In that it deals with the grand transfiguration of human culture from the safe and staid to uncertain limitless potential. Oddly though, Asimov's position in this early work is diametric from the result in Foundation and Earth.
  This dichotomy also appears in the work, it is almost like two books in one. A straightforward, simplistic 'Back to the Future' naive work that was common for the time dealing with simple characters exploring the neat idea of time travel and its paradoxes. Then for the very last few pages we switch gears to a philosophical discussion on man's place in the universe and his destiny.
  For me, the straightforward adventure story of fixing the timestream worked better than the philosophy of fixing the future so mankind will not be safe, but be adventurous and leading to his Galactic Empire/Foundation series. Particularly as I have mentioned Foundation comes right back full circle to a planned safe society rather than an uncertain dynamic society.
  Perhaps this was done intentionally as in this book we are told that the centuries are cyclic with industries and attitudes returning over and over again. It could be Asimov's arcing storyline over this and his other series was hinting that not only did industries and social mores repeat, but that a slower cycle of uncertain expansion alternated with the safe over-controlling method of Eternity in this novel and Gaia/Galaxia at the end of Foundation.
  To try and summarize, the adventure story here will go down easy and please you while the ending will give you things to think about and possibly disturb you.
profile.summary: The Future in Flux

profile.description: THE YEARS OF RICE AND SALT
profile.reviewText:
For the most part this is a well written story of an alternate history where Europe is taken off the map figuratively. Made even better by the device of 3 main characters and some minor characters reincarnating through history. The novel focuses primarily on China and Islam, i.e. the middle and far east but some time is given to the natives of North America becoming a power unto their own and the influence of India. For the majority of the book it is a very interesting revealing of how things may have gone.

 Even the best of the book though is slow-paced and for the final portions the pace becomes glacial. Progress stops, history does not move forward very much and page after page is devoted to speechifying by two of the main characters in one incarnation or another. In this way the book just runs out of steam and stops. A tightening up of these sections and showing progress up through the space age would probably have made for a better novel.

  Was it worth reading? Yes.
  Did it require effort? Yes.
  Was it enjoyable? Mostly.

I feel happy and mostly rewarded that I finished the work, but I would not consider it to be pleasure reading. If the premise intrigues you give it a shot but be prepared that getting through might be a bit of work.
profile.summary: Slow paced journey runs out of steam

profile.description: Capture every detail of every adventure with the go-everywhere case thats optimized for action photography: Life Proof FR Shot for iPhone 6/6s. Equipped with a removable wide-angle lens, it takes in more of the scene for pulse-raising pics and vids. When the days done, flip out the kickstand to replay every minute of the adventure hands free. Plus, the built-in screen cover and custom design deliver peak mobility and functionality.
profile.reviewText:
I had previously had 2 versions of another LifeProof case. The first was good but had some issues with sound/microphone. The next iteration of that model fixed these issues.

This case outperforms that one. First are the looks, with a matte black finish and light green highlights it looks great. Just don't lose it in the dark!! The inclusion of a complete screen rather than the stick on screen is huge. No more having to peel the screen protector on and off at the cashier when a barcode won't scan. Be careful though to clean your screen off perfectly before putting it in the case as any debris left there will be stuck there.

I don't really need the lens, but it is very nice, and the flash now works much better than with my previous case which gave every flash pic a purple tinge. The lens is small and easy to attach and remove. A small leg to prop your phone up in landscape mode is also very useful and doesn't add any bulk to the case.

As with other Lifeproof you will need an extension cable to screw in with your headphones which is provided and some big power cables may not fit The power slot cover is very tight and needs some force to open and you will find the volume and power button also require some force.

The one downside is the screen responsiveness does suffer a bit especially around the edges due to the screen protector. Even after sitting a cup on it to press it down as the instructions dictate. Other than that caveat it really is a superb case to protect your iPhone.
profile.summary: Their Best Case Yet

profile.description: With a career in comics spanning five decades, Dennis O'Neil was for years a group editor at DC Comics and the guiding force behind the Batman mythos during the 1980s and '90s, helping to return the charcater to his roots as a dark, mysterious gothic avenger. As a freelance writer and journalist, O'Neil has produced several novels and works of nonfiction, as well as hundreds of comics, teleplays and short stories, including the bestselling Bantarn novel, Batman: Knightfall and his critically acclaimed Green Lantern comics, Hard-Travelling Heroes.
profile.reviewText:
2.5 stars

  To me, Hal Jordan will always be Green Lantern. However I found the beginning of this work fairly strong. Kyle is endearing as a slacker and a loser who ends up with the ring. He's presented pretty well in having difficulties dealing with the ring and the rest of the JLA. It is a bit off-putting though to return to the alleged origin and see his best friend the Flash sneering at him for being irresponsible.

  After we get rid of the rest of the JLA by magic, which is the one major suspension of disbelief the reader must get over in every one of these solo JLA novels, Kyle must rise to the occasion.

  He does of course, but the story veers crazily at this point into a melange of hard-sf physics, meta-physics and existentialism. Rather than doing much of anything, Kyle engages in lengthy socratic dialogues with his Oan mentor and philosophizes on reality, immortality, the rights and responsibilities of power and on change. Now many of these things should be included in a superhero novel to elevate it above mere action but here it is overdone and done poorly.

  The ending is also inadequate and very unbelievable. Other nonsense includes the idea that Oans created superheroes 10 years ago. Ok, sure, there are many different realities in the DC metaverse, but this is a series and the series must remain consistent. In this case we already have 3 generations of Flashes so this 10 years is nonsense.

  Even as a standalone book, taken apart from the rest of the series the liberties taken with "known history" would be jarring and less than acceptable.

  What I always loved about Green Lantern was the power of the ring that needed to be used with such creativity. Sadly we get little of that here as O'Neil one of the premier GL writers turns it into a hard-sf universe building novel mixed in with meta-physics, and existential philosophy.

  To sum it up, the origin story and the hilarious satire of the action-adventure genre at the start was good. The last half was badly wanting.
profile.summary: Physics, Existentialism and Meta-Physics?

profile.description: Stylish, feather light and seriously powerful, the Drops 360 RP-HJX5 In-Ear Headphones deliver a full range of exceptional sound performance. Its premium 12mm coaxial dual neodymium magnet drivers produce a level of deep, rich bass and clear, high-treble tones (5Hz-25kHz) not often experienced in ultra-compact headphones. Distortion is kept to a minimum with a color-matched aluminum ring on each speaker housing. Panasonic's ultra-soft earpads fit naturally into the ear to stay comfortably in place while walking, working or just relaxing. And no matter where you are, their airtight design fit snugly to reduce ambient noise. For individual comfort and fit, a set of S/M/L earpads is included. Drops 360 also incorporate longer, more direct audio ports to channel high-performance sound directly into the ears for hours of listening enjoyment. RP-HJX5 work seamlessly with iPhone/iPod/iPad, Blackberry and Android devices. An included travel case keeps your headphones safe and sound when not in use.
profile.reviewText:
I rarely give an item 5 stars. However the price of this item combined with the great sound deserves the full 5 stars. I don't believe you will find a better price/sound bargain. The sound is as good as or better than earbuds and headphones I have that cost 10 times as much.

I actually got these for my wife as she find the earbuds that came with the iPhone 6 uncomfortable. After trying them out I didn't want to give them to her. I can definitely hear more of the music I listen to on the iPhone with these, the sound is richer and more dynamic, clearer than both the Apple provided earbuds and the other 3rd party earbuds I have.

There are 3 different types of plugs you can connect to the earbuds to find something most comfortable for your ear, my wife likes the ones pictured, I like the shorter more rounded ones. If this set of earbuds had the mic and controls for pause/back/forward/volume on the cable they would be perfect, but I knew it didn't have them and don't expect that at the price point of this item.
profile.summary: Great sound at a great price!!

top_5.description: HEADPHONES WITH MICROPHONES HD Dolby(R) Digital Plus enhanced sound via exclusive Jabra(R) sound app; In-line controls for easy music & call management; Tough, shatterproof & constructed for ultimate portability; Lightweight & flexible with steel hinges & aluminum frame; Foldable design for quick & easy storage; Premium comfort for extended wear; Memory foam ear cups & padded headband; White
top_5.reviewText:
3.5 stars

Since my original iPhone ear buds gave up the ghost I haven't had a set that had controls on the cable, a feature I really missed. Since then I have gone through many sets of earbuds and they all fell to the same flaw, the cable wearing out where it connects to the iPhone. So I was really excited to get these headphones and see how they worked.

The cable is thick and covered in fabric, as a bonus the connectors to the headphones and the iPhone are encased in hard plastic. No cable bending and wearing out at these critical junction points. This should last for quite some time and not fail due to the wear and tear of the cable bending at these two places. The on cable controls work well though perhaps not intuitively. There are three buttons. The top button for volume increase, the bottom button for volume decrease, the middle button is a multi-function button where one press will pause/resume the song being played or answer the phone, two presses will skip forward to the next song, three will skip back. The buttons work as described without issue.

The controls also feature a microphone enabling you to answer the phone and speak "hands-free", I had someone call me and they told me they heard me loud and clear using the built in microphone.

The sound is very good. Even using the normal iTunes player it is good. Using the Jabra app it is even better, though much louder. The app imports your iTunes library and playlists and allows you to use them, even with shuffle with a few extra options, a dolby sound function, a surround sound function and a variety of equalizers to play with. The dolby funcion does give a fuller, deeper sound and I enjoy using this. The surround sound function also gives a fuller sound though I opted to disable this. I prefer to hear the stereo mix the artist designed rather than have the app mixing things up. The equalizers are fun and I've settled on the "rock" equalizer. Some caveats do exist though, the importing of the library/playlists is slow, though a shuffle does exist you must first select a song to play then skip forward, no random from the start, using the app the volume is loud, in fact when I'm sitting home alone I use iTunes at the lowest volume because the headphones are so loud and using the Jabra app the volume even at the lowest setting is too loud.

My main issue is the fit, maybe my head is freakishly shaped, maybe it is to thin but I have a real problem keeping the headphones on. If I bend my head forward to look down at something, bend over to pick up after my dog the headphones will almost always start sliding off. If my hair happens to be underneath the headphones over my ear they slide off very quickly. As great as the sound is if the headphones can't stay on my head without issue then they become a less viable solution. My primary use of the headphones is for walking my dog, and reading in bed, using the headphones and music to lessen any noises from my wife blasting the television. It does the second very well, the first less so. I'm thining jogging or running in these headphones would be completely out of the question, at least for me.

In conclusion these are really ruggedly built headphones with great sound and controls on the headphone cable that work really well, the sound app is really good at enhancing the music you play but for me the fit is hampering the ability to wear them to do things I might like to do.
top_5.summary: Great Sound, Poor Fit
