profile.summary: Perfect & adorable "first" backpack for little ones!

profile.description: The Singer 2259 Tradition Sewing Machine has the features to make starting a new hobby easy. This sewing machine features an automatic four-step buttonhole, easy stitch selection, and snap-on presser feet. Thread the machine quickly and easily. Just follow the arrows on the machine, and you are threaded in a snap. Nineteen basic stretch and decorative built-in stitches provide options for everything from the most basic garment alterations to more elaborate home decor designs.
profile.reviewText:
This Singer 2277 Tradition Sewing Machine was easy to set up and get working, though I have other machines with many more features, this machine was so basic that nothing impressed or excited me. If you are in the market for a very basic, inexpensive machine, then this might be a good fit for you.

While I haven't experienced a big problem with this machine (just little annoyances so common with sewing machines, like getting tension set perfectly), I have to wonder if the low price is really worth spending on such a basic machine? While this machine might be a good choice for someone who does a rare, simple sewing project, or a child/teen just starting to learn to sew, I also think that there are possibly better machines out there with more features even with just a *slight* increase in price.

I really hesitate to recommend that anyone spend less than one fifty on a sewing machine they think they might use often, and that's my bare minimum. The sewing machine industry is already getting criticism from mature sewers for making machines that are "disposable" these days, rather than the heavy, metal frame our grandmothers used (and are very possibly still using!) This machine seems to be a perfect example, sure the price is low, and it sewed alright for me (the tension was a little fussy at times and it jammed once, but got the job done still) but if you're willing to save up and spend a little more, you can get a lot more features and a machine that could be a lot more reliable.

I also have a Singer Quantum Stylist machine and it's been AMAZING to use. So I'm not opposed to Singer at all, my Quantum Stylist has been my "baby" for a couple years now, has never jammed, and I've never even messed with tension. It's a total power horse of a machine. This Singer 2277, however, pales in comparison. To ME, it's worth it to spend more on a machine that performs and lasts.

I've also had the pleasure of trying out a couple of Brothers recently, and I've been very impressed with that brand, although their machines are lighter and definitely almost all plastic. Thye

I'll keep this Singer 2277 around because I have two daughters who I think I'll be able to teach the basics to using this machine. But I really don't see myself using it often because my other machines have much nicer features. This 2277 Tradition machine is as basic as you can get these days. If you are looking for basic, inexpensive machine that will not be used often or is for a young person, then this might be a good choice--it performed just fine for me. But if you're really looking for either an upgrade machine or something to use regularly for years, I wouldn't necessarily recommend this. Sewing machines are much like cars, I think it's worth it to spend a little more and get something reliable.

I was hoping it'd wow me when I got this machine, and I'd be able to post a review saying, "It turns out a cheap machine CAN be a GOOD machine!" but instead I've just found it to be a very mediocre, beginner's machine. But even if you're a beginner, I think you should start out with a GOOD machine. You can lose interest very easily in sewing if your machine is just a pain to use, and judging from the small tension & jamming issues I had when using this Singer 2277, I think it might be more of a pain than a pleasure to use?
profile.summary: Extremely basic, I can't say the savings is worth it

profile.description: Designed for home or small office use, the Fellowes Cosmic 125 Laminator accommodates 12-1/2 Inches wide documents and features advanced temperature control for consistent results. HeatGuard Technology keeps heat inside so laminator is cool to touch. Offers a heated setting for 3-mil hot pouches and a cold setting for heat-sensitive materials. 5-mil compatible for documents that are index card size or smaller. Heats up in 5 minutes, laminates in 1 minute. Release lever disengages pouch for re-centering or removal. Sturdy carrying handle plus stand-up feet with cord storage. Includes laminating starter kit. The Fellowes Cosmic CL125 12" Personal Laminator, the first laminator designed for home or office use. Award winning*, user-friendly design offers numerous laminating possibilties with minimal adjustment. Dual temperature settings for laminating cold pouches and 3 mil hot pouches. Designed for letter or taboid-size applications up to 9" or 12" wide. Heats up in just 6 minutes and completes a letter-size lamination inless than 1 minute. Safe and comfortable to touch "HeatGuard Technologh". Advanced temperature control for consistent lamination quality. Anti-jamming release lever. Acoustic and visual indicators clearly signal when the laminator is ready to use. Front flap serves as document guide and dust cover. Unique horizontal storage capability. Stand-up feet with cable management system. Carry handle and compact size easy portability.
profile.reviewText:
I think this laminating machine makes a great addition to any home office or homeschool! I have a small home based paper crafting business, and I also am planning on homeschooling - I can already think of so many great uses for a laminator. The Fellowes's Cosmic model is a lighter duty laminator, only meant to be used when laminating items in 3 or 5 mil pouches. There are more heavy duty laminators out there, so make sure this one will meet your needs before buying it. For me, this one does the job quite well, and I've had zero problems with sealing or air pockets so far.

It is easy to set up and use, the instruction manual is simple and to the point. My first laminating job turned out perfectly. It comes with a cleaning sheet you should run through your machine to remove any adhesive left behind, so hopefully that will keep this machine running clean for a long time coming.

There is a handle for easy portability, combined with a cord that wraps around the feet of the machine, this is a very easy to store machine which won't take up much space. It heats up within a few minutes and runs smoothly and quietly. There is a smell when it's turned on, as with all laminating machines in my experience.

Overall this is a very simple, attractive and effective laminator, I'm looking forward to using it more. I'm planning on making my own durable flash cards and "books" for my young children & homeschooling. I like laminating items that I wish to use dry erase markers on - that way the laminated sheet can be cleaned off over and over, this will be especially helpful with homeschooling. The 10 Fellowes laminating pouches that come with this machine were great as well, I've had no issues using them and my papers all come out very clear and crisp looking. Do be sure to follow the directions and use only for items that meet the size requirements for this to effectively seal your laminating pouches.

I can definitely say I recommend this product to those looking for a simple, light duty laminating machine.
profile.summary: Great light duty laminator for the home office or homeschool

profile.description: This listing features a BLENDTEC Classic 570 Blender, Wildside Jar - RED. Brand new. Item Specifics: Commercial-quality 1,570-watt 120 volt, countertop blender with 3 peak horsepower direct-drive motor Includes WildSide blending jar For in-home use in the USA BPA-free Tritan co-polyester jar with patented cold-forged wingtip blades The World's most Advanced Blender
profile.reviewText:
All the rumors are true! Blend Tec is amazing!! With just four buttons, this blender is complete. It is hard core and ready to blend. Will it blend? Yes it will! We have no complaints after the last couple months of making smoothie after smoothie, after blending soups to smooth, after making milkshakes, and after processing ingredients.

Who needs a food processor when you have a Blend Tec blender? I was really quite shocked at the simple four buttons, but after using it many times, no worries here. It is amazing. The power and efficiency in this blender is amazing. And I speak as someone who owned a nice Kitchen-Aid blender for the first 10 years of my married life. This kicks that blender in the behind. I will never go back, I think. Also, I LOVE the design of the cup. The four-sided, measured, easy-pour, easy-clean cup is a delight to use, and so much simpler than my Kitchen-Aid.

I definitely recommend this, or any Blend Tec blender. I'm sold on this brand now that I've had the delight of using it. No-nonsense, super powerful, no complaints!
profile.summary: I'm sold on Blend Tec!- after years of a cute Kitchen-Aid!

profile.description: These pretty little flags are perfect for adorning straws, pencils, toothpicks, candy and more. They're great to personalize for parties, weddings, school projects and sporting events. The removable adhesive is safe for indirect food contact and leaves no residue. The print-to-the-edge feature lets you add full-color backgrounds and sharp text and graphics to the entire label. Choose from a variety of free, easy-to-use templates and designs at avery.com/print to create the exact flag you're looking for.
profile.reviewText:
These sweet little pointed straw flags make party planning and decorating simple and impressive. Avery has done a great job expanding their line in this direction, and I especially love their online templates that make what would otherwise be very COMPLICATED printing and design, really quite easy. You can design and print these straw flags just so to fit the theme and decor of your party.

They printed just great on my new Epson, no complaints there. As someone who has thrown somewhat elaborate parties & showers over the last decade for my friends and family, I've certainly decorated many a paper straw for a party. This ain't my first rodeo, if you get what I'm saying. So my only qualm with this product is the price. I have made my own decorative straw toppers with inexpensive supplies from craft stores, and have never paid this much to do so. 50 cents a piece for a paper that tops a straw seems a bit much, when you can just as easily cut up scrap booking paper, use some rubber stamps or stickers, and make your own.

So with that said, it's up to you: is this price worth it to have pre-cute, easy-to-use straw flags that you can design on Avery.com's template and be ready to go? OR, are you like me and enjoy the art of the craft, and would prefer total control (not just templates) to make your own for pennies on the dollar?

This is overall a good product, don't get me wrong. I'm just not sure I'd buy them again for that price when I have stuff lying around my craft studio to make well more than 24 straw flags. You'll have to decide if it's right for you.
profile.summary: The cost of convenience...

profile.description: Luxurious, complete, solid-brass faucet set, precision manufactured by FREUER. Outstanding build-quality, finishing process, and appearance. This faucet has great looks and versatility; use it in the kitchen, bath or bar. The spout swivels, and the handles have 1/4 turn ceramic valves. Removable aerator. Includes 16" long, braided supply lines (standard 3/8" female compression fittings). Sink drain sold separately.
profile.reviewText:
It's worth noting that this is a smaller, "low duty" faucet. It is intended as a secondary sink or wet bar faucet. Still, we decided to install it in our main kitchen sink for the following reasons:

1. We purchased the Domsjo single apron sink from IKEA, and that sink only comes with one hole. Of course, there are "punch outs" where if you're brave enough you can create more holes in the sink, however, we wanted to keep it simple and are willing to live without a sprayer.
2. We have a small kitchen, so a single basin sink and a smaller faucet fit the style of our kitchen.
3. The look and price were exactly what we were looking for.

The design itself is very elegant, reminiscent of days gone by and perfect for an older home or a kitchen you want to add character to. It's nice and shiny, it works just fine. The flow is actually better than we had originally expected from such a faucet. It installed just fine but was a bit wiggly at first, my husband was able to retrofit it with a block of wood to add more surface area for the faucet to attach to. This might not be a problem with other sinks--our IKEA Domsjo might have had something to do with this.

I like that it stands tall, although it does seem to not come out quite as far as larger kitchen sink faucets would. It arrived very well packaged and the quality seems to be good. If you're looking for this type of faucet--knowing it's a "low-duty" faucet--then I can't think of a reason not to recommend this one.
profile.summary: Great look and fit in my small kitchen!

profile.description: This science kit contains everything to create codes and write secret messages. Discover the science behind using acids and bases to make invisible ink, reveal mysterious messages using colored filters and light waves, learn to write in secret codes, and much more!
profile.reviewText:
This is a fun secret message set that I would have LOVED as a kid. I love that it comes with two sets--because what would be the point of just one?--so a girl can share secret messages with her sister or best friend. There are two boxes, two cipher wheels, two pens with reveal UV lights, basically one of everything for each girl. There are several different secret message methods included, so it's got more variety which makes it more fun and even educational.

Kids that love playing spy games would also love this to add to their spy kits. There is a booklet that explains the ideas behind the secret message methods as well as ideas for use and even games that can be created with the kits. The price is just right for a birthday gift and it's a fun thing to give and receive. Definitely recommended! Will update this review if quality level changes. I don't expect pens and things with these sort of kits to last years, but hopefully will get plenty of good use out of it!
profile.summary: I would have loved this as a kid!

profile.description: Breathe new life into your bedroom decor with the Traditions by Waverly Rustic Retreat 6-Piece Comforter Collection. This beautiful ensemble features a floral paisley pattern on an ivory ground. Comforter set includes one comforter, one tailored 5-box pleat coordinating bed skirt, two coordinating pillow shams and two decorative pillows. Queen set measures 88" x 88" with two 20" x 26" pillow shams and a 60" x 80" bed skirt with a 15" drop. King set measures 104" x 88" with two 20" x 36" pillow shams and a 78" x 80" bed skirt with a 15" drop. 16x16 pillow features ivory pleated face and solid ivory reverse, 12x16 pillow features floral paisley face and ivory reverse. Comforter, shams and bed skirt are machine washable. Wash in cold water on the gentle cycle and tumble dry on low for long lasting beauty. Pillows are spot clean only. 100% Polyester.
profile.reviewText:
I'll start with what I really like about this set: it's price and completeness. At just $50, you get an entire comforter set, shams, bed skirt, and decorative pillows. BAM! Just like that you have a complete set perfect for a guest room or a basic, inexpensive first home starter set. I think you definitely get your money's worth. The quality is decent, like something I'd expect from Walmart or Target. The price is perfect.

I personally thought this set looked prettier in the picture than in real life. It's a bit grandma-style for me. I have a very shabby chic, vintage, cottage style. I thought this would work well in my home as pictured, but it turned out to be more dowdy in person. But that's a personal style thing. I have friends who would LOVE this set. Which is perfect, I'll put it in the guest bedroom to they can enjoy it!
profile.summary: A great inexpensive and complete starter set!

profile.description: This is a unique ice cube tray in that you can push out just a couple of ice cubefor your drink instead of twisting and having large ice cubes all over. The three 11-inch x 4.75-inch trays come in lime green or blue.
profile.reviewText:
These ice trays really attracted me because they look very much like they'd be great: perfect little rounded ice cubes that come out easily with the silicone push buttons on the bottom of each capsule.

Boy, this could not be further from the truth! These ice cubes are VERY difficult to get out. The soft silicone bottoms do nothing once the capsule is filled with water and fully frozen. I found I can get a few cubes, not many, but one or two out, by pressing the tray really hard against my counter. But in doing that, I've already cracked the tray a couple times. This product is trash, don't bother. I decided to visit this Amazon page to see what other reviewers were saying, and frankly I was shocked to see any reviews above 2 stars. The small percentage of people who give these ice trays a good rating have a couple different tips...

First, they say "These work as long as you don't over fill them!" To which I say, if I don't fill these to the top then I'd have TINY ice cubes, and what's the point of that? Plus, how am I supposed to know each time I fill a tray EXACTLY what level to fill each cup--because if it's not right my ice is stuck!

Second, many people say they come right out if you run the ice under warm water for a few seconds every time, or let the tray sit out for a few minutes before trying to get the ice out. Are you kidding me? Look, at the risk of sounding like a spoiled, immediate satisfaction addicted American, if we can send a man to the moon then we can get ice for our drinks without going through a process first! I'm a busy mom on the go, I don't have time to always run a tray under warm water (which I tried, but I *still* had to do some prying) or wait a few minutes for the ice to warm up *just enough* to not melt completely, but so that I can get them out easier. Ridiculous.

Look, let's call a spade a spade: this is a poorly designed ice tray, simple as that. Just because a few reviewers have learned to live with it doesn't mean it's worth it, I say: keep looking! Many people these days have automatic ice makers built into their fridge (including me, until recently mine stopped working), we're used to ice at the push of the button. While these trays LOOK like you can get ice at the push of each silicone button, the truth is it's a pain the rear to use. Keep looking, or do what we've resorted to and just buy bags of ice at the store each week. It's pretty cheap, and much  less frustrating than dealing with this product.
profile.summary: Looks can be deceiving...

profile.description: Bright. Versatile. Indispensable. Energizer vision flashlights bring bold, innovative flashlight technology to virtually any situation, indoors or out. For simple household use or serious Storm preparation, the standard flashlight has come a long way. Energizer vision flashlights use a specially engineered lensing design and LED temperature that provides the most practical light output for a variety of indoor and outdoor applications.
profile.reviewText:
I've always been a heavy, weapon-like Maglite sort of girl. This flashlight feels like the cheaper version of a Maglite, but for around the same price for a basic flashlight. I'll say this, the light is *BRIGHT* and has two settings, a high and a low. That said, it does have a twisting lens like the Maglite flashlights do, so you can't spread out or pinpoint the light. It's just one setting.

The blister package it came in was difficult and annoying to open. I was afraid I would cut myself in the process. Once I finally did get it open, I realized there was no indication--ANYWHERE--to show how the batteries go in. I tried several ways without success before coming here to read other reviews and found out how. The original way I tried it worked, I just hadn't had the cap screwed on tight enough. So the batteries all go in the same direction, positive end facing the lightbulbs. Then you have to struggled with the cap to hold in the batteries while trying to get the threading on the screw cap right. That doesn't sound like a big deal...but it was trickier than it sounds because of the fine threading on the screw cap. The thing was a pain to get on!

Once I finally got it lit up and working, it's a decent enough flashlight. I just think a weightier Maglite for around the same price is way better. Also, there is no hole to attach a strap. The bright LED lights definitely hurt the eyes and illuminate a room, however. Go with your gut, I guess, but this isn't my favorite flashlight.
profile.summary: I prefer Maglites to this situation

profile.description: Design your sound with the new, Studio Balanced Pro4S by Koss, inventors of the world's first SP/3 Stereo phone in 1958.
profile.reviewText:
These Koss headphones arrived beautifully, yet simply, packaged and ready to sound off. While I realize that headphones need to be broken in--sort of like shoes!--and thus take a good 24-72 hours of use to get the drivers to smooth out, still I was puzzled when I first put this set on and turned on my music.

These headphones were significantly more tight, less bassy than most, and overall less indulgent in the music I was playing. I compared them to my Beats and also my JBL Synchros over and over, and the difference was shocking to me. These headphones, at first, seemed SO FLAT. Then I took a second look at the product, the description, and went over to the Koss website to do some investigating.

While it may be obvious to some audiophiles, allow me to help out those less experienced shoppers on these headphones: these are STUDIO HEADPHONES. These are not headphones that are made for those looking to kick back and do some leisurely listening to their favorite tunes. These are not indulgent headphones, they are purposefully flat because they are made for people who are creating and thus need unaltered sound.

From the Koss website itself: "The Pro4S Studio Headphone is specifically crafted for professionals who use headphones every day to create the world's greatest music. Featuring the all-new SLX40 element, tuned for reference, the Pro4S Studio Headphone delivers an incredibly accurate and unbiased sound, perfect for any studio or creative environment."

So, I'm trying to point out here that these headphones are geared toward and created for sound engineers, not leisurely listeners. Just keep that in mind when you're shopping headphones! There is a difference when it comes to "studio headphones". Why? Because when they are creating music, sound engineers need to be able to hear what they are doing with the music, not the headphones. Does that make sense? They need pure, unadulterated sound--so they will purposely avoid headphones that emphasize one area over another. That's a great thing for the professionals!

Now, if you're into that sort of listening, please know I'm not saying you CAN'T enjoy these headphones. They are very high quality, in my opinion. Just realize, they are created specifically for studio use. With YouTube careers, self-publishing musicians, and all the opportunities to make something of yourself these days, a LOT of people can get great use from this sort of headphone! They definitely have their place in the market. IF you are searching for a great, immersive headphone that draws you into the music that has already been engineered to perfection in the studio, you might want to search elsewhere, not because these aren't good headphones--they're great--they just might not be geared toward your needs.

All that aside, here is what I love about these headphones:

- They're comfortable, over the ear headphones with plenty of cushion, great sound isolating
- They fold up quite nicely to be stored safely and flat in your backpack or briefcase, yet they are full size
- The headphone jack can be plugged into either side of the headphones, which also allows for a second listener to connect if that's what you need
- Comes with a carrying case
- Attractive! Call me vain, but I dislike chunky headphones that make me look like Princess Leia, these are slim and slick
- I like the coiled cord! When you have a lot of cords, a coiled one can help keep things tidy.
- Despite being geared toward studio use, once I got used to the difference in the sound, I have to agree that these are high quality headphones

If you're in the need for a great pair of studio headphones, look no further!
profile.summary: So what is a STUDIO headphone? There is a difference with these...

profile.description: The Elite Submersible Pre-Set Aquarium Heater offers accurate and reliable aquarium temperature. It was built with a temperature range of 68 to 86 degrees Fahrenheit. The ceramic heater core allows for even and efficient heat distribution and its waterproof seal prevents humidity from entering the heater. The Elite Submersible Pre-Set Aquarium Heater is suitable for fresh or saltwater aquariums and will help to keep your fish in a comfortable environment.
profile.reviewText:
I'm still learning how to properly care for my beta, it turns out they are a lot more work than you'd expect from a little fish! I may have purchased my beta in naivete, but I quickly learned through all my beta research that these fish like to be kept between 75 & 80 degrees (Fahrenheit, of course). Since adding this heater, I can see a distinct difference in my beta's happiness. It's clear to me that he is much more comfortable in the "toasty" climate this heater provides.

I chose this tank heater after reading several reviews here on Amazon, this one stuck out quite clearly as the best. I am ready to fully agree with my fellow admiring reviewers: this is a great buy! It fits in my 1.5 gallon aquarium just perfectly. Note: while this works in my smaller aquarium, I have to point out my tank is taller than it is wide or deep. This may not fit in an aquarium that is 1.5 gallons but wider rather than tall.

This heater was easy to set up, but you should definitely read the instructions before installing in your tank as this is an electrical appliance that is submerged in water. There is no temperature dial, so you will need a separate thermometer to monitor your aquarium's temperature. It's best to start with the knob turned all the way down and slowly increase over time until you reach the desired temperature.

This heater has worked perfectly in our aquarium and our beta loves & thrives in the temperature - I highly recommend this heater to anyone with a smaller sized tank and fish that prefer a little warmth!
profile.summary: Makes a beta very happy!

profile.description: Design with pleasure, delight and enjoyment in mind. For more than close to 40 years, Mr. Coffee coffeemakers have been found in more kitchens in America than any other brand. The Next Generation Mr. Coffee EJX, VMX, and LMX Series coffeemakers are not exceptions when it comes to style and design as they complement any dcor - in the kitchen and everywhere consumers want to create their own personal coffee experience. For those who recognize that good things start with coffee at home, Mr. Coffee is the brand that leads the way in transforming your favorite coffee bean into your favorite cup of coffee.
profile.reviewText:
Though this is one of the larger coffee makers I've had sitting in my kitchen, it is still an attractive one and I really have grown to love the lit up clock that is bright enough to be a night light in the dark. We have a mostly white kitchen as far as appliances go, but this still fits in nicely.

This coffee pot has a great price point and some nice features like the self-clean and the Pause 'n' Serve feature is a nice touch. It brews coffee quite well, and very quickly, for a machine of this range. Though my favorite will always be percolated coffee, this is the next best thing since we don't have the time to make our coffee in a percolator every day. The pitcher is well designed and doesn't leak or drip easily, the coffee stays nice and hot. This machine takes regular basket style filters and it's easy to program and get started.

If this machine fits your decor & price range, I'd definitely recommend it. Of course, if we encounter any problems down the road, I'll update my review accordingly, but so far it's been a hit for us. I just wish it were a tad bit smaller, but that's my only complaint. Other than that, it's been a great machine to have.
profile.summary: Attractive, well priced, and nice features

profile.description: Acadmie Oil Pastels is a complete set that is ready to use at home or when youre on the go. Includes 24 artist colors in vibrant pigments that can be combined to create the perfect shade or color. A color chart in the top cover provides easy reference for creating endless colors. Directions for 3 techniques are shown on the back of the heavy duty cardboard box. Assorted colors include: Acid Yellow, Cadmium Yellow, Orange, Deep Red, Scarlet, Light Pink, Bright Pink, Purple, Ultramarine, Dark Blue, Blue, Light Blue, Dark Green, Green, Light Green, Lime Green, Khaki, Yellow Ochre, Light Brown, Terracotta, Burnt Umber, Black, Gray and White.
profile.reviewText:
This is a decent price for a decent set of oil pastels, perfect for the student or hobbyist. It has a good starting color palette and the pastels are of good quality and well packaged.

This was my first time creating with oil pastels, though I grew up using soft pastels (my father is an artist and his art supplies were always within reach), so I am used to the blending and smudging techniques that you get with soft pastels. What's the difference between soft pastels and oil pastels?

Oil pastels are created with wax and oil, as opposed to a gum binder used in soft pastels which makes them prone to crumbling. The effect with oil pastels is that you get a crayon-like medium that does not blend or layer as well as soft pastels will. Still, while they are not my personal favorite, there is certainly a place for oil pastels in the artist's studio. They are really quite versatile and can be worked similarly to oil paints, thinning them with turpentine and using them for washes. I would like to try using them for glazing on a sketch. I'll let you know how that goes...

This set is lower end as far as art supplies go, it is priced and prepared for beginners, art hobbyists, students, or children. This is not a set a professional would likely buy (you should see how high the price on top brands can go!) to stock their studio with.

Still, the quality and palette selection you get for this price is pretty darn good, and I cannot think of a reason not to recommend them!
profile.summary: A soft pastel lover tries OIL pastels for the first time...

profile.description: Now your preschooler can enjoy the fun of an RC vehicle without the frustration of a complex remote! The Fisher-Price My Easy RC features an ergonomically designed remote with easy-to-use directional buttons for simple 4-way driving (forward, backward, left and right). The special turn technology allows kids to make the vehicle drive AND turn at the same time by pressing only one button ('left' or 'right') on the remote. With two parent-controlled speeds, you can start your young driver off slowly and then flip the switch to the more exciting expert speed once they've mastered the controller. Plus, the auto shut-off helps conserve battery life to ensure kids get the most mileage out of the My Easy RC.
profile.reviewText:
The three and six year old kids ADORE toys like this. My one-year-old? He's still pretty scared of remote control cars that chase him. It's still amusing to us, though. I think this remote control RC car is perfect! Fun, easy, perfect for little ones.

This toy was easy to use right out of package. I feel these toys help teach children spatial awareness and can be used as a frequent and even a educational toy. The controls has two speeds, and that is a nice feature. The remote control is relatively easy to use and perfect for little ones. I can't think of a reason not to recommend this toy. Fisher-Price is a reasonable brand and a healthy choice, in my opinion.
profile.summary: Kids ADORE this toy

profile.description: Lenovo Factory Refurbished with 90 day warranty. Includes AC adapter and Battery.
profile.reviewText:
I really like my Lenovo U530, overall. It's very thin, good looking, and very fast. I'm not a gamer, though my understanding of this laptop is that it's not geared toward that sort of use anyway. I use this laptop mainly for work, photo editing, blogging, writing, and storing a million photos of my kids and unfinished projects. This is a great laptop for such needs, work and creative uses, not so much for gaming.

The speakers are the best I've found in a laptop, so far. The touch screen and lighted keyboard are my FAVORITE features here. Those are great details that I use often. The overall feel of this laptop is solid and sturdy, I've noticed it doesn't scratch easily--which is great because the finish is beautiful. I love the glossy, bright screen as well. This laptop, compared to my others (I've had HPs I've liked, a Toshiba, an iBook, a Gateway {awful!} and a Sony), has a high-end feel to it.

I have been pleasantly surprised and pleased with how much I like this laptop, it is the first Lenovo I've ever used or owned. The only complaint here is that the touchpad acts up from time to time, I feel this is the one area where this laptop really NEEDS improvement. It catches and is unresponsive every so often. Not enough to ruin what I'm doing, but just mildly annoying when it occasionally happens. All things considered, I think this is a great laptop.
profile.summary: High end feel, low end touchpad, but well liked!

profile.description: The beale pull-down bar faucet from American Standard showcases striking contemporary design and superior performance. Free up your kitchen sink with a bar faucet, giving added functionality to your kitchen. Featuring a convenient pull-down faucet, the beale bar faucet makes it easy to complete a variety of tasks. Two brand-exclusive docking systems, the dock-tite and re-trax, provide smooth operation and keeps the spray head in place when not in use.
profile.reviewText:
Keep in mind this is the BAR faucet. It is not the faucet that has motion-sensing turn on, or a stream AND spray setting switch. I got confused when I ordered it, because the video (at the time) on this product page was featuring the main kitchen faucet with the motion sensing and the two spray settings. But it arrived without those features so I came back and watch the video, and at the end it says, "Bar faucet also available." And that's when I realized my mistake. Note: MY mistake, but still. It was confusing.

My husband really appreciated the LONG hoses that came with this faucet, first of all. That's the first thing he mentioned after installing it. We've had to go out and buy extensions with other faucets because the hoses are pathetically short. We decided to put this in our main kitchen sink, which is a 1 hole sink (perfect for this faucet) from IKEA. We have a LARGE single basin farmhouse apron style sink with butcher block counters. The sink sticks out a good 1.5" from the rest of the counter. We love it, but it's large. Previously we had an IKEA faucet to go with the sink, and they must know their own products because the faucet from IKEA was nice and LONG and the overhang from hold to sink was significant. So after this American Standard faucet was installed, the first thing I noticed was that it doesn't extend very far at all.

In fact, I found myself frustrated with how much water got splashed onto the backsplash and the back of sink "shelf" area where we keep soap. It doesn't even extend far enough to be directly over the drain, which is irritating when it comes to washing food down the hole with some pressure. Also, my husband like the faucet but he's 6 feet tall and long limbed. I'm 5'4" and short limbed, so I found myself really leaning into the sink to wash my hands and use the faucet.

This faucet also has a "chunky" look to it. Not so sleek, not so dainty. And so I felt it didn't match my kitchen very well. A bulky, modern, chubby faucet that didn't reach far enough over the sink. And while it was nice to have a pull out sprayer to wash things down (which our IKEA faucet didn't, which is why we chose to replace it with this) the water is only ever on stream setting so it lacks a punch to wash things down the drain forcefully. I wanted to save myself from having to sponge clean the sink sides and bottom all the time with a pull-out sprayer, but this didn't actually do much more me.

In the end, after a couple days I grew fed up with leaning over my sink farther and getting water splashed all over the back, I asked my husband to take this out and re-install our IKEA faucet. Sure, it doesn't have a pull-out spray hose or...well that's all it didn't have compared to the American Standard faucet...but it does extend far enough over my sink to not be annoying!

I really think they designed this thing too short. For our big farm house sink, extending a few inches at best over the basin isn't going to cut it. Not for us. BUT, it worked well and installed nicely so I cannot discount it on those points. If you want a short, chunky, modern bar faucet that doesn't extend much...then this one's for you!
profile.summary: Lasted a couple days before I couldn't take it anymore...

profile.description: For anyone starting to write, this is an excellent practice book for making upper-case letters. Using dry-erase markers, one can follow the examples and fill a page of practice letters. Requires dry-erase markers (not included with all items).
profile.reviewText:
I recently purchased this printing book from Lakeshore so that my 3-year-old can practice writing letters. A few months ago, this was out of the question as we were working in her pre-school book with similar pages. She only doodled in her pre-school book. This dry erase book is the perfect solution! She can use it over and over and it never gets ruined by use.

She's about 3 1/2 now, and can finally trace the letters! They're not perfect, but instead of saying she "can't do it, it's too hard!" as she did a few months ago, now she can actually trace the letters.

Each page of this book features one letter. At the top are a couple images with the letter, such as a leaf on the "L" page. The first printing line shows the letters with numbered strokes and arrows for the directions they should be written. Then there is a line of pale letters for your child to trace, and finally a couple blank lines so that they can print the letter on their own.

I think we will be using this book a lot as she learns to write. For now my daughter only traces the letters, but I'm sure we'll be using it for more lessons in the future as she learns what directions to write and practicing writing without tracing.

Finally, this is a durable book. The pages are thick and sturdy, nothing my daughter could rip or tear. It's spiral bound and works great with dry erase, the pages haven't stained or been damaged after several uses. I'm sure I'll be teaching my younger children with the same book when the time comes! It's definitely a better investment than those paper pre-school books that are written in once and cannot be re-used.

I would absolutely recommend this book to the home schooling family or those wishing to help teach their children at home. I think it'd make a great addition to pre-schools and day-cares as well.
profile.summary: Helpful starting point for home education

top_5.reviewText:

top_5.description: Please Read Notes: Brand New, International Softcover Edition, Printed in black and white pages, minor self wear on the cover or pages, Sale restriction may be printed on the book, but Book name, contents, and author are exactly same as Hardcover Edition. Fast delivery through DHL/FedEx express.
top_5.reviewText:
First of all, let me tell you to be VERY CAREFUL of reading reviews here on Amazon in regards to this book. One ill-thinking reviewer posts a major spoiler to this book in the FIRST LINE OF THEIR REVIEW. If you read it, first let me say I'm sorry. What a bad review. Second, I am happy to inform you that it's a serious spoiler, but only the penultimate one. There's an even bigger twist lying in the final chapter. And no, you WON'T guess it. I don't care how good you are at these things (and I'm pretty good, The Girl on the Train was obvious to me from halfway through).

Second, I'm honestly surprised that this book has some 1-star reviews. But I guess all the books honestly have their bad reviews. Trust the good ones when it comes to Behind Her Eyes, that is IF you like an edgy psychological thriller. One professional reviewer compared Behind Her Eyes to something Hitchcock. I'd like to highlight that for you. This book doesn't necessarily go supernatural, I wouldn't say that at all. But there is an edgy psychological thriller part to the plot. That's all I want to say, but I think you should consider if you're going to read this book...you might not like it if you're that person who can't watch/read the Hunger Games without ranting, "That could never happen in real life!" Then this book isn't for you. But Sarah Pinborough spins a deliciously devious web of a plot here, and I THOROUGHLY enjoyed it. But she goes no where as crazy as some of Stephen King's thrillers have. I don't get the "hate" I see on Goodreads about how this one strays a *tad* supernatural. It's the slightest tad, but took away nothing from the thrill for me.

Without spoiling anything, I'll say this: we hear stories about near death experiences ALL the time. The concept is not that out there. It was a creepy ending, in fact, especially reading this as a mother! So the few 1-star reviews that are saying the ending was too out there. I'm sorry, but I'm rolling my eyes. It was SHOCKING, but fantastic. It was the type of ending that makes you want to re-read it right away again because it will read totally different now that you KNOW.

Finally, I actually listened to this book on Audible. I love a British-narrated psychological thriller. This is exactly what I want in an audiobook and now I'm sad because I figure there won't be another quite like it in a while. It usually takes a while. But if you're considering the audiobook, this makes a great listen while on the road or cleaning house. The narrators are WONDERFUL (and I'm VERY picky about my narrators) and it was wonderfully produced.

I rarely recommend books on social media or write such enthusiastic reviews right away, but Behind Her Eyes was one of those rare few books that makes me just HAVE to share it with the world. If you can handle a truly edgy psychological thriller, DO IT! Get this one.
top_5.summary: BEWARE other reviews! You don't want to spoil this SHOCKING plot twist ending!!

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "The feature-rich golf GPS watch, the GolfBuddy WT5, takes you one step further with a slimmer design and a more comfortable fit to your wrist than its previous model. You can fully utilize Dynamic Green View and moveable pin placement features with simple press-and-hold buttons. The GolfBuddy WT5 features automatic hole/course recognition, shot distance measurement, digital scorecard, distances to targets and hazards, pin placement, an 8 Hour battery life in Golf Mode and 20 days in Watch Mode. GolfBuddy is a leading innovator in the golf rangefinder industry with a primary goal to provide the most accurate and innovative golf rangefinders in the market. Each of our GPS units comes preloaded with over 37,000 courses worldwide and as always, our products are 100% fee free. We never charge download fees or annual subscriptions. We also guarantee free lifetime course and software updates. Our tagline reads, "Accuracy Matters' and it is a mantra that we, at GolfBuddy, hold near and dear to us as it is reected in our product line.". The summary of the review text is "A little confusing at first, but turned out to be great!".
output:
A friend of mine recently began introducing me to the game of golf. When I saw the GolfBuddy WT5 I thought it would really help me figure out the game and provide a record of my progress.

I was excited when my GolfBuddy arrived. It comes in a mostly black cardboard box, which flips open to reveal the watch mounted inside. There is certainly nothing fancy about the packaging for gift giving purposes, but it's not like it's a Rolex or something, so it's appropriate for the product - plus it looks like it's very recyclable.

I'm a large man with an 8+ inch wrist and the GolfBuddy fit me just fine and is very lightweight and comfortable. A nice feature of the watch is its IPX7 Water Resistance rating, which means it can be submerged in up to 1 meter of water for 30 minutes without damage. So getting stuck in even the most torrential rainstorm will not be a problem for your watch. It's fairly sporty looking and I sometimes wear it as my daily watch as it's also very easy to read. The GPS distance feature is awesome, I use it to track how far I've gone on my evening walks.

The watch has four control buttons, and most functions are performed using only three of them (the fourth is mostly for on/off). When I first read the manual and started trying to use the features I quickly became frustrated. I could picture myself on the course flipping through this stupid little manual trying to figure out how to access all the functions, while my partner grows impatient with me wasting our time together!

Fortunately, I later found a very informative Training/Manual video on the manufacturers website, golfbuddyglobal.com, that runs through the initial setup, and complete feature set of the GolfBuddy. I watched the video and simultaneously performed the functions on my own watch. After a couple of run-throughs, the screens and the icons on each screen started to look familiar and make sense, and I was fairly confident I could use it on the course, with only occasionally referring to the manual if I got stuck.

After reading the other Amazon reviews I noticed some folks had problems with the initial setup and the watch not recognizing their local course; so I took their advice and rebooted the device at initial setup, and updated the course information from my GolfBuddy account making sure to SELECT OVERWRITE for any existing information on the watch memory. I didn't have any problems with setup or course recognition after that.

Out on the links my friend gave me the eye when I showed him my new golf watch. "Only practice will make you a decent golfer", was his response. Throughout the day, however, we BOTH consulted the GolfBuddy for assitance with club selection and avoiding hazards. I kept my own score and subsequently uploaded it to my GolfBuddy account so I can keep track of my progress. Several times during our outing my experienced friend remarked to me: "that damn thing feels like cheating, BUT IT SURE IS HANDY!".

**** RECOMMENDED! - 4 STAR ****

profile.description: Prevent minor damage to your 13.3" laptop screen with this Belkin TrueClear F7P327BT antismudge screen protector that features a strong, yet lightweight, design to help keep your device like new. TrueClear technology ensures optimal screen visibility.
profile.reviewText:
We recently got an HP Pavilion x360 13.3" Touchscreen 360-Degree Laptop and wanted something to protect the screen. The Belkin TrueClear Anti-Smudge Screen Protector seemed like a good choice. When it first arrived in the mail I was a bit concerned because the Belkin protector was in a box that was just a bit too small, so it was curled in a half-circle to fit. It flattened out just fine, however, and no damage was done to the protector.

INSTALLATION

The pictorial instructions Belkin includes with this product certainly leave a lot to be desired. Fortunately, I've installed a number of these screen protectors on numerous laptops, cell phones, & camera screens, and the most important lesson I learned is: START CLEAN. Work on a nice clean table, and first put down a soft, lint-free cloth to protect your device from scratches. Next, clean the screen with alcohol and a microfiber cloth, and dry using a second microfiber cloth. Don't forget the corners! Examine with a flashlight at an angle and make sure you didn't miss any areas and that there is no haze, which indicates it's not thoroughly clean.

You will now invariably have lots of dust and particles on the screen even if it's very clean. (This dust will show up under the screen protector as many tiny bubbles that CANNOT BE REMOVED because the dust permanently adheres to the screen protector adhesive.) I use canned air at this point to blow off the dust from the screen. USE THIS AT YOUR OWN RISK! Canned air has the potential to shoot out jets of super cold liquid that MAY HARM YOUR SCREEN. I've never had any problems in the 7 to 10 years I've been doing this, but I only use short puffs of gas and don't let the can get too cold. Also, always hold the can upright and don't use a brand-new full can for this as there is an increased likelihood of shooting out liquid when it's very full, or tilted!

For a large screen like a laptop, installation is a bit trickier than say a cell phone. Don't remove the whole protective backing at once! Peel back an inch on the narrower side of the protector and line it up as straight as you can with that edge of the laptop screen. Slowly continue peeling and applying, trying to keep the portion of the un-applied protector from laying on the clean screen. You can use your fingers or a credit card to push out bubbles as you apply it. Sometimes it helps to have a second person available as it seems like you need ten hands at once to peel, apply, smooth, hold...repeat, etc!

Once completely applied you may find you have a few stubborn bubbles that didn't release during application. You can try to gently lift a corner of the protector until you reach the offending bubble, then reapply the screen using a credit card to ensure smooth application.

IN USE

Once applied, I found the protector didn't interfere with the use of the touch screen in any way - it was just as responsive as before. I still get some smears and fingerprints with the protector on but they don't seem as noticeable as before it was in place. Visibility through the protector is excellent and I was hard-pressed to notice any difference before and after. My screen in only a 1366 x 768 resolution TN style LCD panel, so nothing really bright or super hi-def. I don't know how the visual performance would be on a really high-quality screen. I like being able to clean the screen most anytime I want without worrying if it will damage the delicate surface if I clean it too often.

I took one star off for the poor, pictorial style installation instructions, and the relatively high cost of this product. This item was fully 10% of the price we paid for our laptop, which seems like an awful lot for a thin piece of plastic! But I suppose if we get longer life out of the laptop it may pay for itself over time.

**** RECOMMENDED - 4 STARS ****
profile.summary: High quality touch-screen protector, but pricey.

I am able to really get in nooks and crannies when cleaning with a bottle brush now. 3) The flip cover keeps the drink opening cleaner. This is nice when the bottle is rolling around in the back seat of your car because your cupholders are filled with cups of coffee. Plus, when it's been in an old backpack it keeps the lint and gunk out of your mouth! 4) I like the added security of the locking button for when the bottle is doing those things in number 3 above. I know I won't have a big puddle of water to clean up later. I suppose the only drawback of some of the new features is more nooks and crannies to hide mold and dirt (the locking tab, hinged flip cover and the added complexity inside the cap will need extra attention to keep really clean.) Most people probably won't care because they have a dishwasher to clean the bottle in. I don't have one so I will need to pay extra attention while hand washing my new bottle. Oh yea, one more thing. Water looks extra cool and refreshing inside this cool blueish color bottle. Both my girlfriend and I remarked on it at the same time when I was filling the bottle for the first time! ***** HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - 5 STAR *****
profile.summary: Nicely redesigned bottle was awesome, until it started leaking!

profile.description: An Amazon Brand.
profile.reviewText:
Based on the price I pretty much expected this item to be on the cheap side when I ordered it, and it definitely is. The biggest problem with these cat trees are the plastic inserts with bolts in the riser tubes that are used to screw the whole thing together. As your cat climbs and scratches and jumps on and off the tree it flexes the hard plastic, which eventually cracks and breaks - and the thing ends up falling apart.

I expected this, so while I was assembling it I put gobs and gobs of hot melt glue at each point where it screwed together. This was a two-person job, one to quickly dispense the hot melt and the other to hold and screw the pieces together immediately before the glue hardened. Maybe if your cat is tiny you can get away with not gluing it together, but my tree is being used by a big, overweight male cat and I knew he was going to be rough on it.

Out of the box the tree has a pretty strong sisal-rope type odor so we let it air out outside for a day before assembling. We sprayed it with cat-nip spray and the cat, Merlin, took to it pretty quickly. It surprised us that he was easily able to climb up to the top roost, and even though nearly half of him hangs out of it, he still enjoys lounging and sleeping up there. He occasionally uses it as a scratching post, but he still seems to prefer the furniture for that!

We've been using it for a few weeks now and it is holding up well, time will tell how well it lasts in a year or so. The price was pretty reasonable for such a large tree, and as long as you don't mind adding some hot melt glue during assembly it should last for a while even with a large cat or two smaller cats.

**** 4 STARS - RECOMMENDED! ****
profile.summary: Works OK, but I Assembled it with Hot Glue

profile.description: Fresh tomato sauce has never been so easy! Make the most delicious sauces, salsas, dips, spreads and even baby food with the Ball freshTECH HarvestPro Sauce Maker. This easy-to-use and quiet machine can process up to 15 quarts of fresh tomato puree in 20 minutes! Save time, effort and mess in the kitchen with the dishwasher-safe parts and a splash guard to help prevent messes. This versatile appliance can process your garden fresh tomatoes, fruits, and vegetables to make a variety of fresh, ready-to-eat and home-canned foods.
profile.reviewText:
As a kid I remember my parents canning tomatoes from our garden. It was a completely manual process and took them many hours and much labor to complete. When I saw the Ball FreshTech Sauce Maker it made me want to try canning myself - but without all the manual labor.

The build quality of the unit is pretty good with sturdy plastic construction throughout. The instructions are very clear with lots of illustrations that tell you exactly how to assemble, use, disassemble and clean the unit. A double-ended cleaning brush used to clean the screens and other parts is thoughtfully included.

We followed one of the recipes in the booklet for making tomato sauce. The machine made short work of the 12 pounds of fresh tomatoes called for in the recipe. The motor was more than powerful enough to easily handle all 12 pounds without stopping. It's not the quietest appliance I've ever used, but it certainly isn't loud either. It's much quieter than a food processor or blender, and maybe just a bit louder than a KitchenAid type stand mixer on high.

Cleanup was fairly simple as all the wet parts are removable from the unit for cleaning in the sink. The brush cleaned the trapped pulp out of the metal screen quite well, and the rest of the parts cleaned up quick and easy with a kitchen sponge and dish washing liquid. All the parts are dish washer safe as well, but for best results I recommend removing any trapped pulp prior to cleaning.

Since we'll probably only use the Ball sauce maker a few times a year we decided to simply put everything back in the factory box for storage (once the parts dried), and stored it on a shelf in our pantry. It is a pretty large unit so it makes sense not to take up valuable cabinet or counter space with it.

We loved the fresh taste of the tomato sauce we made, plus we get to control how much salt and what spices go into it. We had to use hot-house tomatoes for this batch but are looking forward to this summer when we can get some farm fresh tomatoes to make up a huge batch of sauce, and we plan on making a batch of salsa, as well.

Considering the years of use you are likely to get out of this appliance I think it is priced appropriately. If you have your own garden or are able to take advantage of lower cost produce during the summer months, the unit may even pay for itself eventually. Not to mention the health benefits of controlling what goes into your body by avoiding all the salt and preservatives found in commercially prepared sauces.

***** 5 STAR - HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! *****
profile.summary: Sturdy, Powerful, Easy to Clean Sauce Maker

profile.description: What's lurking in your Mattress2 million dust mites and their allergenic feces, which are easily inhaled and can trigger allergies. The Dyson V6 mattress vacuum has powerful suction to remove allergens from your mattress.
profile.reviewText: Please don't be fooled by the word "Mattress" in this product's name, this is a full-featured Dyson hand vac similar to the (lower priced) Dyson V6 Trigger (same as Dyson DC58 Handheld), with two significant improvements: 1) Motorized Mattress Tool: Agitates and removes dust from upholstery. With stiff nylon bristles that agitate mattress fibers, the motorized mattress tool releases dust and allergens. 2) Whole Machine HEPA Filtration: Patented 2 Tier Radial cyclones, a post motor filter and a sealed system to ensure that the air that leaves the machine is cleaner than the air you breathe. This is currently the ONLY Dyson handheld with HEPA filtration. I have always felt Dyson made some of the best vacuum cleaners out there but were severely overpriced compared to other similarly performing brands. My girlfriend has asthma and has had her eye on the Dyson V6 Mattress vac since seeing it advertised on one of those home shopping channels. I was shocked to hear that some sources claim the average 10 year old mattress can nearly double in weight from the accumulation of pet and human hair, skin cells and dust mites (including their feces), along with the dried remains of saliva, sweat and other bodily fluids that get embedded in it - that's pretty gross! So we were pretty excited to have an opportunity to try out the Dyson V6 Mattress. I've had it close to a week now and have used it everyday - several times a day. I guess I understand now why folks get so excited about their Dysons, this is really a well engineered and handsome looking machine. It's constructed of heavy duty precision molded plastic, and the fit and finish are excellent. The V6 feels well balanced to hold and even though you need to continuously hold down the trigger during use, it's very easy to squeeze so your hand doesn't really get tired even after prolonged use. If I had a really big area to clean (like the mattresses), I did find myself switching hands, however, to give the other a break. The V6 comes with the motorized mattress tool, as well as a very handy combination tool, crevice tool, and a mini soft dusting brush. The kit also has a battery charger that you plug into a port on the rear of the vac. A full charge of the powerful 6 cell, 21.6v Li-ion battery takes 3.5 hrs, less if the battery isn't fully depleted. One of the home shopping channels was offering a version of the V6 with a wall mounted charging station/attachment holder included. I really wish Amazon sold that version! After charging up the vac, naturally the first thing we did was vacuum our five year old queen size mattress, and two older twin size mattresses. YES, mattresses are disgusting! We simply couldn't believe how much fine dusty debris we collected from the three mattresses. It took two full charges to complete all the mattresses as we went slowly and ran the MAX suction setting. The battery gets REALLY hot when using the MAX setting continuously. It's very important to let the unit cool for about 10 minutes before re-charging or you may damage the battery and shorten its life. Dyson claims the V6 Mattress is even quieter than the similar Dyson V6 Trigger. I found this V6 Mattress to have a high pitched, somewhat metallic sound to it - it's definitely not quiet, but it's not uncomfortably loud, either. Don't completely believe all the hype about the HEPA filtration ensuring "that the air that leaves the machine is cleaner than the air you breathe". While that may be true in theory, in practice, the spinning brush head kicks up some of that dust into the air while you're vacuuming - I sneezed once when I was doing the mattresses. Overall, I bet with the HEPA filtration it's a lot cleaner than vacuuming with a conventional handheld, though. We each vacuumed out our cars, using the mattress brush on the seats, mats, and carpets, and the rest of the tools elsewhere in the car - the V6 got them looking really nice and clean and it was fairly easy to maneuver. The suction on this handheld vac is EXTRAORDINARY, nearly equal to my mini 1 gal. Shop-Vac but without the annoying cord and fat hose. My car was pretty filthy as I'm not much of a neat freak, and the small dust collection bin on the Dyson needed emptying three or four times, which I did find as a shortcoming of the product. Please Note: the Dyson V6 Mattress is only for vacuuming DRY debris, DO NOT vacuum any liquids or wet solid material with this product! We've since vacuumed all our sofas and chairs and again were surprised by how much gunk was trapped in the upholstery. The motorized mattress tool is surprisingly maneuverable and follows the contours of tufted and uneven fabric surfaces very well - I think the strong suction helps with that. Day to day we usually keep the combination brush in place as it's the best all around tool for quick pick-ups like spilled oatmeal or Cheerios, and picking up dirt, sand and small stones from our entranceway and stairs. After so much use I figured I better clean the two filters, and the rest of the unit to keep it performing well. You only need to remove and rinse the two filters with COLD water (no soap), squeeze and tap the excess moisture out and let them dry for 24 hours - very easy. I also popped-off the dust collection bin and wiped it out with a damp paper towel, and brushed the dust off the rest of the unit, following up with a damp paper towel. The motorized mattress tool is easily disassembled by removing the side port and sliding the brush out to remove the dirt and entangled hair. The whole cleaning process took about 7 minutes. On mixed use of the normal and MAX settings, I guess we are getting a good 10 to 20 minutes per full battery, depending on how much we use the motorized brush and the MAX setting, so Dyson's claim of a 20 minute run time is reasonable. In the instruction manual it states: "If the battery needs replacing please contact the Dyson Helpline.", so I'm not entirely sure if the battery is user replaceable or not. I certainly hope it is, as the V6 is a pretty big investment to make only to have to dispose of it when the battery eventually dies. **** RECOMMENDED! - 4 STAR ****
profile.summary: So Much More Than Just a Mattress Cleaner!

profile.description: Linksys AC1900 Wi-Fi Wireless Dual-Band+ Router with Gigabit & USB 3.0 Ports, Smart Wi-Fi App Enabled to Control Your Network from Anywhere (EA6900)
profile.reviewText:
I'm a bit of a dinosaur when it comes to my internet. I do have a cable internet provider, but I only have the lowest tier service which is 5.5Mbps/1.06Mbps download/upload speeds. It meets my current needs and is affordable. My 12 year old Motorola 802.11g wireless router finally gave up the ghost recently, however, and it was time to move into this century for it's replacement. I wanted a good quality, higher-end model that I wouldn't need to replace for a good long time. After doing some research I found that Cisco/Linksys is just about the preeminent manufacturer of these devices. Linksys' latest and greatest product, the EA6900, seemed to be very feature rich, upgradeable, yet simple enough for a novice like myself to setup.

Setup was indeed a breeze for me. I connected the 3 antennae and let it do it stuff with my netbook and home PC. The software is built into the router so I didn't even need a CD (which is fortunate because my netbook doesn't even have one!)  I just let it setup the default configuration and it worked great. I immediately noticed my video streaming to be smoother with fewer delays for buffering. I realize I'm probably not challenging this router very much with my relatively slow connection, but when I'm ready to upgrade to a faster connection I know the Linksys EA6900 will handle it with ease.

Another thing I am very pleased with is the extra wireless range I'm getting with my netbook. I live on the second floor and sometimes like to relax on the front porch, which is at ground level. Previously, I've never really been able to bring my netbook with me because the connection always kept dropping in and out. I'm happy to say that now I get 3 bars out of 5 on my front porch! I can stream video no problem, and the connection is very stable. It's so relaxing to put my feet up and surf the net or watch a video with the crisp autumn air.

I suppose I will need to look into the additional features this router offers like adding an external hard drive. But for now I am very pleased with it. I think the only drawback I found right now was the relatively high price. But since I intend to use it for many years, the per year cost should be fairly reasonable.

I noticed a few fellow Amazon reviewers commenting they didn't like the look of this router. I barely even noticed what it looked like, let alone cared. But it looked fine to me - it's just a router after all.

**** RECOMMENDED! - 4 STAR ****
profile.summary: Review from a network novice - it works great for me.

profile.description: Indera - Mens Long Sleeve Ultra Heavy Weight Thermal Top 822LS, Natural, Waffle Knit, Extra Heavy Weight 9 Ounces, Highest Quality Construction, Extremely Cold Temperatures, Rib Cuffs, Size Small = 34/36 Medium = 38/40 Large = 42/44 Extra Large = 46/48, 50% Cotton 50% Polyester, Made in USA, #34175 34-175
profile.reviewText:
I've only worn these Indera - Mens Big and Tall LS Ultra Heavy Weight Thermal Tops a few times but I'm very impressed with the quality so far. Mine came with a stick-on label on the packaging that states: "Indira Mills Compay, Yadkinville, NC - DESIGNED & KNIT IN THE USA - An American Company Since 1914". This STICK-ON label suggests two things to me. The thread used is probably imported, and not every one of these thermal tops they sell is knit in the USA, otherwise they would permanently print this info on the package instead of using a stick-on label. Despite these reservations I'm pleased my purchase is supporting American manufacturing.

I am a very large man at 5 ft, 10 in, 360 lb, with a 52 in waist, 29 in inseam (pant length), and 35 in arm length. I ordered the size 6XL and am mostly satisfied with the fit. Because of my large stomach, long arms and torso I typically order my shirts in a long length. I wear a size 3XL to 4XL long in most of my normal shirts. I always order thermal tops several sizes larger because they are DESIGNED to be close fitting as this provides the optimum thermal insulation, plus most folks wear these under another layer so the snug fit keeps things from getting too bunched up. The fit around the largest part of my abdomen is quite snug even in a size 6XL, but the material and weave is naturally stretchy so it's still very comfortable.

I've only washed these thermal tops once so far and even with a warm water wash and drying on HIGH heat there was no shrinkage I could detect - that's very unusual for this type of garment! (The washing instructions call for warm water wash - no bleach, dry on low heat.) The length of these is very long, and after washing, the bottom of the shirt is a full 10.5 in below my waist in the back. I actually find it necessary to fold a few inches of the bottom of the shirt under so it doesn't appear so long! The arm length is also generous with the cuff falling about 1.25 in below my wrist. I'm grateful for the extra available length, as my experience with other thermal tops suggests that these may shrink up considerably with repeated washing.

The fit across my broad shoulders is loose and very comfortable, and the neckline of the garment reaches right up to the base of my neck but is not tight at all. The arms of the shirt are quite loose and move freely. I'm hardly a body-builder, so even a much more muscular person will have plenty of room for the "gun-show".

The weave of the fabric is tight but well ventilated, and these are not at all semi-transparent as some thinner and cheaper thermal tops are. They are marketed as "Ultra Heavy Weight", and are certainly thicker and heavier than any thermal shirt I have owned recently. (Interestingly, the product packaging is labeled "SUPER Heavyweight Thermals" - not Ultra as Amazon lists them.) The 50/50 cotton/poly fabric is a bit scratchy feeling against my skin right now as I've only washed them once (with a dryer sheet). I expect these to soften considerably after a dozen or so washes, as this has been my experience with other thermal tops made with this blend. I much prefer this fabric to 100% cotton as I perspire year round even on cold days, and the poly content combined with the open weave allows these shirts to stay fairly dry even when I'm shoveling snow for several hours.

I'll try to update this review over winter 2016 as I wash and wear them more. From about November to April I wear a thermal top EVERY SINGLE DAY so I expect to have plenty of experience with these.

UPDATE 02-11-2016, 5 MONTHS
I've been wearing these daily and still love them. I now own four all together as I bought a few more. I guess they've been washed five or six times now and they might have shrunk just the tiniest bit - they're still quite long in torso and arm length for me, though. They're still somewhat scratchy feeling against bare skin but have softened a bit since new. We haven't had a really cold winter this year in the northeast, but we keep our place at 62'F day and night and these thermals have kept me nice and warm.

***** 5 STARS - HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! *****
profile.summary: High Quality, Heavyweight Thermal Top with Minimal Shrinkage

profile.description: Lab Equipment & Instruments. Extech EX655 True RMS 600A Clamp Meter with NCV; AC/DC. Manufactured by COLE-PARMER. Extech brand products.
profile.reviewText:
Extech EX655 with Temp Measurement

I was interested in this meter because it measures a lot of different parameters and doesn't cost an arm and a leg. Extech positions itself between the no-name Chinese meters, and top quality meters like Fluke. For the home owner/handyman their products are a good compromise especially if you're only using the meter a few times a month, which is basically my situation. If I was a tradesman I wouldn't hesitate to buy a Fluke, however.

The Extech EX655 has a nice solid case, and provides a secure grip even with sweaty hands thanks to the rubberized orange side panels. I wouldn't say it's as bulletproof feeling as a Fluke but it comes pretty close and costs about half as much as a comparable Fluke meter.

I've used the Extech meter a few times around the house so far just to check it out, and I got comparable readings to several other meters I own for AC/DC voltage and current using both the clamp and test leads, and contact temperature using the thermocouple. The built-in LED light is very useful - sure beats holding a flashlight in your teeth! This is a 6,000 count meter which means it will read up to 59.99A, 599.9A or 599.9A before moving to the next range and thereby losing a digit of precision. 6,000 is a midrange count value, with cheap meters usually in the 2000 to 4000 range, and higher end meters in the 20,000 to 50,000 count range.

It's got a useful CAT III rating of 600V, and a CAT II rating of 1000V meaning you could use this meter pretty much at any job with the exception of maybe utility level work. You might find a limitation, however, in the clamp jaws which accommodate only up to a 350MCM wire size. Overall a very useful meter at a good price .

**** 4 STARS - HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! ****
profile.summary: Full Featured Meter at a Fair Price

profile.description: The Bushnell Legend L-Series Binoculars set the standard for performance in the field with maximum brightness, definition and clarity. With an ultra wide field of view, viewing excellence can be reached by any segment of outdoor enthusiasts. Magnification x Obj Lens: 10x42mm Close Focus: 8ft/1.9m PC-3 Phase Coating: Yes Lens Coating: Fully Multi-Coated Field of View: 340ft at 1000 yards Adapt to Tripod: Yes Eyecups: Twist-Up Locking Diopter: No Eye Relief: 18mm Focus System: Center Exit Pupil: 4.2 mm Prism Glass: BaK-4 Water/Fog Proof: Yes Prism System: Roof Weight: 23.5oz Size Class: Standard.
profile.reviewText: The Bushnell LEGEND-L 10x42mm Binoculars are a mid-priced, Bak-4 roof-prism style binocular suitable for birding, hunting, sightseeing, and concert events. Not to be confused with the older but similar Bushnell Legend "ULTRA HD" 10x42mm, model no. 191042, the review binocular comes from Bushnell's latest premium "LEGEND" Series. The 10x42mm "LEGEND-L" designation, model no. 198104, is the midrange offering in Bushnell's LEGEND Series with the "LEGEND-E" & "LEGEND-M" models rounding out the low and high end, respectively. I also own a pair of the older Bushnell Legend Ultra HD 10x 42mm Roof Prism Binocular, and a pair of Vanguard 10x42 Binocular with ED Glass (Black). All three units are a similar Bak-4 roof-prism style with fully multi-coated lenses and water/fog proof design. I did some back to back testing of all three models and found a lot more similarities than differences. FEEL/HANDLING All three models are approximately the same size, weight, and shape. The older Bushnell ULTRA HD has aggressive rubberized ribbing on the body which does assist in holding the binocs with wet/sweaty hands. The body is somewhat sculpted which my large fingers/hands fall right into naturally and comfortably. The current model Bushnell LEGEND-L, and the Vanguard ENDEAVOR's have a smoother, somewhat textured surface on the body which isn't quite as secure with wet hands. Also, my fingers/hands had just a bit harder time finding the right position compared to the Bushnell ULTRA HD's more sculpted body. FOCUS The review model Bushnell LEGEND-L is the hands down winner on focusing ease and accuracy. Velvet smooth focus and diopter adjustments, the controls seem to move just the right amount - not too fast or slow. The Vanguard ENDEAVOR was a close second, with the Bushnell ULTRA HD trailing a bit behind. As all three models are 10X magnification with a similar field of view, they all exhibited the same amount of unsteadiness when handheld. I prefer a 10X binocular as I like the extra zoom over an 8X model and am able to handhold this higher magnification reasonably well. CLARITY & COLOR The Vanguard ENDEAVOR takes the prize in this category with the Bushnell LEGEND-L a hair behind. For example, when viewing a beautiful juvenile yellow-crowned night heron at roughly 150ft in good light, the ENDEAVOR was slightly better able to resolve the close gray and white striations of the birds head. I will say, however, the Bushnell LEGEND-L made the orange-yellow color of the bird's eye "pop" just a bit more than the other two models. The Bushnell ULTRA HD was a trailing third in this category. It certainly has overall respectable optical performance but isn't quite in the same league when directly compared to the others. BRIGHTNESS The review model Bushnell LEGEND-L offered superior brightness in both bright and low light conditions, but did seem to suffer from slightly more flare in direct sun. The Vanguard ENDEAVOR and the Bushnell ULTRA HD had similar performance in bright light with both models exhibiting somewhat lower overall brightness (but less flare) than the superior LEGEND-L. In low light dusk conditions the Bushnell LEGEND-L excelled as I was able to use these for probably an extra 10 to 20 minutes as the sun went down. CONCLUSION In the end, all three of these models are excellent binoculars and since they are priced very close depending upon available rebates and/or sales you couldn't go wrong with any of them. If I had to choose only one pair, however, I would have to go with the review model BUSHNELL LEGEND-L's because of the better focusing, brightness and color, while still exhibiting excellent clarity. The Vanguard ENDEAVOR was a very close second, with the Bushnell ULTRA HD just a bit behind the better two models. ***** HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - 5 STAR *****
profile.summary: Best in League, All-Purpose Binoculars
