profile.description: The SentrySafe FHW40220 Fireproof Box and Waterproof Box provides durable and reliable protection for your important documents. UL Classified fire protection and ETL Verified water protection offer true peace of mind for your irreplaceable records. Complete with carrying handles for easy transportation and in-lid straps to keep your items organized, this safe is ideal for your personal storage and security needs.
profile.reviewText:
I wanted to give this product a higher rating than 3 Stars, but I couldn't because I don't know for sure what size this unit is, or what fire & water protection it is rated for! As of the date of this review the Amazon product page is rife with errors and omissions. Going to the Sentry site doesn't help because product FHW40220 DOESN'T EVEN EXIST! They have similar product numbers, FHW40120 and FHW40200, which certainly look similar, but how does a consumer know for sure??

Even the Sentry product manual I received with this unit is generic, entitled: "Waterproof Fire-Resistant Chests & Files". It doesn't list what models the manual covers, or what the product fireproof and waterproof specifications are! Even the fire safe itself doesn't have a model number on it! The model number is present only on a sticker on the plain brown outer product box. Now remember, I received this unit free from Amazon Vine to evaluate, so possibly I didn't receive a final retail version, so your actual experience may vary.

Since Amazon and Sentry are pretty stingy with product measurements, I did some of my own. This is a pretty hefty product (which is good); empty it weighs about 42lb., packed completely full of my paperwork it weighed just over 55lb. Inside dimensions are as follows: (I'm giving 2 sets of dimensions, one at the top of the opening, a second set at the inside bottom, because the interior walls taper inward toward the bottom.) TOP: 12"W x 8-1/8"L, BOTTOM: 11-3/4"W x 7-7/8"L,  DEPTH: 9-3/8".

There is some additional storage space inside the top lid as well. The approximate usable dimensions are 11-7/8"W x 7"L x 2"D. The unit includes 2 webbed straps that snap into the lid to secure items kept in that space. Sentry assumes you will use this space to store frequently accessed items like portable hard drives, USB sticks, and CD/DVD media.

Maximum Outside Dimensions:  Approximately 16-1/2"W x 13-3/4"L x 14-1/2"H

Sentry says you can put standard letter sized hanging file folders inside the unit for better organization. With a limited amount of storage space available, I didn't want to waste any of it on hanging files, but that is a convenient option if you want it. I was able to place a full 13lb. of paperwork, which amounted to well over 500 documents, plus I stored a 1GB USB hard drive, and a couple of backup data DVD's in the lid.

I've owned a number of Sentry fire safes in the past so I know from experience it's a good idea to place all paperwork and valuables in large Ziploc bags or Tupperware containers so they don't get damp and musty from the fire protective material Sentry puts inside their safes. It's a hard, white, powdery material that is basically drywall. (Gypsum, or calcium sulfate dihydrate. Don't worry, you can't see or feel this material, it's sandwiched between the hollow plastic body of the safe!) But this material is "hydrated" and chemically contains about 20% water by weight! During an actual fire, as this material is heated it steams off all that water, effectively keeping the contents of the safe hundreds of degrees cooler. That's how every consumer Sentry Fire safe product works. But the rest of the time it makes for a fairly damp environment inside the safe, so the use of Ziploc bags is important to prevent any mold or mustiness. I've read it can reach up to 80% humidity inside a sealed fire safe - a cigar humidor is only 70%!

That's also one of the reasons Sentry warns you NOT to store PEARLS, firearms, weapons, combustible materials, or medications in your safe. Another HUGE reason is THESE SAFES ARE NOT THEFT-RESISTANT!  It's very easy to pry open this safe, or just pick it up and walk away with it! DON'T BUY THIS WITH THE INTENTION OF KEEPING YOUR VALUABLES SAFE FROM THEFT OR TAMPERING! It is NOT designed for that purpose. In addition, the manual warns NOT TO STORE DELICATE ITEMS LIKE JEWELRY, WATCHES, AND PHOTOS DIRECTLY IN THE SAFE. They recommend putting these items in an airtight container first. Sentry and Amazon have done a lackluster job warning consumers about these important limitations in their product description. You shouldn't have to purchase a product and have it delivered to your home before you realize it is completely unsuitable for your needs! Shame on Amazon and Sentry for this.

On a more positive note, this is a nice looking, well designed fire safe. The top cover has an attractive repeating hexagon design that reminds me of aluminum diamond plate. The molded-in side handles are sturdy and secure, and balance the weight of the box, as well as keeping the safe close to your body while lifting and carrying, to reduce strain on your back.

The top opens easily with a small push button activated latch. When opened the lid swings to just a bit past full upright allowing easy access to the storage compartment, and the weight of the base is sufficient to keep the unit securely upright even when the lid is fully open. (Some similarly designed units can tilt backwards and fall over with the lid open.)

The lid latches securely, and the lock is easy to engage with the 2 included tubular lock keys. Again, this is a convenience lock intended to deflect casual attempts at opening your chest. If somebody wanted to get inside your fire chest they could do so in under a minute with a pry-bar!

I'm giving this unit a Marginal Recommendation because it is designed well, and if the fire-proof and water-proof specifications that Amazon lists are accurate, it will provide good protection for both important documents and digital media. I just wish Amazon & Sentry had done a lot better job of describing the product limitations.

***MARGINALLY RECOMMENDED - 3 STARS***
profile.summary: Seemingly decent product, but poor Amazon/Sentry Description & Documentation!

I'm a big fan of baking soda and it's many uses. Arm & Hammer baking soda is a very versatile green cleaner. It's fragrance free, no fumes and good for people that have allergies or asthma. I use it to clean sinks, bathroom, deodorize my fridge, whiten my teeth, antacid, and as a drain cleaner! The internet, along with the Arm & Hammer website, has a wealth of information regarding it's uses.

This product states it's not for use in baking because of it's granulation. It comes in a handy water-resistant, resealable bag with a scoop for measuring the amount you need. I like that because I usually store the cardboard box of baking soda in a plastic bag to prevent clumping and to contain the spillage of powder. (Apparently we were lucky our bag wasn't leaking as MANY reviewers noted. I'm sure Amazon will address this problem soon, though.)

The package states that it has a finer granulation for cleaning. Upon opening the package I noticed it was finer with no clumping. I cleaned my stainless steel sink with it and it rinsed away a bit easier than with the standard type. I have been using a generic baking soda for years and found that it never scratched my sinks, tub surround etc. I can't say I noticed a big difference with this product, and I don't feel at it's current price of $11.99 that it's a very good deal. A 1 pound box at the store is only about a dollar, and I can use it for baking as well!

I would have given it 5 stars for the versatility of baking soda, with superior packaging. I deducted a star, however, because despite the handy resealable package and finer granulation this product is a lot more expensive than the store brands. I can put my baking soda in a plastic bag or container and it's cheaper. The finer granulation didn't make that much of a difference, either.

profile.reviewText:
The first thing I was struck by when I opened the package to the Sony MDR-1R Premium Headphones was the incredible quality of construction. Without even hearing them yet, I thought to myself  "these really are PREMIUM headphones." Of course, that was only a first impression, and all the quality workmanship and materials won't make up for a mediocre sounding product. I am, however, happy to report that after extensive listening these "cans" sound just as good as they look and feel!

I initially spent several hours listening to the Sony 1R's using a variety of sources: Oppo BDP-105 Blu-Ray (w/ built-in audiophile grade headphone amp); Accuphase E-202 vintage integrated amp & Sony CDP-CE335 five-disc CD player; 3rd generation iPod Nano; Sony MHC-1750 "desktop" system. My first impressions were that these are well balanced headphones that (obviously) sound best paired with the highest quality equipment, but are still pretty excellent even when used with lesser sources like the iPod and the Sony desktop system.

I know the theory of product "break-in" is considered voodoo nonsense by many audiophiles, who claim: "if you can't measure the difference after break-in, then it didn't happen". Well I disagree, and always break-in speakers and headphones prior to giving a critical assessment or review. For headphones I use a simple (and free) program found on the JLAB Audio website. I plug the headphones into my computer and run the file continuously at a low to medium volume for about 24 hours straight. The audio burn in file contains a nonstop loop of: white noise, pink noise, radio white noise, 20-20000 Hz frequency sweeps, 10-30000 Hz frequency sweeps, 20-200 Hz frequency sweeps, as well as a minute of silence in between each for a rest period. (I recommend you do this in an unused room, or while you're away at work, because the weird noises get pretty annoying after a few hours of listening to them repeat!) As with the other three pairs of headphones that I have performed this break-in on, I noticed a substantial improvement in bass response afterward.

I evaluated the Sony's mostly on their own, but also occasionally in comparison to my current favorite headphones, the Audio-Technica ATH-M50 Professional Studio Monitor Headphones with Coiled Cable. The M50's are considered by many to be the best headphones in their price class. When I evaluate headphones I tend to unconsciously break down their sound into several categories (in descending order of importance to me): Clarity/Detail; Bass Response; Tonal Balance; Spaciousness/Openness; Comfort; Sound Isolation. These are the attributes that are important to me, you may have other criteria, and/or a different order of importance.

I did most of my critical listening using the Oppo BDP-105 Blu-Ray with a combination of commercial and home burned CD's, MP3 and high-res FLAC files. These will be my "indoor headphones", due to their relatively large size and high value, so I will almost exclusively be using them with the Oppo in my living room, and occasionally with the Sony system in my bedroom. I spent several hours a day over about 2 weeks listening to 70's and 80's rock and pop, modern Top 40, a smattering of well recorded classical, blues, and jazz tracks, and whatever else I was in the mood for, like some female and male vocals, techno and rap.

-- Clarity/Detail --
The Sony's have a wonderful clarity and detail when used with excellent source material. I often found myself closing my eyes and "floating away" when listening to particularly beautiful or well recorded songs. To me that experience is often the essence of headphone listening - the ability to be completely immersed in the world of the song. Listening to music through speakers has a more immediate, and physical sensation for me.

The Sony's didn't do quite as well with lesser recorded material. There's a CD that I use as my "bad recording benchmark", it's Kings of Leon - Come Around Sundown. It a recent work from 2010, but it just always sounds horrible to me when played at any kind of volume. It's too bad because it's a great CD. The Sony's lost a lot of their clarity on this CD, and I think their fine ability to resolve musical detail actually made them sound worse.

-- Bass Response --
Serious bass response here! Very nice especially with the highly processed Top 40 and techno tracks. I'm glad my girlfriend didn't walk in on me during these because I was bobbin' and shakin' my head all over the place seriously getting into the music! (She always giggles at me when she sees me doing that...lol.)  The Sony's are a bit better at bass than my Audio-Technica ATH-M50's.

-- Tonal Balance --
To me tonal balance is a headphone's ability to reproduce sound without over-emphasizing or seriously neglecting highs, mids, or lows. Overall tonal balance was pretty good on the Sony's, but at higher volumes (where I usually listen) the higher-mids became a bit overpowering on some tracks - actually causing me to lower the volume a few times to back it off. It's not horrible, I think it just causes some listening fatigue after a while.

-- Spaciousness/Openness --
This category evaluates the "airiness" and stereo imaging. Since these are closed-back headphones by design, airiness is generally less than an open-air type. I personally am willing to accept this in exchange for the superior bass response afforded by closed-back phones. Despite this, as I described earlier, these headphones have a beautiful, immersive quality to them. I think this is where the Sony's really outshone my Audio-Technica ATH-M50's.

-- Comfort --
With thick, soft cushioning all around, these can best be described as "plush" - think of sinking into a soft leather sofa. The leather ear pads are top quality and the pressure exerted on your ears while wearing is firm but comfortable. After a couple of hours of wearing I did notice some slight discomfort on the tips of my ears possibly from subtle contact with the inside of the headphone's structure. This discomfort was minimal at best, but I thought it worth mentioning. I would say overall fit and comfort are about equal to the  Audio-Technica ATH-M50's, though the Sony's just FEEL much better on your head due to the high quality padding.

-- Sound Isolation --
This attribute is of little concern to me since I'm often listening alone, and very loudly. I know my girlfriend (and maybe even my downstairs neighbors) certainly appreciate the excellent sound isolation of the Sony MDR-1R Premium Headphones. She tells me that she can barely hear them playing in a fairly quiet room even though I'm rocking out. She can't hear any difference in isolation between the Sony's and Audio-Technica's so I guess they're about equal.

Conclusion
I think I have a new favorite pair of headphones! Overall the Sony's edged out my Audio-Technica ATH-M50's. Sound wise they are very close, each with it's own excellent sound signature. However, when you consider the superior quality look and feel, and plush comfort of the Sony's they come out quite a bit ahead. Are they worth the substantial extra cost? (The Sony's are nearly twice the cost of the Audio-Technica's) That's for you to decide what your priorities are. For me the Sony's are worth the extra investment.

4 STARS - RECOMMENDED!
profile.summary: Top of the Line Cans, with a Price to Match.

profile.description: This 6-Piece Ratcheting Bar Clamp and Spreader Set comes with nylon non marring pads to protect and grip work firmly.
profile.reviewText:
NOTE: THIS REVIEW IS FOR THE 6 PIECE SET WITH (2) 12" CLAMPS, AND (4) 4" CLAMPS.

I had a project in mind when I ordered this set. Several years ago I purchased a 75 yr old antique pharmacy balance on eBay, and despite the seller's best efforts to pack the very delicate instrument for shipment, it arrived with some damage. The balance has a beautiful wooden case with glass panels that slide up to give access to the balance beam. Some of the joints holding the wooden case together had separated and cracked during transit. It addition, several small trim pieces broke away from the case.

I purchased some Elmer's carpenter glue and set about piecing the dislodged joints together. I used the 2 large clamps included with the set to secure everything while it dried. Unfortunately, I was only able to use the clamps on the narrow dimension of the cabinet as the long side is 16" and the 12" clamps wouldn't fit. I used several of the small 4" clamps to hold the small trim pieces as they dried.

I was very pleased with the performance of all the clamps I used. It was easy to open them up to within an inch of the piece I was clamping, and them slowly squeeze the trigger to move the clamp into position. The action was smooth and predictable and I didn't have any problems with the clamps loosening significantly over the 24 hours I left them on during drying of the glue. The plastic pads did not damage the wood in any way, though I did put a couple layers of paper towel between the pad and the wood to protect it.

The reason I only give this set 3 stars is the price. My set would have been about 40 bucks with free ship. I had to go to a local Harbor Freight store to buy larger clamps for the long dimension of the cabinet. They had a good assortment of nearly identical quality Chinese made clamps and I was able to get (2) 24" clamps for about eight bucks each, and they had the small 4" clamps for about three bucks each plus tax. I think the 12" ones were around five or six bucks each. I know that Amazon has to ship this item and it has a fairly large footprint because the clamps are arranged side by side on a large display card. Plus, it's pretty heavy so I imagine it was expensive to ship and that's where a lot of the cost comes in. However, I just thought the while thing was a bit over priced.

Other reviewers mentioned their disappointment using these clamps in heavy-duty  applications like joining large pieces of wood where you really want some clamping force. I can't speak to that application, but I would have to say these are probably designed for more light-duty applications such as the balance I repaired, or making some light furniture repairs around the house.

Personally, I think the 12 piece set Amazon sells is a much better value, and much more useful. Unfortunately Amazon doesn't give you any information about the dimensions of the clamps in the set. But based on the product photo and knowing the actual dimensions of my set, I would say you get (2) 12" clamps, (2) 18" clamps, (2) 4" clamps, and (6) assorted plastic spring clamps in sizes that look like about 4" to 6" long. And the price is the same! So it depends on your anticipated applications which set you get.
profile.summary: Useful, but expensive for the quality of the product.

profile.reviewText: NOTE: PLEASE SEE THE "CUSTOMER IMAGES" I HAVE ADDED TO THE AMAZON PRODUCT PAGE - THEY ACCOMPANY THIS REVIEW. Back when I was a lot more serious about my photography hobby I owned a Pelican 1510-004-110 Case with Padded Dividers, Black(1514) hard-sided case with the Pelican 1519 Lid Organizer for 1510 and 1514 Case. I had a Canon 20D dSLR, and a bunch of Canon "L" lenses that I wanted to protect from almost anything. The Pelican case certainly did the job when I was kayaking one day about 10 years ago. The entrance to the waterway from the rental place was right near a bridge that narrowed (and sped-up) the flow. I had my Pelican case strapped to the top of the kayak, and I made the mistake of entering the water at a 90 degree angle not realizing the current that was present. I immediately rolled and my Pelican case (and the $7k worth of equipment in it) was plunged into the water! (Truth be told, I'm not much of a kayaker.) I limped back to the shore with my inverted kayak, and the Pelican case floating along side. Of course there wasn't a drop of water in the case and everything was untouched. That's a nice story to sell you a Pelican 1514, but that was one of exactly three times I ever used that beast of a case. It was just too darn heavy and cumbersome to use on a regular basis - I hated that thing. Today, having sold all my expensive (and ridiculously heavy) camera and lenses, I own a lightweight Canon EOS Rebel T2i 18 MP CMOS APS-C Sensor DIGIC 4 Image Processor Full-HD Movie Mode Digital SLR Camera with a 3.0-Inch LCD and Dedicated Movie Button (Body Only) and a couple of zoom lenses, as well as two Panasonic Lumix big-zoom cameras: the older DMC-FZ28, and the excellent new Panasonic Lumix DMC-FZ200 12.1 MP Digital Camera with CMOS Sensor and 24x Optical Zoom - Black. I was looking for a smaller & lighter rolling camera bag that I wouldn't mind carrying to and from the car for weekend drives, or schlepping through an airport once in a while on vacation. Well the Lowepro LP36398-PAM Pro Roller Lite 150 AW Camera Bag (Black) has filled that need for me perfectly. Even with my Acer Aspire One AO722-0473 11.6-Inch HD Netbook (Espresso Black), and all my camera and miscellaneous gear, the Lowepro 150 AW only weighs 18.5 lbs. fully loaded. (The old Pelican weighed about that EMPTY!) The bag measures about 14" x 20" x 9" including protrusions like the handle and wheels. With the telescoping handle fully extended the bag is about 38" tall. The padded Velcro partitions inside the bag make it easy to fit & protect whatever size gear you own. I've got three cameras and two lenses, a netbook, and all the mice, extra batteries, chargers, and AC adapters that go along with them, and I still have room to spare. The outside walls of the bag are very solid and provide plenty of protection from impact, while the padding inside absorbs shock and keeps everything in place. Fit and finish is excellent, and only high quality fabrics and materials are used on this product. Sure the 150 AW isn't cheap, but that's the price of quality and the extra little details that make it a pleasure to use. Everything about this bag is top-notch from the heavy-duty wrap around zipper with the clever interlocking holes that accept a TSA approved lock Lewis N. Clark Tsa Key Card Lock, to the high-density plastic protective base on the bottom of the bag that doubles as a second handle to allow you to easily hoist the bag two-handed into the airline overhead compartment. This bag has one of the cushiest handles I have ever seen outside a Rolls Royce Phantom! It's downright plush and makes the bag a lot nicer to heft up and down the stairs, and in and out of the car. The cushioned handle is part of a thick nylon webbing that wraps about 2/3's around the bag and forms two additional side handles. The extension handle for the bag isn't padded but it's big and comfortable, and the telescoping extension is made from sturdy aluminum which glides smoothly opened and closed, and locks securely in place in either position. When closed, a tasteful flap with magnetic catch conceals the extension and keeps it from accidentally opening. The bag glides smoothly on a pair of 3 in. diameter wheels. The wheels are hard rubber with stylized rigid plastic hubs, attached with metal hardware. They won't last forever as there is a bit of side to side play in them, but they will stand up to reasonable abuse for several years, I imagine. The wheels are backed with hard-sided plastic protectors to protect from the elements and provide rigidity to the bag. A feature not mentioned in Amazon's product description is a folding rain cover that resides in a hidden Velcro pocket right behind the telescoping extension handle. Even the brochure that was attached to the bag when it arrived doesn't mention this rain cover, or how to use it! (Please see the customer photos I have added to Amazon's product page.) The rain cover is a nice touch but is poorly designed because when used it doesn't fully cover the zipper at the bottom of the bag. Rain could possibly splash up from the sidewalk and permeate that exposed zipper. Something to remember in inclement weather. All in all this is a fine product with many excellent features and deserves a solid 5 star rating despite the minor shortcomings of the rain cover. RECOMMENDED - 5 STARS!

profile.reviewText:
The AT-A-GLANCE, 2016 Erasable Wall Calendar will be very handy to have next year for keeping track of doctors appointments and meetings. Keep in mind it's quite LARGE at almost 3 feet by 4 feet and you will need to dedicate a good chunk of wall space for this. I thought I could put it on a door in the vertical orientation, but it was just about a 1/2" too wide for that and interfered with opening and closing the door! I had to find some wall space to hang it, which unfortunately ended up placing it in a less noticeable and useful location - DARN. In the end, however, I was glad to have mounted it horizontally on the wall, because I realized in the vertical position it would become very uncomfortable entering appointments on the bottom of the calendar while kneeling on the floor!

The calendar comes with a black medium-fine point erasable marker. The tip is about the width of a fine point Sharpie, so it's still fairly broad. I definitely would have preferred a finer point erasable marker be included with this, or preferably one of each size. I find I'm limited to two entries per square with the current marker. I may purchase a finer one so I can fit an additional appointment per square, as I'm sharing this calendar with my girlfriend and it's not uncommon for us to have three or more things going on in a single day between us.

Corrections are fairly easy to make with a damp tissue, or if the entry is older you can dab a corner of a tissue with some alcohol to remove the entry.

The graphics are bright, clear and easy to read at several feet from the calendar. It's made of light card stock and laminated on both sides. Be warned it does crease easily so be gentle if you need to roll it back up or move it around for some reason. Even if it does crease (mine had a few light creases from rough handling during shipping), that the creases tend to smooth out and don't really affect the writing surface too much.

profile.reviewText: This Lexar JumpDrive S35 32GB is my second USB 3.0 flash drive, the other being a PNY Turbo 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive - P-FD64GTBOP-GE. They are both about equally fast on a USB 3.0 connection, but this Lexar JumpDrive seemed faster on a legacy USB 2.0 connection. I use it mostly for moving and sharing 25MB to 2GB audio and video files, as well as an external drive for my OPPO BDP-105 Blu-Ray player. I especially like the swivel design that completely encloses and protects the connector. What isn't evident from the single Amazon photo is that as you swivel the green shell around to close the drive, the USB connector physically RETRACTS INTO the white part of the drive - very clever design and cool to watch! I've had several friends ask me to open and close the drive again so they could see what just happened. The closed drive is very compact and with the included key ring loop it's easy to keep it with you at all times. It does include Encrypt Stick Lite software, which is "an advanced security solution with 256-bit AES encryption". I tried using it once and at first nothing happened. I went to the Lexar site and found you need to have the latest USB 3.0 driver installed on your computer for the Encrypt Stick Lite software to work. There is a link on the site that takes you to an Intel site where you can download the latest driver. After I did that everything worked fine. I don't usually encrypt my files on the drive, but I wanted to make sure it worked in case I need to one day. The rather thin-plastic construction of the JumpDrive S35 is a little more flimsy than I would have liked, but after about a month of several-times-a-week use it's still working great. If I have any durability issues later on I'll be sure to update this review. ***** HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - 5 STAR *****
profile.summary: Fast, Stylish and Reliable USB Flash Drive

profile.description: H Wireless cuts the cord on their highly successful H Series headset line to deliver exceptional audio in a brilliantly designed wireless headset. Crystal clear audio and cutting edge performance on all your platforms. Dont settle - go wireless and limitless. H Wireless is continuously frequency-hopping to preempt and circumvent interference. Most other headsets wait for interference to be detected to change channels - these just avoid it completely.
profile.reviewText:
I was reluctant to spend this kind of money on headphones from a brand I had never even heard of before. I am, however, very glad I took a leap of faith on these because they're an incredible pair of headphones!

FIT & FINISH

These headphones look and feel like the premium price they command. These feature nicely cushioned earphones and headband of supple leather-like vinyl; sturdy matte-black and glossy plastic construction with a rubberized embossed "steelseries" strip on top of the headband; contrasting orange stitching and fabric inside the earcups round out the look.

The control box is a tasteful yet fairly unobtrusive looking black box, with a pleasant looking blue digital display that was easy to read, and fit in nicely with my other audio components.

The only thing missing is any kind of label indicating which earcup is left or right! A surprising omission from headphones of this quality.

CONNECTIVITY

I really wanted to put these headphones through their paces when it came to connections, because I needed to know that I could use them in a variety of applications, otherwise what's the point? I connected the control box a total of seven different ways - four digital connections using an optical cable or USB, and three analog connections using RCA jacks and/or 3.5mm "headphone" jacks.

I connected a four year old Panasonic DMP-BD60 Blu-Ray player, a one year old OPPO BDP-105 Blu-Ray, a one year old LG 47LS4500 LCD TV, and a three year old AMD Althon II based desktop PC running Windows 7. Of the seven connections I attempted, the only one that failed (initially) was the Panasonic Blu-Ray playing an Iron Man-2 Blu-Ray in DTS-HD surround. No matter what settings I tried on the Panasonic or the  SteelSeries H headphones, I could not get the English language programming to play. I could play the alternate languages because these were encoded in Dolby Digital, not the higher quality DTS-HD. I believe this was more a problem with my four year old Panasonic player, than the headphones. I was finally able to play this Blu-Ray in DTS-HD by using the optical out connection from my LG TV, instead of the optical out directly from the Panasonic player.

SOUND QUALITY

Clearly, the SteelSeries H Wireless Headset benefits from a digital connection. In some cases the analog connections produced barely tolerable sound quality. Conversely, the digital connections exhibited crisp and dynamic sound quality, with firm bass, smooth midrange, and transparent highs. The bass was believable, taut and wholly acceptable, but these are not cans for "Bass Heads", however. The surround effects were convincingly produced and felt very immersive especially from high quality source material. Most sources, with the exception of the PC connection, did not produce a high enough sound level for my personal preference. I like rock concert level volumes with my music and movies, so for most people this won't be a problem!

My preferred connection for these headphones is to my PC via USB 2.0. I played a number of HD quality movie files, and high quality music files in FLAC format, and was simply blown away by the quality! Trust me, I'm a 35 yr audiophile and home theater nut, and it takes quite a lot to impress me now, and impress me the SteelSeries H headphones did indeed.

RANGE

One of the things I was most concerned about when I purchased these wireless headphones is that they would have a pathetic range and/or cut out and produce static as I moved around. Nothing could be farther from the truth! I'll be really honest, I'm kind of jaded with the exaggerated claims many manufacturers make about the performance of their products, but the SteelSeries H seem to be the real deal. I was walking (and dancing) around my three-bed apartment, making a sandwich at the other end of the house, in rooms with closed doors, downstairs and outside my apartment - and these headphones never gave me anything but beautiful, crystal clear sound without so much as a drop-out or a bit of static! I truly was impressed. I made some measurements after the fact, and at a maximum I was 43ft. from the receiver, on the same floor and through three walls. In a second measurement, I was 30 ft. from the receiver, down one floor and outside the house.

I also tested these operating right next to a running fan motor, a fluorescent fixture, and finally next to my wireless router - I never heard any difference in sound quality!

COMFORT

These are nicely padded headphones that rest firmly on your head, and resist all but the most vigorous head movements - despite this, I found them to be very comfortable for extended wear. The longest I wore them was about 2.5 hours at a stretch, which is my personal limit for ANY headphones. The volume control was easy to access and responsive, I really didn't use any other controls on the headset except this.

CONCLUSION

While commanding a premium price, at least the SteelSeries H Wireless Headset with Dolby 7.1 Surround Sound offers a commensurate level of sound quality, comfort and performance.

***** HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - 5 STAR *****
profile.summary: I am thoroughly impressed with these headphones!

profile.description: The Sennheiser PC 350 Special Edition 2015 noise blocking gaming headset features performance optimized for competitive gaming. The sound is tailored to provide improved positional accuracy. The closed back design is perfect for immersive LAN gaming, isolating you from any outside noise so you hear even the faintest detail of your game. The professional grade noise cancelling microphone ensures crystal clear communication while delivering a high quality signal, making it the optimal choice also for streaming.
profile.reviewText: The PC 350 Special Edition 2015 headset is Sennheiser's latest edition of their well regarded PC 350, which has been around for a few years now. The 2015 version seems to be identical to last years model in appearance, but Sennheiser claims: "The (2015) Special Edition features an updated and even more durable closed design for gaming in privacy, as well as new design and improved user friendly features." The PC 350 SE 2015 ships in an environmentally friendly, small plain brown cardboard box. This was quite a surprise to me, and I found it to be a bit of a letdown. When you spend this kind of money you expect some nice packaging especially if you plan on giving this as a gift! Another big letdown for me on the 2015 model is it doesn't include the nice zip-up hard case that last years model had. These have the same MSRP as the older model so I'm very surprised at this omission. All that is included in the box is the headphones and a PCV 07 combo audio adapter, which is used to split the combined 1/8" headphone/mic jack into the familiar separate pink and green 1/8" jacks. The headphones do, however, have a quality feel to them with nice matte black plastics, and silver metal accents. The 3m (10ft ) thin, straight cord is attached on the left ear cup, and the soft fabric wrap on the cord in a nice feeling touch. The left earcup mounted mic swings up and down smoothly, yet firmly, and features the usual on/off positional function - down for on, up for off. Easy to place just right, plus it stays put - no unwanted drooping or creeping. The volume control on the right ear cup is easy to locate quickly, and is firm enough to make fine adjustments. The earpads are a soft and supple simulated leather-vinyl material and are VERY comfortable. They really conform nicely to your head as they fit completely over your ears and seal the outside world very well. They hold firmly against your head, but not so much that it hurts. I have worn these for up to three hours continuously and have not experienced any discomfort. They do get a bit sweaty after a while but all of my headphones do that. The headband is padded and comfortable, and the sliding size adjustment features detents to hold the setting and to make it easy to exactly match the left and right fit. These have a large range of size adjustments so I imagine they will fit even large heads. I found the sound quality to be excellent for music, games and movies. These nearly rival the quality of my Audio-Technica ATH-M50 headphones I own just for music. When I first started using the PC 350 SE 2015's, however, I couldn't understand why they sounded so bad, and the volume was so low. Then I remembered these are high impedance headphones at 150 Ohms, so I plugged them into my BEHRINGER MICROAMP HA400 headphone amp and the difference was like night and day! If you don't have a high quality, high output soundcard, be prepared to run these through a headphone amp for best results. Where the PC 350 Special Edition 2015 headphones are really impressive is the sound quality and noise cancellation of the microphone. It's better than on anything I've owned before. The noise cancelling works nearly perfectly; it picks up near whispers, but doesn't pick up your normal breathing - which is amazing to me. I've never used a studio pro microphone, but I imagine this must be pretty close to that. One thing I didn't like was I could hear some microphonics caused by the headphone cord occasionally rubbing against my clothing. It's not too bad, and only really noticeable during the quietest musical passages or in very quiet scenes in a game, but it was definitely there. Overall, these are pretty great headphones, but if you already own the previous version, or if you're being charged anywhere near full MSRP, then I would definitely look elsewhere, especially if these are intended for gift giving. I am giving these 3.5 Stars overall, but rounding up to 4 Stars because of the exceptional mic and great sound quality. **** RECOMMENDED - 4 STARS ****
profile.summary: Great headphones, just don't pay full MSRP price for them.

profile.description: The Vicks Sweet Dreams Cool Mist Humidifier creates cool, visible mist to help temporarily relieve your child's cough and congestion symptoms for better breathing and more comfortable sleep. The ultrasonic Vicks Cool Mist Humidifier has a built-in projector that transforms your child's bedroom with nine dream-inspired images in three themes: sea, safari, and starry night. Designed for small to medium rooms, this sleep humidifier has adjustable mist control and ultra-quiet operation that helps your child rest soundly. The 1-gallon tank allows up to 24 hours of operation, and the air humidifier shuts off automatically when the tank is empty. A large tank opening makes the humidifier easy to fill and clean. The Vicks Sweet Dreams Humidifier doesn't require any filters, and it accepts up to two Vicks VapoPads to provide soothing menthol vapors. A sample Vicks VapoPad is included.
profile.reviewText:
Great for kids, but fun for the kid at heart. This humidifier is small enough to be put on a night stand or on the floor. If you or your child suffers from a stuffy nose due to a cold or the indoor heat creating a dry atmosphere, the Vicks Sweet Dreams Cool Mist Humidifier is for your family.

If you or a little one has to convalesce in bed why not have something entertaining on the ceiling to look at? There are three themes to choose from: safari, dolphin and starry night.  Starry night, my personal favorite, creates a soothing and dreamy effect in my room.

The cool mist worked well at keeping my nose from getting stuffy when the heat is on. Always aim the nozzle away from walls and bedding due to the powerful mist. I used the medium setting and was able to sleep two nights before refilling it.

I didn't use the included Vicks menthol pads as I prefer using Vicks VapoRub directly under my nose if I'm quite stuffy. I surmise the pads would give off a soothing aroma, but for my needs I prefer the tougher stuff.

Filling it up at the kitchen sink is easiest but be careful not to bump or bang the tank. The weekly required maintenance using bleach and vinegar is to prevent mold. This is quite easy to do as the instructions are clear.

I'm ready for the cold season, bring on the chicken soup!

**** 4 STARS - RECOMMENDED! ****
profile.summary: Great for kids, but fun for the kid at heart.

As long as you don't pay full retail for these headphones, they're pretty good overall. Sound quality is nice and 7.1 effects are very good.

My biggest problems with the PlayStation Silver Wired Stereo Headset are comfort - or lack of it, and poor sound insulation. My girlfriend is always asking me to lower the volume because she can hear almost everything coming out of the headphones.

If you can pick-up these headphones for a good price then they are acceptable for shorter gaming sessions, but there are better options out there if you plan on using them a lot.

profile.description: Built to last, the sleek, palm-sized Braven LUX Speaker is IPX5 certified water-resistant so it can be taken virtually anywhere life takes you. The speaker's 12+ hours of wireless playtime and built-in power bank make it an incredible blend of fun and function. For a powerful, immersive left and right stereo experience with even bigger sound, pair any two Braven 7-Series speakers together using Braven's highly-acclaimed TrueWireless™ Technology.
profile.reviewText:
I'll be honest, I didn't have much hope I would be satisfied with the sound quality of a small, self-powered, MONOPHONIC, wireless speaker. I've been an audiophile for over 35 years and I'm very particular about sound quality. I did want a smallish portable music player for picnics and backyard cookouts and I liked the idea of Bluetooth because then everybody could play the music they liked directly from their phones while we hung out.  I also wanted something weather resistant as it will be frequently used outdoors. The Braven LUX is my first encounter with a portable wireless device like this so I don't have anything similar to compare it to.

The LUX is a stylish device with a rainbow-like pattern of perforations on the sides and a convincing pearlescent finish that subtly changes colors slightly as it's rotated about. It feels sturdy and has nice rubberized end caps and bottom.

Bluetooth pairing was fast and easy. I'm a dinosaur and don't own a smartphone at the moment (I had one but it broke so I just went back to my old Samsung slider phone). The Samsung was the first device I paired with the Braven LUX player. It sounded absolutely horrible - exactly what I was afraid of! Fortunately, my girlfriend has an AT&T Z998 smartphone, so we also tried it with the Braven LUX. The sound quality really surprised me - it was like night and day from the Samsung slider.  (I concluded my phone must be broadcasting in mono or at a very reduced bitrate and that's why it sounded so bad.)

The Braven LUX sounds crisp, clean and dynamic, and frankly I don't know how such a small unit can produce such convincing bass. Please don't get the idea this will replace your home-theater subwoofer, but it does produce noticeable bass in a package that has about the same footprint as a smartphone. My fear that it would not sound very good because it's only monophonic was completely unfounded - I didn't even notice that it wasn't in stereo. I can just imagine how good a pair of these units would sound tied together to produce stereo playback. (Unfortunately, I'm not willing to spend another $100 to find out.)

The LUX is capable of producing music volumes that are way above what I would use for normal indoor background music, so I am hopeful it will be very useful outdoors competing with traffic sounds, wind, kids playing, and people talking. (Since we're buried under several feet of snow at the moment I won't be able to test it outdoors for a while.)

I also paired the unit with my home Blu-ray player through the headphone jack using a 1/8" male to 1/8" male aux. cable (not included). It sounded even better than through the Bluetooth connection, but this setup is best for playing CD's as it's obviously not going to do surround sound.

Charging is pretty straightforward, plug it into your computer USB port or an auxiliary USB AC or car charger. It takes around 3 hours for a full charge. I charged up my girlfriend's AT&T Z998 smartphone but it almost completely drained the LUX's 1400 mAh battery to get a full charge on the phone. It's a handy feature to have in a pinch.

I didn't have an opportunity to try out the speakerphone function yet but others have said it works pretty well.

Overall this is an attractive, compact, multi-function unit with very good sound quality for it's size. A slightly larger internal battery would have made it better, and I really wish the removable end cap was tethered in some way, as losing it will nullify the water-resistance of the device.

**** HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - 4 STAR ****
profile.summary: It amazes me how good this little device sounds!

profile.description: High quality cobra home/cell phone link
profile.reviewText:
The Cobra PhoneLynx has been a real money-saver in my friend's household. I've been using my cell phone as my only phone for several years now. My friend wanted to follow suit but happens to live in an area of extremely poor cell coverage. It's strange because just a 1/4 mile from his apartment complex the coverage is fine. He's had to return several cell phones because he just couldn't get any coverage in 98% of his apartment. Only a few areas near windows get 1 or 2 bars and you have to hold the phone just right - making it impossible to actually use the phone for a call.

I got him the PhoneLynx and he is now able to keep the cell phone stationary in that one perfect position to actually get a signal. The setup was simple and the cellphone's bluetooth connection recognized the device in just a few minutes. He uses his cordless phone to make and receive calls anywhere in the apartment now. There are still occasionally times when he can't get a good enough signal even with the PhoneLynx in use to make a call, but that's not the fault of the device, it's just the area's poor signal reception. By moving the cellphone around a bit he is usually able to make the call.

He's still on the fence about getting rid of his home phone but I think he ultimately will soon. He has cut down on his long distance bill already though, by using his cell for free long distance calls.
profile.summary: What a helpful, money-saving product!

profile.description: This Praxis 10-Inch Curved Bread and Wavy Edge Knife is made with the highest quality Japanese steel for easy edge maintenance and rapid sharpening for a razor-sharp edge. The knife contains a natural and comfortable Rosewood handle. The handle is secured with 3 compression rivets to prevent separation.
profile.reviewText:
The 8" Chef Knife with Rosewood Handle is a pretty good knife so far, but I think it's a bit overpriced for the quality. Seems more like a $20 knife, than a $32 one. As some other reviewers have pointed out these knives do not appear to have full tangs as advertised on the Amazon page graphic. Interestingly, the full tang claim is not made on the product packaging or on the Mercer Culinary website, so I think this is only an error with Amazon.

The Praxis Chef Knife is somewhat lightweight for such a large knife, I'm used to better quality knives having a real heft to them. This isn't necessarily a bad thing depending on your needs and the application. Someone with reduced hand/arm strength would appreciate the lighter weight, and because the blade is on the thin side it does have some flex to it which can be useful at times. Despite its light weight the knife feels well balanced in the hand, though.

The blade arrived very sharp and made short work of dicing veggies, and later, cutting and trimming meats. I've only used it a few times so far but it's holding it's edge well. The fit and finish on my knife is very good. The rosewood handle is finished well and is nice and smooth. The tang in the handle isn't absolutely perfectly flush with the cutout of the handle, but it's pretty darn good for this price range.

Just a note. If you plan on giving this knife as a gift, keep in mind it comes in a VERY cheap looking "clamshell" type hanging packaging like you would find on a knife at the dollar store. They didn't spend any money on making the knife look expensive or high quality in any way. Perfectly fine for your own use, but not very special looking to give as a gift.

There is no mention of this on the product packaging, but apparently this knife has a Limited Lifetime Warranty, as found on their website: "Mercer promises the original purchaser to repair or replace, at Mercers option, during the lifetime of the original purchaser, any knife found to be defective in material or workmanship when put to everyday use and cared for according to instructions." You will need to ship it to them with your proof of purchase at your expense, and if they find it was damaged due to defective material or workmanship they will repair the knife or send you a new one at their expense. Not a bad warranty for an inexpensive knife!

Overall, this is a good knife for our household as we're not exactly world class chefs so we really don't need much better quality than this. I still think it should cost a bit less, but prices do go up and down on Amazon so maybe you can find it a bit cheaper than I paid.

**** 4 STARS - RECOMMENDED! ****
profile.summary: Decent quality knife with a good warranty, but a bit overpriced.

profile.reviewText:
I'm surprised they are still selling these since they are nearly useless. I bought 2 for about $16 each delivered on a deal a day website. The first time I used one the charge lasted nearly 2 hours so I was pleased. However, the instructions don't tell you how long to charge the light for, and there is no charge completed indicator, so I charged it for about 24 hours again the second time. I'm pretty sure I fried the batteries by charging that long because I barely got 20 minutes of use the second time! It's too bad because it was a very handy and durable light the one and only time it worked properly (I have dropped it numerous times with no damage!). I determined on the second unit I had bought (using a voltmeter and determining delta V end of charge) that about 5 HOURS IS THE MAX. you should actually charge the light for. But even charging it correctly I only got 30 minutes of runtime. I think the NiMH cells are so old in some of these units that they are shot from not being recharged in such a long time. As another reviewer mentioned, if you get a unit with good batteries they work well. But for 30 bucks I wouldn't want to gamble on getting a good one!

Because I like tinkering with things I totally modified the light and added an 8 AA cell Eneloop rechargeable battery pack. (After opening up the light it turns out there is a tiny 3 cell AAA 600 mAh NiMH battery pack inside the unit - no wonder the run times suck.) I LOVE my light now because it lasts for 4 hours, but out of the box stock, the light is a piece of garbage! Save your money - especially for the ridiculous $30 they are charging now!

Incidentally, I spent about $25, and hours and hours of trial and error work, on the 8 cell battery pack modifications - so while it was educational and fun for me, I wouldn't recommend this to anybody unless you are really good at this type of work. I actually had to add a separate on/off switch between the battery and the light because I was getting substantial parasitic drain on the battery pack even though the stock internal batteries had been disconnected and the light was switched off! Took me days of testing to figure this out.
profile.summary: Battery Life Very Short.

profile.description: Do you want an ultra low profile without compromising functionality? Look no further than the OE120IW recessed, in-wall TV mount. Easily attach your flat screen TV between two wall studs for a nearly flush finish while getting all the benefits of a full motion mount. The preassembled box and mount duo make an otherwise intimidating installation easy for the confident DIYer.
profile.reviewText:
I live in a 1930's construction apartment house which has the old-style lath and plaster walls. This complicates installation of this TV mount considerably, because in addition to having to cut through the outer plaster layer, there are horizontal 3/8" thick wooden slats (or laths) right behind the plaster that also have to be cut to gain access to the studs inside of the wall. In addition, older homes often have non-standard stud widths so it requires a bit more knowledge to locate them. Studs in these older homes are usually 16" or 24" on center, but not always. Due to these complications I decided to hire an installer familiar with older homes to install my OmniMount OE120IW.

At installation time, it turned out I was lucky as my home does have standard 16" on center studs. The installer located the wall studs using a combination of a strong magnet and by drilling a couple of small pilot holes in the wall until he was sure he had located them. After stenciling the template on the wall, he began the very messy job of cutting away the brittle horsehair plaster and cutting through the laths. He asked me to hold a shop-vac near where he was cutting to minimize the debris falling on the floor.

I was worried there wouldn't be enough depth in the wall opening to accept the recessed mount. Remember, the lathing is on BOTH sides of the studs. Fortunately the OnmiMount unit fit just fine in the wall. He pulled the OnmiMount unit back out of the wall after marking where he was going to drill the pilot holes for the lag bolts. He then did something I found surprising. He ran a bead of construction adhesive around and behind the opening where he had cut the lathing away. He said this would help secure the cut laths so they don't move when he installs the lag bolts, plus it will help with reducing vibration, etc., after the install is complete.

After an hour for lunch to let the adhesive setup, he drilled some pilot holes and installed the OnmiMount unit with the lag bolts, and then fitted the snap-on frame. Next, he mounted the hardware on the back of my 47" LCD TV, and together we lifted the TV into place on the in-wall mount.

Originally, I had planned to route all the wiring behind the wall, but when I got an estimate from my installer about how much an electrician would charge to do this because of the plaster and lath construction, I decided to run the wiring in a plastic channel mounted on the wall. For me this was a pretty good solution because I have the TV mounted right next to a corner wall. We first ran a short horizontal channel piece to the corner, and then ran a vertical channel in the corner down to the floor where I was then able to conceal the wires under the baseboard heating unit. This solution saved me a fortune on hiring an electrician, and still looks very neat and clean due to the corner installation of the wire channel.

In use, I love my OmniMount OE120IW. We have five large windows in this room, and the ability to tilt the display in nearly any direction really helps to deal with the reflective glare the windows can produce during certain times of the day. Movement of the set is firm, but not difficult, and it never feels like you are forcing it to move. When we're done watching, the TV folds back nearly flush with the wall, which makes for a very neat and unobtrusive look. In the end I was pleased I went with the wire channels instead of hiring the electrician. Due to the TV's proximity to the corner you can only see about two inches of the horizontal channel. I've since placed a rather tall speaker near that corner of the room so the vertical wire channel is likewise mostly concealed behind the speaker.

***** HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - 5 STAR *****
profile.summary: High Quality TV Mount Works Great in Older Homes, as well

profile.description: Economical, desktop tape dispenser is designed for standard 1/2" or 3/4" by 36 yard rolls. Made of sturdy high-impact plastic with a weighted, nonskid base. Tape is not included.
profile.reviewText:
This is a no-brainer office product at a very reasonable price. However the provided 1" tape core does not fit my rolls of Scotch 810 Magic tape - it is too small. I measured the Scotch tape roll and it is exactly 1". I had to fold up a piece of cardboard and stuff it into an opening in the core to get it to fit my tape rolls. It core looks like it should have included some kind of insert to accommodate the 1" roll.

In fairness I didn't even try to contact the manufacturer to see if there was any kind of remedy. For the price paid, and what it is (a tape dispenser), I didn't have the patience to waste my time on several emails back and forth to resolve this. (Pick your battles!)

So I still recommend the item because it's dirt cheap even with shipping, but don't expect a perfect product out of the box.

profile.description: cooks 3.5 dutch oven
profile.reviewText:
I think the first thing I noticed about this pot when I received it was it is smaller that I thought it would be. That's my fault, not the products', but it's worth mentioning. The enamel finish is nicely applied both inside and out and the pot is very pretty, especially in the blue color. This is nice for serving directly at the table, especially so, because cast iron retains heat so well.

So far we've prepared a nice beef stew and a pot of chili using our dutch oven, and they both came out delicious. The food cooks very evenly without burning the contents at the bottom of the pot, like conventional stainless steel pots can do sometimes. In use I found the handles to be a bit small, especially when the pot is nearly full and I'm holding it with potholders. Despite my initial reservations, the smaller overall size of the pot has not been a problem so far, and having fewer leftovers in the refrigerator to eventually throw away has actually been a blessing!

I was certainly a little put off by all the restrictions you have to follow when using this cookware. First preheat pot on low, then turn up heat. You cant dry cook without liquid or oil. Don't use metal utensils. Dont clean pot with abrasive powder cleaners, etc. I wish Amazon had included these warnings in their product description. Despite these restrictions, however, I'm enjoying using this dutch oven and cleanup isn't too bad with dish washing liquid and a non-scratch sponge.

Since it's Fall now, we're looking forward to cooking up more hearty meals in this pot, and I can see it being handy for preparing serve-yourself dishes for football games and holiday get-togethers.

**** 4 STARS - RECOMMENDED! ****
profile.summary: Nice cookware for preparing hearty meals.

profile.description: Experience a new level of comfort on the PlayStation 4 with the Siberia P100 Lightweight Gaming Headset. The enjoyable, relaxed fit is built for hours and hours of gaming. Next-generation SteelSeries speaker drivers let you hear PlayStation 4 games like never before thanks to the helpful positional audio, incredible immersion and crisp details. This member of the iconic Siberia line brings you breathable, soft-padded earcups on an over-ear design that rests easily on your head. The 3.5mm plug easily connects to your wireless DualShock 4 controller and also works great on mobile devices and other platforms for a new level of audio fidelity no matter where you listen.
profile.reviewText:
Currently the top model in the SteelSeries headset lineup, the Siberia 800 is a recent re-brand of the company's former "H" model wireless headset. Aside from perhaps some subtle cosmetic differences they appear to be the same excellent headphones.

FIT & FINISH

The Siberia P800 headphones feature very plush memory-foam cushioned earphones and headband of supple leather-like vinyl; sturdy matte-black and glossy plastic construction with a rubberized embossed "steelseries" strip on top of the headband, and contrasting orange stitching and fabric inside the earcups round out the look. The control box is a tasteful yet fairly unobtrusive looking black box with a pleasant blue OLED-style digital display that is easy to read even across the room, and fits in nicely with my other black audio components.

Still missing, however, is any kind of label indicating which ear cup is left or right. I had hoped they corrected this omission when SteelSeries did the re-brand of their line, but I guess it didn't happen.

CONNECTIVITY

I needed to know that I could use these headphones in a variety of applications - not just as PS4 gaming phones. I connected the SteelSeries control box to a variety of digital and analog connections using optical cable, USB, RCA stereo jacks, and a 3.5mm headphone-type jack.

--PS4

Setup is pretty straightforward on the PS4, just plug in the optical and USB cables into the SteelSeries control box and your PS4, use the control box to select PS4 and you should be up and running. Sound quality of both the earphones and the mic is crystal clear and very immersive when playing Fallout 4 and Just Cause 3, though I did notice a slightly reduced sound quality when using the 7.1 Dolby surround-sound mode. There is no detectable lag over the wireless connection in either stereo or 7.1 modes.

--PC, Blu-Ray & HDTV Connections

I connected an older Panasonic DMP-BD60 Blu-Ray, an OPPO BDP-105 Blu-Ray, a Samsung UN55JU6700 4K HDTV, and my Win 10 Intel Core i5 desktop PC. All connections, both analog and digital, worked flawlessly, but for some reason the Panasonic Blu-Ray playing an Iron Man-2 Blu-Ray in DTS-HD surround could not get the English language programming to play. I could play the alternate languages because these were encoded in Dolby Digital, not the higher quality DTS-HD. I believe this was more a problem with my six year old Panasonic player and not the headphones. I was finally able to play this Blu-Ray in DTS-HD by using the optical out connection from my Samsung TV, instead of the optical out directly from the Panasonic player.

SOUND QUALITY

Clearly, the Siberia P800 wireless headset benefits from a digital connection - in some cases the RCA and 3.5mm headphone analog connections produced less then ideal sound quality. Conversely, the digital connections all exhibited crisp and dynamic sound quality, with ample bass, smooth midrange, and transparent highs. The bass was believable, taut and wholly acceptable, but these are not cans for serious "Bass Heads". The surround effects were convincingly produced and felt very immersive especially from high quality source material. I found most sources, with the exception of the PC connection, did not produce a high enough volume for my personal preference. I like rock concert levels with my music and movies, so for most people this probably won't be a problem.

For high quality sound reproduction my preferred connection for these headphones is to PC via USB. I played a number of HD quality movie files, and high quality music files in FLAC format, and was blown away by the quality. I'm a long time audiophile and home theater nut, and it takes quite a lot to impress me now, but the SteelSeries Siberia P800 headphones certainly did.

OPERATING RANGE & RUN-TIME

One of the things I was most concerned about when I purchased these wireless headphones is that they would have a pathetic range and/or cut out and produce static as I moved around. Nothing could be farther from the truth. I was walking (and dancing) around my three-bed (wood construction) apartment, making a sandwich at the other end of the house, in rooms with closed doors, downstairs and outside my apartment - and these headphones never gave me anything but beautiful, crystal clear sound without so much as a drop-out or bit of static! I truly was impressed. I made some measurements after the fact, and at a maximum I was 43ft from the receiver, on the same floor and through three walls. In a second measurement, I was 30 ft from the receiver, down one floor and outside the house.

I also tested these operating right next to a running fan motor, a fluorescent fixture, and finally next to my wireless router - I never heard any difference in sound quality.

The inclusion of two lithium-ion rechargeable batteries means you always have a freshly charged battery at the ready when you need it. SteelSeries rates these as 20 hour batteries and that seems about right, though I didn't exactly time the battery life. The control box has a slot where you charge and store the spare battery for when you need it. The spare battery charges up faster than the headphones can use up the existing battery, so there is never any wait for a fully charged battery.

COMFORT & FEATURES

These are nicely padded headphones that rest firmly on your head, and resist all but the most vigorous head movements. I found them to be very comfortable for extended wear - the longest was about 4 - 5 hours at a stretch, which is my personal limit for ANY headphones. The volume control was easy to access and responsive, and it is very convenient to select many of the features on the SteelSeries control box from across the room simply by pressing and rotating the volume knob on the headset. The included instruction manual is really lacking in detail, however, you have to figure out how to use features like the sound equalization, Chatmix, Livemix and Dolby Surround pretty much by trial and error, though admittedly most of the feature set is fairly intuitive. At the moment, the SteelSeries website doesn't offer any additional details about how to use the product. I'm hoping they add additional instruction on their site as they previously did with the H Series branded model.

CONCLUSION

While certainly commanding a premium price, the SteelSeries Siberia P800 Wireless Headset with Dolby 7.1 Surround Sound offers a high level of sound quality, comfort, features and performance for the price. An improved user manual would be much appreciated, but the average user should be able to intuitively operate these headphones without too much trouble.

***** HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! - 5 STAR *****
profile.summary: Excellent wireless headset/headphones for gaming, music and movies

profile.description: The MA63 is an AC/DC current clamp with NCV voltage detector and full overload protection. Manual ranging clamp meter with three Current ranges and AC/DC voltage to 600V. The 6000mA range allows for low current measurements that may be used in the automotive industry. Unique VFC (variable frequency control) mode helps troubleshoot and diagnose HVAC applications that are variable frequency driven. The MA63 also features resistance, capacitance, frequency, diode and continuity measurements as well as data hold low battery indicator and auto power off functions. Complete with test leads, carrying case and two AAA batteries.
profile.reviewText:
Extech MA63 AC/DC

I got this meter primarily for its precise low current DC measurement capability. Great for troubleshooting automotive electrical system problems, it has already helped me find a very slight short in the steering wheel wiring harness on my car that was causing intermittent problems with the headlights . It's now my go to meter because it's compact and has just about every measurement feature I would ever need as a homeowner and shade-tree mechanic. Rated CAT III-300V, CAT III-600V so probably not the meter for an industrial electrician, but great for most other trades.

The non-contact voltage detection (NCV), and true RMS measurement were two things I required for my next meter, so this fit the bill perfectly. I do wish the included carry case was a bit more substantial at this price point, but I guess if it was too bulky it would defeat the benefit of a compact meter.

**** 4 STARS - HIGHLY RECOMMENDED! ****

profile.description: Created by celebrity makeup artist Jillian Dempsey to deliver an instant smoky eye. This luxurious liner is made with organic jojoba oil, organic shea butter and marula oil to give the product a smooth, waterproof finish. The built-in smudger allows you to blend the color for a soft-focus look.
profile.reviewText:
My girlfriend is always excited to try new cosmetics. I gave her the Jillian Dempsey Natural Khol Eyeliner - Rich Brown, to try because I thought she might like it. This review is her experience with the product.

I had high hopes for the Jillian Dempsey Waterproof Kohl Eyeliner because it has three great features:

1. Waterproof
2. Not tested on animals
3. Plant-derived oil and wax based ingredients. No synthetic chemicals or preservatives.

The eyeliner color states rich brown, it's more of a reddish brown when applied. I prefer a neutral brown, not too cool or warm. I have blue eyes, brown hair and fair cool toned skin with pink under tones. The rich brown is too red, harsh and dark even with smudging it to soften the look.

The eyeliner is creamy upon application, however it seems to skip a bit. I will note that I don't have oily lids/skin and it's fall so the weather is cool.

I first applied the eyeliner to my upper lids and water line without my contacts in.  I didn't use the smudger tip to gauge the longevity of the eyeliner.

I checked the mirror 30 minutes later and the eyeliner had smeared and melted. I looked like a hot mess. I was glad to be home and not in public.

The smudge tip is a sponge and wipes the color off your eyes, it defeats the purpose. I use Rimmel Scandaleyes Khol waterproof eyeliner, which I love - no problems with raccoon eyes and it's inexpensive.

I really wanted to like this eyeliner but I can't recommend it because it doesn't live up to it's claim and is expensive.

** NOT RECOMMENDED! - 2 STARS **
profile.summary: Eyeliner Didn't Meet Expectations

profile.description: Computer gaming chassis
profile.reviewText:
I decided my existing eMachines computer needed a case upgrade for expansion and "breathing room" as it sometimes overheated and shut down on very hot summer days. The Antec One Hundred case fit the bill nicely. The case has a very understated and monolithic look I find appealing in an age of over the top Batman/Dark Knight styling.

Installation was pretty straightforward and my stock Asus motherboard fit without a hitch. The case is painted black inside giving it a finished look. The stamped steel components aren't top of the line, but are commensurate with this price point - and no sharp edges. Also, no modular drive rails - everything is secured with screws. Lots of drive bays so future expansion will be a cinch.

The lack of vent holes on the bottom of the case for the power supply was a shortcoming. I ended up mounting my power supply with the fan facing up to get adequate cooling. Decent cable management channels kept everything looking neat and air moving efficiently.

The included 140mm and 120mm fans run very quietly and provide amazing cooling for my system. I no longer expect any problems with shutdown on even the hottest summer days. The angled USB and audio jacks at the top of the case are great as my computer sits near the floor. Wish they were USB 3.0, though. Could also use a bit better documentation. But for this price, the case is a recommended purchase!
profile.summary: Solid Case at a Fair Price.

top_5.description: Prevent minor damage to your 13.3" laptop screen with this Belkin TrueClear F7P327BT antismudge screen protector that features a strong, yet lightweight, design to help keep your device like new. TrueClear technology ensures optimal screen visibility.
top_5.reviewText:
We recently got an HP Pavilion x360 13.3" Touchscreen 360-Degree Laptop and wanted something to protect the screen. The Belkin TrueClear Anti-Smudge Screen Protector seemed like a good choice. When it first arrived in the mail I was a bit concerned because the Belkin protector was in a box that was just a bit too small, so it was curled in a half-circle to fit. It flattened out just fine, however, and no damage was done to the protector.

INSTALLATION

The pictorial instructions Belkin includes with this product certainly leave a lot to be desired. Fortunately, I've installed a number of these screen protectors on numerous laptops, cell phones, & camera screens, and the most important lesson I learned is: START CLEAN. Work on a nice clean table, and first put down a soft, lint-free cloth to protect your device from scratches. Next, clean the screen with alcohol and a microfiber cloth, and dry using a second microfiber cloth. Don't forget the corners! Examine with a flashlight at an angle and make sure you didn't miss any areas and that there is no haze, which indicates it's not thoroughly clean.

You will now invariably have lots of dust and particles on the screen even if it's very clean. (This dust will show up under the screen protector as many tiny bubbles that CANNOT BE REMOVED because the dust permanently adheres to the screen protector adhesive.) I use canned air at this point to blow off the dust from the screen. USE THIS AT YOUR OWN RISK! Canned air has the potential to shoot out jets of super cold liquid that MAY HARM YOUR SCREEN. I've never had any problems in the 7 to 10 years I've been doing this, but I only use short puffs of gas and don't let the can get too cold. Also, always hold the can upright and don't use a brand-new full can for this as there is an increased likelihood of shooting out liquid when it's very full, or tilted!

For a large screen like a laptop, installation is a bit trickier than say a cell phone. Don't remove the whole protective backing at once! Peel back an inch on the narrower side of the protector and line it up as straight as you can with that edge of the laptop screen. Slowly continue peeling and applying, trying to keep the portion of the un-applied protector from laying on the clean screen. You can use your fingers or a credit card to push out bubbles as you apply it. Sometimes it helps to have a second person available as it seems like you need ten hands at once to peel, apply, smooth, hold...repeat, etc!

Once completely applied you may find you have a few stubborn bubbles that didn't release during application. You can try to gently lift a corner of the protector until you reach the offending bubble, then reapply the screen using a credit card to ensure smooth application.

IN USE

Once applied, I found the protector didn't interfere with the use of the touch screen in any way - it was just as responsive as before. I still get some smears and fingerprints with the protector on but they don't seem as noticeable as before it was in place. Visibility through the protector is excellent and I was hard-pressed to notice any difference before and after. My screen in only a 1366 x 768 resolution TN style LCD panel, so nothing really bright or super hi-def. I don't know how the visual performance would be on a really high-quality screen. I like being able to clean the screen most anytime I want without worrying if it will damage the delicate surface if I clean it too often.

I took one star off for the poor, pictorial style installation instructions, and the relatively high cost of this product. This item was fully 10% of the price we paid for our laptop, which seems like an awful lot for a thin piece of plastic! But I suppose if we get longer life out of the laptop it may pay for itself over time.

**** RECOMMENDED - 4 STARS ****
top_5.summary: High quality touch-screen protector, but pricey.

top_5.description: An Amazon Brand.
top_5.reviewText:
Based on the price I pretty much expected this item to be on the cheap side when I ordered it, and it definitely is. The biggest problem with these cat trees are the plastic inserts with bolts in the riser tubes that are used to screw the whole thing together. As your cat climbs and scratches and jumps on and off the tree it flexes the hard plastic, which eventually cracks and breaks - and the thing ends up falling apart.

I expected this, so while I was assembling it I put gobs and gobs of hot melt glue at each point where it screwed together. This was a two-person job, one to quickly dispense the hot melt and the other to hold and screw the pieces together immediately before the glue hardened. Maybe if your cat is tiny you can get away with not gluing it together, but my tree is being used by a big, overweight male cat and I knew he was going to be rough on it.

Out of the box the tree has a pretty strong sisal-rope type odor so we let it air out outside for a day before assembling. We sprayed it with cat-nip spray and the cat, Merlin, took to it pretty quickly. It surprised us that he was easily able to climb up to the top roost, and even though nearly half of him hangs out of it, he still enjoys lounging and sleeping up there. He occasionally uses it as a scratching post, but he still seems to prefer the furniture for that!

We've been using it for a few weeks now and it is holding up well, time will tell how well it lasts in a year or so. The price was pretty reasonable for such a large tree, and as long as you don't mind adding some hot melt glue during assembly it should last for a while even with a large cat or two smaller cats.

**** 4 STARS - RECOMMENDED! ****
