top_5.reviewText: I bought this, believing it would be a quality hammer for my metalworking. Upon opening the package, it became immediately clear this was the cheapest kind of knockoff--a flimsy hammer that wouldn't stand the test of any serious work; it looks more like a child's toy. The worst part is probably the grip--it's cheaply molded around the shaft and immediately came loose. Try using a hammer that will rotate in the grip--impossible!  I contacted the seller immediately for a return, but they gave me some lame excuse, blaming Amazing for not allowing return--pure nonsense!  It's not often I feel ripped off on Amazon, but this is one of those rare exceptions. If you like quality tools, avoid this product like the plague.
top_5.summary: Hammer rotates in its grip--and other poor quality "features"--do not buy!

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "With an impressive bibliography in an array of genres, USA Today bestselling author Traci Hall has garnered a notable fan base. She pens stories guaranteed to touch the heart while transporting the reader to another time and place. Her belief in happily ever after shines through, whether it's a romantic glimpse into history or a love affair for today.". The summary of the review text is "4 a bite at a time Stars!".
output:
Looking for a sweet love story? How about a story about finding yourself, and whats important in life? Ambrosia is definitely the read for you if you said yes to either of these. This is such a fun and light read. It flows so smooth, and its over before you know it, or want it to be.

I will never accept being less than somebody again. I am me, and I count.

Celia Langford has just lost her husband and is wanting a new start.  Shes going from doctors wife, who was expected to be perfect, to a life of beach living and relaxation. She is desperate for a new start. A new business and new life are what she is looking for. But love is not!!

Crossing his legs, he accepted that he was *****, and attracted to a woman who was an uptight mess. Not the way hed thought to start his day.

Nowin walks Dax Smith. Blonde curls, tan, lean body, and a heart of gold. These two could not be any more different, except for the heart of gold ;) Thats what I really enjoyed about this story. Theres no bad guy here. Its just two people living life, helping others, and surviving. And believe me, Celia tries to fight it. Who can fight Daxs charm, though?!? Hes so genuine.

Im almost thirty years old. Ive been married. But I have the giggles because Dax, I think you're cute.

This story has two characters that you cant help but love, and many others that I also enjoyed. Theres no drama, heartache, or frustrating moments. Its a great beach day or pool day read that will put a smile on your face and help you relax. Happy Reading!

profile.description: Alessandra Torre is a USA Today Bestselling author who focuses on contemporary erotica. Her first book, Blindfolded Innocence, was published in July 2012, and was an Erotica #1 Bestseller for two weeks. The sequel to Blindfolded, Masked Innocence, will be released in February 2014. Alessandra lives in the Southern United States and is married, with one young child. She enjoys reading, spending time with her family, and playing with her dogs. Her favorite authors include Lisa Gardner, Gillian Flynn, and Jennifer Crusie. Learn more about Alessandra on her website at www.alessandratorre.com, or you can find her on Twitter (@ReadAlessandra) or her Facebook fanpage.
profile.reviewText:
Oh Brad De Luca, how you make my heart and vagina do things it shouldnt ;) This series has to be one of my all time favorites!!  I accidently (and don't even remember how) started reading Blindfolded Innocence a LONG time ago, and have been in love since. I could never bore of these awesome books. And am quite sad to say that I am finished. I see MANY rereads coming in my future.

Ill be in the office around ten. I ll tell my staff, so you can either be the engaged assistant who looks like shes hiding her engagement, or you can be the confident fiance I know you are.  -Brad

Brad and Julie have come a long way in their relationship and both have grown so much from it. In End of the Innocence I was so freakin proud of them both. Brad has gone from a bossy alpha male to a teddy bear version of an alpha male. And I know that  doesnt make sense to you, but he is still all bossy, aggressive, and alpha, but yet such a sweetheart, too. The places these two have gone and the things they have done in this series will make you laugh, smile, swoon, and go have sex with your significant others ;)

Im not going to kiss you until his **** is deep inside me.  -Julia

Wow!! This is my most favorite Julia quote. Julia has really grown up and I LOVE her!! In End of the Innocence, she is exactly what I love in a female character. She is timid and unsure sometimes, but yet still stands her ground when it matters. She knows exactly when to put Brad in his place, but yet isn't overbearing. You would never have thought it in book one, but this girl can take care of herself.  Lucky her, though, she doesnt have to all the time. Brad is very happy to give her everything she needs. And I mean everything ;)

Now. Hard. Fast. De Luca-style.  -Julia

These two(or three) can make some heat. I could never tire of reading their sexcapades.  Allesandra gives us the perfect amount of suspense, sex, heartwarming moments, and humor in End of the Innocence.

Whether or not our marriage lasted, I would always and forever, madly, deeply love the man.  -Julia

My opinion is that she ended this series very well. End of the Innocence still has so much going on that I was a nervous wreck at the beginning of every chapter. I knew it had to all fall apart at some point and it was just a waiting game for it to happen. But I was pleasantly surprised at how all the events played out. This will sound super silly, but it all warmed my heart and made me love Brad and Julia so much more.

All is well in the land of Brad and Julia and that makes this Book Btch super happy!! This series is a must read in my opinion. I know not everyone will enjoy the events of this series as much as I did but at least give it a try. You might be surprised at how much you enjoy it :)
profile.summary: Perfect ending to the series!!!

profile.description: Marilyn Brant is a New York Times & USA Today bestselling author of contemporary womens fiction, romantic comedy & mystery. She was named the Author of the Year (2013) by the Illinois Association of Teachers of English. She loves all things Jane Austen, has a passion for Sherlock Holmes, is a travel addict and a music junkie, and lives on chocolate and gelato. Visit her website: www.marilynbrant.com
profile.reviewText:
The One That I Want is a good story, but I must say that I had a hard time getting attached to this story. To be honest, I almost gave up on it, but something was telling me to stick it out. And Im happy I did. The second half of Julias story was good. A tad bit predictable, but still good.

Youre a puzzle to me in a number of ways, but you're not trouble, Julia Merriwether Crane.

What makes me hate to have to say all this, is that the writing and the flow of this story is GREAT!! I loved this authors writing style, just not all of this story. And don't get me wrong, I enjoyed the story, just wasn't wowed by it. Yes, I am rambling!! LOL!!  I honestly thought I was starting a love square kind of story, which really excited this drama lover. And maybe that fueled my disappointment a little.

Im told getting into cars with strange men is dangerous.

But, enough about that!! Let me tell you how much I enjoyed Danes character. I enjoyed his honesty, his patience, and his compassion. And I wanted to grab Julia by the shoulders and shake her a few times! Thank goodness she had such a smart daughter and awesome friends, otherwise she would have been a hot mess. Although, she still was at times. As for those other two guystake a hike fellas!!! They never had a chance in my mind.

Its a gift. Never let it go.

This is a sweet second chance love story that even though I didn't give it 4 or 5 stars, I still recommend you give a chance. Different strokes for different folks, right?!? ;)
profile.summary: 3.5 number 49202 stars

profile.description: Jillian Neal is a Romance author that manages to blend her imagination, Southern sass, and loving heart in every novel she pens. She showed her talent for weaving intricate plot lines and showcasing dynamic characters in her seven-book, urban fantasy, series, The Gifted Realm. Her skillset continues to shine in her contemporary series, Gypsy Beach, which will leave you with a longing to pack your bags and move to a tiny beach town full of bohemian charm. She lives outside of Atlanta with her husband and their children.
profile.reviewText:
Looking for a romantic beach read with a little bit of mystery?!? Gypsy Beach was the perfect read for me while I was lying by the pool in beautiful Florida this past week :) Sienna and Ryans second chance love has just enough romance to keep me entertained but yet not make me think too much. LOL! All I wanted to do was relax and read, and that was accomplished.

Gypsy Beach has a way of setting things to rights.

I have found that second chance love stories can either be quite enjoyable or fall flatfor me at least. Im not usually down for the cheesy storylines with all the drama and unbelievable encounters, BUT Gypsy Beach wasn't like that. I cant say I would have been as understanding and forgiving as Sienna was, but I enjoyed her attitude and her easy going ways. I only wish I could be as relaxed and nice as she is ;)

She had no idea what hed said, but that sexy husk of his voice always made heat surge rapidly through her entire body.

Then RyanI felt bad for him, even though I had a little bit harder time connecting with his character. I really couldn't see this tough construction worker kind of guy being as mushy as he is. I know this is the love of his life we are talking about but I was concerned for his man card. LOL!! But, anyways, the poor guy was set up for failure by the two people he should have been able to rely on the most. His situation sucked. This is the classic case of the rich judging those they feel are not worthy of themso sad. I would love to say Ryan should have stood up to them, but he was just a kid and they failed him.

The only person hed ever wanted to prove himself to was Sienna Cooper. His one chance at heaven, and hed blown it.

Dont worry, though, this is a quick, easy, and for the most part happy read. It wasn't an I cant put it down read but also not a boring read. Which for a beach read is perfect!! You know you are going to get that HEA out of it, but there are a few kinks for Sienna and Ryan that have to be fixed along the way.

Plus, another good thing is that I enjoyed all the secondary characters, which made me happy when I saw this is a series. Definitely beach read approved!!
profile.summary: 4 Gypsy blood runs deep stars

profile.description: ASA
profile.reviewText:
Have you read the Marked Men series?!? I sure hope so. Especially if you are fond of tattooed men, alpha males, or just plain bad boys! I personally have read most of this series and loved every one. And was anxiously awaiting Asas story, because of his past. I felt like there was going to be a lot to him.

You and me alone is the dumbest idea I ever had, Red. Dont say I didn't warn you.

But I was VERY surprised by his story. Not that it wasn't a great story, but I wasn't as sucked in to his as much as I was all the others. Bummer, right!! Not really. I still enjoyed it and was happy to see how things worked out for him and Royal. Weird combination, right?!? I definitely went in to this one expecting lots of drama and emotional moments when you take into consideration Asas past and Royals occupation. But, surprisingly, it was very different than what I expected. And thats good, because the author knows how to surprise us with these bad boys ;)

Every time I cant seem to figure out where Im going lately I always end up wherever you are.

Dont get me wrong, though, Asa and Royals story is still very emotional, just not how I expected.  They start out with the heat!! And boy do they have heat!  Here I was thinking Royal was going to reject Asa due to his history. When in reality Royal is the aggressor here. The girl wanted that bad boy and she was determined to get him!! But only after the two get all their emotional baggage straight first.

I knew from firsthand experience that some hurt and some mistakes could weigh you down forever.

Plus, like all the others, the rest of the crew pop in for some updates on their happy little lives. I love reading about how everyone is getting along in their lives. Its a little sad that this series is over. A series like this is easy to become addicted to and the characters start to stick with you after reading about them so many times.

If you haven't started this series, get to it!! It definitely is one that comes highly recommended by this Book Btch :)
profile.summary: 4 second chances matter stars!

profile.description: L.D. Davis has been writing since she was in grade school, leaving a trail of mostly unfinished stories until her first novel, Accidentally On Purpose, was published in 2012. Accidentally On Purpose made the New York Times Best Selling list and soon thereafter, L.D. left her position in retail slavery to write full time. When she isnt writing, Mrs. Davis enjoys reading, watching British period pieces, and gets a little nerdy with some occasional sci-fi. She enjoys the beach, sipping good wine, and embarrassing her children by dancing and singing in public. L.D. lives on the east coast of the United States with her husband, children, and two cats.
profile.reviewText:
Well!!!! I am not sure where to go with this review. I guess I could start with, I finished this book! And I say that because there were a few times that I wanted to give up :( This was not the book for me. I had MANY issues with it.  For starters there was no character build up and Lindsey and Rhys's relationship didn't even feel like a relationship to me. When Lindsey told him she loved him the first time he came over to her house, I thought that was going to be the end of it for me. But!! I kept going. I was hopeful that she would grow up and be a responsible adult. Nope!! Didn't happen.

I feel like this story has a lot of potential but needs so much more. So much more emotion! And so much more romance! I just couldn't believe that things would work out the way they did with what I was given :( But, like I always say, give it a try, because it may not have been the book for me, but it may be a winner for you :)
profile.summary: Not my cup of tea :(

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "2.0" for a product with description "Prince ~ Lotusflow3r". The summary of the review text is "Funky but not stank".
output:
Basically this cd is not good to me. I rank this cd with some of his worse efforts. The guitar playing is very good though and showcases itself perhaps more than any other Prince cd with consistent solos.  It is obvious Prince had an after party mentality for funk on this cd, but somehow he missed the mark.  It is not a horrible cd it just does not make you ever feel like dancing or caring to play that one song over and over.  Some of the guitar rifts are excellent though.
Okay after two weeks of listening to the cd I can ease up a bit and say here are the best songs on the albums to me rated 1-10.
Here- I give a number 7.  I really liked this song but it took a while to grow on me. It really wasn't till I listened to the lyrics clearly. I listened to this song more than any other.  It has a carousel feel to it sorta of like Dionne from The Truth Cd's but in lyrics it's more reminiscent to The Dance on 3121 and Strange Relationship from SOTT)
Dance For Me-I give a number 6(Reminiscent of 319 off Gold but a little better b/c).  His voice sticks in your head and I like the beat. This is a good Prince song.
U're Gonna C Me- I say it's a 9 but we've already heard this so I give it a 7.6.  (I have to lower the number for remixes b/c imagine anyone else redoing a song of their own and putting it on an album)
Chocolate Box-I give a 5.  I would give a 6 but it sounds like it should be played in a gay bar and I'm a man so I can only dig it but so far. His voice sticks in your head with this song. If he came out with this in the 80's it woulda been a hit but it's 2009.
Crimson and Clover-I give a 4 just because I can and if you're Prince and you're gonna do a cover song it has to be great, but that guitar rift bumps it up to a 5.
$- I give a 5.  Definitely reminiscent of MovieStar off Crystal Ball.
77 Beverly Park- I give an eight.  It's only an instrumental though, but it's probably the best song on the 2 cd's.
Colonized Mind-I give a 4 compared to Money Don't Matter, SOTT,  When Will We Be Paid, Avalanche,Planet Earth, and his other political songs. He does have a couple lines in this song worth being heard though and the comparisons of a child with no mother equals a man with no feeling make you think.
Overall this cd is okay.  Even with his funny electro voice it just didn't do it. Like everyone we all expect a lot out of Prince while at the same time trying to lower our expectations, but this cd is just okay.  I can think of too many of his other cd's that are far better but he does have a couple songs that are catchy.  He definitely caught a vibe on this cd, it's just I didn't catch it.  Like I said, it sounds like takes from an afterparty or a B-sides cd. It did not feel like an album.  By this I mean think Dave Chappelle's sketches compared to his stand up or a television show compared to a movie.  I feel like he wanted to be funky on this cd and it came across but it just wasn't stankonia.

profile.description: Vinyl LP pressing. 2014 album from the R&B/Funk superstar. ART OFFICIAL AGE is a classic Prince album, produced, arranged, composed and performed by Prince and Joshua Welton. Sonically the record is a contemporary concoction of soul, R&B and funk. The melodies are immediate and prominent as ever and Prince's vocals are rich and solid, taking full advantage of his vocal range with decidedly, seductive lyrics.
profile.reviewText:
Prince's alter-ego CAMILLE HAS ENTERED THE BUILDING
This album is like head, it sucks in a great way {like Prince's old song Head} to give you an eargasm.
Expectations met. Didn't think he had it in him to funk this much new material up. If this is Art Offical then I never want the artificial.

-I critique Prince on a scale of previous Prince material genius and musical flops that I just didn't like, and I'm not just gonna up him b/c he's my favorite musician. If his album is terrible then it just is. You can read some of my other prince reviews to validate that statement. But, who am I to critique Prince?

Get the cd! It is not just a cd that only Prince fans can enjoy, it's a cd that everyone will enjoy (and for the past 15 years, as a 32 yr old man, I haven't been able to say that about Prince) .
Get the cd b/c The mp3 muffles some of the electronic sounds.{If you want a song for song in depth critique I'll put that in my comment section.}
Criticism:
-My critiques on the cd is the catchy choruses might not be there. You might not repeat the chorus (not many prince songs give you 4 verses of a catchy melodious chorus) but the lyrics are clever and perfectly executed and timed; and timing is very noticeable in the sound on this cd. It just sounds cool and stays cool and funky without the weird rock nerdy voice he sometimes uses (like the Fury song-great song bad delivery tone of voice) or the corny old man trying to be cool lyrics that sometimes come into play.

I can't wait to hear some songs over and over so I can hear things I missed. The multilayered sounds and engineering of this concept focused album beg for repeat listens.

-He still has not worked with other famous producers and a private wish of mine is he would do an album where he allows others to co-produce with him(Babyface, Rza, Quincy Jones, Black Keys, Awol Nation, Bruno Mars, R.Kelly, Timbaland, Pharell Williams, Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis,  Arctic Monkeys, Jack White, Nile Rodgers or duets with duet with El Debarge or Aerosmith, Red Hot Chili. I'd never heard of this dude Joshua Welton but whoever helped Prince on this (including Prince) keep this going. I don't care, pleeeeease keep it going.

-The songs are perfect in length and very,very crafty and interesting but sometimes I wanted to hear even a 4 minute song go longer because the ending seemed cut-off.

-The consistency of mood and feeling on this cd is slightly dark funk-ridden psychedelic- multi layered vocal singing with various combinations of electronic synthesizer beats mixed with guitar,drums, bass, horns and piano music for 80% of the album.  The other 20% are mid-tempo ballads with the instruments highlighted more and an engineering of Prince's voice moving from your right head phone to left speaker.

-The harmonies make you want to wear a condom on your ears.

If I must COMPARE THIS to an album it might be something in the water that makes me think of it sounding like a new relevant fresh flavor of Lovesexy slash 1999 album to me.

BEST PRINCE ALBUMS in order  from best to 2nd best IMO for radio and expectations: Purple Rain, Sign O the Times, Parade, Lovesexy, 1999, Around The World In A Day, Art Official Age, Symbol album, Come, Batman, One Nite Alone, Diamonds and Pearls, Chaos and Disorder, Crystal Ball, Rave un2, The Truth, Rainbow Children,For You the rest are good but.....
Gibberish confession below:
I've been a quietly fanatic Prince fan since 93 and these past 17 years have been rough being a Prince fan except going to his concerts.  He would give an average of 3 or 4 good songs per cd (enough to make me buy it)but the other stuff was ok but not great or cohesive songs that flowed from one to another. This cd is pure great song after great song that flow and have that cohesiveness that since the late 90's lacked in Prince music (except for One Nite Alone, The Truth, The Rainbow, and RaveUn2).
This album is electronic funk that is up to date in technology and musical styles while adding a few Prince tricks and signature musical moves and HONESTLY a few twists and turns we haven't heard from Prince before in this way.  The beats are like a funked out Erotic City vibe and a much better lyrically sounding and engineering mixing than the song 3121.  He doesn't sound like an old man trying to be cool or find his inner James Brown funk. This is funk the way Prince does it and again it is a current sound that works perfectly for him and he nails is.
The ballads are somewhat reminiscent of Until Ur In My Arms Again slash UR Gonna C Me slash original Prince ballad with an edge to them.
I grew up knowing the 90's Prince (Thieves In The Temple video, My Name Is Prince, Get Off) I listened to every released track and all the unreleased tracks I could get my hands on along with buying his concert dvd's bootleg and not. The last great Prince cd that should have sold well commercially to me was Come (Honorable mentions for good cd's of his but too alienating for most listeners and radio were:  One Nite Alone *jazzy cd, Rainbow Children*jazzy cd, Chaos and Disorder*rock, The Vault*, and Raveun2). That was the sexually frustrated and angry dark Prince that I liked, even though nobody I knew in high school in the 90's no longer bought his music.  The 2000 political and religious teaching Prince (Musicology) lyrical Prince was no surprise and was good, but was not the Prince music that I craved. Once he went in the direction, I could pick up his music and buy it but I no longer expected him to rightfully rise up to the top or give me anything musically unexpected anymore AND THEN THERE WAS Art Official Age.  The album we thought he would come out with after New Year's 1999 has finally arrived.  Prince back to his old tricks with a few new ones and a sound that is killing competition and competitive and inventive with the new sounds of electronic engineering, mixing, song writing.
Feel sorry for the guy sometimes because his diversity in music often alienates his listeners and often makes different people/genders want more of one sound they like and another person dislikes the very sound that sounds classic or great to another. Thus, his albums sometimes go everywhere trying to please everyone with 3 great songs and not making anyone completely happy with 13 songs on one album. I can see the difficulty and have been a victim of his music diversity when he will go from jazz to rock n'roll, to opera rock, to slow ballad, to funk, to hip hop, to undefinable simply prince music all on a cd of 10 songs. It is demanding on a listener to incorporate so much on one cd, and although he does all successfully and authentically I prefer his focused concept albums much more and that's what THIS DELIVERS. So if you want Chaos and Disorder Rock Prince then maybe not for you, if you like Erotic City, DMSR, Something In The Water, If Eye Was Ur Girlfriend then this is your Cd.
profile.summary: Album is like head, it sucks in a great way {like Prince's old song Head} to give you an eargasm.

profile.description: PRINCE - HITNRUN PHASE ONE - CD
profile.reviewText:
Not as good as Art Official Age, but a lot better than some of his other stuff (musicology,3121,planet earth,lotusflo3r,2010,Plectrum).
High light songs for me in this order: June (psychadelic toned down daunting song of reminiscing), Mr. Nelson (musical that changes beats and a killer Carlos Santana like solo guitar riff.), Hardrocklover (stripped down dirty guitar song, sexy rock we haven't heard from prince in a while. I didn't like this until I heard it in better quality and it made me like it),X's face :(something about his falsetto in this song works for me. The beat is funky and I just like it. "Black don't crack, beige don't age. Go on take that banana then get back in your cage), 1000X's Hugs and Kisses is a laid back truly R&B tune with Prince 'princing' it up a little bit. It is an easy midtempo stepping beat with a couple of beat changes. It sounds like Prince wanted to keep the song simple and it works. It works, but sometimes I wish he would do a B-sides of just remixes b/c many of his songs sound like he's not done grooving, Ain't About to Stop is a track where you hear a lot of sound fx that sound like the song is in a factory with machines going and there's a band playing hard rock/hip hop beat with Prince singing some and talking melodically through some.  It works for me, although I can understand some people not feeling it so much.  I think he brings the funk on this cd and succeeds. It's definitely in the same vein as an Album with Art Official Age. Same overrall type of feel, this album is just less cohesive; and simply not as good as Art Official Age.

Rant: The songs I like, I read in these reviews are the very songs many others hate. Then the songs that sound stupid to me are the one's many others write about loving. I've said it before, I feel sorry for Prince trying to put that one more Classic album together when this is the case.  It's clear he's on point. He is doing exactly what some love and others don't and vice versa all within the same album.  That has to be pretty confusing when wanting everyone to like every song. If he cares (I kinda don't think he does).  On another note: Josh Welton is doing Prince some good but WHYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY Prince????????? WhY??????????? Why won't he work with well known producers and singers????? It's stupid. He's been in the business almost 40 years and still won't work with known talents in their primes or at least still relevant. For example (Babyface, Sade, Aerosmith is out of their prime but still, Timbaland, D'Angelo, or let Red Hot Chili Peppers do a beat for you, anyone who has plenty of hits on their belts)
profile.summary: Why won't he ever work with bona fide talents in their primes or slightly after their primes???

profile.reviewText: I've only listened to album once.  After the first six songs, I almost took the cd out, in fact I did, and started listening to another cd. I then put it in again after 15 minutes of driving and after song 6 the rest of the songs on the cd sounded really good.  None of the early songs were bad, they just weren't energetic or moving. profile.description: 2014 collaboration between the R&B greats. With an all-time total of 16 Grammy Awards between them, multi-platinum superstars Toni Braxton and Kenny 'Babyface' Edmonds have finally teamed up for their first album of duets together, The album celebrates the strong bond that has been in place between the two artists ever since Babyface and Toni's duet on her smash 1992 debut, "Give U My Heart," which was co-written and co-produced by Babyface.
profile.reviewText:
First off Thank you Babyface for releasing a cd. You take too long to release music!!!!
It has been 9 years since we've seen a solo effort with all new songs from Babyface sung only by Babyface. For those of us who really love his music, this is a PUNISHMENT. The album highlights Toni Braxton moreso than Babyface. I don't know if Babyface was vocally intimidated by Braxton and decided to never really stretch his vocal range or match in harmony or any kind of power to Braxton, but simply he just didn't. I can understand why when you're producing and writing and singing and Braxton has a better voice, but I would've liked to hear Face exert more emotion vocally on this album.  His voice sounds strong and clear again and the production on this cd is great, but as a fan of Babyface and a semi-fan of Toni; I felt Toni was showcased vocally more on this album.
This album is a very solid effort done successfully.  The very first song Rollercoaster is a great song perfect song talking about the ups-and-downs of a relationship and it is lyrically perfect.  Babyface always writes lyrics where he touches on the real depth of a situation and then brings in melodies and choruses rarely ever going too far with lyrics (except on songs like How can u be down, diary, With Him). Those songs are great, but I'm making the point that the album goes everywhere in a relationship therefore he didn't have to try and do it all in one song. Sweat is a song where it is easy sounding. The lyrics are of a man and woman trying to figure out where to go in a relationship after the fighting is over. It is the questioning a relationship phase, sung in babyface's falsetto in a midtempo song.
I'm sure you've heard Hurt you, which I thought was a good song but not great when I heard it on radio and tv, but on cd the quality brings the feeling and emotion out much clearer (It kind of has that Babyface song "The Loneliness" feel to it. Actually if that song was on this cd then I would've given the album 5 stars. This album seemed to miss that one "beyond great" song quality that I wanted.
"I hope you're okay," is about breaking up or separating (not divorced yet) where the other is saying they don't harbor bitterness and that basically the relationship is over but they can remain cool with each other.  The songs beat is upbeat although the lyrics are actually pretty different for a R&B song.
I wish is actually my favorite song on this cd. The lyrics are deep and touching; and as a man listening to it...scary but honest.  I would've loved to hear Babyface on this song. This song stole the album for me.
Take it Back is really reminiscent of a SAde song in my opinion. It is a good smooth song where the lyrics reminisce over the good times in the relationship and wanting to take it back to those times; which must've been better. Reunited is a good song, a quality song. I'd Rather Be broke is more of a contemporary beat song with the lyrics only Babyface can write.  This sounds like it might be a good pick for the the 2nd release song for this album.
Heart Attack is probably the only fast-paced auto-tuned song on album.  It is a simple song that fits.
The D word is probably my favorite song on the cd or tied with the I wish song.  This is classical babyface singing a duet with his real voice and falsetto with a beat that sounds like it is moving through a passage of time and to a destination. The lyrics are about divorce; and again how he will love her even through the divorce but they cannot be together. I hope this will be the next radio hit.
Best songs to ne: Rollercoaster, The D Word, I Wish.

It has been 9 years since we've seen a solo effort with all new songs from Babyface sung only by Babyface.
I thought How Can An Angel Break My Heart duet with Braxton and Babyface was one of the top 3 prettiest male/female duets I've ever heard in all time. Please stop reading now unless you care to read me ramble/gossip now. While I'm rambling I'll go beyond what should be said and just say as a listener it sounds as though his wife cheated on him. From his old songs "With him, The Diary, and a couple songs on this cd," he sings about a woman cheating on her man and although he sings about a man also cheating; it seems more heartfelt when he sings the former. IDK. This cd was a great solid cd with a strong concept. I loved it, but I do have to say it is not his best cd and I kind of wanted more from the two. Toni seemed like she was ready and she was there on this cd to make it great, but Babyface seemed to take a backseat to Braxton and this is what I didn't like from the duet album. I felt this cd was Toni Braxton featuring Babyface (even though Face wrote the songs, played the songs, produced them). This cd was good, but it did not give me that Wow factor that usually Babyface's cd's give me for at least 3 songs.  Again, it is a good cd and great beyond classic compared to what's out today. The concept was excellent and executed perfectly. I just have to state as a fan that the feeling from Babyface in "The Loneliness," "Keeping Secrets," "Where Is My Love," "How Can An Angel Break My Heart," "The Diary" "With Him," and I could keep going; but the point is that emotion (besides I Wish; sung by Braxton) was not on this cd for me and I wanted it. Divorce is emotion. I haven't been divorced but I can guess.
profile.summary: song for song review and an opinion on cd

profile.description: Ten years ago in the town of Harmony, an inexperienced coal miner caused an accident that trapped and killed five men and sent the only survivor, Harry Warden, into a coma. When Harry awoke, exactly one year later on Valentine’s Day, he wanted revenge and brutally murdered 22 people with a pickax before being killed himself. Now, after years of peace, something from Harmony’s dark past has returned. Wearing a miner’s mask and armed with a pickax, an unstoppable killer is on the loose. As his footsteps come ever closer, the townspeople realize in terror that it just might be Harry Warden who has found his way back.
profile.reviewText:
The 3d in this movie is very good as it comes to depth. They even attempt to do quite a bit of out of your screen 3d, but I will be honest.  The out of your screen 3d is barely out of your screen.  Since I've watched over 20 3d movies on my 3dtv I will say it does come out of your screen more than the other dvd's, but seriously the 3d is barely out of your screen. I come from the generation of Terminator at Universal Studios and sadly the Muppets at Universal and the bad Freddie Kruger movie but great out of the screen 3d generation.  These attempts now at out of the screen are sad.
As far as the movie goes it is a good slasher movie with a surprise ending and well acted movie. I enjoyed it a lot and I'm not a fan of slashers (although I have watched more than a hundred).  When it comes to simple slasher teen movies with a nice plot and twist without being corny or trying too hard to be cool this movie does great. It is shot very well and uses 3d perfectly when it comes to depth.

Just a sidenote: I think the movie industry knows audiences want out of the screen 3d, but they want to profit off 3d and 2d movies when they hit shelves in stores and if someone doesn't have a 3d tv (which 99% of the world doesn't) then the out-of-the screen parts of the movie look corny on 2d tv's. Knowing this to be the case, hollywood producers, distributors, and directors have taken off in the media and blogs to lie to audiences telling them that out of the screen 3d is not what audiences want and then stupid regular people go and sign-off on this too. Not like it's a conspiracy, just the fact that dvd's mostly in 2d make more money than truly investing in all the aspects and options of 3d (mainly pop out 3d).
profile.summary: Good movie and 3d. Not enough out of the screen 3d

profile.description: Universally hailed as a thrilling new figure in music for his edgy, lo-fi debut, The Headphone Masterpiece, back in 2002, Cody ChesnuTT is a soul troubadour whose frank, socially conscious ruminations on life continue to challenge popular notions of what modern soul music can look and sound like: a raw storyteller for the people wearing a guitar and a toothpick-chewing smirk; a wide-eyed, intense soul brother in a crazy-fly get-up singing about bedraggled love in the land of Lost Angeles - he's all of that, but wiser now while still wearing poetic license on his skin like a battle scar. The Atlanta native has always stood his own creative ground ever since he first holed himself up in his bedroom to record The Headphone Masterpiece, armed with his DIY musical arsenal: a drum machine, an array of instruments, a dusty four-track cassette recorder and a giant pair of headphones to block out the world. The result was an unvarnished collection of songs -- 36 in total, which alchemized his love of a multitude of styles: classic rock, rhythm and blues, pop, punk and gospel music.
profile.reviewText:
Lyrically the album is superior as his song writing is very conversational and thought provoking yet easier than neo-soul; and this ain't neo-soul it's just I can hear people putting it there when this is really just funk driven soul music. In no way does he sound like Bill Withers but the content of honesty and finding himself while singing and that being heard in his vocal notes like his singing is trying to find which note to catch with his life reminds me of Bill in content only.  The cd has a variety of subject matter from spiritual, to using crack, to well read below if u wanna know; but...
It was funny to see someone else make the comparison to Terence Trent D'arby.  Obviously Cody's is not trying to imitate Terence since his voice registers a little lower, but some of his vocal arrangements do take your ear back to Terence----His lyrics in no way resemble Terence nor do his choruses.  Other vocal similarities are Stevie Wonder without the twisting the voice everywhere.  Trust me he's not trying to sound like these guys but if you need to know where the voice takes you then....yeah it does remind you.  And oh yeah he's from ATL. It woulda helped publicity wise if dre 3000 or Cee-Lo could have been pulled on a song. And's this cd is way better than his last.  His last was creative, poor, definitely different, interesting, incomplete disturbing and satisfying. This one's all good.
Here's a content song by song:
1. Till I meet thee is an easy going melodic/harmonic multilayered voice song with a beat reminiscent of like a garageband with the exception of the serenading horns. It's a song about being once lost and seeking to find things that would make him happy and ended up finding God after trying everything else.  This is a cool song without ever being corny. In the end of the song he goes acapella and showcases his ear.
2. Since my birth- is a song that sounds like a jam session with guitars and horns in the background to keep a simple beat as he calls out each African country.
3. That's still mama is a song speaking from a man's point of view disappointing his mother as he is in jail for being a dopeboy with an assault charge having to call his mother to ask her to testify for him in court and bail him out and then see it from his mother's point of view looking at her son raised in the church venture into the world and do things that make her wander if he she raised him right.  This song he is storytelling and gives a message, saying don't treat your mother any kind of way or your family because these are people that you end up calling on.
This song has a nice uptempo moving beat with the chorus also playing a voice in the song.
4. What kind of Cool  is talking about all the ways we know how to be cool and the ways we know how to front and perpetrate to hide where we really our in our stance in life.  He talks about why we do these things "to say we did it and lived it up," but how the cool eventually runs out and you're left without being able to use your cool to cover up.  The song is sung in a smooth voice with a nice beat to ride to that can remind someone of a Marvin Gaye song and is almost romantic until you listen to the lyrics.
5. Don't Follow Me- Is a very sad song that sounds like it's sung in an empty room with a piano, violin, cello, horn, drums and emptiness. It Is a song that cries to his son not to follow him and how he can follow anything else that might be good or bad, but not to put his hopes in his father and try to follow in his father's footsteps. Just make sure what you do is what you want to do and not what you think your father wants.  He drops his voice pretty low on this song.
6. Everybody's Brother- Song about how he used to be a crackhead and now he's teaching kids in Sunday School.  He goes into how he used to swindle friend's, do anything for money, blame other people, walk out on family etcetera.  It is a simple beat reminiscent of beats on his last cd. The only thing missing in this song is a whistle for the walking beat he provides.
7. Love is more than a wedding day- self-explanatory, but he's saying love is more than spending all your money on a wedding day or a one-night stand or the battle of egos.  An upbeat song with a nice beat and harmonica and tambourine and soft horns as he explains he believes in it.  This song builds up to a celebration and kinda sounds like it can be played at a wedding.
8.  Spell of the Handout- The song changes beats about 3 times. song reminds me of the voice of the funky Stevie Wonder. He talks about the working class, a beggar, 3 piece suit men all under the spell of the class structure that keeps us hypnotized and numb to the real things in the world that can free us.  He speaks how men will do anything to have a share of the class structure and how it can get people 25 years to life in wealth, or corporate jobs, or prison and how it's all similar in the sacrifice of real living they sacrifice for vanity.  The song breaks down it's funky to get even funkier as he takes the listener to church as he talks about how to break free from the handout and handles and give himself and his family a chance at finding themselves.

9.  Don't Wanna Go the other way- a song that races against itself as he is hollering about trying to keep himself going the straight and narrow and resist the other way (which one can guess he's really struggling with staying legit) but how he still sees things on the other side he wants. Song has him singing over clapping hands, a fast beat.  It sounds like a fraternity can step to this as African beats are played, the sound of heavy breathing helps the beat and he chants in an echo of kind of a space solar beat.  Yeah.  This is some original shhh.  He went the other way with this song.
profile.summary: Hmm...Purely definition of folkurban-funk driven lil psychadelic honest lyricism music.

profile.description: 2010 release from the R&B veteran, his first in 16 years. Soulful, sleek and deeply romantic, Second Chance features the first single, "Lay With You" featuring Faith Evans. Second Chance tells El's story of redemption, which followed a period of personal turmoil for the immensely talented singer and songwriter. Co-executive produced by Ron Fair and Pete Farmer, Second Chance features collaborations with 50 Cent ("Format"), and Fabolous ("5 Seconds"). It also unites El DeBarge with some of music's most notable hitmakers, including co-writing and co-production by Babyface, Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis, Mike City, Michael Angelo, Mischke, and the Avila Brothers.
profile.reviewText: Of all El DeBarge's cd's (el debarge, gemini, in the storm, heart mind and soul), and I've listened to all of them and really only three consistently over 20 years I will say this is the best solo effort he has given.  Heart Mind and Soul was a great cd to me also.  I really liked it and still do.  This cd gives a wide range of El in areas I didn't think he could go musically.  He is a musical genius, but honestly he has been a genius who could write or produce three great timeless songs per album after he broke from his family.  And for those that might argue the truth is even when he was with his family they averaged about 3 or 4 good songs per album; it was the compilation of those great songs over the years that make people think El's albums were great when they were great just not song for song great each album.  The range of this album from uptempo, to slow, to ballad, to classic El melodies or hymns over new beats truly amazed me.  There are still songs I don't like and probably never will on this cd, such as the song with Fabolous but for anyone gone 16 years to be able to have an ear like El's and break out of the 80's and into 2010/2011 with a new style and polish the faults in today's music by teaching melodies again is a stroke of genius.  Some of the best parts of the cd was listening to El humm, or El snapping his fingers, or singing without saying words but just harmonizing notes to take the songs in places that were eargasmic.  In short what surprised me was to hear El's timing and command over songs with strong bass driven beats (I expect him to rule over the piano) when he was singing lyrics that overlapped his voice with more lyrics and the lyrics were deeply heartfelt, romantic and spiritual at times lyrics.  I know very well who I am talking about and expect this out of El, but usually only for 3 maybe 4 songs and  Not 10 (there were 3 songs that were okay, not bad just not great). Maybe I'll tighten up this review later, but I had low expectations for El mainly because standards are so high after you've proven 20 years ago that you wrote and sung some of the most beautiful songs and people expect to hear only the great songs again as though back then you never wrote lackluster songs; El exceeded my expectations and for him to be a man a few months from 50 I'd call this more than a second  chance but a delivery.  El delivered on this in the best way imaginable.  Music is not easy.  I rate his cd collection now in this order :Second Chance is 1st, In a Special Way, Heart Mind and Soul, All This Love, and the other's sucked so bad with exception to those 2 or 3 songs they all get last. If you don't believe me then you really weren't buying his albums back in the day--go listen to Gemini, In the Storm, and El Debarge (ha,ha).  Babyface you're next!!!!!The song he wrote for El was fierce.
profile.summary: second chance is #1 of El's solo cd's

This kit comes one 20"x28" softbox to soften your lights. This Studio portrait Kit is easy to use and setup. These lights work great with digital cameras. It is ideal for all level photographers. You will get off almost all the shadow when the light wrap around your subject. The light head has 5 On/off switch so you could adjust the output. This set could be used for digital or video photography. This lighting kit is used for high production work and can be left on all day.
profile.reviewText:
The good? You can put it together correctly and it does work, and once you know how, it is not hard (still not easy). It makes you look professional to have your own softbox lights. They give you a case that should hold up for at least a few uses, as long as you don't put anything extra in it besides these lights.
The bad? I have to be on the side of the people complaining about how hard this was to assemble.  I almost sent these back because I believed this was a scam and they were only selling defective lights incapable of correct assembly. They give you a website to go to that makes it much easier to assemble and shows you the order to assemble it in, because if you think it is as simple as poking the rod through the loop and trying not to break it (which by the way it's meant to bend and probably won't ever break)then you'll be fumbling around for quite a while FRUSTRATED like hell like me. I do not look forward to taking it apart again or reassembling it on a set. I also don't think it's possible to assembe this by yourself.  Even on the video with the girl doing it, they cut the video to show it already done and don't show her inserting each rod by herself.  It's also not 1000 watt, maybe I can buy the lightbulbs and make it so though.
Overall, I'm happy I bought them and happier I didn't break them.

profile.description: 2013 sophomore full-length album from writer, actor, standup comedian and rapper Donald Glover AKA Childish Gambino. The recording process for the album began in 2012 and continued until October 2013. Because the Internet features guest appearances from Chance The Rapper, Jhene Aiko and Azealia Banks, with production handled by Gambino himself, Christian Rich, Thundercat and Ludwig Goransson among others.
profile.reviewText:
Good cd and real authentic to who he is. The man can rhyme. This cd has plenty of songs talking about relationships and some different rhyme schemes and definitely different rhymes. I like the suburb rap coming out. It helps rap music altogether. Quite a few songs on the cd have hooks where someone is singing on them, but it doesn't ruin the cd. Words or lyrics that stand out on album to me. "Look at the recluse, 3005, I ain't invite all these people to my house, Okkk.onomatopoeia" Might not mean much but yo.  His approach to how he raps and when he comes in on beats or when he decides to let the music come in is where he is showing he is music savvy by not only looking for the beat to rhyme on. He's actually paying attention to his delivery and respects the beat enough to acknowledge the beat with his delivery.  Now, here's the bad or criticism. As much as his beef is toward Lupe, he actually in his artistry sounds pretty similar to Lupe and they seem to pull from a similar place. Lupe talks politics too much, and Gambino talks on relationships with women too much. They both use electronic/sometimes techno sounds to impact their rap music. Enough of that. I'm from Lithonia and know the Stone Mountain area and know exactly the area he from. His music is more true to the area than plenty of other rappers from other cities that rap toward doing what they think rap music is supposed to do and don't give off the real feel of the environment they're from. For those who care Stn. Mtn and Lithonia is home to a lot, a bunch of blacks that have money & a quite an equal number of middle class blacks too. President Clinton came and said he had no idea blacks lived that good in the US. It ain't full of mansions, but just educated people. Well, funny thing though is like Gambino said on his other cd; many of the blacks ship their kids out to M-to M schools for education. This exposes a lot of them/us to areas outside of our own suburb and introduce us to others suburbs. Now, that I've pissed off a lot of people with ranting on some stuff that probably ain't got much to do with Gambino.
 I would've liked to hear some songs with different topics. I ain't care for all the singing, but it did make sense to the feel of the album. For a guy with his hands in tv, screenplays and able to rap and be musical and creative with it I can't give dude less than a 4. I hope he gets some respect on this one. It ain't a classic cd when talking about all rap music, but it is one of the best to come out this year and probably will be in 2014 also. It's a good cd.
profile.summary: he didn't compromise the music to rap

profile.description: Produced by Jack White and recorded at his own Third Man Studio in Nashville, Blunderbuss has been described by White as "an album I couldn't have released until now. I've put off making records under my own name for a long time but these songs feel like they could only be presented under my name. These songs were written from scratch, had nothing to do with anyone or anything else but my own expression, my own colors on my own canvas."
profile.reviewText: This cd did not hit me like his others. First thing I noticed off this listen is jack's not doing what he did on other cd's but diving deeper into his music catalogue. The catchy choruses of "Many shades of black" or infectious bass of seven nation was not there.  What is there are the lyrics and storytelling for your ass and a musician weaving in old I mean old country time blues then current rock n' roll and folk songs done perfectly. Most of the songs on this cd somehow put me in the same mindframe of that song about the Milk man and the boy killing on Carolina Drama. Songs like Poor boy are catchy but some of the songs I actually love best are the ones without the catchy choruses (hypocritical kiss, i'm shakin).  Basically this is how he cd hit me.  1Missing pieces caught my ear as an uptempo rock n'roll song with a beat that seems a little bit off from catching itself but completely works the beat is very catchy but he's telling a great story that doesn't lend you to be able to sing with the chorus, but listen greatfully. Great song, liked it first listen and it had me thinking the whole album would move in this direction.  2Sixteen saltines is that hard fast garage rock (tone similar to fell in love with a girl). This song gives the album that punch and fast pace. 3Freedom at 21 is him singing in a rap-like tone that works because of the style of singing voice he uses. It helps to add diversity to the album since he uses a choppy singing voice for most of the cd. 4I'm sure everyone's heard love interruption. Great song. 5Blunderbuss is somewhat reminiscent of a Led Zepellin song that never was. Jack sings on this song and sings in a talking voice over a grand piano and violin. The melody is hypnotic and folksy. "doing what two people need is never on my menu," that line is awkard but describes his attitude to me.  6Hypocritical kiss starts off like it's gonna be symphonic the way the piano introduces itself with a flushing of the keys it leads up to the epicness of a guy having an argument with his girl about why he's right and she's wrong. This is a song that is needed during a time when so many men want to sing apology songs about how men are wrong and stupid.  Love this song, it reminds me i'm a man and have the right to be right (haha). 7Weep themselves starts off with guitars, piano and drums that somehow make me feel like I'm in a western showdown.  Jack speaks of beating his girl up in the first line and talks bad about the guys who are suckers for love.  He's not really singing in this song, but like announcing in a singing tone things that are about men's feelings of the world and relationships. It's a song that takes a stand about the choice of how men decide to be a specific type of man and what they can expect for consequences. 8I'm shakin makes me feel like I'm trapped in rag time song in the 20's and 70's somehow as he describes how a woman makes him feel great and he's shakin from bad nerves. He likens his nervous wreck to leaves on a tree shaking but he's jumping from insecurity and likes it. This is an old time style of song and works for where the rest of the album goes. 9trash tongue is like a Little Richard song. God only knows when I heard someone sound like little richard (maybe Awol Nation) on that one song.  He's telling a song about some monkeys, he breaks into old time piano playing and tamborines. I think i even hear a banjo. This is like some old time Chuck Berry Rock n'roll stuff with Jack growling out blues singing on an rock song. I wanted to hear him scream on this one or have some more fun with it, but it seemed like he was trying to focus on making the song authentic.  10 this song starts off like i'm on a carousel but then leads it's way into being a ballad and then reveals itself to be a definite folk song with a banjo or very old guitar a simple piano playing and a catchy as hell chorus.  Jack sings and tells the story of a poor boy.  This song is an easy going, uptempo, fun song to me.  Some of the greatest love songs are the ones that don't praise love or speak of the good side. 11 this song is like an old gospel 1910 song with folk song lyrics. I hate to put it that far back but I listen to a lot of music and this is definitely Jack showing he can take a song from 1910 and somehow bring Queen remnants out then the original jack white somehow turning this into a lullabye. This song works on so many levels. I wish I was smoking, but that past is gone for me. I would like to know what he was smokin to go there with it though. 12on and on "sun and the moon never change, they just rearrange," parables, philosophies sung in a tenor, a duet partially in harmony, a soft song crooning then changes to somewhat a mix of a jazz, psychadelic rock song. This song just starts to cement the continuity of listenability of the cd that lets you know that no song is going to make it so you don't feel the album. 13 is probably my favorite because of the very weird harmony he uses.  It's jazzy and psychadelic, sorry to say that again but it uses jazz keys and I don't even listen to jazz. it just is.  The only thing rock and roll about the song is Jack's singing in the end. This song is a sing-a-long song and makes you want to be on the road looking at cornfields and blue skies.  The end of the song breaks into a zepellin type rockin out to end the song of with probably one of the most pleasant unique falsettos and harmonies i've heard in a while. Perfect way to end of the cd. To summarize it all I wanted to hear Jack really showcase his vocal range and sing steady long notes and harmonies (like many shades of black) instead he used a choppy singing voice most of the time. I wanted to hear choruses from White Stripes Elephants that make you incapable of getting the song out your head. Instead he introduced me to what seems to be a very natural place for him musically, but new to my ear.  It took a lot of listening until I could hear and love what he was doing. He somehow updated the oldest blues, before Muddy Waters, and brought in himself Jack and 1960's 70's psycadelic era. He left out the 80's vibe completely that some of his other cd's gave to.  Eclectic cd that shows Jack is a musician that has influences but is so educated in music that he is creating, recreating and making style of completely his own.  So many of his songs do this that I just have to give him the credit for being one of the greatest musicians out there today. Great masterpiece classic.
profile.summary: 11times i didn' like it 12th time i loved it

profile.description: D'Arby is a first-rate songwriter, splendid vocalist and versatile musician who wears his influences broadly. And TERENCE TRENT D'ARBY'S VIBRATOR adds up to a musically intoxicating concoction.
profile.reviewText:
This was his LAST great cd. I have listened to his music and admired his voice and words for years. I've listened even to music he didn't release to the publish.  Wildcard is probably his last decent cd and this Vibrator CD showcased all his talent as a singer for everyone and everything with an unbelievable purity in his voice, cadence, loudness, softness, brashness, rock and roll, soul singer, classical, a little latin beat, eccentric singer with a lot of vibrato and raspiness.  He goes into dark places as a Dark Angel calls his name and takes you to sexual places as he awakes from a dream to have a Supermodel with Cheese, on your knees if you Please.
The title of the cd alone informs you of his interest: batteries included.
This cd was absolutely great, impeccable, perfect and whatever other word you want to use to describe the genius that was Terence Trent D'arby.  Now, however with his new name everything he puts out flat out sucks.  It's so bad that I want to buy it but can't force myself to buy it.  It's so terrible lyrically and song crafting wise that I now am convinced that this music from Vibrator, Symphony or Damn, Neither Fish Nor Flesh, and Introducing Could not HAVE BEEN WRITTEN or PRODUCED by HIM.  Maybe he wrote the words, but he did not craft those songs. The music he is doing now is as corny and elementary as it gets; you wouldn't even believe he is the same singer.  There is no way a writer of that caliber from those former albums goes to this degree. I've listened to many other artists Smokey Robinson, Stevie Wonder, Aerosmith who are far from their primes and even still you can hear glitches of their old songwriting and elements that made them great. Why? This is because they were the authors of their own music.  You can't lose that ability to the Degree TTD has lost or never had his.  He never produced those songs by himself and whoever was helping him from Vibrator and previous to that album should be given the credit and he should rehire that person or persons back if he ever wants any relevance in the music industry again. I want to hear him sing good music. I miss his one of a kind voice.  This is the last cd that showcased it.  Spoken as a true fan.
profile.summary: I can't believe he writes his own music, in other words I don't believe it

profile.description: Ps4 The Witcher: Wild Hunt
profile.reviewText:
who is doing these reviews?
I don't like to give it 3 stars but since some people seem to be lying, let me try to say what isn't really said.  The game is okay. The fighting scenes mainly have you pressing square and then R2 to use a magic attack.  That's it for the fighting. Often characters leave your screen and I have a 60 inch screen, and you have to guess where they are to attack.
Now the main problem is the amount of questions you ask people and the length of time on answers and questions is ridiculous. I was not aware I was playing Game of Thrones.  The game feels like 10% fighting and 90% asking people questions.
Then you are give a combined number of around 100 weapons, medicines, powers, wardrobes that you constantly have to repair and power up and none of these enhance your gameplay like a "infamous."
The missions play out as "go save my daughter," you run to save the daughter but first "you must ask Renaldo where his jacket is," then "you must perform in a stageplay to reveal Renaldo," then you must "help Renaldo fight." Renaldo gets killed. Now "you must find out how to find out what Renaldo knew," by asking 40 more questions to get to saving a daughter.
The game does not suck. It is not a bad game.
I think it just tried to hard to do everything (provide story, provide side missions, give good graphics, provide a vast open world, allow players to play cards on the game) and didn't focus hard enough on actual gameplay entertainment.
I'm not a fan of Farcry, but it does a better balance of gameplay and story line and weapons enhancements.
This is why I give it 3 stars.
It's very long, too many questions, good graphics, relaxed gameplay, story that is good but very exhausting and you will skip through some of the story and okay C minus level gameplay.
profile.summary: who is doing these reviews?

profile.description: DANGELO AND THE VANGUARD BLACK MESSIAH
profile.reviewText:
Definitely worth buying and listening to.
First part of my review is my opinion of overrall album. 2nd part is song for song review

It took at least the 5th lesson before I could give it the respect it deserves.
Do yourself a favor and listen to this on good headphones and turn the bass down a little bit and the mids/treb up. You will thank me.
Anyways this cd is unique, original, and of course you catch an influence of D'angelo that hasn't been noted before this and that is a touch of Sly Stone.
Negative first then positive

Overrall I have to change my mind from how I originally felt. Before I felt there were no radio-friendly catchy choruses and I still feel this way when I compare it to Brown Sugar's radio-play songs, these melodies are not mass appeal friendly but more mature, in depth and inventive (instead of his past albums where he just gives you a beat. Here the beat is there but is by a live band and is therefore constantly developed by a symphony of other sounds that compliment the beat), for a developed music ear for listeners that appreciate the quality of music stanza changes, twists and inserts of varying lead instruments all incorporated in one song and from one song to the next. This is musicianship as opposed to a pop-forumula on an assembly line/belt. Really, D'Angelo just doesn't do pop-music, but some of his music is radio friendly.

I wished I could hear more of just his pure voice with NO multi-layering (although his background multivoice layering is beautiful. I also wish that he would just really funk out on one instrument for like two minutes to let us hear his skills as a guitar or keyboard player/musician. If you listen closely you can hear him semi-doing it, but I mean showcasing his vocals and instrument ability to the fullest solo-ish.) I want the grit and grime and dirty funk rock that he is teasing us with in Ain't That Easy and 1000 Deaths.
On some speaker systems the album will sound muddy and sounds will be drowned out by the bass. He multi-layers his voice a lot as usual (except on songs:prayer and really love and another life-where he limits the multilayering down to the chorus and only double layers his lead voice). He sings through mumbles,humms,grunts, screams and crooning and displays a vocal range that is very wide but only seen in short bursts. You will not hear him holding notes longer than 2 seconds or singing fully with his talking chest voice. He is smooth and funky and it is in his excerpt adlib grunts and hollars that I really grow o respect his ear.

I don't hear more than 2 strong hits for the masses on the cd, but the album is a masterpiece/classic. I do listen to this more than any of his other albums. If a person does not give the album the respect that it demands (I say demands b/c on first listening I was far from impressed and closer to let down) to listen to the album in its entirety and not just 1 song or 2 then it is very rewarding.

The album requires repeat listens and did not capture my attention immediately, again maybe due to the soundsystem I was using. His vocals/mumbles and grunts once played absurdly too far behind the instruments and were not showcased unless you have your speaker's equalizer's set with mids, highs, and trebles waaaaay above the bass.

Positives
This album is one helluva catchy stay in your head harmonious-melodic album (again not contradicting that it's not radio chorus catchy or lyrically clich catchy) that I can't get enough of and can't stop listening to simply because of the jazz fused funk ridden hip hop feel and lyrical delivery that I've just never heard combined in an entire album before.
 Black Messiah is soft music with a splintered edge, and oh so funky smelling a slight influence of a little rock n' roll flavor that rears its head shyly.
I would instantly buy the remixes to this entire album if he rocked them out, because some of the songs sound like he wanted to make them longer and go rock n'roll or freestyle jam sessions for jazz swingers (oh, I really don't like jazz, but the way D'angelo does it is perfect daddy-o).
There are a variety of creations of bridges in a song and vocal deliveries; instruments showcased and instruments allowed to freely roam within a song, and his numerous vocal chants/scat with ability with actual words.  WHOEVER is playing that bass is killing it!!!
His vocals seemingly creating melodies on top of melodies that blend in a way where you're-like-"damn, how did he hear that," but you have to listen because it is subtle sometimes and not brash. If you pay attention you can hear he took a lot of time on the subtle cadences and timing of vocals and chants to make sure he wasn't vocally or instrumentally repeating himself but introducing you to a new perspective on the song. This is the secret ingredient to the stew of voodoo he's cooked on the masala of this album.
One second it's the beat changing, then the vocal melodies change, then the bridge and chorus have different takes the second time you hear them, then a certain instrument goes on a very brief solo. This is 70% of the album the other 30% is more standard song crafting (really love, in another life).

I've seen many artists in R&B try to take songs different places and consistently change things in a song, but this is the first album that just keeps doing it successfully,and I repeat "successfully" and R&B album, because some other genres of music also do it successfully (such as rock n roll).
 I think I can say it confidently that this is D'Angelo's melodic and instrumental masterpiece. It is HIS magnus opus.  I hesitate before I can give it a certain high status to be compared with Other musician's best albums, because I still just don't hear more than 2 bona-fide hit songs that will resonate with the masses outside of R&B/neo-soul and some jazz fans.  The music also requires the listener to be patient and try to appreciate it, instead of capturing the listener immediately on first listen and making them like it---in a way some artists (and even D'angelo in the past) do.
I can't see more than 2 songs going above #5 on the charts.

Although he doesn't have those pop hits or hits that you know will just sell 2 million off one-song alone; and he doesn't even have the number of instant hits from his first album that were consistently hits, I do hear and know his music ability has increased light years from his past----because of the different places he takes our ear now gracefully and with ease, whereas all those other songs sounded like he wanted to take you somewhere different musically in Lady or Brown Sugar but he just didn't know how and couldn't do it, therefore those songs which should have been a 3 minute song became a 7  minute song with no new perspective and only beat repeating itself along with the lyrics.
I can see this album going platinum without much commercial advertising, and this shows strength.
I do believe he accomplished his mission within this album by making each song smoothly transition to another. I do think he created a consistent work of genius in this piece and it is one of the best ever (not the best-kinda but kinda like a  81pts compared to the best player ever-23) concept albums that is cohesive, unique and theme driven.
profile.summary: Maynot have more than 2 radio pop hits onLP,but it's a masterpiece. If Prince is Jordan,D'angelo is Kobe81

profile.description: Jack White presents his new album Lazaretto, on Third Man Records/Columbia. Lazaretto inhabits an exciting place in White's expansive discography as the follow-up to 2012's Gold-certified international #1 Blunderbuss, and will be preceded by first single and title track "Lazaretto," to be released later this month.
profile.reviewText:
The order should be:
Lazaretto, would you fight for my love, temporary ground, alone in my home, i think i found the culprit, three women, that black bat licorice, want and able, entitlement, high ball stepper Bonus: One Drink

The album kept confusing me and was waaaaaay to hard a listen the way he arranged his songs.  I'm not saying my opinion is for everybody, but rearranging the tracklisting made one helluva difference in how I enjoyed the album. Honestly, I didn't like the album until I changed the order, but I could hear that the quality was there.

lazaretto- hard rock song with a infectious drum beat sung with a bit of a rap flow in a dirty microphone. Good brief guitar solo at middle of song. This song is very well mixed with various instruments and added electronic sounds.

Song also transitions to show many different bridges in the song without losing the beat.  Song is basically about someone going crazy but metamorphosizing into something greater while everyone wants a piece of him.

I give this song a 10.

would you fight-Mid tempo rock song. The beat corrals the listener like a wild west stand off between two enemies.  The drum solo at the beginning is perfect as it doubles over itself. This song does not follow typical song formats and seems to be more of a unique style and change of starting a song off. The drum beat comes in as a solo, the piano plays hard, then some daunting ghostly falsetto sets the stage and then they all unite to almost a different song but yet perfectly the same song before Jack begins talking to his narcissistic/self-centered lover. He sings about becoming a ghost to avoid his lover who is highly capable of hurting him and wanting more from him.  He challenges her to instead of being worried about what she wants to instead look at him and fight for his love before he leaves her.  The second verse starts Jack philosophizing and making assumptions about relationships of all people.  The beat changes and rallies his cry.

temporary ground-makes you feel like you are on a porch looking down a country road with a banjo in your lap. It is a folk song people.  The keys and strings whine as they are played to an easy feel."the explorers had it easy, they discovered nothing new," "Moving without motion, screaming without sound" "God left us here hanging with an illusion of a home."  Quite a few one one-liners as he poetically describes his state of thought on how things seem basically temporary or not there or moving with or without him.

alone in my home-Piano plays this ditty with an easy tempo.  It is sung with two people. He seems to be seeking asylum in his house so that nobody can hurt him or know him. Nobody is allowed in.

I think I found the culprit-is another showdown song. A winy western theme with an acoustic guitar played for rhythm and a hard piano. It plays like a movie. I don't know why I keep thinking western movies on his songs, but the beat mildly takes you there.  "Birds of a feather may lay together, but the uglier one is always under the gun." His bridges are weird and not normal bridges but they work.  Uglier people are scrutinized and critiqued harder than their prettier counterparts even if they are the same as others, others will say they are negative. Maybe this isn't his point but it sounds like it.

3 women-A fun funky bluesy rock song talking about 3 women he has at the same time. Blends old rhythm vocals from old blues styles for the chorus with a modern drum beat and a talking bluesy vocal for the lines

That black bat licorice- this song is hard rock.  If he did the album with these types of songs it would probably go double platinum. It is the rock n' roll kinda rap vocals singing.  The beat is up to date and the rock feel is definitely in there. Is similar in feel to Lazaretto or Seven Nation Army. "I want to cut out my tongue and let you hold onto it for me, because without my skills to amplify it might get boring."

Want and Able- Is so different it is beautiful.  He tells a story about two concepts of Want (desire) and Able (means to do that which is wanted) as characters in debate over who is right. Probably one of my favorites.
I don't think he needs two voices in this song.  The lyrics are so powerful I don't need to hear a harmony.

Entitlement-slow song. Philosophical song. Mentally stimulating over what's wrong with feeling entitled versus what's right with feeling entitled versus people's judgments on one's motivations.

My opinions on the LP-Since this album is good and very different (possibly too challenging to some listeners) I think he should've made it a double lp, so that people could fully understand and get musically what he is presenting.  Basically these song concepts and styles remind me a little of artists like Prince, who do so many different styles that the listener is lost wondering if they're listening to a folk album, a country album, a wanna-be rap rock album, or a rock n' roll album. A double lp solves this.

Overrall I can say I like it......I hesitate before I admit I like it a lot (probably because I wanted to like it and therefore forced myself to like it.) His last two albums have been pretty hard for me to like but I can say his music is different and likeable. It is also very challenging to the listener since he naturally does not seem to want to follow normal or commonly used approaches to music.  I always have to figure out what he is doing and if he is succeeding musically to what he has set forth in the song. The songs are contagious and they are great, they just are unique and unique some times can be hard to get and demanding. Most people ain't gonna be that patient to get the reward that his style is not just noise but is actually a style that can be mimicked and it does work and it is very rhythmic and melodious.
I wish he would sing a song without whining and just sing with his real voice or his falsetto. His vocals can be choppy at times and sometimes I want to hear his vocal range stretched and showcased. Maybe he can't hold a note for longer than two seconds. I think it's more he just doesn't care to. Anyways you won't hear him hold any notes for long and his voice is whiny and choppy. His guitar playing, the drums and mixture of violins makes for a real rock n'roll album with a couple of folk songs. When I first heard it I thought it was an album with majority folk songs and only a couple of rock n'roll songs. That sucked, until I rearranged the order.
profile.summary: his tracklisting was messed up
