profile.description: In the fall of 1979, one of history's most ingenious and courageous flights to freedom took place when two families fled from Communist East Germany to the West in their own handcrafted hot air balloon. Starring John Hurt (HARRY POTTER AND THE SORCERER'S STONE), Jane Alexander (THE CIDER HOUSE RULES), and Beau Bridges, Walt Disney Pictures brings to the screen this remarkable true story of the Strelzyk and Wetzel families and their daring, death-defying escape.|Moved by accounts of two East German families' daring escape to the West in a hot air balloon, Disney executives urged their European editor to pursue film rights to the story. She did, and eventually, the two families flew to California to provide background material for the story -- and to enjoy a free trip to Disneyland, of course!
profile.reviewText:
There are countless excellent dramatic stories about people who tried and either succeeded or failed to cross the Iron Curtain to the West. Unfortunately, few films have been made on this topic. Night Crossing is just such a story, not only because of its intrisic worth, but because it was one of the very first to bring the topic to the screen at a time when it was nearly impossible to do so in the West, such was the Communist infiltration at the time of all branches of the mass media (East Germany began in 1945 and it wasn't until 1982 that a film on the topic was made). I was particularly surprised that Disney produced the movie, considering its penchant for fluff; maybe they decided to get back at the Communists in Chile who at that time declared (I am NOT making this up!) that Mickey Mouse was a Fascist.

What I found particularly well handled in the film was the tediousness involved in the escape process; it took numerous purchases of cloth to make the balloon, numerous sessions of sewing the material together, numerous trials, numerous equipment modifications, yet the tediousness involved in such endeavors does not weigh in on the viewer, though the efforts are mentioned within the film. Two anomalies that I found in the movie: one, the American/British/Canadian measurement of feet and yards and miles in a continent that uses the metric system. The other were the haircuts by the men. If I remember right, such Western haircuts were anathema and Soviet style haircuts were almost mandatory (the same fashion since 1917).
profile.summary: Slipped by the Stasi

profile.description: From the director of CHICAGO and the producer of WICKED comes a modern twist on the beloved fairy tales you thought you knew. Meryl Streep stars in this epic musical saga about daring to venture INTO THE WOODS. Iconic characters, such as Cinderella, Little Red Riding Hood, Jack and the Beanstalk and Rapunzel, find their fates intertwined with a humble baker and his wife, whose longing to have a child sends them on a quest to reverse a witch's (Streep) curse. With an all-star cast, this spellbinding adventure is everything you could ever wish for.
profile.reviewText:
Meryl Streep hamming it up was the only enjoyable aspect of this movie, which takes several of the famous fairy tales (Jack and the beanstalk, Little Red Riding Hood, Cinderella, Rapunzel) and connects them together in a neverending songfest devoid of any actually catchy tunes. The movie feels like it goes on and on and on; the songs definitely do. At one point, the movie becomes tolerable when it appears to have a happy ending, and then things fall apart and you realize that the damn movie is going to go on and on and on some more and what's worse what little sympathy you have for the characters totally vanishes as they become nasty. Don't bother seeing it, much less buying this. Unless you're a masochist.

None of my family enjoyed it at all, though my daughter had asked that we go see it. I felt so cheated I almost asked the theater for my money back.
profile.summary: Going to the dentist was more enjoyable (I'm serious)

profile.description: The New Founding Fathers of America invite you to celebrate the annual Purge - One night a year, all crime is legal! A young couple work to survive on the streets after their car breaks down right as the annual purge commences.
profile.reviewText:
I wrote an earlier review of the first film, The Purge, which was apparently deleted, so this one will probably suffer the same fate at the hands of some Politically Correct fanatic. Oh well, no harm in trying.

This one has no change in the basic premise: once a year, criminal activity is legally unpunishable. Supposedly, this has resulted in a sharp drop in crime. The repeated emphasis of the movie is that---for some unexplained reason---it is poor people who are usually the target of purge activity, especially (of course) blacks. So in this sequel, the anti-rich message is in your face, more so than in the first and we have scenes where rich people (white of course) hire goons to capture victims so that the rich (white of course) can kill them. Liberally (no pun intended) inter spaced are numerous sarcastic remarks about America. Meantime, a black anti-establishment Che wannabe leads a band of blacks killing rich whites. But aside from the obvious leftist politics (not so subliminal as last time) is that the basic premise is stupid; it is particularly the psychopaths who would indulge in the murders during a purge, not normal people (as the scriptwriter would have us believe), so criminal activity would not diminish year around. Anytime that you have a period of anarchy, that is when the psychopaths flourish.

Specifically, the plot follows a vigilante, a bickering couple and a mother and her motormouth daughter; the only one that doesn't come across as congenitally stupid is the vigilante.
profile.summary: Another film with Marxist undertones by the limousine Communists in Hollywood.

profile.description: Topaz [VHS]
profile.reviewText:
As much as I would have liked to have given this film 5 stars because it was the only one to have been critical of the dictatorship I cannot do so in good conscience. Incidentally, the plot of this movie was based on a true story of espionage: a Russian high official defected with his family and fingered a spy ring in the highest level of France.

All right, why did this film lack the usual Hitchcock touch? Unlike Psycho, the score was terrible as was the dialogue. There were spots where the acting was wooden. Karin Dor's acting was at times overdone. Several times when suspense was going to build up simply failed to do so. Having said that, there were several very good spots scattered here and there.
profile.summary: Topaz is not a gem

profile.description: The very day he's about to drive his family to a new life in the city, geologist Kristian Elkjord senses something wrong with the mountain that overlooks his scenic town. No one wants to believe that this could be the big one, especially with tourist season at its peak, but when a landslide from the Mountain sends tons of rock and earth crashing into the sea, everyone has ten minutes to outrace the resulting tsunami to higher ground in this thrilling action spectacular.
profile.reviewText:
A geologist named Kristian (who dresses like a slob) is leaving his old job which consists of monitoring a mountain that has a gigantic cleft in it and might fall into the fjord causing a mega tsunami which could wipe out a tourist town. The day that he is supposed to leave for a job with an oil company something unusual happens which doesn't make sense, so he (and his daughter; the rest of the family will follow) misses the ferry out of town to talk to his colleagues about an idea that popped into his head. Nothing comes of it and he stays to catch the ferry next day. Things escalate rapidly from that point on.

First of all, the acting by the whole cast is excellent. It's nice to see believable, realistic, superb sci-fi film coming out from Norway (another good one is Occupied). Although it is a disaster movie, it doesn't fall into the grotesque exaggeration typical of disaster movies from Hollywood (if the Hollywood suits had done the film, the whole of Norway would have fallen into the sea).
profile.summary: Another good one from Norway

profile.description: Comedy
profile.reviewText:
Jack Lemmon is a confirmed bachelor who has a perfect life and Terry Thomas is his adoring butler, who also sings the benefits of being a bachelor. Lemmon, incidentally, draws a successful cartoon of a fictional secret agent and he does his own stunts to his own plots, which he then draws. He also has a lawyer friend who has been castrated and lobotomized by his wife. One night, he goes to a bachelor party (which is more like a wake), where the groom announces that the girl called off the wedding at which point every man at the party gets happily drunk. In those days, there was a custom of a beautiful girl coming out of a large fake cake.

Next day, Lemmon finds out that he married the girl who is now in his bed (and is gorgeous, and is Italian, and she doesnt speak English). He cant get a divorce because there are no grounds (remember, it was a different time). His butler is disgusted with him and quits. Soon, Lemmon has gained 40 pounds and the apartment is festooned with enough of the feminine touch to make any man vomit.

Then it gets worse.
profile.summary: The Logical End to the Battle of the Sexes

profile.description: December 1949. Joseph Stalin rules Russia through a brutal regime of terror and systematized torture. Inside Mavrino Prison, the first circle of penal hell in Stalin's Russia, the inmates - physicists, mathematicians, electrical engineers, and technical experts - are forced to operate a scientific research center. The term of their sentence is undefined. A discovery useful to the government could mean freedom. A failure could mean a labor camp in Siberia. From a phone booth on a dark Moscow street, a man makes a furtive and hurried phone call to the American Embassy. His call is being recorded by The Ministry of Security, for whom establishing the caller's identity becomes a matter of mounting urgency. At Mavrino, a voice print analysis machine is in late-stage development. The pressure to complete it becomes relentless. As tension, suspicion and the risk of betrayal mount each scientist must struggle to retain his humanity in the face of overwhelming tyranny.
profile.reviewText:
This is an adaptation of Solshenitzin's first major novel to be smuggled out of the Soviet Union. It is about the first circle of the hell that was the Soviet Gulag. It describes the lives of scientists who were arrested by the NKVD for the most trivial of reasons but the regime decided to bring them back from the slave labor camps in order to use their scientific know how to solve technical problems and work on projects. As such, their lives were a definite improvement from the hell of the camps. Specifically, in this story, the scientists are working on a telephone voice scrambler and in a machine that can match the voice prints of a person who has been recorded on different occasions.

Because the novel was so long (typical of Russian novels), certain scenes were not included. Having said that, I have a couple of issues with this adaptation. First, in the book, a person calls an old friend by public telephone in a vain attempt to warn him off from making a mistake that will land him in the Luyanka. He is not captured but his voice is recorded by the secret police. The individual involved disappears from the book altogether but comes back at the very end of the book. In the movie, a disproportionate amount of time is focused on him and his social circle. Second, in the film the motivation for making the call is changed so that he calls the American embassy to inform the Americans of espionage activities in America. The investigation thereby acquires a degree of legitimacy whereas in the book (and in real life) a full fledged investigation would take place for the most trivial of reasons. Second problem that I have with the movie is the sound track, particularly the "music," which consists of occasional a children's choir that comes across as fingernails across a chalkboard. OK, having said that, I nevertheless recommend this made for TV movie.
profile.summary: The First Circle of the Soviet Hell

profile.description: Anatomy of a Disappearance
profile.reviewText: This novel had potential but it's weak. The first part is as bland and boring as any novel by E. M. Forster, or D.H. Lawrence---nothing much happens and there is a lot of introspection over mundane events or items. The second part is when the young man's father is kidnapped by agents of a foreign country while the family is vacationing in Switzerland, and he and his stepmother attempt to find out the details of his disappearance, which goes nowhere and is never resolved. This is where the writer drops the ball and slowly goes back to being bland and boring and nothing much happens thereafter. True, there are some revelations made and some transient sex, but somehow these two become bland.
profile.summary: Nothing much happens then nothing much happens some more

profile.description: Harry Potter Collezione Completa (8 Blu-Ray)
profile.reviewText:
A socially clumsy English mage by the name of Newt arrives in New York carrying a magical suitcase that contains numerous fantastic animal, which includes a kleptomaniac platypus. His aim is to restore some of them back to the wild in Arizona since he obtained them from traffickers. Some of them get loose and he's trying to recapture them, but comes into trouble with the local association of witches/magicians. He teams up with a chap that only wants to establish a bakery and a witch that has been demoted within the agency. Meanwhile, bad (magical) things are happening in New York independent of Newt and his wayward menagerie.

Good acting and good special effects, so why only 3 stars? I just couldn't force myself to care for any of the characters except for the well meaning baker. There was something missing. One scene in particular made me cringe. It's when Newt tries to recapture a rhinoceros-like creature which is in heat. The whole scene was pathetic.

A couple of good points: Jon Voigt makes an appearance (we see to little of him in movies), and, Rowling continues to lambast the lying, hypocritical media, something she started in the Harry Potter movies.
profile.summary: Something was missing in the film

profile.description: Approximately two hours of colorized archival footage from the turbulent early days of Russian Communism help illuminate the Revolution and it's causes and effects..
profile.reviewText:
This is an excellent documentary of the Bolshevik Revolution, with emphasis on the Kronstadt garrison and sailors, a key component of the revolution. I was initially put off by the idea of it being in color, thinking of the crap from Ted Turner, but you immediately forget the coloring as the details come out. The historical facts are presented, including little details usually overlooked.

Whereas previous depictions of the revolution focus on the Bolshevik leadership and ignore Kronstadt altogether, this particular documentary omits some of the parallel (to Kronstadt) events going on with the leadership, such that Stalin, Kamenev, Zinoviev and others are ignored---but this is not to the detriment of the documentary. I just feel that those events with the leadership should have been mentioned, even if cursory. However, this is nitpicking. It's a great documentary and I, for one, am going to purchase it for my collection.
profile.summary: Kronstadt and the Bolsheviks

profile.description: Vintage paperback
profile.reviewText:
This is another of Heinleins work aimed at youngsters and it is good, much better than another one of his, Time for the Stars. The different types of characters give it an extra push.
 The plot involves a group of high school students in the far future, when interplanetary, and intraplanetary travel is as easy as stepping trough doors. They have enrolled in a survival training course and their final exam consists of being dumped in an unknown environment where they must . . . survive. Initially, I thought it a precursor to The Hunger Games, and, Battle Royale. Anyway, they crux of the story is a surprise which I won't relate in order not to spoil it for the potential reader. A good read for teens and above.
profile.summary: Start all over again

profile.description: Vhs tape in good condition
profile.reviewText:
It's a very, very slow movie revolving around a Chinese-American family in San francisco, yet it held a certain charm for me. I think that it would appeal mostly to persons interested in other cultures. It has practically no plot development yet, again, it's vaguely appealing (I know that there were a lot of details that went right over my head). I was particularly amused about the fact that most of the characters, being bilingual, go back and forth between English and Chinese (sometimes in mid sentence)something that is commonplace with many Hispanic families and educated families in Pakistan and India.

The plot as such is a generation gap between the tradition bound mother (who cannot speak English even though she's been in the US for 40 years) and her hen friends and the younger generation. A fortune teller told her she would die at 62 and she is putting even more pressure on her daughter to get married---asap. Her friends are also urging the daughter to get married. In between is victor Wong, the mother's contemporary, who keeps saying that the good in Chinese culture should be retained while the other junk be jettisoned, but the mom simply won't change.
profile.summary: Good film for certain people

profile.description: This is the untold story of how Mussolini seized power through systematic intimidation, violence and murder.
profile.reviewText: This documentary was a disappointment. Whereas we are flooded with documentaries about the Third Reich, almost nothing exists about Mussolini's Italy so I welcomed the film. First of all, the "color" aspect should be reworded as "colorized" which always looks mediocre. But, that's a minor point. Interviews with modern Italian scholars is dealt with clumsily because there is a simultaneous English translation, which is normal, except when it is done elsewhere (and efficiently) the language that is being translated is reduced so that there is no incoherent conflict. Another thing: Mussolini was wildly popular in Italy, including by the working class (and the makers of the film try to spin a Marxist class struggle to the film)---and for good reason. Whether you like it or not, prior to WWII Mussolini accomplished many great things for the country; he improved the lives of Italians (I don't have the space here, but just to name a few: he eradicated the Mafia, he wiped out malaria in Italy) . The Corporate State is completely ignored. As late as 1972, I met Italians who still sang his praises (and they were NOT Fascists!), but who said that his greatest mistake was entering the war. There are also mistakes in the film; e.g., Dr. Mallett claims that the invasion of Ethiopia was done for the purpose of defying the international order. What rubbish! Italy had been humiliated in the previous century by being the only European power to have been defeated by Africans and the Italians ever since had been itching for a rematch. Etc. It should be noted that, unlike the Nazis, the Italian Fascists almost never killed their opponents prior to the civil war. Anyway, I could go on and on, but my point is that one must be historically accurate if one is going to portray history.
profile.summary: Disappointing but better than nothing.

I didn't see the original TV series, so I'm not going to bitch about the movie like so many people have. Rather, I'm going to review it as it standing alone.

Burton, as usual, combines visual imagery with a Gothic story suffused with humor. Barnabas is a resurrected vampire that got screwed over centuries ago by a witch he spurned and he now goes to his family's estate, where his down on their luck descendants dwell. There are countless jokes having to do with his being a stranger in a strange land and his anachronistic attire and speech. The witch, incidentally, is still around and still wants to rekindle the love and, if that fails, do away with him all over again. It's a silly plot, sure, but what the hell, it was still enjoyable.
top_5.summary: I didn't see the original TV series

top_5.description: At 15, Adele doesn't question it: girls go out with boys. Her life is changed forever when she meets Emma, a young woman with blue hair, who will allow her to discover desire, to assert herself as a woman and as an adult. In front of others, Adele grows, seeks herself, loses herself, finds herself.
top_5.reviewText:
This is a film about a teenage lesbian " coming out of the closet." Adele hangs out with her girlfriends, who often talk about sex. Feeling left out she goes out with a boy and has sex, decides it's not for her and dumps him, breaking his heart. She encounters an older girl,Emma, who dyes her hair blue and immediately hit it off. The prolonged lesbian sex scenes are steaming hot. Their relationship comes closer. At some point she is somehow out of her home, we don't see or hear about her parents. They just drop out of sight. Just like her friends. Just like her school. Then she's teaching children. She moves in with Emma. She gets jealous of Emma and a friend Lise (who may be or may not be screwing behind her back) and decides to start screwing a male colleague behind Emma's back. Predictably, Emma finds out and kicks her out. At a later point, they meet again and Adele tries to reconnect, but is unsuccessful (which went contrary to what one would expect from the usual movie plots). Adele ends up alone.

The two actresses are perfect for the roles, one appearing constantly naive and inexperienced, the other one worldly. If they did not personally enjoy the sex scenes they surely gave a good impression.

Incidentally, the movie takes place in France. I was particularly amused at everyone's posing, trying hard to appear to be a genius. How droll.

The movie could have greatly benefitted from drastic editing. It was too long. A ridiculous amount of time was wasted in seeing Adele teach (on and off about 45 minutes).
top_5.summary: Good but way, way too long.

top_5.description: THE IRON LADY is a surprising and intimate portrait of Margaret Thatcher (Two-time Oscar winner Meryl Streep), the first and only female Prime Minister of The United Kingdom. One of the 20th centurys most famous and influential women, Thatcher came from nowhere to smash through barriers of gender and class to be heard in a male-dominated world.
top_5.reviewText: Streep's performance was superb, which rightfully earned her an Academy Award in her portrayal of The Iron Lady in her twilight. The film was a contrast between Thatcher's mental decline in her old age with her iron determination against a phalanx of "good ole boys---no women allowed," Argentinian dictators, Soviet dictators, IRA terrorists and leftist psychopaths. Contrary to so much leftist propaganda and caricature (no to mention historical falsehoods),Thatcher did so much good for Britain and we only get a glimpse of it---and that glimpse is not very detailed and ever so brief. I understand the movie's emphasis and its accurate portrayal, but there was so much more that they could have focused on instead. Maybe some day we will get a full treatment of her career; that will be an awesome movie.
top_5.summary: Good performance but many details were ommitted

profile.reviewText:
This was an adventuresome book, but I will SPOIL/WARN readers that it contains a really gruesome rape experience for the heroine.  It wasn't graphic, but it was gross enough that it easily sank some horrific images of sexual violence into the imagination. The continued story was still so well written, though, that I did decide to give this book five stars. It's a cliffhanger, so I will be buying the sequel because the book is that good.
profile.summary: Great Book and Sequel

profile.description: Rosanne lives in Birmingham, UK and considers it one of her favourite cities, second only to Rome. She delights in writing for children and young adults and hopes to bring readers to an unfamiliar yet alluring setting. Rosanne was inspired to write when she read the Harry Potter books, and at age fourteen, she wrote romance fanfiction on just about every pairing you could dream up from the HP series. She currently lives with her partner and two bunny rabbits and is working on a post-apocalyptic adventure book for middle grade readers.
profile.reviewText: I liked this book and the authors style. Though I'll have to agree with several reviewers that this book is a hybrid of "Hunger Games" and "Gladiator", the story is still very original.  The nature of the dystopia has its own unique take on bloodthirsty public entertainment using innocent victims, and the unique explanation for this blood sport is horrifying.  People's reactions to being thrown into arenas are a hideous thing to imagine, and I'm still not 100% satisfied with the contestants' ability to remain even sane after what they do. But if I could put myself in that dilemma, I suppose I would also either kill others...or myself. As for the characters, I liked the main character, though I thought the love interest and the obligatory "mean girl" were not strong or unique. The most vivid character is the primary villain, a creepy fellow called a "Shepherd" (ironic name for someone who doesn't do much care-taking). He's not a generic all bad character, but does generate a sizable "creep-out" factor.  What makes the plot line unique is that the ending doesn't effectively resolve more than about 10% of this world's horrible issues. I didn't expect a ridiculously happy ending, but it was a disappointment in some ways. All in all, I'd suggest reading the book: I also hope that any possible sequels will reveal some other kind of "closure" (how I hate that word) and give the characters a little more dimension.
profile.summary: After the Fear Comes What?

profile.description: ALL AUTHOR PROCEEDS DONATED TO THE AMY WINEHOUSE FOUNDATION. Amy Winehouse needs no introduction. A critically acclaimed recording artist, Amy touched millions with her music during her short but extraordinary life. Following her tragic death in July 2011, Mitch Winehouse wants to tell her incredible story in full. "Amy, My Daughter" will take the reader through her mischievous early years, her rise to stardom and to her much publicised struggles with addiction. The book will bring the many layers of her life together - the personal, the private and the public - to create a fitting tribute to his much loved daughter. Using exclusive extracts from the diary Mitch kept that details shocking and concerning events in his daughters life alongside never-before-seen photos of Amy, taken from the family album, "Amy, My Daughter" promises to be the definitive book on an iconic figure who, although tragically taken at an early age, has left a musical legacy that will enthral audiences for many years to come. All proceeds from the book will be donated to The Amy Winehouse Foundation, the charity that Mitch has established in Amy's name to help children and young adults facing difficulty and adversity in their lives.
profile.reviewText:
WARNING:  SEE THE DOCUMENTARY FIRST. THEN YOU WON'T NEED THIS SPECIFIC BOOK, OR WANT TO SPEND MONEY ON IT.

REASON:  Amy Winehouse was such a beautiful soul with a magical voice, and a one in a million talent.  I thought I knew how heartbreaking her story was, but to see the movie and watch her go from a bubbly teenager to a tortured, lost soul was almost unbearable.  I can't complain about the book's grammar or the usual ways a book fails.  But it was truly awful to realize that the two most important men in her life, whom she loved desperately but unwisely, were not only repugnantly self serving, but consistently let her down.

It was brutally, horrifyingly clear in the film that her father's disappearance in her early years, and his reappearance after his daughter's fame and fortune grew (some coincidence) were harmful to her in each case!  Her need for a nurturing, perhaps even a bit more stern guidance from a parent, was unmet. Instead, she wound up with some narcissistic, trash of a husband and another self serving leech: her father. It becomes unavoidably clear that daddy's "love" centered around her career, but not her health and well-being. In fact, Mitch Winehouse probably had as much right to be a parent as a snake does: he was the first one to scorn the idea of early substance abuse programs (you know this from the "Rehab" song). Any other intelligent parent would have dragged her straight to rehab and kicked her boyfriend to the curb.

Of course she had a support net of great friends and other family members.  But with young, susceptible celebrities like Amy Winehouse, it's invariably the soul stealers who have the more powerful effect on them. As a similarly unfortunate singer (Janis Joplin) voiced it best in one of her songs, very ironically, "...Take another little piece of my heart now...."

I can't imagine this lousy excuse of a dad as a legitimate author, so I'm guessing someone "helped" him pen this unfortunate biography anyhow.  I'm going to actually return this book, on principle.  For anyone who really wants to know about this gifted singer's tragically short life, just watch the movie, because what it reveals is the heart wrenching story of the death of innocence. And you'll never get the truth from her father.

I hope her soul is at peace, but I'd hate for the people who brought her down to benefit posthumously in any way! Unfortunately, I bought the book before seeing the film, and now regret that. Even the thought of one cent coming his way via this book is repugnant. But what I really hope for is that Amy Winehouse is at peace, and that the beautiful, engaging young woman who gave so many people joy in her beautiful music, is the one that people continue to remember most of all.
profile.summary: Another Gold Digging Effort by Deadbeat Dad.

profile.description: At last! A budget version of crimp bead covers, to cover your unsightly crimp beads. Gently squeeze shut around the crimped bead using your crimping pliers. This 4mm size will cover 3x2 crimps or smaller (after the beads have been crimped). May be used to cover tornado crimps. Will resemble a 4mm silver color seamed bead when closed. May also be used:. (1) to cover knots! (2) to fill in a gap! Ever made a necklace or bracelet and found an empty space on the strand because the beads settled? Pop one of these on either end of your piece to fill in the gap. Neat. Quantity: 144 (1 Gross)
profile.reviewText:
I like using these more than all the other crimp covers on the market. They can be found in other sizes and antique type colors also. As one reviewer said, they're very tricky to use the first few times. (For me, that was at least twenty times). In time, you develop your own little techniques for using these covers. Finally, they begin to look like just another small added bead.
I strongly suggest getting advice on these by looking at Youtube tutorials first (I'm guessing the manufacturer has at least one).

Then, if you can be patient, you should put in some practice time, so they're easy to use in a real project.  Just cut a few 2-3 inch pieces of thread or soft wire, (keep your leftovers from other projects), get a small pile of crimp beads, and get familiar with using this product.  You can open them a little with your favorite pliers. A good way to set them up is to place them loosely inside the crimping pliers, and set them over the crimp beads. But for some strange reason, they magnetically stick to some tools, so you may have to struggle a bit to place them on the wire manually.
profile.summary: Worth the Effort: A Great Looking Crimp Cover.

profile.description: This item if for 200pcs of these gold plated Filigree hollow ball spacer metal beads, size are approx. 4mm in dia. Hollow and light weight metal beads.
profile.reviewText:
The picture doesn't do these beads any justice!

This is the best spacer bead I have ever discovered. They come in different sizes, and in a delicate silver or gold (not too glitzy).
In the photo it looks like an ugly meteor chunk. But in reality, they're simple beautiful. They have that thin wire, "knit" look.

Instead of a clunky, pock marked bead shown in the photo, they look like expensive filigree work! At first glance I was a bit put off, but as soon as I placed them into a sedate black and gold necklace design, the entire necklace came to life. The compliments on the finished product, and on these "filigree" beads, were very encouraging. I'll definitely be using them frequently, and I plan to add more of these silver and gold filigree ball-spacers to my next bead order.
profile.summary: The Look of Delicate Filigree! Photo doesn't Do Justice To This Product.

profile.description: Bead 'N Stretch is great for beading and making jewelry. It is the strongest and stretchest cord on the market. Just because this cord is so stretchy dont think it will lose it's shape, because it doesn't.
profile.reviewText:
I like this stretch cord, and it's one of two 0.7 mm products I've used.  So far, nothing I've made has broken, and it's a nice middle of the road size between the ultra thin 0.5 mm and the much thicker 0.8 mm or the 1mm.  So this size is my favorite, and since I make a lot of stretch bracelets for other people, I need a product that I trust.

Tying the 0.7 & 0 8mm is not fun, (I generally find that 3 or 4 knots are most reliable).  So if you want enough knots to make something really break-proof, then the final knot has to be hidden inside of beads with slightly bigger openings, or secured under crimp covers. Otherwise, the end product looks pretty tacky.  In general, though, this is my favorite overall elastic beading cord.
profile.summary: The Best of the Bunch

A flexible, cork-wrapped outsole, easy adjustability and the SoftWalk footbed form the ideal trifecta for comfort in this casual slide. The eggcrate footbed is layered with 10m of polyurethane foam and 2mm of EVA underfoot for lasting comfort. Metallic detail adds spark to the soft leather upper, which also features an adjustable buckle on the instep strap for a customized fit.
profile.reviewText:
I love this sandal !!  I have never before purchased a shoe outside of a store because of "problem feet", but I knew this would be worth the risk of an Amazon order because the first pair I bought was a 100% comfortable fit.  I first discovered this particular style (in an orange color) several years ago at a chic store, and paid double the price for them.  But they were worth the money because they're so incredibly comfortable.

Softwalk shoes are known to be among the best on the market, and many of their products work perfectly for those of us who need to wear "comfort shoes", but want a classy look.  That first pair of sandals are one of only two brands of shoes which I've had no problems with.  After 3 years, I've worn my first pair out completely, and I'm still using them. The quilted cushion is heavenly, and there's some level of support. Even though it's a simple slip-on sandal, they do look dressier than other sandals. This particular one can be adjusted a bit also.

Other women always compliment this style, and I couldn't be happier with this purchase.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "A Mystery Novel. A very nice collector's edition, clean and unmarked. Number k1547. Original price 40 cents.". The summary of the review text is "Early John D. MacDonald Shows His Range".
output:
I've only read the Travis McGee books by John D. MacDonald, so I was pleased to see that Random House has reissued many of MacDonald's standalone novels in handsome trade paperback editions.  All These Condemned is an unusual book utilizing multiple narrators in Rashomon fashion to tell the tale of a weekend that ended badly for cosmetics mogul Wilma Ferris.

Despite being written in the mid-1950's and commenting on topics of the day (abstract expressionism, the new medium of television, the hollowness of public relations and advertising, changing sexual mores), All These Condemned holds up very well.  I especially enjoyed how MacDonald is able to create unique narrative voices and to create a fully rounded character with a unique backstory in just a few paragraphs.  What a great storyteller who left us too soon.  Looking forward to the riches that await in his other novels.

profile.description: A passionate account of the tortured life and tragic death of the greatest artist of the nineteenth century by renowned critic and painter Julian Bell Van Gogh is a vivid portrait of the great Impressionist painter that traces his life from the Netherlands where he was born into a family of art dealers through his years in England the Hague and Paris to his final home in Arles where he discovered the luminous style of his late paintings before his suicide at the age of thirty-seven Van Gogh struggled to find his way as an artist Well into his mid-twenties he had achieved virtually nothing except a few charcoal drawings of coal miners Afflicted by mental illness and a mercurial temper he was institutionalized several times toward the end of his life Julian Bell conveys this tragic story with great compassion depicting van Gogh in all his anguished vigor a genius for whom the greatest challenge was to stay alive until he had completed his most fully realized and magnificent works
profile.reviewText:
Not yet ready to tackle the massive biography of Van Gogh of a few years back, I decided to read Julian Bell's brief life of the painter.  A Power Seething was neither a quick nor an easy read, yet I found it rewarding.  Bell assumes a familiarity with art history on the part of the reader, and, although I had some art history courses in college, I found myself googling various artists and paintings referenced in the book in order to get a sense of who was either influencing Van Gogh or what he was rebelling against.

Bell focuses on Van Gogh the painter and his works, trying to downplay the life that became the stuff of melodrama (see, "Lust For Life"). Sometimes Bell lost me as he tried to articulate Van Gogh's mindset and aims.  He quotes large sections of Van Gogh's letters to his brother Theo, which made me want to read more of these missives.

I can't say I'd recommend this biography to the general reader, but for those who want a deeper analysis of Van Gogh's life and work, this could be your cup of tea.
profile.summary: A Brief (and difficult) Biography of Van Gogh

profile.description: Nice vintage set, have books 6,7,8, and 31 available
profile.reviewText:
I read some of the Little House books years ago as a 4th grader and had forgotten about them, especially since the television series distorted the books and in a sad way replaced the books in the mind of the general public.  I was pleased to find this was a quick read, full of documentation of the daily life of a family living apart from civilization.  Food becomes a major preoccupation; growing food, hunting food, and preparing food is described in detail and was fascinating to me as an adult (I don't know how I would have responded as a child reader, probably less favorably).
The Ingalls family's existence seems idyllic in many ways with the only storm cloud on the horizon seeming to be Laura's growing jealously of her older sister Mary.  I'm looking forward to reading the second book in the series.
Highly recommended for all ages.
profile.summary: Not What I Had Expected

profile.description: Thirteen Reasons Why Jay Asher
profile.reviewText: I truly wanted Thirteen Reasons Why to be a good book.  Teen suicide is an all-too real and important topic and I would have loved to have this novel available in my classroom for any student who wished to read it.  Unfortunately, this book fails stylistically (it's just not particularly interesting and drags on at tedious length) and in its characterizations and understanding of human behavior.  Clay, the male classmate listening to Hannah's tapes, seems too flawless as a person and exists only to provide reactions to Hannah's recounting of her life.  Hannah never became real to me and her actions and decisions are baffling.  Other better YA novels on this topic are out there and should receive wider readership than this failed experiment.
profile.summary: Important Subject  Poorly Handled

profile.description: A collection of short stories featuring the 'heart specialist', Parker Pyne. Mrs Packington felt alone, helpless and utterly forlorn. But her life changed when she stumbled upon an advertisement in The Times which read: 'ARE YOU HAPPY? IF NOT, CONSULT MR PARKER PYNE'. Equally adept at putting together the pieces of a marriage or the fragments of a murder mystery, Mr Parker Pyne was possibly the world's most unconventional private eye -- and certainly its most charming.
profile.reviewText:
Parker Pyne Investigates collects all of Agatha Christie's Mr. Parker Pyne stories and while the tales vary in quality, they all provide entertainment.  As others have noted, the early Parker Pyne stories have a Fantasy Island vibe as Parker Pyne makes the dreams of people come true (for a price).  The stories shift into more conventional detective mode as Parker Pyne travels around the world and solves crimes for people along the way by dint of his insights into human nature.  These stories are best read over time rather than devoured all at once as there is a certain sameness to some of the tales, and spacing them out makes them more enjoyable.  I enjoyed the Parker Pyne short stories more than the Jane Marple short stories I've read.
Recommended.
profile.summary: Time Well Spent With Mr. Parker Pyne

profile.description: Paperback. Pub Date :2009-06-25 Pages: 368 Language: English Publisher: HarperCollins UK Everyone knew about the kind of films they showed at the Calliope Club - once the Residents Association and the local Womens Group had given them some free publicity. But when Peter Pascoes dentist suggests that one film in particular is more than just good clean dirty fun. the inspector begins to make a few discreet inquiries. Before they bear fruit. though. the dentist has been accused of having sex with an underage patient. the cinema has been wrecked and its elderly owner murdered.Superintendent Dalziel expects no more from professional men who watch blue films.
profile.reviewText:
A Pinch of Snuff is the fifth Dalziel and Pascoe crime novel by Reginald Hill and after a series of uneven outings as Hill began to realize the possibilities of the duo, the series begins to gel and feel like a familiar friend.  The subject matter in A Pinch of Snuff is disturbing (I remember when public speculation as to whether snuff films existed began to buzz) and Detective Peter Pascoe is rightly disturbed by some of the happenings in the book.  In the last outing Pascoe took a back seat to a broad farce featuring Andy Dalziel; this time we stick with Peter Pascoe throughout the case and his inner thoughts and observations are most amusing.  This book also shows the less than smooth marital relations between Pascoe and his wife Ellie, but also shows the love that binds them.
The plot becomes unraveled near the end and the resolutions are a bit sloppy, but overall the book is most entertaining and I look forward to reading the next book in the series.
profile.summary: Series Begins to Hit Its Stride

profile.description: Peter Bagge createdHate, one of the best-selling and most formative comic book series of the 90s. Born in New York in 1957, after graduating from the School of Visual Arts, Bagge contributed to and, along with R. Crumb, edited the underground anthology Weirdo. Since then Bagge's numerous original graphic novels and collections of comics have won him two Harvey Awards (one for Best Cartoonist in 1991), an Inkpot Award, and garnered six Eisner Award nominations. His social commentary cartoons run in the magazine Reason, and his recent biography of Planned Parenthood founder Margaret Sanger is critically acclaimed. He lives in Seattle, Washington.
profile.reviewText:
I am a big Peter Bagge fan from back in the day and have followed him since his contributions to Weirdo and his own comics Neat Stuff and Hate.  I did not read the original appearances of these short pieces in Reason magazine, so I was glad to have them collected all in one place.  I generally enjoyed reading these thought pieces and exercises in journalism.  The least effective were rants that Bagge labelled as such, but so much of the thinking was conventional or reactionary and not particularly interesting.

Bagge seemed to come alive and show his brilliance in the pieces where he acted as a reporter either at a political convention or on the campaign trail; Bagge's gift for caricature and sardonic mockery flourishes in these pages and I found myself laughing and re-thinking beliefs as Bagge was illustrating his ideas rather than mouthing cranky old man tropes.

This book is best read in small doses and the one-pagers are often more successful than the four-page features.  Not a major work in Bagge's output but definitely worth reading.
profile.summary: Bagge Speaks His Mind

top_5.description: A passionate account of the tortured life and tragic death of the greatest artist of the nineteenth century by renowned critic and painter Julian Bell Van Gogh is a vivid portrait of the great Impressionist painter that traces his life from the Netherlands where he was born into a family of art dealers through his years in England the Hague and Paris to his final home in Arles where he discovered the luminous style of his late paintings before his suicide at the age of thirty-seven Van Gogh struggled to find his way as an artist Well into his mid-twenties he had achieved virtually nothing except a few charcoal drawings of coal miners Afflicted by mental illness and a mercurial temper he was institutionalized several times toward the end of his life Julian Bell conveys this tragic story with great compassion depicting van Gogh in all his anguished vigor a genius for whom the greatest challenge was to stay alive until he had completed his most fully realized and magnificent works
top_5.reviewText:
Not yet ready to tackle the massive biography of Van Gogh of a few years back, I decided to read Julian Bell's brief life of the painter.  A Power Seething was neither a quick nor an easy read, yet I found it rewarding.  Bell assumes a familiarity with art history on the part of the reader, and, although I had some art history courses in college, I found myself googling various artists and paintings referenced in the book in order to get a sense of who was either influencing Van Gogh or what he was rebelling against.

Bell focuses on Van Gogh the painter and his works, trying to downplay the life that became the stuff of melodrama (see, "Lust For Life"). Sometimes Bell lost me as he tried to articulate Van Gogh's mindset and aims.  He quotes large sections of Van Gogh's letters to his brother Theo, which made me want to read more of these missives.

I can't say I'd recommend this biography to the general reader, but for those who want a deeper analysis of Van Gogh's life and work, this could be your cup of tea.
top_5.summary: A Brief (and difficult) Biography of Van Gogh

top_5.description: Nice vintage set, have books 6,7,8, and 31 available
top_5.reviewText:
I read some of the Little House books years ago as a 4th grader and had forgotten about them, especially since the television series distorted the books and in a sad way replaced the books in the mind of the general public.  I was pleased to find this was a quick read, full of documentation of the daily life of a family living apart from civilization.  Food becomes a major preoccupation; growing food, hunting food, and preparing food is described in detail and was fascinating to me as an adult (I don't know how I would have responded as a child reader, probably less favorably).
The Ingalls family's existence seems idyllic in many ways with the only storm cloud on the horizon seeming to be Laura's growing jealously of her older sister Mary.  I'm looking forward to reading the second book in the series.
Highly recommended for all ages.
top_5.summary: Not What I Had Expected

top_5.description: Thirteen Reasons Why Jay Asher
top_5.reviewText: I truly wanted Thirteen Reasons Why to be a good book.  Teen suicide is an all-too real and important topic and I would have loved to have this novel available in my classroom for any student who wished to read it.  Unfortunately, this book fails stylistically (it's just not particularly interesting and drags on at tedious length) and in its characterizations and understanding of human behavior.  Clay, the male classmate listening to Hannah's tapes, seems too flawless as a person and exists only to provide reactions to Hannah's recounting of her life.  Hannah never became real to me and her actions and decisions are baffling.  Other better YA novels on this topic are out there and should receive wider readership than this failed experiment.
top_5.summary: Important Subject  Poorly Handled

top_5.description: A collection of short stories featuring the 'heart specialist', Parker Pyne. Mrs Packington felt alone, helpless and utterly forlorn. But her life changed when she stumbled upon an advertisement in The Times which read: 'ARE YOU HAPPY? IF NOT, CONSULT MR PARKER PYNE'. Equally adept at putting together the pieces of a marriage or the fragments of a murder mystery, Mr Parker Pyne was possibly the world's most unconventional private eye -- and certainly its most charming.
top_5.reviewText:
Parker Pyne Investigates collects all of Agatha Christie's Mr. Parker Pyne stories and while the tales vary in quality, they all provide entertainment.  As others have noted, the early Parker Pyne stories have a Fantasy Island vibe as Parker Pyne makes the dreams of people come true (for a price).  The stories shift into more conventional detective mode as Parker Pyne travels around the world and solves crimes for people along the way by dint of his insights into human nature.  These stories are best read over time rather than devoured all at once as there is a certain sameness to some of the tales, and spacing them out makes them more enjoyable.  I enjoyed the Parker Pyne short stories more than the Jane Marple short stories I've read.
Recommended.
top_5.summary: Time Well Spent With Mr. Parker Pyne

top_5.description: Paperback. Pub Date :2009-06-25 Pages: 368 Language: English Publisher: HarperCollins UK Everyone knew about the kind of films they showed at the Calliope Club - once the Residents Association and the local Womens Group had given them some free publicity. But when Peter Pascoes dentist suggests that one film in particular is more than just good clean dirty fun. the inspector begins to make a few discreet inquiries. Before they bear fruit. though. the dentist has been accused of having sex with an underage patient. the cinema has been wrecked and its elderly owner murdered.Superintendent Dalziel expects no more from professional men who watch blue films.
top_5.reviewText:
A Pinch of Snuff is the fifth Dalziel and Pascoe crime novel by Reginald Hill and after a series of uneven outings as Hill began to realize the possibilities of the duo, the series begins to gel and feel like a familiar friend.  The subject matter in A Pinch of Snuff is disturbing (I remember when public speculation as to whether snuff films existed began to buzz) and Detective Peter Pascoe is rightly disturbed by some of the happenings in the book.  In the last outing Pascoe took a back seat to a broad farce featuring Andy Dalziel; this time we stick with Peter Pascoe throughout the case and his inner thoughts and observations are most amusing.  This book also shows the less than smooth marital relations between Pascoe and his wife Ellie, but also shows the love that binds them.
The plot becomes unraveled near the end and the resolutions are a bit sloppy, but overall the book is most entertaining and I look forward to reading the next book in the series.
top_5.summary: Series Begins to Hit Its Stride

profile.description: Purosol Plasma was originally developed for NASA and the US military for use on high-end electronic displays. Combining the power of organic plant extracts and state-of-the-art green chemistry, it is the worlds most advanced cleaning solution. Purosol Plasma was originally developed for NASA and the US military for use on high-end electronic displays. Combining the power of organic plant extracts and state-of-the-art green chemistry, it is the worlds most advanced cleaning solution.
profile.reviewText:
We have a lot of electronics in our house and the screens are always filthy because we just don't know what to clean them with other than a soft lens cloth, which just doesn't clean off dirt and greasy fingerprints.  This Purosol product is all natural and solvent-free.  It's used on medical and NASA equipment so I was confident it would not ruin my electronics.

The instructions on the bottle says to pray lightly on surface or clean micro-fiber cloth and gently apply to surface in a circular motion.  Wipe dry.

I tried it both ways.  First I sprayed the cloth and wiped my Apple Macbook screen.  It works okay that way on a small surface such as a laptop, iphone or camera screen.  I found that when I tried it on my LCD tvs, it didn't clean as well because the cleaner absorbs into the cloth and it dries very, very fast.  On larger surfaces, it definitely works better to spray the screen and work at it in sections.  The product is unscented as far as I can tell.

The cleaner easily removed my kids' greasy fingerprints on the LCD tv.  It's pricey but worth the price to protect your electronic investments.
profile.summary: Pricey but works very well!

profile.description: Your iPhone 4 has become a big part of your life. With FaceTime video, retina display, multitasking, HD video recording and more - you have got a lot to lose. profile.reviewText: I have the iPhone 4s and read that this case worked great for it despite it being marketed as the iPhone 4 case.  I just wanted to leave my experience for use with the 4s.  It protects and fits great.  I only have 2 small issues. One is that you have to lift the flap to access the earphone port.  My second issue is that I've also found that the touch screen is not as sensitive to touch.  Before I put my Otterbox on, I had a Zagg Invisishield on my screen.  With that on the screen, the Otterbox touch screen worked great and registered every little keystroke.  But it would press onto the inside of the Otter screen and cause a splotchy mark that limited my visual.  I had to remove my Zagg screen shield to get rid of the weird sheen and then I noticed the touch pad wasn't working so great.  I hope this helps anyone deciding on the Defender case.  Overall, I'm pretty happy with it as I tend to drop my phone more often than I'd like to admit and this will protect it against breakage.

The Resurgence case is well protective, sleek and extends my battery life. I do wish that it had the plastic screen shield that my Defender does but that is only thing I'd improve on. Excellent choice to protect your iPhone and extend its use away from an electrical outlet. Recommend!

This case itself is not as padded as I would have liked for a travel case.  However, when used with the leather book cover, I feel that it will be sufficient for my needs.  I do like the side entry for the case.  It makes it easy and convenient to slip the Kindle out of the case.

This is an excellent alternative to the $50+ aftermarket Kindle cases available.
profile.summary: Travel Case for the Amazon Kindle (e-reader)

profile.description: The Power line 1200 + Extra Outlet extends your wired network at 1.2Gbps speeds with Home plug AV2 MIMO. Extra outlet provides convenience and you can add up to 16 adapters to expand your network. Pick-a-plug LED provides the highest possible performance and it sets up in minutes, no need to install software.
profile.reviewText: For years, I have wanted to call the cable company and have another cable outlet installed into my "formal" living room aka "a waste of space". This little gadget has enabled me to stream movies into a room where we do not have a cable outlet but a huge and comfy couch that never gets used. Happy mom here as the kids no longer fight over the tv downstairs anymore!!! Set up was easy, everything is all included in one little package. We couldn't be more pleased and I'm happy I didn't have to sit on the phone with the cable company as they tried to up sell more cable we do not need or bill me for installation of another outlet.
profile.summary: This saved me from having to call cable company

profile.description: Let cooking shine, with the stylish, sturdy Farberware New Traditions Stainless Steel 12-Piece Cookware Set. New Traditions pairs the time-tested trust and reliability of Farberware with durable stainless steel construction and convenience that's ideal for busy homes and families. The cookware features traditional bell-shaped profiles with mirror-polished stainless steel exteriors that deliver a radiant touch of kitchen style; the skillets feature solid aluminum craftsmanship to ensure that these stovetop workhorses heat fast and even, with polished exteriors that coordinate with the rest of the set. Shatter-resistant glass lids provide a handy window on all the delicious cooking while sealing heat and moisture in and the Dutch oven's lid conveniently fits the saut as well. Hand washing the skillets is recommended to preserve the nonstick and the rest of the pots and pans are dishwasher safe for effortless cleanup. This cookware set includes all the essentials for making memorable meals, including three handy Prestige nylon kitchen tools-a slotted turner, slotted spoon and solid spoon-to get tasty dishes started right away. Oven safe to 350 Degree, the cookware set's handles feature classic Farberware styling and most include hanging rings for convenient storage. Shine in the kitchen, so the easy, delicious cooking can shine at every family meal with the sturdy Farberware New Traditions Stainless Steel 12-Piece Cookware Set.
profile.reviewText: This Farberware stainless steel cookware set is an excellent starter or supplemental set for most families. The bell shaped design is very attractive and gives it more of an upscale look, in my opinion. The aluminum allows it to be lighter weight but not so much that it feels flimsy or cheap. The handles feel good in my hand and stay cool to the touch on the stovetop. I love my Le Crueset dutch ovens and casserole dishes and but I have been in need of some new skillets and saucepans. The non stick skillets made for easy clean up but you do not want to clean these in the dishwasher to maintain the non stick finish. The bonus utensil set isn't all that great. I could do without those and opt for an extra small pan or lid but from a marketing standpoint, it adds numbers to the "12 piece set" on the package so that is probably why it's included into the set.
profile.summary: Attractive starter or supplemental set

profile.description: Make mealtime more exciting and nutritious with the Hamilton Beach Digital Steamer. Place the transparent bowls of your choice of vegetables, seafood, or chicken atop the base and set the cooking timer. When done, the steamer beeps and switches to warm.
profile.reviewText:
Cooking healthy has never been so easy. I like using this to steam fish, chicken, shellfish and veggies. It is easy to use and I can have dinner on the table in 30 min or less. Prep work is eliminated and I don't have to babysit the food. I set it and let it do its thing. Cleaning it does take a little more time than a crockpot but using it takes no pre planning. I can throw frozen items in there without having to thaw them out ahead of time. I really like the separate compartments and my kids appreciate that, too, as one of them strongly dislikes anything from the sea (unless it come in a can: tuna lol)
This is a great appliance to have to easy and healthy cooking.
profile.summary: Fast tool to cook healthy.

profile.description: The TRD040615T has a heating power of1500W, 3 power settings, safety thermostat, timer, cord storage and handles for easy transportation. Additionally, it features a new enlarged battery design: The 25% larger (compared to the current DRAGON3) radiant surface ensures a faster air flow emission and increased chimney effect which means better comfort.The reset button must be pushed on the plug.Please Note this product doesnt comes with a remote
profile.reviewText: I'm using this DeLonghi space heater to heat my problematic and drafty family room with hardwood flooring and vaulted ceilings.  I have a gas fireplace with a fan in this room as well as central heat but the heat produced from it is lost in the space that is my vaulted ceilings and the furnace is constantly running due to this and heats up the entire house unnecessarily.  I placed the DeLonghi onto the tile in front of my fireplace, where my kids already know that this area is a "no play" zone, as my fireplace gets very hot as well. The DeLonghi is hot to the touch.  I would not recommend this heater around toddlers as I feel it could cause a burn to the touch.  As far as the heating, it has done a very effective job of heating my drafty family room and maintaining warmth, leaving us toasty and comfortable as we watch tv or hang out. It also heats the adjacent room (kitchen) with a total area of space equaling to about 700 square feet. For a unit with such a small footprint, it does an excellent job of heating such a large area quietly and cost efficiently.
profile.summary: Reliable and constant heat for my drafty vaulted ceiling room

profile.description: The Kenwood MultiPro food processor system combines a full sized food processor and blender in one efficient food processing center. Combine all your food preparation needs to make healthy family meals more efficiently with fresh ingredients, created the way you want every time. With its innovative and patented dual drive system, the MultiPro with speed control delivers precise speed for various tasks - high speed for chopping, grating and blending; slow speed for slicing & dough making.
profile.reviewText: As a person who dislikes clutter in a very bad way, I love the small footprint of this Kenwood Compact Processor and blender. I keep the appliances that I do not use very often stored in the cabinet. Due to this units' compact size, attractive and sleek body, I opt to let this reside on the counter. I often make protein shakes when I come home from the gym and having this out on the counter enables me to start on that as soon as I walk in the door. The motor is not as loud and obnoxious as my old blender and mixes the ingredients to perfection. The reservoir itself is also smaller in size and does not hold as much liquid but for a couple shakes, it's perfect for me.  I do not use a food processor as often so that reservoir stays stored in the cabinet until needed. It chops my veggies to my desired consistency and saves me a ton of trouble when preparing meals. I found clean up pretty easy. There are just a few pieces to clean and reassembling them is a breeze. This unit has 2 speeds. I tend to use the high speed the most for the blender and the low for chopping.  Grating my own blocks of cheese saves me a ton of money on the prestressed variety and it tastes better freshly grated. The feet have suction cups and keep this powerful little gadget from bouncing around.
profile.summary: Small footprint, large performance

profile.description: Give veggies and more the steam treatment with the handy Rachael Ray Hard Enamel Nonstick 3-Quart Covered Steamer Set. This convenient set offers a fast and easy way to steam just about anything, and the handy saucepot is great by itself for making sauces, warming leftovers and more. With a convenient stainless steel steamer insert and sturdy glass lid, this set takes the work out of making delicious vegetables in a healthy way. The pan features solid construction that promotes even heating, helping to reduce hot spots that can burn foods, and has a durable, colorful porcelain enamel exterior. Long-lasting nonstick provides superior food release, making cleanup a snap, and the colorful grippy handles offer a comfortable grasp and are dual riveted for extra strength. Oven safe to 350DegreeF, this set is also dishwasher safe and works well with many other items in the Rachael Ray collections. Steam delicious broccoli, cauliflower and carrots and more with this easy-to-use Rachael Ray Hard Enamel Nonstick 3-Quart Covered Steamer Set.
profile.reviewText:
I've added pics for those interested in seeing the actual color and for size reference to a can of soda.

I am loving this steamer! I have never owned one before and I'm so glad I didn't settle for a cheaper version because even at first glance when you pull it out of the box, you can see and feel that it is top notch quality. It steams my vegetables so evenly and perfectly, I feel like it's made from a restaurant. What I really also found handy is that because it is heat resistant, I can drain the grease from things like ground beef without worrying that I'm going to burn my plastic strainers. The size is smaller but for side dishes, sauces and for just using the strainer, it is perfect. And its size makes for easier cleanup. The color is beautiful and I'm not much of a color-red person but in my kitchen, it compliments and brightens in such a tasteful and fun way. Love!!!
profile.summary: Handy and quality steamer that doubles as a strainer See PICS

profile.description: The Rachael ray Cucina nonstick Bake ware 4-piece set is the perfect bakeware team for delish oven-made foods, from roasted veggies for Rach's double-stuffed butternut squash to a quick 'n' easy batch of morning muffins. This nonstick bakeware is constructed from durable carbon steel that delivers great results, whether used everyday or once in while. profile.reviewText: This pan set is very attractive and unique with its brown color scheme. The mint silicone grips add a nice touch and also provide a little security when reaching for them with a bulky oven mitt on. The nonstick surface performs to perfection and cleans up effortlessly. These pans have a hefty feel to them and weigh more than the other cookie sheets and cake pans I have in my kitchen. I do wish that the muffin pan were a 12 muffin capacity instead of 6. But other than that, I have no complaints.  I was well aware that the muffin pan was a 6 count when I selected it so I can't knock a star off for that. I'm very pleased.
profile.summary: Excellent nonstick surface and solid weight.

profile.description: Imagine if you could shrink down a set of studio speakers so that they fit into your ears. This is exactly what we have done with the Aurvana In-Ear3 Plus. Styled in dark-chrome, it delivers precise audio performance with its Balanced Armature Tweeter and Woofer speakers and optimized sound tube design. The headset's ergonomic one-button in-line microphone with volume adjustment and tangle-free fabric cable let you answer voice calls or control music playback easily on your smartphone or tablet.
profile.reviewText:
These headphones sound good but I wasn't blown away by their performance for music like I thought I would be especially when you consider the retail price. I do like how well I can hear and be heard when using them for phone calls, which I tend to do a great deal of in the car with road noise.

Pros
 good bass range
 great high range
 built well with braided chord
 good noise canceling
 improves quality of phone calls

Cons
 have to push pretty deep into ear to get quality sound
 have to wear around top of ear which can cause soreness
 slip out of ear when active head movement which results in loss of bass and noise cancellation

Overall I find these earphones good for phone usage and the casual gym person that doesn't engage in a lot of head movement like cardio kickboxing or running/jogging.
profile.summary: Neither love them nor hate them. 3 stars.

profile.reviewText: I don't really like this keyboard cover. I have very small hands and I still find it very awkward and uncomfortable to use because of its small iPad mini size.  The keyboard snaps onto the iPad mini as a cover and it protects the screen but I view this keyboard more as a "cool gadget or novelty item" than a functional keyboard. The positioning of the iPad screen is also so close to the keys that I am constantly knocking into it with my hands and I am a very proficient typist. (65-70 wpm) I would not recommend this to someone looking for a portable and wireless keyboard.  I prefer my Anker wireless keyboard to this one even though it is a separate unit and doesn't actually fit onto the iPad in the same way.

profile.description: Color:NIGHT LITE (BLACK/LIME) With LifeProof FR for iPhone 8 Plus, youre free to venture off the beaten path and come back with proof of your triumphs. WaterProof, DirtProof, SnowProof and DropProof, FR braves the elements while blocking them from soaking circuits or clogging ports. Whats more, the integrated screen cover keeps your display pristine, and the custom design leaves every feature and function accessible.
profile.reviewText: When it comes to cases, there is no one case fits all. I like the Lifeproof due to its excellent protection against water damage and dust. I also like that the Lifeproof FRE  completely encases my phone in a waterproof shell. I have not tested (or accidentally dropped my phone while in this case and won't purposely do that!) but it seems like it has good protection. I like that I am able to disinfect my phone daily without worry about water getting into the case and damaging my phone. I haven't had any leaking issues at all and it is cleaned daily.
profile.summary: Excellent waterproof case that does not leak

profile.description: Roaming around town and getting out on the weekends for some fresh air have never been so fun and carefree. The Laurito is designed with a step through frame so you can get on and off the bike easily without having to swing a leg over. It is built from heat treated 6061-T6 aluminum for hassle free durability, and even has eyelets so you can mount it up with a rack and fenders if you want. The 27.5" wheels roll smoothly and the Trail XC suspension fork soaks up the bumps so you can just cruise along in blissful comfort.
profile.reviewText:
I recently purchased my first bike as an adult and I'm very happy with my selection.  I wanted an affordable, entry level bike that would not break the bank. I chose the Diamondback Laurito womens hardtail mountain bike because there are many dirt and gravel trails in my area as well as paved bike paths. I can ride in comfort for hours and feel secure knowing my tires can handle debris and cracks in my path.
What I like about this bike are

I'll add some newborn bike pics to show some of the details of this model.

5'4" tall
30" inseam

I really love this top. I have 4 of them! It is very flattering, modest (doesn't show cleavage) and I wear it with skirts, jeans and shorts. It is also good for the gym. 125 lbs
Size 4
34 DD

profile.description: This jacket's got it all: it's waterproof, breathable, warm and has plenty of pockets.
profile.reviewText: The fit is perfect. I ordered a small and it fits me just as a small would and gives me room to wear a long sleeve shirt layered underneath. I have worn this outside in the rain and it has kept me nice and dry. The built in hand warmers kept my hands warm and still allowed me to use my fingers to access my phone. The pink accents are just too cute and keep this rain jacket looking stylish when so few jackets for this purpose are. I am very happy with this Carhartt. My other Carhatt is a goose down insulated coat that is also weatherproof down but is just a tad more bulky. If you're looking for something with wet weather proofing protection, this Elmire is a great option.
profile.summary: Stylish, non bulky, wet weatherproof jacket

profile.description: If you prefer maximum coffee freshness, the Breville single-cup brewer serves up java perfection every time. This new upgraded model includes quiet pump technology that brews even quieter than previous models and an iced beverage function that dispenses a concentrated 3-1/2-ounce shot of tea or coffee. Simply dilute with ice and water for iced tea or coffee. Patented showerhead delivers precise amount of water for even coffee extraction and superior flavor. The removable 60-ounce water tank brews up to 10 cups of coffee and includes a water filtration system to reduce impurities in order to optimize drink flavor. LCD control includes a digital clock with auto on-off time, five brew strengths, and variable brew temperature. Brewer uses pre-made K-Cup coffee pods or just add your own favorite roast to the reusable My K-Cup. Includes a sample pack of single-use K-Cups available including cocoa and tea. The My K-Cup and included measuring spoon conveniently store in the brewer's top compartment.
profile.reviewText:
I have owned the Keurig B60 for over 2 years and my family has been very pleased with its performance.  My only complaint with the B60 has been the noise but it is literally only 15 seconds of low buzzing while the water is heating up.  I decided to try this Breville mainly because of the iced beverage function.  It looks so nice in my stainless steel kitchen and brews a great cup of coffee!  I will list my pros and cons below.  Please see the picture section for my photos comparing the Keurig B60 and Breville.

Pros:
  stainless steel
  4 cup size settings
  easy to fill reservoir
  iced beverage feature
  compartment for reusable K cup and measuring scoop
  water filter
  quiet

Cons:
  larger footprint
  extremely bright white light buttons
  pricey
profile.summary: Beautiful stainless steel design and cool features

profile.description: Extend the capabilities of your GoPro by getting closer to the action and capturing unique angles. Capture selfies with ease or flip the camera around on the pivoting head to shoot your subject with stability and precision.
profile.reviewText:
This is a great extension for your GoPro. If you're active in the outdoors and want a lightweight pole extension for your GoPro, this is for you. Fully extended, the pole is about 3'. At this length, it works great for group selfies. Collapsed, it's about 1'. The handgrip is great for keeping a good grip on the pole. It's a soft grip and comfortable to hold. Overall, this is a nice GoPro extension pole

profile.description: This Contractor Tool Bag is an excellent storage for a variety of tools and has durable weather resistant fabric.
profile.reviewText: This bag is an ok size for a home handyman using basic tools. top_5.reviewText:
Being a huge fan of Le Creuset cookware, I was unsure I would love this Kitchen Aid casserole dish. I love KitchenAid appliances and was unaware they had a ceramic cookware line.  Upon unpackaging it, I was noting how heavy it is. But after using it to make a large batch of lasagna,  I am enamored. The lid made it convenient to transport to the event I prepared it for and I found it to be a very attractive piece to proudly serve my meal in. I put a lot of time and effort into meals I prepare for parties and gatherings, and I want my presentation to reflect that.

Since this is a larger size, I use it for family style recipes and we often have leftovers. I have refridgerated and stored leftovers in this and clean up was still a breeze. Its larger size takes up a bit of space in my dishwasher but the dishwasher handled it, no problem. What is convenient about a piece this size is that I am able to use it as my mixing bowl as well.  It makes for one less dish to clean up. I brined a chicken in this overnight and roasted it the next day.  The color is subjective to ones personal taste, but I found the green to be subtle and would complement any decor. For my first piece of KitchenAid cookware, I am very pleased.
top_5.summary: Prep, mix and cook all in one dish

top_5.reviewText:
***********March 2011

Well, 4 months into happily using my toaster, it just died one morning with no warning.  I was pretty bummed because I spent months (literally) searching online and in stores for the perfect stainless steel toaster for my counter.  I did not want a huge footprint taking up space on my counter.
I called Haier and they offered to replace my toaster.  I had to send them the cut cord and receipt.  They also requested $14.99 for shipping out the new toaster but I let them know I was not happy about that being only 4 months into using my toaster and they waived that.  I was pleased with the time frame in receiving my replacement.  It only took about 10 days total.  I did have to pay postage to mail out the cord and copy of receipt but that expense was minimal.  Hopefully this one will last.  I will update in a few months or in the event that it abruptly stops working.

November 2010
I haven't had this toaster for very long so I can't review it based on its longevity, but I like it great so far.  I actually really wanted the Breville toaster that is very similar to this one but I can't pay double or triple the price on a toaster, especially with the holidays coming up.  This toaster will easily and evenly toast 4 slices of Oroweat bread (longer than typical sandwich slices)  I really do like the flip up bread warmer on the top.  The lights drop off as the time nears the end.  My kids like to watch that as their Toaster Strudels are heating up.

This is my favorite Prana style and I have a few of these Quinn dresses and also a few Quinn tops. They wash, travel and wear well.
