It must have been all those long nights of women, sex, and cocaine that left nasal passages permanently dilated, long boring days doing crossword puzzles in rehab, IV drips on antibiotics and truck loads of women's underwear thrown on stage.  "Oh, gee.  Another bird on her boyfriend's shoulders flashing her headlights at me.  How droll!!!!"  They lost their way.  Plus there were all those young whippersnappers in spandex and big hair kicking their butts across the stage.

Jagger's solo career inched up to the cliff and then took a sharp nosedive.  Although Jagger did release a couple of excellent albums, Richards put out a few solo albums himself that were more highly regarded by the critics-but neither did well.  A small, silent gasp ran across the entire rock community.  "If Mick Jagger can't do well outside the Stones, what hope is there for the rest of us?  In the sixties and seventies, people would have just killed for a Jagger album.  Now most people can't be bothered."

This album is a piece of junk.  It doesn't come even close to the greatness of TATTOO YOU the Stones began the decade with.  For die-hard fans only.
top_5.summary: POOR, BAD, DISAPPOINTING, HIGHWAY ROBBERY--TRAGIC

top_5.description: LP
top_5.reviewText:
I belong to that class of jazz lovers who don't take too well to vocals.  Sorry.  I realize there is a long tradition of jazz singing; but it just totally passes me by.  I am far more interested in musicians who take their instruments and just play.  And there is a sizable portion of the jazz public that is just like me.

So for my fellow "instrumentalists", I issue this warning.  IF YOU ARE BUYING THIS ALBUM TO HEAR COLTRANE WAIL AWAY, YOU WILL BE WASTING YOUR MONEY.

Now, that having been said, let's consider the virtues of this record.  In all honesty, this should have been labeled Johnny Hartman's record because its really his showcase.  Hartman (previously unknown to me) has a deep, honey toned baritone set of pipes that have an unusual rich quality.  Hartman's singing is also exceptionally clear and well enunciated so that the actual lyrics are communicated with ease.  (May seem like a trivial issue to younger listeners; but us old timers don't hear as well as we once did.  So when you hear Hartman sing and you understand what he is saying THE FIRST TIME around that is quite unique).  Hartman is so good I have to wonder why he is not more well known or remembered.

John Coltrane actually plays more an accompanist than a co-headliner; but he does so very well.  Along with McCoy Tyner on piano, Jimmy Garrison on bass and Elvin Jones on drums, Coltrane provides sensitive and respectful support to Hartman's work-taking only a few occasions to render short, tasteful solos.  All in all, a very successful record that earns all the high marks other reviewers give to it.

But, again, I reserve my full encouragement to buy this record because it is not what most record buyers will be expecting.  It sure wasn't what I was expecting.  For a romantic, well-made vocal album you could hardly do better than this one and I myself will explore further into Johnny Hartman's other records.  Just don't expect to get GIANT STEPS PART TWO here.
top_5.summary: REALLY JOHNNY HARTMAN'S RECORD

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "2.0" for a product with description "Musicophilia: Tales of Music and the Brain". The summary of the review text is "Dr. Sacks is brilliant, but his books put me to sleep.".
output:
I picked up this book in the audiobook format. Settled in to hear Dr. Sacks' tales of brain-injured patients having sudden cravings to, for example, learn to play the piano. And his detailed discourses on the functioning of the mind as we listen to music. Fascinating stories and a fascinating topic. However, Oliver Sacks has a slow, gentle way of speaking, with his lovely accent, and unfortunately, he just manages to make me bored and sleepy. This is a very long-winded book, with laborious details and descriptions. Unfortunately, it just wasn't for me. One must have a lot of patience to get through a book like this.

The author is undoubtedly brilliant and an expert in his field. His writing/speaking style just does not work for me, sadly.

profile.description: Unusual book
profile.reviewText:
I listened to Steve Martin's Born Standing Up, in the audiobook format. Steve Martin is a fabulous writer, who also has a wonderful voice for reading. Thus, this book kept my interest throughout. This is an autobiography of Mr. Martin's rise to fame as a stand-up comic, and then as a world-famous comedian in Saturday Night Live. The story chronicles Mr. Martin's difficult family situation, in particular his distance from his temperamental father. He leaves home at a young age, to pursue first magic, then comedy. For many years, he struggled to make it. Eventually, he was able to spend much time on the road performing, but this was a lonely existence. Sadly, once famed arrived, Mr. Martin's existence only became lonelier, as so-called "friends" merely wanted his autograph, and going out in public was fraught with unwanted attention.

I really enjoyed Mr. Martin's story. It was also great hearing him talk about what it was like to perform on the Johnny Carson show, and other shows of that era, as well as descriptions of the comedians he admired, such as the cast of The Carol Burnett Show.

This is a poignant tale, and a reminder that fame and fortune are not cures for loneliness or family discord. Highly worthwhile read.
profile.summary: Yes, it's the 180th 5-star review of Born Standing Up!

profile.description: Book by Coelho, Paulo
profile.reviewText:
I've wanted to read this book for quite a while, after all the praise it has received. In fact, I tried starting it numerous times, but always stopped after a couple pages. This time, I was determined to give it a whirl. Frankly, it just never grabbed me. Just a simple tale of a boy seeking out a hidden treasure; the book tries to hard to sound wise and philosophical. There are pithy "words of wisdom" all over the place, none of which are meaningful in the slightest. Lots of sayings along the lines of "When one seeks out one's dreams, the world conspires to help one succeed" (as a paraphrased example). Statements like this sort of nonsense are made continuously. We follow the boy as he crosses the desert in search of his dream and his treasure, and follow along as he gets robbed a few times and outwits some armed tribesmen a few times. Nothing grabbed me in this book. The ending is somewhat clever and humorous and ironic, though. I will give the book credit for that.

For me, the book was boring, and a chore to get through. Seems like it might appeal more to young males, so perhaps I was the wrong demographic.
profile.summary: Boring, a chore to get through

profile.description: Paulette Mitchell lives in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and has been a cooking instructor for 25 years, lecturing frequently on health and nutrition. She has published numerous cookbooks, including the best-selling The 15-Minute Vegetarian.
profile.reviewText:
This is really a little gem of a book. It focuses on absolutely delicious vegetarian sandwiches ... not a boring one in the bunch. The recipes use all kinds of breads (including wraps and tortillas), and fillings such as avocado, roasted red pepper, sweet potato, carmelized onion, and other wonderful ingredients. I have made several recipes so far, and they were incredibly good, and astoundingly easy to put together, with ordinary ingredients. Even my meat-and-potatoes husband really enjoyed these vegetarian sandwiches.

These are the kind of sandwiches you would be proud to serve to guests. You'd pay quite a bit to buy sandwiches like these from a restaurant. The cookbook itself is quite beautiful, with plenty of mouth-watering photos, and attractive graphics, all on glossy paper. The recipes are explained clearly, and well organized, with a nice index.

My only complaint about this cookbook is that no nutritional information is provided. This is particularly problematic since many of the recipes use liberal quantities of butter, hummus, and avocado and other ingredients that can pack on the calories and fat (while admittedly also packing on lots of flavor!)

Anyway, despite the lack of nutritional information, I really like this cookbook and recommend it.
profile.summary: Beautiful book, delicious, easy recipes, but no nutritional information

profile.description: A Chronicle of the LIVE 2002 tour
profile.reviewText:
Mr. Williams is very outrageous, very R-rated, very politically incorrect, very high-energy and very hilarious. I listened to this in the car, and I was laughing so hard that it's a wonder I was able to drive at the same time. When I got to my destination, my stomach was sore from all the laughing. I am not usually a fan of profanity, but somehow it works with Robin Williams.

This CD was made 10 years ago, from some of his live performances made around the USA, so not surprisingly, a few of the jokes are a bit dated, but that ends up being a very minor issue.

As usual, Mr. Williams has a great time making fun of everyone ... celebrities, athletes, people from various regions of the U.S., people of various ethnic, religious and racial groups, you name it. Yet somehow, he manages not to offend (at least this listener).

Be forewarned that there is nearly constant use of profanity, and many sexual jokes. However, if you're ok with that, and appreciate Mr. Williams' brand of comedy, prepare yourself for a great time. Nothing better than laughing continuously as I drive to work. Loved it!
profile.summary: I could not stop laughing ...

profile.description: Some cool cats are just too hip for a regular bed. Thats why we introduced the new ThermoKitty Fashion Splash! With 4 happening colors and our incredibly energy efficient 4 watt heater, this bed is sure to please. Its the hottest thing going! Fashion Splash is washable and MET Listed.
profile.reviewText:
I purchased 3 of these cat beds for my two cats, so I can have them in multiple spots in my house. One cat was literally sitting in the bed within one minute of taking it out of the box! I think the soft, fur-like bed is just a nice, appealing fabric for cats. Yes, they were enjoying the cat bed before I even plugged it in! Once I plugged it in, it gradually got warm. It has a very light, gentle warmth. There is really no chance of any kind of burn; it is just a gentle, mild, soothing warmth. It seems to provide only minimal warmth until the cats sit on the bed. (maybe it sense the weight of the cat?)

The cats seem to spend enormous amounts of time sleeping and sometimes just sitting, on these cat beds. They clearly enjoy them, and having a nice, warm place to snuggle and take a nap. And again, I think the fur-like softness of the fabric is a real plus.

It has only been one week, but so far, I am very pleased with these cat beds. I haven't yet washed the fabric, but it is good to know that it is removable for washing.

I can't really think of any negatives so far, except that, of course, the placement of these beds is limited by the length of the electric cord. The cord seems to be several feet long, though. I keep two in my bedroom, near my bed. This seems to minimize the cats' wanting to sleep with me at night, so we all get better sleep! The third one is in the living room. I am very happy with this product.

Just an update: It has now been about two months and these cat beds continue to be extremely popular with my cats. No complaints.

Another update: It has been nearly a year, and these beds are still extremely popular with my cats; this is their place to hang out and their place to sleep. These heated cat beds are one of the best purchases I've ever made! In fact, I'm jealous of my cats ... I wish they made these in a size that would work for the cat owner, as well!
profile.summary: My two cats love these!

profile.description: These patented furniture socks will protect your hardwood, bamboo, laminate and tile floors from scratches and mars with their heavy duty thickness. They feature super strong elastic from top to bottom and rubber grippers on the inside to keep them in place. So easy to install and they can be folded down at the top for a fashionable cuff or pulled up high without the cuff. Package contains 8 ribbed furniture socks, perfect for 2 chairs, barstools or tables. Size Small fits approx. 1 to 1 3/4 inch furniture leg. Please see size chart in pictures. *sizes are approximate US Patent Number 9,877,583
profile.reviewText:
I have had these chair leg socks on my kitchen chairs for several months now. They have stayed on perfectly. They have completely stopped the scratches I was getting on my kitchen floor before that. I had tried using various felt pads before, but they never stayed on for very long. These have solved my problem. I only wish I had found them years ago, before my floor got scratched up.

I like them so much, that I have now placed an order for my dining room chairs, as well.

I notice on the Nancy Protectz website that they recommend placing a felt pad on the chair bottom first, and then placing the sock on, as an extra layer or protection. That makes sense, and I think I will now do that. In any case, these chair leg protectors work as advertised, and they don't fall off. They do get a bit lint-covered on the bottoms, after a while, as would any fabric left on a kitchen floor. So it is a good idea to occasionally brush off the lint. I haven't tried machine washing them yet.

They are a bit pricey for what you are getting (some tiny "socks"), but since they do the job and protect your floors, it ends up being worth the price. Would definitely buy again.
profile.summary: They do what they claim to do

profile.description: Made from a hyper-evaporative material that retains water while remaining dry to the touch, The Original Chilly Pad is an innovative way to cool down while enduring outdoor heat and/or high levels of physical activity. When wet, the towel begins to evaporate and cool, providing cool, soft comfort to the user. When it stops cooling, simply re-wet the towel in hot or cold water and wring it out. Within minutes, its cool again.
profile.reviewText:
I purchased this Chilly Pad, as an impulse buy recently, as I had been dealing with some hot flashes in recent times. I have since used it in several different situations, and have come to really appreciate it. Not only that, but I recently traveled and we experienced a power failure, with the outdoor temperature at 100 degrees. Without access to air conditioning or even a fan, in 100 degree heat, it was super uncomfortable and almost impossible to sleep at night. I really missed my Chilly Pad at that moment, and really wished that I had thought to carry it with me on my trip "just in case". Now the Chilly Pad will be placed on my packing list for future trips where hot weather might be a concern. Now, here are the details, including why I really like this product, and finally, a couple potential drawbacks that could be deal-breakers for some people (such as my husband).

The Chilly Pad is a scarf-shaped piece of fabric that, when wet, stays quite cool against the skin, and seems to stay cool for hours, in my experience. In fact, as I write this review, I am wearing it around my neck, in my house, and I actually am cool to the point of experiencing some chills ... even though, I last wet the Chilly Pad four hours ago, then wore it outdoors, in 90 degree heat earlier today, for over an hour ... and yet it is still wet and cooling me four hours later! That's just remarkable!

It seems to be a rather unique fabric. When wet, it is smooth, completely flexible, and sort of rubbery. It is extremely light-weight to carry or wear. Even wet, it seems to be practically weightless. It cools the skin, as long as it stays wet. However, once it dries, it becomes like a very stiff cardboard-like substance that is completely rigid and unbendable. Therefore, one needs to take care to allow it to dry in a shape (such as rolled up) that is easy to store. Or roll it up into the plastic container in which the Chilly Pad is packaged. Amazingly, the fabric quickly returns to its completely bendable and flexible qualities as soon as it is wet again. My Chilly Pad is bright blue, and I recently wore it to my son's school graduation, where someone complimented me on my pretty scarf! It is also available in lots of other colors.

How does it work? From what I can tell, the secret is in the very subtle texture to the fabric. The texture allows the product to soak up lots of water, and keeps it from drying out for a really long time. The product tends not to get clothing very wet (depending on how hard one wrings the water out of the Chilly Pad when wetting it). However, if one intentionally squeezes the fabric, water will drip out of it. The Chilly Pad I am wearing at this moment still drips lots of water out of it (if I intentionally squeeze it) even now, despite the fact that I wet it four hours ago, and took a long hike outdoors in 90 degree weather earlier today! Wow!

How have I used it? I have used this product both indoors and outdoors. Indoors, I use it to supplement fans or air conditioning, and have used it to help me cool down and fall asleep. I have worn it around my neck, but I sometimes move it to other areas of my body, to cool them down, as well, such as across my torso, over my legs, down my back, and even over my face. I have used it outdoors on hikes, and even use it to wipe sweat off my face. I tend to move it around to different "cold spots" on the Chilly Pad, and to different parts of my body.

Potential drawbacks: To enjoy this product, one has to be comfortable wearing a fabric that is cold, wet, and sort of rubbery, in feel. I think that people, like myself, who do not mind walking around in a wet bathing suit, for example, would like this Chilly Pad, also. However, people who, like my husband, do not like the feel of a wet bathing suit, might not like this product either. Also, it is a bit inconvenient to have to remember to fold or roll up the Chilly Pad into a convenient shape for storing it, as it cannot be reshaped once it is dry. Finally, while it tends not to get clothing very wet, I would still avoid wearing it with any clothing that you do not wish to get wet at all. Similarly, people with hair length at neck-length or longer may find that their hair gets a bit damp when the Chilly Pad is worn around the neck.

For me, this product is absolutely wonderful. During my hike earlier today in 90 degree heat, the Chilly Pad made a noticeable difference in my comfort level. While I was still aware of the heat (especially after hiking up hills for over one hour), it was far more pleasant than it would have been without that Chilly Pad around my neck. Highly recommended, if you do not mind the "cold, rubbery" feel and don't mind if your hair (if neck length or longer) gets slightly wet.
profile.summary: Love it, personally (but it might not be right for everyone)

profile.description: Medium cut compound is formulated with an aggressive blend of nanotechnology polishing agents to restore your cars finish.
profile.reviewText:
A couple months back, I scraped the side of my garage when pulling the car in. As a result, I ended up with a very large area of white paint on one area (over the rear tire) of my lovely metallic red Subaru Legacy. The area was approximately 18 inches long and 2 inches high. I didn't know what to do, and this middle-aged woman had no idea if the white paint could be removed without spending a fortune or destroying the car's finish.

I ended up going into two different auto supply stores and showed them my car. In each case, they recommended that I purchase this Turtle Wax Rubbing Compound for "Medium to Deep Scratches". They also recommended some soft applicator pads and some soft microfiber towels for buffing. After getting two identical recommendations for this product, I worked up the courage to try it, and I am writing this to tell you how it worked out, as I just used the product today.

I have to admit that I was a bit nervous about using this product. I was really afraid that it would damage the beautiful finish on my car. Well, I cautiously applied the product with the applicator pad, and rubbed it in gently, with a back and forth motion, as instructed on the product's label. Then, I used the microfiber cloth to buff. I repeated this action a couple times, and to my amazement, within about five minutes, I had gotten about half the paint marks off! I was so excited that I ran into the house, and had my husband come out to see. He was pretty impressed too! I then worked patiently, applying additional product to the area, rubbing more, and buffing more, over and over. Each time I applied more product, more and more of the paint came off, and I was thrilled to see that I was left with my shiny, red car finish, without a hint of damage.

The product is creamy and white. I guess it has a mild abrasive cleaner in it, but to my fingers it felt quite smooth. It is really gentle, but that's how it manages to fix problems like mine, without damaging the car's finish at all. I was also happy to note that there was no noticeable smell or irritating fumes.

It took time and patience, probably 45 minutes or maybe an hour, and my arm was pretty tired by the end, but I was able to remove 100% of the white paint, and you would never guess that that huge section had been covered in thick, white paint. The car's finish is left perfectly shiny and intact. The results are perfect and so worth it. I am extremely impressed with this product. Five stars. I'd give it ten stars if I could.

I should add that this product is marketed for removing scratches, but I have not used it for that, and cannot comment on how it works for that. However, for removing thick, two month old white paint, this product was absolutely perfect.
profile.summary: Extremely impressed - for removing transferred paint

top_5.description: Unusual book
top_5.reviewText:
I listened to Steve Martin's Born Standing Up, in the audiobook format. Steve Martin is a fabulous writer, who also has a wonderful voice for reading. Thus, this book kept my interest throughout. This is an autobiography of Mr. Martin's rise to fame as a stand-up comic, and then as a world-famous comedian in Saturday Night Live. The story chronicles Mr. Martin's difficult family situation, in particular his distance from his temperamental father. He leaves home at a young age, to pursue first magic, then comedy. For many years, he struggled to make it. Eventually, he was able to spend much time on the road performing, but this was a lonely existence. Sadly, once famed arrived, Mr. Martin's existence only became lonelier, as so-called "friends" merely wanted his autograph, and going out in public was fraught with unwanted attention.

I really enjoyed Mr. Martin's story. It was also great hearing him talk about what it was like to perform on the Johnny Carson show, and other shows of that era, as well as descriptions of the comedians he admired, such as the cast of The Carol Burnett Show.

This is a poignant tale, and a reminder that fame and fortune are not cures for loneliness or family discord. Highly worthwhile read.
top_5.summary: Yes, it's the 180th 5-star review of Born Standing Up!

top_5.description: Book by Coelho, Paulo
top_5.reviewText:
I've wanted to read this book for quite a while, after all the praise it has received. In fact, I tried starting it numerous times, but always stopped after a couple pages. This time, I was determined to give it a whirl. Frankly, it just never grabbed me. Just a simple tale of a boy seeking out a hidden treasure; the book tries to hard to sound wise and philosophical. There are pithy "words of wisdom" all over the place, none of which are meaningful in the slightest. Lots of sayings along the lines of "When one seeks out one's dreams, the world conspires to help one succeed" (as a paraphrased example). Statements like this sort of nonsense are made continuously. We follow the boy as he crosses the desert in search of his dream and his treasure, and follow along as he gets robbed a few times and outwits some armed tribesmen a few times. Nothing grabbed me in this book. The ending is somewhat clever and humorous and ironic, though. I will give the book credit for that.

For me, the book was boring, and a chore to get through. Seems like it might appeal more to young males, so perhaps I was the wrong demographic.
top_5.summary: Boring, a chore to get through

top_5.description: Paulette Mitchell lives in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and has been a cooking instructor for 25 years, lecturing frequently on health and nutrition. She has published numerous cookbooks, including the best-selling The 15-Minute Vegetarian.
top_5.reviewText:
This is really a little gem of a book. It focuses on absolutely delicious vegetarian sandwiches ... not a boring one in the bunch. The recipes use all kinds of breads (including wraps and tortillas), and fillings such as avocado, roasted red pepper, sweet potato, carmelized onion, and other wonderful ingredients. I have made several recipes so far, and they were incredibly good, and astoundingly easy to put together, with ordinary ingredients. Even my meat-and-potatoes husband really enjoyed these vegetarian sandwiches.

These are the kind of sandwiches you would be proud to serve to guests. You'd pay quite a bit to buy sandwiches like these from a restaurant. The cookbook itself is quite beautiful, with plenty of mouth-watering photos, and attractive graphics, all on glossy paper. The recipes are explained clearly, and well organized, with a nice index.

My only complaint about this cookbook is that no nutritional information is provided. This is particularly problematic since many of the recipes use liberal quantities of butter, hummus, and avocado and other ingredients that can pack on the calories and fat (while admittedly also packing on lots of flavor!)

Anyway, despite the lack of nutritional information, I really like this cookbook and recommend it.
top_5.summary: Beautiful book, delicious, easy recipes, but no nutritional information

top_5.description: A Chronicle of the LIVE 2002 tour
top_5.reviewText:
Mr. Williams is very outrageous, very R-rated, very politically incorrect, very high-energy and very hilarious. I listened to this in the car, and I was laughing so hard that it's a wonder I was able to drive at the same time. When I got to my destination, my stomach was sore from all the laughing. I am not usually a fan of profanity, but somehow it works with Robin Williams.

This CD was made 10 years ago, from some of his live performances made around the USA, so not surprisingly, a few of the jokes are a bit dated, but that ends up being a very minor issue.

As usual, Mr. Williams has a great time making fun of everyone ... celebrities, athletes, people from various regions of the U.S., people of various ethnic, religious and racial groups, you name it. Yet somehow, he manages not to offend (at least this listener).

Be forewarned that there is nearly constant use of profanity, and many sexual jokes. However, if you're ok with that, and appreciate Mr. Williams' brand of comedy, prepare yourself for a great time. Nothing better than laughing continuously as I drive to work. Loved it!
top_5.summary: I could not stop laughing ...

top_5.description: Some cool cats are just too hip for a regular bed. Thats why we introduced the new ThermoKitty Fashion Splash! With 4 happening colors and our incredibly energy efficient 4 watt heater, this bed is sure to please. Its the hottest thing going! Fashion Splash is washable and MET Listed.
top_5.reviewText:
I purchased 3 of these cat beds for my two cats, so I can have them in multiple spots in my house. One cat was literally sitting in the bed within one minute of taking it out of the box! I think the soft, fur-like bed is just a nice, appealing fabric for cats. Yes, they were enjoying the cat bed before I even plugged it in! Once I plugged it in, it gradually got warm. It has a very light, gentle warmth. There is really no chance of any kind of burn; it is just a gentle, mild, soothing warmth. It seems to provide only minimal warmth until the cats sit on the bed. (maybe it sense the weight of the cat?)

The cats seem to spend enormous amounts of time sleeping and sometimes just sitting, on these cat beds. They clearly enjoy them, and having a nice, warm place to snuggle and take a nap. And again, I think the fur-like softness of the fabric is a real plus.

It has only been one week, but so far, I am very pleased with these cat beds. I haven't yet washed the fabric, but it is good to know that it is removable for washing.

I can't really think of any negatives so far, except that, of course, the placement of these beds is limited by the length of the electric cord. The cord seems to be several feet long, though. I keep two in my bedroom, near my bed. This seems to minimize the cats' wanting to sleep with me at night, so we all get better sleep! The third one is in the living room. I am very happy with this product.

Just an update: It has now been about two months and these cat beds continue to be extremely popular with my cats. No complaints.

Another update: It has been nearly a year, and these beds are still extremely popular with my cats; this is their place to hang out and their place to sleep. These heated cat beds are one of the best purchases I've ever made! In fact, I'm jealous of my cats ... I wish they made these in a size that would work for the cat owner, as well!
top_5.summary: My two cats love these!

profile.description: Joe Bunting is a professional ghostwriter, writer, and editor. He is the publishers of The Write Practice, a daily online writing workbook twice named as a Top 10 Blog for Writers. He lives in the foothills of the Appalachians with his wife and son.
profile.reviewText:
Joe Bunting's Let Write a Short Story is a brief practical guide to the world of short story writing, for those who wanted to jump on that bandwagon. The book is divided into roughly ten chapters all aimed at one simple mission- helping writers to create and publish a short story. Joe Bunting does a wonderful job of breaking down the elements of good short story writing and getting it published into small digestible chunks. The book is definitely a quick read; however it has plenty of tips and resources within those pages. I was able to read it fully in less than 2 hours. There are writing prompts interspersed throughout the book, which should motivate readers to start the process of finally get around to writing that short story.  I recommend this book for any writer who is seeking to join the ranks of short story writers or short story writers who want additional guidance.

Additional Comments:
This book is geared toward writers, professional and amateur writers. While it is a good read for everyone, it is not the kind of book that you pick up to get into the habit of writing (although you could). The specfic aim is to get writers comfortable with the short story and the short story market.

This book is not written in the typical style of most writer's guidebooks, rather it is in the style of a blog posting, so those expecting a long read with lots of unrelated fluff should look somewhere else. Bunting goes straight to the point, breaking down key elements into outlined and numbered lists for easy application.

If you can, read this book when you are in a place where you have access to the Internet. Bunting makes a lot of references to his online community (TheWritePractice) and other sites that you will want to keep track of.
profile.summary: Helpful guide to finally writing (and publishing) that short story you've been wanting to...

profile.description: Suzanne Strisower, author, certified coach, Rune expert, and creator of one of the most powerful Life Purpose workbooks, 111 Inspirational Life Purpose Quotes and Exercises to Find Your Purpose in Life, also has developed a transformational method to help people quickly release old thoughts and patterns. She was born to speak into peoples hearts and souls. The 30-year span of Suzannes many accomplishments includes extensive work in a range of health and healing vocations, including being the weekly psychic at the prestigious Claremont Hotel and Spa, counseling emotionally disturbed teenagers in residential treatment environments, followed by certification in hypnotherapy to help people heal from within, then to being a healthcare facilities interior designer creating environments that heal, to becoming a sustainable land developer. During the last decade, these pursuits have led her to become a social worker, life coach, author, screenwriter, and radio show host. A member of the Who's Who of American Women, Suzanne has pursued many degrees and many interests to fulfill her life purpose of helping people heal and open their connection to their divine source. First with a Bachelor's in Fine Arts, then a Master's in Counseling Psychology, along with numerous certifications as a clinical hypnotherapist, where she applied intuitive gifts to helping clients reach healing, well being and expanded consciousness, often in single sessions. Suzanne also holds a certification as an Inspired Learning Facilitator, giving her expertise in creating learner-education tools. An International Coach Federation, Professional Certified Coach, Suzanne primarily serves professional women transitioning to more purpose-directed, spiritually led lives. Suzanne has authored two books 111 Inspirational Life Purpose Quotes and Exercises to Find Your Purpose in Life and a unique new-age fortune telling oracle, The Runes of the Four Realms, plus a spiritual feature-film screenplay, Shileah. She contributed to the books Be Happy, Healthy and Wealthy: A Guidebook for Women and Word Colors and hosted a weekly conscious living Living Well Talk Radio show on 96.7FM in Chico, Calif.
profile.reviewText:
Strisower's book is a very unique workbook that encourages you to go beyond normal self-help workbooks. In this workbook, I completed activities that analyzed who I think I am, who I thought I was, and who I think I could be at every stage of my life from childhood onward. This approach, which I haven't seen before in other self-help workbooks allowed me the opportunity to view my life comprehensively, to find themes and trends that I might have missed.

This is not a straightforward, "journal about your life" workbook, rather it's an exploration with a lot of activities deriving from numerology, psychology, spirituality, and religion. One minute you might analyzing your childhood in terms of Maslow's hierarchy and the next you might be analyzing the origin of your name. In all of the activities, though, Strisower keeps pushing you to relate what you find to your own life. How did this shape who you are? What does it mean to you?

The only problem I had with the book was with some of the content. Almost midway through the book, the workbook shifts toward analyzing and understanding the midlife years (who I suspect is the target audience for this book). I have not reached those years yet, so it was a little hard at first to determine how I could apply that to my life.

Overall, this was a good workbook that will take some time to work through if you are open to ideas such as transpersonal psychology, some New Age spirituality, Jungian psychology, and Maslow's hierarchy of needs. For the comprehensive insight that this workbook provides, the time is worth it.
profile.summary: Interesting & Comprehensive Self-help Workbook for Every Stage of Your Life

profile.description: William Shakespeare is widely regarded as the greatest playwright the world has seen. He produced an astonishing amount of work; 37 plays, 154 sonnets, and 5 poems. He died on 23rd April 1616, aged 52, and was buried in the Holy Trinity Church, Stratford.
profile.reviewText:
This is one of the greatest versions that I have ever read about Antony and Cleopatra and my favorite book from the Masters of Rome series. In this book, Colleen McCullogh combines all of the elements that I enjoyed in her other books on ancient Rome: Intricate (and nearly precise) historical detail, intrigues of power and corruption, excellent use of pacing and plot, and an uncanny ability to speak from the character's perspective to make what I believe is a classic. I have read this book (probably) twice now and enjoy it every time I read because I get a different glimpse of the narrative each time.

In this book series, Marc Antony is striving to maintain a balance between his role as second wheel in the Triumvir and conqueror of the East(as the Romans thought of him) and his role as First Man in Rome. That role is challenged by the rise of the unsuspecting Octavian and the growing rise of Cleopatra of Egypt. What happens next is a gamble that goes terribly wrong...

Pros: Exquisite historical detail (some of the best I have ever seen), Uncanny ability to change viewpoint from characters of different genders and cultures, Interesting ending

Cons: May be a little too long and too detailed for those not interested in Ancient Rome
profile.summary: Excellent re-telling of story of love and war with exquisite historical detail

profile.description: Nick and Al have vastly different backgrounds, skill sets and experiences. Nick grew up in a family of entrepreneurs and went on to start up a few large businesses that have generated a couple of hundred million dollars. Al, on the other hand, started on the factory floor before establishing his own martial arts school and becoming an online fat loss trainer. Nick is a personal productivity champion while Al has received an award for his fitness book, Cheeseburger Abs. Their passion for writing brought them together to provide an editing service for non-fiction authors, which quickly blossomed into an all-out search for the easiest, quickest way to write a book. Information on Nick and Als research is published on www.WritersRise.com. You can also listen in on their conversations with best-selling authors and publishing industry experts on The Writers Rise Podcast.
profile.reviewText:
Pros: Good tips for newbie authors. Covers aspects of writing not usually covered in typical writing self-help books (ghost-writing, Title optimization, etc.)

Cons: May be same old story for more experienced authors. Does not cover other aspects of marketing a book that can dramatically impact sales. Concept not workable for most authors (You need more than 30 hours in other words.)

This book was OK, but it didn't really add a lot too my writing or book marketing toolkit that I already knew. It had some good principles (especially about writing), but didn't really have anything novel. I wouldn't say that an author couldn't accomplish the intent behind the book if you are already an accomplished writer with a well-developed story (printing a book in 30 hours), but 99% of writers will need more than the principles in this book to accomplish a "hard-selling" book. If you are looking for some tips to get ideas for your book or fine-tune a book in 30 hours or less,this might be of interest.
profile.summary: Good for newbie authors for writing tips & inspiration; not so helpful for experienced authors (especially marketing)

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "Packing cube set is a travel essential that save your clothes from wrinkles and stains, and make them stay tidy and folded. These travel cube set is lightweight and you can fold it as a small bag , easy to storage.". The summary of the review text is "Mesh allows you to see at a glance what is inside. It also allows your clothing to breathe.".
output:
I have many different brands of foldable packing cubes but am always needing more for my large family. I had no doubt these Wodison Foldable Packing Cubes would work for us. But there were some pleasant surprises!

First, these packing cubes are much larger than they appear. I have posted a picture of the large one to show just how large it is. This should easily hold a weeks worth of clothing for my children. The middle bag, though smaller, is 16 1/2" x 11 2/3 " and nearly 4" tall. As you can tell, with those dimensions, you could hold a lot of clothing or even beach towels.  The smallest bag is my favorite! At 12 1/2" x just under 9 1/2" and nearly 4" tall, this bag does not really fir the category of small. This bag will easily hold a nice amount of clothing. However, on an overnight trip with two of my children, I used this for all of our electronic cords (we have a LOT).

profile.description: I AM LEGEND
profile.reviewText:
I Am Legend is one of the films I greatly anticipated for Winter 2007 and having just emerged from the theater I feel as though a great deal is needed.  Perhaps my hopes were just too high but let's look at this point by point.

I Am Legend is roughly take 6 at the original novel of the same name.  The Omega Man is probably the most popular and, for fans of that movie and older generations, this will prove very disappointing as both films derive multiple themes from the book such as Sam the dog, a woman entering Neville's life, etc, etc.  "IAL" just was not unique enough to satisfy certain fans.  For the general audience, however, there are some redeeming qualities.

The visual were very nice.  New York city was reproduced superbly if not used outright as several blocks were closed off for the filming; kudos.  The "monsters" were kind of freaky but I almost felt a humanistic touch to them as one seemed to express remorse for losing one of his kind (I thought she was his daughter or something) but it's not expanded on.

The acting, which comprises almost solely on Will Smith, is superb.  I still am having trouble finding a movie Will Smith acted poorly in every movie he is in I think about seeing just on that basis.  He performs well as a man living almost entirely alone for several years but remains diligent in his tasks.

The story had potential.  It deviated slightly from the book in terms of the ending but I think almost for the better.  I'm glad the directors took a different approach to the Twilight Zone-esque themes of vampires that the original book took.  DESPITE ALL THIS, the movie was TOO SHORT.  It was barely 90 minutes (I think) and sooo much more could've been explained, expanded upon or even made somewhat kewl.  The ending came too quick and very anti-climatic almost to the bewilderment of the audience.  They didn't even bother to explain how certain things came to be and that really bothered me.

The story is similar to War of the Worlds only the movie didn't suck as much; too many holes, not enough time.  IAL could've easily been an epic but directors settled for a 90-minute money bagger and I'm quite disappointed.  The movie started out awesome but just fell short at the end.

I will still buy this on DVD when it comes out but for theater goers I must give a warning that there are holes.  Also, THIS IS NOT A HORROR FILM.  Several people tried to ward me off due to "horror-elements."  This is not the case.  If anything, it is a thriller.  It is appropriate for most audiences although I wouldn't bring too young of kids.

All in all, a B-.  Diss marks for lack of story and length.  It kills the movie.

profile.description: Best of Americas Funniest Home Videos [VHS]
profile.reviewText:
First and foremost, if you are a parent of a child under 18 spare yourself the anguish and kicking yourself in the rear by not taking your kids to see this,  The same goes for everyone who thinks they'll be offended by it; chances are you will be offended.  In the theatre I saw Borat in, half the audience was laughing or on the floor while the more conservative audience (usually non-college student adults and older viewers) berated us for laughing at the racial and sexist jokes that clutter Borat.

I will admit, Borat goes well over the top in both crude humor and imagry.  The one scene that comes to mind involves wrestling between a naked Borat and his overly obese producer... who is also naked and the fight tends to meander... a lot.  At this point I covered my eyes (while laughing hysterically) and kept demanding the movie Gods to make it stop.  The showing of the full-frontal nudity in males happens twice and while it is seemingly hysterical to myself and other Cohen fans, the general audience in the theatre just gagged or walked out.

As for being whitty and satiracle, I found Borat to be hilarious.  I will not say American culture involves inherant violence and desires to kill all people of Iraq (as Borat more or less "proved" during the Rodeo scene), but he certainly brought out the worst in everyone he encountered.  The scene where he visits a gun shop to get "protection from Jews," the owner just stands there and changes the subject.  Many saw this as condoning the act when the guy was simply trying to be polite and not cause any trouble.

Borat does a great job of taking social norms and taboos and throwing them right into the face of Americans.  For instance, he tries to be friendly on a subway only to be threatened by everyone he encounters and given the social norms in NY, this certainly makes it all the more funny.  Another social norm turned upside down is his treatment of women; when attending a feminist meeting he laughs at the feminists and brings up "research" that women's brains are smaller and keeps refering to one feminist as a guy.

Pertaining to the candid-camera aspect and the controversy thereof; while I sympathize with the people he was extremely rude to such as the dining society... let's think about this.  If someone acting incredibly stupid shows up with a camera screw and is well-financed; he's either a friend of George Soros or it's a prank.  The fraternity guys claimed they were duped into thinking it was a documentary on the fraternity system and yet they didn't question why a guy from Kazachkstan was doing the filming and he was incredibly stupid.  Not to mention one has to know if he's being filmed and with technology today (particularly youtube etc) the film is going to be distributed.

I loved the story; Borat is trying to find Pamela Anderson to make him his wife and it was obvious that one scene where he meets her is staged... but still funny.  Borat encounters many funny figures along the way and his usual antics such as loving women will make crude humor fans laugh.  One of Borat's obvious querps is his disdain for Jews (Cohen is a Jew himself) and the encounter with a Jewish couple at a bed and breakfast, who tried to be very sweet (although it seemed as though it was staged) and trigger the Blair-Witch Project scene that follows.

Again, this is very crude humor appealing to college students, teenagers and Cohen fans like myself.  DO NOT SEE THIS is you think you will be offended or are easily offended.  Cannot stress this enough; which does force me to ding Borat to 4-stars because while I found Borat to be a five-star in my book, it does not appeal to the general audience.  This film was very entertaining for my friends and I to see and was worth the wait; we will get the DVD when it comes out as well.
profile.summary: Extremely Funny for Satire and Cohen Fans... Not So Much For Everyone Else

profile.description: Get minds and bodies moving, the educational, active video gaming system built just for kids ages 3-8 years.
profile.reviewText:
Taking several points from Nintendo, LeapFrog, who have a fantastic track record for interactive educational programs, took what made the Wii grossly successful and tunneled on the once-novel concept of motion controls while throwing out the rest and, thus, creating a product that has great potential but just isn't ready for mass marketing.

The LeapTV Educational Gaming System is a console marred with some very basic issues that should've been resolved during their QA process such as no calibration process, cannot function in anything other than bright lighting, and a lackluster selection of games that are, essentially, the same aside from the artwork differing.  For the price, LeapFrog could've done a whole lot better had they developed their system and games better with actual testers.

From our end, we tested the LeapTV with some friends of the family that had a 4-year old daughter who is absolutely in love with anything Disney princess related.  Both her Dad and I are hardcore gamers and have been for, quite literally, decades (Almost 50 years between the two of us) so we went in knowing what works with the general audience and how the LeapTV would hold up point for point with traditional gaming.  Setup was as easy as any system with the simple HDMI cable (which is mandatory so one MUST have an HDTV) and the power cable but, once we turned the system on, we realized that in both the system menu and in the games themselves there was NO CALIBRATION setup whatsoever.  This means you have to either experiment with placement of the sensor till it's close enough, or stand off to whatever side the sensor is picking you up at.  Either way, it's not nearly as accurate as a Nintendo Wii, a system that came out almost ten years ago and has several educational games that are family friendly.

The LeapTV also doesn't operate well in areas of not perfect brightness so playing in a basement may not work well if it isn't lit up with flood lights.

While the controller is superbly durable (as one would expect from anything used by small children), button placement is terrible for anyone that doesn't have giant adult-sized hands.  The button placement requires anyone with smaller hands, which means virtually all children, to hold the controller with one hand and push buttons with the other, which doesn't translate well when trying to get an uncalibrated controller on screen to work.  If it wasn't for the fact that my friend's daughter was just happy to get something, the games would've been almost unplayable.  This is amplified by the fact that all the games work on almost the exact same concepts just with different artwork to personify them and you're paying the same for one LeapTV game as you would a relatively new Xbox 360 game.

These are lessons that AAA game developers learned long ago such as Steel Battalion for the Kinect (virtually unplayable due to a fundamental design flaw).  Not everything is better with motion controls especially if it doesn't work properly, which the LeapTV does not.

While incorporating motion controls and Wii-esque controls into an educational program is a great idea and I support it, it has to be technologically playable otherwise players, regardless of age, will get frustrated and stop playing.

For the same price as the LeapTV and it's games, get a Nintendo Wii or an Xbox 360 with a Kinect as Sesame Street has a huge selection of Kinect games to choose from... for the same price.
profile.summary: Excellent Concept, Needs Drastic Improvement

profile.description: In Buzz! Quiz TV, the whole world becomes a quiz show network! Included on the disc are over 5,000 questions ranging from music, to movies, sports, and more. Put your knowledge to the test as you play with up to 8 friends - buzzing your way to game show stardom!
profile.reviewText:
One of my largest criticisms of the Playstation 3 is how it lacks being a party machine or a family-friendly one.  I recently purchased Pure and was extremely disappointed to see NO offline multiplayer.  Sony has seriously capitalized on the growing online market, thinking since World of Warcraft has over ten million members, they should be able to pull off the same.  Wrong!

However, as William Shatner once said (again, and again), "There... is... always... hope!"  Enter Buzz!: Quiz TV ("Buzz QT").

In an effort to appeal to the party group that the Nintendo Wii has preyed on and dominated in for over two years, the guys over at Renlentless Software divised Buzz QT to market exclusively for the PS3 to reign in sales over the Wii.  To this extent, they were successful with me as I also own a Nintendo Wii.  I wanted something that would bring the friends together in a setting other than the local bar or bowling alley (that's what Wii Sports is for!).

To a fair extent, Buzz QT brought the friends (and the beer) over to my place to face-off each other in a climactic battle of whits over, what appeared to me, very simple questions.  It was pretty much a battle to see who could hit the button the fastest and often differentiated by several hundreds of a second.  This goes to show how accurate the devices are.  You can't even block the signal by standing in front of your opponents or placing your hands on their controllers (believe me, I tried).

With over 5000 questions, the chance of a repeat question is rare, but has occured over the course of playing over a week.  My only request is that the questions be harder so we actually have to sit there and think.  Questions like, "Who plays Rachel in Friends," are hardly a challenge... especially since Jennifer Anniston is so hot that anyone can remember that.  I guess my other request is that they be so kind as to provide batteries but that's just a prayer on its own.

However, despite the fun my friends and I had playing Buzz QT we got bored of the game after an hour or two and immediately proceeded to kill hoardes of zombies in Left For Dead.  This is an apples to oranges argument, but the buzz (so-to-speak) wore off after a few hours and we desired to play a more complex group game.

Then there's the single-player game.  I like to compare Buzz QT to Mario Party 8, a great game for groups but fairly dull if individually played.  If I want to quiz myself, I'll read on tachyons and quantum physics on that bloody online encyclopedia that's always right.  Trivia games are best suited in groups since it adds the element of competition between someone you can sneer at and make Ace Ventura "loser" taunts at.  You can't do that to a computer, which is nothing more than a think-fast-beat-your-time thingy.  Such a feature does not hold water for very long.

Now, I will admit I have yet to play Scene-It but I have seen it (oy vey, no pun intended) played and while Buzz QT is superior on first impression, it is only an evolutionary step in the right direction and not a revolutionary one.  It's superior, but not by an impressive amount.

All in all, Buzz QT is a great party game!  The online content thingy would be cool to review if I used the internet feature, which I don't.  It's not-so-nice with single player but very worthy if you're having guests over and wish to squash them underneath your boots of superior popular culture wisdom!  *evil laughter*
profile.summary: The Evolutionary, But Not Revolutionary, Party Game

profile.description: year 2002
profile.reviewText:
As a son of a Vietnam Vet, I get the luxury of getting feedback on how realistic war movies really are.  When he took me to go see We Were Soldiers, his first comments was on the terrain.  He said it looked as though it was filmed in California.  But that was the only fault we found.  The combat sequences were excellent and truely realistic, you really had to make sure you own Hueys and planes did NOT shoot at you instead of the enemy.
The helicopter crash was the most realistic one I've seen yet in a war movie where when they crash they don't erupt in a ball of flame but the emmit severl bursts or sparks and the props spin off, the Hueys don't just explode and this was something which the producers worked really hard on and we could tell.
And the NVA and the Viet Cong really did send their troops out as if they were nothing more then dust.  The mentality was there would always be more troops and that was another really good point the movie made.  All in all, a great movie!
profile.summary: Excellent movie in almost all aspects.

profile.description: Ninja Scroll VHS. 1995 Manga Video. Action/Adventure/Anime. English Dubbed.
profile.reviewText:
This was one of the first annimes I ever saw so this movie totally hit me by surprise with the action, suspense, character development and others.  I gave this movie 3 stars for the following reasons:
Two stars for originality and compelling story.
Totally original and very compelling, I only had to watch it once to get the whole movie unlike other annimes that I have watched.  I was somewhat on the edge of my seat as the action got more and more intense.  I loved the 7 devils and their incredible abilities and how Jubei fought with every one of them, but my favorite part was where he fought in the woods with the blind ninja master.  That part was really cool.
I also gave this movie 1 more star for non-stop edge-of-your-seat action.  I never got board once, I never had to fastforward or skip any parts because of the lame or useless dialogue simply because there was none.  Almost every part of the movie was needed... except for some scenes that I will get into later.  As I said earlier, I loved the action sequences and the non-stop ninja techniques used, even if they were a little far fetched.
Now onto the things I think Manga could have taken out:
There were three sex scenes that I believe could've been taken out altogether.  Sexuality in movies is NOT neccesary unless the circumstances have to allow it such as the rape scene in the General's Daughter.  And the last things was excessive gore.  I thought that the blood spraying, skull splitting, blood drinking and massive loss of limbs was too much.  Gore is also not necessary unless the you have to have it, for example Saving Private Ryan or Enemy at the Gates it was needed whereas here it is not.  However this movie is non the less a great movie and well worth the low price amazon.com has set before you.
Whether you are an annime fan or not, this is the movie for you.
profile.summary: Great Movie for Mature Audiences

profile.description: Premium quality Flex blades, easy to install, smooth and quiet operation, superior performance.
profile.reviewText:
Had Michelin and Bosch wiper blades on my 2012 Impala and have been moderately impressed with the former, pretty well with the latter.  However, Bosch wiper blades are expensive and only come in kits of one and the ND winter I survive 9 months out of the year put considerably strain and wear on any wiper blades I use.

I've tried the SilBlades for only a few weeks but, so far, they've performed very well and held up even against ice on the windshield.  They were just as easy to put on as any other (albeit had to really tug to get the packaging tabs off) and encompass the full length of my windshield as advertised.  Upon close inspection the SilBlades are a heavy, durable quality one would expect from heavy-duty blades.

To test this, I waited until it got cold enough overnight to create a thick layer of ice over the windshield and, by that, I meant the next day.  I then turned the engine on, put on the defroster and let the wipers go to work.  Not a recommended method of utilization for any wiper blades, mind you, but an excellent method of testing the durability of the blade's rubber scrapers.  After 10 minutes of continuous wiping I examined the blades and noticed marginal wear, enough to sustain long periods of use.  I performed the test a few more times over the past few weeks and noticed identical results with progressive wear.  I estimate these blades can handle heavy usage up to one year but further testing is needed.

As for their efficiency in the rain, I simply took the car to the local insulated car wash nearby and ran the blades for a few cycles (car needed a wash anyway).  The results were quite satisfactory.

In short, for the price, the SilBlades and a very nice quality for the price and even come in pairs.  If price is an issue, get these over Bosch.
profile.summary: Premium Industrial Quality for a Nice Price

profile.description: Carry all your cards and cash without the bulk. Our handsome Adam bifold holds up to six cards and is crafted of smooth leather.
profile.reviewText:
Needed to replace my aging Stafford wallet as it's age was going on 5 years and the once proud leather was beginning to show it's wear and tear.  The Fossil Adam Front bi-fold has been a great replacement as I've had the Fossil Adam wallet for two weeks but not without it's limitations.

The first positive I noted was the high-quality leather by the aroma of which it graced me once I opened the container it was in.  The feel is great and the compartment seems to be fairly intuitive to what most men want in their wallets.  However, I then noticed the lack of an ID holder forcing me to keep my driver's license in another part of the bill-fold.  Not my first choice but that's the way it goes.

I also had to break in the wallet for a day or two as the folds were quite tight and the wallet kept wanting to open on itself.  Needless to say the wallet doesn't hold a lot of cards, which many men carry.

However, all in all, I like the Fossil Adam bi-fold and it will be my replacement for a while but I could have easily procured a cheaper version elsewhere.

Or REAL chicken, raised with pride right here in the USA. Thats why every Waggin Train Jerky Duo and Smoky Jerky Treat starts with exactly that  Real U.S. Chicken. profile.reviewText:
My dog, a little Cairn terrier, can be a very picky eater at times but he loves his treats and one of our favorite things to do is line up a row of different treats and see which one he picks.
