profile.description: VideoStudio Pro X7 EN Mini-Box. Enjoy the faster easier way to make great-looking videos and slideshows. Corel VideoStudio Pro X7 offers new time-saving 64-bit power faster 4K and HD render times fresh creative content and the new movie-making mode FastFlick. Immerse yourself in the creativity of streamlined workspaces including the improved multi-track timeline. Create a huge range of video projects from action-cam and personal videos to slideshows video blogs screen recordings stop motion animation and much more. Whether creating for YouTube or DVD business or pleasure VideoStudio Pro X7 makes it simple and fun to bring your video vision to any screen.
profile.reviewText:
As a hobby, my buddies and I started a youtube channel devoted to gaming and each of us (crew of five) have editing software of some kind.  I use Final Cut Pro X (FCPX) on my MacBook Pro as does our executive producer while the other three use Windows and, unfortunately with the updates from 7-X making it incompatible with Windows, they have to use other software for editing.  We were thinking of acquiring a few licenses for Adobe Premier as some of us had used it before, but were very fortunate to be able to try Corel VideoStudio Pro X7 and Ultimate Edition (see ultimate edition for related review).

Our co-producer and primary screenwriter tested Corel Pro and, after a month of use he has produced several video prototypes that look almost as good as FCPX albeit with some missing features that are in the Ultimate Edition.

Our screenwriter (Barnard) noted that the editing interface was incredibly comprehensive with your standard storyboard tools and clip editor very similar to FCPX.  He loves the selection of transitions, text editor, features generator (blank screens, shapes, etc.), and much more but laments that it lacks the smooth streamlined feeling of Final Cut.  Perhaps it was his older computer (Windows Vista, yick!) but he did notice a few moments of technical delays and lacking smoothness of operation.  Oh well.

All in all, Corel Pro is good for any amateur filmmaker or personal creating fun family videos that doesn't want to shell out well over $1000 in Mac products for industrial quality.
profile.summary: Quality AV for those Who Cannot Afford Mac Products

profile.description: Eight, elite U.S. Army soldiers are battle ready and at your command in Full Spectrum Warrior. Commissioned by the U.S. Army, this highly realistic combat title features authentic tactical and combat maneuvers, implementation of U.S. Army doctrine, immersive combat environments and incredible AI to bring scenarios to life!
profile.reviewText:
I've always been fascinated with military Spec Ops and the units thereof since I was a kid, and when I read the specifications on Full Spectrum Warrior, I was rather excited to purchase it once it reached the Platinum Hits list.  I picked it up and was pleased with several things while disapointed with others.

I give FSW a 3.8 out of 5.

This is not your typical military game.  Up until a few years ago, US gamers were bombarded with so-called tactical games and first-person shooter games like Delta Force, Doom 3, Counter-Strike and Unreal Tourny.  While these games are extraordinarily fun to play, they lack in realism to the point where you can run in a room guns'a blazing and survive multiple shots while loading your firearm.

FSW takes that concept and turns it upside down.  Now, instead of charging your enemies, you outflank them or you get shot.  This concept is very repetative throughout FSW, but the whole point is to teach you how urban close-quarter battler (CQB) works.  Veterans of Counter-Strike, Unreal or Doom 3 may not like this game because of its slow gameplay and repetitive gameplay, however, military enthusiasts will appreciate the realism applied to the concept of FSW.  So, the pros and cons.

One big downside is the lack of control over the individual units, meaning you cannot shoot their weapons for them unless it's an explosive round.  You may, however, set up individual fire zones, which can save you from being flanked.  But the lack of control still adds a sense of boredom and frustration as a target could be just ducking and shooting behind a wall and when he pops his head out, your men will probably miss over and over until the tango grenades you.

The graphics, for its time, is very smooth.  I loved the details in the weapons and the environment, however, graphics do not make a game.  The story is somewhat propaganda in nature since it seems to praise military intervention of dictators, something that not everyone can agree with, however, this does not take anything away from the game but is worth noting.

Other than that, I loved it.  I love having to actually think really hard about my every move, the game is not really challenging, but the guys with RPGs make me keep my head down.
profile.summary: For Military Enthusiasts, Not Counter-Strike or Unreal Fans

profile.description: Juliet (Academy Award-winner Hilary Swank, Million Dollar Baby), a beautiful doctor, has found the perfect New York apartment to start a new life after separating from her husband. It's got spacious rooms, a spectacular view, and a handy, handsome landlord. But there are secrets behind every wall and terror in every room as Juliet gets the unnerving feeling that she is not alone. She is being watched. She is being stalked. And no one is safe when she discovers the relentless horror on her doorstep. But how do you stop an evil that you can't see...until it's too late? Jeffrey Dean Morgan (Grey's Anatomy) and screen legend Christopher Lee (The Lord of the Rings) costar in this pulse-pounding shocker from famed horror studio Hammer Films (Let Me In).
profile.reviewText:
I'm always up for a good thriller but it seems as though all the good ideas have been used up already and those that have been done are mediocre.  The Resident is somewhat of the latter as it was a novel idea but executed with a half effort.

The Resident is a relatively unique idea for the story as it revolves a creepy stalker renting out a room.  This is nice in that it proves that watching someone sleep with dreamy eyes is NOT romantic, it's being a stalker (You hear that Twilight fans?  It's not cute!  It's called stalking!!).  It brought about some moments of tension but they didn't last long and they were few and far in between.  The film didn't quite grab me the way I wanted to.

Don't get me wrong; Swank, Morgan, and Lee were great as they have always been.  It truly was an all-star cast with a two-time academy award winner, The Comedian, and a Bond villain.  Problem is that a film is like a sports team in that you can't win just on the talent of a few participants.  Without the proper production crew The Resident just didn't quite cut it.

All in all, The Resident is a rental at best.  Sex scene wasn't even that gratifying.  :P
profile.summary: Not Bad, Not Great Either

profile.description: In-Ear, Apple Control Talk - Octagon
profile.reviewText:
Been using a high-end pair of JBL headphones for the past year and have loved them to where I didn't think I would need a new pair anytime soon.  Unfortunately, life happens or, more specifically, a friend's cat with an appetite for mayhem.  When I had the opportunity to try the Monster Octagon set, I reluctantly gave them a shot and have been very satisfied since.

The inner-ear fit seems a little counter-intuitive as they appear to be uncomfortable but, once I figured out what ear size I was (large) from the multiple sizes enclosed, I was pleasantly surprised at just how comfortable the set was.  With the inner-ear fit, the buds stay very snug and secure to prevent them from falling out during normal movement or exercising not to mention they don't cause skin irritation such as ear buds that wrap around the ear rubbing up against the hard cartilage of the ear.  After hours of usage I felt no discomfort at all.

As for sound quality, while they are slightly bass heavy (as one would expect from Monster), the overall sound quality is pretty good.  Not as good as my old pair of JBLs, but pretty good for the price and they certainly aren't the bass-only sound one expects from Beats.  The headphones also seem to eliminate most outside sounds so, while not as noise-canceling as a pair of Bose, they still drown out enough sounds to be used effectively.

Pertaining to the microphone and control set, I noticed that everyone are making their controls compatible almost exclusively with the Apple iOS whereas I have Android (Samsung Note 3).  While I was able to make and take phone calls with the recipient not noticing any detriments to our conversation from the headset, I was only able to pause/play music and not scroll through as I would if I had an iPhone.  I really wish manufactures like Monster, JBL, and Klipsch would make their equipment Android friendly as well given us Android fans are the other half of the market.  My only real ding to the product but a minor one.

All in all, great value headphones in terms of functionality and comfort but I wish they were more Android friendly and a little less bass emphasis.
profile.summary: Good Sound, Fit, and Very Comfortable

profile.description: Michael is avoiding phone calls regarding his dear friend and former lover Chris who is dying back in America. While trying to write, he is disturbed by the noisy surfers next door as they get ready for a weekend away of surf. C.K., one of the surfers, remains behind to surf the local beach. At the beach cafe for lunch with his old friend Angus, Michael again avoids discussing Chris back in America. Angus catches Michael watching C.K. on the beach and teases him but Michael denies any interest in the surfer. Left on his own, Michael watches C.K. catch a series of waves. After a big wave and a wipe out, C.K. disappears in the surf. Michael looses site of C.K. until he sees him on the beach taking off his wetsuit before he heads back home. Michael remains on the beach then makes his way home. Once inside his house, Michael sees C.K. walking towards him on his way to the living room where he makes himself at home. Michael does not know why the surfer is in his house but before the night is over he will discover more about himself than he may have been ready for. Dan Castle
profile.reviewText:
I'm always up for a good story when it comes to movies and The Visitor certainly is no exception.  It's a classic tale of East meets West against the backdrop of our War on Terror and Immigration Policy (such as it is).

The story is simple, yet elegant.  A ROAD (Retired On Active Duty) college professor is just surviving life.  He teaches only one class, rarely works on his book, considers reading a book "co-authoring," and just cannot seem to find his niche in life.  His life changes dramatically when he is forced to attend a conference in NYC to discover strange guests residing in his summer apartment.  I won't give away the rest but the rest of the movie addresses our immigration policy and how we treat illegal immigrants and refugees.

Despite the story's simplicity, it flows fairly well and is quite compelling.  Between the initial friction of the stranger's girlfriend and the professor, the musical tastes of the stranger, and how the professor finds redemption in the most unlikely way (sorry guys, get the movie if you wanna know the rest *RASPBERRY*), the audience has plenty of elements to become involved with and feel a personal connection in some way.

Now, some people I watched The Visitor with had some concerns over the preachiness of the movie itself involving our immigration policy since the majority of the film focuses around the injustice of how we, as a nation, treat detained illegal immigrants.  I agree that the movie is preachy to a certain degree, however, I can also see how The Visitor is also a critique on how we treat refugees (although some will argue there is not difference).  If anything, illegal immigrants escaping Senegal and Syria can be considered political refugees given the volatile situations there now.

Either way, at least the film doesn't distinguish between party lines like many in Hollywood have in recent years, which alienates audiences.  They just distinguish between immigrants/refugees and naturalized citizens.

Now, on to the technical aspects.

The musical accompaniment was lovely.  I don't remember exactly the names of the composers but there was a great deal of classical music and piano works.  While it is almost exclusively public domain selection, it fits perfectly in the scenes whether it's the mother of the stranger cleaning the apartment (which was surprisingly a beautiful scene), or the professor slumping to dinner at his home in Connecticut.

The camera work was non-distracting, which is always a plus.  I cannot stand it when directors try "new" things and end up ruining it for the rest of us.  As far as camera and editing goes, it was very nondescript, which is the way it should be for simplistic movies.  This is not to demean the film; it actually pulled off a simplistic, yet elegant, performance.

All in all, The Visitor is an excellent movie.  It was much better than I anticipated it would be.  I would recommend this for anyone seeking a good drama, a film on multi-culturalism, or need an uplifting tale of a down-and-out man finding redemption.  A- all the way!!
profile.summary: A Tale of Two Worlds... in New York City

profile.description: The ultimate workbench is here! Over 72 pieces of tools, nuts and bolts. Pretend to carve your own wooden baseball bat with the spinning lathe. Pretend to nail down everything with your Power Nailer, which powers up to create realistic sound and has light up feature. Clamp down your projects with the side vise clamp. Layout your tools on the hanging hooks, extended side table, pull down bins and low level shelf. Get ready for some hard work - Workman style!WORKMAN tools look and feel just like the real thing! These realistic tools are rugged, fun and safe for play for ages 3 and up. Heavy duty 72-piece workbench with working tools! Comes with spinning lathe, working grinder and wood working tools Includes realistic B/O Light & Sound Nail Gun Comes with saw, hammer, wrenches, 32 nuts & bolts, 4 tool hangers & more! Plenty of storage area A great, creative learning toy for young builders! Batteries included in power tools.
profile.reviewText:
Do it yourself (DIY) projects are a great way to maintain self-sufficiency and become aware of your home's needs - establishing the importance of DIY at an early age is essential to raise our children to become less reliant on others and more independent.  As such, the Lanard Workman Ultimate Workbench is a great teaching tool in showing kids the basic principles of measuring, tool safety, and the overall importance of DIY.  While the bench itself is great to look at and shows great promise (my fianc kept trying to open the box prematurely and hog it for herself), the overall durability of the workbench is questionable and doesn't really give the person projects to do beyond using one's imagination.

The workbench comes with a toy lathe, nail gun, workbench, nuts and bolts, and a cardboard backdrop that takes about 15-20 minutes to assemble depending on your vision (instructions are very small print).  The lathe is electric in that it lights up, spins, and makes a loud noise.  My first concern with this was safety as a child could get something stuck in there (real life lathes can be quite hazardous to limbs if not operated properly).  I tested the strength of the lathe by trying to get a standard necktie stuck in it to see how much it could pull from a small child.  To my relief, the lathe immediately locks up if any light pressure or resistance is applied so I can rest well knowing children will not lose fingers in it.

As for the electric nail gun... well, we wore out the batteries before getting the set to the rightful test subjects as it makes a cool gun noise and lights up and everything (where were these things when I was growing up in the 80s?!).  However, no real safety concerns there, either.  As for the remainder of the workbench kit, there are no real metal or wooden parts, just safety plastic and, while this is a plus for safety, there is little to do for children over the age of 7.  The lathe has a baseball bat embedded on it and you only get a few nuts and bolts to play with, everything else is left to your imagination.  For our test subjects, a 7 and 9 year old pair of brothers, the 7 year old was able to enjoy pretending he was a grownup while the 9 year old wanted something more.  The cutoff is obvious.

Another interesting note from our test subjects is that the durability doesn't last very long.  The backdrop will easily be the first to go with the electric parts next and one can simply feel them to discern that much.  In short, these are NOT long-term toys by any stretch.  They are great for educational value but require more stuff to do other than use one's imagination and need to be built stronger.
profile.summary: DIY For Kids (While the Durability Last)

profile.description: The highly anticipated family comedy The Smurfs 2 is now a video game! The evil wizard Gargamel has created the Naughties, who kidnap Smurfette from Smurfs Village and imprison her in Paris. It's now up to the Smurfs to travel from the Enchanted Forest, through the busy streets of New York, into Paris, and everywhere in between to save the day and bring Smurfette home safe!
profile.reviewText: Truth be told, there hasn't been a decent movie-inspired game release since Spider-Man 2 for the PS2 (2004) and the last one before that was Goldeneye for the N64 back in the 90s. Such games are designed to be copy/paste mash-ups from other games without any real thought put into them. The developers then slap their names on it, place the trademark logo and themes in it, and hear the almighty sound of "chu-ching!" I was not expecting to be enthralled by Smurfs 2, a disappointing sequel to an OK children's movie, when I had the opportunity to review it. HOWEVER, as Cooking Mama always encouraged me to do, I sucked in my expectations and gave it my best effort... and lasted all of five hours before running away screaming with the Smurf's chant stuck in my head (la, la, la, la, la, laaa!) and it's the games fault! The game is very basic as most film-games usually are. Smurfs 2 is a side-scrolling adventure game similar to Mario 2 as you can choose the character you wish to play as each level, each with their own semi-unique abilities. As you progress through the levels, you will combat and defea-... er... "rescue" woodland creatures under the spell of that old creeper Gargamel. Similar to Mario 2, and every other side-scrolling game there is, the player must avoid obstacles and hostile characters to reach the other side of the level and the points are tallied. Pretty straight forward. Problem though is that Smurfs 2 suffers from a series of issues that have been resolved in previous games that this one is obviously copy/pasted from. It was enough to keep me cursing (albeit subbing all known curse words with "smurf!") much to the amusement of my friends listening in on XBox Live party chat. Now, I realize that this is a kids game designed for gamers MUCH younger than this 30-year-old with salt and pepper hair, but there is a point where developers get lazy in hopes to cash in on the child's familiarity of the franchise combined with the amazing power of, "MOMMY, I WANT IT!!" Gross mistakes get overlooked and the game gets sniffed by the general audience. Let us begin. The first thing that frustrated me were the voices. One of the problems with utilizing quick quips from voice actors for a good smirk is that it doesn't take long for those same quotes to get painstakingly annoying as they get repeated more than political campaign slogans during an election year. This is especially true if you prefer to use one character over another, as I utilized Clumsy-Smurf for his double-jump ability until I unlocked Brainy-Smurf's much more refined version, and had to mute the voices entirely as I kept hearing the same quotes over and over. On top of that, the voices, aside from the narrator, seemed anything but genuine and much less believable. Didn't seem as though the voice actors were even trying. Next was the scoring system and bonuses. In short, they're worthless unless you want to get all the achievements (bleep, bloop!). The Smurfberries act as a life gauge... sort of, as it doesn't matter how many you have as one hit from any hostile will deplete your supply completely and, if you get hit again with no Smurfberries in tow, you restart the level. You get scored on how many Smurfberries and coins you have in your inventory at the end of the level, but only help the player complete challenges and achieve high scores... which lost their luster with online gamerscore and leaderboards. Not to mention few gamers will take to XBox Live to show off their Smurfberry collection. If the scores helped unlock abilities and characters to give the player an edge, they'd retain some importance but they don't. Coins help "rescue" other smurfs, but serve no purpose other than loitering around the village. The only way to unlock new characters to play as is to defeat stage bosses like a giant burping toad, Azrael, and Gargamel. Oh, and there's a Smurfberry multiplier when you build up water vials, which are secured by "rescuing" creatures. Once you build up enough vials, the traditional Smurf chant begins to play on five-second repeat and Smurfberries are worth double. Two problems here. One, the music will make you neurotic as my friends on Live STILL love to torment me with that stupid song. The second is that with the points being worthless and you lose everything when hit anyway, the multipliers are pointless to achieve unless you are going for 100% gamerscore completionist. I won't criticize the game for it's patronizing tutorials and extremely easy boss fights as this game is obviously tailored towards children. My guess is the age range is between 3-8 at best and no higher unless you're a very brave parent playing alongside your kids with your trusty ear plugs. All in all, the game is grossly simplistic, boring, lackluster, tedious at times, really easy at others, and the Smurf chanting will send any sane person into a head-slam-into-wall frenzy after an hour of gameplay. Yup, definitely a game for children. Parents, watch your own risk. If I were to make a better recommendation, I would point towards Rayman Legends as it is a vastly superior game that even I enjoyed thoroughly.
profile.summary: What the Smur, Mate?:  A Smurf-Load of Problems Keeps this Game on the Kid's Shelf

profile.description: From Jerry Bruckheimer, producer of PIRATES OF THE CARIBBEAN, and Jon Turteltaub, director of PHENOMENON, comes NATIONAL TREASURE. It's the thrilling, edge-of-your-seat adventure starring Academy Award(R) winner Nicolas Cage (1995 Best Actor, LEAVING LAS VEGAS) as Benjamin Franklin Gates. Ever since he was a boy, Gates has been obsessed with finding the legendary Knights Templar Treasure, the greatest fortune known to man. As Gates tries to find and decipher ancient riddles that will lead him to it, he's dogged by a ruthless enemy (Sean Bean, THE LORD OF THE RINGS trilogy) who wants the riches for himself. Now in a race against time, Gates must steal one of America's most sacred and guarded documents -- the Declaration of Independence -- or let it, and a key clue to the mystery, fall into dangerous hands. Heart-pounding chases, close calls, and the FBI turn Gates's quest into a high-stakes crime caper and the most exciting treasure hunt you've ever experienced.
profile.reviewText:
Even though the days of the Adventure genre has been slow somewhat lately, taken over by the more serious side of action and military films, some great adventure films come out that make us feel energized at the end.  From the director of Pirates of the Caribbean comes another adventure of epic proportions.

Meet Ben Franklin Gates, an ecentric "treasure protector" on the quest to find the treasure of the Free Masons, supposedly the treasure of all treasures.  Taking on the tradition of six generations, Gates squares off against burning boats in the artic, a restless FBI task force, a ruthless thief, a yelling archivist and plenty of skepticism in the academic community.  Teamed up with the nerdy, feeling left out sidekick Riley, they go quickly from clue to clue trying to find the treasure, but even they get skeptical as to whether the treasure is real or just a legend to fool the British during the American Revolution.

Despite many historical inaccuracies to make the history tie into the movie, it is still a history lesson about the founding fathers and does bring out the American spirit while watching.  I remember emerging from the theatre, wanting to go on my own adventure again just like when I was in elementary school.  The action is pretty good, but not too violent, in fact it's hardly violent at all.  It also has no profanity so all ages can watch it.

The DVD features arn't bad at all.  Buena Vista tried a concept I've never seen before; it's called multilevel treasure hunt, where the more you watch in the special features, the more clues you get to access more special features.  It was cool at first and took me one try to figure out the puzzle.

I watched the alternate ending and I'm glad they kept the ending that's actually in the movie, the trimming was well done after seeing the deleted scenes.  The animatic opening had some interesting parts about the Templars that were actually more intriguing and historically accurate than the movie itself, so they could've done some work there.

Overall, with the historical inaccuracies, I'd give National Treasure a 4.5.  Defintely worth getting when it comes out on May 3rd with the cool special features.
profile.summary: It's About Time We Had Another Adventure!

profile.description: Professional black padfolio with leather-like cover and sleek flexible design takes you through the year in style. Contains one refillable note pad with undated, graphed sheets for notes and room for up to 8 tasks with check-off boxes. Copper accent rivets add sophistication and style. Notes pad has perforated sheets for easy, clean removal. Flap pocket on the inside front cover holds loose sheets. 12.25 x 9.25 x .25 inches overall.
profile.reviewText:
As a hopeful aspiring filmmaker hoping to one day go pro I go to a lot of meetings and take even more notes... or, at least, my lady/assistant does.  I just do the scheduling.  One of the largest challenges to me is note taking and planning as we have to schedule personnel, prop acquisition, location scouting and securing, casting, etc. and that's a hefty task if you don't have a full staff at your disposal.  Note taking is critical to maintain cohesion and any form of order in a project and the LAST thing one should be worried about is what they're taking notes on.

I've used the AT-A-GLANCE meeting planner and loved that and, having tested the Padfolio, I can safely say that it's OK.  It's built durable like any other AT-A-GLANCE product but the pages seem more graph paper with "notes" printed on the top, as if the company had a paper surplus and used it to make this product.  Don't get me wrong, the binding is superb and it's what we needed, but it just didn't wow me like other AT-A-GLANCE products.  The layout could be a lot more friendly for notes but it seems more suitable for basic sketching.

profile.description: Forget everything you've ever seen in a serial killer movie and get ready for the chiller that stunned festival audiences around the world: Notorious murderer Garrick Turrell (AJ Bowen of HOUSE OF THE DEVIL and HATCHET II) has escaped from police custody and resumed his killing spree. His former girlfriend Sarah (Amy Seimetz of ALEXANDER THE LAST) is a recovering alcoholic trying to put her life back together in a new town with a new man (Joe Swanberg of NIGHTS AND WEEKENDS). Her past continues to haunt her. And now her ex-boyfriend is leaving a trail of slaughter in his hunt to find her. From Adam Wingard, the director of the award-winning film POP SKULL and screenwriter Simon Barrett (DEAD BIRDS) comes the movie experience that is emotionally raw, disturbingly graphic and brutally real. Prepare yourself for A HORRIBLE WAY TO DIE.
profile.reviewText:
Usually, at least in theory, photography doesn't make a film or make it great... but it sure as hell can ruin it.  First things first though.

I went into A Horrible Way to Die thinking it was going to be another torture porn film with enough blood and guts to make John Carpenter blush and Uwe Boll actually retire knowing he couldn't sink any lower.  Let's face it, it's next to impossible for horror filmmakers to create anything truly unique anymore as almost every horror film seems to give direct homage, whether intentional or not, to a predecessor or two.  Director Adam Wingard, with unforgettable(??) titles like Home Sick and Pop Skull, attempts something new by portraying an escaped serial killer tracking down his ex-girlfriend... who is also a recovering alcoholic.  Wingard depicts the serial killer sympathetically as even the character seems haunted and remorseful of his actions but... keeps on doing it anyway (Mr. Brooks, anyone?).

An interesting idea given we're force-fed nothing but over-the-top torture porn with no reason other than to satisfy a disgusting appetite for grotesque imagery.  In fact, the film seems to go out of its way to keep things pretty tame and power to Wingard for it.  You also get a certain sense of connection to the couple being trailed by the killer and hope nothing bad comes to them.

However, despite my praise to the story and screenplay, going back to the camerawork... it just ruined everything.  I have never felt so seasick in my life as the camerawork was so shakey that I literally had to ingest some Dramamine to keep my balance.  Realistic shots, like those from Paranormal Activity or Black Hawk Down are a nice touch, but too much can confuse the viewer if not make them sick.  The plot would literally pass me by because I was nauseated by the camera jumping about like a pinball.

The cameras were also constantly out of focus if not downright blurry.  Perhaps this was intention to keep the gore and violence level tame, but all it did was make an already nauseous audience more confused and sick.  It's almost as if the film took the bold move of NOT including the audience.  It ruined the movie.

All in all, Horrible Way to Die had great potential but was lost on really shoddy camerawork, whether intentional or not.  How the film festivals gave the film awards is beyond me.
profile.summary: A Horrible Way to Film a Movie *Dramamine NOT Included*

While red swing line staplers are the thing in office circles these days, there are other products out there worthy of testing and the Rapesco certainly held up to standard and then some.

profile.description: Make delicious waffles just the way you like them using the Oster Titanium Infused DuraCeramic Flip Waffle Maker. This waffle maker is designed with a unique and innovative DuraCeramic nonstick coating that lasts eight times longer and cooks up to 30 percent faster than standard nonstick coatings. The safe and natural ceramic coating is PFOA- and PTFE-free, won't flake or peel, and easily wipes clean, so you can cook foods without worry. This flip waffle maker distributes batter evenly within the plates, cooking your waffles to perfection. Adjustable temperature control lets you accurately set the cooking temperature, so you can easily make light, fluffy waffles or crispy, golden ones. The waffle maker stores vertically, offering efficient, space-saving storage.
profile.reviewText:
My last waffle maker was a hand me down from a time when small appliances had names ending in "o-matic" and were a shade of color one typically associates with the 1980s.  In short, it was old and was LONG overdue for a replacement.  My buddies and I were looking for a better waffle maker and jumped to the chance to try out the Oster.

Now, bear in mind that my buddies and I are confirmed, but hardly eligible, bachelors with as much culinary skills as a 17 year-old recruit on the grill line at McDonalds.  For us, the fine combination of milk and cereal for our daily breakfast is a challenge best left to the professionals.  Problem is two-fold as we A) are sick of eating out for breakfast and B) want something else for our morning meal other than cheap cereal that comes in a generic bag.

The Oster suited our needs very well as, for it's reasonable price, we got something that is easy enough to use without utilizing whatever braincells we have left and is safe to use.  The instructions were not translated from two forms of Chinese or Klingon so they were easy to understand as was the actual operation of the device.  The device is very simple; plug in, pour batter, close lid, turn over, wait for light, remove waffle, feel semi-smart for not burning self, dance in joy, repeat as your hunger necessitates.  One of the handier features is the indication light that alerts the user when the waffles are done as it turns off when it's time to feast.  The sensor on the Oster is very consistent as we've made dozens of waffles with it and the results have always been good and not burnt.

The Oster also cooks very fast and requires little time to power up.  We were able to start making waffles within a few minutes of plugging in and that speed increased once it got up to speed.  This makes creating bulk waffles for larger families easier.

The one thing I wish Oster would address is the steam release.  I got a steam burn the first time I used the Oster as steam escaped the device just below my hand.  After that, I was careful to keep my hands away from that certain spot, but many people may inadvertently find it the same way I did and get burned.  Just be mindful of the steam release and keep your hands away from the device when you turn it over.

Other than that, the Oster is a worthy addition to any kitchen.  It's no super-expensive Kitchenaide that would maker Gordon Ramsay blush, but it does its job well effectively and efficiently.
profile.summary: Easy to Use, Reliable, Effective, With Minor Faults

profile.description: Speed from the streets of Gotham to the floors of your home with the Batman vs. Superman Official Movie Replica RC Batmobile! Its authentic design features incredible brushed metal detail, mechanical turret and responsive linkage steering. Light up the night with 4 powerful front mounted LEDs that directionally track wherever you steer. Its rear after-burner LED glows as you hit the throttle for an incredible burst of speed. The Batmobile is highly manoeuvrable delivering precise and long distance control with 2.4GHz communication. When being stored in the Bat Cave, you can easily re-charge the Batmobile via its USB rechargeable battery. Hold on tight for the most powerful ride of your life with the Batman vs. Superman Official Movie Replica RC Batmobile - Only from Air Hogs!
profile.reviewText:
I have loved Air Hogs' products in the past as they typically blend good quality RC rigs with a price us mere mortals and non-hobbyists can afford.  The Batmobile Air Hogs is OK so long as the vehicle isn't stuck in forward, which only happened a few times but enough to be noticeable.

The controls are meh, pretty basic but the speed and response of the rig itself isn't bad at all.  I actually got some decent enjoyment out of the Batmobile, especially tormenting the cat, but I ultimately took it to work as my coworkers love driving the thing around.  The design of the Batmobile is pretty sturdy as it has survived collisions with desks, chairs, people. a bewildered boss, etc.

profile.description: URBAN ARMOR GEAR products reflect the independent spirit of our designers and represent a dedication to superior quality and craftsmanship. Our feather-light composite cases feature a hard outer shell and a soft impact resistant core. Although visually striking, the unique shape of the case also provides strength while minimizing size and weight. Our design allows full access to your device’s controls and ports, while openings are designed for glare-free flash snapshots and uncompromised audio. The marriage of these design elements and materials working in unison maximizes protection for your device. UAG cases are available in an array of vibrant colors. There is a twelve month manufacturer warranty on each case.
profile.reviewText:
I have always come to depend on UAG for their extremely simple, yet rugged cases and their clear-case for the Samsung S6 Edge is just another example of UAG living up to their reputation.

The case fits on very tightly, as one would expect, and the acrylic materials provide excellent flexibility to get the device in but still exert excellent protection.  The clear coating with black trimming looks really good with the white S6 so I wouldn't recommend it for the black sapphire.

Also, unlike most cases, the UAG does not interfere with the buttons so, while it may seem stiff at first, one can still operate the buttons with ease and not worry about any "runoff" and, by that, I mean having your fingers accidentally hit other buttons while touching the home button.  One of my biggest gripes on open-faced cases is that the case overlaps onto the screen too much so when you hit the home button you repeatedly hit another button cause you have to hover half your thumb over the case.

All in all, the UAG is an excellent case and the clear is perfect for the white S6.
profile.summary: As Rugged As One Would Expect From UAG

profile.description: About Lific: Lific emphasizes quality and practicality without sacrificing fashion and design | Make a splash: Make a bold fashion statement with your phone or choose to blend in | The Mighty Card Defense has color options to match any occasion or mood | Installation: Point a corner of the phone into the case and snap your Galaxy Note 5 case into place
profile.reviewText:
The Lific Mighty Card Case is a good case but not my personal favorite of all that I have tested.

The Mighty Card case fits on nicely and held the Note 5 in place and provides decent protection against the elements whether it be normal wear and tear and drops.  The color was more suited for my friend who tried it, but she had no complaints.  The inside flap for cards, however, is small and compact, meaning it can hold 1-2 cards at most and, even then, it's still a pretty tight fit.  This case would complete the package if it were a folio design with an external flap to cover the front.  I'd recommend a nice glass screen protector to compliment this one.

All in all, a good case but the card holder is too tight for my liking.
profile.summary: Tight But Quite Right

profile.description: The M-Pact Fingerless glove has been designed to combine the utmost dexterity with critical impact resistance for jobs big and small. Sonic welded Thermal Plastic Rubber (TPR) safeguards your knuckles while impact absorbing XRD palm padding reduces shock and vibration associated with hand tools. For comfort, we used form-fitting TrekDry material to help keep your hands dry and comfortable on long workdays. When you need the control of bare hands without sacrificing protection, reach for the M-Pact Fingerless.
profile.reviewText:
For my day job I work as a merchandiser for a big soda company and, as such, I pull between 12-24 pallets a day and over 10,000lbs of product.  Doesn't sound like much but the constant lifting of product in cardboard boxes and dirty pallet jacks wear tremendously on one's hands and the risk of having your fingers smashed is always present.

I used to wear cheap carpenter's gloves that did OK for a while but they didn't provide adequate protection for my knuckles or decent grip.  I've always heard good things about Mechanix gloves from a very diverse group of people from carpenters, laborers, and even members of the US Armed Forces, who use them as shooter's gloves.  Good enough for me!

I settled for the Mechanix M-Pact finglerless gloves and, after three months of constant use, I found that they work wonderfully in some areas but not so much in others.

Pros:  What I like most is that they fit well.  I am 6'5 with proportionately sized hands so I use 2XL gloves and they fit great.  They feel tight at first but only took two days before they felt like another extension of my hands.  I also like how the rubber finger and knuckle guards protect my hands from impact damage (hence the name) as my hands get hit by product daily.  The underside material helps grip product fairly well and makes pulling pallets a lot easier.

Cons:  However, there are two issues I have with the gloves the first being insulation/smell.  The gloves feel air-tight and my hands sweat a lot as a result.  After the massive sweating my hands begin to smell as do the gloves necessitating regular washing, and they seem to do well in the washer (I wash them separately with no detergent or bleach).  The best solution is constant cleaning and get multiple pairs.  Like shoes, you should never wear the same pair everyday to keep the wear down.

My other complain is the velcro strap as it went out in less than a month.  It worked great at first but now they do not hold at all and I had to get used to the feeling that it was about to fall off since the strap is under and not over the wrist like most other gloves.  Again, this is alleviated by having multiple pairs to avoid accelerated wear.

All in all, the M-Pact gloves are a real deal as they provide great protection for your hands but at a VERY reasonable cost.
profile.summary: Laborer Approved but Recommend Several Pairs

profile.description: Sharp shooter looking for Samsung Galaxy S6 Edge cases? CandyShell Grip is the case for you. Taking our patented CandyShell protection and adding no-slip grips, this sleek case is perfect for getting the shot. CandyShell Grip's ridges run along the back and sides for a hold that's ideal for snapping pictures, plus one-handed and two-handed texting, gaming, shooting video and more with your Samsung Galaxy S6 Edge.
profile.reviewText:
Most ruggedized cellphone cases are either too bulky (Otterbox Defender, Lifeproof, etc.) or provide the worst possible traction possible (Otterbox Symmetry) as they can easily slip out of your hands or pocket.

Having worked with a LOT of cellphone cases, one of my favorite brands are Speck as they are military-grade, drop-tested, have excellent anti-heat and impact insulation, and sport some of the best rubber grips for the price.  The S6 case is no different as the grips provide fantastic traction on any surface including a vehicle dashboard, is easy to put on, is super tight with the S6 inside it (which you want), and the buttons are not restricted by the case itself.

The dragon green color is an interesting choice, one that only seems to work well with the black sapphire S6 cool and not so much with the white or gold colors.

profile.summary: Sturdy, Rugged, and Amazing Traction

profile.description: A secret military project endangers Neo-Tokyo when it turns a biker gang member into a rampaging psionic psychopath that only two kids and a group of psionics can stop.
profile.reviewText:
Well, this one was well thought out and planned.  And don't get me wrong, I am very pleased with the movie and am proud to have purchased it.  It's just the reason I give this movie 3 stars is because there were many unanswered question, and some things that could've been left out.
My question is:  Where on earth did all those kids go?  I know some hard core annime fans have their deadset opinions however I still don't quite get the idea.  All I know is that they went away and disapeared.  Is that all?  You know, that sets it up perfectly for a sequel, if there is any Tokoyo left to destroy that is, they certainly banged it up pretty good.
I'm also still confused on who started the nuclear war.  Most people point their fingers towards Akira however I really wonder about that.
And the stuff that could be left out is simple.  The language could've been better.  I'm not a goody two shoes however I expect a little bit of cleanliness in movies.  And the last thing was the scene where the bikers tore that girl's shirt off.  Not needed at all.  I'm glad they took that out in the director's cut.  Sexuality is never needed in a movie unless the circumstances have to permit it.
Overall, a great movie worth purchasing if you love annime.
profile.summary: I liked it a lot, but I did not love it.

profile.description: Sleek and lightweight, this Logitech H130 Stereo Headset is ideal for voice and video chat! profile.reviewText:
In this crazy world shoppers will halt all rational research and objectivity and will go positively bonkers when Wal-Mart offers product X for price Y with value Y being a price that would suggest the product is made from used asbestos, Soviet depleted uranium, and Chinese lead paint.  That said, I NEVER would have suspected that a respectable company like Logitech would follow that path.

The Logitech H130 headset proved as cheap as its price as I tried to use it for World of Warcraft since I can't quite afford a Turtle Beach headset yet. profile.description: Eliminate shampoo and conditioner bottles to make space in your shower by using the Zenna home double shower dispenser with caddy shelf. Provides convenient access to lotions, shampoos, soaps and other Liquid products. Natural push to Palm design dispenses just the right amount of Liquid into your Palm instead of your fingers. profile.reviewText:
This would've been a great product had it held up and, by that, I mean literally held up as it fell down after two months of being in the shower.  It worked well in the meantime, albeit the dispensers wouldn't work with anything with a moderate level of viscosity, but one night my wife and I awoke to a crash in the bathroom, causing me to spring from the bed, home defense weapon system (rolling pin) in hand ready to dispense in house justice on what I thought was either a home intruder or my really evil cat being herself.  After realizing what the crash was I picked up the pieces and examined what caused the crash; the adhesive strips lost complete cohesion and just ripped clean off the caddy leaving the strips on the wall for us to look at every day.

profile.description: Vietcong: Purple Haze takes you into the violence and danger that was Vietnam. Collects the original Vietcong and its sequel, Vietcong: Fist Alpha. Choose from six new weapons, attach bayonets to your rifle, and be on the lookout for attacks from fighter jets & B-52 bombers Join the battle online, on new multiplayer maps All-new campaign editor for fans looking to design their own maps, mods and missions
profile.reviewText:
I must admit, I did not play the PC version so I am not aware of all the stuff I am missing as other reviewers pointed out so bear with me here as I've only played the XBox version.

I found the weapon selection to pretty consistant with the weapons at the time, including some weapons many did not know where used in Vietnam such as the M1 Carbine or the Sterling SMG.  Of course, you eventually move up to the M16 and the M60, but you begin with the M14 as soldiers did in early 1967.  However, I with they would've had more scoped weapons such as the Remmington .30-6, which was an incredibly popular rifle amongst snipers.

I really liked the quick fight feature; it allowed me to get a handle for the weapons before emersing myself in the missions.  It's also fun during multi-player play when you have friends over or whatever.  The two big problems was that you cannot start with enemy weapons such as the NVA side-by-side shotgun, which I thought was a blast playing with.  Secondly, while you do get many options, I wish the enemies would spawn in random places rather than the same spot each time and you could have more enemies to fight.  I found the option "too many!" to be somewhat easy to take on.  I really like places where you're just being overwhelmed while on the defense.

Now the missions were incredibly short.  Some took me less than five minutes to complete.  Reading the reviews comparing the XBox to the PC version, I guess I got shortchanged and that leaves me a little miffed.  Not to mention the enemies can be either really clever or downright stupid.  Several times, I'll set up the squad to ambush a squad of NVA and several will not move while their comrades are being shot as by very loud rifles.  Other times, I'll take a shot at one NVA, he'll run around in circles, stop then resume his previous stance as if nothing happened.  "Must've been a misquito that causes this... hole in me."

Oh, and it seems as though many NVA and VC can take a LOT of hits before going down... or one arm hit and they go down.  It's very weird at times.

Now your squad can either be really handy or very stupid as well.  They're handy in the way if you have your medic (Crocker) and your engineer (Bronson) since one can heal you anytime while the other replentishes your ammo and they seem to be able to do this infinitely.  This can make the game too easy.  Your other squad members can be handy such as your pointman, that spots traps and ambushes but lets you do all the disarming and shooting.  The machinegunner... well, I never see him do anything.  Maybe he does, but I don't see it.

They do say random things during the mission, but usually profanities.  During one mission, one soldier said "f*ck you!" almost a dozen times in a row.  Now, I know combat brings out the vulgarity in people, but not only was it annoying that he said the same thing every time but a bit excessive.  If you're going to make him vulgar, at least mix it up a little.

My biggest beef with the squad is how they sometimes follow you and sometimes they stay put while you go ahead.  It's really annoying when you tell them to follow you, you go ahead, find yourself in a firefight and you turn around to discover they're still 100 meters behind you making smores by the fire having a gay ol' time.

However, this game was still very entertaining and worth purchasing.  Overall, a solid 75% game.  Nothing great, but still fun.
profile.summary: Had Potential, Still Fun to Play Though

profile.description: The Oral-B Deep Sweep 5000 Smartseries rechargeable electric toothbrush with Bluetooth is the worlds first of its kind with Bluetooth connectivity. Bluetooth communication allows the brush to connect with your smartphone to give you real-time feedback on your brushing habits. The Deep Sweep brush head features three bristles zones to reach deep to remove plaque, and 3D cleaning action sweeps side to side and pulsates to break up and remove up to 100% more plaque than a regular manual toothbrush. The pressure sensor lights up if you brush too hard to prevent harmful over-brushing and there are 5 modes and a timer to help you brush for a dentist-recommended 2 minutes. Best of all its brought to you by Oral-B  the #1 brand used by dentists worldwide. Compatible with the following replacement toothbrush heads: CrossAction, 3D White, Sensitive Clean, Precision Clean, FlossAction, TriZone, Deep Sweep, ProWhite, Ortho, PowerTip, and Dual Clean.
profile.reviewText:
Seems like everything has Bluetooth capabilities these days from my speakers, car starter, even my Samsung front-load washer and dryer are Bluetooth enabled (really helps multitasking), but WHO ever thought a toothbrush would need to be Bluetooth enabled is either a pure genius or an even more clever hacker.  When my Oral-B Deep Sweep 5000 (DS-5000) arrived, I was quite excited to try out a new gadget to show off to my eye-rolling lady but what I ended up getting was a near-security breach disguised as a really nice toothbrush.

Let's face it, you can easily purchase a really nice electric toothbrush for under triple digits so the only real reason for spending over that for the DS-5000 is it's BT capabilities and, after rooting around with it for a week, I can safely say that it's not worth it.  The app was the first thing I attempted to putz with before operating the actual toothbrush and when the app requested numerous permissions of which I was not comfortable with such as access to my SD card and calendar.  To me, this is a severe intrusion as even my BT enabled home theater and car stereo do not require that information.  This puts the user at an extreme risk of being hacked and, while unlikely, identity theft is the largest growing crime in the world and I don't want to be part of the statistic.  I strongly urge Oral-B to redesign what the app needs before unleashing such an open Trojan Horse even if their intentions were noble, which I believe they were.  It's just too high a risk and does NOT improve the overall experience.

If the app just allowed one to view what the sensors were reading WITHOUT needing access to my personal information, I would be OK with it otherwise it has NO business accessing my network or anything other than BT settings on my phone.

Now, as to the toothbrush itself, the DS-5000 is a solid machine that gets the job done as well as any other electrical toothbrush.  The triple bristles are very handy in getting gunk and other crap out of my teeth after meal and the motor seems strong enough to get the job done consistently over time.  Overall, it's a good toothbrush... but that app... can't get it out of my mind.

OK, I'm fixated on the app as it really bugs me.  I'd love to use the sensors to determine how to improve what I'm doing but I really can't stand it's seemingly intrusive nature and, no, I won't shut off whole features in my phone settings every time I run the app, that's stupid.

Overall, the DS-5000 could've been a REALLY good toothbrush if the app wasn't so intrusive.  You can get a similar toothbrush for less that doesn't invade your privacy.
profile.summary: Mouth: Secure (Phone, Not So Much and THAT Is A Problem)

profile.description: Introducing the Estes Syncro! The smallest Quadcopter in the World that's ready for action right out of the box. It's so small, it fits easily in the palm of your hand. It's so versatile, it can roll forward and backward and side to side. The included 2.4GHz radio gives you total control. The powerful LiPo battery lets you fly for an extra-long time and charging is easy. Just plug the included USB charger into your computer and you'll be flying in no time.
profile.reviewText:
I love flying quad drones and have two others I've been tinkering with.  I have a spiffy medium-quality drone that I practice with and a POS low-quality collector's item that came with my Prestige Edition of Call of Duty Black Ops 2.  I've always wanted a larger-scale, high quality drone for filming purposes and I've taken it upon myself to train on smaller versions before acquiring a large GoPro drone so this cute Nano quadcopter was a real treat to fly.

After opening the box I realized just how small this thing really is.  It really is just two by two inches and weighs less than most watches.  With this in mind, I feared it would lack stability as most average sized drones are highly susceptible to ANY kind of air flow from wind, air conditioning, breath too heavily, etc; however, the Nano actually holds it's own better than even my medium sized drone.  It only took around 15 minutes to charge the Nano with an easy to understand USB charger, whose red light will turn off when the Nano is fully charged (NOTE:  Be sure to remove the QC sticker on the charger first as THAT is where the light is... took me a few moments to figure that one out).  Syncing up the remote (requires 2 AAA batteries NOT INCLUDED), was as easy as flipping the switch and the Nano alerted me that it was ready for takeoff once the strobe lights on the body went from flashing to steady.

As I had done with other new drones I acquired, I carefully throttled up to test the Nano's power and then realized how much I underestimated its power by testing it on my desk with paper bills nearby, which were quickly dispersed.  Truth be told, the Nano displaces a LOT of air for such a small craft.  After allowing common sense to kick in and deciding to test it on a cleared off dining room table, I conducted a few test takeoff/landing maneuvers and was impressed at how well the gyroscope handles.  It's not perfect and probably will require anyone a few adjustments via the trim controls on the remote, but not bad for its size and price.

However, it was during the second in-flight trial that I noticed some issues the first being the fragility of the propellors.  Like any other operator testing out a new drone I accidentally knocked it into indoor obstacles most notably my barcalounger, kitchen island, girlfriend, etc.  Normally, this does not effect the open exposed propellors but, this time after hitting my couch, I attempted another takeoff since it landed right side up but it wouldn't achieve flight.  I walked over to examine it and realized a rotor was missing.  Thanks to the dark colored propellors and my carpet being white, it took only a few seconds to locate the missing piece.  I wondered if this was a common issue with the propellors falling off and conducted a few more "bump" tests and the parts came off 1/4 times after contact with a hard object even if the impact was marginal.  While the Nano comes with one complete replacement set of parts, it won't take long for more beginner to average pilots to lose all propellors if proper precautions aren't taken such as marking them with a pink marker (which is what I did) to make them easy to find.  They're sturdy enough but can easily be lost given their small size and how frequently they fall off.

I have yet to actually break this drone after two dozen flights and it feels a little sturdy with it's metal parts as opposed to the foam ones I'm used to, but I always worry I'm going to damage it beyond repair with each landing.  More tests may be needed but, after some lengthy testing, it's holding strong.

As for the ease of use, let me say this; drones are not easy to fly especially those under triple digit pricing.  They require constant adjustments and are super sensitive to any movements on the controller.  They are easy to use but very difficult to master and the Nano is no exception.  My girlfriend, a lady that just wanted to play with a flying toy, would fly the Nano from one side of the room to the other... in an attempt to stabilize it.  Like another other low-end drone, the operator must constantly make correct for air flow even in a seemingly still room to prevent it from veering.  It took me a few flights to get it to hover almost perfectly and, even then, precise landing required a few more practice runs.

All in all, I'd recommend the Nano to any beginner as it is an excellent trainer with it's short size, excellent stability, and very responsive nature.  Great place to start if you, like me, want to move up to the larger drones but not shell out a lot of $$ to do so... just be sure to mark the propellors with a bright colored marker before doing so!
profile.summary: Excellent Trainer Drone, Surprisingly Stable, But Not Without Limitations and Words of Caution

profile.description: The single-sided handle design of the FX352 is extremely comfortable and easy-to-grip. One side of the stainless steel frame has a CNC contour-machined G10 handle while the other side is the exposed frame. Deep thumb notching on the top of the blade, handle and frame adds even greater grip and control of the knife, helping to prevent accidental slipping. A 9Cr17Mov stainless steel blade will power through the toughest cutting jobs with ease and is easy to sharpen while still holding a great cutting edge. Thumb studs on both sides of the blade make one-handed opening easy; right or left handed. Backed by Coast's lifetime warranty against defects in materials and workmanship.
profile.reviewText:
This is the third Coast knife I have tested and, I gotta say, I'm not really impressed with Coast.  Tried the FX412 and FX414 and they were disappointing and little more than throw-aways.  Having tried the FX352 I'm definitely saying this is the better of the three but not by much.

Unlike the other two knives I tested, the FX352 has a belt clip and THAT makes all the difference in the world as the other two kept flopping around in my pocket with their heavy weight making them almost impossible to be considered a "pocket knife."  Despite it's shorter length (.5 inches shorter than the usual 4-inch blades), the FX352 feels more balanced than the other two.

However, this is where the good news ends as the FX352 no serration.  It's not that sharp to begin with and, without a serrated edge I'm limited on what else I can use the knife for.  While some people prefer no serration, I don't like being limited on what I can cut as it necessitates carrying another one.

Also, similar to the 412 and 414, the locking mechanism is too small to use if you have a tremor or large hands and, on top of that, it doesn't seem to always lock properly and that makes it a safety issue.

While the 352 is better than the other two Coast knives I tried, for the price I can get a superior Gerber knife that does more for me safely.  I'd recommend shopping around before trying this sucker out.
profile.summary: Better Than Other Coast Knives But Gerber is Still Better

profile.description: Just Dance and Disney are back together, bringing the greatest dance game for the whole family with music from the hottest Disney Channel shows, in Just Dance: Disney Party 2! Dance like the stars from the most popular Disney Channel shows and movies. With a great selection of family favorite songs, fun dances, and kid-friendly gameplay, children of all ages can dance along with family and friends.
profile.reviewText:
As a longtime veteran of Dance Dance Revolution and Dance Central, I thought I could haul my fat 32-year old posterior in front of the Xbox Kinect and show the non-emotional AI in Just Dance Disney 2 just who was the boss of dance.  I was horrible mistaken as the pale white skin hidden very carefully under my shirt came out and influenced my dance moves, which made Kevin James' character in Hitch look like he got moves like Jagger.

Needless to say, this kids game was anything but childs' play but that's not a bad thing, quite the opposite in fact.  While the songs are nothing but contemporary Disney with no classics (can you imagine dancing to (supercalifragilisticexpialidocious?"), this makes the game all the more appealing to kids that love Disney, thus they are exposed to a great entertainment medium that provides great exercise as those playing will do whatever they can to stay in sync with the beat.

The Kinect interface seems to work OK as the device accurately captures what the gamer is doing and the software interrupts it, unlike early Xbox 360 Kinect games *cough*SteelBattalion*cough*.  I'm not a fan of the music, but the kids in the apartment below us seemed to as it didn't take long for us to get a knock at the door... cause they recognized the music, not because I had the Klipsch volume set to 11.

All in all, if you have kids and a Kinect, then THIS is a great game to try to encourage exercise and just have fun... until Pokemon Go comes out.
profile.summary: No Classics?  Eh, No Problem!  Cute Game From an Aged DDR Veteran

profile.description: 100% SAMSUNG SDI Li-ion battery cells only top quality 3,000mAh power bank with detachable flashlight, ultra high charging speed 1.5A Max, triple safety protection technology, for smartphones, tablet PCs, Digital Cameras, Portable Speakers, Gopro and more (Green)
profile.reviewText:
I always try to keep a USB battery backup in my laptop in the event that I to charge my cellphone or smartwatch and I'm nowhere near an outlet or don't have the time.  I've had all kings of backups from your very basic to some that are solar-powered and, after months of working with the TSST, I can safely say it's somewhere in the middle.  The TSST is a battery backup/flashlight that requires you to switch the ends to go from one utility to the other as one cannot use both at once.

The TSST charges as well and efficiently as the others with no real discernible advantage, it's just average.  It is annoying, however, to have to flip around the ends in order to go from charger to flashlight.  This proved cumbersome, especially when I keep a Maglite on me that does the job more effectively .

This isn't to say the TSST isn't a good product, it's just average and doesn't distinguish itself from the rest.
profile.summary: Nifty Idea But Still Average

profile.description: "A 'Wilderness' Survival Guide for the beginning and established unit production managers." --Michael J. Hanly, II (Full Sail University)
profile.reviewText:
I'm working on a moderately-sized documentary film series on the history of the US military and, as a film fan knowing diddly squat about how to actually produce a film, Paula Landry's book has proven quite useful.  The only things I knew about movies coming into working on a fairly substantial film project is that I love movies and most people in Hollywood get it wrong... a lot.  As such, I really wanted to try my hand at it and learned very quickly just how complicated such an elaborate project really is.

Landry's book isn't just for the high school kiddies learning how to use Daddy's camera to make something no one will enjoy but for even those of us working on relatively moderate projects with long-term implications.  A lot of people are under the misconception that producing films mostly revolves around the actual production phase not realizing that the true magic goes into the organization and arranging phase (pre-production) and the editing, composition, and special effects phase after principle photography (post-production).  Landry's book highlights these critical phases (along with phase 3: PROFIT!) and gives enough basics on budgeting and organization to help just about any project.

Granted Landry's book is hardly the authoritative book on the subject but it has given me enough to think about and reference as I just had to balance and propose my equipment budget to potential investors, which is another thing Landry emphasizes.  This book and my experience so far has really given me a newly profound respect for the literally hundreds of people that are rarely praised for being a critical cog in the machine that is Hollywood... even if they usually get it wrong.
profile.summary: Proven Handy for Any Project

profile.description: Did you know Greek yogurt contains up to twice the amount of protein compared to traditional yogurt? Also, Greek yogurt is made by simply straining out liquid whey, so only the protein-rich whey solids remain. Everything you need to create Greek yogurt is included in this easy-to-use Oster CKSTYM1012 Mykonos Greek Digital Yogurt Maker. The Oster Mykonos Greek Yogurt Maker can produce one large batch or can be made as individual servings using the glass jars and lids provided. Recipes include the most popular varieties of milk from whole, reduced fat and skim - as well as soy and almond milk for vegan and lactose-free diets. Depending upon the type of milk used, cook time ranges from 10-12 hours. Cooking overnight or while you're away at work is recommended. In just a few easy steps, you can prepare fresh, homemade yogurt exactly how you like it and save money too! Making your own Greek yogurt at home can save up to 80% vs. store bought Greek yogurt per year. Includes yogurt maker with digital LCD display and timer function, set of 6 - 7oz. glass jars with lids, large 1 qt. plastic container/lid and Greek yogurt strainer. Pieces store neatly in unit. *Note for Customers Outside of North America. Some of our products use electricity for power. We sell electrical products that were made to work with 110V Electrical systems. If you live in a country that utilizes a different electrical system you may need to use a converter for these products to function. The act of using a converter automatically voids the warranty on these products.
profile.reviewText:
I will admit that I know next to nothing about healthier food alternatives other than what that one guy told me on Super-Size Me.  I see a lot of hubbub about Greek yogurt and how it's the greatest thing since the Hemsworth Brothers and I thought I'd give it a try.  I sampled some at the local grocery store while working my route and found the experience grossly underwhelming and a complete waste of money.

After telling my good friend Jim, a Yoga master and health-food 'terrorist' that always attempts to confiscate my Mountain Dew, about my experience in Greek yogurt he told me the wonders of making my own and hot I can tailor it to my liking.  Normally, I would dismiss Jim's lectures on health-food but I really wanted to make some sort of a healthy change in my life that didn't involve quitting caffeine.  When I had the opportunity to try out the Mykonos Greek Yogurt Maker, I jumped on it and, despite the initial frustrations of prepping it for the first time, I've been pretty happy with it.

I didn't know Jack-All about how to prepare Greek yogurt when the maker arrived from Amazon.  As such, when the product arrived I carefully went over the instructions to realize that additional ingredients were required, some of which I had no clue what they were.  After venturing to the nearest health food store and baffling the living bajeebies out of the clerk (imagine a 30-year old, 6'5 male laborer in a 2010 Sturgis Harley Davidson shirt and camouflage pants asking about making Greek yogurt), I picked up some yogurt starter, 2% milk, and a few other things.

The instructions were good in terms of explaining how to get started without making me feel like I needed to come in with a bachelors in sports health before I could turn the device on.  I also found some great recipes online that I wanted to try but decided to start by creating a basic formula without causing it to sprout legs and terrorize the Bismarck countryside thus giving Roger Corman more movie ideas (my experiments in tofu was how Sharknado started... don't ask me how).

I began to mix the ingredients and poured the mixture into the containers for cultivation.  Once the timer on my OTR microwave (it doesn't come with a timer as it seems to depict in the pictures) said it was time to try it, I nervously pulled out the containers and sampled my work.  It was OK, nothing special, but I didn't really add anything either.

I then took the Mykonos to the ultimate authority on health food, my mother, for further testing and a more objective trial.  She already had yogurt starter and began mixing Almond soy milk instead of 2%, threw in granola and chopped fruits, and made a considerably superior to my viscous goo that was beginning to sprout arms and become self-aware.

She commented on how the Mykonos was easier to use than other makers she possessed in the past in terms and didn't have the ugly aesthetics that some modern small appliances do have.  She has been using it since I brought it over and loves it as it allows her to make yogurt she likes, is within the limitations of her food allergies, and produces the same good results consistently... oh yeah, she won't give it back, either.  Sad face.

All in all, while I have no prior experience with yogurt making and, thus, cannot comment on other models, we were happy with the Mykonos and my mother still uses it for her own personal use and for entertaining equally health-conscious friends.
profile.summary: Efficient and Effective for Even Non-Health Food Nuts (Like Myself)

profile.description: A classic Disney animated fairy tale meets with the modern, live-action romantic comedy in Walt Disney Pictures ENCHANTED. Featuring an all-star cast, the film follows the beautiful princess Giselle (AMY ADAMS) as she is banished by an evil queen (SUSAN SARANDON) from her magical, musical animated land and finds herself in the gritty reality of the streets of modern-day Manhattan. Shocked by this strange new environment that doesn't operate on a happily ever after basis, Giselle is now adrift in a chaotic world badly in need of enchantment. But when Giselle begins to fall in love with a charmingly flawed divorce lawyer (PATRICK DEMPSEY) who has come to her aid -- even though she is already promised to a perfect fairy tale prince (JAMES MARSDEN) back home -- she has to wonder: can a storybook view of romance survive in the real world?
profile.reviewText:
I'll be blunt, I'm a stereotypical, young, male college student that enjoys films like Red Dawn, Rambo, The Rock and Aladdin.  In other words, you would NEVER expect me to go to the movie theatre, fork over X amount of money to go see Disney's Enchanted.  It was Thanksgiving and I was at my Mom's place away from college and she wanted to see Enchanted while my brother and I wanted to go see Hitman.  Needless to say, I lost the coin toss.

I went to the theatre and realized my friend John and I were the only males in there that wasn't a grandpa taking his grandchildren or a dad taking his daughters.  I got lots of looks from the audience and felt quite embarrassed.  HOWEVER, throughout the movie I think John and I laughed the hardest and not because we hated it but because we genuinely enjoyed it.  I left the theatre feeling like my money was well spent and later went back to see it again.

One of the emerging trends in Disney films is the inclusion of adult popular culture references in order to keep them from falling asleep or wishing seppuku since they are the ones forking over the money.  Enchanted had numerous references to past Disney films from Snow White, Aladdin, Beauty and the Beast and even Cinderella.  It was enough to keep my interest perked and my laughter on key.

The story is pretty simple, a cartoonish damsel in distress is banished to New York by the evil step-mother and the hilarity of culture clash commences (could be worse, she could've been sent to Canada eh?).  The damsel randomly breaks out in song much to the bewilderment of others, finds animals to clean house and makes dresses out of the most... off-the-wall things.

It's a good mixture of Disney magical adventures, adults humor (but not too vulgar), popular culture adventure and elements that actually make it a family film.  I was happy to spend money to see it again and I recommend this to all Disney fans, families and any popular culture fans.  A 92% overall.
profile.summary: Mom Forced Me to See It, Went to See It Again

profile.description: PowerDirector 13 Ultimate is the fastest and most flexible video editing software in the world. Powered by the 64-bit TrueVelocity engine, PowerDirector provides unparalleled speed in rendering HD videos - including support for the latest 4K UltraHD and H.265/HEVC formats. PowerDirector provides the easiest and most flexible design tools to design and customize your transition and title effects. The Ultimate version also includes premium effects & templates.
profile.reviewText:
When not at my full-time job I run a YouTube channel and have a film crew behind it.  I, primarily use Final Cut Pro X while my other crew members use Corel or Adobe Premier and, as much as I will permanently stand by FCPX, the licenses are expensive and, when one of my own wanted to begin editing, I needed software that wouldn't break bank but still provided the basics.  When I had the privilege to try out Cyberlink's PowerDirector 13 I was excited as I had the perfect test subject to try it on as one of our staffers in Orlando just acquired a new laptop and needed software.

After a week or so, I can say that PW13 is decent, considerably streamlined when I last tried it a few years ago, and worth the money one would invest in it.

The first thing our staffer (Tom) began to experiment with was the sound editor and he said it was, "like playing a good game; easy to understand, hard to master."  He experimented with some of his own recordings (I sent him a Snowball Ice microphone, the only mics we use) and was able to adjust several aspects and perfect his voice/narration.  He liked the streamlined approach and seemingly copy/paste format of the video editor (makes going from one software to another easier if they're similar enough) but didn't like others.

Tom also noted a fairly nice response time and rendering process allowing him to work nearly at speed, which is good for any editor.  I'm satisfied that Tom will make some good final products for us using the software provided, but am still very partial to FCPX and, to a lesser extent, Premier and would love to get licenses for my entire crew but PD13 is good and would recommend it to anyone wanting to edit but doesn't have sufficient funding to get a very expensive Apple license and MacBook Pro.
profile.summary: Not Bad Budget Software

profile.description: Enjoy high-quality sound without disturbance from the outside world with Panasonics RP-HC56-K Noise-Cancelling Headphones. Smart sensor technology detects and counteracts ambient noise for a clearer, more serene listening experience. The compact, pen-style controller lets you easily control volume or turn on noise cancellation with a single touch. The RP-HC56-K includes three pairs of earpads (S/M/L) so youll be sure to get a comfortable fit. A handy travel pouch is included.
profile.reviewText:
My wife and I have tried several noise canceling headphones from the Monster Octagons to Bose and generally enjoyed both of them.  We figured the Panasonic HC800, being lower priced than the others, would reflect the quality of the sound and noise canceling effects but, after a few months of use, my wife has adopted the set as her own personal "husband tuner-outer."

Requiring very little battery use, the HC800 provides excellent sound quality and drowns out most ambient noises while providing a nice, comfortable experience for the user.  My wife was able to tune me out along with most other ambient noise in our apartment while listening to her music and not feel like the headphones were squeezing her head likes others do.

For the price, the HC800s provide an excellent experience that doesn't quite rival Bose or Klipsch but still gives the user something to listen to while tuning out the rest of the world.
profile.summary: Excellent for the Cost

profile.description: Featuring graduated compression, the FUTURO Revitalizing Dress Socks for Men provide lasting support and a stimulating feel that helps keep you energized throughout the day. These fashionable compression socks help improve circulation and help ease the symptoms of moderate leg pain. The FUTURO Revitalizing Dress Socks for Men help keep you on your toes with the compressive support and lasting comfort you need to chalk up another successful day.
profile.reviewText:
I work three jobs and one of them is as an appliance sales rep at a local retailer and, as such, I spend over 10 hours on my feet per day.  I get up at seven in the morning and end my work day around 10-11pm at night.  By the end of said work day my legs and feet are just begging to be amputated from my body.  I've got custom insoles for my hardcore Nunn Bush work shoes and they just don't get cut it so when I had the opportunity to try these new Futuro dress socks, I was all over it!
