Granted, there is no one solution to help with sore feet and restless leg but these new socks helped out a great deal.  The first thing I noticed about the socks is that they're not socks but leggings as they went up past my knees.  To put things into perspective, I'm 6'5 with a size 14 shoe and relatively long legs; to have socks go up that far was just amazing.  To make matters more interesting, the leggings did more than just hug my calves but practically performed a group hug on them.  At first, I thought this was a defect of some kind but I tried them on anyway and, when I got home, I noticed that my restless leg wasn't acting up anymore and it didn't keep me up like it used to.

Lastly, the thin socks allowed my feet to breath better so I didn't have sweaty feet whenever I wear my usual Hanes cotton socks.

All in all, the Futuro socks aren't the one end-all solution but they certainly do help with anyone that is on their feet all day.  A worthy investment.
profile.summary: Retail Tested, Sales Rep Approved

profile.description: Studio G is the best value 5.0" smartphone available. 5 vibrant colors, IPS display and Android Kit Kat 4.4.2 OS which will be upgradable to Android Lollipop 5.0. Built with a powerful 1.3 GHz Quad Core processor wish Mail 400 GPU, which can handle anything you put in its way. With two camera's, a main 5MP autofocus and a frontal VGA camera, the Studio G is a versatile companion to captivate all of life's simple pleasures.
profile.reviewText:
I've played around with a lot of phones for extended periods of time including the iPhone 4S, Casio Commando, LG G3, and my current Samsung Note 4.  Going into this review and looking at the BLU Studio G's price tag I knew that I shouldn't expect current generation quality from it and what I ended up experiencing was an OK phone that does what it is meant to be; a backup smartphone for non-Verizon clients.

Compatibility:

Now, first and foremost, THIS PHONE WILL NOT WORK WITH VERIZON.  The Studio G, while dual-sim, only works with GSM while Verizon uses CDMA making the phone incompatible with Verizon so just know this.  I even called up Verizon, gave them the device's serial number (IMEI) and they told me it wouldn't work so if anyone says otherwise, I'd like to know how.  It WILL, however, work with AT&T, T-Mobile, Metro-PCS, and various other phone providers as GSM is the global standard.  While GSM exclusive, the Studio G is unlocked so you just grab a sim card from your local provider, plug it in, conduct a hardware swap online (most carriers have online support and self-service), and you're good to go.

Functionality:

I conducted a series of tests on the Studio G to see how well it would function under normal smartphones conditions such as internet research, funning apps, games, and video streaming.

The first test involved accessing my Gmail, Facebook, and Twitter accounts.  While accessing and running Google Play seemed noticeably slower than other phones, I expected some degree of relative slowness compared to phones that cost roughly 5-7x this one (IE: the Samsung S6 and the iPhone 6).  The Studio G performed adequately for these functions.

My next test involved downloading the playing certain apps, both offline and DRM (always online), to see how well the Studio G handled a larger workload.  THIS is where the trouble started.  While downloading Crusader's Quest the phone began to get warmer at a noticeable and, soon, alarming rate.  While most phones get a little warm while updating and downloading, this was unusually warm.  Before Crusader's Quest could finish the download I received an error message stating the phone's temperature was too high and I was forced to shut it down to avoid permanent damage.  I waited five minutes to let it cool down and tried again.

While the device did boot up normally, the heat began to build up again once I began to play another game (Tetris) as Crusader's Quest failed to run on it.  Through Tetris I learned the Studio G has a decent touch screen and response time but not the type I would trust playing games that require very quick responses especially if it involved player vs. player (PVP).  I then tried downloading and running Netflix to see how well the Studio G handles streaming.  Once I downloaded and logged into Netflix I gave the phone time to cool down to get the most objective trial.  I then loaded up The Fifth Element (great film, BTW) and didn't last five minutes before I received another temperature warning and had to power down.

I ran into this issue almost every time I played a DRM game but not so much with offline games.  This leads me to believe that the Studio G warms up too high if it needs to transmit a great deal of data even unto WiFi (which was my primary source of data exchange since I'm a Verizon client).  This reinforces my idea that the Studio G is a backup phone only as I can't see myself getting used to such limitations till I get a new one whenever that may be.

Camera:

The camera is OK, a mere 5 megapixel, which is close to the iPhone 6 but still meh, and the camera function is very strobe-ish.

Overall:

All in all, the Studio G is a backup camera with severe limitations but, then again, you get what you pay for.  The Studio G is NOT a longterm solution by any means.
profile.summary: OK For What It Is; A Backup Phone For Non-Verizon Clients

profile.description: A Samsung Galaxy Note 5 case designed for you: Refined, functional, and practical, the High Pro Shield series case fully complements the Galaxy Note 5 and lets the phone's natural beauty shine unhindered
profile.reviewText:
Sturdiness in a case is a must but with a phone like the Samsung Note 5, which is known for being a slippery phone, having a case with good grips is a must.  Truth be told, the entire new line of Samsung are super slippery as the stage 4 gorilla glass on the back has no traction to speak of, whose responsibility falls on the case.  I usually recommend Speck gripped cases as they can maintain position even on a vehicle's dashboard, but I wanted to try the new Verus and, I gotta say, it's very durable but super slippery to the point where it's useless as a case.

The Note 5, with it's aforementioned stage 4 gorilla glass, is a tank to begin with so the only reason for a case is added protection and to provide traction.  Without traction, the Note 5 can easily slip out of a person's pocket, especially if they're wearing tight jeans or yoga pants, and fall to the ground increasing the risk of a break.  The Verus case is just as slippery as my Note 5 kept slipping out of my pocket with little trouble.  It took all of one shift at work for me to retire the Verus for good and go back to my Urban Armor Gear.

Again, the Verus provides excellent protection but it's too slippery to be considered since the Note 5 is a tank to begin with.
profile.summary: Too Slippery for it's Own Good

profile.description: Add Style To Any Room. The chic textured finish of this 32-Inch ECO HDTV sets it apart the pack. Consuming less energy than traditional HDTVs, it exceeds current Energy Star Guidelines by at least 15%. The High Definition resolution and 15,000:1 contrast ratio deliver an exceptional HD viewing experience in a stylish, sophisticated package. Current Version 3.0 ENERGY STAR TV products Specification require that all qualified televisions address both active and standby power (when your TV is on and off). This VIZIO HDTV meets the current minimum standards by 15% saving you money on your utility bills.
profile.reviewText:
OK, first let me just get the ecology-friendly "green" crap out of the way, which we probably do not care much about anyway since we just wanna watch the game/movie/show.  The new Vizio eco-lines consume roughly 85 watts while running (.33 in standby), which is somewhat less than its predecessors.  This will marginally, if at all, effect your electric bill (the switch over from plasma to LCD will save you enough as is), but you can sleep better at night knowing your new green television will save the rainforest for .000000000001 more seconds - that should give the animals plenty of time to duck and cover when the bulldozers come in.

OK, that crap aside, the new Vizio Eco-Line is a considerable improvement over previous models, which were specifically designed for economy and not so much performance.  Vizio has done the unthinkable and focused on performance all the while lowering the costs to just about nothing allowing us mere mortals the opportunity (finally!) to purchase a strong 32 screen at a price we can afford.  Now keep in mind that the standard resolution on the Vizios is still 720p and not 1080p (see Vizio's Java Series if you want a 32-inch in 1080p)) so it's not true-high definition.  The product description states 1080i, but remember that it is only a simulated up-conversion (hence the "i" for interlaced) so it's not all that important.  Besides, most human eyes cannot differentiate 1080p in 37-inch screens on down anyway since the resolution is too highly compacted on smaller screens.

Now, the Eco-Line sports a considerably higher contrast ratio (15,000 dynamic) compared to the older models capping out around 2,000.  Now, I know contrast ratio is arbitrary to the corporation making the screen, however, they do remain consistent within said companies so a switch from 2,000-15,000 is a quantum leap in quality.  The differences between darks and brights is a lot more apparent, giving the picture more differentiation between the colors and presenting a more accurate picture for audiences.  The hertz is still 60 Hz over the more popularized 120 Hz, but again, it's a 32' and not a 47' or a 55'.

Now, the 32 Eco-Line Vizio does sport the usual refinements of its predecessors.  My personal favorite is how it kept the scratch and impact-resistant screen cover.  It can withstand anything short of a direct hit (and no, that is NOT a challenge) from babies throwing small objects to light impact from moving it around.  This feature makes the Vizio line a favorite among families with little ones in the house.

Vizio also still retains the bragging right of being one of the (VERY) few television makes still making them in the US.  Granted the parts are made in China, but the final products are assembled and finished hear.  Sony, Samsung, and Philips still make theirs in Mexico while everyone else pays tribute to the communists.

All in all, the new Vizios have received very positive feedback from the customers I've spoken with whether it was their picture quality, durability and longevity, or the darn fine price.  Vizio has leaped over Sony and Samsung in sales as well as achieved the best-buy title from Consumer Report for several years running and is expected to do so if they keep this trend up.

A great buy!
profile.summary: Considerable Improvements to the Earlier Models With an Economy Price

profile.description: TP-LINK's Archer D7 AC1750 Wireless Dual Band Gigabit ADSL2+ Modem Router is a combined wired/wireless network connection device with integrated wireless router and ADSL modem, reducing hassle of configuration and saving space.Featuring a variety of features and rich functionality, Archer D7 is the perfect hub of your home or business network. It works with top ISPs - Verizon, Fairpoint, WindStream, AT&T. It is not compatible with FiOS, AT&T U-Verse, or VDSL. ( as stated on the box.)
profile.reviewText:
Picked up this beauty to replace my five-year old Belkin router and Motorola modem from my old apartment days as my live-in fianc was complaining about lacking speeds two floors up.  We had a really nice Linksys WiFi signal booster on the first floor but our lacking signals always traced back to our old router, which was situated in the basement as that is where our cable company decided to place the connection.

The router was very easy to setup as I simply connected my MacBook to it and followed the step-by-step instructions.  I then reset the signal booster to the new router and then undertook the major task or resetting ALL our of WiFi devices, which was probably the hardest and most annoying part.  After that, everything working on the first and second floor showed considerable improvement as our laptops on the 2nd floor no longer bottomed out and our tablets received MUCH better signal in the 1st floor solarium where we often watch Netflix.  The Archer D2 has solved a LOT of our connectivity problems caused by our aging Belkin.

While I cannot speak for all other cable providers, the Archer D2 works amazingly well for us and will probably stay with us for quite some time as it's been holding up well for almost a month with no signs of wear or weakening signals.

All in all, a great buy is you just want an easy to use device that produces an excellent signal throughout a 1-2 story/split level home and below.
profile.summary: Excellent Replacement for Aging Router/Modem

profile.description: Smith & Wesson 4505 with 100 BBs
profile.reviewText:
I first came across this sidearm at work; one of the stock workers purchased it and wanted to test the FPS... by shooting himself in the foot.  Through the wool socks this S&W gave him a whelp the size of a dime and he kept it for several days, showing it off whenever he thought a woman would find it a beauty mark... clearly they did not.  After testing it out myself and subsequently being shot myself (he got me from behind) I can personally vouch for the power behind this dandy.

It's 302FPS may not sound like much but between 5-30 feet (typical effective range IMO) you'll know you've been hit and you'll be reminded by that large lump for days.  It's controllability is as much as you would expect from an airsoft gun; somewhat easy to control for medium to large sized hands although I heard complaints from younger shooters with smaller hands that it was harder to control.  The majority of internal parts are hard metals and not the cheap kind you'd expect from CYMA or other lower-end products.  This assures it will last longer than the cheaper competition.

Due to the FPS, this S&W has some greater accuracy than your normal inexpensive spring load, however, the lack of any mounts for a scope means you either have to take it to a machine shop to get one mounted or just take a guess at how to aim.  The clear plastic also makes it look ugly when you try to mount any scopes or add-ons to it since they hardly match.

I should note that I do not like air soft guns that are clear plastic.  I find those cheap and I feel like a third grader playing with a toy gun when I hold it... more so than usual.  It has no asthetic parts such as a supressor (which I find actually stablizes the weapon better), flashlight or scope.  These are kinda downsides to us younger audiences that like kewl looking weapons.

I should also stress to parents this weapon SHOULD NOT BE USED BY SMALL CHILDREN or children unfamiliar with firearm safety.  While this sidearm will not cause any permanent damage, if it can leave two full-grown men groaning in pain for several minutes that have whelps for days, imagine what it can do to smaller children.  Please parents, bear this in mind when purchasing this sidearm or any airsoft weapon.

Overall an 80%.  It's not that asthetically pleasing but it will alert your targets when you aim at them.
profile.summary: Powerful FPS Yet Lacks Asthetics

profile.description: The Kenwood persona line is a collection of kitchen essentials for the ultimate personalized tea and toast experience. Your toaster is not just for breakfast anymore. Adjustable and accurate settings allow you to create personalized favorites. The patented adjustable single toasting slot offers a wide, extra long toasting slot that can accommodate a wide variety of breads, sandwiches and pastries to suit your toasting needs. Take the guesswork out of toasting with the decimated 4 pre-set heating settings, delivering perfect toast, bagels, Panini and croissants every time. The Peek & View function allows you to easily monitor the progress without canceling for precise browning. The included sandwich cage gently cradles sandwiches and Panini for delicious results. Additional features to complete the personalization of the entire browning and toasting process include adjustable browning control and cancel function, Sure grip touch points, manual high rise lever for easy removal of food, cancel button, left and right handed operation, push fit crumb tray and illuminated controls.
profile.reviewText:
Had a cheap Oster toaster for a while and despite the fact that it did it's job I wish it did more beyond toast, bagels, and more toast.  The Kenwood TTM610 toaster was an excellent change of pace and will be an excellent long-term addition to my kitchen as it not only makes toast super well but has the sandwich cage that allows anyone to go well beyond making toast.  The 610 is also sleek, easy to use, and consistently efficient with each project you send it's way.

On to the specifics.

Test No. 1:  Simple Toast

If a toaster can't make toast, it's a complex paperweight so this was the obvious first test.  I was able to fit two medium sized slices of sourdough into the normal tray, close the top with the side lever on the side, clamp it down with the other lever, indicate which level of toast I wanted and pressed the "toast" button.  Within the usual time period of a few minutes I had toast exactly the way I wanted it.  Good, but any toaster can do that.

Test No 2:  Fish Tacos with Spinach and Pita Bread.

I love seafood but my fianc does not.  However, she was able to compromise on trying breaded flounder and she loved it and asked me to experiment more with it.  To me, this was a great opportunity to try flounder fish tacos with pita bread as the pita's thickness and taste makes for a great sandwich bread.  I then baked up some breaded flounder fillets in my wave cooker (great investment BTW), cut up and prepared some spinach leaves, sliced up Colby jack cheese, fried up some bacon, and put them together to make a basic fish taco.  I then placed the taco in the sandwich cage, lowered it into the 610, set the toaster setting to "4," and hit the "panini" button.  After  few minutes I heard the now familiar DING to indicate  that our meal was ready.

I could already tell the results were fantastic as the smell creeped into the office, where the lady was working, and lured her out to see what I was making.  I pulled the tray out and very carefully removed the taco from the cage, which surprisingly cooled down VERY quickly although I wouldn't recommend grabbing the non handle parts.  The fish taco was nice snd golden on the outside but the inside was all melted just right and the condiments lathered even throughout the pita bread.  The pita bread was crispy yet not crumbly allowing my fianc, who just commandeered my newest creation, to try it out with noticeable delight.  Success.  I made three more and the results were the same.

I then conducted several other tests from bagels to English muffins and the results were always positive.  The 610 IS an amazing toaster and I just love the sandwich cage as it negated the need to use a George Foreman grill, which can be messy.  It is relatively easy to use, gives complete control to the user, easy to clean up with it's crumb tray on the bottom, and it's sleek steel look compliments any kitchen.  I will be keeping this one for a while.

BTW:  If you want to try the flounder fish taco with pita recipe, mix it with some fried potato wedges in sea salt and olive oil, some tartar sauce, and A&W Root Beer and you have an awesome summer meal.  ;)
profile.summary: DING!  Panini's are Done!

profile.description: With the Oreck Graphite, it's all about making cleaning easy on you. Moving from carpet to fine Berber and Persian rugs is a no-brainer with the Quickswitch on the handle. It allows you to quickly go from carpet to hardwood to tile without stopping and bending down to adjust the roller brush height.
profile.reviewText:
Having once sold Dyson vacuums in a previous life at Best Buy, I always found it difficult to take other vacuums seriously as they lacked the power and versatility of a Dyson of course, they lacked the heavy price tag as well so I often found myself settling for a cheaper Eureka, Hoover, or Bissell.  Once I had the opportunity to try out the Oreck I gotta say I'm pretty impressed even though the Graphite is premium priced.

I've been utilizing the Oreck Graphite primarily on the ground floor of my house, which is a combination of white carpet and hard wood flooring, which provides an interesting challenge for any vacuum as it has to be multi-floor and still be able to work effectively.  On top of that, with the kitchen door entering the garage where my roommate parks, we get a LOT of dirt and gravel that gets into the entryway and on the rug in front of it, which requires constant cleaning.  In short, we had the perfect testing area for the Graphite and conducted weekly tests for exactly one month.

The graphite was not difficult to assemble as it only took a minute to put the handle on and get the cords ready to go and, like any other Oreck, it's extremely lightweight.  While I may be a 6'5 laborer that lifts 25-50lb boxes consistently on a daily basis, nothing is more annoying than a heavy vacuum that turns horribly on carpet and the Graphite did none of that.  While there is no turning feature such as a wheel pivot, the Graphite was light enough to move with relative easy.  To test it's lightweight nature, I handed it over to my mother, who is 5'4, to see if she appreciated the weight as well; she did.  Mum commented on how it didn't feel like she was lugging around a giant canister or top-heavy beast that made the neighbors think a tornado was coming through.

That brings me to the next point, noise.  With a smaller engine to reduce weight, the motor has two settings, normal and higher than normal.  Truth be told I've never really had a need to go any higher than normal, which is relatively quiet compared to other models but still omnipresent in any house.  This is handy since it doesn't blast your ears or those of any unfortunate canine within a 2-block radius.

As for the power itself, it works very well even on a first sweep.  I was able to effectively vacuum the carpet in front of the door to the garage and get all the gravel and other crap out effectively without causing the motor to scream in protest.  The Graphite, despite a month of sucking of gravel in the kitchen and God knows what on the carpet (I have weird roommates), it is still running strong.

I gotta admit, I was always skeptical about the super lightweight vacuum advertised almost exclusively by an old guy during The Price is RIght but I'm very satisfied with the Graphite and will continue to utilize it till it breaks whenever in the distant future that may be.
profile.summary: Lightweight, Versatile, and Multi-Purpose

profile.description: For common home repairs, vehicle maintenance, and building and remodeling projects, choose the full-range, all-purpose TEKTON 45-pc. 1/4 inch and 3/8 inch Drive Socket Set. It has every size from 3/16 to 3/4 inch and 5 to 19 mm. It also includes a universal joint, power socket adapter, and 6-inch extension not found in other sets. Each socket has a high-torque, 6-point design that grips flat sides of fasteners, not corners, preventing round off. Needing just 5 degrees of swing to operate, the smooth, finely geared 72-tooth ratchet isn't limited by tight spaces. For superior performance, all tools are made from premium chrome vanadium steel and protected by a mirror chrome plated finish. The tough carry case keeps everything organized in your toolbox or work area. It's also ideal to keep in your vehicle for unexpected roadside repairs.
profile.reviewText:
I always believed that every car owner should have an emergency kit of some kind in their trunk and rudimentary knowledge of auto mechanics in the event that one's car breaks down (AAA doesn't hurt, either).  I used to have a decent socket wrench set in there but, after over a decade of being used for other projects and parts began to disappear, I needed to replace it.

The Tekton socket set is an excellent replacement for the price as it contains all the pieces one will need for any do-it-yourself (DIY) projects as well as vehicular maintenance, is made of good material built to last even when compared to name brands like Snap-On, and comes in a nice compact case that can be stored anywhere (in my case, it's in the truck of my primary vehicle).

TESTING METHOD:

To test the Tekton set compared to Snap-On (of which I have a few of their tools), I called over a buddy ("Dave") of mine that is an auto mechanic and asked him to use the set to assist my in changing the car battery in my 2012 Chevy Impala and a few other tasks.  Dave examined the socket wrench, felt up the materials, then looked at me and nodded in satisfaction that the set will do the job well.  We then set to work.  Dave commented that the wrench's torque was "good" and that it felt pretty decent in his hands but didn't quite feel like giving up his expensive Snap-On set.  The Tekton set made short work of our immediate task as we were easily able to remove the bar keeping the battery down and then reapply it with considerable ease when we swapped the battery out.

We then performed other rudimentary tasks with the socket set to see how well it held up under constant use and, after two hours of moving from one project to the next, they still held up rather well and showed no real signs of wear other than minor scuffing.

RESULTS:

Dave and I were quite pleased with the set.  The Tekton handled well under consistent use and the layout of the set made it super easy to pinpoint which socket we needed as ALL sizes were present and played out in ascending order.  The case itself feels sturdy enough to withstand the perils of my trunk and the bright coloring makes it easy to see especially if I'm working in the snow.

All in all, the Tekton socket set is a very good value for the price as it delivers well and doesn't cost the same as name brands such as Snap-On.  A good buy.
profile.summary: Trusted Toolkit That is Now In the Trunk of My Car

profile.description: IRIS 3-Tier Cat Tree Condo has sturdy wood components and heavy-duty hardware. The IRIS 3-Tier Cat Tree Condo is built to give many years of safe, playful fun. It assembles in minutes, and will provide a great space for your cat friend to explore and play. Cleanup is easy with a soft brush or vacuum.
profile.reviewText:
Meet Dax, our 13-month old rescue and one very bored kitty that tends to get into trouble.  We usually keep her entertained with a laser pointer but both my wife and I work so we needed something keep her busy while we're away.  We tried both the IRIS CLF-5 and CLF-021 and, while the CLF-021 was very nice and Dax loves it, the CLF-5 was a pain to assemble and it's so scaled down that even out skinny Dax cannot use it effectively.

Assembly was not fun as the instructions have you start from the top down and the cloth wrappings on the vertical connections do not want to cooperate.  It took me about 45 minutes to get it right as I ended up removing all wrappings from the connectors to get the bolts to line up properly.

As for the product as a whole, it's not, at all, a scratching post, nor does it provide any real use as the platforms and tree house are so small that my tiny Dax cannot use it.  Dax isn't a big cat as she's still growing and when I placed her on the saucer on the right she looked cramped and quickly jumped down.  Truth be told, she only uses the bottom rung to sleep on and that's about it.

This is more for kittens due to it's size and that doesn't do much for owners since you can't keep them kittens forever.  I cannot recommend this product for normal users.
profile.summary: Too Small to be Considered Useable.

profile.description: Using the Belkin Home and Wall Charger with 30-pin cable, you can charge your compatible iPhone, iPad, or iPod. This convenient charger plugs directly into any of your home power outlet. It comes with a detachable 30-pin Charge Sync cable that allows you to charge and sync your device using the USB port on your laptop or PC. The charger's USB port is universal, so you can also use it to charge your Apple devices with a Lightning cable or other devices that use a Micro-USB cable.
profile.reviewText:
Not much can be said of the MIXIT other than it works.

It is a detachable USB wall charger with a 4-foot USB charge cable for the iPhone 4 and 4S, meaning the wall charger can be used to charge anything with a USB connection on one end including a Nintendo 3Ds, Sony PSP, other cell phones, etc.  It charges my iPhone 4S in decent time like any other USB charger but seems to be a little quicker and doesn't seem to wear out like the others.

There are a LOT of third-party USB charge cables that do the EXACT same thing and some for significantly less but, where the MIXIT differs is overall quality and versatility.  I've had many chargers just wear and/or stop charging altogether whereas, after a month on the MIXIT, there seems to be no change in the products performance or charging capabilities.

The price may seem a little steep but this sucker will last longer than those cheapies that you find at every gas station.  Recommend this as the end-all solution for iPhone 4 chargers.
profile.summary: Higher Quality in a Cut-Rate World

profile.description: IRIS 2-Tier Cat Tree Condo has sturdy wood components and heavy-duty hardware. The IRIS 2-Tier Cat Tree Condo is built to give many years of safe, playful fun. It assembles in minutes, and will provide a great space for your cat friend to explore. Cleanup is easy with a soft brush or vacuum.
profile.reviewText:
My wife and I recently adopted a rescue from the local shelter named Dax, she is around one year old and requires a LOT of stimulation and attention especially now that she's bonded with us.  The Iris CLF-5 didn't really do it for us as it was annoying to build and too small for any cat other than a kitten, but the CL-021 was actually what Dax needed as it provides a good amount of scratch material and wasn't too small to use... and I didn't contemplate seppuku while assembling it.

Assembling the CL-021 took roughly 15 minutes, a third of the time it took to build the CLF-5 and it wasn't that much of a chore... except for getting the ball danglers in the right post as the instructions weren't all that clear on what angle they had to be put in.  Truth be told, I broke one of them trying to figure it out but, oh well, still have the other 3.

Once I had it assembled, I put it in our bedroom near the window that Dax likes to perch on and watched her react to this new marvel that came in a box.  She was hesitant at first but eventually started scratching it once I rubbed a cloth on it that I just recently scratched her head with (amazing how effective it is to distinguish their belongings with this technique).  This method marks their territory and gives them a sense of familiarity in the same way they mark people to designate family.

Dax didn't use the upper tier so much as it was a stepping block to the window, which was my intention as I'd rather she takes steps up there rather than leap and knock over whatever is up there.

All in all, the CL-021 is nice albeit the instructions need to be clearer on a few things.
profile.summary: Not Bad to Assemble, Excellent Scratching Post.

profile.description: Brothers in Arms is the only first-person tactical shooter set in WWII. It takes you into the uncensored realitt of military history. You become Sgt. Matt Baker, a squad leader committed to completing his mission and bringing his men home alive. Guide his squad of 101st Airborne Paratroopers as you're immersed in the historic 8-day Normandy invasion; As you play, you'll face difficult choices where you'll weigh the good of the mission against the lives your fellow soldiers - your Brothers In Arms.
profile.reviewText:
This is NOT a game for children or FPS players that love to go in guns-a-blazing like in Golden Eye or counter-strike.  "BIA" is an intense World War Two FPS with squad tactics that take all games to a whole new level.  While the D-Day level in Medal of Honor: Allied Assault was a nice change from the typical John Wayne style FPS that involves almost no tactical thinking beyond cover and concealment, BIA slaps all players in the face with intense realism including realistic war violence, strong language and quick-thinking or you're dead levels.

However, unlike Unreal Tourny or Soldier of Fortune where the graphic violence is just for kicks, BIA shows you the true nature and violence of war from heads exploding to just about anything you've seen in Saving Private Ryan or We Were Soldiers.  War is hell and Ubi Soft made a great effort to show just that as it was meant to be.  The soldiers also talk like real soldiers; foul and vulgar... then again, when you're being shot at constantly, one tends to lose his verbal temper.

The gameplay is also quite impressive with easy to use command systems and a comprehensible overview map allowing the play to use real tactics in order to complete the objectives and the mission.  The enemy AI is pretty impressive compared to other WWII and FPS games I've played so don't expect to easily outwit your enemies.

I also love how you actually have to use the ironsights to accurately shoot your weapon and it diverts your attention away from your surroundings.  This is exactly what happens when you focus on shooting rather then minding your surroundings, which can lead you into an ambush if you're not careful.

The only real beef I have with BIA is the multiplayer; there's no co-op and co-op would've been incredibley fun and would've taught more teamwork then working with an AI squad.  Other than that, this game was incredibly impressive and very challenging in authentic mode... if you don't get cheap shotted by a stray round... then again, this is war.
profile.summary: Intense Wakeup Call for Fanboys!  Welcome to War!

profile.description: This member of the SEAL fixed-blade knife family, the SEAL Strike takes everything SOG has learned from years of real-world deployment and combines it into one spectacular package. This quality AUS-8 stainless steel, partially serrated blade is an excellent field companion for outdoor and underwater adventures. The SEAL Strike is serious business and carries on the tradition of supplying the world's elite military forces. It comes with a standard hard nylon sheath or a deluxe model with built-in cord cutter, single-stage sharpener, and larger attachment points. Be at the ready with the fully capable SEAL Strike.
profile.reviewText:
I usually keep a small fixed blade in the driver's side door of my vehicle in the event of an emergency and am somewhat particular about my blades.  I had a cheap United Cutlery Combat Toothpick there for about two years until I had the opportunity to review the SOG SEAL Strike knife, which is now my personal defense blade in my vehicle due to its superior design and durability.

After testing the SOG SEAL Strike for about two weeks my buddies and I noted the knife is extremely sturdy, sharp, has excellent balance, and the sheath sports several utilitarian features albeit with one moderate flaw that prevents a perfect score.

The blade is just under 5 inches making it ideal for concealment even with the sheath.  The tang is perfectly forged into the handle allowing for fantastic balance and durability since most "survival knifes" have very short tangs and can snap easily.  One simply needs to hold the blade to feel the heavy weight behind it but it's light enough to carry around.

As for how sharp the blade is, we tested it on the usual suspects of cutting targets from twine, paper (trying to slice through a piece of paper without sawing shows true sharpness), plastic ties, summer sausage, kindling, etc. and the SOG SEAL Strike passed beautifully.  For most non-hardened objects little to no sawing was required while the serrated edge provided superior sawing for stronger surfaces with little effort.  In other words, it comes sharp, VERY sharp, and can be kept sharp with the sharpener on the sheath towards the front tip.

One more great feature I liked on the blade itself was, at the bottom of the handle, the knife sports a rugged 'bashing' edge for applying a little brute force trauma to your intended target, giving the user more than one way to enforce order.

The sheath, I found, was a source of great utilitarian features but also of the blade's largest flaw.

1:  The sheath has a sharpener that works.
2:  The sheath also sports a line cutter for twine, nylon cords, cables, etc. and it works great.
3:  A frustrater that I cannot seem to figure out (never could) but I handed it to a hunter friend of mine and he nodded in approval.

However, the sheath does have one design flaw regarding how it is carried and the knife removed from it.  The upper portion of the sheath that supports the handle of the knife is wider than the width of the knife's handle.  The width is due to the belt clip being located at the top of the sheath whereas most other sheaths have them located towards the middle such as my USMC Kabar.  This doesn't sound like an issue until you try an unsheathe the knife and realize that you have to use your fingers to do so less you grab the whole thing and yank the sheath off your belt.  The sheath is also hard polymer so one has to either grip the whole thing or use their fingers with relative delicacy.  Also, the sheath is very bottom heavy which means that the knife, when clipped to one's belt, will flop around and that is quite a nuisance when out and about.  Even if you had the knife attached to your suspenders facing downwards, one would have to exert some delicacy with the fingers to remove the knife from the sheath.

This may not seem like an issue and it isn't in a casual sense.  However, in the field it prevents rapid deployment from the sheath to an open hand and that can be a problem with soldiers, Marines, law enforcement, etc.  This makes the SOG SEAL Strike more of a casual knife and not something for the field but IT IS STILL AN EXCELLENT BLADE.

Despite the flaw with the sheath, the SOG SEAL Strike blade is still an amazing blade that I will keep on me while driving.  I'd recommend it to hunters and enthusiasts but not anyone serving in the field.
profile.summary: Excellent Blade, Great Balance, Sheath Is Good With One Particular Issue

profile.description: The Hat Trick 6 in 1 Golf Divot Repair Tool is a unique and multi-functional golf accessory. It incorporates a divot fixer, magnetic ball marker, bottle opener with a magnetic cap catcher which prevents the bottle cap from falling to the ground, a cigar holder, club rest and can tab opener. The Hat Trick(R) 6 in 1 Divot Tool is a golf green friendly divot tool and comes in three different finishes (Gold, Silver and Matt Nickel). It is a must have for any golfer and can be used on the course or the 19th Hole. This fun golf accessory makes a great gift for Fathers Day, Mothers Day, Birthdays, stocking stuffers and tee prizes for your tournament and is truly a keep sake.
profile.reviewText:
Multi-tools can be about as handy as they are conversation worthy and the "Hat Trick" seems to garner more of a conversation starter than anything else, but still proves somewhat useful as a tool.  Not being a golfer in that I might go miniature golfing or frolfing once or twice a year, I thought I'd give this device a try and show it to some friends of mine, who are golfers, to see what they thought of it.

Now, before going into the golfing side, I decided to try a few things from the non-golfing side to see how practical it is the other 363 days I'm not at a golf course.  To test the Hat Trick for its most obvious task as a bottle opener, I went to a local liquor store to procure some beer that had a non-twist top, which proved more challenging than I thought and had to settle for something called "Woodchuck."  While the beer was nothing short of meh the bottle opener, with it's magnetic ring, was able to open the bottle decently and the cap was, most of the time, caught on the magnet and did not fall but not always.  The magnet seems kinda weak  and one would expect more holding power from a device that is used by people consuming alcohol, and by that, I mean they're not going to be the most dexterous people on the planet at that particular time when they remove the cap from beer #12.

Next I tried the cigar holder as the packaging on the side boasts it does; it kinda did if your cigar is smaller than Churchill size otherwise don't bother.  I then tried the pop can opener and... yeah, I'll stick with my opposable thumbs as that was less cumbersome.

Now, pertaining to the golfing side, I took the Hat Trick to my aforementioned friends that are golf aficionados and they seemed to feel the same way about the golfing tools as I did the beer and practical tools: meh.  I now know what a divot tool is as well as the importance of marking golf balls, but these are tasks that can be easily undertaken with cheaper tools like a marker or your hands.  When one friend handed the Hat Trick back to me, he asked me if the logos on the tool were interchangeable.

I raised a brow and went back to my trusted laptop computer to check the manufacture if they did sell additional logos.  Indeed, Hat Trick does have additional logos, which are primarily college logos from a wide variety including my two alma maters (WSU and UND), but you have to get another tool for that.  Lame.

All in all, this is a trinket, a stocking stuff, and gimmicky tool, but a cute one at that.  It's something that'll start conversations around the 17th hole more efficiently than other boring golf topics like how its always the equipments fault or that the golf cart doesn't have a turbo mode.
profile.summary: Unique Multi-tool for Any Golfer Wanting to Start a Conversation With a Trinket

profile.description: A true working knife, the FX414 has a big checkered aluminum handle on a stainless steel frame. Deep thumb notching on the top of the blade and frame adds even greater grip and control of the knife, helping to prevent accidental slipping. A 7Cr17 stainless steel blade will power through the toughest cutting jobs with ease and is easy to sharpen while still holding a great cutting edge. Thumb studs on both sides of the blade make one-handed opening easy; right or left handed. Backed by Coast's lifetime guarantee against defects in materials and workmanship.
profile.reviewText:
I like to keep a diverse knife collection and was giddy to try several Coast knives recently and found that this particular one is OK and lacks several key features to be competitive with superior, similarly priced knives.

When the FX414 arrived I took a good glance at it and realized a few things I did not like the first being no real way of clipping it on... well, anything.  There's no belt clip or pouch to secure it on oneself and it's sheer weight means that it will flop around in your pocket unless you're wearing really tight jeans and most guys don't.  While carrying it around it would flop from side to side and weigh down whatever I was wearing, especially if I sported shorts as it felt as though it was going to dig a hole through.

Another feature I did not like was the locking mechanism as it is a simple clicking lock that doesn't always engage.  This is a safety issue as an unsecured blade can fall back into place and over the very hand griping the handle.  It's not as though the blade is super sharp (another issue) but it's a little disconcerting.

Lastly, after you have clicked it into the open position, closing it requires precise unlocking of the same clicking mechanism and if you have large or shaky hands (my step-Dad has a tremor and couldn't make it work properly) it becomes too cumbersome to be a handy knife.

All in all, I have MUCH better luck with Gerber knives as they seem to be built better with more quick-convenience features in mind.
profile.summary: Decent but Prefer Gerber

profile.description: The Panasonic SC-PMX9 Networkable HiFi Micro Audio Speaker System features clear, brilliant surround-sound effects that rival larger home theater systems with noise-shaping technology that reduces audio jitter and distortion. It seamlessly syncs with your wireless devices, delivering rich, natural 600W (RMS) sound for a dynamic viewing and listening experience. The SC-PMX9 includes a set of three speakers, each designed to produce a different tone, creating a rich and resonating audio experience. Designed for maximum flexibility, the SC-PMX9 also lets you play music stored on your PC over a LAN network from another room.
profile.reviewText:
An an audiophile I'm very particular about my sound systems as I have a Klipsch Icon surround sound and computer speaker system and a Harmon Kardon Onyx 2 speaker for my office.  The wife wanted something for the bedroom that produced good sound balance for when she's reading or primping in the adjacent bathroom.  The Panasonic SC-PMX9 is an excellent addition to our sound systems and has satisfied our prerequisites flawlessly.

The SC-PMX9 supports several different input modes including Bluetooth, Apple Airplay, red-white stereo, FM radio, and CDs, giving it a wide variety of streaming options with the exception of 3.5mm Auxiliary input, but that can be supplemented with a cheap Y-Splitter cable.  I was able to sync my Samsung Note up to the Panasonic simply by setting the stereo to Bluetooth and it popped right up on my phone's BT menu.  Simple as that.

The sound quality is just amazing.  I decided to christen it's first song with Kenny Loggin's Danger Zone and that perked everything up almost immediately.  The stereo has a near flawless balance between bass and clarity, allowing the listening to hear every song as it was meant to be.

My only real beefs with the SC-PMX9 is I'm not certain if it's worth the hefty price tag and I wish it had a direct 3.5mm AUX input but you do get what you pay for and the latter can be resolved with a cheap cable purchase.

All in all, an amazing device!
profile.summary: High Cost Brings High Quality and Ease of Use

profile.description: The Synchros S200 model sports an ultra-light, durable aluminum frame that comes with angled ear tips, offering hours of seamless listening comfort. And that's just what's on the outside. Proprietary technologies JBL bring your ears advanced JBL sound with perfect audio balance at all frequencies and PureBass performance. In a word, welcome to the premium. With all of this fine-tuned precision designed to fit inside an earbud, it's a sure bet you'll find yourself at a new level of in-ear listening. Tangle resistant flat cable - Whatever configuration your S200 flat cable comes in, it's custom-designed to be tangle resistant.Specifications Type - In-Ear Headphones Driver - Premium 10mm driver Frequency Response - 10Hz - 22kHz Rated Input Power - 5mW Maximum SPL - 108dB @ 5mW Connector - 3.5mm jack
profile.reviewText: Company policy states that we cannot use our cellphones in our vehicles unless we utilize handsfree sets and I, typically, cannot stand Bluetooth ear pieces that can't seem to figure out hot to be comfortable. Meanwhile, corded handsfree sets seem to have figured this one out and have made leaps and bounds in their quality control for both ergonomic comfort and utilitarian pragmatism. In short, they're better. I've been using the JBL S200 for over a month and I will not switch to anything else. Before I get cast off as a cheerleader, let me direct you to my other reviews and show that I am super critical as I'm not too fond of spending money or investing a lot of time in a device that can't even address the basic need of comfort. If it's not comfortable, don't bother and I've negatively reviewed many headsets that were supposed to be superior. I put the S200 through a series of real-world tests in my daily life to see how well it holds up and it is still running strong. Now, here are the basics! The S200 are, indeed premium quality headphones as their sound quality is better than my Skull Candy S2FXDM008 Headphone Earbud, and I love my Skull Candy. The Music on my iPhone 4S comes in very clearly and drowns out most ambient noises. I tested them in my vehicle (with only the right ear covered to comply with state law) while driving home on I-94 between Jamestown and Bismarck, ND (100 miles approximately) as well as outside while mowing the lawn and the S200 drowned out most, but not quite all, ambient noise. I was, however, still able to perfectly hear my music and even the person on the other line. I haven't tried them on an airplane yet but hope to do some international travel next year when my vacation time matures. As for the controls, they are my only real beef albeit a minor one. Since I'm using the iPhone 4S, the controls are very different in that I seem to only be able to control the pause and play button, nothing else. Not exactly debilitating, and I'd never want a full-on remote next to my face, but I would've appreciated something a little more Apple friendly. Now, pertaining to the cellphone features, the S200 works incredibly well. I used the S200 the most when I was doing my photography work outdoors as I'm doing a film shoot for a class I teach using Army men to explain concepts in military science. I would be working in my backyard or at the local park in cold photography gear (it's been snowing outside) while listening to Fleetwood Mac, singing Don't Stop much to the dismay of others, and then the ringtone in my head would chime indicating a phone call. I'd tap the respond button, hold a conversation on my cellphone, and continue my work nonchalantly. I would occasional ask, "how am I sounding," and the person on the other line would comment that I'm much clearer than usual, but they can tell when I turn my head away from the mic but it wasn't debilitating. Regular Bluetooth headsets have the nasty knack of coming out of my ear while I work whereas the S200's earbuds fit comfortably in my ears and did not come out once. Now, the one big thing I tested that I love is how the S200 seems to handle all environments. While I'm not exactly exposing them to an open flame source or sticking them in the freezer, I have been taking them outside in the cold a lot and that can easily destroy any electronic device. Most cords tend to harden up and lose sound quality the more they're exposed to the cold but the S200s seem to work just fine. Wouldn't try wearing them while snow blowing my driveway unless I had headgear on, but I know I can jog with them in less then comfortable weather. Overall, I love my S200s. I use them every chance I need to and am quite satisfied with the overall result!
profile.summary: Use Them Everyday, LOVE Them Everyday!

profile.description: BROKEN STEEL: Continue your existing Fallout 3 game and finish the fight against the Enclave remnants alongside Liberty Prime. Broken Steel moves the level cap for your character from 20 to 30, allowing you to experience even more of the game, including new perks and achievements. Story: You may have dealt the Enclave a serious blow at Project Purity, but their forces are still out there, and still pose a grave threat to the people and security of the Capital Wasteland. In Broken Steel, youll continue your current Fallout 3 character past the events of Project Purity, and work with the Brotherhood of Steel to eradicate the Enclave threat once and for all. Travel to new locations like the Olney Powerworks, wield destructive new weapons like the Tesla Cannon, and fight powerful new creatures like the Super Mutant Overlord. POINT LOOKOUT: Point Lookout opens up a massive new area of the Wasteland  a, dark, murky swampland along the coast of Maryland. So hop on the ferry to the seaside town of Point Lookout, for the most mysterious and open-ended Fallout 3 DLC adventure yet. Story: Buy a ticket and hop onboard the Duchess Gambit, as Tobar the Ferryman takes you to the strange seaside town of Point Lookout. What secrets does the dilapidated boardwalk hold? Who lives in the sprawling mansion? Why is the Punga Fruit so important? And what horrors lie in the depths of the murky swamp? Point Lookout is the most open-ended DLC yet, and allows you to explore a huge, swampy wasteland any way youd like. A completely new quest line allows you uncover the towns hidden secrets and wield powerful new weapons like the Double-Barrel Shotgun against the swamps dangerous, and deformed, denizens.
profile.reviewText:
In my review for the game itself, I stated how I felt the maximum level of 20 was absolutely ridiculous as you can easily achieve this level VERY early in the game.  My other criticism pertained to the "good" ending where, unlike in other roaming RPGs such as Fable II, ends the game prematurely preventing you from going back to explore the rest of the wasteland.

Not anymore!

Broken Steel continues the story with a three primary quests and then allows the player to free roam afterwards.  The level cap has also been raised from the low level of 20 to a not-so-low level of 30.  This does present a problem for gamers that have beaten all the dungeons before installing Broken Steel as the expansion does not have enough quests to reach the level cap.  However, that is where Point Lookout comes in, but more on that later.

Similar to previous expansion packs, such as Operation Anchorage and The Pitt, Broken Steel includes new and powerful weapons such as the Tesla cannon *evil grin*.

A lot of these features, most notably raising the level cap and the divergent "good ending," should have been in the original Fallout 3 game to begin with as it will cost the player however much money to purchase this expansion.  However, Bethesda makes up for the cost with a few more entertaining side quests and another much needed expansion.

Enter Point Lookout.

Within the first hour of exploring Point Lookout, I scavenged more weapons, heal items, ammo, grenades, and various knick knacks (including a Swiffer(tm)) than I did in the first ten hours in the regular game.  Weapons and ammo were extraordinarily plentiful (especially in the Calvert Mansion) as were the relatively tougher enemies, which very closely resembled the protagonists from Redneck Rampage.

Point Lookout is definitely a tribute to redneck survival in Fallout 3 as the game is bursting with hillbilly references including the introduction of a double-barrel shotgun, a level-action rifle, banjo music (sadly, there are no Deliverance references I could find), voodoo wackos, and a LOT of whiskey.  The South will definitely rise again - whether to protest this game or embrace it I really do not know but it certainly takes a jab at them.

However, what really helps with Point Lookout as how the seemingly endless supply of enemies help fuel the player's experience to level 30 since many veteran Fallout 3 gamers explored most of the wasteland prior to the end of the game.  The "tribal" warriors weren't exactly difficult to dispatch, the problem was there were soo darned many of them and they came at you in rushes.

The other great thing about Point Lookout is the introduction of a large new map to explore, namely the swamp wasteland.  While not as large as the capitol wasteland, the swamp wasteland is big enough and will take a fair amount of time to explore and the rewards for doing so are very nice.

All in all, this expansion is a must have for any gamer with Fallout 3, although I do recommend you install it before you go on an exploration rampage since that'll make achieving level 30 that much harder.  I only wish the primary features would've been added in the original Fallout 3, but, oh well.  That's life.

Now, us gamers will anxiously await the next Fallout 3 expansion!!
profile.summary: Yes We Can (Go Beyond Lvl 20)!: A Much Needed Expansion for Fallout 3

profile.description: The Samsung Xpress M2020W printer is perfect for your home office and combines ease of operation with high performance at an affordable price. Samsung Xpress M2020W Laser Printer delivers hassle-free mobile printing and all-around efficiency that are perfect for your cost-conscious SOHO work environment or home office. Quick and easy wireless printer installation gets you up and running fast. Always get reliable quality for crisp black text with Samsungs innovative imaging technology while saving up to 20% on toner with Samsungs Easy Eco Driver. Professional Image Quality: Samsungs ReCP technology improves readability of printed and scanned documents by enhancing thin lines and sharpening edges. You get sharp, solid prints with an effective resolution of up to 1200 x 1200 dpi. Fast Print Speeds: Streamline your workflow and print up to 21 pages per minute, so you can spend more time producing and less time waiting. Compact, Ergonomic Design: The printers small footprint saves space for your home office. And the two-tone design is well suited for todays modern office settings. 1. As of Nov. 1, 2017, HP acquired Samsungs printing business and Samsung printers were added to the HP portfolio of products. Samsung printers enjoy HPs warranty support in accordance with warranty documents accompanying the products.
profile.reviewText:
Been needing a document printer for quite some time given that I am attempting to start up a film production crew and need to print off quite a few forms for either tax, instructions, or agreements/releases.  Nothing was more annoying than to venture over to some office copier store to have them done when I, easily could've been doing them at home.  It was a breath of fresh air to try out the Samsung M2020 since it's easy to setup and user interface are rather friendly even to the most technologically deficient person, and can crank out documents at a very decent speed.

Setup was easy enough as it's wireless nature only needed to connect to the wireless network in my home with it's quick setup guide.  On top of that, it was easy for other devices to connect in such as my MacBook and the personal laptops my crew members bring in.  It's almost as easy as connecting to a wireless network.  I was even able to do some basic printing from my Samsun Note 3, although I doubt I will use that feature very much if at all ever again.

It's small design (7 x 13 x 8 inches) allowed me to nonchalantly place it on one of the dressers in the lab without really needing to make extra space.  It's a space savor to say the least and very easy to move around should you need to.

It's speed is acceptable at around 20 ppm.  Not enough to crank out a thesis but enough for my purposes.

All in all, the M2020 is a great little black and white printer for anyone that prints a lot of documents for a small business that doesn't want to invest in a massive copier and make the space to fit it in.  It's also handy for students printing off papers assuming college hasn't gone all digital and we can text papers in now.  A worthy purchase all the same!
profile.summary: Micro-Office Document Printer for the Small Business Owner or Student

profile.description: A true working knife, the FX412 has a big laminated wood handle on a stainless steel frame. Deep thumb notching on the top of the blade and frame adds even greater grip and control of the knife, helping to prevent accidental slipping. A 7Cr17 stainless steel blade will power through the toughest cutting jobs with ease and is easy to sharpen while still holding a great cutting edge. Thumb studs on both sides of the blade make one-handed opening easy; right or left handed. Backed by Coast's lifetime guarantee against defects in materials and workmanship.
profile.reviewText:
Have tried other Coast knives and the FX412 seems to be little more worse off than the others to the point where I'm considering sticking with Gerber knives for the indefinite future.

While the FX412 is cool looking with its seemingly faux wooden grips and steel blade (most of my knives are matte black) it lacks several features that I consider mandatory in order to be considered an everyday handy knife most notably the lack of a securing mechanism.

Simply put, there is no way to secure the FX412 as there is no belt clip or pouch meaning it will flop around in your pocket.  To make matters worse, this knife is heavy so, to me, it feels as though it's tugging at my pockets especially if I'm wearing shorts.  I don't wear tight pants as the world doesn't need to be exposed to THAT kind of atrocity so there's no way I can secure this "pocket knife" on my person.

Also, similar to other Coast pocket knives, the FX412 doesn't seem to lock properly as it sports a very flimsy locking 'mechanism.'  I cannot safely flip it out that doesn't seem to work half the time and, unless you hear that loud "click" you can assume that it'll fold on itself the instance you try to use it and THAT is a safety hazard.

Lastly, this knife does not seem very capable as it's not sharp at all.  Granted any knife enthusiast will tell you to sharpen it yourself, but this one struggles to cut most things out of the box and I find that disheartening.  Even my Bear Grylls' survival knife was able to cut most things simply out of the box before I had to apply a resharpening.

All in all, for the price, get Gerber blades as they're built better and not throw-away items.
profile.summary: OK, but Throw Away Knife Compared to Gerber

profile.description: Leave a lasting impression on guests at your events, meetings, parties and more with these 2.5 x 8.5 folding tent cards. The name tent cards are made from heavyweight cardstock designed to stand up to frequent folding, making them ideal to use as tented place cards, on buffets or as information cards at farmers markets, boutiques or trade shows. Featuring a subtly embossed frame and micro-perforations for easy separation, these large tent cards are pre-scored so you can easily fold them and convey event communications in a polished, professional way. The blank tent cards are a fantastic canvas for you to personalize with your own creative designs, or select from the thousands of free templates and designs at avery.com/templates for easy customization. You can add crisp, clear text and eye-catching graphics to both sides of these tent place cards, and then print them out on your laser or inkjet printer without any smudges or jams. Save time and money without sacrificing quality using this pack of 100 table tent cards to add a special personalized touch to all your events.
profile.reviewText:
Avery is great for making products that help organize and promote your business. Their business card solutions have helped my small business attain a more professional look and the tent cards have helped us create name cards for our bi-monthly North Dakota Filmmaker's Association meetings as we have newcomers each month and having quick reference cards work a lot better to keep things less intimidating than those gosh awful, "Hi, my name is Rob Lame," stickers.

The quality of the cards feel pretty sturdy as we've reused several cards multiple times to keep cost down and they still hold their figure. They look professional and, thanks to Avery's free online printing service, we were able to print custom labels with their very impressive set of online presets.

Lastly, the 100-card pack means we'll be printing for a VERY long time and the great value price Avery attaches means we can do it without worrying about cost.

These are a must get for anyone planning meetings, conferences, weddings, etc. where people are meeting for the first time and quick references for names are a must.
profile.summary: 100 Count Value Pack That Is Awesome for Events Requiring Quick Name Referencing
