profile.description: The e200 mini Bluetooth headset provides innovative styling and performance without sacrificing comfort. Its cutting edge compact design is built for comfort, convenience and giving you exceptional sound quality with noise suppression and echo cancellation. Delivering over 5 hours of talk time and 180 hours of standby time, the e200 is a Bluetooth workhorse.
profile.reviewText: My job has me go out of town once a week to assist the other guys in Jamestown ND, which is 100 miles away from Bismarck. Used to go to Minot, ND several times a week (110 miles) and really racked up the mileage. Company policy dictates we can only talk on our phones if we're using hands-free devices (IE: bluetooth or speakerphone) and, no, they don't provide them. I've used various BT-enabled devices such as the Samsung HM1200 Bluetooth Headset - Black, Motorola 610, and a few cheapies I found at gas stations to get me through the trip. The only one I actually liked was the Motorola 610, which is OLD school and no longer made, as I could hear over my car engine and the person on the other end could hear me. Ever since, I've been disappointed with just about every headset as either the volume is crap or super uncomfortable. When given the chance to try the Quikcell E200B I went in skeptical and had such practical skepticism confirmed after two trips to Jamestown. I don't know why they have that little rubber loop in the earbud piece, but it rubs against my inner-ear and, after a while, it makes it super tender and sore to the point where I just take it out. Now, I assumed it was to keep it lodged in your ear, but my ears are above-average size meaning it should not be jammed in there. I can only imagine how uncomfortable it would be for someone with smaller ears. It also doesn't stay in there as it comes loose, and hangs on only by the plastic hook that goes around the outer-ear. This makes it hard for me to hear the person on the other end although they can hear me perfectly. I tried keeping it in there for over and hour but my ear got too sore and I kept having to ask the person on the other end to repeat themselves even with the volume on full blast. Perhaps I should man-up and get one of those boom-mic earpieces that truckers use. To ensure I wasn't being unreasonable, I tried using the headpiece outside of my car and while I was walking around normally. While I was able to hear a whole lot better, I still had to ask the other person to repeat themselves a few times. Now, before you claim that I must be hard of hearing, check this out: the electronic voice that tells you the device is on, off, call disconnected, etc. comes in loud and clear. In fact, she has a super sexy London accent that I could REALLY get used to. If I can hear her loud and clear, why not the person on the other line? All in all, the E200B is uncomfortable and too quiet to be considered practical, especially in a vehicle. It has a decent range and the lady has a sexy voice that I will miss but, alas, life goes on. I'd recommend a Samsung or a Motorola over this any day.
profile.summary: Uncomfortable, Overly-Complex, Lacking Sound Quality, but Super Sexy Voice

profile.description: Tired of purchasing cat products that your beloved feline gets bored of quickly? Oliver and Iris Cat Scratcher's serves as both a cat scratcher and lounge that promises to keep your cat companions coming back for more. Custom made for cats who enjoy scratching, playing and lounging around. Ever notice that cats love jumping in and out of cardboard boxes? They love the texture of cardboard and Oliver and Iris scratchers are guaranteed to make cats happy. No more worrying about the ugly old scratching post of old because with the modern design of Oliver and Iris the scratcher is both functional and fits with your home decor. Manufactured with quality standards and top end recyclable materials for a product that stands up to even the most aggressive scratchers and is 100% recyclable.
profile.reviewText:
I've tried multiple cat scratchers with my little furball (Dax) and she's taken a liking to most of them but, when it comes to the Oliver and Iris Premium Cat Scratcher, she really didn't take an interest to it.  I attempted to coax her to investigate it by spritzing the piece with cat nip in front of her prompting her to sniff it, touch it, then walk away.  It's been two weeks and she's really paid no attention to it despite my best efforts.

While others have experienced great results with their feline pets, mine just doesn't seem interested.

However, I can see how cats would like the feel of cardboard to scratch up as something rather soothing and be attracted to it.  It's definitely a good design for other cats... just not mine.
profile.summary: Works for Most Cats... Just Not Mine

profile.description: The first time you try Fiskars PowerGear2 Lopper, youll be amazed  but its not magic, its gears. Fiskars patented-pending technology multiplies your leverage to give you up to 3X more power on every cut. This means you can power through thick branches that you wouldnt be able to cut with traditional loppers. Fiskars updated design includes modified gears and an innovative cam mechanism to optimize your cutting power in the middle of the cut where the branch is thickest and you need it most. The result is that every cut is even easier than Fiskars original PowerGear cutting tools. In fact, this lopper makes cutting so much easier its earned the Arthritis Foundations Ease of Use Commendation.
profile.reviewText:
Like any other home in the suburbs our backyard borders on three properties and, also like any other house in the suburbs, our backyards are privacy entrenched by either a fence-line, thick neck-high bushes or poplar trees to prevent curious neighboring eyes from seeing what I REALLY do in the yard *maniacal laugh*.  Such privacy-enabling greenery requires maintenance and that means regular pruning which, up until now, was only accomplished with landlord supplied hand tools that were more designed for gardening.  It was a pain to say the least.

Fortunately, I had the opportunity to try the Fiskars PowerGear2 and what a blessing THAT has been.  It's elongated 32-inch design gives even this 6'5 gargantuan male's 5'4 fiance the reach she needs when I graciously delegate the task to her of which she promptly hands them back with "the look."  On top of the great reach, the PowerGear was a VERY strong support lever that requires some degree of strength to use or, at least, break it in.  Truth be told, one could get a decent workout opening and closing the loppers as they're very heavy duty and it shows in how effectively they remove anything 2 inches or less.  Wouldn't recommend these for small projects that are more suitable for hand tools.

We tested the loppers out on some overgrown greenery that had been growing out from underneath our deck (1.5-2 inches) and while opening and closing the loppers requires some effort it was still considerably less than if we used standard loppers.  We noticed that as long as you can operate the PowerGear2 you really won't expend any more energy using them on any project with the device's specifications.

All in all, I'm very impressed with the PowerGear2.  Perhaps Fiskars' reputation is well earned after all.  Highly recommend for any home owner.
profile.summary: Heavy Duty for 2" Diameter Projects

profile.description: On first look, Shadow Ops: Red Mercury might look like a military simulation, but it's an intense first-person shooter all the way. The story features covert ops soldier Frank Hayden and his team as they hunt and chase a terrorist group that possesses the deadly weapon red mercury. You'll shoot it out in multiple locations like Syria, France, Russia and more. Red Mercury offers single-player campaign, co-op, and multiplayer game modes. Campaign mode has 24 challenging levels where you'll be prompted to create a profile of Infantry, Ranger, or Green Beret difficulty levels. Med packs and ammunition boxes are dispersed at each level, but the action gets hot, heavy and fast-paced. Enemies use techniques like blind-fire and throwing your grenades back at you so don't expect to get through a level unscathed. But your squad mates are fighters and will support your advancements.
profile.reviewText:
Whatever my expectations were of this game, they were completely thrown in my face as I got something else.  Shadow Ops is not your typical FPS, which is just the way I like it.  Shadow Ops takes you and places you in some of the most hellish combat zones a console game can take you.

While Halo is probably more intense, you're more focused on surviving in Shadow Ops meaning your attention is almost always focused on just making it.  In the urban combat levels there are quite literally a dozen things, noises, explosions and misc elements going about to distract you from keeping an eye on your surroundings.

I must admit, the story is almost laughable had I not read the Red Mercury novel back in the 1990s.  You are Frank Hayden, a Delta Operator that looks, sounds and acts just like Frank Castle aka the Punisher, which is just plain weird.  There is a romance twist and it rather lame if not annoying at times; just ignore it.

The controls are fair, nothing special or too complicated.  The leaning function makes cover and concealment much easier and realistic compared to most games.  Shadow Ops really stresses cover/concealment and alertness almost to the extreme.  To survive even the first level on the easiest setting, you have to watch literally every nook and cranny less some tango will appear out of nowhere and cheap-shot ya or pull a Forrest Gump and nail you in the real.

The musical score is absolutely incredible and with surround sound, the music and sounds will emerse you into the most hellish combat zones the XBox can offer.  I get a huge kick out of hearing bullets literally whizz by my head or hearing teammates yell from behind.  Watching the making of special features, it is absolutely amazing how they got the sounds to work.

The only real beefs I have are your fellow teammates; they are completely worthless and are extremely whiny.  You're supposed to be a Captain, a company grade officer and you're being given orders by a compulsive Master Sergeant... somehow that doesn't make any sense.  They also tend to not hit the enemies in the area, they're accuracy is almost at par with the A-Team.  For what they're worth, they certainly do whine a lot.

Overall, I give Shadow Ops a 93%.
profile.summary: War is Hell, So's this Game at Times

profile.description: The Marlin stapler  a hardworking, practical addition to any desktop. This traditional full-strip, top-loading metal stapler features an ABS top cap for ease of use and a full rubber base for stability. This durable stapler is backed by a 15 year Guarantee and has a capacity of 25 sheets (20lb paper)
profile.reviewText:
While red swing line staplers are the thing in office circles these days, there are other products out there worthy of testing and the Rapesco certainly held up to standard and then some.

To test the Rapesco, I had a bunch of release forms and legal documents that needed epic stapling so my assistant and I set to work.  Now, the bundles of forms increased in number of pages up to 15 (the Rapesco is rated up to 25) and we had over a dozen bundles to work on.  The Rapesco performed seamlessly as we stapled our way to success with little to no effort required.  While it may not be much to look at (at all), the Rapesco is a subtle, relatively low-profile stapler that did exactly as it was advertised to do and at a very affordable cost.  Would recommend this one over high-priced Swing-Line any day.

Milton, indeed, would be proud to keep this one (Office Space reference by the way).
profile.summary: Milton Would Be Proud

profile.description: SeagateBackup Plus Desktop drives are available in capacities up to 8TB and come with a USB 3.0 hub option. With cross-platform compatibility, exceptional reliability and speed, you can back up just about everything. Plus you can conveniently back up and share your digital favorites with the included cloud storage service.
profile.reviewText:
I am a massive film editing enthusiast and just starting picking up small freelance gigs so I rented an office and began to setup a small video editing lab.  One of the largest components needed was hard drive space.  I use Final Cut Pro X and one of the largest overlooked elements is external hard drive space as FCPX transcodes raw footage into massive files that take up a LOT of space in order to run more smoothly.

I have several multi-TB sized hard drives and it doesn't take long for them to fill up as I archive ALL footage.  I've used Seagate hard drives before, both standard and travel (Love my 2TB travel drive) and have never experienced any problems with them whatsoever the 5TB being no exception.  The 5TB I keep primarily for recording raw footage from my Elgato capture card to later be transcoded when needed.  I've already recorded over 200GB of footage from Indie games to use for several reviews.

The device is a good size and shape to help it 'fit in' with all the other hard drives, of which I do stack but since I keep the lab at a comfortable 69F with very constant air circulation, I never worry about overheat.  I also seem to have a very good connection between the hard drive and my Alienware laptop for recording as I've had issues with other brand hard drives with recording footage directly to them.

The 5TB has been sitting at my desk for well over a week storing footage and seems to do just fine with its work, no real negatives that I've noticed and, given how well its predecessors have done, I have faith it will last well into the coming years.

An excellent buy for anyone needing vast storage.
profile.summary: Works In Our Video Lab

profile.description: The Vysk EP1 Privacy Charging Case for the iPhone 5 and 5s protects your privacy while powering your phone. Vysk privacy cases fit seamlessly into your busy life, providing the convenience of a battery charging case, with the privacy and security only Vysk can offer. Did you know hackers can access your phone's cameras to snap pictures and take videos? Simply slide the EP1's camera shutter switch until it clicks, and you and your loved ones are protected. Our custom Vysk privacy apps apply powerful technology to protect your photos, videos and text messages, so you don't have to give privacy a second thought. The Vysk private text app and private gallery app are available for download on the app store. The Vysk EP1 is power-full: A built-in, rechargeable 2200 mAh lithium-ion battery gives you twice the power of your iPhone's battery alone.
profile.reviewText:
In the past I have used Mophie's Juice Packs when I wanted a case with a decent battery backup with a fair degree of protection for my phone.  The Vysk  charging case for the iPhone 5S is an amazing case that provides excellent power backups and moderate to good protection against the elements while offering some interesting privacy options.

First off, the battery backup provides up to 120% of an extra charge in the event of low power.  One simply charges the battery pack through a micro-USB plug on the bottom to charge both devices and, when the phone is low, the user flips a switch to activate the backup, which then charges the phone as if it were plugged into the wall.  While the charge isn't as fast as an Apple name-brand charger, it still charges within a reasonable time period.  The power level of the Vysk can be measured by pushing a button on the back that lights up the logo to indicate how much juice is left.

As for it's durability, the case certainly feels more rugged than most decorative cases but doesn't quite feel like an Otterbox, Speck, or Lifeproof.  However, it feels as though it would provide ample shielding for the iPhone in the event of a drop.  It is also interesting to note that the case, despite it's power capacity and protection, it doesn't add a lot of bulk to the overall phone like Mophie does.  I was able to slip the whole device in my pocket without feeling like I snuck some bricks out of Home Depot.

The device is also screen protector friendly as my Zagg Glass shield was unaffected by the case allowing even the thickest of screen protectors to be employed.  A definite plus.  As for the privacy options, the case comes equipped with a privacy shutter for the camera to prevent N. Korean hackers from pulling a Taylor Swift on your phone and taking pictures without your consent.  I haven't tried the security app that Vysk provides as I didn't feel it was necessary.

All in all, I would recommend Vysk over Mophie any day as it is well worth the price.
profile.summary: Handy Battery Case For All Occasions

profile.description: Bissells Steam Mop Select features a two-sided, flip mop head that allows you to clean twice as much floor before changing the mop pad. Additionally, Bissell has included two distinctly different mop pads with the Steam Mop Select. One pad is soft for use on delicate flooring such as hardwoods and laminates. The other pad has built-in scrubbing strips that make cleaning tough, stuck-on messes easy. The Bissell Steam Mop Select delivers the steam right where you need it, at the floor. It has a static steam manifold that allows the mop head to rotate around it; ensuring the powerful steam is always directed straight to the floor. The Bissell Steam Mop Select is designed to give you an easier, more effective clean, while saving you time so you can get back to doing what you like most.
profile.reviewText:
Working in the appliances section at my work, I've noted that steam is easily one of the most effective, yet gentle, cleaning agent for just about anything especially in the fields of laundry, dishwashers, and flooring.  It roots out anything that doesn't belong without any undesired side effects if done properly (this being the key element).

I got the Bissell Steam Mop 80K6 knowing this and with the preexisting condition that I always get sauce on the floor since I constantly experiment with spaghetti sauce (I laundry a LOT of aprons).  Normally I would use a paper towel with soap to quickly remove the sauce, problem is that the experiments requires constant attention so I usually don't attend to the spill till later after it has hardened.  Using the 80K6 on my floors has considerably helped me in my efforts to keep a (relatively) clean home as I seldom have time for heavy cleaning (I'm writing this on my lunch break BTW).

The 80K6 was very easy to assemble (3 parts) with no tools required and starting working almost immediately.  Like any other steam tool, the reservoir had to be filled and given a few minutes to heat up, but once it got up to speed it was very easy to remove light to moderate stains and build-ups on the floor.  It was easy to move about given its lightweight nature and the downward spraying feature (as opposed to the typical front) made it safe to operate around electrical sockets and corners of cabinets.  I was able to remove all past and present stains save for the hard one in the corner that was left unattended for a week (the best cleaning is prevention and quick response) but that's my fault for not getting to it sooner.

Another thing I noticed about the 80K6 is that it does not adequately clean up larger particles such as meat or small vegetables (peas, corn, onion particles, etc.).  Normally, I would have my automatic quick-response floor cleaning tool, aka my dog Timmy, come by and clean up the spill but since I moved into an apartment that doesn't allow pets without paying a not-so-small fee, I have to resort to other measures.  Despite my handicap, the easiest way to overcome this issue is to pre-clean with a broom and dust mop, easy as that.

After usage, the cloth that cleans the floor can be washed rather than utilizing disposable ones.  This saves a lot of hassle in the long run since it doesn't require more trips to the store to get more.

All in all, the 80K6 is worthy of its price and gets the floor cleaned quickly and effectively so long as you don't let it sit too long.
profile.summary: A Phenomenal Light Weight, Quick Response Floor Cleaner

profile.description: Designed by the French designer David Turpin the MM03 is a contemporary styled Bluetooth handset, finished in a luxurious black or white high- gloss texture. Manufactured with a high quality speaker and microphone, it supports Bluetooth 2.1 multipoint technology, which lets you pair and answer calls on two different Bluetooth devices. This means you can quickly and easily connect the Moshi Moshi 03 to two phones, such as a Smartphone and a personal phone, or a phone and a Bluetooth-enabled device, such as a laptop that you use to make VOIP Internet calls. The handset is supplied with a weighted recharging base for the handset and a silicon mat designed to protect the mobile phone from wear and tear.
profile.reviewText:
My lady is a huge Apple fan with all the latest in Apple gadgets including the iPhone4 so, when I had the opportunity to review the Native Union iPhone headset, I gave it a chance by letting her try it out... and it didn't get much further than that.

She plugged it in the wall outlet, quickly and easily synced up the Bluetooth from her phone and I gave her a call.  She picked up the headset and, after my customary greeting to the love of my life consisting of some suggestive phrases I shall not repeat here, she quickly requested I say it louder.  After repeating aforementioned suggestive greetings two more times it quickly lost its effect and she went right back to using her phone.

We tried reading the manual and checking online to see if others had this problem to discover that many others have and can not figure out how to fix it.  This is the worst possible problem as, without the volume, what's the point.

It was a great idea to have a sleek-looking Bluetooth headset for the house instead of lugging the phone around, but that noise issue really turned us off and, after trying to troubleshoot it for an hour, hasn't really seen any usage since.  If Native Union can come up with a better version with quality sound, I'd gladly consider getting it as I love the concept... just not how they put it into practice.
profile.summary: Novel and Handy Idea but Lacks Approach

profile.description: DescriptionThis is a Tokyo Marui Replica Fully Automatic Airsoft Sub Machine Gun. Rifle is brand new in the box. U.S. Army, Navy, Seal Commando, Counter Strike, Battlefield 2 GUN. This is the next best gun to Tokyo Marui Brand With a fraction of price, you get the similar quality automatic electric gun with the state of the art adjustable Hop Up technology with helps shoot more accurate and harder. It comes in a complete package of charger and rechargeable battery, magazines, bag of BB and accessories. ready to play package. Adjustable hop up, battery charger included, fully loaded, and full size.IncludesCM023 GunChain MagazineBack Up MagazineScope BatteriesBBsSpeed LoaderGogglesGun SlingRetractable StockBarrel CleanerRechargeable Battery & Charger
profile.reviewText:
I've been doing air soft parties with my Air Force buddies for quite some time so I get to try out a diverse selection of air soft weapons from the cheapo single-shot handguns to the full-auto SAW weapons.  The CYMA MP5 was a cheap alternative to purchasing over $100 rifles since you are then entering the price range of real rifles that I find more fun to shoot.

The CYMA MP5 did not take all that long to charge and depsite constant target practice (and constant harassment to my unsuspecting neighbors when they're not looking) and outside usage I have yet worn down the battery to necessitate a recharge.  Despite prior reviews I have yet to experience a problem with the stock 30-round magazine; the drum however, not quite so successful.

As for the power, it's 200+ FPS may not seem like much but that may indicate your battery is low.  I 'tested' the FPS out on my unsuspecting brother from 20 feet away and the lasting whelps on his arms suggest a rather unpleasant that WILL get your attention; for this reason I strongly suggest taking safety precautions to avoid injury.  The rate of fire is consistant, but with any full-auto weapon it is vital to realize there is a difference between sustained fire and continuous fire.  Since air soft guns cannot easily be tweaked to lower the firing rate full-auto airsoft guns are prone to jam unless CO2 powered due to the firing mechanism.

It is vital to understand that you cannot, and should not, just go Rambo and unload like there's no tomorrow.  You run the risk of throwing the firing mechanism out of whack and then you have a busted weapon.  2-3 round bursts are the way of the day even when conducting supressive fire.  BEAR THIS IN MIND when using the CYMA MP5, especially if you're purchasing this for a younger user that may not be familiar with close combat beyond Counter-Strike.

Now, to name some cons; this weapon is cheaply made.  The scope cannot be accurately mounted unless mine came broken.  It seems to makeshift snap on to the upper receiver and easily wabbles.  I compensated by screwing in (with a power tool) a weaver rail and mounted one of my actual red dot scopes.  Now it's semi-accurate up to 30 yards.  My flash light attachment simply does not work and no matter what I tried I couldn't get it to work.  Oh well, never gonna use the thing anyway.  Many people have noted the weapon is prone to jam on the first round and this is true and there's a way to prevent it; pull the cocking hammer back and then slap in the magazine.  Once in, slap down the hammer or you can insert the magazine then pull and release the cocking hammer.

Sometimes the full-auto also jams on the first shot.  To get around this I switched to single-shot, fired, then switched back to full auto since it already primed the next shot.  Then there's the instructions... written VERY poorly.  I've read garage door opener manuals with better translations.  It's almost to the point where I have to read the instructions soley from the pictures.

Other than this, it's a good cheap starter weapon for younger, or novice shooters.  It's also a great product to teach new shooters firearm safety since the basic safety principles still apply (finger off trigger, point in same direction etc).  There are better alternatives for more advanced players but this one is good for beginners and those (like me) that just want a beater.
profile.summary: Excellent Starter Weapon, However, Cheap in Execution

profile.description: Amprobe products range from an extensive line of clamp meters and digital multimeters to industry-specific tools for residential/commercial electricians, HVAC/R technicians, utilities and industrial maintenance professionals. All Amprobe tools undergo rigorous testing to ensure full compliance with the latest IEC and CE safety regulations in Fluke Safety labs for quality and safety you can trust.
profile.reviewText:
I gotta admit, when I had the opportunity to try this thermometer out I thought it was for personal use and not industrial usage but, after trying it on the home front with a unique set of tests, I can verify the Amprobe's usefulness outside it's area of intended use.

The Amprobe is very easy to utilize in that it is literally point and click to determine temperature whether it be celsius (default) or Fahrenheit, which is what I set it to since I'm not quite accustomed to the metric system.  The laser light helps guide the user to whatever it is they are aiming the Amprobe at and can be turned off to conserve power as can the brightness on the LCD readout screen.  The readout screen is also easy to understand even for non-electricians like myself, whose knowledge of electricity extends as far as a the technical operation of a light switch, with it's easy-to-use interface and three-buttons with clear-cut meaning.

It's easy for anyone to use, as safety equipment should be.  If I can figure it out, anyone can.

Now, the tests I used to determine the accuracy of the Amprobe consisted of scanning boiling water, a hot stove top, bath tub water, running shower water, body skin, running electronic equipment, etc.  Basically your everyday household interactions as I determined how hot I like my bath water before jumping in/out (115F) as well as the my preferred temperature for hot cocoa (135F, I can't stand it too hot).  This granted me a greater understanding of the temperatures of the objects I interact with on a daily basis and does provide the necessary safety when handling potentially hot objects especially those I jump in and soak in after a long shift.

I cannot stress enough just how easy this thing is to use and just how accurate it is as I was able to get very consistent readings for over a month and the batteries are still going strong.  Any electrician or those who are safety conscious about cooking would love to have one of these.  I can personally vouch for their usefulness in the home even though they are intended for something very different.
profile.summary: Tested for Regular Home Usage

profile.description: The OBLIQ Slim Meta case for the Apple iPhone 6s Plus / 6 Plus provides a thin, shock absorption, protective polycarbonate case. With extreme protection from drops and scratches, this case truly is the best case for the iPhone 6s Plus and iPhone 6 Plus.
profile.reviewText:
The Obliq Rose Gold case for the iPhone 6s is a quality cellphone case in that it provides moderate protection from drops and spills as well as great aesthetics to compliment the new Rose Gold color, but there are other cases out there that do the same thing only better and not for much more.

To me, one of the benchmark cases that sets the standards for others to follow are from Speck, a company that consistently puts out military-grade cases that also look absolutely gorgeous.  They are roughly $10-20 more but would you risk a $700-1000 device on a mere $20?  Speck also have better grips and insulate from impact damages and overheating.

All in all, the Obliq is good but one can easily do better for not much more.
profile.summary: Very Good Case, But Try Speck Instead

profile.description: Power up on-the-go with the Incipit off GRID Backup Battery Case. Its sturdy, co-molded design delivers double the defense with a hard shell brushed aluminum design body and integrated impact resistant TPE bumper. Equipped with end-to-end protection and 3000 mAh of additional power, the off GRID Backup Battery Case is the perfect companion for all of your daily travels and adventures.
profile.reviewText:
I have tested out the Vysk and Mophie cases before and, while the Incipio holds up very well, it is not as high quality as the Vysk.

The Incipit is, essentially, a battery backup case that provides up to 120% additional charge for the iPhone 6 and charges via a mini USB cable when in need or a recharge.  The Incipio sports a good battery, easy to set in frame that is one piece as opposed to the usual two pieces (Such as the Vysk and Mophie), and the frame provides good protection from drops or impact.

However, there are two things to note about the frame.

First off, the outer shell is smooth and rubbery suggesting that it may wear out after prolonged use.  One of my biggest complaints against case manufactures such as Otterbox (the Defender in particular) is that consistent removing of the case can wear out the rubber and it looses it's grip.  This can lead to poor protecting and a bad grip on the phone.

My next issue is the texture/traction as it's too smooth to remain in one place.  Slippery cases can slip out of a person's hand, pocket, or off the dashboard of a vehicle and go where ever gravity takes it.  Rubber grip marks, such as those found on certain Speck cases, make cases a LOT harder to slip up with and they, typically, don't fall out of a person's pocket or slip out of their hands.

All in all, the Incipio is good, but there are better ones out there.  I prefer Vysk, myself.
profile.summary: Solid, But There Are Better Ones

profile.description: URBAN ARMOR GEAR Galaxy Note 4 cases provide legendary rugged protection for your Samsung Note 4. Built with UAG's signature oversized ports, tactile buttons, and feather-light composite construction, UAG enhances the utility of your Note 4 allowing you to use on your most extreme adventures.
profile.reviewText:
Had an Otterbox Defender on my Note 4 for the longest time and, while I liked it overall, I wanted to try something new as the screen was getting filthy and the rubber began to wear out.  While I currently work in retail and have no real immediate need for anything ruggedized, I wanted something that could withstand the "oops factor" of accidentally being dropped, sat on, or stepped on given the Note 4 is still over $700 to replace.

The Urban Armor Gear is an excellent alternative to anyone wanting to avoid heavy-duty cases such as Otterbox or Life Proof (they tend to negatively reduce sound and the ability to connect headphones) but not spend exorbitant amounts of money on them.  The case fits super snug, the buttons are just stiff enough to not get hit by accident, and the case looks very stylish with its seemingly futuristic tough design.

I will warn against anyone attempting to put this on a Note 3 as we tried and, while the Note 3 did fit, the buttons were off just enough to render the case useless.

I now recommend the Urban Armor Gear to anyone getting a new cellphone that wants to avoid heavy cases with heavy costs but still wants to keep their phone safe.  Only thing I would recommend to compliment the Urban Armor Gear is a good Zagg Glass Shield for added protection to the phone's screen given the case encompasses all but the screen.
profile.summary: Sturdy, Effective, and Stylish

profile.description: Pet Botanics Training Reward Beef Flavor Dog Treats are made with pork liver, real beef and feature a soft, moist consistency and aroma that dogs love. The small size is ideal for repetitive rewards required during training. Meat is the #1 ingredient and real beef is added for the flavor that makes your canine companions tail wag. A natural preservative system is used; no BHA, BHT, soy or ethoxyquin, so you can enjoy peace of mind that your pet's treat is healthy and nutritious. These treats, the original meaty training reward, are sure to motivate your dog to learn and help shorten the learning curve!
profile.reviewText:
My little Timmy (a cream-colored Cairn terrier) can be a stubborn little man and sometimes his instincts get the better of him.  I always try to reinforce adherence to the rules with reward such as praise and w-a-l-k time (he knows that word FAR too well).  However, when doing initial training I try to reinforce learning new rules and tricks with some form of a small treat.  Doggie treats can get too expensive and I don't want to overfeed him with treats less he gain weight.

Cardinal Labs reward treats were very helpful in this regard as their snacks are very small, low calorie, and pack the natural ingredients a canine needs to grow up and not out as most cheap stuff does.  I was also very pleased to see the good ol' "Made in the USA" label that is now a rarity as opposed to a commonality.  My only beef (so to speak) with the product is the smell as they have a very pungent odor but, then again, Timmy doesn't seem to mind.  In fact, it makes him REALLY appreciate them and maybe that's the point.

Either way, the price certainly is right, my dog seems to love them, and they're made all natural and not from lead paint crap one would expect from overseas.
profile.summary: Solid Reinforcement Tool (A Terrier Owner's Perspective)

profile.description: "The Siege Lantern features five C4 power LEDs, four white and one red with five output modes and a battery level indicator built into the on/off button. With the outer lantern globe in place, the light will float. Use the lantern with or without the outer globe cover. Remove the outer globe and hang the body upside down by the D ring for large area lighting needs. Battery replacement is a breeze with the center post orienting the battery cover correctly every time. "
profile.reviewText:
I can remember as a child going camping with my parents and being anything but helpful given my complete lack of knowledge about camping and its components like setting up a tent, hanging up the food in trees, or even starting a fire with... well, anything other than a gallon of 89 octane and a big book of matches.  To this day, I still can't camp with my 4G connection or my Macbook as I find it's easier to sing around the campfire with Katy Perry's E.T. playing on iTunes rather than chanting "kumbaya" along with an acoustic guitar some hippie lugged along.

What has this got to do with the Streamlight 44931?  Well, it's about time someone modernized camping equipment that us techno-geeks can feel safe using even though I've used it for everything BUT camping.  However, if I do go camping, I WILL take it along and here's why!

It's a very effective lantern in that it's bright and energy efficient.  The Streamlight has two light modes, standard bright white and night vision red.  I say "night vision" as the red light allows the user to retain more night vision than they would using a very bright white light.  The user can also easily toggle between a standard constant stream of light or a flashing light for... distress, I assume.  Not sure why you would want to strobe the light, but it's there.

The Streamlight is energy efficient in that it uses three "C" batteries and seems to last a long time.  To put it in prospective, I put fresh batteries in it when I received the product in July and use it every night as a nightstand light instead of a traditional lamp because... I'm a bachelor, we're supposed to improvise.  The original batteries I put in still work even after several months of nightly use.  I even use it to read at night since I don't want to get a traditional lamp.

As for the durability, my friend and I wanted to see just how ruggedized it was so we hung it in the shower, placed the shower head on the "monsoon" setting, and barraged the lantern with a constant stream of water for five minutes.  The Streamlight showed no signs of wear and continued to function.  We even went as far as to drop it in a full bath tub of water and the result was the same... it also floats.

While we have not tested the Streamlight outdoors, it has performed admirably indoors and even in our makeshift "tests" that we subjected it too.

All in all, a good product!
profile.summary: Ruggedized Lantern for the Non-Ruggedized Camper

profile.description: The stunning Seagate Seven portable drive celebrates over 35 years of storage expertise and innovation. This statement product exemplifies advanced storage R&D uniting with world-class industrial design to create the slimmest way to carry 500GB of data. The Seagate Seven enclosure is made entirely of steel, not only to achieve the thinnest external drive, but also for a premium appearance inspired by a bare drive, the essence of storage. The superior experience is extended to the included USB 3.0 cable, a stylish, premium braided design instead of the standard cable found with most external drives. Since the drive is bus powered, meaning it draws power directly from the USB port, and does not require an external power supply, the Seagate Seven is perfect for those on-the-go situations. Push the limits of possible with the thinnest portable drive, Seagate Seven.
profile.reviewText:
I have several Seagate portable hard drives at my disposal including a few 2TB travel drives that work great and, to be honest, I didn't think it would get any more portable this quickly.

With the new Seagate Seven ultra-portable hard drive, one is able to appreciate an even more compact storage drive that is the size of a wallet and super thin but still give the same performance and speed as a regular drive.  I first tested mine out while editing a video promo I was working on in Final Cut Pro X on my Macbook.  I was able to work efficiently and effectively without any real delay from the hard drive.  The sheer compact nature of the hard drive also allowed me to keep the drive tucked away and out of the way so my hands could work freely and take with if necessary.

While somewhat pricey, the Seagate Seven is an excellent portable hard drive for filmmakers needing a readily available and reliable backup storage as well as something fast to work on.  With this in mind, the Seagate Seven is also an excellent choice for anyone working on the go despite it's steeper price.
profile.summary: Higher Priced, by Worth It

profile.description: Stella Deus: The Gate Of Eternity is an incredible game world, completely hand-drawn and with voiced dialogue that brings the world to life. A deadly mist called the "Miasma" spreads across the land, killing all in its path. Having forsaken hope, the inhabitants simply await their deaths -- except a young soldier and female shaman who believe they can stop their eventual extinction.
profile.reviewText:
I love a good RPG with a decent story and not to off-the-well as many games from Japan have been in recent years.  Having just recently finished Stella Deus ("SD") I feel as though I, most certainly, got what I paid for.

SD is a very simple tactical RPG with a three dimensional chessboard, to which the players attack in turn based upon their speed.  Like other tactical RPGs, the players gain experience based on attacks, skills, and spells used on other characters (friend and foe alike) and raised higher based on the level of the target.  The story revolves around a world dying from a miasma and the several factions of the planet fighting over which method is better.  Some prefer to wait for their "peaceful end," others wish to fight to the death, others dare to seek an unlikely prophecy to save the world (guess which one you end up choosing?).  You play Spero, a young and courageous soldier trying to find a way to save the world, he meets a beautiful woman, they fight together, they go an an adventure, yadda, yadda.

That is the game in a nutshell.

SD held my attention for 50+ hours but not because the story was overly-intrigueing, or the fact that the artist put a 'bounce' effect in the female movement animations, but because before you know it you have put over 12 hours in the game and you want to finish what you started.  Before I knew it, I was at 30 hours and then 40, 50, etc.  Most RPG gamers do not like leaving a game after putting so many hours in and I am no exception either.

I spent a good deal of time leveling up in the always-accessible "catacombs," where the player can level up as long as they prefer and unlock more sub-levels as they progress through the game.  After all, they can't have you go all the way up to 99 in just over 20 hours now can they (I did it in 47).  This would be great if leveling up wasn't so darn time-consuming.  It can take well over thirty minutes to an hour to finish one catacomb level and you'd only level up maybe 1-2 levels.  My average time per catacomb level was 20-25 minutes.  Now, multiply that by 99 and you'll see how long it takes to level up to maximum.

The only solace a player can take in this is that, similar to Final Fantasy Tactics, a character accumulates skill points with every action.  Unlike "FFT", however, skill points can be used to raise character attributes typically in incriments of one.  However (AGAIN), like experience points, skill points take a while to accumulate to an amount necessary to raise the aforementioned attributes.

So, in all, the combat system needs to be tweaked to allow faster leveling otherwise a person will spend waaay too much time trying to level and for an almost miniscule amount of increased stats per level.  It just takes too darn long.

The next gameplay option if the item fusion system.  This is an excellent and a horrible addition at the same time.  Great that you can make much better items and equipment (including weapons) than are available at shops, but horrible in how the setup is made.  My biggest problem with the fusion setup is that you can only make one item at a time even if your goal is to make two or more of the same item.  This is not a problem until after chapter five when you begin constructing the best equipment in the whole game.  It is frustrating because you have to start with level 9 items to make level 16 ones and, more often than not, you need to make up to 10 of one item in order to get there.  This means you have to scroll, almost endlessly, through item menus every time you make an object.  This makes the process take forever.  It took me two hours just to make the best swords for ONE character.  Oh yeah, and it is expensive over time as well since level 9 items are not cheap and cost almost as much as a round in the catacombs, requiring more time.  You literally have to cheat or find a money glitch (which there is) to eliminate that process.

Atlus should have simplified things by allowing mass production of fusions.  This means when they ask you to confirm item fusion, you should be allowed to make more than one.  It would have made making the best equipment that much more faster so I'm only limited by how much money I have.

My next beef is with the secret character recruitment.  It is annoying that you have to do certain things in order to get them to begin with, but it is made worse that many of these recruitment processes happen towards the beginning of the game and it becomes too late to fix it.  This has occured with games like Suikoden, but those games didn't take over 30-50 hours to beat (more like 8-20).

There is also little replay value as only the hardest of hardcore gamers will ever want to retry SD, especially with NO new game + option.  I felt obligated to finish the game just so I can say I finished it and could move on to another RPG.

Lastly is the voice acting.  Well... I've rarely heard decent voice acting from a Japanese RPG so I really shouldn't be surprised but SD just doesn't cut it.  The only voice actor I recognized was Viser, who I've heard time and time again in other games including Shadow Ops, X-Men Legends, and numerous anime (I swear, they literally rent these guys from a rent-a-voice-actor center or something).

Despite all the negative remarks I have, I do have some positive remarks.

The first is the game is addicting albeit not in a good way.  It kept my interest for a little while but I will not be playing SD again.  You complete it out of obligation and not out of interest.

The next is the simplicity of the game and lack of weirdness.  Too many times RPGs have some really abstract things including a flambouant male playing the saxaphone as a weapon or a hero who looks more like Meg Ryan than a glorified soccer star (I am not making any of this up).  SD eliminates most of the weirdness albeit with some female characters with revealing clothing and a prince who looke more like an Alice without a shirt on.

All in all, SD is a solid RPG from Japan and holds it's place in my collection of RPGs and will remain there.  It is a great game if you need a cheaper alternative to the more expensive ones out there and want to be addicted to a very long and cumbersome game but otherwise it is a case-filler.

70%

-15 for time-consuming and, often times, frustrating leveling and advancing
-5 for non-user friendly fusion interface
-5 for poor character recruitment
-2 for lousy voice acting
-2 for lackluster story and ending (It could have been better)
profile.summary: Highly Addicting and Indepth but Frustrating as Well

profile.description: Resident Evil 4 Wii
profile.reviewText:
I originally owned Resident Evil 4 for the Gamecube and I was frustrated with the cumbersome sights and aiming mechanism and poor reaction time limited by the controller.  Enter the Nintendo Wii remote.

Obviously you're allowed to aim with the Wii remote as the ubiquitous laser sight is replaced with an ever-present cross hair.  This allows for considerably better accuracy and reaction time.  My first time through my accuracy was around 75% (I know, I'm a terrible person) and my reaction time was pitiful.  With the Wii edition my accuracy went up to 90% and better reaction time.  The downside is the cross hair is always there and can be slightly annoying; I think the laser sighting would've been more appropriate and only present when aiming.  Another downside is you cannot aim scoped weapons (rifles and launchers) with the Wii remote, but with the nunchuck.  It might be better to have allowed aiming with the Wii remote similar to Call of Duty 3 but that's my preference.

Pertaining to the gameplay and graphics they're almost no different than the PSXII or Gamecube version; if there is a difference I certainly didn't notice it.  Don't let this deter you as the gameplay makes up for that and if you're like me and started with the Gamecube version, you get all the bonuses of the PSXII version only you can aim better.  You get the five chapters of Separate Ways (Ada's quest), the special costume 2 set (mafia outfit and Thompson for Leon and the suit of armor for Ashley (annoying to hear but boy it comes in handy A LOT in the castle).

Lastly, there's one Wii exclusive element and that is the trailer for Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles... and there was much rejoicing (Monty Python "yay").  Not much cool stuff for the Wii but oh well.  The release price, however, sets it apart from other Wii titles to the point where it's cheaper than most to purchase.

Overall RE4 for Wii is worth purchasing if you're a Wii owner; it improves your game and you can still enjoy the classic arcade blowing heads off spree.  Wheee!
profile.summary: Excellent Wii Release for Easier Gameplay

profile.description: The keyboard case that's always one idea ahead of the rest. Get more done, more easily wherever you use your Samsung Galaxy Tab A. Type-S is the all-in-one case that protects your tablet and makes typing a breeze. A built-in Bluetooth keyboard features comfortable well-spaced keys, including Android shortcuts. The stable design protects your tablet from tip overs when you type and tap. And the long-life rechargeable battery makes battery changes a thing of the past.
profile.reviewText:
I've always had good luck with Logitech products whether it's their keyboards, mice, or tablet cases.  In fact, I often defer my clients to them instead of the usual selection and they've generally been pretty pleased with them.

The Type-S keyboard fits the Tab A 9.7 perfectly, as expected, and connecting the case to the tablet was just as easy as any other by syncing the devices in the Android settings.  The Type-S also provides basic protection against the elements and the occasional drop, maximizing the life expectancy of the tablet.

My only beef is the initial cost of the device as it is a little steep.  The Type-S is a great case but one can get similar products for 3/4s of what Logitech is asking for.  Beyond that, the Type-S is a great case.
profile.summary: Great Case, Steep Price

profile.description: The Serta Cushioned Comfort Pillow offers the comfort and support of memory foam plus the cushiony softness of fiber in a traditional pillow feel. It gently cradles your head, neck and shoulders while retaining its shape to provide consistent support.
profile.reviewText:
It's the little things that tend to make all the difference in the world, even as much as the right pillow to help get a decent nights rest.

While my job necessitates I get up at 4am and the consistency to that time made my body able to fall asleep relatively easily over time, I did not know how much improvement there could have been until I tried the Serta memory foam pillow.  I've been using it for little over a week and the results have been fantastic.

First thing I noticed was how heavy the pillow is.  It feels almost triple the weight of a normal pillow to the point where I dare engage my lady in a pillow fight for fear of hurting her and inciting her decision that my new sleeping quarters be relocated to the couch.... and she has access to all my Nerf guns.  The heavy weight is rather indicative of the quality/firmness of the memory foam knowing that my thick skull will not sink to the bottom necessitating I grab another pillow to compensate.  My theory was proven correct on the first night when I initially laid down and left my head being cushioned just right without sinking through.

According to my insomniac girlfriend situated next to me, I barely tossed at all compared to how I usually sleep and I didn't reposition the pillow once.  I woke feeling considerably better than I usually do after six hours of sleep and the subsequent nights proved equally successful.  With more than seven days down, I can safely say that the Serta pillow has improved my overall sleeping experience.  The pillow has been so successful that when I come back in the room to kiss my lady for the day, who goes into work at 7, she ALWAYS seized the opportunity and was snuggled up with the pillow.  One night she tried to actually sneak it from me while I slept.  I was sleeping nicely but not THAT nicely.  (sorry, honey!)

All in all, while this pillow may seem pricey think of it this way; sleeping well is a quality of life issue that cascades into everything we do throughout the day and if XX amount of money is what makes you sleep better and your day is better because of it, why not do it!

A worthy buy for anyone!  I highly recommend these pillows and can only imagine how amazing the mattresses are... which the lady is hoping I'll get next.  :P
profile.summary: Heavy, Firm, and Overall Delightful

profile.description: The Honeywell MN Series portable air conditioner has a sleek, modern design cooling and dehumidifying areas up to 450 square feet. With 3-in-1 technology, this portable air conditioner delivers optimum cooling and dehumidification. It also has a fan-only function. The full-function remote control allows you to operate each feature from across the room. Unlike a fixed AC, this unit requires no permanent installation and four caster wheels provide easy mobility between areas. Plus, the auto-evaporation system allows for hours of continuous operation with no water to drain or no bucket to empty. This model comes with everything needed including a flexible exhaust hose and an easy-to-install window venting kit. The window vent can be removed when the unit is not in use.
profile.reviewText:
While the current temperatures in Bismarck between 75-90 F may seem relatively cool compared to other parts of the nation, we still have not-so pleasant humidity to deal with and, living in pre-AC made homes/rentals, some of us have to resort to other methods to keep cool.

As for myself, I rent a room in a pre-AC home with after-market AC only on the ground floor and basement whereas I reside on the third floor with no AC.  This means it gets super hot up there at night even with the windows open.

The opportunity to review the Honeywell MN10 was a godsend and couldn't have arrived sooner and maintains a very good cooling standard well after nearly a month of trying it out.

Now, I may have sold small home appliances at a local store including AC units of various sizes and styles but... that's doesn't mean I installed them or knew how to install them.  Truth be told, I sold major appliances like washers and dryers for years and still have no clue how to install a water hose... safely, at least.

The Honeywell MN10 broke my inept monotony by proving somewhat easy to install.  Just do what any help-line customer service rep will tell you and FOLLOW THE FLIPPIN' MANUAL when installing the AC unit.  Knowing the 10,000 BTU unit would be enough to cover my room and most of the third floor (it's a small split-level home), I found an ideal spot in my room and began to follow the instructions.  The relatively compact size of the unit made it easier to find a place in my room to install it, which is a definite plus.  Didn't take me terribly long to install it with minimal cursing once I followed my own advice and read the manual which, thank God, was written in English unlike others *cough*Samsung*cough*.

Now, it didn't take very long after I powered the unit up to cool down my room and my gauge outside doesn't seem to be hemorrhaging larger numbers to the local power company.

Now, I will say that while the unit is relatively quieter (my last apartment had a modern 8,000 BTU LG that was so loud that I had to turn my Klipsch Icon speakers on my home theater to half power to hear dialog), it is still loud but, then again, it's an indoor AC unit, not an outdoor one that you're not supposed to hear.  I'm no expert but, in my experience, if it's quiet then it's not very effective as a whole.  If anyone knows one that is both efficient, effective, and quiet, let me know!

All in all, I've had very good luck with the Honeywell and would definitely recommend it to others for its ease of installing, use, and effective service that it has provided me... just know that a quiet, effective AC unit doesn't currently exist in my universe... yet.
profile.summary: Efficient and Effective During the Summer in the Midwest

profile.description: This new Foodsaver vacuum sealer has been designed with the sportsman in mind. This unit has a rugged design to handle the toughest jobs. It has improved vacuuming performance, an intelligent sealing system to handle multiple, consecutive jobs and oversized buttons. This unit is equipped with an extra deep drip tray that is removable and easy to clean in the dishwasher. Includes built-in roll holder and cutter to simplify making custom-size bags. Bag material, accessory hose and instruction manual included.
profile.reviewText:
Here, in North Dakota, hunting and fishing is king and that requires a LOT of bagging and tagging.  Between walleye fishing and deer hunting, my fridge is full and my bagging backlogged for years.  With the new Foodsaver, I was hoping to alleviate most of the backlogging and have a ruggedized device that I could carry in the woods for on-site bagging.

The former turned out well while the latter did not.

Anyone thinking this item can work outdoors needs to check the contents list again; the device contains no battery, no DC adapter, and is hardly ruggedized for outdoor use.  On top of that, the bulky design would make it near impossible to carry in a day-pack along with a rifle and 60lbs of gear.  Can only imagine what a battery would do to the weight.

This is not to say the device is not worth attaining, quite the opposite.  The Foodsaver has really been helpful with bagging walleye and northern pike when I brought them back from fishing expeditions.  It is easy to use, heats up quickly, and is easy to clean with a drip catcher.

All in all, the Foodsaver is a decent, albeit expensive addition to my kitchen set but really helps with my fish and hunting needs.
profile.summary: Great for Indoors, Not So Much for Outdoors

profile.description: The Samsung Galaxy S 6 Folio Case (Black) from Urban Armor Gear uses a patented folio design that fuses a soft rubberized binding with a feather light honeycomb core. The unique shape of the case also provides structural rigidity. A precision-engineered cutout on the front of the case insures uncompromised audio with every call, even with cover closed.
profile.reviewText:
I have used UAG products before and have always been very satisfied with them for their rugged designs and stylist looks without sacrificing function or utility like most cheap "ruggedized" cases.

The USAG S6 case fits on very tightly, as one would expect, and the acrylic materials provide excellent flexibility to get the device in but still exert excellent protection.  The clear coating with black trimming looks really good with the white S6 so I wouldn't recommend it for the black sapphire.

Also, unlike most cases, the UAG does not interfere with the buttons so, while it may seem stiff at first, one can still operate the buttons with ease and not worry about any "runoff" and, by that, I mean having your fingers accidentally hit other buttons while touching the home button.  One of my biggest gripes on open-faced cases is that the case overlaps onto the screen too much so when you hit the home button you repeatedly hit another button cause you have to hover half your thumb over the case.

All in all, the UAG is an excellent case and the clear is perfect for the white S6.  A must recommend as well as Speck and Tech21.
profile.summary: UAG's Well-Earned Reputation for Quality Continues

top_5.description: I AM LEGEND
top_5.reviewText:
I Am Legend is one of the films I greatly anticipated for Winter 2007 and having just emerged from the theater I feel as though a great deal is needed.  Perhaps my hopes were just too high but let's look at this point by point.

I Am Legend is roughly take 6 at the original novel of the same name.  The Omega Man is probably the most popular and, for fans of that movie and older generations, this will prove very disappointing as both films derive multiple themes from the book such as Sam the dog, a woman entering Neville's life, etc, etc.  "IAL" just was not unique enough to satisfy certain fans.  For the general audience, however, there are some redeeming qualities.

The visual were very nice.  New York city was reproduced superbly if not used outright as several blocks were closed off for the filming; kudos.  The "monsters" were kind of freaky but I almost felt a humanistic touch to them as one seemed to express remorse for losing one of his kind (I thought she was his daughter or something) but it's not expanded on.

The acting, which comprises almost solely on Will Smith, is superb.  I still am having trouble finding a movie Will Smith acted poorly in every movie he is in I think about seeing just on that basis.  He performs well as a man living almost entirely alone for several years but remains diligent in his tasks.

The story had potential.  It deviated slightly from the book in terms of the ending but I think almost for the better.  I'm glad the directors took a different approach to the Twilight Zone-esque themes of vampires that the original book took.  DESPITE ALL THIS, the movie was TOO SHORT.  It was barely 90 minutes (I think) and sooo much more could've been explained, expanded upon or even made somewhat kewl.  The ending came too quick and very anti-climatic almost to the bewilderment of the audience.  They didn't even bother to explain how certain things came to be and that really bothered me.

The story is similar to War of the Worlds only the movie didn't suck as much; too many holes, not enough time.  IAL could've easily been an epic but directors settled for a 90-minute money bagger and I'm quite disappointed.  The movie started out awesome but just fell short at the end.

I will still buy this on DVD when it comes out but for theater goers I must give a warning that there are holes.  Also, THIS IS NOT A HORROR FILM.  Several people tried to ward me off due to "horror-elements."  This is not the case.  If anything, it is a thriller.  It is appropriate for most audiences although I wouldn't bring too young of kids.

All in all, a B-.  Diss marks for lack of story and length.  It kills the movie.
top_5.summary: Good Acting, Good Visuals, However...

top_5.reviewText:
Before I saw it in theatres I was very excited, however when the movie ended, I was miffed at how cheesy the whole movie was.
It started out good:  Good guys doing the ultimate theft in the Magic School, being caught by the chick.  Then it went downhill from there.  If Jeremey Irons was the badguy, how come we didn't see very much of him?  What was the deal with the heroes sword?  And the ending was the worst of all.  The heroes main sidekick (I forget his name because this movie was soo aweful) did he die?  Was he resurected?  Or like Tupac, abducted?  You tell me, I never figured it out.
This movie had potential to be an excellent movie that could have outdone Lord of the Rings however like Star Wars, the director focused mainly on the special effects which was the only good thing about the movie.
