And sometimes, 2.1 amps is spread through the whole device, meaning multiple iPads will only be charged very slowly. There are no charging compromises with the Supercharger. Charge four iPads at the same time at the single-charge speed. Keep Your Students' iPads Charged During Class1:1 iPad programs in schools are a promising new end tech initiative, but they come with the challenge of having to charge a lot of iPads at the same time. Maybe your students have remembered to bring their iPads to class but forgotten their iPad chargers. Bring one or more USB Superchargers to class, arrange them on the table between students, and you'll have an easy way to keep everyone's iPad up and running. Low or dead batteries can stop learning cold and defeat the benefit of a 1-to-1 iPad program. Now you have the right device to keep the lesson going. Also Charge a Wide Range of USB Devices Each Supercharger port can charge any number of standard USB devices, including iPhone and other smartphones, iPod, portable speakers, Bluetooth headsets, cameras, and more. Everyone will have a use for the Supercharger. Or, use it at home to power up your entire arsenal of devices and be ready to seize the day.
profile.reviewText:
I'd like to think that my family is not a technologically over-saturated group, but somehow we have amassed a ridiculous amount of items that require charging. Even the Tiny One has his "own iPad" since we use the now-defunct 1.0 on Pandora or Spotify as a way for him to listen to "The Alphabet Song" 200 times in a row without us losing our minds.

Thus, this excellent multi-charger, although marketed as ideal for classroom or business use, is just as handy to have at home. Now we can plug in our embarrassing number of iDevices all at once, and have them ready to go in the morning. The higher price might cause hesitation for some, but if you have multiple iPads, you will want the extra power -- it charges two at once quickly and efficiently. (I do agree with the reviewer who pointed out having a simple indicator light would be useful; there is no way of knowing it's on without physically checking if it's plugged in.) The long AC cable is great; no more plugging into extension cords with multiple chunky white USB chargers. We really like the way this product has streamlined the solution to our first-world charging problems!
profile.summary: Charges your ridiculous number of iDevices fast!

profile.description: Reminiscent of his Mohican heritage, Bill Miller's Hear Our Prayer is a Christian worship album that is so intriguing that it compels you to listen. As he mixes his guitar and plaintive flute melodies, he seeks the heart of God in a fashion that is both evocative and inspiring. Bill's fluid voice makes for passionate vocals in worship songs like "I See The Lord," "Hear Our Prayer" and "Father." We hope you'll rejoice to this stirring new album that will engage your soul and move your spirit.
profile.reviewText:
If you're a Bill Miller fan, you'll want this album if just for the last song, his remake of the old spiritual "Ain't Gonna Let Nobody Turn Me Around." This song captures everything we love about Bill.

I was a bit disappointed to find how much the producers of this album had to do with the songwriting. Not sure why they felt the need to write WITH Bill, other than that they wanted to appeal to an audience who may not be familiar with Bill's music but are looking for some 'worship' music. This is great 'worship' music if you compare it to other white stuff out there, but I personally feel that "Ghostdance" and "Spirit Rain" are full of far stronger and truer worship music. If only we sang THOSE songs at church, I'd be able to get more into it. It's cool that Bill is getting to represent the many Native believers in the Jesus Way to the rest of the church, but I hope those who get this CD as their first will go on to buy and love Bill's other music. Still, don't get me wrong, there's some good stuff here, I just wish the other guys had let Bill do ALL the writing for this album.

On the other hand, I like to see this project as Bill reclaiming something. Like in the beautiful old Francis of Assisi hymn (lyrics written almost 800 yrs ago), "All Creatures of Our God" you realize that this is a song for Creator that the first people of this land have sung for a long time while many white brothers sang it hypocritically. And 'Holy Lands' subtley makes you wonder why so many american christians are so passionate about the 'Holy Land' of Israel but don't see this land as being sacred too, having been given by Creator to the First Nations. I see this album also as a humble gift Bill has given to all believers in Creator's Son, and is something that could bridge some chasms. For that, I admire Bill's fearlessness in doing this project, knowing he could get flack for it.
profile.summary: What is "worship" music?

profile.description: A portable blackout blind for when it's still too light to say night night. Anyone who has stayed away from home with little ones will know that it can be tricky to create a snoozy sleeping environment when there is too much light flooding in. The versatile gro anywhere blind has been designed to 'go' anywhere with you, and can be put in place in minutes. Attaches directly to the glass using suction cups, ensuring a close fit that really does block light properly. This new improved version has velcro fastening which is easy to use and quick to adjust, it also features a new stars and moon fabric design. Watch our video to see just how simple it is to make a sunny room fit for your baby to sleep soundly. Adapts to fit any window up to a maximum size of 130cm x 200cm, new improved version reduces to smaller window sizes than previously, whilst maintaining maximum size. New stars and moon design. Comes with handy travel bag. Premium black out material. Velcro fastening is easy to use and quick to adjust.
profile.reviewText:
The Tiny One has slept in a blacked-out room for pretty much forever. This has guaranteed us excellent naps and sleeping through the night, but it does make sleeping at a place that is Not Home a little challenging. Hotels are usually okay as they generally have blackout curtains already, but Other Peoples Homes are almost always a Nap Fail. And as any parent knows, Nap Fail = Not The Most Stellar Day.

Enter the Gro-Anywhere Blindits basically a gigantic sheet of black non-porous plastic with a star & moon design, with velcro and suction cups placed at incomprehensible intervals. I am certain they made sense to whoever was the project manager, but they make no sense to meno matter, this is why you carry pony spring clamps (just search on Amazon, yes, you can buy them here) with you to just clip this on whatever curtain rod you are faced with. Of course, if the window is irregularly-sized, you might need to get creative, but the times Ive had to use this curtain, it did a great job of blocking light and letting the Tiny One get his rest (and the mommy a well-deserved break). Not sure how strong those suction cups are really going to be to hold up a curtain, but since its made to be a temporary solution for Not At Home, Id like to give em the benefit of the doubt.

Its easy to pack and easy to fold and carry. The price is rather steep for what is essentially a large chunk of black shower curtain, but if I was given a choice between Nap Fails and paying $50, Id shell out the dough.
profile.summary: Worth it for traveling

profile.description: 2 ply towel provides better wear and durability with better absorbency; clean and crisp look - combed cotton
profile.reviewText: The more I use this bath "sheet," the more I like it. I've generally used regular-sized towels as I'm not particularly large, but now I'm having trouble going back to a towel that gets completely wet when I dry off. If you have trouble wrapping your towel around you nicely or are in the 6' arena, you owe it to yourself to get a towel like this. It's thick although not fluffy, but not so thick that it won't dry completely by the time you need it again. It does take up a lot of rack space, and hangs closer to the floor than I'd like when hung normally, but that may not bother you. Pricey, but great quality and worth it if this fits your needs you don't need many.
profile.summary: A must for larger humans...a luxury for everyone

top_5.description: Created by celebrity makeup artist Jillian Dempsey to deliver an instant smoky eye. This luxurious liner is made with organic jojoba oil, organic shea butter and marula oil to give the product a smooth, waterproof finish. The built-in smudger allows you to blend the color for a soft-focus look.
top_5.reviewText:
You can't beat the ingredients in this formula...it's oh so natural and has nothing remotely toxic in it. However, that plus seems to always come with a price. I have yet to find a natural formula that stays on all day. That said, my eyelids tend to get a little oily, so if you have drier skin on your eyelids, this eyeliner may have better staying power for you.

It glides on nicely and gives you a nice controlled line--from super skinny to thicker, and it smudges well too. The black is nicely pigmented and a good neutral black. However, I found that I had to reapply within a few hours. So I'm definitely going to have to use primer underneath this one, which I prefer not to do (the fewer the products for me, the better). But it's great to know this eyeliner is gentle and even good for my skin. It won't be my go-to, but it's definitely a quality natural eyeliner that's worth trying out if you care about ingredients.
top_5.summary: Great natural formula--but not exactly waterproof

top_5.description: This item is still sealed in the original packaging.
top_5.reviewText:
In spite of critics' complaints, Tears of the Sun is a successful film on many levels. Of course the conflict details are fictional-- but the details are far from the point of the story; the filmmakers obviously wanted to rather portray the heart of similar conflicts in Africa (such as Uganda, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Sudan) that the West has largely ignored. Thus, the underlying question is: why do we turn a blind eye to such injustice? Could it be that we think Africans are worth less than those with white skin or lucrative natural resources? The filmmakers succeed in causing us to care without over-manipulation, to the point that we must agree with the SEAL who says, "I can't see them as 'packages' any more."

While I felt it was overly brutal for the viewer to watch so many of the SEALs die in the course of the mission (as American movie watchers, we like as many of the 'good guys' to stay alive-- we're only willing to let a couple go for the sake of realism), it drives home this truth: the lives of the refugees they were protecting were just as valuable as theirs. Even though viewers are more familiar with the American characters than the majority of the Nigerians' characters, this equality in value is sucessfully made clear. In the end, we find ourselves, along with the Lieutenant [Willis], understanding why the doctor [Belucci] was unwilling to save her own life while leaving the others to die--their lives were worth just as much as our own. The quote at the end of the film leaves us with this problem to consider as we face our real-life world, just as embroiled in violence and injustice: "The only thing necessary for evil men to triumph is for good men to do nothing."
top_5.summary: Suceeds in communicating the indiscriminate value of all people

top_5.description: Jeaniene Frost is the New York Times, USA Today, and international bestselling author of the Night Huntress series and the Night Huntress World novels. To date, foreign rights for her novels have sold to nineteen different countries. Jeaniene lives in North Carolina with her husband Matthew, who long ago accepted that she rarely cooks and always sleeps in on the weekends. Aside from writing, Jeaniene enjoys reading, poetry, watching movies with her husband, exploring old cemeteries, spelunking and traveling - by car. Airplanes, children, and cook books frighten her.
top_5.reviewText:
Are you kidding me? It's like the author waited to the last minute to put together a plot, chose the most ridiculous conflict possible, and then contrived all kinds of ridiculousness around it. I hate how long series like this seem to often get to this point and suddenly feel they can manufacture some kind of faux-dramatic hardship that will make an awesome strong female protag suddenly weak and annoying in the most not-believable way possible, as if they're following some manufactured conflict formula. Cut her down at the knees until she's so lame that you can !sooprize! your readers and [gasp!] make her come back...EVEN STRONGER! YAY! It's so disrespectful to readers, like we're that easy to manipulate.

The amount of arbitrary junk being thrown around...and I thought the end of the last one, where after lounging around the house waiting forever, everyone fights cartoon zombies then flies in the sky like Hogwarts students over to kill I mean passively watch the villain die...was starting to get random...Everything about this plot went beyond random...it was just lame.

The main conflict was so sketchy it was laughable; the relationship conflict was so fake it was a complete unemotional/unreal bore to slog through; the contrived 'magic' was totally unconvincing; the villain was a totally ridiculous cartoon; the character development was zero. Plus, I'm sick of how much Cat continues to get pawed at like an object by men simply because they're supposedly "red-blooded males" and it doesn't bother her...eyeroll. It's like no matter how badass and snarky she is, she's supposed to take all of it in stride. I understand why so many readers gave up on this series after this farce of a plot. You can easily skip this one if you don't want to give up yet, and you won't miss anything important that won't be repeated in the next one.
top_5.summary: Skip it and miss nothing but annoyance and wasted time!

top_5.description: NEW MEGA MORPHIBIANS from Kid Galaxy! It's an animal, it's a 4x4, it's a speed boat........ no it's a Morphibian! These high-performance radio control amphibious creatures can go anywhere! Dirt, sand, pond or pool; No terrain is too tough or too wet. Featuring sturdy 4x4 turf digging tires for land and wake forming paddle wheel treads for ripping through the water. If you love racing, you'll love the Mega Morphibians Crocodile companion creatures; Mega Morphibian Turtle, Mega Morphibian Snake and Mega Morphibian Lobster, all available now! Easy to use and Fun for Everyone Age 3 years and up.
top_5.reviewText:
First of all, I will save you the insanity-inducing exercise of the Quest for Battery Installation and just say: narrow-stemmed phillips-head screwdriver. Go find it. Good. Okay. Now your experience might be a half-star better. The battery compartment is on the top, and its waaaaay in there, because it needs to be sealed off from that water you're supposedly gonna run this beast through. You will get annoyed. You will recover.

Next, I will tell you that this R/C vehicle runs on a 9V and 3 AAAs and they are not included. Unless you are like me and have a ridiculous amount of 9V batteries in your garage from a past job, you will probably need to beg, borrow, or steal one of those rectangular bits of power from someone before you reveal this toy to your kid. No, you cant have mine. I bet you have AAAs, though, so theres that. And, to be fair, most RC toys require loads of various and sundry batteries.

Finally, I will give you this big hint so that you don't embarrass yourself by driving The Morphibian in ridiculous circles:  the control has 2 tiny joysticky knobs  the right one controls the right wheels; the left controls the left wheels. Meaning you will need to manipulate them in tandem to get it to go where you want.

Why do i give you these hints, you ask? When i could just read the instruction manual? Because THERE IS NONE. Yeah, none.  As in Ikea-style none. Actually, no, scratch that, at least Ikea gives you vaguely helpful stick-figure drawings. No luck here. Oh please, you say, I need no manual. This is an R/C car! I can figure it out!  Okay, great. Good for you.  I hope you do, because you can then teach your kid how to use it.  Good luck with that remote. Its tiny, and the range is okay to meh.

Product description says 3 & up, but it might be a little wack for a 3 yr old to manipulate. My tiny person didn't really care as much about operating it as much as he liked chasing it and watching dad or mom zoom it around. Also, a word about the all-terrain claims  its great on carpet.  Great on cement. Okay on short, mostly-dead grass (we live in drought territory; don't judge). Pretty good with puddles (hence, Amphibious!). Terrible with loose dirt. Has a tendency to wipe out/flip over when terrain changes.

There you have it. Hopefully all these Hints will help you and your kid drive the Morphibian like crazy instead of going crazy yourself.
top_5.summary: How to Not Go Crazy Without an Instruction Manual

top_5.description: While in college, Spokane Reservation best friends Aristotle and Seymour took different paths. Aristotle went back to "the rez," while Seymour began a new life for himself as an openly gay poet. Sixteen years later, the two are reunited, but mutual feelings of hurt and resentment stand in the way of their friendship.
top_5.reviewText:
So very Sherman Alexie. So brilliantly creative. So indie filmmaking at its best. I'll warn you that this will not everyone's cuppa bitter root tea--about as far from Hollyweird as you can get...so if you don't like non-Hollyweird films, don't expect the usual and you may still enjoy this. (Caveat: I rather like Hollyweird...just not all the time.) I would call it the best film about poetry and living in two worlds I've ever seen, but I like poetry and live in two worlds. Still, you might like it even if you don't like poetry or live in two worlds. (Although you have to have gone to a poetry reading or author lecture in a white university or artsy fartsy literary venue to fully appreciate the hilarious intercut scenes of Seymour doing his schtick.) I don't quite know how to say it, but this film totally captured (at least for me) the fear of any artist/writer/etc who leaves where they came from and writes/makes art about their people and is celebrated as an outsider but is never accepted for what they want to be accepted for at home... of being found out as an impostor or being not-accepted by their people in that role. I used to call this my My Name is Asher Lev fear (although I admit never finishing that book), and now I think I have to call it my Seymour Polatkin Fear. (Maybe that makes no sense. eh.)

Anyway. If you dig Evan Adams, he's prit-ty awesome as a Gay Urban Indian Poet...yep. One thing I would want to point out, though, is that even though this film is often categorized as a Gay/Lesbian film and even won some related award, I would not label it like that at all. Yes, the main character is gay, and even as inherently navel-gazing as poetry is (and Evan's Seymour character is), this isn't about gay identity angst (in my opinion). And I don't know who put the tag in here, but I'm sorry, this isn't about 'interracial homoerotica.' I wouldn't want to label it with any other Blockbuster label, but if I had to, I'd say it's a really, really Good Indian Movie about people.

I don't know what took me so long to see this...when it came out and run through the festival circuit I remember trying to get the university theater to run it, and it never worked out. But I bought the soundtrack then, worth it if only for Michelle St. John and Jennifer Kriesberg (the high-voiced chica from Ulali) singing one of the most beautiful songs ever to end a movie with)...but the 49's and Swil Kanam's stuff with Gene Tabagan is awesome, too. It was great to finally see the context of the songs.
top_5.summary: 2 worlds (or maybe 3, or 4 or...)

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "2-wheeled 20 inch satchel". The summary of the review text is "Lipault is my favourite luggage designer for their thick nylon fabrics and bright ...".
output:
Update: used the suitcase to transport some clothes to my mother and brother in the hospital. We don't have a car, so we took the subway and walked. Wheels did well, was able to pull behind me while pushing a stroller with no issues. You do miss the protection beneath the side that sits on the ground if you leave the bag with the handle upright, and somehow it has acquired a tiny hole in the fabric. Have not experienced this with other Lipault bags and am disappointed.

Lipault is my favourite luggage designer for their thick nylon fabrics and bright colours. Their suitcases really stand out in a crowd and are easily recognisable on the belts at baggage claim. I bought this wheeled satchel for those reasons, to use as a weekend bag for short family trips where we can get away with not checking any luggage.

On first impression, it holds up to the standard I consider Lipault to have set with their wheeled suitcases. This carry-on is spacious, the nylon is obviously high-quality, the satchel design is unique and cute, everything from the telescopic handle to the wheels to the zipper of the main compartment has been given obvious thought and consideration. The handle can be stowed beneath a zippered cover and the bag opens in a broad square shape for packing and unpacking.

I was able to toss in 4 days of worth of clothing for myself and my toddler, as well as a puzzle, a small soft body doll, a snack cup, baby food pouches, toiletries and an extra pair of shoes.

It packed it with clothes experimentally and walked it through our hall and outside, and it seems stable.

As other reviewers have noted, there is oddly no
plastic protection on the side of the bag that would be on the floor were you to leave it with the handle upright. The bottom of the bag is well protected. I'm assuming that the shape of the bag prohibits stiff plastic on the sides, as they have to be flexible and taper up towards the handles.

What I wish was different:

No outside pockets
Only one inside pocket

Other:
The colour fuschia looks like a bright pink in the photos but is actually a deeper purple/pink in person. Still pretty, just different.

In short: this is the bag for you if you want a cute wheeled satchel that is actually huge and will hold quite a lot. It is not the bag for you if you actually want a suitcase with more pockets and a sturdier and more traditional shape.

profile.description: Lojel streamline polypropylene 25 inch medium upright spinner luggage is made with a new polypropylene material which provides the case with utmost resistance to shock and scuffing which normally is common in other polypropylene cases. This lightweight spinner with safe and strong burst-free double coil zippers prevents it from breaking open when heavy loaded and from theft. The handles, locks and trolley are designed to retract, leaving all surfaces flush, with nothing to catch on to the surrounding objects. Streamline also offers smooth and effortless movement with its wheels system developed by renowned Japanese hinomoto. With 8 different colors to choose from, there is a perfect streamline for everybody
profile.reviewText:
Update: used it for family travel to Disney world. It went over uneven city pavement, survived a fall onto a sidewalk from on top of a car seat on a wheelchair (don't ask?) and is in total only mildly scratched in a difficult to notice way. The textured plastic does not scuff white or black. Zipper held up better than I expected. Never felt like it would bust, even when pushed to the limit. Held about two weeks worth of toddler clothes, a week's worth of my clothes, a cooler of medicine, swim gear, and a pair of sneakers. Used packing cubes and rolled clothes. Weighed a ton but rolled like a champ with one hand while I pushed either stroller or wheelchair. Very impressed. Would buy Lojel again.

----

I was hesitant to buy this because of the reviews, but it was starkly reduced in price so I took the plunge because we needed another carry on for a trip to Disney World. I'm very glad I did.

The first impression I had of this suitcase was that it seems very sturdy. Yes, it is plastic-y, but the polycarbonate shell is thick and by no means cheap looking. The plastic effect is just heightened because of the late 90's Barbie color and the fact that it's a matte textured finish instead of the glossy finish that is the norm on most plastic hard cases.

I had a flight attendant friend and a relative give it a little spin around the house, and the consensus is that it's a great looking and good quality suitcase for the money. I would judge it to fall somewhere on the spectrum above Delsey and around Travelpro in terms of perceived durability and function. The wheels are very smooth and transition from upright to diagonal without any jarring. The zipper is thick and was very easy to pull around a heavily packed suitcase without feeling like it would split. My TSA locks have been working.

The interior is extremely basic but functional. There'sthe main/larger compartment for clothes etc, with the usual strap to help keep them contained. The other side is divided from this by a zippered mesh wall, creating a second compartment. The fabric is light gray and a sturdy feeling synthetic.

The suitcase is light, even when fully packed. It held a week's worth of clothes for myself and my two year old (8 outfits for me, 10 for her), as well as a pair of sneakers, two pairs toddler sandals, accessories, and pool supplies. This is about what I would expect from a carry on, although more space could be achieved if the suitcase didn't indent where the black handle is. I can't think of a purpose for this indentation other than keeping the handle tucked in so it doesn't snag on anything, but it kills off an extra couple inches of packing space.

All in all, the Streamline hardcase carry on has piqued my interest in the Lojel brand. Its simplicity and understated quality set it aside from many of the cheaper brands you can find in this price range on Amazon. If i had space for one, i would buy a second of these.
profile.summary: I'm very glad I did

This bag is exactly what I was looking for. Much higher quality than all the cheap ones that ship from china on here. It's made form organic cotton that is sturdily woven but still soft as cotton is. You can feel and see the difference. Holds much more than you would think - perfect for farmer's market haul or a trip to the grocery store for 1-2 day's worth of food. I bought a bag similar to this in Paris many years ago but had not been able to find a suitable replacement until now!

profile.description: Rosalina and her friends welcome you to an afternoon tea party at their brand new castle! What a lovely space for your child's imagination to run wild. Measuring 35 1/2" L x 20 3/4" W x 43 1/2" H, this tent will fit great in just about any playroom. Children will adore the vibrantly-colored and nicely detailed scene depicted on the outside of the tent! Tent material is made of polyester and frame is made of plastic rods, making both setting up, putting away and storage a quick breeze. All materials free from harmful chemicals such as fire retardants, water repellents, BPA, PVC and phthalates.
profile.reviewText:
I got this through open box deals, and I feel like the discounted price is more fair. I would maybe pay about $50-70 for this full priced, but not $80-90. $80-90 would be worth it with an organic cotton fabric, metal poles and proof that it was produced fair trade.

It was easy enough to put together, instructions were clear. Took about ten minutes to set up. I like that the cover zips onto the base.

The plastic poles do not feel very sturdy. My daughter is able to easily turn the house into its side while she's inside it, which requires constant supervision. I would have preferred a light metal pole with plastic joints. So far it is holding up though, and the fabric itself is very sturdy. The print is adorable and exactly as pictured.

Gave it four stars because it's very cute and my daughter loses her mind with excitement every time I set it up.

profile.description: Radio Flyer new ultimate EZ fold wagon is designed as a full size wagon for 2 kids that folds compactly. With an easy one hand fold, you can take or store the wagon anywhere. Two kids ride comfortably with 2 seats, 4 cup holders, seatbelts for added safety, and a removable canopy. The telescoping handle is for easy transport when folded. The DuraClean fabric is durable and can be easily wiped clean. A full size wagon with a compact fold to take & store anywhere. For ages 1 1/2 +.
profile.reviewText:
My daughter (nearly 2) is obsessed with her "bye bye". We have the wagon out constantly to use as a bench and hang out with pillows and blankets in the living room, and we've already done some quick trips around the neighbourhood. People stop constantly to ask where we found it - it's such a uniquely adorable collapsible wagon.

We have very limited urban apartment space, so the collapsible feature was a necessity. The wagon folding mechanism is incredibly easy and takes only one hand. The wagon itself is very light and rides well. As for the overturning issue - as with any wagon, try not to take turns too quickly or sharply and all should be well.

My only issue is the lack of a seatbelt. It would have been incredibly easy to have included a lap belt in the design of this. I purchased a 5point harness on Amazon and am going to install the lap part for peace of mind.

profile.description: Looking to provide your child with soothing comfort and protection at night? Get ready for our uniquely designed night light!! Babies, infants and toddlers are tender, innocent creatures. Night time for us adults are pretty much normal, but for them, it can be a time of terror and fear, hence the common phrase- "Fear of the Dark". This can make life difficult for the parent/guardian looking after them, endlessly having to comfort them during the night, resulting in them feeling nothing short of tired. Here at Little Lamby, we have just the nifty little device that solves this problem!  Uniquely designed, with a brightness that does not dazzle the eyes, yet comforts the child  Voice control system that powers device on with the sound of a voice  Battery powered for simple, hassle-free management of the device Your baby will never fear the night again!!! Our design looks colourful and cutesy, so as to provide the child with a greater sense of comfort at night. The illumination will hence keep him or her feeling safe as well as secure during the night, so you can give yourself a break as well!  Unique design with a subtle illumination to not dazzle your child's eyes yet provide comfort  Battery powered for simple, easy use  Voice control technology for added efficiency
profile.reviewText: This nightlight is very cute. Touch activation is easy, and it picks up my 14 month old daughter's raised voice as well as my own, which is perfect for when she wakes up in the middle of the night to deliver her now block-famous battle cries. It takes 4 AAs, not included. Will update when I know how long the batteries last. It comes with wall stickers of a bunny parent and kid driving over the rainbow bridge to get some carrots, but we decided not to use them as they were pretty sticky and might make the paint peel. The night light also comes with a three-pronged tiny nail thing for hanging it, which seems to work well and leaves more discreet holes for renters to refill and paint over. In total, a great buy. Took off one star because I wish it had an option to leave the light on permanently.

profile.description: Get a call with the PlanToys phone! A magnifier screen and a colorful beaded dial pad make a wonderful toy for interactive play and help to develop children's dexterity and cognitive skills. Made in PlayWood. For more than 30 years, PlanToys has been consistently developing its products and activities with a strong commitment to contribute positively to the world. By implementing best practices and taking innovation of toy-making and design to the next level, PlanToys is not only known as being the first company to manufacture wooden toys from preservative-free rubber wood, we are a leading company that has created a new material and process as part of our zero waste goals. profile.reviewText:
Update: at 14 months, having dug it up from the bottom of the toy bin while on the hunt for dolls to swing wildly by their little arms, she found this and suddenly Cares . Play is still centered mostly on chewing on it, so it really is a glorified teether, but for educational purposes she does occasionally shove it into my hands so I can pretend I'm fielding her phone calls. Moral of the story appears to be that this toy is probably for babies/toddlers old enough to recognise either the vaguely technological shape and think 'one of those! This is perfect for shaving down my new teeth!' or 'this is perfect for training mom to be my future secretary!'

I don't wipe my cell phone down nearly enough to let my 9 month old turn it into the glorified teether she wishes it was, so I thought buying her a toy cell phone might do the trick. I wanted to avoid anything flashy and noisy - it really seemed like the shape and size of the phone was what appealed to her. This Plan Toys phone is cute and the right size. I love that the buttons can be pushed and the little strap, but the baby has zero interest in it. Every time I hand it to her, she takes it, holds it out to the side and drops it. I'm hoping she's just too young and will eventually get into it. Took off one star because I feel like the magnifying glass screen would be more interesting if it were a baby mirror or even a colourful picture. It's also made of a funky pulped wood composite, like a lot of 'green' toys seem to be now. I wish the ridge between the front and the back pieces were smoother.

profile.description: Your kids will love to play on the farm with the amazing Pop-it-Up Farm play tent. It comes with a fun printed farm scene play mat that promotes imaginative play and strengthens creativity in kids. The 100% polyester tent is easy to set up and easy to fold away into the compact carry bag. Included are the tent with 2 doors and removable roof and mat. When assembled the tent is 35.5 x 35.5 x 35.5". For 3-6 year olds.
profile.reviewText:
Purchased for a 15 month old who is just beginning to enjoy playing in blanket tents. These tents usually go for $30, but this one was listed for around $20 so I took the plunge despite the lack of reviews.

It is well-constructed and very bright. The inside floor has farm details for make-believe play, and the little door flaps can be tied up for easier entry and exiting. The roof is a separate piece that velcros onto the top. Set up is simple and takes less than a minute.

We have used this tent both indoors and at the beach. The little bag has convenient carrying handles to hang from the stroller. The size has been big enough for both myself and my daughter to fit relatively comfortably for play. I am 5'. I don't think her dad, who is 6'4", could fit inside at all. For a toddler, however, it's a really decently sized tent!

Overall it is well worth the $20. The only downside is that it can be difficult to fold t back up. I usually pride myself on being very good at folding these pop up things, but the tent body is complicated and at times I have worried I would break it while trying. Seems sturdy though, no signs of breakage at all.
profile.summary: ... a 15 month old who is just beginning to enjoy playing in blanket tents

profile.description: Bring your art studio on the go! Faber-Castells Do Art Portable Easel holds all of your art materials in 2 tidy drawers. Recommended by art educators, each easel is stocked full of premium quality Faber-Castell art supplies including Mini Colored Pencils, Beeswax Crayons, Markers, Chalk, Dry Erase Marker, Eraser, Pencil Sharpener and Sketch Pad. Lock the easel in place and secure your paper using the attached clips and create art on the go! Fold the easel back up and youve got a convenient lap desk. This 37 piece art set is great for ages 4+.
profile.reviewText:
First things first: I did buy this primarily for plane travel but think it will be too big for our carry-on. Watch the video for a good representation of the size. That said, we have it brought it out with us and my daughter really enjoys using it.

I bought this for my nearly 17 month old. She's too young for the colored pencils and markers, but the Faber Castell beeswax crayons that come with this are some of the best on the market, and she really enjoys making lines with the chalk.

The case is made of a relatively sturdy plastic. The drawers on the sides are a great touch and very deep for storing a wide assortment of art supplies. The chalkboard works wonderfully, none of that annoying plastic-y chalkboard thing where the chalk won't write on it. It's almost as good as a slate tablet. It also has a little ridge built underneath for holding chalk while in use.

My daughter is fascinated by the dry erase marker and loves to pick the entire case up by the handle and drag it around the house. It is definitely one of if not the best plastic portable easels on the market, and the addition of Faber Castell art supplies puts it in a class of its own.

My only issues are the size, the small amount of crayons (8-10 would have been nicer), and the case does not actually fit the drawing pad. I've also found that I have to stick the entire pad under the clips, otherwise the paper is too thin and slides out.

All that said, i still recommend it above any other.
profile.summary: Watch the video for a good representation of the size

profile.description: Wooden figures are large and chunky with rounded edges, and no upper age limit for playing; even adults are drawn to their simple charm. The minimalist forms of wooden figures combined with their chunkiness and hand made attention to detail ensure a child's imagination is stimulated allowing for hours of play and simultaneous learning. The toys are made predominantly of maple which is durable and characterized by attractive graining. They are sanded, dyed, painted and finished all by hand! the result? timeless and beautifully stylized wooden animals which allow a child's imagination to develop fully while playing and having fun.
profile.reviewText:
Half the time I look at this and go, what the heck was I thinking paying $10 for a toy fox?
It's a beautiful wooden toy fox. My two year old loves it 50% of the time. I love it 100% of the time. I will not kid myself that I bought it entirely for her. She's just as happy with plastic. I'm the one who wants the toy room full of aesthetically pleasing wooden toys (incidentally fewer toys, because the wood are expensive).

It has rounded edges, a whimsical Ostheimer-like paint job, and is made of extremely lightweight but durable wood which has meant fewer injuries and table denting without broken pieces. This separates it from other similar wooden toy foxes.
profile.summary: It's a beautiful wooden toy fox

profile.description: Kleen Kanteen raised the bar when they designed the 18 oz Reflect Bottle with its beautiful finish, bamboo cap , food-grade silicone and stainless steel. It symbolizes Klean Kanteen's deep commitment to continued innovation and the promise to deliver value and quality with integrity. The first of its kind, the Reflect is crafted using sustainably harvested bamboo, food-grade silicone and stainless steel. Beautiful in its simplicity and deliberate in its design, what you don't see on the Reflect is as important as what you do. No paint. No plastic. Bottle is dishwasher safe, bamboo cap is not. Scrub cap with warm soapy water, rinse and dry immediately. Available in brushed or mirrored finish.Capacity: 18 fl oz.
profile.reviewText:
I was so hesitant to buy yet another reusable water bottle that would only disappoint me, or thatd Id be grossed out by after forgetting to wash it for a day. Glad I took the plunge on this. There are no fiddly little crevices, so cleaning is incredibly easy. The cap is one large solid piece. The silicone ring inside comes off for a deeper clean. Relatively leak-proof, and it just looks nice. Kind of like a vintage milk bottle. Ive already saved the cost of the bottle in $1 plastic water bottles, and its nice knowing Im not contributing more plastic waste to landfill or the ocean. Holds a decent amount of water and is very light weight. My issue with glass was the weight. This one is light enough to stick in a backpack without feeling like you need a brace on.
I only notice taste transfer when its been sitting in there a while and its warm.

profile.description: The world's best crayon! Theres never been a crayon so luscious and vibrant as the Brilliant Beeswax Crayons by Faber-Castell. Color lays down soft and smooth and the triangular shape is easy and comfortable for little hands to hold. Bonus, they dont roll off the table or desk! The handy storage case has a snap closure to keep your crayons protected when youre on the go! These crayons are non-toxic, acid free and safety tested for children. Beeswax Crayons are so vibrant you can even use them on black paper! Pair with Watercolor Paints for fun and interesting resist techniques. The 12 pack of beeswax crayons contains the following colors: White, yellow, peach, orange, red, lime, green, sky blue, blue, purple, brown and black. Brilliant Beeswax crayons are recommended for ages 3+.
profile.reviewText: I bought this carrying case for my nearly 2 year old for travel. There is just enough space for a very thin pad of paper or some loose small sheets. the colour selection is broad, with 4+ vibrant hues from each colour group, as well as basic black, white, and grey. It has a range of potential skin tone colors for most* races considering there are only 24 crayons. (*as with most crayons, accuracy is not 100% but it does offer more than just peach and brown). The case itself is sturdy and the besswax crayons have not failed us yet. They are smooth transferring onto paper, bright and vivid, and do not break easily. My daughter loves dropping them into boots and shoes at random. Well worth the $10, although if it matters to you, most of the Faber Castell children's line is produced in China and not in Germany. This is a bummer to me because I know that the quality of worker care in their German factory is regulated and quite high.
profile.summary: The case itself is sturdy and the besswax crayons have not failed us yet

profile.description: The world's best crayon! Theres never been a crayon so luscious and vibrant as the Brilliant Beeswax Crayons by Faber-Castell. Color lays down soft and smooth and the triangular shape is easy and comfortable for little hands to hold. Bonus, they dont roll off the table or desk! The handy storage case has a snap closure to keep your crayons protected when youre on the go! These crayons are non-toxic, acid free and safety tested for children. Brilliant Beeswax crayons are recommended for ages 3+.
profile.reviewText:
Update: After over a month of abuse, the only crayon that broke was snapped in half because my daughter literally jumped on top of it at a weird angle. She has eaten a large chunk off the tip of dark blue and yellow (a budding Van Gogh? For toddlers, it seems, happiness truly can be found in the consumption of a good, bright beeswax yellow). I wouldn't recommend feeding these to your kids for snacks, but considering the speed of their hand-to-mouth action, I'm glad I can rest assured that these are truly non-toxic and generally very difficult to bite into (giving you extra time to wrestle the crayon from your toddler's death grip and calm those tortured screams as you explain in vain that crayons are for art and not for eating). The paper has amazingly also stood up to being slid up and down, scraped against teeth, thrown on the floor, torn at, rubbed against toys and furniture - you name it. I'm really impressed.

These crayons are vibrant and smooth and easy to draw with. I bought them to teach my 13 month old how to scribble, and she instantly took to them and loves making wild lines all over her sketch pad now. They easily washed off our enamel tabletop and tiled bathroom walls, but I have yet to experience any marks on the drywall or on wood. Will update if (hopefully not) I ever have to try and remove anything like that, but Mr Clean's Magic Eraser usually works wonders with those kinds of marks so I am not too worried. I have long been a fan of Faber-Castell, having used them myself for art and their pencils, erasers and pastel highlighters in school when I lived in Germany.

Other reasons for five stars:

The plastic case is a unique and well-thought out addition that holds up really well to grabby little hands that would have torn or eaten straight through cardboard.
The large size makes them easy for my one year old to hold in her fist, and the triangular shape is supposed to eventually help her learn to hold the crayons between three fingers.
They are extremely durable and have held up well to being bit into, thrown, stood on and slammed repeatedly into a pad of paper for what I can only assume was supposed to be a stippling effect.
They are some of the cheapest beeswax crayons on Amazon, but come with 12 great colours.
Like all kids crayons, they are non-toxic.

I would definitely recommend these and will purchase again once these have worn down to nubs.
profile.summary: Great quality, beautiful colours

profile.description: Introducing babies to water can be an interesting affair, some kids will love it, others will be more cautious. The Nemo Baby Seat features a diaper style seat with leg holes. Babies will not only be comfortable, but they can learn to kick underwater which will help with their swimming when the time comes for them to take the next step. Constructed using 3 chambers for added safety and durability, the Nemo Baby Seat is the ideal inflatable to help children learn to have fun in the water.
profile.reviewText:
This was amazingly cheap. We bought it when my daughter was two months old to use in the pool while visiting family in Florida. She was of course very small in it and had to be constantly supported, but it helped us ease into having her in the pool with us during the first few times when we were still so nervous about dropping her. Now that she is approaching her first year, I am looking forward to another visit and to trying this seat out again. I have a feeling she will love it.

It is cut quite deep, but that makes it more difficult for a child to tip it over. The nemo design is cute enough, if simplistic. As far as it goes, a pretty standard pool seat.

I took off one star because the leg holes are cut very wide, which puts a lot of pressure between the legs and seems uncomfortable for a child who doesn't know how to kick yet to help keep afloat a bit better.
profile.summary: I have a feeling she will love it. It is cut quite deep

profile.description: Our most popular theme! Sweet Kisses baby is designed perfectly for cuddles with a super soft body and a fresh scent. Her clothing is the softest cotton and at 16" she's appropriately sized for little arms. Her special feature is a light as air kiss when her leg is pressed. This doll makes a great gift. Give the one you love a kiss today! All Nenuco babies are mildly scented. Your little one wants to be just like you. Nenuco dolls provide aspirational role play for children of all ages to interact with their dolls in fun everyday ways. Just like a real mommy. Nenuco is the doll brand that moms have been giving their daughters for over 50 years. Start your tradition today.
profile.reviewText: My 14 month old loves this doll, hence the 4 stars. I am a big Corolle fan, having grown up on them, but was not as big a fan of their prices for a 'just because' gift. Famosa/Nenuco dolls seem to be closest to Corolle in the sweetness of their faces; some dolls are downright creepy now. Like Corolle, there is a light vanilla scent in the doll's 'skin'. The weight is good. The body is very soft and huggable and 'floppy' for carrying around and sticki into strollers. It is a $10 doll that exceeds the quality I would expect at that price point. The clothes are cute, if thin, and the face is truly sweet. As others have noted, the kissing feature is really just blown air and a clicking sound, my daughter likes it. One point came off for the attached hair ribbon on the head. It's inserted into the vinyl, but I am still sure my daughter will manage to yank it out one day with her crafty little fingers. Considering it says 1+ on the box, I think they should have skipped out on the attached hair ribbon and gone for a hat or something instead.
profile.summary: Famous/Nenuco dolls seem to be closest to Corolle in the sweetness of their faces

profile.description: Sleeveless tribal printed two tone jersey knit long maxi dress featuring a ruched v-neckline. A casual sexy summer maxi dress for all looks and occasions.
profile.reviewText:
Update: this is not a summer dress unless you live in northern Sweden or on the Siberian tundra, where summer means mid-70s at worst. The inside lining is made of polyester and because the dress is tight, it will cling to your abdomen like it's your own personal fabric oven. I wore it for a few hours outside the other day and felt like I was about to keel over; my skin was covered in sweat where the dress had been. It was like no heat could escape. Three stars because I'll still wear it in winter or fall, but the plastic fabric is a major letdown for a dress that markets itself as 100% cotton. I can no longer recommend.

I really wanted to look like Audrey Hepburn but with bigger boobs (they're there, I doubt they're going anywhere). I'm on a limited budget, so the price of this dress is what spoke to me first. I read the reviews and ordered a small (I am 5' and 100-105lbs depending on the time of month, with a 32DD chest when at its biggest because of breastfeeding). The dress comes a few inches below my knee in a modest era-appropriate hemline. The small fits me very well, although the torso is cut for women with a torso about an inch longer than mine. This isn't really noticeable except to me. The fabric is heavy and soft - even softer when washed. I don't actually find that it wrinkles easily, but it will need to be ironed or steamed after washing to get the hem straight again. It looks as fantastic with a petticoat as without!

I took off one star because the belt is way too big. I'll have to cut it and have been using a 2 inch thick Singer ribbon as a sash in the meantime.

Otherwise this is a great, flattering dress in a classic look. Great value for the money.

profile.description: DecoBros Laundry sorter help you to sort different types, color of clothes.
profile.reviewText:
I bought this cart because it looked very sturdy. We are a family of three and do our laundry roughly once a week. The idea of having three separate compartments for laundry really appealed to me, as did the removable bags and the heavy-looking chrome frame. It was easy to assemble and looked great when we first set it up. The wheels are very large and the materials seem high-quality. Only the bags disappointed me, as they seem to be made from a cheaper synthetic canvas and are a darker beige than pictured.

Over the course of the past 8 or so months the cart has begin lilting severely to one side, and there seems to be no way to tighten the poles to one another. We keep it in one spot in our room and it does not move from there. Two of the bags have split open at the corner just from moderate use. If I had known all of this beforehand, I might have gone with a smaller but sturdier hamper.

profile.description: MOMENTUM On-Ear. Stunning sound and sensational style. Beautiful and compact, the MOMENTUM On-Ear embodies the style and substance of Sennheiser's critically acclaimed MOMENTUM headphones in a smaller, lighter, refreshingly fashionable approach. Designed specifically for use with phones, tablets and laptops, MOMENTUM On-Ear is the perfect choice for "on the go" music enthusiasts seeking superb sound quality. MOMENTUM On-Ear employs precision 18-ohm transducers using powerful neodymium magnets. They deliver exceptional detail, superb dynamics and solid bass response. The smooth frequency response has a slightly elevated emphasis in the bass, delivering a full bodied, warm sound. The ear cushions and stainless steel headband are covered in luxurious Alcantara, for exceptional wearing comfort for long listening sessions. MOMENTUM On-Ear is available in a range of fresh pastel and traditional colors carefully selected by an international team of fashion designers. profile.reviewText:
I am not an audiophile. I just wanted good-looking headphones of a higher quality than the apple earbuds I was replacing, that could also double as a fashion statement. I love the suede details on these and the plush earcups. The quality is noticeably better than my apple earbuds (rip), these are comfortable to wear for hours on end, and they look so cool person. A very unique and vintage design. They also come with a storage case, instructions, and two different cables. One is for iPhones with the volume and mic controls. The other is just a basic cable.

I took off one point because they do pull out of the headphone jack on my iPhone 6 a lot easier than my old headphones did, and after a day of pulling one ear back to hear things going on outside, the metal headband is slightly skewed. It's not noticeable when I wear them though.
profile.summary: I love the suede details on these and the plush earcups

profile.description: The KitchenAid Diamond Blender, with exclusive diamond blending system, provides the ultimate blending performance to stir, chop, mix, puree and liquify, with pulse 1-5 settings and crush ice mode. A robust motor, unique one-piece, BPA-Free diamond pitcher, stainless steel blades and electronic controls combine to create a powerful vortex that is fast and thorough for exceptional blending results. Additionally, Intelli-Speed Motor Control senses contents and maintains optimal speed to power through all ingredients.
profile.reviewText:
Upgrade from a Bella bullet-style blender. I use my blender mostly for making smoothies but also for nut "milk" and "cheese". It grinds down spinach, chia seeds, and cashews really well.

I can just throw all the ingredients for a smoothie in together and run it and don't really have to reach in and stir unless I'm being picky about little flecks of spinach and chia seed that get splattered onto the sides. My smoothie routine takes about 5 minutes in the morning, 3 of which are cleaning up and putting away spare ingredients. The cup itself is easy to clean. I use peanut butter in my smoothies by am able to keep the bottom clean by running a quick blend cycle with soapy water after I make my smoothie.

It is aesthetically pleasing in that kind of vintage KitchenAid way. The base is pleasingly heavy and metal. The cup is a very thick plastic. The lid is a softer almost silicone like plastic. I had wanted a Vitamix but will probably never be able to afford one, and I'm very happy with this blender as an alternative. I don't think I'm really missing out.
profile.summary: The cup itself is easy to clean

profile.description: Electrolux ultra Flex canister vacuum offers excellent performance everywhere-designed for superior performance on super plush carpets. With the Flexor performance system, one product is all you need! ultra Flex includes an on/off brush roll switch and 3-level height adjustment so you can clean all floor surfaces, from bare floors to plush carpets. Adjustable suction power lets you reduce suction to safely clean delicate curtains and fabric. A cyclonic system gives you consistent suction power to thoroughly clean your home. With the motion control system-large rear wheels and a low center of gravity-Ultra Flex twists and turns around furniture with ease. The 21 ft. Cord and 8 ft. Hose and telescopic wand combine for 33 feet of cleaning reach. Ultra Flex is compact and lightweight so it's easier for you to get around, get up and down stairs and carry from room to room. It's easy to store with horizontal or vertical Parking options and an automatic cord Rewind. Versatile tools include a crevice tool and dusting brush that store conveniently on the handle, so you can clean crevices and stairs in one quick step. Plus, an upholstery nozzle and bare floor nozzle help you tackle all of your home's surfaces. The premium HEPA filtration captures 99.97percent of dust, allergens and other irritants for a cleaner home. The HEPA filter is also washable, so you can reuse and reduce waste. The slim design of the bag less dust cup and bottom opening let you easily empty the dust cup, reducing the amount of dust escaping into the air. Ultra Flex includes a 5-year limited warranty for your Peace of mind.
profile.reviewText:
Update after nearly a year of use:

Vacuum still sucks like a pro. Can see why Electrolux once tried to brand themselves with "nothing sucks like an Electrolux". All PG-13 jokes aside, we use this multiple times a day and it keeps the floors clean and picks up a ton from the carpets. I use the little brush head for dusting in our bedroom.

We've had several clogs that were pretty easy to clear out by detaching the appropriate bit of tubing and pulling it out.

The only time the suction was affected when it wasn't a clog was because the filters needed cleaning, especially the little tube shaped filter on top of the main canister. Washed and let dry for a day and all was good as new.

Some issues:

Something snapped in the joint of the carpet attachment where it connects to the wand. Doesn't affect cleaning function, but means the wand can no longer stand upright when attached to the power sucker thing. That sucks. It also squeaks and gets stiff sometimes because of the plastic.

I can still highly recommend this vacuum. It really packs a punch.

_____________

I was really torn between this Electrolux model and an entry-level Miele, which on open-box deal worked out to around the same price. The deciding factor in favor of the Electrolux was the power brush head for the carpet and the HEPA filter - both of which have to be purchased extra for the Miele. Plus I'm completely gross and love seeing all the dust I can pick up during a good deep cleaning session.

I vacuum daily, 2-3x a day, and was using a Bissel Zing canister before this. This was my first expensive vacuum, and wow does it make a difference. It picks up so much dust it's almost embarrassing. The first trip around our three bedroom flat took 4 canister-fills of dust off the floors, furniture and shelves. I don't even like cleaning, but as the designated stay-at-home member of a 5 person household with a toddler, I've been laying sacrifices daily at the alters of the ancient Roman gods, Electrolux and Clorox, and I haven't even minded half as much. For whatever twisted reason, the power nozzle is really fun to use, and once you get started with the vacuuming, you want to dust, then bleach, then do laundry, do the dishes.... Our low to medium-pile area rugs look like they've been given a second chance at life, and the hard floors in the hall and kitchen can be walked on with bare feet without encountering a single crumb.

The vacuum itself arrived in the original box with the hose and nozzles and the dust canister disconnected. It was easy to put together. I had it up and running in under 10 minutes. The body is deceptively lightweight despite its flashy, almost bulky appearance. It maneuvers easily across hardwood and medium pile rugs and has yet to flip upside down on me, which is amazing because I have a gift for knocking these little buggers over. The hose itself is long, and the nozzles are all extremely easy to connect and disconnect. The power head you can do with just your foot!

I was disappointed when I opened the box and noticed that the wand was not black metal, but black plastic with an aluminum telescopic piece underneath. I had been looking forward to the more expensive feel of a metal wand and was worried about durability. I do wish it was metal, but I'm not as bothered at this point as the plastic is pretty lightweight and does not look too cheap.

Actually, I don't think this vacuum looks or feels cheap at all. All of the plastic is weighted and sturdy and glossy. Each attachment seems to have been thought out well. The two heads that store in the wand are useful for dusting and sucking dust and dirt out of stroller crevices and the air conditioner vent. I haven't really had any trouble with them falling out, either.

Caveats for some people: The canister does fill up quickly and the 33ft extension will get you through about two rooms and a stretch of hallway or a bathroom. I use three outlets on our roughly 1000 sq ft apartment. This doesn't bother me, as it's a huge improvement on our old vacuum.

The suction power toggle is very useful for transitioning from vacuuming floors to dusting on shelves, plastic splat mats under high chairs, and furniture. Even with the power on low, this vacuum still sucks up Cheerios, crumbs and a AAA battery like it's nobody's business.

The power nozzle for carpets has lights. I never thought I'd want or need this in a vacuum, but it is incredibly useful for vacuuming under furniture or for keeping lights off so I can vacuum in the dark and not blow a fuse with our crappy pre-war wiring.

The only thing I have not yet had much success with is the brush roll clean feature. As another reviewer noted, there may not have been enough hair on it yet.

profile.description: A wonderful first doll for ages birth and up. Babi Corolle Miss Fresh Riviera is 9. 5 inches tall so it's easy to take her along wherever baby goes. She has a soft, cuddly body that's easy for little fingers to grasp and hug. Her smooth vinyl face, delicately scented with vanilla -- a Corolle signature, has a sweet expression that will captivate the very young. Babi Corolle Miss Fresh Riviera will quickly become your little one's favorite play companion. Babi Corolle Miss Fresh Riviera wears a fresh and vibrant green and yellow dress with green sleeves and a print collar. Completing her sewn-on ensemble, a yellow hoodie frames her adorable face. Like all first dolls in the Collection, Babi Corolle Miss Fresh Riviera is machine washable (air dry naturally).
profile.reviewText: Update: My 16 month old carries her "baby" around with her constantly. The small size (which I was iffy on) and soft body make baby easy to tuck under her arm for nap times and to transport around our house. We eventually invested in a second of these dolls, the one with the larger soft red body, and my daughter now sleeps with both babies gathered around her. The smell is still soft vanilla, nowhere near overpowering, even after multiple hot water washes in a commercial machine. I have already given one of these dolls as a gift to a cousin who had a baby. At around $20, they do make for perfect and adorable little gifts and great introductions to the Corolle line for people who might not be familiar. The doll arrived in an adorable box with a mint green background to go with her shirt and shoes. The packaging was amazingly easy - one of the easiest toys I've opened yet. Like all Corolle dolls, she carries a very soft and sweet scent of vanilla. Immediately brought me back to my childhood in the early 90s, playing with my own Corolle dolls. The size is perfect for tiny hands. It will seem small to you as a parent, but this doll fits in the HABA Moover Doll Pram, Red and is perfect for being tucked under baby-sized arms, hugged, lugged around by the foot or hat, 'kissed' (read: sloppily licked), and thrown from the playpen like a short-range missile. We bought this as an early birthday gift for our soon to be 1 year-old daughter. I think all kids, regardless of gender, can benefit from playing with dolls and learning empathy and caregiving skills - and Corolle are just the best of the best. The quality in the stitching, the soft and cute fabrics, the pretty/bright colours, the beautiful face and the extra thoughts like the vanilla scent and sewn-in name tag for labelling set this brand above and beyond so many others. As for the playing - my daughter is a bit of a 'brute' at 11 months and currently enjoys yanking said doll from her pram by the ankle and dangling her King Kong style while she pokes at her eyes. Hopefully the empathy & co will come later. For now, this is a beautiful toy from a great company at a decent price that has stood up well to being stood on on a daily basis. Definitely a toy we will be saving.
profile.summary: adorable play friend for baby

profile.description: The AcuRite 00613 Indoor Humidity Monitor provides all the home comfort information you need, at a glance. Featuring a precision indoor thermometer and hygrometer, and an easy-to-read LCD display, it shows current indoor humidity and temperature, plus daily high and low records. A handy home comfort icon makes it effortless to tell if your indoor humidity is too high, too low, or "OK." Multiple mounting options include a convenient clip, magnets for attaching to a metal surface like a refrigerator, or you can stand it upright on a tabletop. Limited one-year warranty. It's more than accurate, it's AcuRite.
profile.reviewText:
The temperature is displayed accurately and it helps being able to check the room's humidity levels. Seeing the daily highs and lows is also interesting - I like to see what the room went up to while we were out and had the a/c off so that I can compare to the temperature with the a/c on and see how the a/c unit is working.

The device itself feels sturdy and is small enough not to detract from where it is placed. There is a magnet on the back that is fairly strong for sticking it to the fridge. There is also a little swing out leg so that it can stand upright on a table. We have used both with great success.

A very simple and straightforward little thermometer.

profile.description: iTrap by Southern Homewares offers some of the best in the trapping business! The multi-catch humane repeater trap is no exception. It can catch a dozen mice at a time and requires no winding, batteries or maintenance. Simply position the trap in areas of known mouse activity with the opening along the wall and curious mice will enter the one-way trap and BAM they are caught! Clear window in the top means trap can be checked quickly. To release simply take the trap to the desired area, open the lid, and dump the mice out. Can be used with or without bait. Mouse entry holes are 1.38" wide and 1.13" tall. Window measures 7.44" x 3.91". Overall dimensions are 10.38" x 6.25" x 2.05".
profile.reviewText:
The mouse was sneaking into our bread bags, nibbling at hamburger buns and causing domestic disputes about 'who the heck takes a single large bite out a hamburger bun and then puts it back in the bag, hon?' Clearly, it had to go. I will admit that my first instinct was (after wanting to scrub my mouth out and get prophylactic treatment for hanta virus once I realised that I had been using buns from the same bag) to go to the dollar store, buy some snap traps and be done with it. I have an infant at home, and I am a bit of a wimp. That said, I also try not to harm living creatures if I can help it. Catch and release bugs with the paper and cup trick etc etc. I bought this trap after reading reviews on a more popular plastic trap that the mice were apparently gnawing through the lock on, thus achieving a hasty escape.

Despite my mother's head-shaking and the dire warnings from family and friends that New York mice would never be fooled by something so humane and that I would end up buying a brutal snap-trap in the end, I put the trap out the night it came with chunks of hamburger bun inside it. Ten minutes later, I was brushing my teeth and heard a little clinking noise from the kitchen. Walked in to find a pair of beady eyes staring accusingly through the vent slats. I had made sure to put enough hamburger bun in to tide the little guy over until morning (per the instructions of another reviewer), when my boyfriend walked into the park for the Big Release on his way to work. He said it was easy enough to open the trap up and get the mouse out. It's been one month and no further sign of mice. Great trap, well made, worked like a charm. Can definitely recommend.

profile.description: The first publication of Kurt Cobain's diaries, which were found after his death in 1994. Genuinely moving, provocative and candid, and suprisingly funny, pieces of writing which, as a whole, provide a unique account of the rise and fall of a great popular artist and icon.
profile.reviewText:
Kurt's journals are fascinating and claustrophobic and often funny. There is something about reading something in a person's own handwriting that feels intimate and very, very real. As fraught as the subject of literally reading someone's diary is, I think it's actually important in the case of Kurt Cobain to remind people that behind the media-created icons for everything from cool rock'n'roll to depressed victim of himself to 'dirty junkiedom' was an intelligent, clever, witty, angry, funny, loving, frustrated - human being. He was a guy who was once someone's son and someone's lover and who is someone's father. He liked gross cartoons and he wrote letters he never sent to people he was frustrated with and he was fairly left-leaning and liberal, a feminist, not a fan of Jerry Garcia etc etc etc. He had clumsy handwriting. He was humorously self-deprecating. He wrote cool lyrics.

I bought this book for myself and for my boyfriend, as we're both Kurt and Nirvana fans, and the soft cover is great. It's notebook sized with high-quality scans of the journal pages. It feels weird to review someone's journal, so I won't say it was 'a good read' so much as it was interesting and a bit sad.

profile.description: Designed for superior auscultation of the fetal heart. Stethoscope is equipped with chrome-plated brass binaural and stem. The 22 inch black tubing can be easily shortened to facilitate use of the headrest.
profile.reviewText:
My boyfriend could hear her heartbeat at 17 weeks. I have been unable to, which I half-expected. Kind of a bummer, but I only bought this to see if it worked to begin with. Now that I am 28 weeks along, I am going to keep trying and hopefully will get to hear more than the thumps and swishes of her moving around in there (which is also cool).

Update: I heard the heartbeat once at around 30 weeks. Was very exciting. Without midwifery experience, you really have to have a big enough baby to be able to get a sense of how baby is lying and where to listen for the heartbeat, which can be difficult. Even then, if baby is not in a position that the stethoscope can pick up on, you probably won't hear anything either. Still, it does work under the right conditions, and I feel very Call the Midwife listening in.

Because they're made from wax containing all-natural beeswax, these eight crayons hold their light pigments exceptionally well, allowing you to create vibrant, colorful works of art with ease. The crayons are slightly larger than average, which makes them well suited for small hands to grasp. Set comes with handy crayon scraper. profile.reviewText:
We already own the Stockmar block crayons, but Amazon had these for $12, so it seemed worth it to try. Waldorf theories vary with young children, but I find my two year old has an easier time really drawing with traditional stick crayons.

These are very thick and sturdy, smell like beeswax, and come in the useful little metal box that makes transporting convenient. Small enough to throw in a diaper bag, childs backpack, or purse. Ive attached Velcro to the back of them to keep them with a small clipboard and paper, and it makes a good travel coloring set.

As with the block crayons, yellow kind of sucks. Took off a star for that. Why are you so shy, yellow? The colors of the crayons themselves are much darker and moodier than the bright and vivid (apart from yellow) colors of the wax as if transfers onto paper.

These are stiffer and smoother/less sticky than Lyra and harder than the Faber Castell beeswax crayons. They color well, the paper doesnt slip, the thickness is good, and the color names are written in German, which is fun.

top_5.reviewText:
Update: used it for family travel to Disney world. It went over uneven city pavement, survived a fall onto a sidewalk from on top of a car seat on a wheelchair (don't ask?) and is in total only mildly scratched in a difficult to notice way. The textured plastic does not scuff white or black. Zipper held up better than I expected. Never felt like it would bust, even when pushed to the limit. Held about two weeks worth of toddler clothes, a week's worth of my clothes, a cooler of medicine, swim gear, and a pair of sneakers. Used packing cubes and rolled clothes. Weighed a ton but rolled like a champ with one hand while I pushed either stroller or wheelchair. Very impressed. Would buy Lojel again.

----

I was hesitant to buy this because of the reviews, but it was starkly reduced in price so I took the plunge because we needed another carry on for a trip to Disney World. I'm very glad I did.

The first impression I had of this suitcase was that it seems very sturdy. Yes, it is plastic-y, but the polycarbonate shell is thick and by no means cheap looking. The plastic effect is just heightened because of the late 90's Barbie color and the fact that it's a matte textured finish instead of the glossy finish that is the norm on most plastic hard cases.

I had a flight attendant friend and a relative give it a little spin around the house, and the consensus is that it's a great looking and good quality suitcase for the money. I would judge it to fall somewhere on the spectrum above Delsey and around Travelpro in terms of perceived durability and function. The wheels are very smooth and transition from upright to diagonal without any jarring. The zipper is thick and was very easy to pull around a heavily packed suitcase without feeling like it would split. My TSA locks have been working.

The interior is extremely basic but functional. There'sthe main/larger compartment for clothes etc, with the usual strap to help keep them contained. The other side is divided from this by a zippered mesh wall, creating a second compartment. The fabric is light gray and a sturdy feeling synthetic.

The suitcase is light, even when fully packed. It held a week's worth of clothes for myself and my two year old (8 outfits for me, 10 for her), as well as a pair of sneakers, two pairs toddler sandals, accessories, and pool supplies. This is about what I would expect from a carry on, although more space could be achieved if the suitcase didn't indent where the black handle is. I can't think of a purpose for this indentation other than keeping the handle tucked in so it doesn't snag on anything, but it kills off an extra couple inches of packing space.

All in all, the Streamline hardcase carry on has piqued my interest in the Lojel brand. Its simplicity and understated quality set it aside from many of the cheaper brands you can find in this price range on Amazon. If i had space for one, i would buy a second of these.
top_5.summary: I'm very glad I did

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "3.0" for a product with description "WATERMAN Fountain Pen Converter, Standard (56010W). output:
I had recently acquired my first fountain pen and needed ink to go with it. I purchased this particular one because of its price, reviews, and ranking.

I was expected to be blown away but unfortunately I'm not. This ink dries quickly, which is great - that means I won't end up smearing it. However, when it does dry, the color that is left is not a deep black; it's more of a light black to almost blue color. I'm a fan of blue ink (I almost bought blue ink but in the end decided to go with the standard black), but this ink is really neither blue nor black; it's something in between. I thought it might have been the paper I was writing on but it's not. I've tested this on several "types" of paper (journal, ring notebook, copy paper) and the ink looks to be about the same hue on each. I've attached a picture so that you can see for yourself the color that I end up with.

The color is not horrible so I'm going to keep this bottle and use up as much of the ink as I can. However, I'm going to continue looking at other brands in the meantime and hopefully end up buying one that is a true deep black.
