input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "ALIAS - THE COMPLETE THIRD SEASON". The summary of the review text is "A bad day fishing".
output:
There's an expression tht a bad day fishing is still better than the best day at the office.  That's Season 3 in a nutshell.  While it doesn't nearly live up to the glory of Seasons 1 and 2 (wherefore art thou, Lena ???), its still pretty darn good.  How could it not be ?

Sydney has new and exciting personal challenges - such as Vaughn's wife, not to mention missions.  As a mystery woman, Lauren is hardly a replacement for Syd's missing mom.  But on that front we do meet Syd's aunt and sister during S3.  Sloan is as creepy as ever.  Marshall is as zany as ever.  Jack is full of surprises and its great to see more of Weiss this season.

For the Alias faithful, there's plenty of plot twists and disguises - including one with Syd taking her turn as Marshall.  Extras are fairly standard faire, including comentaries, gag reel, and deleted scenes.  There is also a brief "animated Alias" which is unique, in its own way.  If you've been drawn in by this JJ Abrams creation, don't hesitate to pick up Season 3.

profile.description: 2011 album from the Rock legend, one of popular music's most deeply revered figures and the main creative force behind some of the most cherished recordings in rock history. Indeed, it is no exaggeration to call Brian Wilson one of the most influential composers of the last century. On In The Key Of Disney, Brian Wilson rearranges some of Disney's most beloved recordings and makes them uniquely his own. Includes Wilson-ized versions of 'Bare Necessities', 'You've Got A Friend In Me', 'Can You Feel The Love Tonight?', and 'When You Wish Upon A Star'.
profile.reviewText: If you enjoy Brian Wilson's surftastic music and you don't mind a twist on some Disney classics, you're in for quite a treat. IN THE KEY OF DISNEY kicks off with a great re-imagining of Randy Newman's You've Got A Friend in Me. The album really pulls out all of the Beach Boys stops and hits its stride with covers of Baby Mine and Kiss the Girl. Really good stuff. Not every song was a home run with me. The Lion King outing had me reaching for the skip button. That said, there's a lot of good music on IN THE KEY OF DISNEY. If you're a fan of Brian Wilson and The Mouse, then this one is a no-brainer.
profile.summary: Endless Summer at Toontown

profile.description: Batman Impopster Batgirl Harley Quinn Pop! Vinyl Figure: The villains of Gotham are dressing up like Batman and Batgirl! This Batman Impopster Batgirl Harley Quinn Pop! Vinyl Figure features Harley's signature colors applied to Batgirl's classic costume. The Batman Impopster Batgirl Harley Quinn Pop! Vinyl Figure measures approximately 3 3/4-inches tall and comes packaged in a window display box. Ages 14 and up.
profile.reviewText:
The Impopster sub-line of DC Superheroes is sheer genius, in my opinion. Take the Batman figure and paint it as a villain. Penguin, Riddler, even the Wal Mart exclusive Killer Croc. I had looked at quite a few of these Pops before biting the bullet with Harley Batgirl. Now the hardcore collector is probably going to try and find this figure "in the wild". They will want to check the paint job, and (in many instances) the box condition. That said, mine came in pretty good condition. I am an out of box collector, but my box only had one slight ding, and its toward the back so you might not even see it.

The paint job on mine was a little ragged along the face where the red and the black met the white of the face. Also noticed a small white smudge on the hem of the cape. Again, I was completely fine with it, but I could see how some might develop a nervous twitch every time they passed by Harley Batgirl. Aside from the face and cape bit, the rest of my figure looked pretty crisp.

Nitpicks aside, I love this figure. I know its a repaint, but - again - I think the concept is genius. I am quite happy with Batgirl Harley. Its tempted me to pick up the Poison Ivy Batgirl Impopster. I've got to admit, I don't get the BatMAN Harley. But, hey - each collector is going to like what they like. Who am I to judge ? The utility belt and cowl of Batgirl, swirled with Harley's diamonds and red and black colors... I just really like it a lot. One thing I noticed is that the figure does want to tip backwards. There is no stand, so if you don't leave her in box, you may need to set Babs on the back row so she can lean against a wall.
profile.summary: How ya like me now, Bats ?

profile.description: Fun and colorful shell is made from 100 percent injection molded polypropylene, lightweight, flexible and moisture resistant. Protective tongue-in-groove closure protects garments from dust and water. Double spinner wheels. External fully integrated handle system. Split book style opening. Fully lined interior. Molded side feet, recessed TSA accepted combination lock. Worldwide limited 10 year warranty
profile.reviewText:
Got this piece of luggage just before holiday traveling. Because we were travelling in the northeast during winter, the luggage nicely repelled drizzle and snow - keeping the contents clean and dry. We really don't fly all that much, but I can certainly see where this would be a great friend to folks who do fly. First of all, its RED. While it doesn't have a crazy pattern, I would imagine it would be fairly easy to pick out on the baggage carousel. It is a well-constructed hard shell which would protect the contents inside.

The wheels turn, swivel, and roll very nicely. The tow handle was very comfortable. Even though we were only rolling our suitcase across a street or parking lot, it made handling this luggage quite easy. There are also handles in both 'tall' and long mode for hefting it up on to a bed. Inside there is elastic closures and a zipper pouch. Very useful for segregating person A from person B, or clean from dirty. We were away from home for several days and the space was adequate. If it were much more than seven days, it might have been a different story. The eye to detail does travel inside the case with a well-made lining and fixtures. I was not financially compensated for this review. I received a sample for review purposes. The opinions are completely my own based on my experience.
profile.summary: "Well thought out", "Nicely designed"

profile.description: Transformers Age of Extinction Generations Deluxe Class Dinobot Slug Figure
profile.reviewText:
Slug is the most recent redesign of the Dinobot formerly known as Slag. The Dinobots for Transformers 4 are a bit of a mixed bag. While Slug isn't the top of the heap, there is a lot to like about this Triceratops. The first big thing that old school fans will recognize are the red and purple plates that make up much of Slugs dino form. Each of the new dinobots has its own primary color in the new toyline, from slug to scorn to Snarl. Youll also notice the design choice where Slugs body is much more segmented, in contrast to his G1 likeness. It really pops around his head crest.

In robot mode, Slug is a part of this knight aesthetic that flows from Optimus on down through many of the supporting characters. The dino head splits to become two massive shoulder parts and is even attached with a screw where the eye would be in dino mode, which is a fun choice. I will say Im not overly crazy about the way his tail dangles off the back of the robot mode, but its not horrible. Hes got some nice articulation and looks really slick standing next to both Scorn and Grimlock. If you can pick him up for under twenty dollars, hes an easy add. Much more than that, and Id be inclined to look at some of the other TF4 toys first.
profile.summary: A Dino by any other name...

profile.description: Marvel Guardians of the Galaxy Big Blastin Rocket Raccoon Figure
profile.reviewText: A lot of people I have been talking to seem pretty excited about Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy movie, and I think its kind of a no-brainer that Rocket will be popular with kids and adults alike. That said, I really see this version as more of a collectible. Rocket comes pre-loaded with batteries and went right into blasting mode. The little guy pops off various catch-phrases from the movie and fires off his space rifle. The gun barrel spins and lights up. There's all kinds of blasting noise and Rocket hops around, presumably from the kickback of his oversize space-weapon. The reason I think its more of a collectible is we all(ages 12 to 57) got a kick out of Rocket when we set him down on the hard wood floor of our kitchen. We cycled through everything he had to say and watched him blast all of the imaginary baddies. And since then, he's been sitting on a shelf. He looks really cool and will be fun to take down from time to time. But I just have a hard time seeing him as something that would engage kids for long stretches of time. Not the way something like the Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Star-Lord Quad Blaster or LEGO Superheroes 76021 The Milano Spaceship Rescue Building Set might. At the end of the day, Rocket is cool, I just don't know how much of a 'toy' he is.
profile.summary: Lock and Load !

profile.description: Make your stand against evil with this exciting Collection of 4 DC Showcase Animated Shorts starring favorite DC Comics super heroes! Chosen the worlds protector against the Seven Deadly Enemies of Man--pride, envy, greed, hatred, selfishness, laziness and injustice--young Billy Batson accepts his destiny as Captain Marvel. Battling alongside Superman against nefarious Black Adam, Billy soon discovers the challenge super heroes ultimately face: is it revenge or justice? For bounty hunter Jonah Hex and hard-boiled cop turned vengeance ghost The Spectre, getting their hands dirty is part of the job-- maybe even the fun part. But Superman, Green Arrow and Black Canary follow an internal moral code to guide their actions. They know its easy to get lost in the darkness of the fight, especially when villans like Merlyn the Magnificent and Count Vertigo place no value on human life.
profile.reviewText:
I won't enter into the gripe about this being a collection of shorts.  Everyone has already done a decent job at addressing that.  But what I will do is provide my insights into this collection of vignettes from the DC Universe.

SHAZAM - This is the one that brought me to the party.  I was curious to see what they would do with Shazam and the Man of Steel.  Honestly, it was a superpowered street fight.  That's not necessarily a bad thing, but this could have been so much more.

THE SPECTRE - I didn't really know anything about the Spectre before seeing this short.  I think it was well done and like the Crime Noir feel to it.  The ending was especially cool.

GREEN ARROW - I am a bit of a fan of The Green Arrow, whether that's the traditional flavor or the 21st Century Smallville incarnation.  This Emerald Archer outing is a fun ride and draws the viewer in to a quick outing that's a bit Robin Hood, and a bit Die Hard.  Nicely done.

JONAH HEX - Again, I've got to plead ignorance when it comes to Jonah Hex.  The story setting was done well enough.  But I just didn't get much of a feel on who our anti-hero was or why he was so interested in his prey.  The interaction was intriguing enough.  Just not sure what it told me about Jonah Hex, or why i should care.

DC and WB certainly didn't cheap out on the voice talent.  There's a great array of talented actos and actresses here, from series regulars to pleasant surprises.  In the end, I'd say this one is worth a rent, or a bargain-bin clearance.  But save your money for one of the full length features.  This peek through the fence only gives a fleeting glimpse of the heroics.
profile.summary: Entertaining enough, in short bursts

profile.description: These permanently bickering yet inseparable mechanical droids proved their loyalty to their Rebel friends throughout the galactic Civil War and even saved the day a time or two. Now, C-3PO and R2-D2 are back as the 19th installment of the keepsake Series as seen in Star Wars: a new hope. This is the perfect gift for a fan of the original Series or anyone excited for the newest installment. This Ornament is available for a limited time and dated 2015. Copyright & tm lucasfilm LTD.
profile.reviewText: From coffee creamers to Christmas trees, you can't escape Star Wars in 2015. This R2/3PO ornament is a great addition to any fan's collection. Its made by Hallmark, so the quality is there and detailing is very well done. As others have noted, 3PO is not chromed out, but the coloring on R2 is certainly true to form. Do be aware, as with most modern ornaments there is some heft to this piece. If you have an artificial tree, probably not a big deal. If your family prefers live Christmas trees, then you'll just need to make sure that you've got a sturdy branch to hang this one. The dynamic duo of hyperspace is modeled more after episode 4, than The Force Awakens because 3PO has a silver leg, and not a red arm. Its a fun add from Hallmark and will certainly bring a smile to Star Wars fans of all ages.
profile.summary: Festive, this ornament is

profile.description: Phineas And Ferb: Across the 1st And 2nd Dimensions features songs from the Disney Channel series and new music from the Original Movie! Featuring 22 new songs including the hit track "Kick It Up A Notch" featuring Slash.
profile.reviewText:
There is so much to like about Disney's Phineas and Ferb; the terrific characters, the clever storylines, and the amazing music. My family picked up the first CD, the subsequent Summer Belongs to You EP, and now this great collection which features music from the new 2nd Dimension movie.

The thing about most Phineas and Ferb music tracks is they are less than two minutes.  Its good stuff...  but short. As a result, both the first CD and this new collection feature more than twenty tracks.

The new collection includes music from PHINEAS AND FERB: ACROSS THE SECOND DIMENSION, in addition to some offerings from the recent season. Brand New Best Friend and Summer(Where Do We Begin?) are some of the highlights from the new movie, while Platypus Controlling Me is an excellent offering from one of the recent episodes.

Long story short, if you have Phin and Ferb fans in your house, this new collection is another homerun !
profile.summary: Hey, is that Love Handel ?

profile.description: Bring back to life the memories of your visit or let your imagination run free with the music from this Disney CD.   Entrance On this magic night - Once upon a dream Spectromagic Theme Music Float Garden Float Little Mermaid Float Fantasia Float Carousel Float Exit On this magic night - When you wish upon a star
profile.reviewText:
If you're a Disney geek like me - and, lets face it, you're reading a review on a parade soundtrack - then you'll dig this. There was a time when Disney didn't do the best job on releasing in-park music. I think someone finally realized that we can't all get to the Magic Kingdom once a week. So giving us park music like Soarin, Pirates, and Star Tours is a great way to keep us hungry for that next trip to The World.

I grew up on The Main Street Electrical Parade, and I was glad to see it return. But, darnit, if I don't miss Spectromagic. Its a shame that this parade may well be lost to the ages. Thank goodness for this terrific soundtrack to help us relive good times in Orlando. So grab the MP3, insert into your favorite music player, and enjoy. Until next time, please stand clear of the doors !
profile.summary: Thanks for this one, Disney !

profile.description: Motorola HX550 Universal Bluetooth Headset is your complete hands-free solution. Flip open to answer, enjoy crystal clear calls with dual microphone noise reduction and customize your fit with three wearing styles. HX550 features MOTOSPEAK to text with your voice, A2DP, up to 9 hours of talk time and up to 16 days of standby time.Voltage Required: AC 110 V.
profile.reviewText:
Prior to getting this unit I had a Motorola HS850. It was an older unit and was capable in that it allowed me to use my phone "hands free". I didn't feel that it had the best sound quality, though. Additionally, it wasn't comfortable to wear for extended periods of time. The new HX550 is a marked improvement.

Its a good looking unit and very discreet. While the smaller size has contributed to me misplacing once or twice, that's more my fault and not the technology's. I really feel that Motorola has stepped up their game with this headset in that I can hear the other party fine and I have had no complaints about my end being muddy or overly cluttered with background noise. The flexible ear hook is also a marked improvement over its older siblings hard plastic version.

My company phone is a pretty basic flip model so I really can't comment on the ability to dictate to my phone. That said, with as easily as this unit paired with my handset and for as well as it works on the Nuance Voice Commands, I'd wager that it works as billed.

Long story short, if you're in the market for a multi-featured Bluetooth that's as versatile as it is comfortable you'd do well to consider the Motorola HX550.
profile.summary: Useful addition to my company phone

profile.description: Officially licensed by Nintendo. This is a 2 piece set which includes a protector and system pouch for your Nintendo 3DS. It features Mario Kart 7 logo and artwork design. Perfect item to protect and customize your Nintendo 3DS to Mario color. Protector allows you to play game, change Nintendo 3DS game cards, adjust volume, insert and remove your stylus while attached! Nintendo 3DS system and Mario Kart 7 game card not included.
profile.reviewText:
This two-fer from the folks at Hori have put together an interesting set for your 3DS. The kit comes with two clear shells that snap onto your console and a nylon pouch to put your game system in. On the upside, I really like the Mario graphic and on my son's blue 3DS it totally pops. Very sharp. But I'm not convinced that my game is really receiving much in the way of protection, and it adds some extra girth to the unit. I suppose dropping the game with this snap on case would at least shatter the case before busting up the console, so that's a good thing.

The case is also a bit of a marginal proposition. It holds the console and two games. Hardly a competitor for the nice nylon case that I currently use that seats the unit and up to 12 games. At the end of the day, the clamshells are a nice addition, especially if you're a fan of Mario Kart. Its a bit of bling for your 3DS. But I'd be hard pressed to drop to much coin on this set.
profile.summary: Not much to get worked up about

profile.description: Add a touch of elegance to your kitchen with this chip-resistant 16-piece dinnerware set. Made of lead-free stoneware ceramic.
profile.reviewText:
We have had this set for about a month and I wanted to share my thoughts. As the description indicates, the 16 pieces include four of each... mug, bowl, small plate and large plate. The wavy design is rather unusual, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. I will say this. This is a large set. The items are large sitting on your table, in your dishwasher, and we couldn't even use the mugs with our Keurig. I saw someone also mention that it might be challenging to drink from the mugs, due to their squared off form factor. I honestly found the mugs great for cracking eggs into when making up Sunday omelettes.

Its a serviceable enough collection. Though, again, the large plates weren't exactly compatible in our average sized microwave. Your mileage may vary. We sometimes have issues with our current dishes getting a touch warm in the microwave. These didn't seem to have that problem, so I suppose that's a pro. At the end of the day, I don't see us giving up our Pfaltzgraft tableware for this set. It might be nice to use on occasion, but for our family, it certainly didn't fit the bill for daily dishware.
profile.summary: Its alright, and big

profile.description: Not just for recon operations, the all-new UNSC Flame Warthog by Mega Bloks Halo tackles multiple missions. The M12 Force Application Vehicle is the UNSC's primary ground vehicle, commonly used for its scouting and reconnaissance capacity. With an actual working suspension and 360 rotating turret, the highly mobile all-wheel drive "Hog" with all-new flame paintjob is clearly ready for battle! Features two new super-articulated micro action figures with customizable armor, includes 2 Spartan GUNGNIR. Ideal for ages 8 and up!.
profile.reviewText:
Our family - mom, dad, and tween - really enjoy Legos. Periodically we check in with Mega Bloks or KreO, but have been largely disappointed. That said, Mega Bloks has really stepped up their game in the last year. With franchises like Halo and Call of Duty, there's been a lot on the line. This is the second Warthog that we have built in the last year. And while the three of us agree that Mega Bloks hasn't caught Lego yet, they've certainly closed the gap.

This Warthog come with two Spartans and some nice features. About the Spartans... The Halo line is certainly benefiting from the increased articulation spinning out of the Call of Duty sets. That's both good and bad. If you collect and display this set next to an older Halo set, the Spartans will certainly look different. Perhaps even as if they were part of two separate lines. I'm also not necessarily convinced that all of the extra armor 'bits' really enhances the figures.

As to the vehicle itself, its pretty sweet. You've got a mounted turret that swivels, just like you'd see in the games. And the Warthog has some pretty great suspension for a building-block toy of this scale. The blocks have the flames tampoed right on, so there's no messing with stickers after the fact. And the good news is that your earlier generation Spartans will ride nicely in this new ride. Some of the pieces were a little tight, so I still need to ding Mega Bloks on its tolerance. But, all in all, if you are a Halo/Building Block fan... you'll likely dig this set.
profile.summary: Fun to build, and looks great

profile.description: Celebrate the holidays in true Turtle style with your own Turtle-themed Advent Calendar by Mega Bloks Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles! Add a little ninja-ness to your winter festivities when you open a new buildable, Turtles-themed surprise for every day of the holiday season! With 24 surprises to build, the Turtles' Advent Calendar features four buildable, micro action figures with accessories, including one Turtle that you can equip to look like any of the four brothers! Connect with other Mega Bloks Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles sets and build the Turtles' world from the sewers up! Ideal for ages 5 years and older.
profile.reviewText:
Toy-based advent sets have become quite popular. Lego, alone, cranks out several each year. There's Star Wars, Barbie, and Thomas the Tank Engine. Whatever your kid's passion, there's likely an Advent calendar available. The fact that this Turtles set is fairly reasonable in price would certainly be a big draw to any family that has kids who dig the Heroes in a Half-Shell. The problem is, this Advent calendar is kind of minimal, in at least two critical ways.

First, is the fact that the characters don't play a huge role. There is only one turtle fig, and he comes with swappable bandannas. So you can't have all of the Turtles gathered around the tree at the same time. Don't get me wrong, its nice that they do give you the option to display your favorite Ninja Turtle with his signature accessories. But it feels a bit, limited. I would have rather seen another Turtle, before tossing in Casey Jones.

The other downside is that the builds are very minimal. Again, the Lego builds come with quite a few pieces each day. Thats simply not the case with this TMNT calendar, and it feels like a bit of coal in your stocking. Not really sure how two or three pieces constitutes a 'build', unless its snapping a minifig together. Again, just my opinion, YMMV.

If you love the Turtles, especially the Nick incarnation, I can't say this set is terrible. You do get pizzas, and all of the bandannas, and the character accessories. But for the money you'd pay for this Advent calendar, you could have the Lego City calendar... a better bargain in my humble opinion.
profile.summary: Did Shredder Create This ?

profile.description: LUMIX 20X Zoom Camera with Wink-Activated Selfie Feature
profile.reviewText: I know many people who rely on a phone as their primary portable camera. But when I go on vacation I want something with more flexibility. I want a camera that will not only take a good picture, but will allow me to get in close. I do own a full-bodied Nikon DSLR. But I have always preferred to have a "point and shoot" camera in my repertoire. This Lumix really fits the bill nicely. The main thing that I was attracted to was its 20x optical zoom. Its certainly thicker and heavier than my Olympus VR-340 16MP Digital Camera with 10x Optical Zoom (White) (Old Model). But not by much, especially when you consider that nice juicy zoon that is found in this camera. It really gives you the opportunity to get in nice and close to your subject. The zoom rocker is conveniently located around the trigger and very easy to use. I'm also a big fan on the generous LCD on the back of the camera. The viewfinder has all but disappeared from today's digital point and shoot and this screen provides all of the essential information needed to both take and review your pictures. An added bonus on this camera is the ability to flip the screen up, providing for an easy to use "selfie mode". I found the "wink trigger" to be a bit of a gimmick, but the flip screen is still a solid feature. I do have to say its a little disappointing that the camera does not include an SD card. Its probably a cost cutting measure, especially considering that many people may have one sitting around, or that they can transfer from a previous camera. The Lumix does have a little bit of onboard storage, but not much. With additional features like HD video and burst mode, there's certainly many more positives to focus on. I'm looking forward to taking this camera on the next family trip.
profile.summary: Great Zoom on a Point & Shoot

profile.description: Minecraft - PlayStation 3
profile.reviewText: We are no stranger to Minecraft at our house. My 12 year old son is a confirmed legomaniac and loves video games. Could there be a more targeted customer for this amazing, free-roam, sandbox game ? Over the last couple of years we have seen Minecraft on the PC, the ipod Touch, MICROSOFT Microsoft Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition / G2W-00002 /, and the most recent release for the PS3. I grew up with some of the early consoles, and gaming today is not what it was in the 70's and 80's - for better or worse. Minecraft is an awesome game that the whole family can enjoy. There's problem solving, and creativity, and just plain silliness stretched out across this blocky playground that may well remind you of those early days of gaming. As much as my son enjoys the ipod version because he can take it on the road, there's no denying what a console version of Minecraft brings to the table. First and foremost, you can enjoy a much more expansive take on the world. Its just so cool to see all of these blocks stacked, broken down, and rearranged to create everything from axes to castles on the big screen. The multiplayer aspect also allows you to play with your friends just like the good old days when you would spread wooden blocks out on the floor and build together. There are still some things that just make my adult brain twitch just a bit. Things like chopping a tree down from the bottom up and having the leaves just float in the sky. And islands can float in the sky, too - complete with animals that 'spawn' on them. Its just one of those things that makes Minecraft so wierd and fun. If you've got a Sony Computer Entertainment Playstation 3 12GB System, and you love to be creative, you need to give Minecraft a spin. Just be warned... This thing will gobble up a lot of your free time.
profile.summary: Creepers 'gon creep... on PS3

profile.description: Revisit and relive every Amazing Spider-Man comic book ever printed covering over 43 years. Including the mind-blowing 12 Milestones of Amazing Spider-Man spanning March 1963 through June 2006. A total of over 575 complete comic books including Annuals, all articles, Spider-Web column pages, Bullpen Bulletins, Pinups and every single advertisement.
profile.reviewText:
In high school and college I collected the dead tree editions of several Spidey books.  Spectacular and Web Of were my two staples.  But as a die hard Spidey fan, having all of these issues on one disc, is unbelievable.  Going back to Day One and seeing those first appearances is really cool.  Likewise, it was a lot of fun to see where the modern-day story line has gone.

Another great aspect of these archived issues is seeing all of the original ads.  Forget Xbox and Playstation, all the cool kids want an NES or a Genesis under their Christmas tree this year.  Lots of nostalgia for spider-fans of any era.  The compelling art, great story lines, complete with all of the Annuals.  Its all here.  If you love the Webhead, or know someone who does, this is a great way to enjoy all of the storylines, without taking up several closets to archive these issues in the requisite boards, bags, and boxes.

And all of the villains are here.  The various goblins, Sandman, Rhino, right on through to Venom and Carnage.  Plus the super sexy curves of Mary Jane as she's been drawn through the years.  Makes me want to get my hands on some of the other collections available, such as Ghost Rider.
profile.summary: In a word - Amazing !

profile.description: The 4.3 Navi Shield from Lowepro is the protective and inventive way to safeguard your GPS device, power supply and SD or map extension cards. Its compact, slim shape is designed to fit in a glove compartment or sit in a stable position on a center console. The 4.3 Navi Shield features a durable, molded hardshell on the exterior and soft, tricot lining on the interior. A protective, padded pocket with hook/loop closure secures a GPS device. Behind the pocket, a secondary compartment offers a mesh pocket to store a charger and cord, plus two convenient slots for extra SD cards. Inside the lid, you’ll find a handy “cleaning station” with a built-in microfiber cloth to clean the delicate touchscreen. Additional features include a wrap-around dual zipper and a D-ring attachment.
profile.reviewText:
We have been carrying our 4.3 Nuvi around in a case that only accomodates the unit.  From that perspective, the Lowepro is nice.  Certainly an upgrade from what we have been using.  It allows space for the cigarette adapter.  That said...  there isn't space for the mounting bracket.  When I remove the unit from my car, I like to take all evidence that I have a GPS with me.  Just my own personal preference.

Now, once you start carrying around the GPS, and the power cord, and the mounting bracket, you almost need a small camera bag.  One reviewer actually indicated that had been his solution.  So again, its a trade-off.  Perhaps the answer is to slip the mounting bracket into the glove box or center console, and just carry the unit and power supply in the case.

As far as the Lowepro case goes, it seems to be somewhat sturdy, though that would have to be borne out over the long haul.  It is nicely segmented separating the GPS from the cable, to prevent inadvertent scratching.  The zippers are a little stiff, but workable.  There's also some sort of ring on the outer case, though I'm not sure what the thinking there is.  For what it is, the Lowepro is a decent little case.
profile.summary: Its all about trade-offs

profile.description: Radio Flyer new ultimate EZ fold wagon is designed as a full size wagon for 2 kids that folds compactly. With an easy one hand fold, you can take or store the wagon anywhere. Two kids ride comfortably with 2 seats, 4 cup holders, seatbelts for added safety, and a removable canopy. The telescoping handle is for easy transport when folded. The DuraClean fabric is durable and can be easily wiped clean. A full size wagon with a compact fold to take & store anywhere. For ages 1 1/2 +.
profile.reviewText:
My wife and I picked this up to use with our one year old son.  Assembly was easy and straight forward, almost to the point of questioning why it was not done at the factory.  Build quality seems to be great.  The wagon is sturdy when open and has an overall quality feel to it.  The canopy is a nice added convenience to this wagon, though the finish of the canopy seemed to be of somewhat lower quality.  There were quite a few loose ends and strings that needed trimmed up from the sewing.  No big deal and 2 minutes later, all was good.

Fortunately, we received the wagon the week before a local amusement park was set to open.  This park has a variety of terrains from small hills, to loose stone, to paved sidewalk, and of course grass. We decided this would be a great test of our new toy and decided to go for a drive.  The stroller was easy to load into our mid-size cars trunk with little effort.  Once arriving at the park, setting up the stroller was a 3 second job.  The snaps for the canopy were a little difficult for my wife to get secured; otherwise there were no issues with the set up.  One issue we noticed right away was a lack of storage.  Our son wanted to sit in the back of the wagon, so we thought we would throw the diaper bag in the front.  We certainly had some issues with the bag wanting to stay in place.  I am not sure what we would have done if we had two children with us, other than still carrying the bag.

We toted our little one around the park for several hours.  We noticed that the wagon seemed to do very well on all of the terrain, especially where some other wagons were having issues.  Turning the wagon was easy, though the maneuverability takes some time to get accustomed to versus a regular wagon.  The day was a mix of sun and clouds and the canopy proved to be a nice feature shading our son from the sun.  Nearing the end of our excursion, we decided to take down the canopy and quickly realized again, that there is a lack of storage in this wagon.  There is no good way to put the canopy down and bring it with you.  Attempting to put the poles into the wagon provided our son with a new sword toy.  Also the folded canopy kept trying to come open.  Finally we placed it under the diaper bag.  At the end of our day, we returned to our vehicle and had a slight issue with the wagon wanting to roll away on its own.  This was fixed by simply kicking the front tires out to stop them from rolling.  Folding the unit was a breeze; though my wife did have some issues getting the unit completely locked closed (the seat belt was pinched).

Overall this seems to be a solid unit.  It is compact, yet sturdy and lives up to our expectations of what a Radio Flyer should be.  The only real complaints we have are a lack of storage options and no real solution to store the canopy when not in use.  We had a quite a few people stop and ask us about the wagon and did not see another one like it in the park.  There were several other folding wagons there that day and most of the parents seemed to like the fact that Radio Flyer had seatbelts where their wagons did not.  After our short experience with this wagon, we are fairly confident this will be a great wagon.  We recommended it several times to other parents at the park and overall the wagon was a hit.
profile.summary: A lot to like in this Lil Red Wagon

profile.description: HP Roar Plus Wireless Speaker Amplify your senses with the HP Roar Plus Wireless Speaker. Colorful style meets serious sound.
profile.reviewText: Back in the day, Bose owned the "small speaker with a big punch" category. Nowadays, there are a lot of entries in that market. The HP Roar has earned its place for sure. When we received the speaker, it was well packaged, yet easy to open. In very little time we had the plug assembled(there are three possible plugs, depending on your locale), and the speaker was charging. You can charge via a wall outlet or from the USB on your desktop or laptop. We easily paired both an Amazon Kindle and iPad Mini by simply searching the device out. And once connected, we were really impressed. The sound was rich and full, with respectable bass response. Likely not as good as a high end Bose, but still quite impressive. The speaker is also compact. You can sit it almost anywhere and it fills an average room nicely. Also of note, while there are volume controls available on the Roar itself, we were also able to control volume from our device of choice. Volume up, volume down... the Roar responded. Long story short, you don't need a separate stereo in the 21st century. Simply pair your phone, tablet, or ipod via Bluetooth and you've got a great music source for your next party, holiday season, or just for daily use. If you decide to take the Roar mobile there is a lightweight storage bag to keep the speaker in for day trips, or if you are tossing it into the luggage for the next family vacation. Not perfect, but some nice bang for your buck if you are looking for an affordable, and wireless, way to share your favorite music with friends or family.
profile.summary: Good wireless music option

profile.description: With the Air & Sea Drawbridge, it's easy to get cargo wherever it is needed - take it over the bridge by train, or under the bridge by boat. But when the ship is too tall, simply lift the lever, and the bridge will rise with fun dinging sounds. The gates will come down to stop vehicles from passing. Set includes drawbridge with on and off track pieces, toll building, and sailboat vehicle. The drawbridge can be used with all of the items in the GeoTrax System to create an even bigger world.
profile.reviewText:
Our family loves Geotrax.  We started with the simple layout and have added the clock tower, numerous remote trains, and most recently the Bayshore Drawbridge.  It is a great addition to our layout and compliments the Lighthouse that is part of the same series.  But, back to the drawbridge.

The drawbridge features gates that automatically drop whenever the bridge goes up.  There is a boat that can pass between the gap while the bridge is raised.  Much like the elevation packs that make the Geotrax so much, the bridge has teeth built into the surface so the remote trains can easily go up and over the gentle slope of the bridge.

The drawbridge also features a guardhouse much like a real drawbridge.  It not only is a nice touch visually, but the small chimney can be pressed down to ring a small warning bell.  So as the handle can be used to raise the bridge and drop the gates, the guard house can warn your oncoming trains that the bridge is being raised.

The drawbridge is well designed.  It is as sturdy as it is fun.  It's very colorful and connects seemlessly with the existing track.  Another great bridge to compliment the existing suspension bridge, lighthouse, and all of the other existing pieces to your Geotrax world.
profile.summary: Bridging the Geotrax gap

profile.description:
Disney has released different versions of the monorail playset over the years, and this newest one is sure to be the most popular. This toy is based on the Walt Disney World Monorail, and includes new features and accessories. The boxed set includes five cars with working headlights, recorded Monorail spiel (Walt Disney World version), and 14' of track - enough to build a 61'' x 49'' oval. (12 curved and 2 straight pieces included) The Monorail works in both forward and reverse gears. Also included in this new version are eight character figurines. The passenger cars have been updated and now include clear windows, working doors, and a lift-top roof. The Monorail playset is the perfect accessory under a Christmas tree, or just to run around the house any time of year. 

Additional Straight and Curved track is available to expand your set. (Sold separately) If you already own Monorail or spare track from the previous Monorail versions, rest assured that it will work with this new model. You can combine your new and old sets to create the layout of your dreams!

Some light assembly required, and you will need a philips-head screwdriver to install the batteries. Requires two AA batteries, which are not included. The Monorail is ideal for children 4 and up. Monorail color stripe may vary from photo shown.
profile.reviewText:
My wife started a Disney Tree for our family last Christmas.  So when my folks asked me what I wanted for my birthday - and I knew they were headed to WDW - I requested only one thing.  This monorail set takes our Disney Tree to a whole new level.  Let's start with some of the potential downers.  Its somewhat fragile.  Its more of a show piece than an actual toy.  It probably won't hold up to a whole lot of manipulation from junior.  Its also battery powered(2 AA's) so it doesn't have a whole lot of pep.  And even though it can travel in both directions, going backward is even slower than going forward.

That said, this monorail is amazing.  After putting the batteries in, and before even starting the monorail down the track, it announced, "Please Stand Clear of the Doors."  For the WDW fan in your house, there's probably not many other ways to instantly put you in that Disney mindset.  The beams are easily assembled and keep the train in place quite nicely.  It comes with enough track to make an oval, though we opted for a basic circle around our tree.  The monorail has a flashing light on the top of the cab and a headlight at the front of the train, just like the real deal.  You also have the choice to play the announcements or to just have the monorail circle the beam without audio.

I've got to say that, even with its few shortcomings, this monorail rocks.  Its just a terrific way to bring the Disney Parks home for the holiday.  I'm half tempted to pick up another color(Disney cycles through the available trains) when we go to visit Disney World early next year.  For collectors, or for your own family tree, I'd say that this monorail playset is a winner through and through.
profile.summary: The Highway in the Sky

profile.description: I AM LEGEND
profile.reviewText:
I haven't read the novel I Am Legend.  And I haven't seen its original big screen outing, Omega Man, starring Charlton Heston.  However, I recently sat down to watch the latest Will Smith-helmed outing of I Am Legend.  The movie is thrilling, touching, and eye-popping.  It's a great evening's entertainment for fans of action and sci-fi thrillers alike.

Smith is the man who is the key to cancer.  The back story tells us that scientists obviously rocked the world when they unlocked this piece of the genetic puzzle.  What they never could have expected was the plague that would claim more lives than cancer ever did.  And that's the backdrop where we get to know Smith's Robert Neville.

Neville is the only human left in New York City.  This is the visually stunning part of the film.  The CGI really gives us an amazing view of a broken down, overgrown, post-apocalyptic New York.  Neville roars through the city hunting deer from his Ford Mustang.  Tearing up sidewalks, and dodging busses, our hero hunts wild deer with his faithful dog Sam.

At night, the two fortify themselves in Neville's apartment.  They must do this because the plague which rocked the world has turned some of its inhabitants into nocturnal monsters.  They are the key threat to our hero's world, and the one compelling reason that keeps him strong.  He was the one who unlocked Pandora's Box.  And no one else will be able to set things right.

Will Smith has come a long way since his Fresh Prince days.  Outings in films like Independence Day, Hitch, Bad Boys, and The Pursuit of Happyness have cemented Smith as a solid leading man.  I Am Legend gives him a chance to really flex his dramatic muscles.  We see Neville as eccentric hermit, grieving husband, and driven hero.

I Am Legend delivers a solid story with echoes that may leave you wondering `what if' for some time after.
profile.summary: Glad I got to see it

profile.description: Take your Nintendo 3DS on a trip. This Mini Transporter Case for the Nintendo 3DS system is the perfect way to take your system with you no matter where you're headed. Interior pockets firmly secure your system along with up to 12 Nintendo 3DS Game Cards. Plus, it's compatible with the Nintendo DS Lite and Nintendo DSi systems.
profile.reviewText:
Nintendo has ruled the portable game space for years. There's a reason for this. Their systems are reasonably priced, feature great sound and graphics, and are lots of fun ! The thing about a portable gaming system is keeping all of the bits and pieces together. The early Nintendo handheld were simply game and cartridge. The newer systems have added a stylus and the ability to charge on the go. All of this stuff needs a place, both at home and as you travel. Enter this great carrier.

The outer shell is a rugged yet lightweight material. It holds the game unit, cartridges, and accessories firmly while providing easy access at the same time. An outer pocket is held shut with velcro, while the console and cartridges get a nice beefy zipper for two separate sections. There's also a sturdy handle to grab or loop through a belt. It would have been nice to include a dedicated belt loop, but its certainly not a deal breaker that they skipped it.

The side that keeps the DS also has several loops to carry a stylus or four and a charger for the wall or the car. There's a velcro strap to secure the console and the lining for this pouch is soft so that it won't scratch up your Nintendo portable. The carrier is marketed for the new 3DS, but it could just as easily work with the Lite or the DSi.

The back pocket of the carrier is straight up nylon with stretch pockets to hold games. Both the regular DS games and the new notched 3DS games fit snugly in the pouches. There's a total of 12 slots, so being limited to your top three isn't a problem for the next road trip. At the end of the day, this carrier is a real bargain and a great value. The need for a good carrier is important, especially if you were one of the lucky few who got to spend more than $200 on the new 3DS. Better protect that investment, right ? And with this transporter, the 3DS will travel in style and be ready to battle.
profile.summary: Taking the game on the road

profile.description: With the Coby DP356 3.5" digital photo frame with music playback you can display all of your fondest memories. Displays JPEG photo files and plays MP3 and WMA music files. Photo slideshow mode. Digital alarm clock, calendar and temperature display. SD/SDHC card slot, USB port for fast file transfers.
profile.reviewText:
I bought this compact Coby picture frame to take advantage of the many digital pics that we take on vacation and at family gatherings.  All too often they sit on the PC not doing much of anything.  This would give me a nice alternative to the traditional picture frame.  Its strength is also its shortcoming.  The small footprint on this mini picture frame allows you to place it almost anywhere.  But its certainly not the showplace that many larger digital photo frames might be.

To maximize your enjoyment of this little wonder, you'll want to have an SD card on hand.  It doesn't need to be huge.  In fact, if you've been looking to upgrade the card in the family DSLR, this might be your chance.  A simple 1 gig card should me more than abundant for a decent stream of photos.

There are a few other onboard features in this compact picture frame.  The calendar mode is effective as a calendar, period.  If you squint really hard you'll see there is a thumbnail slideshow, with images smaller than a traditional postage stamp.  Not really sure why the folks at Coby even bothered.  There is also a passable music player that will allow you to provide an mp3 soundtrack to your slideshow.  Its not going to replace your trusty iPod, or even your favorite FM radio.  That said, I was able to listen to a ripped CD without any real gripes.  Again, a nice compliment to the office workspace, as it will provide you your own personal soundtrack without annoying fellow co-workers.

Gripes are minor.  In addition to the peculiar micro slideshow in calendar mode the slot for memory leaves the SD card hanging out and exposed.  The base certainly seems deep enough that they could have enveloped the whole card or at least slid it further into the frame housing.  A curious choice in my estimation.

I feel this little frame delivered some nice bang for the buck.  It capably displays my personal photos and offers some additional features, all at a very reasonable price.  Glad I discovered it.
profile.summary: Great for the office

profile.description: Elevate your tablet experience with our Classic Cover for the iPad mini . We've given one of our best-selling favorites a makeover - with the same durable construction and thoughtful design details now in a fresh new look.
profile.reviewText: This case is a great value. I have been using it with my ipad mini with retina display(mini 2) for about a month now. The case is well constructed and holds my tablet very securely. The cover folds flat when open, to make all aspects of the tablet easily accessible, from the power and home buttons to the volume rocker and ear bud jack. You can also use the case as a stand in portrait mode which is awesome for video viewing like You Tube and Netflix. Naturally, I got the case to protect my investment, but its also a good looking addition to enhance my tablet's appearance. The grey and black is a nice neutral look that is perfect for home and at my job. If there was one thing I wish it had was some sort of strap or clasp to keep it shut when not in use, but compared to everything that this case brings to the table... I'm very happy.
profile.summary: I really like it

profile.description: Easily charge and store your Wii Remotes with Nykos Charge Station for Wii. The Charge Station includes 2 NiMH batteries, exclusively designed for the Wii Remote, each providing up to 25 hours of play time. Each battery is easily recharged by placing the Wii Remote in the charging dock. The charging dock conveniently plugs into any standard wall outlet, allowing for rapid recharging of both batteries in 8 hours. The Charge Station includes 2 custom battery covers with contact pass-through points so you can charge the batteries while they are still in the remote. Each battery cover is also rubberized for superior grip during intense gaming sessions. The Charge Station matches the dcor and styling of the Wii, and is small enough to fit in any home entertainment center.
profile.reviewText:
Anytime a friend says they are getting a Wii, this is my first accessory recommendation.  My son and I play the Wii regularly and I can't imagine the kind of batteries we'd be going through in the couple of months we have owned our system.  The Nyko charger works great.

Play to your hearts content and when you are done, just make sure that the Wiimotes find their way back to the charging stand.  You'll know they are sitting down into the cradle because a blue light will come on when they make contact.  Furthermore, you'll know you are at full charge when the light changes from blue to green.

The charger doesn't have a very big footprint and sits neatly next to our TV on our entertainment center.  For those who are diehard fashionistas, its also white, so it matches everything else in the system.  All in all, its a must have accessory for your Wii and Amazon's prices is right on the money, especially when you can get in on free shipping on this item alone !
profile.summary: Couldn't be happier !

profile.description: The 27 LED Super Bright Deluxe Glow Work/Utility Light features super bright, long-lasting LEDs, with an additional 4 directional lights. It is equipped with a magnetic back that will attach to most metal surfaces as well as a strong fold-away swivel hook for easy carrying, use, and storage. The 28 LED Work/Utility Light is ergonomically constructed as well as shockproof and waterproof. Running off of 3 AAA batteries, it is simple to use to get a bright light for any work area.
profile.reviewText:
I had received one as a Christmas gift and had it stuck to our back door. It was handy if we needed to walk the dog or run out to the car at night. The larger panel cast a good deal of light, while the more traditional flashlight position was adequate for the most part. When we had to clean the coils of our fridge we turned it on and stuck it fast so we could see what we were doing.

While the the integrated plastic hook is kind of cheap, the magnet was very secure. In the end, the push button toggle that turns the light on and off just stopped working. Its unfortunate, because - for the most part - I liked this little light and found several uses for it. As others have indicated it suffers from poor build quality in some respects. I think I'd be willing to pay a dollar or so more for a better built version of the same light.
profile.summary: Good while it lasted

profile.description: Alternators are the U.S. version of the Japanese Binaltech line. Each features the same fantastic level of detail but do not feature the die-cast parts of their Japanese cousins.
profile.reviewText: As an adult Transformers collector, I have been a fan of Jazz since Day One(or should I say Gen 1 ?). So, suffice it to say that I was really excited and impressed when the Alternators line debuted and included Jazz. They called him Meister, and he was Mazda not a Porsche, but this one TF I knew I had to add to my collection. In his vehicle mode, Meister looks like a model kit for a Mazda RX-8. Since their 80's debut, the Transformers line has gotten more accurate to its real world counterparts. That said, the Alternators line took the concept to a whole new level. Doors open to reveal passenger compartments. Opening hoods and trunks also expose real-world details. The headlights, the grill, and the rubber tires make this one detailed car. Its a very cool concept. But it wouldn't be a Transformer if the story ended there. At this point I need to say that these 'toys' are not for your five year old. They are extremely detailed and, at certain points, a bit fragile. Transforming takes some patience and an attention to detail that the average kid may not exercise on a daily basis. Heck, these ultra-realistic transformers sometimes tax the patience of adult collectors. The directions may not be always crystal clear. I have found that there are some very helpful videos on You Tube for most of this line. But once you've got Meister switched from car to Robot, you're in for your second round of appreciation. There are some really nice details from the articulated hands to the Autobot details on the shoulders, to the incredible head sculpt used for this figure. If you are a Jazz fan you will be very pleased. Meister is not without his issues. At times he has some balance issues. He's certainly not as stable as Transformers Alternators - Ford Mustang GT (Wheeljack) or Transformers Alternators Jeep Wrangler Rollbar. But he can be posed and I certainly wouldn't hesitate to buy him based on this factor alone. Meister is also just a bit vanilla out of the box. He's a white car with, essentially, no detailing. That can be fixed. A company known as Reprolabels makes a very nice set of "Jazz" decals to bring this Bot back to his G1 glory days. In the end, I'm glad I found him and I am glad I added him to my collection. Meister is a certain standout of the Alternators line and a great part of my adult collection !
profile.summary: So Jazzed to own Meister

profile.description: This Lightning to USB A charging/sync cable lets you connect you iPhone, iPad, or iPod with Lightning connector to charge your device or sync with your media library.
profile.reviewText:
After several years of using the same USB connecting cable, Apple changed up their form factor. When my son got his fifth gen iPod Touch, we found ourselves with a "shortage" of cables. And the charger cable that Apple provides has always been on the shorter side. We needed a cable that would charge the device and allow us to sit on the couch and use it while we did that charging.

There's a lot to like about this Amazon Basics Lightning-compatible cable. First and foremost, its six feet long. Great for use on the sofa. Equally super for use in the vehicle when plugging into our USB-enabled head unit. And then there's the cost. Hands down, this is one of the most reasonably priced iPod cables. It showed up in the 'frustration free' packaging. The cable connected fine with our Belkin clip-on case, and charged the iPod as expected. I would have no hesitation recommending this cable to friends and family.
profile.summary: Perfect for our needs

profile.description: The Next Evolution in Pokemon comes to Nintendo 3DS.
profile.reviewText:
I've been a fan of the franchise since Sapphire. The latest installment does not disappoint. I'll give this to Game Freak, they keep tweaking the game just enough to keep it interesting. In the latest flavors you can buy new clothes for your trainer, and interact with your Pokemon by giving them a scratch on the head. The one feature that has me addicted at the moment, is the Wonder Trade. Even moreso than rushing from gym to gym in search of badges, I keep snatching up Pokemon and thrusting them into the cosmic slot machine. You put a Pokemon out there and randomly receive one back. I've landed everything from the most generic fodder to shiny rares beamed to me from other versions and countries. It really is pretty addictive.

And as far as the game goes, its pretty engaging, as well. The graphics are oh-so-pretty and the battle/puzzle/repeat methodology never seems to get old. With old favorites like Pikachu and Charmander, and a whole new class of Pokemon in the Fairy type, there's all kinds of critters to catch. At the end of the day, if you're a fan of the franchise... there's a lot to like about the newest Pokemon adventures.
profile.summary: In a word - Addictive.

profile.description: Do not pick up flammable or combustible materials (lighter fluid, gasoline, kerosene, etc.) or use in the presence of explosive liquids or vapor
profile.reviewText:
When you have pets you're going to have stains. It comes with the territory. The good news is, ever since we picked up this Bissell Spot Cleaner - we don't have stains for too long.

There really is a lot to like with this unit. It doesn't weigh a whole lot, so its easy to transport, even with the tanks full. Speaking of which - the tanks are very modular. Both the fresh water tank, and the dirty tank, slide easily out of the unit. The clean tank sits solidly upside down so that you can easily add both water and solution.

I also felt that the unit did a really good job handling messes. Shortly after receiving it we had to take care of a hairball stain which came right up. I had extra solution, so I also tried it out on one of our entry way runners. It wasn't perfect, but this was some pretty old, settled, dirt. I was pretty pleased with the dent that the Bissell did put on it.

I must confess, I do miss our wheeled unit that we had previously. Its clearly easier to roll a cleaner back and forth like a vacuum cleaner. That said, I don't recall our older wheeled unit handling the spill as thoroughly as the new one. At the end of the day, I would recommend the Spotclean Pro to a friend !
profile.summary: Spot on, or is it 'Spot Gone' ?

top_5.description: 2011 album from the Rock legend, one of popular music's most deeply revered figures and the main creative force behind some of the most cherished recordings in rock history. Indeed, it is no exaggeration to call Brian Wilson one of the most influential composers of the last century. On In The Key Of Disney, Brian Wilson rearranges some of Disney's most beloved recordings and makes them uniquely his own. Includes Wilson-ized versions of 'Bare Necessities', 'You've Got A Friend In Me', 'Can You Feel The Love Tonight?', and 'When You Wish Upon A Star'.
top_5.reviewText: If you enjoy Brian Wilson's surftastic music and you don't mind a twist on some Disney classics, you're in for quite a treat. IN THE KEY OF DISNEY kicks off with a great re-imagining of Randy Newman's You've Got A Friend in Me. The album really pulls out all of the Beach Boys stops and hits its stride with covers of Baby Mine and Kiss the Girl. Really good stuff. Not every song was a home run with me. The Lion King outing had me reaching for the skip button. That said, there's a lot of good music on IN THE KEY OF DISNEY. If you're a fan of Brian Wilson and The Mouse, then this one is a no-brainer.
top_5.summary: Endless Summer at Toontown

top_5.description: Batman Impopster Batgirl Harley Quinn Pop! Vinyl Figure: The villains of Gotham are dressing up like Batman and Batgirl! This Batman Impopster Batgirl Harley Quinn Pop! Vinyl Figure features Harley's signature colors applied to Batgirl's classic costume. The Batman Impopster Batgirl Harley Quinn Pop! Vinyl Figure measures approximately 3 3/4-inches tall and comes packaged in a window display box. Ages 14 and up.
top_5.reviewText:
The Impopster sub-line of DC Superheroes is sheer genius, in my opinion. Take the Batman figure and paint it as a villain. Penguin, Riddler, even the Wal Mart exclusive Killer Croc. I had looked at quite a few of these Pops before biting the bullet with Harley Batgirl. Now the hardcore collector is probably going to try and find this figure "in the wild". They will want to check the paint job, and (in many instances) the box condition. That said, mine came in pretty good condition. I am an out of box collector, but my box only had one slight ding, and its toward the back so you might not even see it.

The paint job on mine was a little ragged along the face where the red and the black met the white of the face. Also noticed a small white smudge on the hem of the cape. Again, I was completely fine with it, but I could see how some might develop a nervous twitch every time they passed by Harley Batgirl. Aside from the face and cape bit, the rest of my figure looked pretty crisp.

Nitpicks aside, I love this figure. I know its a repaint, but - again - I think the concept is genius. I am quite happy with Batgirl Harley. Its tempted me to pick up the Poison Ivy Batgirl Impopster. I've got to admit, I don't get the BatMAN Harley. But, hey - each collector is going to like what they like. Who am I to judge ? The utility belt and cowl of Batgirl, swirled with Harley's diamonds and red and black colors... I just really like it a lot. One thing I noticed is that the figure does want to tip backwards. There is no stand, so if you don't leave her in box, you may need to set Babs on the back row so she can lean against a wall.
top_5.summary: How ya like me now, Bats ?

top_5.description: Fun and colorful shell is made from 100 percent injection molded polypropylene, lightweight, flexible and moisture resistant. Protective tongue-in-groove closure protects garments from dust and water. Double spinner wheels. External fully integrated handle system. Split book style opening. Fully lined interior. Molded side feet, recessed TSA accepted combination lock. Worldwide limited 10 year warranty
top_5.reviewText:
Got this piece of luggage just before holiday traveling. Because we were travelling in the northeast during winter, the luggage nicely repelled drizzle and snow - keeping the contents clean and dry. We really don't fly all that much, but I can certainly see where this would be a great friend to folks who do fly. First of all, its RED. While it doesn't have a crazy pattern, I would imagine it would be fairly easy to pick out on the baggage carousel. It is a well-constructed hard shell which would protect the contents inside.

The wheels turn, swivel, and roll very nicely. The tow handle was very comfortable. Even though we were only rolling our suitcase across a street or parking lot, it made handling this luggage quite easy. There are also handles in both 'tall' and long mode for hefting it up on to a bed. Inside there is elastic closures and a zipper pouch. Very useful for segregating person A from person B, or clean from dirty. We were away from home for several days and the space was adequate. If it were much more than seven days, it might have been a different story. The eye to detail does travel inside the case with a well-made lining and fixtures. I was not financially compensated for this review. I received a sample for review purposes. The opinions are completely my own based on my experience.
top_5.summary: "Well thought out", "Nicely designed"

top_5.description: Transformers Age of Extinction Generations Deluxe Class Dinobot Slug Figure
top_5.reviewText:
Slug is the most recent redesign of the Dinobot formerly known as Slag. The Dinobots for Transformers 4 are a bit of a mixed bag. While Slug isn't the top of the heap, there is a lot to like about this Triceratops. The first big thing that old school fans will recognize are the red and purple plates that make up much of Slugs dino form. Each of the new dinobots has its own primary color in the new toyline, from slug to scorn to Snarl. Youll also notice the design choice where Slugs body is much more segmented, in contrast to his G1 likeness. It really pops around his head crest.

In robot mode, Slug is a part of this knight aesthetic that flows from Optimus on down through many of the supporting characters. The dino head splits to become two massive shoulder parts and is even attached with a screw where the eye would be in dino mode, which is a fun choice. I will say Im not overly crazy about the way his tail dangles off the back of the robot mode, but its not horrible. Hes got some nice articulation and looks really slick standing next to both Scorn and Grimlock. If you can pick him up for under twenty dollars, hes an easy add. Much more than that, and Id be inclined to look at some of the other TF4 toys first.
top_5.summary: A Dino by any other name...

top_5.description: Marvel Guardians of the Galaxy Big Blastin Rocket Raccoon Figure
top_5.reviewText: A lot of people I have been talking to seem pretty excited about Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy movie, and I think its kind of a no-brainer that Rocket will be popular with kids and adults alike. That said, I really see this version as more of a collectible. Rocket comes pre-loaded with batteries and went right into blasting mode. The little guy pops off various catch-phrases from the movie and fires off his space rifle. The gun barrel spins and lights up. There's all kinds of blasting noise and Rocket hops around, presumably from the kickback of his oversize space-weapon. The reason I think its more of a collectible is we all(ages 12 to 57) got a kick out of Rocket when we set him down on the hard wood floor of our kitchen. We cycled through everything he had to say and watched him blast all of the imaginary baddies. And since then, he's been sitting on a shelf. He looks really cool and will be fun to take down from time to time. But I just have a hard time seeing him as something that would engage kids for long stretches of time. Not the way something like the Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Star-Lord Quad Blaster or LEGO Superheroes 76021 The Milano Spaceship Rescue Building Set might. At the end of the day, Rocket is cool, I just don't know how much of a 'toy' he is.
top_5.summary: Lock and Load !

profile.description: Did you know, law enforcement will not return stolen property if it's not identifiable? Use our engraving pen to permanently label all your important items.
profile.reviewText:
OVERVIEW
I wanted to try this because it looked like a great tool to have for neat projects and gifting.

PROS
+works sorta, but does not engrave very deeply, or well to say the least
+comes with fine and wider engraving tip
+materials tested so far (plastic, metal, glass)

This tool is not worth it's cheap price. I tried it on a metal tag of my dog's collar also ( yes I can draw hearts but this tool actually ruined the tag. I tried about two of these styles and was about to give up before giving these a try when given the option to try these and I am really happy with these pants! They fit well, don't itch (Ihave allergies against certain gummy waist bands so not breaking out was a plus), or cut circulation off.

This was a lifesaver because to get the BMW Z4 on jack stands I needed to jack ip the rear axel at a joint and it had a steady grip and weight distribution of my jack like a charm. any indentation made temporarily immediately disappears after contact.  I did not receive anything from the seller for this review.

profile.description: Dogs cant sweat. They pant to regulate their body temperature. The hotter it gets, the harder they have to work to keep themselves cool. Dogs just want to chill. Theyll need extra help during the warmer months to keep them staying cool... K9 CHILL is the comfortable + safe way to combat overheating , reduce fatigue, prevent heat-stress + alleviate dehydration. Simply moisten K9 CHILL with cold water. K9 CHILL is made with a unique blend of breathable + lightweight materials which allow it to retain moisture for hours longer than an ordinary sponge or cotton towel. K9 CHILL even has a leash hole built in, so your dog can stay cool on the go!
profile.reviewText:
OVERVIEW
I ordered this cooling collar/wrap because it gets really hot all year around where we live and going places or on walks can be -even early or late- a very warm chore for my dogs.

PROS
+small/medium sized collar stretches 8-20 inches. Fit both GSD and my Papillon
+material does stay cool to the touch fir very long
+leash hole
+machine washable
+stretches, 95% Polyester, 5% Spandex

CONS
-item is too large for small breeds, it was very loose on my Papillon, yet double wrapping the collar is WAY too tight for her 9 inch neck. It fit better on my Shepherd. So this item is not very good for very small breeds fit wise.
-it does feel moist, the purpose is cooling, but since the collar will have to me moistened with water first, it's feels like a cool but moist light wrap.
-best for very short haired dogs; both my GSD and Papillon have very short summer cuts but the undercoat still is too thick, so this item won't help much with long/thick coated breeds

ALLTOGETHER
I nice idea/concept and probably great for a Chihuahuas or Doberman or such, but the item did not make a big difference for my dogs and the moisture feel I am sorta not happy about, though the item didn't drip, or evaporated moisture, just felt like it since the material locks the cool/moisture in. I will stay will portable cool pads, portable fans and water on the go instead.
profile.summary: Stays cool but feels moist. Best for short coated dogs

profile.description: Glandex is an oral supplement specifically designed for gland problems in dogs and cats. This formula was developed by leading veterinarians and is a scientific breakthrough in reducing gland problems and is more effective then frequent gland expressing.
profile.reviewText: I have to agree with owners who said this did not work. I had this prescribed by my vet due to two of my dogs having anal gland issues with one needing expression monthly and the other having had chronic infections. We tried everything from pumpkin to fiber add ons, different foods and antibiotics, probiotics, etc. this did not help even after a few months and it even gave my dogs severe diarrhea and indigestion that took months to re-adjust. Can't recommend for severe cases. I ended up having one of my dogs glands removed due to him getting issues the third time around. Recovery took 1-2 weeks but he's is happy and healthy and has no issues or pus filled glands any longer. The other dog I still express monthly but she never had infections, so I won't do surgery on her due to it being more messy than a health issue currently.
profile.summary: Did not work at all and dogs got diarrhea

profile.description: Its a big, scary world out there, and the Monster High ghouls are ready to grab a hold with their claws! This Scare-Mester, theyre participating in a Monster Exchange program that will bring some new students in and send others abroad to learn about each others skull-tures. Heading overseas, Draculaura will take a bite out of Shibooya in Japan, and Lagoona Blue will soak up Madread. Back home at Monster High, Lorna McNessie will make a splash sharing her Rotland upbringing, and Marisol Coxi will show them how her homeland of Monster Picchu rocks. Each wears a gore-geous outfit that monster-mashes skelements of her destination with icons representing her scaritage. Each doll also comes with a Skullette-shaped hairbrush, doll stand and diary documenting her most frightful travel thoughts and experiences. I also found it a bit odd that she doesn't come with any belt, necklace, earrings, bangles or jewelry. Her skin reminded me of a darker tealish- or warm grey (sorta zombie colored, but at least she is not lavender as I first thought. I photographed her with white background to capture the colore better than the site photos because she is not peach skinned like the photos there). The hair is simple but pretty in a darker and brighter pink with neon green, braided streaks. I did put stockings for MH dolls on my doll, because the one piece dress she wears is very short, so that way she looks more "dressed" I guess. Overall a cute doll without misprint, loose hands, messed up hair or wonk eye. So I am happy with this. I also find the furry tufts on the arm and leg molds cute!
profile.summary: Cuter than expected, but accessories are lacking unfortunately

The Arcan true low profile design allows users to get under almost any vehicle to lift and comes at a significantly lower cost compared to other models in the market. profile.reviewText:
Design - this tank on wheels is heavy in a good way. It was required to avoid paying a luxury dealership from lifting my 2010 BMW Z4. input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "2.0" for a product with description "New York Times, USA Today, and International bestselling author, E.K. Blair, takes her readers on an emotional roller coaster with her books. A former first grade teacher with an imagination that runs wild. Daydreaming and zoning out is how she was often found in high school. Blair tends to drift towards everything dark and moody and has been noted as 'The Queen of Dark and Twisted'. Give her a character and she will take pleasure in breaking them down, digging into their core to find what lies underneath. Aside from writing, E.K. Blair finds pleasure in music, drinking her Starbucks in peace, and spending time with her friends. She's a thinker, an artist, a wife, a mom, and everything in between.". The summary of the review text is "Bang-less:  Never Have I Fallen Out of Love With a Series So Quickly".
output:
**This review contains spoilers towards the bottom***

Wow, never have I fallen out of love with a series so fast.  I finished Bang on Wed., gave it a 5 star rating, and couldn't wait to delve into book 2.  What a disappointment this book turned out to be.  In Bang, we witness Nina in her twisted plot to seek revenge.  She was a cold and calculated strategist, who wouldnt allow her emotions to derail her diabolical plans.  In Echo, Nina is no longer the tough-as-nails survivor, she is now a shell, immensely broken.  But that isn't why I fell out of love with this series, Ninas brokenness and her slide into a mental breakdown is the most interesting part of Echo, my problem is all the glorified rape scenes and sexual abuse that appears to be the theme for the second book.  Bang caused me to be uncomfortable because there were so many graphic pedophile scenes, that it felt gratuitous at times, but I let my doubt slide and thought that the author is trying to show us what caused Nina to be so broken.  In Echo, I no longer doubt that the sexual abuse scenes are gratuitous, the book centers on them.  There are several pages where consenting sex is mixed with sexual abuse scenes, that I went from being uncomfortable to wondering if the author can come up with another scenario.  The biggest reason that I was disappointed in Echo, is below, and be aware that it does contain SPOILERS.

******SPOILER WARNING********

I loved Bang, the ending was so full of twists and turns that it left me gulping for air.  Echo makes a mockery of that ending, because everyone who bites the bullet  in Bang, miraculously  survives in Echo.  If you're going to have the balls to give an ending like Bang, then stick to it.  Dont do a do-over with the same characters being reincarnated, its like when a book has a painful characters death, and then pages later, the reader finds out that its all a dream.  Thats bullsh*t, a cheap and easy way to get an emotional rise from the reader.  Where Bang gave us twists and turns, Echo gives us the expected and ridiculous.  The only surprise for me is that Ive grown to dislike Declan immensely.  I understand his hostility and hatred towards Elizabeth/Nina, but I don't understand his desire to hear her recount all the sexual abuse from her childhood and then want to use that knowledge to degrade her even more.  He knows that she is unwell, and yet he uses sexual perverseness to punish her more.  The story is loaded with these scenes, and its too much.  I seriously doubt his love for her, thats its just sex.  He brings her home after she has been kidnapped, raped, and beaten, and he has sex with her that night.  Thats why I say this book is just pages of glorified rape,  sexual abuse, and sex.

The element of surprise is also missing from the story, you know immediately that the characters who perished in Bang, didn't actually die.  When I discovered this, I also predicted which character was tied to the other, and all my predictions came true.  Ill go a step further and tell you a prediction for the 3rd book, Elizabeths mom is the social worker who showed up at her foster parents house, the one who had the familiar face.

Bottom line: I wished that I had walked away from this series after reading Bang.
