profile.reviewText:
*Possible Spoiler Alert*

*Yawn*  Was there a purpose to this book?  Unless the purpose behind this book was an attempt at driving this series into the ground, then congratulations, it was a success.  This book is similar to ordering a box of candies from a company that you've trusted in the past, and they send you  a huge box, and you think that it's going to be filled with all sorts of goodness, but then you open the box, and it's filled with nothing but packing peanuts, and you keep searching thinking that you're going to find something, and finally after going through all the packaging, you find a caramel.  The packing peanuts in this book are the sex scenes, and try as you may to search through all of them, but you aren't going to find a caramel, maybe a piece of butterscotch candy.  Because I enjoy erotica, it pains me to say "Enough with the sex", please, we get it, we also get that they need each other to survive, Gideon is the yin to Eva's yang, he can't breathe without her, his body hurts not being inside her,  they feel each other's presence before they see each other, their skin aches when they part, WE GET THIS, IT WAS ESTABLISHED OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER IN ALL THREE PREVIOUS BOOKS.  Seriously, they have sex before work, while on the way to work, while at work, and then after work, at this point I would be happy just to see either one standing at the water cooler talking to a co-worker about the last episode of The Walking Dead, effing anything but the two of them effing.  It would be nice to read one of having an independent scene without the other waiting in the shadows.  It would be interesting to see Eva going to California without Gideon trailing, as it would to read about Eva going to lunch without Gideon waiting a table close-by, it would have been interesting to read any scene without them together, because as we all find out, they can't be together without engaging in sex.  That's is all there is to this book is the sex, and although I like sex scenes, it would be nice to have a little storyline to go along with it.  I skipped through dozens of pages because the sex is a yawn fest.

This series began with beautiful, wealthy, interesting yet flawed and damaged people, but has turned into a series about beautiful co-dependents that I seriously doubt can take a p*ss without the other one holding his/her hand.  I now loathe Cary, instead of him being a supporter and friend to Eva, all he thinks about is how her every move is going to impact him.  This book is essentially the three of them discussing sex, making each other miserable, whining and complaining, but can't be away from each other for longer than an hour.  C'mon, how ridiculous is it that Gideon wants Cary to move in the penthouse that he and Eva are having remodeled so that Cary doesn't feel deserted.  Gideon has turned into a pansy, frantic schoolgirl, but instead of passing notes of "Do you like me, yes or no?", he sends texts.  Corrine having sex with Angus would be more interesting than to reading this,  watching paint dry on the walls would be more interesting than this story.

As with book three (Entwined with You) in this series, nothing was resolved, nothing new occurred, it was basically a repeat of book three.  The name of this book should have been: Entwined with You Version 2.0, or Gideon Has Sex With Eva Again and Again and Again and Again and Again and Again and Again and Again.

Save your money folks, nothing new going on here.  I included a "Possible Spoiler Alert" because I wasn't sure if saying nothing new occurred would be a spoiler.

profile.description: Julie Hockley, a lawyer by trade and a writer by love, is the author of the bestselling novel Crow's Row. She currently resides in Ontario, Canada, with her family.
profile.reviewText:
I was elated when I discovered that the follow-up to Crow's Row, Scare Crow was released, and couldn't wait to download the book. It has been over a year since I read Crows Row and awaited the follow-up, which is a decade to a reader. Im a patient reader, I never want to rush or place stress on an author to finish a book; its his /her story to write.

My best description for this book is to imagine that you are hungry, absolutely starving, and a driver shows up to take you to a restaurant. She takes you on the most beautiful and scenic route, and then you discover that the road is actually a dead-end street, so then the driver takes a different road, and again, the scenery is as beautiful, but then you discover that its another dead-end street. The same scenario keeps playing over, another decorative route that doesnt lead to the restaurant, and finally you decide that youll settle for any restaurant, it doesnt have to be the one that you were anticipating. You no longer care about the scenic route; you just want to get to a destination. Thats how this story felt to me.

Julie Hockleys writing is beautiful; I don't know any other way to describe her meticulous flow of words. Ms. Hockleys exceptional skill of depicting character and their surroundings pulls in the reader; I was immediately drawn into the story. However, around 80 pages, I began feeling that the scenes that I had read didn't lead anywhere. I didn't understand the importance of Emmy working in the admissions office, and initiating a plan that would allow her to see information about Cameron. In the end, all she ended up was the address of his mother; the same address that she visited in Crows Row. I also couldn't understand Emmys financial situation; in one scene she is scared because she is unemployed, yet she isn't making any effort to attend school to keep her scholarship from being revoked. Emmy is worried if she cant pay rent that she will be homeless, yet she has the cabin that Cameron owned. In one scene, Emmy shows up at a bank with information of an over-seas account written on a wrapper, and when the bank personnel cant help her, unlocking the codes to obtain the account is shelved for a later time. If I thought I was close to being homeless and unemployed, decoding the information to gain access to a potential boatload of money could be important. However, Ill give Emmy a pass since the love of her life is deceased. Emmys desire to remain in that broken-down shack is another aspect that I don't understand. In one scene, she discusses how she isn't close to any of the other tenants, that she doesnt really know them; yet, when Griff show up with money, she cant bear the thought of leaving her roommates or her closet of a room. Then there are all the details that went into describing the cartels, their families, and connections; so much of it was unnecessary information. The Canadian woman who Cameron supports wasn't relevant to this story, and it was just one of many details that didn't really pan out or contribute to the story. Also, I would love to know how many times the name Meatball is written; Im a animal lover, but towards the middle of the story, I was wanting more Cameron and a little less Meatball.

I will say that the scene in Canada was absolute killer, Hockleys account of the brutal and vicious events was fantastic; Hockley didn't romanticize Camerons role. Hockley kept to the raw savagery of an underground crime boss, and didn't sugarcoat Camerons activities. Lets talk about some Cameron; his character has changed, and to me it wasn't for the better. I understand how he missed Emmy, I loved that he missed Emmy, but I felt that he grew a vagina when he lost Emmy. Cameron reminiscing about Emmys 16th birthday party and all the details, it was too wimpy for me. A huge thumbs up for the depiction off Spider and Carly. The couple has changed since they were living at the Farm in Crows Row. Carly is now showing the effects of living in the criminal world, her presence is bleaker; the couples relationship with Cameron is strained. Cracks are beginning to form not only with the couple, but inside the crime family as well. Trust is beginning to waver, and they are at each others throats.

Towards the end of the book, the story began moving at a rapid pace, and then BAM, the book has ended. The events towards the end of the book would have been better suited in the middle of the book and more time dedicated to those scenes. I thought that the book was packed with unnecessary fillers; scenes that didn't impact the story. I felt that the author didn't know where to take the characters.

Julie Hockley s writing skill is so creative and profound, one of the best that Ive seen in any author, but the storyline/plot wasn't there until the very end.
profile.summary: Two and half stars

No highlighting and minimal wear on individual pages.  Originally purchased at Barnes and Nobel for $15 each (combined value of $45).  THIS IS A GREAT DEAL! profile.reviewText:
I devoured the first two Crossfire novels, I mean devoured them, I couldn't put them down until I was finished reading them.  I waited impatiently for this 3rd book to be released, then I saw the ridiculous  price, I decided that I would wait, but curiosity got the best of me.  I downloaded the book on Tuesday, and when I was 11% into the story, I was soon wanting the bedroom scene to just be over.  I was so bored that I didn't bother picking up the book until Thursday and not finishing it until Friday.  I'm not against erotica, but it was tiresome to see the sex scenes repeated over and over.  For any reader that has read the first 2 books, we already know that Gideon is well-endowed, we don't need the same descriptions of how thick it is, or that it spurts a lot. We get that, we've known that since Book 1, what we didn't know was how the Nathan incident was going to pan out, and apparently it wasn't important enough to resolve in this book. There are so many sex scenes and so few scenes with other characters.  Her father's visit was over very quickly, and the outcome of an incident that occurred during his visit was pushed aside.

Bottom line, the sex scenes are fillers for this book so that the issues and plots from the first two books can be dragged out to complete the next two Crossfire books.  Other than Eva feeling more secure in her relationship with Gideon, very little has changed.  Cary is still dating both Trey and Tatiana, Corinne still mourning for Gideon, Eva's mom still trying to track her, and Brett is still harboring feelings for Eva.

I hope that the publishers are happy with my $10 for this book, because it is the last dollar that I will spend on this series.  The book being just mediocre isn't what angers me, it's the greediness.  I also think that the book was filled with sex scenes so that there would be enough material to finish the next two books. Most readers wanted to see the how the twists and plots from Book 2 would end, they were barely addressed. This series went from being one of my favorite to being a series of sell-out and greed.

The packing peanuts in this book are the sex scenes, and try as you may to search through all of them, but you aren't going to find a caramel, maybe a piece of butterscotch candy.  Because I enjoy erotica, it pains me to say "Enough with the sex", please, we get it, we also get that they need each other to survive, Gideon is the yin to Eva's yang, he can't breathe without her, his body hurts not being inside her,  they feel each other's presence before they see each other, their skin aches when they part, WE GET THIS, IT WAS ESTABLISHED OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER IN ALL THREE PREVIOUS BOOKS.  Seriously, they have sex before work, while on the way to work, while at work, and then after work, at this point I would be happy just to see either one standing at the water cooler talking to a co-worker about the last episode of The Walking Dead, effing anything but the two of them effing.  It would be nice to read one of having an independent scene without the other waiting in the shadows.  It would be interesting to see Eva going to California without Gideon trailing, as it would to read about Eva going to lunch without Gideon waiting a table close-by, it would have been interesting to read any scene without them together, because as we all find out, they can't be together without engaging in sex.  That's is all there is to this book is the sex, and although I like sex scenes, it would be nice to have a little storyline to go along with it.  I skipped through dozens of pages because the sex is a yawn fest.

This series began with beautiful, wealthy, interesting yet flawed and damaged people, but has turned into a series about beautiful co-dependents that I seriously doubt can take a p*ss without the other one holding his/her hand.  I now loathe Cary, instead of him being a supporter and friend to Eva, all he thinks about is how her every move is going to impact him.  This book is essentially the three of them discussing sex, making each other miserable, whining and complaining, but can't be away from each other for longer than an hour.  C'mon, how ridiculous is it that Gideon wants Cary to move in the penthouse that he and Eva are having remodeled so that Cary doesn't feel deserted.  Gideon has turned into a pansy, frantic schoolgirl, but instead of passing notes of "Do you like me, yes or no?", he sends texts.  Corrine having sex with Angus would be more interesting than to reading this,  watching paint dry on the walls would be more interesting than this story.

As with book three (Entwined with You) in this series, nothing was resolved, nothing new occurred, it was basically a repeat of book three.  The name of this book should have been: Entwined with You Version 2.0, or Gideon Has Sex With Eva Again and Again and Again and Again and Again and Again and Again and Again.

Save your money folks, nothing new going on here.  I included a "Possible Spoiler Alert" because I wasn't sure if saying nothing new occurred would be a spoiler.
top_5.summary: Save your money, nothing new happening in this book, except to drive the Crossfire Series further into the ground.

top_5.description: Julie Hockley, a lawyer by trade and a writer by love, is the author of the bestselling novel Crow's Row. She currently resides in Ontario, Canada, with her family.
top_5.reviewText:
I was elated when I discovered that the follow-up to Crow's Row, Scare Crow was released, and couldn't wait to download the book. It has been over a year since I read Crows Row and awaited the follow-up, which is a decade to a reader. Im a patient reader, I never want to rush or place stress on an author to finish a book; its his /her story to write.

My best description for this book is to imagine that you are hungry, absolutely starving, and a driver shows up to take you to a restaurant. She takes you on the most beautiful and scenic route, and then you discover that the road is actually a dead-end street, so then the driver takes a different road, and again, the scenery is as beautiful, but then you discover that its another dead-end street. The same scenario keeps playing over, another decorative route that doesnt lead to the restaurant, and finally you decide that youll settle for any restaurant, it doesnt have to be the one that you were anticipating. You no longer care about the scenic route; you just want to get to a destination. Thats how this story felt to me.

Julie Hockleys writing is beautiful; I don't know any other way to describe her meticulous flow of words. Ms. Hockleys exceptional skill of depicting character and their surroundings pulls in the reader; I was immediately drawn into the story. However, around 80 pages, I began feeling that the scenes that I had read didn't lead anywhere. I didn't understand the importance of Emmy working in the admissions office, and initiating a plan that would allow her to see information about Cameron. In the end, all she ended up was the address of his mother; the same address that she visited in Crows Row. I also couldn't understand Emmys financial situation; in one scene she is scared because she is unemployed, yet she isn't making any effort to attend school to keep her scholarship from being revoked. Emmy is worried if she cant pay rent that she will be homeless, yet she has the cabin that Cameron owned. In one scene, Emmy shows up at a bank with information of an over-seas account written on a wrapper, and when the bank personnel cant help her, unlocking the codes to obtain the account is shelved for a later time. If I thought I was close to being homeless and unemployed, decoding the information to gain access to a potential boatload of money could be important. However, Ill give Emmy a pass since the love of her life is deceased. Emmys desire to remain in that broken-down shack is another aspect that I don't understand. In one scene, she discusses how she isn't close to any of the other tenants, that she doesnt really know them; yet, when Griff show up with money, she cant bear the thought of leaving her roommates or her closet of a room. Then there are all the details that went into describing the cartels, their families, and connections; so much of it was unnecessary information. The Canadian woman who Cameron supports wasn't relevant to this story, and it was just one of many details that didn't really pan out or contribute to the story. Also, I would love to know how many times the name Meatball is written; Im a animal lover, but towards the middle of the story, I was wanting more Cameron and a little less Meatball.

I will say that the scene in Canada was absolute killer, Hockleys account of the brutal and vicious events was fantastic; Hockley didn't romanticize Camerons role. Hockley kept to the raw savagery of an underground crime boss, and didn't sugarcoat Camerons activities. Lets talk about some Cameron; his character has changed, and to me it wasn't for the better. I understand how he missed Emmy, I loved that he missed Emmy, but I felt that he grew a vagina when he lost Emmy. Cameron reminiscing about Emmys 16th birthday party and all the details, it was too wimpy for me. A huge thumbs up for the depiction off Spider and Carly. The couple has changed since they were living at the Farm in Crows Row. Carly is now showing the effects of living in the criminal world, her presence is bleaker; the couples relationship with Cameron is strained. Cracks are beginning to form not only with the couple, but inside the crime family as well. Trust is beginning to waver, and they are at each others throats.

Towards the end of the book, the story began moving at a rapid pace, and then BAM, the book has ended. The events towards the end of the book would have been better suited in the middle of the book and more time dedicated to those scenes. I thought that the book was packed with unnecessary fillers; scenes that didn't impact the story. I felt that the author didn't know where to take the characters.

Julie Hockley s writing skill is so creative and profound, one of the best that Ive seen in any author, but the storyline/plot wasn't there until the very end.
top_5.summary: Two and half stars

top_5.description: Sylvia Day Crossfire Series: Bared to You, Reflected in You,  Entwined in You.  Books have been read one time, and are in good condition with some wear on front paperback cover.  No highlighting and minimal wear on individual pages.  Originally purchased at Barnes and Nobel for $15 each (combined value of $45).  THIS IS A GREAT DEAL!  Please contact seller with questions and for more information.  Thank you!
top_5.reviewText:
I devoured the first two Crossfire novels, I mean devoured them, I couldn't put them down until I was finished reading them.  I waited impatiently for this 3rd book to be released, then I saw the ridiculous  price, I decided that I would wait, but curiosity got the best of me.  I downloaded the book on Tuesday, and when I was 11% into the story, I was soon wanting the bedroom scene to just be over.  I was so bored that I didn't bother picking up the book until Thursday and not finishing it until Friday.  I'm not against erotica, but it was tiresome to see the sex scenes repeated over and over.  For any reader that has read the first 2 books, we already know that Gideon is well-endowed, we don't need the same descriptions of how thick it is, or that it spurts a lot. We get that, we've known that since Book 1, what we didn't know was how the Nathan incident was going to pan out, and apparently it wasn't important enough to resolve in this book. There are so many sex scenes and so few scenes with other characters.  Her father's visit was over very quickly, and the outcome of an incident that occurred during his visit was pushed aside.

Bottom line, the sex scenes are fillers for this book so that the issues and plots from the first two books can be dragged out to complete the next two Crossfire books.  Other than Eva feeling more secure in her relationship with Gideon, very little has changed.  Cary is still dating both Trey and Tatiana, Corinne still mourning for Gideon, Eva's mom still trying to track her, and Brett is still harboring feelings for Eva.

I hope that the publishers are happy with my $10 for this book, because it is the last dollar that I will spend on this series.  The book being just mediocre isn't what angers me, it's the greediness.  I also think that the book was filled with sex scenes so that there would be enough material to finish the next two books. Most readers wanted to see the how the twists and plots from Book 2 would end, they were barely addressed. This series went from being one of my favorite to being a series of sell-out and greed.
top_5.summary: My Gideon obsession is officially over.

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "Thermaltake N0028USU HDD Docking Station. The picture is for display only and the hard drive is not included.". The summary of the review text is "Blazing fast, quality built".
output:
Damn FAST: a few minutes to ramp up on a file transfer speed then holds rates steady ABOVE 85 MB/sec! I moved 1.7 TB onto a 2TB SATA in under 5 hours. But this is on a fast system, plugged into the eSATA port of my ASUS P6T mobo running a i7 920 CPU clocked to 3 GHz, w/all programs shut down, except critically needed system processes.  You'll probably get slower transfer speeds if your PC is not as stoked.

I have three different docking stations from different suppliers, and this beats them all on transfer rates. It even beats (by a nose) the transfer speeds on my fully-enclosed Rosewill RX-358-S.

I'm a mechanical engineer myself; one glance and a couple days use, I can tell this Thermaltake BlacX is a quality design, built with quality parts.

Minor complaint: they should have put the power button on the front or top, so you don't have to reach round and try to find it on the back where it is hidden from view.

TIP: the real reason you buy this is to back up to 3.5" SATA, put into anti-static bags, and STORE IN A SAFETY DEPOSIT BOX. You don't do this do you? You should.

I know plenty of people didn't think to do this, then the unexpected happened: some had house broken into all PC's stolen, some had house burned down.

They lost ALL their personal data, everything from home videos to decades of family photos. They had backed up their PC's but had also kept that backup media in the house.  OOOps! Don't do that.

You'll find the 3.5" SATA drives slipped into anti-static bag will still fit into your smaller size safety deposit box (but won't fit if the 3.5" SATA is inside full drive enclosure).

UPDATE: please note that you must "mod" this product if you plan to use it with some of the newer Hitachi Deskstar 7K3000 6GB/s SATA hard drives. Those drives come in the 1.5TB, 2TB, and 3TB sizes. Those drives have the vent hole positioned in exactly a location that is COVERED by the swing door of the BlacX. I have the Hitachi Deskstar 7K3000 HDS723020BLA642, and I had to drill a breather hole through that plastic swing door, so the drive vent hole could get air. Otherwise, if you cover a drive's vent hole, it can overheat and destroy the drive!

profile.description: Vegas Movie Studio Platinum Edition software has everything needed to produce spectacular HD movies. Powerful tools for video compositing, color correction, and surround sound mixing help you get feature-film results in your home studio. To share, upload movies to YouTube, burn to Blu-ray Disc, or author DVDs with custom menus and graphics.
profile.reviewText: I used this software for six months. I am COMPELLED to post this review after discovering what many experienced users know - about the major software bug in all versions of Sony Vegas Movie Studio Platinum 9. I believe even the expensive "pro" version is affected. There IS a complex fix to this bug, but you should evaluate if you are comfortable implementing what many will consider a "complex" and risky fix. Sony was apparently too lazy to correct the software's inability to access beyond 2GB of your PC's RAM for most versions of Windows. This is the problem. They KNOW of this bug. Fixing this probably requires they re-write huge sections of code. Since Sony Vegas cannot utilize more than 2 GB of your PC's RAM, then it will crash when rendering requires more. For example, when you directly edit AVCHD (particularly 1080x1920), Sony Vegas will OFTEN CRASH while rendering to most formats (during the Make Movie phase). A typical example: I dropped just five clips onto the video timeline, for a total length only FIVE minutes long. The source video was 1080x1920p 24fps AVCHD. Sony Vegas was ONLY able to successfully render that 5-minute clip into Windows Media 512 Kbps 320x240 video, and sometimes successfully into MainConcept AVC/AAC *mp4 at 640x480 (typical iPhone-suitable format). So LOW res rendering was OK. Yet, it could NOT render to any higher-res format because it would lock-up and crash part-way through the render, every time. It couldn't even get that five-minute movie rendered out at 720p. It wasn't about THAT video clip; i encoutered this error hundreds of times with various video clips rendering to a wide variety of formats! That is pathetic for a piece of software that claims in every manual and marketing document to support editing native HDV/AVCHD files and exporting to multiple HD formats. You think my PC is too slow? Guess again. I'm running an i7 920 quad-core CPU clocked to 2.7 GHz, with 12 GB SDRAM DDR3 1600Mhz. That's one of the fastest CPU's you can buy, coupled with tons of RAM; what's more, it has a very fast read/write RAID10 hard drive array, plus a super-fast 160GB Intel X25-M SSD (which I edit my video files from). So my PC is screamin' fast and fully configured; so the bug isn't due to limitations of my PC. I'm running Vista 64-bit, but this bug shows up when installed on multiple other versions of windows! This is all reported in the Sony Vegas software user forums. I found the software fix on the sonycreativesoftware web site, under the Support > Forums. NOTE: once I implemented this fix, the problem was INSTANTLY SOLVED: Sony Vegas could immediately render to any format without crashing. Ah, but you need to see how complex the fix is. I'm a Dilbert type; I didn't find the fix complex, but many non-geeks will find this fix too complex. Go to the forums at site sonycreativesoftware, go to Support > Forums , then bring up the FULL search menu (not the single-field search that is at the top right of the window) Then in the "Search Words:" field you should search for "How to fix render crashes" Look for posts by "Mad Pierre", or "david_f_knight" or "blink3times" This fix involves downloading CFF Explorer from ntcore, installing it, then running CFFExplorer as Administrator and MANUALLY re-setting the 2GB limit flag in about FIVE different Sony Vegas run files so they can handle > than 2gig address space. You should find the detailed instructions in the forums before attempting. MY ADVICE: -if you have the money to burn, then just buy something like Adobe Premiere Pro CS4, because you know Adobe worked these kind of major bugs out of its video editing software; Adobe Premiere pro is well known to be stable. -You could buy Sony Vegas Pro 9, expensive yes but at least a little less expensive than Adobe Premiere Pro CS4, and use a custom encoder like MainConcept which the pro users claim fixes these 2GB stability problems. But you need the Sony Vegas Pro 9 version in order to customize the encoder. I would buy Adobe Premiere before I would buy Sony Vegas Pro. -If you do NOT have the money for Adobe Premiere Pro and are thinking about Sony Vegas Platinum 9, then I recommend you first assess if you are computer-savvy enough to implement the bug fix detailed in the Sony Vegas forums (see above). Don't forget that manually editing those files has unknown risks. -You could buy Cineform Neo Scene (or similar) to convert all your source AVCHD files (and other formats!) to avi, then directly edit the avi files in Sony Vegas. On my system (and others report the same) this method also COMPLETELY eliminated the crashes during rendering. Editing avi files also has the benefit eliminating the slowing and frame stutter you see when previewing your timeline movie on a second monitor in "good" or "best" full-screen mode (assuming your PC is fast enough). This is because the avi files are far-less CPU-intensive for Sony Veges to work with. (AVCHD video is highly compressed and CPU-intensive for video editing software to work with). Don't forget to set aside MULTIPLE Terabytes of archive disc space, because of the HUGE file size of the avi versions of your AVCHD files. Yet, all that won't solve all crashes; you'll still crash anytime Sony Vegas needs more than 2GB RAM to render. THINK ON THIS: From a software re-write, bug-fix standpoint, it would have been EASY for Sony Vegas to fix this in rev 9 - IF the fix merely involves re-setting the 2GB limit flag on say five installed files. Why didn't they? Maybe there is more to it; we may imagine that probably re-setting that 2GB limit flag on those files creates OTHER instabilities that are even worse. Otherwise, Sony Vegas would have already implemented that simple (to geeks that is) fix. However, I will note that I have not encountered any "side-effect" instabilities from the CFFExplorer fix.
profile.summary: Good, but CRASHES when hitting the 2GB memory limit

profile.description: A kitchen staple for more than 80 years, Pyrex bakeware is as relevant today as it was in 1915. Made of a durable, high temperature material, Pyrex bakeware is classically beautiful and versatile enough to use in the refrigerator, freezer, oven, microwave, dishwasher and on the table in style.
profile.reviewText:
I grew up seeing my parents use their old PYREX baking glassware in the kitchen.  After college I got my own home and eagerly ordered the new "pyrex" baking glassware.

I soon discovered "pyrex" kitchenware is now cheap junk that's no longer made from the good borosilicate glass

I took my newly bought "pyrex" baking dish (filled with cooked food) out of of a 350F oven and set it on a room temperature stove top.

It SHATTERED VIOLENTLY SPRAYING 350F glass fragments across my kitchen which melted holes in my new linoleum kitchen floor.
I'm lucky I wasn't blinded by hot flying glass fragments. Whew.

You see pyrex kitchenware made after about 1998 uses cheap soda-lime glass that cannot take thermal shock, and shatters easily. I had done what I had seen my parents do countless times (with pre-1998 PYREX glassware): pull  glass cookware out of an oven and place it on a room temperature surface. No problem.

However that will cause pyrex made after 1998 to SHATTER EXPLOSIVELY.

Do not buy this garbage.
profile.summary: Pyrex kitchenware made after 1998 will SHATTER EXPLOSIVELY under common kitchen thermal shock conditions

profile.reviewText:

It is NOT worth it. Quality is not good and they are not properly pre-seasoned (for steam) so on initial we saw them warp non-symmetrically due to steam. Claim of 10" size is a lie. Actual Inner Dia (ID) varies (within a single basket!) from 8.5" to 8 3/4 due to warp. Typ ID is 8 5/8
Yes, they are so out-of-round that ID measures 8.5 one direction and 8 3/4 in other direction

The 24-105mm f/4 is a highly versatile focal range and staple everyday lens. With the increasing resolution power of new sensors, it is designed to bring out the true potential of evolving camera technology. Sigma’s 24-105mm f/4.0 includes proprietary Sigma technology including our Hyper Sonic Motor (HSM) which ensures fast, quiet and accurate autofocusing. The use of Thermally Composite Material (TSC) reduces size and weight and as part of the new Global Vision design, it is compatible with the Sigma USB dock for further customization and the new Mount Conversion Service.Features: For Full Frame and Crop Sensor Cameras 3 Aspherical, 2 SLD, and 2 FLD Elements Thermally Stable Composite Internal Focusing System Hyper Sonic AF Motor Compatible with Sigma USB Dock
profile.reviewText:
Rating five stars because it is a good lens with very strong reviews. However, for any full frame (such as D750) Nikon owners starting to build their first lens kit and thinking of buying Sigma Art 24-105 lens, I share this opinion.

I regret buying it for my D750 - because I should have instead put that money towards buying the first in the "holy trinity" of pro lenses meaning the Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8, and then later buy the Nikon 70-200mm f/2.8, 14-24mm f/2.8

I'm not a pro shooter, but I work at company that has several of them on staff. They told me to NOT buy EITHER the Nikon kit lens (24-120mm F/4) or the obvious alternative Sigma Art 24-105 and instead put that money towards partial payment on the Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8.

I ignored their advice and regret it.

Those pro shooters were giving me really great advice to invest in top quality glass, buying piece by piece over time when you can afford it, to build up a great lens kit (that I'll use my entire life even on the cameras I eventually replace the D750 with)

The Sigma is a fine lens, don't get me wrong. Also not implying here that the Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8 is the optical zoom equivalent of the Sigma Art 24-105

Looking back now, I would rather have that faster (f/2.8) higher quality Nikon lens even though the zoom range is shorter (allowing f/2.8 optics). Besides if you buy the Sigma Art 24-105 you really have to buy the Sigma USB Dock for that lens.

That has you spending close to $1000 - then add the cost of filters for a size not common to your Nikon lenses. Look at the prices of a clean used Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8 and see you don't have to spend too terribly much more to instead get that used Nikon 24-70mm

And finally: this lens is insanely heavy. You just try putting it on a D750 (or heavier) body, then add a speedlight. I could not believe how heavy that is.

I'm going to sell the Sigma Art 24-105 and buy a clean used Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8.
profile.summary: Suggestion for Nikon DSLR owners thinking of buying this lens...

profile.reviewText:
I'm a mech engr and a homeowner. My wife absolutely LOVES the track lighting system I put into our home using Solux True Daylight MR16s. You'll find that just like natural SUNSHINE, these bulbs totally cheer you up as soon as the light hits you. My entire family just loves the light from these bulbs.

COST SAVING TIP:
I did an exhaustive web search in choosing fixtures for these bulbs. I found the lowest cost (but still good quality) track lighting match for SoLux MR16's is the Pro Track SKU 65227 (painted WHITE) or the SKU 79353 (painted BLACK). If you shop around you can get the 65227 or 79353 kit for about $60 which includes the 4-ft track, with 3 sliding light fixtures. Keep in mind that kit assumes you'll wire directly into junction box in your ceiling. If instead (like me) you want a cord (w/in-line switch) coming directly out of track that you can plug into wall outlet, you'll want to additionally get the Pro Track SKU 24323. There are lots of other Pro Track components compatible with the 65227 or 79353 track, which is how I built out a multi-sectional track lighting in our home (at low cost!). I'm not associated in any way with either SoLux or Pro Track, only mention because is nice low-cost match to these bulbs.
Do not mount these bulbs at height where anyone can touch them or housings surrounding them. They get extremely hot.
I chose the 50W x 4700K x 36 deg bulb with the plano-convex diffusers. Thats good choice only if you want soft diffused light thats widely spread (evenly lights up entire rooms). However, you may not wan that specific bulb or the plano-convex diffuser  you want tight light cone, for example, for lighting up a small painting.

If you want to buy the glass diffusers, look at the solux dot net website.

I also like these bulbs, because they can create SPEC light very close to certain lighting standards (assuming you need either 3500K or 4100K or 4700K).

For example, I use Photoshop and I want to see correct colors calibrated under a known ambient light. Thats only way you predict how others will see your images on their monitors.  If you "calibrate" the colors of your LCD monitor under NON-spec light (such as typical home incandescent, or fluorescent lighting), you do NOT get correct calibrated colors because what YOU see on your monitor also depends on ambient lighting bouncing off your monitor (because most calibration units calibrate directly against the LCD monitor so do NOT pick up and correct for corrupting incident ambient light). That problem is solved if you calibrate assuming a particular ambient color temp and luminance intensity level and then you ensure light of that kind is incident on your monitors using SoLux True Daylight bulbs. Plus you feel GREAT because it is like your home office is filled with sunlight.

One final tip: you must block the non-spec light coming out of the BACK of these bulbs, either with light fixtures having opaque housings that stop that back light (from entering your room), OR you buy the "Bulb Shield" or the "black back" version bulbs both at solux dot net. You see, all SoLux MR16 bulbs produce beautiful spec light out the FRONT at reasonable cost using a neat trick of compensation by filtering down (attenuating) certain frequencies and leaking that unwanted light out the back of the builb. If you let that unwanted light into your room, you do NOT have spec ambient light in your room. Once I saw a competitor to SoLux claim that SoLux bulbs failed to produce spec light. That scared me away from these bulbs until I looked at the test methods and discovered those competitors CHEATED (intentionally produced incorrect and manipulative results) by testing ALL the light coming out both front/back of Solux bulbs using a 360-degree integrating sphere). But independent labs who measured only light coming out front of these bulbs found it to be VERY accurate (for this price point) to the specified spectral distribution and color temp

profile.reviewText:
I love Canon products, but there are always exceptions. I hate this VFL-2 product.

Canon created a video light without color-balanced light. Absolutely stupid.

I use this with my Canon VIXIA HF S100. For God sake, the VFL-2 was designed for the VIXIA HF series. Yet, VFL-2 flash photos look yellow. And video light same problem. And you cannot find a color setting on your Cannon camera/camcorder that correctly compensates to correct the yellowish light from this product. Obviously you cannot white balance a momentary flash. Good luck trying to white balance the video light.

This issue with the VFL-2 has been complained about in many Canon camcorder forums. I'm not alone.

On the plus side, the video light is sufficiently bright to be a great help for videotaping otherwise unlit night scenes. I shoot night porno scenes with this video light. (I'm kidding.) Anyway, I notice less of a yellow-ish tint when it lights my video, compared to the far more severe yellow-ish tint when using the VFL-2 for fill-flash. Obviously the color balance is not as far off for the video light source, compared to the flash function of this product.

Also, a big plus: the light location is lifted up enough so that it passes over the 82 mm dia wide angle I have attached to my Canon VIXIA HF S100
So this product can solve the flash-blocked-by-wide-angle-lens problem.

Just keep in mind that every photo has to go into Photoshop or whatever as you attempt to correct that yellowish tint. At least if you care about color correct photos.

profile.reviewText:
I'm extremely impressed with this mask and snorkel set! I took it to Hawaii and it performed flawlessly for hours of snorkeling per day. It is also helpful this exact product is often found in storefront local sporting goods chain store such as Sprts Authrty. So you can try it on there to confirm fit. Then buy from Amazon!
1) The ball value is incredibly effective at keeping water out during waves washing over you (during surface snorkel) and also when you dive down fully underwater
2) Mask has nice wide view
3) Excellent airflow path allows you to easily take very heavy breaths without any airflow resistance
4) Purge value works great.
5) Great build quality. I should know. I have masters in mechanical design.
6) Keeps the water out when using it !

Please note, like any mask I always cleaned it before each day with anti-fog fluid. I used Jaws "Spit" brand but I think any good brand will give good results. Be careful when using anti-fog fluid not to OVER-BUFF it away after you apply it to the inside glass surface. You want to leave a thin film of it on the glass, because if you over-buff you remove it all.

I also followed mask directions to always clean with fresh (not salt) water after days use. And most important: sand scratches glass (because glass is made from sand!). Never toss your mask onto any item covered with sand (such as beach towel). Never carry your mask with other items that could rub sand against it. Simple solution is bring ziplock freezer bag and rinse sand off mask and put into clean zip lock to ensure not scratched by sand.

profile.reviewText:
I was planning to buy this camcorder as a gift for a friend. Then I did my homework. I browsed owner-posted comments in camcorder forums. I borrowed a friend's R10 and tried it out for the day. I went to a camcorder outlet store and spent several hours trying out competitors to this camcorder.  I compared the R10 spec's against its competitors. I spent way more time researching this than you'll ever want to.

I concluded nobody should buy this camcorder.

This camcorder has several critical flaws, and has only a couple minor advantages over its competitors. By the way, I happily own several Canon camcorders (HF S100, and HF M300) so I have nothing against the Canon brand.

MAJOR FLAWS:
-> Poorly isolated microphone records ANNOYING "ticking" noise movement of autofocus mechanism. (This is reported by hundreds of owners in multiple online forums.) Your video ends up with annoying background "woodpecker" sound, very noticeable in video of quieter scenes. (You can solve that by only using your camcorder to record video of woodpeckers!)  It is impractical to try solving this with an external mic, because the R10/R11/R100 has the mic input but no mic mount (are you gonna walk around carrying a camcorder in one hand and a boom mic in the other?)
-> Short spec sheet claims "full 1920 x 1080 recording" but that is a lie because camcorder is limited to 1664 x 936, which it then interpolates up to 1920 x 1080. That's pathetic! (and the result doesn't look as crisp as true 1920 x 1080). Yet for about $40 over the price of the R10 you can buy the Canon M300, which has a sensor that can capture at true 1920 x 1080, and has twice the effective pixels in video mode.
-> This camcorder supports no mounting of any attachments; there is no standard cold (or hot) shoe, or mini Advanced hot shoe.  In many shooting situations, you'll end up with lousy video because you couldn't attach the accessory needed to get good video.
-> It doesn't even have a filter thread to add filters or lenses!  Yet it doesn't even include a integrated wider-angle lens, as seen in some competitor camcorders. Try shooting video of a couple sitting next to each other across the dinner table from you; this camcorder can maybe get ONE of their two faces into the frame, due to lack of wide-angle lens. Yet for a few bucks more you could buy a Canon HF M300/M30/M31/M32 to which you can attach a host lenses/filters such as a wide-angle lens, and also attach other accessories (to mini Advanced hot shoe) and then retain and re-use those accessories when you eventually upgrade to something like the Vixia HF S200/S20/S21
-> The pathetically small 720mAh battery dies way too soon (some owners say under 45 min). This camcorder doesn't use the current standard Canon camcorder batteries (BP-808, BP-819, BP-827, etc.) that are available in a wide range of capacities, and at low cost in non-OEM form.
-> Suffers from washed-out grainy video in low-light (or even medium light), a drawback common to most all Canon camcorders in the HF and FS tiers. Dynamic range also rather limited.

MAJOR ADVANTAGES to the R10/R11/R100:
-> No touch screen! Most competitor camcorders (of similar small size) unfortunately have touch screens that are usually cumbersome to use as result of too many touch locations jammed across a very small (often rather unresponsive) LCD touch surface. I have a Canon camcorder w/o touch screen and a Canon w/a touch screen. I can literally make menu/function adjustments 3X as fast on the non-touch screen Canon. I like the LCD mounted button and 4-way Navi button found on the R10 camcorder.
-> This is a relatively cute looking camcorder and it comes in multiple colors.
-> For English-as-second language customers, this (and most Canon camcorders) support quickly changing all menus to display in one of many available language options, ranging from Euro-languages to Asian languages such as Japanese, Korean, Chinese Simplified or Chinese Traditional, etc.

MY ADVICE:
If you want Canon brand and in this size and tier, consider a camcorder in the M300/M30/M31/M32 series, because they are only approx. $40 more but are a far better camcorder. However, in this size and tier of camcorders, many would recommend other brands such as the Panasonic or Sony, because some camcorders (in same size and tier class) from both those brands are considered superior. You might consider something in the Panasonic HDC-SD60 series, or Sony HDR-CX110 or HDR-CX150.

Finally, I think that the typical NON-techie type consumers looking at these low-end camcorders, will discover they don't like dealing with the CPU-intensive highly-compressed "raw" AVCHD format (MPEG-4 AVC/H.264 ) files that are spit out by many mid and higher tier consumer camcorders. They will be frustrated to find native AVCHD format files won't play on their PC using most media players. More frustration will result when they discover they need a VERY fast PC to edit full HD AVCHD and render it to a conveniently playable format.  I think that non-techie type consumer is better off selecting a camcorder that saves its video (which might be H.264) directly in *.mp4 multimedia container format file, immediately playable on their PC by a multitude of media players.
profile.summary: Multiple Flaws in this model. Avoid it

profile.description: Enjoy year round insect protection with the revolutionary walk-through, auto-close, Hands Free Screen Door. The Bug Off Hands Free Screen Door is the solution for parties and barbecues, providing hands free entry and exit for you, family, guests, and pets. Keep bugs out while letting fresh air in. The magnetic auto-close feature automatically shuts the screen each time you walk through it. It fits French Doors and sliders, plus can be installed in apartments, rentals, and condos. This is a great alternative to expensive custom screens and annoying sliding screens that come off the track. The Hands Free Screen is built with easy height and width adjustment, with 2 height adjust tunnels at the top allowing for installation on odd size doors.
profile.reviewText:
The Bug Off screen only has a couple small (maybe 1" x 2") mating pairs of magnetic tape: one at the bottom edge, and a second about midway between top and bottom. This means that mosquitoes (and other bugs) can sometimes fly through the open seams.  While the seams do typically overlap across the entire vertical length (if closed correctly); nevertheless, in the areas between the magnets, that overlap often has a gap of 1/4 inch or more between the screens. Bugs DO fly through.  That is unavoidable because there are TOO FEW magnet pairs to hold that seam shut.  It is really unacceptable this supplier would use SO FEW pieces of magnetic tape just to save a few pennies on BOM and ASSY cost.

Just a note to buyers that you CAN buy magnetic tape separately from other suppliers, which is handy for helping this "Bug Off" screen CLOSE the seams better and keep bugs out.  For example, search for Master Magnetics 7019 Magnetic Tape"

But we shouldn't have to go buy the mag tape separately in order to fix a lame product
profile.summary: This Bug Off screen only has a couple small pieces of magnetic tape that do only a mediocre job keeping seam sealed

profile.reviewText: Read this and you'll understand why I will NEVER buy another LG blu-ray drive again. You shouldn't either. LG doesn't seem to care about its customers. I will share a "fun" example of life with an LG blu-ray drive in your computer You buy the Verbatim 97344 - 25 GB 6x Blu-ray 20-Disc Spindle because all the other competitor Blu-Ray players can write to this newer (and lower-cost) Low-to-High "LTH" type of Blu-ray media. Most GGW-H20N (or L) may not have factory flashed (initial) firmware allowing drive to write to that media. Maybe there's a firmware update that accomodates "LTH" type of Blu-ray media? OK, so next I spend 20 min searching through LG's horrible support website. Finally, found the firmware in non-obvious location on their site. Hmmm, lets check the README file, where we find these lovely statements: "This firmware software only works in windows mode with Windows 2000/XP. If you encounter problems in flashing the firmware or have any questions, please contact our LG customer support line toll-free at 1-800-243-0000." "This firmware update is for use only on PC's with Windows Vista and Windows XP" My home PC is running 64-bit Windows 7 Ultimate. I want to be clear this drive has always worked fine for me; it is the firmware update that has been the problem. Drive is connected using standard SATA cable. BOTTOM LINE: firmware could not be updated directly on my Windows 7 PC for this drive Yes, tried running the firmware update in compatibility mode (Rght Click -> Properties -> Compatibility -> Run in Windows XP mode) That didn't work either. I followed web instructions (found on some unofficial forum) that workaround is to pull the drive out and connect using the IDE cable of a PC running Windows 2000/XP. Update the firmware, then take it back OUT and put it back into your Windows 7 PC. That worked. That was my PC. Maybe you get lucky on your Windows 7 PC and firmware installs in the standard easy manner. Who knows. But LG's support website continues to NOT list Windows 7 under OS compatibility for this drive.
profile.summary: NOT COMPATIBLE WITH WINDOWS 7

profile.description: The Phantom Aquatics Snorkel Vests are designed to allow you to swim with your head in the water as opposed to life vests that are designed to keep your head out of water. They are inflatable so you can add or subtract air to meet the level of buoyancy needed by the wearer. This vest also offers an adjustable waist and crotch strap in order to secure the vest in place with maximum comfort. Available in Day-Glo yellow, the snorkel vest should be considered a necessary piece of your snorkeling equipment.
profile.reviewText:
Bought two and me and spouse used snorkeling in Hawaii. I'm very impressed!  Product has excellent build quality.

Also in general, if you are on the fence about buying a snorkel vest, I recommend you buy one. Snorkeling (when done with active swimming to see sea life) is surprisingly intense exercise that's very tiring only after an hour or two. At that point you will REALLY be glad you are wearing a snorkel vest to provide flotation because it allows you to rest and catch your breath without having to swim to stay afloat.

The other tip someone gave me that's really important is: buy some full-body UV swimwear (Polyester/ Lycra / Spandex, etc) that's at least SPF30. By "full body" I mean long-sleeve top, and optional but helpful is the yoga pant style full leg bottoms

For example, all local Hawaiians see so many tourists sunburned bright red because those tourists snorkeled without thinking about how suntan lotion washes away quickly and loses effectiveness in saltwater, and they forgot to wear UV protection swimwear.
profile.summary: Highly Recommended. Great design and great build quality

profile.description: Available in a variety of colors, the Artisan Series blender features five speeds plus Pulse Mode and a Crush Ice feature to handle all of your blending tasks. A 0.9 horsepower motor and Intelli-Speed Motor Control ensure superb, consistent performance.
profile.reviewText:
I'm a mechanical engineer who designs consumer products. I don't design blenders or work for a competitor to KitchenAid. However, I have plenty (decades) of design and manufacturing experience with products that involve similar materials and manufacturing processes as seen in this blender.

This KitchenAid model KSB5WH4 is such a poorly designed and manufactured (and functioning!) product I will never buy another KitchenAid product ever again.

1) Has a known manufacturing defect where the "Coupler Drive" (also called "Coupling") P/N 9704230, is molded incorrectly (or molded with incorrect resin) so that it degrades prematurely causing its plastic to become brittle, so soon many of the mating teeth chip off, making product unusable, because it no longer couples to drive the impeller of the pitcher. That coupler is the black circular plastic part you see on the top of the blender base, visible after removing the blender's glass jar/pitcher.  While it is true that coupler part can be ordered online for about $5, it is still an inconvenience to replace it frequently.

2) This blender cavitates horribly - creates air pockets preventint blending / mixing when used with many types of food stuffs and liquids. So to be clear it often does NOT properly circulate material from top to bottom for proper uniform blending

3) This blender CANNOT chop ice to a uniform consistency suitable for making cocktails or smoothie. It always produces chopped ice that has BIG chunks of ice scattered through the slurry. For example, CANNOT make a decent ice slurry for the "frozen" type margarita cocktail.

4) This blender has major problems blending many different types of food/veggies into uniform consistency.

Despite the high price you only get a lame one-year warranty. What makes me so angry about this blender is that you spend extra money hoping you get good blender performance, only to discover this piece-of-junk doesn't even perform as well as for example a $30 blender. We literally took our "cheapie" $30 blender back out of the cupboard and used that instead because it works better, and we put this KitchenAid blender up into that same cupboard to sit and collect dust.
profile.summary: Horrible product DO NOT BUY

profile.description: Brewing tea or coffee has never been so easy. This is the original patented Piao I teapot made by Piao I Enterprise Co., Ltd. While there are many popular infusers on the market, the Piao I has a built-in teapot that allows for the separation of the brew from the tea leaves once the perfect brew has been achieved. It has an upper chamber for brewing tea or coffee to the desired strength. Then just press a button and the perfectly brewed tea will drain into a lower chamber from where it can be poured into a cup for consumption. Any remaining tea, separated from the leaves, retains its perfect strength. Alternatively, the top chamber may be removed and the lower chamber can function as a cup. While this product specifies use for infusing tea, it works equally well for coffee. A splendid device for work and for home. profile.reviewText: I'm a white boy who married a lovely mainland Chinese woman about ten years ago. Her parents also live with us. They have all been educating me about tea for the last ten years. So I now understand plenty about the proper steeping of Chinese tea. We own a second home in China, and have coincidentally returned only days ago from a two week trip there, where we bought lots of good tea! We own FOUR of these teapots, and have used them for years. This product is quite popular in many areas of China because of the quality of this teapot and how well it steeps tea. This teapot has an upper reservoir of about one cup capacity, which lowers into the larger body of the teapot. The bottom of the upper reservoir contains a stainless steel ball stop valve. When you press a small button on the top of the teapot, the ball lifts and tea is strained through a fine stainless steel mesh as it drains into the lower reservoir. Then you refill the upper chamber with hot water for the next infusion. NOTE: everyone I know uses this product only for serving ONE, maybe TWO people; this teapot's capacity is too small for serving larger groups. Typically, owners use this as a "personal teapot" (at work, or wherever), loading it in the morning and infusing off the same tea all day long. That's how I use it EVERY day at work. I strongly recommend this as a personal teapot for steeping LOOSE tea, for these reasons: 1) You can easily increase each successive infusion time (off the same tea as it weakens), to ensure consistent tea intensity: pushing the button quickly vents tea into the lower reservoir, effectively halting the infusion (and fixing the intensity). A glance at the tea color through the transparent reservoir tells you when the intensity is just right. 2) You should always "wash" each new batch of tea leaves, and this teapot is very convenient for that; you simply put the dry tea in and poor hot water into the upper reservoir, swish it through the tea for a few seconds; then vent that directly into the sink to discard that wash water. 3) It is absolutely true this teapot gets more tea (more infusions) out of each gram of tea, compared to any other teapot. However, keeping in mind those last infusions may easily be 5+ minutes steeping time. You yield more tea per load due to the bottom venting ensures the flow of hot water is always down through the tea, also the upper chamber is small so infuses more effectively even when the tea is quite weakened by previous infusions. By the way, here's a tip for those new to steeping Chinese teas. How long to steep tea? Methods vary by tea type, but lets take for example good Chinese green tea. Most common mistake is OVERSTEEPING which results in tea with bitter (over-concentrated) flavor. New good quality loose leaf green tea, the first pass steeping should only be 60 seconds maybe 2 min max. Then you immediately halt steeping by venting the tea into lower chamber Now, to answer an obvious follow-up question: what to use when steeping green tea for more than two people? For that we use: Bodum Chambord 8 cup French Press Coffee Maker, 34 oz., Chrome Bodum CHAMBORD Coffee & Tea Maker, French Press Coffee Maker, Stainless Steel & Heat-Resistant Borosilicate Glass, The Original French Press, Made in Europe, 8 cup, 1 liter, 34 ounces I bought that Bodum after seeing the Hong Kong Hyatt bring that exact model French press to our table when we ordered green tea. Made for coffee but works great for tea also. My Chinese in-laws never previously thought of using a French coffee press for steeping and serving green tea. After they tried the one I bought, they liked it so much now it is only thing they use when making green tea (for serving four or more)
profile.summary: Great personal sized teapot!
