top_5.description: Vegas Movie Studio Platinum Edition software has everything needed to produce spectacular HD movies. Powerful tools for video compositing, color correction, and surround sound mixing help you get feature-film results in your home studio. To share, upload movies to YouTube, burn to Blu-ray Disc, or author DVDs with custom menus and graphics.
top_5.reviewText: I used this software for six months. I am COMPELLED to post this review after discovering what many experienced users know - about the major software bug in all versions of Sony Vegas Movie Studio Platinum 9. I believe even the expensive "pro" version is affected. There IS a complex fix to this bug, but you should evaluate if you are comfortable implementing what many will consider a "complex" and risky fix. Sony was apparently too lazy to correct the software's inability to access beyond 2GB of your PC's RAM for most versions of Windows. This is the problem. They KNOW of this bug. Fixing this probably requires they re-write huge sections of code. Since Sony Vegas cannot utilize more than 2 GB of your PC's RAM, then it will crash when rendering requires more. For example, when you directly edit AVCHD (particularly 1080x1920), Sony Vegas will OFTEN CRASH while rendering to most formats (during the Make Movie phase). A typical example: I dropped just five clips onto the video timeline, for a total length only FIVE minutes long. The source video was 1080x1920p 24fps AVCHD. Sony Vegas was ONLY able to successfully render that 5-minute clip into Windows Media 512 Kbps 320x240 video, and sometimes successfully into MainConcept AVC/AAC *mp4 at 640x480 (typical iPhone-suitable format). So LOW res rendering was OK. Yet, it could NOT render to any higher-res format because it would lock-up and crash part-way through the render, every time. It couldn't even get that five-minute movie rendered out at 720p. It wasn't about THAT video clip; i encoutered this error hundreds of times with various video clips rendering to a wide variety of formats! That is pathetic for a piece of software that claims in every manual and marketing document to support editing native HDV/AVCHD files and exporting to multiple HD formats. You think my PC is too slow? Guess again. I'm running an i7 920 quad-core CPU clocked to 2.7 GHz, with 12 GB SDRAM DDR3 1600Mhz. That's one of the fastest CPU's you can buy, coupled with tons of RAM; what's more, it has a very fast read/write RAID10 hard drive array, plus a super-fast 160GB Intel X25-M SSD (which I edit my video files from). So my PC is screamin' fast and fully configured; so the bug isn't due to limitations of my PC. I'm running Vista 64-bit, but this bug shows up when installed on multiple other versions of windows! This is all reported in the Sony Vegas software user forums. I found the software fix on the sonycreativesoftware web site, under the Support > Forums. NOTE: once I implemented this fix, the problem was INSTANTLY SOLVED: Sony Vegas could immediately render to any format without crashing. Ah, but you need to see how complex the fix is. I'm a Dilbert type; I didn't find the fix complex, but many non-geeks will find this fix too complex. Go to the forums at site sonycreativesoftware, go to Support > Forums , then bring up the FULL search menu (not the single-field search that is at the top right of the window) Then in the "Search Words:" field you should search for "How to fix render crashes" Look for posts by "Mad Pierre", or "david_f_knight" or "blink3times" This fix involves downloading CFF Explorer from ntcore, installing it, then running CFFExplorer as Administrator and MANUALLY re-setting the 2GB limit flag in about FIVE different Sony Vegas run files so they can handle > than 2gig address space. You should find the detailed instructions in the forums before attempting. MY ADVICE: -if you have the money to burn, then just buy something like Adobe Premiere Pro CS4, because you know Adobe worked these kind of major bugs out of its video editing software; Adobe Premiere pro is well known to be stable. -You could buy Sony Vegas Pro 9, expensive yes but at least a little less expensive than Adobe Premiere Pro CS4, and use a custom encoder like MainConcept which the pro users claim fixes these 2GB stability problems. But you need the Sony Vegas Pro 9 version in order to customize the encoder. I would buy Adobe Premiere before I would buy Sony Vegas Pro. -If you do NOT have the money for Adobe Premiere Pro and are thinking about Sony Vegas Platinum 9, then I recommend you first assess if you are computer-savvy enough to implement the bug fix detailed in the Sony Vegas forums (see above). Don't forget that manually editing those files has unknown risks. -You could buy Cineform Neo Scene (or similar) to convert all your source AVCHD files (and other formats!) to avi, then directly edit the avi files in Sony Vegas. On my system (and others report the same) this method also COMPLETELY eliminated the crashes during rendering. Editing avi files also has the benefit eliminating the slowing and frame stutter you see when previewing your timeline movie on a second monitor in "good" or "best" full-screen mode (assuming your PC is fast enough). This is because the avi files are far-less CPU-intensive for Sony Veges to work with. (AVCHD video is highly compressed and CPU-intensive for video editing software to work with). Don't forget to set aside MULTIPLE Terabytes of archive disc space, because of the HUGE file size of the avi versions of your AVCHD files. Yet, all that won't solve all crashes; you'll still crash anytime Sony Vegas needs more than 2GB RAM to render. THINK ON THIS: From a software re-write, bug-fix standpoint, it would have been EASY for Sony Vegas to fix this in rev 9 - IF the fix merely involves re-setting the 2GB limit flag on say five installed files. Why didn't they? Maybe there is more to it; we may imagine that probably re-setting that 2GB limit flag on those files creates OTHER instabilities that are even worse. Otherwise, Sony Vegas would have already implemented that simple (to geeks that is) fix. However, I will note that I have not encountered any "side-effect" instabilities from the CFFExplorer fix.
top_5.summary: Good, but CRASHES when hitting the 2GB memory limit

top_5.description: A kitchen staple for more than 80 years, Pyrex bakeware is as relevant today as it was in 1915. Made of a durable, high temperature material, Pyrex bakeware is classically beautiful and versatile enough to use in the refrigerator, freezer, oven, microwave, dishwasher and on the table in style.
top_5.reviewText:
I grew up seeing my parents use their old PYREX baking glassware in the kitchen.  After college I got my own home and eagerly ordered the new "pyrex" baking glassware.

I soon discovered "pyrex" kitchenware is now cheap junk that's no longer made from the good borosilicate glass

I took my newly bought "pyrex" baking dish (filled with cooked food) out of of a 350F oven and set it on a room temperature stove top.

It SHATTERED VIOLENTLY SPRAYING 350F glass fragments across my kitchen which melted holes in my new linoleum kitchen floor.
I'm lucky I wasn't blinded by hot flying glass fragments. Whew.

You see pyrex kitchenware made after about 1998 uses cheap soda-lime glass that cannot take thermal shock, and shatters easily. I had done what I had seen my parents do countless times (with pre-1998 PYREX glassware): pull  glass cookware out of an oven and place it on a room temperature surface. No problem.

However that will cause pyrex made after 1998 to SHATTER EXPLOSIVELY.

Do not buy this garbage.
top_5.summary: Pyrex kitchenware made after 1998 will SHATTER EXPLOSIVELY under common kitchen thermal shock conditions

top_5.description: The Juvale Bamboo steamer basket is perfect for cooking your food while remaining healthy. This 10" food steamer is two-tiered to enable you to steam twice as much in the same amount of time. The bamboo is a natural finish, constructed for strength and durability. Unlike cheap steamers were the lids wrap and deform over time, this steamer is guaranteed to be of the best quality. This food steamer is a healthy alternative to cooking with oil and grease. It is perfect for any kitchen. Steaming is one of the oldest and most important cooking methods in Chinese cuisine. They use steam to cook everything from breads to soups to dumplings to seafood. Food steamer cooking is a very healthy way to cook because it basically requires no added oils or fats. The most traditional steamer basket is made from bamboo. The bamboo steamer baskets are handmade of natural bamboo with strength and durability. They are attractive enough to be brought directly to the table for serving, and food will stay warm in a covered steamer up to half an hour.
top_5.reviewText:
I bought these to save a few dollars over the cost of higher quality Helen Chen's Bamboo steamer or the more expensive higher quality Joyce Chen brand. I'm not affiliated with either of those brands.

It is NOT worth it. Quality is not good and they are not properly pre-seasoned (for steam) so on initial we saw them warp non-symmetrically due to steam. This caused several bad things to happen on first use: 1) basket warped so lid no longer fits; 2) one end of some of the bamboo stakes popped out of annular slot, and dropped down

Claim of 10" size is a lie. Actual Inner Dia (ID) varies (within a single basket!) from 8.5" to 8 3/4 due to warp. Typ ID is 8 5/8
Yes, they are so out-of-round that ID measures 8.5 one direction and 8 3/4 in other direction
Actual Outer Dia (OD) is about 9 1/2 inches.

So they will NOT fit (!!) the low-cost good quality Steaming Paper inserts made by other brands (Joyce Chen, Helen Chen) for 10" that have ID about 9.5"
top_5.summary: It is NOT worth it. Spend a few dollars and buy a better brand.

top_5.description: The Sigma 24-105mm f/4.0 DG OS HSM Lens for Sony DSLR Cameras is a premium lens designed for full frame cameras and will also work with APS-C sensors with an effective increase in focal length. The 24-105mm f/4 is a highly versatile focal range and staple everyday lens. With the increasing resolution power of new sensors, it is designed to bring out the true potential of evolving camera technology. Sigma’s 24-105mm f/4.0 includes proprietary Sigma technology including our Hyper Sonic Motor (HSM) which ensures fast, quiet and accurate autofocusing. A 9 blade rounded diaphragm creates beautiful background blur, while FLD and SLD glass elements compensate for various aberrations, distortion and curvature. The use of Thermally Composite Material (TSC) reduces size and weight and as part of the new Global Vision design, it is compatible with the Sigma USB dock for further customization and the new Mount Conversion Service.Features: For Full Frame and Crop Sensor Cameras 3 Aspherical, 2 SLD, and 2 FLD Elements Thermally Stable Composite Internal Focusing System Hyper Sonic AF Motor Compatible with Sigma USB Dock
top_5.reviewText:
Rating five stars because it is a good lens with very strong reviews. However, for any full frame (such as D750) Nikon owners starting to build their first lens kit and thinking of buying Sigma Art 24-105 lens, I share this opinion.

I regret buying it for my D750 - because I should have instead put that money towards buying the first in the "holy trinity" of pro lenses meaning the Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8, and then later buy the Nikon 70-200mm f/2.8, 14-24mm f/2.8

I'm not a pro shooter, but I work at company that has several of them on staff. They told me to NOT buy EITHER the Nikon kit lens (24-120mm F/4) or the obvious alternative Sigma Art 24-105 and instead put that money towards partial payment on the Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8.

I ignored their advice and regret it.

Those pro shooters were giving me really great advice to invest in top quality glass, buying piece by piece over time when you can afford it, to build up a great lens kit (that I'll use my entire life even on the cameras I eventually replace the D750 with)

The Sigma is a fine lens, don't get me wrong. Also not implying here that the Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8 is the optical zoom equivalent of the Sigma Art 24-105

Looking back now, I would rather have that faster (f/2.8) higher quality Nikon lens even though the zoom range is shorter (allowing f/2.8 optics). Besides if you buy the Sigma Art 24-105 you really have to buy the Sigma USB Dock for that lens.

That has you spending close to $1000 - then add the cost of filters for a size not common to your Nikon lenses. Look at the prices of a clean used Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8 and see you don't have to spend too terribly much more to instead get that used Nikon 24-70mm

And finally: this lens is insanely heavy. You just try putting it on a D750 (or heavier) body, then add a speedlight. I could not believe how heavy that is.

I'm going to sell the Sigma Art 24-105 and buy a clean used Nikon 24-70mm f/2.8.
top_5.summary: Suggestion for Nikon DSLR owners thinking of buying this lens...

top_5.description: WorkForce 3640 Wireless All-in-One Inkjet Printer
top_5.reviewText:
If like me you were foolish enough to buy this printer, you should IMMEDIATELY prevent any firmware updates: printer Properties => Preferences => Maintenance tab => Software Update => Auto update settings => choose NEVER. Uncheck all

If your firmware gets updated to a certain newer level, then you can NEVER use any after-market ink. If I recall, if your firmware is rev 26. C7. GM21FI. or later you are screwed. You are chained for the life of this printer to buy the ever more expensive Epson ink.

Here's what I would do differently. Go to an aftermarket ink re-seller like inkproducts. Read their list of printers that allow you to use MUCH LESS EXPENSIVE after market ink. Buy one of those printers instead.

UPDATE: 14 months after I bought this printer the print head clogged producing smeared printing on the black ink. I printed history page which showed only 1500 sheets total had printed. I then followed the manual instructions exactly for cleaning a printhead. I did this five times and it DID NOT FIX. Next solution is to use solvent to clean printhead; HOWEVER, THIS  PRINTHEAD CANNOT BE ACCESSED FOR CLEANING

I want to be crystal clear my printer has only used OEM Epson Ink 786 cartridges.

So after only 1500 printed pages and 14 months after buying this printer, it is printing smeared fuzzy for everything that's black color and this is not fixable by any method I found in the Epson manual and Epson forums.
top_5.summary: I REGRET BUYING! PRINTER BLOCKS YOU FROM REFILLING WITH AFTER MARKET INK!

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "The Canon EF 100mm f/2.8L IS USM Macro Lens is the first mid-telephoto macro lens to include Canon's sophisticated Image Stabilization. With the highest quality optics available, combined with near-silent Ultrasonic focusing and life-size close-up capabilities without an adapter, the EF 100mm f/2.8L Macro IS USM is simply unrivaled. The Hybrid Image Stabilization Technology effectively compensates for both angular and shift camera shake during close-up shooting. The lens was developed to expand users' photographing range and allow a wider range of users to easily enjoy macro photography. Suitable for Nature/concert/potrait and close up/product photography". The summary of the review text is "A stunner, that happens to be awesome for macro AND portraits!".
output:
The Canon EF 100mm f/2.8L IS USM lens is a fantastic lens for numerous reasons.  First, it is the classic 100mm macro length.  While perhaps not as compact as a 60mm macro nor does it have the working distance of a 180mm macro, it offers a good compromise between the two in that it still offers a good working distance, is not too large, and with its built-in image-stabilization is actually hand-holdable for macro!  Now, in order to do handheld macro you do need to have a proper flash setup, as standard hotshoe flash will likely not clear the front of the lens for macro given the close distance.  But, if you use off-camera flash, ring flash, or twin flash, you will likely be able to handhold your macro shots using IS.  Now, they will likely not be as sharp as if they were on a tripod, but they will still be usable and this is a huge difference; you will be able to spontaneously capture things you would have missed before while setting up your tripod.

Speaking of the IS, as other reviews mentioned the IS in this unit does make some odd noises (which is normal) but it is effective as it can be.  The one area it is not effective w/ macro though is if you rock forward and backward while taking your handheld shot as the IS cannot accommodate for the image losing focus - for that you'd need to use Liveview constant autofocus.

But, unlike most combo lenses, this lens is also superb for its secondary feature - portraits!  Some of my best portrait shots have come from this lens - it is razor sharp and has exceptional bokeh.  There is a switch on the lens which allows you to adjust the AF mode depending on whether you'll be doing portrait or macro.  It works great all around for both functions.

The package also comes with a lens hood and a lens pouch.  Altogether a fantastic deal.  I don't see any negative with this lens, even the price is reasonable considering you are essentially getting two lenses in one!  This one should be in everyone's kit, whether you are on full frame, crop, or both!

Also, it should be noted that it uses a 67mm filter thread, so the filters and Canon flash accessories that fit the other Canon macro lenses will not fit this one without an adapter.

profile.description: It's Windows reimagined and reinvented from a solid core of Windows 7 speed and reliability. It's an all-new touch interface. It's a new Windows for new devices. And it's easy to try now-whether you're installing it for the first time, or moving from Windows 8 Consumer Preview.
profile.reviewText:
Windows 8, like Vista, appears to be a polarizing product.

But, this is not surprising as Windows 8 offers the largest UI change in Windows since Windows XP.  That is not to say it is in any way bad.  In fact, it is far superior to Windows 7.

However, the learning curve is a bit steep for non-techie users as the tutorial is inadequate.  The operating system itself is extremely intuitive, Microsoft just needs to put a better tutorial in the next version.

Overall a solid win especially if you are willing to give something new a try.  The Live Tiles are much more colorful & informative than icons and it truly feels like you are moving into a new generation of Windows with this release.  One piece of advice, if you are able to procure a model with a touchscreen or upgrade your PC with a touchscreen monitor, that will give you optimal results.  It is not required, but it just feels more natural.

Overall, HIGHLY recommended for the adventurous! :)
profile.summary: A misunderstood but much needed reboot

profile.description: Step into Rift. Whether you're stepping into your favorite game, watching an immersive VR movie, jumping to a destination on the other side of the world, or just spending time with friends in VR, you'll feel like you're really there.
profile.reviewText:
Oculus Rift is truly amazing. I picked this up at a local electronics retailer and couldn't be happier with my purchase.

It is an experience like none other, and if you have an electronics retailer near you that has one for demo, I urge you to try it. You really feel like you are transported to another world when using it. I would try to explain here, but it is best to try it. A few moments in and you will be smiling ear to ear.

I love the product, and the Oculus Store is amazingly well setup for VR as well. It is much less clunky than Valve's SteamVR, though there are still quite a few features that need to be implemented.

I know people are trying to decide between this and VIVE. A few things to consider:

1. Motion controls. Yes, VIVE has them now. But Oculus will have them available for order in 3-4 months and the Oculus motion controls look *much* better. Oculus purchased the team that made the highly acclaimed XBOX 360 controller for Microsoft to make the Oculus controller, and it shows! The Oculus Touch controllers are far more ergonomic and better featured than the VIVE wands, as Oculus Touch can even do finger tracking unlike the VIVE wands. Oculus may be releasing them a few months later, but it appears certainly worth the wait!

2. Exclusive games. Oculus has much more of them than VIVE.

3. Comfort. The Oculus is much more comfortable to wear for extended play sessions with as only fabric comes in contact with your face. Also, compared to the Vive, the Rift is less heavy, has only one cable instead of several, and has integrated headphones.  All of this makes it much easier and more comfortable to slip into VR.

4. Setup. The VIVE requires permanently wall-mounting sensors on your wall; Oculus sensors can be placed easily on a table or stand.

5. Flexibility. VIVE forces you to use the somewhat awkward wands (which feel more like an ice-cream scoop than a natural extension of your hand), while Oculus allows for XBOX controller input or the natural-feeling Oculus Touch controllers.

6. Support. VIVE is owned by HTC, a company that has been near bankruptcy several times in the recent future. Oculus is owned by Facebook - yeah, don't think they are going anywhere anytime soon.

7. Console alliance - Oculus has a strong partnership with Microsoft and XBOX. VIVE is PC-only. This gives Oculus a wider audience and longer legs.

8. Mobile alliance - The Oculus platform has a strong partnership with Samsung and Galaxy smartphones using GearVR, further extending the reach of the Oculus platform.

9. Price - Oculus is $599, VIVE hundreds of dollars more. Oculus lets you get started in VR without dropping a whole paycheck on it.

10. Room space - going back to flexibility, VIVE requires a huge amount of room space to use. Oculus is capable of room-scale tracking as well with Oculus Touch, however you are not *required* to have that much room with Oculus. If you only have a small space, you can still use Oculus seated with a large amount of games. With VIVE you are simply out of luck.

CONCLUSION: While VIVE is easier to find now and was first to market with motion controllers, the above listed points indicate to me that Oculus Rift is the smarter long term purchase. I believe in the long run VIVE will not be as popular and in fact may be fully eclipsed by Oculus Rift at some point. It may be tempting to buy a VIVE since it is easy to find, but I personally believe it is worth the wait for Oculus.

NOTE: Ensure your PC has a fast CPU and at least a GeForce 970 graphics card in order to power this device properly.  Also, the full retail price for this is $599.99, be sure not to overpay from a third party seller!
profile.summary: The next revolution in gaming and entertainment!

profile.description: Catch Phrase Decades Game
profile.reviewText:
In Catch Phrase Decades, two teams (2 players per team minimum) are pitted against one another to see who is best able to communicate with their team member in order to have them guess the word being described.  If your team member can guess the word you are trying to describe, you pass the unit to the other team and they have to start with a new word; this goes back and forth until the buzzer sounds on the unit, at which point the team who is not holding the unit gets a point, or two points if they can guess the word the losing team could not.  You are not allowed to say part of the word being guessed, a word that rhymes with the word being guessed, or the first letter of the word being guessed.

In other words, it is a variation of The $20,000 Pyramid that alternates between teams.  This particular version of Catch Phrase is divided into decade categories from the 70s-10s.  I found the words to be unique and appropriate for each decade category, although there are a lot of names that range from political figures to TV shows - so it is more challenging than the original Catch Phrase.

In terms of the unit, build quality is very good with strong plastics that look like it will hold up over time.  Buttons on the unit work well, and it requires 3 AAA batteries (not included) to power.  I really don't have any complaints with the functionality of the unit, other that if you make a mistake adding team scores you need to clear the scores and start over (holding both team score buttons) instead of just having plus/minus point buttons.

Overall, a fun game to play with friends and family.
profile.summary: Fun for friends and family, you will like this if you enjoyed The $20,000 Pyramid game show.

profile.description: Take a ride on the deluxe big flyer, the performance trike. This award-winning trike is designed to be your child's favorite new ride! the deluxe big flyer is a chopper-style tricycle with sleek racing design. It features a large 16 front wheel with performance grip tread to hug the road and allow your child to take off without slipping or spinning out. The seat is adjustable to grow with your child, and it comes complete with chrome handlebars.
profile.reviewText:
The Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is a well-made big wheel that will give your child freedom to ride.

Item comes in package mostly assembled, with a few steps that have to be taken (such as bolting on the big wheel) that will take 15-25 minutes max.

The bike is made of what feels to be a mostly durable plastic, with lag bolts holding the wheels in place.  Handlebars are metal with rubber grips and overall feels good in the hand.

On the downsides, the manufacturer advertises the special "grip thread" of the big wheel which appears to be pink rubber in the picture.  However, this pink "grip thread" is simply a textured layer of plastic on top of the existing plastic wheel.  the back wheels are also plastic, of the hard and thin variety.  While the whole bike seems durable, the back wheels could be a potential breakage point down the road (if a pot hole is hit!) as the plastic does seem quite thin.

Seat is comfortable and adjusts securely to three settings, with a 5-6" variation in seat height amongst the settings.

Overall a solid product, and appears to be a premium make for the big wheel variety.  Recommended.
profile.summary: Give your child freedom to ride!

profile.description: Looney Labs has created a sweet card game all about serving some very picky guests. No soup, no salad, no entree... it's just desserts! Compete with your fellow waiters to serve guests their favorite goodies before someone else gets to them first. With a kitchen full of mouth-watering offerings, and the cafe filling up with customers, you'll have your hands full making sure everyone gets their just desserts.
profile.reviewText:
Just Desserts is a new Looney Labs game that plays like a hybrid of some of their previous games.  It includes some of the matching aspects as seen in previous games as well as the quality artwork, cards, and box that we have come to expect from Looney Labs products.

Two versions of the game are included, Basic and Advanced.  The Basic rules are a bit too basic for adults, but may be good for younger children similar to Family Fluxx.  The Advanced Rules are good for adults and older kids.

In short, you are a waiter serving desserts.  Goal of the game is to collect 5 guests of different colors or 3 of the same color.  You have an opportunity to either claim unserved guests with your desserts or steal guests from your opponent.  The game offers slightly more strategy than Fluxx as there are many options per play turn and while some is left to chance, it is not as extreme as in Fluxx.

If you liked other Looney Labs games, you will like this one.  If you haven't played Looney Labs card games but are looking for a quick, fun game, this is a good place to start. Recommended.
profile.summary: A fun diversion customizable for all ages.

profile.description: The compact and lightweight EOS 6D full-frame digital SLR camera features a 20.2 Megapixel Full-Frame CMOS sensor, a wide ISO range of 100–25600, expandable to L: 50, H1: 51200, and H2: 102400, for incredible image quality even in low light, and a DIGIC 5+ Image Processor.  The camera also has a new 11-point AF including a high-precision center cross-type AF point with EV -3 sensitivity, continuous shooting up to 4.5 fps, and Full HD video with manual exposure control, multiple frame rates, and the benefits of a Full-Frame sensor provides stunning performance and creative flexibility. The built-in Wi-Fi transmitter allows you to wirelessly transfer your images to social networking sites through CANON iMAGE GATEWAY, or upload virtually anywhere from your iOS or Android smartphone with the free download of the EOS Remote app.
profile.reviewText:
I cannot describe how wonderful the picture quality is for this camera.  Photos come out spectacular even with extreme low light circumstances, and the center point works great for focusing in low light; using a 70-200 f/2.8 paired with this camera I am able to take pictures in near total darkness and still get ability to autofocus w/ output images nearly free of noise.  It has a large enough buffer to take bursts of RAW+JPG without slowing down like cheaper cameras, and build quality is fantastic.  This camera feels great in the hand!

In terms of weaknesses, the autofocus system on this camera is dated with 11 autofocus points only 1 of which is cross-type.  This means it has far less cross-type sensors than a Canon Rebel T5i which costs less than half the price.  That being said, the autofocus does work fine for weddings, regular people shots, and landscapes.  In a scenario with sports or one that requires constant tracking, you will likely be disappointed, though.  So if you want a sports camera, this is not it!  For other general events it is great.

Another weakness is the lack of joystick or touchscreen.  This is an issue as previewing pictures is a bit of a chore using the directional arrows to zoom around images.  If the camera had a touchscreen or joystick, moving the zoomed area around would be much easier.  The lack of joystick also makes changing the autofocus point more of a hassle, though you probably want to be using center point only most of the time.

Finally, contributing to the loss of a star was the EOS Remote Utility. The PC version was a bit of a hassle to install (you need to turn off your firewall to link it up) and there is no app for Lumia Windows Phone & Surface 2 which is disappointing.

In summary, the output of this camera is incredible as is the build quality.  But a dated autofocus system and clunky interface means it is no replacement for the 5DIII.  Still, for the money it is an excellent deal, so I would give it 4/5 stars!
profile.summary: Stunning build & image quality, but has dated autofocus system, lacks joystick/touchscreen, Wifi incompatible w/ Lumia & Surface

profile.description:
Led Zeppelin - The Song Remains the Same [VHS] 

(View amazon detail page)

ASIN:  6300270424 
Binding:  VHS
profile.reviewText:
UPDATE: This flaw was corrected in a silent replacement of the title.  It took over a year for Warner to fix it, but they did fix it.  I have changed my rating of the disc as a result.  I realize some were not happy I was critical of this because the gap is only 7 seconds, but a 7 second dropout during a drum solo is pretty bad IMO.  Some also may not have experienced the glitch due to getting a fixed copy (again, a year after release) or were not streaming TrueHD.

Anyway, good that the glitch is fixed, however it would have been better if Warner had an official replacement program instead of just silently fixing the problem in an unlabelled 2nd pressing.

BELOW IS ORIGINAL REVIEW TEXT:

Unfortunately the Blu-ray version of this concert has a 7-second long sound dropout in the TrueHD soundtrack at timecode 1:40:45 - all copies of the Blu-ray currently available are affected.  The TrueHD soundtrack of the previously released HD DVD does not suffer from this dropout (nor does the Blu-ray's lower quality DD soundtrack), so it is clear this was an encoding goof-up on Warner's part.

This type of QC problem is unacceptable for a product that costs $20, yet Warner has not mentioned any intention of fixing the issue.  Hopefully they get on the ball and set up a replacement program for those who buy this defective disc.

Note that the recent re-release of this disc still suffers from the dropout problem.  Maybe the third time will be the charm... :\
profile.summary: Great Blu-ray concert, originally had a significant glitch but fixed now!

profile.description: CAD StagePass WX1610 Wireless Bodypack System with Lavalier, Earworn Mic and Guitar Cable
profile.reviewText:
The CAD Audio 1610 Wireless Microphone System is perfect for presentations and other scenarios requiring a wireless mic.  Audio is crystal clear and even at 50+ ft the audio remained crystal clear and free of dropouts or static.

The package contains the following:
*Wireless receiver (wireless input, 1 unbalanced 1/4" output, 1 balanced XLR output, front panel channel buttons, volume and squelch controls on rear panel)
*Rack mount ears for wireless receiver
*Wireless transmitter with belt clip (1 mini XLR input, requires 2 AA batteries not included)
*Clip on mic (1 mini XLR output)
*Over the Ear mic (1 mini XLR output)
*Guitar cable (1/4" to mini XLR)
*Unbalanced cable (1/4" to 1/4")
*A/C Power supply for receiver

As one can see from the package list, this is a very complete kit.  The only thing missing is an XLR > XLR cable and that is understandable given the cost of said cables, plus you probably have one around anyway.

Also of note, the receiver is compatible with the CAD Audio TX1200 wireless mic ($89.00 at Amazon currently).  Using this mic will expand the capabilities of the system to perhaps better work for performing artists.

The only downside I can see to this package is that the volume knob for the receiver is rather small and difficult to access, but this is not an issue if the output is going into a mixing board as would likely be the case.

Overall, highly rated if you need a wireless audio presentation system - everything is in the box with this highly versatile unit!
profile.summary: Crystal clear audio with long range.

profile.description: Curved, wide belt provides additional lumbar support to carry heavier gear
profile.reviewText:
Combined with the shoulder straps, this belt is great as it offers very sturdy support for expensive camera gear.  I have personally not seen a more rugged belt than this one in all of my research.

Some complain that unlike the regular speed belt you cannot shift gear 360 degrees due to the back ring, and that is true.  However, this was not an issue for me, 180 degree rotation on each side was just fine.  I appreciate the sturdiness of this belt and will give up the 360 degree rotation for this easily.

It is a bit of a pain to get adjusted at first, but once you set it up right it is extremely easy to use.  Highly recommended.
profile.summary: An event photographers dream belt!

profile.description: Ever wonder what it would be like if cars could fly? Now kids can live that thrill and see a Hot Wheels RC take to the skies with the Street Hawk. This vehicle offers a cool combo of on-ground remote-controlled performance, like proportional ground steering, plus the aerial performance of a plane. The Flying Car RC is durable and lightweight, too, allowing it to perform impressive aerial maneuvers and fly up to 200 feet in the air. It's 2-in-1 RC action right in your own two hands! Street Hawk has a specially-designed Duraform body comprised of expanded polypropylene (EPP), making it lightweight and extremely relilient for long-term durability. Ages 8 and older.
profile.reviewText:
This Hot Wheels Remote Control Flying Car has a unique and innovative design.  It is entirely powered by air, meaning that even when in car mode all of the power comes from two propellers mounted on the wings that blow the car forward - however, they are surprisingly powerful.

There are two modes, car mode and plane mode.  Both modes work fairly well and the main difference is that the car mode restricts the speed of the propellers, preventing the car from taking flight.  Plane mode they go full blast and allow the car to take off.

First, car mode; the car mode is relatively fun though sometimes a bit hard to control.  The car does not always go straight, and though it has alignment buttons on the remote it seems a bit inconsistent, likely due to the nature of the air power.  But, the biggest problem with this mode is that there is no reverse.  So, if you are playing with this in the street, every time you crash into a curb you have to go retrieve the car and straighten it out.  Still, it is quite a bit of fun.

Second, plane mode; the plane mode is where most of the fun resides, as it is relatively challenging to keep the plane aflight.  Often, you might find yourself playing with your son and seeing who can pull off the coolest looking air-ground stunts.  But, it takes a bit of "runway" to get the plane/car going, and its flight path is unpredictable due to the limited controls - meaning that you will likely have more fun in a park than in a cramped area such as a street.  The plane generally flies about 5-10 feet off the ground but usually only stays in the air for less than 10 seconds before either stalling or spinning out of control - but when it lands on the wheels and you can keep driving it does make for quite the fun effect.  Perhaps with more practice and a larger area it would be easier to keep in the air.

Now for the downsides.  Since it is air powered, it needs to be run on flat pavement on a day where there is not much wind - it comes to a dead stop in grass, with no reverse as mentioned earlier.  Next, the remote takes 6 AA batteries which are not included.  Third, it takes 40 minutes to charge - the 40 minute charging downtime might be a dealbreaker for some, but it seems to last for about 20 minutes of playtime.  Fourth, the whole way it charges is fairly complex - first you need to use a screwdriver to take off the backplate of the remote to put batteries in it, then you have to open a hidden compartment to get out the charging cable, and then that cable plugs into the bottom of the plane to charge.  A USB cable was also included so you do not have to drain your batteries to charge the plane. Finally, the plane itself while it does hold up well to crashes the build material is a fairly flimsy foam required in order to keep it light enough to fly - while it can crash repeatedly with no issue, if someone accidentally stepped on it this plane would likely be completely destroyed.

Overall, this is a very fun product and for the price it is quite good.  This is more a toy than a full fledged remote control car/plane, but it is also dramatically cheaper than the typical remote control car/plane.  Therefore, this product is recommended, but it will likely require adult supervision to prevent frustration with your child.

UPDATE: After some more testing, was able to master flying this guy around in the air.  Was able to fly it over my house, into the backyard, and kept it in the air for well over a minute.  Only thing to keep in mind is that it is VERY touchy and there were several times I thought it was a goner but was able to navigate it back without it getting lost.  It also got stuck in a tree, twice, and was able to survive getting knocked out with a pool brush twice.  It survived very large and fast drops to the earth.  However, after a younger one played with it a bit (just as a toy airplane), the rear spoiler was deformed.  Thus, while durable in use, it is in actuality quite fragile.  Still, 4 stars due to the fun!
profile.summary: Fun and innovative family product, with only a few hitches.

profile.description: PRODUCT DESCRIPTION YOUR FAVORITES. YOUR WAY. The K200 series brewer allows you to brew a 4-cup carafe with the same ease and convenience of brewing a single-serve cup  all at the touch of a button. Its so smart, and so simple! And nothing like a typical coffee maker. The Keurig 2.0 K200 brewer also features revolutionary Keurig 2.0 Brewing Technology,designed to read the lid of each K-Cup or K-Carafe pod to brew the perfect beverage every time. Theres even a separate setting for specialty beverages such as hot cocoa, chai, and mochas. Choose from more than 500 varieties of coffee, tea, specialty beverages, and even iced beverages  from over 75 brands you know and love. Just look for the Keurig logo on your favorite varieties of K-Cup and K-Carafe pods.
profile.reviewText:
Before going into the details of this brewer, let me ask you a question:
Do you own a iPhone or know anyone who owns an iPhone?  Is that person having a horrible experience due to Apple's closed ecosystem? Most likely not. Keurig, with Keurig 2.0, is attempting to similarly close the ecosystem on its coffeemakers much like Apple did on the iPhone.  Keurig wants control of and to get a cut of every K-Cup sold, just like Apple has control of and gets a cut of every App sold.

I will explain first below what this all means to me, but please read the rest of the review also to get the details on this awesome machine that I purchased direct from Keurig.

What this means is you can only use cups that are licensed by Keurig.  Meaning, imitation/unlicensed/bootleg K-Cups will not work with this machine.  I do not see the issue with this, though makers of these bootleg cups have started a lawsuit and are even taking out ads on YouTube to give Keurig 2.0 a black eye.  There are plenty of K-Cup brewers from other brands that will brew imitation/unlicensed K-Cups and they are much cheaper than this machine.  But the quality of those brewers and the quality of the imitation/unlicensed K-Cups may vary dramatically from Keurig's machines and licensed K Cups.  Heck, a non-Keurig licensed K-Cup could have toxins in it and there is nothing Keurig could do about it as they have no control over unlicensed K-Cups.  It also means you can't use your own coffee grounds - but why are you buying an expensive Keurig just to use your own grounds?? Doesn't it make more sense to buy a much cheaper traditional coffeemaker if that is what you want to do?  I call reviews implying these changes requiring licensed K-Cups in the Keurig are a nightmare scenario "unfair" as many "reviews" I have seen are just complaints about the new closed ecosystem rather than a review of the actual product beyond that complaint.  Further it appears many have not even contacted Keurig as they are replacing legit older K-Cups that do not work on this machine with newer ones that do work for free for the customer - all you need to do is call.

Bottom line, Keurig wants to close its ecosystem to only use cups licensed by Keurig just like Apple and not support "bootlegs."  If you do not like it, there are a wealth of other options than this machine.  But I still recommend this machine wholeheartedly as it is Keurig's best effort to date, and Keurig will help you get new cups that work if you have a stockpile of licensed older ones that do not.

I do understand some are passionate about the new closed ecosystem, and would like to hear and discuss with you your thoughts in the comments section of this review. Thanks!

Some more details about the machine beyond the ecosystem:

First, the compatibility with *licensed* Keurig pods is outstanding - it supports K-Cups (cheapest), Vue Cups (better flavor) and Carafe Cups (full pot of coffee).  K-Cups can be brewed from 4oz-10oz.  Vue & Carafe Cups can be brewed anywhere from 4oz up to the maximum carafe size depending on which number you select on the touchscreen prior to brewing (for instance 1=Carafe, 4=normal cup, 5=froth), though you really need a carafe cup if you want coffee that is not watered down at 22oz+ sizes.  Technically though if you use a Vue Cup you could brew a 32oz pot of coffee, though it would taste like water without a Carafe Cup - K-Cups on the other hand are restricted to 10oz max.  If you want more than 10oz, buy Vue Packs or Carafe Cups depending how much more you want to make; you can probably get away with 14oz on a Vue pack and still have a decent cup of coffee.

The touchscreen is nice and the best of any Keurig to date, much more advanced than the Vue touchscreen due to having more customization options and better view angles.  The device is slightly taller and slimmer than a Keurig Vue but much lighter.  Still, it brews the best cup of coffee I have tasted from a Keurig, and it is also the best looking machine.

The drip tray just pulls out and the carafe goes in, there is no button release.  This works well unless you plan to move the unit itself a lot, in which case you may find it falling out when you move the unit.  But if your coffeemaker stays stationary like most, this design is a lot easier to release the drip tray compared to previous Keurig coffee makers; this is a necessity as you need to remove the drip tray to use the carafe. which you will likely do frequently.

The carafe the unit comes with is plastic and does not keep coffee warm for more than 10 minutes.  For a bit over $20, you can buy a steel thermal one from Keurig that keeps coffee hot for 40+ minutes, a worthy investment.

The device has a customizable reservoir light which you can adjust to best accent your kitchen.  Time is displayed on the LCD screen and you can customize the color of that as well.  You can even set it up to brew you a cup or carafe of coffee at a set time, such as when you wake up in the morning.

I have experienced zero issues.  No breakages, no spills, no problems.  It just works, and tastes great.

Overall, this coffeemaker is the best Keurig has released.  It is a shame that is overshadowed by the fact that Keurig closed the ecosystem much like Apple did.  Machines like this cost a lot of money to research, develop, and market - and Keurig can sell it to you for a lower price if they know they will recoup some money on the pods.  But if you buy bootleg pods, Keurig gets no money from them and eventually this will likely result in having to pay a lot more for a quality Keurig machine or Keurig simply exiting the market.  Either option is not great, and frankly if you do not want to use Keurig K-Cups/Vue Packs/Carafes, I do not know why you are buying a Keurig in the first place.

***NOTE: Some K-Cups and Vue Packs made prior to June of this year will not work on this machine.  HOWEVER, if you call Keurig's help line they will give you a one-time use coupon to redeem for an equal number of free replacement packs of your choice on their webstore.  Meaning if you have 50 packs that don't work, they will give you a coupon for 50 free packs - at least that is what they did for me.
profile.summary: Keurig's best coffeemaker unfairly maligned due to Keurig's desire to keep a closed ecosystem.

profile.description: 2010 debut album from this band featuring former members of Evanescence joined by American Idol vocalist Carly Smithson. The formidable five-some is comprised of the original members of multi-platinum trailblazing band Evanescence, guitarists Ben Moody and John LeCompt along with drummer Rocky Gray, joined by breakout American Idol finalist Carly Smithson on vocals. Acclaimed bassist Marty O'Brien (Disturbed and Static-X, among others) rounds out We Are the Fallen's unique sound.
profile.reviewText:
Like many people, I thought Evanescence's first album "Fallen" was excellent.  However, I did not like their followup album and their 2010 single just seemed flat to me.  Well, "We Are The Fallen" recreates the sound of the Fallen album with virtually all of the original Evanescence band members - except with a new lead vocalist.  There was clearly some clever wordplay here with the band name as well as the first single off the album "Bury Me Alive" (vs first single Bring me to Life off Fallen).

That being said, this band brings back the sound I really liked from "Fallen" that seemed to have been lost subsequently.  Excellent driving guitar, dark and Moody riffs/vocals, plus they sounded great live too.  An excellent start overall.

Mini review of the individual tracks:
Bury Me Alive: A- / Catchy tune, great guitar work, good intro
Burn: B+ / A harder tune, overall like it quite a bit
Paradigm: B- / Decent
Don't Leave Me Behind: B / Nice tune w/good vocals, I like the faster stuff better though.
Sleep Well My Angel: C+ / Average+
Through Hell: A / Great lyrics, drumwork, hooks
I Will Stay: A- / Very good song
Without You: A / For those dissing the lead singer, listen to this track
St. John: A- / Awesome guitar solo, catchy
I Am Only One: C / Average. The mastering seems to have some weird distortion on this track.
Tear the World Down: B+ / Good song, epic conclusion

Excellent overall!

If you liked "Fallen"-era Evanescence, give this band a shot.  It is pretty much a reboot of their sound, and I am very happy to have that sound back!
profile.summary: If you liked the album "Fallen" by Evanescence but not the followups, look no further.

profile.description: Centon 64GB SDHC UHS-1. Using the latest in memory technologies and design, Centon brings quality, reliable storage products for you to enjoy and depend on.
profile.reviewText:
The title of the review pretty much says it all.  I did a number of tests with different file sizes and depending on the file size this Centon card averaged between 10-40% faster write speed than the 64GB 45 MB/s Sandisk Extreme SDXC UHS-I card that is currently on Amazon.com for $54.99.

I noticed a typo in the Amazon specs.  The card is listed as 80 MB/s read, 20 MB/s write.  This is incorrect, the product packaging claims 105 MB/s read and 50 MB/s write.  I was able to exceed 50 MB/s write with the Centon so I can verify this is the case.  My much more expensive Sandisk card could barely even hit 40 MB/s write.

The card worked great in my high speed Lexar pro SD card reader and worked similarly well in my Canon 6D camera with no formatting required, just worked perfectly out of the box even in long bursts.

Will this card withstand the test of time?  I can't tell you that for sure, as I only had the card for a limited time.  But so far, it is faster than the competition while being ridiculously cheaper and working both in my computer and camera great.  That sounds like its worth a shot to me, if you are on the fence.
profile.summary: Faster than my 45 MB/s Sandisk Extreme UHS-I SD card that cost 3x as much!

profile.description: USB 3.0 SuperSpeed Active Repeater Cable (AB M/M) 25-ft. 3-year limited warranty
profile.reviewText:
This cable does exactly as advertised - it is a 25ft USB 3.0 cable that maintains highest speeds with no disconnect/instability issues.

In fact, when you pair this cable with the "Kinect for Windows" adapter and an XBOX ONE Kinect 2.0 unit, you can get a total of a 34ft run from the Kinect 2.0 to the XBOX ONE - 9ft from the Kinect 2.0 into the Kinect for Windows adapter ($49.99 from Microsoft), then another 25ft from the Kinect for Windows adapter into the XBOX ONE.  This is one of the few ways one can extend the Kinect 2.0 if you need more than the 9ft it comes with.

Well done Tripp Lite for delivering a product that matches advertised speeds unlike many other long USB 3.0 cables being sold!
profile.summary: Maintains USB 3.0 speeds with sensitive devices including Kinect 2.0 / XBOX ONE w/ Kinect for Windows

profile.description: United Solutions introduces their first ever hands free Laundry Tote. This 1.5 bushel Laundry Tote is made from LDPE resin which is very flexible. The tote includes an adjustable Keyhole Lock and Go shoulder strap design that attaches to the tote in any number of places allowing over the shoulder hands free carrying for ease of use and comfort. The Keyhole Lock and Go strap makes it easy for anyone to carry 25 pounds or more of laundry hands free. No matter if you are tall or short; big or small; you can customize the strap length and placement to fit your build. Built-in molded handles in the sides of the tote also allow it to be carried the traditional way. The perfect Laundry Tote for your college bound student or anyone having to carry laundry down the stairs. With United Solutions patent pending design your hands are free to hold on to the stair rail, not your laundry basket. The hands free Laundry Tote even offers a write-on/label panel so everyone in the family can have their own customized Laundry Tote. And don't stop with your dirty laundry - use the hands free tote at the beach. Anytime or anywhere you need to carry multiple items is a good time to grab your United Solutions hands free tote. The hands free Laundry Tote measures 19.5 inch in length by 15 inch wide by 17.5 inch high. Made in the USA.
profile.reviewText:
The United Solutions LN0309 is a taller than usual laundry tote with a movable strap that can be placed nearly anywhere on the basket due to its novel keyhole design.  This will allow easier and less awkward carrying of laundry loads.

However, the basket's plastic seems exceedingly thin, moreso than I am comfortable with.  It is very thin and flexes with little effort; this combined with the tall sides and a lack of stabilizing lip on the top makes me wonder if this basket will hold up over time.  Perhaps the thin plastic is stronger than most plastics, but for now I am not confident this won't crack.  The thin plastic also digs into the hands when carrying via the handles instead of the strap.

In short, great idea and neat design with the strap - but a more sturdy basket would have been preferred.
profile.summary: Convenient strap, but thin plastic calls into question basket durability.

profile.description: Everything armoire with full-length mirror you know what it's like-fighting for the bathroom mirror and trying to get ready while he shaves. You need a space that's all your own. Keep your jewelry, cosmetics and more stashed neatly inside this attractive, locking armoire. He can keep that cluttered sink. You've got your personalized beauty space. What you get mirrored beauty armoire lock with 2 keys inside mirror-so you don't have to close door to examine your makeup 36 brass hooks for necklaces or bracelets-hooks are long enough to double or triple hang earring holders for 30plus pairs-2 over-the-door brackets and hardware for hanging on wall if that is your preference plastic shelf plus 2 deep-cup plastic shelf for brushes, cotton balls ext. 3 wood shelves for bottles 14 plastic supports.
profile.reviewText:
I really wanted to give this a 4 out of 5 star review, however unfortunately the item I received for review came misassembled.  Two screws that hold the right side of the mirror box to the back were not aligned properly and as a result pushed the side away from the back and cracked through to the inside of the unit.  While this does not impede functionality, it does not look nice with the cracks on the wood inside.

This flaw aside, assuming other units do not have the same defect I really do like the practical design and look of the unit. About the only downside of using a product like this is it makes the door heavier to open and the jewelry inside can rattle around. Overall a great unit, assuming you can get one which does not have the assembly defect mine did.

profile.description: Cyberlink.Com Corp. Pdr-Ec00-Rpm0-00 Powerdirector 12 Ultimate
profile.reviewText:
Cyberlink PowerDirector 12 Ultimate is the top of its class, currently competing against offerings such as Nero Video, Corel VideoStudio, and Adobe Premiere Elements.  Unlike those other offerings, Cyberlink here was able to offer both a wide featureset and a high level of polish.  Nero and Corel both have a good (though not as comprehensive) featureset, but are not quite as intuitive to use, while Adobe Premiere Elements seems a bit light in the feature department. profile.summary: Excellent video editing software for enthusiasts and semi-pro videographers.

profile.description: Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home integrates control of connected lights, locks, thermostats, sensors, home entertainment devices, and more-from either an intuitive touch screen remote or handy mobile app.
profile.reviewText:
***CUSTOMER NOTE: The below review was written with consideration of the PC/Mac setup application which is not included in the box and is currently in beta testing.  Chad Thompson (Sr Director of Marketing and Product Mgmt) informed me that he was willing to assist users seeking the PC/Mac app by giving them access to the beta version.  His email address (which he was okay with me posting) is cthompson@logitech.com - please send him an email if you wish to have access to the beta version of the PC/Mac application.

The Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home is the latest and most powerful universal remote released by Logitech's Harmony team.  With this remote, Harmony aspired to create not only a device that can control your electronics, but also home automation "smart" devices.  In some ways, Logitech was largely successful in achieving these goals; in other ways, Logitech still has a ways to go.

In my opinion, the Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home is ergonomically the best remote Logitech has released to date.  Some have commented that moving the transport play/pause/etc buttons to the top of the remote has made them more difficult to access, but I felt if holding the remote as intended it actually makes more sense this way.  While having the transport buttons at the bottom was best prior to the introduction of touch remotes, placing the buttons as close to the touchscreen as possible will yield easiest access.  Logitech has shaped the back of the Harmony Ultimate Home to make it easier for users to access all functions of the remote, and the balance is excellent.  Additionally, the remote's touchscreen allows for gestures (i.e. swipes) in addition to taps meaning that you can now control volume and other functions without having to take your thumb off the touchscreen if you wish.

The specifications are also impressive.  The Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home allows for control of up to 15 devices including smart devices (thermostats, lights, etc) in addition to the electronics it traditionally allows for control of.  The remote operates on RF frequency meaning it will allow you to operate electronics that may be behind you or off to the side in a cabinet while still pointing the remote forwards.  The hub emits IR signals to your devices and if the hub is unable to reach your devices two IR blasters are included to supplement the hub.

Thus, Logitech/Harmony largely succeeded in the features and specifications department.  However, the implementation of this device is where some may run into trouble.

Upon release, the Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home required iOS/Android in order to setup and use even the most basic of functions with the product, making it the first ever Logitech/Harmony product to exclude PC/Mac/Web setup.  In addition, WiFi access is also required for the hub to operate properly.  Since release, Logitech/Harmony has listened to user feedback and is working to make the remote more compatible to allow setup for users who do not own iOS/Android devices or simply wish to use PC/Mac.  Currently, a PC/Mac setup application is in beta which allows users to set up the Harmony in the traditional fashion.

However, even with the beta PC/Mac application currently the Home Automation features are not available unless you own an iOS/Android device.  The only Home Automation devices that will work are the Nest Thermostat and Philips Hue lights.  Logitech/Harmony has communicated to me that they are working on moving the user interfaces in the future for all of the Home Automation devices to the remote to allow one to control everything from the remote instead of requiring you to switch to your smartphone; note that this feature is not yet available even in beta though, so it will likely be a significant wait before those without iOS/Android are able to use the product to the full extent.

Yet, even after everything is moved to the remote sometime in the future, Logitech/Harmony to date has expressed no plans to develop for Windows Tablets or Windows Phones.  While some Windows tablets like the Surface Pro will be able to use the setup application, they will not be able to use the actual device interfaces like iOS/Android tablets.  Additionally, some Windows ARM tablets like the standard Surface will be completely incompatible with the Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home as the only available Windows setup program requires an x86 processor.  Windows on phones also will be completely incompatible with the Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home.  This is somewhat troubling as several other competing home automation products support all three major mobile ecosystems instead of just the two largest as Logitech/Harmony has decided upon. Note that at the bottom of this review I have included a list allows you to see what you can expect the remote to do based on the devices you own.

In summary, the Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home is a fantastic piece of hardware with software that is a work in progress.  Out of the box the device currently will not function at all without an iOS/Android device, however a PC/Mac beta application is available from Logitech/Harmony. Yet, even after said PC/Mac beta application is released, the user will still be unable to use all of the features of the remote without having an iOS/Android device.  In the future, Logitech/Harmony states this will change as they move functions to the remote, however this still fails to address support for the third major mobile ecosystem (Microsoft).

I rate this product as 4 out of 5 stars due to the great hardware and potential of the device.  Hopefully, the promised features and applications that are unavailable to PC/Mac users out of the box will be publically released sooner rather than later.  And, if Logitech wishes to get that 5th star, I would recommend they develop applications for Tablets and Phones that run Windows.  As long as you are aware with the product's requirements and limitations prior to purchasing and are okay with them - and you are technologically saavy - this device will make a fine addition to your gadget collection!

***DETAILED HARMONY ULTIMATE HOME FEATURES/REQUIREMENTS USING LATEST SOFTWARE SORTED BY USER DEVICE

Remote-only control with Windows x86/Mac PC setup
-CAN control up to 15 Standard Devices via remote
-CAN control Nest Thermostat and Phillips Hue Lights via remote
-CANNOT control other home automation devices currently, but a future patch will allow for this per Harmony.

iOS Smartphone/Tablet (i.e. iPhone/iPad)
-CAN setup and control up to 15 Standard Devices
-CAN setup and control Nest Thermostat and Phillips Hue Lights via remote
-CAN setup and control other home automation devices

Android Smartphone/Tablet (i.e. Samsung Galaxy)
-CAN setup and control up to 15 Standard Devices
-CAN setup and control Nest Thermostat and Phillips Hue Lights
-CAN setup and control other home automation devices

Windows on x86 Tablet (i.e. Surface Pro) [keyboard and mouse required]
-CAN setup up to 15 Standard Devices, but CANNOT control them
-CAN setup Nest Thermostat and Phillips Hue Lights, but CANNOT control them
-CANNOT setup other home automation devices currently, but a future patch will allow for this per Harmony.

Windows on ARM Tablet (i.e. Surface)
-Incompatible with product in all aspects due to Logitech/Harmony not developing an app for this class of device.

Windows on Phone (i.e. Lumia)
-Incompatible with product in all aspects due to Logitech/Harmony not developing an app for this class of device.
profile.summary: Fantastic hardware and potential, but not quite yet ready for prime-time.

profile.description: Datacolor SpyderCube---Compact and easy to use reference tool Cube Components: + Chrome Ball + White Faces + Spectrally neutral 18% Grey Faces + Black Trap + Black Face Essential RAW format panion
profile.reviewText:
Those starting out with photography often make the mistake of investing a large sum of money in "high quality" lenses and camera bodies, but fail to invest even modest amounts of money into the accessories that will allow them to get their most out of their equipment.

The Datacolor Spydercube SC200 is an accessory that is definitely worth having if you wish to take your photography to the next level, as it is the ultimate white balance/grey card tool.  It is unique as not many manufacturers are making what is essentially a 3D white balance tool.  Simply, all you need to do is take a picture with this device in the scene prior to taking the photo you intend to take, and then use software in post to correct white/color balance following this.

Using the Datacolor SC200 one can obtain an incredibly accurate whitebalance as the 3D nature of the cube gives your photo processing software more information than a flat grey card would - as it will essentially allow you to consider angle of light source. In addition, it will help prevent crushing blacks and blowing out whites given the multiple shades of color on the cube.

The SpyderCube SC200 includes a tripod mount and also a loop to hang the device, giving you a number of options in placing the SC200.  The only other product I know of like this does not offer such flexible mounting options.

The only downside to this product is that it may not be practical for all photo applications.  Every time you change the position of the camera or light source, you would need to take another photo with this in the scene.  So if you are frequently changing the location of the camera/scene, using this may be impractical.  However, for studio shoots or times when you will leave the camera in one spot for most of the shoot, this is an invaluable device to have in your arsenal.
profile.summary: Innovative 3D White Balance tool worth investing in for studio shoots!

profile.description: Cook quick and tasty meals for the whole family with the George Foreman GR260P Grill. The 4-serving area of the grill is ideal for burgers and chicken for the whole family, or for a smaller meal complete with grilled vegetables. The improved George Tough non-stick coating is 3 times more durable than previous models and removes the need for excess oil and butter. profile.reviewText:
The George Foreman GR260P Classic is a great sandwich machine that brings back the classic feel and size similar to the very first George Foreman grill.

This grill includes a drip tray but does not include the spatula that generally comes with foreman grills to assist with cleaning.  I do not find this to be an issue as the spatula never cleans everything up anyway, and hitting the surface with a paper towel does a much better job.

One feature you might miss from more expensive Foreman grills is the lack of removable/washable trays in this device.  You cannot remove the tray and clean in the sink, instead you must clean the tray while it is inside the device.  On the plus side, this version has a lift built into the feet and does not require additional attachments to raise the rear legs like the original Foreman grill.

Overall, this works well if you are in the market for a Foreman grill.  Removable trays would have been a nice touch to assist with cleanup, but I do not feel losing them is a dealbreaker.  Recommended!

profile.description: Buffalos LinkStation 220 provides easy to use shared storage and backup for all PC and Mac computers, tablets and smartphones on your home network with the security of RAID data protection. Simply connect it to your wireless router for access anywhere in your home. While on the go, Buffalo's WebAccess service allows you to create a free personal cloud for easy remote access anytime, anywhere over the Internet, and even on your iPhone, iPad and Android devices. With LinkStation 220, you can back up multiple computers simultaneously and enjoy uninterrupted access to terabytes of storage anytime, anywhere.
profile.reviewText:
So, first the positives - the Buffalo LinkStation 210 3TB feels relatively sturdy upon first inspection, with the exception of the on/off button that seems a bit too small and flimsy - realistically though, you will probably leave this on all the time.  Noise levels are good, with only slight whooshing sounds once it is fully booted up (4 minutes).  I even like the styling, with the monolithic black slab, red stripe at the top, and white LEDs on the front.  Overall, Buffalo did quite well with this unit and I believe for the tech saavy these personal clouds will be the future as they are more secure since you are hosting them and have control over the data.  Unlike some other reviewers posted, I found the unit fairly easy to set up and get going though I am of expert skill level.

But, there is a pretty large downside for me, and I will update this review if that changes.  On the front of the box, it says "Mobile Support, Access Your Content from Your Tablet and Smartphone Devices" and "Quick Setup with Mobile Device... no computer needed!"  My Smartphone Device is a Nokia Lumia 928 (Windows Phone 8) and my tablet is a Surface Pro 3 (Windows 8.1 Pro).  Buffalo chose not to develop a SmartPhone Navigator touch app for either of these Operating Systems.  So, unfortunately, some of the biggest selling points of this unit simply are not available to a large amount of people.  The SmartPhone Navigator app is available on iOS and Android, but for a product like this where they have competitors with bigger pockets doing the same thing, Buffalo should have went the extra mile here and developed a Windows Phone 8/Windows 8 app.  Also, it would have been nicer if the USB port on the back was USB3.0 instead of USB2.0.

So, while it is a lot of space, sadly I am unable to use all of its features as Buffalo did not develop a Windows touch app.

That being said, if you primarily are looking for a personal cloud drive for an affordable price and you are just looking for typical web interface of a network attached storage drive this may just fit the bill - it does offer a lot of bang for the buck.
profile.summary: Lots of space, but without the app to navigate it!

profile.description: Rowenta intense aqua control humidifier offers the optimal humidity level at home to protect your health. It also comes with an ultimate ultrasonic humidifying technology which creates micro-fine cool water droplets thanks to ceramic disc vibrations. Really quiet up to 40 dB, intense aqua control is the only humidifier to feature a baby mode with 50% humidity and running during 7 hours. Long-Lasting and efficient mist output thanks to its 2 gallon output per day and a 24h runtime. Intense the warm mist function(95 degree f) also guarantees a bacteria-free steam.
profile.reviewText:
The Rowenta HU5120 Intense Aqua Control Ultrasonic Warm Mist 360 Humidifier is an extremely well built unit that is much more portable than the units of yesteryear.  Gone is the large, ugly rectangular box and in its place is this attractive unit.

First off, for best operation ensure you have a table or dresser to place this unit on.  As the display and controls are on the bottom of the unit, it is difficult to use regularly if placed on the floor.

Second, though the unit comes with a filter to reduce scale buildup with tap water (must be replaced every month), I would recommend using distilled water instead of tap water.  While it may be much easier to use tap water than buying distilled water, even with the filter tap water will not be as mineral-free as distilled water.  In addition, the nature of distilled water makes it less likely that harmful bacteria will grow in the tank.

The Rowenta is relatively easy to use with a bright display and responsive controls.  One can choose either warm or cool mist and can set the desired humidity for the unit to reach.  A continuous output mode is also available but not recommended as it may result in an overly humid environment if unmonitored - which can lead to mold growth; note that the unit will auto-shutoff at 90% humidity even in continuous mode.  The unit is very quiet compared to other humidifiers, but not silent.

It is recommended by the manufacturer to clean the entire tank every 2 days, but I feel if you use exclusively distilled water you will likely be able to stretch this out quite a bit and significantly reduce your cleaning.  So, for those who do not enjoy water tank maintenance (who does) you can likely save yourself some hassle by using distilled water.  You will still have to clean the tank, but much less so as the scale buildup will be a non-issue with this type of water.

Overall, recommended as this unit is a few notches above other humidifiers in both build quality and features.
profile.summary: High quality humidifier with a wealth of features to control humidity output.

profile.reviewText:
This Tenba bag is one of the most rugged bags I have ever seen designed for the office-on-the-go.  There are tons of pockets to fit everything from tablets to phones to memory cards to business cards to laptops, and more!  Compartment after compartment folds out, all water resistant, where you can store your mobile office.  There is one very large compartment that could hold a sizeable and thick piece of gear, while the other compartments are much shallower in depth.

Now, while this is extremely useful for an event photographer who will likely need all of those things to pull off a wedding, if you are just looking for a camera bag this is the wrong item.  Amazon calls it the "Executive Bag for Camera," however there is really no part of this bag that would be good for anything more than a compact fixed lens camera - there are no lens dividers or anything like that.

Just don't expect it to be a substitute for a DSLR bag, because that is not what it was designed for.
profile.summary: Rugged all purpose executive bag, but Amazon title misleading.

profile.description: p  Belkins full line of upgrade card allows you to add 5 USB 2.0 ports to your computer through the new PCI Express slot. The card is designed to take advantage of the additional bandwidth and features provided by the new PCI Express I/O interconnection standards. Belkin PCI Express Card not only allow you to simultaneously edit high-resolution graphics to share with family and friends, convert music to digital formats, and watch streaming video, they will also support bandwidth-intensive applications of the future.  /p
profile.reviewText:
This is a good, fast, well-made and reliable card.  But, you are not getting everything that is advertised when you buy one - hence the 3 stars.

Belkin says:
"The Belkin USB 2.0 5-Port PCI Express Card offers the perfect solution for users who want to add Hi-Speed USB 2.0 ports to their computers. The Card is designed to take advantage of the additional bandwidth and features provided by the new PCI Express I/O interconnection standard."

Unfortunately, this statement is false.  Shortly after receiving the card I noticed a little Texas Instruments chip near the PCI-E connector, part#XIO2000A.  So being suspicious, I looked it up.  Turns out it is a PCI-E > PCI bridge chip! So, what you are getting here is in essence the same $30 Belkin standard PCI card that is offered elsewhere, with a bridge interface slapped on it so it works in a PCI-E slot.

Therefore, this card was *NOT* designed to take advantage of PCI-Express. It was designed as a PCI card and a bridge chip was plopped on it to make it work in a PCI-E slot - it is not native PCI-E.  While it is possible the speed increase from a native PCI-E card may have been minimal anyway, the product description offered by Belkin implies that this card is native PCI-E - and the PCI-E > PCI bridge chip is a dead giveaway that this is wholly false.

So, decent piece of hardware, but very overpriced for nothing more than a bridged standard PCI card.  Disappointing.
profile.summary: Good card, false advertising

profile.description: The Frigidaire FAD954DWD 95-pint dehumidifier protects your home from mold and mildew caused by excess moisture. It also helps eliminate bacteria in the air that can make breathing difficult. Frigidaire's 95 pints-per-day dehumidifier is capable of continuous operation when the unit is located near a suitable drain. It features full-function electronic controls, an easily accessible collection container with level indicator and a washable filter that reduces bacteria, room odors and other airborne particles. Its effortless humidity control allows you to control the exact percentage of humidity in your room. The SpaceWise portable design includes integrated side handles and caster wheels making it easy to move your unit from room to room.
profile.reviewText:
Previously to this unit, I have owned both the Frigidaire 70-Pint and 50-pint dehumidifiers.  I have a finished basement, but half of it is underground, thus I get a ton of moisture.  While both Frigidaire units were excellent, the 50-pint was simply overwhelmed.  The 70-pint could get the job done somewhat, but it had to run 24/7 and it still was a bit humid.  I bought multiple Frigidaire units in the past because I was impressed with their reliability and noise profile.

Enter the 95-pint Frigidaire.  This thing blows away the moisture in the air, literally.  I have it hooked up via continuous drain and it is able to tackle my whole basement with ease; it does a much better job than even the 70-pint unit.  Although, it is also larger by about 5" in width and 3" in depth to the 70-pint unit plus it weighs what feels like twice as much; you are best off using 2 people to move this.

However, once in place, moisture problems will be no more. Mold be gone! At the highest setting, it can be a bit loud, but at medium it is more than quiet enough for the typical living space.  At low, it is very quiet but of course less effective as well.

The unit comes with a number of presets and a timer, but it also has manual override for you to tweak settings to your desire.  Once you get to know the machine, you will likely go for the manual override - but the presets are nice for quick adjustments.

Overall, I couldn't be happier with this machine.  It is built like a tank and gets the job done.  Best of all, you can customize its noise and moisture-removing capabilities to your living space.

Highly recommended!!
profile.summary: Lean, mean, moisture-sucking machine!

profile.reviewText:
This battery works great and lasts for a long time, in fact seemingly longer than the stock battery.

However, when you get it, do not just put it in and plug in your laptop as you might be inclined.

Instead, you need to put it in and run your laptop *on battery* down to 7%, then turn off your laptop and do a full recharge with it closed for 12 hours.
