profile.description: How often do you hit the slopes and suddenly it starts to snow? What do you do then? Ride blind down the treacherous mountain, endangering women, children, and trees of all ages? Heck no! Save a tree and a few innocent civilians with a pair of high-quality polycarbonate snow goggles perfect for any extreme sports enthusiast. These goggles are durable and lightweight, with an adjustable strap suitible for even the most bizarre shaped domes. The come in multiple lense color choices to match the rest of your gear, making them a hot commodity for any season. Most importantly, they protect your eyes from any and all danger, so you can spend more time enjoying the fresh powder.
profile.reviewText: I got two pairs of goggles to try out, ("WOLFBIKE" are the others) seeing as how the ones with the individual lenses for each eye were fogging up on me VERY badly, (Global Vision) and I was hoping these would be different. Well, they were, and they weren't. Let me explain. I ride a bicycle commuter/recreationally, and found that these fog up just like the others, only, they clear up faster than the others do, and don't seem to fog up quite as badly. Of course, a nice wind helps this action (of clearing up the fog) along quite nicely! Also, the "Global Vision" ones would stop the fogging up when they got a nice coat of condensation on the inside. Both fogging and condensation are annoying things to happen to your lenses, but to help give you an idea, imagine it this way. Fog on your goggles is like finding your windshield coated with very light frost in the morning. You can SOMEWHAT see through it, but everything you see is an indistinct shape. Condensation on the other hand, is like clear grease, you want it gone, but when you wipe it to get it off, it just smears and makes it harder to see! Both are bad, and make it hard, if not impossible to see, but IF these goggles get a little fog on them, it's just that these are both better and quicker at ridding one of this, and WILL NOT give you the 'condensation' problem!
profile.summary: Great goggles for the price!

profile.description: Professional 9-inch high carbon stainless steel scissors tired of fighting your scissors? Dull blades? Cramping hands? Struggling to make your cut? You have found your solution. At evergreen supply we pride ourselves on providing only the highest quality product and giving you what you need: Premium industrial grade materials - high carbon steel is harder and stronger than the competitions standard stainless razor edge retention - blade stays sharp, even after running through the toughest materials extreme ergonomically designed comfort grip - no harsher metal grips. Rubberized handle hugs your hand comfortably for the quick precise cuts you need, without the pain cut-flat, slanted handle - the angled handle allows you to remain flat on the surface for easy, accurate cutting all purpose- from the office to the workshop, for artists to students. From cutting paper, to fabrics, to leather, this is your tool superior quality & technology - built with supreme craftsmanship. Evergreen supply's professional high carbon stainless steel scissors will be the last pair of scissors you will need.
profile.reviewText: These scissors are amazing! The box they come in can be a little annoying to open, seeing as how it's very tight when it arrives, but once you DO get it open, you find the highest quality scissors I have ever seen, along with the blades being in a clear plastic sheath, and the blades themselves, have a protective coat of 'Cosmoline' (oil) on them. They show their quality in the fact that they have a VERY nice 'heft' (weight) to them, and the fact that they remain close together as you use them, shows another side of their quality. It seems they are two different pieces of metal (each honed to razor sharpness) then riveted together, and the handles are dipped in a rubber coating. Just for kicks, I got a piece of paper, to see if they would slice it by just running the blades through it, and it (not surprisingly) did it! Just make sure to watch your hands around these things, because while they do a great job of cutting JUST about anything you can think of (I wouldn't be too shocked if they cut sheet metal!) they could do the same thing to you if you're not careful!
profile.summary: THE best scissors I have EVER used!

profile.description: The easy-to-use Tactacam does not interfere with your hunt. Simply attach the Tactacam to your Bow, Crossbow, Gun or Scope. Push the power on auto record button to start recording. Push the button again when you want to stop recording. It's that simple.. The new Tactacam is designed for you using the best electronics available. Easy to use; 1 touch operation with vibration indication allows you to hunt and then share your hunt. This small hunting video camera was built with an ultra high quality lens and 12 megapixel lowlight sensor. Instead of using a fisheye lens, which pushes the images away, Tactacam uses a unique lens design, providing a view similar to what we see with the human eye. 20yd shots no longer look like a 100yd shot. Now your 20yd shot will look like 20yds and your 100yd shot will look like 100yds in your video. All this is what makes the NEW Tactacam the best hunting camera on the market. Includes Battery, Universal Mount, Camera Universal Mount, USB Cable with Charging Wall Adapter, Audio End Cap, Waterproof End Cap, Tripod/Adhesive Plate, Two 3M Adhesive Pads and Replacement Waterproofing O-Rings.
profile.reviewText: I REALLY like this camera, and though I am just a 'newbie' (sorry, couldn't think of another word, but think this one best describes me) to not only using a bow, but hunting with one as well. This camera was one of my first major purchases, (well, besides the bow itself) and I was rather impressed with it. I've only been testing it in warm temperatures so far, but will probably need to get another, more advanced one (3.0-4.0?) for better low-light clarity. I realized this is their least expensive camera, and therefore, just the 'base' version, if you will. It's great for what I'm using it for now, but I think I'll need a more robust camera for October, since it'll be a bit cooler. My only real complaint about this camera, is that the sound is at about 5% out of 100%. (yes, it's that bad, but mounting it under a bow, I don't know if that's a good or bad thing) The video is GREAT, and you have the ability to add a timestamp (or not) as well as to leave the "Tactacam" watermark in its place, or remove it! Also, if you have problems getting the pre-installed videos to play, (as I did, think my computer's too old) just search "tactacam" on "Youtube", and you'll find all you need to know!
profile.summary: Great video, but the audio leaves a bit to be desired! Still a great camera though!

profile.description: The Metro flash Master 860 is masterful in its brightness level and performance. While its size remains convenient and easy to tote it delivers maximum brilliant LED light for indoor and outdoor use. Massive Output. With a maximum light output of 860 lumens and runtime of 7 hours the Master860 keeps you safe and noticed at all times. Easy Install. Quick Detach. Master 860 is easy to mount on and remove from your bicycle handlebar and for added security you can keep it with you at all times in the included custom pouch. USB Rechargeable. It can be easily charged on-the-go with the USB port, ensuring that you are not stranded without battery. 5 Modes. Switch easily through the 5 featured lighting modes with a single button, choosing the brightness level that best suits your setting: Flash (90) Low (180) Medium (400) High (860) Strobing (860). Sturdy Designs. The Master860 is crafted with Aero Grade Aluminum Alloy housing and double coated toughened glass to ensure high endurance. Waterproof IPX6.The light can be seen from up to 200 meters away and its Waterproof for extreme conditions. Whether it's a bike ride in the nighttime, a hike in the woods, an unexpected power outage or simply a walk after dark, the Master860 will help keep you safe and your world bright.
profile.reviewText: First, the basics: this flashlight comes with a USB charging cord (so you can charge the battery in the flashlight; which is nice, since I don't want to have to remove the battery and put it in a charger every time I need to), a lanyard, a bag for carrying the flashlight, An instruction booklet, and a battery. Now, for my personal thoughts: I can't BELIEVE this light! It is SO useful in SO many regards! I had a flashlight that I would often use, so I carried it around on my belt. This light is smaller (My previous light was just a little over 6"(152.4mm) whereas this one is an inch shorter; 5"(127mm). Also, the head doesn't have as large of a diameter, and it's 5 TIMES (maybe more) as bright! Also, just an inch shorter may not sound like much, but the fact that I don't have to worry about bumping this light against NEARLY as many things as I had to concern myself with when I was using the other light, is a GREAT relief to me! Also, when I DO bump it against anything (as is certain to happen) it's a LOT tougher than my other light! Another thing, I like the fact that I can carry it around on me for when I may need it, then just pull it out of the holder I use everyday, (I don't use the holder that came with it, but I may, as of yet) and place it into the holder on my bicycle when I go for a ride, AND the fact that it beats the tar out of my other light as far as brightness goes; and I can use it on the trail, street, or whatever I'm riding on that night, makes it THAT much more useful! The other thing I like about it so much, is  the strobe mode (hold the button down from any 'on' mode for 3 seconds) since it resembles a dance-club strobe light, but then has a quick 3 flash succession, then dance-club strobe again, and keeps up this cycle until you turn it off. At any rate, it's a VERY noticeable strobe effect, and WILL get you seen if you're riding a bike, I tried it the other night on MY bicycle, and had drivers yelling (and many other things I won't mention here) so I KNEW they saw me, and you WANT to be seen on the road! It seems you have to be EXTREMELY obnoxious to get a driver's attention these days, but (As I've heard said) "If that's what it takes, that's what I'll do"! Another thing that I'm not used to, (but like all the same) is the fact that you can carry a fresh battery with you, and if your ride goes longer than you expect, (which I've had happen a few times) you can just change the battery, and the light is bright enough to be used alone as well! Nice! The last thing I wish to address is the placement of the switch. It's not as simple as most other flashlights where it's located on the tailcap; and when you're in pulling it out in the dark, it's a little tougher to find the 'on' button, but once you do, you're rewarded with a FLOOD of light! Speaking of which, the light beam seems to be the perfect mix of flood, AND spot! I SO badly wish I could give this flashlight MORE than 5 stars!
profile.summary: The perfect brightness for a dual-use flashlight!

profile.description: Dimension: 7.5"L x 3"W x 6.5"H (one side) Available colors: Black, Red, Blue Suit for: mountain bike, road bike. It's large to hold various items, but it's not so large that it's cumbersome or hits your knees when riding. -The velcro straps have good length on them making them able to fit most bikes. -The velcro straps relies on the upper and lower tube on the bike frame that is "V" shaped to stay secured. The strap that would be closest to the seat cannot slide down because of this. Package Include: Bicycle Frame Pannier x 1 Rainproof Cover x 1 Adjustable Shoulder Strap x 1
profile.reviewText:
I didn't use this for a mountain bike, but used it for a road bike instead. However, I don't think that matters. What matters more, is the fact that it worked well for what I used it for, and seeing as how I used it as storage for my battery pack from my headlight, It worked VERY well! You can use it for anything your heart desires, but that's what I did. Anyway, it comes with (and this caught me off guard) a shoulder strap for carrying it when not on your bike, along with a rain cover. (I guess I didn't read the description of the frame bag on the main page [which I SHOULD have!]) I think it's rather neat how they put two separate storage bags on the left, and one large bag on the right. I carry many things on my bike, so have a triangle frame bag attached to my frame, but also have this bag attached to the top front bar on my frame. Still, this bag is VERY helpful, since I use it to store my phone, (I like that) the battery for my headlight (and I may put on another one, since there's 2 pockets...)  a small tool kit, and an extra tube. (that's what I use it for, you may use it for more, as it's large enough for it) In closing, I'd like to add that this bag has two Velcro closures you can attach together once you've placed it over your bars, and one that attaches horizontally (horizon) to strap to the front of your frame, to prevent the bag from sliding backwards while you ride.

*I received this product at a discount for a fair and unbiased review*
profile.summary: A better bag than I predicted!

profile.description: 5-in-1 multi-tool for any adventure be safe and prepared with this must-have multifunction knife and tool for all of your outdoor activities. We stand by our quality gear, so of course you are always covered by the legendary Xentyx lifetime warranty. Buy with confidence today and always be prepared .
profile.reviewText: I can't BELIEVE how useful this thing is! Shortly after taking it out of the packaging, it came into its own. I needed a flathead screwdriver for a bolt I was taking out of my bicycle, and this tool helped; then about 4 hours later, I needed to tighten a screw while hanging a clock, and this tool is so handy, I just hung it from my belt loop on my pants when I used it earlier on my bike, and now I didn't want to have to get off the ladder, so I grabbed it just to see if it would fit, and my luck (which is usually bad, by the way) was good and it fit! I like the 'carabiner' hook, as when you close it, it can be used as a handle for the knife, giving you great leverage! Also, the 'swing arm' (sorry, can't think of the proper word for it) that opens the carabiner hook, has a threaded cylinder slightly larger than the 'swing arm', and can be used to slide down the 'arm', and screw onto the other straight piece, creating a solid area, where you don't have to worry about the 'swing arm' opening while you're using the knife blade. One last thing...be careful opening the blade, since it's razor sharp (and very useful) from the factory! *I received this product at a discount for a fair, and unbiased review*
profile.summary: A multi-tool with a bite!

profile.description: This Product is 850 lumen output with Cree XM-L LED. New oval spread Enhanced Cycling Optic shines and extra wide beam and distant throw. Water resistant design for all riding conditions. 8 modes (4 steady 2 flashing 1 walking and 1 SOS). 1:15 ~ 22 hour run time. Includes handlebar and helmet mount. Replaceable Li-ion battery stick 140g.Made in United States.
profile.reviewText: Make sure you tighten this down onto your bars as tight as you can make it, since the light's rear section is plastic, but the front 1/3 of the light is aluminum, and will cause the light to start edging forward as you hit bumps you don't even feel! As for everything else, the light itself is very tough, since on one occasion; I attempted to take it off it's mount to recharge it, over-compensated with how much force I applied, and it went skidding across my concrete floor! Immediately afterwards I picked it up to see if it still worked, and besides a bit of concrete dust where it hit (and a nice divot out of the floor) It was fine! I had this mounted to my helmet before this incident, and with it's 8 modes, walk, low, medium, high, boost, day flash (which I haven't used yet), S.O.S., and SteadyPulse (which means the light stays on solidly/constantly, while it flashes as well). It seemed the perfect idea, minus one thing: it's heavier than the "Niterider Lumina 650 Flare" I have, (or maybe the weight is concentrated into a smaller area) and (in my opinion) better to be used on your handlebars, which is where I now have it. Also, unlike the "Expilion 800", the lens on this light is 'fluted', or has vertical (up & down) lines in the lens, to widen the beam; or 'dissipate' it. This gives it a 'flood' type beam, whereas the "Expilion 800" has a 'spot' type beam, which is concentrated into a much narrower area, (hence the name). In any instance, no matter where you want to mount this, you're covered, since it comes with a helmet mount, handlebar mount, recharging cable, and wall adapter. One more thing; if you want extra light, it uses a cylindrical battery that you can merely change with another (that are available here on Amazon) and keep going! Hence, if your present battery gives out, you can take it out, replace it with another charged one and continue with your ride!  Overall, this light is great! I like it better on my handlebars, though. I plan on recommending this to all my cycling friends, (as well as a few on mopeds)!
profile.summary: A great and powerful light!

profile.description: Our Popular Wide Angle Lens is now available in red. Use it to turn you Magicshine MJ-808, MJ-808E, MJ-808U or similar Magicshine copy into a tail light that commands attention, even in the daytime. Simply unscrew the bezel holding the lens and replace the stock lens with our RED wide angle lens. Lens is 39mm in diameter x 1mm thick
profile.reviewText: This works great! I got a "Minoura CS-500 Headset Spacer Mount Accessory Holder" along with a "CREE XML XM-L T6 LED Bike Bicycle Light HeadLight HeadLamp 1200LM Red" and mounted the "Minoura" to my seat post, (I have a '97 Cannondale T-900) then replaced the lens that came with the Bicycle light with this red lens, and I now have myself a 1200 lumen taillight! Let me tell you, if you want drivers to stay off your behind while you're commuting in darkness, or just want them to know you're there, this lens added to a light like the one I added it to, will do a great job! One main thing is, make sure to aim it slightly away from the driver's line of sight, (so you don't blind them, because whether it's got this lens or not, it's still pretty bright, all this lens does is turn the light red and diffuse it a bit) I would also suggest putting the light on its lowest setting (but not strobe) As I said before, it does a nice job of keeping drivers off your behind while commuting at night! Give that set-up I mentioned earlier a try, you'll be seen from MUCH further away!
profile.summary: A simple but useful lens!

profile.description: The Zodiac Dragons 2016 Calendar! Designed and illustrated by artist SixthLeafClover (Christina Yen). Dream Semblance is the new theme of 2016! Each month features a full-page spread of a Zodiac Dragon representing a zodiac sign of the month. NEW Gold foil stamped logo on the front cover!  Zodiac Dragons are based on the Tropical Zodiacs in Western Astrology where the twelve divisions are the signs of each Zodiac. Each dragon, being the celestial body of the sign, is carefully designed and detailed to represent its key features with fascinating characteristics. Includes: USA and International Holidays included, Zodiac Date and Moon Phases, 12 month edition. Each calendar comes in full color on both sides and is printed on premium semi-gloss stock. Binding is saddle-stitch with 1 hole punch at the center of the bottom page for hanging. "Zodiac Dragons Calendar" is a registered trademark.
profile.reviewText: What else can be said, that I didn't already mention in my review of the "2015 Zodiac Dragons Fantasy Wall Calendar Limited Edition" except for the fact that the one posted there, was (admittedly) a copy/paste of my 2014 review. (Since I couldn't think of anything else to say. This one however, is not) These calendars have been amazing me since I first got the 2014 version, (just for a 'trial balloon' so to speak) and I have loved them ever since! The artwork is WONDERFUL, (the other one I got for 2013, was from an author named "Ciruelo", which was good, but didn't come CLOSE to being as good as this one in my opinion) and they have so much more information on them than what most calendars have. Most other calendars just have, well, what numbers occur on what days of the week, how many full weeks in a month, a few holidays, etc. This calendar on the other hand, of course has the signs of the zodiac, (beginning and ending of them), phases of the moon,(and when they occur) and ALL holidays, so no matter where you are in the world, you'll know PRECISELY what days your holiday falls on, (if you lose track of days easily, like I do sometimes) and I STILL can say that I'm learning things from this calendar! They also have a small picture of all the other zodiac dragons, along with their respective months on the back of the calendar, so you can have a peek at your month before it arrives! One other thing, just for information, this one is 1.5" (38.1 mm) wider, and 3" (76.2 mm) longer than the previous edition.
profile.summary: These calendars keep impressing me!

profile.description: Wherever your road leads we know cyclists seek the ultimate ride. With that in mind, Serfas is always striving to make products that reflect those wants and needs. Our 20-plus year commitment to quality, performance and customer service is reflected in our innovative products that are rider-tested and rider approved.
profile.reviewText: I am righteously SHOCKED at how bright this light is! This is one of the few companies that gives you a lumen rating, and ACTUALLY MEANS IT! I'm just so shocked, because I like to review bicycle lights, and have come across quite a few who advertise the lumen rating on their lights as far in excess of what they really are! Alright, maybe I'm wrong, but when I tested this light on bright, against a light boasting 960 lumens, (also on bright [basically as bright as both lights could go]) This "Serfas True 750" blew the other light away! The thing is, I LIKE the brand of light I put it up against, and was both surprised, and disappointed that the 960 lumen light lost! Oh, for reference, this was the light "Night Provision™ ULTRA BRIGHT BX-960 USB Rechargeable Bike Light Headlight & Flashlight LED 960 Lumen". This is the first "Serfas" light I've ever owned, and due to it performing unexpectedly well, I think I'll try a few more lights from "Serfas"! Now, I want to give you some technical details of the light. It ALWAYS starts off (when you first turn it on) in 'Turbo' mode, (since it [unfortunately] has no 'mode memory'). Then it goes high, medium, and low, in that order. If you press the button again, it goes back to 'Turbo'mode. To turn it off, you need to hold down the power button for 2 seconds. It fades out, but comes on like flipping a switch on your bedroom light. However, to get it into the flashing mode (which is like a car with a fast turn signal) you have to hold down the power button to turn off the light, then continue holding the power button down, and it will begin to blink. OR, if you just want to turn on the blink WITHOUT turning on the light, just press the power button and hold it down for 2 seconds. However, this light has something I've never seen before! If you just hold down the power button from completely off, it will flash, but if you turn the flash off, and do it again, it will come on with a solid light! I guess it alternates between the two modes! Weird. Well, I'm not used to it, anyway. As for the measurements, they are :4.5" (114.3 mm) Long x 2" (50.8 mm) Wide x 1.5" (38.1 mm) High/Deep. I intend to add a video when I get the chance to (because I want to share its performance with you) and hopefully, I will soon! (UPDATE 11-22-2016) I also wished to mention, that when I looked at the picture on the main website, The front of the light looked beige. Actually, the piece on the front of the light is more of a gold color, and the gold coloring is metal. The rest of the light (the black part) is plastic. Also, the mini-USB port(for charging) is on the bottom, (in the gold metal area) under a rubber flap. I'll add some photos to show this.
profile.summary: A surprisingly bright light that lives up to its claims!

profile.description: * For the cyclist looking for a true all-in-one solution to riding fast and riding safely when the sun goes down * 650 lumen output with 4 brightness settings plus flash mode * 1W tail light * 1:30 to 18:00 of run time * USB rechargeable * 177 grams
profile.reviewText: I got this for two reasons, 1) The "NiteRider Lumina" has always been a dependable light for me, and 2) The fact that this one has an integrated taillight amazes me! Mind you, the first one that arrived had some kind of malfunction that NiteRider was happy to replace for me, (there are 'inconsistencies' with EVERYthing made - no problem there) I had heard the taillight was independently operable from the main light (which is true) albeit, if you turn the taillight on without the main light, then later turn the main light on, when you turn the main light off (hold the button for 2 seconds) the taillight turns off as well. I was unaware of this, and since I have the light mounted to my helmet, did not know the taillight was off until I arrived home. I suppose the phrase "if all else fails, read the instructions" would have worked here, but I was too exited, and in too much of a rush to bother reading them. I have another taillight on my helmet that took up the space it left when I (unknowingly) turned it off. When I heard the rear light and main light worked independently of each other, I thought that meant TOTALLY independently of each other. Oops! My mistake! I have also learned that if you place two "NiteRider Luminas" close together, the 'Flare' is about 1/2" (12.7mm) longer than the normal "Lumina", which is about 4 1/2 inches (114.3mm) long. All else being equal, this light is very reliable and bright. It comes with instructions, a USB charger cord, a handlebar mount, and a helmet mount. Also, the charging cord for the light is a 'micro' USB. Another thing, like all the other "NiteRider Luminas" I've had, this one is a 'spot' type beam. All in all, I am very pleased with this light, and would not fail to buy another, were the need to arise!
profile.summary: The Lumina with a unique twist!

profile.description: Get 2 for price of one!! Be highly visible. Bright light surrounds you, your family and pets with protection. Protection from motorists and after dusk dangers. They're perfect for concerts and sporting events too. Your seen for your protection and security or to stand out in a crowd. The soft, water/perspiration resistant material hugs you with just a quick flick to cuff anywhere. Comes with a replaceable battery found in stores to use this for years to come. Newly designed and improved for 2016.
profile.reviewText: These are decent 'slap bands'; however, I thought the green color would be MUCH 'louder' (brighter) shall we say? It is VERY, VERY, VERY slightly reflective, (which can be a problem if you have the bad luck of having your batteries go dead on you while you're out late at night),and the material it's made of doesn't 'stick out' to a car's headlights like a 'high-vis' (fluorescent yellow) material would. Also, I do not believe it would be too water-resistant (slight drizzle maybe, NOT a heavy downpour) However, the good part is, the battery (CR2032 button cell) is very easy to get out, just don't put it back in very hard, or the clear plastic piece that the light travels along when it's on, will start to bunch up at the bottom, causing intermittent contact, and not allowing the light to remain on correctly. *I received this product at a discount for a fair and unbiased review*
profile.summary: Decent, but not the best out there...

profile.description: Packing 800-lumen brightness into its compact, durable housing, the rechargeable NiteRider Lumina 800 OLED Bike Light delivers steady, reliable light to keep you visible and to light your way while riding.Battery: Lithium ion.Battery life on high: 1.3 hours.Battery life flashing: 18 hours.Weight : 172 grams.
profile.reviewText: This light puts my "Lumina 500" to shame! Well, not ENTIRELY; still, it is far brighter... Anyway, I really like the O.L.E.D. display, showing the remaining time you have in EACH and every mode, I never realized how useful it would be to know that! The other aspect I really like, is the ability to shut off the display if you're trail riding and the light begins bothering you! I like the brightness it showed me while I was testing it in my basement, but I have since made a vow not to do a review simply on that basis, after a rather embarrassing review I did, so I decided to go for a ride with it. Mind you, it was about 35 degrees Fahrenheit (1.6 Celsius) and the battery was just as good as it would be in far warmer temperatures. I DO have to acknowledge the fact that the buttons on this unit are VERY difficult (but not impossible) to operate with thick gloves on. The video shows low, medium, and high, as well as "walk" mode, and 2 of the flashing modes, (not sure which ones) that I switched between after I took off my left glove. I found the newer 'strap mount' (NiteRider's [cheaper?] replacement of their MUCH more popular 'screw-clamp mount') to be acceptable, but would much prefer their (as previously mentioned) 'screw-clamp mount' (personal opinion, though). Still, the strap mount seems alright on road bikes and light trails, but I wouldn't try it on medium to heavy trails. The 'screw-clamp mount' however, I would. Also, the 'screw-clamp mount' is available as a separate item on Amazon, if you want it.
profile.summary: Another great offering by the famed "NiteRider", but the new 'strap' mount isn't as reliable as the old 'screw-clamp' mount...

profile.description: This product is ultra bright 3W Cree x-lamp LED puts out up to 310 lumens. Day lightning Flash Mode boosts 500+ lumens of lightning-like flashes for added day riding safety. Custom TIR optics for maximum beam angle and throw. Water resistant design for all riding conditions. 5 modes (3 steady 2 flashing). USB rechargeable internal Li-ion battery. Side illumination ports for added visibility 1:30 ~ 10 hour run time. 90g.Made in United States.
profile.reviewText: I'm very impressed with this light! Albeit I've never used it alone, (as I have another light on my handlebars) I did try using it alone once, and as another reviewer stated, it cast somewhat long, and sometimes deep shadows, to where I couldn't tell the difference between a pothole and a 'rise' in the pavement (probably from water getting under the pavement through a crack, then freezing and thawing, thus leaving an uneven spot in the pavement) but having the other light (which is a flood) helped. Albeit the flood light doesn't go far, this light (which is a 'spot' type) is just what I need to help me see further into the darkness. This light usually 'spots' the pavement WELL in advance for me to slow down, then my 'flood' light illuminates the area enough for me to know which direction to go in to avoid the hazard. (I try to stay on the road, if I can)This was just what I needed for an additional light to my flood to help me in the dark! The one thing I like, is that If I'm in the city (I go from urban [city], to sub-urban, to rural (no ambient light), back to urban during my commute) the "Daylightning" mode is great, since I can both be seen (necessary for city commuting) as well as see when it's dark, because it flashes while it stays on! Albeit on high, the battery won't last as long as a "Cygolite Metro", because the "Streak" is only 3.5" (88.9mm), whereas the "Metro" may only be 4.0" (101.6mm) .5" (12.7mm) longer, it is also 0.3-0.5" (7.62-12.7mm) wider,thus allowing for a larger battery. Still, if all you really do is commute, this is the perfect light for you!
profile.summary: A great light for urban cycling!

profile.description: This package contains 2 pairs of Cycle Clear goggles, one with clear lens and one with smoked lens.
profile.reviewText: These goggles are not made cheaply! You can feel that they're not when you first open them! Also, I expected them to be nothing but an elastic strap tied onto the frame, like so many others I've tried and/or seen, but they're sort of a hybrid between the folding 'arms' of a pair of sunglasses, and elastic bands of other goggles. The adjustability of these goggles is easy to figure out, (which is good, since they didn't come with directions) Also, the 'foam' lining, isn't foam, or...IS, I'm not sure? Still, it works better than foam, and when you stop, (if you're in cold temperatures) it fogs a little, but once you get going again, it clears right up! That was what made me fall in love with these goggles, (well that, and the fact that they're built better, and have metal [if only light metal] frames). Not certain what the lenses are made of, though. But if you're looking for a decent pair of budget goggles, these are THE goggles to get!
profile.summary: I was rather surprised at the quality of these 'budget' goggles!

profile.description: Our Silicone Wedding Band is smart and stylish as well as practical. Perfect to wear for physical activities where rigid rings are uncomfortable or unsafe. No more removing or losing your ring for physical activities such as sports, exercise, or playing instruments. Lightweight and comfortable, you won't even know you're wearing a ring. Distinctive double deboss adds subtle flair. Available in black, light grey, or graphite. Simply choose your color and size. Round up for half sizes.
profile.reviewText:
I got this because I wanted to humor my (soon to be?) other half, especially since she wanted to see if I'd like a silicone ring, and (in an odd way) I wanted to see what one would look like on me. Well, it seems neither one of us liked it, albeit it WAS malleable, and unlike a steel banded ring, it would snap before it took your hand, were it to get caught on something. Still, it WOULD cause a dislocation of your finger before it snapped, and steel rings have a much smaller chance of getting caught on something than silicone rings do, seeing as how steel rings usually have a tighter fit than silicone rings. In my opinion, I like steel/titanium/tungsten rings better (and think they look better) than silicone rings.

*I received this discounted product in exchange for a fair and unbiased review*
profile.summary: A nice silicone ring, if you like them.

profile.description: This beautiful ring is 8mm in width and has comfort fit finish. Our rings are hypoallergenic. This ring is made of genuine lightweight hi-tech Ceramic. It is very light, comfortable and are highly scratch resistant shine. So if you are looking for a ring that is scratch proof and forever keep it shine then our Ceramic rings are for you.
profile.reviewText: I ordered this ring since I love the particular shade of blue it comes in. I already have another ring with this shade of blue (which I'll refer to as 'medium blue' going forward) but the other ring I have, is medium blue with silver, and it's tungsten-carbide. I wanted a ring with a different 'feel' to it, so I got one that was ceramic, since I've felt that before, and it was very comfortable! Now I wish my tungsten-carbide ring was ceramic as well, since this one is so comfortable! The only thing I noticed to be different about this ring, is that the black/blue combination isn't as good looking (in my opinion) as the silver/blue tungsten-carbide ring I have. Other than that, this is a VERY nice looking ring, and I have gotten MANY, MANY, MANY compliments on it! Even more than I got with my tungsten-carbide ring! The only regret I have, is that I ordered it a size too small, and have to wear it on my pinky (isn't it strange that it's called a 'pinky' when it isn't pink?) as a result of my error!  Oh, well! This is a beautiful and comfortable ring, never the less!
profile.summary: VERY comfortable and beautiful ring!

profile.description: FEATURES of the Light and Motion Urban 650 Bike Head Light 650 Lumen output certified to the FL-1 Standard Engineered with the highest-level CREE LED and enhanced firmware It is the only light in its class with an accurate 4 level battery charge status indicator so you know if you have the juice to get home Custom engineered reflector optimizes the light to provide the most efficient and effective distribution of light for cycling Amber Side lighting for a full 180 degrees of visibility IP67 Rating - Tested to be fully waterproof in 1 meter of water for 30 minutes SPECIFICATIONS of the Light and Motion Urban 650 Bike Head Light Charge Time : 5.5 hrs System Weight : 121 Gr. Size : 1.2" x 1.2" x 4" Lumens : Flood? High : 650 Med : 300 Low : 150 Run Time High : 1.5 hrs Med : 3 hrs Low : 6 hrs
profile.reviewText: This light is great for urban riding, (which is why they named it the "Light & Motion Urban 650", duh!) but I wouldn't advise taking it on the trails, (which I tried, but was VERY unsuccessful, mind you) I know it's called the "Urban", but I wanted to try it out in other places as well, since it's round, and I like to have a view of everything that is around me when I'm going through the woods at night (even up in the trees, which is why I tried this light)! It did KIND of show up high, but not really...I guess they managed to design this light so that not TOO much light goes up to high, since it's meant for use in the concrete jungles! Anyway, I added a video to show some of my ride in the city, (too embarrassed to show any off road riding [which I do so rarely, It's shameful to show it] since I don't do it very well, and have run into the odd tree, 'nuff said...) I have video of the light, in which I show all its modes; it starts at high, then goes to medium, low, and pulse (not flash). I also realized it has no 'mode memory' and always turns on in the high mode. The rubber strap can be rotated, (to expose the charging plug on the bottom of the light) which can be a real annoyance if you're wearing thick gloves, and you just bump it (actually, for the sake of argument, you can hold the light and move the mount, or hold the mount, and move the light). The rubber band mount (in my opinion) works great for this light though, as the light isn't very heavy, and is not TOO big. There is a small indicator on the rear of the light to let you know the condition of the battery (which is usually green for full, orange for halfway, red for low, and flashing red for REALLY low), and it claims it lasts for 1hour 30min on high, but when I used it, it was about 30 degrees (-1.1 Celsius) outside, and I think that caused the battery to have a much shorter life, as it only lasted about 15 min on a full charge, before going to orange. Overall, I think this light is alright, but maybe I've just been spoiled by the other lights I've used that have higher lumens. Oh well, in summation, if you commute by bicycle at low light, (or nighttime) this light will do good by you, just make sure your commute isn't too long in cold temperatures! (UPDATE 9-21-2016) I was on a ride in the dark yesterday, and albeit I wasn't in the city, since I have now moved this light to my helmet, (since the light has a 'rubber band' type mount, I use one of the light mounts I got with another light that mounts with a stretchable 'rubber band'. [To try to make it less confusing sounding, I'll show you some pictures]) and the light has a unique and great warning feature when the battery is getting low. It will flash every 10 or so seconds (or pulse, which I like better than flash anyway) to inform you of this fact, and you can drop the level of light it is currently at, to get more life out of the battery. I found this out last night, when it took over from my "Magicshine Eagle 700" light that just up and died on me while I was riding on a (VERY dark) rural (country) road! I had to up the output of the "Urban 650", and that got me home, (but just barely, and thankfully, since I had no other lights, and the Urban had been on low the whole ride [before switching it to high]) so I am VERY happy with the "Light & Motion Urban 650", and VERY disappointed with the "Magicshine Eagle 700"! In fact, I think I'll ADD a star, since this light took over where the "Magicshine" left off!
profile.summary: Great light for nighttime or low-light commuting!

profile.description: The USB rechargeable Metro 550 strikes the perfect balance of amazing performance, safety, and versatility. Experience the unquestionable power of 550 lumens at night, optimized through its cyclingtuned optics to maximize your line of sight with exceptional brightness and clarity. With 6 powerful lighting modes (3 steady, 2 flashing, 1 walking), and up to 150 hours of illumination on a single charge, the Metro 550 has you covered night and day. In addition to the steady brightness modes, patent pending SteadyPulse mode alerts motorists with attention grabbing flashes while an overlapping steady beam constantly lights your way at night. For use as daytime running lights, eye catching DayLightning mode emits a boosted 600 lumens of lightning-like flashes to make you stand out in broad daylight. The sturdy quick release handlebar mount keeps the light securely fastened in rough terrain while allowing quick and easy detachment as needed for use as a handy flashlight or for storage while not in use. Buy with confidence in Cygolite, as every light is designed, engineered, and assembled in the USA to rigorous quality and testing protocols - outshining and outlasting cheap imitations. For customer service, email and phone support with live customer personnel offers you fast and easy assistance from right here in the USA.
profile.reviewText: I only wish this were more of a 'spot' type of light, than the 'flood' type it is. Otherwise, I am QUITE shocked and amazed at this light! For the first thing, I like the unique way the 6 modes are lined up! I'm used to the "low, medium, high, flash" set-up. However, since this one has 6 modes, low, medium, high, steadypulse, daylightning, and walk, AND they're arranged differently, I like this light more than those others! The modes are setup like this 1)Low 2)Steadypulse 3) Daylightning 4)Medium 5)High and mode number 6, "walk mode" as it's referred to, is accessed by a prolonged press on the power/mode button, (1.5-2 seconds). The 'daylightning' mode is only recommended for daytime use, and I can see why. I have Epilepsy, and I made the mistake of switching into that mode in a dark area. Luckily I switched it off quickly, or the situation might've turned ugly. It's a VERY bright and fast flash (think dance club strobe light) and is VERY easily seen, so unless the driver of the car is 100% blind, they WILL see it! The other mode I like, and have often used, is the 'steadypulse'. Think of it like this...the light has been turned on to medium, but it's flashing at the same time! Sort of like combining the medium setting with the daylightning setting, only the daylightning isn't as bright as it is alone. It also fits in the mount I have for my "Expilion 850", as I used to have the Expilion on my helmet, but found out it was heavier than I thought, and just to see, after I got the "Metro 550", I checked if it would go into the mount I already had on my helmet for the Expilion, and it did! I then used the handlebar mount for the Metro 550, and mounted the Expilion to it. My personal opinion is that the Expilion is a great light, but if you want one to place on your helmet, go for the Metro line.
profile.summary: One of the best lights from this company!

profile.description: AT-A-GLANCE Daily Desk Calendar Refill is sure to help keep you up-to-date and organized all year long. Covers 12 months January  December making it the perfect resource for year round planning. Scheduling appointments is made easy with this refill, which features half-hourly appointments, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and two pages per weekday. Past, current and future months reference are included for additional planning perspective. This refill fits standard 17-style bases with 2 rings. Each page: 3.5 in. x 6 in.. Overall size: 3.5 in. x 6 in. x 1 in..
profile.reviewText: I started with the 2015 version, and though this one is slightly different, (VERY slightly, but like the saying goes, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it!") I like it just as well, and will get the next year! ESPECIALLY since it gives you room to write things you wish to remember, to do lists, etc. Also since I wasn't entirely sure of the measurements, (I got everything for 2015) I was hoping this would fit on the base I got for the 2015 model (I figured it would, this being a refill) so I went back in my order history, and clicked on the one for the 2015 calendar, and it opened onto this page for the 2016 refill, and hoping I was right, I ordered it. The only difference between this and the 2015 version, is that while they both listed Monday thru Friday on their own 'foldout' pages, (like opening a book, and having both pages show the day, date, and year, along with a small calendar on the upper left of the right-side page showing the whole layout of that particular month,) Saturday and Sunday are now on one page each. I'll explain. Monday - Friday each take up two pages, (like in the last edition) but unlike the 2015 copy, now Saturday is on the left page, and Sunday is on the right page, with no smaller 'calendar' of the entire month on the upper left of the right page - but on the weekends ONLY. If you still have questions about something you would like me to explain better, (or if my explanation was just too confusing) please leave a comment. I'll add some photos to try to help clear up any confusion, though.
profile.summary: I REALLY enjoy this desk calendar!

profile.description: Lezyne was founded on march 1St, 2007, by industry icon micki kozuschek and other industry partners. A former professional triathlete, kozuschek is native to Germany. In the Prime of his athletic career, kozuschek began max cycles and brought affordable, high-quality bicycles and clothing to the German market. Shortly after moving to the USA, kozuschek founded truvativ, which grew to become a leading manufacturer of OEM and aftermarket cycling components. In 2004, kozuschek sold truvativ to SRAM and began a two-year break from the cycling industry to focus on building his dream home and spending time with his family.
profile.reviewText:
This light is just as bright as one of my other 2000 lumen lights, although the light this one puts out is whiter. It's almost like having a 'flood' and 'spot' in one light! It projects a good distance, but that distance also has a 'blob' (for want of a better term) of light, not a concentrated 'hotspot' with a dimmer 'corona' (or ring) around it. The 'blob' is bright enough (depending on your setting, the distance you have it aimed from your bike, and how fast you're going) to give you advanced enough warning of 'nice' hindrances, such as potholes and debris, (if you're city riding) and roots, loose soil and leaves (which can be dangerous) if you're trail riding. The body is aluminum, with a rubber 'on/off' switch on the top, that also has a light showing the state of the battery charge (green for full, orange for caution, red for low) but, unlike the "Lezyne Mega Drive" family of lights, this one doesn't have a removable battery in the rear. Just a place to plug a micro-USB in to charge it. One more thing, I think they somehow messed up the photo, because when I ordered this light, it came with a 'clamshell' type mount, NOT the rubber strap it shows in the picture, which is good, because the light housing is aluminum, far too heavy for a rubber strap to handle! Beam shots and/or video are coming soon!

(UPDATE 1-12-2016)
I did something I'm NOT proud of, and will refrain from doing in the future (I actually never thought I WOULD do this!) I wrote my review from simply doing an 'alpha' (first round) test in my basement. Sorry about that. Now that I have actually ridden with it, (and done a proper "beta" [final stage] test on it) I can tell you the "Fenix BC30" I also have on my bars is MUCH brighter than this light! However, you're probably thinking "But wait a minute, the "Fenix" has a higher lumen rating than this light does!" This is true, but false. Let me explain. While the highest rating on this light is 1200 lumens, and the "Fenix" is 1800, you can only achieve 1800 lumens on the "Fenix" by pressing the remote switch and activating the 'burst' mode it has. Otherwise, it's max output is 1200 lumens. I tried the 1200 lumen setting on the "Fenix" while I still had the "Lezyne Super Drive 1200 XXL" on, and aside from the "Fenix" being a slightly more yellowish light, (which was good, since with the differing light colors, I could tell which light was which) it all BUT eclipsed the "Lezyne"! Therefore, I am subtracting 3 stars, since it's not as bright as I thought, and isn't NEARLY as good as I thought. Would also recommend NOT using it for trail riding either, (if you like seeing where you're going, that is) The "Fenix BC30" will easily be my first choice of bike light from now on, (trail or street) but the "Lezyne Super Drive 1200 XXL" will be my back-up light, unless I get another "Fenix"..... I was just thinking: maybe I'm being too tough on this light...maybe mine has a small defect...I'll give it another try tonight.

(UPDATE 1-18-2016) Sorry the update came so late, but defect or not, I'm standing by my original update.
profile.summary: A (not so) bright and tough light! (UPDATED)

profile.description: Ideal for commutes and trail rides.
profile.reviewText: I tested it in my basement, but since I vowed to never write a review on simply that basis, (and I was impressed with it's performance in the basement at night, though) I took it on a 'test run'. While I was doing so, I realized it was best suited for a commuting light, and really shouldn't be used on trails at all. (My opinion, though). I also found that it is a combination of 'spot' and 'flood', but more the former, than the latter. As for the mount, the "Flex-Tight mount" "Cateye" uses, is a great mount for a light like this, (and maybe the "Volt 700") but I had a "Cateye HL-EL610RC Single Shot Plus LED Bicycle Light" and the "Flex-Tight" mount for that light was HORRID! For all the details on that, go to the link in this review, and read the review written by one "Aaron I" That will tell you what I cannot, (well, would rather not). ANYWAY, back to the review for THIS light! (Sorry about going off topic there) I REALLY like the 'cartridge battery' design, where you can just replace the battery with a new one if you have a long commute, and no way to recharge your battery at work! Simply take another battery, (fully charged, of course) with you, and screw it in when you're heading home, if need be. The light is also VERY light,(in weight) and you won't even notice you have it on your bars! I've added a video, so you can see the beam pattern on pavement, as well as see the difference between lit and unlit pavement. One last thing, the flash of the brighter light was a slip of the thumb where I accidentally pressed the 'burst' button of the "Fenix BC30" I also have on my bars.
profile.summary: Nice commuting light with many features, and very light!

profile.description: This Product is 320 lumen headlight. USB rechargeable. 7 modes. 1:15 ~ 55 hour run time. 74g.Made in United States.
profile.reviewText:
I didn't expect this to be so bright! It's wonderful! I have 2 other lights on the front of my bike, (each one 500 lumens) and just wanted something 'extra' to put on my helmet to see around corners at intersections. I had a "Knog Blinder Arc 1.7" but the problem was that it was too front-heavy, meaning that whenever I came to a stop, I'd have the pleasure of hearing an audible 'klunk' on the top of my helmet. It went back into place afterwards, but just got annoying, so I ordered this, and am VERY pleased, to say the LEAST! The low profile of the light helps it stay in place if I need to make a quick stop, and the daytime running/flashing function of the 4 individual L.E.D.s on the top, help others to see me, and not think I'm part of the background! When I drove a car, I realized that a flashing (and bright) light got my attention MUCH faster than a solid light (no matter how bright it was!) Then, adding the main light, it becomes so bright, you want to make sure you don't aim it at the drivers eyes! You can even set it to blink in 4 of its 7..count 'em..7 modes! In 3 of those 4 blinking modes, the main light
blinks along with the 4 lights up top! The other 3 modes are low, medium, and high. I made the mistake of looking straight at it when I first powered it on; won't do THAT again! Just a word of warning, since the top lights are so small, their light seems MUCH more concentrated and bright. Overall, a great light, and if this had been around before I got those other 2 lights, well, you know where this is going....
profile.summary: The best helmet light I've ever owned!

profile.description: The Volt series are our go-to lights when the days get short. With a wide range of lumen outputs, there's one for every cyclist. No matter where or when you ride, let CatEye light the way and keep you safe.
profile.reviewText: I was using this the other night, and though the temperature was low, (30 degrees Fahrenheit [1.1 degrees Celsius]) The battery didn't seem to show any signs of weakening, like shorter battery life. When I took it for a ride, I can definitely tell you, I'm certainly not going to use it in the city again, because even though there are some dark areas, I don't think I need THIS much light, because even on its lowest setting, it's pretty bright! It's not the easiest to use with thick gloves on either (but CAN be done), but it seems stable enough on your bars to take a bit of fiddling while trying to find the switch, and not lose its aim. However, if you are on a trail (or anywhere for that matter!), I suggest you stop before trying to change modes with gloves on, as it can get a bit difficult otherwise. I did notice that this light is a mix of 'spot' and 'flood', albeit it seems like a little more of the latter, then the former (more flood than spot). I did notice that it puts kind of a 'square' shape where it's aimed, (probably due to the "CatEye" *Opticube* technology) and lights the area up nicely. I didn't estimate the size of the 'square of light' because tilting the light on your bars, could make it larger or smaller, depending on the angle. In my video, if looked at from the side, my light is probably aimed at about (and I'm just guessing here) a 5 degree angle (never took...Geometry...is it? in school). All in all, this is a VERY bright light that is reliable, and seems to handle cold better than other lights I've used. Would recommend! P.S. Unlike another light I reviewed recently, this light DOES have a 'memory mode', along with a quick flash function. Just tap two times in quick succession to access it. The other modes are as follows 1)Dynamic=high 2)Normal=medium 3)All-Night=low 4)HyperConstant=medium+fast flash Then, to shut it off, one 1-2 second press on power button. It comes with no instructions, just the light, handlebar mount, and USB charging cable. Also, in small print, it says "Mount the light unit at least 3cm away from any wireless cycle computer. If a wireless receiver is mounted too close, the transmission may be adversely effected. Just a helpful tip.
profile.summary: VERY bright light, and even on the lowest setting, I would recommend against using it in the city!

profile.description: This back support belt support provides safety will lifting and is comfortable to wear. Great for warehouse workers, stockers, movers or any occupation with frequent lifting, this back support belt features adjustable suspenders and elastic outer panels for added comfort.
profile.reviewText: I had another back belt, but it lacked: A) the shoulder straps this one has, and B) the freedom of movement this one affords. The shoulder straps help it stay in place, as well as assisting you with lifting. (not quite sure HOW, just know it DOES) Also, this can be placed in such a position that it doesn't need to have the pants pulled over it. (The other one doesn't need that either, I just like to have it that way do to my obsessive-compulsiveness) Let's just say this back belt is more focused on well,...helping your back! While my other one is more focused on helping you while in a chair, in other words, in one place, doing one thing, not moving all over the warehouse unloading trucks and towmotors, like this one. My other one, (for which you're probably screaming into your computer or other electronic device by now, saying "JUST TELL ME WHAT IT IS, ALREADY!!!") is this "Mueller Adjustable Lumbar Back Brace, Black, Regular, 1-Count Package" sorry about figuratively holding the bait in front of your nose, not letting you reach it, there. The other thing I find impressive about this belt, that the other (Mueller) didn't have, is the fact that while this belt is held together via hook & loop fasteners (Velcro) It has 3 'connecting points', the main one (the main belt) and two others, (straps to 'tighten' the belt more, if you wish). On the end of all 3 of these 'points', there is a covering over the Velcro, so it doesn't stick to anything you don't want it to. All in all, I think this belt is well thought out, and well designed and will do a good job for its intended use, (and maybe some other uses...) *This product was provided at a discount for a fair and unbiased review* However, I would've written the same review had I purchased it at full price, because this product exceeded my expectations, and it wouldn't have gotten a 5-star review if it didn't deserve it!
profile.summary: A pleasant and surprisingly well thought out back belt!

profile.description: Cute and quite sturdy house carrier for 3 precious little baby animals. House is about 10" long with 3 openings and a carrying strap. Animals are 5" long and have a full body with a small opening in the belly area for your finger.
profile.reviewText: My niece thinks this is the cutest thing! I'm glad she likes it, I was hoping she would, I felt kind of bad giving her that 'laptop' and having it barely last an hour, when she was being GENTLE with it (clears throat). ANYWAY, on to this product! When I ordered it, I thought (since it says 'plush' school bus) it would be plush all the way through, with three holes for the animals. NOT QUITE... The animals are plushies, but the bus is actually soft on the outside, and hollow on the inside: the best way I can think of to describe it, is if you remember those plastic 'grids' they used to sell, (with pictures colored on them) that you could then 'crochet' (or is it knit?) different colored yarns through them in order to 'knit' a picture with the yarn. Anyhow, the inside isn't necessarily rough feeling, but (at the same time) it feels kind of stiff with a slight fuzzy feeling, and you can sort of tell it's got a stiff 'frame', because a fully plush bus might not maintain a constant shape as this one does, but is still safe for children to play with. It comes with 3 plush finger puppets, a Bulldog/Pug, a Monkey, and I THINK the black and white one, is a Baby Panda or Kitten. By The Way, the 'wheels on the bus' DON'T  go 'round and 'round, since they are plush, they don't move at all! *I received this at a discount for a fair and unbiased review*, and I hope you enjoyed my description.
profile.summary: If your child likes plush toys, they'll love this!

profile.description: The Minoura CS-500 is a spare accessory holder that mounts in place of a headset spacer. Made in Japan.
profile.reviewText: This works great on my seatpost, (but I don't think it will work on 'aero'-style seatposts) I got this since I wanted a rear 1200 lumen taillight on my bike, and got the "1200LM 3 Modes CREE 5V XML-T6 USB LED Headlamp..." sold here on Amazon.com to use it with, thinking my "Kmashi 10,000maH" external battery pack would work for it, but either I got a bad one, or the overvoltage sensor in the light, or the battery pack keeps tripping. ANYWAY, back to the subject. I said it fit on my seatpost, (but had to remove it first [piece of advice, mark where your seatpost is with a paint pen or something before you remove it) Once I did, it fit quite well, as will MOST seatposts, however, to make it a bit larger, loosen the bolts by the seatpost/headset spacer mount, then you can tighten them once it's on. The bolts require an 'Allen' wrench (not sure what size, though) and the mount (which can only accept one accessory) has about the outside diameter of a 25.4mm bar.
profile.summary: Another great mount from Minoura!

profile.description: rosman 1322C .22Cal Variable Pump
profile.reviewText: When I first got this pistol, I loved how it looked. I was worried that the stock and handle were just painted black, but this doesn't seem to be the case. The plastic they are made of DOES seem to be of high quality, as I read about in the reviews. I am very happy with this gun, and have only used it as a backyard plinker, so far. It seems rather accurate as the barrel is rifled, even though it's a pistol. I'm doing some target practice to get up to possibly hunting with it. Well, just gophers, and such. Someone else mentioned that it was "ungainly" w/out the stock, which can be bought seperately; then, attached to the grip. However, I disagree with this. Maybe it's a bit large, but I like that. I just think it looks very imposing. This is the first pellet pistol i've had, that is both of .22 "gauge" AND I can pump. No need for Co2! All in all, VERY satisfying purchase. I would recommend this pistol to anyone.
profile.summary: Just as good as I had hoped!

profile.description: Quality constuction, warm fleece material, one size fits most. Great for Police, Military, EMS, and general wear.
profile.reviewText: It seems a little tight (as I have a 7 3/4" [196.85 mm] hat size) But it's GREAT at keeping the warmth in! It just barely comes down around my ears, though. Albeit, the only reason I can see that happening, is because I've got an unnecessarily large dome. The hat itself, is a very soft fleece, and you almost can't tell you have it on, (unless you walk past a mirror, or someone tells you!) Even for me, it may have been tight, but it was STILL very warm and comfortable. It is also so soft and pliable, that I was able to put it in the pocket of my hooded sweatshirt when I took it off. I did it without thinking, and it went into my pocket like it was made to! This hat is a wonderful departure from the norm, as it is comfortable, and not itchy, like so many knit caps I've used. I would suggest getting this, because if I was able to wear it with my big head, and it still came down around my ears, (and I'm 6'2"!) you should have no problems with it fitting, and since it's so warm, you could wear it in very cold weather!
profile.summary: A hat/cap you shouldn't pass up, great for keeping you warm!

top_5.description: Drift is a leading active lifestyle focused technology company that is based out of the U.K. with local offices in North America; US, Canada, and Mexico. Our award winning cameras enable users to capture and share their most exciting moments from their point of view and other unique perspectives. Drift innovation is a UK based vetran in the manufacturing of sports action cameras. Drift Innovation supplies retailers with a global presence in over 40 countries. You can feel comfortable investing in your new Drift Innovation product with U.S. offices and English speaking technical support. Introducing our 8th generation drift camera, the Drift Stealth 2 Action Shot Camera. This innovative little camera is the lightest and smallest Drift camera yet. Its unique design allows you to capture your experiences in a whole new way. The stealth 2 films in 1080 pixels at 30 frames per second with its Aptina CMOS sensor producing crystal clear,high definition footage. This lightweight little camera is made easy to use and can travel anywhere. It only measures out to 80mm x 42mm x 27 mm and weighs only 97 gm. The sports action camera has a top quality 7-element lens that provides an optical view of 137 degrees. Our extreme camera no longer uses a digital narrow angle allowing objects to appear closer and sharper. The drift cameras durability and flex gives it the right protection and support it requires for extreme use.. A versatile camera using the Drift universal clip, can be mounted and adjusted as a helmet camera or bike camera. The Aptina CMOS sensor produces crystal clear, high definition footage so it functions smoothly as a dash camera as well. The stealth 2 action shot cameras rotatable lens, 3 hours recording time and aerodynamic design, makes this a highly advanced and unique POV camera. This extreme camera provides a whole new interaction and a whole new dimension to the way you experience your camera . Our Stealth 2 is the manifestation of a dynamic system deeply integrated with the utmost quality and precision. This is the next generation of action cameras. Backed by a full 12 month manufacturer's warranty.
top_5.reviewText: I LOVE the fact that this camera is so small! The time/date stamp function that it has (that can be turned off if wanted) is WONDERFUL! I wanted to get an in-depth look at the functionality of this camera before I got one, seeing as how on my budget, $199.00 is a LOT of money, and I wanted to be sure of what I was getting (I'm certain others can agree with me!) All I can say is, save up your money and get one! This camera is GREAT! (In fact, I think I'm going to get another one soon!) If you want to see the video I watched that helped me make up my mind to get this camera, look for a review for this camera on "Youtube" done by a person named "Techmoan". It convinced me, and not only is this camera small, and has a 2 1/2 to 3 hour battery life, it's also very light! When my "Metroflash E360" that I purchased here on Amazon.com 3 years ago, finally 'gave up the ghost', I got this camera to replace it, and didn't realize how much heavier the "Metroflash" had been (especially since I have it mounted on my bicycle helmet!) Also, I had thought my "Metroflash" had decent 'low-light' performance, the "Drift Stealth 2" even beat it in THAT respect! On a scale of 1-10, I'd give the video a 10, the audio a 9.3, (the only reason it loses .7 of a point, is because of a whistle from wind noise) and the rain resistance a 10! (It can supposedly be submerged 2 meters [or 6.5 feet] without a waterproof case, but I haven't tried that, nor do I plan to!) I am planning on curing the wind whistle with a product sold here on Amazon.com, called "Micover Stickover-Mini Universal Windscreen for DSLRs, Phones, Laptops, Small Video Cameras" I'll see how it works. I just really enjoy the camera, and would not fail to recommend it to any/everyone! (UPDATE 7-1-2015) The "Micover Stickover" I mentioned in my review, is excellent for cutting out that pesky wind noise I was getting, (even though I only get up to 30mph, seeing as how I'm on a bicycle) and I would recommend it to anybody who wears this as a helmet-cam on a bicycle,(but can't speak for a motorcycle, or motocross racer). (UPDATE 7-20-2015) I now have 3 of these cameras, as well as the "DRIFT GHOST REMOTE CONTROL" and the remote DOES work with this camera. I was able to pair all 3 with that remote, and though you still have to turn each individual camera on by itself, to start recording all I now have to do, is push one button.
top_5.summary: This camera has everything I want, and more!

top_5.description: The New Mini Action Camera From WCI Is The Ultimate Accessory For All Outdoor Sports Recording. Attach the Camera Securely With The Included Strap And Mounts, and Record It All In Real Time. Upload The Video File To Your Computer with The USB Cable, And Store those Memories For A Long, Long Time. Easy, Affordable and User Friendly, It Is a Great Alternative To Other Pricier Models Out There!
top_5.reviewText: I really like this camera, and it has it's drawbacks, but for the price, it beats the living snot out of a GoPro! I have noticed that it has a "flashing" effect when I go outside,(possibly due to the sudden change in the amount of light) but it has great sounding audio! However; once you put it in the waterproof case, that audio is all but non-existent! Maybe when I mount it to my helmet and go for a ride on my bike that'll all change, but when I first tested it, it sounded fine, until I put the case on it. Then the sound lost about 95% of it's clarity. The other thing I noticed, was that the color went from full spectrum, to paled, back to full spectrum, but did so ONLY when a shock occurred, and then, only for a VERY short time. The last thing I noticed, was that it's low light performance was pretty bad, albeit it uses any/all available light sources, just doesn't have any illumination of its own. If you're looking for a starter camera, or if you just want a decent camera for active use, and you don't want a really expensive one (like me) then this is the camera for you! One more thing, the growling/whining noise in the video is not the camera; I have an electric kit on my bike to help me up hills, as there are many where I live, and I'm going up a particularly steep one in the video. Just wanted to show the performance of the camera. (Update 6-26-2014) I got a chance to use it more, and I found out the 'flashing' I mentioned earlier, doesn't happen in the 'HD' mode, and neither does the color instability. Those were both only in the 640X480 resolution. However, the battery life in 'HD' mode (using the video recorder) is shorter than that of 640X480.
top_5.summary: My first helmet cam, but a great choice!

top_5.description: The MetroFlash e360 Wi-Fi Extreme HD Action Camera is designed to capture your everyday most exciting adventure and ventures! Designed for surfers, skaters, motorcyclists, bikers, base jumpers, snowboarders and anyone else who want to capture high definition videos of their most extreme moments, MetroFlash e360 Wi-Fi Extreme HD Action Camera is capable of recording in the most extreme conditions. Attach it to your helm, to your surfboard, on your bike's handlebar or strap it around your waist and shoot your breathtaking action from up close. Armed with Low-Light Performance CMOS image sensor, F2.8 Ultra Wide Sharp lens (170-degree coverage) and built-in Wi-Fi, MetroFlash e360 is always ready to capture and share the action anywhere!.
top_5.reviewText: This is the best camera I have yet seen. It has (not surprisingly) lasted me almost a year, and looks like it will last another with no problems! Even when I was riding in 5 degree temperatures, the battery life was 2 hours on 1080p, and waterproof (without a case) as well! (I found this out the hard way, enough said) Also, since it's mounted to my helmet, it has received its fair share of bumps, knocks, falls, and scrapes, and hasn't shown the least bit of it, (aside from some marks on the housing itself) and continues to work like the day I got it! Another good thing, is that since it doesn't have a display screen to speak of, and it has 'Wi-Fi', I use my "iPhone 5c" as my display screen! The video I put up is just to show the performance of the camera, and albeit, it has a very sensitive microphone, and wind noise is very prevalent, on auto, it switches from bright sun to lower light rather quickly, and as you can see, I went into my basement from a sunny day, and it adjusted almost instantaneously. (P.S.) Amazon lowers the quality a tad, but the video (and audio) quality are excellent when they come directly from the camera! (Update) I like this camera so much, besides being able to take whatever I may dish out, and the clarity of video and sensitivity of the microphone, (along with being waterproof without an external case) the only other thing I would wish for, is the option to add a time/date stamp to the video. Just an OPTION. If you don't want it, don't activate it. I just want it to be available. If it were, I would buy at LEAST 3 more of these cameras (possibly more!) Other than that, this is THE best camera I have EVER had! I've seen tests of the GoPro Hero Black Edition, and this camera wins HANDS DOWN!!!! At LESS than half the price, believe it or not!
top_5.summary: The Metroflash E360: No GoPro, But Just As Good (If Not Better); And Cheaper!

top_5.description: Package included: 1 x Aluminum Case with LOGO 1 x Strap 1 x Base Mount and Bolts 1 x Lens Cap. Designed for GoPro Hero 4
top_5.reviewText:
Though I see many good reviews of this mount, mine seemed to have come with stripped-out threads, and therefore, I can't use it as it was intended. I was going to use it to mount a "Cycliq Fly12" (which has "GoPro" style mounts, and can be placed upside-down on your bars) however, being that said camera/light/alarm (read my review on the "Fly12" page for further details) is quite expensive (like many "GoPro" cameras [the LEAST expensive one is $129.99, which is rather inexpensive, actually; but as for most others....]) with that stripped thread (that came like that from the manufacturer) I didn't want to take the chance it would 'give way' while I was driving down the road, and even though the camera has a safety tether, I STILL don't want to risk a $350.00 camera/light/alarm! Anyway, I'm glad the mount arrives with an Allen wrench to tighten the screws (it fits them, but I can only tighten 1) The mount is geared to fit a 31.8mm  (1.25 in) handlebar, but I used it on a smaller one, a 25.4 mm (1") one, which required I use a thick rubber spacer from one of the lights I didn't require any spacers for (In other words, I did a bit of jury-rigging). Now, to answer the question I had when I first ordered this (that being "how far does this extend from the handlebar?") first off, the length of the entire mount, is 4" (101.6 mm), as far as how far from the handlebar it actually extends, that answer would be 2" (50.8 mm). Also, at the widest point in the area where the "GoPro" type mount is, it's a little over 0.5" wide (12.7 mm). But as I first said, 3 of the 4 screws were stripped out when it arrived, so be careful when you order this, and just be aware that this is possible, yet I hope
you don't have to deal with it as I have.

(UPDATE 11/22/2016)
 I was going to return this mount to get my money back, but it seems they have an exchange policy, and the company (as well as Amazon) were both VERY easy to work with, and they sent me a new mount for no charge, as well as not requiring me to send the other one back! (Actually, what are they going to do with a stripped-out mount, anyway?) They also had it ship VERY fast, (it got here in 2 days, when the original took around a week and a half!) while it worked great, and wasn't stripped at all! I guess the first one just snuck by quality control, and unfortunately got shipped to me! Still, the fact that the company had such great customer service, and replaced the mount so quickly, without a single question, made me VERY happy, along with making another loyal customer! I added 3 stars, since I was so pleased, and they were so easy to work with! Like I said in a previous review, customer service means a LOT to me!
top_5.summary: Good mount extension, just hope the threads aren't stripped out when it arrives! (UPDATED)

I was luckily able to get it turned on (from what I've read, others didn't even get that far!) and enter the time and date stamp, (which I realized was only viewable in the 'car' folder) which was helpful, since I can't turn it off, (due to a 'file error' message) I now know the exact time, day, and date this camera 'gave up the ghost'!
