profile.reviewText: I bought this model on the basis of favorable reviews of other Amazon customers who apparently know more about AA and AAA battery chargers than I do.  I agree with those reviewers who recommended it.  It has multiple charging speeds from high to low, but I always use the low speed to avoid overheating the batteries.  It's easy to operate and to select other features, like the one that fully discharges a partially used battery before recharging it, to avoid giving the battery a "memory" that prevents a full recharge every time.  I guess that's useful, and I use the feature from time to time, but usually I just keep the charger plugged in, I dump the batteries into the clips and take them out when the display reads FULL for each battery, and the batteries come out fully charged and cool, which I think is good (right?).  Based on the recommendations of the other reviewers, I have more confidence that this charger is protecting the long-term interests of my batteries than other chargers, and I've seen nothing to the contrary after having used it a hundred times or more.  I wish they would have included an option for flip-up prongs to plug the charger directly into the wall outlet, like my other charger, which is a Canon, however the present arrangement with a cord works fine for me also.  It's as easy to recharge AAA batteries as for AAs.  I've standardized all my equipment to either AA or AAA (GPS, marine radio, headlamp, everything) so when I go into the backcountry or kayak camping, I can go directly from this charger to my Goal Zero Nomad 10 solar charger (another really nice item!) and I'm covered indoors or outdoors.  Use Sanyo Eneloop batteries and this charger, and you should have no other battery concerns.
profile.summary: Good quality, versatile charger, easy to use

profile.description: Merino wool meets hi-tech: The Biosensor Liners are naturally wicking, naturally anti-odor and touch-screen-friendly thermal merino wool liner gloves with a feathered finish.
profile.reviewText: These are neither a good nor a bad glove; you just need to understand what you're ordering.  This is not a warm glove; it is a LINER, and a very thin, open weave liner at that.  You can see your hand through the loose weave, so you wouldn't wear these for principal cold weather protection for your hands.  They fit nicely and are comfortable with good finger length, and the biosensors work well on touch screens, although I don't understand why OR put biosensors only on the thumb and index fingers instead of on all the finger tips.  The glove is very flimsy and subject to pulls, runs, and catching on things, so I would not think them durable at all.  They also have scratchy tags sewn into the insides at the wrists, which tags are annoying and look difficult to remove.  Mine did not come with the clips shown in the photo (on Amazon) that hold the gloves together when not in use.  These gloves made me think about which fingers I use on my touchscreen, and I realized that I use more than just my thumbs and forefingers (I regularly use my middle finger) so for me this glove does not have enough biosensor tips.  I'm not wholly down on the gloves, but they are obviously really flimsy and apparently not intended to be warm.
profile.summary: Biosensors work fine, but very flimsy and not warm

profile.description: 3/4oz Aquaseal Neoprene Wetsuit Repair Adhesive The industry standard for maximum strength repairs to wetsuits, dry suits and all watersports products. Flexible urethane formula waterproofs, seals and protects against abrasion. Use it to repair fingernail tears, provide a protective coating to high wear areas of a suit, or fix split seams. Be sure to use in a well ventilated area. Store a partially used tube in the freezer for a longer shelf life.
profile.reviewText: I'm a sea kayaker and I wear soft, neoprene gloves when I paddle.  They get holes in them all the time.  I patch the holes with Aquaseal, and I've never had a patch come loose.  As with any material, you need to learn how to use it.  It doesn't like the edges of the patch to be "feathered" to zero (0) thickness.  You want to have the edge of the patch to have some thickness, so the edges aren't so insubstantial that they start to fray.  I've patched so many pairs of  neoprene gloves with this material, so many times, that I have more confidence in the patch material than I do in the neoprene under it.  Now that I've had some experience in applying it, I use it to reinforce high wear areas of brand new gloves before I wear them the first time.  Aquaseal is tough stuff, and tolerably flexible as well, once it has cured, which takes several hours.  You can buy some stuff called "Cotol" (also from McNett) that accelerates the curing process, but I've never used it, nor do I think it's necessary if whatever your application is allows for curing overnight.  It's a good product, but just remember there's a learning curve for how to apply it, and you won't get best results (nice, thin, flexible, even patches) until you've used it a few times.  I apply it using a dental pick, so as to stretch the material from a glob into a uniform patch, and I use the pick to manipulate the material into good contact (don't rely on gravity for that).  A toothpick would also work to apply it.  Just squeezing it out of the tube usually makes an ugly patch.  Something to remember is to NOT let the Aquaseal get on the threads of the tube or the threads of the plastic cap.  If you do, when it cures, you will have glued the cap to the tube and it'll be VERY difficult to get the cap off again.  Allowing that to happen also allows the curing process (around the cap) to proceed down the tube into the material inside the neck of the tube, and soon the neck becomes clogged solid.  After that, you need to start poking holes into the side of the tube to get to the still-liquid Aquaseal, and in a short while the tube is a total loss.  So you have to be very neat and carefully clean the area around the cap before resealing it, or you're going to be buying more Aquaseal.  Because Aquaseal is viscous, and because it cures so slowly (like slow set epoxy), gravity has time to act upon it before it cures, meaning it's not well-suited to vertical applications.  It will run, so flat and level works best.  If you have to use it for something that has a vertical or curved surface which could sag/drip/run, the Cotol might be needed to accelerate the curing time, or you'll need to rotate the object so a gravity sag does not result before it cures.  I like the product and have used it for diverse applications it wasn't intended for, usually with good success.  It's like slow-set clear liquid rubber.  What could you use that for?
profile.summary: Good produce, slow to cure

profile.description: Packing to fist size and inflating with just a couple of breaths, the Exped Air Pillow removes all excuses for leaving a pillow at home. I had my first one go defective shortly before the manufacturer's warranty expired, and I called Exped's customer service, and they very quickly replaced it with another.  I only needed to email a picture of the defect from my iPhone.  No hassle, very impressively handled.  If I had it to do again, I think I'd buy the large pillow, rather than the medium one, this because I'm a side-sleeper and I'd like the pillow a little thicker to keep my neck straight while sleeping on my side. profile.description: Equipped with a fully waterproof construction and an incredibly bright 160 lumens, the Black Diamond Storm is our powerful, all-conditions headlamp. Now featuring our Power Tap Technology, the Storm allows for quick, on-the-fly brightness adjustment with just a finger tap to the side of its touch-sensitive housing. The Storm features a bright, precise beam for after-dark route-finding, as well as proximity, strobe, dimming and red night vision modes to accommodate any lighting needs. An intuitive lock mode also keeps the light from accidentally turning on when stored in your pack or pocket.
profile.reviewText: I've had several of these, the "Storm" water-resistant ones, and the brightness appears to be the same whether the company advertises that to be 100 lumens or 160 lumens.  In either case, the maximum brightness is more than adequate for backpacking type activities.  I have one of these in each of our life jackets as safety equipment, and they remain waterproof until you crack the plastic case and water gets in, then they die.  However, Black Diamond's customer service is quite friendly about replacing a dead one, with few questions, and I like that attitude so I continue buying their brand.  The function switch is logical and easy to use for changing light modes (spot, general area, red, dimmer, strobe), and the adjustability and fit are as good as any other brand I've tried.  Weird story:  I loaned my BD Storm headlamp to a Peruvian guide one night when we were speeding in a launch down the Amazon; he was using it to guide the boat because it was the only light on board.  We hit something in the darkness and he fell overboard, and ended up swimming underwater awhile as he extricated himself from the debris.  It was a bizarre sight because the headlamp continued to work underwater all through his ordeal and rescue.  The same headlamp was still working several years later, none the worse for this incident and several subsequent dunkings in the ocean.
profile.summary: Bright, tough, water-resistant, good customer service

profile.description: Connect your portable Mini USB devices, with the cable out of the way - The USBAMB50CMU 50cm USB to Up Angle Mini USB Cable provides a high quality connection between your Mini USB 2.0 mobile devices (smartphones, GPS, digital cameras, portable hard drives, etc.) and your PC or Mac computer, for everyday tasks such as charging, data synchronization or file transfers. The up-angled Mini USB connector allows you to access your Mini USB devices, while keeping the cable out of the way, and stress away from the port. Perfect for close-range device connections, our shorter mini USB cables provide a portable solution that makes them perfect for carrying as an accessory for your tablet or laptop. Designed and constructed for maximum durability, this high quality USB to Mini USB cable is backed by StarTech.com''s Lifetime Warranty. As an alternative, StarTech.com also offers a 0.5m USB to Down Angle Mini USB Cable (USBAUB50CMD), which provides the same convenience as this up-angled cable, but allows you to connect to your Mini USB device from the opposite direction.
profile.reviewText:
This is a very nice, high quality cable, and it does work for charging Garmin Nuvi car navigators with some limitations.  The limitations are that it doesn't work for "Traffic" because the Garmin charging cable is also the traffic antenna, and a USB cable is not.  There is also an issue with a computer (data) symbol showing up on screen when the Garmin Nuvi does a cold boot-up. The latter is an annoyance.

I spoke with Garmin customer support about the annoyance and here's the story:  the Nuvi uses the same mini-USB port for both charging and for data, like map updates, etc.  The way the Nuvi distinguishes between a Garmin data update attempt from a USB cable and an ordinary charging action (cigarette lighter cable) is by measuring the voltage entering the unit from the cable.  A USB port for data operates at 4.75-5.25v 2.1A, but the Garmin cigarette lighter charging cable operates at 10v 2.4Amax.  This means that the USB is charging at a lower voltage than the regular charging cable.  When the Nuvi receives USB voltage, it assumes that a data transfer is being requested by the user.  Garmin does not make a USB cable that works with the Nuvi because of the common port.

The work-around is that the USB voltage can be made to work for charging by removing and re-inserting the USB connector after the computer (data) symbol appears on screen.  (It takes about 30 seconds on my GPS.)  Upon re-plugging the USB, the Nuvi will drop the data symbol and allow the unit to load maps and boot-up normally, albeit charging at an undervoltage.  The USB then operates as a trickle charger, charging slower than the higher voltage regular charging cable.  The computer symbol annoyance does not then reoccur as long as the unit remains booted.  The annoyance will happen again when you next do a cold re-boot and you'll have to pull and re-insert the USB plug again as described above to do the work-around.  Garmin says the problem doesn't occur on all Nuvi units, but does occur a lot of the time.  On my Nuvi 2595LMT it happens most of the time.  You need to understand this when purchasing the cable so you don't think the cable is at fault.  Notwithstanding the annoyance, I use it and rate the cable, for what it is, at five stars.

Don't make the assumption that "Down-Angle" in the product description means the MiniUSB cable points downwards on a Garmin Nuvi GPS; on my Garmin Nuvi 2595LMT, the connector on the GPS is reversed and the "Up-Angle" connector is the correct fit to have the cable point downwards.  The product photos on Amazon correctly illustrate the position of the connector, so refer to the photo, rather than the Up/Down description that is almost meaningless.  The Garmin's Nuvi GPS right-angle connector (the one supplied by Garmin with the GPS) is 180 opposite the direction that StarTech.com refers to as Down-Angle.  The terms "up" and "down" may be unintentionally misleading in these circumstances.  Best procedure would be to look directly at the orientation of the connector on your GPS and match it to the product photo to order the orientation you need, disregarding whatever may be the meaning of up/down in the product description.
profile.summary: Order "Up-Angle" for Garmin Nuvi

profile.description: Take the right way on the highway with nvi 765T, featuring lane assist. This feature guides you to the proper lane for navigation. The 765T adds hands-free calling to the nvi 755T.
profile.reviewText:
I previously reviewed this product and complained that it flashed advertisements on the screen, which I considered objectionable, and that the advertisements could not be turned off.  That information is published elsewhere on the internet from several sources.  Unfortunately, that information is incorrect.  The advertisements CAN be turned off.  Thanks to a very responsive Garmin customer support department, I learned that the "Traffic" reports that help the navigator avoid traffic jams are the source of the advertisements, called "Offers."  The reason the traffic reports are "free" of charge is that they're paid for by the advertisements.  If you reject the traffic reports (I never wanted them to begin with) you can also reject the "Offers" that go with them.  The misimpression that they can't be turned off arises because the "Traffic" icon only appears when the automobile power cord is attached to the unit.  The power cord contains the FM antenna that brings down the traffic reports and the accompanying advertising.  If the power cord/antenna is not attached, the Traffic icon does not appear in the Settings menu.  So, you can only turn off the Offers when the icon is there to do it with, which means the automobile power cord must be attached.  You can't make the selection on battery power or with the AC power cord because the FM antenna is not present to trigger the Traffic icon.

My remaining criticism of the unit based on its failure to display (in large letters at the top of the screen) the approaching cross streets is still valid.  On older model Garmins, the approaching cross streets were prominently displayed, as an assist for people like myself who are getting on in years, and who can't see street signs so well at night anymore.  The 765T and subsequent models (according to a Garmin rep) now only prominently display the name of the street you're traveling on, which is an almost useless piece of information.  At a minimum, it's a waste of valuable screen space.  I don't know why this change was made, but Garmin should consider putting it back the way it was on the Nuvi 200W, for instance, for those of us who have problems reading street signs at night.
profile.summary: Updated review; Advertisements CAN be turned off

profile.description: A great way to be green and get an excellent product is to make your own soda water at home. iSi is the industry leader and our Austrian made chargers guarantee high quality and taste for you.
profile.reviewText:
I want to second "A. Abdine's" review, which perfectly describes how to use the soda siphon correctly.  Use refrigerated water to begin with, have the bottle chilled before charging the water, shake it at least 20 times, and let the bottle sit in the refrigerator for a while before removing the CO2 cartridge, and the bottle works great.  The bottle itself is well-made and holds a full liter of water, even as limited by the "measuring tube" which comes as part of the bottle.  I use "Leland" cartridges, which seem cheaper than the iSi ones because you can buy them in bulk, and the "fizz" is at least what you get in a Pellegrino bottle, though perhaps less than super-carbonated club soda.  The siphon extracts every bit of water from the bottle, so I think the system works exactly as you would expect. This is like any other tool, use it correctly and it will perform as expected.

(February 2, 2011 Update)  I'm still very enthusiastic about this product, but I wanted to add a couple details.  First, if you screw down the CO2 cartridge too slowly, you lose gas as the bottle charges.  Another reviewer suggests cranking your hand around the charging handle and then turning the charging screw in one quick movement.  This works better than how you'd intuitively do it, but you can improve on even this method by holding the bottle in one hand, and the charging handle in the other, and turning BOTH the bottle and the screw, the bottle in one direction and the charging handle in the other.  You lose almost no gas that way.

My last comment is that iSi is a really good company to deal with.  They have a customer service number where real human beings answer the phone, and they respond to your questions helpfully.  I called them to inquire why my 2248 nozzle didn't contain a small metal screen at the front end, while the identical bottles at Williams-Sonoma had screens.  They said the ones fitted with the metal screen gave a "more forceful stream" and otherwise had no particular benefit.  I recently had an opportunity to try one of the metal screened nozzles, and I found that customer service's evaluation was correct; the Williams-Sonoma bottle gave a more forceful stream and a big fizz when it hit the glass, but the result of the "big fizz" show was that the water lost gas quickly in the glass.  It could be useful if you use syrups in the bottom of the glass or for something like mojitos, but I think you could do the same thing with a spoon, with lesser loss of carbonation.  Both nozzles do have some residual dripping of water trapped in the nozzle in the form of bubbles, which is not a defect in design, but rather something I think is inherent in having bubbles that adhere to the inside of any nozzle until they pop, releasing a few drips of water.
profile.summary: Works great if you use it right

profile.reviewText: I don't know whether I received a level with a defective display, or whether it was a fair example of what is being sold, however (in either case) the display on the unit I received had a very narrow view angle, especially when viewing the numbers off-angle on the left side. I ultimately bought a torpedo level with a display suited to my eyesight needs (a Digi-Pas DWL-280 Pro, IP67 waterproof) which had an LED display, rather than a backlit LCD display.  I think LED is much more visible.  Too bad they don't put the same display on a 24" level.  Anyway, I was disappointed with the display on the Hammerhead HLLT24, but otherwise I liked its design and functionality, except I thought the laser dot placement was not so useful as a laser that projects a crosshairs and a line along the wall, so I felt the laser was not as useful as the line lasers on other models. profile.description: The new Perfect Climate line from K&H Manufacturing has reinvented the wheel when it comes to keeping ice free water available in winter ponds. Every K&H de-icer is safe in all ponds, unlike many of the other de-icers available in the market today. Every one of our de-icers can be used as a floating de-icer out of the box or in seconds converts to a submersible de-icer with the click of a button. In the past, all that was readily available were energy gulping 1000 watt to 1500 watt de-icers; pond owners had no choice but to purchase these expensive to run de-icers, even when they didn-foott need it. When it comes to ice free ponds, K&H Perfect Climate is the choice that makes cents.
profile.reviewText:
I'm using the 250 watt version on my pond with about 330 gallons of water and have found it adequate to keep an air hole open in the ice in Northern Colorado, where it only gets really cold (below zero) for a few weeks every winter.  I have an energy efficient pump that recirculates the water, and I remove the float ring and locate the heater on the bottom of the pond near the pump intake.  Reading through all the customer questions and answers given, and many of the reviews, I wanted to make a few comments which might seem obvious, but seem to form the basis of many of the questions.  It's pointless to speculate what wattage will keep a pond clear of ice in the winter if you don't know all the factors, such as how cold and how long the winters are, how deep the pond is, how exposed the pond surface is to winds, how many square feet of pond surface are exposed to the air and wind, how much of the day the pond is exposed to the sun or shade, and myriad other considerations, not the least of which is how "clear" the surface of the pond needs to be to meet your needs or expectations.

If you have goldfish or koi, all you need is a small hole in the ice to winter over the fish.  The more relevant question is how much money do you want to spend in electrical bills to keep the pond open.  The fish go into hibernation in the winter and don't care how cold the water is unless the pond surface freezes over for an extended period or the pond freezes solid.  It's really costly to keep the water temperature at 45 degrees when 33 degrees will do as well.  It's really costly to keep 50 square feet of surface open when 2 feet will do as well.  One reviewer accused the ineffectiveness of the heater for killing all 8 of his koi.  If all his fish died over the winter, something else killed them, not a short-term freeze over of the surface.

In its answer to several of the questions, the heater seller opined that the heater automatically shuts off when the water temperature reaches 40-45 degrees.  Nothing in the manufacturer's  literature that accompanies the heater specifies that.  If that is true, it would only represent the water temperature immediately surrounding the heater thermostat, not the temperature of all the water in the pond unless the pond water was rapidly recirculating.  There may be an emergency shutoff if the heating element is inadvertently run outside of the water, but there isn't a "thermostat" in the normal sense that I can see.  If there were, it would be listed by the manufacturer as a selling point.  You wouldn't want to rely on that anyway because keeping the water at 45 degrees all winter long would be really costly in terms of your electricity bill.

In my pond, we attach the 250 watt heater to a cheap Christmas lights timer and adjust the number of daily running hours to match the amount of visible ice cover as the season progresses.  You don't want to burn 1500 watts an hour when 250 is enough, and you don't want to run the heater 24 hours when 2 hours is sufficient to keep an air hole in the surface.  If you buy a 1500 watt heater, you run it fewer hours each night, and if you buy a 250 watt heater you run it longer, as needed.  Looking at the pond every day or two and running the heater only as needed is the key to both fish welfare and economy of electrical cost.
profile.summary: Keep electric cost in mind

profile.reviewText:
June, 2017 UPDATE.  I ordered another set of these today and added three photos below to illustrate a point I'm trying to make with this update.  The point is that these are very good for what they're designed to do, but they should be considered "expendable," not a life of the paddle purchase if you regularly paddle difficult waters where your grip on the paddle is very tight.  The wear shown in my photos is what you'd expect after two full seasons of ocean and river paddling.  One photo shows not only the typical wear on the nylon covering, but also typical deterioration of the neoprene rubber beneath it, the result of countless compressions and expansions within a very limited area.  The paddle shaft is visible through one of the holes.  Shoes wear out after heavy use, and so it is with these.  I don't fault that.  Think of the damage to my thumb and fingers if the grips were NOT there.  I bought another set because, after reviewing all the alternatives, these are the best on the market.  The wear is identical whether the grip is black or some other color.

Many reviewers complain that these "slip around" on the shaft.  They do slip and that can't be stopped unless you securely tape them in place, as described in my June, 2015 review below.  The photos show how they're taped.  We don't buy these to accessorize the paddle, but rather to counter a specific problem ("paddler's thumb"), so the aesthetics of tape doesn't matter if tape is necessary to keep the grips where they belong.  Having gone through four sets of these, I've tried everything (two-sided carpet tape, rubber cement, etc.) and nothing ultimately has worked for me other than the tape placements shown in the photos.  If the grip slips only .001" with each stroke, after 1000 strokes the grip will have moved an inch.  After 3000 strokes, three inches.  The neoprene rubber "walks" an imperceptible amount with each stroke, but the strokes add-up.  I recommend 3M "Tough" tape because it seems immune to UV sunlight damage, is easy to work with, and it removes easily after long outdoor use without leaving adhesive residue.

Below are my 2013 and 2015 reviews so you can see my thoughts on this product over time.

June, 2015 UPDATE:  I rated these 5 stars when I last reviewed them, but I've reduced that to 3 based on my last pair.  By now, I've had several pairs, purchased at different times over four years.  The quality of manufacture has slipped, and the manufacturer seems to have listened too much to the whiners who complained that the split-shaft version was initially difficult to get onto the paddle shaft.  Well, now they're loose enough to easily slip on, so easy that they slip around too much in use, making them useless as tactile reference points for where to keep your hands on the paddle.  The newest ones move around and twist during each paddle stroke.  You have no choice but to tape them as I suggested (below) in my original review.  The second gripe is that the sewing of the seams on the newest model is poor, leaving a "lump" where there once was a flat seam.  Yes, you can orient the grips to try to minimize the annoyance of the heavy ribbed seams, but it shouldn't be there to begin with.  They should be sewn as they originally were, not as the new ones are.  I'm going to check-out some of the generic knock-offs, which cost half what these do, in case the knock-offs still have some of the qualities these once had.  For me, a pair lasts only one season before the rubber disintegrates at the pressure points, and before the thin nylon fabric covering begins to discolor badly and wear through.

I've used these extensively on my paddle with a straight carbon shaft on both the ocean and flat water, and I like them.
They aren't perfect, but I would never go back to a bare shaft.  They help prevent paddler's thumb, which is the boney knot that develops on the inside of the thumb from holding the paddle shaft too tightly with your control hand.  Yes, they do slip, but I stopped that with some of the new Scotch "Tough" outdoor, UV resistant duct tape. They do get wet and stay wet longer than a bare shaft, which is not a problem if you habitually wear neoprene gloves.  A very slight amount of power is lost from each stroke in compressing the rubber grips, however with all those things admitted, they're still really nice to have and it's better to have them than not.  You can also stop the slipping (as others have said) with a dab of silicon, or two sided carpet tape, or duct tape.  The idea is to protect your hands, and these do that very well.
profile.summary: Good, but quality of manufacture has slipped

profile.description: Just slide a pair of Yakgrips on to the shaft of your take apart paddle and experience all day comfort while paddling. These comfort paddle grips have the cushiest feel and follow the actual curve of your hands to reduce fatigue, prevent blisters and calluses. Yakgrips ease the pressure on your palms and tendons of your hands so you can get a good grip on you paddle for more efficient paddling. Yakgrips are easy to install. Just wet the inside of the Yakgrip and the paddle shaft with water and slide on. The inner gripping design will keep them where you put them. If you want to remove them just put water under them and on the paddle shaft and pull them off. Yakgrips can be left on the paddle - ready for your next journey.

profile.description: This paddle float is designed with an extra large capacity for maximum buoyancy, quick-release buckles for easy attachment to kayak paddles and a clip-on safety tether to eliminate loss in windy conditions.
profile.reviewText: This is dual chambered, which means there are two air chambers and two blow tubes.  The instructions say it is for paddlers "over 150 lbs."  I am well over 150 lbs.  With both bladders inflated, I think this would give you double flotation, so I assume two bladders is not a safety redundancy issue, but rather an option to give big guys increased flotation when needed.  I liked that a lot.  It still rolls into a surprisingly small package that fit well behind my cockpit seat.  The retainer cord wraps around it and has a little loop that keeps it from unrolling.  The instructions advise to keep it "partially inflated" and under the bungies on the deck. I suppose the partial inflation helps hold it under the bungie and insures that it floats after a capsize.  Eh, okay.  I understand that, but with the attachment leash, I think I'll still store it behind the seat to keep unnecessary junk off the deck.  A well-made and well-considered product though.
profile.summary: Surprisingly large float rolls small

profile.description: For Canon PowerShot G12 Digital Camera Screen Only
profile.reviewText: I bought this for my Canon G12 for under four bucks, including shipping.  The product arrived quickly and undamaged in a plain white envelope, with adequate instructions.  The important thing is that there are 3 of them in the envelope, so in case you make a mistake in application the first time, you have two more chances.  A microfiber cloth is included to clean and get dust off the screen before application.  I succeeded in letting a speck of dust get between the plastic film and the screen, so it created a tiny bubble about a tenth the size of a pinhead, in an inconspicuous part of the screen.  I didn't choose to do it over because, like the similar bubble on the screen protector of my cell phone, it reminds me that it IS a screen protector, not the screen, which I'll appreciate when I succeed in getting something gross on the screen and begin to freak out.  This method of selling 3 rather than one in a kit recognizes the reality that the hassle of taking the order and shipping the product is the seller's real cost of the transaction, not the cost of the protective film itself.  So, I'm really happy with the result.  The film fit the screen perfectly.  A similar screen protector saved my Canon SX10 two years ago when insect repellant on my shirt dissolved the paint off that camera. I don't expect to do that again, but . . .
profile.summary: Great for the price and otherwise

profile.description: 100 ea Leland Soda Chargers Seltzer Chargers CO2
profile.reviewText: There's not much to say about soda chargers.  Mine arrived quickly and they weren't substitutes.  What arrived was 10 boxes of 10 Leland soda cartridges, and I've already gone through about 50 of them without any duds.  The flavor of the water is great and they're the perfect size for my iSi one-liter soda bottle, which I also highly recommend as a quality product.  You wouldn't want more fizz for a liter-size bottle.  You should follow the instructions of Amazon reviewers on the iSi Soda Siphon page to get best results, cold, cold water, cold bottle, shake it 20+ times and let the water sit an hour in the fridge with the cartridge still attached, then remove the cartridge before serving.
profile.summary: Nothing to complain about

profile.description: 1080p HDTV: Better picture quality
profile.reviewText: The infrared (IR) sensor that communicates with the remote controls on this model is located just inside the outer margin of the screen, at the extreme bottom right, 5" from the right edge.  My set came with a manufacturing defect that limited the reliable range of the remotes to less than 10 feet.  With a Tivo remote, to less than 6 feet.  Samsung tech support told me 10 feet was an acceptable range for the remote, although it was less than my normal viewing distance.  After a month of trouble-shooting, I found (by close examination with a flashlight) that a section of silver metallic trim tape had detached from the bottom of the screen, fallen down, and was almost completely blocking the IR sensor.  If you buy this television and have the same problem (really limited range for the IR remotes), locate the IR sensor as I described above and check whether you have the same defect.  I was able to lift and reattach the metal tape using only a dull table knife, thus removing the blockage in front of the sensor.  Technical support didn't figure out the cause of the problem after 6-8 phone calls over a month.  I think that Samsung tech support should have immediately, during the first phone call, asked me to check for a blockage of the sensor, but they never did.  I asked on two occasions where the sensor was located; the first rep couldn't find out where it was located, and the second looked it up and gave me the wrong location.  I can't say much for the quality of Samsung tech support.  Otherwise, the set is fine and I generally agree with comments do other reviewers.
profile.summary: Remote control range issue

top_5.description: Perfect For: This carry-on is spacious, lightweight and durable, made for those who test the limits of their luggage. Sized for a 1-5 day trip. You venture to far-flung corners of the globe, places that test the limits of your luggage. Exploration System is the perfect collection and will perform in the harshest conditions. Made with 100 percent recycled eSeries fabrics and backed by our No Matter What(tm) warranty.
top_5.reviewText: I've critically reviewed various Eagle Creek products before, but I always keep buying them.  The quality of manufacture (in Vietnam) is excellent, but the constantly changing product specifications are bewildering and annoying.  Two other reviewers have gone into that, so I won't repeat it.  I just want to point out that the product dimensions advertised on the Eagle Creek website and on Amazon are incorrect.  The product size advertised is the carry-on legal 14 x 22 x 9, however what arrives is clearly labeled 14 x 22 x 10, which is not strictly legal for airline carry-on.  If you feel strongly about playing by the rules, knowing that your luggage is over carry-on size is vexing, even if the airline usually lets you get away with it.  The Pack-it cubes really don't fit as the Eagle Creek illustration suggests.  The cubic inch interior space advertised is also different than shown on the tag attached to the luggage. The 18" shirt folding Pack-it is really excellent, but it doesn't fit against the back wall of the luggage as shown.  It sits much higher on the interior tubes which contain the handle.  The tubes are very solid and create three long rectangular spaces, on either side and between the tubes, useful space but not as shown.  The ad copy needs to be updated, and the Pack-it illustration needs to more fairly show how the Pack-it cubes fit.  That aside, I like the bag and kept it.  The redesigned lid that opens book-style contains about 2" of space that is perfect for carrying a raincoat or dirty laundry.  I'm glad that EC eliminated the dedicated "shoe box" because I think one open compartment is more versatile than a lot of little spaces presumed to be useful by some luggage designer.  The Tamarac 22 is not overburdened with many little exterior "pockets" that compete for space with the interior luggage compartment when calculating the overall carry-on size.  Much of what goes into the little pockets is better kept in the "personal item" (second bag) allowed as carry-on, whether that is a computer bag or a big purse.  So, I'm okay with just the flat travel document pocket and the top-entry zipper to the lid compartment, which is big enough to carry a light coat or raincoat.  The Pack-it cubes (although they don't fit exactly as shown) solve a lot of organizational problems, eliminating the need for dedicated interior spaces.  I like the new, bigger wheels, as they give the piece more ground clearance than the older in-line skate wheels. The retractable identification tag is well protected beneath the side carry handle, keeping it from being accidentally torn off.  The corner protectors and skid plate between the wheels protect the wear points very well.  So this bag is well-built, simple, versatile, but the size is not as advertised.
top_5.summary: Size is not as advertised

top_5.description: New Insect Blocker technology keeps six-legged pests at bay, Omni-Shade offers UPF 30 sun protection, and Omni-Wick advanced evaporation technology keeps you cool, dry, and collected - leaving you free to focus on the adventure at hand. We package all this perfect protection in a functional package complete with strategic venting, convenient roll-up sleeves, and handy zip-closed security pockets for keeping valuables safe and sound.
top_5.reviewText: I bought this and another Permethrin impregnated shirt (ExOfficio) for a two week jungle trip in southern Costa Rica where mosquitoes and other bugs abound, and where it's always hot and very humid.  Both shirts repelled bugs as advertised, so the differences were mainly evident in terms of cut, comfort and appearance.  Having a square cut front and back allows the shirt to be worn inside or outside the pants.  The other shirt had shirt "tails" front and back so, for aesthetic reasons, could only be worn inside the pants.  The body cut was really nice and, most importantly, the COLOR OF THE FABRIC did not significantly change when parts of the shirt were soaked with sweat or water from brushing against wet vegetation.  The shirt looks the same whether it's wet or dry, so you don't look sweaty or wet, even when you are.  In the kaki color, the ExOfficio shirt looked horrible and sticky immediately after putting it on under high humidity, sweaty conditions.  Any fabric that clings and changes color when sweat-soaked  or rainy is really not a good choice,  So this shirt is a good choice if appearance when wet is a factor.  I liked that the rolled up sleeve retainers were internal and only an inconspicuous button was up on each sleeve, rather than a loop as ornamentation on the outside of the sleeve itself.  I found the fabric was cool and comfortable, wet or dry and at all places in between.  This shirt struck me as cooler to wear than the ExOfficio, and after wearing them alternately, I came to wear this one exclusively, which is possible because it's super-light and you can wash it in a bucket or bathroom sink at the end of the day, then put it on again the next morning, still wet  or dry with equal comfort, and do this day after day.  It fits small, so I'd think of buying it one size up, so it fits loose.  You get better moisture control and mosquito protection with a looser fit.
top_5.summary: Stays good looking when wet or sweaty

top_5.description: Special protection with warmth without giving up the feel for the paddle, helping you retain precise feel and control. The fingerless design has a non- slip grip similar to bare hands, wet or dry. Features:  Extreme pre-curve eliminates gripping fatigue  Off-set seams eliminate irritation & pressure points.
top_5.reviewText: I'm buying a second pair of these because my first pair washed out from under my deck bungies and disappeared under the waves.  The smooth rubber of the fingers and palms had begun to disintegrate after about 10 uses, so it wasn't much of a loss.  The gloves worked great while they lasted.  They protected my hands from sun and paddle shaft abuse, however they needed some way of joining them together, like a snap hook or something, and the rubber material on the inside of the fingers and palms should have been more durable.  I bought the second pair simply because these worked well enough and were a known commodity that didn't require shopping.  Fingerless gloves are easier to store in your PFD than fingered ones, and it's easier to operate a camera and a GPS.  In cold weather, I thought they were at least as warm as those with fingers, once they got wet, and they dried a lot quicker.  I'm using a full-fingered set of gloves now, and I think the fingerless ones give you better control and "feel" a lot drier after getting wet than those with fingers.
top_5.summary: Not very durable, but adequate

top_5.description: Handheld VHF, MFG# HX870, 6 Watts transmit power, Integrated GPS, Class D DSC w/ separate receiver, 2.3" display, waypoint navigation, MOB function, submersible, strobe, noise cancelling TX/RX, USB port.
top_5.reviewText:
I bought this to replace an older model Uniden MHS135DSC that had one glaringly bad feature:  The GPS position disappeared from the radio display the instant the transmit key was pressed, displaying the word "Transmitting" in place of the GPS coordinates, just when you needed to see them.  The Standard Horizon HX870 does NOT have that problem.  The GPS coordinates on the SH870 remain on screen during transmissions, so you can read them directly off the screen while talking with the Coast Guard or others, an essential good design feature.  The radio has good sound, probably due to the incoming and outgoing noise suppression.

I'm a sea kayaker, so I wear the radio on my PFD (life vest) all the time.  I returned the SH870 because it didn't easily fit into the VHF radio pocket of my PFD.  The radio body is larger and boxier that I imagined from the photos, with squared-off corners that would eventually rub holes through the nylon of the life vest pocket.  If you're planning to use this radio on a powerboat, this wouldn't be a problem.  Commercial fishermen in British Columbia swear that Standard Horizon radios are excellent equipment, and I believe them, but they're not too concerned about size and boxy design.

Most kayakers and many small boaters won't keep the radio on all day unless they need to use it, or the weather is questionable enough to keep it on for weather alerts.  For such intermittent use, battery life isn't too important because a half hour of actual use per day will last 20 days with a 10 hour battery.  You can selectively turn off various non-essential radio and GPS functions to stretch battery life, so I think battery life is really not an issue for most boaters.

I turned on the SH870 simultaneously with my Uniden.  The SH870 acquired satellites and displayed accurate GPS position coordinates three or four times faster than the Uniden, impressively quickly.  If you keep the radio off when not using it to preserve battery life, you'll get GPS coordinates really fast when you need to turn it on.

There is a little, transparent, spring loaded, hard plastic door that shields the distress button from being accidentally activated.  The door will catch annoyingly on the fabric of the radio pocket of a PFD, giving the impression that it's particularly damage prone.  The similar door on my Uniden is made from flexible flat rubber which, by comparison, doesn't appear nearly as damage prone.

The unit comes with a very comprehensive owner's manual, and the identical manual is available online so you can download it to a cell phone for use in the field.  The manual is clearly written with side-by-side illustrations.  The manual illustrates many features I don't even understand, but which appear to be very useful to commercial fishermen and other professional users.

The extra large white-background LCD screen is easily readable, however I would have liked it better if it were red/orange like most marine radios.  The placement of the menus and buttons are intuitive and easy to use, however I wonder whether a VHF radio really needs a screen that large, as it contributes to the boxiness and thickness of the radio body.  I usually wear neoprene rubber gloves to protect my hands when paddling in cold northern waters, so the radio buttons seemed a little small for use with gloved hands.  If the screen size was smaller, the buttons could have been larger.  The red illumination of the 870 buttons is dimmer than I'm accustomed to.  So overall, I didn't care for the ergonomics of the boxy body, the white background screen, and the dimly lit, small buttons.

A quibbling point is that the charging cradle doesn't have a red/green light that signals when the battery is charged.  You need to turn on the radio and read the battery strength from the LCD screen.  Another less quibbling point is that the AAA battery module is clunky and not well-designed as compared to the equivalent on a Uniden radio.  You can't switch-out the standard rechargeable battery for the AAA module without opening the waterproof seal of the radio itself.  By comparison, the AAA backup battery compartment on a Uniden is watertight sealed and can be switched with the standard rechargeable battery without opening the watertight seal on the radio body.  Opening the watertight seal of the radio body on a kayak deck, with salt water splashing around, is an invitation to fried electronics.  I doubt this would be an issue for power boaters, but it would be for a kayaker or canoeist.  Bottom line, the AAA battery case should be watertight to protect the spare batteries from seawater, and you shouldn't have to compromise the waterproofing of the entire radio to change batteries.

My last point applies to the GPS feature on all DSC-equipped marine radios.  The GPS is mainly there to display your GPS coordinates on the screen, and to serve the DSC function of transmitting your GPS coordinates as part of the automated DSC distress feature.  You could use the GPS to navigate to a waypoint in an emergency, but the radio GPS is not a substitute for a dedicated GPS on the boat.  The HX870 does have an easily-accessed MOB (man overboard) feature that automatically records the GPS coordinates of the place where the MOB is triggered, and it plots a course back to those coordinates, giving the compass bearing and distance to the MOB coordinates, and starts a timer showing time elapsed since the MOB occurred.

There is a lot of discussion about radio "range" in the questions and reviews, as though the power of the radio and sophistication of the electronics were the only issue.  My experience is that geography, position and weather have much greater importance.  Nobody's radio is going to work well in the twisty canyons of Lake Powell or tucked away in a deep cove on the coast.  VHF is line-of-sight.  So is DSC.  The DSC doesn't go any farther than VHF channel 16, so having DSC isn't a substitute for an EPIRB or PLB, which use satellites to transmit your distress call in difficult terrain or far out away from shipping/boating lanes.
top_5.summary: Many great features, some not

top_5.description: Zipper strategically placed on the bottom for durability & ease of use. Easy to attach to the blower & an adjustable shoulder strap for comfort. Simply fill the bag, unzip the bottom & empty into a container. Bottom zip blower vac replacement bag easy to attach to the blower & an adjustable shoulder strap for comfort simply fill the bag, unzip the bottom & empty into a container fits on models 51539, 51549, 51553, 51573, 51587, 51591, 51598, 51599, 51617, 51618, 51609 & 51619
top_5.reviewText: I'm using this on Model 51609.  This model with a bottom zipper works better than the original, which had a side zipper, this because a considerable amount of dust escapes the bag through the zipper.  Very fine dust (as from dried leaves that the impeller chops up and turns into mulch) also escapes through the bag also, so wear a mask when you use it.  The original bag did the same thing.  This is only the cloth bag, not including the plastic collar that attaches it to the vacuum.  To install it, you recycle the original plastic collar, throw away the original cloth bag and replace it with the new one, using a plastic zip tie.  Replacement with the new bag takes about five minutes.
top_5.summary: Better zipper placement than original

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "Tanya Vought is a hopeless romantic. She loves reading, writing, singing and doing crafts with her children. What started as a lifelong dream became reality. Shes overjoyed that readers will get to read her debut, Granted Wishes. She loves her characters sexy and sassy. She lives in Pennsylvania with her husband and two amazing and imaginative children.". The summary of the review text is "Inexplicably amazing storyline with abiding love ending".
output: I received a free copy of this book in exchange for a review, which I'm happy to do. The premise of this book was an incredible tale of immeasurably and everlasting love, despite the fact that many would scoff at the possibility. Two special individuals, Gracelynn and Giovanni come together under mysterious and unbelievable circumstances, and an assumingly angelic event sprinkles them with a warm friendship that builds to abiding love. At first I was a little impatient with the slightly stilted movement of the story and with Gio and Gracie's romantic build, but gradual is often better than flash. With much sadness and heartache on top of each of them, each dealt with it in their own manner, and brought their dented wholeness to the other. It sort of stalled a bit with the long-distance romance, but built to a great crescendo and the epilogue was magical. I'll read more by this author to see how she develops other characters.

profile.description: Always interested in the arts, S. L. Scott, grew up painting, writing poetry and short stories, and wiling her days away lost in a good book and the movies. With a degree in Journalism, she continued her love of the written word by reading American authors like Salinger and Fitzgerald. She was intrigued by their flawed characters living in picture perfect worlds, but could still debate that the worlds those characters lived in were actually the flawed ones. This dynamic of leaving the reader invested in the words, inspired Scott to start writing with emotion while interjecting an underlying passion into her own stories. Living in the capital of Texas with her family, Scott loves traveling and avocados, beaches, and cooking with her kids. Shes obsessed with epic romances and loves a good plot twist. She dreams of seeing one of her own books made into a movie one day as well as returning to Europe. Her favorite color is blue, but she likens it more toward the sky than the emotion. Her home is filled with the welcoming symbol of the pineapple and finds surfing a challenge though she likes to think shes a pro. Find me on Instagram: S.L.Scott Sign up for The Scott Scoop http://bit.ly/2TheScoop
profile.reviewText: First, the guys of resistance and now the Crow brothers - - they just keep getting better!! If you like a good hot, cocky, love-em-and-leave-em guy gets taken down by sexy, confident, woman, you shafts read this.  Tulsa and his brothers are finally in the bugs, touring, along with Faris Wheel, a rising rock band, also a family band.  Shane and Laird Far is, rock out along with their cousin/twin sister lead singer, Nikki Faris, who happens to be the beauty to end all beauties for Tulsa.  The relationship goes from atomic hot to I-just-want -to-know-you warm and cozy to I'm freaking crazy about you, in the blink of an eye. Just like that, it's over and done for Tulsa Crow, as far as notches on bedposts, and emotionless sex with random chicks.  Nikkei Far is becomes his whole world within a few weeks, and his hers.  It's a deep, consuming but passionately committed bind that occurs very quickly but deeply, told in Ms Scott's phenomenal way. One-click this book NOW!!!
profile.summary: Phew, these Crow brothers. Tulsa is king to his queen Nikki!!!

profile.reviewText: I was proudly and graciously provided an ARC for my review, but I would have purchased this book without hesitation!!  There hasn't been an S.L. Scott book that I haven't enjoyed immensely.  In Spark, you meet Jet Crow and his 2 brothers (Rivers and Tulsa) who make up The Crow Brothers Band.  Then you have Hannah Nichols, who, in a crazy moment of time in her life, hooked up with Jet Crow one night only in a night that changes both of their lives.  The characters in Spark are, as in all of Ms Scott's books, so rich well-rounded, and vivid.  When you read that Jet Crow looks down and up Hannah's body, you almost feel that heated look on your own body.  When Hannah re-enters Jet's life, she drops a bombshell on him, and a horrible misunderstanding leads them into a sort of nemesis - united front pull of forces for good's sake.  The coming together of Jet and Hannah, as well as the resolution of the major conflict in their lives was a wonderful read with so many good feels with smiles, frowns, dropped jaw, tingles and heat, and sometimes laughing out loud!!  I am always anxiously awaiting Ms Scott's next release, and catching up on earlier/other ones I've missed before "discovering" this talented and enchanting author!
profile.summary: A thoroughly tingly, funny, hot, and enjoyable story of love, family, and faith in others!!!!

profile.description: New York Times, USA Today, and International bestselling author, E.K. Blair, takes her readers on an emotional roller coaster with her books. A former first grade teacher with an imagination that runs wild. Daydreaming and zoning out is how she was often found in high school. Blair tends to drift towards everything dark and moody and has been noted as 'The Queen of Dark and Twisted'. Give her a character and she will take pleasure in breaking them down, digging into their core to find what lies underneath. Aside from writing, E.K. Blair finds pleasure in music, drinking her Starbucks in peace, and spending time with her friends. She's a thinker, an artist, a wife, a mom, and everything in between.
profile.reviewText: I fell madly for E.K. Blair with Fading/Falling/Freeing trilogy about Ryan, Candace, and Jase, but Bang and Echo showed me the amazing depth and complexity with which Ms Blair writes fabulous emotional stories.  The surprises that she laid out for us in Bang's sequel were stupendous.  But I think the most incredible thing in Echo was the deep, gut-wrenching emotion that both Nina/Elizabeth and Declan experience and convey to one another.  There is so much angst,soulful rage, passion, and every other known emotion bleeding out from these characters.  It's like a death-defying roller-coaster ride of soul-squeezing feeling from beginning to end.  As much as E.K. conveyed a beautiful, tender, devoted love in her first trilogy, she equally lays out an addicted, frenzied, and utterly conflicted adoration in Elizabeth and Declan.  Bravo, Ms Blair, for your ever-amazing talent and brilliance!!
profile.summary: What a true journey of emotional overdose!!!

profile.description: USA TODAY Bestselling author Julie A. Richman is a native New Yorker living deep in the heart of Texas. A creative writing major in college, reading and writing fiction has always been a passion. Julie began her corporate career in publishing in NYC and writing played a major role throughout her career as she created and wrote marketing, advertising, direct mail and fundraising materials for Fortune 500 corporations, advertising agencies and non-profit organizations. She is an award winning nature photographer plagued with insatiable wanderlust. Julie and her husband have one son and a white German Shepherd named Juneau. Currently, Julie has published Searching for Moore, Moore to Lose, Moore than Forever, Bad Son Rising, the Needing Moore Series Boxed Set, Henry's End, Slave to Love and The Do-Over and has works included in Pink Shades of Words 2014 & 2015, Tempting Fate Boxed Set, Intense Boxed Set and Intense 2 Boxed Set.
profile.reviewText: We know that she took some time with this one, and that it took a lot out of her, but Love on the Edge of Time is more than one can describe.  So much vivid history, so much warmth and love that just winds around as you read this incredible masterpiece.  Msg Rich man weaves a remarkable history amongst Schooner Moore's L9 and Zach, while giving you a glimpse of a love so deep and rich you almost can't imagine.  Where the ideas come from becomes overshadowed by how ingeniously she binds it altogether in such an awesome package.  Jesse and Kylie are such a kaleidoscope couple with multifaceted prisms of personality and problems. You truly feel as if you know them and will be running into them any day.  This all is at the hands of literary romance tale-teller Julie Rich man. Bravo, Julie!
profile.summary: Rich man is pure genius!!!

profile.description: M. Mabie lives in Illinois with her husband. She loves reading and writing romance. M. is an active member of the Indie Author Romance Chicks. She cares about politics, but will not discuss them in public. She uses the same fork at every meal, watches Waynes World while cleaning, and lets her dog sleep on her head. M. Mabie has never been accused of being tight lipped or shy. In fact, if you listen very closely you can probably hear her flapping her gums.
profile.reviewText: I had to go back through the first chapter to re-connect after I'd gotten through about 5 chapters.  Why?  Because I was all of a sudden thinking, "wow this is pretty good, what did I miss in the first chapter?"  I think I was distracted.  I was totally hooked by the 2nd chapter, and although I actually sort of guessed Ben's secret, it still tore out my heart when Tatum learned the truth.  Ms Mabie has a wonderful gift for character development.  I loved loved Tate's quirky but hilarious sense of humor, and Ben's easy-going, sexy manner.  The whole thing with "the Devons" was truly gifted.  And the hippie parentals were such an amusing add.  I was a little disappointed to not learn a little more about Tate's work PA, Neil, but hopefully we'll learn more in another book.  I am anxious to get started on "Bait," and to get to meet her in one week at the Little Rock Book Jam!!  I really like that this story deals with love overcoming a huge obstacle, and the loving way it ended, especially the epilogue.  And the fact that this is the author's first book is utterly amazing.  She's got a bright future!!
profile.summary: Wonderful first book - a true romance HEA!!!

profile.description: S.L. Scott is a New York Times and USA Today Bestselling Author. She has a degree in Journalism and is the author of the novel, Naturally, Charlie, A Prior Engagement, The Welcome to Paradise Series,and several best selling novellas, including Sleeping with Mr. Sexy and Morning Glory--all currently available on Amazon. Pursuing her passion for telling stories, she spends her days escaping into her characters, letting them lead her on their adventures. She is a Contributor to Huffington Post as well as writes for her own blog along with several other popular sites. Travelling, music festivals, and surfing are a few of her hobbies she loves, but she doesn't get to enjoy on a regular basis. She has an obsession with movies, a varied taste in books, and collects Fitz & Floyd teapots. With a memory full of useless trivia facts, and a Keurig addiction, she loves a fun night in with her family as much as a loud night out with her friends. Scott lives in the lively city of Austin with her husband, two young sons, and two Papillons, enjoying life in the beautiful hill country of Texas.
profile.reviewText: I tried to figure out how to rate a 4.5 but couldn't  I loved every single thing about this audio book - - the storyline, the narrator, Alexandria Watts, the humor, the heat, the HEA.  I was delighted to receive a gift of the audio book for The Resistance from Ms Scott, and am more than happy to leave this review for others to use.  I highly recommend the audio book.  I'm going to order the digital copy for my Kindle to re-read in my leisure.  I loved how the unassuming but beautiful Holliday Hughes seemingly tamed the hot rockstar, Jack Dalton aka Johnny Outlaw, head singer for the band The Resistance.  The only 0.5 star thing that sort of disillusioned the naive, pie-in-the-sky part of me is how stubborn and thoughtless Dalton could be to Holliday, leaving her hanging.  But, in thinking it through, I believe that his lifestyle and disillusionment in "normalcy" was more part of that behavior than his not caring for or loving her enough.  Ms Scott has become one of my favorite go-to authors, and while I have a couple of the audio versions of the many books of hers I own, I'd love to eventually get them all.  She rarely if ever fails to give an awesome HEA, she knows knows how to describe desire and attraction and genuine selfless, all-encompassing LOVE, which is why most of us read the romance genre.  I advise all romance/HEA lovers to read and/or hear The Resistance!!
profile.summary: A nearly ideal recipe for sweet, unassuming female tames wild, hot rocker guy!!!

profile.description: Kim Holden lives in Denver, CO with her husband and their son. She works by day, writes by night (and any spare moment in between), and daydreams constantly about imaginary characters, and settings, and plots ...
profile.reviewText: Kim Holden was born with this awesomeness and incredible ability to put words together in such a way that you are transported into the soul and completeness of fictional characters.  Characters who mesh into the chromosomes of your being and the veins of your heart.  The title truly truly says it -- All of It.  Not one time did I ever think of Dimitri as a 16-year old boy.  He was a mature, wise, and complete a young man as I've ever met.  The way he surrounded the wholeness of Veronica (Ronnie) was beyond comprehension, so the surprise at the end, while not totally unexpected, nearly destroyed my heart.  This couple was swathed in a closeness for which every couple should jealously yearn.  The way Msg Holden describes and incorporates such love into the reader's heart is her gift.  Since the first paragraph of Bright Side I read several years ago, I do not hesitate to one-click as fast as my brain-to-finger comprehension will allow any book she writes.  And then she adds Phoenix, which takes what little bit of sanity I have remaining and magnifies and expands it so unrelenting.  Anyone who loves to read relationship, maturity, selflessness, adoration, and timeless love MUST read this book!!
profile.summary: Beyond words that I am inadequate to form!!!

profile.description: Amy Harmon is a Wall Street Journal, USA Today, and New York Times Bestselling author. Her books have been published in eighteen languages, truly a dream come true for a little country girl from Utah. Amy Harmon has written thirteen novels, including the USA Today Bestsellers, Making Faces and Running Barefoot, and the bestselling historical, From Sand and Ash. Her novel, A Different Blue, is a New York Times Bestseller. Her novels The Bird and the Sword and From Sand and Ash were Goodreads Best Books of 2016 and 2017 finalists.
profile.reviewText: From the very first chapter of the very first Amy Harmon book I read some time ago, I've been a believer.  She knows how to gently bring the reader into the silken threads of her story, wrapping you in the complexity and layers of plot and characterization.  By the final paragraph you know each person and each sub-plot like you know your hand. Noah, Cora and Mercedes' story was an awesome journey through time, building like a snowball, gathering twigs and leaves of characters, journeys and mazes, giving you emotion after thrilling emotion.  You know the good part is coming, and that it will cover you all over like warm caramel, and then it's their with all its clickable yumminess.  Noah, Mer, Gia, and the rest all clipped up like a sweet little paper doll.
profile.summary: Msg Harmon never fails to deliver

profile.description: New York Times and USA Today Bestselling author K. Bromberg writes contemporary novels that contain a mixture of sweet, emotional, a whole lot of sexy and a little bit of real. She likes to write strong heroines and damaged heroes who we love to hate and hate to love. Shes a mixture of most of her female characters: sassy, intelligent, stubborn, reserved, outgoing, driven, emotional, strong, and wears her heart on her sleeve. All of which she displays daily with her husband and three children where they live in Southern California. On a whim, K. Bromberg decided to try her hand at this writing thing. Since then she has written The Driven Series (Driven, Fueled, Crashed, Raced, Aced), the standalone Driven Novels (Slow Burn, Sweet Ache, Hard Beat, Down Shift), and a short story titled UnRaveled. She is currently working on new projects and a few surprises for her readers. She loves to hear from her readers so make sure you check her out on social media.
profile.reviewText: I simply do not know how it took me this long t devour this series.  The probably ARE enough word to describe the emotions that flood one while reading and savoring this novel -- I just don't know them all.  What romance-reading woman doesn't search and single the story that gives every single component of deep, immense, near-perfect example of rue, selfless abiding love? Doesn't provide every sigh-inducing magnetic confession and revelation whispered in her ear by a devilishly hunk of man??? Ms Bromberg gifts it all to us with a big red bow of spice, erotic pleasure, twinkling wit and humour, with all the parts of romance we never even thought to desire.  I believe the author may just be "the whole alphabet" of romance writing!!
profile.summary: The checkered flag of romance reading!!!

profile.description: Mia Sheridan is a New York Times, USA Today, and Wall Street Journal Bestselling author. Her passion is weaving true love stories about people destined to be together. Mia lives in Cincinnati, Ohio with her husband. They have four children here on earth and one in heaven. Mia can be found online at www.miasheridan.com or www.facebook.com/miasheridanauthor.
profile.reviewText: Mia Sheridan is one my very very top favorite authors.  Each of her books is a prize in and of itself when it comes to the emotions, rollercoaster, plunge-into-the-lake-of fire love between a man and woman.  Each of her books takes me as a woman to a place where I am adored, treasured, loved like no other.  Grayson was one where so much of the first half of the book was so negative and where the deepness and darkness of Grayson's early life dictated so many of his decisions with Kira, and yet Kira, with all her goodness, accepted Grayson for the broken man he was, and loved him regardless.  But when the love of someone so special as Kira finally penetrates into Grayson's soul, boy did he embrace his love for her as only Mia Sheridan can tell.  One of the best things I love about Mia's books are her Epilogues.  You get such a warm & fuzzy picture of how everything turns out and how special their relationship is, in each situation.  Her books should NOT be passed over!!!
profile.summary: Mia Sheridan does it for me everytime!!!

profile.description: New York Times and USA Today bestselling author Nina Lane writes about a passionate, profound love that can overcome all obstacles. Originally from California, she holds a PhD in Art History and an MA in Library and Information Studies, which means she loves both research and organization. She also enjoys traveling and thinks St. Petersburg, Russia is a city everyone should visit at least once. Although Nina would go back to college for another degree because she's that much of a bookworm and a perpetual student, she now lives the happy life of a full-time writer. Visit Nina at: ninalane.com
profile.reviewText: This final installment of Liv and Dean's epic/awesome/super romantic/hot & steamy/roller-coaster/romantic story could not have been more perfect.  I could never have thought of all the twists, turns, angst, intense emotional ride that Nina Lane gave us in this most marvelous book.  A reader truly FELT every depth of the emotion written on the pages.  The tears flowed effortlessly and often, sometimes happy, sometimes sad or melancholy, but they flowed, especially knowing this was the end.  The frustration for Dean in his ever abiding need to take care of anything and everything that brings Liv unhappiness was so palpable you could feel it.  The frustration for Liv in knowing that she wished she could help Dean while fighting everything dark and looming herself was like nothing I'd ever imagined.  All the explanations and tying of loose ends, and bringing conclusions to each and every character we've loved right along with Liv & Dean was almost magical, certainly if not genius!!  I know that she'll want a bit of a break after writing such an highly-emotional and heart-gripping finale, but I cannot wait to see what Ms Nina has in store for us in the coming months and years!!  Every part of me congratulates Ms Nina for her ultimate success with this most fabulous series, and my gratitude for being able to touch hearts and souls so beautifully with each installment, each chapter and word!!!
profile.summary: The absolute finale in perfection to the most awesome series!!!

profile.description: Julianne MacLean is a USA Today bestselling author of numerous historical romances, including The Highlander Trilogy with St. Martins Press and her popular American Heiress Series with Avon/Harper Collins. She also writes contemporary mainstream fiction, and her recent release The Color of Heaven was a digital bestseller. She is a three-time RITA finalist, and has won numerous awards, including the Booksellers Best Award, the Book Buyers Best Award, and a Reviewers Choice Award from Romantic Times for Best Regency Historical of 2005. She lives in Nova Scotia with her husband and daughter, and is a dedicated member of Romance Writers of Atlantic Canada. Please visit Juliannes website for more information.
profile.reviewText: As romance book "junkie," I inhale all things romance and HEAs.  This one was a recommendation by a book review blog I discovered on Facebook that has never let me down on recommendations, so I thought I'd step out of my "norm" and go for it.  I can't describe how happy I am that I did take that step.  My bucket list contains reading everything written by Ms MacLean, which will be a slow process due to finances.  How she is able to take all these kaleidoscope colored strands of characters, settings, pieces and parts of life and weave them into such a gloriously amazing story that just comes together, makes perfect sense and awes the emotions is beyond me!  When all the pieces come together, the picture is just so inspiring and lifting.  A believer myself, I've never given a lot of thought to "the other side," but this story has allowed me to be okay thinking that my beloveds who have moved on truly are watching over me and care about what happens to me.  I've never had an experience such as what Sophie had, but I'm aware of the possibility of our lives weaving in and out of present, past and future to shape who and what we become.  I've already got another book in this series on my Kindle and hope to experience more of what Ms MacLean's mind and imagination creates on the page and in my heart!
profile.summary: A beautiful and glorious charge to the soul and heart!!!

top_5.description: Always interested in the arts, S. L. Scott, grew up painting, writing poetry and short stories, and wiling her days away lost in a good book and the movies. With a degree in Journalism, she continued her love of the written word by reading American authors like Salinger and Fitzgerald. She was intrigued by their flawed characters living in picture perfect worlds, but could still debate that the worlds those characters lived in were actually the flawed ones. This dynamic of leaving the reader invested in the words, inspired Scott to start writing with emotion while interjecting an underlying passion into her own stories. Living in the capital of Texas with her family, Scott loves traveling and avocados, beaches, and cooking with her kids. Shes obsessed with epic romances and loves a good plot twist. She dreams of seeing one of her own books made into a movie one day as well as returning to Europe. Her favorite color is blue, but she likens it more toward the sky than the emotion. Her home is filled with the welcoming symbol of the pineapple and finds surfing a challenge though she likes to think shes a pro. Find me on Instagram: S.L.Scott Sign up for The Scott Scoop http://bit.ly/2TheScoop
top_5.reviewText: First, the guys of resistance and now the Crow brothers - - they just keep getting better!! If you like a good hot, cocky, love-em-and-leave-em guy gets taken down by sexy, confident, woman, you shafts read this.  Tulsa and his brothers are finally in the bugs, touring, along with Faris Wheel, a rising rock band, also a family band.  Shane and Laird Far is, rock out along with their cousin/twin sister lead singer, Nikki Faris, who happens to be the beauty to end all beauties for Tulsa.  The relationship goes from atomic hot to I-just-want -to-know-you warm and cozy to I'm freaking crazy about you, in the blink of an eye. Just like that, it's over and done for Tulsa Crow, as far as notches on bedposts, and emotionless sex with random chicks.  Nikkei Far is becomes his whole world within a few weeks, and his hers.  It's a deep, consuming but passionately committed bind that occurs very quickly but deeply, told in Ms Scott's phenomenal way. One-click this book NOW!!!
