top_5.description: Finnegan Begin Again is a 1985 made-for-HBO original romantic comedy film starring Mary Tyler Moore and Robert Preston. The movie was filmed in Richmond, Virginia[1] and premiered in February 1985 before being released on video
top_5.reviewText:
This is one of my favorite movies, ever since I first watched it on HBO decades ago.  It is a movie you can watch with just about anyone and not worry about offending.  Robert Preston plays a former investigative reporter whose career has entered the doldrums as he reaches retirement age.  He takes over a column with advice to the lovelorn, but his advice is basically for them to snap out of it and stay with their spouses.  The truth is not romantic, though, and the incoming letters dwindle.

He meets Mary Tyler Moore's character and in a way, becomes one of those lovelorn persons himself, which allows him to be more gentle in his advice.  That is just one part of the plot, however, mostly the story revolves around these two characters as they get to know each other and help each other bring their respective messy lives in order.

The movie is an intelligent romantic comedy, both funny and romantic, with interesting lesser characters especially featuring a superb performance by the actress who plays Preston's ailing wife.

I recorded this on VHS back when it ran, and hung onto it because I liked it, and then transferred it to DVD when I embraced that technology.  The picture quality isn't great, but now that I see it was never released on DVD I am glad to have it.  The reviews of the VHS quality sold here are not very favorable.  But do watch it if you haven't already, and watch it again if you have seen it..
top_5.summary: Wonderful funny and romantic movie about a May/September romance

top_5.description: the words of Rod McKuen and the music of Anita Kerr
top_5.reviewText:
This is not my favorite Rod McKuen/Anita Kerr (San Sebastian Strings) joint effort - 'The Sea" takes that prize. But "Soft Sea" is the first one by them that I owned. Decades ago I heard the song "Body Surfing with the Jet Set" on a compilation pop album and it was so different from the other songs, I sought out the album.  It was New Age music before it seemed like there was New Age music. So I bought it and that led me to the other albums in The Sea series.

These are gentle song-poems mostly, though some of them are a bit more spirited. I wouldn't say it is background music in the way ambient music or say - Winston Marsalis can be. It is more mood music for me. I play it when I am in the mood to feel melancholic.  I don't mean full on melancholia as in sad or depressed, but rather that hollow feeling when you are missing your partner, for example, and you hear a song that makes you smile even as you miss them. Or perhaps it makes you appreciate them more.  I write novels in my spare time, and this music also helps clear my mind sometimes when I am stuck on moving my story along.

If you are unsure whether you want to take the plunge, search for "soft sea mckuen" on YouTube and you can give a listen to a few of the songs from the series of albums.  By the way, it is not Rod McKuen who narrates most of his poems, but rather the husky-voiced actor Jesse Pearson.
top_5.summary: Mood Music (romantic? gentle melancholia?)

top_5.description: After discovering her boyfriend is married, a woman tries to get her ruined life back on track. But when she accidentally meets the wife he's been cheating on, she realises they have much in common, and her sworn enemy becomes her greatest friend. When yet another affair is discovered, all three women team up to plot mutual revenge on their cheating, lying, three-timing ex. Hilarious comedy starring Cameron Diaz, Leslie Mann and Kate Upton.
top_5.reviewText:
At this time there are 1400 reviews of this movie, so I am not going to go into a lot of detail.  Besides, there are some twists in the story, and I wouldn't want to give anything away.  What I will say is that my wife and I started watching this and it seemed to be a stereotypical movie about a cheating husband, and we had our doubts that we would stick with it as it seemed like there must only be two or three directions it could take.

But the movie quickly took a turn that felt rather fresh and new - quite a feat in the romantic comedy genre.  There were plenty of laughs and the developing chemistry between the women was fun to watch.  Having said all that, I will admit that after the twists in the story were played out and the movie settled into its ending, we thought the very end was rather predictable and uninteresting, compared to the rest of the movie.  But really, that was just the last two minutes so it's not like it affected how much we enjoyed the movie.  In a genre like rom-com, it is the chemistry of the stars and high quality writing that leads to quality, and this movie has both.
top_5.summary: Finally a new twist to a romantic comedy

top_5.description: Inspired by a true story, Al Pacino stars as aging 1970s rocker Danny Collins, who can't give up his hard-living ways. But when his manager (Christopher Plummer) uncovers a 40-year-old undelivered letter written to him by John Lennon, he changes course with the help of a new friend (Annette Bening) and embarks on a heartfelt journey to rediscover his family, find true love and begin a second act.
top_5.reviewText:
Although I have enjoyed a lot of Al Pacino's work, I watched this because of Annette Bening.  She sparkled in The American President and Regarding Henry.  This is a different sort of role than those. She seems to almost disappear behind glasses and a demure attitude.  A friend who watched it with us thought at first she was Diane Keaton, except she was too young to be her.  Pacino's role, though he blusters and raises his voice a lot, was a bit restrained for him also - as it was supposed to be.  After all, this story concerned a man whose whole life had been all about him - his pleasures, his needs, but now he was focusing outside himself. Both actors filled their roles well and there was enough chemistry between them to make you root for them.

In a way I think the movie was hijacked by Bobby Cannavale, who plays his son. His is a layered performance.  He could have easily gotten lost in the anger towards Danny Collins that boiled over at times, but the decades of anger were balanced out just enough by the love of his family, which always showed through. That made the last third of the movie believable.

This isn't one those movies I will want to watch again and again, but it is a simple story told well.  It tells us at the beginning that it is sort of based on a true story, and the real "Danny Collins" is shown in the end credits.  They obviously added a lot to make the movie, but they could have gone crazy with it but didn't.
top_5.summary: A simple story told well

top_5.description: Anne Hathaway portrays a young Jane Austen in love in Miramax Films' Becoming Jane, the imaginative and witty romantic comedy about the great untold romance that inspired one of English literature's most celebrated authors. Also starring James McAvoy, Academy Award(R) winner Maggie Smith and Academy Award(R) nominees James Cromwell and Julie Walters, this is an enchanting tale of sense and sensibility, pride and prejudice, aspiration and inspiration as an eligible young woman of the early 19th century dreams of doing the unthinkable - marrying for love.
top_5.reviewText:
If you are a Jane Austen fan you will already know this, but there is quite a cottage industry around her these days. By this I don't just mean that her books get made into movies or TV series every ten years or so, but authors are also busy out there producing sequels to her books, or alternate versions, or otherwise expanding on her works.  This movie is another product of that industry.  It seems we just can't get enough of Austen. (For good reason - she is that good and she left us so little of herself.)

The people who made this movie aren't pretending it is an accurate portrayal of her life as a young Jane falling in love and embarking on her writing career - in the description it is called a "cinematic imagining" of her life.  It is clever in its own way as it suggests that elements from her book Pride and Prejudice were drawn from this early romantic experience. So if the plot seems vaguely familiar to you fans, that is no accident.

I found the movie entertaining enough. I was irritated at first that Jane would fall for this guy, but again, look at Pride and Prejudice.  The sharp wit and intelligence that Austen displays in her books is on display here in Jane, so that is as it should be.  I like her family and how they interact: even her mother becomes a more rounded character during the course of the movie after a harsh beginning.

I have read a lot of snarky or dismissive one-star reviews of "Becoming Jane" on this site, and believe me, if you want a list of one-star movies I can provide it, and they will all be much, much worse than this film.  It's real sin rests on not being accurate, which is the lamentable fate of any story of Austen's life because we know so little. Just relax and enjoy it for what it is: a half-decent entry in the ongoing Austen cottage industry.  (For a wonderful and imaginative example of this, see also Lost in Austen.)
top_5.summary: A decent imagining of Austen's early romance

input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "5.0" for a product with description "Felicia Tatum was born and raised in Tennessee. She began writing at a young age, and finally pursued her passion this past year. The White Aura is her first published novel. She is the mommy to a daughter and a kitty. She enjoys reading and crafting in her free time.". The summary of the review text is "Spoiler Free - SERIES REVIEW".
output:
Amazing. Phenomenal. Addicting. THE WHITE AURA SERIES by Felicia Tatum is a MUST, especially if you're a fan of YA Paranormal Romances! With twists and turns that had me guessing what would happen next, these books were true page turners. I was hooked from the very beginning and they held my attention all the way through.

Felicia Tatum developed fantastic characters that were easy to understand and relate to. Her writing style was, to me, impeccable. The main reason I loved it so much was because it allowed me to see everything through the characters eyes. Aside from the books having different POVs, the amount of details provided created an über clear picture of the scenes unfolding, and yet, they weren't wordy, which is something I hate in books. Honestly, this series felt balanced  another huge PLUS! The books had a bit of everything: passion, drama, suspense, and of course, paranormal aspects, without going over-board or over-doing it.

the moment I saw Livvie, everything changed.

Scotts family had been cursed many, MANY years ago. If they met their heartmate before they (the heartmate) were 17 years and 6 months old, they would die the moment they turned 18. And thats where the problem started. You see, Scott met Olivia (Livvie) when she was 16-ish, only she didn't know him. The moment he laid eyes on her, he knew she was his soulmate. He knew she was meant for him. Being a 5th generation sorcerer meant he had a few great powers, thought, one which included dream-walking.  So he began visiting Livvie in her dreams, waiting for the day she could meet him in real life and fall in love with him.

Thinking she was going insane, Livvie didn't tell anyone, not even her best friend, about Mr. Sexy, the boy shed been dreaming about for the past year. Now 17 years old, Livvie was experiencing things that were making Scotts waiting plan a whole lot more difficult. She was no longer safe.

Waiting plan ABORTED.

They met.

Before Livvie was 18.

A LOT happened to Scott and Olivia. A LOT. Upon meeting, now it was a battle  in more ways than one  not only against the curse, but other enemies. Like I mentioned before, Felicia Tatum delivered twists, turns, and many surprises which you have to experience for yourself, so I won't go into any of the details. But know this  the buildup was amazing!  I seriously enjoyed this series from beginning to end and I cannot wait to read Sadies book: SCORNFUL SADIE!

FIVE STARS to The White Aura, The Vessel, Devlins Descendant, and Unbound Destinies!

profile.description: I'm a book nerd turned writer who loves the 'Hap-pily Ever After' mixed with a bit of suspense, drama, and the occasional cliffhanger! My love of books has brought me on my writing journey. I began writing my first book in July 2012 and since that time I have created 2 series. The first series 'The Reunion Series' debuted in November 2012 and two books followed. My new series 'The Shore Series debuted in March 2014 and claimed Amazon Best Selling status shortly after the release of the first book in the series. There will be continuations of the Shore Series and you never know when a secret project from me may pop up!
profile.reviewText:
"I wanted to hang on to thirty-nine forever and I was fully prepared to do so."

You know a book is truly wonderful when you instantly - fully - connect to the main character and the plot. I fell in love with 39 & Holding from the very first page. I laughed (full on belly-laugh), swooned, squirmed, sighed....... I LOVED it.

MR Joseph's writing style was so damn natural and realistic!!! The things the heroine, Greer, said and thought??? OMG!! Hilarious!!! I've said and thought those things at least once throughout my life!! I will even go on and say that I'm sure most women have too! They may deny it, but come on!! They soooo have - especially when dealing with an ex!!!

Getting over a divorce isn't always a piece of cake, especially when infidelity is a factor, and MR Joseph did an AMAZING job developing this throughout the book. Greer's life changed in a matter of minutes when she came across a very eye-opening email in her husband's inbox. Suffice it to say, her marriage ended. At 39 years old, she found herself divorced with two kids.

"My dear, love isn't measure in length of time. All that counts is when you feel it, grab it. Time is nothing but numbers on a clock."

Enter Dr. Doughnuts. Nick...oh, Nick. SO YUMMY! My goodness, he was perfect!!!! He definitely changed Greer's life in more ways than one. He was exactly what she needed. She actually started living - all thanks to him. I loved reading her reactions to all the emotions and situations that came along with dating and falling in love, especially when she had sworn she wouldn't go through any of this just to avoid the risk of getting hurt...again. Greer's internal battles/dialogue and conversations with her friends were SO realistic and at times, hilarious! It was all very well written and thought out. Mad props to the author! You see, Greer didn't just give herself fully to Nick. She had to think about her kids, her life, and other factors (read the book and you will know what I mean) before actually going for it. So like I said, MR Joseph really did a wonderful job in developing their relationship and characters realistically.

"There's not many imperfect things about you, Greer, but the things that are, they're the things I love the most."

This was truly a wonderful read that I enjoyed from start to finish (LOVED the ending!!!!). It was sassy, funny, hot, and at times, even emotional. I would definitely recommend this book to anyone that loves a good and light romance with some very sexy spice! FIVE STARS!!

"The unexpected things  are the gifts we should cherish the most."
profile.summary: realistic, funny, and sexy!

profile.reviewText:
This series keeps getting better and better! Seriously. Problems and situations seem to be getting more emotional and I am LOVING it. From the other two books in this series, I knew Jesse and Jamie Lynn had a past together, so I was curious to learn just what had happened that caused them to part ways when they so clearly loved each other.

Jamie Lynn had her fair share of issues that made her who she was now. She was a bit closed off but she had her reasons. Very valid reasons. And Jesse? Well, his story was a bit heart-breaking. When both main characters are broken, there is a lot of room for emotional angst and if you've been reading my blog for some time now, then you know that makes me super happy!

In order to move forward, Jesse and Jamie Lynn had to overcome a lot of insecurities and outside forces that were standing in the way of their own happily ever after. The road there was very interesting, angsty, sexy, and it had my full attention the entire time.

Now, to say I want the next book would be an understatement. It will be Rocco's book and I am beyond intrigued! You see, AJ Renee sure loves teasing her readers!

FIVE STARS!
profile.summary: Best one in the series so far!

profile.description: Cassandra doesnt remember a time when she wasnt writing. In fact, the first time she was published was when she was seven years old and won a contest to be published in an American Girl Doll novel. Since then Cassandra has written more novels than she can count and put just as many in the circular bin. Her personal goal with her writing is to show the reader the characters stories through their dialogue and actions instead of just telling the reader what is happening. You can find her at: Instagram and Twitter: @cgiovanniauthor Facebook.com/cassiegiovanni Goodreads Don't forget to sign up for her newsletter for the latest book news!
profile.reviewText:
4.5 Stars! Between unpacking (we bought a house!) and the holidays, my reading time SUFFERED...greatly. Much to my dismay, it took me quite a bit longer to finish reading this book. Boo, I know!! But finally, after sneaking in some much needed and overdue reading time, I finished!

I must say, I really enjoyed Danny and Sky's *heartwarming* story. From their teenage years, they shared an intense and undeniable connection that would undoubtedly withstand the test of time. I knew it. Their chemistry only got stronger as the years passed and while they both had deep scars, they only brought them closer. They bonded even more. While situations caused Danny to not be there for Sky at a very crucial and heartbreaking time, he was there to help her heal. And in many ways, she was as well for him.

One of the things I love most about Cassandra's writing is how she not only tells us a story, but she shows us one. She creates storylines and secondary characters that bring everything full circle...that bring a book to life. You can't help but feel emotionally invested in these different journeys and root for happy endings. I was walking alongside the characters through every up and down, twist and turn. I've noticed that always happens while I'm reading one of Ms. Giovanni's novels.

I cannot wait to see more of these characters! Seriously! Joey, Aaron, Zack-Such great guys! Funny, witty, sexy, down to earth, and completely realistic and relatable. They were my "brothers" too! One other thing I loved about them was that while they were in a band and they'd gotten pretty famous, there wasn't any made up or unnecessary drama that's usually involved in books with musicians. Issues within this book went beyond drama. They were real, heartbreaking situations that brought all of the characters together.

All in all, a great read and one I recommend you pick up!
profile.summary: Great story, as always!!

I am addicted to this series! Totally, completely and irrevocably HOOKED. Im also in love with the characters and the general story they all create. Brandy L Rivers is an author you simply cannot miss!

While this is book #.5 in the series, I started with In Too Deep which is book #1 and then jumped to book #5, Mending Scars. However, Ive now gone back to the beginning and am now reading/listening to them in order, and I must say, my connection is even stronger.

The story was literally brought to life and I loved every minute of it. I did not want to stop listening to it! I took my iPad and headphones everywhere and listened to the book every chance I got! AMAZING. Unputdownable!

Now, about this amazing story

The best thing Jess ever did was moving to Edenton and getting a fresh, new start away from her alpha. She had made the drunken mistake of sleeping with him and his cockiness only got worse. He never really valued her to begin with, he only wanted to own her. Edentons alpha, Slater, was a whole different story. While he wasn't looking to start anything with any of the wolves in his pack, he couldn't help but feel a very strong connection to Jess from the very beginning.

Despite them both fighting their very strong urges, they were meant to be togetherone way or another. Now, you must understand, Jess was also a physic, so while she saw Slater in her future, she wasn't entirely aware of everything that was about to happen. And let me tell you  New Beginnings was action-packed with a perfect balance of drama and hotness! Every scene kept me fully invested, wanting more! And being able to hear the story, made it even more real.

This books, this entire series, is a MUST READ. Top recommendation to any romance reader  whether or not you read Paranormal, you need to check these gems out! FIVE STARS!

profile.reviewText:
Ever since Brandy L Rivers popped my Paranormal Romance cherry, I've been a huge fan of hers. With each book that she releases, my level of stalking increases. No joke.

Brandy L Rivers is the queen of the Paranormal Romance genre!

Both of her PNR series, Others of Edenton and this one, Others of Seattle, are a MUST READ. While most of the books can be read as standalone novels, I would highly suggest you read them all in order, starting with book #0.5 in the Others of Edenton series. There are SO MANY uh-ma-zing characters that you can't help but fall in love with. I am curious to see a family tree, of sorts, with ALL the characters in BOTH series and how they all connect!! It would be a HUGE diagram for sure!! :)

One thing about Ms. Rivers that I truly admire is her ability to make readers love even the not-so-loveable characters! They might in some books be those characters we all love to hate or are unsure of, but then....then, they get their stories. Another thing I really love about these books is how easy it is for me to get lost in this paranormal world. I'm always fully captivated by everything and connect with all the characters from the very beginning!

Storm Wrath was a fantastic addition to the Others of Seattle series. I LOVED KELLAN AND ZOE!! I was rooting for them from page one and I'm happy with how it all wrapped up! From curses to awful parents, this book was full of page-turning paranormal events! Now, like I mentioned above, I would suggest you read this series in order. Just trust me on this. Your connection to the series as a whole will be even deeper. I am seriously planning on taking a month to read ALL the books (re-read most of them) in order. Just the thought of this makes me all kinds of excited!! FIVE STARS!
profile.summary: The queen of the PNR genre does it again!!

profile.description: Book by Madden-Mills, Ilsa
profile.reviewText:
Wow. Okay, I don't feel like this review can do this book any justice in the awesomeness department, but I'm sure going to try. Very Bad Things was even better than I ever imagined. Deep, sexy, passionate, angst-ridden, and downright PHENOMENAL. I felt an emotional connection not only with the book, but with all the characters. I was hooked from the very beginning, all the way till the end. Loved it.

To say theres more to Nora Blakely than meets the eye, would be the understatement of the year! To everyone, she was this perfect student from the perfect, high-class family. Boy, was that far from the truth. Reality was not as nice to Nora as everyone thought.

If you study someone long enough, youll find out their secrets.

At first, it may seem like Nora does and says things just because shes acting out or looking for attention. But no. Everything goes way deeper. As I kept on reading, I realized that her actions were more like reactions to secrets she kept inside. Secrets that were slowly eating her up. Destroying her. So, she just reached a point where she gave up pretending.

Bad decisions can make some darn good memories.  Nora

The moment Nora and Leos eyes found each other for the first time, they had an instant connection, and as a reader, I felt it. It was incredible electrifying, even. Leo Tate is one swoon worthy man!! *sigh* Having lost his parents, he took over the dad role for his younger brother. Moving from LA to Texas, Leo enrolled Sebastian in the Briarcrest Academy, which is where he met the girl that would change his lifeNora.

Shes this beautiful chaos.  Leo

A LOT of things happened a lot which of course, I won't mention because I like to keep my reviews spoiler-free. All I will say is, prepare yourself for one heck of a rollercoaster ride! Leo and Nora didn't go from 0 to 60, like it usually happens in most books. Even though they did have an instant connection, they didn't come together right away and I loved that! This aspect of the book was very realistic. Decisions were made that kept them apart and essentially, life happened. I completely understood Leos reasons for not jumping head first into a relationship with Nora. In many ways, he was just as broken as she was, and simply put, it wasn't their time yet.

I HAVE to mention one specific scene at around 68 or 69%. HOLY CRAP, BATMAN!

This was a lesson in clarity, Leo

Ha! WAS IT EVER!!! I was seriously fanning myself!!!!! WOW!!!!!!!!! Go Nora! I was truly amazed by this scene. *wink*
Overall, I have to say, I LOVED LEO AND NORA!!! Loved them individually and even more so, together. Their chemistry was so intense, I felt it.

We are everlasting. F**cking forever. I love you so much.

This book was wonderfully written. Ilsas writing style flowed smoothly and allowed me to connect completely. The secondary characters were just as interesting as Nora and Leo.  Sebastian, Mila, Teddy, Cuba, and even Drew loved them. I really liked the fact that we got a few scenes with them -- enough to actually know them as characters. I absolutely hated Noras mom, Finn and Tiffani-with-an-i. Ugh! HATED THEM! But they sure did cause some drama Ha. Did they
Im super happy with how Very Bad Things ended. I feel like the whole book was a build up -- the angst, the waiting, the wanting  and it was all worth it. Of course, I want to see more of Nora and Leo, but Im sure we will in the other books.
Very Bad Things made its way to my favorites pile so I HIGHLY RECOMMEND you read it.

 I promised myself that no matter what happened in the future, no matter the rough patches we might come across, Id never give up on us. Fate had known all along we were soulmates. Now, I did too.
profile.summary: If you study someone long enough, youll find out their secrets.

top_5.description: I'm a book nerd turned writer who loves the 'Hap-pily Ever After' mixed with a bit of suspense, drama, and the occasional cliffhanger! My love of books has brought me on my writing journey. I began writing my first book in July 2012 and since that time I have created 2 series. The first series 'The Reunion Series' debuted in November 2012 and two books followed. My new series 'The Shore Series debuted in March 2014 and claimed Amazon Best Selling status shortly after the release of the first book in the series. There will be continuations of the Shore Series and you never know when a secret project from me may pop up!
top_5.reviewText:
"I wanted to hang on to thirty-nine forever and I was fully prepared to do so."

You know a book is truly wonderful when you instantly - fully - connect to the main character and the plot. I fell in love with 39 & Holding from the very first page. I laughed (full on belly-laugh), swooned, squirmed, sighed....... I LOVED it.

MR Joseph's writing style was so damn natural and realistic!!! The things the heroine, Greer, said and thought??? OMG!! Hilarious!!! I've said and thought those things at least once throughout my life!! I will even go on and say that I'm sure most women have too! They may deny it, but come on!! They soooo have - especially when dealing with an ex!!!

Getting over a divorce isn't always a piece of cake, especially when infidelity is a factor, and MR Joseph did an AMAZING job developing this throughout the book. Greer's life changed in a matter of minutes when she came across a very eye-opening email in her husband's inbox. Suffice it to say, her marriage ended. At 39 years old, she found herself divorced with two kids.

"My dear, love isn't measure in length of time. All that counts is when you feel it, grab it. Time is nothing but numbers on a clock."

Enter Dr. Doughnuts. Nick...oh, Nick. SO YUMMY! My goodness, he was perfect!!!! He definitely changed Greer's life in more ways than one. He was exactly what she needed. She actually started living - all thanks to him. I loved reading her reactions to all the emotions and situations that came along with dating and falling in love, especially when she had sworn she wouldn't go through any of this just to avoid the risk of getting hurt...again. Greer's internal battles/dialogue and conversations with her friends were SO realistic and at times, hilarious! It was all very well written and thought out. Mad props to the author! You see, Greer didn't just give herself fully to Nick. She had to think about her kids, her life, and other factors (read the book and you will know what I mean) before actually going for it. So like I said, MR Joseph really did a wonderful job in developing their relationship and characters realistically.

"There's not many imperfect things about you, Greer, but the things that are, they're the things I love the most."

This was truly a wonderful read that I enjoyed from start to finish (LOVED the ending!!!!). It was sassy, funny, hot, and at times, even emotional. I would definitely recommend this book to anyone that loves a good and light romance with some very sexy spice! FIVE STARS!!

"The unexpected things  are the gifts we should cherish the most."
top_5.summary: realistic, funny, and sexy!

She graduated from the University of Central Florida with a B.S. in Psychology and a M.S. in Criminal Justice. She currently resides in Nevada and spends her time with her Air Force husband, three young daughters, dog, and cat. She loves to travel and see family and friends whenever she gets a chance. She has a love of music, movies, and anything that can make her laugh. AJ believes in reading books with humor and mystery that end in a happily ever after to help ease our minds and hearts of lifes daily struggles. For updates on new releases, and to connect with AJ Renee follow her on Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and Goodreads: @/ajreneeauthor. AJ would love to hear from you! You can email her at: ajreneeauthor@gmail.com. Go to www.AJRenee.com to sign-up for her newsletter.
top_5.reviewText:
This series keeps getting better and better! Seriously. Problems and situations seem to be getting more emotional and I am LOVING it. From the other two books in this series, I knew Jesse and Jamie Lynn had a past together, so I was curious to learn just what had happened that caused them to part ways when they so clearly loved each other.

Jamie Lynn had her fair share of issues that made her who she was now. She was a bit closed off but she had her reasons. Very valid reasons. And Jesse? Well, his story was a bit heart-breaking. When both main characters are broken, there is a lot of room for emotional angst and if you've been reading my blog for some time now, then you know that makes me super happy!

In order to move forward, Jesse and Jamie Lynn had to overcome a lot of insecurities and outside forces that were standing in the way of their own happily ever after. The road there was very interesting, angsty, sexy, and it had my full attention the entire time.

Now, to say I want the next book would be an understatement. It will be Rocco's book and I am beyond intrigued! You see, AJ Renee sure loves teasing her readers!

FIVE STARS!
top_5.summary: Best one in the series so far!

top_5.description: Cassandra doesnt remember a time when she wasnt writing. In fact, the first time she was published was when she was seven years old and won a contest to be published in an American Girl Doll novel. Since then Cassandra has written more novels than she can count and put just as many in the circular bin. Her personal goal with her writing is to show the reader the characters stories through their dialogue and actions instead of just telling the reader what is happening. She writes various genres but is most well known for her New Adult novels in various sub-genres including contemporary romance, and speculative fiction. In addition to being a published author, Cassandra is a full-time successful financial marketer. When shes not making the characters in her head come to life she either has her bow and arrows or long board skateboard in hand. Shes happily married to the man of her dreams and they live in the rolling hills of New England with their daughter Hope and their dogs, Bubski and Kanga. You can find her at: Instagram and Twitter: @cgiovanniauthor Facebook.com/cassiegiovanni Goodreads Don't forget to sign up for her newsletter for the latest book news!
top_5.reviewText:
4.5 Stars! Between unpacking (we bought a house!) and the holidays, my reading time SUFFERED...greatly. Much to my dismay, it took me quite a bit longer to finish reading this book. Boo, I know!! But finally, after sneaking in some much needed and overdue reading time, I finished!

I must say, I really enjoyed Danny and Sky's *heartwarming* story. From their teenage years, they shared an intense and undeniable connection that would undoubtedly withstand the test of time. I knew it. Their chemistry only got stronger as the years passed and while they both had deep scars, they only brought them closer. They bonded even more. While situations caused Danny to not be there for Sky at a very crucial and heartbreaking time, he was there to help her heal. And in many ways, she was as well for him.

One of the things I love most about Cassandra's writing is how she not only tells us a story, but she shows us one. She creates storylines and secondary characters that bring everything full circle...that bring a book to life. You can't help but feel emotionally invested in these different journeys and root for happy endings. I was walking alongside the characters through every up and down, twist and turn. I've noticed that always happens while I'm reading one of Ms. Giovanni's novels.

I cannot wait to see more of these characters! Seriously! Joey, Aaron, Zack-Such great guys! Funny, witty, sexy, down to earth, and completely realistic and relatable. They were my "brothers" too! One other thing I loved about them was that while they were in a band and they'd gotten pretty famous, there wasn't any made up or unnecessary drama that's usually involved in books with musicians. Issues within this book went beyond drama. They were real, heartbreaking situations that brought all of the characters together.

All in all, a great read and one I recommend you pick up!
top_5.summary: Great story, as always!!

top_5.description: Brandy L Rivers is a New York Times and USA Today bestselling author. She is kept busy writing the Others of Seattle, Others of Edenton, Combustible, and the Pine Barrens Pack series. An avid reader, Brandy has always loved writing. top_5.reviewText:
MY FAR MY FAVORITE INSTALLMENT IN THE SERIES!!
Erik.
Man, what a swoony guy!!!! I loved, loved, loved him and I absolutely LOVED how much he loved Monique. He did anything for her, even if it meant putting himself in not-so-pleasant situations. I loved his parents too and Monique's dad. Her mom? Meh. Not so much! She got on my last nerve! Not that I could blame her for the attitude and hatred she seemed to feel all the time towards mages, but ughshe pissed me off a lot! I found myself telling her time and time again to back off!

The dead people part of this story was slightly (not-so-slightly) creepy!! I can't imagine living with that gift like Erik did...but he was pretty bad-ass!

There's suspense, drama, action, hotness, and everything a must-read paranormal romance novel should have! Brandy L Rivers truly hit a home-run with DEADLY DESIGN. FIVE STARS!

Lilley
top_5.reviewText: I really enjoyed reading this book.  Even though it had very steamy, kinky , BDSM sex scenes, the book wasn't solely based on that. It definitely went beyond it and the plot was very interesting.  The characters were very well developed throughout the whole book. input: Generate the review text written by a reviewer who has a given an overall rating of "4.0" for a product with description "InterDesign's Classico Sinkware Collection is stylish and functional. This Dish Drainer has a compact design - perfect for small spaces! It holds up to 12 dishes and is made of steel with a rust resistant coating.". The summary of the review text is "Great space saver, but needs more flexibility".
output:
It's not perfectit doesn't handle bowls well or other deep itemsbut this compact dish rack by InterDesign is much more efficient than my previous, standard-size model. It allows the dish rack to function as part of the sink, rather than as a standalone item, and in the process, it frees up a lot of counter space.

Heres the problem: Its really optimized for plates. Consider, how many people are looking for a small dish rack to accommodate 12 plates and nothing else? A typical load for me is 1-2 plates, a frying pan, two glasses, two bowls, and a mug, plus utensils. In theory, this should easily fit the available space. In practice, it's not so easy. Bowls will not fit upright; they must be placed at the sides, where they lay flat and take up over half the rack. This seriously reduces available space. Drinking glasses can be placed in the center or, slightly more awkwardly, along the sides, where their stability is less certain (like the bowls). My frying pan has a hard time fitting, again due to the narrowness of the gaps, though it can often be balanced against the plates.

Again, the overall size is great. And the utensil caddy is well-designed. But I think this rack could benefit from a retooling, to accommodate a fuller range of dishware. Perhaps wider gaps could be inserted towards the front, or maybe the existing design could be retrofitted with attachments (e.g., plastic inserts) to help accommodate larger or deeper items, in a more stable, efficient manner.

profile.description: 100% cotton canvas; heavy enzyme-washed; cotton webbing straps; front flap with antique brass turn-buckles; inside hanging zippered pocket; 12"W x 16"H x 3 1/2"D.
profile.reviewText:
These lightweight canvas field bags by Authentic Pigment are inexpensive and reasonably well-made, but they're not very practical, in my opinion. They lack structure, are not water resistant, and do not fully close or seal. The top flap is more than large enough that your stuff will be mostly protected, but never 100% completely, especially on the sides. Inside, there's a single, free-hanging 6.5" x 7" zippered pocket (shorter if you consider the zipper's positioning), which is just large enough for small items like a pen and pencil, post-its, USB drive, and such. The strap attaches at the back, not at the sides.

I'd forgotten how annoying it can be to walk with a large bag at one's side, bouncing against the body, moving back and forth, rubbing against clothes In general, it's so much easier to use a backpack instead; your possessions will be better protected and they'll stay out of your way, keeping your hands free. Every once in a while, a backpack feels like overkill, and this bag might come in handy. The problem is, it's one more possession to manage. Next thing you know, you'll find yourself using it in situations where it's not the best option and wishing you were using something else instead.
profile.summary: Reasonably well-made; not so practical

profile.description: Jack Kirby's Mister Miracle
profile.reviewText:
This is easily the weakest of the Fourth World titles, and I'm including Jimmy Olsen (which is actually fairly good!). It represents Part 2 of the Mister Miracle saga, issues #1118, and is a slim volume. By this point in time, the other Fourth World comicsNew Gods and The Forever Peoplehad been cancelled by DC, so there wasn't much for Kirby to do but soldier on with Mister Miracle as a solo book. The first issue here is decent, but things quickly devolve into some slap-dash plotting and storytelling. The 3-issue Shilo Norman (orphan protegé and judo expert) arc is thoroughly forgettable and juvenile. The last issue suddenly attempts to tie threads together and move the Fourth World plot forward with a quickie marriage between Scott Free and Big Barda, bringing together most of the major characters in the span of just 20 whirlwind pages. It's a bit bizarre, but also moving, depending on one's mood.

The art ain't bad at allKirby pencils with Royer inksbut the overall quality still seems a little below par, a little cartoonish. An interesting aspect is the approach to tonal shading, which differs from previous installments. The artist here tends to work in flat tones, with lots of light and mid-greys, using white as an accent color. It's a cool style. But after reading this, I kind of appreciated the more sculptural approach used in the first three volumes.

Bottom line: This *does* complete Kirby's original Fourth World series, but not in the way he intended, and there's little that feels essential about it. You'll almost certainly get much more out of the first 3 volumes: New Gods, Mister Miracle, and Forever People. The two Jimmy Olsen books (in color) that followed are also quite fun. I'd consider this book almost an afterthought, for completiststhough still worthwhile for fans of Kirby's artwork. Considering that DC put a wrench in his gears by cancelling the Fourth World series, to expect greatness here would be unrealistic. Everybody has their limits. (BTW, it's ironic that they chose to call this book "Jack Kirby's Fourth World"; it's mostly just a collection of Mister Miracle issues and kind of post-Fourth World. I imagine they did this to avoid calling it Mister Miracle, Vol. 2, because sequels tend to produce diminishing returns.)
profile.summary: Solid artwork, a little cartoonish; bland storytelling

profile.description: This attractively designed and practical bottle stopper produces a completely airtight and leak-proof seal. This package includes three bottle stoppers in assorted colors. Use it to re cork mineral water, wine, beer, champagne, vinegar, oil, and more. Insert the stopper into the bottle and press the lever to seal the bottle airtight.
profile.reviewText:
A good way to test a bottle stopper like this is to remove the foil or labeling from around the neck of an empty bottle, preferably a clear one. Insert the stopper, and then look at the seal or area of contact between the stopper and the bottle, all the way around.

Results for the Joie brand were pretty impressive: Nearly 1/4 of an inch, all around! For comparison, I tried the same test with some generic stoppers purchased at a liquor store years ago, and they were barely able to form a consistent seal, less than 1/16" at its widest. (In the past, I've used Zyliss stoppers; unfortunately, I don't have any of those around to compare.)

My first time using this stopper, I noticed it kept popping out slightly, seating itself at an angle. I was initially concerned by this, but it turns out to have been caused by my closing the stopper one-handed. The seal itself was just fine. A two-handed approach seems to work best: Hold the bottle with one hand, seating the stopper firmly in place with your thumb, while pushing down the lever with your other hand.
profile.summary: A solid seal! Test for yourself

profile.description: This true HEPA Filter captures 99.97% of airborne particles as small as 0.3 microns, including pollen, ragweed and other allergens, viruses, germs, dust mites, mold spores and cigarette smoke. Its AeraSafe antimicrobial treatment provides built-in protection from the growth of odor causing bacteria, mildew and fungi on the True HEPA filter. Compatible with Fellowes AeraMax 100 Air Purifier. With normal usage, it is recommended that you change your filter every 12 months to keep your air purifier running at peak performance. A filter change indicator on your Fellowes AeraMax 100 Air Purifier conveniently notifies you when it's time to replace your True HEPA filter.
profile.reviewText:
I've been having a "sewer gas" odor in my kitchen, following a sink repair made by our building's maintenance staffnot a putrid odor, per se, but the same smell as an open city manhole. I suspected a venting problem from within the wall and was able to get this confirmed by a city plumbing inspector, while maintenance staff were refusing to acknowledge the problem. In the meantime, while I wait for this to get sorted out, I had to try something to quell the odor and clean the air, and this seemed like a reasonable bet. Sadly, it doesn't seem effective in this case. Thinking about it, this filters particles, while my problem is apparently an odor seeping through the wall and may be more of a gas in its nature. That said, this is advertised as filtering an amazing range of pathogens, to the microscopic level, so it seemed worth trying.

I'm not saying this is defective or falsely advertised, just that it may not meet every challenge.
profile.summary: Not great for sewer gas!

profile.description: Includes origin of Dare Devil, Iron Man, Nick Fury, X-men, Silver Surfer
profile.reviewText:
This revised edition of Son of Origins, published by Marvel Comics in 1997, is a hot mess. Do yourself a favor and seek out the original edition instead (published in 1975 by Simon & Schuster).

To start with, the print quality is poor. The pages are thin and have a waxy feeling. The ink looks oily and reflectivesuper-saturated colors reduce legibility, and overprinting of black areas is extremely noticeableyet it's also unevenly absorbed by the paper. The result is spotted blacks that don't look black and flat colors that look mottled, as if printed on a paper towel.

Some of the best stories from the original edition were excised to make room for more modern stories representing the 80s and 90s. Stories that are now missing include Tales of Suspense #97 "The Coming of Whiplash!" and Daredevil #47 "Brother, Take My Hand!", both of which featured outstanding work by artist Gene Colan. The origin of S.H.I.E.L.D. in Strange Tales #135 with its memorable Jack Kirby artwork is also gone, as is the The Watcher's origin story. Stan Lee's original text is largely intact, but it now makes less sense in the context of this new edition, as there's no distinction made between the present tense that Stan was referring to back in 1975 versus the time period in which this revised edition was published.

A quick comparison of the covers of the two editions reveals a world of difference in visual style, and perhaps tells you all you need to know about this edition, one way or the other. Most of the older stories have been recolored in this volume, except for X-Men #1, which made the transition intact (aside from a blurry-looking cover). Silver Surfer #1 is an interesting case: Most of its pages are identical to the book's first edition, but a few apparently went missing, replaced by pages from a later reprint that make use of completely different, digital-age coloring techniques. Presumably, we weren't supposed to notice the difference.

One small point in favor of this edition: The clarity of the linework in Daredevil #1 is dramatically improved. Its digital recoloring is very effective in many ways but occasionally distracting and stylistically inappropriate. Some of the unique, old-fashioned shading techniques apparent in the first edition have been removed, for better or worse.
profile.summary: Oh, how the mighty have fallen!

profile.description: Use the Ek Tools circle scissor pro circle cutter to cut and draw circles from 1-inch to 6-inch diameter. Rotating disc is marked in 1/16-inch increments. Blade shuttle rotates with disc for smooth function and attaches to edge for storage. Replacement blades store in shuttle handle. Includes circle cutter, blade shuttle and 3 replacement blades.
profile.reviewText:
On first impression, this tool seemed incredibly easy to use, but its cuts were not nearly as clean as I expected. On 80lb cardstock, it tended to produce a rough edge, with a tail or burr where the blade cut a slightly different path on its return pass. This happened consistently. It might be an issue with too much tolerance in the rotation of the circular guide mechanism, or perhaps a shift in the blade's cutting angle. To keep a steady angle, it's probably essential to bear down firmly while cutting, so that the shuttle remains fully seated in its marker position and the blade is fully unsheathed.

This was my second circle cutter; my first was an OLFA compass (CMP-1). Although the compass produced a clean edge and a consistent path, aligning it to the center of a print design was nearly impossible. This is where the Circle Scissor Pro excels. Alignment is made easy thanks to perpendicular axes printed onto the transparent cutting guide. Just align these to a centerpoint or corresponding axes on your print design, and you're ready to go. The guide should keep your material firmly in place as you cut; if there's any doubt, just tape down a few corners beforehand.

The rough edges are a problem, though, and I'm currently wondering what I can do to fix this. Specifically, I wonder if EKTools has ever considered including a small glass cutting mat with this? The Circle Scissor Pro is a very bulky tool in terms of its storage profile, and yet there's plenty of unused room within its packaging. Adding a suitable cutting mat might help ensure better results from the start. Glass seems to be recommended; a self-healing mat (what I've been using) may not be the best choice for this type of blade setup.
profile.summary: Easy to use, but slightly rough cuts
